text: The authors propose a general mechanism for robust adaptation: when the modification and reverse-modification rates depend solely on the system activity A and not explicitly on the concentrations of modified/unmodified enzyme — realized when the modifying enzyme R works at saturation and the demodifying enzyme B acts only on the active form — the steady-state activity Ast is set by the enzymes' maximal velocities and Michaelis constant and is independent of the ligand level, making adaptation insensitive to parameter values such as enzyme concentrations.

quotes.quote: A mechanism for robust adaptation, on the other hand, can be obtained when the rates of the modiﬁcation and the reverse-modiﬁcation reactions depend solely on the system activity, A, and not explicitly on the concentrations Em and E.
With such activity-dependent kinetics, the value of the steady-state activity, Ast, is independent of the ligand level, therefore the system is adaptive.

In this way, the system always returns to its steady-state value of activity, exhibiting adaptation. Moreover, with these activity-dependent kinetics, the adaptation properties is insensitive to the values of system parameters (such as enzyme concentrations), so adaptation is robust.
Robust adaptation is achieved when R works at saturation and B acts only on the active form of Em.

text: In this mechanism the steady-state activity itself is not a robust property: it depends on the enzyme concentrations, so the system's activity can be tuned on long timescales (e.g. by changing expression levels of the modifying enzymes) while adaptation is preserved on shorter timescales.

quotes.quote: Note, however, that the steady-state activity itself, which is not a robust property of the network, depends on the enzyme concentrations. Thus, the mechanism presented here still provides a way to control the system activity on long timescales, for example by changing the expression level of the modifying enzymes while preserving adaptation itself on shorter timescales.

b1 subunit downregulation in

text: Transgenic mice with mutations in the leucine zipper domain of PKG that disrupt the PKG-MYPT1 interaction had vascular smooth muscle less sensitive to NO-mediated vasodilatation and were hypertensive compared with control littermates.

quotes.quote:
produced a transgenic mouse with mutations in the LZ
domain of PKG, which disrupts the interaction of PKG
with MYPT1. Compared with control littermates, the
vascular smooth muscle isolated from these mice were
less sensitive to NO-mediated vasodilatation, and thus
these mice were hypertensive.

experiment.system: Transgenic mice with PKG leucine zipper domain mutations versus control littermates
experiment.perturbation: Mutation disrupting PKG-MYPT1 interaction
experiment.measurement: NO-mediated vasodilatation of isolated vascular smooth muscle and blood pressure

text: Transgenic mice expressing only the LZ+ MYPT1 isoform are more sensitive to NO-mediated relaxation and are hypotensive compared with wild-type littermates.

quotes.quote:
transgenic mice
expressing only the LZ+ MYPT1 isoform are more
sensitive to NO-mediated relaxation and hypotensive
compared with WT littermates

experiment.system: Transgenic mice expressing only LZ+ MYPT1 versus wild-type littermates
experiment.perturbation: Forced expression of only the LZ+ MYPT1 splice isoform
experiment.measurement: Sensitivity to NO-mediated relaxation and blood pressure

text: Tra-2b binds E23 and transactivates E23 splicing (exon inclusion) to generate the LZ- MYPT1 isoform, while deletion or mutation of the Tra2b binding site abolished E23 splicing to produce LZ+ MYPT1; in an animal model of portal hypertension Tra-2b is downregulated coincident with decreased LZ+ MYPT1 expression and a shift to LZ- isoforms.

quotes.quote:
These investigators demonstrated
both that Tra-2b binds to E23 and transactivates E23
splicing (exon inclusion) to generate a LZ2 MYPT1
isoform and deletion or mutation of the Tra2b binding
site abolished E23 splicing (exon exclusion) to produce a
LZ+ MYPT1.

in an animal model of portal hypertension,
Tra-2b is downregulated coincident with the decrease in
LZ+ MYPT1 expression (E23 exon exclusion) and the
shift to the expression of LZ2 MYPT1 isoforms

experiment.system: Smooth muscle MYPT1 pre-mRNA splicing; animal model of portal hypertension
experiment.perturbation: Tra-2b binding-site deletion/mutation, Tra-2b siRNA knockdown, portal hypertension induction
experiment.measurement: E23 exon inclusion/exclusion and LZ+/LZ- MYPT1 expression

text: In heart failure, p42/44 MAP kinase is activated and LZ+ MYPT1 expression decreases, while losartan therapy prevents p42/44 MAP kinase activation and preserves LZ+ MYPT1 expression; both ACE inhibitors and ARBs preserve LZ+ MYPT1 expression and sensitivity to NO-mediated vasodilatation.

quotes.quote:
further losartan therapy prevents the ... of p42/44 MAP kinase and preserves LZ+ MYPT1
expression

For the
treatment of heart failure, both ACE inhibitors (Chen
et al., 2006; Chen and Brozovich, 2008) and ARBs
(Ararat and Brozovich, 2009) have been demonstrated
to preserve both LZ+ MYPT1 expression and the
sensitivity to NO-mediated vasodilatation

experiment.system: Animal models of heart failure
experiment.perturbation: Heart failure induction with ACE inhibitor, ARB (losartan) treatment
experiment.measurement: p42/44 MAP kinase activation, LZ+ MYPT1 expression, and NO-mediated vasodilatation

text: In heart failure trials, ACE inhibitors reduced mortality in white patients but showed no benefit in black patients, in whom the combination of hydralazine and isosorbide dinitrate reduced mortality.

quotes.quote:
ACE inhibitors
reduced mortality in white patients, whereas in black
patients, although ACE inhibitors did not show a
benefit, treatment with the combination of hydralazine
and isosorbide dinitrate reduced mortality

experiment.system: Patients with heart failure (V-HeFT trial analysis, white vs black patients)
experiment.perturbation: Treatment with ACE inhibitors/enalapril versus hydralazine plus isosorbide dinitrate versus placebo
experiment.measurement: Mortality

text: Selective inhibition of TRPM4 decreased the stretch-induced transient inward cation current, and inhibition of Src nonreceptor tyrosine kinases decreased myogenic tone; TRPC6 inhibitors and blocking antibodies attenuated stretch-induced TRPM4 current activation.

quotes.quote:
Gonzales et al. (2014) demonstrated
that selective inhibition of TRPM4 decreased the tran-
sient inward cation current induced by membrane
stretch.

both TRPC6
inhibitors and antibodies that bind to an extracellular
epitope of TRPC6, which block TRPC6 currents, atten-
uated the stretch-induced activation of TRPM4 current.

These investigators also demonstrated that the inhibi-
tion of Src nonreceptor tyrosine kinases, which signal
through PLCg, decreased myogenic tone.

experiment.system: vascular smooth muscle / resistance arteries with myogenic tone
experiment.perturbation: pharmacologic inhibition of TRPM4, TRPC6 (inhibitors and blocking antibodies), and Src tyrosine kinases; membrane stretch
experiment.measurement: transient inward cation current, TRPM4 current, myogenic tone

text: Blocking integrin function with anti-integrin antibodies or integrin-specific peptides significantly inhibited the myogenic response.

quotes.quote:
Martinez-Lemus et al. demon-
strated that blocking integrin function with either anti-
integrin antibodies (Martinez-Lemus et al., 2005) or
integrin-specific peptides (Martinez-Lemus et al., 2003)
results in a significant inhibition of the myogenic
response.

experiment.system: resistance arteries
experiment.perturbation: anti-integrin antibodies or integrin-specific peptides
experiment.measurement: myogenic response

text: Serotonin stimulation produced Rho kinase-mediated MYPT1 phosphorylation and Ca2+ sensitization only in the presence of myogenic tone.

quotes.quote:
El-Yazbi et al. (2010)
demonstrated that only in the presence of myogenic
tone, serotonin stimulation produced a Rho kinase-
mediated phosphorylation of MYPT1, which induced a
Ca2+ sensitization of the contractile filaments.

experiment.system: pressurized arteries with myogenic tone
experiment.perturbation: serotonin stimulation, with/without myogenic tone
experiment.measurement: MYPT1 phosphorylation, Ca2+ sensitization

text: Pyk2 inhibition did not change the rapid rise in force and RLC phosphorylation after KCl depolarization, but depressed RLC phosphorylation, Thr-696 and Thr-850 MYPT1 phosphorylation, and force during the sustained phase.

quotes.quote:
although
the inhibition of Pyk2 did not change the rapid increase
in force and RLC phosphorylation in response to KCl
depolarization, Pyk2 inhibition did depress RLC phos-
phorylation, Thr-696, and Thr-850 MYPT1 phosphory-
lation and force during the sustained phase of the
contraction (Mills et al., 2015)

experiment.system: smooth muscle
experiment.perturbation: Pyk2 inhibition during KCl depolarization
experiment.measurement: force, RLC and MYPT1 (Thr-696, Thr-850) phosphorylation

text: Nonmuscle myosin expression represents approximately 10–15% of total myosin in smooth muscle.

quotes.quote:
In smooth muscle, NM myosin expression represents
;10–15% of total myosin (Yuen et al., 2009; Konik et al.,
2013).

experiment.system: smooth muscle tissue
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: NM myosin as fraction of total myosin

numbers.quantity: NM myosin fraction of total myosin

text: In optical tweezers, SM myosin crossbridge displacement occurs in successive steps of 4 and 2 nm, and the duration of the 4-nm phase increases twofold with negative strain and decreases twofold with positive strain.

quotes.quote:
the displacement of the SM crossbridge
occurs in successive steps of 4 and 2 nm. The duration of
the first phase (4-nm displacement) is strain dependent,
increasing by twofold with a negative strain and de-
creasing by twofold with positive strain.

experiment.system: single smooth muscle myosin molecules
experiment.perturbation: applied strain in optical tweezers
experiment.measurement: displacement step size and phase duration

text: NM RLC phosphorylation promotes NM myosin filament assembly and produces a 10-fold increase in the Vmax of the NM myosin actin-activated ATPase.

quotes.quote:
NM RLC
phosphorylation promotes NM myosin filament assem-
bly (Kolega, 2003) and also results in a 10-fold increase
in the Vmax of the NM myosin AMATPase (Cremo et al.,
2001)

experiment.system: nonmuscle myosin in vitro/nonmuscle cells
experiment.perturbation: NM RLC phosphorylation
experiment.measurement: filament assembly; Vmax of actin-activated ATPase

text: During KCl depolarization both SM and NM RLC phosphorylation increased independently of Rho kinase or PKC, whereas with angiotensin II, Rho kinase or PKC inhibition blunted SM RLC phosphorylation but only Rho kinase regulated NM RLC phosphorylation.

quotes.quote:
During KCl de-
polarization of smooth muscle, both SM RLC and NM
RLC phosphorylation increase, and the increase in RLC
phosphorylation is not dependent on either Rho kinase
or PKC (Yuen et al., 2009). However for angiotensin II
(Ang II) activation, inhibition of either Rho kinase or
PKC blunted SM RLC phosphorylation, whereas only a
Rho kinase-dependent pathway regulated NM RLC
phosphorylation (Yuen et al., 2009).

experiment.system: smooth muscle tissue
experiment.perturbation: KCl depolarization or Ang II with Rho kinase or PKC inhibition
experiment.measurement: SM and NM RLC phosphorylation

text: Bladder smooth muscle from mice lacking smooth muscle myosin still contracts, but with a slow tonic response rather than the rapid phasic contraction of wild type, and the force produced by NM myosin in KO tissues is low.

quotes.quote:
Morano et al. (2000) showed that bladder smooth
muscle from transgenic mice lacking smooth muscle
myosin still contract, albeit with a very slow tonic
response, as opposed to the rapid phasic contraction
(with transient peaks in force and Vmax) characteristic
of wild-type bladder smooth muscle

The force produced by NM
myosin in KO tissues is low (Lofgren et al., 2003)

experiment.system: mouse bladder smooth muscle
experiment.perturbation: transgenic knockout of smooth muscle myosin
experiment.measurement: force, contraction kinetics, Vmax

text: Blebbistatin inhibition of the NM actin-activated ATPase reduced force maintenance without affecting the rapid rise in force in phasic smooth muscle, and force maintenance was depressed by 25% in smooth muscle of heterozygous NMIIB KO mice versus wild type.

quotes.quote:
the inhibition of the NM
AMATPase with blebbistatin reduced force mainte-
nance (Rhee et al., 2006); for phasic smooth muscle,
blebbistatin did not affect the rapid rise in force, but
decreased maintained force

when compared
with WT control mice, force maintenance is depressed
by 25% in smooth muscle of heterozygous NMIIB KO
(Yuen et al., 2009)

experiment.system: phasic and tonic smooth muscle; heterozygous NMIIB KO mice
experiment.perturbation: blebbistatin treatment; NMIIB heterozygous knockout
experiment.measurement: peak force and maintained force

numbers.quantity: force maintenance depression in NMIIB het KO

text: For carbachol activation of guinea pig ileum, Rho kinase inhibition did not affect peak force but decreased force maintenance.

quotes.quote:
Sward et al. (2000)
demonstrated for carbachol activation of guinea pig
ileum that inhibition of Rho kinase did not affect peak
force but decreased force maintenance

experiment.system: guinea pig ileum smooth muscle
experiment.perturbation: Rho kinase inhibition during carbachol activation
experiment.measurement: peak force and force maintenance

text: Deletion of the BK channel b1 subunit in mice lowered BK channel open probability 100-fold, impaired the BK current response to Ca2+ sparks, and produced cerebral arteries more constricted at all pressures with resulting hypertension.

quotes.quote:
Brenner et al. (2003) deleted the b1
subunit of the BK channel in mice and demonstrated
that, compared with controls, the open probability of BK
channels was 100-fold lower and the BK current in
response to Ca2+ sparks was impaired in vascular
smooth muscle from the b1 KO animals. Furthermore,
myography demonstrated that cerebral arteries from
the b1 KO animals mice were more constricted at all
pressures, which resulted in hypertension in these
animals.

experiment.system: mice with BK channel b1 subunit deletion
experiment.perturbation: genetic deletion of BK b1 subunit
experiment.measurement: channel open probability, BK current, arterial myography, blood pressure

numbers.quantity: BK open probability in b1 KO

text: Smooth muscle-specific Gq-G11 ablation completely blocked phenylephrine and Ang II contraction and lowered blood pressure, whereas G12-G13 ablation left phenylephrine/serotonin dose-responses and baseline blood pressure unchanged but reduced steady-state force to Ang II, endothelin, vasopressin and U46619; ablation of either attenuated DOCA-salt hypertension.

quotes.quote:
In aortic smooth muscle iso-
lated from the Gq-G11 KO mice, the contractile response
to both phenylephrine and Ang II was completely
blocked, whereas the response to serotonin, endothelin,
vasopressin, and the thromboxane analog U46619 was
inhibited. Ablation of G12-G13 had no effect on the dose-
response relationship for phenylephrine or serotonin,
but it reduced the steady-state force produced by Ang II,
endothelin, vasopressin, and U46619.

blood pressure was no differ-
ent in the mice with ablation of G12-G13, but signifi-
cantly lower in the Gq-G11 KO mice

ablation of either Gq-G11 or
G12-G13 attenuated the increase in blood pressure pro-
duced by DOCA-salt treatment

experiment.system: mice with smooth muscle-specific ablation of Gq-G11 or G12-G13
experiment.perturbation: conditional gene ablation; agonist stimulation; DOCA-salt treatment
experiment.measurement: aortic contractile force, blood pressure

text: eNOS disruption in mice eliminated ACh-mediated aortic relaxation while leaving sodium nitroprusside relaxation unchanged, resulting in hypertension.

quotes.quote:
the
disruption eNOS has been demonstrated to eliminate
ACh-mediated relaxation of aortic smooth muscle rings,
and as would be predicted, the relaxation produced by
sodium nitroprusside was no different in eNOS KO and
WT animals. This defect in vascular reactivity resulted
in hypertension in the eNOS KO mice (Huang et al.,
1995).

experiment.system: eNOS knockout mice
experiment.perturbation: genetic disruption of eNOS
experiment.measurement: aortic ring relaxation to ACh and SNP; blood pressure

text: PKGI KO mice were hypertensive; aortic rings showed normal contractile agonist responses but significantly attenuated ACh- and 8Br-cGMP-mediated relaxation, and 8Br-cGMP failed to attenuate the NE-induced Ca2+ transient in PKGI KO cells.

quotes.quote:
PKGI KO mice were hypertensive
compared with WT littermates (Pfeifer et al., 1998).
These investigators demonstrated compared with WT,
that although the response to contractile agonist was
not different in aortic rings from the PKGI KO, ACh-
and 8Br-cGMP-mediated relaxation was significantly
attenuated. Further preincubation of aortic cells with
8Br-cGMP attenuated the Ca2+ transient in response to
NE in WT aortic smooth muscle cells, but had no effect
on the Ca2+ transient in the PKGI KO aortic smooth
muscle cells.

experiment.system: PKGI knockout mice and aortic smooth muscle cells
experiment.perturbation: PKGI gene knockout; ACh, 8Br-cGMP, NE
experiment.measurement: blood pressure, ring relaxation, Ca2+ transients

text: PKG phosphorylation of RGS-2 translocated it from cytosolic to particulate fractions and decreased Gaq GTPase activity; RGS-2 KO mice showed increased agonist-induced force, reduced NO vasodilation, and elevated blood pressure.

quotes.quote:
They demonstrated that phosphorylation of RGS-2 by
PKG resulted in a translocation of RGS-2 from the
cytosolic to particulate fractions and decreased Gaq
GTPase activity.

agonist-induced force production
was increased and the vasodilatory response to NO was
reduced in aortic smooth muscle from RGS-2 KO mice,
and the resulting increase in vascular tone (relative
vasoconstriction) was responsible for the increase in
blood pressure in RGS-2 KO mice compared with WT
littermates (Tang et al., 2003)

experiment.system: RGS-2 KO mice and aortic smooth muscle; biochemical PKG assays
experiment.perturbation: RGS-2 knockout; PKG phosphorylation of RGS-2
experiment.measurement: RGS-2 subcellular fractionation, Gaq GTPase activity, force, NO vasodilation, blood pressure

text: A knock-in mouse in which the initial four leucine/isoleucine residues of PKGIa were replaced by alanine, disrupting MYPT1 interaction, had aortic rings less sensitive to ACh- and 8Br-cGMP-mediated relaxation and developed hypertension.

quotes.quote:
Michael et al. (2008)
produced a knock-in mouse in which the initial four
leucine/isoluecine residues of PKGIa were replaced by
alanine. This PKGIa LZ mutant does not interact with
MYPT1 (Surks and Mendelsohn, 2003), and as would be
predicted, when compared with WT, aortic rings iso-
lated from the PKGIa LZ mutant were less sensitive to
ACh- and 8Br-cGMP-mediated relaxation, which pro-
duced hypertension.

experiment.system: PKGIa leucine zipper mutant knock-in mice
experiment.perturbation: knock-in replacing four leucine/isoleucine residues with alanine
experiment.measurement: aortic ring relaxation sensitivity, blood pressure

text: Conditional MYPT1 KO mice were hypertensive with increased RLC phosphorylation and force to KCl and agonists, yet the sensitivity of NO/cGMP-mediated relaxation was similar to controls.

quotes.quote:
Qiao et al. (2014) produced a
conditional MYPT1 KO, which were hypertensive com-
pared with WT controls.

resulted in an increase
in the phosphorylation of the RLC as well as force in
response to both KCl depolarization and contractile
agonists. However, surprisingly, the sensitivity of re-
laxation produced by NO/cGMP signaling was similar in
the control and MYPT1 KO mice.

experiment.system: conditional MYPT1 knockout mice, mesenteric arteries
experiment.perturbation: conditional MYPT1 deletion; KCl and agonist stimulation, NO/cGMP
experiment.measurement: blood pressure, RLC phosphorylation, force, relaxation sensitivity

text: Estrogen decreased PE-induced aortic contraction in WT but not iNOS KO mice; estrogen receptor b KO mice showed reduced PE contractile response with unchanged sodium nitroprusside sensitivity, yet developed hypertension.

quotes.quote:
Estrogen was found to
decrease PE-induced contraction of aortic smooth mus-
cle in WT, but not iNOS KO mice.

In vascular rings from estrogen
receptor b KO mice, compared with WT mice, the
contractile response to PE was reduced

The sensitivity of smooth muscle
relaxation to sodium nitroprusside was similar in
estrogen receptor b KO and WT animals. Nonetheless,
in the estrogen receptor b KO animals, the abnormal-
ities in vascular tone produced hypertension.

experiment.system: WT, iNOS KO, and estrogen receptor b KO mice, aortic rings
experiment.perturbation: gene knockouts; estrogen treatment; PE and SNP
experiment.measurement: contractile response, relaxation sensitivity, blood pressure

text: Antisense knockdown of vimentin in smooth muscle inhibits agonist-induced force development.

quotes.quote:
antisense knockdown of vimentin
in smooth muscle inhibits agonist-induced force devel-
opment (Tang, 2008)

experiment.system: smooth muscle
experiment.perturbation: antisense knockdown of vimentin
experiment.measurement: agonist-induced force development

text: Knockout of dystrophin in a mouse model decreases contractility of tracheal rings.

quotes.quote:
Knockout of dystrophin in a mouse model decreases
contractility of tracheal rings (Sharma et al., 2014).

experiment.system: mouse tracheal rings
experiment.perturbation: dystrophin knockout
experiment.measurement: contractility

text: A decline in G-actin content occurs with pressurization or agonist activation of cerebral resistance arteries, increasing contractility without detectable myosin or actin phosphorylation, and is blocked by Rho kinase and PKC inhibitors.

quotes.quote:
Moreno-Dominguez et al. (2014) have reported that a
decline in G-actin content occurs in response to pres-
surization or agonist activation of cerebral resistance
arteries, resulting in an increase in contractility in the
absence of detectable myosin or actin phosphorylation
that could be blocked by Rho kinase and PKC inhibitors.

experiment.system: cerebral resistance arteries
experiment.perturbation: pressurization or agonist activation; Rho kinase and PKC inhibitors
experiment.measurement: G-actin content, contractility, myosin/actin phosphorylation

text: In vascular smooth muscle, phenylephrine increased the overall F/G actin ratio about twofold with a statistically significant polymerization increase only for gamma nonmuscle actin, whereas a phorbol ester produced significant remodeling only of beta nonmuscle actin.

quotes.quote:
found that the overall F/G ratio
increases by about twofold in response to the alpha
agonist phenylephrine, but only gamma nonmuscle
actin displays a statistically significant increase in
polymerization. Interesting, in response to a phorbol
ester, 12-deoxyphorbol 13-isobutyrate 20-acetate, only
beta nonmuscle actin showed significant evidence of
remodeling.

experiment.system: vascular smooth muscle
experiment.perturbation: phenylephrine or phorbol ester (12-deoxyphorbol 13-isobutyrate 20-acetate) stimulation
experiment.measurement: actin isoform F/G ratios

numbers.quantity: overall F/G ratio increase with phenylephrine

text: In contractile vascular smooth muscle cells, zyxin and VASP but not FAK undergo Src-dependent endosomal processing during vasoconstrictor stimulation and regulate vascular contractility and stiffness.

quotes.quote:
Zyxin and vasodilator-stimulated phosphopro-
tein (VASP), but notably not FAK, undergo Src-dependent
endosomal processing and regulate, through processes not
yet fully understood, vascular contractility and stiffness
(Poythress et al., 2013).

experiment.system: contractile vascular smooth muscle cells
experiment.perturbation: vasoconstrictor stimulation; Src dependence
experiment.measurement: focal adhesion protein trafficking, contractility, stiffness

text: Inhibition of actin polymerization prevented agonist-induced inward remodeling of resistance vessels.

quotes.quote:
inhibition of actin polymerization prevented the
agonist-induced inward remodeling of the resistance
vessels (Staiculescu et al., 2013)

experiment.system: resistance vessels
experiment.perturbation: vasoconstrictor agonist with actin polymerization inhibition
experiment.measurement: inward remodeling

text: Smooth muscle-specific deletion of EPHB4 decreased contractile responses to phenylephrine and produced hypotension in male but not female mice, whereas EPHB6 deletion did not alter blood pressure in either sex but elevated blood pressure and enhanced phenylephrine contraction in castrated males.

quotes.quote:
the smooth muscle-specific deletion of
the tyrosine kinase EPHB4 was demonstrated to result in
decreased contractile responses to the agonist phenyl-
ephrine and hypotension in male, but not female, mice
(Wang et al., 2015). Contrasting with these results are
those demonstrating that blood pressure was unaffected
by deletion of the tyrosine kinase EPHB6 in male and
female mice, but blood pressure was elevated and the
contractile response to phenylephrine was enhanced in
castrated male EPHB6 KO mice

experiment.system: EPHB4 smooth muscle-specific KO and EPHB6 KO mice
experiment.perturbation: genetic deletion; castration; phenylephrine
experiment.measurement: contractile response, blood pressure

text: Under optimally physiologic conditions, up to 50% of maximal ex vivo aortic stiffness is observable only after activating VSMCs with an alpha agonist and eliminating NO-mediated vasodilation.

quotes.quote:
Under optimally
physiologic conditions for smooth muscle viability, up to
50% of maximal ex vivo aortic stiffness is observable
only after activating VSMCs by alpha agonist and
eliminating NO-mediated vasodilation (Gao et al.,
2014b)

experiment.system: ex vivo aortic tissue
experiment.perturbation: alpha agonist activation of VSMCs plus elimination of NO-mediated vasodilation
experiment.measurement: aortic material stiffness

numbers.quantity: fraction of maximal ex vivo aortic stiffness requiring VSMC activation

text: Disruption of the FAK-Src signaling complex reduces contractility, stiffness, and biochemical markers of focal adhesion signaling induced by smooth muscle activation, and these mechanisms are defective with aging.

quotes.quote:
disruption of the
FAK-Src signaling complex reduces contractility and
stiffness, as well as biochemical markers of focal
adhesion signaling, induced by smooth muscle activa-
tion (Saphirstein et al., 2013; Saphirstein and Morgan,
2014). Interestingly, these mechanisms are defective
with aging (Gao et al., 2014b)

experiment.system: stimulated vascular smooth muscle / aorta
experiment.perturbation: disruption of FAK-Src signaling complex; aging comparison
experiment.measurement: contractility, stiffness, focal adhesion signaling markers

text: Overexpression of SIRT1 in VSMCs modulated blood pressure by downregulating the Ang II type 1a receptor gene, and resveratrol activated SIRT1 to repress that gene and counteract Ang II-induced hypertension in mice.

quotes.quote:
Overexpression of SIRT1 in VSMCs has been found to
modulate blood pressure by downregulation of the Ang
II type 1a receptor gene (Miyazaki et al., 2008). More-
over, resveratrol treatment activated SIRT1, resulting
in the repression of Ang II type 1a receptor gene
transcription to counteract Ang II-induced hyperten-
sion in mice (Miyazaki et al., 2008).

experiment.system: mice / VSMCs
experiment.perturbation: SIRT1 overexpression; resveratrol treatment; Ang II
experiment.measurement: AT1a receptor gene expression, blood pressure

text: Ang II infusion decreased SIRT1 expression in mouse aorta with increased blood pressure and vascular remodeling, and a VSMC-specific SIRT1 transgene attenuated both.

quotes.quote:
Ang II infusion significantly
decreased the expression of SIRT1 in mouse aorta, which
was associated with increased blood pressure and ele-
vated vascular remodeling. Importantly, a VSMC-specific
SIRT1 transgene attenuated both Ang II-induced in-
creases in blood pressure and vascular remodeling
(Gao et al., 2014a).

experiment.system: mice with VSMC-specific SIRT1 transgene
experiment.perturbation: Ang II infusion; SIRT1 transgene
experiment.measurement: aortic SIRT1 expression, blood pressure, vascular remodeling

text: Smooth muscle-specific Dicer knockout induced embryonic lethality with hemorrhaging, loss of contractile function and reduced VSMC proliferation; inducible SMC-specific Dicer knockdown reduced blood pressure without cardiac dimension change, impaired receptor- and calcium-mediated contraction of small mesenteric arteries, and reduced contractile protein expression.

quotes.quote:
Knockout of
Dicer in vascular smooth muscle (VSM) induced embry-
onic lethality, which was associated with widespread
hemorrhaging, loss of contractile function, and reduced
VSMC proliferation (Albinsson et al., 2010).

Blood pressure was reduced after Dicer
knockdown, with no change in cardiac dimensions. This
was associated with impairment of both receptor- and
calcium-mediated contraction of small mesenteric ar-
teries and reduction of expression of contractile proteins
(Albinsson et al., 2011).

experiment.system: smooth muscle-specific Dicer KO mice (constitutive and tamoxifen-inducible)
experiment.perturbation: Dicer knockout/knockdown
experiment.measurement: viability, blood pressure, mesenteric artery contraction, contractile protein expression

text: Myogenic tone of mesenteric arteries was abolished in Dicer KO mice, associated with loss of calcium influx through the L-type calcium channel.

quotes.quote:
Myogenic tone of mesenteric arteries was abolished
from Dicer KO mice, which was associated with a loss of
calcium influx through the L-type calcium channel
(Bhattachariya et al., 2014).

experiment.system: Dicer KO mouse mesenteric arteries
experiment.perturbation: smooth muscle Dicer knockout
experiment.measurement: myogenic tone, L-type calcium channel calcium influx

text: miR-190 expression was augmented in PASMCs of the hypoxic rat; transfection of pulmonary arterial rings with a miR-190 mimic enhanced vasoconstriction to potassium chloride and phenylephrine, and miR-190 downregulated the potassium channel Kv7.5, raising intracellular calcium.

quotes.quote:
The expression of miR-190 was augmented in
PASMCs of the hypoxic rat, which acts as a model for
pulmonary hypertension. Vasoconstriction to both po-
tassium chloride and phenylephrine was enhanced after
transfection of pulmonary arterial rings with a miR-190
mimic. The same study demonstrated that miR-190
downregulates the protein expression of the potassium
channel Kv7.5, which results in raised intracellular
calcium in PASMCs (Li et al., 2014b).

experiment.system: hypoxic rat pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells and arterial rings
experiment.perturbation: hypoxia; miR-190 mimic transfection
experiment.measurement: miR-190 expression, vasoconstriction, Kv7.5 protein, intracellular calcium

text: miR-328 directly targets the a1C subunit of the L-type calcium channel and was reduced in pulmonary artery from patients with pulmonary hypertension.

quotes.quote:
The miR-328 has
been demonstrated to directly target the a1C subunit of
the L-type calcium channel and was reduced in the
pulmonary artery from patients with pulmonary hyper-
tension, thus enabling an increase in vasoconstriction
(Guo et al., 2012).

experiment.system: pulmonary artery tissue from PH patients; target assays
experiment.perturbation: observational (disease vs control) plus miR-328 targeting
experiment.measurement: miR-328 levels, L-type calcium channel a1C subunit

text: A SNP rs12731181 (A to G) in the prostaglandin F2a receptor was more prevalent in hypertensive Chinese individuals and reduces miR-590-3p binding, increasing receptor expression and enhancing prostaglandin-mediated VSMC contractility.

quotes.quote:
A further study in a
Chinese population identified the SNP rs12731181 (A
to G) in the prostaglandin F2a receptor that was more
prevalent in hypertensive individuals (Xiao et al., 2015).
This polymorphism reduces the likelihood of miR-590-
3p binding, thus increasing prostaglandin F2a receptor
expression and enhancing prostaglandin-mediated con-
tractility of VSMCs (Xiao et al., 2015).

experiment.system: Chinese population cohort; VSMCs
experiment.perturbation: observational genotype association plus miR-590-3p binding analysis
experiment.measurement: SNP prevalence, receptor expression, contractility

text: Anti-miR-145 therapy using the Star:Star-mPEG delivery system reduced the severity of pulmonary hypertension without significant off-target effects in rats with Sugen-5416/hypoxia-induced PAH.

quotes.quote:
anti-miR-145 ther-
apy in rats with Sugen-5416/hypoxia-induced pulmonary
arterial hypertension (PAH) using the Star:Star-mPEG
delivery system, reduced the severity of pulmonary
hypertension
without
significant
off-target
effects
(McLendon et al., 2015).

experiment.system: rats with Sugen-5416/hypoxia-induced PAH

Receptors with known ligands
197
15
12
0
11
Orphans
87 (54)a

experiment.system: human GPCR gene families (Classes A, B, C, Adhesion, Frizzled)
experiment.perturbation: observational — expert curation and tabulation of receptor family membership
experiment.measurement: receptor counts per family split by known-ligand, orphan and sensory categories

numbers.quantity: Class A receptors with known ligands

text: The Frizzled family consists of 10 Frizzled proteins (FZD1-10) and Smoothened (SMO), and the Secretin family is encoded by 15 genes in humans whose ligands are polypeptide hormones of 27-141 amino acid residues, nine of the mammalian receptors responding to structurally related ligands.

quotes.quote: Frizzled family consists of 10 Frizzled proteins (FZD1‐­10) and Smoothened (SMO).

Secretin family, encoded by 15 genes in humans. The ligands for receptors in this family are polypeptide hormones of 27‐­141 amino acid residues; nine of the mammalian receptors respond to ligands 
that are structurally related to one another

experiment.system: human Frizzled and Secretin (Class B) GPCR families
experiment.perturbation: observational — sequence/genomic classification under the GRAFS scheme
experiment.measurement: gene counts and ligand peptide length ranges

text: Adhesion GPCRs are defined by a large extracellular region linked to the 7TM region by a GPCR autoproteolysis-inducing (GAIN) domain of ~320 residues containing a GPCR proteolysis site (GPS); the GAIN domain is an ancient motif also found in PKD1-like proteins and has been suggested to be both required and sufficient for autoproteolysis.

quotes.quote:
at a conserved “GPCR proteolysis site” (GPS) which lies within a much larger (∼320 residue) "GPCR autoproteolysis‐­inducing" (GAIN) domain, which in terms of evolution is an ancient motif also found 
in polycystic kidney disease 1 (PKD1)‐­like proteins, which has been suggested to be both required and sufficient for autoproteolysis [2288].

experiment.system: Adhesion class GPCRs and PKD1-like proteins
experiment.perturbation: observational — structural/domain and phylogenetic analysis reviewed from the literature
experiment.measurement: domain architecture assignment and residue length of the GAIN domain

text: Among 5-HT receptors, RNA editing is described as unique amongst the GPCRs in producing 5-HT2C receptor isoforms that differ in function, such as efficiency and specificity of coupling to Gq/11 and also pharmacology.

quotes.quote:
Unique amongst 
the GPCRs, RNA editing produces 5‐­HT2C receptor isoforms that 
differ in function, such as efficiency and specificity of coupling 
to Gq/11 and also pharmacology [241, 3052].

experiment.system: human 5-HT2C receptor isoforms generated by RNA editing
experiment.perturbation: observational — comparison of edited receptor isoforms reported in the cited literature
experiment.measurement: efficiency and specificity of Gq/11 coupling and pharmacological profile

text: The human 5-HT1B receptor displays a different pharmacology to rodent forms of the receptor, attributed to Thr335 of the human sequence being replaced by Asn in rodent receptors.

quotes.quote:
the human 5‐­HT1B receptor (tabulated) displays a different 
pharmacology to the rodent forms of the receptor due to Thr335 
of the human sequence being replaced by Asn in rodent receptors 
[1040].

experiment.system: human versus rodent 5-HT1B receptors
experiment.perturbation: observational — cross-species sequence comparison of a single residue (Thr335 → Asn)
experiment.measurement: ligand binding pharmacology (pKi/KD) at the receptor

text: Lysergic acid (LSD) and ergotamine show a strong preference for arrestin recruitment over G protein coupling at the 5-HT2B receptor, with no such preference evident at 5-HT1B receptors; DHE (dihydroergocryptine), pergolide and cabergoline also show significant preference for arrestin recruitment over G protein coupling at 5-HT2B receptors.

quotes.quote:
Lysergic acid (LSD) and ergotamine show a strong preference 
for arrestin recruitment over G protein coupling at the 5‐­HT2B re-
ceptor, with no such preference evident at 5‐­HT1B receptors, and 
they also antagonise 5‐­HT7A receptors [2965]. DHE (dihydroergo-
cryptine), pergolide and cabergoline also show significant prefer-
ence for arrestin recruitment over G protein coupling at 5‐­HT2B 
receptors [2965].

experiment.system: 5-HT2B and 5-HT1B receptors
experiment.perturbation: stimulation with ergoline ligands (LSD, ergotamine, dihydroergocryptine, pergolide, cabergoline)
experiment.measurement: comparison of arrestin recruitment versus G protein coupling responses

text: All five (M1-M5) muscarinic acetylcholine receptors are ubiquitously expressed in the human body, with M1, M3, and M5 preferentially coupling to Gq/11 proteins whilst M2 and M4 predominantly couple to Gi/o proteins.

quotes.quote:
All five (M1‐­M5) mAChRs are ubiquitously expressed in the hu-
man body and are therefore attractive targets for many disorders. 
Functionally, M1, M3, and M5 mAChRs preferentially couple to 
Gq/11 proteins, whilst M2 and M4 mAChRs predominantly cou-
ple to Gi/o proteins.

experiment.system: human muscarinic acetylcholine receptor subtypes M1-M5
experiment.perturbation: observational — curated summary of expression and G protein coupling studies
experiment.measurement: tissue expression and preferential G protein coupling assignment

text: Structures of all five mAChRs bound to antagonists show that the orthosteric binding site of this receptor family is absolutely conserved, which the authors state explains why highly selective orthosteric ligand binding to any specific mAChR has been notoriously difficult to achieve.

quotes.quote:
Atomic structures for all five mAChRs bound to an-
tagonists have been determined [1012, 2736, 2807, 2962, 3173].

These structures show that the orthosteric 
binding site of this family of receptor is absolutely conserved and, 
as a consequence, explain why highly selective orthosteric ligand 
binding to any specific mAChR has been notoriously difficult to 
achieve.

experiment.system: M1-M5 muscarinic acetylcholine receptors
experiment.perturbation: structure determination with bound antagonists and agonists (crystallography/cryo-EM)
experiment.measurement: atomic structure of the orthosteric binding pocket compared across subtypes

text: Crystal and cryo-EM structures have been solved for all four adenosine receptors, and the A2A receptor is used as a workhorse in GPCR structure elucidation with almost 100 structures available in the Protein Data Bank.

quotes.quote:
Crystal and cryo‐­EM structures 
for all four adenosine receptors have been solved, occupied by 
either agonists (sometimes in the presence of an allosteric modu-
lator) or antagonists.

The A2A receptor is used as a workhorse in GPCR structure 
elucidation: almost 100 structures are available in the Protein 
Data Bank (www.rcsb.org).

experiment.system: adenosine receptors A1, A2A, A2B, A3
experiment.perturbation: structure determination with bound agonists, antagonists or allosteric modulators
experiment.measurement: count of deposited experimental structures in the Protein Data Bank

numbers.quantity: A2A receptor structures in the PDB

text: A pseudogene exists for the A2B adenosine receptor (ADORA2BP1) with 79% identity to the A2B adenosine receptor cDNA coding sequence, but which is unable to encode a functional receptor.

quotes.quote:
A pseudogene ex-
ists for the A2B adenosine receptor (ADORA2BP1) with 79% iden-
tity to the A2B adenosine receptor cDNA coding sequence, but 
which is unable to encode a functional receptor [1258].

experiment.system: human ADORA2BP1 pseudogene and ADORA2B cDNA
experiment.perturbation: observational — sequence comparison and expression analysis
experiment.measurement: percent sequence identity and functional receptor expression

numbers.quantity: sequence identity to A2B cDNA coding sequence

text: Antagonists at A3 adenosine receptors exhibit marked species differences, such that only MRS1523 and MRS1191 are selective at the rat A3 receptor, and in the absence of other adenosine receptors [3H]DPCPX and [3H]ZM 241385 can also be used to label A2B receptors (KD ca. 30 and 60 nM respectively).

quotes.quote:
Antagonists at A3 receptors exhibit marked species differences, 
such that only MRS1523 and MRS1191 are selective at the rat A3 
receptor. In the absence of other adenosine receptors, [3H]DPCPX 
and [3H]ZM 241385 can also be used to label A2B receptors (KD 
ca. 30 and 60 nM respectively).

experiment.system: rat and human adenosine A2B/A3 receptors
experiment.perturbation: application of antagonists and radioligands ([3H]DPCPX, [3H]ZM 241385) across species/subtypes
experiment.measurement: antagonist selectivity and radioligand dissociation constants (KD)

text: ADGRD1 is reported as a Gs protein-coupled receptor that also couples to Gi proteins, activated by Stachel-sequence peptides and by dihydrotestosterone, with 5-α-dihydrotestosterone regulating skeletal muscle strength through the receptor and the small molecule AP503 established as an ADGRD1-specific and Gs-biased agonist.

quotes.quote:
ADGRD1 a Gs protein‐­coupled receptor [246, 1670]. 5‐­α‐­dihydrotestosterone regulates 
skeletal muscle strength through the receptor. The same study establishes the small 
molecule agonist AP503 as an ADGRD1 specific and Gs‐­biased agonist [3171]. Couples 
also to Gi proteins [1671].

experiment.system: adhesion GPCR ADGRD1 (GPR133)
experiment.perturbation: stimulation with Stachel-derived peptides, dihydrotestosterone, PLXDC2 or the small molecule AP503
experiment.measurement: G protein coupling (Gs/Gi) signalling and skeletal muscle strength

text: ADGRG1 (GPR56) is described as a collagen-responsive platelet receptor sensing shear forces that couples to G13 proteins, with GAIN domain-mediated cleavage required for activation by its natural ligands and a small-molecule agonist; ADGRG1 deficiency in humans leads to bilateral frontoparietal polymicrogyria.

quotes.quote:
ADGRG1 (GPR56) is a collagen‐­responsive platelet receptor sensing shear forces 
[3181].

GAIN domain‐­mediated cleavage is required for activation of ADGRG1 by its 
natural ligands and a small‐­molecule agonist [3262].

ADGRG1 deficiency in humans 
leads to bilateral frontoparietal polymicrogyria [2239].

experiment.system: adhesion GPCR ADGRG1/GPR56 in platelets, human patients and heterologous systems
experiment.perturbation: collagen/shear force exposure, GAIN domain cleavage disruption, agonist application, and loss of receptor function
experiment.measurement: G13 pathway activation, receptor activation by ligands, and neurodevelopmental phenotype (polymicrogyria)

text: ADGRG6 (GPR126) couples to Gs and Gi/o pathways, is a key regulator of Schwann cell-mediated myelination, binds Laminin-211, and types VI and IV collagen are agonists with type VI exhibiting Gi-biased signalling; the prion protein is also an ADGRG6 agonist.

quotes.quote:
ADGRG6 (GPR126) is a key regulator of Schwann cell‐­mediated myelination [1945], 
and couples to Gs and Gi/o pathways [1670, 1931, 2229].

Types VI and IV collagen are agonists 
of ADGRG6 [1322, 3071], with type VI exhibiting Gi‐­biased signalling [1322]. The prion 
protein is an ADGRG6 agonist [1322].

experiment.system: adhesion GPCR ADGRG6/GPR126 and Schwann cells
experiment.perturbation: agonist application (collagen VI and IV, prion protein, Laminin-211, apomorphine) and conditional Adgrg6 deletion
experiment.measurement: Gs and Gi/o pathway signalling and myelination phenotypes

text: The previously described α1C-adrenoceptor is a species homologue corresponding to the pharmacologically defined α1A-adrenoceptor, and some tissues possess α1A-adrenoceptors (termed α1L-adrenoceptors) that display relatively low affinity for prazosin in functional and binding assays; α1A-adrenoceptor C-terminal splice variants form homo- and heterodimers and do not generate a functional α1L-adrenoceptor.

quotes.quote:
The pre-
viously described α1C‐­adrenoceptor is a species homologue that 
corresponds to the pharmacologically defined α1A‐­adrenoceptor 
[1123]. Some tissues possess α1A‐­adrenoceptors (termed α1L‐­
adrenoceptors [792, 1973]) that display relatively low affinity 
in functional and binding assays for prazosin indicative of dif-
ferent receptor states or locations. α1A‐­Adrenoceptor C‐­terminal 
splice variants form homo‐­ and heterodimers, and do not gen-
erate a functional α1L‐­adrenoceptor [2340].

experiment.system: α1-adrenoceptor subtypes in native tissues and heterologous expression systems
experiment.perturbation: expression of α1A C-terminal splice variants and application of prazosin
experiment.measurement: prazosin affinity in functional and radioligand binding assays; dimerisation

text: Recombinant α1D-adrenoceptors have been shown in some heterologous systems to be mainly located intracellularly, but cell-surface localization is encouraged by truncation of the N-terminus or by co-expression and heterodimer formation with α1B- or β2-adrenoceptors; in blood vessels all three α1-adrenoceptor subtypes are located both at the cell surface and intracellularly.

quotes.quote:
Recombinant α1D‐­
adrenoceptors have been shown in some heterologous systems 
to be mainly located intracellularly but cell‐­surface localiza-
tion is encouraged by truncation of the N‐­terminus, or by co‐­
expression and formation of heterodimers of with α1B‐­α1B‐­ or 
β2–β2‐­adrenoceptors [1014, 2879]. In blood vessels all three α1‐­
‐­adrenoceptor subtypes are located both at the cell surface and 
intracellularly [1878, 1879].

experiment.system: recombinant α1D-adrenoceptors in heterologous expression systems and native blood vessels
experiment.perturbation: N-terminal truncation and co-expression with α1B- or β2-adrenoceptors
experiment.measurement: subcellular localization (cell surface versus intracellular)

text: The structure of the α2B-adrenoceptor has been determined by cryo-EM in complex with dexmedetomidine and Gαo at a resolution of 2.9 Å.

quotes.quote:
The 
structure of the α2B‐­adrenoceptor has recently been determined 
by cryo‐­EM in complex with dexmedetomidine and Gαo at a reso-
lution of 2.9 Å providing insights into the structural requirements 
required for interactions with α2‐­adrenoceptor agonists [3204].

experiment.system: human α2B-adrenoceptor–Gαo complex
experiment.perturbation: complex formation with the agonist dexmedetomidine and Gαo
experiment.measurement: cryo-EM structure resolution

text: AT1 and AT2 angiotensin receptors have around 30% sequence similarity; AT1 receptors are predominantly coupled to Gq/11 but also recruit β-arrestins and stimulate G protein-independent β-arrestin signaling, and while most species express a single AGTR1 gene located on chromosome 3, two related Agtr1a and Agtr1b receptor genes are expressed in rodents.

quotes.quote: which have around 30% sequence similarity

AT1 receptors are predominantly coupled to Gq/11 
[599, 1350, 3223], however they also recruit β‐­arrestins and stim-
ulate G protein‐­independent β‐­arrestin signaling [1271, 1755, 
3213]. Most species express a single AGTR1 gene located on chro-
mosome 3, but two related Agtr1a and Agtr1b receptor genes are 
expressed in rodents.

experiment.system: AT1 and AT2 angiotensin receptors across species
experiment.perturbation: observational — sequence comparison and curated signalling assay results
experiment.measurement: percent sequence similarity, G protein and β-arrestin coupling, gene copy number

text: Expression of the X chromosome-linked AGTR2 gene is higher in females than males, and the AT2 receptor is much less abundant than the AT1 receptor in adult tissues and is upregulated in pathological conditions, counteracting several of the growth responses initiated by AT1 receptors.

quotes.quote:
Expression of the X chromosome‐­linked 
AGTR2 gene is higher in females than males [2468].

The AT2 receptor counteracts several of the 
growth responses initiated by AT1 receptors. The AT2 receptor is 
much less abundant than the AT1 receptor in adult tissues and 
is upregulated in pathological conditions.

experiment.system: adult tissues expressing angiotensin AT1 and AT2 receptors
experiment.perturbation: observational — comparison between sexes and between healthy and pathological conditions
experiment.measurement: AGTR2 gene expression level and receptor abundance relative to AT1; growth responses

text: An AT3 receptor was proposed based on cDNA isolated from a neuroblastoma cell line, but the guide states existence of a genuine AGTR3 gene and AT3 receptor are not confirmed at this time; there is however evidence for an AT4 receptor that specifically binds angiotensin IV and is located in the brain and kidney.

quotes.quote:
An AT3 receptor was proposed based 
on cDNA isolated from a neuroblastoma cell line, but existence 
of a genuine AGTR3 gene and AT3 receptor are not confirmed at 
this time. However, there is evidence for an AT4 receptor that 
specifically binds angiotensin IV (AGT, P01019) (AGT; P01019) 
and is located in the brain and kidney.

experiment.system: putative AT3 and AT4 angiotensin receptors in neuroblastoma cells, brain and kidney
experiment.perturbation: observational — cDNA isolation and angiotensin IV binding studies
experiment.measurement: gene identification and ligand binding/tissue localisation

text: The apelin receptor responds to apelin, a 36 amino-acid peptide derived initially from bovine stomach, with apelin-36, apelin-13 and [Pyr1]apelin-13 the predominant endogenous ligands cleaved from a 77 amino-acid precursor peptide, and the potency order for the heterologously expressed human apelin receptor is [Pyr1]apelin-13 ≥ apelin-13 > apelin-36 with pD2 values ranging from 9.5 to 8.6.

quotes.quote:
responds to apelin, 
a 36 amino‐­acid peptide derived initially from bovine stomach. 
Apelin‐­36 (APLN, Q9ULZ1), apelin‐­13 (APLN, Q9ULZ1) and [Pyr1]
apelin‐­13 (APLN, Q9ULZ1) are the predominant endogenous li-
gands which are cleaved from a 77 amino‐­acid precursor peptide
Comments: Potency order determined for heterologously expressed human apelin receptor (pD2 values range from 9.5 to 8.6).
[Pyr1]apelin‐­13 (APLN, Q9ULZ1) ≥apelin‐­13 (APLN, Q9ULZ1) > apelin‐­36 (APLN, Q9ULZ1) [748, 2798]

experiment.system: heterologously expressed human apelin receptor (APLNR)
experiment.perturbation: application of endogenous apelin isoforms (apelin-36, apelin-13, [Pyr1]apelin-13)
experiment.measurement: agonist potency (pD2) and rank order

text: The modified peptide apelin-13(F13A) was reported to block the hypotensive response to apelin in rat in vivo, however this peptide exhibits agonist activity in HEK293 cells stably expressing the recombinant apelin receptor.

quotes.quote:
A modified apelin‐­13 peptide, apelin‐­13(F13A) was reported to block the hypotensive response to apelin in rat in vivo [1600], 
however, this peptide exhibits agonist activity in HEK293 cells stably expressing the recombinant apelin receptor [748].

experiment.system: rat in vivo cardiovascular system and HEK293 cells stably expressing the recombinant apelin receptor
experiment.perturbation: administration of the modified peptide apelin-13(F13A)
experiment.measurement: hypotensive response in vivo and receptor agonist activity in vitro

text: The guide reports a potency order of endogenous bile acids at the GPBA receptor, with lithocholic acid most potent.

quotes.quote:
Potency order of endogenous ligands
lithocholic acid > deoxycholic acid > chenodeoxycholic acid, cholic acid

experiment.system: Human GPBA (GPBAR1) receptor
experiment.perturbation: observational (expert curation of published bile acid pharmacology)
experiment.measurement: rank potency order of endogenous ligands

text: Mammalian bombesin receptors comprise 3 subtypes (BB1, BB2, BB3) that couple primarily to the Gq/11 and G12/13 families of G proteins, with BB3 remaining an orphan receptor.

quotes.quote:
Mammalian bombesin (Bn) receptors comprise 3 
subtypes: BB1, BB2, BB3

The three Bn receptor subtypes 
couple primarily to the Gq/11 and G12/13 family of G proteins

BB3 is an 
orphan receptor, although some propose it is constitutively ac-
tive

experiment.system: Mammalian bombesin receptor subtypes
experiment.perturbation: observational (curation of receptor classification and coupling literature)
experiment.measurement: receptor subtype nomenclature and G protein coupling assignment

numbers.quantity: number of mammalian bombesin receptor subtypes

text: MK-5046 is reported to function as an allosteric agonist for hBRS-3, described as the first for any bombesin receptor, and cryo-EM structures of BRS3 with heterotrimeric Gq were reported bound to BA1 and to MK-5046.

quotes.quote:
A recent study [2336] shows that MK‐­5046 functions as an allosteric agonist for 
hBRS‐­3 (the first for any BnR).

reported the cryo‐­EM structures of BRS3 in complex with the heterotrimeric Gq protein in its active states: one bound to the pan‐­BnR agonist 
BA1 and the other bound to the synthetic BRS3‐­specific agonist MK‐­5046

experiment.system: Human BRS3 (BB3) receptor
experiment.perturbation: MK-5046 and BA1 agonist binding; complex formation with heterotrimeric Gq
experiment.measurement: allosteric agonist pharmacology and cryo-EM structure determination

text: Bradykinin B1 and B2 receptor selective antagonists are tabulated with affinities including icatibant (pKi 10.2) and deucrictibant (pKi 9.3) at B2, and B-9958 (pKi 9.2–10.3) at B1.

quotes.quote: icatibant (pKi 10.2) [55], deucrictibant (pKi 9.3) [1631, 1632]

experiment.system: Human bradykinin B1 and B2 receptors
experiment.perturbation: selective antagonist application
experiment.measurement: antagonist affinity (pKi)

text: Calcitonin family receptor phenotypes are generated by the genes CALCR and CALCRL together with three RAMPs (RAMP1, RAMP2, RAMP3), single TM domain proteins of ca. 150 amino acids.

quotes.quote:
are generated by the genes 
CALCR (which codes for the calcitonin receptor, CTR) and CAL-
CRL (which codes for the calcitonin receptor‐­like receptor, CLR

which are single TM domain proteins of ca. 150 amino 
acids, identified as a family of three members; RAMP1, RAMP2 
and RAMP3

experiment.system: Calcitonin/CGRP receptor family (CTR, CLR with RAMPs)
experiment.perturbation: observational (curation; RAMP co-expression alters receptor phenotype)
experiment.measurement: receptor complex nomenclature, gene assignment, RAMP protein size

text: Transfection of human CTR with any RAMP generates receptors with high affinity for both salmon calcitonin and amylin, and the guide notes AMY receptor pharmacology in transfected cells likely reflects a mixed receptor population including RAMP-free CTR.

quotes.quote:
most of this work has likely used 
a mixed population of receptors, encompassing RAMP‐­coupled 
CTR as well as CTR alone

Transfection 
of human CTR with any RAMP can generate receptors with a high 
affinity for both salmon calcitonin and amylin and varying affin-
ity for different antagonists

experiment.system: Cells transfected with human CTR and RAMPs
experiment.perturbation: co-transfection of CTR with RAMPs
experiment.measurement: radioligand binding affinity and functional responses to calcitonin/amylin

text: The CGRP receptor antagonist olcegepant is listed with pKi 10.7–11 and ubrogepant with pKB 10.8, while adrenomedullin-(22-52) at AM1 has pKi 7–7.8.

quotes.quote:
adrenomedullin‐­
(22‐­52) (human) (pKi 
7–7.8) [1075]

experiment.system: Human CGRP and AM1 receptors
experiment.perturbation: antagonist application
experiment.measurement: antagonist affinity (pKi/pKB)

text: The calcium-sensing receptor responds to divalent/trivalent cations, polyamines and polycations as agonists, while L-amino acids, glutamyl peptides, ionic strength and pH act as allosteric modulators, with L-amino acids identified as co-agonists requiring concomitant calcium binding for full activation.

quotes.quote:
While divalent/trivalent cations, polyamines and poly-
cations are CaS receptor agonists [322, 2318], L‐­amino acids, glu-
tamyl peptides, ionic strength and pH are allosteric modulators of 
agonist function

L‐­amino 
acids have been identified as "co‐­agonists", with both concom-
itant calcium and L‐­amino acid binding required for full recep-
tor activation

experiment.system: Human CaS receptor (CASR)
experiment.perturbation: application of cations, polyamines, L-amino acids, glutamyl peptides; varied pH and ionic strength
experiment.measurement: receptor activation/agonist sensitivity

text: The CaS receptor is reported to couple primarily to Gq/11, G12/13 and Gi/o, to act as a homodimer that can only couple one G protein at a time, and to form heteromers with GABAB and mGlu1/5 receptors.

quotes.quote:
The CaS receptor primarily couples to Gq/11, G12/13 and Gi/o [590, 
898, 1188, 2823], but in some cell types can couple to Gs [1799]. 
The CaS receptor acts as a homodimer [849, 3220], but which can 
only couple one G protein at a time

the 
CaS receptor can also form heteromers with Class C GABAB [427, 
463] and mGlu1/5 receptors [843]

experiment.system: CaS receptor in cellular expression systems
experiment.perturbation: observational (curation of G protein coupling and dimerisation studies)
experiment.measurement: G protein coupling profile and receptor oligomerisation

text: Loss-of-function CaS receptor mutations cause familial hypocalciuric hypercalcaemia or neonatal severe hyperparathyroidism, and Casr null mice exhibit similar increases in PTH secretion and blood calcium levels; gain-of-function mutations are associated with autosomal dominant hypocalcaemia and Bartter syndrome type V.

quotes.quote:
patients with loss‐­of‐­function CaS recep-
tor mutations who develop familial hypocalciuric hypercalcaemia 
(heterozygous mutations) or neonatal severe hyperparathyroidism

and in Casr null mice [426, 1138], which exhibit sim-
ilar increases in PTH secretion and blood calcium levels. Gain‐­of‐­
function CaS mutations are associated with autosomal dominant 
hypocalcaemia and Bartter syndrome type V

experiment.system: Human patients with CASR mutations and Casr null mice
experiment.perturbation: loss-of-function or gain-of-function CASR mutation / gene knockout
experiment.measurement: PTH secretion, blood calcium levels, clinical phenotype

text: Cannabinoid CB1 selective antagonists are tabulated with JD5037 (pKi 9.5) and rimonabant (pKi 7.9–8.7), while CB2 selective antagonists include SR144528 (pKi 8.3–9.2) and AM-630 (pKi 7.5).

experiment.system: Human CB1 and CB2 cannabinoid receptors
experiment.perturbation: selective antagonist application
experiment.measurement: antagonist affinity (pKi)

text: Chemerin, a chemoattractant protein and adipokine, is the endogenous ligand for both chemerin family receptors; Chemerin1 is also activated by resolvin E1, and GPR1 was renamed Chemerin2 upon de-orphanisation.

quotes.quote:
chemerin (RARRES2, Q99969), has been 
shown to be the endogenous ligand for both chemerin family receptors. Chemerin1 was the founding family member, and when GPR1 was de‐­orphanised it was re‐­named Chermerin2 [1375]. Chemerin1 
is also activated by the lipid‐­derived, anti‐­inflammatory ligand resolvin E1 (RvE1)

experiment.system: Human chemerin receptors CMKLR1 and CMKLR2
experiment.perturbation: observational (curation of ligand pairing studies)
experiment.measurement: endogenous ligand assignment and nomenclature

text: Chemokines are classified into four structural subclasses by cysteine number and spacing: CC (n= 28), CXC (n= 17), CX3C (n= 1) and C (n= 2).

quotes.quote:
CC (also known as β‐­chemokines; n= 28), CXC (also known as 
α‐­chemokines; n= 17) and CX3C (n= 1) chemokines all have four 
conserved cysteines, with zero, one and three amino acids separat-
ing the first two cysteines respectively. C chemokines (n= 2) have 
only the second and fourth cysteines found in other chemokines.

experiment.system: Human chemokine family
experiment.perturbation: observational (sequence-based structural classification)
experiment.measurement: number and arrangement of conserved cysteines; subclass membership counts

text: Many chemokine receptors function as HIV co-receptors, but CCR5 is stated to be the only one demonstrated to play an essential role in HIV/AIDS pathogenesis.

quotes.quote:
Many chemokine 
receptors function as HIV co‐­receptors, but CCR5 is the only one 
demonstrated to play an essential role in HIV/AIDS pathogene-
sis.

experiment.system: Human chemokine receptors and HIV-1
experiment.perturbation: observational (curation of HIV co-receptor literature)
experiment.measurement: assignment of co-receptor role in HIV/AIDS pathogenesis

text: Three chemokine receptor antagonists plus the CXCR4 antagonist mavorixafor are noted as FDA-approved: maraviroc (CCR5) for HIV/AIDS, plerixafor (CXCR4) for stem cell mobilization, mogamulizumab (CCR4 blocking antibody) for mycosis fungoides or Sezary syndrome, and mavorixafor for WHIM syndrome.

quotes.quote:
Three chemokine receptor antagonists have now 
been approved by the FDA: 1) the CCR5 antagonist maraviroc 
(Pfizer) for treatment of HIV/AIDS in patients with CCR5‐­using 
strains; and 2) the CXCR4 antagonist plerixafor (Sanofi) for he-
matopoietic stem cell mobilization

and 3) the 
CCR4 blocking antibody Poteligeo (mogamulizumab‐­kpkc, Kyo-
wa Kirin, Inc.) for mycosis fungoides or Sezary syndrome; and the 
CXCR4 antagonist mavorixafor for WHIM syndrome.

experiment.system: Human chemokine receptors CCR5, CCR4, CXCR4

text: In the global structure of E. coli and yeast transcription networks, FFLs and SIMs are integrated into DORs that occur in a single layer with no DOR at the output of another DOR, and long regulatory cascades are rare, most genes being regulated one step from their activator.

quotes.quote:
This 
kind of arrangement shows that FFLs and SIMs are inte-
grated into the DORs. The DORs occur in a single layer: 
there is no DOR at the output of a second DOR.

long regula-
tory cascades are rare55; most genes are regulated just one 
step away from their activator

experiment.system: Transcription networks of E. coli and yeast
experiment.perturbation: observational (compact motif-based network representation)
experiment.measurement: Layer structure and cascade length statistics

text: The mapped Bacillus subtilis sporulation network is composed of interlocked C1-FFLs and I1-FFLs whose delay and pulse functions generate a three-wave temporal programme: a pulse of Z1, then a pulse of Z2, then late Z3 expression.

quotes.quote:
The network that regulates 
this process8 includes several transcription factors that 
are arranged in linked C1-FFLs and I1-FFLs (FIG. 7c).

The result is a 
three-wave temporal pattern: first a pulse of Z1 expres-
sion, followed by a pulse of Z2 expression, followed by 
expression of the ‘late’ Z3 genes

experiment.system: Bacillus subtilis sporulation transcription network
experiment.perturbation: Starvation signal Sx activating Spo0A (X1)
experiment.measurement: Temporal waves of gene expression for gene groups Z1, Z2, Z3

text: Network motifs appear to have arisen largely by convergent rather than conservative evolution: homologous output genes in different organisms are regulated by FFLs whose regulators X and Y are generally non-homologous, sometimes belonging to different transcription factor families.

quotes.quote:
If the two FFLs had a 
common-ancestor FFL, the regulators X and Y in these 
systems would also be homologous. However, this is 
generally not the case. The sequence of the regulators 
is sometimes so different that they are classed into com-
pletely different transcription factor families.

experiment.system: Transcription networks of multiple organisms
experiment.perturbation: observational (cross-species comparison of regulators of homologous genes)
experiment.measurement: Sequence homology of regulators X and Y in corresponding motifs

text: Transcription networks rewire rapidly on evolutionary timescales — only a few mutations remove a regulator binding site and lose a network arrow — so even closely related organisms living in different environments often use different network motifs to regulate a given gene.

quotes.quote:
it takes 
only a few mutations to remove the binding site of a regu-
lator in a given promoter, and thereby lose an arrow in a 
network70,71. Hence, even closely related organisms often 
have different network motifs to regulate a given gene, 
provided that they live in different environments, as was 
demonstrated by Babu et al.72.

experiment.system: Prokaryotic transcriptional regulatory networks across related species
experiment.perturbation: observational (comparative analysis across species/environments)
experiment.measurement: Presence/absence of regulatory arrows and motifs for given genes

text: Composite negative-feedback loops combining a transcriptional arm and a protein–protein interaction arm, such as p53–Mdm2, appear much more common than purely transcriptional negative-feedback loops, and such loops embedded in additional interactions can generate oscillations in individual living cells.

quotes.quote:
Experiments on individual living 
cells have shown that negative-feedback loops, 
embedded within additional interactions, can sometimes 
generate oscillations, whereby the levels of X and Y rise 
and fall79–82.

experiment.system: Integrated transcription-regulation and protein–protein interaction networks; individual living cells (e.g. p53–Mdm2)
experiment.perturbation: observational network motif detection; stress/DNA-damage stimulation in single-cell experiments
experiment.measurement: Motif abundance counts; time-lapse protein level dynamics

text: Signal-transduction (protein modification) networks display FFLs plus motifs absent from transcription networks such as the diamond, which combine into multi-layer perceptron motifs of three or more layers of signalling proteins.

quotes.quote:
Signal-transduction networks show feedforward loops (FFLs), as well as motifs that are not present in 
transcription networks, such as the diamond pattern. Diamonds combine to form multi-layer perceptron motifs that 
are composed of three or more layers of signalling proteins89.

experiment.system: Protein modification / signal-transduction networks
experiment.perturbation: observational (motif detection versus randomized networks)
experiment.measurement: Subgraph pattern counts (diamonds, perceptrons, FFLs)

text: Neuronal synaptic networks exhibit motifs: cortical circuitry harbours FFL-connected neuron triplets, the fully mapped C. elegans synaptic network shows FFLs, diamonds, multi-layered perceptrons and two-neuron feedback loops, and mammalian networks show significant motifs assayed by electrical measurements of neuron tetrads.

quotes.quote:
Cortical circuitry harbours 
triplets of neurons that are connected as FFLs93.

The fully mapped synaptic 
network of Caenorhabditis elegans95 shows motifs including FFLs7, diamonds and multi-layered perceptrons89,96, as well 
as two-neuron feedback loops97. Mammalian neuronal networks also display significant network motifs98, as assayed 
using electrical measurements of neuron tetrads99.

experiment.system: Synaptic connection networks (cortex, C. elegans, mammalian local cortical circuits)
experiment.perturbation: observational (anatomical/electrophysiological connectivity mapping)
experiment.measurement: Motif counts in synaptic connectivity graphs; electrical recordings of neuron tetrads

text: Cytokine capture and microchip assays showed that T cells produce cytokines at a constant rate while they are producing.

quotes.quote:
cytokine capture and microchip 
assays15 have shown that T cells produce cytokines at a constant rate while they are 
producing16

experiment.system: T cells
experiment.perturbation: observational (activated T cells assayed)
experiment.measurement: single-cell cytokine capture and microchip assays of per-cell secretion rate

text: Cytokines bound to receptors are endocytosed at a typical rate of 1 to 5 molecules per hour, which allows receptor abundance measured by quantitative FACS to be used to estimate cytokine consumption rate.

quotes.quote:
Cytokine receptor abundance 
can be used to estimate the rate of cytokine consumption, as cytokines bind to receptors 
according to well-characterized biophysical models and are endocytosed at a typical rate of 
1 to 5 molecules per hour14.

experiment.system: cytokine-consuming immune cells
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: quantitative fluorescence-activated cell sorting of surface cytokine receptor abundance and endocytosis rate

text: Numerical integration of the reaction–diffusion equation for cytokines predicted sharp spatial gradients and substantial leakage of cytokine outwards from a T cell immunological synapse, permitting paracrine signaling.

quotes.quote:
Extensive numerical integration has shown that the solution of this equation generically 
could produce sharp spatial gradients in cytokine concentration8.

one can expect substantial leakage of the cytokine outwards 
from the synapse, which would enable paracrine signaling between cells

experiment.system: computational model of cytokine diffusion, production and consumption in three dimensions
experiment.perturbation: numerical integration of the partial-differential equation across parameters
experiment.measurement: predicted spatial cytokine concentration profiles/gradients

text: With leukocyte radius rcell ≈ 5–10μm and cytokine diffusion coefficient Dcytokine ≈ 100 μm2/sec, the timescale above which cells can be treated as point sources in a continuous cytokine field is about 1s.

quotes.quote:
where rcell is the radius of the leukocyte 
(rcell ≈ 5–10μm) and Dcytokine is the diffusion co-efficient for the cytokine in solution 
(typically, Dcytokine ≈ 100 μm2/sec), as confirmed in a recent experimental study17.

τcontinuous ∝

verdict_note: Claim text and numbers match the paper (rcell 5-10 um, D ~100 um2/sec, tau ~1s), but the experiment field asserts a specific methodology ('microfluidic optical imaging of cytokine diffusion in live lymph node tissue') that the excerpt does not contain; the paper says only 'as confirmed in a recent experimental study17'.

experiment.system: cytokine diffusion in tissue/solution
experiment.perturbation: observational; analytical scaling estimate with parameters confirmed by microfluidic optical imaging of cytokine diffusion in live lymph node tissue
