text: Ex vivo and in vivo experiments validated the diffusion–consumption theory, with the cytokine communication length scale λcytokine ranging from 100 μm early in an immune response down to only a few μm when consuming cells are numerous or clustered around producers.

quotes.quote:
This theoretical result was 
validated experimentally ex vivo and in vivo, with λcytokine ranging from 100 μm (at the 
beginning of an immune response when few cells consume the cytokine of interest) down to 
only a few μm (when cytokine-consuming cells are generated and/or are clustered around 
cytokine-producing cells)16.

experiment.system: dense lymphoid tissue ex vivo and in vivo
experiment.perturbation: varying the number/density of cytokine-consuming cells
experiment.measurement: spatial range (length scale) of cytokine propagation and signaling

text: In an engineered yeast strain secreting and sensing α factor, changing secretion rate, receptor level, extracellular degradation rate and feedback strength together with decreasing cell density switched populations from autocrine to bimodal to global paracrine activation, with heterogeneous secrete-and-sense responses at the cellular scale (< 500 μm) and a homogeneous field at the systems-wide scale (> 500 μm).

quotes.quote:
By engineering a yeast strain to secrete and sense a 
small protein (α factor), the authors of this study built a tunable system with which to 
explore all configurations of cell-to-cell communication.

resulted in 
populations of cells switching from autocrine activation, to bimodal (both autocrine and 
paracrine) activation to global (paracrine) activation, specifically when these parameters 
were changed in conjunction with decreasing cell densities.

the cellular scale (< 500 μm), whereby secrete-and-sense responses are 
heterogeneous, and the systems-wide scale (> 500 μm), whereby the cytokine field is 
homogenous

experiment.system: engineered yeast strain secreting and sensing α factor
experiment.perturbation: tuning secretion rate, receptor level, extracellular degradation rate, positive feedback strength and cell density
experiment.measurement: population-level activation mode (autocrine/bimodal/global) and spatial scales of response

text: In NK cells, secretion of the cytolytic granule protein perforin was polarized whereas secretion of IFNγ and TNF was multidirectional.

quotes.quote:
a comparison of secretion of the cytolytic granule protein 
perforin and the cytokines IFNγ and TNF showed that they have polarized and
multidirectional secretion mechanisms, respectively36.

experiment.system: natural killer cells forming synapses with targets
experiment.perturbation: observational comparison of granule versus cytokine secretion
experiment.measurement: directionality of secretion by imaging

text: In an in vivo model of T cell activation, CD4+ T cells within homotypic clusters captured IL-2 and phosphorylated STAT5 more efficiently than T cells in isolation.

quotes.quote:
The study showed that T cells that are part of a homotypic 
cluster capture IL-2 and phosphorylate STAT5 more efficiently than do T cells in isolation.

experiment.system: in vivo animal model of CD4+ T cell activation
experiment.perturbation: comparison of clustered versus isolated T cells
experiment.measurement: IL-2 capture and STAT5 phosphorylation

text: In vitro imaging of activated TH cells revealed two directionally distinct cytokine secretion pathways: IL-2, IFNγ and IL-10 were secreted synaptically, whereas TNF, IL-4 and CCL4 were secreted multidirectionally.

quotes.quote:
The study showed direct synaptic secretion of IL-2, interferon-γ (IFNγ) and IL-10, 
whereas tumor necrosis factor (TNF), IL-4 and CC-chemokine ligand 4 (CCL4) were 
secreted in a multidirectional manner39.

experiment.system: activated T helper cells conjugated with APCs in vitro
experiment.perturbation: observational, per-cytokine comparison
experiment.measurement: imaging of secretion directionality

text: In mice infected with Heligmosomoides polygyrus or Toxoplasma gondii, there was ubiquitous phosphorylation of STAT6 or STAT1, respectively, in immune cells throughout the reactive lymph nodes, implying saturated JAK–STAT signalling.

quotes.quote:
There was ubiquitous 
phosphorylation of signal transducer and activator of transcription 6 (STAT6) or STAT1, 
respectively, in immune cells throughout the reactive lymph nodes of these mice.

experiment.system: mouse lymph nodes
experiment.perturbation: infection with Heligmosomoides polygyrus or Toxoplasma gondii
experiment.measurement: in situ STAT6/STAT1 phosphorylation across lymph node

text: In CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes, IFNγ secretion was polarized towards the immunological synapse but its effects were not confined to the target cell, attributed to leakiness of the synaptic seal permitting activation of nearby cells.

quotes.quote:
a study in CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs) 
showed that although IFNγ secretion from CTLs was polarized towards the immunological 
synapse, its effects were not confined to the target cell alone35.

experiment.system: CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes with antigenic target cells
experiment.perturbation: observational, comparison of antigenic target versus bystander cells
experiment.measurement: IFNγ secretion directionality and IFNγ-induced responses in bystander cells

text: In an analytically solvable model of macrophage–fibroblast growth factor exchange, homeostatic stability required one cell population to be at carrying capacity, and only rapid endocytosis of cytokines greatly expanded the stable parameter range; the anchoring requirement did not expand for systems of three or four interacting cell types.

quotes.quote:
They showed that, to achieve homeostatic stability, 
one of the cell populations must be at carrying capacity

only the rapid 
endocytosis of cytokines could greatly expand the range of parameters whereby both 
symbiotic populations maintain stable numbers47

generalized 
this result to larger cell systems (with three or four interacting cell types) and showed that 
the need for anchoring conditions does not expand in larger systems

experiment.system: mathematical two-cell (macrophage–fibroblast) circuit exchanging CSF1 and PDGF, extended to three- and four-cell systems
experiment.perturbation: varying negative-feedback mechanisms (endocytosis, receptor adaptation, cross-inhibition) and parameters, and imposing carrying capacity
experiment.measurement: analytical/numerical stability of cell population numbers

text: At homeostasis approximately 6 × 1012 molecules of free EPO circulate in a normal human, at most one EPO molecule per erythrocyte given typically 20 trillion erythrocytes, a steady-state free EPO concentration typically 10-fold lower than that needed for a half-maximal response of primary colony-forming unit erythroid cells; circulating EPO increases by a factor of 100 during trauma-induced hypoxia.

quotes.quote:
EPO is typically 
maintained at a low level during homeostasis50–52 with approximately 6 × 1012 molecules of 
free EPO circulating in the blood of a normal human individual; this equates to, at most, one 
EPO molecule per erythrocyte (healthy individuals have typically 20 trillion erythrocytes in 
their blood). In addition, this steady-state concentration of free EPO is typically 10-fold 
lower than the concentration that is necessary to induce 50% of a response for primary 
colony-forming unit erythroid cells53,54. Note that the concentration of circulating EPO 
increases by a factor of 100 during trauma-induced hypoxia (for example, anaemia or blood 
loss).

experiment.system: human blood erythropoietin–erythrocyte system
experiment.perturbation: observational at homeostasis versus trauma-induced hypoxia (anaemia or blood loss)
experiment.measurement: serum EPO concentration/molecule counts, erythrocyte numbers, and EC50 for colony-forming unit erythroid cells

numbers.quantity: ratio of steady-state EPO to EC50

text: Using bone marrow chimeras with IL-7 receptor-knockout and wild-type bone marrow plus antibody-tagged cell depletion, T cell homeostasis was shown to be enforced by innate lymphoid cells, which are present at less than 0.1% frequency in lymphoid organs yet sustain IL-7 consumption, unlike T cells that downregulate the IL-7 receptor α-subunit.

quotes.quote:
Using a combination of bone marrow chimeras (with IL-7 
receptor-knockout and wild-type bone marrow), as well as cell depletion by antibody 
tagging, it was shown that T cell homeostasis is enforced by innate lymphoid cells (ILCs)61. 
Although ILCs are present at a low frequency in lymphoid organs (less than 0.1%), they can 
sustain their consumption of IL-7, unlike T cells that adapt their response to IL-7 by 
downregulating expression of the IL-7 receptor α-subunit62.

experiment.system: mouse lymphoid organs
experiment.perturbation: bone marrow chimeras with IL-7 receptor-knockout versus wild-type marrow, and antibody-mediated cell depletion
experiment.measurement: IL-7 availability/consumption and T cell homeostasis

text: Work by Hodgkin and colleagues described a T cell calculus converting individual signals into a linear additive effect on cell division time, with combined anti-CD28 and IL-4 treatment computing to an arithmetic sum of the individual responses; later work showed TCR signals, costimulation and cytokine signals add linearly to set a T cell's division destiny.

quotes.quote:
described a calculus performed by T cells to 
convert individual signals into a linear additive effect on cell division time that in turn leads 
to an exponential increase in proliferation rate71. One of the key observations in the study 
was the effect on cell division of combined anti-CD28 and IL-4 treatment, which computed 
to an arithmetic sum of the individual responses.

the division 
destiny of a T cell is regulated72 as a linear combination of TCR signals (signal 1) and 
qualitatively and quantitatively different combinations of APC-derived costimulation (signal 
2) and cytokine-induced signals (signal 3)

experiment.system: T cells in culture
experiment.perturbation: stimulation with individual and combined signals (anti-CD28, IL-4; antigen affinity, costimulation, cytokines)
experiment.measurement: cell division time, number of divisions before quiescence (division destiny), combined with mathematical modeling

text: Strongly activated CD8+ T cells were shown to induce proliferation of weakly activated T cells in their microenvironment via IL-2-mediated paracrine signals, lowering the weakly activated cells' threshold of activation.

quotes.quote:
A related report showed that strongly activated 
CD8+ T cells can induce proliferation of weakly activated T cells in their microenvironment 
by IL-2-mediated paracrine signals9.

experiment.system: mixed populations of strongly and weakly activated CD8+ T cells
experiment.perturbation: antigen stimulation of varying strength / co-culture with strong responders
experiment.measurement: proliferation and activation threshold of weakly activated cells, with mathematical modelling

text: CD4+ T cells responding to combinations of cytokine inputs showed a continuum of differentiation fates rather than discrete phenotypes, with the mean response to a combination of multiple cytokines being a linear sum of the responses to the individual cytokines, captured by a segmented linear regression model that predicted responses to new input conditions.

quotes.quote:
The results show that rather than having discrete phenotypes, cells 
responding to combinations of cytokine inputs have a continuum of differentiation fates. 
Mathematical modelling of the data revealed that the mean response to a combination of 
multiple cytokines is a linear sum of the responses elicited by the individual cytokines. This 
behaviour could be explained by a segmented linear regression model that could also 
correctly predict the response to new input conditions.

experiment.system: CD4+ T cells
experiment.perturbation: stimulation with individual cytokines and their combinations
experiment.measurement: differentiation-state readouts fitted by segmented linear regression modelling

text: Analysis of high-throughput transcriptomic data from human plasmacytoid dendritic cells and monocytes stimulated with combinations of microbial and host-derived ligands revealed an inhibitory effect of TLR ligands on cytokine-induced gene expression in pDCs, even though the individual stimuli strongly induced gene expression.

quotes.quote:
The analysis shows a surprising inhibitory effect of Toll-
like receptor (TLR) ligands on cytokine-induced activation of gene expression in pDCs, even 
though the individual stimuli (TLR ligands and cytokines given separately) strongly induced 
gene expression.

experiment.system: human plasmacytoid dendritic cells and monocytes
experiment.perturbation: stimulation with combinations of microbial and host-derived ligands versus individual stimuli
experiment.measurement: high-throughput transcriptomic gene expression, classified by a pattern-matching mathematical formalism

text: An artificial neural network trained on intracellular calcium responses to binary combinations of six agonists of platelet activation correctly predicted responses to more complex input conditions.

quotes.quote:
By training a neural network model of 
intracellular calcium response to binary combinations of six agonists, the authors could 
correctly predict the response of more complex input conditions.

experiment.system: human platelets
experiment.perturbation: binary and higher-order combinations of six activating agonists
experiment.measurement: intracellular calcium response, modelled by an artificial neural network

text: The authors estimate that in a 96-well suppression assay of 50,000 Treg cells in 200μl, 10 pMol of IL-2 amounts to 25,000 IL-2 molecules per Treg cell, and with 10,000 IL-2 receptors per Treg cell all IL-2 would be consumed within approximately 1 hour; the same holds in vivo with 10,000 Treg cells per lymph node in a reaction volume of 20μl.

quotes.quote:
For example, in a culture of 50,000 regulatory T (Treg) cells in a classical 96-well 
suppression assay (Vassay = 200μl), 10 pMol of IL-2 can be generated, which amounts to 
25,000 molecules of IL-2 per Treg cell. Considering that each Treg cell can express 10,000 
IL-2 receptors, all IL-2 would be consumed within approximately 1 hour (assuming a 
typical rate of endocytosis of 1 to 5 molecules per hour per receptor).

with 10,000 Treg cells per lymph 
node and a reaction volume of 20μl: again, it will take approximately 1 hour for the Treg 
cells to endocytose 10pMol of cytokine.

experiment.system: Treg cell suppression assay in vitro and Treg cells in a lymph node in vivo
experiment.perturbation: calculation from IL-2 concentration, cell number, receptor number and endocytosis rate
experiment.measurement: molecules of IL-2 per cell and characteristic timescale of cytokine consumption

text: In a coarse-grained survey of 15 commercially available homodimeric ligands on NMuMG BRE-reporter cells, many ligand pairs gave stronger or weaker responses than expected from their individual effects; BMP3 combined antagonistically with almost every other ligand, and BMP7 and BMP4 each showed a mixture of antagonistic and synergistic interactions.

quotes.quote:
We performed a coarse-grained 
survey of 15 commercially available homodimeric ligands (Fig. 2A).

Many individual ligand pairs generated stronger or weaker responses than expected given 
their individual effects (Fig. 2A, S1G, H). For example, BMP3 combined antagonistically 
with almost every other ligand.

BMP7 and BMP4 each 
exhibited a mixture of antagonistic and synergistic interactions with other ligands.

experiment.system: NMuMG epithelial reporter cell line with BRE-driven H2B-Citrine
experiment.perturbation: each of 15 homodimeric BMP ligands alone, at twice base concentration, and in pairs
experiment.measurement: reporter fluorescence at 24h normalized to no-ligand basal activity

text: Two-dimensional titrations over three orders of magnitude in NMuMG reporter cells showed three qualitatively distinct integration modes: BMP4+BMP9 additive, BMP4+GDF5 ratiometric (output approximating the ratio of the two ligand concentrations), and BMP4+BMP10 'imbalance detection', in which each potent individual activator becomes inhibitory in the presence of high concentrations of the other.

quotes.quote:
BMP4 and 
BMP9 increased pathway activity both individually and in combination, exhibiting an 
additive response

GDF5 reduced activation by BMP4 in 
a dose-dependent fashion, such that pathway output approximated the ratio of the 
concentrations of the two ligands (Fig. 2D, S2A).

BMP4 and BMP10 were potent 
activators individually, but each became inhibitory in the presence of high concentrations of 
the other ligand, resulting in a weaker response when both ligands were present

We termed this integration mode “imbalance detection” because it responds maximally to 
extreme ratios (imbalances) of the two ligand concentrations.

experiment.system: NMuMG BRE-reporter cells
experiment.perturbation: 2-D matrices of logarithmically spaced concentrations of BMP4 paired with BMP9, GDF5, or BMP10
experiment.measurement: reporter fluorescence at 24h (relative activity)

text: Pathway activity was independent of ligand composition in the additive case, monotonically dependent in the ratiometric case, and non-monotonically dependent in imbalance detection; imbalance detection became indistinguishable from the additive response at ligand concentrations <10ng/ml.

quotes.quote:
pathway activity is independent of ligand 
composition in the additive case (Fig. 2F), monotonically dependent in the ratiometric case 
(Fig. 2G), and non-monotonically dependent in the imbalance detection case

The only exception 
is imbalance detection, which at ligand concentrations <10ng/ml becomes indistinguishable 
from the additive response (Fig. 2C).

experiment.system: NMuMG BRE-reporter cells
experiment.perturbation: varying relative ligand concentrations at fixed total ligand concentration
experiment.measurement: reporter activity along composition contours

numbers.quantity: concentration below which imbalance detection is indistinguishable from additive

text: Smad1/5/8 phosphorylation measured by immunostaining and Western blot 20 minutes after ligand addition showed qualitatively similar response profiles to the fluorescent reporter, indicating the computations emerge within 20 minutes; Erk1/2 did not respond to BMP stimulation in this cell context.

quotes.quote:
we measured Smad1/5/8 
phosphorylation at 20 minutes after stimulation with select ligand pairs, using 
immunostaining (Fig. 3A) and Western blots (Fig. S2E, F). Both measurements revealed 
qualitatively similar response profiles as the fluorescent reporter, indicating that 
computations emerge within 20 minutes

Erk1/2, a non-canonical output (Nohe et al. 2004), did not 
respond to BMP stimulation in this cell context (Fig S2G).

experiment.system: NMuMG cells
experiment.perturbation: select BMP ligand pairs for 20 minutes
experiment.measurement: phospho-Smad1/5/8 immunostaining/flow cytometry and Western blot; phospho-p44/42 MAPK blot

text: Time-lapse imaging of reporter expression under BMP4 and/or BMP10 showed the imbalance detection response could be identified by 6h and persisted for more than 96h, with the relative level of activation by the combination remaining constant.

quotes.quote: The imbalance detection response could be identified by 6h and persisted for more than 96h.

the relative level of activation caused by the combination of BMP4 and BMP10, 
compared to the individual ligands, remained constant (Fig. S3B)

experiment.system: NMuMG reporter cells mixed with parental cells
experiment.perturbation: BMP4 and/or BMP10 addition
experiment.measurement: time-lapse imaging of reporter fluorescence over time

text: Knock-down of the negative feedback regulator Smad6 did not qualitatively change the response profile shapes, and BMP9-induced Bmpr2 upregulation (a 2-fold increase with 400ng/ml BMP9) appeared only at ~12 hours, too late to explain computations arising earlier.

quotes.quote:
knock-down of Smad6 did 
not qualitatively change the shape of the response profiles (Fig. S3C–E).

Addition of 400ng/ml BMP9 generated a 2-fold increase in Bmpr2 expression (Fig. 
S3F). However, even this relatively modest effect appeared only at ~12 hours

experiment.system: NMuMG reporter cells
experiment.perturbation: siRNA knock-down of Smad6; addition of 400ng/ml BMP9
experiment.measurement: 2-D ligand response profiles; Bmpr2 protein levels by immunoblot over time

text: Individually depleting expressed secreted/surface BMP modulators by siRNA did not affect the type of response profile generated by BMP4 with BMP9, BMP10, or GDF5, and perturbing heparan sulfate proteoglycans with heparinase or chlorate had minimal effects.

quotes.quote:
Individually depleting each of these factors using siRNAs (Fig. 3C) did not affect the 
type of response profile generated by BMP4 in combination with BMP9, BMP10, or GDF5 
(Fig. 3D–G).

Enzymatically perturbing HSPGs with heparinase or inhibiting 
their biosynthesis with CaClO3 showed minimal effects on the response of the pathway to 
BMP combinations (Fig S3G–J).

experiment.system: NMuMG reporter cells
experiment.perturbation: siRNA depletion of expressed BMP modifiers (e.g. Fst, RGMb, Twsg1); heparinase I/III treatment; chlorate treatment
experiment.measurement: 2-D ligand response profiles by flow cytometry

text: A minimal model of promiscuous competitive receptor-ligand binding with two ligands and two variants of each receptor type, simulated for 100,000 random parameter sets, produced response profiles occupying a continuous inverted-triangle region in RLS-LIC space with three vertices corresponding to ratiometric, imbalance detection, and a newly predicted 'balance detection' behavior, with additive at RLS=1, LIC=0 and all other functions interpolating between archetypes.

quotes.quote:
we computed the input-
output behavior of the system for 100,000 random parameter sets (Fig. S4A).

the simulated systems occupied a 
continuous region that loosely conformed to an inverted triangle (Fig. 4C, S4E). Two 
vertices of the triangle strikingly resembled the ratiometric and imbalance detection 
functions observed experimentally

represented a new predicted behavior, which we termed ‘balance detection’ 
because it shows a maximal response when both ligands are present at a specific ratio. All 
other functions, including the additive interaction at RLS=1, LIC=0 (top middle, Fig. 4C), 
interpolated between these three archetypal functions

experiment.system: (2,2,2) mathematical model of promiscuous receptor-ligand interactions
experiment.perturbation: 100,000 randomly sampled biochemical and receptor-expression parameter sets
experiment.measurement: computed 2D input-output functions summarized by Relative Ligand Strength and Ligand Interference Coefficient

numbers.quantity: RLS and LIC of additive interaction

text: When model parameters were restricted to a biologically relevant range, all archetypal behaviors still occurred but showed enrichment for the additive, balance detection, and imbalance detection response profiles.

quotes.quote:
All archetypal behaviors occurred, whether parameters were chosen from a full 
range of values, or restricted to a biologically relevant range (Supplementary). However, 
parameters in the biological range showed an enrichment for the additive, balance detection, 
and imbalance detection response profiles (Fig. S5E).

experiment.system: (2,2,2) model
experiment.perturbation: 100,000 parameter sets sampled from literature-constrained biological ranges of receptor counts, ligand levels, affinities
experiment.measurement: frequency of each response-profile type across a 9×9 ligand concentration matrix

text: In the model, the archetypes map to distinct parameter regimes: additive when the two ligands form complexes with similar phosphorylation activities; ratiometric when complexes of one ligand are much more active so the weaker ligand competitively inhibits; imbalance detection when each receptor preferentially binds the ligand with which it forms a less active complex; and balance detection when the relative affinities are reversed to favor more active complexes.

quotes.quote:
additive responses occur when the two ligands are approximately equivalent, 
forming signaling complexes with similar phosphorylation activities

ratiometric behaviors occur when signaling complexes containing one 
ligand have higher activities than those containing the other

Imbalance detection occurs when each receptor preferentially binds to a distinct ligand with 
which it forms a less active signaling complex (Fig. 5C, S6C).

balance detection occurs through a similar 
mechanism, except that the relative affinities are reversed, favoring formation of more active 
signaling complexes when both ligands are present

experiment.system: (2,2,2) model of promiscuous receptor-ligand binding
experiment.perturbation: analysis of parameter regimes (affinities K and complex activities ε) producing each archetype
experiment.measurement: steady-state signal S as a function of two ligand concentrations

text: In the model at high ligand concentrations the solution depends only on ratios between ligands and not their absolute levels, distinguishing the archetypal computations from Boolean logic gates, which require input thresholds.

quotes.quote:
When ligand concentrations are large, Lj ≫ 1, the 1/Lj 
vanishes and the solution depends only on ratios between ligands and not on their absolute 
levels.

a key feature of Boolean logic is the existence of threshold levels that 
can be used to binarize inputs.

experiment.system: mathematical model of promiscuous receptor-ligand interactions
experiment.perturbation: analytical limit of large ligand concentration in the steady-state equations
experiment.measurement: functional dependence of signal output on ligand ratios Rjj'

text: Varying receptor expression levels in the model while holding biochemical parameters fixed showed that some parameter sets produced only a limited range of integration modes while others were versatile, generating a diverse range of computations.

quotes.quote:
some biochemical parameter sets produced only a limited range of ligand integration modes 
(Fig. 6A, left), while others were more versatile, capable of generating a diverse range of 
computations as receptor expression levels were varied (Fig. 6A, right).

we selected 
1000 random biochemical parameter sets. For each, we simulated the model with varying 
expression levels of each of the 4 receptor subunits

experiment.system: (2,2,2) model
experiment.perturbation: systematic log-uniform variation of the four receptor expression levels for 1000 fixed biochemical parameter sets
experiment.measurement: distribution of LIC and RLS values

numbers.quantity: biochemical parameter sets in versatility search

text: E14 mouse embryonic stem cells, which express less Bmpr2 and Acvr1 and more Acvr2b than NMuMG, exhibited different response profiles for the same ligands; most strikingly BMP4 and BMP9 integrated additively in NMuMG and NIH-3T3 but showed the balance detection archetype in ES cells, validating the model's balance-detection prediction.

quotes.quote:
we compared the response of NMuMG cells to E14 mouse embryonic stem (ES) 
cells, which express less Bmpr2 and Acvr1 and more Acvr2b (Fig. 6B). As a control, we 
also analyzed NIH-3T3 fibroblasts, which had similar receptor expression to NMuMG cells

BMP4 and BMP9 integrated in an 
additive fashion in NMuMG and NIH-3T3, but showed the balance detection archetype in

these results also 
validate the model prediction of balance detection (Fig. 4G).

experiment.system: NMuMG, NIH-3T3, and E14 mouse ES BRE-reporter cell lines
experiment.perturbation: observational comparison of cell lines exposed to the same 2-D ligand matrices
experiment.measurement: RNAseq receptor expression (FPKM) and reporter fluorescence response profiles

text: Direct manipulation of receptor expression in NMuMG cells reprogrammed computations: siRNA depletion of Bmpr2 changed the BMP4-BMP9 response from additive to ratiometric; ectopic Bmpr1b let GDF5 activate rather than inhibit, converting the ratiometric BMP4-GDF5 interaction to additive, while combining ectopic Bmpr1b with Bmpr2 depletion inverted the ratiometric response; and ectopic Alk1 removed BMP4-BMP10 competition, generating the predicted additive response.

quotes.quote:
Depletion of the 
most highly expressed type II receptor in this cell type, Bmpr2, with siRNA, changed the 
BMP4-BMP9 response from additive to ratiometric (Fig. 6F, S7C).

ectopically expressed Bmpr1b, which is known to mediate GDF5 
signaling (Nishitoh et al., 1996), enabled GDF5 to activate, rather than inhibit, the pathway, 
and thereby reprogrammed the ratiometric BMP4-GDF5 interaction to an additive one

combining ectopic Bmpr1b to enable GDF5 signaling with 
depletion of Bmpr2 to reduce BMP4-dependent signaling inverted the ratiometric response

we ectopically expressed the Alk1 receptor, which is 
known to mediate BMP9 and BMP10 signaling (David et al., 2007). This perturbation 
indeed removed competition, generating the predicted additive response (Fig. 6H, S7C).

experiment.system: NMuMG BRE-reporter cells
experiment.perturbation: siRNA knockdown of Bmpr2; PiggyBac overexpression of Bmpr1b or Alk1; combined Bmpr1b overexpression with Bmpr2 knockdown
experiment.measurement: 2-D ligand response profiles by flow cytometry

text: In model simulations with a fixed receptor-expression coefficient of variation of v = 0.25, extrinsic noise generated comparatively small quantitative changes in response profiles relative to intrinsic noise, and the differences were generally insufficient to change the class of input-output function observed.

quotes.quote: we used a fixed coefficient of variation, v = 0.25.

We find that extrinsic noise generates comparatively small quantitative changes in response 
profiles relative to intrinsic noise, with the combination of extrinsic and intrinsic noise showing an intermediate effect.

While these differences are generally insufficient to change the class of input-output 
function observed, we find that intrinsic noise produces greater variability in the phenotypic 
parameters.

experiment.system: (2,2,2) model, 100 parameter sets from each of 5 regions of RLS-LIC space
experiment.perturbation: gamma-distributed extrinsic, intrinsic, or mixed noise added to receptor expression levels
experiment.measurement: spread of RLS and LIC across perturbations

text: In the model, finite extracellular volume preserved all four behaviors, but the two models differed at intermediate ligand levels, where the finite-volume model produced a sharper dependence on ligand concentration, or equivalently a reduced input dynamic range.

quotes.quote:
We see that the distribution of behaviors remains 
similar with all four behavior arising even in the finite volume regime (Fig S5A).

they differ specifically at intermediate ligand levels (Fig S5B), 
where the finite model produces a sharper dependence on ligand concentration, or, 
equivalently, a reduced input dynamic range.

experiment.system: mathematical model of promiscuous receptor-ligand interactions
experiment.perturbation: replacing the infinite-volume assumption with finite extracellular volume steady-state equations
experiment.measurement: numerically solved input-output response profiles compared between models

text: Reporter expression in the NMuMG BRE line correlated with Smad1/5/8 phosphorylation and endogenous BMP target gene expression; pSmad levels reached steady state within 90 min after an elevated transient, and reporter fluorescence accumulated at an approximately constant rate for up to 48h, motivating a 24h analysis time point.

quotes.quote:
Reporter expression 
correlated with phosphorylation of Smad1/5/8 and with endogenous BMP target gene 
expression (Fig. S1A–C), and exhibited a unimodal distribution for each ligand 
concentration (Fig. S1D). After an elevated transient response to BMP addition, pSmad 
levels reached a steady state within 90 min (Fig. S1E). The steady-state behavior was also 
reflected in reporter fluorescence, which accumulated at an approximately constant rate over 
time for up to 48h (Fig. S1F).

experiment.system: NMuMG cells with stably integrated BRE-driven H2B-Citrine reporter
experiment.perturbation: BMP ligand addition over a concentration and time course
experiment.measurement: flow cytometry reporter fluorescence, phospho-Smad1/5/8, and endogenous target gene expression

text: The same two-dimensional response profiles were observed using independently generated reporter cell lines and were independent of the ligand supplier.

quotes.quote:
We note that the same two-
dimensional response profiles were observed using independently generated reporter cell 
lines, indicating that they do not reflect aspects of the chromatin configuration of a specific 
reporter integration site (Fig. S2C). The integration functions were also independent of the 
ligand supplier (Fig. S2D).

experiment.system: NMuMG reporter cell lines including a PiggyBac-integrated BRE reporter
experiment.perturbation: same 2-D ligand matrices using ligands from R&D Systems versus Peprotech; different reporter integration sites
experiment.measurement: reporter fluorescence response profiles

text: EMTA ebBRET biosensors detect activation of the 12 G protein subtypes via translocation of effector domains (p63-RhoGEF, Rap1GAP, PDZ-RhoGEF) to the plasma membrane without modifying receptors or G proteins except Gs; profiling 100 therapeutically relevant human GPCRs produced 1500 pathway-specific concentration-response curves.

quotes.quote:
Here, we present a set of BRET sensors monitoring the activation of the 12 G protein subtypes 
based on the translocation of their effectors to the plasma membrane (EMTA). Unlike most of 
the existing detection systems, EMTA does not require modification of receptors or G proteins 
(except for Gs).

Profiling of 100 therapeutically relevant human 
GPCRs resulted in 1500 pathway-­specific concentration-­response curves and revealed a great 
diversity of coupling profiles ranging from exquisite selectivity to broad promiscuity.

experiment.system: HEK293 cells expressing 100 human GPCRs with ebBRET effector-RlucII/rGFP-CAAX biosensors
experiment.perturbation: agonist concentration-response stimulation across 15 pathways
experiment.measurement: ebBRET ratio; Emax and pEC50

text: The Gi/o sensor (Rap1GAP-RlucII) response to dopamine at D2 was unaffected by the Gq/11 inhibitor UBO-QIC but completely blocked by pertussis toxin for all Gαi/o members except Gαz.

quotes.quote:
The dopamine-­promoted increase in ebBRET between 
Rap1GAP-­RlucII and rGFP-­CAAX in the presence of Gαi/o subunits was not affected by the Gq/11-­selective 
inhibitor UBO-­QIC

the Gαi/o family inhib-
itor, pertussis toxin (PTX), completely blocked the response for all members of Gαi/o family except for Gαz, 
known to be insensitive to PTX

experiment.system: HEK293 cells transfected with D2 receptor, Gαi/o subunits and Rap1GAP-RlucII/rGFP-CAAX
experiment.perturbation: dopamine concentration-response with or without UBO-QIC or PTX pretreatment
experiment.measurement: ebBRET ratio and Emax

text: The Gq/11 sensor (p63-RhoGEF-RlucII) response to GnRH at GnRHR was not significantly affected by PTX (p = 0.077, 0.0636 and 0.073 for Gq, G11, and G14) whereas UBO-QIC blocked all Gαq/11 members except Gα15.

quotes.quote:
The ebBRET increase observed in the presence of different 
Gαq/11 subunits was not significantly (p = 0.077, 0.0636 and 0.073 for Gq, G11, and G14, respectively) affected 
by PTX (Figure 2B, right), whereas UBO-­QIC completely blocked the response for all members of Gαq/11 
family except for Gα15, known to be insensitive to UBO-­QIC

experiment.system: HEK293 cells transfected with GnRH receptor, Gαq/11 subunits and p63-RhoGEF-RlucII/rGFP-CAAX
experiment.perturbation: GnRH concentration-response with or without PTX or UBO-QIC
experiment.measurement: ebBRET ratio, Emax, unpaired t-test p values

text: Genetic deletion of Gi/o or Gq/11 subtypes completely abolished D2- or GnRHR-induced responses in the absence of heterologously expressed G proteins, indicating the sensors detect endogenous G protein activation.

quotes.quote:
These 
two G protein-­specific EMTA were sensitive enough to detect responses elicited by endogenous G proteins 
since deletion of Gi/o (ΔGi/o) or Gq/11 (ΔGq/11) subtypes completely abolished the responses induced by D2 or 
GnRHR activation in the absence of heterologously expressed G proteins

experiment.system: parental and ΔGi/o or ΔGq/11 HEK293 cells with D2 or GnRHR and EMTA sensors
experiment.perturbation: CRISPR deletion of G protein families; agonist stimulation
experiment.measurement: ebBRET response

text: CB1-promoted PDZ-RhoGEF-RlucII/rGFP-CAAX ebBRET with Gα12 or Gα13 was insensitive to UBO-QIC and PTX, and in ΔG12/13 cells signal was observed only upon reintroduction of Gα12 or Gα13.

quotes.quote:
The ebBRET between PDZ-­RhoGEF-­RlucII and rGFP-­CAAX 
in the presence of Gα12 or Gα13 promoted by the cannabinoid agonist WIN-­55,212–2 was not affected by 
UBO-­QIC (Figure 2C, top left), nor PTX

PDZ-­RhoGEF-­RlucII/rGFP-­CAAX ebBRET was observed 
only following reintroduction of either Gα12 (ΔG12/13_+G12) or Gα13 (ΔG12/13_+G13)

experiment.system: HEK293 and ΔG12/13 HEK293 cells expressing CB1 and PDZ-RhoGEF-RlucII/rGFP-CAAX
experiment.perturbation: WIN-55,212–2 stimulation ± UBO-QIC/PTX; Gα12 or Gα13 re-expression
experiment.measurement: ebBRET concentration-response

text: Side-by-side comparison showed significantly larger assay windows for EMTA than for BRET assays based on Gαβγ dissociation, for the 6 Gα subunits tested across eight selected receptors.

quotes.quote:
a direct side-­by-­side comparison of the signals 
detected with EMTA vs. BRET assays based on Gαβγ dissociation (Gαβγ) (Galés et al., 2005; Galés 
et al., 2006; Olsen et al., 2020), that reveals a significantly larger assay windows for EMTA for the 6 
Gα subunits tested for eight selected receptors

experiment.system: HEK293 cells with EMTA sensors vs Gαβγ dissociation BRET sensors
experiment.perturbation: agonist stimulation of eight receptors across 6 Gα subunits
experiment.measurement: assay window of BRET signal

text: For the Gαs sensor, lithocholic acid at GPBA produced a concentration-dependent decrease in Gαs-RlucII/rGFP-CAAX ebBRET, cholera toxin also decreased ebBRET, the signal was insensitive to UBO-QIC and PTX, and the potency matched that for cAMP production measured with an EPAC biosensor.

quotes.quote:
lithocholic acid stimulation resulted in a concentration-­dependent 
decrease in ebBRET between Gαs-­RlucII and rGFP-­CAAX (Figure 2D, left). Cholera toxin (CTX), which 
directly activates Gαs (De Haan and Hirst, 2004), led to a decrease in ebBRET

The potency of 
lithocholic acid to promote Gs dissociation from the plasma membrane was well in line with its potency 
to increase cAMP production as assessed using a BRET²-based EPAC biosensor

experiment.system: HEK293 cells expressing GPBA receptor with Gαs-RlucII/rGFP-CAAX or EPAC biosensor
experiment.perturbation: lithocholic acid or CTX; ± UBO-QIC/PTX
experiment.measurement: ebBRET ratio, potency

text: Across the 100 profiled GPCRs, 29% coupled to only one G protein family and 36%, 25% and 10% coupled to 2, 3 or 4 families; among single-family couplers, Gi/o was favored (27% of Gi/o-coupling receptors activated only that family, versus 0, 2.4 and 9.1% for G12/13, Gq/11 and Gs).

quotes.quote:
In our dataset, which is the first using unmodified GPCRs and Gα proteins (except for Gs), 29% of 
the receptors coupled to only one family, whereas others displayed more promiscuity by coupling 
to 2, 3, or 4 families (36%, 25%, and 10%, respectively). Receptors coupling to a single G protein 
family favored the members of the Gi/o family. Indeed, 27% of the receptors coupling to Gi/o only acti-
vated this subtype family in comparison to 0, 2.4 and 9.1% for receptors activating G12/13, Gq/11, and 
Gs, respectively

experiment.system: 100 human GPCRs in HEK293 cells with EMTA biosensors
experiment.perturbation: agonist stimulation, coupling called by Emax threshold criteria
experiment.measurement: proportion of receptors coupling to each number of G protein families

numbers.quantity: exclusive coupling for G12/13, Gq/11, Gs

text: Gi/o family members were the most frequently activated (89% of tested receptors), versus 33%, 49% and 45% for Gs, G12/13 and Gq/11 (excluding Gα15), while Gα15 was activated by 81% of receptors.

quotes.quote:
the Gi/o family 
members were the most commonly activated, with 89% of the tested receptors activating a Gi/o family 
member. In contrast, only 33%, 49%, and 45% of the receptors activate Gs, G12/13, or Gq/11 (excluding 
Gα15) family members, respectively. Not surprisingly, and consistent with its reported promiscuous 
coupling, Gα15 was found to be activated by 81% of the receptors.

experiment.system: 100 human GPCRs with EMTA biosensors in HEK293 cells
experiment.perturbation: agonist stimulation; threshold-based coupling calls
experiment.measurement: frequency of receptors activating each Gα family/subunit

text: Intra-family selectivity was observed: 33% of Gi/o-coupled receptors coupled to only a subpopulation of the family, and within Gq/11 only 44% activated all members, 45% activated only Gα15 and 11% engaged two or three members.

quotes.quote:
For instance, 33% of Gi/o-­coupled receptors can couple to only a subpopulation of the family 
(Figure 4—figure supplement 1A). For the Gq/11 family, only 44% activate all family members with 45% 
activating only Gα15 and 11% engaging only two or three members of the family.

experiment.system: 100 GPCR EMTA coupling dataset
experiment.perturbation: observational analysis of subtype-level coupling calls
experiment.measurement: percentage of receptors per intra-family coupling pattern

numbers.quantity: Gq/11 couplers engaging two or three members

text: Serotonin 5-HT2B activated only GαoB and Gαz and GPR65 selectively activated GαoB, examples of intra-Gi/o-family coupling selectivity.

quotes.quote:
A striking example of intra-­family coupling selectivity is 
the serotonin 5-­HT2B that activates only GαoB and Gαz and GPR65 that selectively activates GαoB.

experiment.system: HEK293 cells expressing 5-HT2B or GPR65 with Gi/o EMTA sensors
experiment.perturbation: agonist concentration-response
experiment.measurement: per-subunit coupling calls from Emax

text: 22% of receptors recruited neither βarrestin1 nor 2 even with overexpressed GRK2; among recruiters 1.3% were βarrestin1-selective, 6.4% βarrestin2-selective and 92.3% recruited both; GRK2 overexpression potentiated βarrestin2 recruitment for 68% of receptors.

quotes.quote:
our analysis shows that 22% of receptors did not recruit 
βarrestin 1 or 2, even in the presence of overexpressed GRK2 (Figure 4D). Among the receptors able 
to recruit βarrestins, only a very small number selectively recruited βarrestin1 (1.3%) or βarrestin2 
(6.4%), most of them recruiting both βarrestins in the presence of GRK2 (92.3%)

Over-
expression of GRK2 potentiated the recruitment of βarrestin2 for 68% of receptors

experiment.system: HEK293 cells expressing each of 100 GPCRs with βarrestin1/2-RlucII and rGFP-CAAX ± GRK2
experiment.perturbation: agonist stimulation; GRK2 co-expression
experiment.measurement: ebBRET-based βarrestin recruitment calls

text: Newly identified G12/13 couplings were confirmed orthogonally: FP and CysLT2 ligand stimulation activated Rho (PKN biosensor) and ezrin (MyrPB-Ezrin biosensor) insensitively to the Gq/11 inhibitor YM-254890.

quotes.quote:
Ligand stimulation of FP and CysLT2 receptors led to 
Rho and ezrin activation (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A), that were insensitive to the Gq/11 inhibitor 
YM-­254890, confirming that these receptors activate Gα12/13.

experiment.system: HEK293 cells expressing FP or CysLT2 with PKN-RBD-RlucII or MyrPB-Ezrin-RlucII and rGFP-CAAX, no heterologous G proteins
experiment.perturbation: agonist stimulation ± YM-254890
experiment.measurement: BRET signal for Rho/ezrin activation

text: Newly identified G15 couplings were confirmed by calcium assays: Gα15 expression increased PGE2- and Dynorphin A-promoted calcium responses at EP2 and κOR, and rendered α2AAR and V2 agonist-evoked calcium responses insensitive to YM-254890.

quotes.quote:
For prostaglandin E2 (EP2) and κ-opioid (κOR) receptors, which 
couple to G15 but no other Gq/11 members, expression of Gα15 significantly increased the PGE2- and 
Dynorphin A- promoted calcium responses.

the calcium response evoked by α2AAR 
and V2 agonists following Gα15 expression was completely insensitive to YM-­254890

verdict_note: Claim text and numbers match p.11; the experiment field's 'FLIPR' readout detail is not stated in the excerpt (paper says only 'calcium responses'), but this does not alter the substance.

experiment.system: HEK293 cells (lacking endogenous Gα15) expressing EP2, κOR, α2AAR or V2 ± Gα15
experiment.perturbation: heterologous Gα15 expression; agonist stimulation ± YM-254890
experiment.measurement: FLIPR calcium fluorescence responses

text: EMTA detected constitutive activity and inverse agonism: increasing A1 receptor transfection raised basal Gαi2-sensor ebBRET and DPCPX dose-dependently reduced it, while increasing CB1 expression produced ligand-independent Gz activation fully blocked by rimonabant.

quotes.quote:
Transfection of increasing amounts of adenosine A1 receptor (A1) led to a receptor-­dependent 
increase in basal ebBRET of the Gαi2-­activation sensor (Figure  5A, left), reflecting A1 constitu-
tive activity. The A1 inverse agonist DPCPX (Lu et  al., 2014) dose-­dependently decreased the 
constitutive A1-­mediated activation of Gαi2

increase CB1 expression led to a ligand-­independent constitutive activation 
of Gz, that could be completely blocked by the CB1 inverse agonist rimonabant.

experiment.system: HEK293 cells with Rap1GAP-RlucII/rGFP-CAAX plus Gαi2 or Gαz and increasing A1 or CB1 plasmid
experiment.perturbation: receptor plasmid titration; DPCPX or rimonabant treatment
experiment.measurement: basal and ligand-modulated ebBRET (BRET2 ratio, % of control)

text: EMTA detected biased signaling at AT1: the angiotensin analogs SII, saralasin and TRV027 promoted efficient βarrestin2 recruitment but marginal or no Gαq, Gαi2 or Gα13 activation, unlike angiotensin II which activated all.

quotes.quote:
angiotensin analogs such as SII, saralasin or TRV027 displayed biased 
signaling by promoting efficient βarrestin2 recruitment but marginal or no Gαq, Gαi2, or Gα13 activation 
as compared to angiotensin II that activated all G proteins and βarrestin2 (Figure 5B).

experiment.system: HEK293 cells expressing AT1 with Gαq, Gαi2, Gα13 or βarrestin2 EMTA sensors
experiment.perturbation: concentration-response with AngII, SII, saralasin, TRV027
experiment.measurement: response as % Emax of AngII

text: Two naturally occurring GPR17 E/DRY-motif variants altered functional selectivity: Asp128Asn retained WT-like Gαi2 activity but lost Gαq and βarrestin2 activation, whereas Arg129His increased constitutive βarrestin2 recruitment and lost Gαi2 and Gαq signaling.

quotes.quote:
Whereas the Asp128Asn variant displayed 
WT-­like activity on Gαi2, it lost the ability to activate Gαq and βarrestin2. In contrast, variant Arg129His 
at the neighboring position resulted in an increased constitutive βarrestin2 recruitment and a loss of 
Gαi2 and Gαq protein signaling.

experiment.system: HEK293 cells co-expressing WT or variant GPR17 (isoform 2) with EMTA biosensors
experiment.perturbation: point mutations Asp128Asn, Arg129His; MDL 29,951 concentration-response
experiment.measurement: ebBRET response as % Emax of WT

text: The Gz/G15 screen revealed ligand cross-reactivity: α2AAR was activated by dopamine and serotonin and D2 by noradrenaline and serotonin, confirmed by block with the selective antagonists eticlopride and WB4101; eticlopride had negligible effect on dopamine-mediated Gαi2/GαoB activation in α2AAR-expressing cells, indicating direct activation.

quotes.quote:
These included the activation of the 
α2AAR by dopamine and serotonin, the D2 by noradrenaline and serotonin, and of the CB1 and CB2 
receptors by acetylcholine (Figure 6B–C). The activation of D2 by noradrenaline and serotonin was 
confirmed by the ability of the D2-­family selective antagonist eticlopride to block the dopamine-, 
serotonin-, and noradrenaline-­promoted responses

Direct activation of the α2AAR by dopamine was confirmed by showing 
that treatment with the D2-­family receptor selective antagonist eticlopride had negligible effect on 
dopamine-­mediated activation of Gαi2 and GαoB in cells heterologously expressing α2AAR

experiment.system: HEK293 cells expressing D2 or α2AAR with Gz/G15, Gαi2, GαoB or βarrestin2+GRK2 sensors
experiment.perturbation: non-cognate ligand stimulation in agonist mode; antagonist (eticlopride, WB4101) pretreatment in antagonist mode
experiment.measurement: ebBRET response as % of dopamine or noradrenaline response

text: Acetylcholine activation of CB1/CB2 was shown to be indirect: the GαoB response was blocked by both the CB inverse agonist AM-630 and atropine (which did not block WIN55,212-2), absent in parental cells, and abolished by the Gq/11 inhibitor UBO-QIC while WIN55,212-2 responses persisted.

quotes.quote:
the activation 
was completely inhibited by both the CB inverse agonist AM-­630 and by the cholinergic antagonist 
atropine (Figure 6C, left). Yet the response evoked by the CB selective agonist WIN55,212 2 was not 
blocked by atropine

UBO-­QIC pre-­treatment blocked acetylcholine- but not WIN55,212–2-­mediated GαoB 
activation (Figure 6C, right). These results demonstrate that CB1 activation by acetylcholine is indirect

experiment.system: HEK293 cells expressing CB1 with Rap1GAP-RlucII/rGFP-CAAX and untagged GαoB
experiment.perturbation: acetylcholine or WIN55,212–2 stimulation ± AM-630, atropine, or UBO-QIC
experiment.measurement: ebBRET as % of WIN55,212–2 response

text: EMTA detected Gαi2 activation by endogenous receptors and, in some cases, endogenous G proteins: endogenous S1P1 in iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes and FPR2 in HL-60 cells with heterologous Gαi2, and endogenous FPR2 in HL-60 cells and PAR2 in HEK293 cells with endogenous Gi/o proteins.

quotes.quote:
Concentration-­dependent 
activation of Gαi2 protein by (A) endogenous S1P1 receptor in iPSC-­derived cardiomyocytes transfected with heterologous Gαi2, (B) endogenous FPR2 
in promyelocytic HL-­60 cells transfected with heterologous Gαi2, (C) endogenous FPR2 in promyelocytic HL-­60 cells with endogenous Gi/o proteins and 
(D) endogenous PAR2 receptor in HEK293 cells with endogenous Gi/o proteins.

experiment.system: iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes, HL-60 cells and HEK293 cells transfected with Rap1GAP-RlucII/rGFP-CAAX
experiment.perturbation: agonist concentration-response at endogenous receptors, ± heterologous Gαi2
experiment.measurement: BRET2 ratio as % of vehicle response

text: Potencies of EMTA responses were not affected by genetic deletion of G protein family members nor by overexpression of G proteins, GPCRs or effector-RlucII; titration of receptor, G protein or effector amounts changed only response amplitude, not pEC50.

quotes.quote:
competition with 
endogenous G proteins did not occur to a significant extent since the potencies of the responses 
to a given G protein subtype were not affected by genetic deletion of the different G protein

overexpres-
sion of G proteins, GPCRs or effectors-­RlucII did not affect the potencies of the responses observed

As expected, only the amplitude 
of the response was affected.

experiment.system: HEK293 parental and G protein knockout cells with EMTA sensors, e.g. ETA receptor titration
experiment.perturbation: genetic deletion of G protein families; titration of Gα subunit, receptor or effector-RlucII DNA
experiment.measurement: absolute pEC50 values from concentration-response curves

text: decoupleR contains 11 different methods for biological activity estimation, including AUCell, fast GSEA, GSVA, over-representation analysis, univariate linear model and VIPER, and provides a consensus score computed as a mean z-score across methods.

quotes.quote:
Currently, decoupleR contains 11 different methods (Fig. 1A), these
include popular methods such as AUCell (Aibar et al., 2017), fast
GSEA (Korotkevich et al., 2021), GSVA (Ha¨nzelmann et al., 2013),
over-representation
analysis,
univariate
linear
model
(ULM)
adapted from Teschendorff and Wang (2020), VIPER (Alvarez
et al., 2016) and others

decoupleR also provides a consensus score obtained by computing a
mean z-score across methods (Supplementary Note).

experiment.system: decoupleR R/Python software package
experiment.perturbation: observational (software description)
experiment.measurement: count and identity of implemented activity-inference methods

text: Across methods, inferred activities were generally similar, with a median Spearman correlation between methods of 0.52 for transcriptomics and 0.65 for phospho-proteomics, and moderate agreement in the top 5% ranked regulators (median Jaccard indexes 0.23 and 0.21, respectively).

quotes.quote:
with a median Spearman correlation of activities between methods
of 0.52, and 0.65 for transcriptomics and phospho-proteomics, re-
spectively (Fig. 1B). There was also a moderate agreement between
methods in the top 5% ranked regulators (median Jaccard indexes
of 0.23 and 0.21, respectively; Supplementary Fig. S2).

experiment.perturbation: observational comparison of activity scores across the methods implemented in decoupleR
experiment.measurement: Spearman correlation of activities between methods; Jaccard index of top 5% ranked regulators

numbers.quantity: median Spearman correlation between methods, transcriptomics
median Spearman correlation between methods, phospho-proteomics
median Jaccard index of top 5% regulators, transcriptomics
median Jaccard index of top 5% regulators, phospho-proteomics

text: In recovery of perturbed regulators, the top three performing approaches were consensus, multivariate linear model and ULM.

quotes.quote:
Despite these similarities, methods showed different perform-
ances at predicting perturbed regulators (Supplementary Fig. S3).
Some of them performed consistently better than the others
(Supplementary Table S3; Fig. 1C), the top three being: consen-
sus, multivariate linear model and ULM.

experiment.measurement: predictive performance in recovering the perturbed regulator across methods

text: Methods that leverage interaction weights performed better when those weights were taken into account (P-value <2.2e-16, one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test).

quotes.quote:
Moreover, methods that
leverage weights perform better when those are taken into ac-
count (P-value <2.2e-16; one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test;
Supplementary Fig. S4).

text: decoupleR wraps the meta-resource OmniPath, comprising over 100 databases of prior knowledge, giving access to cell-type marker databases, gene regulatory networks and pathway footprints.

quotes.quote: Moreover, it leverages OmniPath, a meta-resource comprising over 100 databases of prior knowledge.

decoupleR offers easy to use wrappers to query the meta-database
OmniPath (Tu¨rei et al., 2021), making it easy to flexibly access
processed resources such as cell-type marker databases, gene regula-
tory networks or pathway footprints

experiment.system: decoupleR package with OmniPath meta-database
experiment.perturbation: observational (software capability description)
experiment.measurement: number of prior knowledge databases accessible and resource types provided

text: INK-ATTAC and GFP transcript levels were significantly elevated in adipose tissue, skeletal muscle and eye of BubR1H/H;INK-ATTAC-3 and -5 mice, but not in liver and heart where endogenous p16Ink4a is not induced.

quotes.quote:
Quantitative
reverse transcription–polymerase chain reaction (qRT–PCR) analysis of various tissues from
BubR1H/H;INK-ATTAC-3 and -5 mice demonstrated that INK-ATTAC and GFP transcript
levels were significantly elevated in adipose tissue, skeletal muscle and eye, but not in
tissues in which endogenous p16Ink4a is not induced, including liver and heart

experiment.system: BubR1H/H;INK-ATTAC-3 and -5 mice, various tissues (observational tissue survey)
experiment.perturbation: observational (genotype comparison)
experiment.measurement: qRT–PCR of INK-ATTAC and GFP transcripts

text: In bone marrow cells from 2-month-old WT;INK-ATTAC-3 and -5 mice, rosiglitazone treatment induced Flag-tagged FKBP–Casp8 expression in a high proportion of cells, whereas untreated cells did not express it.

quotes.quote:
we
harvested bone marrow cells from 2-month-old wild-type (WT);INK-ATTAC-3 and -5 mice
and cultured them in the absence or presence of rosiglitazone, a drug that can induce cellular
senescence and p16Ink4a expression through activation of PPARγ16. Immunofluorescence
microscopy revealed that a high proportion of cells expressed Flag-tagged FKBP–Casp8 in
the presence of rosiglitazone, but not in its absence

experiment.system: Cultured bone marrow cells from 2-month-old WT;INK-ATTAC mice
experiment.perturbation: 1 μM rosiglitazone vs vehicle
experiment.measurement: Immunofluorescence staining for Flag (FKBP–Casp8)

numbers.quantity: mouse age at bone marrow harvest

text: GFP+ cells FACS-sorted from inguinal adipose tissue of aged BubR1H/H;INK-ATTAC mice expressed much higher levels of p16Ink4a and other senescence markers than GFP− cells, and INK-ATTAC expression correlated with senescence-marker expression in IAT while aged BubR1H/H;INK-ATTAC fat stained strongly for SA-β-Gal.

quotes.quote:
Fat tissue of aged BubR1H/H;INK-ATTAC mice stained strongly for
senescence-associated-β-galactosidase (SA-β-Gal; Fig. 1e). qRT–PCR analysis
demonstrated that INK-ATTAC expression correlates with expression of senescence
markers in IAT

GFP+
cells not only expressed much higher levels of p16Ink4a than GFP− cells but also had
elevated levels of other key senescence markers

experiment.system: Inguinal adipose tissue of aged BubR1H/H;INK-ATTAC mice
experiment.perturbation: observational; FACS separation of GFP+ vs GFP− cells
experiment.measurement: SA-β-Gal staining and qRT–PCR of senescence markers

text: In WT;INK-ATTAC-3 MEFs, oncogenic Ras expression and serial passaging produced GFP+ subpopulations that stained positively for SA-β-Gal, in contrast to the GFP− cells; serial passaging and H-ras expression yielded cultures with approximately 90% and 50% GFP+ cells, respectively.

quotes.quote:
two conditions that induce p16Ink4a expression and senescence in primary
mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs), ectopic expression of oncogenic Ras and serial
passaging12,17,18, produced a subpopulation of GFP+ WT;INK-ATTAC-3 MEFs that, in
contrast to the remaining GFP− cells, stained positively for SA-β-Gal

(serial
passaging and H-ras expression yielded cultures with approximately 90% and 50% GFP+
cells, respectively)

experiment.system: Primary WT;INK-ATTAC-3 mouse embryonic fibroblasts
experiment.perturbation: H-rasG12V retroviral expression or serial passaging (12–15 passages in 20% O2)
experiment.measurement: FACS sorting of GFP+/GFP− and SA-β-Gal staining

text: Life-long AP20187 treatment (every third day from 3 weeks of age) of BubR1H/H;INK-ATTAC-3 and -5 mice substantially delayed onset of lordokyphosis and cataracts compared with untreated mice; these phenotypes were not delayed when AP20187 was given to BubR1H/H mice lacking INK-ATTAC.

quotes.quote:
we established cohorts of BubR1H/H;INK-ATTAC-3 and -5 mice, which were either
treated with AP20187 every third day beginning at 3 weeks of age or left untreated.

treated mice of both BubR1H/H;INK-ATTAC lines had substantially
delayed onset of lordokyphosis (a measure of sarcopenia onset in this model15) and cataracts
compared to untreated mice

The above age-related phenotypes were not
delayed upon AP20187 treatment of BubR1H/H mice lacking INK-ATTAC

experiment.system: BubR1H/H;INK-ATTAC-3 and -5 mice and BubR1H/H controls lacking the transgene
experiment.perturbation: AP20187 (0.2 μg g−1 i.p.) every 3 days from weaning vs untreated
experiment.measurement: Bi-weekly scoring of lordokyphosis and cataract incidence (log-rank tests)

text: Life-long AP20187 treatment prevented adipose tissue loss in BubR1H/H;INK-ATTAC mice: DEXA showed preserved adiposity, all major fat depots were larger, individual adipocytes were markedly increased in size, and lateral skin contained significantly more subdermal adipose tissue.

quotes.quote:
Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA) scans of
BubR1H/H;INK-ATTAC mice confirmed that AP20187 treatment prevented loss of adipose
tissue (Fig. 2f). All major fat deposits were larger in AP20187-treated BubR1H/H;INK-
ATTAC animals (Fig. 2f) and individual adipocytes were markedly increased in size (Fig.
2g). Consistent with this generally increased adiposity, lateral skin contained significantly
more subdermal adipose tissue

experiment.system: 10-month-old BubR1H/H;INK-ATTAC female mice
experiment.perturbation: Life-long AP20187 vs untreated
experiment.measurement: DEXA total body adipose tissue, fat depot weights, fat cell diameter, subdermal adipose layer thickness

text: p16Ink4a-independent BubR1H/H phenotypes (cardiac arrhythmias and arterial wall stiffening) were not attenuated by AP20187 in BubR1H/H;INK-ATTAC mice, correlating with lack of INK-ATTAC induction in heart and aorta, and overall survival was not substantially extended.

quotes.quote:
Age-related phenotypes of BubR1H/H mice that arise in a p16Ink4a-independent fashion, such
as cardiac arrhythmias and arterial wall stiffening14, were not attenuated in AP20187-treated
BubR1H/H;INK-ATTAC mice (Supplementary Fig. 5a, b). This correlated with lack of INK-
ATTAC induction in heart and aorta

which could
explain why the overall survival of AP20187-treated BubR1H/H;INK-ATTAC mice was not
substantially extended

experiment.system: BubR1H/H;INK-ATTAC mice
experiment.perturbation: Life-long AP20187 vs untreated
experiment.measurement: Ultrasound cardiac arrhythmia measurement, arterial wall stiffening, survival curves (log-rank)

text: WT;INK-ATTAC mice treated continuously with AP20187 until 8 months of age showed no overtly negative side effects (data not shown).

quotes.quote:
To examine whether clearance of p16Ink4a-
positive cells might have any overtly negative side effects, WT;INK-ATTAC mice were
continuously treated with AP20187 until 8 months of age; however, no such effects were
observed (data not shown).

experiment.system: WT;INK-ATTAC mice
experiment.perturbation: Continuous AP20187 treatment until 8 months of age
experiment.measurement: Observation for overt negative side effects

text: AP20187-treated BubR1H/H;INK-ATTAC mice showed marked decreases in SA-β-Gal staining and senescence-associated markers in inguinal adipose tissue, with similar reductions in skeletal muscle and eye, and BrdU incorporation was lower in IAT and muscle of untreated than treated animals.

quotes.quote:
The IAT of AP20187-treated
BubR1H/H;INK-ATTAC mice showed a marked decrease in SA-β-Gal staining compared
with the IAT of untreated counterparts (Fig. 3a). Corresponding decreases in other
senescence-associated markers were also observed, as well as expected reductions in INK-
ATTAC and GFP (Fig. 3b and Supplementary Fig. 6a). Skeletal muscle and eye had a
similar reduction in senescence indicators (Fig. 3c, d and Supplementary Fig. 6b, c). BrdU
incorporation was lower in IAT and muscle tissue of untreated than treated animals

The
expression of all genes is significantly decreased upon AP20187 treatment (P < 0.05) with
the exception of GFP in the eye.

experiment.system: 10-month-old BubR1H/H;INK-ATTAC-3 female mice, IAT, gastrocnemius and eye
experiment.perturbation: Life-long AP20187 vs untreated
experiment.measurement: SA-β-Gal staining, qRT–PCR of senescence markers, in vivo BrdU incorporation

text: Late-life AP20187 treatment started at 5 months and assessed at 10 months increased mean muscle fibre diameters, improved treadmill performance, enlarged most fat depots, and significantly increased adipocyte size and subdermal adipose layer thickness, while already-matured cataracts remained unchanged.

quotes.quote:
we started AP20187 treatment of BubR1H/H;INK-ATTAC
mice at 5 months instead of weaning age and measured p16Ink4a-dependent age-related
phenotypes at 10 months. Cataracts had already fully maturated by the onset of AP20187
treatment and remained unchanged (data not shown). Importantly, late-life treated animals
had increased mean muscle fibre diameters and showed improved performance in treadmill
exercise tests (Fig. 4a, b). Furthermore, most fat depots of these animals were enlarged and
adipocyte cell size and subdermal adipose layer thickness were significantly increased

experiment.system: BubR1H/H;INK-ATTAC-3 and -5 female mice
experiment.perturbation: AP20187 every 3 days from 5 months of age ('late-life') vs untreated
experiment.measurement: Muscle fibre diameter, treadmill exercise, fat depot weights, fat cell diameter, subdermal adipose thickness at 10 months

text: Senescence markers were substantially reduced in fat and skeletal muscle of late-life AP20187-treated animals, and comparison with 5-month-old untreated BubR1H/H;INK-ATTAC-5 mice indicated the muscle and fat improvements reflect attenuated progression of age-related decline rather than a reversal of ageing.

quotes.quote:
Senescence markers were substantially reduced in both fat and skeletal muscle of
AP20187-treated animals (Fig. 4f, g and Supplementary Fig. 7). Analysis of 5-month-old
untreated BubR1H/H;INK-ATTAC-5 mice revealed that the observed improvements in
skeletal muscle and fat of late-life treated 10-month-old BubR1H/H;INK-ATTAC-5 mice
reflect attenuated progression of age-related declines rather than a reversal of ageing

experiment.system: BubR1H/H;INK-ATTAC-5 mice at 5 months (untreated baseline) and 10 months (±late-life AP20187)
experiment.perturbation: Late-life AP20187 vs untreated, with 5-month untreated baseline comparison
experiment.measurement: SA-β-Gal staining and qRT–PCR senescence markers in IAT and gastrocnemius; muscle fibre and fat measures

text: The review reports estimates that PtdIns represents ~10–20% (mol%) of total cellular phospholipids while PtdIns4P and PtdIns(4,5)P2 constitute ~0.2–1%, with PtdIns4P and PtdIns(4,5)P2 showing about 2–5% of the labeling relative to PtdIns after long-term [3H]inositol labeling.

quotes.quote:
PtdIns repre-
sents 10–20% (mol%) of total cellular phospholipids,
whereas PtdIns4P and PtdIns(4,5)P2 constitute 0.2–1%.
Based on long-term [3H]inositol labeling, PtdIns4P and
PtdIns(4,5)P2 have about 2–5% of the labeling relative to
PtdIns

experiment.system: various cells and tissues
experiment.perturbation: observational (lipid mass estimates and long-term [3H]inositol labeling)
experiment.measurement: phosphoinositide abundance as mol% of total phospholipids and relative radiolabel incorporation

text: Recent estimates place plasma membrane PtdIns(4,5)P2 density between 5,000–20,000 molecules/µm2, with PtdIns(3,4,5)P3 about 2–5% of PtdIns(4,5)P2 and PtdIns3P about 20–30% of PtdIns4P.

quotes.quote:
Recent estimates of PtdIns(4,5)P2
density in the plasma membrane (PM) ranged between
5,000–20,000 molecules/m2 (421). The other PPIs con-
tribute even smaller amounts, PtdIns(3,4,5)P3 being about
2–5% of PtdIns(4,5)P2 and PtdIns3P about 20–30% of
PtdIns4P.

experiment.system: mammalian cell plasma membrane
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: PtdIns(4,5)P2 surface density and relative abundances of other phosphoinositides

text: Folch identified inositol in the ethanol-insoluble phospholipid fraction of bovine brain and determined that it contained phosphates and inositol in a molar ratio of 2:1, a lipid termed diphosphoinositide.

quotes.quote:
Jordi Folch who identiﬁed inositol in the etha-
nol-insoluble phospholipid fraction of bovine brain and
determined that it contained phosphates and inositol in a
molar ratio of 2:1 (450)

experiment.system: bovine brain phospholipid extracts
experiment.perturbation: observational (chemical fractionation)
experiment.measurement: molar ratio of phosphate to inositol

text: SMIT1 has a Km of ~30 µM for myo-inositol, SMIT2 a higher Km of ~150 µM, and HMIT a lower affinity with Km of ~100 µM but high capacity and highest expression in the brain.

quotes.quote:
SMIT1 has a Km of 30 M for myo-inositol, and it shows
highest expression in kidney medulla and MDCK cells

SMIT-2
has higher Km (150 M) (274), and it shows wider tissue
distribution (1292). HMIT is a H/myo-inositol cotrans-
porter that has a lower afﬁnity (Km of  100 M) but high
capacity. It shows highest expression in the brain

experiment.system: mammalian myo-inositol transporters SMIT1, SMIT2, HMIT
experiment.perturbation: observational (transport assays and expression profiling)
experiment.measurement: Km for myo-inositol and tissue expression

text: SMIT1 knockout mice develop normally but die from congenital central apnea due to abnormal respiratory rhythmogenesis, showing more than 90% reduction in brain and more than 80% in whole body myo-inositol content while brain PtdIns levels remain completely normal.

quotes.quote:
SMIT1 knockout mice develop normally but die from
congenital central apnea due to abnormal respiratory
rhythmogenesis (138, 195). These mice have more than
90% reduction in brain and more than 80% in whole body
myo-inositol content. Yet, their brain PtdIns levels are com-
pletely normal

experiment.system: SMIT1 knockout mice
experiment.perturbation: germline SMIT1 gene deletion
experiment.measurement: survival/respiratory phenotype, myo-inositol content, brain PtdIns levels

text: Pik1p inactivation by temperature-sensitive alleles causes ~50% decrease in cellular PtdIns4P and PtdIns(4,5)P2 levels, with distorted Golgi membranes, vacuole fragmentation, and defective actin polarization.

quotes.quote:
Pik1p inactiva-
tion by temperature-sensitive alleles causes 50% decrease
in cellular PtdIns4P and PtdIns(4,5)P2 levels (64, 1655).
Pik1ts strains show greatly distorted and exaggerated Golgi
membranes, vacuole fragmentation, and defective actin po-
larization at the budding pole

experiment.system: Saccharomyces cerevisiae Pik1ts strains
experiment.perturbation: temperature-sensitive inactivation of Pik1p
experiment.measurement: cellular PtdIns4P/PtdIns(4,5)P2 levels and Golgi/vacuole/actin morphology

text: Based on mass measurements, ~50% of the total cellular PtdIns(4,5)P2 pool is synthesized via wortmannin-sensitive PI4Ks, though the membrane distribution of that fraction remains to be determined.

quotes.quote:
Based on mass measurements, 50% of the total
cellular PtdIns(4,5)P2 pool is synthesized via Wm-sensitive
PI4Ks (1615), but what fraction of this is found in the
different membranes has yet to be determined.

experiment.system: cultured mammalian cells
experiment.perturbation: wortmannin inhibition of PI 4-kinases
experiment.measurement: mass measurement of PtdIns(4,5)P2 pools

text: A gene-trapped mouse lacking detectable PI4K2A protein develops and is born normal but succumbs to late-onset spinocerebellar degeneration with lipofuscin-like depositions, gliosis, loss of most Purkinje cells, and axonal degeneration in the spinal cord; a screen of patients with autosomal recessive hereditary paraplegia failed to identify pathogenic changes in PI4K2A.

quotes.quote:
The homozygous mice develop
and are born normal in spite of the lack of detectable
PI4K2A protein, but they succumb to late-onset spinocere-
bellar degeneration (1408). These animals develop severe
lipofuscin-like depositions in the cerebellum associated
with gliosis, and lose most of their Purkinje cells.

failed to identify pathogenic changes
in the PI4K2A gene (270)

experiment.system: gene-trapped PI4K2A mouse; human hereditary paraplegia patient cohort
experiment.perturbation: PI4K2A gene trap truncation; observational patient gene screening
experiment.measurement: neuropathology, survival, and PI4K2A sequence variants

text: Substrate specificity of PIP kinases is determined by the activation loop within their catalytic domains and can be reversed by swapping activation loops between the type I and type II forms.

quotes.quote:
The substrate spec-
iﬁcity of the enzymes is determined by the activation loop
within their catalytic domains and can be reversed by swap-
ping activation loops between the type I and type II forms
(832).

experiment.system: type I and type II PIP kinases
experiment.perturbation: chimeric swapping of activation loops between isoform types
experiment.measurement: lipid substrate specificity of the kinase

text: Vps34p is less sensitive to wortmannin (IC50 ~3 µM) than the mammalian PI 3-kinases (~2–5 nM), especially the class I enzymes.

quotes.quote:
Vps34p is less sensitive to the PI 3-ki-
nase inhibitor Wm (IC50: 3 M) than the mammalian PI
3-kinases (2–5 nM), especially the class I enzymes (1446).

experiment.system: yeast Vps34p and mammalian PI 3-kinases
experiment.perturbation: wortmannin inhibition
experiment.measurement: IC50 of lipid kinase activity

text: Yeast cells with deleted Vps34p lack PtdIns 3-kinase activity and the lipid PtdIns3P, indicating this enzyme is the sole source of PtdIns3P in yeast, and the enzyme can only phosphorylate PtdIns but not further phosphorylated PPIs.

quotes.quote:
Yeast cells with deleted Vps34p lack PtdIns 3-kinase activ-
ity and the lipid PtdIns3P, indicating that this enzyme is the
sole source of this lipid in yeast (1367, 1446). The enzyme is
unique among PI 3-kinases in that it can only phosphorylate
PtdIns but not further phosphorylated PPIs (1446).

experiment.system: Saccharomyces cerevisiae vps34 deletion strains
experiment.perturbation: deletion of VPS34
experiment.measurement: PtdIns 3-kinase activity and PtdIns3P levels; in vitro substrate specificity

text: Inhibition of PIKfyve by RNAi depletion, dominant negative expression, or the selective inhibitor YM2016636 leads to massive vacuolization of swollen endocytic compartments with defects in fluid phase endocytosis and retrograde endosome-to-TGN transport; germline PIKfyve deletion in mice is embryonic lethal at the preimplantation stage.

quotes.quote:
inhibition of PIKfyve function either by
RNAi-mediated depletion (1316), expression of a domi-
nant negative version (684), or pharmacological inhibition
(with a selective PIKfyve inhibitor, YM2016636; Ref. 723)
leads to massive vacuolization. These vacuoles represent
swollen endocytic compartments and are associated with
defects in ﬂuid phase endocytosis (684) and in retrograde
transport from the endosomes to the TGN (1316).

Germline deletion of PIKfyve in mice is embryonic
lethal in the preimplantation stage, and MEF cells from
heterozygotes show an increased sensitivity to the PIKfyve
inhibitor YM201636 (682).

experiment.system: cultured mammalian cells and mice
experiment.perturbation: PIKfyve RNAi, dominant negative expression, pharmacological inhibition, germline deletion
experiment.measurement: endocytic compartment morphology, fluid-phase endocytosis, retrograde transport, embryonic viability

text: A debilitating mutation in one allele of PIKfyve causes Francois-Neetens mouchetée corneal fleck dystrophy in humans, characterized by multiple focal vacuolization in the cornea.

quotes.quote:
A debilitating mutation in one
allele of PIKfyve causes Francois-Neetens mouchetée cor-
neal ﬂeck dystrophy in humans characterized by multiple
focal vacuolization in the cornea (901).

experiment.system: human patients with corneal fleck dystrophy
experiment.perturbation: observational (naturally occurring heterozygous PIKfyve mutation)
experiment.measurement: genetic linkage and corneal histopathology

text: In FcγR-mediated phagocytosis, PIPKIγ-deficient bone marrow-derived macrophages showed highly polymerized actin and impaired attachment of opsonized particles with increased RhoA and decreased Rac1 activation (corrected ratio remedied the attachment defect), while PIPKIα-deficient BMMs showed no attachment defect but impaired particle ingestion due to defective WASP and Arp 2/3-dependent actin polymerization.

quotes.quote:
where PIPKI-deﬁcient bone marrow-
derived macrophages (BMM) showed the presence of
highly polymerized actin and impaired attachment of the
opsonized particles. In contrast, BMMs from PIPKI-deﬁ-
cient mice showed no attachment defect, but instead a prob-
lem with particle ingestion (989). Remarkably, PIPKI-de-
ﬁcient cells showed increased RhoA and decreased Rac1
activation, and correction of the distorted activated RhoA/
Rac1 ratio remedied the attachment defect (989).

experiment.system: bone marrow-derived macrophages from PIPKIγ- and PIPKIα-deficient mice
experiment.perturbation: genetic deletion of specific PIP5K isoforms; FcγR-mediated phagocytosis of opsonized particles
experiment.measurement: particle attachment and ingestion, actin polymerization, RhoA/Rac1 activation

text: Ultraviolet irradiation increased nuclear PtdIns5P levels via p38 MAP-kinase-mediated phosphorylation of PIPKIIβ at Ser236 that decreased kinase activity, with the elevated PtdIns5P interacting with the ING2 protein via a PHD domain; Ser236 phosphorylation does not affect association with the -α enzyme.
