traviolet irradiation increased nuclear PtdIns5P levels by a
cascade of events that included p38 MAP-kinase mediated
phosphorylation of PIPKII at Ser236 leading to decreased
activity. Decreased activity of the kinase led to the elevation
of PtdIns5P, which, in turn, interacts with the ING2 protein
via a PHD domain.

it was impor-
tant to show that Ser236 phosphorylation of - does not
affect its association with -

experiment.system: mammalian cell nuclei
experiment.perturbation: ultraviolet irradiation; PIPKIIβ Ser236 phosphorylation
experiment.measurement: nuclear PtdIns5P levels, kinase activity, ING2 binding, heterodimer association

text: Deletion of PIPKIIβ in mice increases insulin sensitivity by enhancing Akt activation in muscle, while overexpression studies suggest the enzyme attenuates insulin signaling; consistently, generation of PtdIns5P in the PM by the bacterial phosphatase IpgD enhances Akt activity.

quotes.quote:
Deletion of PIPKII in mice increases insu-
lin sensitivity by enhancing Akt activation in muscle (848),
and overexpression studies suggest that the enzyme attenu-
ates insulin signaling (218). In agreement with these data,
generation of PtdIns5P in the PM by the bacterial phospha-
tase IpgD enhances Akt activity (1206)

experiment.system: mice and cultured cells
experiment.perturbation: PIPKIIβ gene deletion, overexpression, or bacterial IpgD-mediated PtdIns5P generation
experiment.measurement: insulin sensitivity and Akt activation

text: Homozygous deletion of PI3Kα in mouse is embryonic lethal, as is knock-in replacement with the catalytically inactive D933A mutant; mice heterozygous for this mutation showed reduced growth, hyperinsulinemia with glucose intolerance, hyperphagia, and adiposity.

quotes.quote:
Homozygous deletion of PI3K in mouse is embryonic le-
thal(143)andsoisthehomozygousreplacement(“knock-in”)of
the kinase with a catalytically inactive mutant, D933A
(457). Mice heterozygous for this mutation showed re-
duced growth, hyperinsulinemia with glucose intoler-
ance, hyperphagia, and adiposity, all signs of reduced
insulin sensitivity

experiment.system: mice
experiment.perturbation: PI3Kα gene deletion or D933A kinase-dead knock-in (homozygous and heterozygous)
experiment.measurement: embryonic viability, growth, insulin/glucose metabolic phenotypes

text: Oncogenic mutations in human PI3KCA cluster mostly in two regions coding for the helical and kinase domains, with additional ones in the NH2-terminal and C2 domains, and are found at especially high percentage in colorectal cancers and glioblastomas; oncogenic PI3Kα mutants suffice to promote proliferation and dissemination of cancer cells injected into nude mice.

quotes.quote:
It has been noted that the mutations cluster mostly in
two regions that code for the helical and kinase domains of
PI3K and some other ones within the NH2-terminal and
C2 domains (1334).

identiﬁed in a variety of cancers, at especially high percent-
age in colorectal cancers and glioblastomas

It was
also demonstrated that oncogenic mutants of PI3K are
sufﬁcient to promote cell proliferation and dissemination of
cancer cells when injected into nude mice

experiment.system: human tumor genome sequencing and nude mouse xenografts
experiment.perturbation: observational mutation surveys; expression of oncogenic PI3Kα mutants in injected cancer cells
experiment.measurement: mutation frequency/clustering and tumor cell proliferation and dissemination

text: Deletion of PI3Kβ was initially reported to cause early embryonic lethality, but later strategies replacing the enzyme with a catalytically inactive K805R form or deleting exons critical for catalytic activity unexpectedly yielded viable animals that developed to adulthood, with heterozygotes born at a sub-Mendelian ratio.

quotes.quote:
An initial study reported early embryonic lethality
in mice after deletion of PI3K (142). Later studies using
different strategies, either replacing the enzyme with a cat-
alytically inactive (K805R) form (261) or deleting exons
critical for catalytic activity (534), unexpectedly showed
that these animals were viable and developed to adulthood.
However, heterozygous mice in either case were born at a
sub-Mendelian ratio

experiment.system: mice
experiment.perturbation: PI3Kβ gene deletion, K805R kinase-dead knock-in, or exon deletion
experiment.measurement: embryonic viability, adult development, Mendelian birth ratios

text: Morpholino-induced downregulation of PI4KA in zebrafish embryos caused massive and complex developmental defects especially affecting the brain and characterized by lack of pectoral fins, a defect traced to impaired Fgf signaling and phenocopied by PI 3-kinase inhibitors.

quotes.quote:
Morpholino-induced downregulation of PI4KA in zebraﬁsh
embryos caused massive and complex developmental de-
fects especially affecting the brain and were characterized
by lack of pectoral ﬁns. This latter defect could be traced to
impaired Fgf signaling and was phenocopied by PI 3-kinase
inhibitors

experiment.system: zebrafish embryos
experiment.perturbation: morpholino knockdown of PI4KA; PI 3-kinase inhibitor treatment
experiment.measurement: developmental morphology (brain, pectoral fins) and Fgf signaling

text: RNAi screens for host factors required for the hepatitis C virus infection cycle identified PI4KA as a critical protein for HCV replication in the liver, and PI4KA interacts with the HCV viral protein NS5A.

quotes.quote:
A series of
recent studies using RNAi screens to search for cellular host
factors required for the infection cycle of hepatitic C virus
(HCV), identiﬁed PI4KA as a critical protein for HCV rep-
lication in the liver (122, 166, 1513, 1577, 1597).

This is
supported by the ﬁnding that PI4KA interacts with the HCV

experiment.system: HCV-infected liver cells
experiment.perturbation: genome-wide RNAi knockdown of host factors
experiment.measurement: HCV replication and PI4KA–NS5A interaction

text: PIP5K1γ deficiency notwithstanding, a single copy of the PIP5KIγ gene is able to support normal mouse development and life to adulthood despite clearly distinguishable roles of the type I PIP5K enzymes in specific cellular functions.

quotes.quote:
a single copy of the PIP5KI gene is able to support
normal mouse development and life to adulthood (1644) in
spite of clearly distinguishable roles of these enzymes in
speciﬁc cellular functions

experiment.system: mice with reduced PIP5KIγ gene dosage
experiment.perturbation: genetic reduction to a single PIP5KIγ gene copy
experiment.measurement: development and survival to adulthood

text: Type II PI4Ks are tightly membrane-bound due to palmitoylation of a conserved stretch of cysteines within their catalytic domains, and the majority of PI4K2A and PI4K2B were found in intracellular membranes, mostly associated with the TGN and endosomes by immunocytochemical analysis, contrary to earlier assumptions of a plasma membrane role.

quotes.quote:
Type II PI4Ks are tightly membrane-bound proteins, due to
the palmitoylation of a conserved stretch of cysteines within
their catalytic domains (108, 109).

it was
surprising to ﬁnd the majority of PI4K2A and PI4K2B en-
zymes in intracellular membranes, mostly associated with
the TGN and endosomes by immunocytochemical analysis

experiment.system: cultured mammalian cells expressing type II PI4Ks
experiment.perturbation: observational (biochemical palmitoylation analysis and immunocytochemistry)
experiment.measurement: membrane association and subcellular localization

text: Disruption of the gene Fwd encoding PI4KB in Drosophila results in male infertility due to a cytokinesis defect during spermatogenesis, while disruption of both Arabidopsis PI4KB homologs manifests in a defect in root hair growth.

quotes.quote:

experiment.measurement: fertility/cytokinesis during spermatogenesis; root hair growth

text: The p101 regulatory subunit greatly enhances the Gbetagamma sensitivity of PI3Kgamma without changing its Ras sensitivity, whereas p84/p110gamma complexes are not sensitized to Gbetagamma and instead require Ras binding for membrane recruitment and GPCR activation.

text: PI3Kgamma-deficient animals showed that the enzyme is critical in amplifying mast cell degranulation responses, and the knockout animals were protected from systemic anaphylaxis.

experiment.measurement: mast cell degranulation and systemic anaphylaxis

knockout mice developed

a kinase-independent function of PI3K in

text: SYNJ1 knockout mice are born seemingly normally but die shortly after birth, showing accumulation of clathrin-coated vesicles in nerve termini due to an uncoating defect and poor recycling into a fusion-competent synaptic vesicle pool.

experiment.perturbation: genetic deletion of SYNJ1

phatase, or Inpp5B) that does not contain a Sac1 domain

ogous 75-kDa 5-phosphatase Inpp5b (722). Combined in-

early embryonic lethality (722).

replacement of the
mouse Inpp5b with the human INPP5B version in an Ocrl

experiment.perturbation: Ocrl deletion, Ocrl/Inpp5b double inactivation, humanized INPP5B replacement
experiment.measurement: viability and disease-like phenotypes

text: Homozygous Inpp5B-deficient mice are viable and appear normal but have testicular degeneration and defective sperm function after sexual maturation, with reduced sperm motility and reduced ability to fertilize eggs.

quotes.quote:
Homozygous mice deﬁcient in Inpp5B are viable and ap-
pear normal, but do have testicular degeneration and defec-
tive sperm functions that manifest after sexual maturation
(722). The sperm of these mice show reduced motility and
reduced ability to fertilize eggs (722, 992).

experiment.system: Inpp5B knockout mice
experiment.perturbation: genetic deletion of Inpp5B
experiment.measurement: testicular histology, sperm motility and fertilization capacity

text: A G129E PTEN mutation identified in a family with Cowden disease eliminates lipid but spares protein phosphatase activity, indicating the tumor suppressive function of PTEN is primarily associated with its lipid phosphatase activity.

a G129E mutation identiﬁed in a family with Cowden dis-
ease eliminates lipid but spares the protein phosphatase
activity of the enzyme (481, 1103).

studies showed that the tumor suppressive function of
PTEN is primarily associated with its lipid phosphatase
activity.

experiment.system: PTEN enzyme and Cowden disease family genetics
experiment.perturbation: G129E point mutation
experiment.measurement: lipid versus protein phosphatase activity and tumor predisposition

text: MTM1 knockout mice show perinatal mortality and surviving pups develop centronuclear myopathy with histology reminiscent of human XLMTM; conditional tissue-specific knockouts showed skeletal muscle MTM1 deficiency is the underlying cause and that maintenance, not development, of muscle requires the enzyme.

quotes.quote:
MTM1 knockout mice show
perinatal mortality, and the pups that are born alive quickly
succumb into muscle weakness and develop centronuclear
myopathy with histological ﬁndings reminiscent of those
seen in human XLMTM disease (196).

ciency in skeletal muscle is the underlying cause of the

experiment.system: MTM1 knockout and conditional tissue-specific knockout mice
experiment.perturbation: global and tissue-specific MTM1 deletion
experiment.measurement: survival, muscle strength, muscle histology

text: A genetrap mouse lacking functional Sac2 shows no major abnormalities but is more susceptible to isoproterenol-induced cardiac hypertrophy, whereas Sac2 overexpression in hearts protects animals from developing cardiac hypertrophy.

genetrap mouse lacking a functional Sac2 shows no major

experiment.system: Sac2 genetrap and cardiac Sac2-overexpressing mice
experiment.perturbation: isoproterenol administration
experiment.measurement: cardiac hypertrophy

the response to muscarinic stimuli was greatly reduced,

text: PLCdelta1 knockout mice are viable but lose hair within 10 days of birth, are susceptible to skin inflammation and develop skin tumors, with keratinocytes showing impaired Ca2+ signal, PKC activation and NFAT transcriptional activity.

experiment.perturbation: genetic deletion of PLCdelta4

text: PLCε is both an activator and a downstream target of Ras/Rap1: its Ras GEF domain can activate Rap1 while its two RA domains bind H-Ras and Rap1, with the second (R2) more important.

The Ras
GEF domain can activate Rap1 (736), while the two RA

PLC  is both an activator and a downstream target of Ras/
Rap1

experiment.system: mammalian PLCε protein domains with Ras/Rap1 GTPases

text: Studies in astrocytes from PLCε-null mice showed PLCε is a major contributor to InsP3/DAG generation after LPA, thrombin, and S1P receptor stimulation, with LPA and S1P using pertussis toxin-sensitive Gi/o proteins and thrombin using RhoA via G12/13.

experiment.system: astrocytes from PLCε-deficient mice
experiment.perturbation: PLCε gene deletion plus GPCR agonist stimulation (LPA, thrombin, S1P)
experiment.measurement: InsP3/DAG formation

text: Two PLCε-deficient mouse lines differ in phenotype: catalytically inactive truncation mice have aortic and pulmonary semilunar valve defects with ventricular dilation and hypertrophy not seen in full-knockout mice, while full-knockout mice are more susceptible to cardiac hypertrophy and have impaired cardiac contractility.

experiment.perturbation: full PLCε deletion vs. truncated catalytically inactive PLCε allele
experiment.measurement: cardiac developmental and functional phenotypes

text: In yeast, Sec14 mutants defective in PtdIns but not PtdCho transfer can rescue the secretory defect of Sec14-deleted strains, and genetic interference with PtdCho synthesis or deletion of Kes1p bypasses Sec14p secretory defects; 'Sec14 bypass' requires the functional yeast PLD enzyme Spo14p.

PtdIns but not PtdCho transfer are able to rescue the secre-
tory defect of Sec14-deleted strains (1217)

Remarkably, genetic interference with PtdCho synthesis
rescues Sec14p secretory defects (272)

Importantly, “Sec14 bypass” conditions require
a functional yeast PLD enzyme, Spo14p

experiment.system: yeast (Sec14-deleted strains)
experiment.perturbation: expression of transfer-defective Sec14 mutants; genetic interference with PtdCho synthesis; Kes1p deletion; Spo14p loss

text: Mammalian PITPs show little sequence homology to yeast Sec14p yet can partially rescue yeast Sec14–1ts defects (but not SEC14 deletions), and Sec14p can restore PLC activity in mammalian cells; unlike for Sec14p, the PtdIns transfer activity of mammalian PITPs is important for complementation of the Sec14 defect in yeast.

show little sequence homology to the yeast Sec14p

text: PITPα-deleted mice are born normal but develop spinocerebellar degeneration, hypoglycemia, and intestinal and hepatic steatosis and die by day 12; cells from these mice showed no significant change in phosphoinositide content or in secretion, exocytosis, endocytosis, or signaling, and a PtdIns binding-deficient mutant cannot rescue the null phenotype.

text: Drosophila RdgB mutants develop light-induced retinal degeneration and impaired electroretinogram responses; these defects are fully remedied by full-length RdgB or its isolated PITP domain but not by rat PITPα or a chimeric rat PITPα-RdgB protein, and mammalian Nir2 and Nir3 can rescue the fly visual defects with Nir2 working better.

meric protein with a rat PITP fused to the rest of Dro-

are also able to rescue the visual de-

text: In mouse, Nir3 knockout mice show no obvious phenotype while Nir2 knockout is embryonic lethal; Nir2 is Golgi localized where it helps maintain DG levels, associates with lipid droplets after oleic acid treatment, and changes localization with the cell cycle.

text: Phosphoinositide regulation of ion channels/transporters was first clearly postulated for the Na+/Ca2+ exchanger (NCX1) and KATP potassium channels in giant excised patches of the heart, where current 'rundown' in excised patches was reversed by adding ATP or inositol lipids to the cytosolic face of the membrane.

has been ﬁrst clearly postulated in the case of Na/Ca2
exchanger (NCX1) and KATP potassium channels studied
in giant excised patches of the heart (616). In this and

to the cytosolic face of the membrane.

experiment.perturbation: patch excision causing lipid loss; addition of ATP or inositol lipids to cytosolic face

Golgi membranes and the actin cytoskeleton through its
binding to unconventional myosin, MYO18A (357).

The
yeast homolog of GOLPH3, Vps74p, also binds PtdIns4P,
and its steady-state Golgi localization requires Pik1p (357,
1731).

experiment.system: mammalian Golgi and yeast
experiment.perturbation: PtdIns4P-binding domain screening; manipulation of GOLPH3/MYO18A and Pik1p
experiment.measurement: lipid binding specificity, Golgi morphology, and localization

text: Autophagosome formation was found to require PtdIns 3-phosphatases such as Jumpy (MTMR14), suggesting that PtdIns3P turnover matters more than actual levels in this process.

quotes.quote:
What was surprising, though, was the ﬁnding that autopha-
gosome formation also requires PtdIns 3-phosphatases,
such as Jumpy (MTMR14) (1631, 1632), which suggests
that the turnover of PtdIns3P must be more important than
the actual levels during this process.

experiment.system: cells undergoing autophagy
experiment.perturbation: manipulation of PtdIns 3-phosphatase Jumpy/MTMR14
experiment.measurement: autophagosome formation

text: Amino acid sensing by mTORC1 is mediated by Rag GTPases and requires translocation of the mTORC1 complex to the surface of the lysosomes, with the class III PI3K hVPS34 also important for this amino acid sensing pathway.

quotes.quote:
the amino acid sensing,
however, is mediated by a different pathway that involves
the Rag GTPases (785, 1336) and one that requires trans-
location of the mTORC1 complex to the surface of the
lysosomes (1335, 1829). Curiously, the Class III PI3K
hVPS34 was found to be important for the amino acid
sensing pathway for mTORC1 activation (536, 1143).

experiment.system: mammalian cells
experiment.perturbation: amino acid stimulation; manipulation of Rag GTPases and hVPS34
experiment.measurement: mTORC1 activation and lysosomal translocation

text: Fab1p-deleted yeast strains have enlarged vacuoles and impaired transport of CPY to the vacuole, with associated weakened vacuole acidification and chromosomal segregation defects.

quotes.quote:
It is well established that
Fab1p deleted yeast strains have huge vacuoles and im-
paired transport of CPY to the vacuole (498). These defects
are also associated with weakened vacuole acidiﬁcation
(1159) and chromosomal segregation defects, the latter
probably secondary to the enlarged vacuoles (1757).

experiment.system: yeast strains
experiment.perturbation: deletion of the PtdIns(3,5)P2-producing kinase Fab1p
experiment.measurement: vacuole size, CPY transport, vacuolar acidification, chromosome segregation

text: Knock-down of PI4KII abolished Golgi recruitment of the adaptor AP-1 and impaired recruitment of AP-3 in endosomes, and knock-down of type II PI4K causes enlargement of prelysosomal/lysosomal compartments; PI4K is required for lysosomal delivery of β-glucocerebrosidase and its receptor LIMP-2.

quotes.quote:
Knock-down of
PI4KII abolished the Golgi recruitment of the heterotetra-
meric adaptor AP-1 (1680), and also impaired the recruit-
ment of AP-3 in endosomes (1330).

knock-down of type II PI4K causes en-
largement of prelysosomal/lysosomal compartments (298,
741, 1128), and PI4K is required for lysosomal delivery of
the Gaucher disease enzyme -glucocerebrosidase and its
receptor, LIMP-2 (741)

experiment.system: cultured mammalian cells
experiment.perturbation: knock-down of type II PI4K
experiment.measurement: adaptor recruitment, compartment morphology, lysosomal enzyme delivery

text: Phosphoinositide changes in nuclei of Swiss 3T3 cells stimulated with IGF-I differed significantly from those at the plasma membrane, and nuclear lipids localized to the nuclear lamina rather than membranes.

quotes.quote:
phosphoinositide
changes in the nuclei of Swiss 3T3 cells stimulated with
IGF-I were found signiﬁcantly different from those elicited
at the PM, and the nuclear lipids were identiﬁed in the
nuclear lamina rather than in the membranes (360, 1001).

experiment.system: Swiss 3T3 cells
experiment.perturbation: IGF-I stimulation
experiment.measurement: nuclear versus plasma membrane phosphoinositide changes and lipid localization

text: ING2 binds nuclear PtdIns5P via its PHD domain, associates with histone deacetylases and chromatin, and induces apoptosis via increased p53 acetylation, both of which require PtdIns5P.

quotes.quote:
The protein that re-
sponds to nuclear PtdIns5P is ING2, which speciﬁcally
binds this lipid with its PHD domain. The ING2 protein
associates with histone deacetylases and the chromatin
(522, 837) and, hence, regulates histone acetylation. ING2
induces apoptosis via increased p53 acetylation both of
which requires PtdIns5P (522).

experiment.system: nuclear ING2 in mammalian cells
experiment.perturbation: manipulation of nuclear PtdIns5P levels
experiment.measurement: lipid binding, p53 acetylation, apoptosis

text: PI3K inhibition alone is not very effective in K-Ras mutant-driven cancer cell lines, although K-Ras-p110 interaction or the presence of p85 subunits is important for K-Ras-induced carcinogenesis.

quotes.quote:
However, PI3K in-
hibition alone is not very effective in K-Ras mutant-driven
cancer cell lines (539), although it has been shown that
K-Ras-p110 interaction (539) or the presence of p85 sub-
units is important for K-Ras-induced carcinogenesis (404).

experiment.system: K-Ras mutant-driven cancer cell lines and mouse carcinogenesis models
experiment.perturbation: PI3K inhibition; disruption of K-Ras–p110 interaction or p85 subunits
experiment.measurement: cancer cell growth/carcinogenesis

text: Mutations in one allele of the Sac3/Fig4 phosphatase have been detected in 2% of ALS and PLS patients.

quotes.quote:
mutations in one allele of the Sac3/Fig4 phosphatase
have been detected in 2% of ALS (amyotrophic lateral scle-
rosis or Lou Gehrig’s disease) and PLS (primary lateral scle-
rosis) patients (252).

experiment.system: ALS and PLS patient cohorts
experiment.perturbation: observational (genetic screening)
experiment.measurement: frequency of Sac3/Fig4 allelic mutations

numbers.quantity: fraction of ALS/PLS patients with Sac3/Fig4 mutation

text: PI4K2A gene-trapped mice develop late-onset spinocerebellar degeneration, whereas no mutations in the human PI4K2A gene were found in patients with a similar condition.

quotes.quote:
PI4K2A gene-trapped mice develop late-onset
spinocerebellar degeneration (1408). Notably, though, no
mutations in the human PI4K2A gene were found in pa-
tients suffering from a similar condition (270).

experiment.system: gene-trapped mice; human patients
experiment.perturbation: PI4K2A gene trap; observational patient sequencing
experiment.measurement: spinocerebellar degeneration phenotype; PI4K2A mutation detection

text: Some studies found association of an SNP in the PI4KA promoter region with the schizophrenia phenotype and suggested PI4KA as a modifier in schizophrenia associated with 22q11.2 deletion syndromes.

quotes.quote:
However, some studies also
found association with an SNP in the PI4KA promoter re-
gion with the schizophrenia phenotype (1326, 1648) and
suggested that the PI4KA gene could be a modiﬁer in cases
of schizophrenia associated with 22q11.2 deletion syn-
dromes (1648).

experiment.system: human schizophrenia genetic association cohorts
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: SNP association with schizophrenia phenotype

text: Hepatitis C virus requires PtdIns4P specifically made by PI4KA for replication, and PI4KA activity is stimulated by the viral protein NS5A; some enteroviruses such as Polio or Coxsackie need PtdIns4P made by PI4KB for their replication organelle.

quotes.quote:
Most recently
it was discovered that hepatitis C virus requires PtdIns4P,
speciﬁcally made by PI4KA for replication (122, 1513,
1577, 1597).

requires the PI4KA enzyme whose activity is stim-
ulated by one of the viral proteins, NS5A (38, 910, 1267,
1514). Some enteroviruses, such as Polio or Coxsackie,
need PtdIns4P made by PI4KB to generate their replication
organelle (656).

experiment.system: virus-infected host cells
experiment.perturbation: depletion/inhibition of PI4KA or PI4KB; NS5A expression
experiment.measurement: viral replication and PI4K activity

text: Mycobacterium tuberculosis uses its own PtdIns-mannoside to inhibit PtdIns3P production and secretes the phosphatase SapM capable of dephosphorylating PtdIns3P, while also synthesizing PtdIns3P apparently as an intermediate of PtdIns synthesis rather than by PtdIns phosphorylation.

quotes.quote:
It uses its own PtdIns-
mannoside to inhibit PtdIns3P production (256) but also se-
cretes a phosphatase, called SapM capable of dephosphorylat-
ing PtdIns3P (1630).

While inhibiting PtdIns3P production of the host,
Mycobacteria also synthesize PtdIns3P (1085), apparently as
an intermediate of PtdIns synthesis and not as a result of PtdIns
phosphorylation (1084).

experiment.system: Mycobacterium tuberculosis in macrophages
experiment.perturbation: bacterial PtdIns-mannoside and SapM secretion
experiment.measurement: host PtdIns3P levels and bacterial PtdIns3P synthesis

text: Plasmodium falciparum produces its own inositol lipid kinases — a class III PI3K ortholog PfPI3K, a PI4K ortholog PFE0485w, and a PIP 5-kinase — and increases the levels of several inositol lipid isomers in infected red blood cells.

quotes.quote:
also produces its own inositol lipid kinases, a class III
PI3K ortholog PfPI3K (1533, 1596), a PI4K ortholog
PFE0485w (826), and a PIP 5-kinase (864) and also in-
creases the levels of several inositol lipid isomers in the
infected red blood cells (399, 1533).

experiment.system: Plasmodium falciparum-infected red blood cells
experiment.perturbation: observational (parasite infection)
experiment.measurement: parasite kinase identification and inositol lipid isomer levels

text: An inactivating mutation within the PIP 5-kinase Iγ gene causes severe developmental abnormalities with perinatal lethality; the author notes this is the only such report of loss of function of an inositol lipid kinase in human disease.

quotes.quote:
[see the only report on an
inactivating mutation within the PIP 5-kinase I gene that
causes severe developmental abnormalities with perinatal
lethality (1119)]

experiment.system: human patients
experiment.perturbation: observational (inactivating PIP 5-kinase I gene mutation)
experiment.measurement: developmental abnormalities and perinatal lethality

text: P granules in C. elegans germ cells behave as liquids: they fuse and relax to spheres, proteins within them are highly mobile and exchange rapidly with cytoplasm, and under shear force the granules flow, deform around other structures and undergo fission.

quotes.quote:
P granules fuse with one another14 and 
subsequently relax back into a spherical shape

Photobleaching experiments demonstrated that proteins are highly mobile within 
P granules, and also exchange rapidly with the surrounding cytoplasm14. Critically, under 
shear force, P granules can freely flow and deform around surfaces of other structures, as 
well as undergo fission14.

experiment.system: P granules in C. elegans germ cells
experiment.perturbation: photobleaching and applied shear force during live imaging
experiment.measurement: fusion/relaxation to sphere, fluorescence recovery, deformation and fission

text: Photobleaching recovery experiments over decades showed that components of membraneless organelles, though stably concentrated for hours to days, exchange with the surrounding medium on timescales of seconds to minutes, and like-organelles fuse upon contact.

quotes.quote:
These 
can remain stably concentrated within the structures for hours to days, yet decades of 
photobleaching recovery experiments consistently showed that many of these organelles 
could exchange with the surrounding medium on timescales of seconds to minutes5–7. They 
also displayed unexpected behaviours such as two of the same type fusing upon contact8–14.

experiment.system: membraneless compartments in eukaryotic cells (nucleoli, Cajal bodies, PML bodies etc.)
experiment.perturbation: photobleaching; observational live imaging
experiment.measurement: fluorescence recovery timescales and fusion events

text: The multivalent Nephrin–Nck–N-WASP system, assembling via pTyr–SH2 and SH3–PRM interactions, forms phase separated liquid droplets in solution and phase separated clusters on lipid bilayers when Nephrin is membrane-attached in vitro.

quotes.quote:
This assembly produces both phase separated liquid droplets suspended in solution19 and 
phase separated clusters on lipid bilayers when Nephrin is attached to membranes in vitro25

experiment.system: purified Nephrin, Nck and N-WASP, in solution and on model lipid bilayers
experiment.perturbation: mixing multivalent components; tethering Nephrin to membranes
experiment.measurement: microscopic observation of droplet/cluster formation

text: In engineered multivalent model systems (polySH3–polyPRM, multi-RNA-binding-domain proteins with repeated RNA, polySUMO–polySIM), valency and interaction affinity are key parameters: higher valency and affinity promote assembly into larger structures, enable phase separation at lower concentrations, and decrease molecular rearrangement dynamics within droplets.

quotes.quote: Experiments with these molecules have identified valency (that is, the number of

interaction modules) and affinity between the interacting modules as key parameters 
controlling phase separation. Higher valency and affinity both promote assembly into larger 
structures, enabling phase separation at lower concentrations (Fig. 2j), and decrease the 
dynamic rearrangements of molecules within phase separated droplets19,25.

experiment.system: engineered repeat proteins (polySH3/polyPRM, polySUMO/polySIM, RNA-binding repeats)
experiment.perturbation: varying valency and module affinity
experiment.measurement: threshold concentration for phase separation and droplet molecular dynamics

text: Assembly and phase separation are distinct phenomena: engineered tandem-repeat WW domain proteins polymerize when mixed with multivalent PRM partners yet remain a single macroscopically homogeneous phase.

quotes.quote:
engineered proteins consisting of tandem repeated WW domains [G] readily polymerize 
when mixed with multivalent PRM-containing partners. However, this assembly remains a 
single, macroscopically homogeneous phase30,31.

experiment.system: engineered tandem WW-domain proteins with multivalent PRM ligands in vitro
experiment.perturbation: mixing the two multivalent components
experiment.measurement: macroscopic phase behaviour (presence/absence of demixing)

text: Aromatic and charged residues drive IDR phase separation: DDX4's Phe-Gly repeats engage cation-pi interactions with Arg; mutation of aromatic residues in BuGZ and the Nephrin intracellular domain decreases phase separation; and for a given net charge, clustered (blocky) charge patterning promotes phase separation whereas uniform distribution disfavours it.

quotes.quote:
The IDR in DDX4, for 
example, contains numerous Phe-Gly repeats whose aromatic rings appear to promote phase 
separation by engaging in cation-pi interactions [G] with Arg residues intra- and 
intermolecularly22

mutation of aromatic residues in BuGZ and in the Nephrin intracellular domain (NICD) 
decreases their ability to phase separate41,43.

for 
the same net molecular charge, when the charge is uniformly distributed phase separation is 
disfavoured, whereas when charged residues are clustered phase separation is 
promoted22,32,43,46.

experiment.system: IDR-containing proteins (DDX4, BuGZ, NICD) in vitro and in cells
experiment.perturbation: mutation of aromatic residues; alteration of charge patterning
experiment.measurement: phase separation propensity/droplet formation

text: IDRs from FUS, Taf15, hnRNPA2, EWS and CIRBP form solid-like hydrogels when concentrated in vitro, and X-ray diffraction, electron microscopy and chemical footprinting indicate these hydrogels contain long filaments generated from b-strand interactions resembling amyloid fibres.

quotes.quote:
The IDRs from RNA-binding proteins FUS, Taf15, hnRNPA2, EWS, and CIRBP form solid-
like hydrogels when concentrated in vitro21,40,47

Based on a 
combination of X-ray diffraction, electron microscopy, and chemical footprinting [G] data, 
these hydrogels contain long filaments that appear to be generated from interactions between 
stretches of b-strands, similar to those observed in amyloid fibres

experiment.system: purified IDRs of RNA-binding proteins in vitro
experiment.perturbation: concentrating the IDRs to form hydrogels
experiment.measurement: X-ray diffraction, electron microscopy, chemical footprinting

text: Condensate formation depends on components exceeding a threshold concentration: nucleoli in C. elegans embryos form only when Fib1 is above a threshold concentration, decreasing nucleolar component concentration by increasing cell volume decreases nucleolar size, and expanding isolated nuclei in hypotonic solution reversibly dissolves PML bodies and nucleoli.

quotes.quote:
nucleoli in C. 
elegans embryos form only when the nucleolar component Fib1 (and perhaps other key 
molecules) is above a threshold concentration53.

expanding the volume of 
isolated nuclei by placing them in a hypotonic solution leads to a reversible dissolution of 
PML bodies and nucleoli59. Likewise, in C. elegans embryos decreasing the concentration of 
nucleolar components by increasing cell volume, leads to nucleolar size decrease53.

experiment.system: C. elegans embryo nucleoli; isolated nuclei with PML bodies and nucleoli
experiment.perturbation: varying component concentration via cell volume; hypotonic swelling of nuclei
experiment.measurement: presence/size of condensates by microscopy

text: Post-translational modification and ligand binding tune the phase separation threshold: more pTyr residues in Nephrin and LAT assemblies promote phase separation, Arg methylation hinders DDX4 phase separation, SUMOylation of PML influences number and structure of PML bodies, and RNA lowers the concentration at which PGL3 phase separates while MEX-5, which competes for RNA, raises the PGL3 solubility limit.

quotes.quote:
higher numbers of pTyr 
residues promote phase separation, enabling control of phase separation through modulating 
the activity of kinases and phosphatases19,25,26. Similarly, phase separation of the nuage [G] 
protein DDX4 is hindered by Arg methylation, which likely decreases the number of cation-
pi interactions22.

the solubility of a P granule component, PGL3, decreases in vitro in 
the presence of RNA; in other words, PGL-3 phase separates at lower concentrations. 
Proteins that compete for RNA binding with PGL3, such as MEX-5, can then increase the 
solubility limit of PGL3 in the presence of RNA

experiment.system: Nephrin/LAT signalling assemblies, DDX4, PML protein, PGL3 with RNA and MEX-5
experiment.perturbation: phosphorylation, Arg methylation, SUMOylation, addition of RNA or competitor MEX-5
experiment.measurement: phase separation threshold concentration; number/structure of PML bodies

text: Compositional control of condensates follows scaffold–client stoichiometry rules: polySUMO–polySIM droplets in vitro and in cells recruit low-valency clients depending on the relative scaffold stoichiometry, with large changes in client recruitment from very small stoichiometric changes near equality, and higher-valency clients recruited more strongly; perturbing scaffold stoichiometry in PML nuclear bodies and yeast P bodies likewise changed client recruitment.

quotes.quote:
phase separated droplets formed by polySUMO–polySIM scaffolds differentially 
recruited low valency clients (e.g. GFP-SUMO or GFP-SIM) depending on the relative 
stoichiometries of the scaffold components (Fig.3a and 3b).

around 
stoichiometric equality even very small changes in relative concentrations of polySUMO 
and polySIM could drive large changes in client recruitment. In addition, clients with higher 
valency (for example containing more than one SUMO domain) were recruited more 
strongly (Fig. 3c).

perturbing scaffold stoichiometries (by mutating 
SUMOylation sites or modulating cellular mRNA levels, respectively), resulted in changes 
in client recruitment.

experiment.system: polySUMO–polySIM model scaffolds in vitro and in cells; mammalian PML nuclear bodies; yeast P bodies
experiment.perturbation: altering scaffold SUMO:SIM ratio, client valency, mutating SUMOylation sites, modulating mRNA levels
experiment.measurement: client partitioning/recruitment into droplets and bodies

text: Reconstituted LAT signalling clusters selectively exclude negatively charged proteins and concentrate positively charged ones, and reconstituted T-cell receptor signalling clusters concentrate kinases while excluding phosphatases, stabilizing the phosphorylation-dependent clusters.

quotes.quote:
This was shown recently in reconstituted LAT signalling 
clusters, which selectively exclude negatively charged proteins and concentrate positively 
charged proteins, probably because the scaffold components of this Condensate are highly 
negatively charged26.

reconstituted T-cell receptor signalling clusters concentrate kinases but exclude 
phosphatases, stabilizing the phosphorylation-dependent clusters26.

experiment.system: reconstituted LAT/T-cell receptor signalling clusters on membranes
experiment.perturbation: addition of charged proteins, kinases and phosphatases to reconstituted clusters
experiment.measurement: partitioning/exclusion of proteins from clusters

text: IDR-based condensates mature: droplets of proteins such as FUS, Pub1, LSm4, eIF4GII, Tia1, hnRNPA1, Whi3 and Fib1 that are initially fluid become more viscoelastic over the course of several hours, eventually behaving as solids and ceasing to exchange molecules with the surroundings; maturation is not observed for droplets formed by modular-domain proteins.

quotes.quote:
many droplets formed by IDR-containing 
proteins that are initially fluid become more viscoelastic over the course of several hours

eventually behaving as 
solids and ceasing to exchange molecules with the surroundings. This process is referred to 
as maturation, or hardening

Note that maturation is not observed with 
phase separated liquids formed by proteins composed of modular domains; in these systems 
dynamic behaviours are constant

experiment.system: in vitro droplets of IDR-containing proteins vs modular-domain proteins
experiment.perturbation: incubation over time (aging)
experiment.measurement: viscoelasticity, FRAP exchange, droplet morphology

text: Material properties are encoded in part by prion-like domains: the prion-domain protein XVelo of Xenopus Balbiani bodies forms solid-like structures when expressed from baculovirus and its prion-like domain forms solids, whereas the prion-like domain of FUS forms liquids.

quotes.quote:
In Xenopus oocytes they are formed from a prion-domain containing 
protein called XVelo, which when expressed from baculovirus forms solid-like structures. 
Other proteins containing prion-like domain, such as FUS, form liquids in vitro15. Indeed, 
expression of the prion-like domain of FUS forms liquids, while that of Xvelo forms 
solids71.

experiment.system: XVelo and FUS prion-like domains, baculovirus expression / in vitro
experiment.perturbation: expressing isolated prion-like domains
experiment.measurement: material state (liquid vs solid) of the assemblies

text: Droplet maturation in vitro occurs together with macroscopic formation of filamentous structures, fully matured droplets contain amyloid-like filaments observable by electron microscopy, and Balbiani bodies are rich in b-sheet as assessed by Thioflavin T staining; chemical footprinting suggests fibre formation in condensates also occurs in cells.

quotes.quote:
droplet maturation occurs in vitro concomitant with macroscopic formation of filamentous 
structures15,34–36,42,48, and fully matured droplets contain amyloid-like filaments observable 
by electron microscopy21,42,71. Balbiani bodies are rich in b-sheet as assessed by Thioflavin 
T staining. Chemical footprinting studies suggest that fibre formation in Condensates also 
occurs in cells48.

experiment.system: in vitro matured protein droplets; Balbiani bodies; cells
experiment.perturbation: aging of droplets; observational staining
experiment.measurement: electron microscopy of filaments, Thioflavin T staining, chemical footprinting

text: Energy-dependent processes regulate condensate dynamics: ATP depletion increases the viscosity of stress granules and nucleoli, and several ATPases regulate stress granule dynamics, increasing or decreasing their persistence.

quotes.quote:
Indeed, depletion of ATP increases the viscosity of stress granules 
and nucleoli13,51. Moreover, several ATPases can regulate the dynamics of stress granules, 
increasing or decreasing their persistence49,51.

experiment.system: stress granules and nucleoli in cells
experiment.perturbation: ATP depletion; perturbation of ATPases
experiment.measurement: granule viscosity and persistence

text: Nucleoli are multiphase condensates whose subcompartments have distinct viscosities, surface tensions and compositions, with encapsulation of one subcompartment by another enabled by the distinct surface tensions of the phases.

quotes.quote:
A recent study examined this in detail for nucleoli, 
demonstrating that the subcompartments have distinct viscosities, surface tensions and 
compositions70. The encapsulation of one subcompartment by another is enabled by the 
distinct surface tensions of the phases

experiment.system: nucleoli and reconstituted nucleolar components
experiment.perturbation: observational; physical characterization of coexisting phases
experiment.measurement: viscosity, surface tension, composition of subcompartments

text: Condensates can accelerate reactions: the total solution activity of the Hammerhead ribozyme can increase up to ~70-fold when concentrated with its substrate RNA strand into phase separated droplets in vitro, and actin polymerization rates are substantially accelerated by concentrating Arp2/3 and N-WASP into Nephrin–Nck–N-WASP droplets or membrane clusters; histone mRNA-processing rate is significantly reduced when key components fail to concentrate in the histone locus body.

quotes.quote:
the total solution activity of 
the Hammerhead ribozyme [G] can increase up to ~70-fold when it is concentrated along 
with its substrate RNA strand into phase separated droplets in vitro99. Actin polymerization 
rates can also be substantially accelerated by concentrating the Arp2/3 complex and N-
WASP into Nephrin–Nck–N-WASP-based droplets or clusters on model membranes19,25.

the rate 
of histone mRNA-processing is significantly reduced when key components of this process 
fail to concentrate within the histone locus body96.

experiment.system: Hammerhead ribozyme in aqueous two-phase droplets; Nephrin–Nck–N-WASP droplets/clusters with Arp2/3; histone locus bodies in cells
experiment.perturbation: concentrating enzyme with substrate into condensed phase; preventing component concentration in histone locus body
experiment.measurement: reaction rate / total solution activity

numbers.quantity: increase in Hammerhead ribozyme total solution activity

text: Concentration into a condensed phase does not always accelerate reactions: disrupting Cajal body formation and dispersing guide RNAs in the nucleoplasm does not appear to affect the efficiency of small nuclear RNA modification, and purine biosynthetic enzyme activity was not significantly enhanced when concentrated with substrate into droplets in vitro, owing to lower specific activities within the droplets.

quotes.quote:
disrupting 
Cajal body formation and thereby dispersing guide RNAs in the nucleoplasm does not seem 
to affect the efficiency of small nuclear RNA modification22,100. Similarly, the activity of 
enzymes in the purine biosynthetic pathway was not significantly enhanced when they were 
concentrated with their substrate into phase separated droplets in vitro101.
This lack of

enhancement was due to the lower specific activities of the enzymes towards their substrates 
within the droplets as compared to their activity in solution.

experiment.system: Cajal bodies/guide RNAs in cells; purine biosynthetic enzymes in phase separated droplets in vitro
experiment.perturbation: disrupting Cajal body formation; concentrating enzymes with substrates into droplets
experiment.measurement: snRNA modification efficiency; enzyme specific activity

text: Enzyme clustering can direct metabolic flux: clustering the branch point enzyme carB with one downstream enzyme, pyrB, but not another, argI, directed carbamoyl phosphate flux to favour pyrimidine and disfavour arginine in Escherichia coli.

quotes.quote:
clustering the 
metabolic branch point enzyme, carB, with one downstream enzyme, pyrB, but not another, 
argI, was shown to direct the metabolic flux of carbamoyl phosphate to favour pyrimidine 
and disfavour arginine in Escherichia coli106.

experiment.system: Escherichia coli metabolic pathway enzymes
experiment.perturbation: engineered clustering of carB with pyrB or argI
experiment.measurement: metabolic flux of carbamoyl phosphate to pyrimidine vs arginine

text: The authors report unpublished observations that one type of condensate typically constitutes only 1–2 % of the cellular volume, implying that effective sequestration would require very high partition coefficients.

quotes.quote:
Since one type of Condensate typically constitutes only 1–2 % of the cellular 
volume (unpublished observations from Rosen and Hyman labs), strong inhibition (high 
depletion of the molecule from the surrounding nucleo- or cytoplasm) would require very 
high partition coefficients [G] for the sequestered component.

experiment.system: cells containing biomolecular condensates (Rosen and Hyman labs, unpublished)
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: fraction of cellular volume occupied by one condensate type

numbers.quantity: fraction of cellular volume of one condensate type

text: Phase separation can be switched sharply by minute changes in physical parameters: changes of 1 °C can cause condensation or dissolution of BUgZ, DDX4, hnRNPA1 or FUS droplets, and modest changes in salt concentration have similar effects.

quotes.quote:
changes of 1 °C can cause condensation or dissolution of BUgZ, DDX4, hnRNPA1 
or FUS droplets22,34,41. Modest changes in salt concentration can have similar effects22,42.

experiment.system: in vitro droplets of BUgZ, DDX4, hnRNPA1, FUS
experiment.perturbation: small changes in temperature or salt concentration
experiment.measurement: droplet condensation or dissolution

text: Genetic studies indicate that only a small subset of condensate components are scaffolds essential for formation — for example PML is the only protein known to be essential to form PML nuclear bodies, Spd5 for C. elegans centrosomes, TIA1 for stress granules, NEAT1 non-coding RNA for paraspeckles and mRNAs for P bodies — while the majority of components are dispensable clients.

quotes.quote:
For example, PML is the 
only protein known to be essential to form PML nuclear bodies66. Similarly, Spd5 is the key 
component necessary for formation of C. elegans centrosomes67, TIA1 for stress granules68, 
the NEAT1 non-coding RNA for paraspeckles [G], and mRNAs for P bodies2.

experiment.system: PML bodies, centrosomes, stress granules, paraspeckles, P bodies
experiment.perturbation: genetic depletion/knockout of candidate components
experiment.measurement: presence or absence of condensate formation

text: Decreasing the number of Gly/Ser-Phe/Tyr-Gly/Ser motifs in hnRNPA2 and FUS decreases the efficiency of their recruitment into IDR-based droplets in vitro and into stress granules in cells, respectively, by reducing client valency.

quotes.quote:
decreasing 
the number of Gly/Ser-Phe/Tyr-Gly/Ser motifs in hnRNPA2 and FUS decreases the 
efficiency of their recruitment into IDR-based droplets in vitro48 and into stress granules in 
cells40, respectively by reducing the valency of these clients.

experiment.system: hnRNPA2 and FUS as clients of IDR-based droplets in vitro and stress granules in cells
experiment.perturbation: reducing the number of Gly/Ser-Phe/Tyr-Gly/Ser motifs
experiment.measurement: recruitment efficiency into droplets/granules

text: Nuclear bodies including Cajal bodies, PML bodies, histone locus bodies, nuclear speckles and nucleoli can be induced by experimentally concentrating their key components at a particular cellular site, and condensate sizes scale with expression levels of key components for engineered DDX4 and NICD as well as natural condensates.

quotes.quote:
This has, indeed, been observed quantitatively with engineered DDX4 and NICD as well as 
qualitatively with natural Condensates, such as PML bodies, nucleoli, P bodies, stress 
granules and centrosomes22,43, whose sizes scale with expression levels of key components.

speckles (artificial) and nucleoli (natural) can be induced by experimentally concentrating 
their key components at a particular cellular site54–58.

pocket proteins inhibit E2F activity (FIG. 1). Whi5 is phosphorylated by G1 cyclin–Cdk,

text: PIP-mediated regulatory mechanisms controlling PP1 holoenzyme formation include regulated proteolysis of PIPs, phosphorylation of Ser/Thr residues in or near RVxF-type docking sequences that reduces binding affinity for the RVxF-binding channel, recruitment or release of inhibitory PIPs, allosteric regulation by metabolites or proteins, masking of substrate phosphosites by 14-3-3 proteins, and competition of PIPs for the same PP1 binding sites.

quotes.quote:
Recent data show that the concentration of several PIPs is controlled by
regulated proteolysis [69–72]. Moreover, many signaling pathways interfere with the
affinity of specific PIPs for PP1. For example, phosphorylation of Ser/Thr residues in or
near RVxF-type docking sequences is often associated with a reduced binding affinity for
the RVxF-binding channel [54]. Signaling can also result in the recruitment or release of
inhibitory PIPs [11,19,73]. Another PIP control mechanism involves positive or negative
allosteric regulation by metabolites or other proteins [74,75]. The PP1-mediated
dephosphorylation of some substrate- PIPs is restrained through regulated masking of the
phosphorylated residues by 14-3-3 proteins [20,23,76–78]. Finally, PP1–PIP complexes are
highly dynamic and different PIPs compete for the same PP1 binding sites [77,78].

text: Simulations by Harmon and colleagues predicted that linker length and linker-solvent interactions determine whether multivalent proteins assemble with or without concomitant phase separation: very short linkers favor dimers and inhibit phase separation, solvent-favorable linkers give sol-gel transitions in homogeneous solution, and solvent-unfavorable linkers promote phase separation.

quotes.quote:
Using simulations, Harmon and colleagues 
predicted that the linkers between modular binding domains will strongly influence whether 
proteins assemble with or without concomitant phase separation (58). Very short linkers 
favor formation of dimers over large oligomers and therefore inhibit phase separation.

Linkers with favorable interactions with solvent 
inhibit phase separation, since they are highly extended (corresponding to a large excluded 
volume), thus leading to sol-gel transitions in homogeneous solution. In contrast, linkers 
with unfavorable interactions with solvent will promote phase separation

experiment.system: computational model of multivalent proteins with modular binding domains and linkers
experiment.perturbation: varying linker length and linker–solvent interaction
experiment.measurement: simulated propensity for gelation versus phase separation

text: Computational modeling of the Rubisco–EPYC1 pyrenoid system, in which Rubisco has eight binding sites for EPYC1 and EPYC1 has four binding sites for Rubisco, predicts a "magic number" effect in which LLPS is inhibited at equal module concentrations due to formation of closed oligomers, giving unexpectedly sharp phase transitions.

quotes.quote:
Rubisco has eight binding sites for EPYC1, while EPYC1 has four binding sites for 
Rubisco. Modeling suggests that such systems will exhibit a “magic number” effect where 
certain numbers of particles form an unusually stable state.

In this situation, LLPS is 
inhibited when the molecules are at the same module concentration due to formation of 
closed oligomers that do not further polymerize.

is predicted to give rise to unexpectedly 
sharp phase transitions.

experiment.system: computational model of multivalent Rubisco–EPYC1 binding (pyrenoid)
experiment.perturbation: varying relative valency and stoichiometry of binding modules
experiment.measurement: predicted phase behavior / phase diagram

text: On fluid bilayers, membrane-attached monovalent proteins have low affinity for soluble bi-valent antibodies at low density, but the apparent affinity increases as the monovalent protein density increases, indicating density-dependent multivalency.

text: When mixed with multivalent carbohydrates in vitro, galectin-3 rapidly precipitates into micrometer-sized irregularly shaped clusters over a narrow range of carbohydrate concentrations, suggested to represent a solid phase; separately, the disordered N-terminal domain of galectin-3 was shown to undergo LLPS through multivalent interactions with other galectin-3 carbohydrate recognition domains.

over a narrow range of carbohydrate concentrations and was suggested to represent a solid

text: In vitro reconstitutions demonstrated that multivalent interactions between phospho-LAT, Grb2 and Sos1 promote LLPS forming micron-scale clusters on membranes, and that pLAT with either Grb2 and Sos1, or Gads and SLP-76, is sufficient; reconstitution of the pathway from the TCR ζ-chain to the Arp2/3 complex showed the clusters potently assembled actin filaments on the bilayer.

interactions of pLAT with either Grb2 and Sos1, or Gads and SLP-76 are sufficient to

text: In the reconstituted LAT system, clustering had three functional consequences: increased specific actin assembly activity, electrostatic sorting in which positively charged proteins concentrated in LAT clusters while negatively charged proteins were excluded, and correlation of in vitro phase separation with in vivo MAPK signaling in T cells.

First, it increased 
the specific actin assembly activity of molecules in the pathway

positively charged proteins 
concentrated in LAT clusters while negatively charged proteins were excluded, producing a 
distinct chemical environment from the surrounding membrane. Finally, in vitro phase

text: During Jurkat T cell activation on α-TCR antibody-coated fluid bilayers, LAT clusters form at the periphery and move radially inward, with Nck dissociating approximately half-way through the trajectory where actin architecture changes from a branched network to actin arcs; reconstitutions showed Nck and N-WASP basic regions act as high-density clutches, and clusters engineered with a constitutive basic clutch deviated from the normal trajectory.

LAT clusters form at the periphery of the cell-membrane interface and move radially toward 
its center through the actions of cortical actomyosin. Nck, and presumably its ligand, WASP, 
were found to dissociate from clusters approximately half-way through this trajectory.

In biochemical reconstitutions it was shown that Nck and the 
WASP homolog, N-WASP, contain basic regions that, at high density, act as clutches that 
couple LAT cluster movement to actomyosin movement.

clusters that constitutively contain a basic clutch were found to 
deviate from their normal trajectory from periphery to center of the cell-membrane interface.

experiment.perturbation: cluster composition changes, including constitutive basic clutch in clusters
experiment.measurement: imaging of cluster trajectories, composition, and actin architecture

text: ZAP-70 transiently associates with single TCR molecules but persistently localizes with TCR clusters, indicating that stable ZAP-70 recruitment to the TCR requires TCR clustering.

since stable ZAP-70 recruitment to the TCR requires

the

text: Addition of Nck and N-WASP to phosphorylated nephrin tail leads to LLPS in solution and micrometer-scale clusters on supported lipid bilayers; in vitro clustering occurs sharply above a threshold Nck concentration that is raised by decreasing nephrin pTyr sites or Nck SH3 domains, and in cells nephrin cluster probability increases with Nck expression in an SH3 valency-dependent manner, with clusters showing liquid-like fusion and exchange.

solution or membrane
