readily reversible and easily disrupted by competition with other Ub binding domains or 
high salt concentrations (Peth et al., 2010). This initial binding depends only on the presence 
of a Ub chain, is independent of ATP hydrolysis, and even occurs at 4°C. In contrast, the 
second tight-binding step that commits the substrate to degradation requires ATP hydrolysis 
and a loosely folded region in the substrate

experiment.system: purified 26S proteasomes with ubiquitylated substrates
experiment.perturbation: competition with Ub-binding domains, high salt, low temperature, ATP hydrolysis blockade
experiment.measurement: retention of substrate binding to the 26S

numbers.quantity: temperature at which initial binding still occurs

text: In vitro yeast 26S lacking either Rpn13 or Rpn10's UIM domain show ~50% reduced conjugate binding, and proteasomes lacking both retain about 20% of normal 26S affinity for Ub conjugates.

quotes.quote:
In 
vitro yeast 26S lacking either Rpn13 or the UIM domain of Rpn10 show reduced binding of 
conjugates by ∼50% (Peth et al., 2010).

purified proteasomes lacking both Rpn13 and Rpn10's 
UIM domain retain about 20% the affinity of normal 26S for Ub conjugates (Peth et al., 
2010)

experiment.system: purified yeast 26S proteasomes
experiment.perturbation: deletion of Rpn13 and/or the Rpn10 UIM domain
experiment.measurement: binding affinity for ubiquitin conjugates

numbers.quantity: reduction in conjugate binding with single deletion

text: Rpn1 was identified as a conjugate binding subunit containing two sites: T1, where UBL-UBA proteins and Ub chains bind, and T2, where the UBL domain of the DUB Ubp6 binds.

quotes.quote:
Rpn1 contains two conjugate binding 
sites: T1, where UBL-UBA proteins and Ub chains bind, and T2, where the UbL domain of 
the DUB Ubp6 binds (Shi et al., 2016).

experiment.system: yeast proteasome subunit Rpn1 with Ub chains, UBL-UBA proteins and Ubp6
experiment.perturbation: binding assays/structural mapping of Rpn1 sites
experiment.measurement: identification of distinct binding sites T1 and T2

numbers.quantity: number of conjugate binding sites on Rpn1

text: On proteasome inhibition or impaired 26S function, the 26S-associated ligase Ube3c ubiquitylates Rpn13, which prevents further conjugate binding and inactivates the 26S; in plants the same modification instead targets the 26S to autophagy.

quotes.quote:
Rpn13 becomes ubiquitylated 
by the 26S-associated Ub ligase Ube3c (Besche et al., 2014; Jacobson et al., 2014). This 
modification prevents further binding of Ub conjugates inactivating the 26S

in plants, 
where proteasome inhibition also causes Rpn13 ubiquitylation, this modification targets the 
26S to autophagy (Marshall et al., 2015)

experiment.system: mammalian and plant cells and their 26S proteasomes
experiment.perturbation: proteasome inhibitors, heat shock, or expression of aggregation-prone proteins
experiment.measurement: Rpn13 ubiquitylation, conjugate binding to 26S, proteasome fate

text: For ubiquitylated DHFR, longer chains of 5-9 ubiquitins gave greater proteasome affinity but did not change its degradation rate, indicating binding is not the rate-limiting step for this protein.

quotes.quote:
these investigators actually 
found that longer chains containing 5-9 ubiquitins on dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) 
provided greater affinity for proteasomes, but did not change its degradation rate (Thrower et 
al., 2000). Thus, for this protein, binding to the 26S is not the rate-limiting step in 
proteasomal degradation.

experiment.system: purified proteasomes with ubiquitylated DHFR
experiment.perturbation: varying K48 Ub chain length
experiment.measurement: proteasome binding affinity and degradation rate

numbers.quantity: Ub chain lengths giving greater affinity

text: Single-molecule imaging of fluorescent Ub conjugates showed degradation rates increased with the number of attached ubiquitins up to eight (the longest chain measured), and multi-ubiquitylated substrates had longer dwell times than those with the same number of Ub in a single chain, while a single Ub contributed little to 26S binding.

quotes.quote:
Lu et 
al using fluorescent Ub conjugates and single-molecule imaging to measure both the 
degradation rate and the dwell-time of conjugates on the 26S before they are either released 
or degraded (Lu et al., 2015). Degradation rates increased with the number of Ub molecules 
attached up to eight (the longest chain measured). Multi-ubiquitylated substrates had longer 
dwell times than ones with the same number of Ub molecules in a single chain (Lu et al., 
2015). However, a single Ub on the substrate contributed little to 26S binding.

experiment.system: purified 26S proteasomes with fluorescent ubiquitin conjugates
experiment.perturbation: varying number and distribution of attached ubiquitins
experiment.measurement: single-molecule degradation rate and dwell-time

text: Upon proteasome inhibition in cells, ubiquitylated proteins accumulate containing all seven different Ub linkage types except K63, yet purified proteasomes bind K63 and K48 conjugates with similar high affinities and degrade them rapidly; K63 chains instead bind ESCRT proteins and are shunted to lysosomes.

quotes.quote:
Upon proteasome inhibition in cells, ubiquitylated proteins accumulate that contain all seven 
different types of Ub linkages except K63 (Xu et al., 2009)

proteins bearing K63 
and K48 Ub chains bind to purified proteasomes with similar high affinities (Peth et al., 
2010) and are degraded rapidly (Hofmann and Pickart, 2001). However, in the cytosol, K63 
chains do not typically reach the 26S because they bind preferentially to ESCRT proteins 
and are thereby shunted to lysosomes (Nathan et al., 2013).

experiment.system: cells and purified proteasomes
experiment.perturbation: proteasome inhibition; comparison of K48 vs K63 chain-bearing substrates
experiment.measurement: quantitative proteomics of accumulated linkage types; proteasome binding affinity and degradation rate

text: Forked chains formed on adjacent lysines of the donor Ub are not degraded, and cytosolic UIM proteins such as Rpn10 prevent this dead-end ubiquitylation, whereas branched chains with more distantly separated lysines are efficiently degraded.

quotes.quote:
If two Ub chains are formed on adjacent lysines of the donor Ub, creating a forked 
chain, they are not degraded (Kim et al., 2009). Although purified RING E3s tend to form 
such non-degradable forked chains, cytosolic UIM proteins (e.g. Rpn10) have the surprising 
capacity to prevent this apparent dead-end ubiquitylation (Kim et al., 2009). By contrast, 
proteasomes efficiently degrade substrates bearing branched chains

experiment.system: in vitro ubiquitylation with purified RING E3s and proteasomes
experiment.perturbation: formation of forked vs branched chains; addition of UIM proteins (Rpn10)
experiment.measurement: chain composition and proteasomal degradation

text: Methotrexate-bound DHFR assumes a tightly folded structure that prevents its degradation without affecting initial Ub-dependent binding to the 26S, blocking instead the transition to the tightly bound committed state.

quotes.quote:
in the presence of its inhibitor, the widely-used drug methotrexate, DHFR assumes a tightly 
folded structure that prevents DHFR degradation (Johnston et al., 1995; Thrower et al., 
2000). Methotrexate does not affect the initial Ub-dependent binding to the 26S, but does 
block the transition to the tightly bound, committed state (Peth et al., 2010).

experiment.system: ubiquitylated DHFR with purified 26S proteasomes and cells
experiment.perturbation: addition of methotrexate to stabilize DHFR folding
experiment.measurement: degradation rate and initial vs tight binding to the 26S

text: Analysis of sequences promoting proteasomal degradation concluded the unstructured region should contain at least 30 amino acids, have little flexibility, and be composed of varied amino acids biased toward hydrophobic residues.

quotes.quote:
to 
promote degradation, the unstructured region should contain at least 30 amino acids (van der 
Lee et al., 2014), have little flexibility and be composed of varied amino acids, but biased 
towards hydrophobic residues (Yu et al., 2016)

experiment.system: model substrates with defined unstructured initiation regions
experiment.perturbation: variation of length, flexibility, and composition of the unstructured region
experiment.measurement: proteasomal degradation efficiency

text: Cells maintain free ubiquitin at about 20μM; deleting Ubp6/Usp14 prevents efficient Ub recycling and reduces proteolysis unless Ub is overexpressed, and mice lacking Usp14 in neurons develop Ub deficiency, synaptic dysfunction and ataxia reversed by Ub overexpression.

quotes.quote:
Cells maintain high concentrations (∼20μM) 
of free Ub (Kaiser et al., 2011), but deleting Ubp6/Usp14 prevents efficient Ub recycling 
leading to proteasomal destruction of Ub.

In yeast lacking 
Ubp6, proteolysis is reduced, unless Ub is also overexpressed (Hanna et al., 2003). 
Similarly, mice lacking Usp14 in neurons develop Ub deficiency leading to synaptic 
dysfunction and ataxia (Wilson et al., 2002), which is also reversed by Ub overexpression

experiment.system: yeast and mouse neurons
experiment.perturbation: deletion of Ubp6/Usp14, with or without ubiquitin overexpression
experiment.measurement: free ubiquitin levels, rates of proteolysis, growth, synaptic function and ataxia phenotype

text: Inactivating Rpn11 traps ubiquitylated proteins on the 26S; Rpn11 is positioned just above the substrate entry channel and can scan substrates as they enter the ATPase ring.

quotes.quote:
Inactivating 
Rpn11 traps ubiquitylated proteins on the 26S (Matyskiela et al., 2013). Rpn11 is positioned 
just above the substrate entry channel (Beck et al., 2012; Lander et al., 2012), and thus can 
scan substrates as they enter the ATPase ring.

experiment.system: 26S proteasome with ubiquitylated substrates
experiment.perturbation: inactivation of the Rpn11 metalloprotease
experiment.measurement: retention of ubiquitylated substrates on the 26S; cryo-EM positioning of Rpn11

text: Usp14/Ubp6 acts in a kinetic competition: it shortens substrate dwell-time by deubiquitylation and allosterically reduces degradation in the absence of conjugates, while binding of Ub conjugates to its active site allosterically stimulates 20S gate opening and substrate entry; small-molecule Usp14 inhibitors were developed to enhance degradation.

quotes.quote:
In deubiquitinating substrates, Usp14 and Uch37 also serve to limit the substrate's dwell-
time on the 26S (Crosas et al., 2006). These DUB activities thus constitute a timing 
mechanism determining whether a conjugate becomes committed to degradation or released 
from the 26S and escapes destruction

provided the rationale for their 
development of small molecule Usp14 inhibitors to enhance substrate degradation (Lee et 
al., 2010)

The binding of Ub conjugates to the active site of Usp14 allosterically stimulates substrate entry into the 20S 
which involves opening its gated central pore

experiment.system: purified 26S proteasomes and cells
experiment.perturbation: Ub conjugate binding to Usp14, Usp14 deletion, small-molecule Usp14 inhibitors
experiment.measurement: substrate dwell-time, deubiquitylation rate, 20S gate opening and degradation

text: Proteasomes from cells lacking Usp14 show higher ATPase, peptidase, and Rpn11 activity than WT and can even degrade some non-ubiquitylated proteins.

quotes.quote:
Proteasomes from cells lacking Usp14 show higher ATPase, peptidase, and Rpn11 
activity than those in WT, and can even degrade some non-ubiquitylated proteins (Kim and 
Goldberg, unpublished).

experiment.system: proteasomes purified from cells lacking Usp14 versus wild type
experiment.perturbation: loss of Usp14
experiment.measurement: ATPase, peptidase, Rpn11 activities and degradation of non-ubiquitylated proteins

text: 20S gate opening occurs when the C-terminal HbYX motifs of three 19S ATPases (Rpt2, Rpt3, and Rpt5) bind lysines in the inter-subunit pockets of the 20S outer ring upon nucleotide binding, displacing the α-subunit N-termini; deleting one or two of these N-terminal extensions increases hydrolysis of peptides and proteins even in vivo.

quotes.quote:
The importance of this gate has been demonstrated by deletion of one or two of 
these N-terminal extensions, which increases the hydrolysis of peptides and proteins even in 
vivo (Bajorek et al., 2003; Choi et al., 2016). Biochemical and structural studies established 
that gate opening occurs when the C-terminal HbYX (Hydrophobic-Tyrosine-X) motifs on 
three of the 19S ATPases (Rpt2, Rpt3, and Rpt5) bind to lysines in the inter-subunit pockets 
of the 20S's outer ring

experiment.system: 20S/26S proteasomes in vitro and in cells
experiment.perturbation: deletion of one or two 20S α-subunit N-terminal extensions; HbYX motif binding upon nucleotide binding
experiment.measurement: peptide and protein hydrolysis rates; structural position of α-subunit N-termini

numbers.quantity: number of 19S ATPases bearing HbYX motifs

text: Binding of a Ub conjugate or of ATPγS causes widening and alignment of the ATPase substrate channel and repositions Rpn11 so its active site lies just above the channel opening, and conjugate binding to Usp14 exposes Rpn11's active site and enhances its catalytic activity.

quotes.quote:
The most prominent changes observed by cryo-EM are the widening of the central substrate 
transit channel through the ATPase ring and its alignment with the gated entry into the 20S.

In the basal state, Rpn11's active site faces 
away from the ATPases' substrate entry channel and is blocked by other subunits, but upon 
activation, it is repositioned so that its active site lies just above the opening of this channel

the binding of Ub conjugates to Usp14 exposes Rpn11's active site (Bashore et al., 2015) and 
enhances its catalytic activity.

experiment.system: 26S proteasome
experiment.perturbation: binding of ubiquitylated substrate or non-hydrolyzable ATPγS
experiment.measurement: cryo-EM conformational states; Rpn11 position and catalytic activity

text: PAN normally binds two ATPs plus two ADPs leaving two sites unoccupied; FRET analysis indicated the two ATPs bind adjacent subunits, with cooperativity from an arginine finger contributed to the neighboring subunit's nucleotide site, and loss of any one nucleotide-binding site markedly reduces particle ATPase activity.

quotes.quote:
Though all six subunits 
are identical, PAN normally binds two ATPs plus two ADPs, leaving two sites unoccupied 
(Smith et al., 2011).

recent, elegant FRET 
analysis indicated that the two ATPs bind to adjacent subunits (Kim et al., 2015).

an arginine residue from one subunit, “the arginine finger”, contributes 
to the nucleotide-binding site on the adjacent subunit (Kim et al., 2015).

the loss of any one 
nucleotide-binding site markedly reduces the ATPase activity of the particle (Peth et al., 
2013b)

experiment.system: archaeal PAN ATPase and 26S proteasome
experiment.perturbation: nucleotide binding analysis by FRET; mutation eliminating individual nucleotide-binding sites
experiment.measurement: occupancy of nucleotide sites and ATPase activity

text: The rate of ATP hydrolysis by the 26S increases 2-3 fold upon binding a Ub conjugate; ATPase activation requires both a Ub chain interacting with Usp14 or Uch37 and a loosely folded polypeptide, and the two signals need not be covalently linked since Ub aldehyde or a Ub chain (but not free Ub) plus casein suffices.

quotes.quote:
The rate of ATP hydrolysis by the 26S complex increases 2-3 fold upon binding a Ub 
conjugate (Peth et al., 2013b).

These two signals do not have to be covalently linked; the 19S ATPases can be activated by 
addition of Ub aldehyde or a Ub chain (but not free Ub) together with casein (Peth et al., 
2013a).

experiment.system: purified 26S proteasomes
experiment.perturbation: addition of Ub conjugates, or Ub aldehyde/Ub chain together with casein
experiment.measurement: rate of ATP hydrolysis

numbers.quantity: fold increase in 26S ATP hydrolysis on conjugate binding

text: Single-molecule analyses showed ClpXP unfolding of a GFP-fusion depends on power generated by pore loops requiring frequent and forceful pulling, whereas translocation by the 26S or PAN is more processive and depends predominantly on the force generated by the pore loops rather than the frequency of pulling.

quotes.quote: Martin and colleagues recently used single-

molecule analysis to analyze the unfolding of a GFP-fusion protein by ClpXP and showed 
that unfolding depends of the power generated by the pore loops and thus requires frequent 
and forceful pulling on the substrate (Rodriguez-Aliaga et al., 2016). However, Smith an 
coworkers showed that translocation by the 26S or PAN is more processive than by ClpXP 
and depends predominantly on the force generated by the pore loops rather than the 
frequency with which these loops pull on the substrate (Snoberger et al., 2017).

experiment.system: ClpXP with GFP-fusion substrate; 26S proteasome and PAN
experiment.perturbation: pore-loop variants and single-molecule force measurement
experiment.measurement: unfolding/translocation processivity, pulling force and frequency

text: At Vmax it takes roughly 50-80 ATP molecules and about 23 seconds for a purified 26S to degrade a ubiquitylated DHFR molecule, and folate binding doubles both the ATP consumed and the time required; degradation of ubiquitylated Sic1, twice the size of DHFR, requires about twice the time and ATP.

quotes.quote:
For example, at Vmax, it takes roughly 50–80 ATP molecules and about 23 seconds 
for a purified 26S to degrade a ubiquitylated DHFR molecule. If, however, DHFR binds the 
substrate folate and thus assumes a more tightly-folded conformation, the number of ATP 
molecules consumed and the time necessary to degrade DHFR doubles (Peth et al., 2013b).

Degradation of ubiquitylated Sic1, a loosely folded protein that is twice the size 
of DHFR, requires about twice the time and ATP.

experiment.system: purified 26S proteasomes with ubiquitylated DHFR and Sic1
experiment.perturbation: addition of folate to tighten DHFR folding; comparison of substrate size
experiment.measurement: ATP molecules consumed and time per substrate molecule degraded

numbers.quantity: ATP molecules per ubiquitylated DHFR degraded

text: The authors state that these energy-cost measurements indicate conjugate degradation consumes about a third of the ATP required for ribosomal synthesis of polypeptides, while noting proteolysis in vivo must consume even more ATP for ubiquitylation and repeated binding/deubiquitylation cycles.

quotes.quote:
These measurements of the energy costs 
for 26S function indicate that conjugate degradation consumes about a third of the ATP 
required for ribosomal synthesis of polypeptides, but proteolysis in vivo must consume even 
more ATP to support substrate ubiquitylation and perhaps repeated rounds of proteasomal 
binding and deubiquitylation before degradation occurs.

experiment.system: purified 26S proteasome degradation reactions
experiment.perturbation: observational comparison with ribosomal synthesis energy costs
experiment.measurement: ATP consumed per substrate degraded relative to synthesis

numbers.quantity: ATP for conjugate degradation relative to ribosomal synthesis

text: Cryo-EM of the 26S initially revealed two states and further studies recognized four different forms, but the authors state strong evidence that these states function sequentially during degradation is lacking in most studies.

quotes.quote:
Initially two states of the 26S were recognized (Matyskiela et al., 2013), but further 
studies led to the recognition of four different forms (Chen et al., 2016; Schweitzer et al., 
2016). These structures were solved with and without Usp14, ATPγS, ATP, or ADP-AlFx 
present or with Rpn11 inactivated to capture a substrate during translocation.

although strong evidence that these different states function 
sequentially during degradation is lacking in most studies

experiment.system: yeast and human 26S proteasomes
experiment.perturbation: presence/absence of Usp14, ATPγS, ATP, ADP-AlFx, or Rpn11 inactivation
experiment.measurement: single-particle cryo-EM classification into conformational states

numbers.quantity: conformational forms recognized in further studies

text: By fitting individual particles from high-resolution cryo-EM of fixed cells to previous images, about 80% of 26S proteasomes in cultured hypothalamic neurons were found to be in the inactive or substrate-free state.

quotes.quote:
By computationally 
fitting individual particles to previous cryo-EM images, they found that about 80% of the 
26S in cultured hypothalamic neurons were in the inactive or substrate-free state (Asano et 
al., 2015).

experiment.system: cultured hypothalamic neurons
experiment.perturbation: observational (in-cell cryo-electron tomography of fixed cells)
experiment.measurement: fraction of 26S particles classified as inactive/substrate-free

numbers.quantity: fraction of neuronal 26S in inactive/substrate-free state

text: Loss of 26S activity has been demonstrated in neurons infected by PrPsc and in brains of mice overproducing mutant tau, where overexpression of aggregation-prone tau decreased the capacity of brain 26S to degrade Ub conjugates, ATP, and peptides while ubiquitylated proteins and model UPP substrates accumulated with phospho-tau.

quotes.quote:
clear loss of 26S activity has now been 
demonstrated in neurons infected by the prion protein, PrPsc, the cause of Bovine 
Spongiform Encephalitis (Mad Cow Disease) (Deriziotis et al., 2011), and in the brains of 
mice overproducing mutant tau in a model of Frontotemporal Dementia (Myeku et al., 
2016). Overexpression of the disease-associated, aggregation-prone tau led to a decreased 
capacity of brain 26S to degrade Ub conjugates, ATP, and peptides (Myeku et al., 2016). As 
proteasome function decreased ubiquitylated proteins and model UPP substrates 
accumulated in neurons along with phospho-tau.

experiment.system: neurons infected with PrPsc; mouse model of Frontotemporal Dementia overproducing mutant tau
experiment.perturbation: prion infection or overexpression of aggregation-prone mutant tau
experiment.measurement: 26S degradation of Ub conjugates, ATP hydrolysis, peptidase activity; accumulation of ubiquitylated proteins and reporter substrates

text: Raising cAMP and activating PKA phosphorylates the 19S subunit Rpn6, increasing rates of hydrolysis of peptides, ATP, and Ub conjugates and enhancing breakdown only of short-lived proteins (not long-lived ones); treating a mouse model of Frontotemporal Dementia with an agent that raised cAMP and activated brain proteasomes reversed accumulation of phospho-tau and failure of proteostasis.

quotes.quote:
raising cAMP and activation of protein kinase A (PKA) causes phosphorylation of 
the 19S subunit Rpn6 (Lokireddy et al., 2015), which increases the rates of hydrolysis of 
peptides, ATP, and Ub conjugates

This activation of proteasomes leads to enhanced 
breakdown only of short-lived cell proteins

Surprisingly, this 
phosphorylation does not promote degradation of long-lived proteins, which comprise the 
bulk of cell constituents.

treatment of a mouse model of Frontotemporal Dementia 
with an agent that raised cAMP and activated brain proteasomes reversed the accumulation 
of phospho-tau and the failure of proteostasis (Myeku et al., 2016)

experiment.system: cultured cells and mouse model of Frontotemporal Dementia
experiment.perturbation: raising cAMP / activating PKA to phosphorylate Rpn6
experiment.measurement: proteasomal hydrolysis of peptides, ATP and Ub conjugates; degradation of short- vs long-lived proteins; phospho-tau accumulation

text: Rpn6 phosphorylation and proteasome activation were observed upon treatment of hepatocytes with glucagon or epinephrine and heart with epinephrine, as well as in muscle upon intense exercise or after a brief fast.

quotes.quote:
Rpn6 phosphorylation and proteasome activation 
were recently observed upon treatment of hepatocytes with glucagon or epinephrine and 
heart with epinephrine, as well as in muscle upon intense exercise or after a brief fast 
(Lokireddy et al, submitted).

experiment.system: hepatocytes, heart, and muscle
experiment.perturbation: glucagon or epinephrine treatment; intense exercise or brief fast
experiment.measurement: Rpn6 phosphorylation and proteasome activity

text: Phosphorylation of the ATPase subunit Rpt3 by DYRK2 increases 26S activity and promotes progression through S-phase and cell proliferation; other kinases including PKG in the heart and CaMKII in neurons (which promotes proteasomal movement into dendrites) were reported to modify Rpt6.

quotes.quote:
Guo et al recently demonstrated that phosphorylation of the ATPase subunit 
Rpt3 by DYRK2 also increases 26S activity and promotes progression through S-phase and 
cell proliferation (Guo et al., 2016).

including PKG in the mammalian heart (Ranek et al., 2013) and CamKII in 
neurons, which promotes proteasomal movement into dendrites (Bingol et al., 2010). These
kinases were reported to modify the ATPase subunit Rpt6

experiment.system: mammalian cells, heart, and neurons
experiment.perturbation: kinase-mediated phosphorylation of proteasome ATPase subunits (DYRK2 on Rpt3; PKG, CaMKII on Rpt6)
experiment.measurement: 26S activity, cell-cycle progression and proliferation; proteasome localization

text: Proteasome abundance is regulated by feedback: in yeast the short-lived transcription factor Rpn4 accumulates when proteasome function is impaired and stimulates proteasome production, while in higher eukaryotes proteasome inhibition leads to Ddi2 cleavage of ER-bound Nrf1, whose released fragment enters the nucleus and induces expression of all 26S subunits, p97, and its cofactors.

quotes.quote:
In yeast, a simple feedback system exists in which the expression of 26S genes is activated by 
the short-lived transcription factor, Rpn4 (Xie and Varshavsky, 2001). If proteasome function 
is impaired, Rpn4 accumulates and stimulates proteasome production.

When proteasomes are inhibited, 
Nrf1 is cleaved by the endoprotease Ddi2 (Koizumi et al., 2016; Lehrbach and Ruvkun, 
2016; Sha and Goldberg, 2016). The released fragment enters the nucleus and induces 
expression of all 26S subunits, p97, and its cofactors.

experiment.system: yeast and mammalian/higher eukaryotic cells
experiment.perturbation: proteasome inhibition or impairment
experiment.measurement: Rpn4 accumulation, Nrf1 processing, and induction of proteasome subunit and p97 expression

text: In mouse models of β-thalassemia caused by imbalance of hemoglobin subunits and Charcot Marie Tooth disease due to myelin mutations, 26S function is impaired but cells partially compensate by increasing Nrf1 processing and proteasome production.

quotes.quote:
in mouse models of β-thalassemia caused by an imbalance of hemoglobin subunits 
(Khandros et al., 2012) or Charcot Marie Tooth disease due to myelin mutations (VerPlank,

2017), 26S function is impaired, but the cells partially compensate by increasing Nrf1 
processing and proteasome production.

experiment.system: mouse models of β-thalassemia and Charcot Marie Tooth disease
experiment.perturbation: disease-causing hemoglobin subunit imbalance or myelin mutations
experiment.measurement: 26S proteasome function, Nrf1 processing and proteasome production

text: The authors report a large-scale characterization of the SASP using antibody arrays to quantitatively measure factors secreted by human fibroblasts and epithelial cells, as well as mouse fibroblasts.

quotes.quote:
We recently
provided a large-scale characterization of the SASP, using antibody arrays to quantitatively
measure factors secreted by human fibroblasts and epithelial cells (18), as well as mouse
fibroblasts

experiment.system: human fibroblasts and epithelial cells; mouse fibroblasts
experiment.perturbation: senescence induction (observational comparison of senescent vs presenescent secretomes)
experiment.measurement: antibody arrays quantifying secreted factors

text: Antibody array profiling found that levels of many secreted factors, including anti-inflammatory factors such as IL-2, -4, -10, -11, and -12 and factors such as Fractalkine (CX3CL-1), GCP-2, GITR, PDGF-BB, and LIGHT, do not change when fibroblasts are induced to senesce by X-irradiation, RAS overexpression, or replicative exhaustion, and no factor was significantly downregulated in different senescent states.

quotes.quote:
these unchanged secreted molecules are anti-inflammatory soluble factors such as IL-2, -4,
-10, -11, and -12 (18). Fractalkine (CX3CL-1), GCP-2, GITR, PDGF-BB, and LIGHT (all
essential to leukocyte differentiation or proliferation) also remain unchanged when
fibroblasts are induced to senesce by X-irradiation, RAS overexpression, or replicative
exhaustion. Intriguingly, no factor was significantly downregulated in different senescent
states (18).

experiment.system: human fibroblasts
experiment.perturbation: senescence induced by X-irradiation, RAS overexpression, or replicative exhaustion
experiment.measurement: antibody array measurement of secreted factor levels

text: Fibroblasts induced to senesce by oncogenic RAS oversecrete more GM-CSF, IL-6, -7, -8, -1b, -13, and GROa than cells senesced by other means, and secrete ENA-78, I-309, G-CSF, and IFN-g that are not secreted by other senescent cells; cells senescing with dysfunctional p53 develop a SASP resembling that caused by oncogenic RAS.

quotes.quote:
fibroblasts induced to senesce by
oncogenic RAS oversecrete more GM-CSF, IL-6, -7, -8, -1β, -13, and GROα than do cells
induced to senesce by other means. Moreover, such cells secrete high levels of factors such
as ENA-78, I-309, G-CSF, and interferon (IFN)-γ that are not secreted by other senescent
cells.

Cells that senesce with dysfunctional p53
develop a SASP that resembles the SASP caused by oncogenic RAS (18).

experiment.system: human fibroblasts
experiment.perturbation: senescence induced by oncogenic RAS, p53 inactivation, or other inducers (replicative exhaustion, telomere disruption, X-irradiation, chromatin disruption)
experiment.measurement: antibody array comparison of secreted factor profiles

text: Cells induced to senesce by overexpression of p16INK4a do not express a SASP despite other hallmarks of senescence, secreting significantly lower levels of SASP factors than cells senesced by most other inducers.

quotes.quote:
cells induced to senesce by overexpression of the p16INK4a tumor-
suppressor protein do not express a SASP despite other hallmarks of senescence

Cells induced to senesce by ectopic p16INK4a expression secrete
significantly lower levels of SASP factors compared to cells induced to senesce by most
other senescence inducers.

experiment.system: cultured human fibroblasts
experiment.perturbation: ectopic overexpression of p16INK4a versus other senescence inducers
experiment.measurement: secreted SASP factor levels and senescence hallmarks

text: In culture, cells develop a full SASP more than 5 days after senescence induction whereas growth arrests within 24 h of damage, with SASP factors not all secreted at the same time; loss of p53 or gain of oncogenic RAS leads to more rapid acquisition of the SASP.

quotes.quote:
In culture, cells
develop a full SASP >5 days after senescence induction, and the cells’ growth arrests within
24 h of damage. Not all SASP factors begin to be secreted at the same time.

Genetic alterations, such as loss of p53 or gain of oncogenic RAS, lead to a more rapid
acquisition of the SASP

experiment.system: cultured cells (human fibroblasts and other cell types)
experiment.perturbation: senescence induction (damage), with or without p53 loss / oncogenic RAS
experiment.measurement: time course of secreted factor levels and growth arrest

numbers.quantity: time to full SASP after senescence induction
time to growth arrest after damage

text: Under standard culture conditions with 20% oxygen, mouse cells undergo an arrest termed senescence that does not include a SASP, whereas under physiological 3% oxygen the mouse SASP closely resembles the human SASP.

quotes.quote:
Under standard cell-culture
conditions, which include 20% oxygen, mouse cells undergo an arrest that has been termed
senescence but that does not include a SASP. By contrast, under physiological 3% oxygen,
the mouse SASP closely resembles the human SASP.

experiment.system: mouse fibroblasts
experiment.perturbation: culture at 20% versus 3% oxygen during senescence
experiment.measurement: secreted factor profile (SASP) compared with human SASP

text: A large proportion of the SASP of senescent fibroblasts is irreversible once established: senescent human fibroblasts expressing low levels of p16INK4a can revert and resume proliferation upon p53 inactivation, yet these reverted cells retain the SASP.

quotes.quote:
Our data suggest that a large proportion of the SASP of senescent fibroblasts is irreversible
once established (18). Indeed, senescent human fibroblasts that express low levels of
p16INK4a can revert and resume proliferation upon p53 inactivation (102). These reverted
cells, however, retain the SASP (18).

experiment.system: senescent human fibroblasts with low p16INK4a
experiment.perturbation: p53 inactivation to reverse the senescence arrest
experiment.measurement: resumption of proliferation and persistence of secreted SASP factors

text: p53 actively restrains the SASP: loss of p53 activity in senescing or damaged fibroblasts greatly enhances the SASP and its stimulatory effects on malignant epithelial cells.

quotes.quote: we found that p53 actively restrains the SASP,

loss of p53 activity by senescing or damaged fibroblasts greatly enhances the
SASP and the stimulatory effects of the SASP on malignant epithelial cells

experiment.system: human fibroblasts co-cultured with / conditioned medium on malignant epithelial cells
experiment.perturbation: p53 inactivation in senescing or damaged fibroblasts
experiment.measurement: secreted SASP factor levels and stimulation of malignant epithelial cells

text: In breast cancer cell-culture models, high levels of IL-6 and -8 secreted by senescent fibroblasts are responsible for enhancing the invasiveness of a panel of cancer cell lines.

quotes.quote:
In breast cancer, high levels of
IL-6 and -8 secreted by senescent fibroblasts are responsible for enhancing the invasiveness
of a panel of cancer cell lines in cell-culture models (18).

experiment.system: breast cancer cell lines with senescent human fibroblasts
experiment.perturbation: exposure to senescent fibroblast secretions / IL-6 and IL-8
experiment.measurement: cancer cell invasiveness in culture

text: Weakly tumorigenic mammary epithelial cells undergo morphologic changes in culture resembling an epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition in the presence of senescent conditioned medium, an effect attributable to IL-6 and -8.

quotes.quote:
weakly tumorigenic pancreatic (117) and mammary (18) epithelial cells
undergo morphologic changes in culture that resemble an epithelial-to-mesenchymal
transition in the presence of a senescent conditioned medium. The effect on mammary
epithelial cells is attributable to IL-6 and -8 (18)

experiment.system: weakly tumorigenic mammary epithelial cells in culture
experiment.perturbation: treatment with senescent cell conditioned medium
experiment.measurement: epithelial-to-mesenchymal-like morphologic changes

text: In mouse xenografts of breast cancer cells, blood vessel density was significantly higher when tumors developed in the presence of senescent but not presenescent fibroblasts.

quotes.quote:
The proangiogenic effects of the SASP were shown in vivo in mouse
xenografts of breast cancer cells. The blood vessel density was significantly higher when the
tumors developed in the presence of senescent but not presenescent fibroblasts (127).

experiment.system: mouse xenografts of breast cancer cells
experiment.perturbation: co-injection with senescent versus presenescent fibroblasts
experiment.measurement: tumor blood vessel density

text: A greater than 50-fold increase in plasminogen activator activity has been reported in senescent endothelial cells and lung and skin fibroblasts.

quotes.quote:
Indeed, a >50-fold increase in plasminogen
activator activity has been reported in senescent endothelial cells and lung and skin
fibroblasts (83, 84).

experiment.system: endothelial cells and lung and skin fibroblasts
experiment.perturbation: cellular senescence
experiment.measurement: plasminogen activator activity

text: Gene (mRNA) expression profiles of senescent cells determined by microarrays resemble the profiles of secreted proteins determined by antibody arrays, and SASP-constituent genes show physical clustering.

quotes.quote:
Overall, the gene (mRNA) expression profiles of senescent cells determined by microarrays
resemble the profiles of secreted proteins determined by antibody arrays (18; J.P. Coppé &
J. Campisi, unpublished data).
is suggested by the physical clustering of genes that constitute the SASP

experiment.system: senescent human/mouse cells
experiment.perturbation: senescence induction (observational comparison)
experiment.measurement: microarray mRNA profiles versus antibody array secreted protein profiles; genomic position of SASP genes

text: The authors describe the ISR as converging on phosphorylation of a single serine (Ser51) of eIF2α by four kinases (PERK, GCN2, PKR, HRI), which blocks eIF2's guanine nucleotide exchange factor eIF2B and reduces general protein synthesis while paradoxically increasing translation of specific uORF-containing mRNAs such as ATF4.

quotes.quote:
The various stresses are sensed by four specialized kinases (PERK, GCN2, PKR and HRI) that 
converge on phosphorylation of a single serine on the eukaryotic translation initiation factor 
eIF2. eIF2 phosphorylation blocks the action of eIF2’s guanine nucleotide exchange factor termed 
eIF2B, resulting in a general reduction in protein synthesis. Paradoxically, phosphorylation of eIF2 
also triggers the translation of specific mRNAs, including key transcription factors, such as ATF4.

Upon stress, the α subunit of eIF2 is phosphorylated at Ser51, yielding eIF2-P and ISR 
activation.

experiment.system: mammalian and yeast cells (literature synthesis of ISR signaling)
experiment.perturbation: diverse cellular stresses (proteostasis defects, nutrient deprivation, viral infection, oxidative stress) activating eIF2 kinases
experiment.measurement: eIF2α Ser51 phosphorylation, global protein synthesis rates, and translation of specific mRNAs

text: Structural work on human eIF2B–eIF2 complexes showed eIF2B is a twofold symmetric decamer built from two eIF2Bβγδε heterotetramers and an eIF2Bα2 homodimer, with eIF2γ's nucleotide binding site sandwiched between two eIF2Bε domains, explaining why the decamer is more active than incompletely assembled building blocks.

quotes.quote:
eIF2B is composed of 
two copies of five different subunits (α, β, δ, γ, and ε) that assemble into a large twofold 
symmetric heterodecamer

Structures of human eIF2B complexed with its substrate, 
eIF2, illuminate the mechanism of guanine nucleotide exchange and explain why the eIF2B 
decamer is more active than its incompletely assembled building blocks

experiment.system: human eIF2B in complex with eIF2 (structural studies reviewed)
experiment.perturbation: observational (structure determination of eIF2B alone and bound to eIF2)
experiment.measurement: complex architecture and subunit interfaces; nucleotide binding pocket conformation

text: Phosphorylated eIF2 (eIF2-P) binds a distinct site on eIF2B via a hydrophobic surface patch and sterically blocks positioning of eIF2 at the catalytic domain of eIF2Bε, acting as a potent noncompetitive inhibitor of eIF2B.

quotes.quote:
Binding of eIF2-P to eIF2B sterically interferes 
with proper positioning of eIF2 to the catalytic domain of eIF2Bε (Fig. 2D). In this way, 
eIF2-P acts as a potent noncompetitive inhibitor of eIF2B.

experiment.system: eIF2B–eIF2-P complexes (structural and biophysical studies reviewed)
experiment.perturbation: eIF2α Ser51 phosphorylation
experiment.measurement: binding site occupancy and inhibition mode of eIF2B GEF activity

text: ISRIB binds a deep pocket bridging the eIF2B tetramer-tetramer symmetry interface and acts as an eIF2B activator by assembling decamers from subcomplexes; cryo-EM of the human eIF2B decamer bound to ISRIB was resolved at 2.7 Å.

quotes.quote:
ISRIB binds to eIF2B and enhances 
its activity by promoting its assembly
binding pocket that bridges across the eIF2B tetramer-tetramer symmetry interface

Top view of the human eIF2B decamer bound to ISRIB. The cryo-EM density at a 
resolution of 2.7 Å shows ISRIB bound in a deep central binding pocket.

experiment.system: human eIF2B complexes with the small molecule ISRIB
experiment.perturbation: ISRIB addition
experiment.measurement: cryo-EM structure and eIF2B assembly/activity

numbers.quantity: cryo-EM resolution of human eIF2B decamer bound to ISRIB

text: ISRIB's mechanism produces a bell-shaped dose-response: once eIF2-P exceeds a threshold and eIF2B tetramers are depleted, ISRIB can no longer replenish decamers and does not inhibit the ISR, which the authors say explains ISRIB's lack of overt in vivo toxicity even at saturating concentrations.

quotes.quote:
Therefore, as the eIF2-P concentration exceeds 
a certain threshold—that is, when the ISR is strongly activated—ISRIB can no longer 
replenish the depleted pool of eIF2B decamers. Under these conditions, therefore, ISRIB 
does not inhibit the ISR (Fig. 2E) (22, 23). The resulting bell-shaped response to increasing 
stress explains why ISRIB displays no overt toxicity when administered in vivo—even at 
saturating concentrations.

experiment.system: cells with graded ISR activation and animals administered ISRIB
experiment.perturbation: increasing stress/eIF2-P levels combined with ISRIB treatment
experiment.measurement: ISR inhibition as a function of activation level; in vivo toxicity

text: Two eIF2-directed phosphatase complexes reset eIF2-P: PP1 with the constitutive regulatory subunit CReP gives slow steady dephosphorylation, whereas GADD34 is induced by increased eIF2-P via uORF-mediated translational control and ATF4-driven transcription, forming a negative feedback loop.

quotes.quote:
CReP is constitutively expressed, leading to a slow but steady rate of eIF2-P 
dephosphorylation (60). By contrast, GADD34 expression is induced as a consequence of 
increased eIF2-P abundance, thus acting in a feedback loop that antagonizes the relative 
strength of ISR activation

experiment.system: mammalian cells
experiment.perturbation: ISR activation raising eIF2-P; genetic/expression manipulation of GADD34 and CReP
experiment.measurement: eIF2-P dephosphorylation rates and GADD34 mRNA/protein induction

text: Genome-wide studies identified 5′ uORFs in ~50% of all mRNAs, yet why only a subset are translationally controlled by the ISR remains unknown according to the authors.

quotes.quote:
More recently, genome-wide studies identified 5′ uORFs in ~50% of all mRNAs (74, 75). 
How only a subset of genes containing 5′ uORFs are translationally controlled by the 
ISR remains unknown.

experiment.system: mammalian transcriptomes
experiment.perturbation: observational (genome-wide translation initiation site mapping / ribosome profiling)
experiment.measurement: fraction of mRNAs containing 5′ uORFs

text: Homozygous disruption of eIF2 phosphorylation or ablation of PERK causes postnatal lethality in mice, and loss of both eIF2 phosphatase complexes is incompatible with life, likely from protein synthesis shutdown during embryogenesis.

quotes.quote:
Homozygous disruption of eIF2 phosphorylation or ablation of the eIF2 kinase PERK 
leads to postnatal lethality in mice (78, 79)

persistent activation of the 
ISR in mice lacking the two eIF2 phosphatase complexes is incompatible with life, likely 
due to shutdown of protein synthesis during embryogenesis

experiment.system: mice
experiment.perturbation: genetic ablation of eIF2 phosphorylation, PERK, or both eIF2 phosphatase complexes
experiment.measurement: viability/survival

text: Human mutations that reduce ternary complex formation cause cognitive and metabolic disease: CReP loss-of-function mutations map to the PP1 binding site and increase eIF2-P, causing intellectual disability, short stature and diabetes; eIF2γ mutations cause MEHMO syndrome; and mutations in each of the five eIF2B subunits cause vanishing white matter leukoencephalopathy, whose cellular and mouse pathologies can be rescued by ISRIB and 2BAct.

quotes.quote:
Homozygous loss-of-function mutations in the gene encoding CReP are associated with 
intellectual disability, short stature, and diabetes (81, 82). These rare mutations map to the 
PP1 binding site of CReP and destabilize the CReP•PP1 phosphatase complex, thereby 
increasing eIF2-P.

Mutations in each of the five subunits of eIF2B occur in a rare autosomal recessive 
leukoencephalopathy with vanishing white matter

the pathologies associated with cells and mice bearing human 
hypomorphic VWM mutations can be rescued by ISRIB and ISRIB-like molecules (2BAct), 
which enhance the cellular pool of available TC and restore translation rates

experiment.system: human patients and cell/mouse models bearing VWM eIF2B mutations
experiment.perturbation: disease-causing mutations; treatment with ISRIB or 2BAct
experiment.measurement: clinical phenotypes, eIF2-P/TC levels, translation rates and pathology rescue

text: Loss-of-function mutations that impair ISR induction also cause disease: PERK mutations cause Wolcott-Rallison syndrome with early-onset diabetes and multiple epiphyseal dysplasia, recapitulated in PERK knockout mice with growth retardation, neonatal diabetes and skeletal malformation, and GCN2 mutations cause a rare form of pulmonary arterial hypertension.

quotes.quote:
Mutations in PERK are associated with a rare 
autosomal recessive disease, Wolcott-Rallison syndrome (WRS), characterized by early-
onset diabetes and multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (96). PERK knockout mice recapitulate the 
human phenotype, showing growth retardation, neonatal diabetes, and skeletal malformation

Mutations in the gene encoding GCN2 have been identified in a rare form of pulmonary 
arterial hypertension

experiment.system: human patients and knockout mice
experiment.perturbation: loss-of-function mutation/knockout of PERK or GCN2
experiment.measurement: clinical and organismal phenotypes (glycemia, growth, skeletal, pulmonary vasculature)

text: Convergent genetic and pharmacological evidence indicates the ISR bidirectionally gates long-term memory: mice lacking GCN2 or PKR and eIF2α Ser51Ala heterozygous knock-in mice show facilitated long-term memory, PKR/PERK inhibitors and ISRIB enhance long-term memory in rodents and birds, while Sal003 injection or pharmacogenetic PKR activation impairs it.

quotes.quote:
genetic inhibition of the ISR in mice lacking GCN2 or PKR, or eIF2 
heterozygous knock-in mice, in which in one allele of eIF2(α) Ser51 is replaced by alanine, 
facilitate long-term memory formation (110–113).

PKR and PERK inhibitors, and 
ISRIB, enhance long-term memory in rodents (19, 112–114) and birds (115).

hippocampal or basolateral amygdala injection of Sal003 (65, 66), 
or pharmacogenetic activation of PKR in the hippocampus, impairs long-term memory in 
both rodents and birds

experiment.system: rodents and birds (hippocampus, basolateral amygdala)
experiment.perturbation: genetic deletion/knock-in of ISR components; pharmacological ISR inhibition (ISRIB, PKR/PERK inhibitors) or activation (Sal003, pharmacogenetic PKR)
experiment.measurement: long-term memory formation in behavioral tasks

text: Behavioral training, L-LTP-inducing stimulation, and drugs of abuse negatively regulate the ISR, measured as reduced eIF2-P in hippocampus and ventral tegmental area, and ribosome profiling showed behavioral training induces a hippocampal protein synthesis signature mimicking that of ISR-reduced animals.

quotes.quote:
negatively regulates the ISR, as determined by reduced 
eIF2-P concentrations in the hippocampus and ventral tegmental area (VTA)

behavioral training induces a protein synthesis signature that mimics that of animals in 
which the ISR is reduced, as determined by ribosome profiling

experiment.system: rodent hippocampus and ventral tegmental area
experiment.perturbation: long-term potentiation induction, behavioral training, or drugs of abuse
experiment.measurement: eIF2-P concentration and ribosome profiling of translational state

text: ISR activation, evidenced by eIF2-P and kinase phosphorylation in post-mortem brains and animal models, is reported across Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, Huntington disease, ALS, traumatic brain injury, Down syndrome and Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, and causes cognitive defects in mouse models of traumatic brain injury, aging and Alzheimer's disease, although the authors note negative results have also been reported.

quotes.quote:
This activation is evidenced by detection of eIF2-P and phosphorylation of 
PKR, PERK and GCN2 in post-mortem brains from individuals and animal models of 
cognitive and neurodegenerative disorders, including Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s 
disease, Huntington disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), traumatic brain injury, 
Down syndrome, and Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (30, 109, 132–136). Notably, ISR 
activation causes cognitive defects in mouse models of traumatic brain injury (137, 138), 
aging (114), and Alzheimer’s disease (139–143), although negative results have also been 
reported (144, 145).

experiment.system: human post-mortem brains and mouse disease models
experiment.perturbation: observational disease state; genetic/pharmacological ISR manipulation in mouse models
experiment.measurement: eIF2-P and ISR kinase phosphorylation; cognitive performance

text: In a mouse model of Down syndrome, genetic and pharmacological inhibition of PKR or activation of eIF2B with ISRIB reversed the aberrant translational program and the deficits in synaptic plasticity and long-term memory; the authors note most Down syndrome individuals develop Alzheimer's disease-type dementia at age 45.

quotes.quote:
Genetic and pharmacological inhibition of the upstream ISR-sensor kinase PKR or 
activation of eIF2B with ISRIB reverses the aberrant translational program and deficits 
in synaptic plasticity and long-term memory in a mouse model of Down syndrome

with most Down syndrome 
individuals developing Alzheimer’s disease-type dementia at age 45

experiment.system: mouse model of Down syndrome
experiment.perturbation: genetic and pharmacological PKR inhibition; ISRIB-mediated eIF2B activation
experiment.measurement: translational program, synaptic plasticity, and long-term memory

numbers.quantity: age at which most Down syndrome individuals develop Alzheimer's-type dementia

text: Suppressing ISR-mediated translational reprogramming is neuroprotective across models: in prion-diseased mice, GADD34 overexpression, ISRIB, PERK inhibitor or trazodone rescued neuronal loss; PERK inhibition protected in two Drosophila Parkinson models and a mouse frontotemporal dementia model; genetic PERK inhibition prevented neurodegeneration in an Alzheimer's mouse model; and ISRIB prevented hypoxia-induced cell death in a human 3D model of hypoxic brain injury.

quotes.quote:
In a mouse model of prion disease, genetic and pharmacological suppression of the 
ISR by either overexpressing GADD34 in the brain, or treatment with ISRIB, PERK 
inhibitor, or trazodone, an antidepressant claimed to increase TC complex formation by an 
unknown mechanism, rescued neuronal loss and improved neuronal survival

pharmacological inhibition of PERK was neuroprotective in two 
different Drosophila models of early-onset Parkinson disease (151), as well as in a mouse 
model of frontotemporal dementia (152). Moreover, genetic inhibition of PERK prevented 
neurodegeneration in a mouse model of Alzheimer’s disease

can be prevented 
by ISRIB in a human cellular three-dimensional (3D) model of hypoxic brain injury

experiment.system: prion-infected mice, Drosophila Parkinson models, mouse frontotemporal dementia and Alzheimer's models, human 3D hypoxic brain injury model
experiment.perturbation: GADD34 overexpression, ISRIB, PERK inhibitor, trazodone, or genetic PERK inhibition
experiment.measurement: neuronal loss/survival and neurodegeneration

text: In myelination disorders the ISR's role is bidirectional: GCN2 protects oligodendrocytes and white matter during branched-chain amino acid deficiency and PERK protects against demyelination in experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis, while in Charcot-Marie-Tooth mouse models with increased eIF2-P, GADD34 germline ablation or sephin1 improved motor function and reduced demyelination yet removing one copy of PERK also partially reversed pathology.

quotes.quote:
Whereas GCN2 protects oligodendrocytes and white matter during branch 
amino acid deficiency (160), PERK protects from demyelination and axonal degeneration in 
a mouse model of experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (161).

in 
mouse models of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease that exhibit increased eIF2-P concentrations, 
germline ablation (162, 163) or pharmacological inhibition of GADD34 with sephin1 
improved motor function and reduced demyelination (164). Counterintuitively, in the same 
model, removing one copy of PERK in all or just in Schwann cells partially reversed 
the pathology

experiment.system: mouse models of amino acid deficiency, experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis, and Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease
experiment.perturbation: genetic ablation of GCN2/PERK/GADD34 or sephin1 treatment
experiment.measurement: demyelination, axonal degeneration, and motor function

text: In pancreatic β-cells both inhibition and permanent activation of the ISR are pathogenic: PERK-deficient mice and mice in which eIF2 cannot be phosphorylated recapitulate the human β-cell dysfunction and hyperglycemia of Wolcott-Rallison syndrome, while eIF2γ mutations that reduce TC and translation fidelity, and CReP loss-of-function, are associated with hyperglycemia and diabetes with increased β-cell apoptosis via CHOP.

quotes.quote:
The human phenotype associated with 
β-cell dysfunction and hyperglycemia is recapitulated in mice in which the ISR has been 
genetically inhibited (eg., in PERK-deficient mice, or in mice in which eIF2 cannot be 
phosphorylated)

Patients carrying a specific mutation in eIF2(γ), which results in 
a decrease in TC and translation fidelity, exhibit hyperglycemia and diabetes (86, 174). 
Accordingly, reduced TC owing to a loss-of-function mutation in CReP has been associated 
with diabetes (81). CReP-deficient β-cells are more susceptible to apoptosis

experiment.system: human patients and mouse pancreatic β-cells
experiment.perturbation: genetic inhibition of the ISR (PERK deletion, non-phosphorylatable eIF2) or mutations that persistently activate it (eIF2γ, CReP)
experiment.measurement: glycemic control, β-cell function and apoptosis

text: In cancer, early studies showed that inhibiting the PKR branch or eIF2 phosphorylation transformed mouse fibroblasts and increased tumor formation in immune-deficient mice, yet deletion of PKR or overall reduction of eIF2-P in mice was not tumorigenic in vivo, a paradox the authors attribute to the ISR controlling both prosurvival and pro-death mechanisms.

quotes.quote:
Early studies showed that inhibition 
of either the PKR branch of the ISR or phosphorylation of eIF2 led to transformation 
of mouse fibroblasts and increased tumor formation in immune-deficient mice (182–185). 
Paradoxically, deletion of PKR or overall reduction of eIF2-P in mice was not tumorigenic 
in vivo

experiment.system: mouse fibroblasts, immune-deficient mice, and PKR/eIF2-P mutant mice
experiment.perturbation: inhibition or deletion of PKR; reduction of eIF2 phosphorylation
experiment.measurement: cell transformation and tumor formation in vivo

text: In PTEN-ablated, MYC-overexpressing metastatic prostate cancer models the PERK branch of the ISR is activated and limits protein synthesis, and removing this regulation with ISRIB selectively killed patient-derived metastatic prostate cancer cells in xenograft mouse models; acute deletion of ATF4 delays MYC-driven tumor progression and increases survival, and tumors lacking GCN2 or ATF4 grow more slowly.

quotes.quote:
in mouse and human models of aggressive metastatic prostate cancer, in which the tumor 
suppressor PTEN is ablated and the oncogene MYC is overexpressed, the PERK branch of 
the ISR is activated and limits protein synthesis rates. Removing this regulation with ISRIB 
selectively killed patient-derived metastatic prostate cancer cells in xenograft mouse models 
(192). Similarly, acute deletion of the ISR effector ATF4 substantially delays MYC-driven 
tumor progression and increases survival in mice (193).
Tumors lacking GCN2 or ATF4 grow more slowly

experiment.system: mouse and human metastatic prostate cancer models, patient-derived xenografts, MYC-driven tumor mice
experiment.perturbation: ISRIB treatment; acute ATF4 deletion; GCN2 or ATF4 loss
experiment.measurement: cancer cell killing, protein synthesis rates, tumor growth and survival

text: The ISR is embedded in innate immunity: translation inhibition by the ISR activates NF-κB by lowering the steady-state concentration of the short-lived inhibitor IκB independently of the ATF4 axis, NF-κB activation to intracellular pathogens depends on the ISR kinase HRI via HSPB8 and NOD1/2 inflammasome assembly, and IL-6 is transcriptionally up-regulated by ATF4 as a direct ISR target gene.

quotes.quote:
The translation 
inhibition exerted by the ISR activates NF-κB activation by lowering IκB’s steady-state 
concentration. Notably, this control does not require the ATF4 axis of the ISR (200, 201).

NF-κB activation in response to intracellular pathogens is crucially 
dependent on the ISR kinase HRI (202).

Another inflammatory cytokine, 
IL-6, is transcriptionally up-regulated by ATF4 and hence is encoded by a direct ISR target 
gene

experiment.system: mammalian cells challenged with intracellular pathogens or ER stress
experiment.perturbation: ISR activation / HRI and ATF4 pathway manipulation
experiment.measurement: IκB abundance, NF-κB activation, inflammasome assembly, cytokine expression

text: The authors note that each kinase in the human kinome is estimated to phosphorylate on average more than 10 substrates, making the paucity of known substrates other than eIF2 for the eIF2 kinases surprising, with Nrf2 cited as a PERK substrate.

quotes.quote:
it is estimated that each kinase in the 
human kinome phosphorylates on average more than 10 substrates (208). Thus, the paucity 
of other substrates for the eIF2 kinases is surprising, and it will be important to rule in or 
out the possibility that other substrates functionally modulate the ISR, such Nrf2, which 
is phosphorylated by PERK (209).

experiment.system: human kinome phosphorylation networks
experiment.perturbation: observational (global phosphorylation network analysis)
experiment.measurement: average number of substrates per kinase

text: The authors profiled single-cell transcriptomic responses to each of 86 cytokines across more than 17 immune cell types in mouse lymph nodes in vivo, yielding high-quality transcriptomes for 386,703 cells.

quotes.quote:
we systematically profiled single-cell transcriptomic (single-cell RNA 
sequencing (scRNA-seq)) responses to 86 cytokines across more 
than 17 immune cell types in mouse lymph nodes in vivo
high-quality single-cell transcriptomes for 386,703 cells

experiment.system: wild-type C57BL/6 mouse skin-draining lymph nodes
experiment.perturbation: subcutaneous/intradermal injection of each of 86 carrier-free cytokines or PBS, three mice per cytokine, lymph nodes collected 4 h later
experiment.measurement: droplet-based (10x Genomics) scRNA-seq of lymph node cells

text: Across cytokine–cell type combinations the authors identified an average of 51 differentially expressed genes (range 0–1,510), with 72% of cytokine-responsive DEGs being upregulated.

quotes.quote:
We identified an average of 51 DEGs (span of 0–1,510) per 
cytokine–cell type combination, and the majority (72%) of the DEGs 
responding to cytokines were upregulated rather than downregu-
lated.

experiment.system: mouse lymph node immune cell types after cytokine injection
experiment.perturbation: cytokine versus PBS injection
experiment.measurement: differential gene expression per cell type (two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test, FDR-adjusted P < 0.05)

numbers.quantity: average DEGs per cytokine–cell type combination

text: Certain cytokines (IFNα1, IFNβ, IL-1α, IL-1β, IL-18, IL-36α, IL-15 and TNF) induced strong gene expression changes in nearly all cell types, while others preferentially targeted one lineage, e.g. IL-21 the lymphoid and IL-3 the myeloid lineage.

quotes.quote:
Certain cytokines, such as IFNα1, IFNβ, IL-1α, 
IL-1β, IL-18, IL-36α, IL-15 and TNF, induced strong changes in gene expres-
sion in nearly all cell types. Some cytokines preferentially targeted one 
lineage (for example, IL-21 affected the lymphoid lineage, whereas IL-3 
affected the myeloid lineage)

experiment.system: mouse lymph node cell types
experiment.perturbation: injection of each of 86 cytokines vs PBS
experiment.measurement: global map of transcriptomic change magnitude (Euclidean distance between cytokine- and PBS-treated centroids) plus DEG counts per cell type

text: Most genes upregulated in response to a given cytokine were specific to a single cell type, regardless of DEG thresholds; the most shared DEGs were for IFNα1 and IFNβ across all cell types.

quotes.quote:
Most of the upregu-
lated genes in response to a particular cytokine were specific to one 
cell type regardless of thresholds for defining DEGs

The most shared DEGs were for IFNα1 and IFNβ 
(across all cell types), IL-4 (across several combinations of cell types), 
and IL-2, IL-15 and IL-18

experiment.system: seven representative mouse lymph node immune cell types (max 100 cells per cytokine treatment per cell type)
experiment.perturbation: each cytokine vs PBS
experiment.measurement: count of upregulated DEGs (log2FC > 0.3, FDR < 0.05) grouped by cell-type sharing pattern, at varying thresholds

text: IFNα1 and IFNβ induced common antiviral gene programmes across almost all cell types (GP27, GP33, GP34), whereas IL-1α and IL-1β induced highly cell-type-specific gene programmes, including chemokine/inflammatory genes such as Cd14 in neutrophils (GP27), migration genes including Ccr7 in MigDCs and Langerhans cells (GP12), and Hif1a and Ctla4 in Treg cells (GP22).

quotes.quote:
IFNα1 and IFNβ, as expected, induced 
common antiviral GPs across almost all cell types (GP numbers GP27, 
GP33 and GP34) but also some lineage-specific and cell-type-specific 
programmes. By contrast, IL-1α and IL-1β, pro-inflammatory cytokines 
with many known functions in the activation of both innate and adaptive 
immune cells19, induced highly cell-type-specific GPs

(1) neutrophils upregulating chemokine and inflammatory genes such 
as Cd14 (GP27), consistent with their role as first responders; (2) MigDCs 
and Langerhans cells upregulating migration programmes including 
Ccr7 (GP12); and (3) Treg cells inducing Hif1a and Ctla4 that can medi-
ate immune suppression (GP22)

experiment.system: mouse lymph node immune cell types
experiment.perturbation: IFNα1/IFNβ or IL-1α/IL-1β injection vs PBS
experiment.measurement: non-negative matrix factorization gene programmes with per-cell-type enrichment (effect size > 1, FDR-adjusted P < 0.01, Wilcoxon rank-sum test)

text: Some cell-type-specific responses were attributable to secondary effects of induced cytokines: IL-2, IL-12, IL-15 and IL-18 induced Ifng in NK cells, with B cells, DCs and macrophages then strongly expressing IFNγ signatures.

quotes.quote:
some responses could be attrib-
uted to secondary effects to induced cytokines, such as the induction 
of Ifng (which encodes IFNγ) in NK cells by IL-2, IL-12, IL-15 and IL-18, 
which probably in turn stimulate B cells, DCs and macrophages to 
strongly express IFNγ signatures

experiment.system: mouse lymph node NK cells and other immune cell types
experiment.perturbation: injection of each of 86 cytokines vs PBS
experiment.measurement: Ifng expression in NK cells and IFNγ-signature scores (summed normalized expression of IFNγ-induced genes) across cell types

text: Subclustering of each immune cell type defined 66 major cytokine-driven polarization states, each induced by one or a handful of dominant cytokine drivers.

quotes.quote:
We subclustered each immune cell type and defined 
66 major polarization states as subclusters significantly enriched for 
cytokine-treated relative to PBS-treated cells and expressing meaning-
ful biological programmes

Each polarization state was induced by 
one or a handful of dominant cytokine drivers

experiment.system: each immune cell type from the mouse lymph node cytokine atlas
experiment.perturbation: cytokine injection vs PBS
experiment.measurement: per-cell-type subclustering (PCA/UMAP) with hypergeometric enrichment of cytokine-treated cells (FDR-adjusted P < 0.01) and marker gene/DEG analysis

text: Macrophage polarization recapitulated known states: IFNγ induced a 'Mac-b' state overexpressing M1-associated genes Cxcl9 and Cxcl10, while IL-4 and IL-13 induced a distinct 'Mac-e' state marked by Chchd10, Glrx and Retnla.

quotes.quote:
IFNγ induced a ‘Mac-b’ state that overexpresses 
M1-associated pro-inflammatory genes (for example, Cxcl9 and Cxcl10).

text: LDHA-deficient mouse B16 melanomas grow more slowly than wild-type tumours in immunocompetent but not Rag2−/−Il2Rg−/− hosts, with increased infiltration by IFNG-producing CTLs and NK cells.

text: TREG cells are resistant to lactate's antiproliferative effects due to FOXP3-imposed metabolic reprogramming, import lactate via MCT1 to increase PD-1 expression through NFATC1, and require MCT1 intratumorally to preserve immunosuppressive function partly via moesin lactylation favouring TGFB1–SMAD3 signalling.

immunosuppressive CD4+CD25+FOXP3+ 
regulatory T (TREG) cells are considerably resistant to the antiproliferative effects of lactate

the ability of intracellular lactate accumulation to 
promote the lactylation of moesin (MSN), hence favoring immunosuppressive transforming 
growth factor beta 1 (TGFB1) signaling via SMAD family member 3 (SMAD3)38

text: In highly glycolytic mouse melanomas, HCCs and CRCs, PD-1 blockade promotes TREG immunosuppressive activity and lacks therapeutic effect, a resistance reversible by pharmacological or genetic LDHA inhibition; conversely, mouse TNBCs with reduced glycolysis respond to CTLA4 inhibitors with TREG destabilization toward an effector-like TNF/IFNG-secreting state.

programmed cell death 1 (PDCD1, best known 
as PD-1) blockage actively promotes the immunosuppressive activity of TREG cells and 
hence has no therapeutic effects, a resistance phenotype that can be successfully reverted 
by pharmacological or genetic LDHA inhibition36,38

mouse TNBCs with 
reduced glycolytic activity have been shown to respond to immune checkpoint inhibitors 
(ICIs) specific for cytotoxic T lymphocyte-associated protein 4 (CTLA4) along with the

text: Lactate signals to tumour-associated macrophages via GPR132 promoting M2-like repolarization and metastasis in mouse TNBC models, with GPR132 levels correlating with M2-like TAM signatures, metastasis and poor outcome in TNBC patients; in Stk11-loss lung carcinoma models lactate accumulates via MCT4 and signals through HCAR1/GPR81.

text: C-176 and C-178 were specific for mouse STING, but introduction of butyl and hexyl alkyl groups at the 4-position of the phenyl ring (C-170 and C-171) conferred activity against both human and mouse STING; SAR showed both the nitro group and furan moiety were essential for activity.

text: Endogenous nitro fatty acids formed after HSV infection, nitrolinoleic acid (NO2-cLA) and nitrooleic acid (NO2-OA), covalently modify STING via Michael addition; NO2-FA reduced type I interferons in response to HSV-2 infection in THP-1 cells and BMDMs, NO2-OA alkylated Cys88, Cys91 and His16 non-selectively, and NO2-OA treatment almost completely inhibited the pTBK1 increase in fibroblasts from patients with SAVI bearing the STING-N154S alteration.

They showed 
that endogenous nitro fatty acids (NO2-​FA) such as 
nitrolinoleic acid (NO2 -​cLA) and nitrooleic acid (NO2-​
OA) covalently modify STING via a Michael addition 
into the nitro alkene of the fatty acids. Cell-​based studies 
with NO2-​FA led to reduction of type I interferons in 
response to HSV-2 infection in both THP-1 cells and 
in BMDMs. The authors showed that NO2-​OA alky-
lated both Cys88 and Cys91, in addition to alkylation 
of His16, in a non-​selective fashion. Additional studies 
in fibroblasts from patients with SAVI, all bearing the 
gain-​of-​function STING-​N154S alteration, showed that 
the increase in pTBK1 was almost completely inhibited 
by NO2-​OA treatment.

text: Purified TRIKA1 has an apparent size of 35 kDa by gel filtration and resolves into 16 and 19 kDa bands; peptide mass fingerprinting identified 9 peptides matching human Ubc13 for the 16 kDa protein and 11 peptides matching a Uev1 isoform such as Uev1A for the 19 kDa protein.

This factor has an apparent molecu-
lar size of 35 kDa based on gel filtration chromatography

TRAF6 catalyzed the assembly of K63-linked polyUb
chains from a K63 Ub mutant in the presence of E1

sporin (STS) significantly inhibited IKK activity in the

we looked for a short

upstream of the thymidine kinase (TK) promoter, this
DNA sequence confers TGFβ-mediated induction in

the

text: Mutating the CAGA boxes in the human PAI-1 promoter reduced TGFβ induction progressively with one and two sites mutated, and mutation of all three sites rendered the promoter almost unable to respond to TGFβ, while basal transcription of mutant and wild-type promoters was comparable.

quotes.quote:
Mutation of one of the three sites led to a
reduction in TGFβ induction compared with the wild-type
promoter (Figure 2, ∆b1, ∆b2 and ∆b3 mutants). With
two sites, the reduction was greater

when all
three sites were mutated, the PAI-1 promoter was almost
unable to respond to TGFβ

in the
absence of TGFβ, the rate of transcription of the mutant
promoters and the wild-type PAI-1 promoter were com-
parable.

text: In Mv1Lu cells, constitutively activated ALK-4/T206D and ALK-5/T204D activated the CAGA box reporter, whereas ALK-2/Q207D, ALK-3/Q233D and ALK-6/Q204D had no effect, indicating activation by TGFβ and activin but not BMP receptor signalling.

expres-
sion of ALK-4/T206D and ALK-5/T204D led to transcrip-
tional activation of the CAGA box reporter vector. In
contrast, expression of ALK-2/Q207D, ALK-3/Q233D

that the CAGA sequence is activated by TGFβ and activin,
but not by BMP-induced signalling in Mv1Lu cells.

We could identify binding
complexes present only with nuclear extracts from cells

an excess of the non-radiolabelled

displaces the corresponding band

We could detect a supershift of the TGFβ-dependent

the

structural similarities, including a cystine knot

BMP-9 exists as disulfide-bonded dimers as well as stable dimers without a

they 
have a glycosylated, disulfide-rich ectodomain of about 100 amino acids, a transmembrane

The mammalian genome 
encodes five type II and seven type I receptors

TβRII receptor dimers without the need for TβRI receptors, whereas TβRI receptors have

affinity for both the TβRII or TβRI receptors in the absence of TβRI or TβRII, respectively, 
suggesting a random sequential assembly process

mostly with KD values around 10−11, which contrasts with the lower affinities of growth

plasma membrane is much lower, often 10-fold lower, than that of RTKs, ranging around

text: Betaglycan, a transmembrane proteoglycan, binds all three TGF-βs with highest affinity for TGF-β2, binds TβRI and TβRII independently and stabilizes their association, thereby enhancing TGF-β signaling; its cleaved ectodomain instead sequesters TGF-β and dampens responses.

Betaglycan is a single-pass transmembrane proteoglycan with chondroitin and heparin 
sulfate side chains in its extracellular domain that binds all three TGF-βs, yet with highest 
affinity for TGF-β2 (78).

Conversely, however, betaglycan can be cleaved to release its ectodomain that then functions

text: Endoglin binds TGF-β1 and -β3 and promotes TGF-β signaling through ALK-1 while inhibiting signaling through TβRI, and binds BMP-9 and BMP-10 with high affinity, whereas it binds activin A, BMP-7 and BMP-2 only in association with the corresponding type II receptors.

through ALK-1, a predominant BMP type I receptor, while inhibiting signaling through the 
type I receptor TβRI, also known as ALK-5 (61, 75). Endoglin also binds activin A, BMP-7

text: N-glycosylation facilitates transport of TβRII to the cell surface and impaired glycosylation decreases ligand binding to TβRII, so inhibition of N-glycosylation reduces TGF-β responsiveness; ectodomain N-glycosylation enhances BMP-2 binding to BMP-RII but not to ActRII or ActRIIB.

N-glycosylation facilitates transport of the TβRII receptor to the cell 
surface (102), and impaired glycosylation decreases ligand binding to TβRII (104). 
Consequently, inhibition of N-glycosylation reduces TGF-β responsiveness (102). 
Additionally, ectodomain N-glycosylation enhances the binding of BMP-2 to the BMP-RII 
but not the ActRII or ActRIIB type II receptors (103).

text: The metalloprotease TACE/ADAM17 cleaves TβRI but not TβRII in response to ERK or p38 MAPK signaling, so mitogenic and inflammatory stimuli dampen TGF-β signaling without decreasing ligand binding to TβRII; γ-secretase then releases the TβRI cytoplasmic domain, which translocates to the nucleus and controls target gene transcription.

quotes.quote:
The transmembrane metalloprotease 
TACE, also known as ADAM17, cleaves TβRI, but not the TβRII receptor, in response to 
ERK or p38 MAPK signaling (107, 108).

TACE-mediated ectodomain 
shedding of TβRI is followed, through the activity of γ-secretase, by intracellular release of 
the TβRI cytoplasmic domain, which translocates into the nucleus where it controls 
transcription of target genes (109, 110).

text: Glucose at 25 mM and insulin both induce rapid transport of intracellular TβRII and TβRI to the cell surface via AKT activation, which phosphorylates the RabGAP AS160 to relieve intracellular receptor retention.
