transport of intracellular TβRII and TβRI receptors to the cell surface (111, 112). This 
induction results from rapid activation of AKT, which phosphorylates the intracellular, 
membrane-associated Rab guanosine triphosphatase (GTPase)-activating protein (RabGAP) 
AS160, thus relieving the intracellular retention and promoting cell surface transport of both 
TβRII and TβRI (112)

experiment.system: cultured cells with intracellular pools of TβRI and TβRII
experiment.perturbation: treatment with 25 mM glucose or insulin (AKT activation)
experiment.measurement: cell-surface abundance of TβRI and TβRII, AS160 phosphorylation

text: Neddylation of TβRII, but not TβRI, mediated by the NEDD8 E2 enzyme Ubc12 and E3 ligase c-Cbl, stabilizes the receptor and enhances TGF-β signaling, and is reversed by the de-neddylase NEDP1.

quotes.quote:
TβRII neddylation is mediated by the 
NEDD8 E2 conjugating enzyme Ubc12 and the E3 ligase c-Cbl, and stabilizes the receptor, 
presumably by opposing ubiquitylation and degradation while promoting TβRII 
internalization, and thus enhancing TGF-β signaling (124).

experiment.system: cells expressing TβRII
experiment.perturbation: NEDD8 conjugation by Ubc12/c-Cbl and de-neddylation by NEDP1
experiment.measurement: receptor stability, internalization and TGF-β signaling

text: Ligand-induced type II receptor phosphorylation of the type I receptor GS domain at serines and a threonine releases the 12 kd immunophilin FKBP12, relieving inhibition of the type I receptor kinase; FKBP12 association prevents signaling in the absence of ligand.

quotes.quote:
This stabilization enables the type II receptors to 
phosphorylate the type I receptors in their juxtamembrane GS domain at serines and a 
threonine, which then induces conformational changes that release the 12 kd immunophilin 
FKBP12 from the GS domain (133, 134). This dissociation relieves the inhibitory interaction 
of the kinase domain with the GS domain, and activates the kinase of the type I receptors

experiment.system: TGF-β family tetrameric receptor complexes
experiment.perturbation: ligand binding and GS-domain phosphorylation
experiment.measurement: FKBP12 dissociation and type I receptor kinase activation

text: Autophosphorylation of TβRII at Ser213 and Ser249 enhances its kinase activity, whereas autophosphorylation at Ser416 attenuates it, and tyrosine phosphorylation, by autophosphorylation or by Src, enhances TβRII activity.

quotes.quote:
Autophosphorylation at Ser213 and Ser249 enhances the kinase activity of 
TβRII, whereas autophosphorylation at Ser416 attenuates it (139). Phosphorylation on Tyr, 
either through autophosphorylation (67) or by Src (140), enhances the TβRII activity (67).

experiment.system: TβRII receptor kinase
experiment.perturbation: autophosphorylation at defined sites; Src-mediated tyrosine phosphorylation
experiment.measurement: TβRII kinase activity

text: TGF-β-induced TβRI phosphorylation promotes Lys389 sumoylation of TβRI, which facilitates recruitment and activation of effector Smads and Smad-mediated signaling.

quotes.quote:
TGF-β-induced TβRI phosphorylation also promotes 
Lys389 sumoylation of TβRI, which facilitates the recruitment and activation of effector 
Smads, and Smad-mediated signaling (141).

experiment.system: cells expressing TβRI
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β stimulation and TβRI sumoylation at Lys389
experiment.measurement: effector Smad recruitment/activation and Smad-mediated signaling

text: The mammalian genome encodes eight Smads; Smad2 and Smad3 act as R-Smads for activin and TGF-β signaling, Smad1, Smad5 and Smad8 mediate responses to BMPs and GDFs, and Smad4 is the common partner in trimeric complexes and does not require activation by type I receptors.

quotes.quote:
The mammalian genome encodes eight Smads, including the inhibitory Smads, Smad6 and 
Smad7

Smad2 and Smad3 act as R-
Smads for activin and TGF-β signaling, whereas Smad1, Smad5 and Smad8 mediate

Smad4, the common partner for the activated R-Smads in trimeric Smad 
complexes, does not require activation by type I receptors (151, 152).

experiment.system: mammalian Smad proteins
experiment.perturbation: ligand stimulation (activin/TGF-β versus BMP/GDF)
experiment.measurement: which Smads are receptor-activated and complex composition

numbers.quantity: Smads encoded in the mammalian genome

text: Receptor-Smad specificity is set by the type I receptor: phosphorylated GS domain presents a negatively charged surface interfacing with a basic patch in the R-Smad MH2 domain, while a cluster of four amino acids in the receptor L45 loop interfaces with the L3 loop of the R-Smad MH2 domain.

quotes.quote:
Phosphorylation of 
the GS domain by the type II receptors enables this negatively charged surface of the type I 
receptor to interface with a basic patch in the MH2 domain, whereas a cluster of four amino 
acids in the receptor’s L45 loop provides receptor-Smad specificity by interfacing with 
complementary amino acids in the L3 loop of the R-Smad MH2 domain (63).

experiment.system: type I receptor–R-Smad complexes
experiment.perturbation: GS-domain phosphorylation; L45/L3 loop sequence determinants
experiment.measurement: structural interface and receptor-Smad selectivity

numbers.quantity: amino acids in the L45 loop conferring specificity

text: TGF-β-induced heterotrimers of Smad2, Smad3 and Smad4 are abundantly formed and target distinct genes from complexes containing pairs of Smad2 or Smad3; complexes of two Smad3s and one Smad2, and of one R-Smad with two Smad4 molecules, are prevalent in TGF-β-treated hepatoma cells.

quotes.quote:
TGF-β-
induced heterotrimers of Smad2, Smad3 and Smad4 are abundantly formed, but differ 
functionally from complexes that contain pairs of Smad2 or Smad3, and target distinct genes 
(175). Also trimers that consist of only activated R-Smads have been observed (160, 175), 
and complexes of two Smad3s and one Smad2 are prevalent in TGF-β-treated hepatoma 
cells, as are complexes of one R-Smad and two Smad4 molecules (175).

experiment.system: hepatoma cells
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β treatment
experiment.measurement: Smad trimer composition and target gene sets

text: R-Smads and Smad4 bind DNA through an 11 amino acid β-hairpin in their MH1 domains; the Smad3/Smad4 optimal sequence is AGAC or its reverse complement GTCT while Smad1 and Smad5 prefer GGCGCC, yet ChIP analyses revealed preferential binding of all R-Smads and Smad4 to GC-rich sequences approximating GGCGC or GGCCG.

quotes.quote:
all R-Smads and Smad4 can bind 
DNA directly through an 11 amino acid β-hairpin in their MH1 domains

For Smad3 and 
Smad4, this sequence is AGAC or its reverse complement GTCT (152, 190–192), while 
Smad1 and Smad5 prefer GGCGCC (152, 193).

Additional ChIP analyses, however, revealed preferential binding of all R-Smads and Smad4 
to GC-rich sequences that approximate a consensus sequence GGCGC or GGCCG

experiment.system: Smad proteins and genomic DNA
experiment.perturbation: observational (ChIP and in vitro binding-site selection)
experiment.measurement: preferred DNA binding sequences

text: Without association with sequence-specific transcription factors, Smads bind DNA only weakly, with a Kd of around 1 × 10−7 M, whereas sequence-specific transcription factors often bind DNA with Kds of 10−9 to 10−11 M.

quotes.quote:
Without this 
association, Smads bind DNA only weakly, meaning with a Kd of around 1 × 10−7 M (153), 
whereas sequence-specific transcription factors often bind DNA with Kds of 10−9 to 10−11 
M.

experiment.system: Smad proteins and DNA binding sites
experiment.perturbation: presence or absence of partner transcription factor
experiment.measurement: DNA binding dissociation constant

text: Smad4 is required for or strongly enhances R-Smad-mediated transcription activation of many genes, yet many target genes are still activated by R-Smads in the absence of Smad4, albeit often to a much lower extent.

quotes.quote:
Smad4 is required for or strongly enhances R-Smad-mediated 
transcription activation of many genes, consistent with its role as coactivator, yet many target 
genes are still activated by R-Smads in the absence of Smad4, albeit often to a much lower 
extent than in the presence of Smad4 (208).

experiment.system: cells with and without functional Smad4
experiment.perturbation: Smad4 inactivation
experiment.measurement: R-Smad-mediated target gene transcription

text: Smad complexes direct histone modifications: recruitment of Suv39h1 or SETDB1 confers TGF-β-induced H3K9 methylation and transcription repression at the Il2 and Snai1 promoters respectively, Smad3-mediated recruitment of the H3K4 methyltransferase SET9 targets the ACTA2 gene, and p300 enzymatic activity is required for Smad2-mediated transcription activation.

quotes.quote:
Recruitment of Suv39h1 (213) or SETDB1 (214) confer TGF-β-induced 
H3K9 methylation and transcription repression at promoter sequences of the Il2 and Snai1 
genes, respectively (187,188), while Smad3-mediated recruitment of the H3K4 
methyltransferase SET9 targets the ACTA2 gene (215).

The enzymatic activity of p300 is required for Smad2-mediated transcription 
activation, suggesting that chromatin remodeling is required for transcription activation by 
Smads (210).

experiment.system: TGF-β-stimulated cells at Il2, Snai1 and ACTA2 promoters
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β stimulation; recruitment or loss of histone-modifying enzymes
experiment.measurement: histone methylation marks and target gene transcription

text: TGF-β signaling directly controls RNA processing: Smad3 associates with the RNA-binding protein PCBP1/hnRNPE1 to direct changes in CD44 pre-mRNA splicing yielding distinct CD44 isoforms, and Smad-mediated repression of ESRP1 and ESRP2 alters splicing.

quotes.quote:
TGF-β 
induces changes in RNA splicing through Smad-mediated repression of genes encoding 
splicing regulators, such as the epithelial splicing regulatory factors ESRP1 and ESRP2 
(227).

in response to TGF-β, Smad3 was shown to 
associate with the RNA-binding protein PCBP1, also known as hnRNPE1, and thus directs 
changes in splicing of the CD44 pre-mRNA, yielding functionally distinct CD44 isoforms 
(228).

experiment.system: cells undergoing TGF-β signaling
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β stimulation
experiment.measurement: CD44 pre-mRNA splicing pattern and splicing regulator expression

text: TGF-β- and BMP-activated Smads associate with a Smad-binding dsRNA motif in select pri-miRNAs and with the p68 RNA helicase in complex with Drosha RNAse, promoting pri-miRNA processing into miRNAs.

quotes.quote:
TGF-β- and 
BMP-activated Smads were seen to associate with a Smad-binding dsRNA motif in select 
pri-miRNAs and with the p68 RNA helicase in complex with Drosha RNAse, and thus 
promote the pri-miRNA processing into miRNAs (151, 232, 233).

experiment.system: cells with TGF-β- or BMP-activated Smads
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β or BMP stimulation
experiment.measurement: Smad association with pri-miRNAs/p68-Drosha and pri-miRNA processing into miRNAs

text: Smad2 and/or Smad3 associate with the METTL3-METLL14-WAPP m6A-methyltransferase complex and recruit it to targeted nascent pre-mRNAs, resulting in co-transcriptional adenosine methylation, promoting their degradation and decreasing expression of encoded proteins.

quotes.quote:
Smad2 and/or Smad3 were 
shown to associate with the METTL3-METLL14-WAPP complex, which N6-methylates 
adenosine in RNA (Fig. 5F). Smad-mediated recruitment of this m6A-methyltransferase 
complex at targeted nascent pre-mRNAs results in their co-transcriptional adenosine 
methylation, consequently promoting their degradation, and decreased expression of 
encoded proteins (235).

experiment.system: cells with activated Smad2/Smad3
experiment.perturbation: Smad-mediated recruitment of the m6A methyltransferase complex
experiment.measurement: pre-mRNA adenosine methylation, transcript degradation and protein expression

text: Inhibitory Smads repress R-Smad activation at two levels: MH2-mediated association with type I receptors prevents R-Smad recruitment, and competition with Smad4 for binding to R-Smads represses formation of R-Smad–Smad4 complexes at target genes.

quotes.quote:
The inhibitory Smads repress ligand-induced R-Smad activation at two levels (136). Their 
association with type I receptors through interfaces that primarily involve their MH2 
domains prevents R-Smad recruitment through their MH2 domains to type I receptors

the competition of an inhibitory Smad 
with Smad4 for binding to R-Smads represses the formation of R-Smad complexes with 
Smad4 as transcription coactivator at target genes (241)

experiment.system: cells expressing inhibitory Smad6/Smad7 with type I receptors and R-Smads
experiment.perturbation: inhibitory Smad association/competition
experiment.measurement: R-Smad receptor recruitment, activation, and Smad4 complex formation

text: Ligand-induced Arg methylation of Smad6 and/or Smad7 by the type II receptor-associated methyltransferase PRMT1 causes their dissociation from type I receptors, which precedes and enables effector Smad recruitment and C-terminal activation.

quotes.quote:
The ligand-induced conformational 
changes in the receptor complex (63) enable the arginine methyltransferase PRMT1, which 
is associated with the type II receptors, to methylate Smad6 or Smad7, resulting in their 
dissociation from the type I receptors (137, 138). Thus, PRMT1-mediated methylation of 
inhibitory Smads and their dissociation from the type I receptors precede and enable the 
recruitment of the effector Smads for subsequent activation through C-terminal 
phosphorylation

experiment.system: TGF-β family receptor complexes with inhibitory Smads
experiment.perturbation: ligand binding and PRMT1-mediated arginine methylation
experiment.measurement: Smad6/Smad7 dissociation from type I receptors and effector Smad recruitment

text: Mono-ubiquitylation has site-specific effects on Smads: Smad2 mono-ubiquitylation enhances association with TβRI, Smad3 MH1-domain mono-ubiquitylation interferes with DNA binding, MH2-domain mono-ubiquitylation after CDK8/CDK9 phosphorylation interferes with complex formation, Smad4 mono-ubiquitylation at Lys507 promotes trimer formation with Smad3 and TGF-β-induced transcription while enhancing nuclear export, and Smad6 mono-ubiquitylation impairs binding to the BMP type I receptor.

quotes.quote:
Smad2 mono-
ubiquitylation enhances its association with the TβRI receptor (264), whereas Smad3 mono-
ubiquitylation in its MH1 domain interferes with Smad3 binding to DNA (265), and Smad3 
mono-ubiquitylation in its MH2 domain, after phosphorylation by CDK8 or CDK9, 
interferes with Smad complex formation (266). Smad4 mono-ubiquitylation at Lys507 in its 
MH2 domain promotes trimer formation with Smad3, and TGF-β-induced transcription, yet 
also enhances its nuclear export (267)

Smad6 mono-ubiquitylation impairs its binding to the BMP type I receptor 
(269).

experiment.system: Smad proteins in TGF-β/BMP-stimulated cells
experiment.perturbation: mono-ubiquitylation at defined domains/lysines; CDK8/CDK9 phosphorylation
experiment.measurement: receptor association, DNA binding, complex formation, transcription and nuclear export

text: TGF-β and BMPs often induce ERK/MAPK signaling within 5–10 min with kinetics similar to RTKs but at lower levels, and TGF-β-induced activation depends on ShcA, with p52ShcA recruited to the tyrosine-phosphorylated TβRI and phosphorylated on serine and tyrosine, promoting ShcA-Grb2-SOS complex formation and Ras activation.

quotes.quote:
TGF-β and BMPs often induce ERK/MAPK signaling within 5–10 min, with similar 
kinetics as RTKs, albeit at lower levels (286, 287). The activation of this pathway by TGF-β 
depends on ShcA (68). TGF-β induces p52ShcA recruitment, through its phosphotyrosine-
binding SH2 and PTΒ domains, to the tyrosine-phosphorylated TβRI receptor, and ShcA 
phosphorylation on serine and tyrosine (68).

TGF-β-
induced ShcA phosphorylation on tyrosine promotes the formation of ShcA-Grb2-SOS 
complexes and Ras activation, leading to MEK1 and/or MEK2, and ERK/MAPK activation

experiment.system: cultured cells expressing TGF-β receptors and ShcA
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β or BMP stimulation; ShcA dependence
experiment.measurement: ERK/MAPK activation kinetics, ShcA phosphorylation and complex formation

text: p52ShcA and Smad3 compete for TβRI association, so p52ShcA both initiates ERK/MAPK activation and represses TGF-β-induced Smad3 activation, with ShcA expression defining the balance between the two outputs; TGF-β-induced ERK/MAPK signaling occurs in caveolar lipid-raft microdomains whereas Smad signaling associates with clathrin-mediated endocytosis.

quotes.quote:
p52ShcA association with TβRI precludes Smad recruitment, since 
p52ShcA and Smad3 compete for TβRI association (291). Consequently, p52ShcA not only 
initiates ERK/MAPK pathway activation, but also represses TGF-β-induced Smad3 
activation, and ShcA expression defines the balance between TGF-β-induced Smad and 
ERK/MAPK signaling (291).

TGF-β-induced ERK/MAPK signaling occurs in caveolar lipid-raft 
microdomains (284), whereas Smad signaling associates with clathrin-mediated endocytosis

experiment.system: cells expressing TβRI, ShcA and Smad3
experiment.perturbation: varying ShcA expression; subcellular compartment localization
experiment.measurement: TβRI association, Smad3 activation versus ERK/MAPK activation

text: TGF-β induces TAK1 recruitment to receptor complexes via the E3 ligases TRAF6 or TRAF4, whose intramolecular polyubiquitylation scaffolds TAK1 ubiquitylation and activation, leading to JNK and p38 MAPK activation without requiring direct phosphorylation by the type I receptor kinases.

quotes.quote:
TGF-β induces TAK1 recruitment to TGF-β receptor complexes, through association with 
the RING domain E3 ubiquitin ligases TRAF6 or TRAF4 (299–301). This association 
induces intramolecular TRAF6 or TRAF4 polyubiquitylation, allowing either to serve as a 
scaffold for TAK1 activation. TAK1 is then ubiquitylated by TRAF6 or TRAF4 at a site that 
does not lead to degradation but is required for its activation, resulting in JNK and p38 
MAPK activation (283, 300, 301). This mechanism of pathway activation does not require 
direct phosphorylation by the type I receptor kinases (299, 300)

experiment.system: cells with TGF-β receptor complexes, TRAF6/TRAF4 and TAK1
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β stimulation; type I receptor kinase requirement
experiment.measurement: TAK1 recruitment and ubiquitylation, JNK and p38 MAPK activation

text: Blocking p38 MAPK activation, silencing TRAF6 expression or interfering with TAK1 function prevents TGF-β- or BMP-induced apoptosis, and p38 MAPK activation and TRAF6 or TRAF4 expression or ubiquitylation are required for TGF-β-induced EMT.

quotes.quote:
blocking p38 MAPK 
activation, silencing TRAF6 expression or interfering with TAK1 function prevent TGF-β- 
or BMP-induced apoptosis (296, 299, 300, 305–307). p38 MAPK activation and TRAF6 or 
TRAF4 expression or ubiquitylation are also required for TGF-β-induced EMT

experiment.system: cultured cells responding to TGF-β or BMP
experiment.perturbation: p38 MAPK inhibition, TRAF6 silencing, TAK1 interference
experiment.measurement: ligand-induced apoptosis and EMT

text: Two mechanisms of TGF-β-induced AKT activation are reported: TβRI kinase-dependent activation with the PI3K regulatory subunit p85 associating constitutively with TβRII and with TβRI upon TGF-β, and TRAF6-mediated p85 ubiquitylation that activates PI3 kinase and AKT without requiring the TβRI kinase.

quotes.quote:
In several cell systems, TGF-β-induced AKT activation requires the TβRI kinase, and the 
regulatory PI3-kinase subunit, p85, was seen to associate constitutively with the TβRII 
receptor, and with TβRI in response to TGF-β (315).
TGF-β can induce p85 ubiquitylation by TGF-

β receptor-associated TRAF6, resulting in its association with the TβRI receptor, and 
activation of PI3 kinase and AKT (317). In this scenario, TGF-β-induced PI3 kinase and 
AKT activation does not require the TβRI kinase (317).

experiment.system: multiple cell systems with TGF-β receptors, p85/PI3K and TRAF6
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β stimulation; TβRI kinase dependence; TRAF6-mediated ubiquitylation
experiment.measurement: p85 association/ubiquitylation and AKT activation

text: JAK1 constitutively associated with TβRI directly activates STAT3 signaling in response to TGF-β in hepatic stellate cells and fibroblasts independently of Smad signaling, followed by a second wave of JAK1-STAT3 signaling that depends on new protein synthesis.

quotes.quote:
JAK1 that associates constitutively with the TβRI receptor 
directly activates STAT3 signaling in response to TGF-β in hepatic stellate cells and 
fibroblasts, independently of Smad signaling (331). Like several other non-Smad signaling 
pathways, such direct TGF-β-induced JAK1-STAT3 activation is context-dependent, and 
followed by a second wave of JAK1-STAT3 signaling that depends on new protein synthesis 
(331).

experiment.system: hepatic stellate cells and fibroblasts
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β stimulation (and Smad independence)
experiment.measurement: JAK1-STAT3 activation kinetics and protein-synthesis dependence

text: TGF-β induces transient RhoA activation in epithelial cells within 5 min and BMP rapidly induces RhoA and Rho-associated kinase activation in mesenchymal cells during spreading, yet TGF-β also represses RhoA activity at tight junctions during epithelial junction dissolution.

quotes.quote:
TGF-β induces transient RhoA activation in epithelial cells 
within 5 min (332, 333), and BMP rapidly induces activation of RhoA and Rho-associated 
kinase in mesenchymal cells during cell spreading (334). Remarkably, TGF-β induces 
repression of RhoA activity at tight junctions of epithelial cells during TGF-β-induced 
epithelial junction dissolution (335)

experiment.system: epithelial and mesenchymal cells
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β or BMP stimulation
experiment.measurement: RhoA and Rho-associated kinase activation, including subcellular localization at tight junctions

text: In response to TGF-β, receptor-associated TRAF6 recruits presenilin to TβRI, activates it by polyubiquitylation and ubiquitylates the TβRI cytoplasmic domain before γ-secretase cleavage; the released domain translocates into the nucleus, associates with p300 and promotes activation of genes that facilitate cell invasion.

quotes.quote:
In 
response to TGF-β, TGF-β receptor-associated TRAF6 recruits presenilin, a component of 
the γ-secretase complex, to TβRI, activates presenilin through polyubiquitylation, and 
ubiquitylates the TβRI cytoplasmic domain prior to its intramembranous cleavage. The 
ubiquitylated TβRI cytoplasmic domain then translocates into the nucleus, associates with 
the coactivator p300, and promotes the activation of genes that facilitate cell invasion (109, 
110).

experiment.system: cancer cells expressing TβRI, TRAF6 and γ-secretase
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β stimulation and TRAF6-mediated ubiquitylation/γ-secretase cleavage
experiment.measurement: nuclear translocation of TβRI cytoplasmic domain and activation of invasion genes

text: Time-dependent dissection of early TGF-β-induced changes in the phospho-proteome revealed a plethora of phosphorylation changes that do not require Smad-mediated gene expression.

quotes.quote:
time-dependent dissection of early TGF-β-induced changes in the phospho-
proteome revealed a plethora of phosphorylation changes that do not require Smad-mediated 
gene expression (343)

experiment.system: TGF-β-stimulated cells
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β stimulation over a time course
experiment.measurement: phospho-proteome changes and their dependence on Smad-mediated gene expression

text: Release of myostatin and GDF11 from latency depends on cleavage of the pro-domain by BMP1 and mTolloid metalloproteases, and no evidence exists for integrin-mediated activation of these latent complexes, whereas latent TGF-β1 activation involves the integrins αvβ1, αvβ6, and αvβ8 together with proteases.

quotes.quote:
interaction 
of the pro-segment with integrins—notably the integrins αvβ1, αvβ6, and αvβ8—enables 
stress-induced, integrin-mediated changes in conformation of the latent TGF-β complex that 
result in the release of active TGF-β1

No evidence exists for integrin-
mediated activation of latent myostatin and GDF11 complexes. Rather, the release of 
myostatin and GDF11 from latency depends on cleavage of the pro-domain by BMP1 and 
mTolloid metalloproteases (50, 51).

experiment.system: latent TGF-β1, myostatin/GDF8 and GDF11 complexes
experiment.perturbation: integrin engagement or metalloprotease (BMP1/mTolloid) cleavage of the pro-domain
experiment.measurement: release of active mature ligand from the latent complex

text: GDF15, structurally a bona fide TGF-β family member, does not act through TGF-β family receptors but binds GFRAL, a transmembrane receptor related to GFRα receptors that signals through association with Ret1, activating pathways commonly associated with receptor tyrosine kinases.

quotes.quote:
Growth/
differentiation factor 15 (GDF15), which is structurally seen as a bona fide member of the 
TGF-β family (2), does not act through TGF-β family receptors either. Rather, it binds to 
GFRα-like (GFRAL), a transmembrane receptor that is related to the GFRα receptors and 
also signals through association with Ret1, thus activating signaling pathways commonly 
associated with receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs) (16, 17).

experiment.system: GDF15 and candidate receptors
experiment.perturbation: observational (receptor binding and signaling assays)
experiment.measurement: receptor identity and downstream pathway activation

text: Cripto, a GPI-anchored EGF-CFC family protein with affinity for ActRIB (ALK-4), enables Nodal binding to the activin receptor complex and thus Nodal signaling, whereas its absence promotes activin signaling and prevents Nodal signaling; Cripto also binds TGF-β and prevents its binding to TβRI.

quotes.quote:
Cripto enables Nodal binding to the activin receptor complex, thus 
activating Nodal signaling, whereas its absence promotes activin signaling and prevents 
Nodal signaling (75, 89, 90). Cripto also binds TGF-β and prevents its binding to the TβRI 
receptor (91).

experiment.system: cells expressing activin/Nodal receptor complexes
experiment.perturbation: presence or absence of Cripto
experiment.measurement: Nodal versus activin ligand binding and signaling; TGF-β binding to TβRI

text: Dab2 associates with the TGF-β type I receptor and promotes clathrin-mediated endocytosis of receptor complexes, so increased Dab2 expression enhances TGF-β-induced Smad activation, whereas antiviral RLR signaling activates IRF-3, which associates with Smad3 and prevents its recruitment to TβRI, attenuating TGF-β-induced Smad3 activation and gene expression.

quotes.quote:
Dab2, which 
associates with the TGF-β type I receptor, promotes clathrin-mediated endocytosis of the 
receptor complexes; thus, increased Dab2 expression enhances TGF-β-induced Smad 
activation (162, 163). Conversely, antiviral RLR signaling results in activation of IRF-3, 
which then associates with Smad3, thus preventing its recruitment to TβRI and attenuating 
TGF-β-induced Smad3 activation and gene expression.

experiment.system: cells with TGF-β receptor complexes, Dab2 and IRF-3
experiment.perturbation: increased Dab2 expression; antiviral RLR signaling
experiment.measurement: receptor endocytosis, Smad3 recruitment/activation and gene expression

text: Wnt effector GSK3β, CDK8 and CDK9 phosphorylate activated Smad2 and Smad3 in the linker region, generating a motif recognized by the E3 ligase Nedd4L that leads to ubiquitylation and degradation; CDK8 and CDK9 also phosphorylate the Smad1 linker, leading to Smad1 recognition by Smurf1 or Nedd4L and degradation.

quotes.quote:
the Wnt signaling effector GSK3β, as well as CDK8 and CDK9 
phosphorylate activated Smad2 and Smad3 in the linker region, and the phosphorylated 
motif is then recognized by the E3 ubiquitin ligase Nedd4L, resulting in ubiquitylation and 
degradation. CDK8 and CDK9 also phosphorylate the Smad1 linker, leading to recognition 
of Smad1 by Smurf1 or Nedd4L, and Smad1 degradation (154, 259, 260).

experiment.system: activated R-Smads in cells
experiment.perturbation: linker phosphorylation by GSK3β, CDK8 or CDK9
experiment.measurement: E3 ligase recognition, Smad ubiquitylation and degradation

text: Normal cultured human fibroblasts display a finite capacity for cell division before entering an irreversible growth arrest termed replicative senescence.

quotes.quote:
Hayflick and Moorhead demonstrated in 1961 that normal cultured human fibroblasts 
display a finite capacity for cell division before entering an irreversible growth arrest known 
as replicative senescence1.

experiment.system: cultured normal human diploid fibroblasts
experiment.perturbation: observational (serial passaging in culture)
experiment.measurement: number of cell divisions before growth arrest

text: Mice lacking p16 are predisposed to spontaneous tumour formation.

quotes.quote:
Indeed, mice lacking p16 
are predisposed to spontaneous tumour formation5.

experiment.system: mice
experiment.perturbation: genetic loss of p16
experiment.measurement: spontaneous tumour incidence

text: Inhibition of DDR signalling kinases (ATM, ATR, CHK1 and CHK2) allows senescent cells to re-enter the cell cycle.

quotes.quote:
Inhibition of DDR signalling kinases (ATM, ATR, CHK1 and CHK2) allows senescent cells 
to re-enter the cell cycle7,24,25.

experiment.system: senescent cells in culture
experiment.perturbation: inhibition of DDR kinases ATM, ATR, CHK1, CHK2
experiment.measurement: cell cycle re-entry

text: One or a few DDR-signalling telomeres suffice to trigger replicative cellular senescence, and forced telomerase expression prevents cellular senescence and promotes unlimited proliferation.

quotes.quote:
One or a 
few DDR signalling telomeres are sufficient to trigger replicative cellular senescence33, and 
forced expression of telomerase prevents cellular senescence and promotes unlimited cell 
proliferation34.

experiment.system: human cells in culture
experiment.perturbation: telomere shortening / forced telomerase expression
experiment.measurement: DDR-positive telomere number and proliferative capacity

text: Oncogene-induced ROS generated by NADPH oxidases can induce cellular senescence by boosting the initial hyperproliferative phase associated with altered DNA replication and DNA damage accumulation.

quotes.quote:
oncogene-induced ROS, generated by NADPH oxidases, can induce cellular senescence by 
boosting the initial hyperproliferative phase associated with altered DNA replication and 
DNA damage accumulation45

experiment.system: oncogene-expressing cells
experiment.perturbation: oncogene activation and modulation of NADPH oxidase-derived ROS
experiment.measurement: hyperproliferation, DNA damage and senescence

text: Depletion of mitochondrial sirtuins or selective chemical inhibition of mitochondrial function triggers senescence, and mitochondrial dysfunction-associated senescence (MiDAS) exhibits a distinct cell-non-autonomous programme.

quotes.quote:
depletion of 
mitochondrial sirtuins, a group of evolutionarily conserved proteins that regulate ageing 
across different species, as well as selective chemical inhibition of mitochondrial function, 
triggers senescence47.

mitochondrial dysfunction-
associated senescence (MiDAs), which is characterized by a distinct phenotype, exhibits a 
unique cell-non-autonomous programme

experiment.system: cultured cells
experiment.perturbation: depletion of mitochondrial sirtuins or chemical inhibition of mitochondrial function
experiment.measurement: senescence markers and secretory phenotype

text: SAHF enforce a DDR-resistant heterochromatin structure that restrains DDR signalling; HDAC inhibitor treatment relaxes chromatin, boosts DDR signalling and causes apoptotic cell death, an early example of a senolytic approach.

quotes.quote:
Rather, SAHF enforce a DDR-resistant heterochromatin structure that 
restrains DDR signalling52. Indeed, treatment with histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitors, 
which induce chromatin relaxation, boosts DDR signalling with consequent cell death by 
apoptosis.

experiment.system: oncogene-induced senescent cells with SAHF
experiment.perturbation: HDAC inhibitor treatment (chromatin relaxation)
experiment.measurement: DDR signalling and apoptosis

text: A core SASP programme comprising IL-6, IL-8 (CXCL8) and MCP1 was reported in all types of in vitro-generated senescent cells, with the oncogenic trigger greatly amplifying protein secretion compared with replicative or irradiation-induced senescence.

quotes.quote:
with the oncogenic trigger greatly amplifying protein secretion compared with replicative or 
irradiation-induced senescence75.

a core SASP programme 
comprising mainly proinflammatory interleukin-6 (IL-6), CXC chemokine ligand 8 
(CXCL8, hereafter named IL-8) and monocyte chemoattractant protein 1 (MCP1; also 
known as CCL2) was reported in all types of in vitro-generated senescent cells75.

experiment.system: in vitro-generated senescent cells of multiple types
experiment.perturbation: different senescence triggers (oncogene, replicative exhaustion, irradiation)
experiment.measurement: secreted protein profiling

text: Depletion of the DDR regulators ATM, NBS1 and CHK2 dampens cytokine production in response to genotoxic stress, whereas inhibition of p53 further enhances SASP.

quotes.quote:
ATM, NBS1 and CHK2 prime SASP genes for activation, as depletion of these DDR 
upstream regulators dampens cytokine production in response to genotoxic stress86. 
Inhibition of p53 has the opposite effect, as it further enhances SASP following a 
senescence-inducing insult86

experiment.system: cells undergoing genotoxic stress-induced senescence
experiment.perturbation: depletion of ATM, NBS1, CHK2; inhibition of p53
experiment.measurement: inflammatory cytokine secretion (SASP)

text: Activation of the stress-inducible MAPK p38 is both necessary and sufficient to trigger growth arrest and SASP even in the absence of DNA damage.

quotes.quote:
the activation of the 
stress-inducible MAPK p38 was proven both necessary and sufficient to trigger growth 
arrest and SASP even in the absence of DNA damage88.

experiment.system: cultured cells
experiment.perturbation: gain and loss of p38 MAPK activity
experiment.measurement: growth arrest and SASP expression

text: HMGB2 depletion diminishes SASP without affecting the senescence growth arrest in oncogene-induced senescent cells.

quotes.quote:
HMGB2 directly binds and specifically regulates 
SASP gene expression in oncogene-induced senescent cells, and its depletion diminishes 
SASP without affecting the senescence growth arrest108.

experiment.system: oncogene-induced senescent cells
experiment.perturbation: HMGB2 depletion
experiment.measurement: SASP gene expression and proliferation arrest

text: cGAS–STING genetic depletion reduces the proinflammatory SASP and mitigates senescence immunosurveillance in vivo senescence models.

quotes.quote:
cGAS–STING genetic depletion reduces the proinflammatory SASP and 
mitigates senescence immunosurveillance in senescence models in vivo.

experiment.system: in vivo senescence models
experiment.perturbation: genetic depletion of cGAS–STING
experiment.measurement: proinflammatory SASP and immune clearance of senescent cells

text: Treatment with nucleoside reverse-transcriptase inhibitors limits senescence-associated detrimental SASP effects and ameliorates chronic inflammation in aged animals; strong type I interferon induction in senescent cells was partly caused by transposable element reactivation via cGAS–STING.

quotes.quote:
This 
distinctively strong induction of type I interferon was found to be partly caused by 
reactivation of transposable elements and consequent to cGAS–STING activation62. 
Treatment with nucleoside reverse-transcriptase inhibitors, which inhibit retrotransposition 
of transposable elements, limits the senescence-associated detrimental effects of SASP and 
ameliorates chronic inflammation in aged animals62,119.

experiment.system: senescent cells and aged animals
experiment.perturbation: nucleoside reverse-transcriptase inhibitor treatment
experiment.measurement: type I interferon response, SASP effects and chronic inflammation

text: Single-cell transcriptomic analysis of human HSCs revealed dose-dependent activation of senescence-like programmes in response to DSBs, with p53 activation and proinflammatory programmes and reduced clonogenic potential, engraftment capacity and lineage output on transplantation.

quotes.quote:
Single-cell transcriptomic 
analysis of human HSCs revealed a dose-dependent activation of senescence-like 
programmes in response to DSBs, which were characterized by activation of p53 and the 
induction of proinflammatory programmes that resulted in reduced clonogenic potential, 
engraftment capacity and lineage output on transplantation126.

experiment.system: human haematopoietic stem cells
experiment.perturbation: induction of DNA double-strand breaks at varying doses
experiment.measurement: single-cell transcriptomics, clonogenic potential, engraftment and lineage output

text: Ionizing radiation induces differentiation of hair bulb melanocyte stem cells after one round of cell division, causing fur greying; differentiation was associated with persistent DDR activation and enhanced in Atm-knockout mice, without detection of p16 or SA-β-gal.

quotes.quote:
exposure of mice to ionizing radiation leads to fur greying, which is due to damage-
induced differentiation of hair bulb melanocyte stem cells after one round of cell division124. 
Although some markers of cellular senescence, such as p16 and SA-β-gal activity, were not 
detected, differentiation of melanocyte stem cells was associated with persistent DDR 
activation and was enhanced in Atm-knockout mice124.

experiment.system: mouse hair bulb melanocyte stem cells (wild-type and Atm-knockout)
experiment.perturbation: ionizing radiation exposure
experiment.measurement: fur greying, differentiation markers, DDR foci, p16 and SA-β-gal

text: Ionizing radiation-induced DNA damage in mouse neural stem cells promotes loss of stemness gene expression and astrocytic differentiation controlled by ATM and BMP2 signalling, confirmed by lineage tracing in the subventricular zone of irradiated mice.

quotes.quote:
DNA damage, for example induced by ionizing radiation, has been shown to promote 
differentiation and induce cellular senescence in mouse neural stem cells128. DNA damage 
led to a loss of expression of stemness genes and a general induction of a transcriptional 
profile indicative of differentiation into astrocytes. This cell differentiation programme was 
controlled by ATM and by soluble factors, in particular through BMP2 signalling128. 
Lineage tracing experiments in vivo in irradiated mice confirmed the induction of expression 
of differentiation markers in the subventricular zone of the brain

experiment.system: mouse neural stem cells in vitro and in irradiated mice
experiment.perturbation: ionizing radiation; ATM and BMP2 signalling manipulation
experiment.measurement: stemness/differentiation transcriptional profiles and lineage tracing

text: Ageing mouse neurons accumulate DDR, heterochromatin and SASP markers including IL-6 secretion and SA-β-gal; a short period of dietary restriction prevented their accumulation, phenotypes were exacerbated in telomerase-inactivated mice, and p21 loss reduced many markers.

quotes.quote:
Markers of DDR signalling, heterochromatin induction 
and activation of SASP, including the secretion of IL-6 and accumulation of SA-β-gal, were 
all detected in different types of neurons in ageing mice, and a short period of dietary 
restriction prevented their accumulation134. Such phenotypes were exacerbated in 
telomerase-inactivated mice, while p21 loss reduced many of these markers.

experiment.system: postmitotic neurons in ageing mice, telomerase-inactivated mice and p21-null mice
experiment.perturbation: ageing, dietary restriction, telomerase inactivation, p21 loss
experiment.measurement: DDR, heterochromatin, IL-6 secretion and SA-β-gal markers

text: In old mice, osteocytes show telomeric dysfunction markers and accumulate p16, and SASP activation in osteocytes promotes osteoclast activity impairing bone strength; senolytic drugs reduced bone loss.

quotes.quote:
In old mice, osteocytes show markers of 
telomeric dysfunction and accumulate p16. SASP activation in osteocytes was shown to 
promote osteoclast activity, thus impairing bone strength. In this context, senolytic drugs 
reduced bone loss139.

experiment.system: osteocytes in old mice
experiment.perturbation: ageing; senolytic drug treatment
experiment.measurement: telomere dysfunction markers, p16, osteoclast activity, bone loss

text: Persistent telomeric DNA damage in cardiomyocytes drives senescence with p16 and p21 induction and a non-canonical SASP contributing to cardiac hypertrophy and fibrosis; genetic and pharmacological clearance of p16-expressing senescent cells ameliorated heart function in aged mice.

quotes.quote:
persistent telomeric DNA damage in cardiomyocytes drives a senescence 
phenotype characterized by induction of p16 and p21 and a non-canonical SASP programme 
that contributes to cardiac hypertrophy and fibrosis140. Indeed, genetic and pharmacological 
clearance of p16-expressing senescent cells ameliorated heart functions in aged mice140.

experiment.system: aged mouse cardiomyocytes/heart
experiment.perturbation: genetic and pharmacological clearance of p16-expressing cells
experiment.measurement: senescence markers, cardiac hypertrophy/fibrosis and heart function

text: In liver fibrosis, senescence limits proliferation of ECM-producing activated hepatic stellate cells and SASP from these cells attracts NK cells that eliminate them, restoring liver homeostasis.

quotes.quote:
in liver fibrosis, a condition associated with scarring 
of the liver and decrease in its function, senescence limits the proliferation and expansion of 
ECM-producing activated hepatic stellate cells145,146. This response limits the progression 
of the pathology following liver damage. SASP from these cells attracts natural killer (NK) 
cells that eliminate senescent cells from the liver to restore liver homeostasis145.

experiment.system: mouse liver fibrosis model with activated hepatic stellate cells
experiment.perturbation: liver damage-induced fibrosis; senescence programme
experiment.measurement: stellate cell proliferation, NK cell recruitment, fibrosis resolution

text: In zebrafish, senescence impairment prevents fin regeneration following amputation.

quotes.quote:
In zebrafish, senescence 
impairment prevents fin regeneration following amputation149

experiment.system: zebrafish fin
experiment.perturbation: amputation with impairment of senescence
experiment.measurement: regeneration outcome

text: Transplantation of relatively few senescent cells caused tissue dysfunction and shortened lifespan in mice, demonstrating that cellular senescence is causative for frailty and age-associated diseases.

quotes.quote:
That cellular 
senescence is causative for frailty and age-associated diseases was demonstrated by 
transplantation of relatively few senescent cells and observation of tissue dysfunction and 
shortened lifespan in mice174.

experiment.system: mice
experiment.perturbation: transplantation of senescent cells
experiment.measurement: tissue/physical dysfunction and lifespan

text: Atherosclerotic plaques from LDL receptor-null mice accumulate SA-β-Gal and p16-positive endothelial cells, vascular smooth muscle cells and macrophages; removal of p16-positive cells in p16-3MR and INK-ATTAC mice genetically or with senolytics reduced plaque formation and progression while dampening the SASP.

quotes.quote:
atherosclerotic plaques from LDL receptor-null mice were found to accumulate 
high amounts of SA-β-Gal and p16-positive endothelial cells, vascular smooth muscle cells 
and macrophages. Removal of p16-positive cells in both p16-3MR and INK-ATTAC 
transgenic mice by both genetic methods and senolytics reduced plaque formation and 
progression, while dampening the SASP175.

experiment.system: LDL receptor-null atherosclerosis-prone mice carrying p16-3MR or INK-ATTAC
experiment.perturbation: genetic or senolytic removal of p16-positive cells
experiment.measurement: plaque formation/progression and SASP

text: Cellular senescence is a cell-autonomous barrier to OSKM reprogramming in vitro, whereas in vivo OSKM expression induces senescence and SASP that promotes reprogramming in a paracrine manner, with IL-6 crucial for iPS cell generation.

quotes.quote:
In vitro studies demonstrated that cellular 
senescence is a potent cell-autonomous barrier for transcription factor-mediated 
reprograming using OCT4, SOX2, KLF4 and MYC (commonly referred to as OSKM)

Senescence induction is necessary for efficient cell reprograming, as SASP 
factor production promotes reprogramming into induced pluripotent stem cells in a paracrine 
manner184. IL-6 produced in the SASP appears to be crucial for the generation of induced 
pluripotent stem cells in this context.

experiment.system: cells in vitro and mouse tissues in vivo
experiment.perturbation: OSKM expression and tissue damage
experiment.measurement: reprogramming efficiency, senescence and SASP factors

text: The SASP component interferon-γ induces cellular senescence and tissue ageing in mice with shortened telomeres, and abrogation of interferon-γ signalling rescues ageing-related phenotypes and extends lifespan.

quotes.quote:
the SASP component interferon-γ induces cellular 
senescence and tissue ageing in mice with shortened telomeres, and abrogation of interferon-
γ signalling rescues ageing-related phenotypes and extends lifespan187.

experiment.system: mice with shortened telomeres
experiment.perturbation: abrogation of interferon-γ signalling
experiment.measurement: senescence, ageing phenotypes and lifespan

text: Short-term exposure to the SASP promoted expression of stem cell markers and increased regenerative capacity of mouse keratinocytes and skeletal muscle in vivo, whereas prolonged exposure resulted in paracrine-induced senescence.

quotes.quote:
short-term exposure to 
the SASP promoted expression of stem cell markers and increased the regenerative capacity 
of mouse keratinocytes189 and of skeletal muscle190 in vivo. However, prolonged exposure 
to the SASP resulted in paracrine-induced senescence

experiment.system: mouse keratinocytes and skeletal muscle in vivo
experiment.perturbation: short-term versus prolonged SASP exposure
experiment.measurement: stem cell marker expression, regenerative capacity and paracrine senescence

text: Mice expressing ~10% of normal BubR1 levels develop progeroid features including shortened lifespan, cataracts, lordokyphosis, lipodystrophy and infertility very early in life, with high p16 in adipose tissue, skeletal muscle and eyes.

quotes.quote:
Mice expressing ~10% of normal BubR1 levels 
develop a variety of progeroid features, including shortened lifespan, cataracts, 
lordokyphosis, lipodystrophy and infertility very early in life191. Adipose tissue, skeletal 
muscle and the eyes of BubR1 hypomorphic mice express high levels of p16 and other 
senescence-associated features192.

experiment.system: BubR1 hypomorphic mice
experiment.perturbation: genetic reduction of BubR1 expression
experiment.measurement: progeroid phenotypes and senescence markers

text: In BubR1-mutant mice, p16 knockout attenuated age-related deterioration of adipose tissue, skeletal muscle and eye, whereas genetically preventing p19ARF accumulation did not.

quotes.quote:
In the absence of p16, the age-
related deterioration of adipose tissue, skeletal muscle and eye was attenuated193. 
Importantly, genetically preventing the accumulation of p19ARF, a tumour suppressor that 
modulates the stability of p53 by influencing MDM2-mediated destruction, did not result in 
similar prevention193

experiment.system: BubR1 hypomorphic mice crossed to Cdkn2a p16-knockout or p19ARF-deficient mice
experiment.perturbation: genetic deletion of p16 or p19ARF
experiment.measurement: age-related tissue deterioration

text: Removing p16-expressing cells from weaning age in BubR1 hypomorphic INK-ATTAC mice attenuated senescent cell accumulation and premature ageing in skeletal muscle, eye and adipose tissue; in naturally aged INK-ATTAC mice clearance increased median lifespan of male and female mice in different genetic backgrounds and increased healthspan (reduced kidney scarring, cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, cardiac stress intolerance, cataractogenesis and lipodystrophy).

quotes.quote:
treatment of BubR1 hypomorphic mice harbouring the INK-ATTAC transgene to remove 
p16-expressing cells beginning at weaning age attenuated the accumulation of senescent 
cells and premature ageing in skeletal muscle, eye and adipose tissue11. A second study 
using the INK-ATTAC system in naturally aged mice corroborated these findings194 and 
increased median lifespan of both male and female mice in different genetic backgrounds 
and increased healthspan, as indicated by reduced kidney scarring, cardiomyocyte 
hypertrophy, cardiac stress intolerance, cataractogenesis and lipodystrophy194.

experiment.system: INK-ATTAC transgenic mice (BubR1 hypomorphic and naturally aged)
experiment.perturbation: drug-induced elimination of p16-expressing senescent cells
experiment.measurement: senescent cell burden, ageing phenotypes, median lifespan and healthspan measures

text: Administration of dasatinib and quercetin reduced expression of p16 and SA-β-gal in phase I clinical trials in patients with diabetic kidney disease and idiopathic pulmonary disease.

quotes.quote:
the administration of dasatinib and quercetin has shown 
effectiveness in reducing the expression of p16 and SA-β-gal in a phase I clinical trial 
among patients with diabetic kidney disease211 and idiopathic pulmonary disease212.

experiment.system: patients with diabetic kidney disease and idiopathic pulmonary disease
experiment.perturbation: dasatinib and quercetin administration in phase I clinical trial
experiment.measurement: p16 and SA-β-gal expression

text: Nanoparticles coated with galacto-oligosaccharides preferentially deliver cytotoxic cargo to senescent cells because of their higher SA-β-gal activity.

quotes.quote:
Nanoparticles containing either fluorophores or cytotoxic agents coated with 
galacto-oligosaccharides were found to preferentially deliver cytotoxic cargo to senescent 
cells because of the higher level of SA-β-gal activity in these cells218.

experiment.system: senescent versus non-senescent cells
experiment.perturbation: treatment with galacto-oligosaccharide-coated nanoparticles carrying fluorophores or cytotoxic agents
experiment.measurement: cargo delivery and killing selectivity

text: Stimulation of the innate immune response with poly(I:C) improves senescent cell clearance.

quotes.quote:
Stimulation of innate immune response with poly(I:C), a 
simulator of viral infection, improves senescent cell clearance145.

experiment.system: mouse tissue containing senescent cells
experiment.perturbation: poly(I:C) administration
experiment.measurement: senescent cell clearance

text: Senolytic CAR T cell therapy can attenuate senescence-associated diseases; unbiased screens for senescent-cell surface markers showed low overlap, each experiment identifying distinct markers.

quotes.quote:
Exciting recent work 
has demonstrated that senolytic CAR T cell therapy can attenuate senescence-associated 
diseases226. Several studies used unbiased approaches to identify such markers227–229. 
However, the overlap between the extracellular markers identified by the aforementioned 
strategies is low, when each experiment identified distinct markers

experiment.system: mouse models of senescence-associated disease; senescent cell surface proteomic screens
experiment.perturbation: CAR T cells directed at senescent cell surface antigens
experiment.measurement: disease phenotype attenuation and marker identification overlap

text: Rapamycin treatment (and its analogue RAD001) attenuated the protumorigenic SASP, prevented senescence, impaired SASP-mediated immune recognition of oncogene-expressing cells and ameliorated liver dysfunction in naturally aged mice, and rapamycin increased lifespan and delayed ageing-related dysfunctions in mice.

quotes.quote:
Treatment with rapamycin (and its analogue RAD001)232 attenuated the protumorigenic 
SASP230, prevented senescence233, impaired SASP-mediated immune recognition of 
oncogene-expressing cells and ameliorated liver dysfunction in naturally aged mice231. ... Additionally, rapamycin treatment increased lifespan and delayed certain 
ageing-related dysfunctions in mice234.

experiment.system: cells and mice, including naturally aged mice
experiment.perturbation: mTOR inhibition with rapamycin or RAD001
experiment.measurement: SASP, senescence, immune recognition, liver function, lifespan

text: Use of telomeric antisense oligonucleotides in a mouse model of Hutchinson–Gilford progeria syndrome reduced DDR activation, senescence marker levels and SASP induction, improved tissue homeostasis and extended lifespan.

quotes.quote:
The use of telomeric ASOs in a mouse model of Hutchinson–Gilford progeria syndrome (an 
accelerated ageing syndrome) effectively reduced DDR activation, the levels of senescence 
markers and SASP induction, improved tissue homeostasis and extended lifespan251.

experiment.system: mouse model of Hutchinson–Gilford progeria syndrome
experiment.perturbation: telomeric antisense oligonucleotide treatment
experiment.measurement: DDR activation, senescence markers, SASP, tissue homeostasis, lifespan

text: Caloric restriction reduces p16 levels and transcriptional expression of senescence-associated genes including SASP genes in mice and in the colon of healthy human individuals, and in mice reduced the DDR and improved telomere maintenance.

quotes.quote:
it was reported that caloric restriction reduces p16 levels and the 
transcriptional expression of genes associated with cellular senescence, including SASP 
genes, in mice and in the colon of healthy human individuals256,257. Caloric restriction in 
mice reduced the DDR and improved telomere maintenance258.

experiment.system: mice and healthy human individuals
experiment.perturbation: caloric restriction
experiment.measurement: p16 levels, senescence/SASP gene expression, DDR markers, telomere maintenance

text: Systemic delivery of the telomerase gene Tert reduces several senescence markers and ageing-related conditions and extends the lifespan of wild-type mice; in mouse models of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, AAV particles delivering Tert reduced DDR and senescence markers and improved lung function.

quotes.quote:
Systemic delivery of Tert reduces several senescence markers and ageing-related conditions 
and extends the lifespan of wild-type mice, thus demonstrating that telomeric DDR 
activation plays a role in natural ageing263.

adeno-associated virus particles delivering Tert have been 
shown to reduce DDR and the level of senescence markers and improve lung function265.

experiment.system: wild-type mice and mouse models of pulmonary fibrosis
experiment.perturbation: viral delivery of the telomerase gene Tert
experiment.measurement: senescence markers, DDR, lung function and lifespan

text: Blood exchange between young and old mice led to a significant reduction in cellular senescence and SASP marker expression in multiple aged tissues, while senescence markers increased in young animals exposed to old blood.

quotes.quote:
it was 
reported that blood exchange between young and old mice led to a significant reduction in 
cellular senescence and SASP marker expression in multiple aged tissues, while at the same 
time the levels of senescence markers were increased in the young animals exposed to old 
blood270.

experiment.system: young and old mice
experiment.perturbation: blood exchange between young and old animals
experiment.measurement: cellular senescence and SASP marker expression in tissues

text: The paper states that senescence-associated-β-galactosidase (SA-β-gal), the first and most widely used senescent-cell biomarker, is detectable by histochemical staining in most senescent cells and generally absent from presenescent, quiescent, immortal and transformed cells, although it can also accumulate in serum-starved or overconfluent cultured cells and may mark a macrophage subpopulation in vivo.

quotes.quote:
The first and still the most widely used biomarker to detect senescent cells in cultured 
cells and in fresh tissue samples is the accumulation of a lysosomal enzyme termed 
‘senescence-associated-β-galactosidase’ (SA-β-gal)275. This marker is detectable by 
histochemical staining in most senescent cells and is generally not found in presenescent, 
quiescent or immortal and transformed cells, although SA-β-gal can also accumulate in 
serum-starved or overconfluent cells in tissue culture and may mark a specific 
subpopulation of macrophages in vivo as part of a reversible response to immune 
stimuli276.

experiment.system: cultured cells and fresh tissue samples (including in vivo macrophages)
experiment.perturbation: observational comparison of senescent versus presenescent, quiescent, immortal/transformed, serum-starved or overconfluent cells
experiment.measurement: histochemical SA-β-gal staining

text: The paper reports that senescent cells show enlarged flat morphology with an increased cytoplasm-to-nucleus ratio, that increased cell size may causatively drive senescence-associated growth arrest, and that in vivo SA-β-gal-positive senescent cells have increased cell size compared with SA-β-gal-negative cells at the single-cell level.

quotes.quote:
a recent study suggests that increased cell size may play a causative role in 
driving the senescence-associated growth arrest278. In addition, in vivo, SA-β-gal-
positive senescent cells have increased cell size compared with SA-β-gal-negative cells as 
identified on a single-cell level279.

experiment.system: senescent cells in culture and in vivo tissues
experiment.perturbation: observational (comparison of SA-β-gal-positive versus SA-β-gal-negative cells)
experiment.measurement: single-cell morphology/cell size and cytoplasm-to-nucleus ratio

text: The paper states that SASP alone cannot serve as a reliable senescence biomarker because senescence triggered by p16 overexpression does not entail an altered SASP transcriptional programme.

quotes.quote:
However, SASP alone 
cannot be used as a reliable senescence biomarker: indeed, senescence triggered by p16 
overexpression does not entail an altered SASP transcriptional programme85.

experiment.system: cells rendered senescent by p16 overexpression
experiment.perturbation: p16 overexpression
experiment.measurement: SASP transcriptional programme (IL-6, IL-8 transcript and protein levels)

text: The paper reports that in oncogene-induced senescent cells LC3B associates with lamin B1 and contributes to its lysosomal degradation, that lamin-associated chromatin domains are transported to lysosomes by the same mechanism contributing to cytosolic chromatin fragments, and that inhibition of autophagy prevents lamin B1 degradation and preserves nuclear envelope integrity.

quotes.quote:
LC3B, a ubiquitin-
like autophagic protein, was found to be associated with the nuclear envelope protein 
lamin B1 and to contribute to its degradation in the lysosomes in oncogene-induced 
senescent cells59,60.

Inhibition of autophagy prevents lamin B1 degradation and ensures nuclear envelope 
integrity in senescent cells59.

experiment.system: oncogene-induced senescent cells
experiment.perturbation: inhibition of autophagy
experiment.measurement: lamin B1 degradation, nuclear envelope integrity, cytosolic chromatin fragment accumulation

text: The paper reports that in therapy-induced senescence of cancer cells autophagy is triggered to cope with accumulating toxic macromolecules and that its pharmacological targeting leads to elimination of senescent cells.

quotes.quote:
In the context of therapy-induced senescence for cancer cells, it was also shown that 
autophagy was triggered as a consequence of senescence establishment to cope with the 
increased load of accumulating toxic macromolecules, and its pharmacological targeting 
led to senescent cell elimination288.

experiment.system: cancer cells undergoing therapy-induced senescence
experiment.perturbation: pharmacological targeting of autophagy
experiment.measurement: senescent cell survival/elimination

text: The paper reports that basal autophagy in adult muscle stem cells maintains stemness by repressing senescence, that autophagic activity declines with ageing alongside regenerative capacity with accumulation of senescent satellite cells in geriatric mice, and that autophagy restoration in old satellite cells prevents senescence and rescues regenerative capacity.

quotes.quote:
In adult muscle 
stem cells, basal autophagy maintains stemness by repressing senescence. During ageing, 
the autophagic activity in muscle stem cells (satellite cells) declines alongside stem cell 
regenerative capacity, with consequent accumulation of senescent satellite cells in 
geriatric mice. autophagy restoration in old satellite cells prevents senescence and rescues 
their regenerative capacity289.

experiment.system: mouse muscle stem cells (satellite cells) from young and geriatric mice
experiment.perturbation: restoration of autophagy in old satellite cells
experiment.measurement: senescence markers and regenerative capacity

text: The paper reports that a high-throughput screen for compounds alleviating replicative senescence identified the ATM inhibitor KU-60019, which enhances autophagic flux by restoring lysosomal activity through blocking phosphorylation of the vacuolar protein ATP6V1G1, and which also recovered mitochondrial function and alleviated senescence phenotypes.

quotes.quote:
a recent high-throughput screening aimed at identifying compounds that 
alleviate replicative senescence revealed that the ataxia telangiectasia mutated (ATM) 
inhibitor KU-60019 enhances the autophagic flux by restoring functional lysosomal 
activity by blocking the phosphorylation of the vacuolar protein ATP6V1G1. ATM 
inhibitor treatment also recovered mitochondrial functions and alleviated senescence 
phenotypes274.

experiment.system: replicatively senescent cells in a chemical high-throughput screen
experiment.perturbation: treatment with the ATM inhibitor KU-60019
experiment.measurement: autophagic flux, lysosomal and mitochondrial function, ATP6V1G1 phosphorylation, senescence phenotypes

text: The paper reports that enhancing autophagic activity under excessive oxidative stress by mTOR inhibition delays cellular senescence and functionally restores both mitochondrial and lysosomal functions.

quotes.quote:
enhancing autophagic activity under excessive oxidative stress by 
mTOR inhibition delays cellular senescence and functionally restores both mitochondrial 
and lysosomal functions290.

experiment.system: cells under oxidative stress-induced senescence
experiment.perturbation: mTOR inhibition to enhance autophagy
experiment.measurement: senescence onset, mitochondrial and lysosomal function

text: The paper's compendium of senotherapeutics tabulates senolytics and senomorphics with their targets and clinical status, including dasatinib and quercetin in phase II trials for chronic kidney disease (NCT02848131) and skeletal health (NCT04313634) and phase I/II for Alzheimer disease (NCT04063124), fisetin in phase I/II for knee osteoarthritis (NCT04210986), and UBX0101 in phase II for knee osteoarthritis (NCT04129944).

quotes.quote:
Dasatinib
Pan-receptor tyrosine kinases (including ephrin B1)
Phase II, (NCT02848131) for chronic kidney disease, phase II (NCT04313634) for 
skeletal health, phase I/II (NCT04063124) for Alzheimer disease

Fisetin
PI3K/AKT/mTOR
Pphase I/II (NCT04210986) for osteoarthritis of the knee, phase II (NCT04313634) for 
skeletal health

UBX0101
MDM2 and p32
Phase II (NCT04129944) for osteoarthritis of the knee

experiment.system: senolytic and senomorphic compounds in preclinical models and human clinical trials
experiment.perturbation: observational compilation of compound targets and trial status
experiment.measurement: reported drug target and clinical trial phase/indication

text: Proteomics with a chemical probe resembling an E2–ubiquitin intermediate applied to cell lysates reacted with almost all E3s bearing a catalytic Cys, and identified MYCBP2 as a RING-domain E3 with a previously unrecognized catalytic Cys, defining the RING–Cys–relay (RCR) mechanism in which ubiquitin is relayed between two Cys and ligated to Thr.

quotes.quote:
Proteomics studies revealed that when the 
probe was applied to cell lysates, it reacted with almost 
all E3s with a catalytic Cys known to receive ubiquitin 
from an E2 (that is, HECT-family and RBR-family E3s). 
However, MYCBP2 stood out as having a RING domain, 
but lacking a recognizable E3 domain with a catalytic 
Cys.

ubiqui-
tin is transferred from the E2 Cys to one and then the 
other MYCBP2 catalytic Cys, and ubiquitin is ultimately 
ligated to Thr

experiment.system: human E3 ligase MYCBP2 in cell lysates and recombinant biochemistry
experiment.perturbation: activity-based chemical probe mimicking E2–ubiquitin; mutational analysis
experiment.measurement: mass spectrometry proteomics, crystal structures, ubiquitin discharge assays

text: Thr, rather than Lys or Ser, preferentially discharged ubiquitin from the MYCBP2 RCR domain, and an active site pocket adjacent to the second catalytic Cys loop binds and positions the Thr.

quotes.quote:
Thr, not Lys or Ser, prefer-
entially discharged ubiquitin from the RCR domain of 
MYCBP2.

an active site pocket, 
adjacent to the loop harbouring the second Cys, binds 
and positions the Thr for ubiquitylation.

experiment.system: recombinant MYCBP2 RCR domain
experiment.perturbation: offering Thr, Lys or Ser nucleophiles; mutations
experiment.measurement: ubiquitin discharge assays and crystal structures

text: Knock-in mice carrying a mutation that abolishes the MYCBP2 RCR E3 mechanism and non-Lys ubiquitylation show a striking neurodevelopmental phenotype, and their axons are protected in models of injury.

quotes.quote:
Knock-in mice 
harbouring a mutation that abolishes the RCR E3 mech-
anism and non-Lys ubiquitylation have a striking neuro­
developmental phenotype23. Furthermore, axons are 
protected in models of injury

experiment.system: knock-in mice with catalytically dead MYCBP2 RCR domain

text: The RING E3 DELTEX3L ubiquitylates ADP-ribose: in the presence of E1, E2 and the DELTEX3L–PARP9 complex the C terminus of ubiquitin was ADP-ribosylated in an NAD+-dependent reaction, DELTEX3L alone suffices, and structures show an ADPR-binding domain positioned relative to the RING domain; the modification blocks the ubiquitin C terminus but is reversible by DUBs.

molecules, although the modification can be reversed 
by deubiquitylating enzymes (DUBs)

With

for removing ubiquitin from the various amino acid

text: Legionella pneumophila SidE-family enzymes catalyse phosphoribosyl-ubiquitylation via Arg42 of ubiquitin onto substrate Ser residues without ATP or E1/E2/E3, using mART and PDE domains, and phosphoribosylated ubiquitinome analyses show these enzymes target more than 180 structurally and functionally diverse substrates.

quotes.quote:
First, ubiquitin is conjugated 
not via the highly conserved C-terminal Gly76 but via 
Arg42, which is unprecedented; second, conjugation 
is via linkage to Ser residues in the substrate instead of 
Lys residues; third, conjugation proceeds without ATP 
and E1, E2 and E3 enzymes, and instead uses only one 
bacterial enzyme that catalyses the entire ubiquityla-
tion reaction36.

Phosphoribosylated 
ubiquitinome analyses show that SidE family enzymes 
target more than 180 structurally and function-
ally diverse substrates40

experiment.system: L. pneumophila SidE-family effectors and infected host cells
experiment.perturbation: bacterial effector-mediated ubiquitylation; reconstitution without E1/E2/E3 and ATP

text: DupA and DupB act as phosphoribosyl-ubiquitin-specific DUBs through a PDE domain structurally corresponding to that of SidE; they show strong selective affinity for ubiquitin and phosphoribosyl-ubiquitylated peptides, and point mutations weakening these affinities are sufficient to convert them into SidE-type ubiquitin ligases.

quotes.quote:
Whereas the PDE domains of SidE enzymes do not 
bind to phosphoribosyl-ubiquitylated substrates and 
have moderate binding affinity for ubiquitin, DupA 
and DupB show strong and selective affinity for ubiqui-
tin and phosphoribosyl-ubiquitylated peptides. Indeed, 
point mutations weakening the affinities of DupA and 
DupB PDE domains for phosphoribosyl-ubiquitylated 
peptides are sufficient to convert them into SidE-type 
ubiquitin ligases40.

experiment.system: L. pneumophila DupA/DupB PDE domains in vitro
experiment.perturbation: point mutations weakening substrate affinity
experiment.measurement: binding affinity and switch from deubiquitylation to ligation activity

text: Bacterial deamidases convert Gln40 of NEDD8/ubiquitin to Glu40: Cif targets NEDD8 and inhibits NEDD8-dependent CRL activation without impairing NEDD8 conjugation, abolishing degradation of CRL substrates p21 and p27 and arresting cells at G2–M or G1–S; CHBP also deamidates ubiquitin Gln40, and deamidated ubiquitin cannot be transferred from E2 to acceptor Lys.

quotes.quote:
NEDD8 deamida-
tion does not impair the conjugation of NEDD8 onto cul-
lin proteins, but precludes the non-covalent interactions 
between NEDD8 and cullins

ubiquitylation and degradation of 
multiple CRL substrates, such as the cyclin-dependent 
kinase inhibitors p21 and p27, are abolished, disrupting

text: The L. pneumophila effector MavC deamidates ubiquitin Gln40 and catalyses transglutamination that covalently links Gln40 of ubiquitin to Lys92 or Lys94 of UBE2N without E1 or ATP, yielding an inactive UBE2N–ubiquitin complex that accumulates in infected cells; MvcA, which is 50% identical to MavC, hydrolyses this isopeptide bond and restores UBE2N activity.

MavC was found not only to deamidate Gln40 
but also to catalyse a transglutamination reaction that 
covalently links Gln40 of ubiquitin to Lys92 or Lys94 of

resulting atypical UBE2N–ubiquitin complex does not 
possess E2 activity and accumulates in infected cells61

MvcA, which is 50% identical 
to MavC, was found to act as a DUB that specifically 
hydrolyses the isopeptide bond between ubiquitin and

experiment.system: UBE2N with L. pneumophila effectors MavC and MvcA; infected cells
experiment.perturbation: effector-catalysed transglutamination and reverse hydrolysis

text: The lipid A moiety of bacterial LPS serves as the first site of ubiquitylation, catalysed by host E3 RNF213 and obligatory for recruitment of LUBAC, which adds Met1-linked chains that dock autophagy receptors and trigger autophagy in Salmonella enterica-infected cells; LPS ubiquitylation does not require the RNF213 RING domain but depends on other domains including a dynein-like AAA+ domain and a non-canonical zinc-finger with conserved Cys4462, and E3 activity appears allosterically regulated by ATP.

quotes.quote:
a recent study63 showed that the 
lipid A moiety of bacterial lipopolysaccharide (LPS), 
serves as the first site of ubiquitylation.

is catalysed by the host 
E3 ubiquitin ligase RING finger protein 213 (RNF213) 
and is obligatory for the recruitment of the LUBAC E3 
ligase, which adds Met1-linked ubiquitin chains onto 
the pre-existing ubiquitin moieties.

ubiquitylation of LPS diverges from this 
well-established mechanism and does not require the 
RNF213 RING domain. Instead, it depends on other 
domains, including a dynein-like AAA+ domain69

a non-canonical zinc-finger domain (containing the 
strictly conserved Cys4462) might function as the E3 
active site for LPS ubiquitylation70. Moreover, E3 activ-
ity seems to be allosterically regulated by ATP70.

verdict_note: The zinc-finger element is asserted as an established dependency, but the paper hedges: 'although the precise mechanism of ubiquitin attachment remains unclear, initial studies indicate that a non-canonical zinc-finger domain (containing the strictly conserved Cys4462) might function as the E3 active site'. Other components (lipid A as first ubiquitylation site, RNF213 catalysis, obligatory LUBAC recruitment, Met1 chains, RING-independence, AAA+ domain, ATP allostery) are faithful.

experiment.system: Salmonella enterica-infected mammalian cells and RNF213 biochemistry
experiment.perturbation: RNF213 domain mutations; bacterial infection
experiment.measurement: ubiquitylation of lipid A/LPS, LUBAC recruitment, autophagy receptor recruitment

text: Papain-like proteases of SARS-CoV and SARS-CoV-2 have divergent specificities among ubiquitin, NEDD8 and ISG15: SARS-CoV preferentially cleaves Lys48-ubiquitylated substrates whereas SARS-CoV-2 PL(pro) prefers ISG15-conjugated substrates, and SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern circulating in 2021 carried a mutation in the ubiquitin/ISG15-sensing region that enhances Lys48–ubiquitin chain cleavage relative to the original variant.

text: Cryo-EM of substrate-engaged 26S proteasome complexes, trapped by ubiquitin bound to inactivated DUB Rpn11, showed the substrate traversing from the Rpn11-bound ubiquitin through the AAA ATPase centre into the proteolytic chamber; only the proximal ubiquitin directly linked to the substrate was visualized despite long polyubiquitin chains, and ubiquitin was found to modulate rates of switching between 26S conformations, mainly affecting substrate engagement and capture.

One study generated proteasome complexes with sub-
strate polypeptide threaded into the proteolytic chamber

Although the sub-
strates used for structural studies had long polyubiqui-
tin chains, only the proximal ubiquitin directly linked 
to the substrate could be visualized.

revealed further 
intricate regulation by ubiquitin that includes impact-
ing the rates of switching between functionally distinct

to affect substrate engagement and capture

text: Structures of the Cdc48 cofactor Npl4–Ufd1 show it binds three ubiquitins in an arrangement attainable only by Lys48 linkages, and a cryo-EM structure of budding yeast Cdc48 unfolding a substrate, trapped by motor mutation or nucleotide analogues, showed a relatively proximal ubiquitin within the Lys48 chain is itself unfolded and threaded into the central pore.

text: Structures of NEDD8-modified CUL1 CRLs bound to UBE2D family members or ARIH1 show NEDD8 makes non-covalent contacts with the CUL1 domain it is linked to, is allosterically stabilized in a loop-out conformation with the Ile44 patch exposed that readers specifically recognize, and in turn facilitates CRL conformational changes; by contrast, in a NEDD8-modified CUL5 CRL bound to ARIH2, ARIH2 neither contacts nor approaches NEDD8, which instead reshapes CUL5 to create new ARIH2-binding surfaces.

text: Senescent primary cells induced by oncogenic HRasV12, DNA damage, or replication exhaustion exhibit cytoplasmic chromatin fragments (CCF) staining with DAPI, γH2AX and H3K27me3, and cGAS coalesces into puncta that colocalize with CCF in senescent cells whereas it is diffuse in proliferating cells.

Senescence of multiple primary cell types, induced by oncogenic HRasV12, DNA damage, 
or replication exhaustion, exhibits CCF that stain with DAPI, γH2AX, and H3K27me3 (Fig. 
1a and Extended Data Fig. 1a–c).
cGAS in proliferating cells displays a diffuse pattern, but coalesces into

sharp and bright puncta that colocalize with CCF in senescent cells (Fig. 1a and Extended 
Data Fig. 1c–f)

verdict_note: Claim text matches the quoted sentences verbatim; the 'MEFs expressing Flag-tagged cGAS' element of the system field is not mentioned in the excerpt (which names IMR90/BJ fibroblasts), but this does not alter the claim's substance.

experiment.system: Primary human fibroblasts (IMR90, BJ) and MEFs expressing Flag-tagged cGAS
experiment.perturbation: Senescence induction by oncogenic HRasV12, etoposide DNA damage, or replicative exhaustion
experiment.measurement: Confocal immunofluorescence for DAPI, γH2AX, H3K27me3 and cGAS localization

text: cGAS activation measured as cGAMP production was detected in cells transfected with dsDNA90 and in senescent cells triggered by various means, and STING showed activation hallmarks (homo-dimer formation, aggregate redistribution) correlating with CCF induction and IL1α expression.

STING activation correlates with induction of CCF and expression of the pro-inflammatory 
gene IL1α (Fig. 1c and Extended Data Fig. 1k).

experiment.perturbation: dsDNA90 transfection or senescence induction
experiment.measurement: cGAMP by nano-LC-MS/MS; STING dimer immunoblot under non-reducing conditions; STING immunofluorescence

Senescence associates with robust 
induction of CCF and pro-inflammatory genes, but not interferon genes (Extended Data Fig.

p38 inhibitor

Furthermore, the cultured media derived from senescence, particularly IL1α, suppress 
dsDNA90-induced interferon β (Extended Data Fig. 2g–i).

experiment.perturbation: p38 inhibitor SB203580; transfer of senescent conditioned media or recombinant IL1α followed by dsDNA90 transfection

text: Stable knockdown of cGAS or STING does not affect several senescence markers but greatly compromises activation of key SASP factors; RNA-seq GO analysis of top downregulated genes in cGAS-deficient senescent cells showed significant enrichment of the SASP program, and reduced SASP was confirmed at the secreted protein level.

While disruption of cGAS or STING does not affect 
several markers of senescence (Fig. 2c and Extended Data Fig. 3b), the activation of key 
SASP factors is greatly compromised (Fig. 2c and Extended Data Fig. 3c–d). We 
subsequently performed RNA-sequencing in control and cGAS-deficient cells undergoing 
DNA-damage-induced senescence, using two independent biological replicates. Gene 
Ontology (GO) analysis of the top downregulated genes in cGAS-deficient cells revealed 
significant enrichment of the SASP program

The role of cGAS-STING in 
mediating the SASP was confirmed at the secreted protein level in the conditioned media 
(Fig. 2f and Extended Data Fig. 3g–h).

experiment.system: IMR90 primary human fibroblasts with shRNA against cGAS or STING
experiment.perturbation: shRNA knockdown of cGAS or STING before etoposide- or Ras-induced senescence
experiment.measurement: Immunoblot of senescence/SASP markers, RT-qPCR, RNA-seq with GO analysis, cytokine array of conditioned media

senescence establishment, STING or cGAS was inactivated, which does not revert
