experiment.perturbation: shRNA knockdown of STING, cGAS, or IFI16 after senescence establishment
experiment.measurement: RT-qPCR of SASP genes

text: Overexpression of Lamin B1 has little effect on γH2AX, p-ATM S1981 and p-p53 S15 induction but significantly impairs induction of CCF, STING dimer, p65 phosphorylation and SASP gene expression, while exogenous delivery of cytoplasmic DNA or chromatin fragments induces cGAS-dependent activation of SASP genes.

text: In mice exposed to a sub-lethal 4 Gy ionizing irradiation, cGAMP and cytoplasmic chromatin are stimulated in hepatocytes; γH2AX accumulates in liver of both wild-type and Sting-null mice but IL1α induction is significantly attenuated in null mice, and three months after IR wild-type but not null mice exhibit massive hair greying.

This procedure stimulates cGAMP and cytoplasmic chromatin in hepatocytes 
(Extended Data Fig. 5a–b). While IR promotes γH2AX accumulation in the liver of both 
wild-type and the null mice, the induction of IL1α is significantly attenuated in the null 
mice (Fig. 3a and Extended Data Fig. 5c). Three months after IR, wild-type mice, but not the

For ionizing radiation, mice were 
subjected to a sub-lethal dose of 4 Gy irradiation, and were harvested 7 days post the

verdict_note: 4 Gy sub-lethal dose confirmed in Methods; all phenotypes match the quoted passage.

experiment.system: STING+/+ and STING−/− C57BL/6 mice
experiment.perturbation: Sub-lethal 4 Gy ionizing irradiation
experiment.measurement: Liver immunohistochemistry for γH2AX and IL1α, hepatocyte cGAMP by nano-LC-MS, CCF imaging, hair greying phenotype

text: After hydrodynamic delivery of NRasV12/luciferase transposon, NRasV12 but not the D38A mutant induces liver inflammation and hepatocyte cytoplasmic chromatin; Sting-null liver shows comparable senescence but attenuated inflammation, deficient SASP gene induction and immune cell marker accumulation.

text: Wild-type mice show significantly reduced numbers of NRasV12-expressing hepatocytes from day 6 to day 12 and gradual reduction of liver luciferase luminescence, whereas Sting-null mice fail to clear them and luciferase persists; eight months following injection, intrahepatic NRas-positive tumors were observed in null but not wild-type mice, and STING re-expression in null liver restored cytokine expression, inflammation and immune-mediated clearance.

quotes.quote:
While wild-type mice show 
significantly reduced numbers of NRasV12-expressing cells from day 6 to day 12, the null 
mice fail to do so (Fig. 3e).

we found that wild-type mice show gradual reduction of luciferase luminescence in the 
liver, whereas the luciferase activity persists in the null mice (Fig. 3g). Impaired clearance of 
NRasV12-hepatocytes can lead to malignancies26. Eight months following the injection, 
intrahepatic tumors positive for NRas were observed in the null mice but not in the wild-type 
mice (Fig. 3h and Extended Data Fig. 6g). The role of STING in this model was confirmed 
by re-expression of STING in the null liver, which results in restoration of cytokine 
expression, inflammation, and immune-mediated clearance (Extended Data Fig. 7a–e).

Fig. 8a), and the expression of pro-inflammatory genes, mediated by the cGAS-STING

text: Cytoplasmic chromatin is present in multiple cancer cell lines, stains positive for DAPI and γH2AX, colocalizes with cGAS, and is negatively regulated by Lamin B1; pro-inflammatory gene expression in these cells is regulated by cGAS, STING and Lamin B1, and across ten breast cancer cell lines cytoplasmic chromatin associates with pro-inflammatory gene expression.

We discovered that cytoplasmic chromatin in the investigated cancer cells stains positive for 
DAPI and γH2AX, colocalizes with cGAS, and is negatively regulated by Lamin B1 
(Extended Data Fig. 8d–f). Moreover, the expression of pro-inflammatory genes is regulated 
by cGAS, STING, and Lamin B1 (Extended Data Fig. 8g and Supplementary Table 2),

we exploited the cancer cell

of RNAs are shared by OMM and ERM, with almost 95% of shared mRNAs encoding

Our analysis (Figure 3J) reveals remarkable concordance 
between RNA and protein localization at steady state. For example, the ERM-proximal 
transcriptome preferentially codes for proteins that localize to the ER, Golgi and vesicles, 
rather than proteins that localize to the nucleus, nucleolus or cytosol.

our 
data also show that mRNAs enriched in nuclear locations tend to code for proteins enriched 
in nuclear speckles and nucleoplasm, but not the plasma membrane (Figure 3J, S3A–B).

(X-inactive specific transcript), a nuclear lncRNA, is enriched at the nuclear lamina but not 
the nearby nuclear pore (Figure 3B).

noncoding RNAs

shows intron retention within the nuclear locations, but not cytosolic ones (Figure 4A).

nucleolus-associated domains (NADs)(Dillinger et al., 2017; van Koningsbruggen et al.,

After treatment of cells with CHX, we observed a dramatic increase in the number of 
mitochondrial genes and their extent of OMM enrichment (Figure 6B, 6D)

most-CHX-enriched mitochondrial genes have higher TargetP scores on average (Figure 6E–

text: Puromycin treatment removed the vast majority of CHX-enriched mRNAs from the OMM while a subpopulation remained; PUR-enriched top genes were not higher in TargetP and were more likely to encode mitochondrial ribosome and OXPHOS components. CCCP-enriched genes resembled PUR-enriched genes.

The vast majority of CHX-enriched mRNAs were no longer observed at the OMM, 
consistent with the hypothesis that the localization of these transcripts depends on an intact 
ribosome complex (Figure 6B, S6E). Nonetheless, a subpopulation of mRNAs remained 
clearly associated with the OMM after PUR; the top OMM-localized genes were not higher 
in TargetP, in contrast to CHX-enriched genes (Figure 6F). Functional class analysis 
revealed that PUR-enriched genes have a higher likelihood of encoding mitochondrial 
ribosome and oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) components

similar to PUR-enriched genes (Figure 6F–G, 6J).

text: A random-forest classifier using 6-mer RNA features predicted OMM versus ERM localization much better for RNA-dependent (PUR-enriched) transcripts than for ribosome-dependent transcripts, while the converse held when training on the N-terminal 100 amino acid peptide sequence.

quotes.quote:
We trained a random-forest classification algorithm to predict localization of 
these two categories of transcripts to the OMM versus the ERM (which we used as 
“background”), using 6-mers as RNA features (Methods). The resulting classifier was much 
better at predicting localization of RNA-dependent transcripts relative to ribosome-
dependent ones (Figure 7B). The converse result was obtained when using the corresponding 
N-terminal 100 amino acid peptide for training (Figure 7C–D), suggesting that the peptide 
sequence is more predictive for ribosome-dependent transcripts.

experiment.perturbation: in silico classification (random forest, 10-fold cross-validation)
experiment.measurement: ROC curves / classification performance

text: Nocodazole time-course APEX-seq showed the majority of RNAs disappear rapidly from the OMM, for both mRNAs encoding mitochondrial proteins and other RNAs, with at least three response patterns; the largest cluster's half-life dissociation data could be fit by a log-normal distribution, and half-lives were obtained for 461 of the 768 transcripts in Cluster 2.

quotes.quote:
Analysis of NOC time-course data (Figure 7H–I, S7F–G, Table S6) showed that the majority 
of RNAs disappear rapidly from the OMM following NOC treatment. This decrease is 
observed for both mRNAs that encode mitochondrial proteins, and other RNAs (Figure 7J). 
Further analysis resolved at least three patterns of responses to NOC (Figure 7K–L). The 
largest cluster shows rapid loss from the OMM with half-life dissociation data that could be 
fit by a log-normal distribution (Figure 7M)

We obtained half-lives for 461 of the 768 transcripts in Cluster 2 
(Figure 7K).

experiment.measurement: time-resolved OMM APEX-seq enrichment; non-linear regression half-life fits

and the MAPK cascade exhibited a Michae-
lian response to Mos, then the system would
have a stable on state and an unstable off
state (Fig. 3, B and C). Any nonzero level of
Mos phosphorylation, added malE-Mos, or
MAPK activity would trigger the feedback
loop and drive the system to its on state.

ultrasensitive response to Mos, then the sys-
tem would have both a stable off state and a

direct comparison of MDSCs from tumour-bearing mice and

CD124. In addition, sorted CD115+ or CD124+ MDSCs from EL-4 tumour-bearing mice had
the same ability to suppress T-cell proliferation on a per cell basis as did CD115- or
CD124-MDSCs.

experiment.system: EL-4 tumour-bearing mice and naive mice
experiment.perturbation: cell sorting by CD115/CD124 expression
experiment.measurement: surface marker expression and per-cell T-cell proliferation suppression

text: In many mouse tumour models 20–40% of nucleated splenocytes are MDSCs, versus 2-4% in normal mice, and up to a tenfold increase in MDSC numbers was detected in the blood of patients with different cancers.

quotes.quote:
In addition, up to a tenfold increase in MDSC
numbers was detected in the blood of patients with different types of cancer11, 12, 21, 22. In
many mouse tumour models, as many as 20–40% of nucleated splenocytes are represented by
MDSCs (in contrast to the 2-4% seen in normal mice).

experiment.system: tumour-bearing mice and cancer patients
experiment.perturbation: tumour inoculation or spontaneous tumour development; observational in patients
experiment.measurement: MDSC frequency in spleen and blood

numbers.quantity: MDSC fraction of nucleated splenocytes in tumour models
increase in blood MDSC in cancer patients

text: MDSCs from tumour-bearing mice have markedly increased phosphorylated STAT3 versus IMCs from naive mice; STAT3 inhibition in haematopoietic progenitors abrogated tumour-derived-factor-driven MDSC expansion, and STAT3 ablation or selective inhibitors reduced MDSC expansion and increased T-cell responses in tumour-bearing mice.

quotes.quote:
MDSCs from tumour-bearing mice have markedly increased levels
of phosphorylated STAT3 compared with IMCs from naive mice45. Exposure of
haematopoietic progenitor cells to tumour-cell-conditioned medium resulted in the activation
of JAK2 and STAT3 and was associated with an expansion of MDSCs in vitro, whereas
inhibition of STAT3 expression in haematopoietic progenitor cells abrogated the effect of
tumour-derived factors on MDSC expansion46. Ablation of STAT3 expression in conditional
knockout mice or selective STAT3 inhibitors markedly reduced the expansion of MDSCs and
increased T-cell responses in tumour-bearing mice

experiment.system: tumour-bearing mice, conditional STAT3 knockout mice, haematopoietic progenitor cells
experiment.perturbation: tumour-conditioned medium exposure; STAT3 ablation or selective inhibition
experiment.measurement: phospho-STAT3 levels, MDSC expansion, T-cell responses

text: STAT3-dependent upregulation of S100A8/S100A9 prevented myeloid progenitor differentiation and expanded MDSCs in spleens of tumour-bearing and naive S100A9-transgenic mice, whereas S100A9-deficient mice showed no MDSC expansion after tumour or CFA challenge; blocking S100A8/A9 binding with a carboxylated glycan-specific antibody reduced MDSC levels in blood and secondary lymphoid organs.

quotes.quote:
STAT3-dependent upregulation of S100A8 and S100A9 expression by
myeloid progenitor cells prevented their differentiation and resulted in the expansion of
MDSCs in the spleens of tumor-bearing and naive S100A9-transgenic mice. By contrast,
MDSCs did not expand in the peripheral blood and spleens of mice deficient for S100A9
following challenge with tumour cells or CFA49.

Blocking the
binding of S100A8 and S100A9 to their receptors on MDSCs in vivo with a carboxylated
glycan-specific antibody reduced MDSC levels in the blood and secondary lymphoid organs
of tumour-bearing mice

experiment.system: S100A9-transgenic and S100A9-deficient mice; tumour-bearing mice
experiment.perturbation: tumour or CFA challenge; carboxylated glycan-specific antibody blockade
experiment.measurement: MDSC numbers in blood, spleen and secondary lymphoid organs

text: MDSCs from Stat1-/- mice failed to upregulate ARG1 and iNOS expression and did not inhibit T-cell responses, and blockade of IFNγ abolishes MDSC-mediated T-cell suppression.

quotes.quote:
Blockade of IFNγ, which is produced by activated T cells, abolishes MDSC-mediated T-cell
suppression17, 52.

MDSCs from
Stat1-/- mice failed to up regulate ARG1 and iNOS expression and therefore did not inhibit T-
cell responses

experiment.system: MDSCs from Stat1-/- mice and wild-type mice
experiment.perturbation: STAT1 gene deletion; IFNγ blockade
experiment.measurement: ARG1/iNOS expression and T-cell suppression assays

text: In polymicrobial sepsis induced by caecal ligation and puncture, splenic MDSC expansion was MyD88-dependent, while TLR4-deficient and wild-type mice showed comparable expansion.

quotes.quote:
was shown to result in an expansion of the MDSC
population in the spleen that was dependent on the TLR adaptor molecule myeloid
differentiation primary-response gene 88 (MyD88)26. However, wild-type mice and mice
lacking a functional TLR4 protein had comparable expansion of the MDSC during
polymicrobial sepsis

experiment.system: mice with polymicrobial sepsis (caecal ligation and puncture); MyD88- and TLR4-deficient mice
experiment.perturbation: caecal ligation and puncture; genetic deficiency of MyD88 or TLR4
experiment.measurement: splenic MDSC population expansion

text: Inhibition of ROS production by MDSCs isolated from mice and cancer patients completely abrogated their suppressive effect in vitro, and ligation of MDSC integrins contributed to increased ROS production upon MDSC–T-cell interaction.

quotes.quote:
Inhibition of ROS production
by MDSCs isolated from mice and patients with cancer completely abrogated the suppressive
effect of these cells in vitro10, 13, 67. Interestingly, ligation of integrins expressed on the surface
of MDSCs was shown to contribute to increased ROS production following the interaction of
MDSCs with T cells

experiment.system: MDSCs isolated from tumour-bearing mice and cancer patients
experiment.perturbation: pharmacological inhibition of ROS production; integrin ligation
experiment.measurement: in vitro T-cell suppression and ROS production

text: Granulocytic MDSCs expressed high ROS and low NO whereas monocytic MDSCs expressed low ROS and high NO, both expressed ARG1, and both suppressed antigen-specific T-cell proliferation to an equal extent.

quotes.quote:
The granulocytic subset of MDSC was found to express high levels
of ROS and low levels of NO, whereas the monocytic subset expressed low levels of ROS and
high levels of NO and both subsets expressed ARG16

suppressed antigen-specific T-cell proliferation to an equal extent, despite their different
mechanisms of action.

experiment.system: MDSC subsets from tumour-bearing mice
experiment.perturbation: subset sorting (granulocytic vs monocytic)
experiment.measurement: ROS, NO, ARG1 expression and antigen-specific T-cell proliferation suppression

text: Movahedi et al. reported two distinct MDSC subsets in tumour-bearing mice that both suppressed antigen-specific T-cell responses but by distinct mechanisms: ARG1-dependent for the granulocytic subset versus STAT1- and iNOS-dependent for the monocyte fraction.

quotes.quote:
The suppressive activity of the granulocytic subset was ARG1-dependent, in
contrast to the STAT1- and iNOS-dependent mechanism of the monocyte fraction17.

experiment.system: tumour-bearing mice
experiment.perturbation: isolation of mononuclear and polymorphonuclear MDSC subsets
experiment.measurement: antigen-specific T-cell suppression and dependence on ARG1/STAT1/iNOS

text: In Trypanosoma cruzi infection monocytic MDSCs produced NO and strongly inhibited T-cell proliferation, while granulocytic MDSCs produced low NO and did not inhibit proliferation although they produced superoxide.

quotes.quote:
In this case, monocytic MDSCs
produced NO and strongly inhibited T-cell proliferation, and granulocytic MDSCs produced
low levels of NO and did not inhibit T-cell proliferation, although they did produce
superoxide15.

experiment.system: mice infected with Trypanosoma cruzi
experiment.perturbation: infection; separation of MDSC subsets
experiment.measurement: NO and superoxide production and T-cell proliferation inhibition

text: Peroxynitrite produced by MDSCs during direct contact with T cells nitrates the TCR and CD8 molecules, altering peptide binding and rendering T cells unresponsive to antigen-specific stimulation while retaining responsiveness to nonspecific stimuli; this was also observed in vivo in tumour-bearing mice.

quotes.quote:
we have demonstrated that peroxynitrite production by MDSCs during direct contact
with T cells results in nitration of the T-cell receptor (TCR) and CD8 molecules, which alters
the specific peptide binding of the T cells and renders them unresponsive to antigen-specific
stimulation. However, the T cells maintained their responsiveness to nonspecific stimuli80.
This phenomenon of MDSC induced antigen-specific T-cell unresponsiveness was also
observed in vivo in tumour-bearing mice53.

experiment.system: MDSC–T-cell co-cultures and tumour-bearing mice
experiment.perturbation: direct MDSC–T-cell contact / MDSC-derived peroxynitrite
experiment.measurement: TCR/CD8 nitration, peptide binding, antigen-specific vs nonspecific T-cell responsiveness

text: In human prostate adenocarcinomas infiltrated by unresponsive terminally-differentiated CD8+ T cells bearing high nitrotyrosine, inhibiting arginase and iNOS activity decreased tyrosine nitration and restored T-cell responsiveness to tumour antigens.

quotes.quote:
Inhibiting the activity of arginase and iNOS, which are expressed in malignant
but not in normal prostate tissue and are key enzymes of L-arginine metabolism,, led to
decreased tyrosine nitration and restoration of T-cell responsiveness to tumour antigens79.

experiment.system: human prostate adenocarcinoma tissue and infiltrating CD8+ T cells
experiment.perturbation: pharmacological inhibition of arginase and iNOS
experiment.measurement: tyrosine nitration levels and T-cell responsiveness to tumour antigens

text: Blockade of MDSC–T-cell interactions with an MHC-class-I-specific antibody abrogated MDSC-mediated inhibition of T-cell responses in vitro, and MHC-class-I-restricted MDSC-mediated CD8+ T-cell suppression was also shown in vivo in tumour models and in an inflammatory bowel disease model.

quotes.quote:
blockade of MDSC–T-cell
interactions with a MHC-class-I-specific antibody abrogated MDSC-mediated inhibition of T-

cell responses in vitro86. The MHC-class-I-restricted nature of MDSC-mediated CD8+ T-cell
suppression has also been demonstrated in vivo in tumor models53 and in the model of
inflammatory bowel disease

experiment.system: MDSC–T-cell co-cultures; tumour models and inflammatory bowel disease model in vivo
experiment.perturbation: MHC-class-I-specific blocking antibody
experiment.measurement: CD8+ T-cell response suppression

text: MDSCs migrating into the tumour site upregulate ARG1 and iNOS, downregulate ROS and/or differentiate into TAMs, with NO and arginase levels much higher than in MDSCs of peripheral lymphoid organs of the same animals.

quotes.quote:
MDSCs actively migrate into the tumour
site10, where they upregulate the expression of ARG1 and iNOS, downregulate the production
of ROS and/or rapidly differentiate into tumour-associated macrophages (TAMs) 52. The levels
of NO and arginase produced by tumour-associated MDSCs and TAMs are much higher than
those of MDSCs found in peripheral lymphoid organs of the same animals.

experiment.system: tumour-bearing mice
experiment.perturbation: observational comparison of tumour site vs peripheral lymphoid organs
experiment.measurement: ARG1/iNOS expression, NO and arginase levels, ROS production

text: Vitamin A-deficient mice or mice treated with a pan-retinoic-acid-receptor antagonist show MDSC expansion in bone marrow and spleen, whereas therapeutic ATRA substantially decreases MDSCs in cancer patients and tumour-bearing mice and induces their differentiation into DCs and macrophages, via upregulated glutathione synthesis and reduced ROS.

quotes.quote:
Mice that are
deficient in vitamin A94 or that have been treated with a pan-retinoic-acid-receptor
antagonist95, show an expansion of MDSCs in the bone marrow and spleen. Conversely,
therapeutic concentrations of all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA) results in substantial decrease in
the presence of MDSCs in cancer patients and tumour-bearing mice. ATRA induced MDSCs
to differentiate into DCs and macrophages in vitro and in vivo

The main mechanism of ATRA-mediated
differentiation involved an upregulation of glutathione synthesis and a reduction in ROS levels
in MDSCs

experiment.system: vitamin A-deficient mice, tumour-bearing mice, cancer patients
experiment.perturbation: vitamin A deficiency, pan-RAR antagonist, or ATRA treatment
experiment.measurement: MDSC numbers, differentiation into DCs/macrophages, glutathione and ROS levels

text: Combining ATRA with two different types of cancer vaccine prolonged the anti-tumour vaccine effect in two different tumour models, and ATRA administration to patients with metastatic renal cell carcinoma substantially decreased peripheral blood MDSC numbers and improved antigen-specific T-cell responses.

quotes.quote:
the combination of ATRA and two different types of
cancer vaccine prolonged the anti-tumour effect of the vaccine treatment in two different
tumour models 96. Moreover, administration of ATRA to patients with metastatic renal cell
carcinoma resulted in a substantial decrease in the number of MDSCs in the peripheral blood
and improved antigen-specific response of T cells

experiment.system: tumour-bearing mice; patients with metastatic renal cell carcinoma
experiment.perturbation: ATRA alone or combined with cancer vaccines
experiment.measurement: anti-tumour effect duration, blood MDSC numbers, antigen-specific T-cell responses

numbers.quantity: cancer vaccine types combined with ATRA

text: In a clinical trial of 15 patients with refractory solid tumours, VEGF–trap treatment showed no effect on MDSC numbers and did not increase T-cell responses, whereas VEGF-specific antibody (avastin) treatment of metastatic renal cell cancer patients decreased the CD11b+VEGFR1+ MDSC population in peripheral blood.

quotes.quote:
in a clinical trial of 15 patients with refractory solid
tumours, treatment with VEGF–trap (a fusion protein that binds all forms of VEGF-A and
placental growth factor) showed no effect on MDSC numbers and did not result in increased
T-cell responses99. By contrast, treatment of patients with metastatic renal cell cancer with a
VEGF-specific blocking antibody (known as avastin) resulted in a decrease in the size of a
CD11b+VEGFR1+ population of MDSCs in the peripheral blood

experiment.system: patients with refractory solid tumours and metastatic renal cell cancer
experiment.perturbation: VEGF–trap or VEGF-specific antibody (avastin) treatment
experiment.measurement: blood MDSC numbers and T-cell responses

text: Blocking SCF interaction with c-kit decreased MDSC expansion and tumour angiogenesis in tumour-bearing mice, and MMP-9 inhibition decreased MDSC numbers in spleen and tumour tissue with significant delay of spontaneous NeuT tumour growth in transgenic BALB/c mice.

quotes.quote:
Inhibition of SCF-mediated signalling by blocking its interaction with its
receptor, c-kit, decreased MDSC expansion and tumor angiogenesis39.

inhibition of matrix metalloproteinase 9 function in tumor-
bearing mice decreased the number of MDSCs in the spleen and tumour tissues and resulted
in a significant delay in the growth of spontaneous NeuT tumours in transgenic BALB/c
mice101.

experiment.system: tumour-bearing mice; NeuT transgenic BALB/c mice
experiment.perturbation: SCF/c-kit blockade; MMP-9 inhibition
experiment.measurement: MDSC numbers, tumour angiogenesis, tumour growth

text: COX2 inhibitors downregulated MDSC ARG1 expression and improved antitumour T-cell responses and immunotherapy efficacy, and phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors such as sildenafil downregulated arginase and iNOS expression by MDSCs, inducing anti-tumour immune responses and marked delay of tumour progression in several mouse models.

quotes.quote:
COX2 inhibitors were found to downregulate the expression of ARG1
by MDSCs, which improved antitumour T-cell responses and enhanced the therapeutic efficacy
of immunotherapy102, 103. Similarly, phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors such as sildenafil were
found to downregulate the expression of arginase and iNOS expression by MDSCs, thereby
inhibiting their suppressive function in growing tumours104. This resulted in the induction of
a measurable anti-tumour immune response and a marked delay of tumour progression in
several mouse models

experiment.system: tumour-bearing mice
experiment.perturbation: COX2 inhibitors or phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors (sildenafil)
experiment.measurement: MDSC ARG1/iNOS expression, antitumour T-cell responses, tumour progression

text: Nitroaspirin limited ARG1 and iNOS activity in spleen MDSCs and, combined with endogenous retroviral gp70 antigen vaccination, inhibited MDSC function and increased the number and function of tumour-antigen-specific T cells.

quotes.quote:
One such drug, nitroaspirin, was found to limit the activity of ARG1
and iNOS in spleen MDSCs105. In combination with vaccination with endogenous retroviral
gp70 antigen, nitroaspirin inhibited MDSCs function and increased the number and function
of tumour-antigen-specific T cells105.

experiment.system: tumour-bearing mice
experiment.perturbation: nitroaspirin treatment alone or with gp70 antigen vaccination
experiment.measurement: splenic MDSC ARG1/iNOS activity and tumour-antigen-specific T-cell number and function

text: Gemcitabine administration to mice bearing large tumours dramatically reduced splenic MDSC numbers without significantly decreasing T or B cells and improved immunotherapy-induced anti-tumour responses; in 17 patients with early-stage breast cancer treated with doxorubicin–cyclophosphamide, peripheral blood MDSC levels decreased.

quotes.quote:
Administration of one such drug, gemcitabine, to mice
that were bearing large tumours resulted in a dramatic reduction in the number of MDSCs in
the spleen and resulted in a marked improvement in the anti-tumour response induced by
immunotherapy106, 107. This effect was specific to MDSCs, as a significant decrease in the
number of T or B cells was not observed in these animals. Furthermore, in a study of 17 patients
with early-stage breast cancer that were treated with doxorubicin–cyclophosphamide
chemotherapy, a decrease in the level of MDSCs in the peripheral blood was observed22.

experiment.system: tumour-bearing mice; patients with early-stage breast cancer
experiment.perturbation: gemcitabine treatment; doxorubicin–cyclophosphamide chemotherapy
experiment.measurement: MDSC, T- and B-cell numbers and anti-tumour response

text: In healthy individuals, immature myeloid cells with the described MDSC phenotype comprise ∼0.5% of peripheral blood mononuclear cells.

quotes.quote:
In healthy individuals, immature myeloid cells
with described above phenotype comprise ∼0.5% of peripheral blood mononuclear cells.

experiment.system: peripheral blood of healthy human individuals
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: frequency of phenotypically defined immature myeloid cells among PBMCs

numbers.quantity: immature myeloid cells among PBMCs in healthy individuals

text: MDSC-mediated induction of FOXP3+ TReg cells required activation of tumour-specific T cells plus IFNγ and IL-10 but was independent of NO; in 1D8 ovarian tumour-bearing mice it required MDSC expression of CTLA-4, and in a lymphoma model required arginase and antigen capture/presentation but not TGFβ, whereas other studies found MDSCs had little or no role in TReg expansion.

quotes.quote:
The
induction of TReg cells by MDSCs was found to require the activation of tumour-specific T-
cells and the presence of IFNγ and IL-10 but was independent of NO19. In mice bearing 1D8
ovarian tumours, the induction of TReg cells by MDSCs required the expression of cytotoxic
lymphocyte antigen 4 (CTLA-4; also known as CD152) by MDSCs18. In a mouse model of
lymphoma, MDSCs were shown to induce TReg-cell expansion through a mechanism that
required arginase and the capture, processing and presentation of tumour-associated antigens
by MDSCs, but not TGFβ58.

Movahedi et al. found that the percentage of TReg
cells was invariably high throughout tumour growth and did not relate to the kinetics of
expansion of the MDSC population, suggesting that MDSCs were not involved in TReg-cell
expansion17.

experiment.system: tumour-bearing mice (1D8 ovarian tumour, lymphoma models) and rat kidney allograft model
experiment.perturbation: blockade/deficiency of IFNγ, IL-10, NO, CTLA-4, arginase or TGFβ
experiment.measurement: de novo FOXP3+ TReg cell induction/expansion

text: Trials of Brodalumab (anti-IL-17RA) and Secukinumab (anti-IL-17A) in Crohn's disease were terminated for lack of efficacy and/or disease exacerbation; no anti-IL-17RA group improved Crohn's Disease Activity Index versus placebo, and fungal infections occurred in 9% of Secukinumab patients versus 0% on placebo.

quotes.quote:
Unexpectedly, trials of 
Brodalumab (anti-IL-17RA) and Secukinumab (anti-IL-17A) for Crohn’s Disease were 
terminated due to lack of efficacy and/or disease exacerbation161, 162. None of the anti-
IL-17RA treatment groups showed improvement in Crohn’s Disease Activity Index 
response compared to placebo.

A higher frequency of fungal infections was 
observed in patients on Secukinumab (9%) compared with placebo (0%)

experiment.system: patients with moderate-to-severe Crohn's disease
experiment.perturbation: anti-IL-17RA (Brodalumab) or anti-IL-17A (Secukinumab) versus placebo
experiment.measurement: Crohn's Disease Activity Index response and frequency of fungal infections

text: Post hoc analysis of the anti-IL-17A Crohn's trial found that the subgroup of treated patients with disease exacerbation had elevated inflammatory markers including CRP and fecal calprotectin, which are known targets of IL-23 and IL-22.

quotes.quote:
post hoc analysis revealed that the subgroup of anti-
IL-17A-treated patients with disease exacerbation had elevated inflammatory markers 
including CRP and fecal calprotectin (Reg3g), which are known targets of IL-23 and IL-22.

experiment.system: Crohn's disease patients treated with anti-IL-17A
experiment.perturbation: anti-IL-17A antibody treatment (post hoc subgroup analysis)
experiment.measurement: levels of CRP and fecal calprotectin

text: Ustekinumab (anti-p40) testing in moderate to severe Crohn's disease showed that patients with elevated CRP, colonic inflammation, and primary anti-TNF failures had better overall treatment response rates.

quotes.quote:
Ustekinumab, which targets the p40 unit of both IL-12 and IL-23, was tested in 
patients with moderate to severe Crohn’s disease160. The study showed that patients with 
elevated C reactive protein (CRP), colonic inflammation, and primaly anti-TNF ‘failures’ 
had better overall treatment response rates.

experiment.system: patients with moderate to severe Crohn's disease
experiment.perturbation: ustekinumab (anti-p40 of IL-12/IL-23)
experiment.measurement: treatment response rates stratified by CRP, colonic inflammation and prior anti-TNF failure

text: Restricting IL-23R deficiency to T cells arrested Th17 cells at an early activation stage and rendered them unable to mediate encephalitogenicity in EAE; IL-23R is also needed for GM-CSF co-expression, and GM-CSF-deficient mice are resistant to EAE while GM-CSF-deficient Th17 cells cannot transfer EAE.

quotes.quote:
By using an approach that restricts IL-23R deficiency to T cells, we have shown that without 
IL-23 signaling, Th17 cells are arrested at an early activation stage and are unable to 
mediate encephalitogenicity in EAE 48. Subsequent studies revealed that IL-23R is needed 
for co-expression of GM-CSF; accordingly, GM-CSF-deficient mice are resistant to EAE 
and GM-CSF-deficient TH17 cells cannot transfer EAE to naive recipients

experiment.system: mice with T cell-restricted IL-23R deficiency and GM-CSF-deficient mice/T cells
experiment.perturbation: genetic deletion of IL-23R in T cells; GM-CSF deficiency; adoptive transfer into naive recipients
experiment.measurement: Th17 activation state, GM-CSF co-expression, EAE development

text: Committed IL-23R+ Th17 cells are highly resistant to IL-27- and IL-2-mediated suppression, and pathogenic Th17 cells induced by IL-23 in the absence of TGFβ express reduced levels of AHR, C-MAF and IL-10 compared with TGFβ-driven Th17 cells.

quotes.quote:
Indeed, committed IL-23R+ Th17 cells are highly resistant to 
IL-27- and IL-2-mediated suppression62.

Pathogenic Th17 cells induced by IL-23 in the absence of TGFβ also express reduced levels 
of aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR), C-MAF and IL-10 compared with TGFβ driven Th17 
cells53, 59.

experiment.system: in vitro polarized mouse Th17 cells
experiment.perturbation: exposure to IL-27 or IL-2; IL-23 polarization in the absence versus presence of TGFβ
experiment.measurement: suppression of Th17 responses; expression of AHR, C-MAF and IL-10

text: Il6-/- mice cannot generate Th17 cells and are protected from EAE and collagen-induced arthritis, and Il1r1-/- mice fail to develop antigen-specific Th17 cells and are resistant to EAE.

quotes.quote:
Consequently, 
Il6−/− mice are unable to generate Th17 cells and are protected from developing 
experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE)32 and collagen-induced arthritis 
(CIA)33.
Il1r1−/− mice fail to develop antigen-specific Th17 cells and are resistant to EAE34.

experiment.system: Il6-/- and Il1r1-/- mice
experiment.perturbation: genetic deletion of IL-6 or IL-1R1, followed by EAE or CIA induction
experiment.measurement: Th17 cell generation and disease incidence/severity

text: IL-1β induces mTOR phosphorylation in Th17 cells, and rapamycin treatment or mTOR-deficiency completely abolishes IL-1β-induced Th17 cell proliferation.

quotes.quote:
Mechanistically, IL-1β induces 
phosphorylation of the mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) in Th17 cells and thereby 
enhances the metabolic fitness of rapidly dividing Th17 cells during inflammation. Indeed, 
rapamycin treatment or mTOR-deficiency completely abolishes IL-1β-induced Th17 cell 
proliferation36.

experiment.system: mouse Th17 cells
experiment.perturbation: IL-1β stimulation with rapamycin treatment or mTOR deficiency
experiment.measurement: mTOR phosphorylation and Th17 cell proliferation

text: Human in vitro Th17 differentiation requirements for TGFβ differ across laboratories: three groups reported TGFβ is required, whereas two other groups found a cocktail of IL-1β, IL-6 and IL-23 sufficient.

quotes.quote:
three separate research groups show that 
TGFβ is required for in vitro Th17 cell development, whereas two other research groups 
found that a cocktail of IL-1β, IL-6 and IL-23 is sufficient to drive Th17 differentiation41–45.

experiment.system: human T cells (peripheral blood or umbilical cord blood) in vitro
experiment.perturbation: polarization with or without TGFβ, or with IL-1β/IL-6/IL-23
experiment.measurement: Th17 cell differentiation

text: Th17 cells generated in vitro by TGFβ plus IL-6 are only weakly pathogenic and require subsequent IL-23 exposure to become pathogenic; Th17 cells can also be generated by IL-1β, IL-6 and IL-23 in a TGFβ-independent manner, and these cells are T-bet+ and co-express IFNγ and GM-CSF.

quotes.quote:
Although the combination of TGFβ and IL-6 efficiently generates Th17 cells in vitro, the 
cells generated by this cocktail are only weakly pathogenic, and subsequent exposure to 
IL-23 is essential to drive pathogenicity21, 46–50.

Th17 cells could be 
generated in response to IL-1β, IL-6 and IL-23 in a TGFβ-independent manner50. 
Interestingly, these TGFβ-independent IL-23R+, RORγt+ Th17 cells are also T-bet+ and co-
express IFNγ and GM-CSF

experiment.system: naive mouse CD4+ T cells polarized in vitro
experiment.perturbation: polarization with TGFβ+IL-6 versus IL-1β/IL-6/IL-23, with or without subsequent IL-23
experiment.measurement: pathogenicity and expression of IL-23R, RORγt, T-bet, IFNγ and GM-CSF

text: TGFβ3 was reported to promote pathogenic Th17 cells by upregulating IL-23R expression, and TGFβ3 was itself induced by IL-23, acting in a feed-forward loop that amplifies IL-23 signaling.

quotes.quote:
it was 
proposed that TGFβ3 promotes pathogenic TH17 cells by upregulating IL-23R expression53. 
Interestingly, TGFβ3 was induced by IL-23 and acted endogenously in a feed forward loop
to enhance IL-23R expression, thereby amplifying the IL-23 signal53.

experiment.system: mouse Th17 cells
experiment.perturbation: TGFβ3 exposure and IL-23 stimulation
experiment.measurement: IL-23R expression and Th17 pathogenicity

text: Rorc-/- mice lack Th17 cells and exhibit reduced autoimmune disease severity, while enhanced RORγt expression in naive CD4+ T cells induces genes essential for Th17 differentiation.

quotes.quote:
RORγt serves as the master 
regulator for TH17 cells, and Rorc−/− mice lack TH17 cells and exhibit reduced autoimmune 
disease severity12. In contrast, enhanced expression of RORγt in naïve CD4+ T cells induces 
key genes essential for TH17 cell differentiation12.

experiment.system: Rorc-/- mice and naive CD4+ T cells
experiment.perturbation: genetic deletion or forced overexpression of RORγt
experiment.measurement: Th17 cell numbers, Th17 gene induction, autoimmune disease severity

text: ChIP-Seq analysis showed that STAT3 directly regulates Il17, Il17f and Il23r and controls Rorc, Batf and Irf4, and binds promoters of Il17a and Il17f as well as intergenic enhancer regions that undergo histone modifications during differentiation.

quotes.quote:
ChIP-Seq 
analysis has demonstrated that STAT3 directly regulates the Th17 cytokine and cytokine 
receptor genes Il17, Il17f and Il23r, and it also controls expression of the Th17-specific 
transcription factors Rorc, Batf, and Irf4 31. In addition, STAT3 binds both the promoter 
regions of Il17a and Il17f and their intergenic regions with enhancer elements that undergo 
histone modifications during differentiation31.

experiment.system: mouse Th17 cells
experiment.perturbation: observational (ChIP-Seq of STAT3 occupancy) with STAT3 deficiency
experiment.measurement: genome-wide STAT3 binding and target gene expression

text: BATF is essential for Th17 differentiation: Batf-/- mice are resistant to EAE, have normal TGFβ and IL-6 signaling and upregulate RORγt early but fail to maintain it, and RORγt overexpression only partially rescues the Th17 defect; BATF-JUNB dimers bind the Il17, Il21 and Il22 promoters.

quotes.quote:
A study from 2009 
showed that BATF is essential for TH17 differentiation, and mice lacking BATF are 
resistant to EAE69. Batf−/− mice have normal TGFβ and IL-6 signaling and can upregulate 
RORγt early on during T cell development, but fail to maintain RORγt expression. 
However, overexpression of RORγt could only partially rescue Th17 defects in Batf−/− cells

BATF forms a dimer with JUNB that binds directly to the promoters of Il17, Il21 and Il22 in 
Th17 cells.

experiment.system: Batf-/- mice and T cells
experiment.perturbation: BATF deletion, RORγt overexpression rescue, EAE induction
experiment.measurement: Th17 differentiation, RORγt expression, IL-17 expression, EAE susceptibility, promoter binding

text: IRF4-deficient mice are protected from EAE and show a Th17 differentiation defect stemming from impaired RORγt expression, with RORγt overexpression only partially restoring IL-17 production.

quotes.quote:
IRF4-deficient mice are protected from 
EAE and exhibit a defect in TH17 differentiation that stems from impaired RORγt 
expression. However, similar to BATF, overexpression of RORγt in Irf4−/− T cells could 
only partially restore IL-17 production

experiment.system: Irf4-/- mice and T cells
experiment.perturbation: IRF4 deletion with RORγt overexpression rescue; EAE induction
experiment.measurement: Th17 differentiation, IL-17 production, EAE susceptibility

text: ChIP-Seq revealed striking overlap between BATF and IRF4 promoter occupancy in Th17 cells, including co-occupancy in non-polarized Th0 cells; BATF, IRF4 and STAT3 deficiency substantially reduces p300 binding whereas lack of RORγt has almost no effect on the enhancer landscape, and only Il17, Il17f and Il23r are exclusively RORγt-dependent.

quotes.quote:
A comprehensive ChIP-Seq analysis revealed a striking overlap 
between BATF and IRF4 promoter occupancy in Th17 cells73.

Surprisingly, co-occupancy by these 
transcription factors was also observed in TCR activated but non-polarized Th0 cells.

Strikingly, BATF, IRF4 and STAT3 deficiency substantially 
reduces p300 binding, but a lack of RORγt has almost no effect on the enhancer landscape.

in fact only a few Th17 genes
—Il17, Il17f, and Il23r—are exclusively dependent on RORγt 73.

experiment.system: mouse Th17 and Th0 cells
experiment.perturbation: deficiency of BATF, IRF4, STAT3 or RORγt
experiment.measurement: ChIP-Seq transcription factor and p300 occupancy; gene dependence

text: HIF-1α is induced upon TCR activation and further enhanced by hypoxia and IL-6/STAT3 signals; it directly binds and drives RORγt transcription, forms a complex with RORγt and p300 to drive IL-17 expression, and complexes with FOXP3 to target it for proteasomal degradation.

quotes.quote:
HIF-1α is induced upon TCR 
activation, and its expression is further enhanced by hypoxic conditions associated with 
tissue inflammation as well as IL-6-and STAT3-dependent differentiation signals77. 
Mechanistically, HIF-1α directly binds and drives transcription of RORγt and forms a 
complex with RORγt and p300 to drive IL-17 expression. HIF-1α can also form a complex 
with FOXP3, and targets it for proteasomal degradation.

experiment.system: mouse CD4+ T cells
experiment.perturbation: TCR activation, hypoxia and IL-6/STAT3 signaling
experiment.measurement: HIF-1α expression, RORγt transcription, IL-17 expression, FOXP3 degradation

text: Genome-wide histone modification analysis showed Th17 cells display both active (H3K4me3) and repressive (H3K27me3) marks on Tbx21 and Gata3, whereas Th1 and Th2 cells show only repressive marks on Rorc and Il17 loci.

quotes.quote:
Interestingly, Th17 cells display both active and repressive histone marks on Tbx21 
and Gata3, whereas Th1 and Th2 cells show only repressive marks on Rorc and Il17 loci.

experiment.system: differentiated mouse CD4+ T helper subsets
experiment.perturbation: observational (in vitro polarization to Th1, Th2, Th17)
experiment.measurement: genome-wide H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 marks at lineage-specifying loci

text: Fate-mapping mice in which Il17a-Cre marks IL-17-expressing cells with YFP demonstrated that bona fide Th17 cells can be destabilized and converted to Th1 cells under appropriate environmental stimuli, a result confirmed by histone modification analysis of IL-17+ cells captured from the inflamed intestine.

quotes.quote:
Crossing the Il17a-Cre allele to Rosa26-
enhanced yellow fluorescence protein (YFP) reporter mice generated a fate mapping system 
in which Il17-expressing cells are permanently marked with YFP. This cell tagging system 
has demonstrated that “bona fide” Th17 cells can be destabilized and converted to Th1 cells 
under proper environmental stimuli. Histone modification analysis of cytokine bead 
captured IL-17+ cells from the inflamed intestine confirmed these results81.

experiment.system: Il17a-Cre × Rosa26-YFP fate-mapping mice; inflamed mouse intestine
experiment.perturbation: in vivo inflammatory stimulation
experiment.measurement: YFP+ cell phenotype conversion to Th1 and histone modifications

text: The authors report unpublished data that BLIMP1 (Prdm1) is induced by IL-23 and acts as both activator and repressor to induce Th17 maturation, coordinating with RORγt to enhance IL-23R and GM-CSF while repressing IL-2, Bcl2, Foxp3 and Gata3, and directly engaging the Il23r, Il17f and csf2 loci near RORγt, p300 and STAT3.

quotes.quote:
We have recently identified that transcription factor B-lymphocyte-induced maturation protein 1 
(BLIMP1, which is encoded by Prdm1) is induced by IL-23 and acts both as a gene activator 
and repressor to induce Th17 maturation (Unpublished data, R. Jain and D. J. Cua). BLIMP1 
coordinates with RORγt to enhance expression of IL-23R and GM-CSF while 
simultaneously repressing IL-2 and alternate fate determining factors (such as Bcl2, Foxp3, 
Gata3). Interestingly, BLIMP1 directly engages the Il23r, Il17f and csf2 loci in close 
proximity to RORγt, p300 and STAT3

experiment.system: mouse Th17 cells (unpublished data of the authors)
experiment.perturbation: IL-23 stimulation and BLIMP1 analysis
experiment.measurement: BLIMP1 induction, target gene expression, and locus occupancy at Il23r, Il17f and csf2

text: IL-17RA is the founding member of a receptor family of five subunits (IL-17RA–IL-17RE) sharing the SEFIR cytoplasmic motif; IL-17RA is required for IL-25 signaling with IL-17RB and IL-17C signaling with IL-17RE, and the SEFIR adaptor ACT1 is essential for signal transduction by all analyzed IL-17R family members.

quotes.quote:
the IL-17R (now known as 
IL-17RA) was the founding member of a new subclass of cytokine receptors, which 
comprises five receptor subunits, IL-17RA–IL-17RE, that have homology to one another but 
not to other receptor families82

IL-17RA is essential for signaling through IL-17E (also 
known as IL-25) when partnered with IL-17RB, and also for signaling through IL-17C when 
partnered with IL-17RE85, 86. The only other protein identified to have a SEFIR domain is 
the adaptor ACT1 (also known as CIKS)87; indeed, ACT1 is essential for signal transduction 
by all analyzed IL-17R family members82, 88, 89.

experiment.system: IL-17 receptor family in mammalian cells
experiment.perturbation: receptor subunit and ACT1 loss-of-function; cytokine stimulation
experiment.measurement: IL-17 family cytokine signaling responses

text: ACT1 recruits TRAF6 and acts as an E3 ligase mediating its ubiquitination, leading to canonical NF-κB and MAPK (ERK, p38, JNK) activation; IL-17 activation of these pathways is impaired in the absence of ACT1 or TRAF6, and ACT1 can alternatively recruit TRAF2/TRAF5 to promote mRNA stability via SF2/ASF or HuR complexes.

quotes.quote:
ACT1 serves both as a signaling 
adaptor, to recruit tumour necrosis factor receptor (TNFR)-associated factor (TRAF) 
proteins to direct activation of several downstream signaling cascades88, and as an E3 ligase 
to mediate ubiquitination of TRAF691. Recruitment and ubiquitination of TRAF6 leads to 
activation of the canonical NF-κB pathway and the mitogen-activated protein kinase 
(MAPK) pathways, which include extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK), p38 and JUN 
N-terminal kinase (JNK). Consequently, activation of these pathways by IL-17 is impaired 
in the absence of either ACT1 or TRAF688, 89, 92. Alternatively, ACT1 can recruit TRAF2 
and TRAF5, which promote activation of an mRNA stability pathway

experiment.system: IL-17-responsive cells and ACT1- or TRAF6-deficient cells
experiment.perturbation: IL-17 stimulation with loss of ACT1 or TRAF6
experiment.measurement: NF-κB and MAPK activation, TRAF6 ubiquitination, mRNA stability

text: ACT1 phosphorylation is mediated by IKKi (IKKε) and TBK1, and ACT1 stability requires hsp90: inhibition of hsp90 causes proteasomal degradation of ACT1 and defective IL-17 signaling; most Act1-/- mouse phenotypes resemble Il17ra-/- mice.

quotes.quote:
Regulation of these alternative pathways occurs via inducible ACT1 
phosphorylation, which is mediated by Ikki (Ikkε) and TBK1 (Figure 4)95, 96. ACT1 
function and stability is in turn regulated by the chaperone protein hsp90. Inhibition of 
hsp90 results in proteasomal degradation of ACT1, which in turn leads to defective IL-17 
signaling97. ACT1 appears to be required for most IL-17-dependent signaling events98 and 
the majority of phenotypes Act1−/− mice are similar to Il17ra−/− mice.

experiment.system: IL-17-responsive cells; Act1-/- and Il17ra-/- mice
experiment.perturbation: hsp90 inhibition; genetic deletion of Act1 or Il17ra
experiment.measurement: ACT1 protein levels, IL-17 signaling output, mouse phenotypes

text: IL-17 target genes require C/EBP as well as NF-κB elements: deletion of either element in the Il6 and Lcn2 promoters renders them insensitive to IL-17 signals, and IL-17 induces C/EBPδ mRNA and protein and to a lesser extent C/EBPβ.

quotes.quote:
For example, the Il6 and Lcn2 promoters require both NF-κB and 
C/EBP elements, as deletion of either element renders their promoters insensitive to IL-17-
mediated signals104, 105. IL-17 induces expression of C/EBPδ mRNA and protein, and to a 
lesser extent C/EBPβ104, 106.

experiment.system: IL-17-responsive cells with Il6 and Lcn2 promoter reporters
experiment.perturbation: deletion of NF-κB or C/EBP promoter elements; IL-17 stimulation
experiment.measurement: promoter responsiveness and C/EBPδ/β expression

text: IL-17 and IL-17F are modest activators on their own but act cooperatively with TNFα, IFNγ, IL-22, lymphotoxin, IL-1β and lipopolysaccharide; in synovial tissue IL-17 upregulates TNFRII expression, and IL-17 upregulates IκBζ, a positive regulator of NF-κB.

quotes.quote:
On their own, IL-17 (and IL-17F) are modest activators of signaling, but they function 
cooperatively with other pro-inflammatory molecules, particularly TNFα but also IFNγ, 
IL-22, lymphotoxin, IL-1β and lipopolysaccharide109.

In synovial 
tissue, IL-17 upregulates TNFRII expression, and thereby enhances responsiveness to TNFα 
signaling110.

IL-17 also upregulates 
expression of IκBζ — a positive regulator of the NF-κB family

experiment.system: IL-17-responsive cells including synovial tissue/synoviocytes
experiment.perturbation: IL-17 stimulation alone or with TNFα and other inflammatory mediators
experiment.measurement: target gene induction, TNFRII and IκBζ expression, mRNA stability

text: USP25 removes K63-linked ubiquitin chains from TRAF6 and TRAF5, inhibiting IL-17 target gene transcription and IL-17-induced mRNA stability; USP25 deficiency is associated with enhanced IL-17-dependent pulmonary inflammation and increased EAE susceptibility.

quotes.quote:
ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase 25 (USP25) removes K63-linked ubiquitin 
chains on both TRAF6 and TRAF5, which inhibits transcription of IL-17 target genes as 
well as IL-17-induced mRNA stability USP25 deficiency is associated with enhanced IL-17-
dependent pulmonary inflammation and increased susceptibility to EAE113.

experiment.system: USP25-deficient mice and cells
experiment.perturbation: genetic loss of USP25; IL-17 stimulation; EAE induction
experiment.measurement: TRAF ubiquitination, IL-17 target gene transcription/mRNA stability, pulmonary inflammation, EAE severity

text: A20 (Tnfaip3) is a feedback inhibitor of IL-17 signaling: IL-17 induces Tnfaip3 mRNA and A20 protein, triggering TRAF6 deubiquitination and downregulation of NF-κB and MAPK (particularly JNK) activation; A20 binds IL-17RA via the CBAD and associates with APC5, while knockdown of TAX1BP1 or ITCH does not inhibit IL-17 signaling.

quotes.quote:
IL-17 induces expression of Tnfaip3 mRNA and A20 protein levels, which triggers 
deubiquitination of TRAF6 and downregulation of NF-κB and MAPK activation 
(particularly JNK). Notably, A20 associates directly with IL-17RA through the receptor’s C-
terminal “C/EBPβ activation domain” (CBAD)114.

However, knockdown of either TAX1BP1 or 
ITCH do not inhibit IL-17 signaling, which suggests that A20 might use alternate adaptors. 
Indeed, we found that A20 associates with anaphase-promoting complex subunit 5 
(APC5)121, 122

experiment.system: IL-17-responsive cells
experiment.perturbation: IL-17 stimulation; A20 manipulation; knockdown of TAX1BP1 or ITCH
experiment.measurement: A20 expression, TRAF6 ubiquitination, NF-κB/MAPK activation, protein association with IL-17RA and APC5

text: IL-17R signaling is inhibited by the β-TrCP ubiquitin ligase complex, which induces K48 ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of phosphorylated ACT1; TRAF3 and TRAF4 compete with ACT1/TRAF6 binding and limit IL-17-mediated development of EAE, and deletion of the IL-17RA CBAD enhances IL-17 signaling.

quotes.quote:
IL-17R signaling is inhibited by the Ub ligase 
complex β-TrCP, which induces K48 ubiquitination on phosphorylated forms of ACT1 that 
in turn leads to its degradation through the proteasome

TRAF3 competes with ACT1 for 
binding to IL-17RA and thereby dampens IL-17-dependent signals116. Similarly, TRAF4 
directly binds Act1 upon IL-17 stimulation and competes for its association with TRAF6. 
Consistently, TRAF3 and TRAF4 limit IL-17-mediated development of EAE116, 126.

deletion of the CBAD was 
shown several years ago in a structure-function analysis of IL-17RA to enhance IL-17 
signaling117

experiment.system: IL-17-responsive cells and mice with TRAF3/TRAF4 manipulation
experiment.perturbation: β-TrCP-mediated ACT1 degradation; TRAF3/TRAF4 binding competition; IL-17RA CBAD deletion; EAE induction
experiment.measurement: ACT1 levels, IL-17-dependent signaling, EAE development

text: MiR-155 in CD4+ T cells positively regulates Th17 differentiation and MiR155-/- or miRNA-silenced mice are resistant to EAE; MiR-23b restrains IL-17-induced NF-κB activation by targeting TAB2/3 and IKKα, and patients with RA and SLE show reduced miR-23b expression.

quotes.quote:
The microRNA MiR-155 expressed in CD4+ T cells positively regulates Th17 
differentiation127

Consequently, MiR155−/− mice 
or mice in which this miRNA is silenced are resistant to EAE127, 129. In terms of signaling, 
MiR-23b keeps IL-17-induced NF-κB activation in check by targeting the degradation of 
TAB2/3 and IKKα. Consistently, patients with RA and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) 
show reduced expression of miR-23b 130.

experiment.system: MiR155-/- or miR-155-silenced mice; IL-17-responsive cells; patients with RA and SLE
experiment.perturbation: miR-155 deletion/silencing; miR-23b targeting; EAE induction
experiment.measurement: Th17 differentiation, EAE susceptibility, NF-κB activation, miR-23b expression levels

text: C/EBPβ is both a positive and negative regulator of the IL-17 pathway: it transactivates IL-17 target genes, but its phosphorylation by ERK and GSK3β — dependent on the IL-17RA CBAD — correlates with decreased IL-17-induced gene expression.

quotes.quote:
Although C/EBPβ can 
positively transactivate IL-17 target genes104, C/EBP phosphorylation of C/EBPβ by the 
kinases Erk and GSK3β correlates with a decrease in IL-17-induced gene expression. 
Notably, phosphorylation through GSK3β is dependent on the CBAD

experiment.system: IL-17-responsive cells
experiment.perturbation: IL-17 stimulation; ERK/GSK3β-mediated C/EBPβ phosphorylation; CBAD dependence
experiment.measurement: IL-17-induced target gene expression

text: IL-17- and IL-17R-knockout mice show increased susceptibility to a wide range of pathogens, whereas humans with mutations in the Th17 pathway show a much more restricted phenotype dominated by susceptibility to commensal Candida albicans.

quotes.quote:
Experiments using IL-17- and IL-17R-knockout mouse models 
have demonstrated increased susceptibility to a wide variety of infectious organisms, 
including bacteria, parasites, fungi and viruses. However, examination of families or 
individuals with specific mutations in the Th17 pathway indicated a surprisingly limited role 
for Th17 cells and IL-17 in immunity to infections, with susceptibility to commensal fungi 
(mainly the commensal Candida albicans) by far the dominant disease seen in these settings

experiment.system: IL-17/IL-17R-knockout mice and human families with Th17-pathway mutations
experiment.perturbation: genetic loss of IL-17 or IL-17R (mice); naturally occurring mutations (humans)
experiment.measurement: susceptibility to infectious organisms

text: Human deficiencies in the Th17/IL-17 axis are linked to chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis: AD-HIES patients with dominant-negative STAT3 mutations have reduced Th17 frequency with CMC, S. aureus and pulmonary infections; CMC is also associated with CARD9, IL12RB1, IL12B or STAT1 mutations, APS-1/APECED neutralizing antibodies against Th17 cytokines, and null IL17RA or ACT1 or dominant-negative IL17F mutations.

quotes.quote:
patients with AD-HIES have autosomal dominant-negative mutations in 
STAT3 that are associated with reduced frequency of Th17 cells and susceptibility to chronic 
mucocutaneous candidiasis (CMC), Staphylococcus aureus infections and pulmonary 
infections66, 132. The reduced frequency of Th17 cells in CMC is associated with mutations 
that impair fungal sensing (CARD9), IL-23 signaling (IL12RB1, IL12B) or enhance negative 
regulation of Th17 differentiation (STAT1) 133–135. Similarly, CMC but not other infections 
occurs patients with APS-1/APECED, who have naturally-occurring neutralizing antibodies 
against Th17 cytokines136, 137. Null mutations in IL17RA or ACT1 and dominant-negative 
mutations in IL17F also promote CMC and some staphylococcal infections138, 139.

experiment.system: human patients with inherited mutations affecting the Th17 pathway
experiment.perturbation: observational (naturally occurring mutations and autoantibodies)
experiment.measurement: Th17 cell frequency and infection susceptibility (CMC, staphylococcal, pulmonary)

text: Intradermal IL-23 administration in a preclinical model induced psoriasiform features including dermal acanthosis, neutrophil recruitment and infiltration of IL-17- and IL-22-producing T cells, and inhibition of IL-23 significantly reduced IL-17 and IL-22 in psoriatic lesional skin.

quotes.quote:
its 
ability to induce psoriasiform characteristics in a preclinical model of intradermal IL-23 
administration143. Injection of IL-23 promoted dermal acanthosis, neutrophil recruitment, 
and infiltration of IL-17- and IL-22-producing T cells. In addition, inhibition of IL-23 led to 
significant reduction of IL-17 and IL-22 in psoriatic lesional skin

experiment.system: preclinical mouse skin model and psoriatic lesional skin
experiment.perturbation: intradermal IL-23 injection; IL-23 inhibition
experiment.measurement: dermal acanthosis, neutrophil recruitment, IL-17/IL-22-producing T cell infiltration and cytokine levels

text: The authors report that RORγt+ IL-23R+CD3+CD4-CD8-Sca1+ entheseal resident cells produce IL-17 and IL-22 that are the major cause of STAT3-dependent osteoblast-mediated bone remodeling in spondyloarthropathy.

quotes.quote:
We have recently uncovered the presence of RORγt+ IL-23R
+CD3+CD4-CD8-Sca1+ entheseal resident cells and that their production of IL-17 and 
IL-22 are the major cause of STAT3-dependent osteoblast-mediated bone remodeling142.

experiment.system: mouse entheseal tissue / spondyloarthropathy model
experiment.perturbation: IL-23 acting on entheseal resident T cells
experiment.measurement: identification of entheseal resident cell phenotype, IL-17/IL-22 production, osteoblast-mediated new bone formation

text: Ankylosing spondylitis is associated with substantial extra-articular comorbidity: uveitis affects 40% of patients and up to 70% of patients have microscopically evident bowel inflammation.

quotes.quote:
Indeed, uveitis accounts for significant comorbidity in 
ankylosing spondylitis, affecting 40% of patients. In addition, up to 70% of patients with 
ankylosing spondylitis have microscopically evident bowel inflammation150.

experiment.system: patients with ankylosing spondylitis
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: prevalence of uveitis and of microscopically evident bowel inflammation

text: GWAS have identified multiple IL-23R SNPs associated with protection from or susceptibility to ankylosing spondylitis, psoriasis and IBD, and the same IL-23R SNPs found in ankylosing spondylitis and psoriasis were present in Crohn's disease patients along with Nod2/Card15 variants.

quotes.quote:
Recently GWAS have identified multiple SNPs in IL-23R, which are associated 
with either protection from ankylosing spondylitis, psoriasis, IBD or increased susceptibility 
to these autoimmune conditions54–58.

The same IL-23R SNPs found in individuals with ankylosing spondylitis and psoriasis were 
present in patients with Crohn’s disease along with Nod2 / Card15 (sensor for bacterial cell 
wall)54, 151, 152.

experiment.system: human patient cohorts with AS, psoriasis, IBD/Crohn's disease
experiment.perturbation: observational genome-wide association analysis
experiment.measurement: SNP associations at IL23R and NOD2/CARD15 with disease susceptibility or protection

text: In Crohn's disease, increased expression of IL-17A mRNA and intracellular protein in the intestinal mucosa has been reported, and elevated fecal IL-17A levels were described in active disease.

quotes.quote:
In Crohn’s disease, increased expression of 
IL-17A mRNA and intracellular protein in the intestinal mucosa has been reported153. 
Elevated fecal IL-17A levels were also described in active Crohn’s disease154.

experiment.system: patients with Crohn's disease
experiment.perturbation: observational (disease versus control)
experiment.measurement: intestinal mucosal IL-17A mRNA/protein and fecal IL-17A levels

text: Il17-/- mice have increased gut mucosal permeability, predisposing to higher incidence and severity of IBD, which the authors offer as an explanation for why blocking IL-17 may worsen Crohn's disease.

quotes.quote:
Indeed, Il17-/-mice have increased gut 
mucosal permeability, predisposing to higher incidence and severity of IBD 163

experiment.system: Il17-/- mice
experiment.perturbation: genetic deletion of IL-17 with colitis induction
experiment.measurement: gut mucosal permeability and IBD incidence/severity

text: Experiments using Il17-, Il22-, Il23a- or Il23ra-deficient mice and antibody-mediated inhibition demonstrated a requirement for these cytokines in EAE, CAIA, CIA, IBD, AS and psoriasis disease models.

quotes.quote:
Experiments using Il17-, Il22-, Il23a- or Il23ra-deficient mice as well as antibody-mediated 
inhibition have demonstrated a requirement for these cytokines in EAE, CAIA, CIA, IBD, 
AS, and psoriasis disease models4, 5, 25, 142, 143.

experiment.system: mouse models of EAE, CAIA, CIA, IBD, AS and psoriasis
experiment.perturbation: genetic deletion of Il17, Il22, Il23a or Il23ra, or antibody-mediated cytokine inhibition
experiment.measurement: disease development/severity

text: Suppression of JAK and TYK2-dependent STAT3 activation as well as direct small-molecule inhibition of RORγt demonstrated efficacy in preclinical disease models.

quotes.quote: Indeed, suppression of JAK and TYK2-dependent STAT3 activation166, 167 as well as direct

inhibition of RORγt—using small molecule pharmacologic agents—have demonstrated 
impressive efficacy in preclinical disease models168–171.

experiment.system: preclinical (mouse) inflammatory disease models
experiment.perturbation: pharmacologic suppression of JAK/TYK2-STAT3 signaling or small-molecule RORγt inhibition
experiment.measurement: disease efficacy readouts in the models

text: The NCCD proposes an updated classification of cell death subroutines based on mechanistic and essential rather than correlative aspects, providing molecularly oriented definitions of terms including intrinsic apoptosis, extrinsic apoptosis, MPT-driven necrosis, necroptosis, ferroptosis, pyroptosis, parthanatos, entotic cell death, NETotic cell death, lysosome-dependent cell death, autophagy-dependent cell death, immunogenic cell death, cellular senescence, and mitotic catastrophe.

quotes.quote:
we propose an updated
classiﬁcation of cell death subroutines focusing on mechanistic and essential (as opposed to correlative and dispensable)
aspects of the process

As we provide molecularly oriented deﬁnitions of terms including intrinsic apoptosis, extrinsic
apoptosis, mitochondrial permeability transition (MPT)-driven necrosis, necroptosis, ferroptosis, pyroptosis, parthanatos,
entotic cell death, NETotic cell death, lysosome-dependent cell death, autophagy-dependent cell death, immunogenic cell
death, cellular senescence, and mitotic catastrophe

experiment.system: published cell death literature reviewed by the Nomenclature Committee on Cell Death
experiment.perturbation: observational (consensus classification exercise)
experiment.measurement: definitional criteria based on genetic, biochemical, pharmacological and functional evidence

text: Co-deletion of Bax and Bak1 renders a large panel of cell types profoundly resistant to diverse lethal stimuli, a phenotype exacerbated in some settings by co-deletion of Bok, and causes perinatal lethality in mice due to severe developmental defects.

quotes.quote:
the co-deletion of Bax and Bak1 not only renders a large
panel of cell types profoundly resistant to diverse lethal
stimuli [74], a phenotype that in some settings can be
exacerbated by the co-deletion of Bok [123], but also causes
perinatal lethality in mice as a consequence of severe
developmental defects [124]

experiment.system: mouse cells and mice with Bax/Bak1 (and Bok) deletion
experiment.perturbation: genetic co-deletion of Bax and Bak1 (± Bok), exposure to lethal stimuli
experiment.measurement: cell death resistance; mouse survival and developmental phenotype

text: Transformed cells lacking all major BH3 activators (BID, BIM, PUMA, and NOXA) can still undergo apoptosis in response to DNA-damaging agents or downregulation of BCL2, BCL-XL, and MCL1, while overexpression of BH3-only sensitizers induces minimal apoptosis in such cells.

quotes.quote:
transformed cells lacking
all major BH3 activators (i.e., BID, BIM, PUMA, and
NOXA) can still undergo apoptosis in response to DNA-
damaging agents or downregulation of BCL2, BCL-XL, and
MCL1 [64]

overexpression of BH3-only sensitizers induces minimal
apoptosis in cells lacking BID, BIM, PUMA, and NOXA
[64]

experiment.system: transformed cell lines genetically deleted for BID, BIM, PUMA, NOXA
experiment.perturbation: DNA-damaging agents, downregulation of anti-apoptotic BCL2 proteins, or overexpression of BH3-only sensitizers
experiment.measurement: apoptosis induction

text: Bok−/−, Bax−/−Bok−/− and Bak1−/−Bok−/− mice display no obvious abnormalities except for persistence of primordial follicle oocytes in aged Bax−/−Bok−/− females, implying compensation of BOK functions by BAX and/or BAK.

quotes.quote:
Bok−/−, Bax−/−Bok−/−as
well as Bak1−/−Bok−/−mice display no obvious abnorm-
alities (except for persistence of primordial follicle oocytes
in aged Bax−/−Bok−/−females) [154, 155]

experiment.system: knockout mice
experiment.perturbation: genetic deletion of Bok alone or with Bax or Bak1
experiment.measurement: gross phenotypic abnormalities, oocyte persistence

text: Blocking post-mitochondrial caspase activation genetically or with inhibitors such as Z-VAD-fmk and Q-VD-OPh generally delays but does not prevent intrinsic apoptosis in vitro and in vivo, promoting a switch to other types of RCD.

quotes.quote:
blocking
post-mitochondrial
caspase
activation
by
genetic means or with speciﬁc pharmacological inhibitors

generally delays (but does not prevent)
intrinsic apoptosis in vitro and in vivo (at least in the
mammalian system), as it promotes a switch to other types
of RCD [17, 225]

experiment.system: mammalian cells and animals undergoing intrinsic apoptosis
experiment.perturbation: genetic or pharmacological (Z-VAD-fmk, Q-VD-OPh) caspase inhibition
experiment.measurement: kinetics and occurrence of cell death, RCD modality

text: CASP3 promotes phosphatidylserine exposure by cleaving XKR8 and by inactivating flippases ATP11A and ATP11C, as shown by absent or reduced PS translocation in cells expressing non-cleavable ATP11C and in developing erythrocytes from Atp11a−/− mice.

quotes.quote:
resulting
in
inhibition
of
their
ﬂippase
activity
and
PS exposure, as demonstrated by absent or reduced PS
translocation on the cell surface of cells expressing a
non-cleavable ATP11C or developing erythrocytes from
Atp11a−/−mice [219–221]

experiment.system: cells expressing non-cleavable ATP11C; erythrocytes from Atp11a−/− mice
experiment.perturbation: mutation of caspase cleavage site / gene knockout
experiment.measurement: phosphatidylserine translocation to cell surface

text: In type I cells extrinsic apoptosis cannot be inhibited by BCL2 overexpression, co-deletion of Bax and Bak1, or loss of BID, whereas in type II cells extrinsic apoptosis requires CASP8-mediated cleavage of BID.

quotes.quote:
the
CASP8-dependent proteolytic maturation of executioner
CASP3 and CASP7 sufﬁces to drive RCD, which cannot be
inhibited by the transgene-driven overexpression of anti-
apoptotic BCL2 proteins, the co-deletion of Bax and Bak1,
or the loss of BID [308, 309]

extrinsic apoptosis requires the
proteolytic cleavage of BID by CASP8 [70, 311, 312]

experiment.system: type I cells (thymocytes, mature lymphocytes) and type II cells (hepatocytes, pancreatic β cells, cancer cells)
experiment.perturbation: death receptor ligation with BCL2 transgene overexpression, Bax/Bak1 co-deletion, or BID loss
experiment.measurement: apoptosis execution

text: CYPD is described as the only protein whose in vivo requirement for MPT induction has been formally validated with robust genetic tools, and CYPD inhibitors including cyclosporin A, sanglifehrin A and JW47 limit MPT-driven necrosis and confer protection in multiple rodent disease models; however, the CIRCUS trial completed in 2015 failed to confirm previous 2008 findings of cardioprotection by cyclosporine in acute myocardial infarction.

quotes.quote:
peptidylprolyl
isomerase F (PPIF; best known as cyclophilin D, CYPD) is
the only protein whose in vivo requirement for MPT induc-
tion has been formally validated with robust genetic tools

pharmacological inhibitors of CYPD
including cyclosporin A (CsA) [376 379–381], sanglifehrin A
(SfA) [382, 383], and JW47 [384] limit MPT-driven necrosis
and confer protection in multiple rodent models of disease

a large randomized clinical study com-
pleted in 2015 (the CIRCUS trial) failed to conﬁrm previous
ﬁndings from 2008 [386] on the cardioprotective effects of
cyclosporine administered before percutaneous coronary
