motif to enable trimer assembly and thus, formation of a phase-
separated condensate at the site of recruitment. This enables
local enrichment of GFP, which enhances the visualization of
genomic loci targeted by the sgRNA in live cells.

experiment.system: live cells expressing CRISPR FISHer components
experiment.perturbation: sgRNA-directed recruitment of PCP-GFP-trimer to genomic loci
experiment.measurement: local GFP fluorescence enrichment at loci

text: Tutucci et al. generated the MBSV6 reporter system with a modified MS2 coat protein of reduced binding affinity, enabling tracking of mRNAs without preventing their degradation and allowing detection of rapid mRNA turnover and single-molecule mRNA imaging in live mammalian cells.

quotes.quote:
Tutucci et al. generated the
MBSV6 reporter system by engineering a modified MCP with
reduced binding affinity to enable tracking of mRNAs without
preventing their degradation.135 This allowed for the detection
of rapid mRNA turnover and single-molecule mRNA imaging
in live mammalian cells.

experiment.system: live mammalian cells expressing MS2-tagged mRNA and modified MCP-FP
experiment.perturbation: engineering reduced MCP binding affinity
experiment.measurement: single-molecule mRNA fluorescence imaging and turnover

text: An MS2-based reporter tracked β-actin mRNA in vivo in the cerebral cortex of live mice through optical cranial window imaging and two-photon microscopy.

quotes.quote:
A generalizable reporter based on the MS2 system
was developed to track β-actin mRNA in vivo in the cerebral
cortex of live mice through optical cranial window imaging and
two-photon (2P) microscopy.

experiment.system: live mice expressing MS2-tagged β-actin mRNA and FP-MCP
experiment.perturbation: observational in vivo imaging via cranial window
experiment.measurement: two-photon fluorescence imaging of mRNA particles

text: Using SunTag-based mRNA translation imaging platforms, the Zhuang lab identified transient regulation of translation upon environmental stress, the Singer lab's SINAPS visualized protein insertion into the ER during translation, and the Tanenbaum group characterized ribosome stalling through long-term imaging of mRNAs.

quotes.quote:
The Zhuang lab utilized their
platform to identify transient regulation of translation upon
environmental stress.144 The Singer lab applied their trans-
lation imaging system, called SINAPS (single-molecule
imaging of nascent peptides) to study subcellular translation
at the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), enabling them to visualize
protein insertion into the ER during translation.145 Finally, the
Tanenbaum group used their platform to conducted long-term
imaging of mRNAs and characterize ribosome stalling.

experiment.system: live cells expressing SunTag-based mRNA reporters with PP7/MS2 stem-loops and GFP-scFV
experiment.perturbation: environmental stress; observational long-term imaging
experiment.measurement: single-molecule fluorescence signal amplification at translating mRNAs

text: Mitochondria-targeted DsRed and mCherry tended to aggregate at lysosomes, whereas the bright, fast-maturing TurboRFP did not aggregate at lysosomes; imaging of mitochondria-targeted TurboRFP revealed that immortalized human amniotic epithelial cells can transfer healthy mitochondria to HEK293T cells with damaged mitochondrial DNA and mitochondrial dysfunction.

quotes.quote:
Yang
and colleagues recently identified aggregation of RFPs used in
the study of mitochondrial transfer, including DsRed and
mCherry. These RFPs tended to aggregate at lysosomes

Taiko et al. identified a bright, fast-maturing RFP, TurboRFP, which
did not aggregate at lysosomes and was suitable for visualizing
intercellular transfer of viable mitochondria. Imaging of
mitochondria-targeted TurboRFP revealed that immortalized
human amniotic epithelial cells can transfer healthy mitochon-
dria to HEK293T cells with damaged mitochondrial DNA and
mitochondrial dysfunction.

experiment.system: co-cultured immortalized human amniotic epithelial cells and HEK293T cells with damaged mitochondrial DNA
experiment.perturbation: expression of mitochondria-targeted RFP variants (DsRed, mCherry, TurboRFP)
experiment.measurement: fluorescence imaging of RFP localization and intercellular mitochondrial transfer

text: A BCCP/BPL biotinylation-based labeling strategy, with BCCP fused to GFP and an NLS and BPL anchored to a transmembrane domain, localized fluorescence to the nuclear envelope and enabled imaging of its breakdown and reformation during mitosis; cytoskeletal labeling of β-actin and α-tubulin was also accomplished with this approach.

quotes.quote:
BCCP-GFP-NLS interacts with BPL and local-
izes to the nuclear envelope, potentially without disrupting
native behavior. This approach enabled imaging and character-
ization of the dynamic breakdown and reformation of the
nuclear envelope during mitosis. Cytoskeletal labeling (β-actin
and α-tubulin) was also accomplished using this approach.

experiment.system: live cells expressing BCCP-GFP-NLS and membrane-anchored BPL
experiment.perturbation: biotinylation-mediated complex formation; mitotic progression
experiment.measurement: fluorescence imaging of nuclear envelope and cytoskeletal structures

text: mCherry Timer FPs used to track delivery of LAMP-2A to lysosomes suggested that LAMP-2A is trafficked first to the plasma membrane from the Golgi, then to early and recycling endosomes, and finally to lysosomes.

quotes.quote:
mCherry Timer FPs have been used
to track delivery of LAMP-2A to lysosomes and characterize its
trafficking pathway.22 Through this approach, Subach et al.
suggested that LAMP-2A is trafficked first to the plasma
membrane from the Golgi, then to early and recycling
endosomes, and finally to lysosomes.

experiment.system: cells expressing LAMP-2A tagged with mCherry Timer FP
experiment.perturbation: observational time-dependent color conversion of timer FP
experiment.measurement: blue/red fluorescence localization over trafficking route

text: A BiFC system with split Venus fragments fused to the cytoplasmic faces of ER and mitochondrial membranes detected ER-mitochondrial contact sites and identified motile ER-mito contact sites that were modulated by ER stress or serum-deprivation.

quotes.quote:
A BiFC system was used to detect ER-
mitochondrial contact sites through fusion of split Venus
fragments to the cytoplasmic faces of the ER and
mitochondrial membranes.160 This application led to the
identification of motile ER-mito contact sites that were
modulated by ER stress or serum-deprivation.

experiment.system: cells expressing split Venus targeted to ER and mitochondrial membranes
experiment.perturbation: ER stress or serum deprivation
experiment.measurement: reconstituted Venus fluorescence at contact sites and their motility

text: A FRET-FLIM system with GFP fused to the Golgi membrane protein TGN46 and mCherry to the ER membrane protein cytochrome b5 identified ER-Golgi contact sites via decreased GFP fluorescence lifetime, and was used in an siRNA screen to identify ER- and Golgi-resident proteins (including VAP and ORP proteins) involved in forming these contact sites; organelle contact site proximity is typically in the range of 10−80 nm.

quotes.quote:
Specifically, GFP
was fused to the Golgi membrane protein TGN46 and
mCherry to the ER membrane protein cytochrome b5. FRET
between the two proteins decreased the GFP fluorescence
lifetime, enabling the identification of ER-Golgi contacts using
FRET-FLIM measurements. This strategy was then used to
conduct an siRNA screen to identify the specific ER- and
Golgi-resident proteins involved in the formation of these
specific contact sites.

This proximity is
typically in the range of 10−80 nm but can occur at greater
distances as well.

experiment.system: cells expressing GFP-TGN46 and mCherry-cytochrome b5
experiment.perturbation: siRNA knockdown of candidate ER/Golgi proteins
experiment.measurement: GFP donor fluorescence lifetime (FRET-FLIM) at contact sites

text: The irreversible nature of BiFC has been exploited to 'glue' chloroplasts in plant cells to one another and regulate organellar interactions, and was later used to manipulate the plant metabolome.

quotes.quote:
the irreversible
feature of BiFC has been used to “glue” chloroplasts in plant
cells to one another and regulate organellar interactions.163
The application of BiFC as an organellar glue was later used by
Ishikawa and colleagues to manipulate the plant metabolome

experiment.system: plant cells expressing split-FP fragments targeted to chloroplasts
experiment.perturbation: irreversible BiFC complementation tethering organelles
experiment.measurement: organelle interactions and metabolome changes

text: mGRASP used GFP1−10 and GFP11 fused to fragments of the pre- and postsynaptic proteins neurexin 1β and neuroligin-1 so that proximity permits GFP reconstitution and visualization of interacting synaptic membranes; SynView subsequently fused GFP1−10 and GFP11 to the full-length synaptic proteins neurexin-1β and neuroligin-1 or neuroligin-2, marking synapses with GFP fluorescence via PPI.

quotes.quote:
Kim et al.
developed mGRASP, a fragment-complementation-based
labeling approach that utilizes GFP1−10 and GFP11 fused to
fragments of the pre- and postsynaptic proteins neurexin 1β
and neuroligin-1, such that proximity of the protein fragments
will permit GFP reconstitution and visualization of interacting
synaptic membranes.166 Tsetsenis and colleagues then
developed SynView, which fused GFP1−10 and GFP11 to the
full-length synaptic proteins (neurexin-1β and neuroligin-1 or
neuroligin-2) that bind trans-synaptically, thereby marking
synapses with GFP fluorescence via PPI.

experiment.system: neurons expressing split GFP fused to synaptic adhesion proteins
experiment.perturbation: trans-synaptic protein binding driving fragment proximity
experiment.measurement: reconstituted GFP fluorescence at synapses

text: A 'leaky FP' approach modifying mCherry with a membrane-permeable TATk peptide (sLP-mCherry), coexpressed with GFP in breast cancer cells injected into mice, allowed FACS identification of metastatic niche cells in the lung and led to identification of a lung epithelial compartment in the metastatic niche exhibiting dedifferentiation and tissue stem cell-like features.

quotes.quote:
the authors modified
mCherry with a membrane-permeable trans-activator of

transcription (TATk) peptide to generate sLP-mCherry. This
construct was coexpressed with GFP in breast cancer cells that
were introduced into mice via tail-vein injection.

The use of this FP-based technology led
to the identification of a lung epithelial compartment in the
metastatic niche that exhibits dedifferentiation and tissue stem
cell-like features.

experiment.system: mice receiving tail-vein injection of breast cancer cells expressing sLP-mCherry and GFP
experiment.perturbation: metastatic seeding to lung; FP transfer to neighboring niche cells
experiment.measurement: FACS selection for mCherry fluorescence and downstream single-cell sequencing

text: Lineage tracing was achieved via homologous recombination in mouse embryonic stem cells driving nuclear-localized Cerulean, plasma membrane-targeted mKate2, and tamoxifen-inducible EYFP expression only in melanocytes.

quotes.quote:
homologous recombination in mouse
embryonic stem cells (ESCs) was utilized to drive expression
of nuclear-localized Cerulean, plasma membrane-targeted
mKate2, and tamoxifen-inducible expression of EYFP only in
melanocytes to achieve lineage tracing.

experiment.system: mouse embryonic stem cells / melanocytes
experiment.perturbation: homologous recombination and tamoxifen induction
experiment.measurement: multicolor fluorescence lineage tracing

text: Optical barcoding introduced up to three spectrally distinct FPs combined in six different constructs into target cells as a genetic barcode; an extension using six spectrally distinct FPs with up to three colors expressed at once yielded up to 41 distinct barcodes made up of 3, 2, or 1 color, and tumor heterogeneity was characterized by identifying expressed FPs using flow cytometry.

quotes.quote:
which uses a fluorescent barcoding system with the
introduction of up to three spectrally distinct FPs, combined
in six different constructs, into target cells, wherein the
combination of FPs expressed serves as a genetic barcode for
each cell.172

Six
spectrally distinct FPs were utilized, and cells were allowed to
express up to three colors at once to yield up to 41 distinct
barcodes, made up of 3, 2, or 1 color. Tumor heterogeneity of
cell populations was characterized by identifying expressed FPs
using flow cytometry.

experiment.system: tumor cell populations expressing combinatorial FP barcodes
experiment.perturbation: introduction of combinatorial FP constructs
experiment.measurement: flow cytometry identification of expressed FP combinations

text: Multiclonal tracking of tumor cells expressing different combinations of 3 FPs yielded insights into the immune escape signature.

quotes.quote:
An analogous system was used to
conduct multiclonal tracking of tumor cells expressing different
combinations of 3 FPs to gain key biological insights into the
immune escape signature.

experiment.system: tumor cell clones labeled with FP combinations
experiment.perturbation: observational multiclonal tracking
experiment.measurement: fluorescence-based clone identification and immune escape signature

text: Katushka, a relatively bright, fast maturing, and pH- and photostable FP with an emission maximum at 635 nm extending into the infrared at >700 nm, was validated for in vivo imaging in Xenopus laevis embryos.

quotes.quote:
An early example of this type of FP is Katushka, a relatively
bright, fast maturing, and pH- and photostable FP with an
emission maximum at 635 nm that extends to the infrared at
>700 nm.176 Katushka was validated for in vivo imaging in
Xenopus laevis embryos.

experiment.system: Xenopus laevis embryos expressing Katushka
experiment.perturbation: observational in vivo imaging
experiment.measurement: far-red fluorescence emission and in vivo detectability

text: Enhanced miRFPs were used to achieve two-color, whole-body in vivo imaging in mice, and iRFP, a far-red FP that does not require biliverdin supplementation in vivo, exhibited a higher signal-to-noise ratio than comparable FPs in mice at the time of its development.

quotes.quote:
Enhanced
miRFPs were used to achieve two-color, whole-body in vivo
imaging in mice via STED microscopy.76

iRFP is one example of a far-red FP
that does not require biliverdin supplementation in vivo and
exhibited a higher signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) than comparable
FPs in mice at the time of its development.

experiment.system: mice expressing NIR/far-red FPs (miRFPs, iRFP)
experiment.perturbation: observational whole-body in vivo imaging, with/without biliverdin supplementation
experiment.measurement: multicolor fluorescence detection and signal-to-noise ratio

text: tdTomato expressed in Mycobacterium tuberculosis under an L5 mycobacterial promoter was used to image subcutaneous and pulmonary infections in live mice and determine bacterial load.

quotes.quote:
tdTomato, a red FP, was expressed in Mycobacterium
tuberculosis under an L5 mycobacterial promoter to image
subcutaneous and pulmonary infections in live mice and to
determine bacterial load.

experiment.system: live mice infected with tdTomato-expressing Mycobacterium tuberculosis
experiment.perturbation: subcutaneous and pulmonary infection
experiment.measurement: in vivo red fluorescence imaging and bacterial load

text: RFP expression combined with MRI using the clinical contrast agent gadobutrol, serving as a pseudo-optical clearing agent, enhanced in vivo imaging of fluorescently labeled subcutaneous tumor xenografts.

quotes.quote:
RFP expression has also been
combined with MRI using the clinical MR contrast agent
gadobutrol, which serves as a pseudo-optical clearing agent, to
enhance in vivo imaging of fluorescently labeled subcutaneous
tumor xenografts

experiment.system: mice bearing RFP-labeled subcutaneous tumor xenografts
experiment.perturbation: administration of gadobutrol MR contrast agent
experiment.measurement: in vivo fluorescence imaging combined with MRI

text: The ZifCY and ZapCY sensors were used to detect subcellular zinc ion (Zn2+) levels at various compartments based on their relative Zn2+ affinities.

quotes.quote:
the ZifCY and ZapCY sensors, which were used to detect
subcellular zinc ion (Zn2+) levels at various compartments
based on their relative Zn2+ affinities

experiment.system: cells expressing ZifCY and ZapCY biosensors targeted to subcellular compartments
experiment.perturbation: observational (sensor affinity variation across compartments)
experiment.measurement: sensor fluorescence readout of Zn2+ levels

text: cpFP-based single-component sensors tend to show significantly higher responses and sensitivity when compared side-by-side with similar multicomponent biosensors, though cpFPs are available in a limited range of colors; five circularly permuted far-red FPs with excitation and emission wavelengths >600 nm have been developed based on mMaroon1 and mCarmine.

quotes.quote:
Importantly, these cpFP-based single-component sensors
tend to show significantly higher responses and sensitivity
when compared side-by-side with similar multicomponent
biosensors.

five circularly permuted far-red FPs
with excitation and emission wavelengths >600 nm have been
developed based on mMaroon1 and mCarmine.

experiment.system: genetically encoded biosensors with single-FP (cpFP) versus multicomponent reporting units
experiment.perturbation: side-by-side comparison of sensor designs; circular permutation of far-red FPs
experiment.measurement: fluorescence response amplitude/sensitivity; excitation and emission wavelengths

text: The 'extension for enhanced visualization by evading extra FRET' (Eevee, or EV) linker, consisting of a series of flexible (SAGG)n repeats, separates the FPs and minimizes energy transfer in the low-FRET state, giving a greater difference between the 'on' and 'off' states of the reporter and therefore a greater dynamic range.

quotes.quote:
Another, complementary
strategy is to include a long flexible linker, such as the
“extension for enhanced visualization by evading extra FRET”
(Eevee, or EV) linker developed by Komatsu et al. in the
Matsuda lab, to separate the FPs and minimize energy transfer
in the low-FRET state.211 The EV linker consists of a series of
flexible (SAGG)n repeats

This results in a greater difference between
the “on” and “off” states of the reporter, and therefore a greater
dynamic range.

experiment.system: FRET-based genetically encoded biosensors
experiment.perturbation: insertion of long flexible (SAGG)n EV linker between sensing unit and FPs
experiment.measurement: FRET dynamic range between on and off states

text: Varying the linkers joining the cpFP to the sensing unit has allowed engineering of large improvements in dynamic range in single-component sensors; the authors state ideal linkers are difficult to determine through rational design, making random mutagenesis of linker residues the best way to develop a functional biosensor, with a single round of linker randomization and screening sometimes sufficient and more commonly several rounds of directed evolution applied.

quotes.quote:
Varying the linkers that join the cpFP
to the sensing unit has allowed for the engineering of large
improvements in dynamic range in these types of
sensors.202,212,213 The ideal linkers to use for any given
biosensor are difficult to determine through rational design,
making random mutagenesis of the linker residues the best way
to develop a functional biosensor. In some cases, a single round
of linker randomization and screening may be sufficient to
identify a well-performing sensor.213 More commonly,
however, several rounds of mutagenesis of the linkers or
other parts of the sensor are applied in a directed evolution
approach.

experiment.system: single-component (cpFP-based) genetically encoded biosensors
experiment.perturbation: random mutagenesis/randomization of linker residues and directed evolution
experiment.measurement: biosensor dynamic range and performance in screening

text: Kinase translocation reporters fuse a single FP to a kinase substrate containing both a nuclear localization and nuclear export signal, such that phosphorylation of the substrate disrupts the NLS and nuclear export of fluorescence serves as the readout.

quotes.quote:
Kinase translocation reporters
(KTRs) are another type of translocation-based sensor, in
which a single FP is fused to a kinase substrate that contains
both a nuclear localization (NLS) and nuclear export signal
(NES). Upon phosphorylation of the substrate, the NLS is
disrupted, allowing nuclear export of fluorescence to serve as
the readout

experiment.system: cells expressing kinase translocation reporters
experiment.perturbation: kinase-mediated phosphorylation of the substrate peptide
experiment.measurement: nucleocytoplasmic distribution of FP fluorescence

text: LLPS-based sensor designs fuse each half of a split sensing unit to an oligomerization domain such as tetrameric or hexameric HOTag coiled-coils, so that activation of a cellular signal triggers multivalent interactions and formation of droplet-like biosensor condensates visualized as redistribution of FP fluorescence from the cytosol to punctate structures.

quotes.quote:
LLPS-based sensor designs utilize
a bimolecular design, in which each half of the split sensing
unit is fused to an oligomerization domain, such as tetrameric
or hexameric HOTag coiled-coils. One part of this bimolecular
switch also incorporates the FP reporting unit. Activation of a
cellular signal triggers multivalent interactions between sensing
unit oligomers, resulting in the formation of droplet-like
biosensor condensates, visualized as the redistribution of FP
fluorescence from the cytosol to these punctate structures

experiment.system: cells expressing split LLPS-based biosensors with HOTag oligomerization domains
experiment.perturbation: activation of the target cellular signal
experiment.measurement: redistribution of FP fluorescence into punctate condensates

text: ddFP pairs consist of a dimly fluorescent FP-A and a nonfluorescent FP-B in which FP-A greatly increases in brightness upon binding of FP-B, and ratiometric readouts can be obtained via ddFP exchange, in which multiple FP-As of different colors compete for the same FP-B.

quotes.quote:
ddFP pairs consist of a dimly fluorescent
FP-A and a nonfluorescent FP-B, in which FP-A greatly
increases in brightness upon binding of FP-B

a ratiometric readout
can be obtained by taking advantage of the fact that multiple
FP-As (e.g., RFP-A and GFP-A) can bind the same FP-B,
leading to a phenomenon known as ddFP exchange.

experiment.system: dimerization-dependent FP pairs (ddRFP, ddGFP, ddYFP) in biosensor scaffolds
experiment.perturbation: sensing-unit conformational change altering ddFP dimer formation
experiment.measurement: fluorescence intensity or emission ratio

text: A single cysteine-to-serine mutation in the peroxide sensor HyPer yields SypHer, a "dead" sensor insensitive to peroxide but still sensitive to pH, used to account for pH changes in HyPer and HyPerRed experiments.

quotes.quote:
in the case of peroxide sensors like
HyPer or HyPerRed, a single mutation of a cysteine to a serine
renders HyPer insensitive to peroxide, but still sensitive to
pH.223 This “dead” sensor, termed SypHer, has subsequently
been used to account for pH changes in peroxide-sensing
experiments with HyPer and HyPerRed.

experiment.system: HyPer/HyPerRed peroxide biosensors in cells
experiment.perturbation: cysteine-to-serine point mutation of the sensing cysteine
experiment.measurement: fluorescence response to peroxide versus pH

text: Histidine scanning of the GFP chromophore environment produced ratiometric pHluorin, whose 395/470 nm excitation ratio increases with pH between pH 7.5−5.5, and ecliptic pHluorin, which loses fluorescence at 470 nm excitation with acidification, with complete loss at pH < 6.0.

quotes.quote:
Ratiometric pHluorin increases in excitation ratio (395/470
nm) with increasing pH (between pH 7.5−5.5), whereas
ecliptic pHluorin decreases in fluorescence at 470 nm
excitation with more acidic pH, with complete loss of
fluorescence at pH < 6.0.230

experiment.system: GFP-derived pH sensors (pHluorin variants)
experiment.perturbation: histidine-scanning mutagenesis of chromophore H-bond network residues; pH titration
experiment.measurement: excitation ratio 395/470 nm and 470 nm excited fluorescence intensity versus pH

numbers.quantity: pH range of ratiometric pHluorin response
pH of complete fluorescence loss for ecliptic pHluorin

text: pHLIM uses pH-dependent changes in the fluorescence lifetime of mApple to sense pH from 4.6 to 7.4 and was used to detect the pH of endolysosomal compartments in mammalian cells.

quotes.quote:
relied upon pH-dependent changes in the
fluorescence lifetime of mApple, a red-emitting FP

This
new sensor can sense pH changes from 4.6 to 7.4 and was
utilized to detect the pH of various endolysosomal compart-
ments in mammalian cells.

experiment.system: pHLIM sensor in mammalian cells
experiment.perturbation: pH variation across endolysosomal compartments
experiment.measurement: fluorescence lifetime of mApple

text: pH-Lemon, a FRET sensor pairing pH-sensitive EYFP with pH-resistant mTurquoise2, reports acidification as an increased cyan-to-yellow emission ratio for pH changes from 7.5 to 4.5.

quotes.quote:
As the EYFP
chromophore becomes protonated and thus quenched under
acidic conditions, the FRET efficiency decreases, resulting in
an increased cyan-to-yellow emission ratio for detecting
changes in pH from 7.5 to 4.5.

experiment.system: pH-Lemon FRET biosensor in acidic cellular compartments
experiment.perturbation: acidification of the compartment
experiment.measurement: cyan-to-yellow emission ratio (FRET efficiency)

text: RpH-LAMP1-3xFLAG, a ratiometric pHluorin-mCherry sensor fused to LAMP1, localized to lysosomes and reported lysosomal pH from 7.1−4.2, tracking pH over 5 h across cell cycle stages and during cell migration.

quotes.quote:
The sensor was well localized to lysosomes and
exhibited sensitivity to pH values relevant to the lysosomal
lumen (pH 7.1−4.2). Using this biosensor, pH was tracked in
the lysosomes of cells undergoing various stages of the cell
cycle over 5 h and during cell migration.239

experiment.system: lysosomes of cultured cells expressing RpH-LAMP1-3xFLAG
experiment.perturbation: observational tracking across cell cycle stages and migration
experiment.measurement: ratiometric pHluorin/mCherry emission as lysosomal pH

text: FIRE-pHLy, built from mTFP1 and mCherry sandwiching LAMP1, detects lysosomal pH within 6.0−3.5 and was used in primary neurons and iPSCs to study lysosomal pH during neurodegeneration and aging.

quotes.quote:
Ponsford and colleagues developed FIRE-pHLy, another
ratiometric pH sensor for detecting lysosomal pH within the
range of 6.0−3.5.

The sensor was used in
primary neurons and iPSCs to elucidate lysosomal pH changes
during neurodegeneration and aging.240

experiment.system: primary neurons and iPSCs expressing FIRE-pHLy
experiment.perturbation: observational (neurodegeneration and aging contexts)
experiment.measurement: ratiometric mTFP1/mCherry emission as lysosomal pH

text: Neuronal exocytic vesicles are acidic (pH 5.6) and become alkaline (pH 7.4) upon fusion with the plasma membrane, a change tracked with pH sensors.

quotes.quote:
At
neuronal synapses, exocytic vesicles are acidic (pH 5.6) but
become alkaline (pH 7.4) upon fusion with the plasma
membrane.231

experiment.system: neuronal synapses
experiment.perturbation: vesicle fusion with plasma membrane during exocytosis
experiment.measurement: luminal pH reported by pH-sensitive FPs

text: Tandem mRFP-GFP fused to LC3 reports autophagy progression because GFP fluorescence is quenched upon autophagosome-lysosome fusion while mRFP fluorescence remains stable.

quotes.quote:
Kimura et al. fused
mRFP and GFP in tandem to LC3 to be expressed in the
autophagosome lumen. Upon autophagosome fusion with
lysosomes, GFP fluorescence is quenched, but mRFP
fluorescence is stable, providing a fluorescent readout of
autophagy progression.250

experiment.system: live cells expressing mRFP-GFP-LC3 in the autophagosome lumen
experiment.perturbation: autophagy induction / autophagosome-lysosome fusion
experiment.measurement: GFP vs mRFP fluorescence in puncta

text: mito-SRAI, a FRET sensor pairing acid-resistant afCFP (TOLLES) with acid-denatured YPet, was targeted to the mitochondrial matrix to detect mitophagy in mouse embryonic fibroblasts and in vivo in nondopaminergic neurons of the mouse midbrain, and was used in a high-throughput screen that identified several hits inducing mitophagy.

quotes.quote:
SRAI was targeted
to the mitochondrial matrix to enable detection of mitophagy
in mouse embryonic fibroblasts and in vivo in nondopaminer-
gic neurons of the mouse midbrain. Furthermore, mito-SRAI
was used to screen for therapeutic inducers of mitophagy in a
high-throughput context. Katayama and colleagues identified
several hits that induce mitophagy in cells,255

experiment.system: mouse embryonic fibroblasts, mouse midbrain neurons in vivo, and high-throughput cell screen
experiment.perturbation: mitophagy induction; compound library screening
experiment.measurement: FRET between TOLLES and YPet reporting compartment acidification

text: GFP fluorescence polarization was used as a thermal nanoprobe to map intracellular temperature in HeLa and U87 glioma cells with 0.4 °C temperature precision.

quotes.quote:
Another study in 2012 also directly
used GFP as a thermal nanoprobe to map intracellular
temperature in HeLa and U87 glioma cells with 0.4 °C
temperature precision.

experiment.system: HeLa and U87 glioma cells expressing GFP
experiment.perturbation: intracellular temperature variation
experiment.measurement: fluorescence polarization of GFP emission

text: mRFP1 variants in E. coli showed fluorescence intensity decreasing with increasing temperature, with a temperature change from 4 to 40 °C yielding a 40.5% decrease in fluorescence intensity, attributed by the authors to thermal quenching.

quotes.quote:
Fluorescence intensity
decreased with increasing temperature, which Deepankumar
and colleagues postulated was due to thermal quenching of
mRFP1 fluorescence, wherein a temperature change from 4 to
40 °C yielded a 40.5% decrease in fluorescence intensity.262

experiment.system: mRFP1 variants expressed in E. coli
experiment.perturbation: temperature change from 4 to 40 °C
experiment.measurement: fluorescence intensity

text: B-gTEMP, a tandem fusion of mNeonGreen and tdTomato relying on thermal quenching, reports temperature with 155 μs time resolution and 0.042 °C temperature resolution.

quotes.quote:
B-gTEMP incorporates
the tandem fusion of mNeonGreen and tdTomato to report on
temperature changes with greater SNR, faster kinetics, and
greater sensitivity (155 μs time resolution, 0.042 °C temper-
ature resolution).

experiment.system: B-gTEMP ratiometric temperature sensor
experiment.perturbation: temperature changes
experiment.measurement: ratiometric fluorescence intensity; time and temperature resolution

text: ELP-TEMP, a FRET sensor with an elastin-like polypeptide between mTurquoise2 and mVenus, exhibited the highest temperature sensitivity available at the time, 45.1 ± 8.1% response/1 °C in the range of 33−40 °C.

quotes.quote:
ELP-
TEMP exhibited the highest temperature sensitivity (45.1 ±
8.1% response/1 °C in the range of 33−40 °C) compared with
other sensors available at the time.265

experiment.system: ELP-TEMP FRET temperature sensor
experiment.perturbation: temperature change within 33−40 °C
experiment.measurement: FRET efficiency response per °C

text: stFRET, a Cerulean-Venus pair linked by an α helix, showed reduced FRET upon force loading and, when inserted into actinin and filamin, revealed greater mechanical stress at the leading edge of migrating cells than at the trailing edge; an improved variant with a more relaxed helical peptide gave a 50% decrease in FRET within the 5−7 pN range.

quotes.quote:
when inserted into actinin and filamin, stFRET
revealed greater mechanical stress at the leading edge of
migrating cells than at the trailing edge.275 stFRET was later
improved by incorporating a more relaxed (less rigid) helical
peptide as the sensing unit to achieve a wider dynamic range
within the 5−7 pN range (50% decrease in FRET in response
to increased force)

experiment.system: stFRET inserted into actinin and filamin in migrating cells
experiment.perturbation: mechanical force loading during cell migration
experiment.measurement: FRET efficiency

text: cpstFRET, using circularly permuted Cerulean and Venus, positioned the FRET pair closer in the relaxed state to maximize signal difference and has 30% lower molecular weight than the original stFRET.

quotes.quote:
Incorporating
circularly permuted versions of Cerulean and Venus allowed
the FRET pair to be positioned closer together and in a more
favorable orientation in the basal (relaxed) state, thus
maximizing the signal difference from the stretched state.277
An added benefit of this variant is its smaller size (30% lower
molecular weight) compared to the original stFRET

experiment.system: cpstFRET strain sensor
experiment.perturbation: circular permutation of the FRET pair; mechanical stretch
experiment.measurement: FRET signal difference between relaxed and stretched states; molecular weight

text: TSMod, a 40-amino-acid flagelliform elastic domain between Venus and mTFP1 inserted into vinculin, was responsive to stress from 1 to 6 pN in laser-tweezer validation and revealed higher force in focal adhesions at the leading edge than at the trailing edge of migrating cells.

quotes.quote:
In vitro validation using
laser tweezers to cyclically apply stress revealed that the sensor
is responsive to stress from 1 to 6 pN. In live cells, the
mechanical force experienced by vinculin during cell migration
was mapped to reveal higher force in focal adhesions at the
leading edge of the cell compared with the trailing edge.278

experiment.system: TSMod inserted into vinculin; in vitro purified sensor and live migrating cells
experiment.perturbation: cyclic stress application with laser tweezers; cell migration
experiment.measurement: FRET efficiency versus applied force

text: HP35-based tension sensors between YPet and mCherry, using the 35-amino-acid villin headpiece peptide or its HP35st mutant, gave sensors with response thresholds of 7 and 10 pN and were incorporated into Talin to characterize forces during cell adhesion and rigidity sensing.

quotes.quote:
HP35 is an ultrafast-folding peptide that goes through an
equilibrium unfolding/folding transition in response to
mechanical forces of ∼7 pN, and a mutant version responds
to 10 pN forces (HP35st). By incorporating either of these two
peptides, two different sensors were developed with response
thresholds of 7 and 10 pN.

experiment.system: HP35/HP35st tension sensors inserted into Talin in cells
experiment.perturbation: mechanical force during cell adhesion and extracellular rigidity sensing
experiment.measurement: FRET between YPet and mCherry

text: A condensation-based force sensor with dimeric coiled coils that unfold under forces of 2−14 pN was inserted into the yeast endocytic protein Hip1R with a C-terminal GFP, and condensate diameter and number per cell served as the force readout.

quotes.quote:
Ren et al’s biosensor
includes dimeric coiled coils that unfold to expose hydro-
phobic interaction surfaces upon exposure to forces in the
range of 2−14 pN.

Quantification of condensate diameter and number of
condensates per cell served as a readout of force.

experiment.system: yeast endocytic sites, Hip1R-coiled-coil-GFP fusion
experiment.perturbation: endogenous mechanical force at endocytic sites
experiment.measurement: condensate diameter and number of condensates per cell

text: Three FRET sensors built with 25-, 40-, and 50-amino-acid spider silk peptide repeats detected a wider range of forces, with the shortest peptide giving the widest sensing range at 2−11 pN.

quotes.quote:
Three
FRET sensors were developed in 2016 incorporating 25-, 40-,
and 50-amino-acid peptide repeats from spider silk to detect a
wider range of forces, with the shortest peptide having the
widest range of force sensing at 2−11 pN.284

experiment.system: FRET tension sensors with spider silk peptide repeats
experiment.perturbation: varying peptide repeat length; applied force
experiment.measurement: FRET-based force sensing range

text: FL-TSM, a FRET tension sensor with a ferredoxin-like linker between YPet and mCherry, is sensitive to 3−5 pN forces and gives a digital response above a ~3 pN threshold; it was tested in talin and multiplexed with an orthogonal mTFP1/LSSmOrange talin sensor.

quotes.quote:
This sensor is sensitive to 3−5 pN forces,
and incorporates a ferredoxin-like linker peptide that has a
more immediate response to forces above a certain threshold
(∼3 pN) to yield a “digital response”.

experiment.system: FL-TSM inserted into talin in cells
experiment.perturbation: mechanical force on talin; multiplexing with orthogonal talin sensor
experiment.measurement: FRET between YPet and mCherry

text: A rational tension-sensor design study in vinculin identified the mechanical properties and length of the tension sensing domain, the physical separation between the two FP chromophores, and the relative orientation of the two FPs as the most important determinants of mechanical sensitivity.

quotes.quote:
The most important properties that defined
the mechanical sensitivity of tension sensors were identified to
be the mechanical properties and length of the tension sensing
domain, the physical separation between the two FP
chromophores, and the relative orientation of the two FPs.

experiment.system: tension sensors expressed in vinculin in cells (in cellulo characterization plus in silico modeling)
experiment.perturbation: systematic modification of sensor tension-sensing domains and FP arrangement
experiment.measurement: predicted and measured sensor mechanical sensitivity

text: CrGE, a FRET molecular crowding sensor with two α-helical peptides between mCerulean and mCitrine, showed increased FRET under high-crowding conditions in vitro with Ficoll PM70 or PEG and in E. coli, and was not sensitive to small molecules, ions, or DNA.

quotes.quote:
CrGE was characterized in vitro using Ficoll
PM70 or polyethylene glycol (PEG) as the crowding agent, as
well as in E. coli. Increased FRET was observed under high-
crowding conditions. Importantly, CrGE is not sensitive to
small molecules, ions, or DNA.

experiment.system: purified CrGE in vitro and expressed in E. coli
experiment.perturbation: addition of crowding agents Ficoll PM70 or PEG
experiment.measurement: FRET efficiency

text: CrGE2.3, using mEGFP and mScarlet-I, revealed age-dependent changes in organellar crowding in yeast and that stability of crowding, rather than absolute crowding levels, predicted lifespan; its FPs had similar maturation kinetics, making it suitable for long-term imaging unlike the original CrGE.

quotes.quote:
CrGE2.3 was used to
reveal age-dependent changes in organellar crowding in yeast
and that stability of crowding, rather than absolute crowding
levels, was a suitable predictor of lifespan in this model
organism. The FPs in CrGE2.3 had similar chromophore
maturation kinetics, which made this sensor more suitable for
long-term imaging experiments, whereas the original CrGE was
limited to short-term imaging.288

experiment.system: yeast expressing CrGE2.3
experiment.perturbation: aging (observational over lifespan)
experiment.measurement: FRET-reported organellar crowding correlated with lifespan

text: CRONOS targeted to the nucleolus via fusion to NPM1 reported reduced molecular crowding within the nucleolus upon inhibition of transcription or induction of environmental stress.

quotes.quote:
Upon inhibition
of transcription or induction of environmental stress, molecular
crowding levels within the nucleolus were reduced, as sensed
by CRONOS.290

experiment.system: cells expressing CRONOS-NPM1 targeted to the nucleolus
experiment.perturbation: transcription inhibition or environmental stress
experiment.measurement: FRET between mNeonGreen and mScarlet-I as crowding readout

text: Monomeric FPs including mCherry, mRFP, mCitrine, and mEGFP showed significant decreases in fluorescence lifetime in vitro upon PEG exposure; mCherry-tagged HP1α lifetime imaging revealed a transition to less heterogeneous, less dense nuclear condensates in early differentiated versus undifferentiated mouse embryonic stem cells.

quotes.quote:
certain monomeric FPs,
including mCherry, mRFP, mCitrine, and mEGFP, exhibited
significant decreases in fluorescence lifetime in vitro upon
exposure to polyethylene glycol PEG.

Upon differentiation, the biosensor revealed a
transition to a less heterogeneous and less dense population of
nuclear condensates compared to the highly heterogeneous
distribution of condensates in undifferentiated cells.

experiment.system: purified monomeric FPs in vitro; mCherry-HP1α in mouse embryonic stem cells
experiment.perturbation: PEG crowding in vitro; stem cell differentiation
experiment.measurement: fluorescence lifetime

text: FLaSH, the first VSD-based voltage biosensor, inserts GFP into the cytosolic C-terminal tail of the Shaker K+ channel after S6 and shows an ~5% decrease in GFP fluorescence intensity upon membrane depolarization.

quotes.quote:
Upon membrane depolarization, the channel undergoes a
conformational change that leads to an ∼5% decrease in GFP
fluorescence intensity.

experiment.system: FLaSH (GFP in Shaker K+ channel C-terminal tail)
experiment.perturbation: membrane depolarization
experiment.measurement: GFP fluorescence intensity change

text: Mermaid, a FRET GEVI using the Ci-VSP VSD with UKG and mKO, gave a 40% emission ratio change upon a 100 mV voltage change but had fast (7.3−17.4 ms) and slow (98−638 ms) response components; Mermaid2 with CFP/YFP improved kinetics to 0.93 ms "on" and 10.3 ms "off".

quotes.quote:
Mermaid yielded a greatly improved dynamic
range, with a 40% emission ratio change upon a 100 mV
voltage change. However, the biosensor response exhibited fast
(7.3−17.4 ms) and slow (98−638 ms) components

resulting in
slightly improved dynamic range and “on”/”off” kinetics (0.93
ms “on”, 10.3 ms “off”).304

experiment.system: Mermaid and Mermaid2 FRET GEVIs in cells
experiment.perturbation: 100 mV membrane depolarization
experiment.measurement: emission ratio change and on/off response kinetics

text: ArcLight A242, combining Ci-VSD with ecliptic pHluorin carrying an A227D mutation, exhibited a 35% fluorescence intensity decrease in response to 100 mV depolarization in HEK293 cells but with ~10 ms response time lacked temporal resolution for spike detection; the variant Bongwoori resolved action potentials with a response time of approximately 6−7 ms.

quotes.quote:
The final ArcLight A242 variant exhibited a 35% fluorescence
intensity decrease in response to 100 mV depolarization in
HEK293 cells. Despite the high voltage sensitivity, ArcLight
lacked the temporal resolution necessary for spike detection
(∼10 ms reported response time).

including the
GEVI Bongwoori, which was able to resolve action potentials
in neurons with a reported response time of approximately 6−
7 ms.298

experiment.system: ArcLight variants in HEK293 cells and neurons
experiment.perturbation: 100 mV membrane depolarization; action potentials
experiment.measurement: fluorescence intensity change and response time

text: ASAP1, made by inserting cpGFP into the S3−S4 extracellular loop of Gallus gallus VSP, loses fluorescence upon depolarization with on/off kinetics of ~2 ms.

quotes.quote:
observed that the inserted cpGFP undergoes a loss of
fluorescence intensity in response to membrane depolarization.
ASAP1 was a great improvement in terms of response time,
with on/off kinetics of ∼2 ms

experiment.system: ASAP1 (cpGFP in S3−S4 loop of Gallus gallus VSP) in cells
experiment.perturbation: membrane depolarization
experiment.measurement: fluorescence intensity change and on/off kinetics

text: ASAP4e, generated by screening mutations at two GFP sites to invert the response followed by structure-guided tuning, yields a 210% fluorescence increase within the physiological voltage range with activation kinetics of 2.6 ms at room temperature, and was used for long-term in vivo imaging of voltage and Ca2+ in behaving mice.

quotes.quote:
These efforts
yielded a sensor with a 210% fluorescence increase within the
physiological voltage range, along with high temporal
resolution (activation kinetics of 2.6 ms at room temperature).
These properties of ASAP4e were harnessed to achieve long-
term in vivo imaging of voltage and Ca2+ changes in behaving
mice.215

experiment.system: ASAP4e in cells and in behaving mice
experiment.perturbation: mutational screening at two GFP sites; membrane depolarization
experiment.measurement: fluorescence increase and activation kinetics

text: Archer1, incorporating Arch3 (D95E//T99C) with EGFP plus membrane-trafficking and ER-export sequences, exhibits a 25−40% fluorescence intensity change in response to action potentials and was used to image neuronal network activity in C. elegans.

quotes.quote:
Archer1 incorporates Arch3
(D95E//T99C) tagged with EGFP as a reference, along with
membrane-trafficking and ER-export sequences to enhance
plasma membrane localization, and exhibits a 25−40%
fluorescence intensity change in response to action poten-
tials.316

experiment.system: Archer1 in neurons and C. elegans neuronal networks
experiment.perturbation: action potentials
experiment.measurement: fluorescence intensity change

text: Four eFRET GEVIs made by fusing QuasAr2 to eGFP, Citrine, mOrange2, or mRuby2 generated average intensity decreases ranging from 7.7 to 13.1% following 100 mV membrane depolarization in HEK293 cells.

quotes.quote:
They introduced 4
new GEVIs by fusing QuasAr2310 to eGFP, Citrine, mOrange2,
or mRuby2. These sensors generated average intensity
decreases ranging from 7.7 to 13.1% following 100 mV
membrane depolarization in HEK293 cells.

experiment.system: QuasAr2-based eFRET GEVIs in HEK293 cells
experiment.perturbation: 100 mV membrane depolarization
experiment.measurement: average donor fluorescence intensity decrease

text: Screening 13 short linkers in the red GEVI scaffold VSD-FR189−188 yielded variants with 25-fold faster response kinetics, and one linker length inverted the fluorescence change from negative to positive, though dynamic range was not improved.

quotes.quote:
A total of 13 different
short linkers were tested, yielding variants with 25-fold faster
response kinetics. A specific linker length that inverts the
fluorescence change from negative to positive was also
identified

While dynamic range was not improved, the rapid
kinetics are a significant improvement.

experiment.system: red GEVI scaffold VSD-FR189−188 (CiVSD in cpFusionRed)
experiment.perturbation: testing 13 different short linkers
experiment.measurement: response kinetics, direction of fluorescence change, dynamic range

text: The Photopick screening platform, using coexpressed photoconvertible mEos4a for phototagging, patterned illumination and FACS sorting of mutant GEVI libraries, evolved Arch-based GEVIs into QuasAr6a (improved SNR) and QuasAr6b (improved kinetics) with higher brightness in cultured neurons and in vivo mouse brains.

quotes.quote:
a new screening
platform was developed in 2023, called Photopick,217 which
was used to evolve Arch-based GEVIs to generate variants with
improved SNR (QuasAr6a) and kinetics (QuasAr6b), as well
as higher brightness in cultured neurons and in vivo mouse
brains.

experiment.system: mutant GEVI libraries in mammalian cells, cultured neurons, mouse brain in vivo
experiment.perturbation: directed evolution with mEos4a phototagging, patterned illumination, FACS sorting
experiment.measurement: SNR, kinetics, brightness of GEVI variants

text: Replacing ECFP with mCerulean3 in the Cameleon scaffold improved emission-ratiometric FRET performance and gave single-exponential fluorescence decay for FLIM readout, enabling detection of mitochondrial Ca2+ changes in brain slices and cardiomyocytes.

quotes.quote:
A
recent development along these lines saw the replacement of
ECFP in the Cameleon scaffold with mCerulean3 to detect
mitochondrial changes in Ca2+ in both brain slices and
cardiomyocytes. mCerulean3 has improved quantum yield
compared to ECFP, resulting in better performance in
emission-ratiometric FRET imaging, as well as a single-
exponential fluorescence decay, enabling improved readout
using FLIM.339

experiment.system: Cameleon-scaffold GECI in brain slices and cardiomyocytes
experiment.perturbation: replacement of ECFP donor with mCerulean3
experiment.measurement: emission-ratiometric FRET and fluorescence lifetime (FLIM)

text: Troponin C-based Twitch Ca2+ sensors contain two Ca2+ binding sites compared to four in CaM/M13, giving a more linear Ca2+ response and less Ca2+ buffering.

quotes.quote:
These troponin-based Ca2+ sensors
contain fewer Ca2+ binding sites as compared to CaM/M13
(two as compared to four), which results in a Ca2+ sensor with
a more linear response to Ca2+, and less buffering of
Ca2+.342,343

experiment.system: Twitch series FRET Ca2+ sensors versus CaM/M13-based sensors
experiment.perturbation: substitution of Troponin C C-terminus as Ca2+ binding domain
experiment.measurement: linearity of Ca2+ response and Ca2+ buffering

numbers.quantity: Ca2+ binding sites, troponin vs CaM/M13

text: GCaMP, using CaM/M13 flanking cpEGFP, elicited 150% ΔF/F upon purinergic receptor stimulation and allowed improved imaging of Ca2+ transients in HEK cells and mouse myotubes.

quotes.quote:
utilizes the CaM/M13
Ca2+ sensing domain flanking cpEGFP, which elicits large
changes in fluorescence upon Ca2+ binding (150% ΔF/F upon
purinergic receptor stimulation). The improved brightness and
dynamic range of this sensor over previous cpFP-based
scaffolds allowed for improved imaging of Ca2+ transients in
HEK cells and mouse myotubes.210

experiment.system: GCaMP expressed in HEK cells and mouse myotubes
experiment.perturbation: purinergic receptor stimulation
experiment.measurement: ΔF/F fluorescence change

text: G-GECO1 was derived from GCaMP3 by directed evolution and error-prone PCR with a colony-based screen, and contained four mutations relative to GCaMP3, two within the FP and two within the CaM portion.

quotes.quote:
The resulting G-GECO
construct contained four mutations relative to GCaMP3,
with two mutations within the FP itself, and two within the
CaM portion of the sensor.

experiment.system: GCaMP3-derived variant library in bacterial colonies
experiment.perturbation: directed evolution and random mutagenesis via error-prone PCR
experiment.measurement: colony-based screen for Ca2+-dependent fluorescence change; mutation identification

text: NEMO sensors, based on mNeonGreen, exhibited a dynamic range of over 400-fold compared to 15.8-fold for NCaMP7.

quotes.quote:
The dynamic range of mNeonGreen-based sensors
was further improved with the development of NEMO sensors,
which exhibited a dynamic range of over 400-fold as compared
to 15.8-fold for NCaMP7.348

experiment.system: NEMO and NCaMP7 mNeonGreen-based GECIs
experiment.perturbation: Ca2+ binding/saturation
experiment.measurement: fluorescence dynamic range fold change

text: Tq-Ca-FLITS, an mTurquoise2-based single-FP Ca2+ sensor, shows a 1.3 ns change in fluorescence lifetime upon intracellular Ca2+ elevation with ionomycin, and frequency-domain FLIM enabled quantified Ca2+ monitoring during trans-endothelial leukocyte migration with a time resolution of around 13 s.

quotes.quote:
Tq-Ca-FLITS shows a 1.3 ns change in
fluorescence lifetime in response to intracellular Ca2+ elevation
using the Ca2+ ionophore ionomycin.201

quantification during trans-endothelial migration of leukocytes,
with a time-resolution of around 13 s.

experiment.system: cells and organoids expressing Tq-Ca-FLITS
experiment.perturbation: ionomycin-induced intracellular Ca2+ elevation; leukocyte trans-endothelial migration
experiment.measurement: fluorescence lifetime by frequency-domain FLIM

text: CaMPARI, a circularly permuted mEos2 coupled to a CaM/M13 switch, undergoes green-to-red photoconversion under violet light only in the presence of Ca2+, providing an integrated record of Ca2+ events; it also shows an inverse (decreasing green) Ca2+-dependent intensity response.

quotes.quote:
However, CaMPARI also displays the green-to-
red photoconversion behavior of mEos2 when exposed to
violet light, but only in the presence of Ca2+. Thus, a readout of
red fluorescence can be used to provide an integrated record of
Ca2+ signaling events that occurred over the course of the
experiment time, defined by violet illumination.

experiment.system: CaMPARI expressed in cells
experiment.perturbation: violet light illumination in the presence or absence of Ca2+
experiment.measurement: green-to-red photoconversion and green fluorescence intensity

text: Recent work reported that CaMPARI2 has not only lower basal photoactivation rates but also lower Ca2+-induced photoactivation in vivo compared to CaMPARI, suggesting it is less effective as a Ca2+ integrator than the original construct.

quotes.quote:
recent work by Das et al. has
suggested that the modifications made in generating
CaMPARI2 resulted in not only in lower basal photoactivation
rates but also lower Ca2+-induced photoactivation in vivo as
compared to CaMPARI.352 This work suggests that
CaMPARI2 is thus actually less effective as a Ca2+ integrator
than the original construct

experiment.system: CaMPARI2 versus CaMPARI in vivo
experiment.perturbation: Ca2+-dependent violet photoconversion
experiment.measurement: basal and Ca2+-induced photoactivation rates

text: The FRET Zn2+ sensor eZinCh-2 exhibits a ΔR/R0 of 4 and a Kd of ~1 nM, though eZinCh sensors are prone to aggregation, notably for ER-targeted versions.

quotes.quote:
eZinCh series, with eZinCh-2 exhibiting a ΔR/R0 of 4 and a Kd
of ∼1 nM.357 However, the eZinCh sensors are prone to
aggregation, demonstrated especially in the case of ER-targeted
sensors

experiment.system: eZinCh-2 FRET Zn2+ sensor (including ER-targeted versions)
experiment.perturbation: Zn2+ titration
experiment.measurement: emission ratio change ΔR/R0 and apparent Kd

text: eCALWY, using weakly associating non-monomeric FPs to stabilize the Zn2+-free high-FRET state, has slightly lower Zn2+ affinity but a 2.4-fold emission ratio change upon Zn2+ binding.

quotes.quote:
This
modification resulted in a sensor with slightly lower Zn2+
affinity but a 2.4-fold emission ratio change upon Zn2+
binding.360

experiment.system: eCALWY FRET Zn2+ sensor
experiment.perturbation: substitution with weakly associating non-monomeric FPs; Zn2+ binding
experiment.measurement: emission ratio change and Zn2+ affinity

text: The ZifCY Cys2His2 zinc-finger sensor showed a 2.2-fold emission ratio change with an apparent affinity of 1.7 μM, while the His4 variant showed a 4-fold ratio change with a 160 μM Kd; the sensors were used to investigate glutamate uptake and mitochondrial Zn2+ sequestration.

quotes.quote:
The Cys2His2 version demonstrated a 2.2-fold change in
emission ratio with an apparent affinity of 1.7 μM, while the
His4 version showed a 4-fold ratio change and had a 160 μM
Kd.361 These sensors were used to investigate the connection
between glutamate uptake and mitochondrial Zn2+ sequestra-
tion.

experiment.system: ZifCY FRET Zn2+ sensor variants in cells
experiment.perturbation: Cys2His2 versus His4 zinc-finger variants; Zn2+ titration and glutamate uptake
experiment.measurement: emission ratio change and apparent Zn2+ affinity

text: ZapCY, optimized from Zap1 zinc fingers with Ca2+-sensor-like linkers and Citrine in place of YFP, detected ER Zn2+ changes that ZifCY could not, but was basally saturated when expressed in the cytosol.

quotes.quote:
While ZifCY was unable to detect changes in Zn2+
in the ER, the more sensitive ZapCY could do so, although it
was basally saturated when expressed in the cytosol.

experiment.system: ZapCY and ZifCY FRET Zn2+ sensors targeted to the ER and cytosol of cells
experiment.perturbation: linker modification and YFP-to-Citrine swap; Zn2+ changes
experiment.measurement: FRET emission ratio in ER and cytosol

text: ZapCV2, made by replacing the YFP acceptor with cpVenus, has a Zn2+ affinity leaving it partially saturated at rest in the cytosol of most mammalian cells, enabling detection of both increases and decreases in Zn2+, and was used to correlate Zn2+ dynamics with ERK and Akt signaling.

quotes.quote:
ZapCV2 additionally exhibits a
Zn2+ affinity that allows it to be partially saturated at rest in the
cytosol of most mammalian cells, enabling this sensor to detect
both increases and decreases in Zn2+.363 ZapCV2 has
subsequently been used to correlate Zn2+ dynamics with
ERK and Akt signaling.364

experiment.system: ZapCV2 in cytosol of mammalian cells
experiment.perturbation: YFP acceptor replaced with cpVenus; Zn2+ increases and decreases
experiment.measurement: FRET emission ratio; correlation with ERK and Akt signaling

text: An anisotropy and dynamic light-scattering assay determined that the eCFP and Venus FRET partners in ZifCV1.173 dimerized in the absence of Zn2+, prompting rational design of variants altering dimerization affinity.

quotes.quote:
Slocum and co-workers used an
anisotropy and dynamic light-scattering-based assay to
determine that the eCFP and Venus FRET partners in
ZifCV1.173 dimerized in the absence of Zn2+, prompting
efforts to rationally design variants that increase or decrease
dimerization affinity and improve dynamic range.365

experiment.system: ZifCV1.173 sensor in vitro
experiment.perturbation: absence versus presence of Zn2+
experiment.measurement: fluorescence anisotropy and dynamic light scattering to assess FP dimerization

text: Using the acceptor FP in the FRET-based ZapCY1 and eCALWY-4 sensors as a pH sensor enabled pH corrections to Zn2+ measurements in populations of vesicles.

quotes.quote:
Recent work by Pratt and co-workers addresses
this problem in part by using the acceptor FP in the FRET-
based ZapCY1 and eCALWY-4 sensors as a pH sensor,
enabling pH corrections to Zn2+ measurements in populations
of vesicles.366

experiment.system: vesicle populations expressing ZapCY1 and eCALWY-4
experiment.perturbation: pH variation across compartments
experiment.measurement: acceptor FP fluorescence as pH readout used to correct Zn2+ FRET measurements

text: GZnP3, using Zap1 zinc finger domains around a cpGFP reporting unit, expresses well on the extracellular face of the plasma membrane and was used to report Zn2+ signaling in neurons in relation to TRPML1 channel activation.

quotes.quote:
termed GZnP3, uses the
Zap1 zinc finger domains around a cpGFP reporting unit and
expresses well on the extracellular face of the plasma
membrane. GZnP3 has been used to report on Zn2+ signaling
in neurons in relation to TRPML1 channel activation.369

experiment.system: neurons expressing GZnP3 on the extracellular face of the plasma membrane
experiment.perturbation: TRPML1 channel activation
experiment.measurement: cpGFP fluorescence as Zn2+ readout

text: FRISZ, based on cpmMaroon185−186 with two zinc hooks appended to the new termini, was used to detect synaptic Zn2+ release in brain slices and awake behaving mice.

quotes.quote:
FRISZ is based on cpmMaroon185−186, with two zinc hooks
appended to each of the new termini. This sensor has been
utilized to detect synaptic Zn2+ release in both brain slices and
awake behaving mice.370

experiment.system: brain slices and awake behaving mice expressing FRISZ
experiment.perturbation: synaptic Zn2+ release
experiment.measurement: far-red fluorescence intensity

text: GINKO1, made by inserting the Kbp scaffold into eGFP, works as an intensiometric or excitation-ratiometric K+ probe with greater dynamic range and K+ affinity than the FRET-based sensors but with additional Na+ sensitivity; GINKO2 exhibits 20-fold ΔR/R0 and improved K+ over Na+ selectivity at the cost of K+ affinity, and was applied in bacteria, Arabidopsis, mice and Drosophila.

quotes.quote:
with greater dynamic range and affinity for K+ than
either FRET-based sensor. However, it suffers from additional
sensitivity to Na+ as compared to the KIRIN and GEPII
scaffolds.373 The GINKO scaffold was rapidly improved upon
using structure-guided optimization and directed evolution,
yielding GINKO2, which exhibits 20-fold ΔR/R0 and
improved selectivity for K+ over Na+ (at the cost of K+
affinity).203 GINKO2 has been applied in numerous biological
systems, including bacteria, Arabidopsis, mice, and Drosophila.

experiment.system: GINKO1/GINKO2 single-FP K+ sensors in bacteria, Arabidopsis, mice and Drosophila
experiment.perturbation: structure-guided optimization and directed evolution; K+ and Na+ exposure
experiment.measurement: excitation ratio change ΔR/R0, dynamic range, ion selectivity

text: KRaION sensors, made by inserting Kbp into mNeonGreen, were produced in a series with varied affinities and excitation-ratiometric K+ responses using NMR and genome mining, and were used as scaffolds to identify the ion-binding site of E. coli Kbp and to test Kbp homologues from other organisms.

quotes.quote:
A combination of NMR and
genome mining was used to refine and produce multiple
KRaION sensors in a series with varied affinities and
excitation-ratiometric responses to K+.374 Crucially, for the
future of the field, these authors used their KRaION sensors as
scaffolds to identify the ion-binding site of E. coli Kbp.

experiment.system: KRaION sensors (Kbp inserted into mNeonGreen)
experiment.perturbation: NMR-guided and genome-mining-guided variant construction; K+ exposure
experiment.measurement: excitation-ratiometric fluorescence response and K+ affinity; ion-binding site identification

text: MagIC, a non-FRET ratiometric probe fusing reference mCherry to a Mg2+-sensitive cpVenus variant, unlike MagFRET could enter the nucleus and was more amenable to subcellular targeting.

quotes.quote:
Koldenkova et al. developed a non-FRET ratiometric probe,
composed of a fusion between a reference mCherry and a
Mg2+-sensitive variant of cpVenus, termed MagIC.377 Unlike
MagFRET, this construct could enter the nucleus and was
more amenable to subcellular targeting.377

experiment.system: MagIC probe expressed in cells
experiment.perturbation: Mg2+ changes; subcellular targeting
experiment.measurement: ratiometric cpVenus/mCherry fluorescence and localization

text: A CreiLOV FMN-based FP sensor with a bacterial LOV Cu(II)-binding domain was demonstrated as a Cu(II) reporter in E. coli cultures but has not yet been validated in mammalian cells.

quotes.quote:
This CreiLOV based sensor has been demonstrated as a
Cu(II) reporter in E. coli cultures. However, this scaffold has
not yet been validated in mammalian cells and may be limited
to bacterial investigations of Cu(II) activity.381,382

experiment.system: E. coli cultures expressing CreiLOV-based sensor
experiment.perturbation: Cu(II) exposure
experiment.measurement: FMN-based FP fluorescence

text: miRFPs were shown to change fluorescence intensity upon binding many types of divalent metal cations, with the most pronounced intensity change so far demonstrated with Cu(II) binding.

quotes.quote:
miRFPs have recently been demonstrated to exhibit a change
in fluorescence intensity upon binding with many types of
divalent metal cations. The most pronounced change in
intensity so far has been demonstrated with Cu(II) binding.

experiment.system: miRFP near-infrared fluorescent proteins
