demonstrated that the Camuiα response would abruptly
terminate during prolonged Ca2+ oscillations, whereas
FRESCA continued to respond, suggesting that FRESCA is
more suitable for long-term imaging than Camuiα.

experiment.system: Cells expressing the FRET-based CaMKII activity sensor FRESCA versus the CaMKII activation sensor Camuiα
experiment.perturbation: prolonged Ca2+ oscillations
experiment.measurement: FRET response over time (side-by-side comparison)

text: The single-FP CaMKII activity reporter CaMKAR showed a 100% excitation-ratio increase in response to Ca2+ elevation in HEK293T cells and was used in a high-throughput drug repurposing screen that identified previously unrecognized CaMKII inhibitors with clinically relevant potency.

quotes.quote:
CaMKAR showed a 100% excitation-ratio
increase in response to Ca2+ elevation in HEK293T cells and
was sensitive enough to be used in a high-throughput drug
repurposing screen and identified several previously unrecog-
nized CaMKII inhibitors with clinically relevant potency.

experiment.system: HEK293T cells expressing CaMKAR (cpGFP between a CaMKIIδ autophosphorylation substrate peptide and FHA1)
experiment.perturbation: Ca2+ elevation; high-throughput drug repurposing screen
experiment.measurement: excitation-ratio change; inhibitor identification

text: Using AMPKAR, energy stress was found to induce cytosolic AMPK activity whereas Ca2+ induced AMPK activity in both the cytosol and nucleus.

quotes.quote:
energy stress was found to induce cytosolic AMPK
activity, whereas Ca2+ induced AMPK activity in both the
cytosol and nucleus.

experiment.system: Cells expressing the FRET-based AMPK activity reporter AMPKAR
experiment.perturbation: energy stress or Ca2+ elevation
experiment.measurement: subcellular AMPK activity (FRET emission ratio) in cytosol and nucleus

text: Plasma membrane AMPK activity was difficult to detect even with the improved sensor ABKAR, which had twice the dynamic range of AMPKAR; splitting ABKAR into the bimolecular sensor bimAMPKAR greatly increased the dynamic range of the plasma membrane-targeted sensor and allowed investigation of bidirectional regulation of plasma membrane AMPK activity by PKA signaling.

quotes.quote:
plasma membrane AMPK
activity was difficult to detect, even using an improved sensor
(ABKAR) with twice the dynamic range of AMPKAR.

Switching to a bimolecular design greatly increased the
dynamic range of the plasma membrane-targeted sensor,
which allowed Depry and colleagues to investigate the
bidirectional regulation of plasma membrane AMPK activity
by PKA signaling.

experiment.system: Live cells expressing plasma membrane-targeted AMPK activity reporters (AMPKAR, ABKAR, bimAMPKAR)
experiment.perturbation: AMPK-activating stimuli and PKA signaling manipulation
experiment.measurement: FRET dynamic range and plasma membrane AMPK activity

numbers.quantity: ABKAR dynamic range relative to AMPKAR

text: ExRai-AMPKAR showed a roughly 2-fold maximum excitation ratio change in response to AMPK activation and was used to dissect AMPK activity dynamics at mitochondria, the lysosome, and in the nucleus.

quotes.quote:
Using ExRai-AMPKAR, which showed
a rougly 2-fold maximum excitation ratio change in response to
AMPK activation, the authors were able to dissect spatial
AMPK signaling in greater detail, illuminating the dynamics
and regulation of AMPK activity at mitochondria, the
lysosome, and in the nucleus.

experiment.system: Live cells expressing the single-FP ExRai-AMPKAR targeted to subcellular compartments
experiment.perturbation: AMPK activation
experiment.measurement: maximum excitation ratio change and compartment-specific AMPK activity

numbers.quantity: maximum excitation ratio change of ExRai-AMPKAR

text: AMPfret reported conformational changes induced by AMP/ADP binding, and its responses were unaffected by Thr172 phosphorylation state, suggesting adenylate-induced conformational switching is independent of activation loop phosphorylation.

quotes.quote:
AMPfret successfully reported conforma-
tional changes induced by AMP/ADP binding. Notably,
AMPfret respones were unaffected by the Thr172 phosphor-
ylation state, suggesting that adenylate-induced conformational
switching is independent of activation loop phosphoryla-
tion.

experiment.system: AMPK subunits fused with CFP/YFP (AMPfret1.0 and AMPfret2.0)
experiment.perturbation: AMP/ADP binding; varying Thr172 phosphorylation state
experiment.measurement: FRET change reporting AMPK conformational state

text: Screening SH2 domains for a PDGFR reporter revealed that the source of the SH2 domain is crucial to selectivity: SH2 domains from Nck-2 and Shp-2, but not Src, specifically bound the activated PDGFR reporter.

quotes.quote:
This work revealed that the source of the
SH2 domain is crucial to the selectivity of the PDGFR
biosensor, as SH2 domains from Nck-2 and Shp-2 but not Src
specifically bound the activated PDGFR reporter.

experiment.system: PDGFR FRET reporter containing a phospho-Tyr751 substrate and candidate SH2 PAABDs
experiment.perturbation: substitution of SH2 domains from different effector proteins
experiment.measurement: binding/selectivity of SH2 domain to the activated reporter

text: The first Src activity reporter was also phosphorylated by Abl, Lck, and EGFR in validation experiments, casting doubt on its specificity; replacing the substrate with a p130cas-derived sequence resolved this issue.

quotes.quote:
However, validation experiments revealed that the reporter was
also phosphorylated by Abl, Lck, and EGFR, casting doubt on
the specificity of this reporter.

Wang et al. later replaced the
substrate with a sequence derived from the endogenous c-Src
substrate p130cas, which resolved this issue.

experiment.system: FRET-based Src activity reporter with library-screen-derived substrate versus p130cas-derived substrate
experiment.perturbation: exposure to other tyrosine kinases (Abl, Lck, EGFR); substrate replacement
experiment.measurement: reporter phosphorylation/specificity

text: A single mutation in the phosphotyrosine-binding pocket of the SH2 domain, predicted to reduce basal FRET, significantly increased sensor dynamic range; applying this to a Fyn biosensor targeted to plasma membrane microdomains gave different growth factor-induced FRET responses for Lyn- versus Fyn-derived targeting motifs, suggesting functionally distinct plasma membrane raft subtypes, with relatively high Fyn activity also detected in the perinuclear region.

quotes.quote:
introducing a single mutation within the phosphotyrosine-
binding pocket in the SH2 domain, which was predicted to
affect the binding affinity and reduce basal FRET, was also
found to significantly increased the dynamic range of the
sensor.

The authors observed different growth
factor-induced FRET responses from sensors tagged with
targeting motifs from either Lyn kinase or Fyn kinase itself,
suggesting the presence of functionally distinct subtypes of
plasma membrane rafts. Relatively high levels of Fyn activity
were also detected in the perinuclear region

experiment.system: Living cells expressing FRET-based Fyn biosensors targeted with Lyn or Fyn membrane motifs
experiment.perturbation: SH2-pocket point mutation; growth factor stimulation
experiment.measurement: FRET dynamic range and localized FRET responses

text: FAK-SPARK biosensors detect subcellular FAK activity without subcellular targeting because droplets form only where active FAK is present, achieving visualization of FAK activity within single focal adhesions.

quotes.quote:
FAK-SPARK biosensors can detect subcellular
FAK activity without being targeted to subcellular locations,
as FAK-SPARK droplets only form in places where active FAK
is present, achieving visualization of FAK activity within single
focal adhesions.

experiment.system: Cells expressing FAK-SPARK phase-separation biosensor
experiment.perturbation: observational (endogenous FAK activity)
experiment.measurement: droplet formation imaged at focal adhesions

text: FRET-seq, a high-throughput sequencing-based screen of self-activating FRET biosensor libraries sorted by FACS, yielded Fyn and ZAP70 biosensors with improved dynamic ranges.

quotes.quote:
Liu et al. applied FRET-seq to screen
for optimized substrate sequences and obtain Fyn and ZAP70
biosensors with improved dynamic ranges.

experiment.system: Libraries of 'self-activating' (sa)FRET kinase biosensor variants in mammalian cells
experiment.perturbation: tethering to an active kinase or negative control; FACS sorting on FRET signal
experiment.measurement: biosensor sequences recovered by high-throughput sequencing; dynamic range of selected variants

text: Using the FAK activation sensor CYFAK413, PIP2-containing vesicles were found to induce a conformational change and activate FAK in vitro, with PIP2 binding a basic patch in the FERM domain, and perturbing PIP2 levels altered FAK activation in living cells.

quotes.quote:
Using CYFAK413, the
authors found that PIP2-containing vesicles induced a
conformational change and activated FAK in vitro, with PIP2
binding a basic patch within the FERM domain, and that
perturbing PIP2 levels altered FAK activation in living cells.

experiment.system: CYFAK413 (CFP at FAK N-terminus, YFP inserted at residue 413) in vitro and in living cells
experiment.perturbation: PIP2-containing vesicles; perturbation of cellular PIP2 levels
experiment.measurement: FRET emission ratio reporting FAK conformational activation

text: TORCAR, built by flanking full-length 4EBP1 with a CFP/YFP pair, reports mTORC1 phosphorylation as an increase in the cyan/yellow emission ratio and revealed location- and stimulus-specific mTORC1 activity patterns in live cells; the authors note current mTORC1 sensors show very low dynamic range and sensitivity.

quotes.quote:
Phosphorylation of 4EBP1 by
mTORC1 induces a conformational change within the
biosensor that leads to an increase in the cyan/yellow emission
ratio.

Currently, mTORC1 sensors show very low
dynamic range and sensitivity, limiting their wider use.
Nevertheless, TORCAR has revealed location- and stimulus-
specific mTORC1 activity patterns in live cells.

experiment.system: Live cells expressing the FRET-based mTORC1 reporter TORCAR
experiment.perturbation: mTORC1-modulating stimuli; subcellular targeting
experiment.measurement: cyan/yellow emission ratio

text: A FRET-based histidine kinase activation sensor sandwiching CckA between mRuby3 and mClover3 shows increased FRET in the active state and was used to screen histidine kinase inhibitors and monitor conformational changes in bacteria during the bacterial cell cycle.

quotes.quote:
This FRET-based biosensor includes a sensing
domain that incorporates CckA, a bacterial histidine kinase
that undergoes a conformational change when active, which is
sandwiched between mRuby3 and mClover3. These two FPs
undergo increased FRET in the active state of the kinase.

Using this sensor, Duvall and Childers conducted a screen of
histidine kinase inhibitors and monitored histidine kinase
conformational changes in bacteria during the bacterial cell
cycle.

experiment.system: Bacteria expressing a CckA-based FRET sensor (mRuby3/mClover3)
experiment.perturbation: histidine kinase inhibitor screen; cell cycle progression
experiment.measurement: FRET change reporting kinase conformation

text: Early GFP-Raf1-RBD translocation sensors with ectopically expressed Ras showed oncogenic HRas and NRas active at the plasma membrane, ER, and Golgi with different kinetics, whereas appending multiple tandem RBD copies removed the need for Ras overexpression and revealed active Ras accumulating at the plasma membrane but not the Golgi.

quotes.quote:
Oncogenic HRas and NRas were thus found to be active at the
plasma membrane, ER, and Golgi with different kinetics and to
engage in different signaling pathways.

This approach revealed that active Ras accumulated at the plasma
membrane but not the Golgi.

experiment.system: Cells expressing GFP-tagged Raf1-RBD translocation sensors (single or tandem RBD copies), with or without ectopic Ras
experiment.perturbation: Ras overexpression versus increased sensor affinity via tandem RBDs
experiment.measurement: subcellular relocalization of the GFP-tagged RBD

text: Systematic comparison of translocation-based Rho sensor variants by relocalization efficiency and specificity produced dimericTomato-2xrGBD, which visualized a small pool of Rho proteins activated at the Golgi in addition to plasma membrane Rho activation.

quotes.quote:
Mahlandt et al. systematically compared different
sensor variants by quantifying the relocalization efficiency and
specificity for different Rho-family proteins,740 ultimately
resulting in the development of an improved translocation-
based Rho sensor (dimericTomato-2xrGBD) that was able to
visualize a small pool of Rho proteins activated at the Golgi

experiment.system: Cells expressing translocation-based RhoA sensor variants
experiment.perturbation: variation of FP color, rGBD copy number and sensor design
experiment.measurement: relocalization efficiency and specificity; subcellular Rho activity imaging

text: Co-imaging Cdc42 and RhoA biosensors during wound healing in Xenopus oocytes showed RhoA and Cdc42 form discrete rings around the wound whose formation, segregation, and movement depended on microtubules.

quotes.quote:
Co-imaging Cdc42
and RhoA biosensors during wound healing in Xenopus oocytes
revealed that RhoA and Cdc42 form discrete rings around the
wound and that the formation, segregation, and movement of
these rings depended on microtubules.

experiment.system: Xenopus oocytes expressing translocation-based Cdc42 (WASP-derived) and RhoA (rGBD) biosensors
experiment.perturbation: wounding; microtubule perturbation
experiment.measurement: co-imaging of biosensor ring formation and movement

text: Raichu-Ras exhibited high specificity to Ras over other Ras family proteins, and imaging Raichu-Ras and Raichu-Rap1 in EGF-stimulated COS-7 cells showed Ras activated at the peripheral plasma membrane while Rap1 was activated at perinuclear regions.

quotes.quote:
Raichu-Ras exhibited
high specificity to Ras over other Ras family proteins.

Spatiotemporal
activation images of EGF-stimulated Ras and Rap1 revealed
that Ras was activated at the peripheral plasma membrane
while Rap1 was activated at perinuclear regions.

experiment.system: COS-7 cells expressing Raichu-Ras or Raichu-Rap1 FRET biosensors
experiment.perturbation: EGF stimulation
experiment.measurement: spatiotemporal FRET emission ratio images

text: Adding a second, GTPase-binding-deficient PBD as an autoinhibitory domain to Raichu-Cdc42 minimized off-state FRET and increased the overall dynamic range.

quotes.quote:
one that interacts with intramolecular Cdc42 to
drive the FRET change and a second GTPase-binding-
deficient mutant that serves as an autoinhibitory domain for
PBD to minimize off-state FRET, thus increasing the overall
dynamic range.

experiment.system: Raichu-Cdc42 FRET biosensor variants
experiment.perturbation: inclusion of two p21-binding domains, one binding-deficient
experiment.measurement: off-state FRET and dynamic range

text: Dark acceptors ShadowG and ShadowY increased the sensitivity and SNR of the FRas sensor, and pairing ShadowY with Clover achieved reduced cell-to-cell variability in 2pFLIM measurements in small neuronal compartments in mouse brains.

quotes.quote:
later efforts at FP
engineering generated dark acceptors such as ShadowG675 and
ShadowY,753 both of which increased the sensitivity and SNR
of FRas. ShadowY was paired with the green-emitting FP
Clover to achieve reduced cell-to-cell variability in 2pFLIM
measurements in small neuronal compartments in mouse
brains.

experiment.system: Bimolecular FRas FRET sensor (RBD and HRas tagged with donor/acceptor) in cells and mouse brain neurons
experiment.perturbation: substitution of acceptor FP with dark acceptors ShadowG or ShadowY
experiment.measurement: sensitivity, SNR, and cell-to-cell variability in 2pFLIM

text: A bimolecular RhoA sensor using mCyRFP-tagged RhoA as donor and mMaroon-tagged Rhotekin as acceptor enabled simultaneous dual-color 2p-FLIM together with the EGFP-based CaMKII reporter Green-Camui.

quotes.quote:
Laviv et al.
developed a RhoA sensor using a bimolecular design
containing mCyRFP-tagged RhoA as the FRET donor and
mMaroon tagged-Rhotekin as the acceptor, which enabled
simultaneous, dual-color 2p-FLIM along with an EGFP-based
CaMKII reporter, Green-Camui.

experiment.system: Cells co-expressing mCyRFP/mMaroon RhoA FRET sensor and Green-Camui
experiment.perturbation: simultaneous 2P excitation multiplexing
experiment.measurement: dual-color 2p-FLIM fluorescence lifetime

text: RasAR, which uses a pseudoligand from the effector binding region of Ras that is displaced by active Ras binding to the Raf1 RBD (decreasing FRET), detected cellular Ras activity and captured the dynamics of oncogenic KRasG12C in live cells treated with an FDA-approved Ras inhibitor.

quotes.quote:
RasAR was shown to successfully detect cellular Ras activity
and captured the dynamics of oncogenic KRasG12C in live
cells treated with an FDA-approved Ras inhibitor

experiment.system: Live cells expressing the pseudoligand-based FRET reporter RasAR and oncogenic KRasG12C
experiment.perturbation: treatment with an FDA-approved Ras inhibitor
experiment.measurement: FRET efficiency change reporting Ras activity

text: A ddFP-based bimolecular Ras biosensor was generalizable to Rac1 and Cdc42, enabled optogenetic manipulation of confined local GTPase activation via FGFR or TrkB signaling, and a red-shifted version detected GTPase activity in the primary motor cortex in awake mice.

quotes.quote:
This design was shown to be generalizable and
was applied to other small GTPases, such as Rac1 and
Cdc42.756 The ddFP-based design also enabled optogenetic
manipulation of confined local GTPase activation via fibroblast
growth factor receptor (FGFR) or tropomyosin receptor
kinase B (TrkB) signaling

A red-shifted
version of the ddFP-based sensor was also able to detect
GTPase activity in the primary motor cortex in awake mice

experiment.system: Cells and awake mice expressing ddGFP-based (FP-A/FP-B) GTPase sensors fused to Ras/Rac1/Cdc42 and RBD
experiment.perturbation: optogenetic activation of FGFR or TrkB signaling; in vivo imaging
experiment.measurement: green (or red-shifted) fluorescence turn-on upon GTPase-RBD interaction

text: A FRET sensor with eCFP fused to the β-O-GlcNAc-binding protein GalD, a modified casein kinase substrate sequence, and Venus reports β-O-GlcNAcylation as an increase in the yellow/cyan emission ratio.

quotes.quote:
β-O-GlcNAcylation of the substrate sequence
induces GalD binding, resulting in a conformational change
that increases the yellow/cyan emission ratio.

experiment.system: Live cells expressing the eCFP-GalD-substrate-Venus FRET glycosylation sensor
experiment.perturbation: O-GlcNAcylation of the substrate sequence
experiment.measurement: yellow/cyan emission ratio

text: UGAcS, a cpGFP-in-murG ratiometric UDP-GlcNAc sensor, was also shown to bind and detect UDP and UTP, potentially producing nonspecific signals; the red sensor bapaUGAc exhibited greater selectivity for UDP-GlcNAc over UDP and UTP than UGAcS but showed slight sensitivity to UDP-GalNAc, and was multiplexed with UGAcS to probe ER and cytosolic UDP-GlcNAc simultaneously.

quotes.quote:
However, UGAcS was also shown to bind and
detect UDP and UTP, potentially resulting in nonspecific
signals.

BapaUGAc exhibited
greater sensitivity for UDP-GlcNAc over UDP and UTP
compared to UGAcS but exhibited slight sensitivity to a similar
molecule, UDP-GalNAc.

BapaUGAc was also multiplexed with the green UGAcS
sensor to probe changes in UDP-GlcNAc levels in the ER and
cytosol simultaneously.

experiment.system: Cells expressing UGAcS (cpGFP in inactive E. coli murG) and bapaUGAc (boronolectin-ecpmApple), targeted to ER, Golgi and cytosol
experiment.perturbation: exposure to UDP-GlcNAc, UDP, UTP, UDP-GalNAc; metabolic and pharmacological disruptions
experiment.measurement: ratiometric / turn-off fluorescence responses

text: A bimolecular FLIM-FRET approach with ubiquitin-labeled REACh and EGFP fused to a PEST ubiquitylation substrate reports ubiquitylation as a decrease in EGFP fluorescence lifetime.

quotes.quote:
Proximity between REACh and
EGFP leads to a decrease in the EGFP fluorescence lifetime
(as well as quenching of EGFP emission, but this requires a
reference FP for proper quantification) and indicates
interaction between ubiquitin and a ubiquitylation substrate,
and thus ubiquitylation.

experiment.system: Cells co-expressing REACh-ubiquitin and EGFP fused to a PEST ubiquitylation substrate
experiment.perturbation: ubiquitylation of the substrate (proof of concept)
experiment.measurement: EGFP fluorescence lifetime / quenching

text: A β-TrCP activity sensor made by fusing a noncanonical degron motif recognized by β-TrCP to YFP reports ubiquitylation as a decrease in YFP fluorescence as the reporter is degraded.

quotes.quote:
Upon ubiquitylation of the biosensor, YFP
fluorescence decreases as the reporter is degraded.

experiment.system: Cells expressing YFP fused to a β-TrCP-recognized degron motif
experiment.perturbation: β-TrCP/SCF-mediated ubiquitylation of the reporter
experiment.measurement: YFP fluorescence intensity

text: A FRET-based H3K9me3 biosensor consisting of full-length histone H3 linked to the HP1 chromodomain flanked by ECFP and YPet, overexpressed in mammalian cells, revealed dynamic regulation of H3K9 trimethylation during mitosis with a marked decrease in methylation during G2 phase.

quotes.quote:
Imaging the H3K9me3
biosensor, which was overexpressed in mammalian cells,
revealed dynamic regulation of this PTM during mitosis,
with a marked decrease in methylation during the G2 phase of
the cell cycle.

experiment.system: Mammalian cells overexpressing the ECFP/YPet H3K9me3 FRET biosensor
experiment.perturbation: observational across cell cycle/mitosis
experiment.measurement: yellow/cyan emission ratio

text: Histac, a FRET sensor with Venus and CFP flanking a BRDT bromodomain and full-length histone H4, reports H4 acetylation as an increase in the cyan/yellow emission ratio, was validated in COS7 cells to identify changes in histone H4 acetylation during mitosis, and was later used to study p300/CBP activity and identify inhibitors in live cells.

quotes.quote:
Upon acetylation of
histone H4, the BRDT domain binds, leading to a conforma-
tional change that increases in the cyan/yellow emission ratio.
Histac was validated in COS7 cells and used to identify
changes in histone H4 acetylation during mitosis.

Histac
was later utilized by Dancy et al. to study the activity of the
histone acetyltransferase p300/CBP and identify inhibitors of
the complex in live cells.

experiment.system: COS7 and other live cells expressing the Histac FRET sensor
experiment.perturbation: mitotic progression; p300/CBP inhibitor treatment
experiment.measurement: cyan/yellow emission ratio

text: A mintbody (scFv antibody fused to EGFP) specific for H3K9 acetylation allowed quantification of the nuclear-to-cytoplasmic EGFP ratio as a readout for changes in acetylation, and the approach was expanded to detect H4K20 methylation.

quotes.quote:
This
approach allowed them to quantify the nuclear-to-cytoplasmic
ratio of EGFP as a readout for changes in acetylation.781 The
scFV or mintbody-based approach was further expanded to
detect H4K20 methylation using another mintbody specific for
that residue.

experiment.system: Live cells expressing modification-specific intracellular antibodies (mintbodies) fused to EGFP
experiment.perturbation: changes in histone H3K9 acetylation / H4K20 methylation
experiment.measurement: nuclear-to-cytoplasmic EGFP fluorescence ratio

text: NANOMS, FRET biosensors incorporating N-terminal myristoylation-site membrane-targeting sequences of Gαi2, Yes, or Src fused to FPs, use plasma membrane localization as a myristoylation readout and were used to screen for compounds inhibiting myristoyl transferases.

quotes.quote:
Biosensor localization to the plasma membrane can serve as
the readout for myristoylation, and this approach was utilized
to screen for chemical compounds that inhibit myristoyl
transferases that enable membrane anchorage.

experiment.system: Cells expressing NANOMS FRET biosensors with Gαi2, Yes, or Src membrane-targeting sequences
experiment.perturbation: chemical compound screen against myristoyl transferases
experiment.measurement: plasma membrane nanoclustering/localization via FRET

text: FUCCI, a bimolecular system fusing mKO2 to human Cdt1 (amino acids 30−120) and mAG1 to the first 110 residues of human Geminin, reports G1 versus S/G2/M phases and was used to characterize cell cycle states during epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and wound healing in cultured cells and in developing neural tissue of FUCCI transgenic mice.

quotes.quote:
FUCCI is a bimolecular system which fuses mKO2,
an orange-emitting FP, to human Cdt1 (amino acids 30−120)
and, separately, the green-emitting FP mAG1 to the first 110
residues of human Geminin.

The first version of FUCCI therefore reports
on G1 or S/G2/M phases and was used to characterize cell
cycle states during epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and
wound healing in cultured cells as well as in the developing
neural tissue of FUCCI transgenic mice.

experiment.system: Cultured cells and FUCCI transgenic mice expressing mKO2-hCdt1(30−120) and mAG1-hGeminin(1−110)
experiment.perturbation: epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and wound healing; observational in developing neural tissue
experiment.measurement: orange/green fluorescence indicating cell cycle phase

numbers.quantity: human Cdt1 fragment used in FUCCI
human Geminin fragment used in FUCCI

text: Ki67p-FUCCI, which places FUCCI-like sensing components (Cdt1 and hGeminin tagged to mCherry and mAG) under a cell cycle-responsive Ki67 proximal promoter, turns off expression in quiescent and nondividing cells, making G0 cells and slowly dividing cells distinguishable.

quotes.quote:
Ki67p-FUCCI was developed using a
cell cycle-responsive Ki67 proximal promoter that enables
expression of the sensor only when cells enter the cell cycle,
thereby turning expression off in quiescent and nondividing
cells.

Through this system, however, cells in the
quiescent (G0) state and slowly dividing cells are distinguish-
able.

experiment.system: Cells expressing Ki67p-FUCCI (mCherry-Cdt1 and mAG-hGeminin under Ki67 proximal promoter)
experiment.perturbation: cell cycle entry versus quiescence
experiment.measurement: fluorescence expression and cell cycle state classification

text: PCNA-mRuby, generated by inserting mRuby in frame with the first exon of one allele of PCNA, enabled single-color cell-cycle tracking, and a machine-learning-based approach classified cell cycle states from the dynamic behavior and expression of PCNA-mRuby.

quotes.quote:
Zerjatke et al. inserted mRuby in frame with the first
exon of one allele of PCNA.790 Using a machine-learning-
based approach, the authors classified cell cycle states based on
dynamic behavior and expression of PCNA-mRuby.

experiment.system: Live cells with endogenous knock-in PCNA-mRuby
experiment.perturbation: observational (native cell cycle progression)
experiment.measurement: single-color fluorescence dynamics classified by machine learning

text: A translocation-based CDK sensor whose substrate traffics from the nucleus to the cytoplasm upon increased CDK activity distinguished G1 from G0 phase in vivo in zebrafish, and a combined mcm-4 promoter transcriptional reporter plus CDK activity reporter was used to distinguish G1 or quiescent cells in C. elegans.

quotes.quote:
a translocation-based
CDK sensor that consists of a CDK substrate that traffics from

the nucleus to the cytoplasm upon increased CDK activity was
developed to distinguish G1 phase from G0 phase in vivo in
zebrafish.

An
mcm-4 promoter was incorporated to reveal Rb/E2F-mediated
transcriptional control, and the CDK activity reporter was then
used to distinguish G1 or quiescent cells in C. elegans.

experiment.system: Zebrafish and C. elegans expressing a translocation-based CDK activity reporter (human DNA helicase B fragment between NLS and NES tagged to GFP or mKate)
experiment.perturbation: observational cell cycle entry/exit; mcm-4 promoter transcriptional reporting
experiment.measurement: nucleocytoplasmic distribution of the FP-tagged CDK substrate

text: In the FLARE and Cal-Light integrator designs, TEVp cleavage releasing the transcription factor occurs only in the presence of both light and Ca2+; FLARE was used to drive opsin expression to manipulate neuronal function in FLARE-positive cells in vivo in the motor cortex of mice.

quotes.quote:
Cleavage
only occurs in the presence of both light and Ca2+, releasing
the transcription factor to enter the nucleus and induce target
gene transcription.

This very
approach was demonstrated by driving the expression of an
opsin to manipulate neuronal function in FLARE-positive cells
in vivo in the motor cortex of mice.

experiment.system: Cells and mouse motor cortex expressing light- and Ca2+-gated transcriptional integrators (FLARE, Cal-Light)
experiment.perturbation: blue light illumination combined with Ca2+ elevation
experiment.measurement: TEVp cleavage-dependent reporter/opsin gene transcription and neuronal manipulation

text: FLiCRE was used to label cells in the nucleus accumbens of mice in vivo, and single-cell RNA sequencing of FLiCRE-labeled cells identified distinct cell types based on their responses to Ca2+ excitatory conditions.

quotes.quote:
This integrator was
used to label cells in the nucleus accumbens of mice in vivo. By
performing single-cell RNA sequencing on FLiCRE-labeled
cells, the authors were able to identify distinct cell types in the
nucleus accumbens based on their responses to Ca2+ excitatory
conditions

experiment.system: Mouse nucleus accumbens neurons expressing the FLiCRE Ca2+/light-gated integrator
experiment.perturbation: Ca2+ excitatory conditions plus light gating
experiment.measurement: transcriptional labeling followed by single-cell RNA sequencing

text: CNiFERs — cells stably expressing a neurotransmitter-selective GPCR together with the FRET-based Ca2+ indicator TN-XXL — report neurotransmitter binding as a Ca2+-driven FRET response and were validated to detect neurotransmitter release in vivo by 2P laser scanning microscopy after implantation into brains of adult mice.

quotes.quote:
Upon GPCR
activation, endogenous G-proteins trigger cytosolic Ca2+
elevation, which in turn induces a FRET response from TN-
XXL (Figure 14c). CNiFERs were validated to detect
neurotransmitter release in vivo under 2P laser scanning
microscopy following implantation into the brains of adult
mice.

experiment.system: Engineered cells (CNiFERs) expressing a specific GPCR plus TN-XXL, implanted into adult mouse brain
experiment.perturbation: neurotransmitter (e.g., dopamine, norepinephrine, acetylcholine) release
experiment.measurement: FRET response under 2P laser scanning microscopy

text: The trimolecular iTango system, in which blue light plus dopamine binding to DRD2 reconstitutes TEVp to release tTA and drive EGFP expression, was used in live mice to label the dopamine-sensitive population of neurons and identify subsets involved in various behaviors.

quotes.quote:
Lee
and colleagues were able to use this system in live mice to label
the dopamine-sensitive population of neurons in the mouse
brain. Furthermore, the subset of dopamine-sensitive neurons
involved in various behaviors were identified.

experiment.system: Live mice expressing the trimolecular iTango system (DRD2-CIBN-TEVseq-AsLOV2-tTA, CRY2PHR-TEVp C-fragment, β-arrestin2-TEVp N-fragment)
experiment.perturbation: blue light exposure combined with dopamine binding to DRD2
experiment.measurement: EGFP marker gene expression labeling neurons; behavioral association

text: Cryo-EM of an engineered full-length mouse JAK1 (V657F) bound to a zippered IFNλR1 Box1/Box2 peptide yielded a 3.6Å 2:2 complex with C2 symmetry, modeled as full-length JAK1 (Pro32-Lys1153) plus a 37 amino acid IFNλR1 segment (Pro255-Leu291).

quotes.quote:
3D reconstruction of selected particles generated a 3.6Å nominal resolution map of the 
2:2 JAK1-IFNλR1 complex with C2 symmetry (Fig. S2–3).

culminating in an atomic model of full-length JAK1 (Pro32-Lys1153) and a 37 amino acid 
segment of IFNλR1 Box1/Box2 (Pro255-Leu291).

experiment.system: Full-length mouse JAK1-V657F co-expressed in insect cells with soluble GCN4-zippered IFNλR1 Box1/Box2 ('mini-IFNλR1'), BS3 cross-linked with tandem BC2 nanobody
experiment.perturbation: protein engineering: V657F mutation, zipper-dimerized receptor ICD mimic
experiment.measurement: single-particle cryo-EM 3D reconstruction and atomic model building

text: Co-expression of mini-IFNλR1 with either wild-type or V657F full-length JAK1 in insect cells increased JAK1 activation loop phosphorylation by western blot.

quotes.quote:
Co-expression of the soluble zippered IFNλR1 ICD peptide (‘mini-IFNλR1’) with either 
full-length wild-type (WT) JAK1 or JAK1-V657F protein resulted in increased activation 
loop phosphorylation as measured by western blot, validating the construct design strategy 
(Fig. 1C).

experiment.system: T. ni insect cells expressing full-length WT or V657F JAK1
experiment.perturbation: co-expression of soluble zippered mini-IFNλR1
experiment.measurement: immunoblot of JAK phosphorylation and total expression two days post-infection

text: In cells expressing an EpoR receptor carrying the IFNλR1 Box1/Box2 chimera, Epo stimulation induced JAK1 phosphorylation, whereas wild-type EpoR selectively induced JAK2 phosphorylation, indicating the JAK1-IFNλR1 dimer is signaling-competent.

quotes.quote:
As expected, 
Epo stimulation selectively induced JAK2 phosphorylation in cells expressing wild-type 
EpoR. In cells expressing the EpoR-IFNλR1 Box1/Box2 chimera, Epo stimulation resulted 
in phosphorylation of JAK1, indicating the JAK1-IFNλR1 dimer is signaling-competent

NIH 3T3 
cells transiently expressing mEpoR or mEpoR-IFNλR1 chimera were stimulated with 
Epo for 20 min prior to analysis of JAK phosphorylation by immunoblot.

experiment.system: NIH 3T3 cells transiently expressing mEpoR or mEpoR-IFNλR1 Box1/Box2 chimera
experiment.perturbation: Epo stimulation for 20 min
experiment.measurement: immunoblot of JAK1/JAK2 phosphorylation

text: In the structure, JAK1 FERM-SH2 modules sit above inward-facing PK domains that form a head-to-head dimer at the center of the complex, placing the C-terminal TK domains at the base facing outwards with accessible catalytic clefts.

quotes.quote:
The FERM-SH2 modules sit above inward-facing PK domains, which form a head-
to-head dimer at the center of the complex. The close association between the FERM-SH2 
and PK domains positions the C-terminal TK domains at the base of the JAK1 dimer, facing 
outwards with their catalytic clefts accessible for phosphotransferase activity.

experiment.system: 2:2 JAK1-IFNλR1 cryo-EM complex
experiment.perturbation: observational (structure determination)
experiment.measurement: domain architecture in the refined atomic model

text: The IFNλR1 peptide binds an extended groove on JAK1 FERM-SH2 through Box1 and Box2, burying approximately 1650Å2 of surface, with Box1 Leu266 and Phe268 inserting into a FERM hydrophobic pocket of Val194, Phe247 and Phe251, and Box2 contacts including an Glu284–His509 salt bridge and a Thr532 hydrogen bond.

quotes.quote:
continuous density is observed for the IFNλR1 
peptide, which binds along an extended groove on the surface of the FERM-SH2 through its 
the Box1 and Box2 motifs, burying approximately 1650Å2 of surface (Fig 3B).

forms a short 310 helix which positions 
Leu266 and Phe268 of the peptide into a hydrophobic pocket in the JAK1 FERM domain 
consisting of Val194, Phe247, and Phe251

a salt bridge interaction between Glu284 in 
IFNλR1 and His509 in the JAK1 SH2 domain and a hydrogen bonding interaction between 
Thr532 in SH2 βG1 and the backbone carbonyl of IFNλR1 Phe285.

experiment.system: JAK1-IFNλR1 cryo-EM structure
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: interface analysis and buried surface area from the model

text: The JAK1 FERM domain forms a broad interface with the PK C-lobe and catalytic loop burying approximately 1100Å2 (involving PK αI Arg838 and Arg842), while the PK-αG helix contacts the TK N-lobe and PK-TK linker over 580Å2, including a Glu800–Arg929 salt bridge.

quotes.quote:
the JAK1 FERM domain forms a broad interface with the 
C-lobe and catalytic loop of the PK domain, burying approximately 1100Å2.

Arg838 in PK αI contacts residues P370 and I372 in FERM 
while Arg842 interacts with the backbone and side chain of Tyr422 in the FERM-SH2 linker

the PK-αG helix forms a limited 
interaction with the N-lobe of the TK domain and the PK-TK linker which buries 580Å2 
surface area (Fig. 3D). This site consists of a salt bridge between PK-αG Glu800 and Arg929 
in TK-αC

experiment.system: JAK1-IFNλR1 cryo-EM structure
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: buried surface area and contact analysis of intramolecular domain interfaces

text: The PK domains adopt an inactive conformation (closed activation loop, outward-rotated catalytic glutamate, adenosine bound, lacking a canonical DFG motif), while the TK domains adopt an active conformation with open activation loop, inward-facing catalytic glutamate and bound ADP.

quotes.quote:
The PK domains adopt an inactive conformation as evidenced by a closed activation loop 
and an outward rotation of the catalytic glutamate on the C-helix (Fig. 3E). Although we 
observe adenosine within the nucleotide-binding site, the PK domain lacks the canonical 
DFG motif necessary for catalytic activity

the TK domains adopt an active 
conformation with open activation loop, catalytic glutamate facing inwards towards the 
active site, and ADP bound at the nucleotide-binding site (Fig. 3F).

experiment.system: JAK1-IFNλR1 cryo-EM structure
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: kinase-domain conformational features and bound nucleotide density in the model

text: The JAK1 homodimer fulcrum is formed by SH2-PK linkers and PK N-lobes interacting through a tightly packed hydrophobic cluster of six phenylalanine residues and an anti-parallel β sheet, with Phe574, Phe635 and the oncogenic V657F forming a phenylalanine triad per monomer.

quotes.quote:
The central fulcrum of the JAK1 homodimer is formed by the SH2-PK linker and 
PK N-lobes from individual JAK1 monomers, which interact through a tightly packed 
hydrophobic cluster of six phenylalanine residues, and an anti-parallel β sheet

anti-parallel β sheets 
from SH2-PK linkers form a lid that projects Phe574 into the hydrophobic interface 
(Fig. 4C, Fig. S4B). Below the lid, Phe635 from the αC-helix abuts oncogenic V657F 
(corresponding to JAK2 V617F) on β4, completing the phenylalanine triad in the JAK1 
monomer.

experiment.system: JAK1-V657F–IFNλR1 cryo-EM structure
experiment.perturbation: observational (V657F-bearing construct)
experiment.measurement: cryo-EM density and residue-level interface analysis of the PK dimer

text: Modeling wild-type Val657 into the structure left an unfilled pocket at the dimer interface with poorer shape complementarity (VF:0.53, WT:0.51) and decreased side-chain buried surface area by approximately 20%, from 67Å2 to 55Å2.

quotes.quote:
The smaller Val side chain results in an unfilled pocket within the dimer interface 
and correspondingly poorer shape complementarity (VF:0.53, WT:0.51), decreasing buried 
surface area of the side chain by approximately 20% from 67Å2 to 55Å2 (Fig. 4D, Table S2).

verdict_note: Claim text and numbers match the paper verbatim; the 'built in Coot' detail in the experiment field is not in the supplied excerpt but is peripheral and does not alter the assertion.

experiment.system: JAK1 V657F cryo-EM structure vs. in silico wild-type Val657 model built in Coot
experiment.perturbation: in silico reversion of Phe657 to Val657
experiment.measurement: shape complementarity score and buried side-chain surface area

numbers.quantity: side-chain buried surface area, VF vs WT

text: A homology model of the JAK2 PK dimer built from a published JAK2 PK monomer structure showed the conserved Phe side chains playing a structural role similar to that observed in JAK1, which the authors take as evidence the JAK1 result generalizes to the JAK/TYK family.

quotes.quote:
We generated a homology 
model of the JAK2 PK dimer based on a previously published structure of JAK2 PK 
monomer (42). Consistent with a shared mechanism for activation by V617F, the conserved

Phe side chains play a similar structural role as we see here in JAK1, giving confidence that 
the JAK1 structural results are generalizable to the JAK/TYK family (Fig. S5, Fig. S6).

experiment.system: JAK2 pseudokinase domain
experiment.perturbation: in silico homology modeling of a JAK2 PK dimer onto the JAK1 PK dimer
experiment.measurement: comparison of conserved Phe side-chain positions at the modeled interface

text: Aligning a previously reported autoinhibited TYK2 PK-TK structure to the FERM-SH2-PK module of the JAK1 dimer produced a compact monomer model in which the TK folds back onto FERM-SH2, and this closed state is incompatible with JAK dimerization due to a steric clash between the PK domain and the opposing FERM domain.

quotes.quote:
we aligned a 
previously reported structure of the autoinhibited TYK2 PK-TK domain fragment to the 
FERM-SH2-PK module from the full-length JAK1 dimer complex (Fig. 6A, left) (18). 
This model suggests a compact JAK monomer in which the TK is folded back on the 
FERM-SH2 domain, thereby occluding the activation loop and kinase active site to mediate 
autoinhibition. This closed state is incompatible with JAK dimerization due to a steric clash 
between the PK domain and opposing FERM domain within the JAK dimer.

experiment.system: JAK1 dimer cryo-EM model plus hTYK2 PK-TK crystal structure (PDB 4OLI)
experiment.perturbation: in silico docking/superposition of the autoinhibited PK-TK fragment
experiment.measurement: steric compatibility of the modeled closed state with the observed dimer

text: Mapping two previously defined classes of activating JAK2 mutations onto the active JAK1-IFNλR1 structure showed that mutations increasing JAK phosphorylation without inducing receptor dimerization cluster at the FERM-PK-TK interface of the autoinhibited model, whereas mutations increasing both phosphorylation and dimerization reside at the PK-PK dimerization interface.

quotes.quote:
Mapping these 
two classes of mutations onto the active JAK1-IFNλR1 structure indicates that mutations 
which increase JAK phosphorylation without inducing dimerization cluster at the FERM-
PK-TK interface in the autoinhibited model, suggesting that destabilizing this inter-domain 
interaction releases JAK from autoinhibition (Fig. 6B). Conversely, those mutations that 
induce JAK phosphorylation and receptor dimerization reside at the PK-PK dimerization 
interface, favoring JAK dimerization (Fig. 6C).

Residues are labeled according 
to their position in mJAK1: Ala722 (JAK2 Ile682→Phe), Arg723 (JAK2 Arg683→Gly), 
Phe733 (JAK2 Phe694→Leu).

experiment.system: Active JAK1-IFNλR1 structure plus autoinhibited model, with JAK2 mutants previously classified by single-molecule receptor tracking and phosphorylation
experiment.perturbation: observational (mapping of published mutation classes onto the structures)
experiment.measurement: spatial clustering of each mutation class at defined interfaces

text: Mutations that introduce flexibility into the Cullin scaffold backbone greatly limit substrate ubiquitination, indicating that simple tethering alone is not sufficient and that scaffold rigidity/orientational specificity is required.

quotes.quote:
However, simple tethering alone is not sufficient to stimulate substrate
ubiquitination - the Cullin scaffold backbone must be rigid to function properly (Fig. 3B)
(32). Mutations that introduce flexibility into the scaffold greatly limit substrate
ubiquitination (33), presumably because of loss of orientational specificity.

experiment.system: Cullin-RING-F Box ubiquitin ligase complex tethering substrate and E2 enzyme
experiment.perturbation: mutations introducing flexibility into the Cullin scaffold backbone
experiment.measurement: substrate ubiquitination

text: Mathematical models predict a biphasic scaffold-concentration effect — increasing scaffold first promotes and then, in excess of partner proteins, inhibits partner interaction — and this has been observed experimentally for Ste5 in the yeast mating MAPK pathway (though the authors note the degree of inhibition at high Ste5 expression is small) and for JIP1 overexpression inhibiting JNK signaling.

quotes.quote:
Mathematical models predict that increasing the concentration of scaffold protein will first
favor increased interaction between partner proteins, but then, at higher concentrations (in
excess of the component partner proteins), will titrate partner proteins into separate
complexes, thus inhibiting their interaction (Fig. 3C) (34). Some hint of this biphasic effect
has been demonstrated experimentally for the scaffold protein Ste5 in the yeast mating
MAPK pathway response (35), although the degree of inhibition at high scaffold protein
expression is small. Inhibition of JNK MAPK signaling due to over-expression of the JNK
interacting protein 1 (JIP1) scaffold also demonstrates the biphasic effect (36).

experiment.system: yeast mating MAPK pathway (Ste5) and mammalian JNK pathway (JIP1); mathematical models
experiment.perturbation: varying/over-expressing scaffold protein concentration
experiment.measurement: pathway response / extent of partner interaction and signaling output

text: KSR allosterically activates the Raf kinase domain via its kinase-like domain, and Raf activity does not decrease biphasically with increasing KSR; instead increased KSR binding monotonically increases the amount of active Raf.

quotes.quote:
the KSR scaffold protein also allosterically activates the kinase domain
of Raf (Fig. 4B) (38). This allosteric effect of KSR is mediated by a kinase-like domain in
KSR which binds to and activates Raf. This scaffold function appears to be distinct from
canonical tethering because there is no indication that Raf activity biphasically decreases
with increasing concentrations of KSR (38). Instead, binding of increased amounts of KSR
to Raf monotonically increases the amount of active Raf enzyme.

experiment.system: mammalian ERK MAPK cascade components KSR and Raf
experiment.perturbation: varying KSR concentration / KSR binding to Raf
experiment.measurement: Raf kinase activity (amount of active Raf)

text: The VWA domain of the Ste5 scaffold acts as a co-activator required to allow the MAPKK Ste7 to phosphorylate the MAPK Fus3; without scaffold, activated Ste7 cannot phosphorylate Fus3 although it phosphorylates other substrates, and the VWA domain does not modulate Ste7–Fus3 association.

quotes.quote:
A von Willebrand factor type A (VWA) domain in this scaffold protein is
required to allosterically unlock the MAPK Fus3 so that it becomes a good substrate for the
MAPKK Ste7 - in the absence of scaffold, activated Ste7 cannot phosphorylate the MAPK
Fus3, although it is catalytically competent to phosphorylate other potential substrates

it
does not appear to modulate the association of the MAPKK Ste7 with the MAPK Fus3; instead it
specifically enhances the phosphorylation of Fus3 by Ste7

experiment.system: yeast mating MAPK components Ste5 VWA domain, Ste7, Fus3 (in vitro reconstitution)
experiment.perturbation: presence/absence of Ste5 VWA domain
experiment.measurement: phosphorylation of Fus3 by Ste7; Ste7–Fus3 association

text: ERK-mediated feedback phosphorylation of the KSR scaffold and Raf disrupts MAPKKK binding to KSR and shuts down pathway activation; mutation of the KSR phosphorylation sites causes scaffold dissociation from the plasma membrane and abnormal, sustained pathway activation.

quotes.quote:
These modifications
disrupt binding of the MAPKKK to the KSR scaffold and shut down pathway activation
(Fig. 1D) (24). Mutation of the KSR phosphorylation sites results in dissociation of the
scaffold from the plasma membrane and abnormal pathway dynamics, including sustained
pathway activation.

experiment.system: mammalian KSR-scaffolded three-tiered MAPK pathway
experiment.perturbation: mutation of KSR feedback phosphorylation sites
experiment.measurement: KSR membrane localization, Raf–KSR binding, pathway activation dynamics

text: Phosphorylation of the yeast Ste5 PM helix by Cdk1 blocks scaffold association with the plasma membrane, attenuating mating signaling after cells commit to Start of the cell cycle.

quotes.quote:
Phosphorylation of the yeast Ste5 scaffold protein by the cell-cycle regulated
kinase, cyclin-dependent kinase 1 (Cdk1), blocks association of the scaffold with the plasma
membrane, thereby specifically attenuating mating signaling after cells have committed to
the ‘Start’ (G1-S transition) of the cell cycle

experiment.system: yeast mating MAPK pathway, Ste5 scaffold
experiment.perturbation: Cdk1 phosphorylation of Ste5 PM helix (cell-cycle stage)
experiment.measurement: Ste5 membrane association and mating pathway signaling

text: Upon T cell activation, Zap70 phosphorylates tyrosine motifs on the scaffolds LAT and SLP-76, creating docking sites for SH2-domain proteins; this phosphorylation-induced assembly triggers downstream T cell activation pathways, whereas basally LAT and SLP-76 do not assemble active complexes.

quotes.quote:
Under basal
conditions, LAT and SLP-76 do not assemble active signaling complexes. However, upon T
cell activation, the tyrosine kinase Zap70 is activated and recruited to the T cell receptor and
phosphorylates a number of tyrosine motifs within the scaffold proteins LAT and SLP-76.
These phosphorylated sites act as docking motifs for several Src Homology 2 (SH2)
domain-containing proteins (10, 26). The phosphorylation-induced assembly of this complex
triggers the major downstream pathways of T cell activation.

experiment.system: T cells, LAT/SLP-76 scaffold complexes
experiment.perturbation: T cell receptor activation
experiment.measurement: scaffold tyrosine phosphorylation, SH2-protein recruitment, downstream pathway activation

text: YopM from Yersinia pestis is a scaffold-like protein secreted into host immune cells that links two kinases (Rsk1 and Prk2) that do not normally interact; their binding and activation by YopM is necessary for Y. pestis virulence.

quotes.quote:
The pathogenic bacteria, Yersinia pestis, produces a scaffold-like protein
(YopM) that artificially links together two kinases (Rsk1 and Prk2) that do not normally
interact (Fig. 5A). YopM is secreted into host immune cells, and although the exact
consequence of linking these two kinases is unclear, the binding and activation of the Rsk1
and Prk2 kinases by YopM is necessary for Y. pestis virulence (41, 42).

experiment.system: Yersinia pestis infection of host immune cells
experiment.perturbation: YopM expression/secretion (and loss of Rsk1/Prk2 binding)
experiment.measurement: kinase binding and activation; bacterial virulence

text: Fusing functional elements of the yeast mating and high-osmolarity MAPK scaffold proteins into a chimeric scaffold redirected a mating input to an osmolarity response.

quotes.quote:
This strategy was successfully used in S. cerevisiae
to link the mating and high osmolarity stress MAPK pathway scaffold proteins so that a
mating input resulted in an osmolarity response (Fig. 5B) (45).

experiment.system: S. cerevisiae MAPK pathways
experiment.perturbation: engineered chimeric Ste5–Pbs2 scaffold
experiment.measurement: pathway output (osmolarity response to mating input)

text: Modular recruitment of positive and negative effectors (e.g., phosphatases) to the Ste5 scaffold generated synthetic feedback loops that dramatically altered dynamics and dose-response behaviors of the yeast mating MAPK pathway.

quotes.quote:
A design strategy using modular
recruitment of positive and negative effectors to the Ste5 scaffold generated feedback loops
that result in a diverse array of MAPK pathway responses (46). By tethering components
such as phosphatases to a scaffold-kinase signaling complex, the dynamics and dose-
response behaviors of the yeast mating MAPK pathway were altered dramatically (Fig. 5C).

experiment.system: yeast mating MAPK pathway with engineered Ste5 scaffold
experiment.perturbation: tethering positive/negative effectors (e.g. phosphatases) to the scaffold
experiment.measurement: pathway dynamics and dose-response

text: An artificial scaffold protein tethering three enzymes of a synthetic metabolic pathway in E. coli enhanced mevalonate production by ~100-fold.

quotes.quote:
Remarkably, an artificial
scaffold protein that tethered together three enzymes in a synthetic metabolic pathway in E.
coli was found to enhance mevalonate production by ~100-fold (Fig. 5D) (50).

experiment.system: synthetic mevalonate pathway in E. coli
experiment.perturbation: expression of an artificial scaffold tethering three pathway enzymes
experiment.measurement: mevalonate titer

text: Phosphorylation of at least 4 sites on Ste5 depends on Fus3 recruitment through the Fus3-binding domain; these sites inhibit pathway activity, and mutation of the Fus3-BD does not prevent mating but yields a much more graded shmooing response to α-factor.

quotes.quote:
Phosphorylation of at least 4
sites on the Ste5 scaffold is dependent on recruitment of Fus3 though the Fus3-BD.
These regulatory phosphorylation sites on the scaffold inhibit pathway activity and are
thought to help shape the ultrasensitive cell morphology response (shmooing) that occurs
during mating. Mutation of the Fus3-BD does not prevent mating but rather leads to a
much more graded shmooing response when stimulated by α-factor (27, 28, 39).

experiment.system: yeast mating pathway, Ste5 scaffold
experiment.perturbation: mutation of the Fus3-binding domain of Ste5
experiment.measurement: Ste5 phosphorylation, mating, dose-response of shmooing to α-factor

text: For an enzyme that brings together two small-molecule substrates, the effective concentration may be as large as 10^8 M, a consequence of avoiding the entropic penalty of molecules finding one another in solution; estimates of the entropic penalty for bringing two protein molecules together vary widely.

quotes.quote: For an enzyme that brings together two small-molecule substrates, the effective concentration may be as large as 108 M (29).

Theoretical and experimental estimates for the entropic penalty for bringing two protein
molecules together vary widely, however (30, 31).

experiment.system: enzymes binding two small-molecule substrates (physical-organic analysis)
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: effective concentration of tethered substrates

text: Compared with other mechanically ventilated groups, patients with SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia had similar age, race and sex profiles but significantly higher self-reported Hispanic or Latino ethnicity and body mass index.

quotes.quote:
Compared with these patients, patients with 
SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia had similar age, race and sex profiles, but had 
a significantly higher self-reported Hispanic or Latino ethnicity and 
body mass index (Fig. 1c–f, Extended Data Table 1).

experiment.system: 88 patients with SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia vs 253 mechanically ventilated comparison patients (SCRIPT cohort)
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: demographic comparison (age, race, sex, ethnicity, BMI) with statistical tests

text: Patients with severe SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia had longer ICU length of stay and longer duration of ventilation than all comparison groups, with severity of illness (SOFA, APS) similar to other pneumonia, and mortality not different from the rest of the cohort (25% versus 35%, P = 0.10, χ2 = 2.63).

quotes.quote:
Patients with severe SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia had 
longer lengths of stay in the ICU and required longer periods of ventila-
tion compared with all pneumonia and non-pneumonia controls (Fig. 1i, 
j).

Mortality in patients with COVID-19 was similar 
to patients in other groups (25% versus 35%, P = 0.10, χ2 = 2.63, χ2-tests of 
proportions).

experiment.system: SCRIPT cohort of mechanically ventilated patients
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: ICU length of stay, duration of mechanical ventilation, SOFA/APS scores, mortality

text: On the day of first BAL, patients with severe SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia had increased C-reactive protein compared with other pneumonias, whereas other inflammation biomarkers were at similar levels.

quotes.quote:
On the day that their first BAL samples were taken, patients with severe 
SARS-CoV-2 pneumonia had increased levels of C-reactive protein com-
pared with patients with other pneumonias, whereas other biomarkers 
of inflammation were found at similar levels (Extended Data Fig. 1d–i).

experiment.system: SCRIPT cohort BAL patients
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: clinical blood biomarkers (CRP, D-dimer, ferritin, procalcitonin, CPK, LDH)

text: k-means clustering of the 1,194 significantly variable genes across diagnosis in alveolar macrophages identified 5 clusters; the majority of COVID-19 patients clustered together, with cluster 1 containing interferon-response genes and the chemokine genes CCL7, CCL8 and CCL13.

quotes.quote:
k-means clustering of the 1,194 significantly 
variable genes (q < 0.05, likelihood-ratio test) across diagnosis identi-
fied 5 clusters (Fig. 2c, Supplementary Data 1–3). Notably, the majority 
of patients with COVID-19 clustered together. Cluster 1 contained genes 
specifically upregulated in patients with COVID-19 and was character-
ized by genes involved in the response to interferon. Cluster 1 also 
included genes encoding the chemokines CCL7, CCL8 and CCL13, which 
drive recruitment of monocytes and T cells.

experiment.system: flow cytometry-sorted CD206hi alveolar macrophages from BAL within 48 h of intubation (COVID-19, other pneumonia, non-pneumonia controls, healthy volunteers)
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: bulk RNA-seq, likelihood-ratio test for variable genes and k-means clustering

text: SARS-CoV-2 transcripts were detected in alveolar macrophage transcriptomes from 67% of samples with PCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, and in 38% of these both positive- and negative-strand transcripts were detected.

quotes.quote:
We detected SARS-CoV-2 
transcripts in alveolar macrophage transcriptomes from 67% of samples 
with PCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection. In 38% of these samples, we 
detected both positive- and negative-strand SARS-CoV-2 transcripts 
(Extended Data Fig. 3b, c).

experiment.system: sorted alveolar macrophages from BAL of PCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 patients
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: bulk RNA-seq reads aligned to hybrid human/SARS-CoV-2/influenza genome including an added negative-strand transcript

text: WGCNA identified macrophage maturation modules: module 4 correlated positively with the percentage of CD206hi alveolar macrophages (R = 0.61) and module 12 negatively (R = −0.62).

quotes.quote:
we identified modules related to macrophage 
maturation, including module 4, which exhibited a positive correla-
tion with the percentage of CD206hi alveolar macrophages (R = 0.61), 
and module 12, which exhibited a negative correlation with percent-
age of CD206hi macrophages (R = −0.62) (Extended Data Fig. 5c).

experiment.system: bulk RNA-seq of sorted alveolar macrophages with paired flow cytometry
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: WGCNA module correlation with CD206hi macrophage percentage

text: In serial COVID-19 samples, interferon-response gene expression decreased over time in patients discharged home (five patients) or to an inpatient facility (two patients) but was largely unchanged in those discharged to a LTAC (five patients) or who died (two patients); SARS-CoV-2 transcript abundance correlated negatively with time since intubation (ρ = −0.49).

quotes.quote:
Analysis of the serial samples from patients with COVID-19 who were 
discharged home (five patients) or to an inpatient facility (two patients) 
demonstrated decreased expression of interferon-response genes as 
the disease progressed, whereas in patients who were discharged to

a long-term acute care facility (LTAC) (five patients) or who died (two 
patients), the expression of interferon-response genes was largely 
unchanged (Extended Data Fig. 5h). Consistent with these findings, 
we observed a significant negative correlation between abundance 
of SARS-CoV-2 transcripts in patients with confirmed COVID-19 and 
the time since intubation (ρ = −0.49, Spearman correlation)

experiment.system: serial BAL alveolar macrophage samples from patients with COVID-19
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: bulk RNA-seq interferon-response gene expression over time and Spearman correlation of SARS-CoV-2 transcript abundance with days since intubation

numbers.quantity: correlation of SARS-CoV-2 transcripts with time since intubation

text: Integrated single-cell RNA-seq of 77,146 cells from 10 patients with severe COVID-19 resolved six alveolar macrophage clusters: four monocyte-derived (MoAM) clusters characterized by CCL2 expression with gradually increasing maturation genes, and two tissue-resident (TRAM) clusters.

quotes.quote:
Alveolar macrophages contained six clusters. Four clusters 
of monocyte-derived alveolar macrophages (MoAMs) were charac-
terized by CCL2 expression and gradually increasing expression of 
genes associated with alveolar macrophage maturation. The other two 
clusters expressed markers of tissue-resident alveolar macrophages 
(TRAM) (Fig. 4b, Extended Data Fig. 6a).

UMAP plot showing integrated analysis of 77,146 cells isolated from 10 
patients with severe COVID-19 within 48 h after intubation.

experiment.system: BAL cells from 10 patients with severe COVID-19 collected within 48 h of intubation (plus two additional patients)
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: single-cell RNA-seq with integration, clustering and marker gene expression

text: Type I interferon expression was not detected in the single-cell dataset, whereas IFNG expression was detected in T cells from all ten patients with COVID-19.

quotes.quote:
We did not detect expres-
sion of type I interferons in our single-cell dataset or in other publicly 
available single-cell RNA-seq datasets9,10 obtained from BAL fluid later 
in the clinical course of patients with COVID-19 (data not shown). By 
contrast, expression of type II interferon (IFNG) was detected in T cells 
from all ten patients with COVID-19 (Fig. 4c, Extended Data Fig. 6b).

experiment.system: BAL single-cell RNA-seq from 10 patients with severe COVID-19
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: per-cluster expression of type I interferon genes and IFNG

text: SARS-CoV-2 transcripts were detected in epithelial cells and also in migratory CCR7+ dendritic cells and the MoAM2 and TRAM2 clusters, which do not express ACE2; more positive- than negative-strand transcripts were detected in both single-cell and bulk RNA-seq.

quotes.quote:
As expected, positive- and negative-strand SARS-CoV-2 transcripts 
were detected in epithelial cells. We also detected SARS-CoV-2 tran-
scripts in migratory CCR7+ dendritic cells, and MoAM2 and TRAM2 
clusters, which do not express ACE2 (Fig. 4d, Extended Data Fig. 6c).

we detected more transcripts for positive compared with 
negative strands in both our single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data (Fig. 4d,
