text: Phosphorylation of the R-Smad linker region by Erk MAPK, CDKs, and GSK3β inhibits Smad nuclear accumulation; linker phosphorylation by cyclin C-CDK8 or cyclin T-CDK9 primes secondary GSK3 phosphorylation, generates binding sites for E3 ubiquitin ligases such as Smurf1 and NEDD4-2, targets Smads for degradation, and triggers recruitment of YAP or Pin1.

quotes.quote:
The phos-
phorylation of the linker region of R-Smads by
Erk MAPK (Kretzschmar et al. 1997), CDKs
(Matsuura et al. 2004; Wang et al. 2009), and
GSK3b (Fuentealba et al. 2007; Millet et al.
2009) has been shown to inhibit Smad nuclear
accumulation.

This phos-
phorylation step primes the secondary phos-
phorylation of the linker region by GSK3,
generates binding sites for E3 ubiquitin ligases,
such as Smurf1 and NEDD4-2, and targets
Smad proteins for degradation

Linker phosphorylation
by CDK8 or CDK9 also triggers the recruitment
of Yes-associated protein (YAP)

experiment.system: cells expressing R-Smads with kinases CDK8/CDK9, GSK3, Erk MAPK
experiment.perturbation: kinase-mediated linker phosphorylation / mutation of linker sites
experiment.measurement: Smad nuclear accumulation, E3 ligase binding, Smad degradation, YAP/Pin1 recruitment

text: TRAF2-deficient cells retain relatively intact TNF signaling to NF-κB despite deficient AP-1 activation, and TRAF5 knockouts also show normal NF-κB activation by TNF, whereas TRAF2/5 double knockout cells are defective in IKK activation.

quotes.quote:
despite deficiencies in AP-1 activation, TRAF2-deficient cells 
have relatively intact TNF signaling to NF-κB (Yeh et al., 1997). 
TRAF5 was also shown to interact with the TNFR1 signaling 
complex, yet TRAF5 knockouts also exhibit normal NF-κB 
activation by TNF; TRAF2/5 double knockout cells, however, 
are defective in IKK activation

experiment.system: TRAF2-deficient, TRAF5-deficient and TRAF2/5 double knockout cells
experiment.perturbation: gene knockout plus TNF stimulation
experiment.measurement: IKK/NF-κB and AP-1 activation

text: Knockdown of the K63-specific E2 ligase Ubc13 blocks TRAF2 autoubiquitination but not NF-κB activation, and ubc13−/− macrophages show a similar lack of effect, while another group observed partial defects in TNF signaling to NF-κB in ubc13+/− heterozygous macrophages and splenocytes.

quotes.quote:
knockdown of the 
K63-specific E2 ligase Ubc13 blocks TRAF2 autoubiquitination 
but not activation of NF-κB, while ubc13−/− macrophages show 
a similar lack of effect on NF-κB activation

another group did 
observe partial defects in TNF signaling to NF-κB in ubc13+/− 
heterozygous macrophages and splenocytes

experiment.system: macrophages and splenocytes with Ubc13 knockdown or knockout
experiment.perturbation: Ubc13 depletion/deletion plus TNF stimulation
experiment.measurement: TRAF2 autoubiquitination and NF-κB activation

text: Reconstitution of TRAF6-deficient cells with a TRAF6 mutant lacking the RING finger completely restored IL-1-induced NF-κB activation but not JNK activation, whereas a TRAF6 RING finger point mutation was reported unable to restore NF-κB activation in TRAF6 knockout cells.

quotes.quote:
Reconstitu-
tion of TRAF6-deficient cells with a TRAF6 mutant lacking the 
signature motif of E3 RING-finger ligases—that is, the RING fin-
ger itself—completely restored IL-1-induced activation of NF-κB 
but not activation of JNK (Kobayashi et al., 2001). More recently, 
however, it has been shown that a ring finger point muta-
tion of TRAF6 is unable to restore NF-κB activation in TRAF6 
knockout cells

experiment.system: TRAF6-deficient/knockout cells
experiment.perturbation: reconstitution with RING-deleted or RING point-mutant TRAF6, IL-1 stimulation
experiment.measurement: NF-κB and JNK activation

text: TRAF3 negatively regulates NIK by inducing its ubiquitination and degradation in the resting state, and the lethality of TRAF3-deficient mice was rescued genetically by deleting the p100 gene.

quotes.quote:
In the resting 
state, TRAF3 induces NIK ubiquitination and degradation, but 
upon stimulation TRAF3 undergoes signal-dependent degra-
dation

this negative role of TRAF3 has been demonstrated genetically 
by rescuing the lethality of TRAF3-deficient mice by deleting 
the p100 gene

experiment.system: TRAF3-deficient mice and cells
experiment.perturbation: TRAF3 deletion combined with p100 gene deletion
experiment.measurement: NIK levels/noncanonical pathway activation and mouse viability

text: RIP1 binds NEMO and is essential for TNFα-induced IKK and NF-κB activation; in the absence of RIP1, IKK is still recruited through TRAF2 but is not activated, and RIP1 kinase activity is dispensable for IKK activation.

quotes.quote:
RIP1 binds to NEMO and is essential for TNFα-induced IKK 
and NF-κB activation

In the absence of RIP1, IKK 
recruitment occurs through TRAF2 but does not lead to IKK 
activation

surprisingly RIP1 kinase 
activity was shown to be dispensable for IKK activation

experiment.system: RIP1-deficient cells in TNFR1 signaling
experiment.perturbation: RIP1 deletion or kinase-dead RIP1, TNFα stimulation
experiment.measurement: IKK recruitment and IKK/NF-κB activation

text: TNFα-induced RIP1 ubiquitination is completely abolished in traf2−/− cells while TNFα-induced IKK activation remains partly intact, and RIP1 lysine acceptor mutants that fail to be ubiquitinated also do not associate with TNFR1.

quotes.quote:
the RIP1 lysine 
acceptor mutants that fail to be ubiquitinated also do not asso-
ciate with TNFR1

while TNFα-induced 
RIP1 ubiquitination appears to be completely abolished in 
traf2−/− cells, TNFα-induced IKK activation remains partly intact

experiment.system: traf2−/− cells and cells expressing RIP1 lysine acceptor mutants
experiment.perturbation: TRAF2 deletion or RIP1 lysine mutation, TNFα stimulation
experiment.measurement: RIP1 ubiquitination, TNFR1 association, IKK activation

text: Most NF-κB signaling pathways are normal in the absence of RIP3, and RIP1 is not required for activation of the noncanonical pathway through CD40 or LTβR.

quotes.quote:
most NF-κB signaling pathways are normal in the 
absence of RIP3

RIP1 is not required for activation of the 
noncanonical pathway through CD40 or LTβR

experiment.system: RIP3-deficient and RIP1-deficient cells
experiment.perturbation: gene deletion, receptor stimulation (CD40, LTβR)
experiment.measurement: NF-κB activation

text: Genetic ablation of TAK1 gives variable deficiencies across canonical pathways — TNFR1 signaling to NF-κB appears completely abolished — while the LTβR pathway does not depend on TAK1.

quotes.quote:
genetic ablation of TAK1 reveals vari-
able NF-κB activation deficiencies in different canonical sig-
naling pathways. TNFR1 signaling to NF-κB appears com-
pletely abolished

even though the pathways triggered by 
LTβR lead to IKK through many of the same signaling inter-
mediates, this pathway does not depend on TAK1

experiment.system: TAK1-deficient cells/mice
experiment.perturbation: TAK1 genetic ablation, stimulation via TNFR1, antigen receptor or LTβR
experiment.measurement: NF-κB activation

text: Mice deficient in IKKα survive embryonic development but die perinatally with aborted epidermal and skeletal development, while NEMO-deficient mice die embryonically of massive hepatocyte apoptosis and NEMO-deficient cells show a more severe and broader loss of NF-κB activation than IKKβ knockout cells.

quotes.quote:
Mice 
deficient in IKKα survive embryonic development but die perinatally due to multiple morphological 
defects, in particular aborted epidermal and skeletal develop-
ment.

NEMO-deficient mice also die embryonically of massive 
hepatocyte apoptosis. NEMO-deficient cells exhibit a more 
severe and broader loss of NF-κB activation than do IKKβ 
knockout cells

experiment.system: IKKα, IKKβ and NEMO knockout mice and cells
experiment.perturbation: targeted gene disruption
experiment.measurement: viability, developmental phenotype, NF-κB activation

text: NEMO trimers with a predicted molecular weight of 150,000 elute at an apparent molecular weight of 550 kDa upon gel filtration, and recombinant NEMO and IKKβ associate in a 2:2 molar ratio whose minimal interaction domains form a tetramer that can further assemble into octamers and dodecamers.

quotes.quote:
NEMO 
trimers with a predicted molecular weight of 150,000 elute at 
an apparent molecular weight of 550 kDa upon gel filtration

Recombinant NEMO 
and IKKβ appear to associate in a 2:2 molar ratio and the mini-
mum interaction domains form a dimer of dimers (tetramer) that 
can further assemble into octamers and dodecamers

experiment.system: recombinant NEMO and IKKβ in vitro
experiment.perturbation: in vitro reconstitution/gel filtration and biophysical analysis
experiment.measurement: apparent molecular weight, stoichiometry and oligomeric state

text: Competition experiments and biophysical analyses with the NBD peptide indicate IKKβ binds NEMO with considerably higher affinity than IKKα, and IKKα is less sensitive to mutation of two NBD residues (Asp749 and Trp742) that abolish IKKβ binding to NEMO.

quotes.quote:
Competition experiments and biophysical analy-
ses using the NBD peptide indicate that IKKβ binds to NEMO 
with considerably higher affinity than IKKα

IKKα is less sensitive to 
mutation of two residues within the NBD (Asp749 and Trp742) 
that abolish IKKβ binding to NEMO

experiment.system: IKKα/IKKβ NBD peptides and NEMO
experiment.perturbation: NBD peptide competition and point mutation of Asp749/Trp742
experiment.measurement: binding affinity to NEMO

text: The kinase activity of wild-type IKKβ expressed in yeast is increased by coexpression of NEMO, whereas activity of IKK with T loop serines mutated to glutamic acid is high and unchanged by NEMO coexpression.

quotes.quote:
the kinase activ-
ity of wild-type IKKβ expressed in yeast is increased by coex-
pression of NEMO; however, the activity of IKK in which the T 
loop serines have been mutated to glutamic acid is high and 
unchanged by coexpression of NEMO

experiment.system: human IKKβ reconstituted in yeast
experiment.perturbation: NEMO coexpression; T loop serine-to-glutamic acid mutation
experiment.measurement: IKK kinase activity

text: Kinase-active IKKβ transautophosphorylates kinase-dead IKKβ, an activation requiring leucine zipper-dependent dimerization or artificially enforced oligomerization; deletion or mutation of the leucine zipper blocks activation of overexpressed IKKs but activity is restored by forced oligomerization using an unrelated dimerization interface.

quotes.quote:
kinase-active IKKβ is capable 
of transautophosphorylation of kinase-dead IKKβ, and this 
activation requires leucine zipper-dependent dimerization or 
artificially enforced oligomerization

kinase activity can be restored by forced oli-
gomerization of IKK using an unrelated dimerization interface

experiment.system: overexpressed wild-type and kinase-dead IKKβ
experiment.perturbation: leucine zipper deletion/mutation and forced oligomerization via an unrelated dimerization interface
experiment.measurement: IKK transautophosphorylation and kinase activity

text: Phosphorylation of the IKK NBD serine residue Ser740 inhibits IKK activity and prevents augmentation of recombinant IKK activity by NEMO coexpression, while IKK lacking the NBD exhibits constitutive activity without stimulation and Ser740Ala IKK continues to interact with NEMO.

quotes.quote:
phosphorylation of the IKK NBD serine residues (Ser740) 
inhibits IKK activity and prevents augmentation of recombi-
nant IKK activity by coexpression with NEMO

IKK lacking the NBD, on the other 
hand, exhibits constitutive activity in the absence of stimula-
tion

Because IKK containing Ser740 mutated 
to Ala continues to interact with NEMO

experiment.system: recombinant/overexpressed IKK with NEMO
experiment.perturbation: NBD deletion or Ser740 phosphorylation/mutation to Ala
experiment.measurement: IKK kinase activity and NEMO interaction

text: NEMO becomes phosphorylated at Ser68 within the IKK-binding domain in a stimulus-dependent manner, disrupting NEMO dimers and the IKK–NEMO interaction and thereby terminating signaling.

quotes.quote:
NEMO becomes phosphorylated 
at Ser68 within the IKK-binding domain following stimulation. 
This phosphorylation occurs in a stimulus-dependent manner 
and induces the disruption of NEMO dimers and interaction 
between IKK and NEMO, thereby terminating signaling

experiment.system: stimulated cells expressing NEMO
experiment.perturbation: receptor stimulation; analysis of NEMO Ser68 phosphorylation
experiment.measurement: NEMO dimerization and IKK–NEMO interaction

text: Cells deficient in all three typical IκB proteins show relatively normal nuclear/cytoplasmic p65 distribution but significantly increased basal NF-κB-dependent gene expression, and stimulus-induced activation of canonical NF-κB requires the three typical IκB proteins.

quotes.quote:
cells that lack all three 
subunits show relatively normal nuclear/cytpolasmic p65 distri-
bution but significantly increased basal NF-κB-dependent gene 
expression

This work also definitively confirmed that stimulus-induced 
activation of canonical NF-κB requires the three typical IκB pro-
teins

experiment.system: MEFs lacking IκBα, IκBβ and IκBε
experiment.perturbation: combinatorial IκB gene deletion, stimulation
experiment.measurement: p65 subcellular distribution and NF-κB-dependent gene expression

text: Kinetics of NF-κB inactivation can be grossly restored by placing a different IκB, e.g., IκBβ, under the control of the IκBα promoter, while IκBβ deletion does not dramatically affect NF-κB response kinetics as seen with IκBα or IκBε deletion.

quotes.quote:
the kinetics of NF-κB 
inactivation can be grossly restored by placing a different IκB, 
e.g., IκBβ, under the control of the IκBα promoter

deletion of IκBβ does not dramatically affect 
the kinetics of the NF-κB responses as seen in the deletion of 
IκBα or ε

experiment.system: mouse cells with IκB gene knockouts and IκBβ knocked into the IκBα locus
experiment.perturbation: gene replacement/deletion plus canonical stimulation (e.g., TNF-α)
experiment.measurement: kinetics of NF-κB activation and inactivation

text: Normal processing of p105 to p50 occurs in an E1 Ub-activating enzyme-deficient cell line, supporting p105 processing via the 20S proteasome independent of ubiquitination and posttranslationally.

quotes.quote:
Normal process-
ing of p105 to p50 in an E1 Ub-activating enzyme-deficient 
cell line, complemented by in vitro analysis, strongly suggests 
that p105 processing can occur via the 20S proteasome, inde-
pendent of ubiquitination, and in a manner that is inconsistent 
with cotranslational processing

experiment.system: E1 ubiquitin-activating enzyme-deficient cell line plus in vitro system
experiment.perturbation: loss of E1 activity
experiment.measurement: p105 processing to p50

text: Phosphorylation of p100 at serines 866, 870, and 872 (Ser865, 869, and 871 in human p100) leads to recruitment of SCFβTrCP and polyubiquitination of Lys855, with subsequent degradation or processing to p52; processing of p100 requires IKKα and NIK.

quotes.quote:
Phos-
phorylation of p100 at serines 866, 870, and 872 (Ser865, 869, 
and 871 in human p100) leads to the recruitment of SCFβTrCP, 
polyubiquitination of Lys855

Processing of p100 requires IKKα and is predominantly stim-
ulus dependent

experiment.system: cells expressing p100 with IKKα/NIK signaling
experiment.perturbation: stimulation and mutation of p100 phosphoacceptor/ubiquitination residues; IKKα requirement
experiment.measurement: p100 phosphorylation, ubiquitination and processing to p52

text: In the absence of IκBζ, LPS- or IL-1-induced expression of a subset of NF-κB-regulated genes is lost; IκBζ associates with p50 on the IL-6 promoter, and IL-6 is not inducibly expressed in IκBζ knockout cells.

quotes.quote:
in the absence of 
IκBζ, LPS- or IL-1-induced expression of a subset of NF-κB-
regulated genes is lost

IκBζ is 
found associated with p50 on the promoter of IL-6, which is not 
inducibly expressed in IκBζ knockout cells

experiment.system: IκBζ knockout cells
experiment.perturbation: IκBζ deletion with LPS or IL-1 stimulation
experiment.measurement: NF-κB target gene expression and promoter occupancy by IκBζ/p50

text: PKA phosphorylates p65 at Ser276 following IκBα degradation, promoting interaction with CBP and p300, and MSK1−/−MSK2−/− cells have diminished transcriptional activity in response to TNF.

quotes.quote:
phosphory-
lates p65 at Ser276, promoting the interaction of p65 with the 
transcriptional coactivators CBP (CREB-binding protein) and 
p300

MSK1−/−MSK2−/− cells have diminished 
transcriptional activity in response to TNF

experiment.system: cells with PKA/MSK1/2 activity; MSK1−/−MSK2−/− cells
experiment.perturbation: kinase deletion, TNF stimulation
experiment.measurement: p65 Ser276 phosphorylation, CBP/p300 interaction, NF-κB transcriptional activity

text: Acetylation of p65 Lys310 enhances transcriptional activity without altering DNA or IκB binding; Lys310 acetylation is blocked in the absence of Ser276 phosphorylation or by overexpressing catalytically inactive PKAc, and Ser536 phosphorylation significantly enhances Lys310 acetylation.

quotes.quote:
it is acetylation of Lys310 that has most clearly been shown 
to enhance transcriptional activity without altering binding 
to DNA or IκB (Chen et al., 2002b). Acetylation of Lys310 is 
blocked either in the absence of phosphorylation of Ser276 
or by overexpressing catalytically inactive PKAc

Ser536 phosphoryla-
tion, while not completely required, significantly enhanced 
Lys310 acetylation

experiment.system: cells expressing wild-type and mutant p65
experiment.perturbation: Ser276/Ser536 mutation and catalytically inactive PKAc overexpression
experiment.measurement: p65 Lys310 acetylation, DNA/IκB binding and transcriptional activity

text: IKKα phosphorylates CBP in a stimulus-dependent manner, upregulating CBP activity and increasing its binding to p65 while decreasing binding to p53; in IKKα−/− cells binding of CBP to CREB is increased.

quotes.quote:
IKKα phosphorylates CBP in a stimulus-dependent manner, 
inducing upregulation of CBP activity, increased binding to 
p65, and decreased binding to p53

Interestingly in IKKα−/− cells, 
binding of CBP to CREB is increased

experiment.system: cells including IKKα−/− fibroblasts
experiment.perturbation: IKKα deletion and stimulus-induced CBP phosphorylation
experiment.measurement: CBP phosphorylation and binding to p65, p53 and CREB

text: IKKα represses transcription of the tumor suppressor Maspin by acting at the maspin promoter, supporting a direct mechanism of IKKα action independent of NF-κB; IKKα also contributes to termination of inflammatory transcriptional responses in macrophages, possibly by promoting nuclear degradation of p65 and c-Rel.

quotes.quote:
the recent demonstration 
that IKKα represses transcription of the tumor suppressor 
Maspin by acting at the maspin promoter strongly supports 
a direct mechanism of action by IKKα that is independent of 
NF-κB

IKKα is also involved in termination of inflam-
matory transcriptional responses in macrophages, possi-
bly by promoting the nuclear degradation of both p65 and 
c-Rel

experiment.system: macrophages and prostate cancer cells
experiment.perturbation: manipulation of IKKα (deletion/nuclear IKKα activity)
experiment.measurement: maspin promoter occupancy/transcription and inflammatory gene expression, p65/c-Rel levels

text: Dephosphorylation scores computed from MRBLE:Dephos were highly reproducible across experimental replicates for both PP1 and PP2A-B55, despite the PP1 preparation having higher activity than the PP2A-B55 preparation.

quotes.quote:
Although the PP1 preparation had
higher activity than the PP2A-B55 preparation, resulting in much
larger differences between initial and final peptide phosphorylation
levels for PP1 (Appendix Fig S2–S4), “dephosphorylation scores”
calculated
in
this
manner
were
highly
reproducible
across
experimental replicates for both proteins

experiment.system: MRBLE:Dephos bead peptide library
experiment.perturbation: incubation with recombinant PP1 or PP2A-B55 purified from HeLa cells, in triplicate
experiment.measurement: per-peptide dephosphorylation score compared across replicate experiments

text: MRBLE:Dephos results were compared to a standard malachite-green phosphate release assay on a panel of five phosphorylated proline-directed Thr sites and gave comparable patterns of specificity.

quotes.quote:
we compared MRBLE:Dephos results to a standard
phosphate release assay with a panel of five phosphorylated
proline-directed Thr sites and found that MRBLE:Dephos results
gave comparable patterns of specificity (Fig 1F).

experiment.system: phosphopeptides with proline-directed Thr sites
experiment.perturbation: dephosphorylation by PP1 or PP2A-B55 in solution vs on beads
experiment.measurement: malachite green phosphate release compared with MRBLE dephos score

text: Phosphoproteomics of nocodazole-arrested HeLa mitotic lysates treated for 5 min with specific PP1 (Nipp1) or PP2A-B55 (thio-Arpp19) inhibitors identified 38,173 phosphorylation sites, of which 2,116 and 751 increased by 1.5-fold or more after PP2A-B55 or PP1 inhibition respectively, with only 152 sites (5.6%) increased in both conditions.

quotes.quote: This resulted in the identification of 38,173

phosphorylation sites of which 2,116 and 751 were significantly
increased in phosphorylation by 1.5-fold or more after PP2A-B55 or
PP1 inhibition, respectively (Dataset EV1). Only 152 sites (5.6%)
showed an increase in both conditions attesting to high specificity of
the phosphatases.

experiment.system: nocodazole-arrested HeLa mitotic cell lysates (ATP-depleted, mimicking mitotic exit)
experiment.perturbation: addition of Nipp1 central domain (PP1 inhibitor) or thiophosphorylated Arpp19 (PP2A-B55 inhibitor) for 5 min, versus RVxF-mutant Nipp1 and Arpp19 S62A controls
experiment.measurement: TMT-labeled phosphopeptide enrichment and LC-MS/MS quantification of site abundance changes

text: Known regulated sites validated the lysate assay: B55-regulated sites on ENSA S67 and Arpp19 S62 were identified, and the reported PP1-regulated site H3S28 was stabilized specifically by adding Nipp1.

quotes.quote:
We identified known B55-regulated sites on the
B55 inhibitor ENSA S67 and Arpp19 S62 (Williams et al, 2014),
confirming that PP2A-B55 is active in our assay conditions and
inhibited when adding thio-Arpp19. Furthermore, the reported PP1-
regulated site H3S28 was stabilized specifically by adding Nipp1

experiment.system: mitotic HeLa lysates
experiment.perturbation: thio-Arpp19 or Nipp1 inhibitor addition vs controls
experiment.measurement: TMT phosphoproteomic quantification of known marker sites

text: The PP2A-B55-regulated site set overlapped 124 of 203 phosphorylation sites on 95 proteins (61%) previously identified as high-confidence B55 substrates by Cundell et al, whereas PP1-dependent sites overlapped only 13 of 302 sites from PP1-depleted mitotic cells and 10 of 777 from PP1-catalytic-subunit-addition lysates; the authors attribute the limited PP1 overlap to differences between short-term Nipp1 inhibition and RNAi or purified-PP1 addition approaches.

quotes.quote:
Comparison to previous screens of PP2A-B55 substrates revealed
an overlap of 124 of 203 phosphorylation sites on 95 proteins identi-
fied by Cundell et al (2016) as high-confidence B55 substrates using
siRNA depletion of B55 or MASTL. This 61% overlap

we only identified a few sites that
were previously shown to be PP1 dependent in MS analysis of
mitotic cells depleted of PP1 (Holder et al, 2020) (13 of 302) or in
phosphatases inhibited cell lysates after the addition of PP1 catalytic
subunit (Hoermann et al, 2020) (10 of 777). Our short-term inhibi-
tion of PP1 using Nipp1 is quite distinct from a more long-term inhi-
bition using RNAi of PP1 potentially explaining the limited overlap.

experiment.system: regulated site lists from mitotic lysate phosphoproteomics
experiment.perturbation: observational comparison to published PP1/PP2A-B55 substrate datasets
experiment.measurement: counts and percentage of overlapping phosphorylation sites

numbers.quantity: B55 site overlap with Cundell et al
PP1 site overlap with Holder et al
PP1 site overlap with Hoermann et al

text: Of the 2,116 sites increased upon Arpp19 addition, 1,185 were detected in the Nipp1-treated sample, and 548 of the 751 sites increased upon Nipp1 addition were detected in the Arpp19-treated samples; the authors suggest incomplete detection reflects increased site occupancy enabling detection of otherwise low-abundant sites.

quotes.quote:
revealed that 1,185 of the 2,116 sites significantly increased upon
Arpp19 addition were detected in the Nipp1-treated sample, and
conversely, 548 of the 751 phosphorylation sites significantly
increased upon Nipp1 addition were detected in the Arpp19-treated
samples.

experiment.system: mitotic HeLa lysate TMT phosphoproteomics dataset
experiment.perturbation: Nipp1 vs thio-Arpp19 inhibition
experiment.measurement: cross-detection counts of regulated sites between conditions

numbers.quantity: Arpp19-increased sites detected in Nipp1 sample
Nipp1-increased sites detected in Arpp19 samples

text: PRC1 was dephosphorylated by both PP1 and PP2A-B55 but at distinct sites, showing that the two phosphatases can act on the same protein.

quotes.quote:
Interestingly, proteins like PRC1 were dephosphorylated by
both PP1 and PP2A-B55 but at distinct sites, showing that the two
phosphatases can act on the same protein potentially to regulate dif-
ferent functional aspects.

experiment.system: mitotic HeLa lysates
experiment.perturbation: Nipp1 or thio-Arpp19 inhibition
experiment.measurement: site-level phosphoproteomic assignment of regulated sites per protein

text: In live-cell imaging, Venus/YFP-tagged INCENP S61E failed to translocate to the central spindle during anaphase unlike INCENP WT, and INCENP RNAi cells complemented with S61E showed around 60% binucleated cells; the INCENP T59V S61E mutant also failed to translocate, suggesting S61E affects both T59 dephosphorylation and possibly Mklp2 binding.

quotes.quote:
In contrast to INCENP WT,
S61E did not translocate to the central spindle during anaphase in
agreement with a lack of T59 dephosphorylation (Fig 3D).

we observed around 60% of binucleated
cells in INCENP S61E-complemented cells (Fig 3E). To determine if
the cellular effects of the S61E mutation were purely attributed to a
lack of T59 dephosphorylation, we investigated if the T59V muta-
tion could rescue the S61E phenotype. However, the INCENP T59V
S61E mutant was unable to translocate to the central spindle
(Fig 3D). This suggests that the S61E mutation both affect T59
dephosphorylation and possibly Mklp2 binding.

experiment.system: HeLa cells depleted of endogenous INCENP by RNAi and expressing RNAi-resistant YFP-INCENP WT, S61E, or T59V S61E
experiment.perturbation: INCENP RNAi plus point-mutant complementation
experiment.measurement: time-lapse live-cell microscopy of central spindle localization at anaphase and percentage of binucleated cells

numbers.quantity: binucleated cells in INCENP S61E complementation

text: Mitotic interactome mapping of PP1γ and B55α by YFP affinity purification and miniTurbo proximity labeling identified 923 PP1 interactors and 141 B55 interactors; overlaying with the phosphoproteomic data revealed 319 PP1-regulated sites in the PP1 interactome and 100 PP2A-B55-regulated sites in the B55 interactome.

quotes.quote:
This
resulted in the identification of 923 PP1 interactors and 141 B55
interactors (Dataset EV2). These identified proteins can constitute
both regulators and substrates. Comparing this to the phosphopro-
teomic data revealed that there were 319 PP1-regulated sites in the
PP1 interactome and 100 PP2A-B55-regulated sites in the B55 inter-
actome (Fig 4A and B).

experiment.system: HeLa/FRT/TRex stable cell lines expressing YFP-, BioID- or TurboID-tagged PP1 or B55, synchronized in mitosis
experiment.perturbation: affinity purification and biotin proximity labeling versus controls (twofold enrichment, P < 0.05)
experiment.measurement: label-free LC-MS/MS identification of interactors, intersected with regulated phosphosite lists

text: Integrating interactomes, STRING data and regulated sites produced networks showing that known RVxF-containing proteins such as KNL1 (CASC5), RIF1 and RepoMan (CDCA2) were PP1 substrates and may scaffold dephosphorylation of associated proteins (e.g., CASC5 scaffolding PP1 dephosphorylation of CENPC S261), while PP2A-B55 regulated dephosphorylation of several nucleoporins consistent with Nup153 and TPR being in the interactomes.

quotes.quote:
Several known RVxF-
containing proteins such as KNL1 (CASC5), RIF1, and RepoMan
(CDCA2) were substrates of PP1 as expected but our network analy-
sis also suggested that these proteins coordinate dephosphorylation
of associated proteins. As an example, CASC5 (KNL1) could scaffold
PP1 dephosphorylation of CENPC S261, a phosphorylation site in a
nuclear localization sequence. In agreement with previous work,
PP2A-B55 regulated dephosphorylation of several nucleoporins at
mitotic exit consistent with Nup153 and TPR being present in the
interactomes

experiment.system: integrated PP1/B55 mitotic interactomes, STRING database associations and regulated phosphosites
experiment.perturbation: observational network construction (Cytoscape) with known/predicted RVxF motif annotation
experiment.measurement: network of complexes and dephosphorylation sites

text: MRBLE-Pep measurement of PP1 binding to a Nipp1-derived RVxF/RxVxF peptide library over eight PP1 concentrations yielded absolute affinities that were highly reproducible across replicates over three orders of magnitude and identified substitutions that both enhanced and ablated binding.

quotes.quote:
Repeating these experiments
over eight different PP1 concentrations enabled acquisition of
concentration-dependent binding curves; fitting the mean intensity
of all beads with a given code at different concentrations of PP1γ
and fitting to a Langmuir isotherm made it possible to quantify
absolute affinities

Measured affinities
identified substitutions that both enhanced and ablated binding
(Fig 5B) and were highly reproducible across experimental repli-
cates over three orders of magnitude (Fig 5C).

experiment.system: MRBLE bead-bound library of Nipp1-derived peptides (AKNSRVTFSEDDEII / AKNRAVTFSEDDEII variants)
experiment.perturbation: incubation with PP1 over eight concentrations, with systematic amino acid substitutions and phosphorylations
experiment.measurement: anti-PP1 antibody/Alexa 647 fluorescence per code fit to Langmuir isotherms to obtain Kd

text: Analysis of the PP1 dephosphorylome revealed 15 RVxF motifs that were dephosphorylated by PP1, and phosphopeptide assays confirmed PP1 dephosphorylates RVxF motifs; a Nipp1 peptide with a mutated RVxF motif (RVpTF to RApTA) was still efficiently dephosphorylated, suggesting dephosphorylation of RVxF motifs is independent of PP1 binding to the motif.

quotes.quote:
we analyzed our PP1 dephosphorylome for reg-
ulated sites in RVxF motifs. This revealed 15 RVxF motifs that were
dephosphorylated by PP1 (Appendix Fig S12C). Using several phos-
phopeptides, we confirmed that PP1 could indeed dephosphorylate
RVxF motifs (Appendix Fig S12D). The dephosphorylation of a
Nipp1 peptide with a mutated RVxF motif (RVpTF to RApTA) was
still efficiently dephosphorylated by PP1, suggesting that dephos-
phorylation of RVxF motifs is independent of PP1 binding to the
motif

experiment.system: PP1 mitotic dephosphorylome sites and synthetic RVxF phosphopeptides including a Nipp1 RApTA mutant
experiment.perturbation: mutation of the RVxF motif (RVpTF to RApTA); in vitro PP1 treatment
experiment.measurement: count of regulated RVxF-motif sites and in vitro peptide dephosphorylation assays

text: Efficient gp130 activation could not be achieved with a single agonistic monoclonal antibody but required two distinct monoclonal antibodies, with the minimal requirement being one intact antibody plus the Fab of the second.

quotes.quote:
Unlike many other
receptors, efﬁcient gp130 activation could not be achieved by a
single antibody, but requires the action of two distinct monoclonal
antibodies [39,40]. The minimal requirement for receptor activ-
ation is one intact antibody and the Fab (fragment antigen binding)
of the second antibody.

experiment.system: cells expressing gp130
experiment.perturbation: stimulation with agonistic monoclonal antibodies against gp130, intact or as Fab fragments
experiment.measurement: gp130 receptor activation/downstream signalling

text: Insertion of one to four alanine residues into the membrane-proximal intracellular region of gp130 showed that full activation of the receptor was only obtained with the wild-type and the + 3A-mutant.

quotes.quote:
insertion of one to four alanine residues into the
membrane-proximal intracellular region of gp130 demonstrated
that full activation of the receptor (i.e. induction of target genes)
was only obtained with the wild-type and the + 3A-mutant [45].

experiment.system: cells expressing gp130 juxtamembrane insertion mutants
experiment.perturbation: insertion of one to four alanine residues into the membrane-proximal intracellular region
experiment.measurement: receptor activation measured as induction of target genes

text: A FRAP analysis with fluorescent fusion proteins revealed that JAK1 mobility is approx. 100-fold lower than a typical cytoplasmic protein and similar to that of gp130, and antibody-mediated immobilization of gp130 co-immobilized JAK1.

quotes.quote:
a recent FRAP (ﬂuorescence recovery after photo-
bleaching) analysis with ﬂuorescent fusion proteins revealed
that JAK1 does not diffuse like a typical cytoplasmic protein.
Instead, its mobility is approx. 100-fold lower and similar to the
one of the transmembrane protein gp130. Interestingly, immo-
bilization of gp130 by antibodies leads to a concomitant im-
mobilization of JAK1

experiment.system: cells expressing fluorescent JAK1 and gp130 fusion proteins
experiment.perturbation: photobleaching; antibody-mediated immobilization of gp130
experiment.measurement: fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (mobility)

numbers.quantity: JAK1 mobility relative to typical cytoplasmic protein

text: Deletion of the proline-rich box1 or mutation of two critical proline residues within box1 abrogates JAK binding to gp130, OSMR or LIFR, and mutation of the single amino acid Trp666 in the interbox1–2 region of gp130 abrogates JAK binding and inactivates the receptor complex.

quotes.quote:
Deletion of the proline-rich box1 or mutation of two
critical proline residues within box1 abrogates receptor binding
of JAKs to gp130, OSMR or LIFR [49,53,54].

mutation of a single
amino acid (Trp666) abrogates JAK binding and thereby leads to
inactivation of the receptor complex [54].

experiment.system: cytokine receptor chains gp130, OSMR, LIFR in transfected cells
experiment.perturbation: deletion/point mutation of box1 prolines and Trp666
experiment.measurement: JAK co-precipitation/receptor binding and signalling

text: Substitution of Trp652 with alanine within the gp130 box1 region has no effect on JAK1 association but abrogates JAK1 activation, and signal transduction is drastically impaired even when only one chain of the gp130 dimer carries W652A.

quotes.quote:
substitution of Trp652 with
alanine (W652A) within the box1 region has no effect on JAK1
association but abrogates JAK1 activation. Signal transduction
is even drastically impaired if only one chain within a gp130
dimer carries the W652A mutation [55].

experiment.system: cells expressing gp130 W652A mutants
experiment.perturbation: W652A point mutation, in one or both chains of the dimer
experiment.measurement: JAK1 association and activation; signal transduction

text: Co-expression of JAK1, JAK2 and TYK2 enhances surface expression of the human OSMR independently of kinase activity; human fibrosarcoma cells lacking JAK1 express less OSMR at their surface than parental cells, and transient JAK1 transfection restores surface receptor amounts.

quotes.quote:
Co-expression of JAK1, JAK2 and TYK2 substantially en-
hances the surface expression of the human OSMR. While kinase
activity is dispensible for this effect

human ﬁbrosarcoma
cells lacking JAK1 express less OSMR at their surface compared
with the parental cells, but transient transfection of JAK1 can
again increase the amount of surface-expressed receptors [49].

experiment.system: human fibrosarcoma cells lacking JAK1 and transfected cells expressing OSMR
experiment.perturbation: co-expression/transient transfection of JAK1, JAK2, TYK2
experiment.measurement: OSMR cell surface expression

text: STAT3 binds phospho-YXXQ motifs in gp130 (Y767RHQ, Y814FKQ, Y905LPQ, Y915MPQ) and LIFR (Y981QPQ, Y1001KPQ, Y1028RPQ), whereas STAT1 is recruited to the more restricted consensus pYXPQ (Y905LPQ and Y915MPQ in gp130).

quotes.quote:
STAT3 binds to phospho (p)YXXQ motifs (Y767RHQ, Y814FKQ,
Y905LPQ and Y915MPQ in gp130; Y981QPQ, Y1001KPQ and
Y1028RPQ in LIFR) [81,84–86], STAT1 is recruited to the more
restricted consensus sequence pYXPQ (Y905LPQ and Y915MPQ
in gp130) [84].

experiment.system: gp130 and LIFR cytoplasmic tyrosine motifs
experiment.perturbation: receptor tyrosine motif mutagenesis/phosphopeptide binding
experiment.measurement: STAT1 and STAT3 recruitment

text: Arg31 of STAT1 is methylated by PRMT-1; methylation occurs without cytokine stimulation and independently of tyrosine or serine phosphorylation but requires an intact STAT1 SH2 domain, and methylated STAT1 has a higher tendency to associate with DNA because its interaction with PIAS1 is weaker.

quotes.quote:
STAT1 methylation is observed in the absence of cytokine
stimulation, independent of tyrosine or serine phosphorylation,
but requires the intact STAT1 SH2 domain. Compared with the
unmethylated protein, methylated STAT1 has a higher tendency
to associate with DNA, since its interaction with PIAS (protein
inhibitor of activated STATs) 1 ... seems to be
weaker [106].

experiment.system: STAT1 in cytokine-stimulated and unstimulated cells
experiment.perturbation: cytokine stimulation, SH2-domain mutation, PRMT-1 methylation
experiment.measurement: STAT1 arginine methylation, DNA association, PIAS1 interaction

text: Substitution of gp130 Tyr759 with phenylalanine impairs SHP2 recruitment and phosphorylation and leads to enhanced IL-6 as well as LIF and OSM signal transduction, while it impairs IL-6-induced MAPK cascade activation; mice expressing gp130 lacking Tyr759 display splenomegaly, lymphadenopathy and an enhanced acute-phase reaction.

quotes.quote:
substitution with phenylalanine impairs SHP2 recruit-
ment and phosphorylation [81] and leads to enhanced IL-6
[131,157,158], as well as LIF and OSM, signal transduction
[159].

the IL-6-
induced activation of the MAPK cascade is impaired by mutation
of Tyr759 within gp130

mice expressing gp130 lacking
Tyr759 display splenomegaly, lymphadenopathy and an enhanced
acute-phase reaction [161].

experiment.system: cells and mice expressing gp130 Tyr759Phe/Tyr759-deficient receptors
experiment.perturbation: Tyr759 to phenylalanine substitution / deletion
experiment.measurement: SHP2 recruitment and phosphorylation, IL-6/LIF/OSM signalling, MAPK activation, in vivo phenotype

text: Overexpression of dominant-negative SHP2 mutants leads to enhanced receptor, JAK, STAT and SHP2 phosphorylation.

quotes.quote:
Overexpression of
dominant-negative SHP2 mutants leads to enhanced receptor,
JAK, STAT and SHP2 phosphorylation [160].

experiment.system: cells with IL-6-type cytokine signalling components
experiment.perturbation: overexpression of dominant-negative SHP2 mutants
experiment.measurement: tyrosine phosphorylation of receptor, JAK, STAT and SHP2

text: Mutation of the SHP2 recruitment site Tyr759 within gp130 impairs the interaction of Gab1 with SHP2 and PI3K, IL-6-induced Gab1–SHP2 association leads to ERK2 activation, and Gab1-deficient fibroblasts show markedly reduced MAPK activity in response to IL-6.

quotes.quote:
mutation of Tyr759,
the SHP2 recruitment site within gp130, impairs the interaction
of Gab1 with SHP2 and PI3K

IL-6-induced association of Gab1
with SHP2 leads to activation of ERK2 [135]. As expected, Gab1-
deﬁcient ﬁbroblasts show a markedly reduced MAPK activity in
response to IL-6 [136].

experiment.system: IL-6-stimulated cells and Gab1-deficient fibroblasts
experiment.perturbation: gp130 Tyr759 mutation; Gab1 deficiency; IL-6 stimulation
experiment.measurement: Gab1–SHP2/PI3K interaction and ERK2/MAPK activity

text: Expression of a fusion protein comprising the PH domain of Gab1 and active SHP2 induces constitutive MEK1 and ERK2 activation.

quotes.quote:
expression of a fusion protein comprising the PH domain of
Gab1 and active SHP2 induces constitutive MEK1 (MAPK/ERK
kinase) and ERK2 activation [137].

experiment.system: cells transfected with a Gab1-PH–active SHP2 fusion protein
experiment.perturbation: expression of the fusion protein targeting SHP2 to the membrane
experiment.measurement: MEK1 and ERK2 activation

text: In MK2-deficient macrophages the half-life of IL-6 mRNA was reduced by more than 10-fold, and deletion of the AU-rich element of TNFα mRNA abrogates the effect of MK-2.

quotes.quote:
It was shown in MK2-deﬁcient
macrophages that the half-life of IL-6 mRNA was reduced by
more than 10-fold. Deletion of the AU-rich element of the TNFα
(tumour necrosis factor-α) mRNA abrogates the effect of MK-2
[218].

experiment.system: MK2-deficient macrophages
experiment.perturbation: MK2 deficiency; deletion of the AU-rich element of TNFα mRNA
experiment.measurement: cytokine mRNA half-life

numbers.quantity: reduction of IL-6 mRNA half-life in MK2-deficient macrophages

text: Binding studies with phosphopeptides indicate SOCS3 binds pTyr759 of gp130 with much higher affinity than pTyr1007 within the JAK2 activation loop, and the affinity of SOCS3 for gp130 peptides is even slightly higher than that of SHP2.

quotes.quote:
the afﬁnity of SOCS3 to bind to gp130 peptides is
even slightly higher than that of SHP2 [204].

Binding studies with phosphopeptides
suggest that SOCS3 binds pTyr759 of gp130 with much higher
afﬁnity than pTyr1007 within the activation loop of JAK2 [198].

experiment.system: purified SOCS3 and SHP2 with gp130/JAK2 phosphopeptides
experiment.perturbation: in vitro phosphopeptide binding assays
experiment.measurement: binding affinity

text: LPS and TNFα inhibit IL-6-mediated STAT3 activation in macrophages, most likely through de novo synthesis of SOCS3, while IL-1, TNF-α and LPS also inhibit IL-6-dependent STAT activation in macrophages through mechanisms not dependent on de novo protein synthesis; both routes depend on the p38 stress kinase.

quotes.quote:
LPS
(lipopolysaccharide) and the pro-inﬂammatory cytokine TNFα
have been shown to inhibit IL-6-mediated STAT3 activation in
macrophages. This inhibition is most likely due to induction
of the de novo synthesis of the JAK-inhibitor SOCS3 [229].

other data show that IL-1, TNF-α and LPS
inhibit IL-6-dependent STAT activation in macrophages through
mechanisms which do not depend on de novo protein synthesis
[231,232]. Interestingly, both SOCS3-dependent and SOCS3-in-
dependent inhibitory mechanisms of pro-inﬂammatory stimuli
depend on the p38 stress kinase [229,231,233].

experiment.system: macrophages
experiment.perturbation: treatment with LPS, TNFα or IL-1 prior to IL-6 stimulation; protein synthesis and p38 inhibition
experiment.measurement: IL-6-induced STAT3/STAT activation and SOCS3 induction

text: In human hepatoma cells IL-1β stimulation induces no SOCS3, and NF-κB was identified as the mediator of IL-1β-dependent suppression of IL-6-induced α2M expression; at least one intact NF-κB and one intact STAT3 consensus site is required for STAT3-dependent activation of the α2M promoter.

quotes.quote:
However, no SOCS3 induction
is observed upon IL-1β stimulation of human hepatoma cells.
Instead, NF-κB was identiﬁed as a mediator for IL-1β-dependent
suppression of IL-6-induced α2M (α2- macroglobulin) expression
in liver cells [236].

although NF-κB acts as a competitive inhibitor
for STAT3 DNA-binding, at least one intact NF-κB and one
intact STAT3 consensus site is crucial for the STAT3-dependent
activation of the α2M gene promoter [236]

experiment.system: human hepatoma/liver cells with the α2M promoter
experiment.perturbation: IL-1β and IL-6 stimulation; mutation of NF-κB and STAT3 consensus sites
experiment.measurement: SOCS3 induction, α2M expression and promoter activation

text: FKHR specifically enhanced the activity of STAT3-dependent promoters such as the α2M promoter but not a STAT5-responsive promoter, and FKHR and STAT3 can be co-immunoprecipitated and co-localize in the nucleus of IL-6-treated HepG2 cells.

quotes.quote:
FKHR speciﬁcally enhanced
the activity of STAT3-dependent promoters, such as the α2M
promoter, but not that of a STAT5-responsive promoter. Further-
more, FKHR and STAT3 can be co-immunoprecipitated and
co-localize in the nucleus of IL-6-treated HepG2 cells [149].

experiment.system: IL-6-treated HepG2 hepatoma cells
experiment.perturbation: FKHR expression; IL-6 stimulation
experiment.measurement: promoter reporter activity, co-immunoprecipitation and nuclear co-localization

text: STAT3 and EZI physically interact as shown by co-immunoprecipitation, and an EZI mutant predominantly localized in the cytoplasm inhibited nuclear localization of STAT3 and STAT3-mediated transactivation.

quotes.quote:
STAT3 and EZI physically interact as demon-
strated by co-immunoprecipitation. Interestingly, an EZI mutant
predominantly localized in the cytoplasm inhibited nuclear lo-
calization of STAT3, as well as STAT3-mediated transactivation.

experiment.system: cells expressing STAT3 and EZI
experiment.perturbation: expression of a cytoplasmically localized EZI mutant
experiment.measurement: co-immunoprecipitation, STAT3 nuclear localization and transactivation

text: Deletion of the acidic region (amino acids 771–811) of gp130, to which the Src family kinase Hck binds, reduces IL-6-induced Hck kinase activity, ERK activation, dephosphorylation of Pyk2 and proliferation of transfected pro-B Ba/F3 cells.

quotes.quote:
The Src family kinase Hck has recently been shown to
associate with an acidic region (amino acids 771–811) of gp130
[65]. Deletion of these amino acids reduces IL-6-induced Hck
kinase activity, ERK (extracellular-regulated kinase) activation,
dephosphorylation of Pyk2 and proliferation of transfected pro-
B Ba/F3 cells [65].

experiment.system: transfected pro-B Ba/F3 cells expressing gp130
experiment.perturbation: deletion of gp130 amino acids 771–811
experiment.measurement: Hck kinase activity, ERK activation, Pyk2 dephosphorylation, proliferation

text: A gp130 construct lacking box2 co-precipitates with JAK1 only when the kinase is over-expressed, and addition of the box1–2 region to the C-terminal part of a gp130 mutant unable to associate with JAKs in the membrane-proximal region did not restore JAK association.

quotes.quote:
a gp130 construct lacking box2 co-
precipitates with JAK1 only when the kinase is over-expressed
[55].

addition of the box1–2
region to the C-terminal part of a gp130 mutant, which was unable
to associate with JAKs in the membrane-proximal region, did not
restore JAK association [45].

experiment.system: cells expressing gp130 box deletion/relocation mutants
experiment.perturbation: deletion of box2; transfer of box1–2 to the C-terminus; JAK1 over-expression
experiment.measurement: JAK1 co-precipitation with gp130

text: The C-termini of the two cytokine-binding modules in the gp130 homodimer are separated by a distance of about 9 nm, and deletion of the membrane-proximal FNIII domains leads to signalling incompetent receptors.

quotes.quote:
It has been shown that these domains
are necessary for coupling ligand binding and signal transduction,
since deletion of these domains leads to signalling incompetent
receptors [36,37]. A domain model of the IL-6 receptor complex
[36], as well as the recent X-ray data [24], show that the C-termini
of the two CBMs in the gp130 homodimer are separated by a
distance of about 9 nm.

experiment.system: gp130 receptor complex
experiment.perturbation: deletion of membrane-proximal FNIII domains; X-ray structure/domain modelling
experiment.measurement: signalling competence; inter-CBM C-terminal distance

numbers.quantity: separation of CBM C-termini in gp130 homodimer

text: In cells lacking JAK1, IL-6 signal transduction is greatly impaired, whereas gp130, LIFR and OSMR bind JAK1, JAK2 and TYK2.

quotes.quote:
The signal transducing chains gp130, LIFR and OSMR bind to
JAK1, JAK2 and TYK2 [47–50]. Of these, JAK1 plays an essential
role, because in cells lacking JAK1 IL-6 signal transduction is
greatly impaired [51,52,134].

experiment.system: JAK1-deficient cell lines
experiment.perturbation: loss of JAK1
experiment.measurement: IL-6-induced signal transduction; JAK association with receptor chains

text: PKCδ associates IL-6 dependently with STAT3 and phosphorylates it on Ser727, leading to an inhibition of STAT3 DNA binding and transcriptional activity, and sequential activation of Vav, Rac-1, MKK-4 and PKCδ is necessary for IL-6-mediated STAT3 Ser727 phosphorylation and transactivation in HepG2 cells.

quotes.quote:
PKCδ associates
IL-6 dependently with STAT3 and phosphorylates it on Ser727,
leading to an inhibition of STAT3 DNA binding and transcript-
ional activity [94]. A sequential activation of Vav, Rac-1, MKK-4
(MAP kinase kinase 4) and PKCδ is necessary for the IL-6-
mediated STAT3 Ser727 phosphorylation and transactivation in
HepG2 cells.

experiment.system: HepG2 cells and several cell lines
experiment.perturbation: IL-6 stimulation; manipulation of Vav, Rac-1, MKK-4, PKCδ
experiment.measurement: STAT3 Ser727 phosphorylation, DNA binding and transactivation

text: PIAS1 specifically inhibits DNA binding of activated STAT1 and STAT1-mediated gene induction after IFN stimulation, PIAS3 inhibits STAT3-mediated gene expression after IL-6 stimulation, and PIASy inhibits STAT1-mediated gene activation without affecting STAT1 DNA-binding activity.

quotes.quote:
Whereas PIAS1 speciﬁcally inhibits DNA binding of activated
STAT1 and thus STAT1-mediated gene induction (after IFN
stimulation) [179], PIAS3 was found to be speciﬁc for the in-
hibition of STAT3-mediated gene expression (after IL-6 stimu-
lation) [178].

Recently, PIASy was
found to also inhibit STAT1-mediated gene activation [181]. In
contrast with PIAS1, however, it did not affect STAT1 DNA-
binding activity.

experiment.system: cells expressing PIAS proteins and STAT-responsive genes
experiment.perturbation: PIAS1/PIAS3/PIASy expression with IFN or IL-6 stimulation
experiment.measurement: STAT DNA binding and gene induction

text: In response to IL-2, Epo, EGF and PDGF, SOCS3 becomes tyrosine phosphorylated at Tyr204 and Tyr221 within the SOCS box, and phosphorylation of Tyr221 recruits p120 RasGAP leading to sustained ERK activation.

quotes.quote:
In
response to IL-2, Epo, EGF, and PDGF, SOCS3 (suppressor
of cytokine signalling 3) becomes tyrosine phosphorylated, and
subsequently binds and inactivates Ras/GTPase-activating pro-
tein.

Phosphorylation occurs at
two tyrosine residues (Tyr204 and Tyr221) within the SOCS box
and phosphorylation of Tyr221 recruits p120 RasGAP leading to
sustained ERK activation [139].

experiment.system: cells stimulated with IL-2, Epo, EGF or PDGF
experiment.perturbation: cytokine/growth factor stimulation; SOCS3 tyrosine phosphorylation
experiment.measurement: SOCS3 phosphorylation, RasGAP binding, Ras/ERK activity

text: SOCS protein expression is rapidly up-regulated by IL-6 (CIS, SOCS1, SOCS2 and SOCS3), LIF (CIS, SOCS1, SOCS2 and SOCS3), IL-11 (SOCS3) and OSM (CIS, SOCS1 and SOCS3), and SOCS1 blocks JAK activity more efficiently than SOCS3.

quotes.quote:
Expression of SOCS proteins was found
to be rapidly up-regulated by IL-6 (CIS, SOCS1, SOCS2
and SOCS3), LIF (CIS, SOCS1, SOCS2 and SOCS3), IL-11
(SOCS3) and OSM (CIS, SOCS1 and SOCS3) [32,190,192,193].

SOCS1 blocks JAK activity more efﬁciently than
SOCS3 [205].

experiment.system: cells responsive to IL-6-type cytokines
experiment.perturbation: stimulation with IL-6, LIF, IL-11 or OSM; SOCS1/SOCS3 expression
experiment.measurement: SOCS mRNA/protein induction; JAK activity

text: The adaptor protein Shc is recruited to the OSMR via Tyr861 in its cytoplasmic region, whereas the OSMR does not recruit SHP2; gp130 Tyr759 and LIFR Tyr974 are crucial for MAPK cascade activation.

quotes.quote:
Initial analyses concerning
gp130- and LIFR-mediated activation of MAPKs identiﬁed the
SHP2 (SH2-domain-containing tyrosine phosphatase)-binding
site Tyr759 of gp130 [81] and Tyr974 of LIFR to be crucial for the
activation of the MAPK cascade [127]. In contrast with gp130 and
LIFR, the OSMR does not recruit SHP2.

the adaptor protein Shc (SH2-
and collagen-homology-domain-containing protein) (Figure 4) is
recruited to the receptor via Tyr861 in the cytoplasmic region of
the OSMR [128]

experiment.system: cells expressing gp130, LIFR or OSMR receptor mutants
experiment.perturbation: mutation of receptor cytoplasmic tyrosine residues
experiment.measurement: adaptor recruitment (SHP2, Shc) and MAPK activation

text: PI3K activation upon IL-6 treatment is cell-type specific; no significant Akt activation could be observed in IL-6-treated HepG2 hepatoma cells, whereas in human Hep3B hepatoma cells IL-6 activates the PI3K/Akt pathway necessary for its anti-apoptotic effect during transforming growth factor β treatment.

quotes.quote:
in human Hep3B hepatoma cells IL-6
leads to activation of the PI3K/Akt pathway necessary for the
anti-apoptotic effect of IL-6 during transforming growth factor β
treatment [148]. It should be noted, however, that PI3K activation
upon IL-6 treatment is observed in a cell-type speciﬁc manner;
e.g. no signiﬁcant Akt activation could be observed in IL-6-
treated HepG2 hepatoma cells [149].

experiment.system: human Hep3B and HepG2 hepatoma cells
experiment.perturbation: IL-6 treatment (with TGFβ in Hep3B)
experiment.measurement: PI3K/Akt activation and apoptosis

text: KSHV-IL-6 binds the gp130 homodimer in the absence of any α-receptor, but with lower affinity compared with IL-6–IL-6Rα–gp130 ternary complexes.

quotes.quote:
KSHV-IL-6 binds
the gp130 homodimer in the absence of any α-receptor [16], but
with lower afﬁnity as compared with IL-6–IL-6Rα–gp130 ternary
complexes.

experiment.system: gp130-expressing cells/receptor binding assays with viral IL-6
experiment.perturbation: binding of KSHV-IL-6 without α-receptor versus IL-6 ternary complex
experiment.measurement: binding affinity to gp130

text: Soluble IL-6Rα potentiates the antagonistic activity of soluble gp130 on IL-6 responses.

quotes.quote:
It has been demonstrated that sIL-6Rα
potentiates the antagonistic activity of sgp130.

experiment.system: IL-6-responsive cells with soluble receptors
experiment.perturbation: addition of soluble IL-6Rα together with soluble gp130
experiment.measurement: IL-6 response/antagonism

text: To become secreted, CLC must be co-expressed with either CLF-1 or CNTFRα, and after secretion of the CLC–CLF-1 or CLC–CNTFRα complexes signalling is dependent on CNTFRα and occurs via gp130–LIFR heterodimers.

quotes.quote:
To become secreted, CLC must be co-
expressed with either CLF-1 (cytokine-like factor-1) or CNTFRα.
CLF-1 resembles a soluble cytokine receptor and speciﬁcally
binds CLC. After secretion of the CLC–CLF-1 or CLC–CNTFRα
complexes, signalling is dependent on CNTFRα and occurs via
gp130–LIFR heterodimers.

experiment.system: cells expressing CLC with CLF-1 or CNTFRα
experiment.perturbation: co-expression of CLC with CLF-1 or CNTFRα
experiment.measurement: CLC secretion and receptor-complex-dependent signalling

text: Artificially dimerized STAT proteins that are not phosphorylated also accumulate in the nucleus, and nuclear accumulation of constitutively active STAT proteins is independent from endocytosis.

quotes.quote:
Artiﬁcially dimerized STAT proteins
that are not phosphorylated also accumulate in the nucleus
[110,111].

nuclear accumulation of constitutively
active STAT proteins is independent from endocytosis, because in
these cases the STATs are not recruited to any plasma membrane
receptor [110,114].

experiment.system: cells expressing artificially dimerized or constitutively active STAT proteins
experiment.perturbation: forced dimerization without tyrosine phosphorylation; constitutive activation
experiment.measurement: nuclear accumulation of STATs

text: The nuclear phosphatase counteracting IFNγ-activated STAT1 was identified as the nuclear isoform of the T-cell PTP TC45, and STAT1 methylated at Arg31 is a better substrate for T-cell PTP than non-methylated STAT1.

quotes.quote:
Meanwhile, this phosphatase has
been identiﬁed as the nuclear isoform of the T-cell PTP TC45
[174,175]. Interestingly, STAT1 methylated at Arg31 is a better
substrate for T-cell PTP than non-methylated STAT1.

experiment.system: IFNγ-activated STAT1 and T-cell PTP
experiment.perturbation: IFNγ stimulation; STAT1 Arg31 methylation status
experiment.measurement: STAT1 dephosphorylation/phosphatase substrate efficiency

text: The cytoplasmic variant of PTPε, PTPεC, selectively inhibits IL-6-induced gp130, JAK and STAT activation and affects the kinetics of the onset of STAT3 activation, whereas SHP2 modulates the amount and amplitude of STAT3 activity.

quotes.quote:
The cytoplasmic variant of PTPε, PTPεC, is expressed
in haematopoietic cells and has been shown to selectively inhibit
IL-6-induced gp130, JAK and STAT activation [168]. Whereas
SHP2 modulates the amount and amplitude of STAT3 activity
[131,158], PTPεC affects the kinetics of the onset of STAT3
activation [169].

experiment.system: haematopoietic cells expressing PTPεC
experiment.perturbation: PTPεC expression during IL-6 stimulation
experiment.measurement: gp130, JAK and STAT3 activation amplitude and kinetics

text: Mass spectrometry of YFP-B56a purified from asynchronous HeLa cells identified 239 proteins significantly enriched (p < 0.01) relative to YFP-B55a purifications.

quotes.quote:
In total, 239 proteins were signiﬁcantly enriched (p <
0.01) in the YFP-B56a puriﬁcation, including both known and
previously unidentiﬁed interactors

experiment.system: HeLa cells stably expressing YFP-B56a or YFP-B55a
experiment.perturbation: YFP affinity purification of B56a versus B55a holoenzymes
experiment.measurement: mass spectrometry identification of co-purifying proteins, volcano plot enrichment

text: Alanine scanning of KIF4A and GEF-H1 C-terminal conserved regions defined residues critical for B56a binding: KIF4A C1224, I1227, E1229, or E1230 substitutions prevented co-purification (S1225 and P1226 compromised binding less), and GEF-H1 M967, I970, and E972 substitutions prevented co-purification while E973 decreased binding.

quotes.quote:
For KIF4A, alanine substitution
of C1224, I1227, E1229, or E1230 pre-
vented the co-puriﬁcation of Myc-KIF4A with YPF-B56a,
whereas alanine substitution of S1225 and P1226 compromised
binding to a lesser degree. For GEF-H1, alanine substitution of

text: An in silico search using disorder, conservation, and a PSSM built from 13 validated human motifs identified 164 putative LxxIxE motifs in the human proteome; 30 out of 239 proteins co-purifying with YFP-B56a contained a conserved LxxIxE motif versus 1 out of 255 proteins co-purifying with YFP-B55a.

we generated a position-spe-
ciﬁc scoring matrix (PSSM) from the 13 validated human motifs
(Figures S5A–S5C and 1F). Applying these three criteria, we
identiﬁed 164 putative LxxIxE motifs within the human proteome
(Table S4). Attesting to the stringency of the search parameters,
30 out of 239 proteins speciﬁcally co-purifying with YFP-B56a
from our mass spectrometry screen contained a conserved
LxxIxE motif, compared with 1 out of 255 proteins speciﬁcally
co-purifying with YFP-B55a.

nation factor BRCA2 and the neuronal potassium channel
KCNH8 for validation (Figure S2). In both cases, alanine substi-
tutions within their predicted LxxIxE motifs led to loss of B56a

predicted

Marburgvirus, and Cuevavirus (Figure S2). Similarly, putative
motifs were identiﬁed in the Integrase enzyme of all Deltaretrovir-
idae family members including Human T cell leukemia virus 1

We validated the ability
of these viral LxxIxE motifs to bind PP2A-B56 in IP experiments,
as described above (Figures S4J and S4K).

text: A GEF-H1 LxxIxE peptide, but not a mutant peptide, outcompeted co-purification of YFP-B56a with separase, KIF4A, BubR1, Axin1, and GEF-H1, indicating a shared binding site.

Using an in vitro peptide competition assay, we
found that a peptide encompassing the LxxIxE motif of GEF-
H1 was able to outcompete the co-puriﬁcation of YFP-B56a
with separase, KIF4A, BubR1, Axin1, and GEF-H1 itself,whereas

text: Evolutionary conservation mapping onto the PP2A-B56g holoenzyme structure revealed a conserved, surface-exposed linear pocket formed by HEAT repeats 3-5 with a hydrophobic patch at one end and a basic patch at the other.

This analysis revealed the existence of a remarkably
well-conserved and surface-exposed pocket on B56, with con-
tributions from residues in HEAT repeats 3–5. The pocket is
linear, with a hydrophobic patch in one end and a basic patch
in the opposite end

quotes.quote:
residues contributing to the hydrophobic patch (Y215Q, I256S,
and F260Q) or the basic patch (R222E, R226E, and K265E)
were mutated. Additionally, two conserved glycine residues
positioned at the entrance of the putative binding pocket were
substituted with more bulky residues (G216Q and G259Q).

Seven out of the eight mutations
in the putative binding pocket strongly reduced binding to these
proteins, whereas binding to the catalytic and scaffolding sub-
units of the PP2A holoenzyme was unaffected

experiment.system: HeLa cells stably expressing WT or mutant YFP-B56a

text: Unrestrained HADDOCK docking of the high-affinity KIF4A LxxIxE peptide into the B56a pocket placed the peptide in an alpha helical conformation interrupted by a proline, with C-terminal acidic residues contacting the basic patch and the two key hydrophobic residues in the hydrophobic section.

The docking solutions
yielding the highest scores in HADDOCK (Trellet et al., 2015)
revealed the KIF4A peptide in an alpha helical conformation

disrupted in the middle by the presence of a proline (Figures 2D
and S5D). The acidic residues in the C-terminal end contact the
basic patch of the B56 subunit, while the two key hydrophobic
residues interact with the more hydrophobic section of the bind-
ing pocket.
