experiment.perturbation: unrestrained molecular docking incorporating B56a mutational data
experiment.measurement: HADDOCK docking scores and modeled binding pose

text: The binding pocket is functionally conserved: Myc-tagged S. cerevisiae Mad3 co-purified with human YFP-B56aWT dependent on an intact motif but not with YFP-B56aR222E, and YFP-tagged yeast B56 (Rts1) expressed in human cells co-purified endogenous separase, KIF4A, and BubR1, interactions strongly reduced by the Rts1R446E mutation corresponding to human B56aR222E.

quotes.quote:
a Myc-tagged version
of the S. cerevisiae BubR1 ortholog (Mad3), which contains a
putative LxxIxE motif, co-puriﬁed with human YFP-B56aWT in a
manner dependent on an intact motif, but did not co-purify
with YFP-B56aR222E (Figure S5E). Furthermore, YFP-tagged
S. cerevisiae B56 (Rts1) expressed in human cells could co-
purify endogenous human separase, KIF4A, and BubR1. Impor-
tantly, these interactions were strongly reduced by an Rts1R446E
mutation that corresponds to the human B56aR222E mutation

experiment.system: human cells expressing human YFP-B56a or yeast YFP-Rts1 with Myc-Mad3
experiment.perturbation: motif mutation and pocket mutations B56aR222E / Rts1R446E
experiment.measurement: immunopurification and immunoblotting of co-purifying proteins

text: Mutating the RacGAP1 LxxIxE motif (RacGAP1-2A-YFP, L143A-I146A) disrupted PP2A-B56 binding and correlated with increased phosphorylation of RacGAP1 S157 and S170, while the constructs were expressed at near-endogenous levels and localized properly to the central spindle.

quotes.quote:
Using phospho-speciﬁc anti-RacGAP1 antibodies recog-
nizing phosphorylated S157 and S170 (Burkard et al., 2009),
we investigated the effect of mutating the LxxIxE motif. Disrupt-
ing the binding to PP2A-B56 correlated with increased phos-
phorylation of S157 and S170 on RacGAP1 (Figures 3D–3G).

Both RacGAP1 constructs were expressed at near-endogenous
levels and showed proper localization to the central spindle

experiment.system: stable HeLa cell lines expressing RNAi-resistant WT RacGAP1-YFP or RacGAP1-2A-YFP with endogenous RacGAP1 depleted
experiment.perturbation: two point mutations (L143A-I146A) in the RacGAP1 LxxIxE motif
experiment.measurement: phospho-specific S157/S170 immunofluorescence quantification and immunoblotting of GFP-Trap purifications

text: RacGAP1 siRNA depletion caused cytokinesis failure in approximately 85% of cells; WT RacGAP1-YFP largely rescued the defect while RacGAP1-2A-YFP was significantly less effective (8.4% ± 4.9% versus 30.2% ± 6.0% bi-nucleated cells; p < 0.0001).

quotes.quote:
Depletion of endogenous RacGAP1 with small interfering RNA
(siRNA) led to cytokinesis failure in approximately 85% of cells
(Figures 3C and 3H). WT RacGAP1-YFP was largely able to
rescue the cytokinesis defects of endogenous RacGAP1 deple-
tion, whereas rescue with the RacGAP1-2A-YFP derivative was
signiﬁcantly less effective (8.4% ± 4.9% versus 30.2% ± 6.0%,
respectively; p < 0.0001; Figure 3H).

experiment.system: HeLa Flp-In T-REx cells expressing RNAi-resistant RacGAP1-YFP variants
experiment.perturbation: siRNA depletion of endogenous RacGAP1 with rescue by WT or 2A LxxIxE-mutant RacGAP1
experiment.measurement: live-cell imaging quantification of bi-nucleated cells (mean ± 99% confidence interval, n > 214 per condition, two-tailed unpaired t test)

text: Engineering the FOXO3 LxxIxE motif to progressively higher B56 affinity (confirmed by ITC and IP) produced graded increased nuclear localization at steady state, faster nuclear translocation kinetics and higher final steady-state nuclear levels after PI3K inhibition with LY294002, and AKT/14-3-3-site phosphorylation that inversely correlated with B56 binding affinity.

quotes.quote:
ITC and IP exper-
iments conﬁrmed a graded increase in the afﬁnities between B56
and the various FOXO3 derivatives (Figures 4A and 4B).

en-
gineered FOXO3 variants showed translocation to the nucleus in
a manner that correlated with binding afﬁnity to B56 (Figures 4C
and4D).Furthermore,when cellswere exposedto thePI3Kfamily
inhibitor LY294002, which prevents activation of the AKT kinase,
the FOXO3 derivatives containing high-afﬁnity LxxIxE motifs
translocated to the nucleus with faster kinetics and reached a
higher ﬁnal steady-state level than derivatives with lower-afﬁnity
motifs (Figures 4E and 4F). Importantly, AKT phosphorylation of
FOXO3, and the phosphorylation status of sites responsible for
binding to 14-3-3 proteins, inversely correlated with binding afﬁn-
ity between B56 and FOXO3 (Figures 4G and 4H).

experiment.system: HeLa cells expressing YFP-tagged or Myc-tagged engineered FOXO3 LxxIxE variants; recombinant B56a with FOXO3 peptides
experiment.perturbation: genetic engineering of the FOXO3 LxxIxE motif to graded affinities; PI3K inhibition with LY294002
experiment.measurement: ITC affinities, GFP-Trap co-purification immunoblots, live-cell imaging nucleo-cytoplasmic ratio (images every 3 min, minimum of eight cells per time point), phospho-AKT-substrate (RxxpS/T) and 14-3-3 site (LxRxxpS/T) immunoblots

text: AMPK is a heterotrimeric complex of one catalytic α-subunit and two regulatory subunits β and γ; in humans there are two α-subunits (α1, α2), two β-subunits and three γ-subunits, so all combinations potentially create 12 distinct AMPK complexes.

quotes.quote:
AMPK is a heterotrimeric complex composed of a catalytic α-subunit and two regulatory 
subunits, β and γ

In humans, there are two α-subunits, α1 and α2, encoded by the genes 
PRKAA1 and PRKAA2 (REF. 32), two β-subunits, β1 and β2, encoded by PRKAB1 and 
PRKAB2 (REF. 33), and three γ-subunits, γ1, γ2 and γ3, encoded by PRKAG1, PRKAG2 
and PRKAG3 (REF. 34). Each AMPK complex is composed of one α-subunit, one β-
subunit and one γ-subunit, and all combinations are possible, thus potentially creating 12 
distinct AMPK complexes35.

experiment.system: human/vertebrate AMPK subunit genes
experiment.perturbation: observational (gene identification and subunit composition analysis)
experiment.measurement: identification of subunit isoforms and enumeration of possible heterotrimer combinations

text: AMP binding to the γ-subunit enhances AMPK activity through three mechanisms — proposed stimulation of Thr172 phosphorylation (challenged by in vitro results showing no effect), inhibition of Thr172 dephosphorylation by phosphatases, and allosteric activation of already-phosphorylated AMPK; ATP also binds the CBS domains so AMPK responds to the ATP-to-AMP ratio rather than total nucleotide levels.

quotes.quote: AMP binding to the γ-subunit enhances AMPK activity through three distinct mechanisms.

both of these models have been 
challenged by other results showing no effect of AMP on the phosphorylation of Thr172 by 
the upstream kinase in vitro40,43–45. Second, AMP inhibits the dephosphorylation of Thr172 
by protecting it from phosphatases46. Last, AMP causes allosteric activation of AMPK 
already phosphorylated on Thr172

ATP is also 
able to bind to the CBS domains on the γ-subunit, which allows AMPK to respond to 
changes in the ATP-to-AMP ratio rather than changes in total nucleotide levels and thus to 
act as a real sensor of energy levels38.

experiment.system: purified/in vitro AMPK complexes and cells
experiment.perturbation: addition of AMP, ADP or ATP to AMPK
experiment.measurement: Thr172 phosphorylation, dephosphorylation by phosphatases, and kinase activity

text: In muscle only the α1β2γ1, α2β2γ1 and α2β2γ3 complexes are detected, and following exercise only the α2β2γ3 complex is activated by Thr172 phosphorylation despite being less abundant than γ1-containing complexes, whereas the mitochondrial inhibitor PT-1 specifically activates γ1-containing complexes in muscle.

quotes.quote:
For example, in muscle, only the 
α1β2γ1, α2β2γ1 and α2β2γ3 complexes are detected. Moreover, following exercise, only 
the α2β2γ3 complex is activated by Thr172 phosphorylation, even though this complex is 
not as abundant as the γ1-containing complexes47. This specificity for the γ3-containing 
complex is in contrast to the effect of the mitochondrial inhibitor PT-1, which specifically 
activates γ1-containing complexes in muscle48.

experiment.system: skeletal muscle (human/mouse)
experiment.perturbation: exercise, or treatment with the mitochondrial inhibitor PT-1
experiment.measurement: complex-specific Thr172 phosphorylation and AMPK activity of isoform-defined complexes

text: Genetic inactivation of Lkb1 in mice shows LKB1 is responsible for the majority of AMPK activation under energy stress in most mammalian tissues examined, and cells devoid of LKB1 show that LKB1 mediates nearly all AMPK activation in response to mitochondrial insults and low-energy conditions.

quotes.quote:
Studies of 
mice in which Lkb1 (also known as Stk11) has been genetically inactivated reveal that 
LKB1 is responsible for the majority of AMPK activation under energy stress in most 
mammalian tissues examined, including crucial metabolic tissues such as the liver and 
muscle60–64. Studies of cells devoid of LKB1 indicate that LKB1 mediates nearly all of the 
activation of AMPK in response to mitochondrial insults and low-energy conditions65.

experiment.system: mice with genetically inactivated Lkb1 and LKB1-null cells
experiment.perturbation: genetic deletion of Lkb1; energy stress / mitochondrial insults
experiment.measurement: AMPK activation (Thr172 phosphorylation/activity)

text: CAMKK2 can directly phosphorylate AMPK on Thr172 in response to calcium flux independently of LKB1 and nucleotide levels, and in LKB1-null cells CAMKK2 maintains some AMPK activity still sensitive to changes in the ATP-to-AMP ratio, explaining residual AMPK activity in LKB1-deficient tumours.

quotes.quote:
AMPK can also be directly phosphorylated on Thr172 in 
response to calcium flux by the calcium-sensitive kinase CAMKK2

In 
LKB1-null cells, CAMKK2 is able to maintain some AMPK activity that is still sensitive to 
changes in the ATP-to-AMP ratio80. This CAMKK2-dependent activation of AMPK 
explains the observation of residual AMPK activity in LKB1-deficient tumours.

experiment.system: LKB1-null mammalian cells and tissues
experiment.perturbation: increased intracellular calcium / CAMKK2 activation in absence of LKB1
experiment.measurement: AMPK Thr172 phosphorylation and residual AMPK activity

text: A proposed glucose-sensing mechanism holds that glucose starvation activates AMPK independently of the canonical AMP-dependent allosteric mechanism: decreased fructose-1,6-bisphosphate is sensed by aldolase, which regulates AMPK–axin binding and stimulates formation of the AMPK–axin complex at the lysosome.

quotes.quote:
the authors propose that glucose starvation activates AMPK independently of the 
canonical AMP-dependent allosteric mechanism. Rather, binding of the glycolytic enzyme 
aldolase to its substrate fructose-1,6-bisphosphate (FBP) regulates AMPK–axin binding and 
AMPK activity56. Thus, under conditions of glucose starvation, FBP levels decrease, which 
is sensed by aldolase and stimulates the formation of the AMPK–axin complex at the 
lysosome56.

experiment.system: cultured cells with lysosomal AMPK–axin–LKB1 complexes
experiment.perturbation: glucose starvation / manipulation of FBP and aldolase
experiment.measurement: AMPK–axin complex formation and AMPK activity

text: AMPK inhibits anabolism by inhibitory phosphorylation of ACC1 and ACC2 and of HMG-CoA reductase, of glycogen synthases GYS1 and GYS2, and of GFAT1, and inhibits mTORC1 by two independent mechanisms: activation of TSC2 and inhibition of the mTORC1 subunit RAPTOR.

quotes.quote:
The first pathway to be identified was the inhibition of lipid and sterol synthesis by 
AMPK through inhibitory phosphorylation of the acetyl-CoA carboxylases ACC1 and 
ACC2, which catalyse the first step in de novo lipid synthesis, and inhibitory 
phosphorylation of HMG-CoA reductase (HMGCR)

AMPK also prevents the 
storage of glycogen by inhibitory phosphorylation of the glycogen synthases GYS1 and 
GYS2 (REF. 87) and inhibits hexosamine synthesis and O-GlcNAc modification of cellular 
proteins via phosphorylation of GFAT1
AMPK activation leads to the inhibition of mTORC1 by two independent

mechanisms: the activation of the negative mTORC1 regulator TSC2 (also known as 
tuberin)4 and the inhibition of the mTORC1 subunit RAPTOR5.

experiment.system: mammalian cells and liver
experiment.perturbation: AMPK activation (energy stress) / phosphorylation of substrates
experiment.measurement: substrate phosphorylation and enzyme/mTORC1 activity

text: Mouse knock-in mutants bearing Ser79Ala in ACC1 and Ser221Ala in ACC2 revealed that these AMPK sites are important for lipid homeostasis and for the therapeutic effects of metformin, with both ACC1 and ACC2 contributing redundantly to lipid homeostasis.

quotes.quote:
Studies using mouse models with knock-in mutations of 
Ser79Ala in ACC1 and Ser221Ala in ACC2 revealed that these sites are indeed important 
for the regulation of lipid homeostasis and the therapeutic effects of metformin downstream 
of AMPK105 (BOX 1). In addition, both ACC1 and ACC2 contributed to the regulation of 
lipid homeostasis, showing redundancy in function between ACC1 and ACC2.

experiment.system: mice with knock-in ACC1 Ser79Ala and ACC2 Ser221Ala mutations
experiment.perturbation: loss of AMPK phosphorylation sites on ACC1/ACC2; metformin treatment
experiment.measurement: lipid homeostasis and metformin therapeutic response (insulin sensitivity/blood glucose)

text: Muscles from ACC2 Ser221Ala knock-in mice have decreased basal fatty acid oxidation compared with wild-type muscle and are resistant to the fatty acid oxidation-promoting effect of AICAR, but these differences were lost upon exercise.

quotes.quote:
muscles from ACC2 Ser221Ala 
knock-in mice have decreased basal fatty acid oxidation compared with wild-type muscle 
and are resistant to the fatty acid oxidation-promoting effect of AICAR153.

upon exercise, these differences were lost, suggesting that exercise induces changes in fatty 
acid oxidation that are independent of the AMPK–ACC–malonyl-CoA axis154.

experiment.system: skeletal muscle of ACC2 Ser221Ala knock-in mice vs wild type
experiment.perturbation: AICAR treatment or exercise
experiment.measurement: fatty acid oxidation rate

text: Genetic evidence links AMPK to mitochondrial biogenesis: mice expressing a dominant-negative AMPK mutant failed to induce mitochondrial biogenesis under energy stress, mice lacking AMPK β1/β2 subunits or LKB1 show decreased muscle mitochondrial content, muscle-specific LKB1 knockout mice fail to increase mitochondrial biogenesis after exercise, and overexpression of a constitutively active AMPK γ3 subunit induced mitochondrial biogenesis and increased PGC1α expression.

quotes.quote:
Furthermore, over expression of a constitutively active AMPK γ3 
subunit in mice induced mitochondrial biogenesis111. Loss-of-function experiments also 
revealed a role for AMPK in the maintenance of mitochondrial biogenesis. Mice expressing 
a dominant-negative mutant of AMPK failed to induce mitochondrial biogenesis under 
energy stress16. Mice lacking the AMPK β1/β2 sub units112 or the upstream kinase LKB1 
(REFS 113,114) show decreased mitochondrial content in muscle, and mice with muscle-
specific LKB1 knockout fail to increase mitochondrial biogenesis after exercise113.

overexpression of the constitutively active AMPK γ3 subunit increased PGC1α 
expression111

experiment.system: mouse skeletal muscle with AMPK/LKB1 genetic manipulations
experiment.perturbation: dominant-negative AMPK, β1/β2 or LKB1 knockout, constitutively active γ3 overexpression; chronic energy stress or exercise
experiment.measurement: mitochondrial content/biogenesis and PGC1α expression

text: Two sites on PGC1α, Thr177 and Ser538, have been reported to be phosphorylated by AMPK in vitro, and transcriptional upregulation of several oxidative-metabolism genes upon AMPK activation required PGC1α; the authors state additional studies are needed to define whether these are AMPK target sites in vivo.

quotes.quote:
it has been reported that the transcriptional upregulation of 
several genes involved in oxidative metabolism upon AMPK activation required PGC1α17

Two sites on PGC1α have been reported to be phosphorylated by AMPK in 
vitro: Thr177 and Ser538 (REF. 17). Additional studies are needed to define whether they 
are AMPK target sites in vivo.

experiment.system: skeletal muscle cells / in vitro kinase assays
experiment.perturbation: AMPK activation; loss of PGC1α
experiment.measurement: PGC1α phosphorylation site mapping and oxidative-metabolism gene expression

numbers.quantity: PGC1α sites phosphorylated by AMPK in vitro

text: AMPK was shown to be required for mitochondrial fragmentation induced by the complex I and complex III inhibitors rotenone and antimycin A, and AMPK activation by direct small-molecule activators in the absence of mitochondrial damage is sufficient to induce mitochondrial fission.

quotes.quote:
AMPK was recently shown to be required for the fragmentation 
of mitochondria induced by rotenone and antimycin A, which are inhibitors of complex I 
and complex III, respectively, of the mitochondrial respiratory chain. Surprisingly, AMPK 
activation through direct small-molecule activators, in the absence of mitochondrial damage, 
is sufficient to induce mitochondrial fission15.

experiment.system: cultured mammalian cells with/without AMPK
experiment.perturbation: rotenone or antimycin A treatment; direct small-molecule AMPK activators
experiment.measurement: mitochondrial network morphology (fragmentation/fission)

text: Proteomics and bioinformatics substrate screens identified two AMPK phosphorylation sites, Ser155 and Ser173, on mitochondrial fission factor (MFF), the primary DRP1 receptor on the mitochondrial outer membrane, and AMPK activation increased DRP1 localization at mitochondria in a manner dependent on the AMPK phosphorylation sites in MFF.

quotes.quote:
Proteomics and bioinformatics screens to 
identify new substrates of AMPK identified two phosphorylation sites, Ser155 and Ser173, 
on a core component of the mitochondrial fission pathway, mitochondrial fission factor 
(MFF)15,28.

activation of AMPK results in increased localization 
of DRP1 at the mitochondria, an effect that is dependent on the presence of the AMPK 
phosphorylation sites in MFF15

experiment.system: cultured mammalian cells; phospho-proteomic substrate screens
experiment.perturbation: AMPK activation; expression of MFF lacking AMPK phosphorylation sites
experiment.measurement: MFF phosphorylation site identification and DRP1 mitochondrial localization

numbers.quantity: AMPK phosphorylation sites identified on MFF

text: AMPK directly phosphorylates ULK1 on at least four residues (Ser467, Ser555, Thr574 and Ser637); using ULK1-knockout cells reconstituted with non-phosphorylatable mutants, this phosphorylation was shown to be important for autophagy and cell survival during starvation and metabolic stress, and cells expressing such mutants accumulate defective mitochondria.

quotes.quote:
AMPK directly phosphorylates ULK1 on at least four residues: Ser467, Ser555, 
Thr574 and Ser637 (REFS 14,170) (FIG. 4). Using ULK1-knockout cell lines and 
reconstitution with non-phosphorylatable mutants, phosphorylation of ULK1 by AMPK was 
shown to be important for autophagy and cell survival during starvation and metabolic 
stress. Strikingly, cells expressing ULK1 mutants that cannot be phosphorylated by AMPK 
also appear to accumulate defective mitochondria

experiment.system: ULK1-knockout cell lines reconstituted with wild-type or non-phosphorylatable ULK1
experiment.perturbation: starvation/metabolic stress with loss of AMPK phosphorylation sites on ULK1
experiment.measurement: autophagy, cell survival, and accumulation of defective mitochondria

text: AMPK has been reported to phosphorylate additional core autophagy components — Ser761 on ATG9, Thr133 and Ser135 on VPS34, Ser91 and Ser94 on Beclin1, Thr50 on RACK1 and Thr32 on PAQR3 — though the authors note some of these represent suboptimal AMPK sites that have not been independently validated.

quotes.quote:
AMPK has been reported to phosphorylate residues on other core components of the 
autophagy pathway, such as Ser761 on ATG9 (REF. 180), Thr133 and Ser135 on VPS34 
(REF. 181), Ser91 and Ser94 on Beclin1 (REFS 181,182), Thr50 on the VPS34-associated 
protein RACK1 (REF. 183) and Thr32 on PAQR3, an ATG14L–VPS34 scaffolding 
protein184. Some of these phosphorylation events represent suboptimal AMPK sites and 
have not been independently validated

experiment.system: mammalian cells, autophagy pathway components
experiment.perturbation: AMPK activation / phosphosite mapping
experiment.measurement: identification of phosphorylated residues on ATG9, VPS34, Beclin1, RACK1 and PAQR3

text: Evidence for a mitochondrial pool of AMPK includes myristoylation of the AMPK β-subunit causing AMPK localization to mitochondria where it regulates mitophagy, AMPK phosphorylation of ULK1 on Ser555 regulating ULK1 recruitment to mitochondria during mitophagy, and small-peptide AMPK activity probes indicating a mitochondrial pool that regulates ATP levels independently of cytosolic AMPK.

quotes.quote:
myristoylation of the β-
subunit of AMPK causes AMPK to localize to mitochondria, where it could regulate the 
specific removal of damaged mitochondria by mitophagy53. Interestingly, phosphorylation 
of ULK1 on Ser555 by AMPK has been shown to regulate recruitment of ULK1 to 
mitochondria during mitophagy

Small-peptide probes for AMPK activity also suggest the existence of a mitochondrial pool 
of AMPK that can specifically regulate ATP levels independently of cytosolic AMPK190.

verdict_note: The paper hedges the myristoylation result: AMPK localizes to mitochondria 'where it could regulate the specific removal of damaged mitochondria by mitophagy'; the claim asserts that it does regulate mitophagy, dropping the conditional. The ULK1 Ser555 and peptide-probe elements are faithful.

experiment.system: cultured mammalian cells expressing myristoylated AMPK β-subunit, ULK1 phospho-mutants, and genetically encoded AMPK activity probes
experiment.perturbation: β-subunit myristoylation; ULK1 Ser555 phosphorylation; compartment-targeted AMPK sensors/actuators
experiment.measurement: subcellular localization of AMPK and ULK1, mitophagy, and compartmental ATP levels

text: AMPK regulates autophagy and lysosome gene transcription: AMPK phosphorylation of FOXO3 stimulates its transcriptional activity under energy stress and represses SKP2 mRNA, increasing CARM1 levels that co-activate TFEB; AMPK activity controls lysosomal biogenesis through TFEB during embryonic stem cell differentiation into embryoid bodies; and AMPK-dependent phosphorylation of ACSS2 induces its nuclear translocation to stimulate TFEB-dependent gene expression.

AMPK phosphorylation of FOXO3 
stimulates its transcriptional activity under conditions of energy stress20.

it was shown that AMPK activity controls lysosomal biogenesis 
through TFEB during embryonic stem cell differentiation into embryoid bodies26.

AMPK 
phosphorylation of FOXO3 was shown to repress the expression of the mRNA encoding 
SKP2, which is part of the SCF E3 ubiquitin ligase complex that degrades the histone 
demethylase CARM1 (REF. 25). The net effect of AMPK activation was increased levels of 
CARM1, which acted as a co-activator for TFEB to promote the expression of lysosomal 
genes

it was reported that AMPK-dependent phosphorylation of the 
lipogenic enzyme ACSS2 induced its translocation to the nucleus, where it stimulated 
TFEB-dependent gene expression204.

experiment.system: mammalian cells and mouse embryonic stem cells differentiating into embryoid bodies
experiment.perturbation: AMPK activation/loss; phosphorylation of FOXO3 and ACSS2
experiment.measurement: transcriptional activity, SKP2 mRNA and CARM1 levels, TFEB-dependent lysosomal gene expression, lysosomal biogenesis

text: Two recent studies showed direct AMPK activation improves type 2 diabetes symptoms in animal models: a pan-specific AMPK activator improved diabetes symptoms in rodents and monkeys, and another direct activator increased muscle glucose uptake and reduced blood glucose, with liver AMPK inactivation having no effect on drug efficacy while muscle-specific AMPK deletion abolished it.

quotes.quote:
two recent studies 
have revealed that direct AMPK activation indeed improves symptoms of type 2 diabetes 
in multiple animal models. One study revealed that a pan-specific AMPK activator 
improved diabetes symptoms in several animal models, including rodents and monkeys84. 
In another study, a direct AMPK activator increased glucose uptake in muscle and 
reduced blood glucose in type 2 diabetes models83. Interestingly, inactivation of AMPK 
in the liver had no effect on the efficacy of the drug, whereas muscle-specific deletion of 
AMPK abolished the effect of the drug, establishing muscle AMPK as a key therapeutic 
target in type 2 diabetes83.

experiment.system: rodent and non-human primate type 2 diabetes models, including liver- and muscle-specific AMPK knockout mice
experiment.perturbation: treatment with direct/pan-specific small-molecule AMPK activators; tissue-specific AMPK deletion
experiment.measurement: diabetes symptoms, muscle glucose uptake and blood glucose levels

numbers.quantity: recent studies of direct AMPK activation in diabetes models

text: In mice bearing the fluorescent pMitoTimer reporter in skeletal muscle, dominant-negative AMPK suppressed acute-exercise-induced ULK1 phosphorylation, mitophagy and lysosomal biogenesis, while conditional deletion of Ulk1 abolished acute-exercise-induced mitophagy but had no effect on lysosomal biogenesis.

quotes.quote:
In an elegant study244 in skeletal muscle of mice bearing a fluorescent reporter gene 
pMitoTimer that measures oxidative stress and mitophagy in vivo, the authors demonstrated 
that dominant-negative AMPK suppresses acute-exercise-induced ULK1 phosphorylation, 
mitophagy and lysosomal biogenesis. Conditional deletion of Ulk1 resulted in loss of acute-
exercise-induced mitophagy but had no effect on lysosomal biogenesis

experiment.system: mouse skeletal muscle expressing the pMitoTimer reporter
experiment.perturbation: acute exercise in dominant-negative AMPK mice or with conditional Ulk1 deletion
experiment.measurement: ULK1 phosphorylation, mitophagy and lysosomal biogenesis in vivo

text: ACC2 carries an amino-terminal hydrophobic sequence targeting it to the mitochondrial outer membrane, making it the first identified mitochondrial substrate of AMPK, and AMPK phosphorylation of Ser79 in ACC1 and Ser221 in ACC2 inactivates ACC activity.

quotes.quote:
ACC2 has an additional amino-terminal hydrophobic sequence that specifically 
targets it to the mitochondrial outer membrane and therefore represents the first identified 
mitochondrial substrate of AMPK152. Upon activation of AMPK, phosphorylation of Ser79 
in ACC1 and Ser221 in ACC2 results in the inactivation of ACC activity.

experiment.system: mammalian cells expressing ACC1 and ACC2
experiment.perturbation: AMPK activation and phosphorylation of ACC sites; subcellular localization analysis
experiment.measurement: ACC subcellular localization and ACC enzymatic activity

text: AMPK stimulates catabolism by phosphorylating TXNIP and TBC1D1 to increase plasma membrane localization of GLUT1 and GLUT4 respectively, phosphorylating PLD1 to indirectly increase glucose uptake, phosphorylating PFKFB3 to increase glycolytic flux via PFK1, and stimulating lipases such as ATGL to release fatty acids from triglyceride stores.

quotes.quote:
Phosphorylation of 
TXNIP13 and TBC1D1 (REF. 101) increases the plasma membrane localization of GLUT1 
and GLUT4, respectively. Phosphorylation of phospholipase D1 (PLD1) by AMPK has also 
been shown to indirectly increase glucose uptake102. AMPK also increases flux through the 
glycolytic pathway by phosphorylating PFKFB3 (6-phosphofructo-2-kinase/fructose-2, 6-
bisphosphatase 3), which affects the activity of PFK1, a rate-limiting enzyme in glycolysis11 
(FIG. 2). In addition to stimulating glucose utilization, AMPK also pushes cells towards 
using their lipid stores. This is achieved by stimulating lipases such as adipose triglyceride 
lipase (ATGL; also known as PNPLA2) to release fatty acids from triglyceride stores9.

experiment.system: mammalian cells and tissues (muscle, adipose)
experiment.perturbation: AMPK activation/phosphorylation of TXNIP, TBC1D1, PLD1, PFKFB3 and ATGL
experiment.measurement: glucose transporter localization, glucose uptake, glycolytic flux and fatty acid release

text: TNF-alpha stimulation of various human and mouse cell lines produced a two-phase NF-kB activation profile resembling strongly damped oscillations, distinct from the prediction of a minimal two-component system.

tain 17 partially overlapping parameters that

These pa-
rameters were about sevenfold lower than those

els, suggesting previously unrecognized cross-
regulation in the expression of IB genes.

a very shallow dose-response curve was obtained

well described by the prediction based on parameters measured from the activation time 
distribution (Fig. 2B).

experiment.system: SOSFL/Grb2 on pLAT- and Ras-functionalized supported membrane microarrays
experiment.perturbation: observational; single SOS recruitment events that dissociate without activating
experiment.measurement: membrane dwell time before unbinding without activation (rejection time histogram), compared to kinetic model prediction

text: Fitting the kinetic model to the data indicates SOS activation on membranes passes through at least one rate-limiting kinetic intermediate with transition rate kN = 0.02 s−1 and dissociation rate k−1 = 0.016 s−1.

quotes.quote:
indicating that SOS activation on membranes involves progressing through at least one rate- 
limiting kinetic intermediate, with a low transition rate (kN) of 0.02 s−1.
the fitted values are kN = 0.02 s−1 and k−1 = 0.016 s−1

experiment.system: SOSFL/Grb2 supported-membrane single-molecule assay
experiment.perturbation: observational; model fitting (N = 1 intermediate) to measured distributions
experiment.measurement: fitted transition rate constant kN and dissociation rate constant k−1

text: Omitting Grb2 reduced SOS membrane recruitment by ~90%.

quotes.quote:
If Grb2 was not included, we observed ~90% lower SOS 
recruitment.

experiment.system: SOSFL on supported membranes with pLAT and Ras
experiment.perturbation: omission of Grb2 from solution
experiment.measurement: single-molecule SOS membrane recruitment by TIRF microscopy

numbers.quantity: reduction in SOS recruitment without Grb2

text: SOSFL activated without Grb2 and the SOScatPR construct lacking N-terminal autoinhibition both show exponentially shaped activation time distributions over the experimental time scale of 1 to 200 s, indicating single-step activation without the kinetic intermediate, whereas removing PIP2 decreased the activation rate while retaining the rise-and-fall shape.

quotes.quote:
Cases (i) and (ii) 
result in single-step activation (i.e., the activation time distribution is exponentially shaped) 
over the experimental time scale of 1 to 200 s.

Case 
(iii), lacking PIP2 in the membrane, exemplifies the scenario where the activation pathway 
on the membrane is hindered, as revealed by a decreased activation rate, yet the kinetic 
bottleneck is retained, as revealed by the rise-and-fall shape of the activation time 
distribution (Fig. 3I).

experiment.system: supported membranes with pLAT and Ras
experiment.perturbation: three orthogonal conditions: Grb2 omitted; SOScatPR construct lacking N-terminal autoinhibitory domains; membranes lacking PIP2
experiment.measurement: single-molecule activation time distributions and activation rates compared with Grb2-mediated SOSFL

text: The ratio prej(t)/pact(t) decays with SOS dwell time for SOSFL, indicating kinetic proofreading, while it is near-constant for SOScatPR molecules lacking kinetic intermediates.

quotes.quote:
The kinetic intermediate defined by autoinhibition 
release greatly enhances the proofreading capability, as evident from the decaying functional 
form of the prej(t)/pact(t) curve for SOSFL (Fig. 3, J and M). By contrast, a weakly 
discriminating process will have a near-constant curve, as observed for SOScatPR molecules 
lacking kinetic intermediates

experiment.system: single-molecule corral assay of SOSFL versus SOScatPR on supported membranes
experiment.perturbation: comparison of full-length SOS with autoinhibition-lacking SOScatPR
experiment.measurement: ratio of rejection to activation counts as a function of SOS dwell time

text: Adding 50 nM of the catalytically inert SOS PR domain, which promotes LAT assembly, substantially increased the rate of Ras activation; the twofold increase in SOSFL recruitment is insufficient to explain the eightfold increase in Ras activation, and the enhancement was absent at low LAT densities and abolished at PR domain concentrations ≥100 nM.

quotes.quote:
we observed that 
the rate of Ras activation increased substantially when the PR domain was added (50 nM) 
(Fig. 4, C to E), suggesting that LAT assemblies promote Ras activation. Notably, this 
enhanced activation by the PR domain was absent at low LAT densities, where assemblies 
cannot form; titrating the PR domains to a higher concentration (≥100 nM in our 
experiments) also abolished this enhancement by outcompeting SOSFL (fig. S7). 
Furthermore, the twofold increase in SOSFL recruitment with the PR domain is insufficient 
to explain the eightfold increase in Ras activation (Fig. 4, C to E).

experiment.system: SOSFL/Grb2 on pLAT- and Ras-functionalized corralled supported membranes
experiment.perturbation: titration of the SOS PR domain (50 nM; ≥100 nM) and variation of LAT density
experiment.measurement: rate of Ras activation (RBD intensity per corral) and SOSFL recruitment

text: After accounting for recruitment, the roughly fourfold net increase in Ras activation per SOS molecule upon PR domain addition is comparable to the model estimate based on the mean dwell time change from ~4 to 6 s.

quotes.quote:
The roughly fourfold net increase in 
Ras activation per SOS molecule (after accounting for recruitment) is comparable to the 
estimation on the basis of mean dwell time changes (from ~4 to 6 s).

experiment.system: SOSFL/Grb2 corral assay with LAT assembly tuned by the SOS PR domain
experiment.perturbation: addition of the SOS PR domain to induce LAT assembly
experiment.measurement: Ras activation per SOS molecule and single-molecule SOS dwell time distributions, compared with model calculation of Pact versus mean dwell time

numbers.quantity: net increase in Ras activation per SOS molecule

text: Single-molecule tracking indicates that stable SOS recruitment (dwell time > 1 s) is mediated primarily by Grb2 rather than PIP2 or Ras, and mobility analysis indicates stably recruited SOS interacts with at least two LAT molecules via multiple Grb2 molecules.

quotes.quote:
Single-molecule tracking of SOS shows that the initial stable 
recruitment of SOS (dwell time > 1 s) is mediated primarily by Grb2 instead of PIP2 or Ras 
(figs. S4 and S5). Furthermore, mobility analysis indicates that stably recruited SOS is 
interacting with at least two LAT molecules via multiple Grb2 molecules (fig. S6).

experiment.system: SOSFL on supported membranes with pLAT, PIP2 and Ras
experiment.perturbation: comparison of recruitment components (Grb2, PIP2, Ras)
experiment.measurement: single-molecule tracking of dwell times and diffusive mobility

text: In the reconstitution, proteins were laterally mobile at typical densities of <100, ~800, and ~500 μm−2 for Hck, LAT, and Ras, with small variations (<10%) across different arrays, and the Grb2-mediated recruitment rate of SOSFL was 3 × 10−3 s−1 μm−2.

quotes.quote:
All of these proteins reconstituted on supported membranes were 
laterally mobile, with typical densities of <100, ~800, and ~500 μm−2 for Hck, LAT, and 
Ras, respectively.

Both LAT and Ras showed small 
variations (<10%) across different arrays (fig. S1).

The Grb2-mediated recruitment rate of SOSFL 
was 3 × 10−3 s−1 μm−2.

experiment.system: supported lipid bilayer microarrays with His6-Hck, His6-LAT and covalently attached H-Ras
experiment.perturbation: observational characterization of the reconstituted membrane system
experiment.measurement: fluorescence-based protein surface densities, array-to-array variation, and SOSFL recruitment rate

text: An ENU screen for embryonic patterning mutations identified two mouse mutants, wimple (wim) and flexo (fxo), that lack ventral neural cell types and show other phenotypes characteristic of defects in Sonic hedgehog signalling; wim is an allele of the mouse homologue of IFT172 and fxo is a new hypomorphic allele of polaris, the mouse homologue of IFT88.

quotes.quote:
In a screen for
embryonic patterning mutations induced by ethylnitrosourea,
here we identify two mouse mutants, wimple (wim) and ﬂexo
(fxo), that lack ventral neural cell types and show other pheno-
types characteristic of defects in Sonic hedgehog signalling. Both
mutations disrupt IFT proteins: the wim mutation is an allele of
the previously uncharacterized mouse homologue of IFT172; and

fxo is a new hypomorphic allele of polaris, the mouse homologue
of IFT88.

experiment.system: Mouse embryos from an ENU mutagenesis screen
experiment.perturbation: ENU-induced recessive mutations; genetic mapping and sequencing
experiment.measurement: Embryonic morphology, neural cell type markers, positional cloning

text: wim embryos arrested at E10.5-11.5 with an open neural tube in the head lacking the normal ventral midline groove, whereas fxo mutant embryos showed a sharp mesencephalic flexure angle at E9.5-10.5 and arrested at E12.5-13.5 with abnormal brain morphology and preaxial polydactyly.

quotes.quote:
wim embryos
arrested at embryonic day 10.5–11.5 (E10.5–11.5) with an open
neural tube in the head that lacked the normal groove on the ventral
midline (Fig. 1b)

fxo
mutant embryos had an unusually sharp angle of the mesencephalic
ﬂexure at E9.5–10.5 (Fig. 1c) and arrested at E12.5–13.5 with
abnormal brain morphology and preaxial polydactyly

experiment.system: wim and fxo mutant mouse embryos
experiment.perturbation: observational (homozygous recessive mutants vs wild type)
experiment.measurement: Embryonic morphology at successive stages

text: wim mapped to a 484-kilobase interval on chromosome 5 (from a cross with 2,600 opportunities for recombination), and the only sequence change identified was a T to C mutation in the mouse IFT172 homologue causing a Leu1564Pro substitution near the carboxy terminus.

quotes.quote:
We mapped wim to a 484-kilobase (kb) interval on chromosome
5. We evaluated all genes in that interval as candidates, and the only
mutation that we identiﬁed in the wim chromosome was a T to C
mutation in the mouse homologue of IFT172

This mutation causes a leucine to pro-
line substitution (Leu1564Pro) near the carboxy terminus of the
protein

In a mapping cross of 2,600 opportunities for recombination, wim was mapped to a
484-kb interval between D5Ski122 and D5Ski114

experiment.system: wim mutant mouse embryos (C3H congenic; C57BL/6 parental)
experiment.perturbation: observational (mapping cross and candidate gene sequencing)
experiment.measurement: Recombination mapping and coding-region sequencing of candidate genes

text: Wim was required for left-right asymmetry and nodal cilia formation: heart looping polarity was reversed in 40% (58 of 146) of E9.5 wim embryos, nodal-lacZ was bilaterally expressed in five out of eight wim embryos, and node cells of wim embryos lacked all cilia by SEM.

quotes.quote:
the
polarity of heart looping was reversed in 40% (58 of 146) of E9.5
wim embryos (data not shown), and an early marker of left–right
asymmetry, nodal–lacZ (ref. 5), showed abnormal bilateral
expression in wim (Fig. 1e, f). Like polaristm1Rpw mutants, the
node cells of wim embryos lacked all cilia (Fig. 1g–j)

in ﬁve out of
eight wim embryos, nodal–lacZ expression was observed bilaterally (f), and three
other wim embryos showed the wild-type expression pattern

experiment.system: wim mutant mouse embryos (E8.0–E9.5)
experiment.perturbation: observational (wim homozygotes vs wild-type littermates)
experiment.measurement: Heart looping polarity, nodal–lacZ expression, scanning electron microscopy of the node

text: polaristm1Rpw null embryos lacked floor plate, V3 interneuron and motor neuron markers, whereas the hypomorphic polarisfxo embryos had a weaker phenotype with floor plate absent at most levels but V3 interneuron and motor neuron markers expressed.

quotes.quote:
We conﬁrmed that polar-
istm1Rpw homozgyous embryos do not express markers of the ﬂoor
plate (ref. 4 and Fig. 2b), and found that other ventral cell types,
including V3 interneurons and motor neurons, were also absent in
polaristm1Rpw-null mutants (Fig. 2f and data not shown). polarisfxo
embryos had a weaker neural phenotype: the ﬂoor plate was absent
at most levels in the neural tube (Fig. 2c), whereas markers of V3
interneurons and motor neurons were expressed (Fig. 2g and data
not shown).

experiment.system: E10.5 polaristm1Rpw and polarisfxo mutant mouse neural tubes
experiment.perturbation: observational (null vs hypomorphic polaris alleles vs wild type)
experiment.measurement: Immunohistochemical staining for Shh (floor plate), HB9 (motor neurons), V3 interneuron markers

text: The wim neural patterning phenotype was indistinguishable from polaristm1Rpw: floor plate, V3 interneuron progenitor and motor neuron markers were not expressed; wim over the Hdhdf4J deletion gave the same pattern as wim homozygotes, indicating wim is a null or nearly null allele.

quotes.quote:
The neural patterning phenotype of wim was indistinguishable
from that of polaristm1Rpw embryos: markers of the ﬂoor plate, V3
interneuron progenitors and motor neurons were not expressed
(Fig. 2d, h, and Supplementary Figs 2a–d and 3e–f). Embryos that
carried the wim mutation in trans to Hdhdf4J, a large deletion that
uncovers the wim interval6, expressed neural markers in the same
pattern as wim homozygous embryos (data not shown), indicating
that wim is a null or nearly null allele.

experiment.system: wim homozygous and wim/Hdhdf4J transheterozygous mouse embryos
experiment.perturbation: genetic: wim in trans to a deficiency uncovering the interval
experiment.measurement: Neural marker expression in the neural tube

text: Loss of ventral neural cell types in wim and polaristm1Rpw was slightly less severe than in Shh mutants but very similar to Gli2 Gli3 double mutants: Pax7 was expressed in its normal dorsal domain and some lateral fates such as V2 interneurons were specified.

quotes.quote:
The loss of ventral neural cell
types in wim and polaristm1Rpw was slightly less severe than that of
Shh mutants, but very similar to that of double mutants lacking Gli2
and Gli3, the transcription factors that regulate Hedgehog (Hh)
target gene expression7. For example, like Gli2 Gli3 double mutants
and unlike Shh mutants8,9, Pax7 was expressed in its normal dorsal
domain in polaristm1Rpw and wim (Fig. 2m–p) and some lateral cell
fates (such as V2 interneurons) were speciﬁed

experiment.system: E10.5 wim and polaristm1Rpw mutant mouse neural tubes
experiment.perturbation: observational (comparison of mutant marker patterns with published Shh and Gli2 Gli3 mutants)
experiment.measurement: Immunostaining for Pax7 and V2 interneuron markers

text: E9.5 Kif3a mutant embryos did not specify a floor plate or V3 interneuron progenitors and expressed the lateral marker Pax6 at high levels across the ventral midline, so three IFT proteins — Wim, Polaris and Kif3a — are all required for specification of ventral neural cell types.

quotes.quote:
We found that E9.5 Kif3a mutant embryos did not
specify a ﬂoor plate or V3 interneuron progenitors and expressed
the lateral marker Pax6 at high levels across the ventral midline of
the neural tube (Supplementary Fig. 4). Thus, three IFT proteins,

Wim, Polaris and Kif3a, are all required for speciﬁcation of ventral
neural cell types.

experiment.system: E9.5 Kif3atm1Maz mutant mouse embryos
experiment.perturbation: observational (Kif3a homozygous mutants vs littermate controls)
experiment.measurement: Floor plate, V3 progenitor and Pax6 marker expression in the neural tube

text: The notochord was specified normally and expressed wild-type amounts of Shh in E9.5 wim, polaris and Kif3a embryos, suggesting the neural patterning defect is not the result of abnormal notochord development.

quotes.quote:
We found,
however, that the notochord was speciﬁed normally and expressed
wild-type amounts of Shh in E9.5 wim, polaris and Kif3a embryos
(Supplementary Figs 3a–d and 4a, b, and data not shown),
suggesting that the neural patterning defect is not the result of
abnormal notochord development.

experiment.system: E9.5 wim, polaris and Kif3a mutant mouse embryos
experiment.perturbation: observational (mutant vs wild type)
experiment.measurement: Shh expression and notochord specification by in situ hybridization/immunostaining

text: Ptch1-lacZ, a direct transcriptional target of Hh signalling, was greatly reduced in the neural tube of wim, polarisfxo and Kif3a mutants, and also at other sites of Hh signalling including somites, posterior limb bud and gut.

quotes.quote:
Ptch1–lacZ expression was greatly reduced in the neural tube of
wim, polarisfxo and Kif3a mutants (Fig. 3a–h), indicating that the
IFTmutants did not specify ventral cell types because they failed to
activate Shh targets normally. Ptch1–lacZ was expressed in other
sites of Hh signalling in wild-type embryos, including somites,
the posterior limb bud and the gut (Fig. 3a, b). The expression of
Ptch1–lacZ was greatly reduced at these sites in wim, polarisfxo and
Kif3a mutants (Fig. 3c–h)

experiment.system: E9.5 mouse embryos carrying one copy of the Ptch1–lacZ reporter in wim, polarisfxo or Kif3a mutant backgrounds
experiment.perturbation: genetic loss of IFT genes
experiment.measurement: X-Gal staining of Ptch1–lacZ in whole mounts and sections

text: wim Ptch1, polarisfxo Ptch1 and Kif3a Ptch1 double mutants were morphologically indistinguishable from the respective single IFT mutants and expressed the same low levels of Ptch1-lacZ, rather than the high levels seen in Ptch1 mutants, placing IFT proteins downstream of Ptch1 inside neural cells.

quotes.quote:
wim Ptch1, polarisfxo
Ptch1 and Kif3a Ptch1 double mutants were morphologically indis-
tinguishable from the respective wim, polarisfxo and Kif3a single
mutants (Fig. 3). Ptch1–lacZ was highly expressed in most cells of
Ptch1 homozygous mutants (Fig. 3i, j). By contrast, wim Ptch1,
polarisfxo Ptch1 and Kif3a Ptch1 double mutants expressed the same
low levels of Ptch1–lacZ as wim, polarisfxo and Kif3a single mutants
(Fig. 3k–p). Because the IFTmutations blocked the activation of the
Shh pathway caused by loss of Ptch1, IFT proteins must be required
for a step in the Shh signalling pathway downstream of Ptch1 inside
neural cells.

experiment.system: Mouse double mutant embryos (IFT gene; Ptch1tm1Mps lacZ)
experiment.perturbation: epistasis: removing Ptch1 in an IFT mutant background
experiment.measurement: Embryo morphology and Ptch1–lacZ reporter expression

text: wim Rab23 and polaristm1Rpw Rab23 double mutants failed to specify ventral neural cell types, like the IFT single mutants and in contrast to the ventral fate expansion of Rab23 single mutants, placing wim and polaris downstream of Ptch1, Smo and Rab23.

quotes.quote:
In contrast to the expansion of ventral cell fates
in Rab23 mutants13,14, wim Rab23 and polaristm1Rpw Rab23 double
mutants failed to specify ventral neural cell types (Fig. 4b, c, g, h)
like wim and polaristm1Rpw single mutants (Fig. 2b, d, f, h). Thus,
wim and polaris are required for signalling in the Shh pathway at a
step downstream of Ptch1, Smo and Rab23.

experiment.system: E10.5 mouse double mutant embryos (wim or polaristm1Rpw with Rab23opb2)
experiment.perturbation: epistasis: combining IFT mutations with a Rab23 negative-regulator mutation
experiment.measurement: Expression of Shh, HB9 and Pax6 in the spinal cord

text: Motor neurons that were not specified in wim and polaristm1Rpw single mutants were rescued in wim Gli3 and polaristm1Rpw Gli3 double mutants, with more motor neurons specified in caudal than rostral regions; the authors interpret this as wild-type Wim and Polaris antagonizing production or activity of the Gli3 repressor.

quotes.quote:
Motor neurons, which were not
speciﬁed in wim and polaristm1Rpw mutants (Fig. 2f, h), were rescued
in wim Gli3 and polaristm1Rpw Gli3 double mutants (Fig. 4i, j).

A simple interpretation of these results is that the
wild-type Wim and Polaris antagonize production or activity of the
Gli3 repressor.

More motor neurons were speciﬁed in caudal
than in rostral regions of the wim Gli3 and polaris tm1Rpw Gli3 neural tube

experiment.system: E10.5 mouse double mutant embryos (wim or polaristm1Rpw with Gli3XT-J)
experiment.perturbation: epistasis: removing Gli3 in an IFT mutant background
experiment.measurement: HB9 motor neuron marker and Pax6 expression in the spinal cord

text: Chemokines are classified into four subfamilies (CC, CXC, CX3C, XC) based on the configuration of the two cysteines closest to the N terminus; there is a sole CX3C chemokine and two XC forms in humans and one in mice.

quotes.quote:
Variation in the pre-
cise conﬁguration of the two cysteines closest to the N
terminus allows chemokines to be split into four

The sole CX3C chemokine has
three amino acids between these two cysteines, while
XC chemokines, of which there are two forms in
humans and one in mice, lack the ﬁrst and the third
cysteines of the motif.

experiment.system: mammalian chemokine protein family (human and mouse sequences)
experiment.perturbation: observational (sequence classification)
experiment.measurement: arrangement of conserved cysteine residues in the mature protein and subfamily assignment

text: Chemokines with the same name in different species are not always functional orthologues: human CCL8 binds human CCR2 while mouse CCL8 is a CCR8 ligand, and mouse CCL3 is functionally more like human CCL3L1 than human CCL3.

quotes.quote:
for example, human CCL8 binds
to the human CCR2 receptor, while mouse CCL8 is a
CCR8 ligand [10], and mouse CCL3 is functionally
more like human CCL3L1 than human CCL3 [11]

experiment.system: human and mouse chemokine orthologue pairs
experiment.perturbation: observational (cross-species comparison)
experiment.measurement: receptor binding specificity and functional activity

text: Chemokine–chemokine interactome mapping shows that human CXCL4 and CCL5 can each heterodimerize/oligomerize with over 20 other chemokines from the CC, CXC, and XC subfamilies, via CC- and CXC-type interfaces in which activity is typically enhanced and inhibited, respectively.

quotes.quote:
human CXCL4 and
CCL5, for example, can each heterodimerize/oligomer-
ize with over 20 other chemokines from CC, CXC, and
XC subfamilies [40]. The structures formed rely on two
types of interfaces, referred to as CC- and CXC-type, in
which chemokine activity is typically enhanced and
inhibited,
respectively
[40].

experiment.system: human chemokines in vitro
experiment.perturbation: observational (interactome mapping of pairwise chemokine interactions)
experiment.measurement: heterodimerization/oligomerization partners and resulting chemokine activity

numbers.quantity: chemokine partners of CXCL4 and CCL5

text: Post-translational modification alters chemokine activity: nitration of tyrosine residues in CCL2 reduces its ability to attract monocytes through CCR2, and citrullination reduces the chemotactic activity of CXCL8, CXCL10, and CXCL11 and prevents conversion of CXCL8 into a more active shortened form by blocking thrombin- and plasmin-mediated N-terminal trimming.

quotes.quote:
nitration of tyrosine residues in CCL2 by reactive
nitrogen species reduces the ability of this chemokine
to attract monocytes through its receptor CCR2 [45],
while arginine residues in a number of chemokines can
be converted into citrulline by the enzyme peptidy-
larginine deiminase: this reduces the chemotactic activ-
ity of CXCL8, CXCL10, and CXCL11

prevents
conversion of CXCL8 into a more active shortened

experiment.system: purified chemokines and responding leukocytes
experiment.perturbation: nitration by reactive nitrogen species; citrullination by peptidylarginine deiminase
experiment.measurement: chemotactic activity/monocyte attraction and susceptibility to proteolytic N-terminal trimming

text: MMP-mediated N-terminal trimming has chemokine-dependent effects: it typically enhances the activity of CXCR2 ligands and of CC chemokines with extended N-termini (CCL6, CCL9, CCL23), while CXCL12 is inactivated by MMPs and CCR2 ligands are converted into receptor antagonists.

quotes.quote:
MMP-mediated
N-terminal
trimming
typically
enhances the activity of CXCR2 ligands, and of CC
chemokines with extended N-termini (CCL6, CCL9,
CCL23), while CXCL12 is inactivated by MMPs and
CCR2 ligands are converted into receptor antagonists
[50].

experiment.system: chemokines exposed to matrix metalloproteinases in vitro
experiment.perturbation: MMP-mediated proteolytic trimming of the chemokine N terminus
experiment.measurement: receptor-activating (agonist/antagonist) activity of the processed chemokine

text: DC-mediated cleavage of the highly charged C terminus of CCL21 releases a form with much higher diffusivity than the full-length ECM-anchored protein.

quotes.quote:
DC-mediated
cleavage of CCL21 removes the highly charged C ter-
minus that anchors it to the ECM, thereby releasing a
version of this key DC attractant that has much higher
diffusivity than the full-length protein [51].

experiment.system: CCL21 with dendritic cells / ECM
experiment.perturbation: DC-mediated proteolytic cleavage of the CCL21 C terminus
experiment.measurement: ECM binding and diffusivity of the chemokine

text: The conventional chemokine receptor family comprises 18 cCKRs — 10 CCRs, 6 CXCRs, and a single CX3CR and XCR — and six cCKRs have been reported to show biased signaling.

quotes.quote:
There are currently 18 cCKRs named according to
the predominant type of chemokine they bind

There
are 10 CCRs, 6 CXCRs, and a single CX3CR and
XCR.

Currently, six cCKRs
have been reported to show biased signaling [88].

experiment.system: human/mouse conventional chemokine receptor family
experiment.perturbation: observational (literature census, Fig. 1)
experiment.measurement: number of receptors per subclass and number reported to show ligand-biased signaling

numbers.quantity: cCKRs reported to show biased signaling

text: Some cCKRs are activated by nonchemokine ligands: b-defensins can activate CCR6, HMGB1 is emerging as a CXCR4 ligand, and cells expressing CXCR2 or CXCR4 migrate in response to macrophage migration inhibitory factor.

quotes.quote:
b-defensins can activate CCR6
[89]; the ‘alarmin’ high mobility group box 1 protein
(HMGB1) is emerging as a key CXCR4 ligand [90,91];
and cells expressing CXCR2 or CXCR4 migrate in
response to macrophage migration inhibitory factor
(MIF)

experiment.system: cells expressing individual chemokine receptors
experiment.perturbation: stimulation with nonchemokine ligands (b-defensins, HMGB1, MIF)
experiment.measurement: receptor activation and cell migration

text: CXCR4 and particularly CCR5 are coreceptors mediating HIV entry, docking gp120 after it binds CD4; homozygosity for the nonfunctional D32-CCR5 allele profoundly protects against HIV infection and heterozygosity is associated with slowed progression to AIDS in most cohorts, while after West Nile Virus infection D32-CCR5 homozygosity increases the likelihood of encephalitic symptoms and of dying from the infection.

quotes.quote:
CXCR4, and particularly
CCR5, are vital coreceptors mediating HIV entry into
cells and can dock to the HIV gp120 envelope protein
after it has bound CD4

homozygosity for the non-
functional
D32-CCR5
allele
profoundly
protects
against HIV infection, while D32-CCR5 heterozygosity
is associated with slowed progression to AIDS in most
cohorts of HIV-infected people

Nile Virus, D32-CCR5 homozygosity increases the like-
lihood of developing encephalitic symptoms, and of
dying from the infection [145]

experiment.system: human cohorts carrying the D32-CCR5 allele; HIV and West Nile Virus infection
experiment.perturbation: natural genetic loss-of-function of CCR5 (D32 allele, homozygous/heterozygous)
experiment.measurement: susceptibility to HIV infection, rate of progression to AIDS, and West Nile encephalitis/mortality

text: Multiple pathogens target chemokine receptors: Toxoplasma gondii cyclophilin-18 binds and signals through CCR5, RSV glycoprotein G infects a subset of B cells through CX3CR1, and Staphylococcus aureus LukED and HlgAB target ACKR1 and various cCKRs to lyse erythrocytes and kill leukocytes.

quotes.quote:
cyclophilin-18 from Toxoplasma gondii binds to,
and signals through, CCR5 [147]; respiratory syncytial
virus (RSV) uses it’s glycoprotein G to infect a subset of
B cells through CX3CR1 [148]; and Staphylococcus
aureus leukotoxin ED (LukED) and c-hemolysin AB
toxin (HlgAB) target ACKR1 and various cCKRs to
lyse
erythrocytes
and
kill
leukocytes,
respectively

experiment.system: host cells expressing chemokine receptors challenged with microbial products
experiment.perturbation: exposure to pathogen-encoded proteins (C-18, RSV glycoprotein G, LukED, HlgAB)
experiment.measurement: receptor engagement/signaling, cell infection, erythrocyte lysis and leukocyte killing

text: ACKR2 acts as a chemokine scavenger: it constitutively shuttles to and from the cell surface without needing chemokine-induced signals, internalizes chemokines it encounters, and the internalized chemokine is dislodged from the receptor and degraded.

quotes.quote:
It constitutively shuttles to and from cell sur-
faces without needing chemokine-induced signals to do
so, and internalizes any chemokines it encounters while
exposed to the extracellular space [179,180]. Internal-
ized
chemokine
is
dislodged
from
ACKR2
and
degraded [179,180].

experiment.system: cells expressing ACKR2
experiment.perturbation: exposure to extracellular chemokine (with/without chemokine-induced signaling)
experiment.measurement: receptor surface trafficking, chemokine internalization and degradation

text: ACKR1 shapes chemokine availability and blood cell phenotypes: it transports chemokines across endothelial cells for presentation to blood-borne leukocytes and, on erythrocytes, buffers chemokine abundance in the blood; the absence of ACKR1 from erythrocytes also appears to cause benign ethnic neutropenia.

quotes.quote:
ACKR1
transports chemokines across endothelial cells for pre-
sentation to blood-borne leukocytes [157,158], and, on
erythrocytes, ACKR1 buffers chemokine abundance in
the blood [159–163]

transcriptional

atinocytes prevents the formation of adherens

veloping axon and disruption of their activity

ing edge protrusive structures as might be ex-

vation of the serine/threonine kinase GSK3

ing edge

larization

text: In a pan-cancer analysis, TP53 mutation is strongly and universally associated with copy number variation, and TP53-mutant cancers are typically aneuploid with gross changes in whole chromosome numbers.

quotes.quote:
the association between TP53 mutation and copy 
number variation (CNVs) is strong and universal in a pan-cancer analysis (Ciriello et al., 2013). Also, cancers harboring TP53 mutations are typically aneuploid, with gross changes 
in numbers of whole chromosomes

experiment.system: human tumor genomes across cancer types (pan-cancer analysis)
experiment.perturbation: observational (naturally occurring TP53 mutation status)
experiment.measurement: association of TP53 mutation with copy number variation and aneuploidy

text: p53 loss dysregulates the spindle assembly checkpoint by derepressing MAD2, increasing the rate of chromosome missegregation and tetraploidization, and in tetraploid cells increases multipolar mitoses.

quotes.quote:
p53 loss dysregulates the spindle assembly checkpoint by 
derepressing MAD2, leading to an increased rate of chromosome missegregation and 
tetraploidization (Schvartzman et al., 2011). In the context of tetraploid cells, p53 loss leads 
to an increased rate of multipolar mitoses and subsequent chromosome missegregation

experiment.system: mammalian cells, including tetraploid cells
experiment.perturbation: p53 loss / Rb and p53 pathway inhibition
experiment.measurement: rate of chromosome missegregation, tetraploidization, multipolar mitoses

text: Chromothripsis is significantly more prevalent in tumors harboring TP53 mutations, and telomere dysfunction after p53 and RB inactivation initiates breakage-fusion-bridge cycles contributing to chromothripsis.

quotes.quote:
telomere dysfunction initiates chromosome breakage-fusion-bridge cycles that 
contribute to chromothripsis (Maciejowski et al., 2015). Although the extent to which 
chromothripsis fosters tumorigenesis remains an open question, the phenomenon is 
significantly more prevalent in tumors harboring TP53 mutations

verdict_note: Claim text matches p. 3 verbatim; the 'pediatric medulloblastoma' detail in the experiment field is not in the excerpt but does not alter or contradict the claim.

experiment.perturbation: observational TP53 mutation status; p53 and RB inactivation with telomere erosion
experiment.measurement: prevalence of chromothripsis / chromosome rearrangement events

text: p53 represses retrotransposons via epigenetic silencing rather than apoptosis; p53 binding to sites within LINE and other transposon sequences associates with their downregulation, and repetitive element expression is significantly associated with p53 status in mouse and human tumors.

quotes.quote:
p53 binding to target sites within LINE elements and other 
transposon sequences are associated with their downregulation (Chang et al., 2007). p53-
mediated repression is dependent on epigenetic silencing of retrotransposon loci and not 
apoptosis

there is a significant association between repetitive element expression and p53 
status in mouse and human tumors

experiment.system: mouse and human cells/tumors, drosophila mobile element models
experiment.perturbation: p53 loss/mutation; experimental activation of mobile elements
experiment.measurement: retrotransposon expression, reintegration competence, repetitive element expression versus p53 status

text: Meta-analysis of 16 genome-wide datasets identified only about 60 genes as common p53 targets, with no universal p53 target gene set emerging.

quotes.quote:
Meta-analyses 
from 16 genome-wide datasets revealed that only about 60 genes were implicated as 
common targets (Fischer, 2017)

experiment.perturbation: varied methods of p53 induction across studies (meta-analysis)
experiment.measurement: number of genes implicated as common p53 targets

text: p53 has opposing effects on the same metabolic processes depending on cell type: in breast and lung cancer cells p53 inhibits glycolysis by attenuating glucose uptake or repressing glycolytic enzymes, whereas in muscle cells p53 induces glycolytic enzymes.

quotes.quote:
in breast 
and lung cancer cells, p53 inhibits glycolysis by attenuating glucose uptake (Zhang et al., 
2013) or repressing the expression of glycolytic enzymes (Kim et al., 2013). By contrast, in 
muscle cells, p53 induces glycolytic enzymes

experiment.system: breast and lung cancer cells; muscle cells

experiment.measurement: glucose uptake and glycolytic enzyme expression

text: p53 activation kinetics dictate target gene bias: the p21 promoter responds to short pulses of p53 activity whereas the pro-apoptotic target FAS does not, so a short pulse drives proliferative arrest while a sustained signal induces apoptosis.

quotes.quote:
the p21 
promoter is sensitive to short pulses of p53 activity whereas the pro-apoptotic p53 target 
FAS is not; consequently, a short pulse drives proliferative arrest but a sustained signal 
induces apoptosis

experiment.system: cultured mammalian cells
experiment.perturbation: pulsed versus sustained p53 activation
experiment.measurement: target gene induction (p21, FAS) and cell fate (arrest versus apoptosis)

text: Chromatin context gates p53 output: in embryonic stem cells p53 binds the p21 promoter but p21 is not efficiently activated, dependent on cell-type-specific repressive H3K27me3 marks, and CTCF insulation of the PUMA locus governs whether PUMA is expressed and apoptosis occurs.

quotes.quote:
CTCF insulates the PUMA locus from repressive histone modifications under 
certain conditions, governing whether PUMA is expressed and apoptosis occurs (Gomes and 
Espinosa, 2010b). In embryonic stem cells (ESCs), p53 can be induced to bind to the p21 
promoter, but p21 is not efficiently activated, dependent on cell-type-specific repressive 
histone H3K27me3 marks at the locus

experiment.system: human embryonic stem cells and other cell lines
experiment.perturbation: p53 induction; chromatin/CTCF manipulation
experiment.measurement: p53 promoter binding, target gene (p21, PUMA) expression, apoptosis

text: ATM signaling protects cells from p53-mediated apoptosis without changing p53-driven transcriptional output, instead blocking autophagy and thereby maintaining mitochondrial homeostasis and suppressing ROS.

quotes.quote:
ATM signaling protects cells from p53-
mediated apoptosis, not by changing p53-driven transcriptional output, but by blocking 
autophagy, thus maintaining mitochondrial homeostasis and suppressing ROS levels

experiment.perturbation: modulation of ATM signaling

text: Mice deficient for p21, Puma, and Noxa do not develop thymic lymphoma, indicating p53-mediated cell cycle arrest and apoptosis can be dispensable for tumor suppression in that setting.

mice deficient for

text: Mice with the apoptosis-deficient, arrest-competent p53R175P and p53E180R alleles show extended tumor-free survival relative to p53-null animals, and their tumors exhibit far less chromosomal instability than p53-null tumors.

the tumor-derived p53R175P and p53E180R alleles show 
defects in apoptosis while retaining the capability to provoke cell cycle arrest, so that mice

marked anti-tumor response, the nature of which depends on the model employed (Martins

the

certain p53 mutant 
proteins have a penchant for aggregation into amyloid-like structures (reviewed in de

against mutant p53 can protect mice from cancer produced by transplanted tumors (Roth et

majority of tumor-infiltrating CD8+ T cells (TILs) in B16F10 (B16) or CT26 tumors had

text: Partially TOX-deficient (TOX+/-) tumor-specific T cells controlled tumor growth significantly better than WT cells.

text: Model analysis shows a single-site phosphorylation cycle generates only ultrasensitive, not discontinuous switches, but adding positive feedback from the phosphorylated form to its kinase yields three steady-state solutions over a wide parameter range with hysteresis (bistability); adding a further negative feedback on kinase or phosphatase synthesis/degradation converts the switch into a relaxation oscillator.

quotes.quote:
A single-site phosphorylation
cycle generates only ultrasensitive, but not discontinuous switches. Yet, positive feedback
from the phosphorylated form (Mp) to its kinase can render this cycle into a bistable switch.

In a wide parameter range, there are three
distinct solutions to the steady-state relationship vkin = vphos . The low and high Mp
concentrations correspond to stable “Off” and “On” states, whereas the intermediate state
is unstable. The steady-state Mp dependence on the input kinase (phosphatase) activity
(known as one-dimensional bifurcation diagram) displays hysteresis, the hallmark of
bistability

If, in addition, the phosphorylated form Mp inhibits transcription/translation of the kinase
protein or promotes its degradation (Supplementary Eqs.S2-S3 and Table S3), thereby
creating negative feedback, the universal cycle becomes a relaxation oscillator

experiment.perturbation: addition of positive feedback from Mp to the kinase, plus negative feedback on kinase/phosphatase synthesis or degradation
experiment.measurement: steady-state solutions, bifurcation diagram/hysteresis, and oscillatory time courses

text: Analysis of reported kinetic data suggests that a single MAPK cascade level, e.g. the dual phosphorylation ERK cycle, can exhibit bistability and hysteresis within a certain parameter range, a prediction the author states is awaiting experimental verification; similarly, because Cdc25 and Wee1 can be multiply phosphorylated, the entire CDK/cyclin system is predicted to display multiple steady states.

text: Modelling of protein-modification cycles shows ultrasensitivity arises when converting enzymes operate near saturation but is decreased by sequestration of the signalling protein and can disappear if converting enzymes are inhibited or saturated by their products, whereas distributive multi-site phosphorylation increases output-input sensitivity dramatically, resisting the sequestration effect and leading to switch-like responses.

quotes.quote:
The well-known property of these cycles is
“ultrasensitivity” to input signals, which occurs when the converting enzymes operate near
saturation60. Depending on the degree of saturation, the response of either interconvertible
form ranges from a merely hyperbolic to an extremely steep sigmoidal curve. Sequestration of
a signalling protein by converting enzymes significantly decreases sigmoidicity of responses.
Likewise, ultrasensitivity can disappear if converting enzymes are inhibited or saturated by
their products61. By contrast, multi-site phosphorylation (following a distributive, multi-
collision mechanism62) was shown to increase output-input sensitivity dramatically, resisting
the sequestration effect and leading to switch-like responses62-65.

experiment.measurement: steepness (sigmoidicity) of the output-input steady-state response curve

an event that requires dynamic opening of com-
