experiment.system: UBA domains (e.g. hHR23, Mud1) with Lys48-linked diubiquitin
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: NMR/structural analysis of the UBA-diubiquitin complex

text: The Lys63-linkage-specific antibody contacts the C terminus and Ile36 patch of the distal ubiquitin and residues preceding Lys63 of the proximal ubiquitin, requiring a compact Lys63-linked diubiquitin in which the linkage is accessible.

quotes.quote:
the Lys63-linkage-
speciﬁc antibody interacts with the C terminus
of the distal ubiquitin as well as with its Ile36
patch (Figure 5e) (90). Although Lys63 on the
proximal Ub is not contacted, residues closely
preceding Lys63 mediate antibody binding. In-
terestingly, this interaction requires a compact
Lys63-linked diubiquitin in which the linkage
is accessible to the antibody (90).

experiment.system: Lys63-linkage-specific antibody Fab bound to Lys63-linked diubiquitin
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: crystal structure of the Fab-diubiquitin complex (pdb 3dvg)

text: The NEMO UBAN domain forms a symmetric dimer with two adjacent ubiquitin-binding sites recognizing the distal Ile44 patch and the proximal Phe4 patch of Met1-linked diubiquitin, with Gln2 of the proximal ubiquitin making key interactions; Lys63-linked diubiquitin can only bind the distal site with weaker affinity.

quotes.quote:
NEMO forms a symmetric dimer
that has two adjacent ubiquitin-binding sites,
with one recognizing the distal Ile44 patch and
the second binding to the proximal Phe4 patch
(Figure 5d ) (21). Although the peptide bond
between ubiquitin molecules is not directly
contacted, Gln2 of the proximal ubiquitin
makes key interactions (21). Similar interac-
tions are not accessible for the proximal unit
in Lys63-linked diubiquitin, which can only
bind the distal site with weaker afﬁnity (93).

experiment.system: NEMO UBAN domain with Met1- or Lys63-linked diubiquitin
experiment.perturbation: comparison of chain linkage types
experiment.measurement: crystal structures and binding affinity

text: One A20 zinc-finger domain makes distinct interactions with three ubiquitin molecules, binding the Ile44 patch, the TEK-box, and a surface surrounding Asp58 of distinct ubiquitin moieties; although the ubiquitins were not covalently linked, all Lys63 side chains were near an adjacent ubiquitin C terminus.

quotes.quote:
NMR and crystallographic analysis
revealed distinct interactions between one
A20 zinc-ﬁnger domain and three ubiquitin
molecules (Figure 5f ) (94). A20 binds the
Ile44 patch, the TEK-box, and a surface sur-
rounding Asp58 of distinct ubiquitin moieties.
Although the ubiquitin molecules were not
covalently linked, all Lys63 side chains were in
proximity to an adjacent ubiquitin C-terminus

experiment.system: A20 ZnF4 domain with ubiquitin
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: NMR and X-ray crystallographic analysis (pdb 3oj3)

numbers.quantity: ubiquitin molecules bound by one A20 zinc-finger domain

text: The USP5/IsoT ZnF-UBP domain binds the free ubiquitin C terminus including the Gly-Gly sequence with nanomolar affinity, mediating substrate binding and preferential disassembly of unanchored chains from their proximal end; USP5 can nonetheless act on attached chains with activity comparable to other USP enzymes.

quotes.quote:
Using
its N-terminal ZnF-UBP domain, the DUB
USP5/IsoT binds this free C terminus of
ubiquitin, including the Gly-Gly sequence,
with nanomolar afﬁnity (Figure 5g) (20, 99).

preferentially disassemble unanchored chains
from their proximal end (20, 99). Because of the
latter property, USP5 has been used to validate
the role of unanchored chains in signaling (97,
98); however, it should be noted that USP5
can act on attached chains with an activity that
is comparable to other USP enzymes (30).

experiment.system: DUB USP5/IsoT with unanchored and substrate-attached ubiquitin chains
experiment.perturbation: observational binding/cleavage assays
experiment.measurement: binding affinity of ZnF-UBP for free ubiquitin C terminus and chain disassembly activity

text: Human cells contain about 55 USPs, 14 OTU DUBs, 10 JAMM family DUBs, 4 ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolases and 4 Josephin domain DUBs.

quotes.quote:
Human cells
contain ∼55 USPs, 14 ovarian tumor DUBs
(OTUs), 10 JAMM family DUBs, 4 ubiquitin
C-terminal hydrolases (UCHs) and 4 Josephin
domain DUBs (96).

experiment.system: human deubiquitinase complement
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: bioinformatic enumeration of DUB family members

text: Most USP DUBs are active against all linkages and also hydrolyze the isopeptide bond between substrate and first ubiquitin, an exception being CYLD, which prefers Met1- and Lys63-linked chains.

quotes.quote:
most USPs are
active against all linkages (22, 32, 35) and also
hydrolyze the isopeptide bond between the
substrate and the ﬁrst ubiquitin. An exception
from this nonspeciﬁcity is CYLD, which
prefers Met1- and Lys63-linked chains (35, 98,
106).

experiment.system: purified USP-family DUBs and defined-linkage ubiquitin chains
experiment.perturbation: in vitro cleavage of chains of different linkages
experiment.measurement: linkage preference of hydrolysis

text: Several DUBs are linkage specific: JAMM family DUBs (AMSH, AMSH-LP, BRCC36, POH1) are often Lys63 specific, OTUB1 is specific for Lys48 linkages, Cezanne for Lys11 linkages, and Trabid for Lys29 and Lys33 linkages.

quotes.quote:
JAMM family DUBs are often Lys63
speciﬁc, as seen for AMSH (107), AMSH-
LP (108), BRCC36, and POH1 (109). In
addition, linkage-speciﬁc OTU DUBs have
been described; these descriptions showed that
OTUB1 is speciﬁc for Lys48 linkages (110,
111), Cezanne is speciﬁc for Lys11 linkages
(30), and Trabid is speciﬁc for Lys29 and Lys33
linkages (32, 112).

experiment.system: purified JAMM and OTU family DUBs with defined-linkage ubiquitin chains
experiment.perturbation: in vitro cleavage assays across linkage panels
experiment.measurement: linkage specificity of chain hydrolysis

text: AMSH-LP binds the open conformation of Lys63-linked diubiquitin and contacts Gln62 and Glu64 of the proximal ubiquitin, explaining JAMM family linkage specificity; Trabid instead uses an Ankyrin-repeat UBD upstream of its catalytic OTU domain to position the proximal ubiquitin.

quotes.quote:
AMSH-LP binds to the open
conformation of the Lys63-linked diubiquitin
and contacts Gln62 and Glu64 of the proximal
ubiquitin.

this enzyme uses an
Ankyrin-repeat UBD directly upstream of the
catalytic OTU domain to position the proximal
ubiquitin (112).

experiment.system: AMSH-LP with Lys63-linked diubiquitin; Trabid
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: X-ray crystal structures of DUB-chain complexes

text: A20 combines DUB and E3 domains and has been proposed to first deubiquitylate Lys63-modified proteins and then modify them with Lys48-linked chains to trigger degradation; in vitro A20 prefers to cleave Lys48-linked ubiquitin chains.

quotes.quote:
It has
been proposed that A20 ﬁrst deubiquitylates
Lys63-modiﬁed proteins and then modiﬁes
them with Lys48-linked chains to trigger their
degradation.

Indeed,
A20 prefers to cleave Lys48-linked ubiquitin
chains in vitro (117, 118)

experiment.system: A20 in NF-κB signaling and in vitro chain cleavage assays
experiment.perturbation: observational / in vitro cleavage of chains of different linkages
experiment.measurement: chain editing of substrates (linkage-specific antibodies) and in vitro cleavage preference

text: Lys48 linkages are the most abundant linkage in all organisms subjected to quantitative proteomic analysis, and their levels increase rapidly when the proteasome is inhibited; atypical linkages also accumulate upon proteasome inhibition.

quotes.quote:
As a result, Lys48
linkages are the most abundant linkage in all
organisms subjected to quantitative proteomic
analysis, and their levels increase rapidly when
the proteasome is inhibited (11, 12, 125, 128).

These
atypical
linkages
accumulate
upon
proteasome inhibition (12), suggesting that

experiment.system: cells analyzed by quantitative ubiquitin proteomics
experiment.perturbation: proteasome inhibition
experiment.measurement: abundance of ubiquitin chain linkages by mass spectrometry

text: Lys11-linked chains bind proteasomal receptors and trigger mitotic degradation of cell cycle regulators; in human cells Lys11 linkages accumulate dramatically upon APC/C activation, and inhibition of Lys11-linked chain formation stabilizes APC/C substrates and causes cell cycle arrest.

quotes.quote:
Indeed, Lys11-linked chains bind proteasomal
receptors and trigger degradation of cell cycle
regulators during mitosis (23, 31, 52). In human
cells, Lys11 linkages accumulate dramatically
upon activation of the responsible E3, the
APC/C, and inhibition of Lys11-linked chain
formation stabilizes APC/C-substrates and
leads to cell cycle arrest (23, 31).

experiment.system: human cells and extracts with APC/C substrates
experiment.perturbation: APC/C activation and inhibition of Lys11-linked chain formation (ubiquitin mutants / linkage-specific antibodies)
experiment.measurement: Lys11 linkage abundance, substrate stability, and cell cycle progression

text: Proteasomal subunits show plasticity in substrate recognition: Rpn13 binds monoubiquitin and Lys48-linked diubiquitin with similar affinity, S5a/Rpn10 interacts with chains of multiple topologies, and shuttling factors show only modest preference for Lys48 over Lys63 linkages.

quotes.quote:
Rpn13 binds
monoubiquitin and Lys48-linked diubiquitin
with similar afﬁnity (134), S5a/Rpn10 interacts
with chains of multiple topologies (135), and
various proteasomal shuttling factors show
only modest preference for Lys48 compared to
Lys63 linkages (136).

experiment.system: proteasomal ubiquitin receptors and shuttling factors with ubiquitin/chains
experiment.perturbation: comparison of monoubiquitin and different chain linkages
experiment.measurement: binding affinity/preference

text: Deletion of the proteasome-binding domain in Ufd4 does not affect ubiquitylation but inhibits substrate turnover.

quotes.quote:
deletion of a proteasome-binding
domain in Ufd4 does not affect ubiquitylation,
but inhibits substrate turnover (139).

experiment.system: yeast E3 Ufd4 and its substrates
experiment.perturbation: deletion of the proteasome-binding region of Ufd4
experiment.measurement: substrate ubiquitylation and proteolysis

text: Mutation of all ubiquitylation sites in EGFR did not block endocytosis but strongly affected its routing to lysosomes, and deubiquitylation by Usp8 or AMSH can lead to recycling of EGFR to the plasma membrane.

quotes.quote:
This was demonstrated
with EGFR for which mutation of all ubiq-
uitylation sites did not block endocytosis but
strongly affected its routing to lysosomes (143,
144). As a result, deubiquitylation by Usp8 or
AMSH can lead to recycling of EGFR to the
plasma membrane (145, 146).

experiment.system: EGFR in mammalian cells
experiment.perturbation: mutation of EGFR ubiquitylation sites; DUB (Usp8/AMSH) activity
experiment.measurement: receptor internalization and lysosomal routing/recycling

text: ESCRT complexes bind ubiquitin with a modest preference for Lys63 linkages, and autophagy adaptor molecules bind substrates with a moderate preference for Lys63-linked chains.

quotes.quote:
Ubiquitylated
membrane
proteins
are
recognized by different ESCRT complexes,
which bind ubiquitin with a modest preference
for Lys63 linkages (147, 148).

The aggregates are coupled to
autophagosomes by adaptor molecules, which
bind to substrates with a moderate preference
for Lys63-linked chains (149).

experiment.system: ESCRT complexes and autophagy receptors with ubiquitin chains
experiment.perturbation: comparison of chain linkage types
experiment.measurement: binding preference

text: In response to DNA damage PCNA is monoubiquitylated, recruiting Y family DNA polymerases through PIP-box plus UBZ/UBM domain contacts that displace replicative polymerases; the signal is turned off by Usp1-dependent deubiquitylation, which also terminates FANCD2/FANCI monoubiquitylation-dependent FAN1 recruitment.

quotes.quote:
In response to DNA damage,
PCNA is monoubiquitylated (4, 151), which
recruits Y family DNA polymerases (152, 153).
These polymerases recognize PCNA through
a PCNA-interaction motif, the PIP-box, and
ubiquitin through UBZ or UBM domains,
leading to a high-afﬁnity interaction that
replaces replicative polymerases from PCNA.

the recruitment
signal for Y family polymerases is turned off
by Usp1-dependent deubiquitylation, allowing
the replication machinery to return to its
normal state (154). Similarly, monoubiquity-
lation of FANCD2 and FANCI, two proteins
involved in DNA repair, recruits the FAN1
nuclease, and this signaling event is also turned
off by Usp1 (155–158).

experiment.system: PCNA and FANCD2/FANCI in DNA-damaged cells
experiment.perturbation: DNA damage; Usp1-dependent deubiquitylation
experiment.measurement: monoubiquitylation status and recruitment of Y family polymerases/FAN1

text: Lys63-linked chains serve scaffolding roles: modification of a spliceosomal protein stabilizes an snRNP complex reorganized upon Usp4-dependent deubiquitylation, and modification of a ribosomal protein stabilizes polysomes to promote translation.

quotes.quote:
The modiﬁcation
of a spliceosomal protein with Lys63-linked
chains stabilizes an snRNP complex, which is
reorganized upon Usp4-dependent deubiqui-
tylation (159, 160). Similarly, modiﬁcation of
a ribosomal protein with Lys63-linked chains
stabilizes polysomes to promote translation
(161).

experiment.system: spliceosomal snRNP and ribosome/polysomes
experiment.perturbation: Lys63-linked ubiquitylation and Usp4-dependent deubiquitylation
experiment.measurement: complex stability and translation

text: Unanchored Lys63-linked ubiquitin chains mediate activation of TAK1 and IKK kinases and of the RIG-I antiviral protein; RIG-I binds Lys63-linked, but not Lys48- or Met1-linked, chains through tandem CARD domains, leading to dimerization and downstream signaling.

quotes.quote:
Unan-
chored Lys63-linked ubiquitin chains mediate
the activation of TAK1 and IKK kinases and
the RIG-I antiviral protein (97, 98, 167). RIG-I
binds Lys63-linked, but not Lys48- or Met1-
linked, chains through tandem CARD domains
(97), which leads to RIG-I dimerization and
facilitates downstream signaling events (167).

experiment.system: reconstituted RIG-I/TAK1/IKK signaling with unanchored ubiquitin chains
experiment.perturbation: addition of unanchored chains of defined linkages; USP5 treatment
experiment.measurement: kinase activation, chain binding and RIG-I dimerization

text: Ubiquitylation can impair interactions: monoubiquitylation of Smad4 blocks association with Smad2 and USP9X deubiquitylation relieves this, monoubiquitylation of endocytic adaptors causes an intramolecular UBD interaction blocking cargo recognition, and Lys48-linked chains on Met4 bind an internal UIM to block coactivator engagement.

quotes.quote:
For example, monoubiquitylation of Smad4
blocks its association with the transcriptional
cofactor Smad2 (168). By deubiquitylating
Smad4, USP9X relieves the impediment for
cofactor binding and triggers transcriptional
activation.

leads to an intramolecular interaction between
the conjugate and the adaptor’s UBD and
blocks the ability of the adaptor to recognize
its ubiquitylated cargo (170).

Met4 is modiﬁed
by SCFMet30 with Lys48-linked chains, which
bind to an internal UIM in Met4 and block its
ability to engage with coactivators (124).

experiment.system: Smad4, endocytic adaptors, and yeast transcription factor Met4
experiment.perturbation: monoubiquitylation/Lys48 chain modification and deubiquitylation (USP9X)
experiment.measurement: protein-protein interaction with partners/cargo/coactivators

text: The proteasome can activate proteins by cleaving off inhibitory domains, as in NF-κB precursor processing and yeast SPT23 processing (brought about by Rsp5), and cleavage of NF-κB might require multimonoubiquitylation.

quotes.quote:
The protea-
some can also activate a protein by cleaving
off inhibitory domains, as seen for proteasomal
cleavage of an NF-κB precursor (174).

Proteasomal processing might involve atypi-
cal linkages, as cleavage of NF-κB might re-
quire multimonoubiquitylation (177), whereas
SPT23-processing is brought about by Rsp5, an
E3 that catalyzes monoubiquitylation or Lys63-
linked chain formation (175).

experiment.system: NF-κB p105 precursor and yeast transcription factor SPT23
experiment.perturbation: ubiquitylation with defined modification types and proteasomal processing
experiment.measurement: proteolytic processing and transcription factor release/activation

text: Tumor necrosis factor α receptor engagement initiates multiple ubiquitylation events—Lys63-linked chains by TRAF6, mixed Lys11/Lys63-linked chains by cIAP1, and Met1-linked chains on NEMO by LUBAC—with Met1 chains recognized by NEMO's own UBAN domain and Lys63-linked chains activating IKK by promoting binding to the TAK1 kinase complex.

quotes.quote:
Binding of the tumor necrosis
factor α to its membrane receptor initiates a va-
riety of ubiquitylation events, such as formation
of Lys63-linked chains by TRAF6 (60), mixed
Lys11/Lys63-linked chains by the RING E3
ligase cIAP1 (7, 179), or Met1-linked chains by
LUBAC (82). LUBAC modiﬁes NEMO, a sub-
unit of the IκBα kinase (IKK) complex.

Lys63-linked chains activate IKK by
promoting its binding to the upstream TAK1
kinase complex (181).

experiment.system: TNFα-stimulated cells and the IKK/NEMO complex
experiment.perturbation: TNFα receptor stimulation and E3-dependent ubiquitylation
experiment.measurement: chain linkage formation, NEMO binding and IKK activation

text: The E2 Ube2E3/UbcM2 is transported into the nucleus only when charged with a thioester-linked ubiquitin, and the ubiquitin-loaded enzyme is bound by an importin-family transport factor.

quotes.quote:
the
E2 Ube2E3/UbcM2 is transported into the
nucleus only when it is charged with a thioester-
linked ubiquitin (182). The ubiquitin-loaded
Ube2E3 is bound by a transport factor of the
importin family

experiment.system: E2 enzyme Ube2E3/UbcM2 in cells
experiment.perturbation: ubiquitin charging of the E2 (thioester formation)
experiment.measurement: nuclear import and importin binding

text: Multimonoubiquitylation on several C-terminal lysines exports p53 from the nucleus, and in-frame ubiquitin fusions to p53 suffice to drive nuclear export in a manner dependent on p53's nuclear export signal; USP10 reverses p53 monoubiquitylation to allow reimport and reactivation.

quotes.quote:
Following its multimonoubiq-
uitylation, the transcription factor p53 is ex-
ported out of the nucleus (183). p53 is modiﬁed
on several C-terminal lysine residues, and
in-frame fusions of ubiquitin to p53 are

sufﬁcient to drive its nuclear export (5).
Because cytoplasmic accumulation of these
fusions depends on a nuclear export signal in
p53, monoubiquitylation likely changes the
accessibility of the nuclear export sequence
in p53 to the export machinery, rather than
being an export signal itself. As opposed to p53
degradation, monoubiquitylation of p53 can be
reversed by USP10, which allows reimport and
reactivation (184).

experiment.system: p53 in cells
experiment.perturbation: multimonoubiquitylation, in-frame ubiquitin-p53 fusions, and USP10 deubiquitylation
experiment.measurement: p53 subcellular localization (nuclear export/reimport)

text: Efflux of bodipy cholesterol from cultured fibroblasts is reduced by SHH, which blocks PTCH activity.

quotes.quote:
First, efflux of bodipy
cholesterol from cultured fibroblasts is reduced by SHH, which
blocks PTCH activity (Bidet et al., 2011).

experiment.system: cultured fibroblasts
experiment.perturbation: SHH addition to block PTCH activity
experiment.measurement: efflux of bodipy cholesterol

text: Overexpression of PTCH reduces cholesterol accessibility in the inner leaflet of the plasma membrane to a protein probe, suggesting PTCH decreases either the abundance or chemical potential of inner leaflet cholesterol.

quotes.quote:
Second, overexpression
of PTCH reduces cholesterol accessibility in the inner leaflet of the
plasma membrane to a protein probe, which suggests that PTCH
decreases either the abundance or chemical potential of inner leaflet
cholesterol (Zhang et al., 2018).

experiment.system: cells overexpressing PTCH
experiment.perturbation: PTCH overexpression
experiment.measurement: cholesterol accessibility in inner leaflet reported by a protein probe

text: Cryo-EM structures show PTCH resembles RND transporters and is composed of two pseudo-symmetrical segments, each with a transmembrane domain of six TM helices and one extracellular domain between TM1 and TM2; TM2-TM6 forms a sterol sensing domain.

quotes.quote:
Recently published cryo-electron microscopy
(cryo-EM) structures reveal that PTCH resembles RND transporters
and is composed of two pseudo-symmetrical segments

Each
segment includes a transmembrane domain (TMD) composed of six
TM helices and one extracellular domain (ECD) interposed between
TM1 and TM2.

In PTCH, TM2-TM6 forms a sterol sensing
domain (SSD; dark blue in Fig. 2A)

experiment.system: purified PTCH protein
experiment.perturbation: observational (structure determination)
experiment.measurement: cryo-EM structure/architecture

text: PTCH structures show extra cryo-EM density consistent with a ligand in two places, a hydrophobic pocket within ECD1 and a V-shaped cavity adjacent to the SSD, connected by a potential tunnel; the authors note the resolution is insufficient for conclusive identification of the density.

quotes.quote:
The structures note the presence of extra cryo-EM
density, consistent with a ligand, in two places – a hydrophobic

pocket within ECD1 and a V-shaped cavity adjacent to the SSD and
facing the outer leaflet of the plasma membrane

Although these electron densities are consistent with a
sterol-like molecule, the resolution is insufficient for conclusive
identification.

experiment.system: PTCH cryo-EM structures
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: extra electron density and putative tunnel

text: A lower resolution cryo-EM structure of PTCH carrying mutations in both ligand-binding sites is much more flexible than the ligand-bound structures and reveals a concerted 'twisting' motion.

quotes.quote:
A lower resolution cryo-EM structure of PTCH carrying
mutations in both ligand-binding sites is much more flexible than
the ligand-bound structures and reveals a potential conformational
change, a concerted ‘twisting’ motion that might be part of the
transport cycle (Gong et al., 2018).

experiment.system: PTCH with mutations in both ligand-binding sites
experiment.perturbation: mutation of both ligand-binding sites
experiment.measurement: cryo-EM structure and flexibility

text: PTCHΔLoop2, a mutant of PTCH that cannot bind and respond to SHH and lacks the entire ECD2, is fully capable of inhibiting SMO.

quotes.quote:
For example, a mutant of PTCH that
cannot bind and respond to SHH (Briscoe et al., 2001), called
PTCHΔLoop2, lacks the entire ECD2 but is fully capable of
inhibiting SMO

experiment.system: cells expressing PTCH mutant
experiment.perturbation: deletion of ECD2 (PTCHΔLoop2)
experiment.measurement: SMO inhibition / SHH responsiveness

text: A structure determined under physiological calcium concentrations with a dually lipidated SHH ligand reveals a 1SHH:2PTCH complex in which one interface is between ECD1 and the calcium- and zinc-binding surface of SHH, while at the second interface the N-terminal palmitoyl group and subsequent 15 amino acids of SHH insert into the PTCH protein core and the C-terminal cholesteroyl moiety inserts into ECD1, occluding the putative tunnel.

quotes.quote:
A third structure, determined
under physiological calcium concentrations with a dually lipidated
SHH ligand, reveals a complex with a 1SHH:2PTCH stoichiometry
(Qi et al., 2018b).

At the second interface, the
N-terminal palmitoyl group and subsequent 15 amino acids of SHH
are inserted into the protein core of PTCH, and the C-terminal
cholesteroyl moiety of SHH is inserted into ECD1

Both SHH-attached lipids occlude the putative
tunnel that connects the ECD1 and SSD sterol binding sites

experiment.system: purified SHH-PTCH complex
experiment.perturbation: observational (dually lipidated SHH, physiological calcium)
experiment.measurement: cryo-EM structure and stoichiometry

text: A palmitoylated 22 amino-acid N-terminal peptide of SHH (Palm-SHH22) is sufficient to inhibit PTCH function at high (micromolar) concentrations but, unlike intact SHH, cannot trigger PTCH endocytosis and degradation.

quotes.quote:
A palmitoylated 22 amino-acid N-terminal peptide of SHH
(Palm-SHH22) is sufficient to inhibit PTCH function at high
(micromolar) concentrations

However, unlike intact SHH, Palm-SHH22 cannot trigger
PTCH endocytosis and degradation.

experiment.system: cultured cells with PTCH
experiment.perturbation: treatment with palmitoylated 22-amino-acid SHH peptide
experiment.measurement: PTCH inhibition; PTCH endocytosis and degradation

text: SHH lacking its N-terminal nine amino acids and the palmitate (SHHΔ9) fails to inactivate PTCH but still binds PTCH with high affinity and induces its endocytosis and degradation; SHH lacking only the palmitate can still activate HH signaling in vitro and in vivo with lower potency.

quotes.quote:
Conversely, SHH lacking
its N–terminal nine amino acids and the palmitate (SHHΔ9)
fails to inactivate PTCH, but can still bind PTCH with high affinity
and induce its endocytosis and degradation

SHH lacking a palmitate (but including its N-terminal nine amino
acids) can activate HH signaling both in vitro and in vivo, albeit with
lower potency

experiment.system: cells and embryos treated with SHH variants
experiment.perturbation: deletion of N-terminal nine amino acids/palmitate of SHH
experiment.measurement: PTCH inactivation, binding affinity, endocytosis/degradation, signaling activity

text: The first multi-domain SMO structure reveals a cholesterol molecule bound to the CRD site in the same position that oxysterols were predicted to bind; mutations in the CRD site that prevent cholesterol binding impair HH signaling in cultured cells and mouse embryos.

quotes.quote:
The first multi-domain structure of SMO unexpectedly reveals a
cholesterol molecule bound to the CRD site in the same position that
oxysterols were predicted to bind

Mutations in the CRD site
that prevent cholesterol binding impair HH signaling in cultured
cells (Byrne et al., 2016) and mouse embryos (Xiao et al., 2017).

experiment.system: SMO protein crystals; cultured cells and mouse embryos
experiment.perturbation: CRD site mutations preventing cholesterol binding
experiment.measurement: crystal structure; HH signaling activity

text: Two independent studies demonstrate that cholesterol is sufficient to activate signaling even in the absence of HH ligands, and low doses of cholesterol (but not oxysterols) synergize with SHH in signaling assays; mutations that prevent oxysterol activation while leaving cholesterol activation intact have little effect on SHH-induced signaling.

quotes.quote:
Two independent studies demonstrate that cholesterol is sufficient
to activate signaling even in the absence of HH ligands

show that mutations that prevent oxysterol
activation (but leave cholesterol activation intact) have little effect
on SHH-induced signaling. Low doses of cholesterol (but not
oxysterols) synergize with SHH in signaling assays

experiment.system: cultured cell HH signaling assays
experiment.perturbation: cholesterol or oxysterol addition; CRD mutations discriminating cholesterol vs oxysterol activation
experiment.measurement: HH pathway activation/reporter signaling

text: Complete deletion of the SMO CRD (SMOΔCRD), or mutations that destabilize the CRD-TMD interface or the linker domain or that introduce glycosylation sites at the CRD-TMD interface, increase constitutive ligand-independent SMO activity; SMOΔCRD is markedly less sensitive to PTCH but its activity can be suppressed by PTCH overexpression.

quotes.quote:
Complete
deletion of the CRD (in SMOΔCRD), or mutations that
destabilize the CRD-TMD interface, increase the constitutive
(ligand-independent) signaling activity of SMO in cells

SMOΔCRD is markedly less sensitive to PTCH, but
its activity can be suppressed by PTCH overexpression

mutations that destabilize the linker domain that connects the CRD
to TMD or that introduce glycosylation sites at the CRD-TMD
interface increase the constitutive activity of SMO

experiment.system: cultured cells expressing SMO variants
experiment.perturbation: CRD deletion, CRD-TMD interface/linker mutations, PTCH overexpression
experiment.measurement: constitutive SMO signaling activity and PTCH sensitivity

text: Small angle X-ray scattering shows that SMO activation involves movement of the CRD relative to the TMD.

quotes.quote:
Small angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) shows that activation
involves the movement of the CRD relative to the TMD (Byrne
et al., 2016).

experiment.system: purified SMO protein
experiment.perturbation: activation state comparison
experiment.measurement: small angle X-ray scattering

text: A putative active-state SMO structure highlights a cation-pi 'ionic lock' between an arginine and a tryptophan at the cytoplasmic end of the TM bundle, which is broken by known oncogenic mutations that activate SMO and is conserved in the FZD group of WNT receptors.

quotes.quote:
One of the putative active-state structures highlights a
cation-pi bond (the ‘ionic lock’) between an arginine and a
tryptophan residue at the cytoplasmic end of the TM bundle

This ionic lock is broken by known
oncogenic mutations that activate SMO and is also conserved in
the FZD group of WNT receptors (Wright et al., 2019).

experiment.system: SMO structures and class F receptors
experiment.perturbation: oncogenic activating mutations

text: A high-resolution NRR crystal structure shows the HD domain making extensive contacts with three calcium-binding LNR modules, with S1 in an unstructured loop and S2 in a β-strand buried in an inaccessible pocket; steric occlusion by the LNR-AB linker and stabilization by LNR-B/HD-C interactions prevent premature cleavage, so LNR-A, the LNR-AB linker and LNR-B must all be removed to produce constitutive signaling.

globular folded domain that makes extensive contacts with the three calcium-binding LNR
modules (LNR-A, B and C, Figure 3B). S1 is located within an unstructured loop that does not
contribute to the stability of the HD domain

Direct steric occlusion (by the LNR-AB linker) and global domain
stabilization (by interactions between LNR-B and the HD-C helix) both prevent premature
cleavage of the receptor in the absence of ligand. Thus, LNR-A, the LNR-AB linker, and LNR-
B must all be removed to produce molecules with constitutive signaling activity.

analyzing mice homozygous for the Notch V1744G allele (Huppert et al., 2000), which was

text: Scissile bond selection by γ-secretase depends on subcellular localization: at the plasma membrane the bond between G1743 and V1744 is preferentially cleaved generating stable NICD-V, whereas in endosomes the L1746–S1747 bond is preferentially hydrolyzed generating labile NICD-L and NICD-S; the K1749R substitution, previously interpreted as abolishing mono-ubiquitination and endocytosis, also shifts scissile bond preference to labile NICD species with loss of Notch activity.

text: Live-cell time-lapse microscopy of HeLa cells expressing YFP-B55i showed a significant delay in the metaphase to anaphase transition compared with controls, while the duration of prometaphase was not affected.

we expressed YFP-­tagged versions of 
B55i and B55i CTRL in HeLa cells and analyzed their effect on mi-
totic exit, which is a cellular process that depends on PP2A-­B55 
activity (39, 40). Using live-­cell time-­lapse microscopy, we observed 
a significant delay in the metaphase to anaphase transition in cells 
expressing B55i inhibitor, while the duration of prometaphase was 
not affected (Fig. 3E).

text: Inducing B55i expression, but not the mutant control, in HeLa cells caused a specific accumulation of the NEXT complex RNA targets proRBM39, proDNAJB4, and proDDX6, supporting an impact of PP2A-B55α on NEXT complex function.

strates. This revealed a specific accumulation of the NEXT targets

trol, was induced, supporting an impact of PP2A-­B55α on NEXT

text: AF2 modeling identified RBM7 R143 as critical for B55α binding, confirmed by immunopurification of YFP-tagged full-length RBM7 in cells and by affinity measurements of RBM7 peptides spanning residues 129 to 158; comparative MS of RBM7 WT versus R143A detected no defect in NEXT complex assembly (ZCCHC8 and MTR4/MTREX) but efficient uncoupling of PP2A-B55 binding.

ficient uncoupling of PP2A-­B55 binding of RBM7 R143A (Fig. 4C).

our AF2 model showed that phosphorylation of S136 in

text: In mouse embryonic stem cells where endogenous RBM7 was inducibly degraded via dTAG and complemented with RBM7 variants, RBM7 WT fully suppressed the increased NEXT substrate RNA levels arising upon removal of endogenous RBM7, whereas both the RBM7 S136 and R143 mutants failed to do so, with OCT4 mRNA included as a non-NEXT-substrate control.

mentation system in mouse embryonic stem (mES) cells where endog-
enous RBM7 could be inducibly degraded using the dTAG system

RBM7 variants

we

phosphorylation

while Balan et al. [34] also
