text: Across triplicate injections, the 7-, 15-, and 30-min active gradient methods detected 56.7%, 61.8%, and 62.7% of phosphosites in all three replicates, and median RSDs were 21.4%, 10.9% and 12.6% respectively, with the authors attributing the 7-min imprecision to insufficient sampling across narrower elution peaks.

quotes.quote:
The 7-,15-, and 30-
min active gradient methods resulted in 56.7%, 61.8%, and 62.7% of
phosphosites detected across all three injection replicates, respec-
tively.

The 15- and 30-min active
gradients achieved median RSDs of 10.9 and 12.6%. Not unexpectedly,
the 7-min active gradient method has considerably reduced precision
(21.4% median RSD), most likely due to insufﬁcient sampling across the
narrower elution peaks

experiment.system: HEK293T phosphopeptides, triplicate injections on Orbitrap Astral DIA
experiment.perturbation: Varying active gradient length (7, 15, 30 min)
experiment.measurement: Fraction of phosphosites detected in all three replicates and median %RSD of site quantities

text: In a human/maize entrapment search, internal and external FDR curves disagreed at lower q-values but converged at approximately the 1% FDR threshold.

quotes.quote:
For lower q-values the
internal and external FDRs disagree; however, these curves converge
at approximately the 1% FDR threshold, suggesting that the identiﬁ-
cations reported here are reliable.

experiment.system: HEK293T DIA phosphoproteomics data
experiment.perturbation: Library-free entrapment search against combined human and maize protein database
experiment.measurement: Internal (Spectronaut) vs external (maize) FDR for all and phospho precursors

text: In a phosphoproline decoy search, S, T, and Y showed substantial highly confident localized phosphosites whereas P did not.

quotes.quote:
we searched these data with phosphorylated proline
as a variable modiﬁcation where any detected proline phosphorylation
is false47. S, T, and Y all have a signiﬁcant amount of highly conﬁdent
localized phosphosites whereas the P does not

experiment.system: HEK293T DIA data
experiment.perturbation: Library-free search including phosphoproline as a decoy variable modification
experiment.measurement: Cumulative distribution of localization probabilities by amino acid

text: Using 225 synthetic phosphopeptide standards spiked into a yeast phosphopeptide background as ground truth, the site localization error rate ranged between 1 and 5 percent depending on the localization probability cutoff.

quotes.quote:
Note this same 225 synthetic phosphopeptide mix has
been used by others

From
these data we conclude that, depending on localization probability
cutoff, the error rate ranges between 1 and 5 percent, a similar trend as
the previous study

experiment.system: 225 synthetic phosphopeptide standards spiked into complex yeast tryptic phosphopeptides
experiment.perturbation: Varying localization probability cutoff
experiment.measurement: Localization error rate computed against ground-truth reference sheet

text: In a dilution series of phosphopeptide standards from 10,000 to 39 attomole on-column into constant yeast background analyzed with the 15-min DIA method, the majority of phosphosite calibration curves had R2 values greater than 0.95, and at 39 attomole half of the phosphorylation sites were detected across all three injections.

quotes.quote:
phosphopeptide standards were diluted from 10,000 to 39 attomole
(per standard, on-column) into a constant complex mixture of yeast

Fig. 2J conﬁrms that the majority of the phosphosite calibration curves
have R2 values greater than 0.95, indicating good quantitative linearity.
Supplementary Fig. 3C conﬁrms that even at loads as low as 39
attomole, half of the phosphorylation sites were detected across all
three injections.

experiment.system: Synthetic phosphopeptide standards in constant yeast phosphopeptide background
experiment.perturbation: Five-point four-fold dilution series, 10,000 to 39 attomole per standard on column
experiment.measurement: Linear fit R2 between MS intensity and load; detection across triplicate injections

text: In a replicated HeLa EGF-stimulation experiment analyzed with a 15-min gradient, the Orbitrap Astral method gave the deepest phosphoproteome with near 60% phosphosite completeness across replicates from approximately three-fold more localized sites than timsTOF Pro or Orbitrap Ascend, while the Orbitrap Ascend showed the highest phosphosite overlap at 64%.

quotes.quote:
The Orbitrap Astral method provided the
deepest phosphoproteomic analysis and yielded near 60% phospho-
site completeness across replicates from approximately three-fold
more localized sites as compared to either the timsTOF Pro or Orbitrap
Ascend instruments.

Interestingly, the Orbitrap
Ascend generated the highest level of phosphosite overlap of all three
instruments at 64%.

experiment.system: HeLa cells cultured in triplicate, 15 min EGF stimulation, phosphopeptide enrichment
experiment.perturbation: Same samples/searches analyzed on Orbitrap Astral vs Orbitrap Ascend vs published timsTOF Pro dia-PASEF data, 15-min active gradient
experiment.measurement: Localized phosphosite counts and completeness across triplicates (Spectronaut library-free)

text: Intensity distributions of phosphosites detected in all three EGF-stimulated replicates showed that phosphosites unique to the Orbitrap Astral dataset were biased toward lower intensities, whereas timsTOF Pro-unique sites were distributed more evenly across the intensity range; the authors interpret this as improved Astral sensitivity and larger dynamic range.

quotes.quote:
Both plots
reveal that the unique phosphosites in the Orbitrap Astral dataset are
biased toward lower intensities. In contrast, unique phosphosites for
the timsTOF Pro dataset are distributed more evenly across the
intensity range (Fig. 3D). These observations suggest that our Orbi-
trap Astral exhibits improved sensitivity, resulting in a larger
dynamic range.

experiment.system: EGF-stimulated HeLa phosphoproteomes on three platforms
experiment.perturbation: observational comparison of platform-unique vs shared sites
experiment.measurement: log2 intensity distributions of phosphosites detected in 3 of 3 replicates

text: Differential expression analysis (fold-change > 2, p < 0.05 by two-sided t-test without multiple testing correction) between control and EGF-stimulated samples detected EGFR phosphosites across platforms, and pathway enrichment gave the EGF/EGFR signaling pathway as the top enriched term for all three platforms.

quotes.quote:
Phosphorylation
sites occurring directly on the EGFR are labeled, many of which are
detected across all platforms. To further compare we performed a
pathway enrichment analysis from each dataset (Fig. 3G)—all three
platforms had the EGF/EGFR signaling pathway as the top enriched
term.

phosphosites meeting
the differential expression criteria (fold-change > 2, p < 0.05 via two-sided t-test
without multiple testing correction) indicated in blue

experiment.system: EGF-stimulated vs control HeLa phosphoproteomes on Astral, Ascend, timsTOF Pro
experiment.perturbation: 15 min EGF stimulation vs control
experiment.measurement: Volcano-plot differential expression and Enrichr/NCATS BioPlanet pathway enrichment

text: Phosphopeptides from 12 mouse tissues, offline fractionated into four fractions each and analyzed with a 15-min DIA method, required 12 h of active acquisition and yielded 81,120 unique phosphorylation sites, with per-tissue counts ranging from ~20,000 to 40,000.

quotes.quote:
In total, this
experiment required 12 h of active data acquisition time and resulted
in the detection of 81,120 unique phosphorylation sites

Depending upon the source tissue, the number of identiﬁed
phosphorylation sites ranged from ~20,000 to 40,000 sites (Fig. 4B).

experiment.system: Twelve distinct mouse tissues (C57BL6/J), phosphopeptide-enriched
experiment.perturbation: observational atlas; offline fractionation into four fractions per tissue
experiment.measurement: Unique localized phosphosites by 15-min DIA nLC-MS/MS on Orbitrap Astral

text: Of the 81,120 unique mouse sites, 61,088 localized to S, 16,276 to T, and 3756 to Y, with ~4.6% of total sites from pY, compared with previous studies placing the number closer to ~2%.

quotes.quote:
Of the 81,120 unique sites identiﬁed, 61,088 were localized to S; 16,276
localized to T; and 3756 to Y. It is noteworthy that ~4.6% of the total
sites identiﬁed stem from pY. Previous studies have placed this num-
ber closer to ~2% and often rely on pY-speciﬁc antibodies for enrich-
ment

experiment.system: Mouse 12-tissue phosphoproteome atlas
experiment.perturbation: observational; Ti-IMAC enrichment without pY antibody enrichment
experiment.measurement: Residue-type distribution of localized phosphosites

text: Compared with the reprocessed Huttlin et al. 2010 mouse atlas (35,965 sites over 10 days of MS analysis), the method here provided a 5-fold boost in localized phosphosites per tissue in ~1/24th the time, with median 55.3% overlap in detected sites per tissue.

quotes.quote:
Huttlin and co-workers described
the ﬁrst mouse phosphoproteome atlas, reporting 35,965 phosphor-
ylation sites detected following 10 days of MS analysis

On a per tissue
comparison, the method leveraged here provides a 5-fold boost in the
number of localized phosphorylation sites in ~1/24th the time.

we see good overlap in detection
of sites (median 55.3%)

experiment.system: Mouse tissue phosphoproteomes
experiment.perturbation: Comparison of this Orbitrap Astral DIA atlas vs Huttlin et al. raw data reprocessed in MaxQuant with matching database and similar quality filters
experiment.measurement: Localized phosphosite counts per tissue and overlap fraction

text: Tissue-specificity analysis showed a large portion of sites with single-tissue specificity in both studies, but a sizeable number of sites detected across all twelve tissues in this study, contrasting with the Huttlin work; both studies showed concordance between number of tissues in which a site was detected and its signal strength.

quotes.quote:
a large portion of phosphorylation sites appear to have single tissue
speciﬁcity; however, our results indicate that a sizeable number of sites
are detected across all twelve tissues. This result contrasts with the
Huttlin work

both studies show
concordance between number of tissues detected and overall signal
strength (i.e., abundance).

experiment.system: Mouse 12-tissue phosphoproteome atlas vs Huttlin et al. reprocessed data
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: Distribution of sites by number of tissues observed in, and detected peak intensity per category

text: Compared with the Giansanti et al. multi-tissue study (90-min gradient DDA on Q Exactive HF), the Orbitrap Astral detected 2–3 times more phosphosites per tissue despite a 6-fold shorter measurement time, with median 64.2% agreement versus 55.3% for Huttlin et al.; the pY portion in the Giansanti study is 1.1% versus 4.6% here.

quotes.quote:
Despite a 6-fold shorter measurement time, the Orbitrap Astral
detected 2–3 times more phosphosites per tissue, with improved
agreement with our dataset compared to Huttlin et al. (median 64.2%
versus 55.3%; Supplementary Fig. 6A).

The portion of pY in this
study is 1.1% (Supplementary Fig. 6C), which additionally highlights the
capability of combining Astral sensitivity with DIA acquisition to
enable the detection of 4.6% pY in our data.

experiment.system: Mouse multi-tissue phosphoproteomes
experiment.perturbation: Comparison of this atlas vs Giansanti et al. 90-min gradient DDA on Q Exactive Orbitrap HF
experiment.measurement: Phosphosites per tissue, dataset agreement, pY fraction

text: Mapping the 81,120 phosphorylation sites onto AlphaFold-predicted structures showed a striking prevalence for phosphosites to lie in low pLDDT confidence regions relative to all S/T/Y or all amino acids, with sites detected in all tissues showing a slightly higher preference; all observed amino acids in non-enriched proteomics did not follow this trend, and confidence scores increased with distance from the phosphorylated residue.

quotes.quote:
we mapped the 81,120 phosphor-
ylation sites detected here onto protein structures predicted by
AlphaFold

we observed a striking prevalence for these sites to be in low
conﬁdence regions (Fig. 5C), especially when compared to all S, T, and
Y residues or even all amino acids. Phosphorylation sites that were
detected in all tissues had an even slightly higher preference for these
low-conﬁdence regions. However, all amino acids observed in non-
enriched proteomics experiments did not follow the same trend
examination of the

surrounding environment shows the conﬁdence scores are increasing
with distance from the phosphorylated residue

experiment.system: Mouse atlas phosphosites mapped to UniProt AlphaFold structural library
experiment.perturbation: observational; comparison to all S/T/Y and all amino acid backgrounds
experiment.measurement: Per-residue pLDDT confidence score distributions

text: Applying a published kinase prediction tool profiling 303 serine/threonine kinases to the atlas, half of all phosphorylation sites were predicted to be targeted by 24 or more kinases.

quotes.quote:
we applied a recently published kinase predic-
tion tool38, which was developed by using synthetic peptide libraries to
proﬁle the substrate sequence speciﬁcity of 303 serine/threonine
kinases (Fig. 5D).

half of all phosphorylation sites were predicted to be tar-
geted by 24 or more kinases (Fig. 5E).

experiment.system: Mouse phosphoproteome atlas sites and flanking regions
experiment.perturbation: observational; query against kinase library website for 303 Ser/Thr kinases
experiment.measurement: Number of kinases scoring above the 90th percentile per site

text: Comparison to the PhosphoSitePlus mouse dataset revealed 38,454 previously unidentified phosphorylation sites, constituting 53% of the total identified sites, and 55% of known mitochondrial proteins harbored at least one phosphorylation site.

quotes.quote:
revealing a capture of 38,454 previously uni-
dentiﬁed phosphorylation sites, constituting 53% of the total identiﬁed
sites within our dataset (Fig. 6A). Upon categorizing phosphorylation
sites, we observed a signiﬁcant representation of mitochondrial pro-
teins, with 55% of known mitochondrial proteins harboring at least one
phosphorylation site (Fig. 6B).

experiment.system: Mouse 12-tissue phosphoproteome atlas
experiment.perturbation: observational; comparison against PhosphoSitePlus (downloaded August 22, 2023) and MitoCarta 3.0
experiment.measurement: Counts/fractions of novel sites and phosphorylated mitochondrial proteins

text: Intersection analysis of mitochondrial phosphorylation sites across tissues found liver to harbor the most unique phosphorylation sites, with these unique liver sites showing the largest proportion of mitochondrial matrix proteins.

quotes.quote:
we calcu-
lated the intersections of all mitochondrial phosphorylation sites
across tissues and found the liver to harbor the most unique phos-
phorylation sites (Fig. 6D). Moreover, these unique liver phosphor-
ylation sites showed the largest proportion of mitochondrial matrix
proteins

experiment.system: Mitochondrial subset (MitoCarta 3.0) of mouse 12-tissue phosphoproteome
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: Intersection sizes of tissue-specific mitochondrial phosphosites and sub-mitochondrial localization

text: CPS1, the most phosphorylated protein among liver-unique sites, carried 40 detected phosphorylation sites, 22 of which had not been reported previously and none functionally characterized; site S913 in the L2 integrating domain overlaps a known severe disease-causing missense variant p.S913L.

quotes.quote:
We identiﬁed
carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I (CPS1) to harbor the most phos-
phorylation sites in this group (Fig. 6E).

Notably, 40 phosphorylation sites were detected on CPS1, which
is the ﬁrst and rate-limiting enzyme of the urea cycle. None of these
phosphorylation sites have been functionally characterized, and 22 of
these sites have not been reported previously (Fig. 6F)

The phosphorylation site S913, located within the L2 integrating
domain, overlaps with a known severe disease-causing missense var-
iant in CPS1 (p.S913L)65

experiment.system: Mouse liver mitochondrial phosphoproteome; CPS1 protein
experiment.perturbation: observational; annotation against PhosphoSitePlus and HGMD human variants
experiment.measurement: Count of detected and novel CPS1 phosphosites and overlap with disease variants

text: Y1450 was identified as a conserved phosphorylated residue in the C-terminal L4 NAG-binding domain of CPS1, proximal to the R1453 residue required for NAG binding and the site of two patient variants (p.R1453W and p.R1453Q); structural modeling showed shifts in the Y1450-R1453-containing helix upon NAG binding.

quotes.quote:
We identify Y1450 as a conserved phos-
phorylated residue in this domain, which is located proximal to the key
R1453 residue that is required for NAG binding and is the location of
two patient variants (c.4357C>T and c.4358G>A resulting in p.R1453W
and p.R1453Q, respectively)67 (Fig. 6G).

Structural model-
ing demonstrates shifts in this Y1450-R1453-containing helix of CPS1
upon NAG binding, highlighting the conformational change of the
R1453 residue and its proximity to the Y1450 residue (Fig. 6H).

experiment.system: CPS1 in mouse phosphoproteome atlas; human CPS1 crystal structures (PDB 5DOT Apo, 5DOU NAG)
experiment.perturbation: observational; Clustal Omega orthologue alignment and PyMOL structural modeling of Apo vs NAG-bound states
experiment.measurement: Phosphosite detection, sequence conservation, and modeled residue positions

text: Brain tissue showed the highest prevalence of tissue-unique phosphorylation sites and the strongest abundance changes among pan-tissue sites; using an absolute z-score threshold of 2, 9541 phosphorylation site outliers were found in brain, accounting for 23% of all outliers across the twelve tissues.

quotes.quote:
brain tissue showed the highest prevalence of unique
phosphorylation sites (i.e., sites deﬁned as exclusive to a singular tis-
sue, Fig. 7A).

By
applying the same absolute z-score threshold of 2, we found 9541
phosphorylation site outliers in the brain (Fig. 7B), accounting for 23%
of all outliers across all twelve tissues.

experiment.system: Mouse 12-tissue phosphoproteome atlas
experiment.perturbation: observational; z-score analysis of site abundances (including imputed values) with absolute cutoff of 2
experiment.measurement: Counts of tissue-unique sites and z-score outliers per tissue

text: Cross-species scRNA-seq of human and mouse (KPC) PDAC identified a myofibroblastic CAF subpopulation (myCAFs) expressing genes of smooth muscle contraction, focal adhesion, ECM organization and collagen formation, located adjacent to neoplastic cells, with marker genes including TAGLN, MYL9, TPM1/2, MMP11, POSTN and HOPX in addition to high αSMA.

quotes.quote:
Cross-species analysis of human and 
mouse (KPC model) PDAC tumors by immunostaining 25 and scRNA-seq analysis 44 
identified a subpopulation of myofibroblastic CAFs which was termed myCAFs

These cells express genes associated with smooth muscle contraction, focal adhesion, ECM 
organization, and collagen formation, and are located adjacent to neoplastic cells.

experiment.system: human and mouse (KPC model) PDAC tumors
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: single-cell RNA sequencing and immunostaining of CAF marker gene expression

text: scRNA-seq of human lung adenocarcinoma at different disease stages identified seven fibroblast subpopulations, three ECM-related (COL13A1+ and COL14A1+ matrix fibroblasts and ACTA2+/TAGLN+ myofibroblasts); matrix fibroblasts dominated normal lung and early-stage tumors while myofibroblasts dominated advanced-stage tumors.

quotes.quote:
scRNA-seq of tissues obtained from patients with 
lung adenocarcinoma at different stages of the disease identified seven subpopulations 
of fibroblasts, three of which were functionally related to ECM modulation

The matrix-related fibroblasts (COL13A1+ and COL14A1+) were the main 
subpopulations present in normal lungs and early-stage tumors. In contrast, myofibroblasts 
were dominant in advanced stage tumors

experiment.system: human lung adenocarcinoma tissues across disease stages
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: scRNA-seq clustering of fibroblast subpopulations and marker expression

text: scRNA-seq of human NSCLC revealed five distinct CAF types based on collagen and ECM molecule expression, with one subpopulation high in myogenesis genes including ACTA2 and another strongly expressing EMT and ECM genes.

quotes.quote:
scRNA-seq of human non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC; squamous cell and 
adenocarcinoma) revealed five distinct CAFs types based on the expression of a unique 
repertoire of collagens and other ECM molecules.

experiment.system: human NSCLC (squamous cell and adenocarcinoma) tumors
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: scRNA-seq classification of CAF types by collagen/ECM gene expression

text: In a mouse model of desmoplastic liver metastasis induced by hemisplenic injection of PDAC and colorectal cancer cell lines, scRNA-seq showed myofibroblastic CAFs comprised more than half of the total analyzed CAFs; in a 3D culture model collagen type I acted as a mechanical barrier restricting tumor expansion and invasiveness whereas hyaluronic acid promoted tumor growth and spread.

quotes.quote:
scRNA-seq 
revealed that myofibroblastic CAFs comprised more than half of the total analyzed CAFs

in a 3D culture model, 
collagen type I acted as a mechanical barrier restricting tumor expansion and invasiveness, 
whereas hyaluronic acid promoted tumor growth and spread

experiment.system: mouse desmoplastic liver metastasis model (hemisplenic injection of PDAC and CRC cell lines) and 3D culture
experiment.perturbation: tumor cell line injection; matrix component (collagen I vs hyaluronic acid) in 3D culture
experiment.measurement: scRNA-seq CAF composition; tumor expansion/invasiveness in 3D culture

text: scRNA-seq of the stromal compartment in a transplantable murine melanoma model at distinct time points identified three temporally distinct subpopulations, S1 ("immune"), S2 ("desmoplastic") and S3 ("contractile"), with early tumors comprising mainly S1 and S2 and mid/late tumors enriched for S2 and S3; the subsets were also validated in human melanoma.

quotes.quote:
scRNA-seq profiling of the stromal compartment in a transplantable model of murine 
melanoma at distinct time points of tumor development identified three functionally and 
temporally distinct subpopulations, referred to as S1 ("immune"), S2 ("desmoplastic") and 
S3 ("contractile"), which were also validated in human melanoma.

Temporal analysis revealed dynamic changes whereby early tumors primarily comprised 
S1 ("Immune") and S2 ("desmoplastic") cells, whereas mid and late tumors exhibited S2 
("desmoplastic") and S3 ("contractile") enrichment

experiment.system: transplantable murine melanoma model and human melanoma
experiment.perturbation: tumor transplantation, sampling at distinct time points of tumor development
experiment.measurement: scRNA-seq of stromal subpopulations and their temporal abundance

text: scRNA-seq of human primary, recurrent and lung metastatic osteosarcoma identified three CAF subclusters; the ACTA2+/MYL9High/LUMHigh subcluster, which also expressed osteoblast markers IBSP and SPP1, was the major CAF source in primary and recurrent lesions, whereas the DES+/ACTA2Low/COL14A1Low subcluster predominated in lung metastases.

quotes.quote:
Three CAF subclusters were identified: (1) 
COL14A1+ matrix fibroblasts, (2) DES+/ACTA2Low/COL14A1Low fibroblasts (indicative 
of smooth muscle-like cells), and (3) ACTA2+/MYL9High/LUMHigh fibroblasts

this subcluster was the major 
source of CAFs both in primary and recurrent lesions, whereas subcluster 2 was the 
main component in lung metastases

experiment.system: human osteosarcoma primary, recurrent and lung metastatic lesions
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: scRNA-seq identification and relative abundance of CAF subclusters

text: Reference component analysis of scRNA-seq from human primary colorectal tumors and matched normal mucosa identified two CAF subtypes: CAF-B expressing myofibroblast markers ACTA2, TAGLN and PDGFA, and CAF-A expressing ECM genes MMP2, DCN and COL1A2, with upstream regulators TGFβ1 and SMAD3 activated in both.

quotes.quote:
A scRNA-seq study in human primary colorectal 
tumors and matched normal mucosa used a method termed reference component analysis 
to identify two distinct subtypes of CAFs (CAF-A and CAF-B).

Activation of the upstream regulators TGFβ1 and SMAD3 in both CAF 
subtypes suggests common regulation of these two functional states

experiment.system: human primary colorectal tumors and matched normal mucosa
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: scRNA-seq with reference component analysis of CAF marker/regulator expression

text: In PDAC, iCAFs were distinguished from myCAFs by low αSMA expression, were spatially separated from myCAFs and cancer cells, secreted IL-6, IL-11 and LIF, had an IL-1-driven transcriptomic profile, and the two subsets could interconvert in vitro depending on growth conditions.

quotes.quote:
iCAFs 
were shown to be spatially separated from myCAFs and from the cancer cells, secreted 
inflammatory mediators such as IL-6, IL-11, and LIF, and had a unique transcriptomic 
profile driven by IL-1 signaling 70. The two subsets could interconvert, at least in 
vitro, depending on growth conditions

experiment.system: human and murine pancreatic cancer, including in vitro fibroblast cultures
experiment.perturbation: varying growth/culture conditions
experiment.measurement: marker and cytokine expression, spatial localization, subset interconversion

text: scRNA-seq of human pancreatic CAFs identified csCAFs expressing complement regulatory factors C3, C7, CFB, CFD, CFH and CFI, located close to cancer cells in stage I PDAC and decreasing during tumor progression.

quotes.quote:
CAFs expressing complement regulatory factors (C3, C7, CFB, CFD, CFH, and CFI) which 
can promote inflammation and immune activity in the TME appear in close proximity to 
pancreatic cancer cells in stage I PDAC, and decrease during tumor progression73.

experiment.system: human PDAC samples across stages
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: scRNA-seq with weighted gene co-expression network analysis of complement gene expression and localization

text: CyTOF analysis of murine pancreatic tumors showed that Hedgehog pathway inhibition increases the proportion of iCAFs versus myCAFs, sequesters repressive myeloid cells, inhibits CD8+ T cell tumor infiltration and promotes FOXP3+ Treg accumulation, generating an immunosuppressive TME.

quotes.quote:
CyTOF analysis of murine pancreatic tumors demonstrated that Hedgehog 
pathway inhibition increases the proportion of iCAFs versus myCAFs, sequesters repressive 
myeloid immune cells and inhibits CD8+ T cell tumor infiltration, while promoting FOXP3+ 
Treg accumulation, thus generating an immunosuppressive TME

experiment.system: murine pancreatic tumors
experiment.perturbation: Hedgehog pathway inhibition
experiment.measurement: CyTOF quantification of CAF subsets and immune cell populations

text: Mass cytometry of murine and human PDAC identified fibroblast subsets with high versus low CD105 (ENG) expression with opposing effects on immune activity and tumor growth: CD105Low CAFs showed antigen presentation modules (MHC-II, CD74) and correlated with T cell proliferation, while CD105High CAFs inversely correlated with certain CD4 and CD8 T cell subsets; the suppressive effects of CD105Low CAFs required intact immunity but not their antigen-presenting capabilities.

quotes.quote:
Single-cell analysis using mass cytometry on murine and human PDAC samples unveiled 
fibroblast subsets with high versus low CD105 (ENG) expression that had opposing effects 
on immune activity and tumor growth 77.

The suppressive effects of CD105Low CAFs depended on proper immune activity 
that was abrogated in immune deficient animals, but did not rely on their antigen presenting 
capabilities

experiment.system: murine and human PDAC, including immune deficient animals
experiment.perturbation: CD105-high vs CD105-low fibroblast subsets; immune-deficient host background
experiment.measurement: mass cytometry profiling, T cell subset correlations, tumor growth

text: In murine pancreatic cancer models, PDPNHigh CAFs diverged into two subpopulations through IL-1 and TGFβ signaling; the TGFβ-driven CAFs accumulating in PDAC were identified by LRRC15 expression and correlated with poor response to anti-PD-L1 therapy.

quotes.quote:
PDPNHigh CAFs were shown to play an immune regulatory 
role in PDAC, where they diverged into two subpopulations through IL-1 and TGFβ 
signaling. The TGFβ-driven CAFs which accumulated in PDAC were identified by LRRC15 
expression and correlated with poor response to anti-PD-L1 therapy

experiment.system: murine pancreatic cancer models and patient data
experiment.perturbation: IL-1 and TGFβ signaling; anti-PD-L1 therapy
experiment.measurement: scRNA-seq of CAF subpopulations and correlation with immunotherapy response

text: scRNA-seq in a mouse TNBC model revealed two proinflammatory and two immunomodulatory CAF subpopulations within PDPN+ CAFs (pCAFs) compared with S100a4+ CAFs (sCAFs); immunomodulatory pCAFs diverged into Ly6cLow and Ly6cHigh subpopulations, the latter inhibiting T cell proliferation and activation in vitro with abundance drastically reduced during tumor development, and both pCAFs and sCAFs were distinguishable in human breast cancer cohorts.

quotes.quote:
scRNA-seq in a 
mouse model of TNBC revealed two proinflammatory and two immunomodulatory CAF 
subpopulations within a subset of PDPN+ CAFs (pCAFs) compared to S100a4+ CAFs 
(sCAFs).

The immunomodulatory pCAFs in TNBC diverged into Ly6cLow and 
Ly6cHigh subpopulations, with the latter shown to inhibit T cell proliferation and activation 
in vitro and their relative abundance drastically reduced during tumor development

experiment.system: mouse model of triple-negative breast cancer and human breast cancer cohorts
experiment.perturbation: observational over tumor development; in vitro co-culture with T cells
experiment.measurement: scRNA-seq CAF subpopulation identification and T cell proliferation/activation assays

text: Single-cell analysis of the stromal compartment in human TNBC patients found high-inflammatory CAF signatures associated with T cell dysfunction and poor survival.

quotes.quote:
Single-cell analysis of the stromal compartment in human TNBC patients revealed that 
high-inflammatory CAF signatures are associated with T cell dysfunction and poor survival 
in TNBC 79

experiment.system: human TNBC patient tumors
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: single-cell stromal profiling correlated with T cell dysfunction and patient survival

text: In human breast cancer, four CAF subsets (CAF-S1-S4) were defined by CD29, FAP, FSP1, αSMA, PDGFRβ and CAV1 expression, with CAF-S1 recruiting CD4+CD25+ T cells through CXCL12 and promoting Treg differentiation; subsequent scRNA-seq of CAF-S1 highlighted eight subpopulations, three resembling PDAC iCAFs and enriched in TNBC versus luminal breast cancer, which was more enriched in myCAFs.

quotes.quote:
A separate study identified four CAF subsets (CAF-S1-S4, based on expression of CD29, 
FAP, FSP1, αSMA, PDGFRβ, and CAV1) in human breast cancer, of which CAF-S1 
demonstrated immunomodulatory activities including recruitment of CD4+CD25+ T cells 
through CXCL12 and promotion of Treg differentiation 26. Subsequent scRNA-seq analysis 
conducted on the CAF-S1 subset highlighted eight subpopulations, three of which resembled 
the iCAFs discovered in PDAC

The three iCAF-like subsets were enriched in patients with TNBC compared to luminal 
breast cancer, which were more enriched in myCAFs

experiment.system: human breast cancer tumors
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: marker-based FACS subset definition, scRNA-seq subpopulation analysis, T cell recruitment and Treg differentiation assays

numbers.quantity: CAF subsets in human breast cancer

text: In mesenchymal high-grade serous ovarian cancer, FACS-isolated CAF-S1 cells marked by high CD29, FAP and FSP1 were associated with immunosuppression by increasing attraction, survival and differentiation of CD25+FOXP3+ T lymphocytes via CXCL12β expression, and with worse prognosis.

quotes.quote:
The CAF-S1 subset, marked by high expression of CD29, FAP, and FSP1, was associated 
with immunosuppressive functions by increasing attraction, survival, and differentiation of 
CD25+FOXP3+ T lymphocytes, via its expression of CXCL12β and was associated with 
worse prognosis

experiment.system: patients with mesenchymal high-grade serous ovarian cancer
experiment.perturbation: observational; FACS isolation of CAF subsets
experiment.measurement: T lymphocyte attraction/survival/differentiation assays and prognosis association

text: scRNA-seq of human ICC identified 6 CAF subpopulations, the major subset being CD146+ vascular CAFs expressing IL-6 and CCL8; ligand-receptor analysis indicated vCAFs may interact with carcinoma cells via IL-6/IL-6R, promoting tumor growth and stemness, and CD146+ vCAFs localized mainly to the tumor core and microvasculature.

quotes.quote:
6 CAF 
subpopulations were reported in human ICC54. The major subset among them were CD146+ 
vascular CAFs (vCAFs), expressing inflammatory mediators such as IL-6 and CCL8

IHC and multiplex immunofluorescence staining revealed that CD146+ vCAFs 
mainly localized to the tumor core and microvasculature

experiment.system: human intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma samples
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: scRNA-seq with ligand-receptor interaction analysis, IHC and multiplex immunofluorescence

text: scRNA-seq combined with ligand-receptor analysis in a mouse model of ICC demonstrated that the HGF-MET signaling axis promotes tumor growth, with HGF expressed in inflammatory CAFs and scar-associated macrophages and MET in cancer cells in patient ICC and liver metastases.

quotes.quote:
scRNA-seq combined with ligand-receptor analysis in a mouse model of ICC demonstrated 
that the HGF-MET signaling axis promotes tumor growth and may also be relevant in 
patients 89

single-cell combined with spatial analysis 
of patient samples with ICC and liver metastases demonstrated that HGF is expressed in 
both CAFs and SAMs and may interact with cancer cells expressing MET

verdict_note: Claim text matches the paper, but the experiment field asserts 'HGF-MET axis manipulation in mouse model'; the excerpt describes only scRNA-seq combined with ligand-receptor (and spatial) analysis, with no perturbation of the axis reported.

experiment.system: mouse model of ICC and human ICC/liver metastasis samples
experiment.perturbation: observational; HGF-MET axis manipulation in mouse model
experiment.measurement: scRNA-seq with ligand-receptor and spatial analysis; tumor growth

text: apCAFs expressing MHC class II related genes were described in the mouse KPC model and human PDAC and were capable of partially activating CD4+ T cells in vitro by TCR ligation in an antigen-dependent manner, but expressed low levels of the co-stimulatory molecules CD80, CD86 and CD40; they could convert into myCAFs under certain culture conditions.

quotes.quote:
These cells, termed apCAFs, were capable of partially activating CD4+ T cells in vitro 
by TCR ligation in an antigen-dependent manner. However, they expressed low levels of 
the CD80, CD86 and CD40 co-stimulatory molecules required for full T cell activation.

they were able to convert into myCAFs under 
certain culture conditions 44.

experiment.system: mouse KPC model and human PDAC tumors; in vitro CAF-T cell cultures
experiment.perturbation: TCR ligation/antigen exposure; altered culture conditions
experiment.measurement: scRNA-seq, RNA in situ hybridization, IHC, imaging mass cytometry; CD4+ T cell activation

text: Reanalysis of published scRNA-seq datasets indicated apCAFs may originate from mesothelial cells through IL-1- and TGFβ-induced down-regulation of mesothelial features and upregulation of fibroblastic ones, consistent with a separate analysis reporting transcriptional similarity and clustering of apCAFs with mesothelial cells.

quotes.quote:
recent study reanalyzing published scRNA-seq datasets indicated that apCAFs may originate 
from mesothelial cells through the IL-1- and TGFβ-induced down-regulation of mesothelial 
features and upregulation of fibroblastic ones 11.

experiment.system: published PDAC scRNA-seq datasets (mouse models)
experiment.perturbation: IL-1 and TGFβ signaling
experiment.measurement: reanalysis of transcriptional clustering of mesothelial and apCAF signatures

text: In a mouse TNBC model, apCAFs were a subset of the S100A4+ sCAF population appearing predominantly at advanced stages of tumor progression and metastases, and a high ratio of sCAFs to PDPN+ pCAFs correlated with BRCA mutations and improved disease outcome in breast cancer patients.

quotes.quote:
A high 
ratio of sCAFs to the other dominant CAF population, PDPN+ pCAFs, correlated with 
BRCA mutations in the cancer cells and with improved disease outcome in patients with 
breast cancer

Temporal analysis of 
CAFs during different stages of tumor progression demonstrated that apCAFs appeared 
predominantly at advanced stages of tumor progression and metastases 13.

experiment.system: mouse model of triple-negative breast cancer and human breast cancer patients
experiment.perturbation: observational across tumor progression stages
experiment.measurement: scRNA-seq CAF subset ratios correlated with BRCA mutation status and outcome

text: scRNA-seq of PDAC patient tissues with different degrees of desmoplasia identified metabolic CAFs (meCAFs), predominant in loose-type (low desmoplasia) PDAC and using glycolysis as a major metabolic mode; patients with abundant meCAFs had a higher risk of metastasis but better response to PD-1 blockade.

quotes.quote:
scRNA-seq in tissues from PDAC patients with different degrees of desmoplasia identified 
a novel subtype of CAFs with a highly activated metabolic state, termed metabolic CAFs 
(meCAFs), which were found predominantly in loose-type (low desmoplasia) PDAC and 
utilized glycolysis as a major metabolic mode.

Although PDAC patients with abundant meCAFs had a higher 
risk of metastasis, they had a better immunotherapy response when treated with PD-1 
blockade46.

experiment.system: human PDAC tissues with varying desmoplasia
experiment.perturbation: observational; PD-1 blockade treatment in patients
experiment.measurement: scRNA-seq, multiplex immunofluorescence of PLA2G2A+ meCAFs, metastasis risk and immunotherapy response

text: scRNA-seq in the MMTV-PyMT mouse model identified CD63+ CAFs predominantly at advanced breast carcinoma stages that promote tamoxifen resistance by secreting exosomal miR-22 to downregulate ERα and PTEN; co-culture of human CD63+ CAFs with ERα+ breast cancer cells conferred tamoxifen resistance, and an anti-CD63 neutralizing antibody enhanced tamoxifen sensitivity in tumor-bearing mice.

quotes.quote:
This subset promoted breast cancer 
resistance to tamoxifen by secreting exosomal miR-22 thereby downregulating estrogen 
receptor-α (ERα) and PTEN in cancer cells.

Co-culture of human primary breast CD63+ CAFs 
with ERα+ human breast cancer cells endowed tamoxifen resistance, and treatment with 
an anti-CD63 neutralizing antibody enhanced tamoxifen sensitivity in breast tumor-bearing 
mice 94.

experiment.system: MMTV-PyMT mouse breast carcinoma, human primary breast CAF/cancer cell co-cultures, tumor-bearing mice
experiment.perturbation: CD63+ CAF co-culture; anti-CD63 neutralizing antibody with tamoxifen
experiment.measurement: scRNA-seq subset identification, ERα/PTEN expression, tamoxifen sensitivity

text: scRNA-seq of mouse intestinal mesenchyme identified PdgfrαLow fibroblasts with high Ptgs2 (COX2) expression, termed rare pericryptal Ptgs2-expressing fibroblasts, near the crypt stem cell zone; genetic ablation of Ptgs2 in fibroblasts was sufficient to prevent tumor initiation in the ApcMin/+ and azoxymethane models of intestinal cancer.

quotes.quote:
scRNA-seq analysis of the mouse intestinal mesenchyme unveiled a subset of PdgfrαLow 
fibroblasts expressing high levels of Ptgs2 (COX2) 95.

Genetic ablation of Ptgs2 in fibroblasts was sufficient to prevent tumor initiation in 
the ApcMin/+ and azoxymethane models of intestinal cancer.

experiment.system: mouse intestinal mesenchyme; ApcMin/+ and azoxymethane intestinal cancer models
experiment.perturbation: fibroblast-specific genetic ablation of Ptgs2
experiment.measurement: scRNA-seq identification and tumor initiation

text: scRNA-seq of normal murine colon revealed crypt-bottom fibroblasts (CBFs) defined by low PDGFRα and high CD34 and CD90, which maintained intestinal stem cell proliferation through canonical Wnt ligands (Wnt2, Wnt2b), Wnt potentiators (Rspo3) and Bmp antagonists (Grem1).

quotes.quote:
An additional scRNA-seq study on normal murine colon also revealed a subset 
of crypt-bottom fibroblasts (CBFs) defined by low PDGFRα and high CD34 and CD90 
expression 96. CBFs maintained intestinal stem cell proliferation through expression of 
canonical Wnt ligands (Wnt2 and Wnt2b), Wnt signaling potentiators (Rspo3), and Bmp 
antagonists (Grem1) 96.

experiment.system: normal murine colon
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: scRNA-seq marker definition and intestinal stem cell proliferation

text: Across breast cancer subtypes, luminal A tumors contained a larger CAF-S2 subpopulation, HER2+ tumors accumulated CAF-S4, and TNBC tumors were enriched in either CAF-S1 or S4.

quotes.quote:
Breast cancer luminal A tumors were found to contain a larger CAF-S2 
subpopulation, HER2+ tumors promoted accumulation of CAF-S4, and TNBC tumors 
were enriched in either CAF-S1 or S426.

experiment.system: human breast cancer tumors of different molecular subtypes
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: CAF subset composition by marker-based classification

text: A cross-tissue analysis of fibroblasts from normal and perturbed disease states in human and mouse suggested universal fibroblast states exist in normal tissues serving as reservoirs yielding specialized activated fibroblasts in disease, with two universal populations marked by Pi16+ and Col15a1+ identified using scRNA-seq with pseudotime inference; both universal and specialized subtypes were similar between human and mouse.

quotes.quote:
A recent cross-
tissue analysis of fibroblasts from normal and perturbed disease states in human and mouse 
suggested that universal fibroblast states exist in normal tissues, serving as reservoirs 
that yield specialized and activated fibroblasts in disease 97. Both the universal and the 
specialized CAF subtypes were similar between human and mouse.

scRNA-seq in conjunction with pseudotime inference was used to 
identify two possible universal fibroblast populations marked by Pi16+ and Col15a1+ 97.

experiment.system: fibroblasts across tissues from normal and perturbed disease states in human and mouse
experiment.perturbation: disease/perturbed tissue states versus normal
experiment.measurement: cross-tissue scRNA-seq with pseudotime inference of fibroblast states

text: scRNA-seq of a syngeneic transplantable TNBC mouse model identified two distinct ECM-remodeling/wound-healing CAF states marked by Fbn1 and Mfap5 or Acta2 and Thbs2, both derived from the PDPN+ pCAF population, which dominated the pCAF population at advanced tumor stages.

quotes.quote:
In a syngeneic mouse model of transplantable triple-negative 
breast cancer (TNBC), ECM remodeling or wound healing signatures were identified in two 
distinct CAF states, marked by Fbn1 and Mfap5 or Acta2 and Thbs2, respectively 13.

At advanced tumor stages, the two myofibroblastic 
subsets dominated the pCAF population 13.

experiment.system: syngeneic transplantable mouse TNBC model
experiment.perturbation: observational across tumor stages
experiment.measurement: scRNA-seq CAF state identification and subset abundance

text: scRNA-seq of human postmenopausal breast tissue identified two collagen-expressing fibroblast subsets whose gene signatures significantly overlapped with a gene profile exclusively associated with luminal breast tumors among 1,100 breast tumors in TCGA.

quotes.quote:
A comparison between the gene signatures of 
postmenopausal fibroblast subsets and the gene expression profiles of 1,100 breast tumors 
in The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) dataset revealed significant overlap with a gene 
profile exclusively associated with luminal breast tumors

experiment.system: human postmenopausal breast tissue and TCGA breast tumor expression profiles
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: scRNA-seq fibroblast subset signatures compared to bulk tumor expression profiles

text: scRNA-seq of human urothelial bladder carcinoma identified mCAFs similar to PDAC myCAFs and marked by RGS5, whose accumulation in tumors correlated with poor patient survival.

quotes.quote:
A study of human urothelial bladder carcinoma 58 
identified a subset of CAFs termed mCAFs, with similar characteristics to the myCAFs

Accumulation of mCAFs in the 
tumor correlated with poor patient survival 58.

experiment.system: human urothelial bladder carcinoma
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: scRNA-seq CAF subset identification and survival correlation

text: Single-cell analysis of subsolid nodules from patients with early-stage lung adenocarcinoma revealed enrichment of immunomodulatory fibroblasts characterized by TNF and IL-6-JAK/STAT signaling and enriched for CXCL12/14, which decrease in lung adenocarcinoma and metastases.

quotes.quote:
Single-cell analysis of subsolid nodules (SSN) from patients with early-stage 
lung adenocarcinoma revealed enrichment of immunomodulatory fibroblasts, characterized 
by TNF and IL-6-JAK/STAT signaling and enriched for CXCL12/14, which decrease in 
lung adenocarcinoma and metastases 84.

experiment.system: human pulmonary subsolid nodules, lung adenocarcinoma and metastases
experiment.perturbation: observational across lesion stages
experiment.measurement: scRNA-seq fibroblast subpopulation abundance and pathway enrichment

text: A study using published lung scRNA-seq data and a metric for physiologically relevant MHC class II gene expression defined a population of potential apCAFs in human lung cancer and in mice, with dense apCAF regions in human lung tumors defining immunologically active regions with increased CD4+ T cell infiltration and alveolar epithelial cells proposed as their origin.

quotes.quote:
A recent study 
suggested that dense apCAF regions in human lung tumors define immunologically active 
regions with increased CD4+ T cell infiltration 91. Leveraging published scRNA-seq data 37 
and a defined metric for assessing physiologically relevant MHC class II gene expression, 
this study defined a population of potential apCAFs in human lung cancer and in mice, and 
proposed alveolar epithelial cells as their potential origin.

experiment.system: human lung tumors and mouse lung tumor models
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: published scRNA-seq reanalysis with MHC class II expression metric and spatial CD4+ T cell infiltration

text: scRNA-seq of a MMTV-PyMT mouse breast cancer model revealed a CAF subpopulation enriched for angiogenic genes and associated with blood vessels, designated vascular CAFs (vCAFs), and mCAFs in this model were most abundant in the invasive part of tumors within collagen-rich streaks.

quotes.quote:
scRNA-seq of CAFs from the MMTV-PyMT transgenic mouse model of breast cancer 
revealed a subpopulation enriched for expression of angiogenic genes, which was associated 
with blood vessels and designated vascular CAFs (vCAFs) 30.

The spatial location of mCAFs was linked to their function as they were most abundant in 
the invasive part of the tumors, particularly within collagen-rich streaks.

experiment.system: MMTV-PyMT transgenic mouse breast tumors
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: scRNA-seq subpopulation identification with spatial localization

text: scRNA-seq of human intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma identified matrix CAFs (mCAFs) expressing low ACTA2 but high ECM genes including collagens, POSTN, FN1, LUM, DCN and VCAN, located in the invasive front of the tumor predominantly within collagen-rich streaks.

quotes.quote:
identified a subpopulation designated as 
matrix CAFs (mCAFs), expressing low levels of ACTA2 but high levels of ECM-associated 
genes including various collagens, POSTN, FN1, LUM, DCN and VCAN.

these POSTN+ mCAFs were found in the invasive front 
of the tumor, predominantly within collagen-rich streaks, suggesting a close association with 
tumor invasiveness

experiment.system: human intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma tissue
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: scRNA-seq subpopulation gene expression and spatial localization

text: scRNA-seq of human ovarian tumors identified TGFβ-CAFs resembling a combination of the myCAF and TGFβ-driven CAF subsets described in PDAC, with markers including POSTN, ACTA2, MMP11, TAGLN and FN1; in a separate study of serous ovarian cancer, collagens and MMP-associated genes were upregulated in primary and metastatic tumor fibroblasts compared to normal.

quotes.quote:
High-resolution scRNA-seq dissection of human ovarian tumors revealed a subset of CAFs, 
annotated as TGFβ-CAFs, which resembled a combination of the myCAF and TGFβ-driven 
CAF subsets described in PDAC

Collagens and 
MMP-associated genes were upregulated in the primary and metastatic tumor fibroblasts 
when compared to normal

experiment.system: human ovarian tumors, including primary tumors, metastatic omentum and normal ovary
experiment.perturbation: observational (tumor versus normal comparison)
experiment.measurement: scRNA-seq subpopulation identification and differential gene expression

text: Single-cell analysis of fibroblasts from murine skin wound healing, human fibrotic skin, murine lung and liver fibrosis identified activated myofibroblast states with pro-fibrogenic signatures reminiscent of myofibroblastic CAFs, but did not identify distinct inflammatory/immune-regulatory fibroblast subpopulations, whereas colonic fibroblasts from ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease patients contained both inflammatory fibroblasts and myofibroblasts.

quotes.quote:
Contrary to CAFs, these wound healing and fibrosis studies did not identify 
distinct subpopulations of inflammatory/immune-regulatory fibroblasts.

or from the ileal biopsies of patients with Crohn’s disease67 identified both inflammatory 
fibroblasts and myofibroblasts.

experiment.system: murine skin wounds, human fibrotic skin, murine lung and liver fibrosis, and colon/ileum of ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease patients
experiment.perturbation: injury/fibrosis/inflammatory disease versus healthy tissue
experiment.measurement: single-cell RNA-seq fibroblast subpopulation identification

text: scRNA-seq of stromal cells in healthy and myocardial infarct-injured mouse hearts revealed normal fibroblasts characterized by PDGFRα and Ly6a (Sca1), activated fibroblasts in injured tissue upregulating fibrogenic and/or contractile proteins similarly to myofibroblastic CAFs, and an F-Wntx subpopulation expressing Wnt signaling inhibitors with an anti-fibrotic phenotype.

quotes.quote:
Normal fibroblasts were 
characterized by PDGFRα and Ly6a (Sca1) expression, whereas activated fibroblasts in 
injured heart tissue upregulated fibrogenic (e.g. POSTN, collagens) and/or contractile 
proteins (e.g. aSMA), similarly to myofibroblastic CAFs.

a subpopulation of fibroblasts termed F-Wntx in both normal and myocardial infarction-
associated tissue, which expressed Wnt signaling inhibitors and had an anti-fibrotic 
phenotype

experiment.system: healthy and myocardial infarct-injured mouse hearts
experiment.perturbation: myocardial infarction injury
experiment.measurement: scRNA-seq of stromal fibroblast subpopulations and marker expression

text: scRNA-seq of human prostate tumors revealed two distinct CAF clusters, myofibroblastic and ECM-associated, with the ECM-associated subpopulation enriched for transcription factors CREB3L1 and PLAGL1 and the myofibroblastic subpopulation increased for HOXB2 and MAFB; in mouse prostate stroma, Sca-1+CD90Low fibroblasts expressed Fn1 plus cytokines, chemokines and complement components (Ccl2, Ccl7, Ccl11, Cxcl1, Cxcl2, C3).

quotes.quote:
Analysis of 
human prostate tumors unveiled two distinct clusters representing either myofibroblastic or 
ECM-associated phenotypes, which was supported by enrichment in the ECM-associated 
subpopulation of CREB3L1 and PLAGL1, transcription factors known to control ECM 
production and composition, compared to increase of HOXB2 and MAFB in the 
myofibroblastic subpopulation 39.

A study of 
mouse prostate stromal cells found that Sca-1+CD90Low fibroblasts express ECM-related 
genes such as Fn1 but also cytokines, chemokines and complement components (Ccl2, 
Ccl7, Ccl11, Cxcl1, Cxcl2, and C3) 85

experiment.system: human prostate tumors and mouse prostate stromal cells
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: scRNA-seq cluster identification and marker/transcription factor enrichment

text: In gastric cancer, scRNA-seq demonstrated a stage-dependent increase in three CAF subsets within a stromal meta-cluster, two expressing myofibroblastic genes such as ACTA2 and TAGLN and one inducing collagen-associated genes correlated with INHBA signaling.

quotes.quote:
In gastric cancer, 
a stage dependent increase in three CAF subsets belonging to a stromal meta-cluster 
with endothelial cells and pericytes was demonstrated: two subsets exhibited expression 
of myofibroblastic genes such as ACTA2 and TAGLN, whereas a specific cluster induced 
expression of collagen associated genes that were correlated with INHBA signaling 59

experiment.system: human gastric cancer
experiment.perturbation: observational across disease stages
experiment.measurement: single-cell atlas of CAF subsets and gene program correlation

text: In HeLa cells with five autophagy receptors knocked out (pentaKO), COXII degradation after mitochondrial damage was blocked, as it was in ATG5 knockout cells, whereas COXII was degraded in wild-type cells expressing parkin.

quotes.quote:
After oligomycin and
antimycin A treatment, COXII was degraded in wild-type cells
expressing parkin, but not in pentaKOs or ATG5 knockout HeLa
cells, indicating a block in mitophagy (Fig. 1b, c, Supplementary
Table 1 and Extended Data Fig. 1a).

experiment.system: HeLa cells (wild-type, pentaKO, ATG5 KO) expressing mCherry-parkin
experiment.perturbation: genome-editing knockout of five autophagy receptors; oligomycin/antimycin A treatment
experiment.measurement: immunoblot quantification of COXII levels

text: After 24 h of oligomycin/antimycin A, wild-type cells were nearly devoid of mtDNA whereas mtDNA was retained in pentaKOs and ATG5 knockouts.

quotes.quote:
After 24 h of oligomycin/antimycin A treat-
ment, wild-type cells were nearly devoid of mtDNA, whereas mtDNA
was retained in pentaKOs and ATG5 knockouts (Fig. 1d, e).

experiment.system: mCherry-parkin-expressing wild-type, pentaKO and ATG5 knockout HeLa cells
experiment.perturbation: 24 h oligomycin/antimycin A
experiment.measurement: immunofluorescence quantification of mtDNA nucleoid stain remaining

text: Parkin translocation to mitochondria and proteasomal degradation of MFN1 and TOM20 were comparable in wild-type and pentaKO cells.

quotes.quote:
Parkin
translocated to mitochondria (Extended Data Fig. 1c), and MFN1 and
TOM20 (also known as TOMM20) were degraded via the proteasome
comparably in wild-type and pentaKOs

experiment.system: wild-type and pentaKO HeLa cells expressing mCherry-parkin
experiment.perturbation: oligomycin/antimycin A (with or without MG132)
experiment.measurement: immunoblotting of MFN1/TOM20 and imaging of parkin translocation

text: All five receptors translocated to mitochondria after damage, but in pentaKOs only GFP-NDP52, GFP-OPTN and, to a lesser extent, GFP-TAX1BP1 rescued mitophagy; TOLLIP neither recruited nor rescued.

quotes.quote:
However, in pentaKOs, only green fluorescent protein
(GFP)-tagged NDP52, GFP–OPTN and, to a lesser extent, GFP–
TAX1BP1 rescued mitophagy (Fig. 1f, g).

TOLLIP12, neither recruited to mitochondria nor
rescued
mitophagy
after
oligomycin/antimycin
A
treatment

experiment.system: pentaKO HeLa cells expressing mCherry-parkin and individual GFP-tagged receptors
experiment.perturbation: re-expression of each receptor; oligomycin/antimycin A
experiment.measurement: COXII immunoblot quantification and mitochondrial translocation imaging

text: NDP52 or OPTN single knockout caused no mitophagy defect, whereas NDP52/OPTN double knockout, and to a greater extent NDP52/OPTN/TAX1BP1 triple knockout, inhibited mitophagy, with no compensatory expression change in remaining receptors.

quotes.quote:
NDP52 or OPTN knockout alone caused no defect in mitophagy,
whereas the NDP52/OPTN DKO and to a greater extent the
NDP52/OPTN/TAX1BP1 triple knockout inhibited mitophagy
(Fig. 2a–d and Extended Data Fig. 2a, b).

experiment.system: OPTN KO, NDP52 KO, NDP52/OPTN DKO and NDP52/OPTN/TAX1BP1 TKO HeLa cells expressing mCherry-parkin
experiment.perturbation: gene knockout; oligomycin/antimycin A
experiment.measurement: COXII immunoblot and mtDNA stain quantification

text: In pentaKOs, UBAN-disrupting OPTN mutants Q398X, D474N and E478G failed to translocate to mitochondria or rescue mitophagy; OPTN(S177A) weakly rescued while OPTN(E50K) robustly translocated and substantially rescued.

quotes.quote:
In pentaKOs, the UBAN domain-disrupting mutants
OPTN (Q398X), OPTN(D474N) and OPTN(E478G) (Extended
Data Fig. 2d) failed to translocate to mitochondria (Extended Data
Fig. 2e, f) or rescue mitophagy (Fig. 2e and Extended Data Fig. 2g).
OPTN(S177A) weakly rescued mitophagy and minimally translo-
cated to mitochondria, whereas OPTN(E50K) robustly translocated
and substantially rescued mitophagy

experiment.system: pentaKO HeLa cells expressing mCherry-parkin and mutant GFP-OPTN
experiment.perturbation: expression of OPTN disease/domain mutants; oligomycin/antimycin A
experiment.measurement: COXII quantification and mitochondrial translocation imaging

text: NDP52(V248A) fully recruited to mitochondria and rescued mitophagy, whereas NDP52 lacking its zinc-finger ubiquitin-binding domains did not.

quotes.quote:
NDP52(V248A) fully recruited to mitochondria and
rescued mitophagy, but a mutant lacking the zinc-finger ubiquitin-
binding domains (NDP52(DZF))18 did not

experiment.system: pentaKO HeLa cells expressing mCherry-parkin and mutant GFP-NDP52
experiment.perturbation: expression of NDP52 V248A or ΔZF; oligomycin/antimycin A
experiment.measurement: COXII quantification and translocation imaging

text: TBK1 auto-phosphorylation at Ser172 occurred in a parkin-dependent manner after 3 h of oligomycin/antimycin A only in cells expressing OPTN; prolonged treatment induced moderate TBK1 phosphorylation without parkin but still requiring PINK1.

quotes.quote:
TBK1 auto-phosphorylation
at Ser172 is indicative of TBK1 activation20 and occurs in a parkin-
dependent manner after 3 h of oligomycin/antimycin A treatment,
but only in cells expressing OPTN (Extended Data Fig. 3b, lanes 4 and
10). Prolonged oligomycin and antimycin A treatment induces mod-
erate TBK1 phosphorylation in the absence of parkin, but still requires
PINK1

experiment.system: wild-type, receptor-knockout and PINK1 knockout HeLa cells ± mCherry-parkin
experiment.perturbation: oligomycin/antimycin A treatment
experiment.measurement: immunoblot for pTBK1(S172)

text: Among TBK1 knockout, TBK1/OPTN DKO and TBK1/NDP52 DKO cells, only TBK1/NDP52 DKOs displayed defective mitophagy; this defect was rescued by wild-type TBK1 or OPTN(S177D) but not by kinase-dead TBK1(K38M).

quotes.quote:
Parkin translocated to mitochondria in all
cell lines, however, only TBK1/NDP52 DKOs displayed defective
mitophagy (Extended Data Fig. 3e and Fig. 2g–j). Mitophagy in
TBK1/NDP52 DKOs was rescued by wild-type TBK1 or phospho-
mimetic OPTN (OPTN(S177D)), but not by kinase-dead TBK1
(TBK1(K38M); Extended Data Fig. 3g–i).

experiment.system: TBK1 KO, TBK1/OPTN DKO and TBK1/NDP52 DKO HeLa cells expressing mCherry-parkin
experiment.perturbation: knockout plus rescue constructs; oligomycin/antimycin A
experiment.measurement: COXII immunoblot and mtDNA stain quantification

text: Rapalog-induced targeting of PINK1 to undamaged mitochondria in parkin-free HeLa cells recruited mCherry-OPTN and mCherry-NDP52, but not p62; recruitment required PINK1 kinase activity and receptor ubiquitin binding, as OPTN(D474N) and NDP52(ΔZF) failed to recruit.

quotes.quote:
This recruits OPTN and NDP52 to mito-
chondria (Fig. 3a, b), but not p62 (Fig. 3b and Extended Data Fig. 4c).
OPTN and NDP52 recruitment requires PINK1 kinase activity
(Fig. 3a, b) and receptor–ubiquitin binding, as the OPTN(D474N)
and NDP52(DZF) mutants fail to recruit after rapalog treatment

experiment.system: HeLa cells lacking parkin expressing FRB-Fis1, PINK1Δ110–YFP–2xFKBP (WT or kinase-dead) and mCherry-tagged receptors
experiment.perturbation: rapalog-induced chemical targeting of PINK1 to mitochondria; kinase-dead and ubiquitin-binding mutants
experiment.measurement: microscopy counting of cells with mitochondrial receptor localization

text: In the mt-mKeima FACS assay, only 1% (range 0.89–1.15) of wild-type or pentaKO cells showed mitophagy with cytosolic PINK1; rapalog recruitment of PINK1 to mitochondria increased mitophagy ~sevenfold in wild-type cells and ~eightfold with overexpressed OPTN, while pentaKO cells showed no increase.

quotes.quote:
Only 1% (range 0.89–1.15) of wild-type or
pentaKO cells display mitophagy when PINK1 is cytosolic. However,
when PINK1 is recruited to mitochondria with rapalog, mitophagy
increases ,sevenfold in wild-type cells and ,eightfold with overex-
pressed OPTN (Table 1 and Extended Data Fig. 5a). PentaKO cells
showed no increase in mitophagy after targeting PINK1 to mitochon-
dria

experiment.system: wild-type and pentaKO HeLa cells expressing mt-mKeima, FRB-Fis1 and PINK1Δ110–YFP–2xFKBP
experiment.perturbation: rapalog-induced PINK1 mitochondrial targeting; OPTN overexpression
experiment.measurement: FACS ratiometric mt-mKeima lysosomal-positive percentage

text: Rescue of pentaKOs with Flag/HA-OPTN or Flag/HA-NDP52 increased rapalog-induced mitophagy more than fivefold or fourfold respectively, whereas p62 or ubiquitin-binding mutants (OPTN(Q398X), OPTN(D474N), NDP52(ΔZF)) failed to increase mitophagy above baseline; OPTN(E50K), OPTN(S177A) and NDP52(V248A) rescued.

quotes.quote:
When rescued with Flag/
haemagglutinin (HA)-tagged OPTN or NDP52, pentaKOs displayed
an increase in mitophagy of more than fivefold or fourfold, respect-
ively (Table 1 and Extended Data Fig. 5b–e). Rescue with Flag/HA–
p62 or ubiquitin-binding mutants (OPTN(Q398X), OPTN(D474N)
and NDP52 (DZF)) failed to increase mitophagy above baseline, but

other mutants (OPTN(E50K), OPTN(S177A) and NDP52(V248A))
rescued mitophagy (Table 1 and Extended Data Fig. 5c–f).

experiment.system: pentaKO HeLa cells expressing FRB-Fis1, PINK1Δ110–YFP–2xFKBP, mt-mKeima and Flag/HA-tagged receptors
experiment.perturbation: receptor rescue (wild-type and mutants); rapalog treatment
experiment.measurement: FACS mt-mKeima mitophagy percentage and fold change

text: Humans have 58 known RTKs, which fall into twenty subfamilies, all sharing a similar architecture with an extracellular ligand-binding region, a single transmembrane helix, and a cytoplasmic tyrosine kinase domain plus C-terminal and juxtamembrane regulatory regions.

quotes.quote:
Humans have 58 known RTKs, which fall into twenty
subfamilies (Figure 1). All RTKs have a similar molecular architecture, with a ligand-
binding region in the extracellular domain, a single transmembrane helix, and a cytoplasmic
region that contains the protein tyrosine kinase (TK) domain plus additional carboxy (C-)
terminal and juxtamembrane regulatory regions.

experiment.system: human proteome RTK complement
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: sequence/structure-based classification of receptors into subfamilies and domain architectures

text: In the NGF-induced TrkA dimer, the extracellular regions of the two TrkA molecules do not contact one another; only each Ig-C2 domain contacts the dimeric NGF ligand, so the ligand provides the entire dimer interface — with the authors' caveat that a 30 amino acid juxtamembrane region is missing from the most complete TrkA structure.

quotes.quote:
In the
NGF-induced dimer, the extracellular regions of the two TrkA molecules do not contact one
another. Only the Ig-C2 domain of each receptor molecule contacts the dimeric NGF ligand

with the caveat that a 30 amino acid juxtamembrane region is missing from the most
complete TrkA structure (Wehrman et al., 2007).

experiment.system: TrkA extracellular region in complex with NGF
experiment.perturbation: NGF binding (crystallized complex)
experiment.measurement: X-ray crystal structure of the dimer interface

numbers.quantity: juxtamembrane region missing from TrkA structure

text: SCF binds KIT through the first three of five Ig-like domains, which are structurally unaltered on ligand binding, while D4 and D5 reorient upon dimerization and make homotypic contacts across the dimer interface; oncogenic gain-of-function mutations map to D5 and are thought to stabilize these activating interactions.

quotes.quote:
Each
SCF molecule binds to one molecule of KIT through contacts with the first three (of five)
Ig-like domains in the KIT extracellular region

the two Ig-like domains closest to
the plasma membrane (D4 and D5) undergo a significant reorientation upon KIT
dimerization (Yuzawa et al., 2007). D4 and D5 make important homotypic interactions
across the dimer interface (Figure 2B), which properly orient the two KIT molecules for
activation. Oncogenic gain-of-function mutations are found in the D5 domain of KIT and
are thought to stabilize these activating interactions.

experiment.system: KIT extracellular region with stem cell factor
experiment.perturbation: SCF binding; comparison of liganded and unliganded receptor
experiment.measurement: X-ray crystallographic domain positions and dimer interface contacts

text: An X-ray structure of a 2:2:2 complex of FGFR1c extracellular region, FGF2 and heparin showed each receptor contacting both FGF and heparin, each FGF contacting both receptors, and direct D2–D2 receptor-receptor contacts, so receptor-ligand, receptor-heparin, ligand-heparin and receptor-receptor interactions all cooperate to stabilize the dimer.

quotes.quote:
An X-ray crystal structure of a dimeric complex containing the
FGFR1c extracellular region, FGF2, and heparin in a 2:2:2 ratio (Schlessinger et al., 2000)
showed that each receptor molecule simultaneously contacts both FGF and heparin

Thus, receptor-ligand, receptor-heparin, ligand-heparin and receptor-
receptor interactions all cooperate to stabilize the FGFR dimer.

experiment.system: FGFR1c extracellular region with FGF2 and heparin
experiment.perturbation: co-crystallization of ternary complex
experiment.measurement: X-ray crystal structure and stoichiometry of the dimeric complex

text: FGFR ligand binding is autoinhibited intramolecularly: affinity of FGFRs for FGFs or HSPGs increases when either D1 or an 8-residue 'acid box' in the D1–D2 linker is removed, because D1 competes with the D2/D3 ligand-binding site and the acid box occupies the heparin-binding canyon.

quotes.quote:
The affinity of FGFRs for FGFs or HSPGs (heparan sulfate proteoglycans)
is increased when either D1 or an 8-residue ‘acid box’ in the D1–D2 linker (Figure 1) is
removed.

experiment.system: FGFR extracellular region
experiment.perturbation: deletion of D1 or of the 8-residue acid box
experiment.measurement: binding affinity for FGFs/HSPGs and structural analysis of intramolecular contacts

text: Structures of the EGFR extracellular region showed dimerization is entirely receptor-mediated: the bivalent ligand contacts two sites (Domains I and III) within a single receptor, driving conformational changes that unmask a Domain II dimerization arm otherwise buried by intramolecular contacts with Domain IV in a 'tethered' autoinhibited conformation.

quotes.quote:
Structures of the EGFR extracellular region revealed that dimerization is entirely ‘receptor-
mediated,’ as depicted in Figure 2D (Garrett et al., 2002; Ogiso et al., 2002).

Before ligand binds, this arm is
completely buried by intramolecular interactions with Domain IV that stabilize a ‘tethered’
conformation in which both ligand binding and dimerization are autoinhibited

experiment.system: EGFR/ErbB extracellular region
experiment.perturbation: comparison of ligand-bound and unliganded (tethered) receptor structures
experiment.measurement: X-ray crystal structures of ligand contacts and dimer interface

text: A structure of the insulin receptor TKD showed cis-autoinhibition by the activation loop, in which Y1162 projects into the active site and occludes access of both ATP and protein substrates; trans-phosphorylation of Y1162 by the partner kinase within the dimer disrupts this and allows the active configuration.

quotes.quote:
A key tyrosine (Y1162) in the activation loop of the insulin receptor TKD
projects into the active site as if poised to be autophosphorylated by its own kinase domain

When insulin activates the receptor, Y1162 in one TKD within the dimer becomes
phosphorylated by its partner (together with two additional tyrosines), and this trans-
phosphorylation disrupts the cis-autoinhibitory interactions.

experiment.system: insulin receptor tyrosine kinase domain
experiment.perturbation: insulin-induced activation / activation-loop autophosphorylation
experiment.measurement: crystal structures of autoinhibited and activated TKD

text: FGFR1 activation-loop tyrosines do not block the substrate site directly but make intramolecular contacts that cis-autoinhibit the kinase by occluding the protein-substrate binding site while leaving the ATP site accessible; trans-phosphorylation on FGF-induced dimerization relieves this.

quotes.quote:
Instead, they participate in a unique set of intramolecular contacts that stabilize the
inactive conformation of the kinase, in turn cis-autoinhibiting the FGFR1 TKD by occluding
the protein-substrate binding site but not the ATP binding site.

experiment.system: FGFR1 tyrosine kinase domain
experiment.perturbation: FGF-induced dimerization / activation-loop trans-phosphorylation
experiment.measurement: crystal structures of inactive and active kinase conformations

text: MuSK, Flt3, KIT and Eph family RTKs are cis-autoinhibited by juxtamembrane sequences that contact the TKD including the activation loop; mutations disrupting these juxtamembrane interactions in the KIT/PDGFR family constitutively activate the receptors and are frequently found in cancers.

quotes.quote:
The best known example is
‘juxtamembrane autoinhibition,’ exemplified by MuSK (Till et al., 2002), Flt3 (Griffith et
al., 2004), KIT (Mol et al., 2004) and Eph family RTKs (Wybenga-Groot et al., 2001).

Mutations that disrupt the
autoinhibitory juxtamembrane interactions in the KIT/PDGFR family constitutively activate
these RTKs and are frequently found in cancers

experiment.system: MuSK, Flt3, KIT, Eph receptor kinase domains and cancer-derived mutants
experiment.perturbation: juxtamembrane mutations; receptor dimerization/trans-phosphorylation
experiment.measurement: crystal structures of autoinhibited kinases and receptor activation state of mutants

text: The Tie2 kinase domain is cis-autoinhibited by a C-terminal tail region containing autophosphorylation sites that blocks substrate access to the active site, and its nucleotide-binding loop adopts an inactive configuration even though the activation loop is active-like without phosphorylation.

quotes.quote:
Although the activation loop of its TKD
exists in an active-like conformation even without phosphorylation (Shewchuk et al., 2000),
the nucleotide-binding loop of Tie2 adopts an inactive configuration. Moreover, a region in
the C-terminal tail that contains tyrosine autophosphorylation sites blocks substrate access to
the active site, representing a third form of reversible cis-autoinhibition

experiment.system: Tie2 tyrosine kinase domain
experiment.perturbation: C-terminal tail deletion / structural comparison
experiment.measurement: crystal structure and kinase activity

text: Crystallographic and mutational studies showed EGFR TKDs form an asymmetric dimer in which the C-lobe of an 'Activator' kinase contacts the N-lobe of a 'Receiver' kinase, disrupting cis-autoinhibitory interactions so the Receiver adopts the active configuration without activation loop phosphorylation; mutations in this interface in EGFR or ErbB4 impair activation of the intact receptors.

quotes.quote:
The EGFR TKD forms an
asymmetric dimer (Figure 2F) in which the C-lobe of one TKD, called the ‘Activator,’
makes intimate contacts with the N-lobe of the second TKD, called the ‘Receiver.’

mutations in the asymmetric TKD dimer interface of EGFR or
ErbB4 impair normal activation of the intact receptors (Qiu et al., 2008; Zhang et al., 2006).

experiment.system: EGFR and ErbB4 kinase domains and intact receptors
experiment.perturbation: mutation of the asymmetric dimer interface
experiment.measurement: crystal structures and receptor activation/kinase activity

text: The intracellular juxtamembrane region of EGFR promotes rather than inhibits activation: part of the Receiver kinase's juxtamembrane region 'cradles' the Activator C-lobe to promote dimerization and allosteric activation, and certain lung cancer mutations appear to activate EGFR by stabilizing these juxtamembrane interactions.

quotes.quote:
Part of the juxtamembrane region of the Receiver kinase
‘cradles’ the C-lobe of the Activator kinase in the dimer represented in Figure 2F. This
interaction promotes dimerization and thus, allosteric activation of the Receiver.

Certain mutations in
lung cancer appear to promote EGFR activation by stabilizing these juxtamembrane
interactions (Red Brewer et al., 2009).

experiment.system: EGFR kinase domain with juxtamembrane segment; lung cancer mutants
experiment.perturbation: juxtamembrane deletion/mutation
experiment.measurement: structural and biochemical analysis of dimerization and kinase activation

Autophosphorylation of the activation loop
in the insulin receptor TKD increases its catalytic efficiency by 50–200 fold (Cobb et al.,

text: In the insulin and IGF-1 receptor kinases the three activation loop sites are phosphorylated in a fixed order Y1162, Y1158, then Y1163 (insulin receptor numbering), with the first event causing the largest increase in Vmax, the second the largest drop in KM for substrates, and the third a modest effect on both.

quotes.quote:
the three sites in the activation
loop are phosphorylated in the same order: Y1162, Y1158, and then Y1163 (using insulin

The first phosphorylation event causes the largest increase in Vmax; the second event causes
the largest drop in KM for substrates (Favelyukis et al., 2001); and the third event has a
modest effect on both.

text: FGFR1 autophosphorylation proceeds in three phases: first-phase Y653 phosphorylation increases kinase activity by ~10–50 fold; second-phase sites are phosphorylated in the order Y583, Y463, Y585 to create docking sites; and third-phase Y654 phosphorylation elevates activity a further 10 fold to reach 100–500 times basal levels.

quotes.quote:
Studies with FGFR1 showed that autophosphorylation of Y653 in the
activation loop is the key autophosphorylation event during the first-phase, which increases
kinase activity by ~10–50 fold (Furdui et al., 2006).

Y583, which lies in an extra loop within
the TKD called the kinase insert, is trans-autophosphorylated first. Y463 in the
juxtamembrane region is phosphorylated next and is followed by Y585 in the kinase insert.

a further autophosphorylation event
occurs in the FGFR1 activation loop (at Y654) that elevates kinase activity an additional 10
fold (Furdui et al., 2006) to reach 100–500 times basal levels.

experiment.system: FGFR1 kinase domain in vitro
experiment.perturbation: time-resolved sequential autophosphorylation
experiment.measurement: order of site phosphorylation and fold-change in kinase activity

numbers.quantity: final FGFR1 activity relative to basal

text: A crystal structure of a PLCγ1 fragment containing both SH2 domains bound to the phosphorylated FGFR1 intracellular domain showed the N-terminal SH2 domain binds >15 times more strongly than the C-terminal SH2, with a KD of 33nM versus more than one micromolar for phosphopeptide binding, due to a secondary site contacting the FGFR1 kinase C-lobe that is crucial for FGFR1-mediated PLCγ1 activation in cells.

quotes.quote:
Although the two PLCγ1 SH2 domains bind with similar affinities to
phosphopeptides corresponding to FGFR1 pY766, the N-terminal SH2 domain binds >15
times more strongly than the C-terminal SH2 to phosphorylated FGFR1 intracellular domain
(Bae et al., 2009). The KD for PLCγ1 N-terminal SH2 domain binding to phosphorylated
FGFR1 intracellular domain is 33nM, compared with the more ‘normal’ KD value for its
binding to phosphopeptides of more than one micromolar.

the N-terminal
PLCγ1 SH2 domain uses a separate specificity-determining site that buries almost the same
surface area and is crucial for FGFR1-mediated PLCγ1 activation in cells.

experiment.perturbation: crystallography plus mutagenesis of the secondary binding site; comparison with phosphopeptide binding

Although the resulting network for EGFR (Jones et al., 2006), for example, contained many

simply overexpressing EGFR or the insulin

a map of the signaling network influenced by the EGFR node (Oda et al., 2005) contains 211

Sustained activation of EGFR is accompanied by
ligand-induced production of H2O2 and other reactive oxygen species (ROS), mediated by
PI-3 kinase and Rac dependent activation of NADPH-oxidase (Bae et al., 1997). These ROS
transiently inhibit PTP activity by oxidizing a crucial cysteine in the phosphatase active site
