PKC can phosphorylate
T654 in the juxtamembrane domain of EGFR (Figure 4A). This eliminates high affinity
binding of EGF to cell-surface EGFR (Ullrich and Schlessinger, 1990) and thus inhibits
EGFR activation in a negative feedback loop.

MAP kinase inactivates the EGFR itself, by phosphorylating T669 in the juxtamembrane
region (Li et al., 2008).

experiment.perturbation: EGFR stimulation activating PKC/MAPK; threonine phosphorylation of EGFR

text: MAPK negatively feeds back on its own upstream regulators: phosphorylation of Sos by MAPK impairs Sos/Grb2 interactions and reduces Sos membrane recruitment, dampening Ras activation, and MAPK phosphorylation of Raf reduces Raf kinase activity and diminishes MAPKK and MAPK phosphorylation; MAPK also phosphorylates Gab1, IRS1 and FRS2 docking proteins.

quotes.quote:
Direct phosphorylation of Sos by MAPK impairs Sos/Grb2 interactions and thus reduces
Sos recruitment to the membrane, in turn dampening Ras activation (Buday et al., 1995). In
addition, MAPK phosphorylates its upstream regulator Raf (Ueki et al., 1994), leading to a
reduction in Raf kinase activity

MAPK
activation leads to Gab1 phosphorylation, which diminishes the ability of Gab1 to recruit
and activate PI3K (Gual et al., 2001). The IRS1 and FRS2 docking proteins are also
phosphorylated by MAPK in similar negative feedback loops

experiment.perturbation: MAPK-dependent phosphorylation of Sos, Raf, Gab1, IRS1, FRS2
experiment.measurement: complex formation, Raf kinase activity, Ras/PI3K activation

text: Several signal attenuators were identified among 'delayed early gene' products induced by EGFR signaling with a delay of more than 40 minutes, including transcriptional repressors ID2, NAB2, FOSL1 and JUNB, KLF-2 and -6, the RNA-binding protein ZFP36, and several dual-specificity phosphatases.

Amit et al. (2007) identified several signal attenuators among the
group of ‘delayed early gene’ products induced by EGFR signaling with a delay of more
than 40 minutes. These included several known transcriptional repressors, including ID2,
NAB2, FOSL1, and JUNB, which attenuate EGF-driven transcription

quotes.quote:
The key difference is
additional positive feedback from MAPK to Raf when the system is activated by NGF, in
contrast with only negative feedback loops (Figure 4A) in EGF-treated cells.

it appears to involve PKCδ because combined treatment of cells
with EGF and a PKC Activator could mimic NGF-induced sustained MAPK activation (and
differentiation).

experiment.perturbation: NGF versus EGF stimulation; EGF plus PKC activator

text: NGF but not EGF promotes sustained Rap1 activation leading to sustained B-Raf activation; NGF-activated TrkA forms a long-lived complex containing FRS2, Crk and the Rap-specific GEF C3G, whereas Rap1 is only transiently activated by EGFR and both receptors activate Ras only transiently due to Ras-GAP negative feedback.

phases created by SH3m/PRMn mixtures showed multi-phasic intensity autocorrelation 
curves with a complex distribution of relaxation times spanning 0.2–20 ms (Supplementary 
Fig. 13) or beyond (Fig. 2c). Some of these relaxation times scale non-linearly with the 
square of scattering angle (q2, Supplementary Fig. 13).

experiment.system: Pooled droplet phase of SH3m/PRMn mixtures (including SH35+PRM(N-WASP)8)
experiment.perturbation: observational (droplets pooled after formation)
experiment.measurement: Single- and multi-angle dynamic light scattering intensity autocorrelation

text: Photobleaching showed diffusion of droplet constituents slowed by ~3 orders of magnitude relative to free diffusion in water, with recovery rate correlating inversely with monomer-monomer affinity and valency; small molecule fluorophores and EGFP move rapidly within droplets.

quotes.quote:
Third, photobleaching studies showed that the diffusion of the droplet 
constituents is slowed by ~3 orders of magnitude relative to free diffusion in water (not 
shown). Further, the photobleaching recovery rate correlates inversely with monomer-
monomer affinity and valency (Supplementary Fig. 14)

Small molecule fluorophores and EGFP can enter and 
move rapidly within the droplets (Supplementary Fig. 15).

experiment.system: In vitro droplets containing OG-SH34 and SH3m/PRMn variants
experiment.perturbation: Photobleaching of a 5 μm spot with 488 nm laser in droplets >20 μm diameter
experiment.measurement: FRAP recovery kinetics fit to single exponential

text: Electron cryo-microscopy of flash-frozen SH35+PRM5 solutions showed round electron dense objects 50~500 nm in diameter with edges irregular on the ~10 nm scale; such objects were absent with either component alone or with components mixed below the droplet concentration.

quotes.quote:
microscopic images of SH35+PRM5 solutions flash frozen immediately after mixing showed 
numerous round, electron dense objects with diameters of 50~500 nm (Fig. 2d; 
Supplementary Fig. 16). These objects were not observed with high concentrations of either 
SH35 or PRM5 alone, or with the two components mixed below the droplet concentration.

their edges were 
highly irregular on the ~10 nm scale, suggesting they contained large but disordered 
molecular species, consistent with a crosslinked gel.

experiment.system: SH35+PRM5 solutions in vitro
experiment.perturbation: Mixing components (vs single components or sub-threshold mixtures), blotting and flash freezing
experiment.measurement: Low-dose electron cryo-microscopy imaging

text: In the droplet phase the fractional saturation of SH3/PRM binding sites is estimated to be 3–5-fold higher than needed to induce the sol-gel transition.

quotes.quote:
First, at the 
extremely high concentrations in the droplet phase, the fractional saturation of SH3/PRM 
binding sites is estimated to be 3–5-fold higher than that needed to induce the sol-gel 
transition16

experiment.system: SH3m/PRMn droplet phase
experiment.perturbation: observational (estimation from measured droplet concentrations)
experiment.measurement: Calculated fractional saturation compared with theoretical sol-gel threshold

text: Co-expression of mCherry-SH35 and eGFP-PRM5 in HeLa cells produced 0.5~2 μm cytoplasmic puncta containing both fluorophores; puncta were absent with either protein alone or with mCherry-SH35 + eGFP-PRM3, and did not stain with vesicle markers or a lipid dye.

quotes.quote:
Co- 
expression of mCherry-SH35 and eGFP-PRM5 in HeLa cells results in formation of 0.5~2 
μm diameter, cytoplasmic puncta containing both fluorophores (Fig. 3a). Puncta are not 
observed in cells expressing either protein alone, or in cells co-expressing mCherry-SH35 + 
eGFP-PRM3, indicating that their formation is dependent on interaction between the two 
high-valent molecules. The puncta do not stain with a large range of vesicle markers or a 
lipid dye

experiment.system: HeLa cells transfected with mCherry-SH35 and/or eGFP-PRM5 (or eGFP-PRM3)
experiment.perturbation: Co-expression vs single expression vs lower-valency PRM3
experiment.measurement: Confocal fluorescence imaging of puncta; vesicle marker/lipid dye staining

text: Both mCherry and eGFP fluorescence of cellular puncta recovered in ~10 seconds after photobleaching, indicating rapid exchange with the surrounding cytoplasm.

quotes.quote:
Both mCherry and eGFP fluorescence of the bodies recover in ~10 
seconds after photobleaching (Fig. 3b), indicating rapid exchange of both components with 
the surrounding cytoplasm and suggesting a dynamic, liquid-like nature.

experiment.system: HeLa cells co-expressing mCherry-SH35 and eGFP-PRM5
experiment.perturbation: Photobleaching of individual puncta with 488 nm laser line
experiment.measurement: FRAP recovery time of mCherry and eGFP fluorescence

text: Addition of Nck to N-WASP (GBD-P-VCA) caused droplet formation, and adding di-phosphorylated nephrin tail peptide (2pY) lowered the phase boundary for both proteins by ≥2-fold, with a more pronounced effect for 3pY peptide at the same total pY concentration, shifting the boundary from μM to nM regimes.

quotes.quote:
Addition of Nck to an N-WASP construct (GBD-P-VCA, Supplementary Table 1; called N-
WASP hereafter) causes droplet formation as in the model systems above (Fig. 4b). 
Addition of a di-phosphorylated nephrin tail peptide (2pY) drops the phase boundary for 
both proteins by ≥2-fold (Fig. 4c)

This effect is even more pronounced when nephrin 3pY 
peptide is added (to the same total pY concentration) (Fig. 4d).

consequently shifting the phase 
boundary from μM (Fig. 4b) to nM (Fig. 4d) regimes

experiment.system: Purified nephrin tail peptides, Nck and N-WASP (GBD-P-VCA) in vitro
experiment.perturbation: Titration of Nck/N-WASP concentrations ± 4.5 μm 2pY or 3 μm 3pY nephrin peptides
experiment.measurement: Phase diagram scoring of droplet formation by microscopy

text: When reactions containing N-WASP above its phase separation concentration were stained with phalloidin, numerous actin filament bundles were observed within the droplets.

quotes.quote:
when 
reactions containing N-WASP above its phase separation concentration are stained with 
phalloidin, numerous actin filament bundles are observed within the droplets (Fig. 4f).

experiment.system: Droplets containing 3 μM nephrin 3pY, 10 μM Nck and 2 μM N-WASP
experiment.perturbation: Addition of rhodamine-actin (4 μM), 300 nM Alexa 488 phalloidin and 10 nM Arp2/3 complex
experiment.measurement: Confocal microscopy of actin filament bundles in droplets

text: Of the 28 known binding partners of the Nck SH2 domain, 14 are predicted or demonstrated to contain three or more pY binding sites.

quotes.quote:
Of the 28 known binding 
partners of the Nck SH2 domain, 14 are predicted or demonstrated to contain three or more 
pY binding sites23,24

experiment.perturbation: observational (database survey and motif prediction)
experiment.measurement: Count of partners with three or more pY binding sites

text: IL-17A, IL-17A/F and IL-17F all signal through the IL-17RA–IL-17RC complex and mediate qualitatively similar but quantitatively distinct signals, with a potency order of IL-17A > IL-A/F > IL-17F.

quotes.quote: All three ligands mediate qualitatively similar but quantitatively distinct signals, with
IL-17A > IL-A/F > IL-17F in terms of signaling potency7.

experiment.system: cells expressing the IL-17RA/IL-17RC receptor complex
experiment.perturbation: stimulation with IL-17A, IL-17A/F heterodimer or IL-17F
experiment.measurement: relative signaling potency

text: IL-17RD is reported to serve as an alternate receptor subunit for IL-17A but not IL-17F.

quotes.quote:
A recent report suggests 
that IL-17RD may serve as an alternate receptor subunit for IL-17A, but surprisingly not 
IL-17F8.

experiment.system: psoriasis-like skin inflammation model / IL-17 receptor complexes
experiment.perturbation: testing IL-17RD as receptor subunit for IL-17A versus IL-17F
experiment.measurement: receptor usage/ligand response

text: Structure-function studies indicated that the SEFIR domain constitutes an interaction platform between Act1 and IL-17 receptors, and peptides blocking that interaction reduce IL-17-mediated pathology.

quotes.quote:
Structure-function 
studies indicated that the SEFIR constitutes an interaction platform between Act1 and IL-17 
receptors; hence peptides that block such interactions reduce IL-17-mediated pathology13.

experiment.system: IL-17 receptor–Act1 complexes and in vivo inflammation models
experiment.perturbation: decoy peptides blocking Act1–IL-17RA interaction
experiment.measurement: IL-17-mediated inflammatory pathology

text: Act1 is degraded via K48-linked polyubiquitination catalyzed by the F-box E3 ligase β-TrCP in response to prolonged IL-17 stimulation.

quotes.quote:
Act1 is subjected to proteasomal degradation 
upon modification with lysine (K)48-linked polyubiquitin chain16. This process catalyzed by 
an F-box E3 ubiquitin ligase, β-transducin repeat-containing protein (β-TrCP), in response 
to prolonged IL-17 stimulation.

experiment.system: IL-17-responsive cells
experiment.perturbation: persistent IL-17 stimulation
experiment.measurement: Act1 ubiquitination and protein degradation

text: IL-17RA contains a C-terminal CBAD region with TRAF-binding sites required to activate C/EBPβ, a domain absent from IL-17RC and other family members.

quotes.quote:
IL-17RA, the largest member of the family, additionally encodes a distinct C-terminal region 
that contains TRAF-binding sites and which is required to activate the transcription factor 
CCAAT/enhancer binding protein β (C/EBPβ); hence, this region has been dubbed a 
“CBAD” (C/EBPβ-activating domain)18, 21.

experiment.system: cells expressing IL-17RA deletion mutants
experiment.perturbation: truncation/deletion of the IL-17RA C-terminal domain
experiment.measurement: C/EBPβ activation and target gene expression

text: Act1 E3 ligase activity is required for IL-17-induced NF-κB activation: TRAF6 binds the Act1 TRAF-binding motif, receives K63-linked polyubiquitin, and activates TAK1 leading to NF-κB and MAPK activation.

quotes.quote:
The E3 ligase activity of Act1 is required for IL-17-induced NF-κB 
activation14. After the recruitment of Act1 to the IL-17 receptor complex, TRAF6 binds to 
the TRAF-binding motif in Act1, resulting in conjugation of K63-linked polyubiquitin chain 
to TRAF614. Polyubiquitinated TRAF6 then activates TGFβ-activated kinase 1 (TAK1), 
leading to NF-κB activation.

experiment.system: IL-17-stimulated cells
experiment.perturbation: mutation/loss of Act1 E3 ligase activity
experiment.measurement: TRAF6 ubiquitination, TAK1 and NF-κB/MAPK activation

text: Negative regulators constrain the TRAF6 arm: A20 is recruited via the CBAD to IL-17RA and removes Act1-mediated polyubiquitin from TRAF6; USP25 deubiquitinates TRAF6 and limits EAE pathology; TRAF4 competes with TRAF6 for Act1 so TRAF4 deficiency enhances IL-17-activated genes and sensitizes mice to EAE; TRAF3 binds the CBAD and its overexpression attenuates EAE severity.

quotes.quote:
A20 is recruited via the CBAD to IL-17RA and removes Act1-
mediated polyubiquitin chain on TRAF6, tempering activation in a negative-feedback 
circuit25, 26. Similarly, USP25 can also deubiquitinate TRAF6, limiting IL-17-induced 
signaling and the pathology of IL-17-dependent experimental autoimmune 
encephalomyelitis (EAE)27. In addition, TRAF4 competes with TRAF6 for the TRAF-
binding motif on Act1. Consequently, deficiency of TRAF4 enhances IL-17-activated genes 
and sensitizes mice to EAE28, 29
overexpression of TRAF3 attenuates the severity of EAE.

experiment.system: mice and IL-17-responsive cells
experiment.perturbation: deficiency or overexpression of A20, USP25, TRAF4, TRAF3
experiment.measurement: IL-17 target gene induction and EAE disease severity

text: IkBζ (Nfkbiz) positively promotes IL-17-induced gene expression, and Nfkbiz-deficient mice resemble IL-17-deficient mice in resistance to imiquimod-induced dermatitis.

quotes.quote:
IkBζ, encoded by Nfkbiz, positively promotes expression of 
IL-17-induced genes30, 31, 32, though a comprehensive determination of its direct versus 
indirect targets has not been reported. Hence, Nfkbiz–/– mice show similarities to IL-17-
deficient mice in disease resistance to imiquimod (IMQ)-induced dermatitis33

experiment.system: Nfkbiz-/- mice
experiment.perturbation: imiquimod-induced dermatitis (psoriasis model)
experiment.measurement: disease resistance and IL-17-induced gene expression

text: C/EBP binding sites are over-represented in proximal promoters of IL-17-induced genes, and IL-17 signaling triggers MEK- and GSK3β-dependent phosphorylation of C/EBPβ via the IL-17RA CBAD subdomain, an event linked to reduced IL-17 signaling.

quotes.quote:
Binding sites for C/EBPs are over-represented within the proximal promoters of genes 
induced upon IL-17 signaling23.

IL-17 signaling triggers phosphorylation of C/EBPβ by a 
MEK-dependent pathway and glycogen synthase kinase 3β (GSK3β) via the IL-17RA 
CBAD subdomain, an event linked to reduced IL-17 signaling21

experiment.system: IL-17-stimulated cells with IL-17RA CBAD mutants
experiment.perturbation: IL-17 stimulation; MEK/GSK3β pathway and CBAD manipulation
experiment.measurement: C/EBPβ phosphorylation and IL-17 signaling output

text: Regnase-1 (Zc3h12a) degrades actively translated IL-17-induced transcripts including Il6 and Nfkbiz, and Regnase-1-deficient mice show exacerbated IL-17-mediated pathology in EAE, pulmonary inflammation and IMQ-driven dermatitis, while Regnase-1 deficiency improves IL-17-dependent immunity to Candida albicans.

quotes.quote:
Regnase-1 degrades mRNAs that are undergoing active translation; these include 
prototypical IL-17-induced transcripts such as Il6 and Nfkbiz, but under some circumstances 
Il17ra and Il17rc43. Consequently, Regnase-1-deficient mice exhibit exacerbated IL-17-
mediated pathology during EAE, pulmonary inflammation and IMQ-driven dermatitis; 
conversely, Regnase-1 deficiency improves IL-17-dependent immunity to Candida albicans 
infections43, 44.

experiment.system: Regnase-1-deficient mice
experiment.perturbation: Regnase-1 (Zc3h12a) deficiency; EAE, pulmonary inflammation, IMQ dermatitis, C. albicans infection
experiment.measurement: target mRNA decay and disease/infection outcomes

text: miR-23b targets mRNAs encoding TAB2, TAB3 and IKK-α to dampen NF-κB activation and is downregulated by IL-17, while miR-30a degrades Traf3ip2 (Act1) mRNA and inhibits IL-17 signaling.

quotes.quote:
The microRNA miR-23b 
was found to target mRNAs encoding TAB2, TAB3 and IKK-α, dampening NF-κB 
activation. Interestingly, IL-17 downregulates miR-23b transcription, causing feedback 
activation of IL-17 signaling activity47 (Fig. 2a). Moreover, miR-30a degrades Traf3ip2 
mRNA (encoding Act1) and consequently inhibits IL-17 signaling48.

experiment.system: IL-17-responsive cells and autoimmune inflammation models
experiment.perturbation: miR-23b or miR-30a manipulation; IL-17 stimulation
experiment.measurement: target mRNA levels and NF-κB/IL-17 signaling activity

text: IL-17 signals synergistically with NF-κB-activating cytokines (TNFα, lymphotoxin), IFN-γ (STAT1), IL-13 (STAT6), TGF-β (SMADs), and microbial products including LPS and the C. albicans toxin candidalysin, which signals through c-Fos.

quotes.quote:
In addition to cooperating with cytokines that activate NF-κB such as 
TNFα or lymphotoxin, IL-17 signals cooperatively with IFN-γ (which activates STAT1), 
IL-13 (STAT6), TGF-β (SMADs). IL-17 also synergizes with microbial products such as 
bacterial LPS and candidalysin, a fungal pore-forming toxin produced by Candida albicans 
that signals through c-Fos35, 49, 50, 51.

experiment.system: IL-17-responsive epithelial and other target cells
experiment.perturbation: co-stimulation of IL-17 with other cytokines or microbial products
experiment.measurement: synergistic target gene induction

text: In skin stem cells, IL-17A induces an EGFR-mediated Act1–TRAF4–ERK5 cascade in which TRAF4 tethers EGFR to the IL-17R complex and Act1 recruits Src for EGFR transactivation; the extracellular domain of EGFR was dispensable, indicating ligand-independent transactivation.

quotes.quote:
An IL-17A–induced epidermal growth factor 
receptor (EGFR)-mediated Act1–TRAF4–ERK5 cascade has been identified in skin stem 
cells that are involved in wound healing and tumorigenesis52, 53.

Upon IL-17A stimulation, TRAF4 tethers 
EGFR to the IL-17R complex, which is followed by EGFR transactivation via Src 
recruitment through interactions with Act152. Importantly, the extracellular domain of EGFR 
was dispensable52, indicating that this cascade occurs independently of EGFR ligands.

experiment.system: skin stem cells / keratinocytes
experiment.perturbation: IL-17A stimulation; EGFR extracellular domain deletion and TRAF4/Act1 manipulation
experiment.measurement: EGFR transactivation and MEKK3-MEK5-ERK5 activation

text: Deletion analysis revealed IL-17RA, IL-17RC and EGFR all contain TRAF4-binding motifs, and TRAF4 binds the EGFR juxtamembrane region in response to EGF but the EGFR C-terminal tail in response to IL-17A.

quotes.quote:
Deletion analysis revealed that IL-17RA, IL-17RC and EGFR all contained TRAF4-
binding motifs.
TRAF4 binds to a motif in the juxtamembrane segment of EGFR in response to EGF to

promote autophosphorylation58, whereas TRAF4 binds to the C-terminal tail of EGFR in 
response to IL-17A to promote EGFR transactivation52.

experiment.system: cells expressing receptor deletion mutants
experiment.perturbation: deletion mapping; EGF versus IL-17A stimulation
experiment.measurement: TRAF4 binding sites and EGFR activation

text: The IL-17A-induced EGFR–Act1–TRAF4–ERK5 cascade was most strongly activated in Lrig1-marked skin stem cells, which express a high level of TRAF4, and this cascade drives expansion and migration of Lrig1+ stem cells and progeny for re-epithelialization after wounding.

quotes.quote:
the IL-17A–induced EGFR-mediated Act1–
TRAF4–ERK5 signaling cascade was most strongly activated in a stem cell population 
marked by a negative regulator of EGFR, Lrig159, which exhibits a high level of TRAF4 
expression52.

IL-17A-induced EGFR-ERK5 signaling cascade drives 
the expansion and migration of Lrig1+ stem cells and their progenies to participate in re-
epithelialization in response to wounding.

experiment.system: mouse skin Lrig1+ hair follicle stem cells
experiment.perturbation: IL-17A stimulation and skin wounding
experiment.measurement: ERK5 pathway activation, stem cell expansion/migration and re-epithelialization

text: In colonic epithelial cells, Act1 binds GRB2 to prevent its association with SOS1; upon IL-17 stimulation Act1 is recruited to IL-17RA, releasing GRB2 and enhancing FGF2-induced ERK1/2 phosphorylation, and in vivo ERK1/2 activation in colonic epithelium relies on FGF2–IL-17A cooperation.

quotes.quote:
In vivo, the activation of ERK1/2 in colonic epithelial cells relies on cooperation between 
FGF2 and IL-17A60. At the nexus of this cooperation is Act1, which binds to the adaptor 
GRB2, preventing its association with guanine nucleotide exchange factor SOS1. Following 
IL-17 stimulation, Act1 is recruited to IL-17RA, thereby releasing GRB2 and enhancing 
FGF2-induced ERK1/2 phosphorylation.

experiment.system: colonic epithelial cells in vivo and in vitro
experiment.perturbation: IL-17A and FGF2 co-stimulation; Act1/GRB2 interaction analysis
experiment.measurement: ERK1/2 phosphorylation and GRB2-SOS1 association

text: ERK5 plays a non-redundant role in IL-17-dependent KRAS G12D-driven skin tumorigenesis, and ERK1/2 and ERK5 regulate distinct sets of genes.

quotes.quote:
Curiously, despite their 
similarities, ERK1/2 and ERK5 regulate distinct sets of genes63. ERK5 plays a non-
redundant role in IL-17-dependent KRAS G12D-driven skin tumorigenesis52, 53, 64.

experiment.system: mouse KRAS G12D-driven skin tumor models
experiment.perturbation: ERK5 loss/inhibition in IL-17-dependent tumorigenesis
experiment.measurement: tumor formation and gene expression programs

text: IL-17A co-signaling with NOTCH1 requires NOTCH1 ligands, unlike its ligand-independent cooperativity with EGFR.

quotes.quote:
Notably, IL-17A co-signaling with NOTCH1 requires NOTCH1 ligands66, which differs 
from its cooperativity with EGFR.

experiment.perturbation: IL-17A stimulation with or without NOTCH1 ligand engagement
experiment.measurement: NOTCH1 activation/co-signaling

text: The CARD14 mutant CARD14E138A is associated with especially strong NF-κB activation and Card14E138A/+ mice develop spontaneous psoriasis-like skin inflammation; unexpectedly, CARD14 deficiency impaired IL-17A-induced signaling to NF-κB, JNK1/2 and p38 via a CBM complex with Bcl10 and MALT1, and overexpressed CARD14 interacted with Act1 and TRAF6, enhanced by IL-17A.

One mutant, CARD14E138A, is associated with especially 
strong NF-κB activation. Consistently, Card14E138A/+ mice develop spontaneous psoriasis-
like skin inflammation. Unexpectedly, a CARD14 deficiency impaired IL-17A-induced 
signaling to NF-κB, JNK1/2 and p38 by forming a complex with Bcl10 and MALT1 (the

Overexpressed CARD14 interacted with Act1 and TRAF6, which was enhanced 
by IL-17A stimulation68.

experiment.perturbation: CARD14 gain-of-function mutation, deficiency, or overexpression; IL-17A stimulation
experiment.measurement: NF-κB/JNK/p38 activation, protein interactions, skin inflammation

text: Syk was shown to associate with Act1, TRAF6 and IL-17RA and to facilitate IL-17A-induced NF-κB activation.

quotes.quote:
In a separate study, Syk kinase was also shown to associate with 
Act1, TRAF6 and IL-17RA and to facilitate IL-17A-induced NF-κB69.

experiment.system: keratinocytes
experiment.perturbation: Syk manipulation with IL-17A stimulation
experiment.measurement: protein association and NF-κB-dependent CCL20 expression

text: IL-17 strongly induces neutrophils indirectly via G-CSF, MCP-1 and CXC chemokines produced by non-hematopoietic target cells, and IL-17 deficiency is nearly always associated with reduced neutrophil activation.

quotes.quote:
IL-17 strongly induces neutrophils, an effect that is achieved indirectly by production of G-
CSF, MCP-1 and CXC chemokines from non-hematopoietic target cells. Commensurate 
with this, IL-17 deficiency is nearly always associated with reduced neutrophil activation5.

experiment.system: mice and non-hematopoietic target cells
experiment.perturbation: IL-17 deficiency or stimulation
experiment.measurement: chemokine/G-CSF production and neutrophil activation

text: Patients with mutations in IL-17R components (IL17RA, IL17RC, ACT1) show a dominance of mucocutaneous infections by Candida albicans and S. aureus, yet candidiasis is only a minor problem in humans taking anti-IL-17 biologics, a finding mirrored in mice given IL-17 blocking antibodies.

quotes.quote:
Enlightening observations made in patients with mutations encoding IL-17R components 
(IL17RA, IL17RC, ACT1) revealed a surprising dominance of mucocutaneous infections by
Candida albicans and S. aureus in humans (Table 1)76.

candidiasis is only a minor 
problem in humans taking anti-IL-17 biologic drugs, a finding mirrored in mice given 
blocking antibodies to IL-1767, 80, implying that only threshold levels of IL-17 are needed to 
prevent candidiasis.

text: IL-17 is required for effective responses to experimental fungal vaccines targeting Blastomyces, Histoplasma and Coccidioides, and for Pneumocystis TH1, TH2 and TH17 responses act redundantly.

quotes.quote:
IL-17 is needed for effective responses to 
experimental fungal vaccines, for example targeting Blastomyces, Histoplasma and 
Coccidioides82, 83, 84, 85. Pneumocystis is a true opportunist, in that TH1, TH2 and TH17 cell 
responses act redundantly to mediate immunity to this fungus.

experiment.perturbation: IL-17/TH17 deficiency during vaccination or infection
experiment.measurement: protective immunity against fungal challenge

text: IL-17 drives tissue regeneration: blockade of IL-17 delays re-epithelialization of wounded mouse skin, IL-17 acts on hair follicle Lrig1+ stem cells whose progeny mediate wound closure, IL-17 signaling induces rapidly proliferating progenitors that promote colon epithelium repair in chemically induced colitis, and IL-17-induced RegIIIγ is critical for skin wound closure.

Blockade of 
IL-17 delays re-epithelialization of wounded mouse skin. IL-17 acts directly on Lrig1+ stem 
cells in the hair follicle, which are central to tissue repair.

Similar observations have been 
made in chemically induced colitis, where IL-17 signaling induces a population of rapidly 
proliferating progenitors that promote colon epithelium repair62

IL-17-induced 
expression of the anti-microbial peptide RegIIIγ is critical for wound closure in skin88

experiment.system: mouse skin wounding and chemically induced colitis models
experiment.perturbation: IL-17 blockade or IL-17 signaling manipulation
experiment.measurement: re-epithelialization, progenitor proliferation, wound closure

text: In the gut, IL-17 signaling contributes to adenoma formation by enhancing proliferation and survival of enterocytes harboring Apc mutations, and epithelial IL-17 signaling mediates colitis-associated and carcinogenic bacteria-induced tumorigenesis as well as papilloma and squamous cell carcinomas in skin tumorigenesis models.

quotes.quote:
In the gut, IL-17 signaling contributes to adenoma 
formation by enhancing the proliferation and survival of enterocytes harboring mutations in 
the Adenomatous polyposis coli (Apc) gene61.

Epithelial 
IL-17 signaling has been shown to mediate colitis-associated and carcinogenic bacteria-
induced tumorigenesis, as well as papilloma and squamous cell carcinomas in models of 
skin tumorigenesis52, 53, 62, 92.

experiment.system: mouse intestinal and skin tumor models
experiment.perturbation: epithelial IL-17 receptor signaling deletion/blockade in Apc-mutant or carcinogen models
experiment.measurement: adenoma/papilloma formation and enterocyte proliferation and survival

text: Lineage tracing in chemical-induced inflammation-associated and oncogenic Kras-driven wounding-induced skin cancer models showed progeny of Lrig1+ cells contribute to IL-17-driven tumorigenesis, and IL-17 promotes pancreatic tuft cell development and stem cell features of pancreatic cancer cells, accelerating neoplasia progression.

quotes.quote:
In chemical-induced inflammation-associated and 
oncogenic Kras-driven wounding-induced skin cancer models, lineage tracing showed that 
progeny of Lrig1+ cells contribute to tumorigenesis driven by IL-1752. In parallel, IL-17 
promotes development of pancreatic tuft cells and stem cell features of pancreatic cancer 
cells, accelerating pancreatic neoplasia progression91.

experiment.system: mouse skin cancer and pancreatic neoplasia models
experiment.perturbation: IL-17 signaling manipulation with Lrig1 lineage tracing
experiment.measurement: tumor cell origin, stem cell features and neoplasia progression

text: Mouse models of collagen-induced arthritis and EAE demonstrated that TH17 rather than TH1 cells are the dominant instigators of autoimmune pathology, and blockade or deletion of IL-17 and IL-23 reduced disease signs in several autoimmune model systems.

quotes.quote:
Mouse models such as collagen-induced arthritis (CIA, representing rheumatoid arthritis) 
and EAE (multiple sclerosis) demonstrated that TH17 rather than TH1 cells are the dominant 
instigators of autoimmune pathology101. Accordingly, blockade or deletion of IL-17 and 
IL-23 in mice reduced disease signs in several autoimmune model systems.

experiment.perturbation: blockade or genetic deletion of IL-17 and IL-23
experiment.measurement: disease signs/severity

text: Anti-IL-17A biologics secukinumab and ixekizumab show striking efficacy in psoriasis and also work in psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis and at least a subset of RA patients; in preclinical models IL-17 blockade ameliorates allergic asthma and COPD pathologies, and IL-17 airway activity positively correlates with disease severity in asthma and COPD patients.

quotes.quote:
The efficacy of anti-IL-17A biologics 
secukinumab and ixekizumab in psoriasis is particularly striking67, 104, and these drugs also 
work in psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, and at least a subset of RA patients105.

blockade of IL-17 also ameliorates pathologies triggered by 
environmental challenges in models of allergic asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary

IL-17 airway activity positively correlates with disease severity in asthma and 
COPD patients108, 109.

experiment.system: human clinical trials and preclinical airway disease models
experiment.perturbation: anti-IL-17A antibody treatment; observational patient airway IL-17 activity
experiment.measurement: clinical response and disease severity correlation

text: IL-17 signaling in fibroblastic reticular cells drives increased glucose uptake and metabolic function via induction of IkBζ, which is required for glucose uptake and CPT1A expression; in EAE and colitis lymph node inflammation, absence of IL-17 signaling causes activated FRCs to experience nutrient stress and increased apoptosis with failed expansion, and only FRCs from previously activated lymph nodes show a metabolic response to IL-17.

quotes.quote:
recent studies have demonstrated that IL-17 signaling in FRCs drives increased glucose 
uptake and metabolic function110. IL-17 induces the transcriptional coactivator IkBζ, which 
is essential for the metabolic reprogramming of FRCs through genes that control 
mitochondrial function. IkBζ is required for increased glucose uptake and for expression of 
CPT1A, the rate-limiting transporter for fatty acid oxidation (FAO)110.

During local LN inflammation that occurs in EAE and colitis, 
the absence of IL-17 signaling causes activated FRCs to experience nutrient stress and 
increased apoptosis, leading to failed expansion of these stromal cells despite LN 
hypercellularity110. Interestingly, only FRCs from previously activated LNs (e.g. from 
immunized mice) show a metabolic response to IL-17 stimulation

experiment.system: mouse lymph node fibroblastic reticular cells in EAE and colitis
experiment.perturbation: loss of IL-17 signaling or IkBζ; IL-17 stimulation of FRCs
experiment.measurement: glucose uptake, CPT1A expression, FRC apoptosis and expansion

text: During Mycobacterium or Pneumocystis infection IL-17 induces stromal chemokines such as CXCL13 to organize iBALT, and during EAE IL-17 signals synergistically with lymphotoxin to drive differentiation of FRC-like cells from meningeal stromal cells.

quotes.quote:
During infections with Mycobacterium or Pneumocystis, IL-17 induces stromal cell 
production of chemokines such as CXCL13 to attract and organize T and B cells in iBALT, 
and these structures support the local TH17 response against pathogens111, 112.

In EAE, IL-17 
synergistically signals with lymphotoxin to drive differentiation of FRC-like cells from 
meningeal stromal cells113.

experiment.system: mouse lung infection and EAE meninges
experiment.perturbation: IL-17 signaling loss/stimulation with lymphotoxin
experiment.measurement: CXCL13 production, iBALT and tertiary lymphoid follicle formation

text: Human genetic defects associated with IL-17 immunity include autosomal recessive IL-17RA, IL-17RC and ACT1 mutations and an autosomal dominant IL-17F dominant-negative mutation at position 65, all causing chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis; IL-17RC mutations impair responses to IL-17A and IL-17F but leave IL-17E/IL-25 responses normal, and the ACT1 missense mutation in the SEFIR domain abolishes ACT1 interaction with IL-17R.

quotes.quote:
Dominant-negative mutation at position 65 in tde 
IL-17F polypeptide chain.

Mutations of Il17rc which lead to tde absence of 
IL-17RC protein expression and impaired 
response to IL-17A and IL-17F homo- and 
heterodimers but normal response to IL-17E/
IL-25

Missense mutation in tde SEFIR domain of 
ACT1, which abolishes tde interaction of ACT1 
witd IL-17R

experiment.system: patients with inborn errors of IL-17 immunity
experiment.perturbation: observational (naturally occurring germline mutations)
experiment.measurement: protein expression, IL-17 ligand responsiveness and candidiasis susceptibility

text: The crystal structure of the MyD88:IRAK4:IRAK2 death domain complex, determined at 3.4 Å resolution, is a left-handed helical oligomer of 6 MyD88, 4 IRAK4 and 4 IRAK2 DDs.

quotes.quote:
we report the crystal structure of the MyD88: IRAK4: IRAK2 death domain (DD) complex, which 
surprisingly reveals a left-handed helical oligomer that consists of 6 MyD88, 4 IRAK4 and 4 
IRAK2 DDs.

We crystallized the MyD88: IRAK4: IRAK2 DD complex and determined its structure at 
3.4 Å resolution using multiple heavy atom derivatives that included Au, Hg, Pt, Se and Ta 
cluster

experiment.system: DDs of human MyD88 (20–117), IRAK4 (4–106) and IRAK2 (1–112) co-expressed in E. coli and co-purified
experiment.perturbation: observational (crystallization and heavy-atom phasing)
experiment.measurement: X-ray crystallography, model building, subunit assignment via Se positions

text: MyD88 DD and IRAK4 DD form a binary complex with a measured molecular mass of 135.4 kDa (0.5% error) by MALS, and a ternary complex including IRAK2 DD elutes at an apparent mass of ~180 kDa.

quotes.quote:
MyD88 DD interacted with IRAK4 DD to form a binary 
Myddosome complex that eluted from a gel filtration column with a molecular mass of 
135.4 kDa (0.5% error) as measured by multi-angle light scattering (MALS)

a ternary Myddosome complex that also contains IRAK2 DD were 
formed and eluted with an apparent molecular mass of ~180 kDa.

experiment.system: co-expressed MyD88/IRAK4 (± IRAK2) death domains
experiment.perturbation: inclusion or omission of IRAK2 DD in co-expression
experiment.measurement: gel filtration chromatography with multi-angle light scattering

text: The ternary Myddosome is a tower-shaped structure about 110 Å high and about 70 Å in diameter with approximately four layers: MyD88 at the bottom two layers, IRAK4 in the middle and IRAK2 at the top.

quotes.quote:
The ternary Myddosome complex forms a tower-shaped structure of about 110 Å in height 
and about 70 Å in diameter (Fig. 1a). It contains approximately four layers, with MyD88 at 
the bottom two layers, IRAK4 in the middle layer and IRAK2 at the top layer.

experiment.system: MyD88:IRAK4:IRAK2 DD crystal structure
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: dimensional and layer analysis of the refined atomic model

text: In the single-stranded left-handed helix, adjacent DD molecules are related by a rotation of 98 ± 2 ° and a translation along the helical axis of about 6 Å, giving approximately 3.7 DD molecules per turn over almost four turns.

quotes.quote:
In the helical oligomer, the adjacent individual DD molecules are related by a rotation 
of 98 ± 2 ° and a translation along the helical axis of about 6 Å.

The DD molecules complete almost four turns, with approximately 3.7 DD 
molecules per turn.

experiment.system: MyD88:IRAK4:IRAK2 DD crystal structure
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: helical symmetry parameters derived from the atomic model

text: Interactions in the helical assembly fall into three types (I, II, III) that superimpose well across the different DD pairs; type I and type II bury more surface area than type III.

quotes.quote:
The interactions in the helical assembly can be classified into three types. Type I and type II 
mostly mediate interactions between the layers while type III represents contacts between 
adjacent DD molecules in the helical spiral

Superposition of the three type I interaction pairs, MyD88: MyD88, MyD88: IRAK4, and 
IRAK4: IRAK2, showed that they are highly similar to one another

The type I 
and type II interactions are more extensive in buried surface areas than the type III 
interaction

experiment.system: MyD88:IRAK4:IRAK2 DD crystal structure
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: interface classification, structural superposition and buried surface area analysis

text: Structure-based mutagenesis identified IRAK2 residues Y6, W62, M66 and R67 and IRAK4 residues F25, Q50, F51, R54 and A95 as critical for the IRAK2:IRAK4 interaction, consistent with IRAK2 recruitment requiring a composite site of three IRAK4 molecules.

quotes.quote:
The importance of these sites in the IRAK2: 
IRAK4 interaction were also confirmed by structure-based mutagenesis, which identified 
Y6, W62, M66 and R67 of IRAK2 (Supplementary Fig. 9d) and F25, Q50, F51, R54, and 
A95 of IRAK4 (Supplementary Fig. 9e) as critical residues.

experiment.system: recombinant IRAK2 and IRAK4 DD proteins expressed in E. coli
experiment.perturbation: site-directed mutations at modeled IRAK2:IRAK4 interface residues
experiment.measurement: pull-down of DD partners assessed by SDS-PAGE

text: Charge and shape complementarity between the top and bottom surfaces of MyD88 is weak, with shape complementarity scores between MyD88 DDs in the range of 0.3 and 0.4, the lowest among all interactions in the complex, whereas IRAK4:MyD88 and IRAK2:IRAK4 interfaces show good charge and shape complementarity.

quotes.quote:
Inspection 
of the top and bottom surfaces of MyD88 layers suggested that the charge complementarity 
between these surfaces is weak (Fig. 2f). In addition, the shape complementarity scores (Sc) 
35 between MyD88 DDs (such as the type II and type III interactions) are in the range of 0.3 
and 0.4, the lowest among all the interactions in the complex

the 
bottom surface of IRAK4 matches well with the top surface of MyD88 both in charge 
complementarity (Fig. 2f) and in shape complementarity as shown in the Sc scores

experiment.system: MyD88:IRAK4:IRAK2 DD crystal structure
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: electrostatic surface inspection and shape complementarity (Sc) score calculation

text: Because of incompatibility between the top and bottom surfaces of IRAK2, only one layer of IRAK2 can assemble into the helical oligomer.

quotes.quote: Because of the incompatibility between the top

and bottom surfaces of IRAK2, only one layer of IRAK2 can assemble into the helical 
oligomer (Fig. 2g).

experiment.system: MyD88:IRAK4:IRAK2 DD crystal structure
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: surface charge complementarity analysis of IRAK2 top and bottom faces

text: Reconstitution shows hierarchical assembly: MyD88 DD and IRAK4 DD form a stable complex, whereas IRAK2 DD does not form a stable complex with MyD88 or IRAK4 alone and instead binds the MyD88:IRAK4 complex.

quotes.quote:
MyD88 DD and IRAK4 DD 
formed a stable complex while IRAK2 DD did not form a stable complex with either 
MyD88 or IRAK4 alone. Instead, IRAK2 DD interacts with the MyD88: IRAK4 complex.

experiment.system: recombinant MyD88, IRAK4 and IRAK2 death domains
experiment.perturbation: reconstitution with different pairwise and ternary combinations of DDs
experiment.measurement: complex formation assessed by co-purification/pull-down (Supplementary Fig. 10)

text: The IRAK4 F25D mutation impaired IRAK4 pull-down of IRAK2 and also weakened pull-down of MyD88, indicating that a stabilized type III interaction among IRAK4 DDs contributes to Myddosome assembly.

quotes.quote:
Unexpectedly, the F25D mutation not only 
impaired the ability of IRAK4 to pull down IRAK2, but also weakened the ability of IRAK4 
to pull down MyD88 (Supplementary Fig. 9e), suggesting that a stabilized type III 
interaction among IRAK4 DDs is important for Myddosome assembly.

experiment.system: recombinant IRAK4 DD with MyD88 and IRAK2 DD lysates
experiment.perturbation: IRAK4 F25D point mutation
experiment.measurement: Ni-NTA pull-down followed by SDS-PAGE

text: In the crystal structure the C-terminal tail of IRAK4 DD points toward the IRAK2 DD layer and that of IRAK2 DD points toward the IRAK4 DD layer, an arrangement that would bring IRAK4 kinase domains into proximity of IRAK1 or IRAK2 for phosphorylation.

quotes.quote:
The C-
terminal tail of IRAK4 DD points toward the IRAK2 DD layer, while the C-terminal tail of 
IRAK2 DD points toward the IRAK4 DD layer. This arrangement would then bring the 
kinase domains of IRAK4 to the proximity of IRAK1 or IRAK2 to allow efficient 
phosphorylation by IRAK4 (Fig. 3b).

experiment.system: MyD88:IRAK4:IRAK2 DD crystal structure
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: inspection of DD C-terminal tail orientations relative to layers

text: DALI structural homology search shows IRAK4 DD is most similar to Tube DD while IRAK2 DD is most similar to Pelle DD, supporting Tube as the IRAK4 homologue in Drosophila Toll signaling.

quotes.quote:
Structural homology 
search using DALI 45 supports this conclusion because IRAK4 DD is most similar to Tube 
DD while IRAK2 DD is most similar to Pelle DD (Supplementary Table 4).

experiment.system: solved MyD88/IRAK4/IRAK2 DD structures versus PDB
experiment.perturbation: observational (computational)
experiment.measurement: DALI structural similarity ranking

text: Superposition of the Tube:Pelle DD complex onto a type II IRAK4:IRAK2 pair superimposes well with a slight orientational difference, and a combined model yields an elongated dMyD88:Tube:Pelle complex whose shape resembles the SAXS-derived kidney-shaped outline, with no direct dMyD88-Pelle contact.

quotes.quote:
Superposition of the known structure of the 
Tube: Pelle DD complex 47 onto a pair of type II IRAK4: IRAK2 interaction showed that 
they superimpose well with a slight orientational difference (Fig. 4a)

The shape of the ternary complex model is similar to the 
kidney shaped outline of the dMyD88: Tube: Pelle complex derived from small angle X-ray 
scattering (SAXS) 46.

There is no direct interaction between dMyD88 
and Pelle in our model of the complex, which is consistent with earlier biochemical studies

experiment.system: Drosophila Tube:Pelle DD crystal structure and the mammalian Myddosome structure
experiment.perturbation: observational (computational superposition/modelling)
experiment.measurement: structural superposition and comparison with published SAXS envelope and mutation data

text: Published Tube mutations R34E, K87E and R126E and dMyD88 mutations D113K, D163K, D166K and D169K/D170K that block Tube-dMyD88 interaction map onto the modeled interface, supporting the model.

quotes.quote:
The validity of the ternary complex model is supported by published mutations, R34E, 
K87E and R126E of Tube and D113K, D163K, D166K, and D169K/D170K of dMyD88, 
that prevented interaction between Tube and dMyD8848. R34, K87, and R126 reside on the 
side of Tube modeled to interact with dMyD88

experiment.system: model of the dMyD88:Tube:Pelle DD complex
experiment.perturbation: mapping of previously published interaction-blocking point mutations
experiment.measurement: location of mutated residues relative to modeled interface

text: The three interface types in the Myddosome are similar to those in the PIDD:RAIDD complex, differing by rotations of 25.8°, 19.9° and 34° for type I, II and III respectively.

quotes.quote:
Superposition of analogous 
interactions showed that the type I, II and III interactions differ by rotational differences of 
25.8°, 19.9° and 34°, respectively.

experiment.system: Myddosome and PIDD:RAIDD crystal structures
experiment.perturbation: observational (computational superposition)
experiment.measurement: rotational differences between analogous interfaces

text: Re-inspection of the PIDD:RAIDD complex shows it can be seen as a double-stranded left-handed helical oligomer, one strand with three PIDD and three RAIDD DDs and the other with two PIDD and four RAIDD DDs, accounting for the 5:7 stoichiometry.

quotes.quote:
We discovered that the PIDD: RAIDD complex may be seen as 
a double stranded left-handed helical oligomer (Fig. 4e–4g). One strand has three PIDD DD 
and three RAIDD DD molecules and the other strand contains two PIDD DDs and four 
RAIDD DDs, leading to the 5: 7 stoichiometry of the PIDD DD: RAIDD DD complex.

experiment.system: published PIDD:RAIDD DD complex structure
experiment.perturbation: observational (re-analysis guided by Myddosome helical symmetry)
experiment.measurement: helical strand decomposition and stoichiometry assignment

text: MyD88 DD has a short H3 and an extraordinarily long H6 extending from residue 99 to residue 120, indicating the MyD88 DD boundary extends into the intermediate domain so that deletion of the ID would truncate the DD.

quotes.quote:
MyD88 has a short H3 and an extraordinarily long H6 from 
residue 99 to the end of the construct at residue 120, which includes part of the intermediate 
domain (ID, residues 110–154).

DD boundary of MyD88 does not end until about residue 120 and deletion of the MyD88 ID 
would result in a truncated DD.

experiment.system: MyD88 DD within the ternary crystal structure
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: secondary-structure/domain boundary assignment from the atomic model

text: Two-photon glutamate uncaging at an identified spine induces LTP at that spine while nearby synapses only microns away are not potentiated.

quotes.quote:
An identified
spine can be stimulated using two-photon glutamate uncaging.

glutamate pulse with submicron dimensions that directly targets the identified spine and
induces LTP at the synapse on that spine. Nearby synapses that are only microns away are
not potentiated

experiment.system: hippocampal dendritic spines
experiment.perturbation: two-photon glutamate uncaging at a single identified spine
experiment.measurement: AMPAR-mediated EPSC potentiation at stimulated versus adjacent spines

text: Using the Camui FRET sensor with 2pFLIM, CaMKII is activated within seconds of stimulation, restricted to the stimulated spine, and decays to baseline within ~1 min; the T286A mutant decays within seconds.

quotes.quote:
CaMKII is
activated within seconds after the start of synaptic stimulation and that the activation is
restricted to the stimulated spine (FIG. 1)22. At the end of stimulation, CaMKII activity
decays to baseline levels within ~1 min. By contrast, when using a mutant variant of
CaMKII (T286A) that cannot be autophosphorylated, the activity of the enzyme decays
within seconds.

experiment.system: single dendritic spines of hippocampal neurons expressing Camui CaMKII sensor
experiment.perturbation: two-photon glutamate uncaging LTP induction; comparison with T286A CaMKII
experiment.measurement: FRET by two-photon fluorescence lifetime imaging

numbers.quantity: CaMKII activity decay time after stimulation

text: CaMKII activation can be inhibited by either the fast buffer BAPTA or the slow buffer EGTA, implying dependence on bulk spine-head calcium; bulk calcium produced by voltage-dependent calcium channel depolarization is not sufficient to activate CaMKII.

quotes.quote:
showed that CaMKII activation can be
inhibited by either BAPTA or EGTA, implying that activation of this enzyme is dependent
on an elevation of calcium in the bulk of the spine head22. However, a nanodomain process
may also be required for such activation, as a bulk calcium signal, when produced by
depolarization of voltage-dependent calcium channels, is not sufficient to activate CaMKII.

experiment.system: dendritic spines of hippocampal neurons
experiment.perturbation: loading with fast (BAPTA) or slow (EGTA) calcium buffers; depolarization-evoked calcium entry
experiment.measurement: CaMKII activation imaging

text: Calmodulin has a higher on-rate constant for calcium binding than calbindin, and at its intracellular concentration of ~100 μM can account for much of the 'fast calcium buffer'; CaMKII subunits are present in spines at ~100μM.

quotes.quote:
the on-rate constant for
calcium binding to calmodulin is significantly higher than it is for calcium binding to
calbindin

because of the high intracellular concentration of
calmodulin (~100 μM) and its high on-rate constant for calcium binding, this protein can
account for much of what has been termed the ‘fast calcium buffer’

which are present in spines at a concentration of
~100μM34

experiment.system: calmodulin and calcium buffers in pyramidal cell spines
experiment.perturbation: reconstitution experiments and computer simulations (observational for concentrations)
experiment.measurement: calcium binding on-rate constants and buffer capacity

text: Formation of autonomous CaMKII has a Hill coefficient of approximately eight with respect to calcium, and autonomous activity is up to five times higher with calmodulin bound.

quotes.quote:
The autonomous activity of CaMKII for
phosphorylating various substrates is up to five times higher with calmodulin bound than
it is when calmodulin is not bound126. Formation of autonomous CaMKII has a Hill
coefficient of approximately eight with respect to calcium, indicating a virtual
threshold 151.

experiment.system: purified CaMKII holoenzyme
experiment.perturbation: varying calcium/calmodulin concentrations
experiment.measurement: substrate phosphorylation / autonomous activity and Hill coefficient

numbers.quantity: Hill coefficient for autonomous CaMKII formation vs calcium
fold increase in autonomous activity with calmodulin bound

text: Chemically induced LTP produced a two-fold increase in the amount of CaMKII per unit length of the PSD, measured one hour after induction by electron microscopy immunolabeling.

quotes.quote:
LTP induction, which was chemically induced, produced a two-fold increase in the
amount of CaMKII per unit length of the PSD, as measured one hour after LTP induction

experiment.system: hippocampal neurons, postsynaptic densities
experiment.perturbation: chemically induced LTP
experiment.measurement: electron microscopy immunolabeling of CaMKII per unit PSD length at 1 hour

numbers.quantity: increase in CaMKII per unit PSD length

text: NMDAR activation in hippocampal slices doubles the amount of CaMKII–NMDAR complex by coimmunoprecipitation; the I205K T-site mutation blocks complex formation and attenuates translocation in HEK293 cells, and complexes formed after ionophore-mediated calcium entry persisted more than 30 min after calcium removal.

quotes.quote:
A I205K-
encoding mutation in CaMKII, which affects the so-called T-site of the enzyme (BOX 1),
blocks complex formation and strongly attenuates CaMKII translocation in HEK293 cells
expressing CaMKII and NMDARs46. Activation of NMDARs in hippocampal slices leads to
a two-fold increase in the amount of the CaMKII–NMDAR complex (FIG. 4D), as
determined by coimmunoprecipitation experiments43. In experiments in which CaMKII
translocation was caused by ionophore-mediated calcium entry, once CaMKII become
bound to an NMDAR via the T-site, the complex persisted for more than 30 min after the
removal of calcium47.

experiment.system: hippocampal slices; HEK293 cells expressing CaMKII and NMDARs; neuronal cultures
experiment.perturbation: NMDAR activation, I205K T-site mutation, ionophore-mediated calcium entry then calcium removal
experiment.measurement: coimmunoprecipitation of CaMKII–NMDAR complex; CaMKII translocation imaging

numbers.quantity: increase in CaMKII–NMDAR complex after NMDAR activation

text: Transgenic mice overexpressing the NR2B cytoplasmic tail have CaMKII–NMDAR complex reduced by 20–50%, a reduction in LTP of ~50%, and learning deficits; overexpression of NR2B variants mutated near S1303 that block CaMKII binding greatly reduces LTP.

quotes.quote:
LTP is greatly reduced by overexpression of mutant variants of NR2B (variants
with mutations affecting residues near S1303) that block CaMKII binding to the NMDAR49

Transgenic mice have been generated that overexpress the
cytoplasmic tail of NR2B, which interferes with the formation of the CaMKII–NMDAR
complex and reduces the level of this complex by 20–50%51. These animals have a
reduction in LTP of ~50% and exhibit learning deficits.

experiment.system: transgenic mice and hippocampal neurons
experiment.perturbation: overexpression of NR2B cytoplasmic tail or NR2B mutants blocking CaMKII binding
experiment.measurement: CaMKII–NMDAR complex level, LTP magnitude, learning behaviour

text: Molecular counting at the PSD gives about 80 CaMKII holoenzymes per average spine, a PSD-95:NR1 molar ratio of about 7:1 (PSD-95:NMDAR 14:1), ~300 PSD-95 molecules, and an estimate of 20–25 NMDARs per synapse.

quotes.quote:
PSDs in the average spine contain about 80 CaMKII holoenzymes and the molar ratio of
PSD-95 (a synaptic scaffolding protein) to NR1 is about 7:152, 53. Thus, assuming that each
NMDAR has two NR1 subunits, the PSD-95:NMDAR molar ratio is 14:1. The absolute
number of PSD-95 molecules is ~30052, 54, so a rough estimate of NMDARs per synapse is
20–25.

experiment.system: hippocampal postsynaptic densities
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: quantitative estimates of molecular copy number and molar ratios

numbers.quantity: CaMKII holoenzymes per average spine PSD

text: S831 phosphorylation of GluR1 increases during LTP and increases AMPAR channel conductance by enhancing the probability of high conductance states rather than changing state magnitudes; the effect requires stargazin for GluR1/GluR2 receptors, and the GluR1 S831A knockin reduces LTP only when S845 phosphorylation is also prevented.

quotes.quote:
Single-channel recordings show that S831 phosphorylation does not change
the magnitude of any of the conductance states of AMPARs but, rather, enhances the
probability that high conductance states will be activated by intermediate glutamate
concentrations78. Interestingly, for AMPARs containing both GluR1 and GluR2, the ability
of S831 phosphorylation to increase channel conductance only occurs if stargazin is
present

one would expect that a knockin mutation encoding GluR1 S831A by itself
would decrease the magnitude of LTP. Such an effect, however, is not observed unless
GluR1 S845 phosphorylation is also prevented80.

experiment.system: AMPA receptors in CA1 pyramidal cells and knockin mice
experiment.perturbation: S831 phospho-site mutation/pseudophosphorylation, stargazin presence, CaMKII expression
experiment.measurement: single-channel conductance recordings and LTP magnitude

text: pHluorin-tagged AMPAR imaging shows LTP at single spines causes a rapid increase in exocytotic events lasting about a minute in the stimulated spine and in dendrites within 3 μm; inhibiting exocytosis proteins does not affect the first 20 minutes of LTP but reduces later potentiation.

quotes.quote:
After induction of LTP at single spines, a rapid increase occurs in the rate of
exocytotic events, a rise that lasts for about a minute. These events occur in the stimulated
spine and also in dendrites within 3 μm from the stimulated spine.

However, inhibition of any of these proteins does not affect the
first 20 minutes of LTP, although it does strongly reduce potentiation at later times

experiment.system: hippocampal neurons expressing pHluorin-tagged AMPARs
experiment.perturbation: single-spine LTP induction; inhibition of RAS–ERK, RAB-GTPases, SNAREs, syntaxin 4/13, myosin V
experiment.measurement: pHluorin exocytosis events and EPSC potentiation time course

numbers.quantity: LTP phase unaffected by exocytosis inhibition

text: Mutating the putative CaMKII phosphorylation sites of stargazin did not affect AMPAR surface expression but prevented enhancement of synaptic transmission after LTP induction, whereas pseudophosphorylated stargazin enhanced transmission and occluded LTP.

quotes.quote:
Although
these mutations did not affect the surface expression of AMPARs, they did prevent these
channels from enhancing synaptic transmission after LTP induction (Fig. 4). Conversely,
pseudophosphorylation of stargazin led to enhanced transmission that occluded LTP.

experiment.system: CA1 pyramidal cells expressing stargazin mutants
experiment.perturbation: mutation of stargazin CaMKII phosphorylation sites to alanine (S9A) or pseudophosphorylation (S9D)
experiment.measurement: AMPAR surface expression and EPSC/LTP recordings

text: Quantum-dot single-particle tracking shows AMPARs diffuse freely under basal conditions and become captured at synapses upon CaMKII activation; capture is blocked by non-phosphorylatable stargazin, CaMKII inhibition, or a CaMKII mutant unable to bind NMDARs.

quotes.quote: Under basal conditions, AMPARs diffused freely

in the extrasynaptic space while pausing only briefly at synaptic locations. Upon activation
of CaMKII by NMDA application or synaptic input, diffusing AMPARs were captured at
synapses (Fig. 4). The arrest of AMPARs at stimulated synapses is dependent on the
phosphorylation of stargazin, as receptors with non-phosphorylatable stargazin did not
exhibit immobilization at synapses. Immobilization of AMPARs could also be blocked by
inhibition of CaMKII.

Capture
was also prevented by expressing a mutant variant of CaMKII that is unable to bind
NMDARs but still allows CaMKII activation.

experiment.system: cultured neurons with quantum-dot-labelled AMPARs
experiment.perturbation: NMDA application or synaptic input; non-phosphorylatable stargazin, CaMKII inhibition, NMDAR-binding-deficient CaMKII
experiment.measurement: single-particle tracking of AMPAR diffusion and synaptic immobilization

text: Applying a saturating concentration of a ligand disrupting PDZ-1 and PDZ-2 interactions rapidly reduced CA1 EPSCs and mEPSCs by only 45%, indicating only a component of AMPAR transmission depends on the stargazin–PSD-95 interaction.

quotes.quote:
Application of a ligand that disrupts both PDZ-1 and
PDZ-2 interactions produced a rapid reduction in EPSCs and miniature EPSCs (mEPSCs).
The fact that the saturating concentration of the ligand produced only a 45% reduction in
these currents indicates that only a component of AMPAR-mediated transmission is
dependent on the stargazin–PSD-95 interaction.

experiment.system: CA1 basal synaptic transmission
experiment.perturbation: application of PDZ-1/PDZ-2 disrupting ligand at saturating concentration
experiment.measurement: EPSC and mEPSC amplitude

text: Electron microscope tomography shows synaptic PSD-95 oriented perpendicular to the membrane with the stargazin-binding PDZ-1 and -2 domains situated 15 nm from the membrane.

quotes.quote:
Synaptic PSD-95 has been visualized by electron microscope tomography
and is oriented perpendicular to the membrane with the PDZ-1 and -2 domains that bind
stargazin situated quite far (15 nm) from the membrane

experiment.system: synaptic PSD-95 in situ
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: electron microscope tomography of PSD-95 orientation and domain distance

numbers.quantity: distance of PDZ-1/-2 domains from membrane

text: Transient treatment of a hippocampal slice with a CN compound reversed saturated LTP and reduced the amount of CaMKII–NMDAR complex, while additional LTP could still be induced; inhibitors acting mainly at the catalytic S-site do not reverse LTP.

quotes.quote:
transient treatment of a hippocampal slice with CN compound reversed LTP, allowing
additional LTP to be induced107. In parallel experiments, it was shown that CN inhibitor
reduced the amount of the CaMKII–NMDAR complex in the slice.

other CaMKII inhibitors bind mainly to the catalytic site of the enzyme (the S-site) and only
weakly to the T-site. The latter type of inhibitor does not reverse LTP109, 110.

experiment.system: hippocampal slices with saturated LTP
experiment.perturbation: transient application of CN compounds (T-site CaMKII inhibitors) versus S-site inhibitors
experiment.measurement: EPSC/LTP magnitude, re-inducibility, CaMKII–NMDAR complex level

text: LTP is accompanied by a rapid and persistent increase in spine volume that can be mimicked by overexpression of active CaMKII holoenzymes, and a mutation in CaMKII that specifically interferes with its dendritic synthesis blocks late LTP and greatly reduces PSD CaMKII content.

quotes.quote:
LTP is accompanied by a rapid and persistent increase
in spine volume (Fig. 1), an increase that can be mimicked by overexpression of active
CaMKII holoenzymes11.

A mutation in CaMKII that specifically interferes with its dendritic synthesis
blocks late LTP and greatly reduces the CaMKII content of the PSD120.

experiment.system: hippocampal spines and CaMKII mutant mice
experiment.perturbation: LTP induction; overexpression of active CaMKII holoenzymes; mutation blocking dendritic CaMKII synthesis
experiment.measurement: spine volume imaging, late LTP, PSD CaMKII content

text: Overexpression of T286D CaMKII leads to synaptic weakening and occlusion with LTD unless T305 and T306 phosphorylation is prevented by additional mutations; phosphorylation of these sites prevents CaMKII binding to the PSD and produces learning deficits.

quotes.quote:
overexpression of T286D CaMKII (to mimic the phosphorylated state) actually leads to
synaptic weakening (and occlusion with long-term depression (LTD)) unless T305 and T306
phosphorylation is prevented by additional mutations128. Phosphorylation of these sites
