tively)

experiment.system: nonredundant set of cloned and predicted human kinase protein sequences
experiment.perturbation: observational; pairwise comparison against Celera, Ensembl and GenPept best matches
experiment.measurement: percentage sequence difference and counts of discrepant/misannotated entries

text: All 518 kinases are found in at least one expressed sequence database (dbEST, Incyte, GenBank cDNAs), indicating all are genuine transcribed genes, and about 90% are present in gene predictions from the Celera and public genome databases, although those predictions are often fragmentary, inaccurate or misannotated.

quotes.quote:
All 518 kinases are found in at least one of
the expressed sequence databases (dbEST,
Incyte, and GenBank cDNAs), indicating that
all are genuine, transcribed genes.

All 518 genes are
covered by some EST sequence, and 90%
are present in gene predictions from the
Celera and public genome databases, al-
though those predictions are often fragmen-
tary or inaccurate and are frequently misan-
notated (39).

experiment.system: 518 human kinase gene set
experiment.perturbation: observational; search of EST/cDNA databases and genome gene prediction sets
experiment.measurement: fraction of kinases with EST coverage and with genome-project gene predictions

numbers.quantity: kinases present in Celera/public gene predictions

text: New members were found even in well-studied families: one new CDK (CDK11, a close paralog of CDK8 with 91% protein sequence identity over most of their length), four new Nek kinases bringing the human total to 11, and two new Ste11/MAP3K plus two new Ste20/MAP4K genes with restricted expression — for example only 14 ESTs are known from MAP3K8, all but one from testis, lung or brain libraries.

quotes.quote:
One new mem-
ber of the cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK)
family was found: CDK11 is a close paralog
of CDK8 (91% protein sequence identity for

we discovered four
new Neks to bring the human total to 11 Nek
kinases.

we found two new
Ste11/MAP3K (MAP kinase kinase kinase)
and two new Ste20/MAP4K (MAP kinase
kinase kinase kinase) genes, all of which have
restricted expression

only 14 ESTs are known from MAP3K8, and
all but one derive from testis, lung, or brain
libraries

experiment.system: human genomic, cDNA and EST sequence databases
experiment.perturbation: observational; HMM-based discovery plus EST tissue-library tallying
experiment.measurement: counts of newly identified family members, sequence identity, and EST counts by tissue

text: AKT is activated by growth factors in a PI3K-dependent manner, established using PDGF receptor mutants in which AKT activation depended exclusively on PI3K binding to the receptor.

quotes.quote:
Franke, Kaplan and Tsichlis working with PDGF receptor 
mutants developed by Kazlauskas showed that stimulation of cells with PDGF results in the 
activation of AKT in a manner that depends exclusively on the ability of PI3K to bind to the 
PDGF receptor (Franke et al., 1995).

experiment.system: cells expressing PDGF receptor mutants
experiment.perturbation: PDGF stimulation with receptor mutants disrupting PI3K binding
experiment.measurement: AKT activation

text: The AKT PH domain binds PIP3, and PI3,4P2 binding induces partial activation of the kinase in vitro.

quotes.quote:
AKT possesses a Pleckstrin 
Homology (PH) domain at its amino-terminus, which Downes and Alessi initially showed 
can bind to PIP3 (James et al., 1996). Subsequently, both PI3,4P2 and PIP3 were shown to 
directly bind to the PH domain of AKT, and PI3,4P2 binding was found to induce partial 
activation of the protein kinase in vitro

experiment.system: purified AKT PH domain / AKT protein in vitro
experiment.perturbation: addition of phosphoinositides (PIP3, PI3,4P2)
experiment.measurement: lipid binding and kinase activation

text: PTEN was characterized as a PIP3 phosphatase, opposing PI3K activity.

quotes.quote:
PI3K activity is opposed by the tumor suppressor PTEN, first cloned 
by the Parsons and Steck laboratories (Li et al., 1997; Steck et al., 1997), and characterized 
as a PIP3 phosphatase by Dixon (Maehama and Dixon, 1998).

experiment.system: PTEN protein and cells
experiment.perturbation: observational/biochemical assay of PTEN on PIP3
experiment.measurement: phosphatase activity toward PIP3

text: GSK-3β was identified as the first substrate of AKT in insulin-stimulated cells, and this enabled definition of the optimal AKT consensus phosphorylation motif, which has facilitated discovery of over a hundred AKT substrates.

quotes.quote:
leading to the discovery that GSK-3β is a substrate of AKT 
in insulin-stimulated cells (Cross et al., 1995). The identification of this first substrate of 
AKT was also instrumental in subsequent studies to define the optimal AKT consensus 
phosphorylation motif (Alessi et al., 1996b), which has since facilitated the discovery of 
over a hundred AKT substrates linked to cell physiology and disease.

experiment.system: insulin-stimulated cells
experiment.perturbation: insulin stimulation
experiment.measurement: GSK-3β phosphorylation by AKT; peptide library definition of consensus motif

text: PI3K activation drives phosphorylation of AKT1 at T308 in the activation loop and S473 in the C-terminal hydrophobic motif, with both required for maximal kinase activation; corresponding residues are AKT2 T309/S474 and AKT3 T305/S472.

quotes.quote:
Activation of PI3K results in the phosphorylation of two key residues on AKT1, T308 in the 
activation, or T-loop, of the catalytic protein kinase core, and S473 in a C-terminal 
hydrophobic motif (Alessi et al., 1996a) (Figure 1A,B). Phosphorylation of both residues is 
required for maximal activation of the kinase. Regulation also occurs on corresponding 
residues in AKT2 (T309 and S474) and AKT3 (T305 and S472).

experiment.system: growth factor/insulin-stimulated cells
experiment.perturbation: PI3K activation by stimulation
experiment.measurement: site-specific AKT phosphorylation and kinase activity

text: PDK1 phosphorylates AKT1 at T308, an event required for AKT activity; PDK1 also phosphorylates the activation loop of other AGC kinases, but AKT appears to be the only obligate PIP3-dependent PDK1 target among them.

quotes.quote:
The phosphoinositide-
dependent protein kinase 1 (PDK1) was discovered for its ability to phosphorylate AKT1 at 
T308, which is required for AKT activity (Alessi et al., 1997; Stokoe et al., 1997).

However, none of these kinases possess a PIP3-
binding domain, and AKT appears to be the only obligate PIP3-dependent PDK1 target 
amongst this group (Collins et al., 2003; McManus et al., 2004).

experiment.system: cells and in vitro kinase assays; PDK1 knock-in/knockout studies
experiment.perturbation: PDK1 activity/docking-site mutation
experiment.measurement: AKT T308 phosphorylation and AGC kinase activation loop phosphorylation

text: mTORC2 is the primary AKT S473 kinase; S473 phosphorylation stabilizes T308 phosphorylation and the activation state of AKT, and mTORC2 kinase activity assayed in immunopurifications is stimulated by growth factors in a PI3K-dependent manner.

quotes.quote:
The 
primary AKT S473 kinase is the mechanistic target of rapamcyin (mTOR) complex 2 
(mTORC2) (Sarbassov et al., 2005)

phosphorylation of S473 stabilizes 
T308 phosphorylation and the activation state of AKT

The protein kinase 
activity of mTORC2, assayed in immunopurifications, is stimulated by growth factors in a 
PI3K-dependent manner (Huang et al., 2008; Sarbassov et al., 2005).

experiment.system: mammalian cells; immunopurified mTORC2
experiment.perturbation: growth factor stimulation, PI3K inhibition, mTORC2 disruption
experiment.measurement: in vitro kinase activity toward AKT and AKT S473/T308 phosphorylation

text: DNA-PK can substitute for mTORC2 in phosphorylating AKT S473 in response to DNA damage.

quotes.quote:
the mTOR-related kinase DNA-dependent protein kinase (DNA-PK) can substitute 
for the activity of mTORC2 for AKT S473 phosphorylation in response to DNA damage 
(Bozulic et al., 2008)

experiment.system: cells
experiment.perturbation: DNA damage
experiment.measurement: AKT S473 phosphorylation

text: Phosphorylated AKT can be detected intracellularly and phosphorylate substrates up to two hours post-stimulation, while a recent study reports that PIP3 binding allosterically activates AKT and dissociation from PIP3 is rate-limiting for AKT dephosphorylation and inactivation.

quotes.quote:
Since phosphorylated AKT can be detected 
intracellularly and can phosphorylate substrates up to two hours post-stimulation (Kunkel et 
al., 2005)

a recent study found that PIP3 
binding allosterically activates AKT and that dissociation from PIP3 is rate-limiting for Akt 
dephosphorylation and inactivation (Ebner et al., 2017a)

experiment.system: cultured cells with AKT activity reporters
experiment.perturbation: growth factor stimulation; PIP3 binding/dissociation
experiment.measurement: AKT substrate phosphorylation kinetics and AKT dephosphorylation

text: Loss of the PI3,4P2 phosphatase INPP4B leads to elevated PI3,4P2 at endosomes and activation of AKT2.

quotes.quote:
This model is supported by studies on the PI3,4P2 phosphatase and 
tumor suppressor INPP4B,, the loss of which leads to elevated PI3,4P2 at endosomes and 
activation of AKT2

experiment.system: cells/mouse models
experiment.perturbation: INPP4B loss
experiment.measurement: endosomal PI3,4P2 levels and AKT2 activation

text: mTORC2 constitutively phosphorylates AKT T450 in the turn motif co-translationally, an event required for proper folding of the nascent AKT polypeptide.

quotes.quote:
T450 in a region termed the turn-motif is constitutively phosphorylated by mTORC2, 
occurs co-translationally and is required for proper folding of the nascent AKT polypeptide 
(Facchinetti et al., 2008; Ikenoue et al., 2008)

experiment.system: cells lacking mTORC2 components
experiment.perturbation: mTORC2 ablation / T450 mutation
experiment.measurement: AKT T450 phosphorylation, folding and stability

text: PP2A dephosphorylates AKT T308 leading to kinase inactivation, while PHLPP1 and PHLPP2 were identified as the physiological AKT S473 phosphatases acting on specific AKT isoforms; PHLPP1/2 expression is reduced or lost in many cancers.

quotes.quote:
Protein 
phosphatase 2A (PP2A) dephosphorylates AKT T308, leading to kinase inactivation 
(Andjelkovic et al., 1996).

The PH domain leucine-rich repeat protein 
phosphatases (PHLPP1 and PHLPP2) were discovered as the physiological AKT S473 
phosphatases (Gao et al., 2005). PHLPP1 and PHLPP2 dephosphorylate S473 on specific 
AKT isoforms (Brognard et al., 2007).

PHLPP1/2 expression is reduced or 
lost in many cancers (Chen et al., 2011).

experiment.system: mammalian cells and tumor samples
experiment.perturbation: phosphatase expression/knockdown
experiment.measurement: AKT T308 and S473 phosphorylation; PHLPP expression in cancers

text: AKT phosphorylates substrates primarily within a minimal consensus motif R-X-R-X-X-S/T-ϕ, though some established substrates such as AMPK and ACLY have a Pro rather than Arg at the -5 position.

quotes.quote:
AKT 
phosphorylates these targets on Ser/Thr residues primarily within a minimal consensus 
recognition motif of R-X-R-X-X-S/T-ϕ (where X is any amino acid and ϕ denotes a 
preference for large hydrophobic residues)

including 
the AMP-regulated protein kinase (AMPK) and ATP-citrate lyase (ACLY), both of which 
have a Pro residue at the -5 position, rather than the canonical Arg residue (Berwick et al., 
2002; Horman et al., 2006).

experiment.system: AKT substrate proteins in cells and in vitro
experiment.perturbation: observational (peptide/substrate sequence analysis and phosphorylation assays)
experiment.measurement: phosphorylation site sequence context

text: AKT inhibits GSK3 via phosphorylation of conserved N-terminal residues (GSK3α S21, GSK3β S9), creating an intramolecular pseudosubstrate that occludes the phosphate-binding pocket; knock-in mice lacking these sites are impaired for insulin-stimulated glycogen synthesis in muscle.

quotes.quote:
AKT exerts an 
inhibitory phosphorylation on an amino-terminal motif conserved in both GSK3α (S21) and 
GSK3β (S9).

The AKT-mediated 
phosphorylation of GSK3 on the amino-terminus creates an intramolecular pseudosubstrate 
that occludes the phosphate-binding pocket and inhibits substrate accessibility to GSK3

Knock-in mice lacking the AKT 
phosphorylation sites on GSK3α and β (Gsk3αS21A; Gsk3βS9A) are impaired for insulin-
stimulated glycogen synthesis in muscle (McManus et al., 2005).

experiment.system: Gsk3αS21A;Gsk3βS9A knock-in mice and cells
experiment.perturbation: knock-in mutation of AKT phosphorylation sites on GSK3; insulin stimulation
experiment.measurement: glycogen synthesis in muscle; GSK3 substrate accessibility

text: The two GSK3 isoforms share 85% sequence homology and are functionally redundant in some contexts, with isoform-specific functions identified in specific tissues.

quotes.quote:
The two isoforms, GSK3α and β, share 85% sequence homology and 
are functionally redundant in some contexts, but isoform-specific functions have been 
identified in specific tissues (Kaidanovich-Beilin and Woodgett, 2011).

experiment.system: GSK3α and GSK3β in mammalian tissues
experiment.perturbation: observational (sequence comparison and isoform genetic studies)
experiment.measurement: sequence homology and tissue phenotypes

text: AKT phosphorylates three conserved residues on FoxO factors (including T24 and S256 on FoxO1), generating 14-3-3 binding motifs that drive nuclear export and cytosolic sequestration, attenuating the FoxO transcriptional program.

quotes.quote:
Activation 
of PI3K-AKT signaling leads to acute translocation of FoxO proteins out of the nucleus and 
attenuation of their transcriptional program (Brunet et al., 1999; Kops et al., 1999). AKT 
mediates this regulation through direct phosphorylation of three conserved residues on these 
factors (Figure 4A). Phosphorylation of the most amino-terminal site and a second site 
within a nuclear localization sequence (NLS) on the FoxO proteins (T24 and S256 on 
FoxO1) generates recognition motifs for the 14-3-3 family of phospho-binding proteins, 
which facilitate the export and sequestration of phosphorylated FoxO proteins in the cytosol

experiment.system: growth-factor stimulated mammalian cells
experiment.perturbation: PI3K-AKT activation; FoxO phosphosite mutation
experiment.measurement: FoxO nuclear/cytosolic localization, 14-3-3 binding, target gene expression

text: Genetic epistasis places FoxO downstream of AKT: in C. elegans, dauer arrest from depletion of akt-1 and akt-2 was completely rescued by loss of daf-16; in mice, hepatic insulin resistance and hyperglycemia from liver-specific Akt1/Akt2 ablation were reversed by co-deletion of Foxo1.

quotes.quote:
This connection was first recognized in C. 
elegans, where dauer stage arrest induced by depletion of the two AKT isoforms (akt-1 and 
akt-2) was completely rescued by loss of the sole FoxO family member (daf-16) (Paradis 
and Ruvkun, 1998). In mice, liver-specific ablation of Akt1 and Akt2 gives rise to severe 
hepatic insulin resistance and hyperglycemia, phenotypes that are reversed by co-deletion of 
the primary isoform of FoxO in the liver, Foxo1 (Lu et al., 2012).

experiment.system: C. elegans; mice with liver-specific Akt1/Akt2 deletion
experiment.perturbation: AKT isoform depletion with or without daf-16/Foxo1 co-deletion
experiment.measurement: dauer arrest; hepatic insulin resistance and glycemia

text: AKT activates mTORC1 primarily by phosphorylating and inhibiting TSC2, whose Rheb-GAP activity keeps Rheb GDP-bound; growth factor stimulation releases the TSC complex from Rheb at the lysosome in a manner dependent on AKT and its five phosphorylation sites on TSC2.

quotes.quote:
The primary mechanism by which AKT activates mTORC1 is through the phosphorylation 
and inhibition of tuberous sclerosis complex 2 (TSC2, also known as tuberin)

Growth factor stimulation causes immediate release 
of the TSC complex from Rheb at this location in a manner that is dependent on AKT and 
its five-phosphorylation sites on TSC2 (Figure 5A,B).

experiment.system: mammalian cells, including cells lacking AKT phosphorylation sites on TSC2
experiment.perturbation: growth factor stimulation; TSC2 phosphosite mutation
experiment.measurement: TSC complex localization at Rheb/lysosome and mTORC1 signaling

text: mTOR S2448, once attributed to AKT, is phosphorylated by S6K downstream of mTORC1 on mTOR within both mTORC1 and mTORC2, and mutation of S2448 does not appear to influence mTOR function.

quotes.quote:
However, 
subsequent studies demonstrated that S2448 is 
phosphorylated by S6K downstream of mTORC1 (Chiang and Abraham, 2005; Holz and 
Blenis, 2005), and this phosphorylation occurs on mTOR within both mTORC1 and 
mTORC2 (Rosner et al., 2010). Furthermore, mutation of S2448 does not appear to 
influence mTOR function, and its functional significance remains unknown.

experiment.system: mammalian cells
experiment.perturbation: S6K/mTORC1 inhibition; S2448 mutation
experiment.measurement: mTOR S2448 phosphorylation and mTOR function

text: AKT phosphorylates PRAS40 on T246, relieving its inhibition of mTORC1, but insulin fails to activate mTORC1 signaling in cells lacking the AKT phosphorylation sites on TSC2 despite normal induction of PRAS40 phosphorylation, indicating the TSC-Rheb circuit is dominant over PRAS40 in some settings.

quotes.quote:
AKT phosphorylates PRAS40 on T246 (Kovacina et al., 2003), and this substrate has 
become a reliable readout of AKT activity in cells and tissues. PRAS40 has inhibitory 
activity toward mTORC1 that is attenuated upon T246 phosphorylation

Furthermore, insulin fails to activate mTORC1 signaling in cells lacking the AKT 
phosphorylation sites on TSC2, despite normal induction of PRAS40 phosphorylation 
(Menon et al., 2014). Thus, the TSC-Rheb circuit appears to be dominant over PRAS40 for 
mTORC1 regulation by Akt, at least in some settings.

experiment.system: cells with TSC2 AKT-site mutations or PRAS40 loss
experiment.perturbation: insulin stimulation; TSC2 phosphosite mutation; PRAS40 loss
experiment.measurement: mTORC1 signaling and PRAS40 T246 phosphorylation

text: mTORC1 feedback-inhibits AKT: short-term rapamycin enhances AKT responsiveness to RTK signaling, mTORC1-driven serine phosphorylation of IRS1/2 promotes their degradation and dampens PI3K activation, and mTORC1 phosphorylation of GRB10 stabilizes it to attenuate insulin/IGF1 receptor signaling.

quotes.quote:
It has been recognized for many years that short-term treatment with the mTORC1 
inhibitor rapamycin enhances the responsiveness of AKT to RTK signaling, most notably to 
insulin and IGF1 (Manning, 2004). Much of this regulation has been attributed to mTORC1-
dependent degradation of the insulin receptor substrates (IRS) IRS1 and IRS2

The mTORC1-mediated phosphorylation of GRB10 stabilizes the 
protein and enhances its ability to attenuate signaling from the insulin/IGF1 receptors and 
IRS proteins, thus blocking PI3K-AKT activation.

experiment.system: mammalian cells
experiment.perturbation: rapamycin/mTORC1 inhibition; mTORC1 activation
experiment.measurement: IRS1/2 levels, GRB10 phosphorylation/stability, AKT activation by insulin/IGF1

text: S6K1-mediated phosphorylation of the mTORC2 components Rictor (T1135) and Sin1 (T86, T398) decreases mTORC2-dependent AKT S473 phosphorylation without apparently affecting mTORC2 activity toward other substrates such as AKT T450.

quotes.quote:
S6K1-mediated 
phosphorylation of the mTORC2 components Rictor (T1135) and Sin1 (T86, T398) 
decreases the mTORC2-dependent phosphorylation of AKT-S473 (Dibble et al., 2009; 
Julien et al., 2010; Liu et al., 2013b). Curiously, this regulation of mTORC2 does not appear 
to affect its activity toward other substrates, including AKT T450.

experiment.system: mammalian cells
experiment.perturbation: S6K1 activity / Rictor and Sin1 phosphosite mutation
experiment.measurement: AKT S473 and T450 phosphorylation

text: Prolonged inhibition of AKT signaling enhances expression of the insulin and IGF1 receptors and HER3 through FoxO-dependent transcriptional induction, sensitizing cells to subsequent growth factor-mediated PI3K-AKT activation.

quotes.quote:
Prolonged inhibition of AKT signaling was found to enhance 
expression of the insulin and IGF1 receptors and HER3 through FoxO-dependent 
transcriptional induction, thereby rendering cells more prone to subsequent growth factor-
mediated activation of PI3K-AKT signaling (Chandarlapaty et al., 2011).

experiment.system: cancer cell lines
experiment.perturbation: pharmacological inhibition of PI3K, AKT, and/or mTOR
experiment.measurement: RTK expression levels and PI3K-AKT pathway activation

text: mTOR inhibitors acutely activate EGF receptor family members without immediate effects on receptor levels, an effect most prominent with mTOR kinase inhibitors rather than rapamycin.

quotes.quote:
This includes members of the EGF Receptor family (EGFR, ErbB2/Her2, 
Erb3/Her3, and Erb4/Her4), which are acutely activated upon mTOR inhibition, without 
immediate effects on receptor levels (Rodrik-Outmezguine et al., 2011). While the post-
translational mechanisms underlying this regulation are not currently known, the effects are 
most prominently seen with mTOR kinase inhibitors, rather than the allosteric inhibitor 
rapamycin.

experiment.system: cancer cells
experiment.perturbation: mTOR kinase inhibitors vs rapamycin
experiment.measurement: EGFR family receptor activation and levels

text: AKT phosphorylates c-RAF on S259 and B-RAF on the equivalent site S364, inhibiting RAF activation or downstream signaling by promoting 14-3-3 binding.

quotes.quote:
AKT phosphorylates c-RAF on 
S259 and an equivalent site on B-RAF (S364), which inhibits RAF activation or downstream 
signaling by promoting binding to 14-3-3 proteins

experiment.system: mammalian cells and in vitro kinase assays
experiment.perturbation: AKT-mediated phosphorylation / phosphosite mutation
experiment.measurement: RAF activation, 14-3-3 binding, ERK pathway signaling

text: An unbiased kinome-wide siRNA screen showed that attenuation of ERK signaling generally enhances AKT activation.

quotes.quote:
An unbiased kinome-wide siRNA screen revealed that attenuation of 
ERK signaling results in a general enhancement of AKT activation, indicating that there are 
likely to be additional inhibitory mechanisms between these pathways (Lu et al., 2011).

experiment.system: cultured cells
experiment.perturbation: kinome-wide siRNA knockdown
experiment.measurement: AKT activation

text: AMPK and AKT both induce glucose uptake in metabolic tissues through phosphorylation and inhibition of the RAB-GAPs TBC1D1 and TBC1D4/AS160, driving GLUT4 translocation, but respond to distinct cues (insulin for AKT, ATP depletion for AMPK).

quotes.quote:
AMPK and AKT can both induce glucose 
uptake in metabolic tissues, such as skeletal muscle, through their respective 
phosphorylation and inhibition of the RAB-GAPs TBC1D1 and TBC1D4/AS160, resulting 
in RAB-mediated translocation of GLUT4 to the plasma membrane (Chavez et al., 2008; 
Eguez et al., 2005; Sano et al., 2003). While both kinases stimulate glucose uptake, they do 
so in response to distinct cues: AKT in response to insulin and AMPK in response to ATP 
depletion, such as occurs during muscle contraction.

experiment.system: skeletal muscle and adipocytes
experiment.perturbation: insulin stimulation or AMPK activation; TBC1D1/TBC1D4 phosphosite manipulation
experiment.measurement: GLUT4 translocation and glucose uptake

text: Substrate regulation by AKT is redundant with related kinases: RSK or S6K can phosphorylate the GSK3 N-terminal inhibitory sites, SGK can phosphorylate FOXO3a T32, RSK can phosphorylate TSC2 sites S939 and T1462, and SGK1 or SGK3 can replace AKT for TSC2 phosphorylation and mTORC1 induction in cancer cells after prolonged PI3K or AKT inhibitor exposure, providing a resistance mechanism.

quotes.quote:
The N-terminal inhibitory site on GSK3 isoforms 
(GSK3α-S21, GSK3β-S9) can be phosphorylated by RSK or S6K, downstream of ERK or 
mTORC1 signaling, respectively (Kaidanovich-Beilin and Woodgett, 2011). The 
sequestration of FOXO3a in the cytosol can also be promoted by SGK-mediated 
phosphorylation of T32 (Brunet et al., 2001).

RSK-mediated phosphorylation of at least two of the AKT sites 
on TSC2 (S939 and T1462)

Interestingly, SGK1 or SGK3 can also replace AKT for phosphorylation of 
TSC2 and induction of mTORC1 signaling, which was revealed in cancer cells upon 
prolonged exposure to pharmacological inhibitors of PI3K or AKT and provides a 
mechanism of cellular resistance to such inhibitors (Bago et al., 2016; Castel et al., 2016).

experiment.system: cancer cells and cultured mammalian cells
experiment.perturbation: prolonged PI3K or AKT inhibition; ERK-RSK/S6K/SGK activity manipulation
experiment.measurement: substrate phosphorylation (GSK3, FOXO3a, TSC2) and mTORC1 signaling

text: Upon loss of mTORC2, T308 phosphorylation is stabilized by unknown mechanisms giving sustained AKT signaling, with the notable exception of AKT-mediated FOXO phosphorylation, which is attenuated despite the T308 compensation.

quotes.quote:
Upon loss of mTORC2, unknown mechanisms are induced to stabilize T308 
phosphorylation resulting in sustained AKT signaling (Guertin et al., 2006; Jacinto et al., 
2006). The one notable exception is the AKT-mediated phosphorylation of FOXO isoforms, 
which is attenuated in the absence of mTORC2, despite the T308 compensation.

experiment.system: cells/mice lacking mTORC2 components
experiment.perturbation: genetic or pharmacological mTORC2 inhibition
experiment.measurement: AKT T308 phosphorylation and substrate (FOXO) phosphorylation

text: AKT isoforms show context-dependent, non-redundant functions in cancer: in breast cancer studies AKT1 suppresses migration and metastasis while AKT2 promotes metastatic dissemination; in PTEN-inactivated prostate cancer cells AKT2 is exclusively required for cell-autonomous tumor maintenance, whereas in Pten+/− mice AKT1 appears to suppress prostate tumor development and AKT2 ablation has little impact.

quotes.quote:
in prostate cancer cells with PTEN inactivation, AKT2 is exclusively required for 
cell-autonomous tumor maintenance (Chin et al., 2014), whereas in Pten+/− mice, the AKT1 
isoform appears to suppresses prostate tumor development (Chen et al., 2006), while 
ablation of AKT2 has little impact (Xu et al., 2012).

experiment.system: mouse breast and prostate cancer models; PTEN-inactivated prostate cancer cells
experiment.perturbation: AKT isoform genetic ablation
experiment.measurement: migration, metastasis, tumor development/maintenance

text: Mouse knockouts reveal isoform-specific AKT functions: Akt1−/− mice display growth retardation and perinatal lethality, Akt2−/− mice develop a diabetes-like syndrome, and Akt3−/− mice display decreased brain size, consistent with AKT1 being most widely expressed, AKT2 enriched in insulin-responsive metabolic tissues, and AKT3 in the brain.

quotes.quote:
with AKT1 being the most widely expressed, AKT2 being enriched in insulin-responsive 
metabolic tissues, and AKT3 in the brain. Consistent with this tissue distribution, Akt1−/− 
mice display growth retardation and perinatal lethality (Chen et al., 2001; Cho et al., 2001b), 
Akt2−/− mice develop a diabetes-like syndrome (Cho et al., 2001a), Akt3−/− mice display 
decreased brain size (Easton et al., 2005; Tschopp et al., 2005)

experiment.system: Akt isoform knockout mice
experiment.perturbation: germline deletion of Akt1, Akt2, or Akt3
experiment.measurement: growth, viability, glucose homeostasis, brain size

text: Human overgrowth syndromes map to AKT-pathway mutations: Proteus syndrome is caused by a gain of function AKT1 E17K mutation in the PH domain; patients with AKT2 E17K instead show severe insulin-independent hypoglycemia, asymmetric overgrowth and obesity; and AKT3 E17K patients develop brain overgrowth and megalencephaly.

quotes.quote:
The genetic basis for PS 
is a gain of function mutation in AKT1 at E17K in the PH domain (Lindhurst et al., 2011).

Patients with activating mutations in AKT2 at E17K do 
not develop PS, but instead display severe insulin-independent hypoglycemia, asymmetric 
overgrowth and obesity (Hussain et al., 2011). Patients with the equivalent AKT3 E17K 
mutation develop brain overgrowth and megalencephaly (Poduri et al., 2012).

experiment.system: human patients with overgrowth syndromes
experiment.perturbation: observational (germline/somatic mosaic AKT mutations)
experiment.measurement: genotype-phenotype association

text: AKT1 E17K, the first-described somatic activating AKT mutation, is a low frequency (1.5% −9%) recurring mutation in breast cancers that confers constitutive kinase activation via a charge switch allowing constitutive membrane localization, but is incapable of promoting tumorigenesis without other driver mutations.

quotes.quote:
AKT1 E17K is a low frequency (1.5% −9%) recurring mutation in breast 
cancers (Rudolph et al., 2016). This mutation confers constitutive kinase activation due to a 
charge switch at Glu17 in the phosphoinositide-binding pocket of the PH domain that allows 
constitutive membrane localization of Akt (Carpten et al., 2007; Landgraf et al., 2008). 
However, AKT1 E17K is incapable of promoting tumorigenesis in the absence of other 
driver mutations (Lauring et al., 2010; Mancini et al., 2016).

experiment.system: human breast cancers; cells/mice expressing AKT1 E17K
experiment.perturbation: E17K mutation expression; tumor sequencing
experiment.measurement: mutation frequency, AKT membrane localization/activity, tumorigenesis

numbers.quantity: AKT1 E17K frequency in breast cancer

text: AKT3 E17K has been identified as a recurring mutation, particularly in melanoma, whereas AKT2 E17K was found in one breast cancer patient in a large scale sequencing effort and does not appear to be a recurring event in breast cancer.

quotes.quote:
While 
the equivalent AKT2 E17K mutation has been identified in one breast cancer patient though 
a large scale sequencing effort (Stephens et al., 2012), AKT2 E17K does not appear to be a

recurring event in breast cancer. By contrast, the equivalent AKT3 E17K has been identified 
as a recurring mutation, particularly in melanoma (Davies et al., 2008).

experiment.system: human tumor cohorts (breast cancer, melanoma)
experiment.perturbation: observational large-scale sequencing
experiment.measurement: mutation recurrence

numbers.quantity: breast cancer patients with AKT2 E17K

text: eNOS is an AKT1-specific substrate in endothelial cells, and loss of AKT1, but not AKT2, in mouse ECs results in reduced NO release and impaired angiogenesis.

quotes.quote:
endothelial nitric oxide (NO) synthase (eNOS), which 
controls vascular tone, is an AKT1-specific substrate in endothelial cells (Lee et al., 2014). 
Thus, loss of AKT1, but not AKT2, in mouse ECs results in reduced NO release and 
impaired angiogenesis (Ackah et al., 2005).

experiment.system: mouse endothelial cells
experiment.perturbation: AKT1 or AKT2 loss
experiment.measurement: NO release and angiogenesis

text: AKT isoforms have distinct roles in atherosclerosis: loss of Akt1 enhances development and severity of atherosclerosis in mouse models, mice lacking AKT2 (but not AKT1) in hematopoietic cells display decreased atherosclerotic lesions, and AKT3 knockout mice have enhanced atherosclerosis due to increased foam cell formation from enhanced lipoprotein uptake by Akt3-deficient macrophages.

quotes.quote:
with loss of Akt1 enhancing the development and 
severity of atherosclerosis in mouse models (Fernandez-Hernando et al., 2007; Fernandez-
Hernando et al., 2009).

Mice lacking AKT2, but not AKT1, in hematopoietic cells 
display decreased atherosclerotic lesions (Babaev et al., 2014). By contrast, AKT3 knockout 
mice have enhanced development of atherosclerosis due to an increase in formation of foam 
cells, which appears to be an intrinsic property of Akt3-deficient macrophages resulting 
from enhanced uptake of lipoproteins (Ding et al., 2012).

experiment.system: mouse atherosclerosis models with Akt isoform deletion
experiment.perturbation: Akt1, Akt2 (hematopoietic), or Akt3 knockout
experiment.measurement: atherosclerotic lesion development and foam cell formation

text: Akt2 knockout mice exhibit insulin resistance and glucose intolerance and have type-2 diabetes, and rare dominant negative mutations in AKT2 underlie severe diabetes in humans.

quotes.quote:
As such, Akt2 knockout mice exhibit 
insulin resistance and glucose intolerance and have type-2 diabetes (Cho et al., 2001a; 
Garofalo et al., 2003). Interestingly, rare dominant negative mutations in AKT2 have been 
found to underlie the genetic development of severe diabetes in humans (George et al., 
2004).

experiment.system: Akt2 knockout mice; human families with AKT2 mutations
experiment.perturbation: Akt2 deletion; dominant negative AKT2 mutation
experiment.measurement: insulin sensitivity, glucose tolerance, diabetes phenotype

text: Uncontrolled hepatic glucose production and insulin resistance in mice with liver-specific loss of Akt1 and Akt2 is reversed by co-deletion of Foxo1, indicating FoxO1 inhibition is an essential hepatic function of AKT and that in the absence of FoxO1 hepatic AKT signaling appears dispensable for control of glucose metabolism by fasting and feeding.

quotes.quote:
Strikingly, the uncontrolled hepatic glucose production and insulin 
resistance in mice with liver-specific loss of Akt1 and Akt2 is reversed by co-deletion of 
Foxo1 (Lu et al., 2012), providing definitive genetic evidence that inhibition of FoxO1 is an 
essential function of AKT in the liver. A particularly surprising implication of this finding is 
that in the absence of FoxO1, hepatic AKT signaling appears to be dispensable for the 
control of glucose metabolism by fasting and feeding.

experiment.system: mice with liver-specific Akt1/Akt2 deletion
experiment.perturbation: co-deletion of Foxo1
experiment.measurement: hepatic glucose production and insulin resistance

text: Insulin-stimulated, AKT2-dependent promotion of glycogen synthesis in the liver occurs through an unknown mechanism independent of GSK3 phosphorylation.

quotes.quote:
However, the insulin-stimulated, AKT2-dependent promotion of glycogen synthesis in the 
liver has been found to occur through an unknown mechanism that is independent of GSK3 
phosphorylation (Wan et al., 2013).

experiment.system: mouse liver / hepatocytes
experiment.perturbation: insulin stimulation; AKT2 loss; GSK3 phosphosite manipulation
experiment.measurement: hepatic glycogen synthesis

text: Induction of SREBP1c and de novo lipid synthesis in the liver depends on both AKT2 and mTORC1, with FoxO1 suppression also contributing.

quotes.quote:
Induction of SREBP1c and lipid synthesis in the liver has been found to depend on 
both AKT2 and mTORC1, with FoxO1 suppression also contributing in this setting (Wang et 
al., 2015).

experiment.system: mouse liver
experiment.perturbation: genetic loss of AKT2, mTORC1 inhibition, FoxO1 manipulation
experiment.measurement: SREBP1c induction and lipid synthesis

text: An essential role for AKT in insulin suppression of lipolysis is not fully established: adipose-specific Rictor knockout causes failure of insulin to block lipolysis, whereas mice lacking AKT2 show only a partial defect; and although insulin fails to inhibit lipolysis in PDE3B knockout mice, re-expression of either wild-type PDE3B or the S273A phosphorylation-site mutant restores insulin's ability to block lipolysis.

quotes.quote:
Adipose-specific knockout of the mTORC2 component Rictor, which leads 
to attenuation of AKT signaling, results in a failure of insulin to block lipolysis (Kumar et 
al., 2010), but mice lacking AKT2 exhibit only a partial defect in insulin-mediated 
suppression of lipolysis (Koren et al., 2015).

Consistent with this being a 
key point of regulation, insulin fails to inhibit lipolysis in PDE3B knockout mice (Choi et 
al., 2006). However, the ability of insulin to block lipolysis is restored to PDE3B-null 
adipocytes with re-expression of either wild-type PDE3B or a phosphorylation-site mutant 
(S273A)

experiment.system: mouse adipose tissue and adipocytes
experiment.perturbation: adipose Rictor knockout, Akt2 knockout, PDE3B knockout with WT or S273A re-expression
experiment.measurement: insulin-mediated suppression of lipolysis

text: AKT phosphorylates PDE3B on S273, which appears to enhance its ability to hydrolyze cAMP and thereby block PKA activation.

quotes.quote:
AKT has been found to directly phosphorylate 
phosphodiesterase 3B (PDE3B) on S273, which appears to enhance its ability to hydrolyze 
cAMP, thereby blocking PKA activation (Kitamura et al., 1999).

experiment.system: adipocytes / biochemical assay
experiment.perturbation: AKT-mediated phosphorylation of PDE3B
experiment.measurement: cAMP hydrolysis and PKA activation

text: Rapamycin-mediated inhibition of mTORC1 increases plasma lipids in humans and S6K1 knockout mice show a similar phenotype with decreased adiposity, effects attributed to mTORC1 suppression of lipolysis, since mTORC1 inhibition induces lipolysis in cultured adipocytes with increased ATGL expression and PKA-dependent HSL phosphorylation.

quotes.quote:
Rapamycin-mediated inhibition of 
mTORC1, downstream of Akt, leads to an increase in plasma lipids in humans (Morrisett et 
al., 2002), and S6K1 knockout mice show a similar phenotype with a corresponding 
decrease in adiposity (Um et al., 2004). These effects have been attributed to a role for 
mTORC1 in suppressing lipolysis, as mTORC1 inhibition induces lipolysis in cultured 
adipocytes, which correlates with increased ATGL expression and PKA-dependent 
activating phosphorylation of HSL

experiment.system: humans on rapamycin; S6K1 knockout mice; cultured adipocytes
experiment.perturbation: mTORC1 inhibition / S6K1 deletion
experiment.measurement: plasma lipids, adiposity, lipolysis, ATGL expression and HSL phosphorylation

text: Insulin-stimulated PI3K-AKT signaling, predominantly via AKT2, drives GLUT4 translocation to the plasma membrane; AKT2 associates with GLUT4-containing vesicles, and AKT phosphorylation of the Rab-GAP TBC1D4/AS160 at multiple sites drives 14-3-3 binding and release of vesicle retention.

quotes.quote:
Insulin-stimulated PI3K-AKT signaling leads to rapid 
translocation of the primary glucose transporter in these tissues, GLUT4, to the plasma 
membrane (Leto and Saltiel, 2012). AKT2 has been found to associate with GLUT4-
containing vesicles and promotes their trafficking and plasma membrane fusion in response 
to insulin (Calera et al., 1998; Ng et al., 2008).

The 
best characterized of these is the Rab-GAP TBC1D4 (or AS160), which acts to retain Glut4-
containing vesicles in the cytosol, a function that is disrupted by AKT-mediated 
phosphorylation of multiple regulatory sites leading to TBC1D4 binding to 14-3-3 proteins

experiment.system: adipose tissue and skeletal muscle / adipocytes
experiment.perturbation: insulin stimulation; AKT2 and TBC1D4 manipulation
experiment.measurement: GLUT4 translocation, vesicle association, 14-3-3 binding

text: AKT suppresses muscle protein breakdown through inhibition of FoxO, blocking expression of the muscle E3-ubiquitin ligases atrogin-1 and MuRF1.

quotes.quote:
AKT suppresses muscle protein breakdown through 
its inhibition of FoxO, thereby blocking expression of genes encoding the major muscle E3-
ubiquitin ligases atrogin-1 and MuRF1 (Lee et al., 2004; Sandri et al., 2004; Stitt et al., 
2004).

experiment.system: skeletal muscle / myotubes
experiment.perturbation: AKT-FoxO signaling manipulation
experiment.measurement: atrogin-1 and MuRF1 expression and protein breakdown

text: Hypothalamic FoxO1 promotes food intake via transcriptional induction of NPY and AgRP, and AKT-mediated inhibition of FoxO1 in NPY/AgRP neurons blocks synthesis of these peptides in response to insulin or leptin; hypothalamic mTORC1-S6K1 signaling also blocks their production.

quotes.quote:
Hypothalamic 
FoxO1 promotes food intake through the transcriptional induction of neuropeptide Y (NPY) 
and agouti-related peptide (AgRP), two major orexigenic peptides (Kim et al., 2006). AKT-
mediated inhibition of FoxO1 in NPY/AgRP-producing neurons blocks the synthesis of 
these peptides in response to insulin or leptin. The production of NPY and AgRP is also 
blocked by hypothalamic mTORC1-S6K1 signaling

experiment.system: rodent hypothalamus / NPY-AgRP neurons
experiment.perturbation: insulin or leptin stimulation; FoxO1 and mTORC1-S6K1 manipulation
experiment.measurement: NPY and AgRP expression and food intake

text: AKT signaling promotes M2 macrophage polarization, with isoform-specific differences: Akt1 null macrophages are polarized toward M1 and Akt2 null macrophages toward M2; rapamycin selectively kills human M2 macrophages while enhancing M1 polarization; and AKT-induced glucose uptake, glycolysis and cytosolic acetyl-CoA production promote M2 polarization via histone acetylation, with increased ACLY-activating phosphorylation and protein levels downstream of AKT and mTORC1.

quotes.quote:
differential effects have been reported for 
AKT isoform-specific knockouts, with Akt1 null macrophages polarized toward the M1 
state and Akt2 null macrophages toward M2 (Arranz et al., 2012; Babaev et al., 2014).

rapamycin has been found to selectively kill human M2 
macrophages, while enhancing M1 polarization (Mercalli et al., 2013).

AKT-induced glucose uptake, glycolysis, and 
production of cytosolic acetyl-CoA were recently found to promote M2 polarization by 
enhancing gene expression of specific targets in the M2 program, an effect largely attributed 
to epigenetic changes through directed histone acetylation (Covarrubias et al., 2016). An 
increase in ACLY-activating phosphorylation and protein levels downstream of AKT and 
mTORC1 were responsible for the increase in acetyl-CoA available for chromatin 
modifications.

experiment.system: mouse and human macrophages
experiment.perturbation: Akt1/Akt2 knockout; rapamycin; AKT-mTORC1-ACLY manipulation
experiment.measurement: M1/M2 polarization markers, gene expression, acetyl-CoA and histone acetylation

text: AKT signaling may suppress M1 polarization through inhibition of FoxO1, which promotes expression of key M1 genes such as TLR4.

quotes.quote:
One mechanism by which AKT signaling might suppress M1 polarization in 
favor of M2 is through its inhibition of FoxO1, which promotes the expression of key M1 
genes involved in inflammatory signaling, such as TLR4 (Fan et al., 2010).

experiment.system: macrophages
experiment.perturbation: FoxO1 manipulation
experiment.measurement: Tlr4/M1 gene expression

text: AKT isoforms have opposing functions in neutrophils: mouse genetics implicate PI3Kγ, AKT2 and GSK3 in the response to GPCR agonists including chemotaxis and respiratory burst, while Akt1-deficient neutrophils display enhanced migration and bacterial killing.

quotes.quote:
PI3Kγ, AKT2, and GSK3 are involved in the 
neutrophil response to GPCR agonists (e.g., fMLP), with mouse genetics demonstrating a 
prominent role in both neutrophil chemotaxis and induction of the respiratory burst involved 
in microbial killing

with Akt1-deficient neutrophils displaying enhanced migration 
and bacterial killing (Liu et al., 2013a)

experiment.system: mouse neutrophils
experiment.perturbation: genetic deletion of PI3Kγ/Akt isoforms; fMLP stimulation
experiment.measurement: chemotaxis, migration, respiratory burst, bacterial killing

text: In B-cell development, PI3K-AKT signaling is required for transition of pro-B cells into IgM-expressing immature B cells, requiring AKT-dependent inhibition of FoxO1, a transcriptional activator of the Rag1 and Rag2 loci.

quotes.quote:
In B-cell 
development, PI3K-AKT signaling is required for transition of pro-B cells into IgM-
expressing immature B cells (Okkenhaug et al., 2002). This process requires suppression of 
the recombination-activating gene (RAG) loci Rag1 and Rag2, which is mediated through 
AKT-dependent inhibition of FoxO1, a transcriptional activator of these genes (Amin and 
Schlissel, 2008).

experiment.system: mouse B-cell development
experiment.perturbation: PI3K-AKT/FoxO1 genetic manipulation
experiment.measurement: Rag1/Rag2 expression and pro-B to immature B cell transition

text: AKT signaling to the TSC-mTORC1 circuit and FOXO family promotes Th1, Th2 and Th17 differentiation while hindering Treg development, and mTORC1 is essential for CD8+ CTL differentiation and expansion while attenuating memory CD8+ T cell development.

quotes.quote:
The differentiation and clonal expansion of these populations involves AKT 
signaling to the TSC-mTORC1 circuit and FOXO family members, which serve to promote 
Th1, Th2 and Th17 cell differentiation while hindering the development of 
immunosuppressive Tregs

However, mTORC1 plays an essential role in the 
differentiation and expansion of CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs), while attenuating 
the development of memory CD8+ T cells (Pollizzi et al., 2015).

experiment.system: mouse CD4+ and CD8+ T cells
experiment.perturbation: genetic/pharmacological manipulation of mTOR, TSC and FOXO
experiment.measurement: T-helper subset and CTL/memory differentiation and expansion

text: Localized PI3K-AKT pathway activation and its inhibitory phosphorylation of GSK3 drives axon specification in neurites of developing neurons by activating CRMP-2, which associates with axonal growth cones in a GSK3-inhibited manner.

quotes.quote:
Localized PI3K-AKT pathway activation and its inhibitory phosphorylation of GSK3 
drives axon specification in neurites of developing neurons by activating collapsin response 
mediator protein 2 (CRMP-2), which associates with axonal growth cones in a manner that 
is inhibited by GSK3 (Jiang et al., 2005; Yoshimura et al., 2005).

experiment.system: developing neurons
experiment.perturbation: PI3K-AKT/GSK3 manipulation
experiment.measurement: axon specification and CRMP-2 activity/localization

text: In the brains of Alzheimer's patients, AKT signaling to GSK3 and mTORC1 appears elevated; GSK3 directly phosphorylates amyloid precursor protein, presenilin, and tau, though whether this GSK3 function is influenced by AKT signaling is not clear.

quotes.quote:
In the brains of Alzheimer’s patience, AKT signaling to GSK3 and 
mTORC1 appears elevated (An et al., 2003; Griffin et al., 2005).

GSK3 has been implicated in Alzheimer’s disease and directly phosphorylates several 
proteins that contribute to the pathology of the disease, including amyloid precursor protein, 
presenilin, and tau (Kaidanovich-Beilin and Woodgett, 2011) (Figure 3). However, it is not 
clear whether this function of GSK3 is influenced by AKT signaling.

experiment.system: human Alzheimer's disease brain tissue; GSK3 substrates
experiment.perturbation: observational (post-mortem comparison)
experiment.measurement: AKT/GSK3/mTORC1 pathway phosphorylation; GSK3 substrate phosphorylation

text: Gsk3αS21A; Gsk3βS9A knock-in mice are developmentally normal but sensitive to hyperactivity with anxiety-associated phenotypes in response to environmental changes and stress, while Gsk3αS21 or Gsk3β+S9 mice display anti-depression like behaviors mimicking lithium treatment.

quotes.quote:
Gsk3αS21 or Gsk3β+S9 mice display anti-
depression like behaviors that mimic those of animals on lithium, a GSK3 selective inhibitor 
used to treat mood disorders. While Gsk3αS21A; Gsk3βS9A mice are developmentally 
normal (McManus et al., 2005), they are sensitive to hyperactivity with phenotypes 
associated with anxiety in response to environmental changes and stress

experiment.system: GSK3 phosphosite knock-in mice
experiment.perturbation: knock-in mutation of AKT sites on GSK3; environmental stress; lithium comparison
experiment.measurement: behavioral phenotypes (depression-like, hyperactivity, anxiety)

text: Over 50% of human tumors display hyperactivation of AKT.

quotes.quote: Over 50% of human tumors display hyperactivation of AKT.

experiment.system: human tumors
experiment.perturbation: observational survey
experiment.measurement: frequency of AKT hyperactivation

text: The PI3K inhibitors LY294002 and wortmannin, in addition to blocking all PI3K isoforms, also directly inhibit mTOR, leading the authors to recommend they no longer be used to draw specific conclusions about PI3K or AKT function.

quotes.quote:
However, 
subsequent studies showed that both compounds, in addition to blocking all PI3K isoforms, 
also directly inhibit mTOR, which is a PI3K-related protein kinase (Brunn et al., 1996). As 
more specific and potent PI3K and AKT inhibitors have since been developed, it is highly 
recommended that wortmannin and LY294002 no longer be used to make specific

experiment.system: mTOR and PI3K enzymes/cells
experiment.perturbation: treatment with wortmannin or LY294002
experiment.measurement: inhibition of mTOR signaling functions

text: Clinical development of the pan-AKT inhibitor GSK690693 was terminated due to dose-limiting toxicities associated with hyperglycemia that are likely on target, despite preclinical efficacy.

quotes.quote:
GSK690693 
inhibits all AKT isoforms and showed efficacy in a number of preclinical studies, but dose-
limiting toxicities that are likely on target, associated with hyperglycemia, led to termination 
of the clinical development of this drug (Crouthamel et al., 2009; Rhodes et al., 2008).

experiment.system: preclinical tumor models and clinical trial patients
experiment.perturbation: GSK690693 treatment
experiment.measurement: antitumor efficacy and hyperglycemia toxicity

text: The AKT inhibitor GDC0068 (Ipatasertib) showed efficacy in preclinical models with PTEN inactivation or PIK3CA mutation, but a phase I trial did not reveal significant antitumor activity; Afuresertib/GSK2110183 inhibits AKT1 in the subnanomolar and AKT2 and AKT3 in the low nanomolar range and appears well-tolerated in phase I trials.

quotes.quote:
Although 
GDC0068 has shown efficacy in preclinical models with PTEN inactivation or PIK3CA 
mutation (Lin et al., 2013), a phase I trial did not reveal significant antitumor activity (Saura 
et al., 2017). Afuresertib or GSK2110183, which inhibits AKT1 in the subnanomolar and 
AKT2 and AKT3 in the low nanomolar range, has also shown potent activity in preclinical 
models and in phase I trials appears to be well-tolerated (Dumble et al., 2014).

experiment.system: preclinical tumor models and phase I clinical trials
experiment.perturbation: GDC0068 or afuresertib treatment
experiment.measurement: antitumor activity, potency, tolerability

text: Catalytic AKT inhibitors block substrate phosphorylation dose-dependently but protect AKT from dephosphorylation at T308 and S473 and enhance PI3,4P2 and PIP3 binding via a PH-released conformation with enhanced membrane binding; in direct comparison they show less efficacy in promoting cell death than PH-domain-targeting allosteric inhibitors.

quotes.quote:
Catalytic AKT inhibitors block the phosphorylation of downstream substrates in a dose-
dependent manner, but actually protect AKT from dephosphorylation at T308 and S473 (Lin 
et al., 2012; Okuzumi et al., 2009). Moreover, catalytic AKT inhibitors actually enhance 
PI3,4P2 and PIP3 binding, since the kinase adopts a conformation where the PH domain is 
released from its inhibitory interactions with the catalytic domain, leading to enhanced 
membrane binding (Vivanco et al., 2014). In a direct comparison, catalytic inhibitors show 
less efficacy in promoting cell death than allosteric inhibitors that target the PH domain 
(Vivanco et al., 2014)

experiment.system: cancer cells expressing AKT
experiment.perturbation: catalytic vs allosteric AKT inhibitor treatment
experiment.measurement: AKT phosphorylation, lipid/membrane binding, substrate phosphorylation, cell death

text: The allosteric AKT inhibitor MK2206 induces robust cancer cell death alone and in combination, but has not shown significant efficacy in the clinic as single agent therapy; the constitutively membrane-bound AKT E17K allele is less sensitive to MK2206.

quotes.quote:
MK2206 is a specific, potent and orally bioavailable allosteric AKT inhibitor that targets 
both the PH and catalytic domains (Hirai et al., 2010) and induces robust cancer cell death 
both alone and in combination with other compounds (Wisinski et al., 2016). As single agent 
therapy, however, MK2206 has not shown significant efficacy in the clinic (Ma et al., 2016).

Consistent with the notion that the 
AKT E17K mutation is constitutively membrane bound, this oncogenic AKT allele is less 
sensitive to MK2206 (Parikh et al., 2012).

experiment.system: cancer cell lines and clinical trials
experiment.perturbation: MK2206 treatment; AKT E17K expression
experiment.measurement: cell death, clinical efficacy, inhibitor sensitivity

text: In trials selecting patients for pathway mutations such as AKT1 E17K, a number of patients showed partial responses when treated with AZD5363; separately, relief of feedback inhibition in AKT inhibitor-treated tumors causes a rebound with robust PI3K pathway activation, and increased expression of SGK isoforms is a resistance mechanism.

quotes.quote: In trials where patients were selected for the presence

of pathway mutations, for example the AKT1 E17K mutation, a number of patients showed 
partial responses when treated with AZD5363 (Davies et al., 2012). Moreover, the relief of 
feedback inhibition in tumors treated with AKT inhibitors leads to a rebound effect resulting 
in robust PI3K pathway activation, thereby limiting the efficacy of such inhibitors, at least as 
single agents (Chandarlapaty et al., 2011).

These resistance mechanisms include increased expression of 
SGK isoforms (Bago et al., 2016; Sommer et al., 2013)

experiment.system: patients with pathway-mutant tumors; tumor models
experiment.perturbation: AZD5363/AKT inhibitor treatment with mutation-based patient selection
experiment.measurement: clinical response, PI3K pathway rebound, SGK expression

text: PI3K pathway mutations such as oncogenic PIK3CA do not always coincide with elevated AKT phosphorylation, with other PI3K effectors such as SGK isoforms driving downstream signaling in some settings.

quotes.quote:
Importantly, PI3K pathway mutations, such as 
oncogenic PIK3CA, do not always coincide with elevated phosphorylation of AKT, with 
other PI3K effectors such as SGK isoforms driving downstream signaling in some settings 
(Vasudevan et al., 2009).

experiment.system: PIK3CA-mutant cancer cells
experiment.perturbation: observational comparison of PIK3CA mutation status
experiment.measurement: AKT phosphorylation and SGK-driven downstream signaling

text: The review reports that gain-of-function alleles of Ras, Raf, MEK, or ERK can compensate for defects in ligand or receptor in the Let-23, sevenless, and torso signaling pathways.

quotes.quote:
Strikingly 
for the Let-23, sevenless, and torso signaling pathways, 
defects in ligand or receptor can be compensated for by 
gain-of-function alleles of Ras (Fortini et al., 1992), Raf 
(Dickson et al., 1992; Han et al., 1994), MEK (Tsuda et 
al., 1993), or extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) 
(Brunner et al., 1994b), all of which lie in the same signaling 
pathway

experiment.system: C. elegans Let-23 and Drosophila sevenless/torso receptor tyrosine kinase pathways
experiment.perturbation: gain-of-function alleles of Ras, Raf, MEK, or ERK in ligand/receptor-defective backgrounds
experiment.measurement: genetic rescue of cell fate determination defects

text: Expression of constitutively activated MEK generated by site-directed mutagenesis induces mitogenesis and transformation in fibroblasts and differentiation of PC12 cells.

quotes.quote:
expression of constitutively acti- 
vated forms of MEK, generated by site-directed mutagene- 
sis, induces mitogenesis and transformation in fibroblasts 
as well as differentiation of PC12 cells (Cowley et al., 1994; 
Mansour et al., 1994)

experiment.perturbation: expression of site-directed constitutively activated MEK mutants
experiment.measurement: mitogenesis/transformation and differentiation

text: MEK is activated by Raf phosphorylation of two serine residues four amino acids apart in kinase subdomain VIII, and substituting these residues with acidic amino acids leads to partial activation of MEK.

quotes.quote:
Activation of MEK has 
been shown to result from phosphorylation by Raf of two 
serine residues that are four amino acids apart in kinase 
subdomain VIII

Substitu- 
tion of the serine or threonine residues in this consensus 
with acidic amino acids to mimic phosphorylation leads 
to partial activation in MEK

experiment.perturbation: Raf phosphorylation; substitution of consensus Ser/Thr with acidic residues
experiment.measurement: MEK kinase activation; sequence comparison of MAPKK family

numbers.quantity: spacing of the two serine residues

text: Raf activation by receptor tyrosine kinases requires two signals: Ras recruits Raf to the plasma membrane, where another, unknown tyrosine kinase-generated signal fully activates it.

quotes.quote:
Recent work demonstrates that the role of 
Ras is to recruit Raf to the plasma membrane (Leevers 
et al., 1994; Stokoe et al., 1994), where another tyrosine 
kinase-generated signal fully activates the membrane- 
bound Raf

one signal is the forma- 
tion of RasGTP, while the other is unknown

experiment.system: mammalian cells with receptor tyrosine kinase signaling
experiment.perturbation: membrane targeting of Raf / Ras activation
experiment.measurement: Raf kinase activation

text: In PC12 cells, NGF gives persistent elevation of RasGTP and ERK activation sustained for several hours, whereas EGF gives only short-lived RasGTP rise and short-lived ERK activation; NGF but not EGF stimulates tyrosine phosphorylation of an 80 kDa protein, SNT.

quotes.quote:
NGF stimulation 
results in a persistent elevation of RasGTP, whereas EGF 
produces only a short-lived rise in RasGTP (Muroya et 
al., 1992). ERK (MAPK) activation is sustained for several 
hours following NGF stimulation, but it is short lived after 
EGF stimulation

the NGF, but not the EGF, stimulation 
of tyrosine phosphorylation of an 80 kDa protein, SNT

experiment.perturbation: NGF versus EGF stimulation

text: Manipulating receptor number in PC12 cells changes ERK duration and outcome: transfected PDGF receptor, overexpressed insulin receptor, and overexpressed EGF receptor each give sustained ERK activation and differentiation, while PC12 lines with reduced TrkA-NGF receptor number show transient ERK activation and proliferate in response to NGF.

quotes.quote:
transfection of platelet-derived 
growth factor receptor constructs leads to PDGF-depen- 
dent differentiation and sustained activation of ERKs 
(Heasley and Johnson, 1992). The endogenous insulin 
receptor of PC12 cells does not trigger RasGTP loading, 
ERK activation, or differentiation (Ohmichi et al., 1993); 
however, if it is overexpressed, ERK is activated and differ- 
entiation results

In 
these cells, the number of TrkA-NGF receptor molecules 
per cell is reduced, ERK activation is transient, and the 
response to NGF is proliferation

text: Interfering MEK1 mutants block ligand activation of ERK and PC12 differentiation, while activating MEK mutants induce neurite outgrowth without differentiating factors; this induction is not blocked by microinjection of Ras neutralizing antibodies that block ligand-activated differentiation.

quotes.quote:
The 
interfering mutants block ligand activation of ERK and 
block differentiation of PC12 cells, whereas the activating 
mutants induce neurite outgrowth in the absence of differ- 
entiating factors (Cowley et al., 1994)

induction of differentiation by activated MEK is 
not blocked by microinjection of Ras neutralizing antibod- 
ies, which block ligand-activated differentiation

quotes.quote:
In every 
case examined thus far in PC12 cells, sustained ERK acti- 
vation is associated with translocation of ERKs to the nu- 
cleus (Traverse et al., 1992, 1994; Nguyen et al., 1993; 
Dikic et al., 1994), whereas transient activation does not 
lead to nuclear translocation.

the 
quantitative difference in ERK activation is translated into 
a qualitative difference in transcription factor activation

A serious limitation in applying this model to other sys- 
tems is that it is based wholly on experiments with PC12 
cells.

it is clear that in fibroblasts, sustained 
activation of ERKs is associated with proliferation, not dif- 
ferentiation (Meloche et al., 1992; Mansour et al., 1994;

text: Recruitment of PI3-kinase p85 subunits to the NGF receptor or the fibroblast growth factor receptor is reported to be unnecessary for PC12 differentiation and not to affect ERK activation.

PI3-kinase activation by recruitment of 
p85 subunits to either the NGF receptor or the fibroblast 
growth factor receptor is not necessary for the differentia- 
tion response of PC12 cells and does not appear to affect 
ERK activation (Obermeier et al., 1994; Spivak-Kroizman 
et al., 1994)

text: Mice lacking the integrin β6 subunit develop exaggerated inflammatory responses in lungs and skin but are protected from tissue fibrosis in multiple tissues, phenotypes consistent with a deficit in TGF-β.

Integrin β6 (Itgb6) knockout mice develop exaggerated inflammatory 
responses in the lungs and skin but are protected from tissue fibrosis in multiple tissues.33-35 
Both phenotypic features are consistent with a deficit in TGF-β.

Mice lacking Itgb8 die during 
embryonic development or immediately after birth from intracerebral hemorrhage caused by 
defective vascular development in the central nervous system.37 Intracerebral hemorrhage in 
these mice is caused by the absence of αvβ8 on neuroepithelial cells which activates TGF-β 
for presentation to endothelial cells.38
