experiment.perturbation: germline/cell-type deletion of Itgb8
experiment.measurement: survival, intracerebral hemorrhage, CNS vascular development

text: Blocking αvβ6 antibody in Itgb8 knockout mice bred to bypass perinatal mortality, or crossing to Itgb6-null mice, recapitulates most developmental phenotypes of TGF-β1 and TGF-β3 knockout mice, including severe multiorgan inflammation and cleft palate.

quotes.quote:
Administration of αvβ6 blocking antibody to Itgb8 knockout mice bred 
to bypass perinatal mortality, or crossing these mice to mice lacking Itgb6 recapitulates 
most of the developmental phenotypes of mice lacking TGF-β1 and TGF-β3.40 These 
phenotypes include severe multiorgan inflammation (a central feature of TGF-β1 knockout 
mice) and cleft palate (seen in TGF-β3 knockout mice).

experiment.system: Itgb8 knockout mice; Itgb6/Itgb8 double-deficient mice
experiment.perturbation: αvβ6 blocking antibody or Itgb6 deletion on Itgb8-null background
experiment.measurement: developmental phenotypes (multiorgan inflammation, cleft palate)

text: Deletion of the integrin αv subunit from fibroblasts or treatment with a small molecule αvβ1 inhibitor gives equivalent protection from hepatic and pulmonary fibrosis, supporting αvβ1 as the main TGF-β activating integrin in fibroblasts.

quotes.quote:
Equivalent protection from hepatic and pulmonary fibrosis by deletion of the 
integrin αv subunit from fibroblasts or treating mice with a small molecule inhibitor to 
the αvβ1 integrin support the idea that αvβ1 is the main TGF-β activating integrin in 
fibroblasts.41

experiment.system: mouse models of hepatic and pulmonary fibrosis
experiment.perturbation: fibroblast-specific αv deletion or small-molecule αvβ1 inhibitor
experiment.measurement: fibrosis protection

text: Deletion of LTBP1 inhibits αvβ6-mediated TGF-β activation, and the defect is rescued by a fusion protein of the LAP-tethering and fibronectin-binding domains of LTBP1.

quotes.quote:
Deletion of LTBP1, required for tethering the latent complex to the extracellular matrix, also 
inhibits αvβ6-mediated TGF-β activation, and this defect can be rescued by a fusion protein 
composed of the LAP-tethering and fibronectin-binding domains of LTBP1.45

experiment.system: cells with latent TGF-β and αvβ6
experiment.perturbation: LTBP1 deletion and rescue with LTBP1 domain fusion protein
experiment.measurement: TGF-β activation

text: TGF-β activation by αvβ8 is retained after deletion of the entire β8 cytoplasmic domain; cryo-EM data and activation of a mutant latent TGF-β that cannot release cytokine from LAP suggest αvβ8 induces a conformational change allowing receptor binding without release.

quotes.quote:
TGF-β activation 
by integrin αvβ8 is retained even after the entire β8 cytoplasmic domain is deleted. 
Recent high resolution cryo-EM structural data, together with studies showing that αvβ8 
can activate a mutant form of latent TGF-β that cannot release the active cytokine from 
LAP, suggest that αvβ8 binding to LAP induces a conformational change in the latent 
complex that allows the captive TGF-β to bind to its receptors without release from LAP.46

experiment.system: αvβ8-expressing cells and latent TGF-β complexes
experiment.perturbation: β8 cytoplasmic domain deletion; non-releasable latent TGF-β mutant; cryo-EM structure determination
experiment.measurement: TGF-β activation and complex conformation

text: Deletion of Itgb8 from neuroepithelial cells produces a phenotype very similar to deletion of TGF-β receptors in microglia, which do not express Itgb8.

quotes.quote:
deletion of Itgb8 from neuroepithelial cells results in 
a very similar phenotype as deletion of TGF-β receptors in microglia, which do not express 
Itgb8.47

experiment.system: conditional knockout mice
experiment.perturbation: neuroepithelial Itgb8 deletion vs microglial TGF-β receptor deletion
experiment.measurement: phenotype comparison

text: Mammalian genomes include 7 type I receptors and 5 type II receptors bound in pairwise combinations by specific TGF-β family ligands.

quotes.quote:
Mammalian genomes include 7 type I receptors 
and 5 type II receptors9 which are bound in various pairwise combinations by specific 
ligands

experiment.system: mammalian genomes
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: count of type I and type II receptor genes

text: Receptor-activated SMAD complexes bind hundreds of genomic loci where CDK8 and CDK9 phosphorylate the SMAD linker, stimulating transcriptional activity, while GSK3β-mediated linker phosphorylation creates binding sites for SMURF1/2 and NEDD4L that mark SMADs for degradation.

quotes.quote:
Receptor-activated SMAD complexes bind to hundreds of genomic loci in the nucleus, 
where SMADs undergo phosphorylation at the linker region by the RNA polymerase 
II (RNAPII) kinases CDK8 and CDK9.56 This stimulates the transcriptional activity of 
SMAD complexes while leading to further phosphorylation of the linker by glycogen 
synthase kinase 3β. GSK3β creates binding sites for the HECT domain ubiquitin ligases 
SMURF1/2 (in SMAD1 and 5) and NEDD4L (in SMAD2 and 3) to mark the activated 
SMADs for degradation.

experiment.system: SMAD transcriptional complexes in cells
experiment.perturbation: observational/biochemical analysis of kinases and ubiquitin ligases
experiment.measurement: SMAD linker phosphorylation, transcriptional activity, degradation

text: All R-SMADs and SMAD4 bind with similar affinity to 5-bp GC-rich motif variants including CAGAC and GGCGC, so DNA binding alone is insufficient to dictate pathway- and cell-type-specific target gene choice.

quotes.quote:
all R-SMADs and SMAD4 bind with similar affinity 
to 5-bp GC-rich motif variants including CAGAC, GGCGC, and others.94 Although the 
DNA binding activity of SMADs is necessary for their function, it is insufficient to dictate 
pathway-specific and cell-type specific choice of TGF-β target genes.

experiment.system: purified SMAD proteins and DNA motifs
experiment.perturbation: observational binding assays
experiment.measurement: DNA binding affinity to GC-rich motifs

text: Tgfb1 knockout mice die of multiorgan inflammation early in life, a phenotype substantially rescued by loss of MHC class II; T cell-specific deletion of Tgfbr2 early in development causes a similar phenotype.

quotes.quote:
These roles were apparent in Tgfb1 knockout 
mice, which die of multiorgan inflammation early in life.104 This phenotype is substantially 
rescued by loss of MHC class II,105 ... T cell–specific deletion of Tgfbr2 early in development causes 
a similar phenotype,106,107

experiment.system: Tgfb1 knockout and T cell-specific Tgfbr2 knockout mice
experiment.perturbation: gene deletion; combined loss of MHC class II
experiment.measurement: multiorgan inflammation and survival

text: Deletion of Tgfbr2 from dendritic cells in mice leads to multiorgan inflammation and death by 15 weeks of age; TGFBR2-deficient DCs express normal MHC class II and costimulatory molecules but produce more IFN-γ and have reduced ability to induce Treg cells.

quotes.quote:
Deletion of Tgfbr2 from DCs in mice leads to multiorgan inflammation and death 
by 15 weeks of age.113 DCs lacking TGFBR2 express normal levels of MHC class II and 
costimulatory molecules but produce more interferon γ (IFN-γ), which reduces their ability 
to induce Treg cells.

experiment.system: mice with DC-specific Tgfbr2 deletion
experiment.perturbation: conditional Tgfbr2 deletion in dendritic cells
experiment.measurement: survival, inflammation, MHC II/costimulatory expression, IFN-γ production, Treg induction

text: Loss of Itgb8 in RORγt+ thetis cells causes colitis, and these cells require TGF-β-activating integrin αvβ8 for intestinal pTreg differentiation.

quotes.quote:
a subtype of 
RORγt + antigen-presenting cells, called thetis cells (TC), induce pTreg differentiation in 
intestinal lymph nodes during early life and require TGF-β-activating integrin αvβ8 for 
intestinal pTreg differentiation. Loss of Itgb8 in these cells causes colitis

experiment.system: mice with Itgb8 deletion in RORγt+ thetis cells
experiment.perturbation: conditional Itgb8 deletion
experiment.measurement: intestinal pTreg differentiation and colitis

text: Disabling TGF-β signaling in CD4+ cells of mammary tumor-bearing mice augmented IL-4 production in TH2 cells but not IFN-γ production in TH1 cells, leading to tumor regression.

quotes.quote:
Disabling 
TGF-β signaling in CD4+ cells in mammary tumor-bearing mice augmented IL-4 production 
in TH2 cells (but not IFN-γ production in TH1 cells) leading to tumor regression.119

experiment.system: mammary tumor-bearing mice
experiment.perturbation: disabling TGF-β signaling in CD4+ T cells
experiment.measurement: IL-4 and IFN-γ production; tumor growth

text: Mice lacking TGFBR2 on T cells or lacking integrin αvβ8 on DCs have reduced numbers of TH17 cells and are protected from Experimental Autoimmune Encephalomyelitis; TGF-β-blocking antibody also protects against EAE while T cell overexpression of active TGF-β exacerbates CNS inflammation and EAE.

quotes.quote:
Mice lacking TGFBR2 on T cells and mice lacking 
the TGF-β activating integrin αvβ8 on DCs have reduced numbers of TH17 cells and are 
protected from developing Experimental Autoimmune Encephalomyelitis (EAE)

TGF-β-blocking antibody also protects against EAE 
while overexpression of active TGF-β by T cells exacerbates CNS inflammation and 
EAE.122

experiment.system: mouse EAE model
experiment.perturbation: T cell Tgfbr2 deletion, DC αvβ8 loss, TGF-β blocking antibody, T cell overexpression of active TGF-β
experiment.measurement: TH17 cell numbers and EAE disease severity

text: Low TGF-β concentrations inhibit IL-23 receptor expression and favor Foxp3, whereas high concentrations with IL-6 upregulate the IL-23 receptor and favor RORγt expression and TH17 induction in naive CD4+ T cells.

quotes.quote:
Low TGF-β concentrations inhibit the expression of the IL-23 receptor and favor 
Foxp3 expression, while high concentrations in conjunction with IL-6 upregulate the IL-23 
receptor and favor RORγt expression and TH17 cell induction.120

experiment.system: naïve CD4+ T cells
experiment.perturbation: varying TGF-β concentration with or without IL-6
experiment.measurement: IL-23 receptor, Foxp3 and RORγt expression; TH17 induction

text: Mice lacking TGF-β1 or TGFBR2 in T cells display marked reductions in peripheral FOXP3+ Treg cell numbers, and TGF-β-activated SMADs cooperate with STAT5 and NFAT to induce FOXP3 expression in naive CD4+ T cells.

quotes.quote:
TGF-β-activated SMADs cooperate with STAT5 and nuclear factor of 
activated T cells (NFAT) to induce expression of FOXP3 in naive CD4+ T cells125 ... Mice lacking TGF-β1 or TGFBR2 in T cells display marked reductions in FOXP3+ Treg 
cell numbers in the periphery

experiment.system: mice with T cell-specific TGF-β1 or Tgfbr2 deletion; naive CD4+ T cells
experiment.perturbation: gene deletion; TGF-β stimulation
experiment.measurement: peripheral FOXP3+ Treg numbers; FOXP3 induction

text: Mice lacking a Foxp3 enhancer required for TGF-β-mediated pTreg induction do not develop the severe early-onset multiorgan inflammation of mice lacking all Treg cells, but older mice lacking pTreg cells develop TH2-mediated pathology in lung and intestine.

quotes.quote:
Mice lacking a particular Foxp3 enhancer that is required 
for TGF-β-mediated pTreg induction do not develop the severe, early-onset multiorgan 
inflammation seen in mice lacking all Treg cells ... However, older mice lacking pTreg cells develop TH2-mediated 
pathology in lung and intestine,128

experiment.system: mice lacking a Foxp3 enhancer (pTreg-deficient)
experiment.perturbation: genetic deletion of a Foxp3 enhancer
experiment.measurement: multiorgan inflammation; lung and intestinal TH2-mediated pathology with age

text: Complete loss of TGF-β signaling in T cells inhibits CD8+ T cell development, whereas expression of dominant-negative TGFBR2 leads to expansion of CD8+ T cells.

quotes.quote:
In vivo, expression of a CD2-driven or CD4-driven dominant-negative TGFBR2 construct, 
which reduces TGF-β signaling, leads to expansion of CD8+ T cells. However, complete 
loss of TGF-β signaling in T cells inhibits CD8+ T cell development,107

experiment.system: mice
experiment.perturbation: CD2- or CD4-driven dominant-negative TGFBR2; complete loss of T cell TGF-β signaling
experiment.measurement: CD8+ T cell development and expansion

text: TGF-β suppresses cytotoxic T cell effector functions by inhibiting expression of perforin, IFN-γ, and granzymes A and B through SMADs partnered with ATF1.

quotes.quote:
TGF-β 
suppresses multiple effector functions of cytotoxic T cells, inhibiting expression of perforin, 
IFN-γ and granzymes A and B through SMADs in partnership with ATF1.130

experiment.system: cytotoxic CD8+ T cells
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β treatment
experiment.measurement: perforin, IFN-γ, granzyme A/B expression

text: TGF-β suppresses NK cell function by inhibiting NKG2D and NKp30 expression, inducing mir-183 which reduces DAP12, and inhibiting activating responses to IL-15.

quotes.quote:
TGF-β inhibits the expression of cell-surface 
receptors NKG2D and NKp30 ... TGF-β also induces the expression mir-183 in NK cells, which 
reduces expression of the adaptor protein, DAP12, thus inhibiting responses to cytotoxic 
NK receptors including NKG2D.134 TGF-β further suppresses NK cell activity by inhibiting 
activating responses to IL-15.135

experiment.system: NK cells
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β treatment
experiment.measurement: NKG2D/NKp30 expression, mir-183 and DAP12 levels, IL-15 responses

text: Mice lacking TGFBR2 in myeloid cells show increased anti-tumor immunity, decreased tumor growth and metastasis, and increased predisposition to stroke, effects attributed to increased pro-inflammatory cytokine production by macrophages.

quotes.quote:
Mice 
lacking TGFBR2 in myeloid cells demonstrate increased anti-tumor immunity, decreased 
tumor growth and metastasis and an increased predisposition to stroke.140,141
the decrease in metastases

verdict_note: The paper attributes only the decreased metastases and the stroke predisposition to increased pro-inflammatory cytokine production by TGF-β-unresponsive macrophages, and explicitly notes that 'the mechanisms underlying these events differ among models'; the claim generalizes this mechanism to all the listed phenotypes (including increased anti-tumor immunity and decreased tumor growth) and drops the caveat.

experiment.system: mice with myeloid-specific Tgfbr2 deletion
experiment.perturbation: conditional Tgfbr2 deletion in myeloid cells
experiment.measurement: anti-tumor immunity, tumor growth and metastasis, stroke predisposition

text: Deletion of αvβ8 from neuroepithelial cells or of Tgfbr2 or Tgfb1 in microglia each cause progressive motor defects and persistence of dysmature microglia, phenotypes rescued by post-natal deletion of microglia; adult macrophage Tgfbr2 deletion changes gene expression without dramatic functional impairment.

quotes.quote:
Deletion of αvβ8 
from neuroepithelial cells or deletion of Tgfbr2 or Tgfb1 in microglia each lead to the 
same phenotype of profound and progressive motor defects and persistence of dysmature 
microglia.47 The motor defects and many of the associated anatomic abnormalities in the 
brains of these mice can be rescued by post-natal deletion of microglia.

deletion of Tgfbr2 from macrophages of adult mice results in many of the same changes in 
macrophage gene expression without dramatic functional impairment.143

experiment.system: conditional knockout mice (neuroepithelium, microglia, adult macrophages)
experiment.perturbation: deletion of Itgb8/Tgfbr2/Tgfb1; post-natal microglia depletion
experiment.measurement: motor function, microglial maturation, macrophage gene expression

text: Fibrillar collagens produced abundantly in TGF-β activated fibroblasts have a high content (10%) of proline, and TGF-β supports collagen production by increasing mitochondrial oxidation of glucose and glutamine to drive proline biosynthesis.

quotes.quote:
Fibrillar collagens are produced abundantly in TGF-β activated fibroblasts and 
have a high content (10%) of proline. TGF-β supports the bioenergetic demands of 
collagen production by increasing the mitochondrial oxidation of glucose and glutamine. 
Mitochondrial redox generation promotes proline biosynthesis from glutamine for collagen 
production while preventing the generation of deleterious reactive oxygen species.149

experiment.system: TGF-β activated fibroblasts
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β treatment
experiment.measurement: collagen proline content, mitochondrial glucose/glutamine oxidation, proline biosynthesis

text: Injection of TGF-β1 into skin or transgenic/adenoviral overexpression of TGF-β in lung causes extensive tissue fibrosis, and TGF-β-blocking antibodies prevent fibrosis in skin, liver, lung, and kidney.

quotes.quote:
Injection of TGF-β1 into the skin or transgenic 
or adenovirus-mediated overexpression of TGF-β in the lung cause extensive tissue 
fibrosis.154,155 TGF-β-blocking antibodies prevent fibrosis in the skin, liver, lung, and 
kidney.13

experiment.system: mouse skin, lung, liver, kidney
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β1 injection or overexpression; TGF-β-blocking antibodies
experiment.measurement: tissue fibrosis

text: Deletion of TGF-β receptors from epithelial cells inhibits pulmonary fibrosis induced by intratracheal bleomycin.

quotes.quote:
deletion of TGF-β receptors from epithelial cells inhibits pulmonary 
fibrosis induced by intratracheal delivery of bleomycin.158

experiment.system: mouse bleomycin lung fibrosis model
experiment.perturbation: epithelial deletion of TGF-β receptors
experiment.measurement: pulmonary fibrosis

text: Induction of SOX4 by TGF-β in pancreatic epithelial progenitors requires SMAD2 and SMAD3 but not SMAD4, in line with the requirement of SMAD2 and SMAD3, but not SMAD4, for pancreas development.

quotes.quote:
induction of 
the transcription factor SOX4 by TGF-β in pancreatic epithelial progenitors requires SMAD2 
and SMAD3 but not SMAD4.82 This is in line with the requirement of SMAD2 and 
SMAD3, but not SMAD4, for pancreas development.83,84

experiment.system: pancreatic epithelial progenitors; mouse pancreas development
experiment.perturbation: loss of SMAD2/SMAD3 or SMAD4
experiment.measurement: TGF-β-induced SOX4 expression; pancreas development

text: Loss of Tgfbr2 accelerates tumor progression in pancreatic, intestinal, oral mucosa, and skin epithelia harboring KRAS or HRAS oncogenes, while conditional ablation of Tgfbr2 or Smad4 alone causes only mild hyperplasia; pre-malignant progenitors with KRAS or HRAS mutations undergo apoptosis in response to TGF-β.

quotes.quote:
Conditional ablation of Tgfbr2 or Smad4 in pancreatic, intestinal, oral mucosa, and skin 
epithelia in mice does not interfere with the development of these tissues and causes 
only a mild hyperplasia. However, loss of Tgfbr2 accelerates tumor progression when 
these tissues harbor KRAS or HRAS oncogenes.83,185,188,189

pre-malignant pancreatic, 
intestinal, and skin epithelial progenitors with KRAS or HRAS mutations undergo 
apoptosis in response to TGF-β

experiment.system: genetically engineered mouse models of PDAC, CRC, skin and oral tumors
experiment.perturbation: conditional Tgfbr2 or Smad4 ablation with KRAS/HRAS oncogenes
experiment.measurement: tissue hyperplasia, tumor progression, apoptosis of pre-malignant progenitors

text: In pre-malignant pancreatic cells with mutant Kras, dysregulated MAPKs activate RREB1, which pairs with TGF-β-activated SMADs to induce SNAIL and an EMT; SNAIL inhibits KLF5, driving SOX4 to activate Bim and other pro-apoptotic genes.

quotes.quote:
In pre-malignant pancreatic cells with mutant Kras, the dysregulated 
MAPKs strongly activate RREB1, which pairs with TGF-β-activated SMADs to trigger 
an intense induction of SNAIL expression and an EMT (Figure 5B). As a transcriptional 
repressor of epithelial genes, SNAIL inhibits KLF5 expression, driving SOX4 to activate
the expression of Bim and other pro-apoptotic genes.

experiment.system: normal and pre-malignant pancreatic epithelial progenitors with mutant Kras
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β stimulation on Kras-mutant background
experiment.measurement: RREB1/SMAD-driven SNAIL, KLF5, SOX4 and pro-apoptotic gene expression; apoptosis

text: Analysis of TGF-β pathway alterations in 9,125 tumors across 33 cancer types profiled by The Cancer Genome Atlas showed these alterations are frequent in carcinomas of pancreas, gastrointestinal tract, lungs, breast, bladder, prostate, endometrium and head and neck, as well as low-grade gliomas and diffuse large B-cell lymphomas, and are mostly loss-of-function.

quotes.quote: Analysis of pathway mutations, copy-

number changes, and other genetic alterations in 9,125 tumors profiled by The Cancer 
Genome Atlas in 33 cancer types showed that these alterations are frequent in carcinomas 
of the pancreas, gastrointestinal tract, lungs, breast, bladder, prostate, endometrium, and 
head and neck, as well as in low-grade gliomas and diffuse large B-cell lymphomas.206 
Most of these alterations are loss-of-function events selected during tumor progression.

experiment.system: TCGA tumor cohort
experiment.perturbation: observational genomic profiling
experiment.measurement: frequency of TGF-β pathway mutations and copy-number alterations

text: Restoring SMAD4 expression in PDAC tumor cells that developed with Smad4 loss makes these cells undergo massive apoptosis in response to TGF-β; PDACs with intact TGF-β components lack apoptotic responses due to TGF-β-SMAD upregulation of ID1, which decouples EMT from apoptosis by neutralizing SOX4.

quotes.quote:
Restoring SMAD4 expression in PDAC tumor cells that developed with Smad4 loss makes 
these cells undergo massive apoptosis in response to TGF-β.82,209

In these cells, TGF-β-SMAD signaling 
upregulates ID1 expression, which decouples EMT from apoptosis by neutralizing the 
effects of SOX4.

experiment.system: PDAC tumor cells
experiment.perturbation: SMAD4 re-expression; TGF-β treatment
experiment.measurement: apoptosis; ID1 expression and EMT/apoptosis coupling

text: Human HNSCCs show early-stage SMAD4 loss and mice with Smad4 deletion develop spontaneous HNSCCs and genomic instability; SMAD4 loss is associated with decreased BRCA1 expression, elevated mutational burden, and sensitivity to PARP inhibitors.

quotes.quote:
human head and neck squamous cell carcinomas (HNSCCs) show loss of 
SMAD4 at an early-stage, and mice with Smad4 deletion develop spontaneous HNSCCs 
and genomic instability, suggesting that loss of SMAD4 is a tumor-initiating event in 
this context.210 In these tumors, SMAD4 loss is associated with decreased expression of 
BRCA1 and an elevated mutational burden accompanied with sensitivity to PARP inhibitors.

experiment.system: human HNSCC samples and Smad4-deleted mice
experiment.perturbation: Smad4 deletion; PARP inhibitor treatment
experiment.measurement: tumor formation, genomic instability, BRCA1 expression, mutational burden, drug sensitivity

text: In mouse models of HER2+ breast cancer, expression of a constitutively active Tgfbr1 transgene in mammary epithelial cells decreased mammary tumor growth rate but accelerated lung metastasis.

quotes.quote:
In mouse models of HER2+ breast cancer, expression of a constitutively active Tgfbr1 
transgene in mammary epithelial cells decreased the growth rate of mammary tumors but 
accelerated lung metastasis from these tumors.200

experiment.system: mouse models of HER2+ breast cancer
experiment.perturbation: mammary epithelial expression of constitutively active Tgfbr1 transgene
experiment.measurement: tumor growth rate and lung metastasis

text: Approximately half of solid tumors are histologically 'immune excluded' with CD8+ T cells around the tumor periphery in a dense collagen band; these tumors are generally resistant to checkpoint inhibitors and show gene expression suggestive of increased TGF-β signaling.

quotes.quote:
Approximately half of solid tumors can be characterized histologically as “immune 
excluded”, in which CD8+ T cells accumulate around the periphery of the tumor in a 
dense collagen-containing band but fail to infiltrate the tumor itself. These tumors are 
generally resistant to checkpoint inhibitors and exhibit a gene expression pattern suggestive 
of increased TGF-β signaling.

experiment.system: human solid tumors
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: histological CD8+ T cell distribution, checkpoint inhibitor response, TGF-β gene expression signature

numbers.quantity: proportion of solid tumors that are immune excluded

text: In syngeneic murine models, TGF-β inhibitor treatment can induce immune checkpoint sensitivity in immune-excluded tumors, promoting CD8+ T cell infiltration into the tumor core, increasing granzyme B and interferon production, and in many cases inducing long-term anti-tumor immunity; similar effects follow inhibition of the αvβ8 integrin.

quotes.quote:
Recent evidence from syngeneic murine models suggests 
that immune checkpoint sensitivity can be induced in some immune-excluded tumors by 
treatment with TGF-β inhibitors. This treatment promotes CD8+ T cell infiltration into the 
core of the tumor, increases granzyme B and interferon production by infiltrating T cells 
and in many cases leads to induction of long-term anti-tumor immunity.192,214,215 Similar 
effects can be caused by inhibition of the TGF-β-activating αvβ8 integrin,216-218

experiment.system: syngeneic mouse tumor models
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β inhibitors or αvβ8 integrin inhibition with checkpoint blockade
experiment.measurement: CD8+ T cell infiltration, granzyme B/interferon production, anti-tumor immunity

text: TGF-β signaling in cancer cells in an orthotopic mammary tumor model promoted local invasion and hematogenous dissemination by inducing EMT and a switch from cohesive to single-cell motility, and activation of platelet-stored TGF-β coating colon cancer cells induced EMT and extravasation in mouse lungs.

quotes.quote:
TGF-β 
signaling in cancer cells in an orthotopic mammary tumor model promoted local invasion 
and hematogenous dissemination by inducing EMT and a switch from cohesive cell motility 
to single-cell motility.228 ... The activation of TGF-β stored in blood platelets coating colon 
cancer cells induced EMT and extravasation of cancer cell in the lungs of mice.229

experiment.system: orthotopic mouse mammary tumor model; colon cancer cells in mice
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β signaling/platelet-derived TGF-β activation
experiment.measurement: invasion, motility mode, dissemination, extravasation

text: In mouse models of metastatic dormancy, disseminated tumor cells localize to perivascular regions and remain dormant for many months, entering quiescence in response to TGF-β and autocrine WNT inhibition; quiescent cells downregulate MHC class I, NK receptor ligands and STING to evade immunity and are cleared upon cycle reentry.

quotes.quote:
In mouse models of metastatic dormancy, disseminated 
tumor cells localize to perivascular regions where they are able to remain dormant for 
many months.201,234 ... are primed to enter quiescence in 
response to TGF-β and autocrine WNT inhibition.202,234,235

Quiescent cells downregulate MHC class I molecules,236,237 NK receptor ligands234 and 
STING (stimulator of interferon genes)202 to evade elimination by the immune system. 
Dormant cancer cells reentering the cycle re-express these mediators of immune recognition 
and consequently are cleared by the combined action of T cells and NK cells.

experiment.system: mouse models of metastatic dormancy
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β signaling and WNT inhibition in disseminated tumor cells
experiment.measurement: dormancy duration/localization, MHC I, NK ligand and STING expression, immune clearance

text: A 12-week phase 2 study of a dual αvβ1/αvβ6 small-molecule inhibitor in 67 patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis showed no significant on-target toxicity and apparent dose-dependent efficacy in slowing loss of lung function and radiographic fibrosis progression.

quotes.quote:
recently released data for a 12-week phase 2 study of the αvβ1/αvβ6 
inhibitor in 67 patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis showed no significant on-target 
toxicity and an apparent dose dependent efficacy in slowing the rate of loss of lung function 
and progression of radiographic evidence of fibrosis.

experiment.system: patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
experiment.perturbation: dual small-molecule αvβ1/αvβ6 inhibitor, 12 weeks
experiment.measurement: on-target toxicity, rate of lung function loss, radiographic fibrosis progression

text: EGCG protects mice from bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis; upon covalent inhibition of LOXL2 the compound is converted into a potent irreversible inhibitor of TGFBR2, and biopsies from patients who received EGCG showed significant reductions in extractable collagen and other indicators of active fibrosis compared with placebo.

quotes.quote:
the identification of epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) as a natural product found in several 
fruits and green teas which protects mice from bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis.249 
Efforts to identify its mechanism of action showed that when EGCG covalently inhibits lysyl 
oxidase homolog 2 (LOXL2), the compound itself is converted into a potent, irreversible 
inhibitor of TGFBR2.

Biopsies from patients who received EGCG 
showed significant reductions in extractable collagen and other indicators of active fibrosis 
compared to patients treated with placebo.250

experiment.perturbation: EGCG treatment
experiment.measurement: pulmonary fibrosis; LOXL2/TGFBR2 inhibition; extractable collagen and fibrosis indicators in biopsies

text: NOX4 expression is increased in activated fibroblasts, and NOX4 inhibition reduces collagen production from these cells in vitro and inhibits pulmonary fibrosis in vivo; aged mice show more prolonged fibrosis after a single dose of bleomycin and NOX4 inhibition blocks fibrosis persistence in aged mice.

quotes.quote:
NOX4 expression is increased in 
activated fibroblasts and inhibition of NOX4 reduces collagen production from these cells in 
vitro and inhibits pulmonary fibrosis in vivo.252
Aged mice also exhibit more prolonged

fibrosis after a single dose of bleomycin than young mice do, and inhibition of NOX4 
inhibits fibrosis persistence in aged mice.253

experiment.perturbation: NOX4 inhibition

text: Inherited mutations in TGFB1 encoding a hyperactive TGF-β1 variant cause Camurati-Engelmann disease, and mutations in TGFB2, TGFB3, TGFBR1, TGFBR2 and SMAD3 cause the five known types of Loeys-Dietz aortic aneurysm syndrome, whose affected tissues show heightened TGF-β signaling despite functionally weakened mutant proteins.

Inherited mutations in TGFB1 encoding a hyperactive TGF-
β1 variant cause Camurati-Engelmann disease

Inherited 
and occasionally spontaneous mutations in TGFB2, TGFB3, TGFBR1, TGFBR2, and 
SMAD3 cause the five known types of Loeys-Dietz aortic aneurysm syndrome

while the mutant alleles causing Loeys-Dietz syndrome encode functionally weakened 
protein products, the affected tissues show heightened TGF-β signaling activity

text: The rodent intestinal helminth Heligmosomoides polygyrus encodes a structurally unrelated TGF-β mimic (Hp-TGM) that binds TGF-β receptors in host T cells to suppress immune attack.

quotes.quote:
The rodent intestinal parasitic helminth Heligmosomoides 
polygyrus encodes a structurally unrelated TGF-β mimic (Hp-TGM) which binds to TGF-β 
receptors in host T cells to suppress immune attack.67

experiment.perturbation: Hp-TGM binding to TGF-β receptors

text: In the absence of TGF-β, SMAD4 complexes with SKI and SKIL to recruit HDACs and prevent leaky target gene expression; in CD4+ T cells this complex inhibits RORγt expression to prevent TH17 differentiation, and failure of SMAD4 with SKI to inhibit intestinal CD8+ T cells triggers chronic inflammatory bowel disease.

from approximately 3–30 min. This is different than the classical C5 
convertase, for which a natural stabilizer has not been described.

experiment.system: Alternative pathway C5 convertase with properdin
experiment.perturbation: Properdin binding/stabilization of the AP C5 convertase
experiment.measurement: Convertase half-life

numbers.quantity: AP C5 convertase half-life with properdin stabilization

text: Thrombin cleaves C5 poorly at R751 (the C5 convertase site) but cleaves it at an alternate site R947 generating C5T and C5bT intermediates, and C5bT formed a C5bT-9 MAC with significantly more lytic activity than C5b-9; coagulation factors IXa, XIa, Xa and plasmin also cleave C3 and C5.

quotes.quote:
Thrombin, human coagulation 
factors IXa, XIa, Xa, and plasmin were all found to effectively 
cleave C3 and C5 (218).

Thrombin cleaves C5 poorly at R751, which is the site 
of action of the C5 convertase (220). However, it does cleave C5 at 
an alternate site, R947, generating intermediates C5T and C5bT.

Interestingly, C5bT formed a C5bT-9 
MAC with significantly more lytic activity than with C5b-9.

experiment.system: Purified C5/C3 with thrombin, coagulation factors IXa, XIa, Xa, and plasmin
experiment.perturbation: Exposure of C3 and C5 to coagulation proteases instead of complement convertases
experiment.measurement: Cleavage site identification, fragment generation, and lytic activity of resulting MAC

numbers.quantity: alternate thrombin cleavage site in C5

text: MAC forms large, 10 nm wide pores in the target membrane; a single MAC contains up to 18 C9 molecules forming a tubular channel, though only one or two C9 molecules are sufficient to form functional pores.

quotes.quote:
Activation of the terminal complement pathway results in formation 
of MAC that form large, 10 nm wide, pores in the target membrane 
(207).

A single MAC contains 
up to 18 C9 molecules forming a tubular channel. However, only 
one or two C9 molecules are sufficient to form functional pores 
(227, 228).

experiment.system: C5b-9 membrane attack complex on target membranes
experiment.perturbation: Terminal pathway activation assembling C5b with C6–C9
experiment.measurement: Pore diameter and C9 stoichiometry required for functional pores

numbers.quantity: C9 molecules sufficient for functional pore

text: Metabolically inert cells such as erythrocytes or liposomes are lysed by a single functional MAC, whereas metabolically active nucleated cells resist lysis and require insertion of multiple MACs with calcium flux to be killed; C5b-9 can be removed within minutes by vesicle shedding or internalization.

quotes.quote:
Each functional MAC is sufficient to lyse by colloid osmosis 
in the membrane of metabolically inert cells, like erythrocytes 
or liposomes (229).

Metabolically active nucleated cells 
are also resistant to lysis by complement (228, 232). In order to 
induce killing in these cells, multiple MACs must be inserted in 
the cell membrane together with coordination of calcium flux

the lytic terminal complex of complement C5b-9 can 
be removed within minutes of its deposition on the membrane of 
target cells either by shedding via membrane vesicles (exocytosis) 
or by internalization and degradation (246–249).

experiment.system: Erythrocytes/liposomes versus nucleated cells bearing MAC
experiment.perturbation: MAC insertion into target membranes
experiment.measurement: Lysis susceptibility, MAC number required, and MAC removal kinetics

text: In the absence of a cell membrane, binding of C8 to C5b-7 induces conformational changes causing loss of pore-forming ability so that C8 acts as a MAC inhibitor; soluble sC5b-7, sC5b-8 and sC5b-9 are scavenged by clusterin and vitronectin, and CD59 blocks membrane perforation by C5b-8 and C5b-9 by interacting with the MACPF domains.

quotes.quote:
In the absence of a cell membrane, the binding of C8 to C5b-7 
induces conformation changes that result in a loss of ability to 
form pores, causing it to act as a MAC inhibitor (235). If soluble 
dead-end products sC5b-7, sC5b-8, and sC5b-9 are generated in 
fluid phase and do not bind to a membrane, they are scavenged 
by clusterin and vitronectin.

The GPI anchored protein, CD59 is expressed on most cell types 
(239, 240) and blocks membrane perforation by C5b-8 and C5b-9 
(241, 242). CD59 does not bind free C8 and C9, but does interact 
with the MACPF domain of each protein upon conformational 
changes associated with C5b-9 complex formation

experiment.system: Terminal complement complexes in fluid phase and on host cell membranes
experiment.perturbation: Presence/absence of a cell membrane; action of clusterin, vitronectin and CD59
experiment.measurement: Pore formation and MAC inhibition

text: C3a and C5a are small (10–14 kDa) peptides adopting alpha-helical conformations with four- and three-helical bundles respectively; the C5a core links its C-terminal domain by a short loop containing two adjacent arginines in position 62 and 74.

quotes.quote:
These small (10–14 kDa) peptides play a 
critical role in supporting inflammation and activation of cells that 
express anaphylatoxin receptors (250).

Structural data show that both human C3a and C5a adopt an 
alpha-helical conformation with four- and three-helical bundles, 
respectively (Figure 13). The C5a crystal structure has a core 
domain constituted as an antiparallel alpha-helical bundle and 
the C-terminal domain links the core domain by a short loop 
containing two adjacent arginines in position 62 and 74 (265)

experiment.system: Human anaphylatoxins C3a and C5a
experiment.perturbation: observational; structural (crystallographic) characterization
experiment.measurement: Molecular mass, helical bundle topology, and receptor-interacting residues

numbers.quantity: adjacent arginine positions in C5a loop

text: Carboxypeptidase N converts C3a and C5a to desArg forms; human C5a desArg has 90% weaker pro-inflammatory activity than C5a and adopts a three-helix bundle, whereas murine C5a desArg is as potent as murine C5a and retains a four-helix bundle. C3a desArg has a very similar structure to C3a but cannot bind C3aR.

quotes.quote:
these two fragments are rapidly converted by 
carboxypeptidase N to C3a desArg and C5a desArg by cleavage at 
the C-terminal arginine (266, 267). C3a desArg has a very similar 
structure to C3a (268), but is incapable of binding to C3aR.

Due to this conformational change, human C5a 
desArg has 90% weaker pro-inflammatory activity compared to 
C5a (270). In contrast, murine C5a desArg is as potent as the 
murine C5a upon binding to C5aR on murine cells (271)

experiment.system: Human and murine C5a/C5a desArg and C3a/C3a desArg with their receptors
experiment.perturbation: Carboxypeptidase N cleavage of the C-terminal arginine
experiment.measurement: Pro-inflammatory activity, receptor binding, and helical bundle conformation

numbers.quantity: reduction of pro-inflammatory activity of human C5a desArg

text: The C3a-binding site of C3aR lies in the large second extracellular loop containing sulfotyrosine 174, critical for C3a docking, and the interaction induces phosphorylation of PI3K, Akt and MAPK leading to chemokine synthesis.

quotes.quote:
The C3a-
binding site of C3aR is located in the large second extracellular loop 
that contains a sulfotyrosine 174, which is critical for C3a docking 
(272). This interaction induces phosphorylation of intracellular 
pathways including PI3K, Akt, and MAPK leading to chemokine 
synthesis (273).

experiment.system: C3a receptor (C3aR), a GPCR, engaged by C3a
experiment.perturbation: C3a binding to C3aR; sulfotyrosine 174 identification
experiment.measurement: Binding-site mapping and downstream phosphorylation/chemokine synthesis

text: C5L2 has seven transmembrane domains but is not G protein-coupled due to an amino acid alteration in the DRY sequence; C5a has lower affinity to C5L2 than C5a desArg, C5L2 acts as a negative regulator of anaphylatoxin activity, and C5L2–C5aR heterodimers induce C5aR internalization required for late-stage ERK signaling.

quotes.quote:
C5L2 is again composed of seven transmembrane domains, 
however it is not coupled with G protein due to an amino acid 
alteration at the end of the third transmembrane in the DRY 
sequence (286). C5a has lower affinity to C5L2 compared to C5a 
desArg (287) and recently it has been demonstrated that C5L2 is a 
negative regulator of anaphylatoxin activity (288). It has also been 
reported that C5L2 and C5aR form a heterodimer (289) and this 
complex induces internalization of C5aR upon C5a binding (290). 
This internalization is essential for the induction of the late stage 
of ERK signaling (291, 292).

experiment.system: Receptor C5L2 and C5aR on cells binding C5a/C5a desArg
experiment.perturbation: C5a or C5a desArg binding; heterodimer formation
experiment.measurement: Receptor affinity, G-protein coupling, receptor internalization and ERK signaling

text: C3d serves as a molecular adjuvant by lowering the threshold for B-cell activation by 1000–10,000-fold, acting through CR2 (CD21) in a co-receptor complex with CD19 and CD81; the CR2 binding site lies in the TED domain of iC3b/C3d and the C3d-binding site in the two N-terminal CCP domains of CR2.

quotes.quote:
C3d 
serves as a molecular adjuvant by lowering the threshold for 
B-cell activation by 1000–10,000-fold (297).

the 
binding site for CR2 in iC3b and C3d lies within the common 
TED domain (298). The C3d-binding site is located in the two 
N-terminal CCP domains of CR2 (299).

experiment.system: B-cells expressing CR2 (CD21)/CD19/CD81 with C3d-opsonized antigen
experiment.perturbation: C3d opsonization of surface antigen
experiment.measurement: Threshold for B-cell activation; mapping of CR2/C3d binding sites

numbers.quantity: lowering of B-cell activation threshold by C3d

text: Two crystal structures of the CR2:C3d complex disagree: the 2001 structure showed only the CCP2 domain of CR2 interacting with C3d, while a 2010 structure showed both CCP1 and CCP2 involved, in agreement with mutagenesis data; the discrepancy may be due to the high zinc concentration in the 2001 crystallization buffer.

quotes.quote:
the first 
one, described in 2001 by Szakonyi et al. (300), showed that 
only the CCP2 domain of CR2 interacts with C3d. Contrary 
to this result, biochemical studies showed that mutations on 
several basic residues on CCP1 domain affected C3d binding to 
CR2 (301). In 2010, a second structure was proposed (302) in 
agreement with the mutagenesis data (301) where both CCP1 and 
CCP2 are involved in the interaction

One possible 
explanation for the discrepancy between structures could be due 
to the high concentration of zinc in the crystallization buffer from 
2001 leading to a non-physiological complex.

experiment.system: CR2:C3d complex
experiment.perturbation: X-ray crystallization under differing buffer conditions; mutagenesis of CCP1 basic residues
experiment.measurement: Domain interfaces engaged in C3d binding

text: CR3 and CR4 both bind iC3b but differ in recognized fragments: CR3 recognizes C3d via the VWF-A (αI) domain binding the TED domain in a divalent metal ion-dependent manner, while CR4 binds the C3c portion of iC3b at an interface between MG3 and MG4 observed by low-resolution electron microscopy.

quotes.quote:
CR3 and CR4 differ in their profile of recognized C3 fragments 
because both receptors bind to iC3b, but CR3 recognizes C3d, while 
CR4 binds to C3c, suggesting that the two receptors have distinct 
binding sites on the iC3b molecule (Figure 14) (305, 306). The iC3b 
and C3d binding site of CR3 is located in the VWF-A domain of 
the α-chain, also called αI domain, and binds in a divalent metal 
ion-dependent manner (307).

The architecture of the complex has only been 
observed at low resolution, by electron microscopy and displays
a CR4 binding site at the interface between MG3 and MG4 (306).

experiment.system: Integrin complement receptors CR3 (CD11b/CD18) and CR4 (CD11c/CD18) with iC3b/C3d/C3c
experiment.perturbation: observational; binding studies and electron microscopy of receptor–ligand complexes
experiment.measurement: C3 fragment specificity and binding-site localization

text: CRIg binds C3b and iC3b via a site in the MG ring of the β chain engaging MG3 and MG6 domains, acts as an inhibitor of the AP preventing entry of C3 and C5 substrates into the C3 convertase, and does not bind intact C3 because a conformational change in MG3 during C3-to-C3b transition forms the binding site.

quotes.quote:
CRIg acts as an inhibitor of the 
AP preventing the entry of the substrate molecule C3 and C5 into 
the C3 convertase (312). The CRIg-binding site on C3b is located 
in the MG ring of the β chain, engaging MG3 and MG6 domains. 
A conformational change in MG3 during the transition of C3 to 
C3b contributes to the formation of the CRIg-binding site and 
explains why CRIg binds to C3b and iC3b, but not to intact C3.

experiment.system: Complement receptor of the immunoglobulin superfamily (CRIg) with C3, C3b and iC3b
experiment.perturbation: observational; structural/binding characterization and AP inhibition assays
experiment.measurement: CRIg binding-site localization and inhibition of substrate entry into the C3 convertase

text: Without appropriate treatment, atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome leads to end stage renal disease in approximately 60% of patients.

quotes.quote:
Without appropriate treatment, it leads to end stage 
renal disease in approximately 60% of patients (313, 314).

experiment.system: Patients with atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS)
experiment.perturbation: observational; absence of appropriate treatment
experiment.measurement: Proportion progressing to end stage renal disease

numbers.quantity: aHUS patients reaching end stage renal disease untreated

text: The majority of FH mutations found in aHUS patients do not induce quantitative protein deficiency and are located in the C-terminus (CCP19–20); mapping onto the C3d–FH19–20 complex showed residues decreasing C3b binding map to the C3b/C3d-binding site in CCP19, while residues affecting both C3b and GAG interaction are located in the FH CCP20 interface.

quotes.quote:
The 
majority of the mutations in FH found in aHUS patients does 
not induce protein quantitative deficiency and are located in the 
C-terminus of the protein (CCP19–20).

revealed that the residues which 
decreased C3b-binding mapped to the C3b/C3d-binding site 
of FH in CCP19. The residues that affected both C3b and GAG 
interaction were located in the FH CCP20 interface (Figure 15B).

experiment.system: aHUS patient FH mutations mapped onto the C3d–FH19–20 structure
experiment.perturbation: Disease-associated FH mutations
experiment.measurement: C3b and GAG binding and structural localization of mutated residues

text: C3 mutations found in aHUS are not randomly distributed but cluster alongside FH CCP1–4 and CCP19–20 binding sites and functionally decrease FH binding; C3 mutations that decreased MCP binding mapped to an area overlapping the FH CCP-3–4-binding site but did not affect CR1 binding, suggesting CR1 is not involved in aHUS.

quotes.quote:
These genetic changes are not randomly distributed but cluster 
alongside FH CCP1–4 and CCP19–20 binding sites (Figure 15C) 
(142, 315, 319, 320). Functional analysis revealed that mutations 
located in the FH-binding sites resulted in decreased FH binding, 
thus showing the link with aHUS.

C3 mutations that decreased 
MCP binding mapped in an area overlapping with the FH CCP-
3–4-binding site (142). However, these mutations did not affect 
CR1  binding suggesting that the CR1 binding site is distinct 
and that CR1 is not involved in aHUS (142).

experiment.system: aHUS patient C3 mutants and complement regulators FH, MCP, CR1
experiment.perturbation: Disease-associated C3 mutations
experiment.measurement: FH, MCP and CR1 binding and mutation mapping on C3b structure

text: aHUS mutations in FB are located in multiple domains and in more than half of the cases far from any known binding sites; mutations within the C3b-binding site induced an overactive or regulation-resistant C3 convertase, whereas mutations far from this interface showed no functional defect in FB functional tests.

quotes.quote: Mutations in FB were located in multiple

domains of the protein and in more than half of the cases they were 
far from any known binding sites (321). Mutations located within 
the C3b-binding site did induced formation of an overactive C3 
convertase or a convertase resistant to regulation (321–323). The 
mutations far from this binding interface showed no functional 
defect as observed by FB functional tests (321).

experiment.system: aHUS patient Factor B mutants
experiment.perturbation: Disease-associated FB mutations at and away from the C3b-binding interface
experiment.measurement: FB functional tests of C3 convertase formation, activity and regulation resistance

numbers.quantity: FB aHUS mutations far from known binding sites

text: The monoclonal antibody Eculizumab targets human C5 with an epitope that interacts with the C5–C5 convertase contact interface, preventing C5 entry into the convertase and blocking generation of C5a and C5b-9 while leaving the C3 convertases unaffected; it has been accepted for treatment of PNH and aHUS.

quotes.quote:
The Eculizumab binding epitope on C5 interacts with the contact 
interface between C5 and the C5 convertase (211) preventing the 
entry of C5 into the C5 convertase and blocking further cleav-
age and generation of the bioactive fragments C5a and C5b-9. 
Eculizumab blocks the terminal complement pathway but leaves 
the C3 convertases unaffected. Eculizumab showed significant 
improvement in clinical outcome and has been accepted for 
treatment of complement-mediated diseases including paroxysmal 
nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH) (327) and aHUS (328, 329)

experiment.system: Human C5 and C5 convertases; patients with PNH and aHUS
experiment.perturbation: Administration/binding of the anti-C5 monoclonal antibody Eculizumab
experiment.measurement: C5 cleavage blockade (C5a, C5b-9 generation) and clinical outcome

text: Compstatin, a 13-residue peptide, binds MG4 and MG5 of C3c and C3b and blocks C3 cleavage by steric hindrance of substrate entry into convertase complexes, with efficacy in vitro and in animal models of extracorporeal circulation, sepsis, and PNH; both Compstatin and Eculizumab are species-specific, acting in humans and monkeys but not mice or rats.

quotes.quote:
Compstatin is a 
13-residue peptide that is being tested pre-clinically. It binds to C3 
and blocks its cleavage (330, 331). Compstatin binds to MG4 and 
MG5 of C3c and C3b where it undergoes a large conformational 
change upon interaction (332) causing steric hindrance of the 
substrate C3 to the convertase complexes

Compstatin has shown efficacy 
in complement blocking in vitro and in animal models including 
extracorporeal circulation (333), sepsis (334), and PNH (335). 
Both Compstatin and Eculizumab are species-specific and act only 
in humans and monkeys, but not in mice or rats

experiment.system: C3 in vitro and animal models (extracorporeal circulation, sepsis, PNH)
experiment.perturbation: Administration of the 13-residue peptide inhibitor Compstatin
experiment.measurement: C3 cleavage/complement blockade and cross-species activity

text: Mini-FH molecules containing CCP1–4 and CCP19–20 bind C3b and C3d with high affinity and show better efficacy than native FH in in vitro models of aHUS and PNH; the hybrid TT30 (FH CCP1–5 plus CR2 CCP1–4) interacts simultaneously with C3b and C3d and, with its murine analog, showed significant improvement in models of AMD, ischemia/reperfusion injury, and PNH.

quotes.quote:
Mini FH molecules, containing CCP1–4 and 
CCP19–20 bind C3b and C3d with high affinity and show better 
efficacy compared to native FH in in vitro models of aHUS (336) 
and PNH (337). A hybrid molecule TT30, containing FH CCP1–5 
and CR2 CCP1–4 is designed to accumulate preferentially at sites 
already under complement-mediated attack (338).

TT30 and its murine analog showed 
significant improvement in models of AMD, ischemia/reperfusion 
injury, and PNH (340–342).

experiment.system: Engineered complement regulators (mini-FH, TT30) in in vitro aHUS/PNH models and animal disease models
experiment.perturbation: Administration of mini-FH or TT30 versus native FH
experiment.measurement: C3b/C3d binding affinity and complement-mediated disease readouts

text: Six structurally distinct DUB families are described: USPs (54 members in humans), OTUs (16), UCHs (4), Josephins (4), MINDYs (4), and the Zn-dependent JAMM metalloproteases (16 members).

quotes.quote:
the ubiquitin-speciﬁc proteases (USPs; 54 members in humans), the ovarian
tumor proteases (OTUs; 16 members), the ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolases (UCHs; 4 members),
the Josephin family (4 members) (27, 28), and as of late, the motif interacting with ubiquitin (MIU)-
containing novel DUB family [MINDYs; 4 members (30)]

a family of Zn-dependent JAB1/MPN/MOV34 metalloprotease
DUBs ( JAMMs, also known as MPN+; 16 members) exists

experiment.system: human DUB complement
experiment.perturbation: observational (structural and sequence classification)
experiment.measurement: family assignment and member counts

text: Mass spectrometry studies found that each of the 11 serine, threonine, and tyrosine residues of ubiquitin can be phosphorylated in cells, and Ser65 phosphorylation induces a conformational change linked to mitophagy.

quotes.quote:
Ubiquitin contains 11 serine, threonine, and tyrosine
residues, and mass spectrometry studies have found that each residue can be phosphorylated in
cells
Ser65 phosphorylation induces a conformational change (21)

experiment.system: cellular ubiquitin
experiment.perturbation: observational (cells analyzed by mass spectrometry); structural analysis of Ser65-phosphoubiquitin
experiment.measurement: detection of phosphorylation sites; ubiquitin conformation

text: Kinetic studies on USP21 revealed 80-fold higher DUB activity compared with its deISGylation activity.

quotes.quote:
Kinetic studies on one such enzyme, USP21, revealed 80-fold
higher DUB activity as compared with deISGylation activity (36)

experiment.system: purified USP21 with ubiquitin and ISG15 substrates
experiment.perturbation: substrate swap (ubiquitin vs ISG15)
experiment.measurement: enzyme kinetics of cleavage

numbers.quantity: fold higher DUB vs deISGylation activity of USP21

text: USP21 processes Lys6 polyubiquitin exclusively from the distal end (exo-cleavage) while cleaving Lys63 chains at any linkage, despite similar diubiquitin cleavage rates, because Lys6 of the S1-bound ubiquitin lies at the DUB interface while Lys63 is solvent exposed.

quotes.quote:
A ubiquitin molecule bound
to the S1 site of USP21 features a solvent-exposed Lys63 residue that can be distally extended,
enabling endo-cleavage of Lys63-linked chains (36). In contrast, Lys6 of the distal ubiquitin is

USP21 processes Lys6 polyubiquitin exclusively from the distal end (10)
while cleaving Lys63 chains at any linkage (36). In other words, despite similar diubiquitin cleavage
rates (36), USP21 has to act four times to remove Lys6 tetraubiquitin

experiment.system: USP21 with Lys6- and Lys63-linked polyubiquitin in vitro plus USP21–ubiquitin structure
experiment.perturbation: comparison of chain linkage types
experiment.measurement: cleavage products/position and diubiquitin cleavage rates

text: The DUB S1 site interface with ubiquitin is extensive, covering 20–40% of the bound ubiquitin, yet monoubiquitin affinities of DUBs can be in the micromolar range with largely polar, water-mediated contacts.

quotes.quote:
The
interface between the S1 site and ubiquitin is typically extensive, covering 20–40% of the bound
ubiquitin molecule (28). ... despite high enzymatic activity, monoubiquitin afﬁnities
of DUBs can be in the micromolar range

experiment.system: DUB–ubiquitin crystal structures across DUB classes
experiment.perturbation: observational (structural and binding analyses)
experiment.measurement: buried surface area and binding affinity

numbers.quantity: fraction of ubiquitin buried at S1 site

text: MINDY-1 is a Lys48-specific DUB that cleaves long Lys48 chains only from the distal end (exo-activity), with its two tandem MIUs identified as Lys48-specific UBDs and the MINDY domain adopting a unique cysteine-protease fold.

quotes.quote:
the two tandem MIUs of the unstudied protein FAM63A, the founding member of this family now referred
to as MINDY-1, were found to be Lys48-speciﬁc UBDs (30, 51). A neighboring domain of unknown function, now
termed the MINDY domain, was subsequently shown to exhibit DUB activity with an exquisite selectivity toward
Lys48-linked chains.

full-length MINDY-1 shows a high preference
for long Lys48 chains, which is accompanied by a remarkable exo-activity, cleaving polyubiquitin only from the
distal end.

experiment.system: recombinant MINDY-1/FAM63A and orthologs with polyubiquitin chains; covalent MINDY-1–ubiquitin complex
experiment.perturbation: chain type and length variation; domain dissection
experiment.measurement: cleavage specificity/position and crystal structure

text: OTUB1 is Lys48-specific, and E2 binding (e.g., UBE2N or UBE2D) stabilizes its N-terminal ubiquitin-binding helix and significantly enhances catalytic activity, while the E2-conjugated donor ubiquitin occupies the OTUB1 S1' site and blocks the E2 from ubiquitination reactions.

quotes.quote:
OTUB1 contains a structurally disordered N-terminal ubiquitin-binding helix
that is stabilized upon binding to an E2, such as UBE2N or UBE2D (81–83), and this interac-
tion signiﬁcantly enhances OTUB1 catalytic activity (55, 83). Importantly, when the E2 enzyme
is charged with ubiquitin at its catalytic cysteine, this donor ubiquitin occupies the S1′ site of
OTUB1 (81, 82). In such a setting, the E2 cannot participate in ubiquitination reactions

experiment.system: OTUB1 with E2 enzymes and ubiquitin chains in vitro/structures
experiment.perturbation: addition of E2 (charged or uncharged)
experiment.measurement: OTUB1 catalytic activity, structure, and E2 ubiquitin transfer

text: OTULIN binds Met1-linked diubiquitin with a Kd of 120 nM versus 12 μM for Lys63 diubiquitin, cannot cleave Lys63 chains even at high enzyme concentrations, and is activated by Glu16 of the proximal ubiquitin; mutation of this residue does not impair chain binding but reduces kcat 240-fold.

quotes.quote:
In addition to preferential binding of Met1-
linked diubiquitin [Kd of 120 nM, compared with 12 μM for Lys63 diubiquitin (47)], OTULIN
is unable to cleave Lys63-linked chains even at high enzyme concentrations.

Glu16 of the proximal ubiquitin resolves an inhibitory conformation and aligns the catalytic
triad. Consistent with a substrate-assisted mechanism, mutation of this residue does not impair
chain binding but prevents chain hydrolysis (240-fold reduction in kcat).

experiment.system: purified OTULIN with Met1- and Lys63-linked diubiquitin; OTULIN crystal structures
experiment.perturbation: linkage-type variation and ubiquitin Glu16 mutation
experiment.measurement: binding affinity (Kd), hydrolysis rate (kcat), structure

text: Cezanne and Cezanne2 are the only DUBs known to target Lys11-linked chains with high specificity; crystal structures show Cezanne is autoinhibited without ubiquitin and forms its S1' site in situ only when Lys11 diubiquitin binds across the active site, with linkage specificity driven by kcat activation.

quotes.quote:
Cezanne is autoinhibited in the absence of ubiquitin but
is able to bind all chain types via an exposed S1 site. Strikingly, an S1′ site is not present unless
Lys11 diubiquitin is bound across the active site.
Similarly, Cezanne relies on kcat activation by Lys11 diubiquitin (57).

experiment.system: Cezanne (OTU family) with diubiquitin of different linkages; crystal structures of unbound and diubiquitin-bound states
experiment.perturbation: binding of Lys11 diubiquitin; residue interactions
experiment.measurement: structural conformation and catalytic turnover

text: S1' sites can be supplied in trans: AMSH and AMSH-LP have low activity in isolation but are strongly enhanced by STAM, and an AMSH-STAM fusion protein is a highly active Lys63-specific enzyme.

quotes.quote:
The Lys63-speciﬁc DUBs AMSH and
AMSH-LP (68, 75) possess low DUB activity in isolation, which is strongly enhanced by STAM
Consequently, an AMSH-STAM fusion protein is a highly active Lys63-speciﬁc enzyme (55).

experiment.system: AMSH/AMSH-LP with Lys63-linked ubiquitin substrates
experiment.perturbation: addition of STAM or fusion of AMSH to STAM
experiment.measurement: deubiquitinase activity

text: Phosphorylation of Ser177 in the OTUD5/DUBA catalytic domain activates the enzyme; the crystal structure of phosphorylated OTUD5 bound to ubiquitin shows the phosphorylated loop folding over the ubiquitin C terminus and excluding water from the active site.

quotes.quote:
The enzyme is activated by phosphorylation
of Ser177 in the catalytic domain. A crystal structure of phosphorylated OTUD5 in complex with
ubiquitin revealed how the phosphorylated loop folds over the ubiquitin C terminus to stabilize
the enzyme and exclude water from the active site (130)

experiment.system: OTUD5/DUBA in complex with ubiquitin
experiment.perturbation: Ser177 phosphorylation
experiment.measurement: DUB activity and crystal structure

text: Oxidation reversibly inactivates cysteine-protease DUBs: A20 structures in different oxidation states show the sulfenic acid intermediate stabilized within the OTU domain, protecting against irreversible oxidation to sulfinic or sulfonic acid.

quotes.quote:
A series
of high-resolution A20 structures in different oxidized states revealed how normally unstable
hydroxylation intermediates [cysteine sulfenic acid (SOH)] are stabilized by interactions within
the OTU domain (Figure 7b) (144). This stabilization protects A20 from immediate irreversible
oxidation [i.e., from further oxidation to sulﬁnic (SO2H) or sulfonic (SO3H) acid]

experiment.system: A20 OTU domain crystals; OTU, USP and UCH family DUBs in vitro and in vivo
experiment.perturbation: oxidation by reactive oxygen species
experiment.measurement: catalytic activity and high-resolution structures of oxidation states

text: Accessory domains allosterically boost USP activity: removal of the USP5 N-terminal ZnF-UBP, which is tightly bound to the catalytic core and does not bind ubiquitin, results in >1,000-fold reduced activity toward ubiquitin–AMC, and the USP7 HUBL domains plus C-terminal peptide enhance USP7 activity 100-fold by binding the switching loop.

SPATA2 (spermatogenesis-associated protein 2), which was recently shown

monoubiq-
uitination of Lys99 located at the beginning of a UIM activates the enzyme (141). Importantly,

text: In HT1080 I-kBmut cells (NF-kB-unresponsive), TNF-induced apoptosis was slow, with caspase-3 activity detectable only 4 hr after TNF addition, and involved processing of caspase-8, caspase-3, and caspase-2; it was inhibited by zVAD-fmk at concentrations as low as 5 microM.

able in resistant cells. Importantly, FLIPL was predomi-

text: The Reactome IDG portal framework, trained with a random forest of 106 protein or gene pairwise relationship features, infers functional involvement of unannotated proteins in pathways via pathway enrichment analysis and fuzzy logic simulation; inferences were validated by mining PubMed abstracts, analyzing independent single cell RNA-seq data, and manual curation of a sample, and pilot work suggests the strategy can link about half the ~6300 'dark' proteins to Reactome pathways.

quotes.quote:
Our framework, trained with a random for- 
est of 106 protein or gene pairwise relationship features, in- 
fers functional involvement of proteins in individual pathways 
based on pathway enrichment analysis and fuzzy logic based 
simulation. We validated these inferences by mining PubMed 
abstracts, analyzing independent single cell RNA-seq data and 
manually curating a sample of the inferred ‘dark’ protein path- 
way assignments.

Pi- 
lot work suggests that this strategy can generate ‘guilt by as- 
sociation’ relationships between about half the ∼6300 ‘dark’ 
proteins and Reactome pathways

experiment.system: Reactome IDG web portal computational framework over human proteins not manually curated in Reactome
experiment.perturbation: random forest model trained on 106 pairwise relationship features; pathway enrichment and fuzzy logic simulation

In the first, the drug binds its 
target human protein. In the second, the drug:protein com- 
plex regulates the reaction that the protein would otherwise 
mediate. Using this model, we have annotated, so far, the ef- 
fects of 1033 chemical drugs and 86 protein drugs.

scaling even 
this basic annotation process to encompass the vast and grow- 
ing catalogs of drugs and their targets is impractical

New material that

were first released in June 2023

12 previously released events that have been revised but 
not re-reviewed (four-star)

In the past two years, for 
example, 1990 (4.5%) of the 43300 terms in the Gene Ontol- 
ogy have been changed by additions, obsoletions, or merges

one canonical protein entry for each gene product, has col- 
lapsed their previous collection of hundreds of HLA-A, B,

text: Reactome's variant annotation strategy distinguishes two reaction types: loss-of-function variants yield reactions with inputs but no outputs, while gain-of-function or regulation-insensitive variants yield reactions with abnormal outputs or normal outputs under abnormal conditions, and cross-referencing each variant reaction to its normal counterpart enables side-by-side comparison of normal and variant reaction networks.

quotes.quote:
If 
the variant protein has lost its normal function, reactions that 
require the wild-type protein as an input, catalyst, or regulator 
fail, having inputs but no outputs. If a variant gene product 
has gained a novel function or lost sensitivity to normal reg- 
ulatory processes, reactions result with abnormal outputs or 
normal outputs under abnormal conditions (Figure 1 ).

Cross-referencing each variant 
reaction to its normal counterpart and thus to the pathway 
or pathways in which the normal counterpart functions al- 
lows the generation and side-by-side comparison of normal 
and variant / mutant reaction networks

the primary target of autophagy seems to be diffuse cytosolic proteins, not inclusion

and secrete saliva in secretory granules, showed high expression of 
proteins related to vesicle transport and glycosylation along with 
known acinar cell markers such as α-amylase (AMY1A), CA6 and 
PIP (Extended Data Fig. 4b). In contrast, ductal cells expressed high 
levels of mitochondria and metabolism-related proteins required 
to meet the high energy demand for saliva secretion25

experiment.system: Archived FFPE normal parotid gland tissue stained by IHC for EpCAM
experiment.perturbation: supervised ML classification of acinar vs duct cells on morphological features followed by LMD isolation
experiment.measurement: MS-based quantitative proteome comparison and pathway enrichment

text: Comparing six normal-appearing replicates with nine neoplastic regions from the same salivary gland acinic cell carcinoma section, within-group proteome correlation was excellent (Pearson r > 0.96) while normal versus cancer correlation was lower (Pearson r = 0.8); acinar markers were downregulated in carcinoma while interferon response proteins (MX1, HLA-A) and the proto-oncogene SRC were upregulated, and IHC of CNN1, SRC, CK5 and FASN confirmed the proteomic results.

quotes.quote:
Analyzing 
six normal-appearing replicates and nine neoplastic regions showed 
excellent within-group proteome correlation (Pearson r > 0.96). 
The lower correlation of normal cells and cancer cells reflected 
disease-specific and cell-type-specific proteome changes (Pearson 
r = 0.8; Fig. 4d,e and Supplementary Table 6). Acinar cell mark-
ers in the carcinoma were significantly downregulated, consistent 
with previous reports25. DVP allowed us to discover upregulation 
of interferon response proteins (for example, MX1 and HLA-A; 
Supplementary Table 6) and the proto-oncogene SRC, both

We validated the proteomic 
findings using IHC analysis of significantly enriched proteins in 
either normal-appearing or cancererous tissue. This resulted in the 
selection of CNN1, SRC, CK5 and FASN (Fig. 4f), which confirmed 
our proteomic results, demonstrated the absence of contamination 
and supported the specificity of our DVP approach.

experiment.system: Archived FFPE salivary gland acinic cell carcinoma tissue section
experiment.perturbation: DVP isolation of malignant versus benign acinar cells from different regions of the same section
experiment.measurement: ddaPASEF MS proteomes, Pearson correlations, two-sided t-test (FDR < 0.05, s0 = 0.1, n = 6 normal, n = 9 cancer) and IHC validation

text: In a 17-year-old archived primary melanoma FFPE section co-stained for SOX10 and CD146, ML predicted five classes with defined spatial distribution and the authors isolated and profiled 27 different samples from seven unique regions (normal melanocytes, melanoma in situ, radial and vertical growth melanoma), typically collecting around 100 cells per sample, yielding reproducible disease-state and region-specific proteomes.

quotes.quote:
ML pre-
dicted five classes with clearly defined spatial distribution: class 1, 
melanoma in situ; class 2, predominantly tumor; class 3, cells of the 
tumor microenvironment; class 4, enriched in CD146-high regions; 
and class 5, enriched in CD146-low regions.

we 
typically collected around 100 cells per sample (Methods). Including 
replicates, we isolated and profiled 27 different samples obtained 
from seven unique regions of the same tissue section, including nor-
mal melanocytes, melanoma in situ and primary melanoma from the 
radial and vertical growth phases (Fig. 5a–d). We found high quan-
titative reproducibility among biological replicates, resulting in dis-
ease state and region-specific proteomes (Fig. 5e–g).

We co-stained 
FFPE-embedded primary tumor material preserved for 17 years 
with two markers, SOX10 and CD146, to map melanoma cells.

experiment.system: Archived primary human melanoma FFPE tissue section immunohistochemically stained for SOX10 and CD146
experiment.perturbation: pathologist-guided and ML-based cell classification followed by region-resolved LMD isolation
experiment.measurement: diaPASEF MS proteomes, correlation matrix and PCA across 27 samples

text: Across melanoma progression stages, proteins involved in oxidative phosphorylation and mitochondrial function gradually increased from melanocytes to melanoma in situ to invasive melanoma, while antigen presentation and interferon response proteins were downregulated relative to melanoma in situ; pre-cancerous versus primary melanoma differences involved immune cell signaling and cell metabolism and coincided with reduced melanogenesis.

quotes.quote:
Pre-cancerous 
(melanoma in situ) and primary melanoma showed differences in 
proteins involved in immune cell signaling and cell metabolism and 
coincided with reduced melanogenesis (Supplementary Table 7 and 
Extended Data Fig. 5d).

Expression of proteins involved in oxidative 
phosphorylation and mitochondria function gradually increased 
from melanocytes, melanoma in situ to invasive melanoma, indi-
cating a dependency on mitochondrial respiration in the advanced 
tumor stages (Fig. 5h–j, Extended Data Fig. 5c and Supplementary 
Tables 7–9). Conversely, proteins involved in antigen presentation 
and interferon response were downregulated when compared to 
melanoma in situ
h, Unsupervised hierarchical clustering based on all 1,910 ANOVA significant (FDR < 0.05) protein groups.

experiment.system: Spatially resolved cell classes from one primary melanoma tissue section (melanocytes, in situ, radial, vertical growth, CD146-high/low, stroma)
experiment.perturbation: observational comparison across spatially defined disease stages
experiment.measurement: ANOVA (FDR < 0.05) significant protein groups, hierarchical clustering and pathway-level z-scores mapped onto tissue coordinates

text: Mouse and human Smad7 cDNAs predict proteins of 426 amino-acid residues with 98% identity, and Smad7 is most related to Smad6 with 36% and 56% sequence identities in the N-terminal and MH2 domains respectively.

quotes.quote:
Sequence analysis of isolated mouse and
human cDNAs predict that mouse Smad7 and human Smad7 have
426 amino-acid residues with 98% identity (Fig. 1a). Smad7 is most
related to Smad6 (ref. 13), with 36% and 56% sequence identities in
the amino-terminal domain and the carboxy-terminal Mad homol-
ogy (MH)2 domain, respectively.

experiment.system: Isolated mouse and human Smad7 cDNAs
experiment.perturbation: observational (cDNA cloning from EST/library screening)
experiment.measurement: predicted amino-acid sequence comparison / identity

text: RNA blot analysis detected one main Smad7 transcript of approximately 4.4 kilobases, with highest expression among analysed mouse tissues in the lung.

quotes.quote:
RNA blot analysis with a Smad7 probe revealed
one main transcript of approximately 4.4 kilobases (Fig. 1b).
Among the tissues analysed, the highest expression of Smad7 was
found in the lung.

experiment.system: Panel of mouse tissue mRNAs
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: Northern (RNA) blot hybridization with Smad7 probe

text: Transfection of Smad7, but not Smad2, into Mv1Lu mink lung epithelial cells inhibited TGF-beta1-induced p3TPLux luciferase activity.
