we transfected the TGFb-inducible p3TPLux
luciferase reporter construct, which contains the PAI-1 promoter,
into Mv1Lu mink epithelial cells in the absence or presence of
Smad7 cDNA. Smad7 was found to inhibit TGFb1-induced lucifer-
ase activity (Fig. 2a).

Transfection of
Smad7, but not Smad2, in Mv1Lu cells blocks the TGFb-induced p3TPLux
response.

experiment.system: Mv1Lu mink epithelial cells with p3TPLux reporter
experiment.perturbation: Smad7 (or Smad2) cDNA transfection ± TGF-beta1
experiment.measurement: relative luciferase activity

text: Co-transfection of Smad7 in R-mutant cells inhibited the p3TPLux response induced by constitutively active TbR-I and ActR-IB.

quotes.quote:
the induction of p3TPLux response
by constitutively active variants of the TGF-b receptor TbR-I and a
structurally related type IB receptor for activin (ActR-IB), when
transfected in R-mutant cells, was also inhibited by co-transfection
with Smad7

experiment.system: R mutant cells with p3TPLux reporter
experiment.perturbation: transfection of constitutively active TbR-I or ActR-IB ± Smad7
experiment.measurement: relative luciferase activity

text: In HaCaT human keratinocytes, Smad7 but not Smad1 or Smad2 antagonized the TGF-beta-induced p21Lux transcriptional response.

quotes.quote:
Smad1 or Smad2, was found to antagonize the TGFb-induced
transcriptional response with a luciferase reporter construct con-
taining the p21 CDK inhibitor promoter (p21Lux)13 in human
keratinocytes (HaCaT) (Fig. 2c).

experiment.system: HaCaT human keratinocytes with p21Lux reporter
experiment.perturbation: transfection of Smad7, Smad1 or Smad2 ± TGF-beta1
experiment.measurement: relative luciferase activity

text: Flag-tagged Smad7 gave essentially the same antagonistic effect on TGF-beta signalling as untagged Smad7.

quotes.quote:
Smad7 and N-terminally Flag-
tagged Smad7 (F-Smad7) gave essentially the same antagonistic
results on TGF-b signalling, suggesting that N-terminal tagging
does not interfere with Smad7 function.

experiment.system: Mammalian cells with TGF-beta-responsive luciferase reporters
experiment.perturbation: transfection of Smad7 versus N-terminally Flag-tagged Smad7
experiment.measurement: reporter-based TGF-beta signalling antagonism

text: Microinjection of Smad7 RNA into both blastomeres of two-cell Xenopus embryos inhibited mesoderm formation: head and tail structures were absent or severely deficient in 80% of injected embryos (n = 168), as were muscle (n = 60) and notochord (n = 48).

quotes.quote:
microinjection of RNA encoding Smad7 into both blastomeres of
two-cell embryos inhibited mesoderm formation. Speciﬁcally, head
and tail structures were absent or severely deﬁcient in 80% of
injected embryos (n ¼ 168; Fig. 2e), as were mesodermal derivatives
such as muscle (n ¼ 60; Fig. 2f) and notochord (n ¼ 48; Fig. 2g).

Injection of 500 pg synthetic RNA encoding either Smad7 or myc-
epitope tag (MT)29 into each blastomere of two-cell embryos

experiment.system: Xenopus two-cell embryos cultured to tailbud stage
experiment.perturbation: injection of 500 pg Smad7 RNA (versus MT control RNA) into each blastomere
experiment.measurement: morphology and immunostaining for muscle and notochord

text: Injection of Smad7 RNA into the equatorial region of one blastomere of two-cell embryos prevented brachyury expression on the injected side.

quotes.quote:
Injection of Smad7 RNA into the equatorial
region of one blastomere of two-cell embryos prevented brachyury
expression on one side of the embryo (Fig. 2i).

experiment.system: Xenopus two-cell embryos
experiment.perturbation: unilateral equatorial injection of Smad7 RNA (versus MT RNA)
experiment.measurement: whole-mount in situ hybridization for brachyury

text: In Xenopus animal caps, both activin and Vg1 induced brachyury expression, and coexpression of Smad7 inhibited brachyury induction by 60%.

quotes.quote:
Both activin
and Vg1 induced expression of brachyury in ectodermal explants
(animal caps), but coexpression of Smad7 inhibited brachyury
induction by 60% (data not shown)

experiment.system: Xenopus animal-cap ectodermal explants
experiment.perturbation: injection of 200 pg activin-bB or BMP–Vg1 chimaera RNA alone or with 400 pg Smad7 RNA
experiment.measurement: RT-PCR quantification of brachyury expression relative to EF-1a

text: Flag-Smad7 co-immunoprecipitated efficiently with the affinity-labelled TGF-beta receptor complex, interacting with both wild-type and kinase-inactive TbR-I when complexed with wild-type TbR-II, but not with complexes containing kinase-deficient TbR-II or with TbR-II alone, indicating that TbR-II-mediated transphosphorylation of TbR-I is required for Smad7 association.

quotes.quote:
We found that Smad7 interacted very efﬁ-
ciently with the TGF-b receptor complex (Fig. 3). Smad7 interacted
with wild-type TbR-I as well as kinase-inactive TbR-I in complex
with wild-type TbR-II. In contrast, Smad2 and Smad3 interact
stably only with complex of kinase-deﬁcient TbR-I and wild-type
TbR-II (refs 4, 5). No interaction was observed between Smad7 and
a heteromeric complex of kinase-deﬁcient TbR-II and TbR-I, or
with TbR-II alone (Fig. 3). Thus transphosphorylation of TbR-I by
TbR-II kinase is required for the association of Smad7 with TbR-I.

experiment.system: COS cells transfected with F-Smad7 plus wild-type or kinase-deficient TbR-I/TbR-II
experiment.perturbation: receptor kinase-deficient mutants; 125I-TGF-beta1 affinity labelling
experiment.measurement: anti-Flag immunoprecipitation, SDS-PAGE, Bio-Imager

text: Smad7 showed no (or only very weak) phosphorylation in cells transfected with constitutively active TbR-I and ActR-IB or with wild-type TbR-I/TbR-II plus ligand, whereas Smad2 phosphorylation increased upon receptor coexpression and further with TGF-beta1; Smad7 lacks the conserved SS(M/V)S carboxy-tail motif.

quotes.quote:
As expected, Smad2 phosphorylation was increased
upon coexpression with receptors, and addition of TGF-b1 led to
a further increase2,4–6. However, we observed no (or only very weak)
phosphorylation of Smad7 in cells transfected with constitutively
active forms of TbR-I and ActR-IB, or in cells transfected with wild
type TbR-I and TbR-II after stimulation with ligand (Fig. 4a). Thus,
despite its direct association with TbR-I, Smad7 is not a substrate
for the TGFbR-I kinase. Notably, Smad7 lacks the conserved SS(M/
V)S motif in its carboxy tail (Fig. 1a)

experiment.system: COS cells transfected with F-Smad7 or Smad2 ± receptors
experiment.perturbation: coexpression of wild-type or constitutively active receptors and TGF-beta1 stimulation
experiment.measurement: [32P]orthophosphate labelling and immunoprecipitation

text: Smad7 inhibited TGF-beta1-induced phosphorylation of Smad2 and Smad3 in COS cells; a Smad7 level twice as high as that of Smad3 sufficed to significantly decrease receptor-mediated Smad3 phosphorylation, while receptor-independent overexpression phosphorylation was not blocked.

quotes.quote:
Smad7 inhibited
the TGFb1-induced phosphorylation of Smad2 (Fig. 4b, c) and
Smad3 (Fig. 4d, e). A Smad7 level twice as high as that of Smad3 was
sufﬁcient to cause a signiﬁcant decrease in TGFb-induced receptor-
mediated phosphorylation of Smad3.

Smad7 appears not to block this
receptor-independent phosphorylation.

experiment.system: COS cells transfected with TGF-beta receptors and SMAD proteins
experiment.perturbation: co-transfection of Smad7 (6 or 12 µg) with Smad2/Smad3 ± TGF-beta1
experiment.measurement: [32P]orthophosphate labelling, immunoprecipitation, 32P/35S ratio by Bio-Imager

text: Co-transfection of Smad2 or Smad3 with Smad7 reduced the antagonistic effect of Smad7 in a TGF-beta1-induced p3TPLux assay.

quotes.quote:
co-
transfection of Smad2 or Smad3 with Smad7 reduced the antag-
onistic effect of Smad7 in a TGFb1-induced p3TPLux assay (data
not shown)

experiment.system: Cells with p3TPLux reporter
experiment.perturbation: co-transfection of Smad2 or Smad3 with Smad7 ± TGF-beta1

text: Smad7 also blocked BMP signalling: it associated with BMPR-Is and inhibited Smad1 phosphorylation in cultured mammalian cells, and injection of Smad7 RNA into ventral cells of Xenopus embryos led to formation of an incomplete secondary dorsal axis (both unpublished results).

Smad7 associated with BMPR-Is and inhibited
phosphorylation of Smad1 in cultured mammalian cells (A.N.,
unpublished results). In addition, injection of Smad7 RNA into
ventral cells of Xenopus embryos phenocopies the effect of blocking
the BMP signalling pathway, and led to formation of an incomplete
secondary dorsal axis (J.L.C., unpublished results).

experiment.perturbation: Smad7 expression / ventral injection of Smad7 RNA
experiment.measurement: receptor association and Smad1 phosphorylation; embryonic axis phenotype

text: Northern blot analysis of Mv1Lu, SW1736 and HaCaT cells showed Smad7 mRNA, but not Smad2, Smad3 or Smad4 mRNA, was rapidly induced by TGF-beta1; in Mv1Lu cells Smad7 mRNA was induced fourfold more after 30 min of TGF-beta stimulation.

revealed that Smad7
mRNA, but not Smad2, Smad3 or Smad4 mRNA, was rapidly
induced in response to TGF-b1 stimulation (Fig. 5a, b). In
Mv1Lu cells, Smad7 mRNA was induced fourfold more after

TGF-b1 was observed in the presence of cycloheximide (CHX),
indicating that de novo protein synthesis is not required for this
response. Smad7 mRNA was actually superinduced in the presence
of TGF-b1 and CHX (Fig. 5b)

Treatment with CHX alone only slightly increased the basal
Smad7 mRNA level (data not shown).

experiment.system: Mv1Lu and HaCaT cells

the phorbol
ester TPA (12-O-tetradecamoylphorbol-13-acetate), which like

PAI-1 mRNA, but not Smad7, is induced on
TPA (10 nM) stimulation.

text: In SK-N-AS cells expressing RelA-DsRed with control EGFP instead of IκBα-EGFP, 97% responded and 91% showed N-C oscillations, which appeared more synchronous between cells in the first three cycles than in cells also expressing IκBα-EGFP.

In trans-
fected cells expressing RelA-DsRed and
control EGFP (Fig. 2C), 97% responded
and 91% of cells showed N-C oscillations.
These oscillations appeared more synchro-
nous between cells in the first three cycles

compared with cells that also expressed
I0B"-EGFP, which suggests that the sys-
tem was sensitive to variation in I0B"
levels, thus contributing to the degree of
cell-to-cell asynchrony.

When HeLa cells
were continually stimulated with TNF"

oscillations that were markedly damped.

experiment.measurement: time-lapse imaging of RelA-DsRed N:C ratio

However, when TNF" was added to SK-N-
AS cells (Fig. 2B) or HeLa cells (Fig. 2E) as

occupancy was observed with no subsequent
cycles of RelA movement.

(figs. S4 and S5) showed that SK-N-AS and

When SK-
N-AS cells were treated with an alternative

(VP16),

of
the
cells

nuclear occupancy (figs. S13 and S14 and

tion damping and successive peak timing
were highly reproducible, but because of
phase differences, this was not apparent at

ferent between HeLa and SK-N-AS cells.

we used
the CRM1-dependent nuclear export inhib-
itor leptomycin B (LMB) to trap RelA in

dependent luciferase reporter gene expres-

text: Injection of mice with one dose of recombinant IL-1 three days before infection with Pseudomonas aeruginosa protected the mice against mortality.

experiment.system: mice

text: BCG immunization of mice induces T cell-independent protection against secondary infection with Candida albicans or Schistosoma mansoni.

text: An attenuated, germination-incapable PCA-2 strain of C. albicans injected into mice protects against the virulent CA-6 strain, and this protection also occurs in athymic and Rag1-deficient mice and depends on macrophages and proinflammatory cytokine production.

text: Herpes virus latency increases resistance to Listeria monocytogenes and Yersinia pestis via enhanced IFNγ production and systemic macrophage activation, and Nippostrongylus brasiliensis infection induces a long-term macrophage phenotype conferring T and B lymphocyte-independent protection from reinfection.

(H3K4me1)) and the consolidation of histone 3 lysine 4

text: Immune gene-priming lncRNAs (IPLs) exploit preformed 3D looping contacts to bring the H3K4me3 histone-modifying complex near promoters of responsive innate immune genes; insertion of an IPL into the mouse preformed chemokine TAD conferred rapid, robust, uniform transcription and accessibility to training by β-glucan, a property those genes lacked without the IPL.

IPLs exploit preformed 3D looping con-
tacts to bring the H3K4me3 histone-​modifying com-
plex close to the promoters of highly responsive innate 
immune genes, permitting their epigenetic activation 
and training. The insertion of an IPL in the mouse pre-
formed chemokine TAD confers these genes with the 
ability to transcriptionally respond rapidly and robustly 
(uniformly across all cells in the population) and to be 
accessible to training by β-​glucan. The latter is a property 
they previously did not have in the absence of the IPL

text: After BCG exposure in mouse HSCs, acquisition of open chromatin measured by ATAC-seq begins in HSCs and acetylation drives opening of specific TADs, with the locations of these marks at least partially preserved through differentiation into myeloid and lymphoid lineage cells.

exposure, the acquisition of open chromatin as meas-
ured by assay for transposase-​accessible chromatin using 
sequencing (ATAC-​seq) begins in HSCs, and acetyla-
tion drives the opening of specific TADs32. The specific 
locations of these marks are, at least partially, preserved 
through the differentiation of HSCs into different mye-
loid and lymphoid lineage cells32.

experiment.perturbation: BCG exposure

text: Individuals with enhanced containment of M. tuberculosis replication after BCG vaccination displayed a wide loss of DNA methylation among promoters of immune pathway genes compared with non-responders, and a follow-up study identified 43 genes with differential methylation patterns in BCG-naive responders versus non-responders.

individuals who exhibit an 
enhanced containment of M. tuberculosis replication after

ation among promoters of genes belonging to immune

text: Increased aerobic glycolysis is a hallmark of β-glucan-trained monocytes mediated by AKT, mTOR and HIF1α, and blockade of the AKT–mTOR–HIF1α pathway abrogates trained immunity; BCG-induced trained immunity likewise requires reprogramming of monocyte metabolism towards aerobic glycolysis.

quotes.quote:
Increased aerobic glycolysis is a hallmark 
of β-​glucan-​trained monocytes; this is mediated by a 
pathway that involves the activity of AKT, mechanistic 
target of rapamycin (mTOR) and hypoxia-​inducible 
factor 1α (HIF1α). Consistently, blockade of the AKT–
mTOR–HIF1α pathway abrogates trained immunity129. 
Furthermore, BCG-​induced trained immunity requires 
the functional reprogramming of monocyte metab-
olism towards aerobic glycolysis

experiment.system: human monocytes
experiment.perturbation: β-glucan or BCG training; pharmacological blockade of AKT–mTOR–HIF1α
experiment.measurement: glycolytic rate and trained cytokine responses

text: Human β-glucan-trained monocytes accumulate the TCA metabolite fumarate, which influences epigenetic reprogramming by downregulating KDM5 histone demethylase activity, revealing crosstalk between glycolysis and glutaminolysis in trained immunity.

quotes.quote:
Subsequent studies with integrated metabolomic 
and transcriptomic analyses of human β-​glucan-​trained 
monocytes revealed crosstalk between glycolysis and 
glutaminolysis in trained immunity131. Trained mono-
cytes accumulate the tricarboxylic acid cycle (TCA) 
metabolite fumarate, which influences epigenetic repro-
gramming by downregulating the activity of KDM5 
histone demethylases131.

experiment.system: human monocytes
experiment.perturbation: β-glucan training
experiment.measurement: integrated metabolomics/transcriptomics, fumarate levels, KDM5 activity

text: Itaconate-induced tolerance in human monocytes is counteracted by β-glucan-induced trained immunity, as β-glucan inhibits expression of IRG1, the enzyme responsible for itaconate generation, resulting in elevated expression of succinate dehydrogenase.

quotes.quote:
itaconate-​induced tolerance in 
human monocytes is counteracted by β-​glucan-​induced 
trained immunity as β-​glucan inhibits the expression of 
immune-​responsive gene 1 (IRG1) protein, the enzyme 
responsible for itaconate generation. Consistent with 
fumarate accumulation in β-​glucan-​trained mono-
cytes131, β-​glucan-​mediated inhibition of IRG1 results in 
elevated expression of succinate dehydrogenase138.

experiment.system: human monocytes
experiment.perturbation: β-glucan training versus itaconate/LPS-induced tolerance
experiment.measurement: IRG1 expression, succinate dehydrogenase expression, tolerance/training phenotype

text: β-glucan-induced training of HSPCs confers a long-term myelopoiesis bias associated with accumulation of cholesterol esters and lipids with more saturated acyl chains, and inhibition of HMG-CoA reductase diminishes β-glucan-induced HSPC expansion and myelopoiesis, possibly acting via upregulation of CD131.

quotes.quote:
The 
long-​term myelopoiesis bias conferred to HSPCs by 
β-​glucan-​induced training is associated with accumu-
lation of cholesterol esters and lipids with more satu-
rated acyl chains104. Inhibition of HMG-​CoA reductase 
diminishes β-​glucan-​induced HSPC population expan-
sion and myelopoiesis104.

experiment.perturbation: β-glucan training with or without HMG-CoA reductase inhibition

text: In atherosclerosis-prone Ldlr−/− mice, 4 weeks of a Western-type diet induced proinflammatory transcriptional and epigenetic reprogramming of circulating monocytes and bone marrow myeloid progenitors and increased inflammatory responses to subsequent innate stimuli; this phenotype persisted after another 4 weeks on chow diet despite cholesterol and systemic inflammatory markers returning to normal.

quotes.quote:
In atherosclerosis- 
prone Ldlr−/− mice, 4 weeks of such a Western-​type diet 
induced profound proinflammatory transcriptional and 
epigenetic reprogramming of circulating monocytes 
and their bone marrow myeloid progenitor cells. The 
dietary intervention induced increased inflammatory 
responses to subsequent innate immune stimuli. This 
trained immunity phenotype persisted even after the 
mice had been switched to a standard chow diet for 
another 4 weeks, despite circulating cholesterol levels 
and systemic inflammatory markers returning to nor-
mal8.

experiment.system: Ldlr−/− mice
experiment.perturbation: 4 weeks Western-type diet followed by 4 weeks chow diet
experiment.measurement: monocyte/progenitor transcriptome and epigenome, inflammatory responses to innate stimuli, cholesterol and inflammatory markers

text: Monocytes from patients with familial hypercholesterolaemia show enhanced cytokine production capacity and H3K4me3 enrichment on their promoters that remains present even after 3 months of cholesterol-lowering statin treatment, and monocytes from patients with severe coronary artery atherosclerosis exhibit a trained phenotype with enhanced cytokine production, glycolytic metabolism and histone methylation changes.

quotes.quote:
monocytes from patients with 
familial hypercholesterolaemia are characterized by an 
enhanced cytokine production capacity and enrich-
ment of H3K4me3 on their promoters, which remains 
present even after 3 months of cholesterol-​lowering sta-
tin treatment148. Furthermore, circulating monocytes 
from patients with severe coronary artery atheroscle-
rosis exhibit a trained immune phenotype in terms of 
enhanced cytokine production capacity and glycolytic 
metabolism and epigenetic reprogramming at the level 
of histone methylation149,150.

experiment.system: circulating monocytes from patients with familial hypercholesterolaemia or coronary artery atherosclerosis
experiment.perturbation: observational; statin treatment for 3 months in FH patients
experiment.measurement: ex vivo cytokine production, H3K4me3 at promoters, glycolytic metabolism

text: In a mouse heart transplantation model, donor allografts upregulated vimentin and HMGB1 which locally trained graft-infiltrating monocyte-derived cells; short-term treatment with an mTOR-inhibiting high-density lipoprotein nanobiologic prevented aerobic glycolysis and the epigenetic modifications of trained immunity, yielding regulatory Ly6Clow macrophage-like cells that prevented alloreactive CD8+ T cell immunity, promoted CD4+ regulatory T cell expansion and improved allograft survival.

quotes.quote:
recently showed in a mouse heart trans-
plantation model that donor allografts upregulate 
vimentin and HMGB1, which induced local training 
of graft-​infiltrating monocyte-​derived cells. Short-​term 
treatment with a high-​density lipoprotein nanobiologic 
that specifically inhibited mTOR in myeloid cells was 
able to prevent aerobic glycolysis and epigenetic mod-
ifications underlying trained immunity. The resulting 
Ly6Clow monocyte-​derived macrophage-​like cells with 
a regulatory phenotype prevented alloreactive CD8+ 
T cell-​mediated immunity and promoted tolerogenic 
CD4+ regulatory T cell expansion, which improved 
allograft survival.

experiment.system: mouse heart transplantation model
experiment.perturbation: short-term treatment with myeloid-targeted mTOR-inhibiting HDL nanobiologic
experiment.measurement: myeloid glycolysis and epigenetic marks, T cell responses, allograft survival

text: Peripheral application of inflammatory stimuli in a mouse model of Alzheimer disease leads to long-lasting training of microglia that exacerbates cerebral β-amyloidosis, accompanied by activating epigenetic changes at the HIF1A gene locus and changes in microglial transcription and protein expression; by contrast, the pathophysiology of acute stroke is unaltered by prior peripheral immune stimulation.

quotes.quote:
Peripheral application of 
inflammatory stimuli in a mouse model of Alzheimer 
disease leads to long-​lasting training of microglia, the 
brain-​resident macrophages, which exacerbates cere-
bral β-​amyloidosis154. The functional changes of micro-
glia are accompanied by activating epigenetic changes 
at the HIF1A gene locus

The pathophysiology 
of acute stroke is unaltered by prior peripheral immune 
stimulation154

experiment.system: mouse models of Alzheimer disease and stroke
experiment.perturbation: peripheral inflammatory stimulation
experiment.measurement: microglial epigenetic/transcriptional state, cerebral β-amyloidosis, stroke pathophysiology

text: In patients with cerebral small vessel disease, peripheral blood-derived monocytes showed trained immunity characteristics such as enhanced IL-6 and IL-8 production after ex vivo stimulation, associated with disease severity and progression; the authors note a causal link to small vessel pathophysiology remains to be determined.

quotes.quote:
In patients with cer-
ebral small vessel disease, peripheral blood-​derived 
monocytes showed trained immunity characteris-
tics such as enhanced IL-6 and IL-8 production after 
ex vivo stimulation, which was also associated with 
the severity and progression of the disease157. A causal 
link to the pathophysiology of the small vessels in the 
brain remains to be determined.

experiment.system: patients with cerebral small vessel disease (observational)
experiment.perturbation: ex vivo stimulation of peripheral blood monocytes
experiment.measurement: IL-6 and IL-8 production; association with disease severity/progression

text: Tumours can reprogramme infiltrating innate immune cells toward an anti-inflammatory, immunoparalysis-like phenotype; monocytes from patients with chronic lymphocytic leukaemia show low levels of cytokine production, high phagocytic activity and impaired antigen presentation.

quotes.quote:
mono-
cytes from patients with chronic lymphocytic leukaemia 
show low levels of cytokine production, high phagocytic 
activity and impaired antigen presentation162.

experiment.perturbation: observational (tumour-associated reprogramming)

text: The authors note that providing BCG to low-weight African children at birth rather than in the subsequent weeks or months is associated with a reduction of neonatal mortality by a third.

quotes.quote:
providing bacillus Calmette–Guérin (BCG) to low-​weight 
African children at birth rather than in the subsequent weeks or months is associated 
with a reduction of neonatal mortality by a third40.

experiment.perturbation: BCG vaccination at birth versus later administration
experiment.measurement: neonatal mortality

text: Phosphoproteomic surveys have identified over 300,000 phosphorylation sites, with more than 50,000 distinct sites in a single cell line, at least 75% of detected proteins being phosphoproteins in a specific cell line and over 85% of detected proteins overall reported as phosphorylated.

quotes.quote:
Mass spectrometry-based proteomic and phosphoproteomic analyses have identified over 
300,000 phosphorylation sites [1], with more than 50,000 distinct phosphorylation sites 
detected in a single cell line [2].

with at least 75% of detected proteins being phosphoproteins in a specific 
cell line and over 85% of detected proteins overall reported as phosphorylated [2,3]

experiment.perturbation: observational

text: Although S:T:Y residue frequency in the human proteome is 2.5:1.8:1, 32P-orthophosphate labeling with acid hydrolysis measured a pS:pT:pY distribution of 184:15:1, validated by mass spectrometry phosphoproteomics at 162:31:1.

quotes.quote:
The frequency of S:T:Y residues is 2.5:1.8:1 in the human proteome. However, experiments 
employing labeling of cells with 32P-orthophosphate followed by acid hydrolysis determined 
a phospho-amino acid distribution of pS:pT:pY of 184:15:1 [18]. This ratio was validated by 
mass spectrometry-based phosphoproteomic analyses (pS:pT:pY distribution of 162:31:1) 
[2].

experiment.system: human cells/proteome
experiment.perturbation: 32P-orthophosphate labeling followed by acid hydrolysis; and MS-based phosphoproteomics
experiment.measurement: phospho-amino acid ratio pS:pT:pY versus residue frequency

text: More than 90% of S/T phosphorylation occurs in intrinsically disordered regions, which are enriched for S relative to ordered regions, whereas T residues are equally distributed between disordered and ordered regions.

quotes.quote:
The 
majority (more than 90%) of S/T phosphorylation occurs in intrinsically disordered regions, 
which are enriched for S compared to ordered regions [19–22]. In contrast, Ts are equally 
distributed between disordered and ordered protein regions [19,22].

experiment.system: human phosphoproteome and protein disorder annotations
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: fraction of phosphosites in intrinsically disordered regions and residue composition

text: PP1 and PP2A catalytic subunits prefer pT over pS: in vitro assays with PP2A holoenzymes from rabbit skeletal muscle and PP1 catalytic subunit from dog liver showed pT preference, and mass spectrometry analysis of dephosphorylation of over 25,000 randomized synthetic phosphopeptides by purified PP1 and PP2A catalytic subunits confirmed the pT preference in vitro.

quotes.quote:
in vitro analysis of PP2A holoenzymes purified 
from rabbit skeletal muscle and the PP1 catalytic subunit purified from dog liver 
revealed a preference for the dephosphorylation of pT [31–35]. A comprehensive mass 
spectrometry-based analysis of dephosphorylation events of over 25,000 randomized 
synthetic phosphopeptides by purified PP1 and PP2A catalytic subunits confirmed their pT 
preference in vitro [9].

experiment.system: purified PP1 and PP2A catalytic subunits/holoenzymes with synthetic phosphopeptides
experiment.perturbation: in vitro dephosphorylation of randomized phosphopeptide libraries
experiment.measurement: mass spectrometry-based dephosphorylation rates at pT versus pS

text: Depletion of PP2A regulatory subunit B55 or inhibition of PP2A-B55 activity preferentially stabilized T over S phosphorylation sites in cell lysates, whereas inhibition of PP2A-B56 dephosphorylation by substrate competition in cells equally affected pT and pS.

quotes.quote:
Further, depletion of PP2A substrate binding-regulatory subunit B55 
or inhibition of PP2A-B55 activity preferentially stabilized T over S phosphorylation sites 
in cell lysates (Figure 2B) [11,29]. However, inhibition of PP2A-B56 dephosphorylation 
through substrate competition in cells equally affects pT and pS [29]

experiment.system: cells/cell lysates with PP2A holoenzymes
experiment.perturbation: depletion or inhibition of B55; substrate-competition inhibition of PP2A-B56
experiment.measurement: phosphoproteomic stabilization of pT versus pS sites

text: Due to a more extensive acidic groove on the surface of PPP1C compared to PPP2C, PPP1C has a more pronounced preference for basophilic phosphorylation site consensus motifs than PPP2C.

quotes.quote:
Due to a more extensive acidic groove on 
the surface of PPP1C compared to PPP2C, PPP1C has a more pronounced preference for 
basophilic phosphorylation site consensus motifs than PPP2C [9].

experiment.system: purified PPP1C and PPP2C catalytic subunits
experiment.perturbation: observational comparison of catalytic surface grooves with phosphopeptide dephosphorylation
experiment.measurement: preference for basophilic consensus motifs

text: Acidic patches on B55 and B56 regulatory subunits promote dephosphorylation of sites with basic residues N-terminal to the phosphorylation site; in vitro, dephosphorylation of peptide substrates by PP2A-B55 could be increased by including N-terminal basic amino acids.

quotes.quote:
For PP2A holoenzymes, acidic patches on the B55 and B56 regulatory subunits promote 
dephosphorylation of sites with basic residues amino (N)-terminal to the phosphorylation 
site [9,11,29,32,39]. In vitro, dephosphorylation of peptide substrates by PP2A-B55 could be 
increased by including N-terminal basic amino acids [32].

experiment.system: PP2A-B55 holoenzyme with synthetic peptide substrates
experiment.perturbation: inclusion of N-terminal basic amino acids in peptide substrates
experiment.measurement: in vitro dephosphorylation rate

text: Proline-directed phosphopeptides (pSP/pTP) are generally poor substrates for PP1 and PP2A, with PP2A-B55 dephosphorylating proline-directed sites more efficiently than PP2A-B56, PP2A-PR72, or PP1; siRNA depletion of B55 pathway components showed a PP2A-B55 preference for proline-directed sites, specifically pTP.

quotes.quote:
Peptides containing a pS and pT with proline in the +1 position (pSP/pTP) are generally 
poor substrates for PP1 [31,35] and PP2A [35], with PP2A-B55 dephosphorylating proline-
directed phosphorylation site with higher efficiency than PP2A-B56, PP2A-PR72, or PP1 
[29,31,35,40,41] (Figure 2A). In support of this, using siRNA-mediated depletion of B55 
pathway components, Cundell et al. [11] demonstrated a preference of PP2A-B55 for 
proline-directed sites, specifically pTP (Figure 2B).

experiment.system: human cells and in vitro phosphopeptide assays with PP1/PP2A holoenzymes
experiment.perturbation: siRNA-mediated depletion of B55 pathway components
experiment.measurement: dephosphorylation efficiency/site preference for proline-directed pTP/pSP sites

text: A bipartite polybasic motif N-terminal (position −16 to −11) and C-terminal (position +2 to +6) of the phosphorylation site was enriched in candidate PP2A-B55 substrates, and mutation of these basic amino acids to alanines reduced dephosphorylation rates.

quotes.quote:
Furthermore, they identified a bipartite 
polybasic motif N (position −16 to −11) and carboxyl (C)-terminal (position +2 to +6) from 
the phosphorylation site enriched in candidate PP2A-B55 substrates and demonstrated that 
mutation of these basic amino acids to alanines reduced the dephosphorylation rates [11].

experiment.system: candidate PP2A-B55 substrates
experiment.perturbation: mutation of bipartite polybasic motif basic residues to alanines
experiment.measurement: dephosphorylation rates

text: Dephosphorylation of pSP/pTP by PP2A-B55 is conformation specific, occurring only for the trans and not the cis isomer, with isomerization catalyzed by the prolyl isomerase Pin1.

quotes.quote:
Intriguingly, dephosphorylation of pSP/pTP by PP2A-B55 is conformation specific and only 
occurs for the trans, not cis, isomer [42]. Isomerization of pSP/pTP is catalyzed by the prolyl 
isomerase Pin1

verdict_note: Claim text matches the paper, but the experiment field specifies substrates '(e.g., Cdc25C, tau)' for the Pin1/trans-isomer finding; the excerpt names no substrates in this context, so the experiment description adds detail the paper does not contain.

experiment.system: PP2A-B55 with pSP/pTP substrates (e.g., Cdc25C, tau)
experiment.perturbation: Pin1-catalyzed cis/trans isomerization of the phospho-Ser/Thr-Pro bond
experiment.measurement: isomer-specific dephosphorylation

text: Using protein-based inhibitors, Kruse et al. confirmed the pTP/pSP preference of PP2A-B55 and found PP2A-B56 preferentially dephosphorylated sites with basic amino acids in the −2 and −3 position while deselecting pTP/pSP; in mitotic cells PP2A-B56 also preferred acidic residues at −2, and in vitro assays showed acidic residues C-terminal to the site abrogated PP2A-B56α dephosphorylation.

quotes.quote:
Using protein-based inhibitors, Kruse et al. [29] confirmed the pTP/pSP preference of 
PP2A-B55, and found that PP2A-B56 preferentially dephosphorylated sites with basic

amino acids in the −2 and −3 position and deselected pTP/pSP (Figure 2B). Intriguingly, 
they found in mitotic cells a preference of PP2A-B56 for acidic residues in the −2 position 
N-terminal to the phosphorylation site

In vitro dephosphorylation 
assays confirmed these preferences and deselections of PP2A-B56α and revealed that acidic 
residues C-terminal to the phosphorylation site abrogated the ability of PP2A-B56α to 
dephosphorylate the site [29].

experiment.system: PP2A-B55 and PP2A-B56 holoenzymes in cells and in vitro with short phosphopeptides
experiment.perturbation: protein-based inhibitors (substrate competition) in cells; sequence variation in phosphopeptides in vitro
experiment.measurement: site-specific dephosphorylation preferences and deselections

text: Structural studies revealed a hydrophobic groove on the PP1 catalytic subunit that binds over 200 regulatory proteins by recognizing the RVxF consensus SLiM, which often co-occurs with SILK, KiR, ΦΦ or the structural MyPhoNE motif.

Structural studies revealed a hydrophobic groove on the PP1 catalytic subunit that binds to 
over 200 regulatory proteins by recognizing a SLiM with the consensus sequence RVxF 
(Figure 2A) [51–55].
RVxF motifs often co-occur with a second SLiM such

as the SILK, KiR, or ΦΦ motif, or the structural myosin phosphatase N-terminal element 
(MyPhoNE) motif (Figure 2A) [52,54,55,60–63].

experiment.system: PP1 catalytic subunit and its regulatory proteins
experiment.perturbation: observational structural/biochemical analysis of PP1–regulator complexes
experiment.measurement: identification of binding grooves and consensus docking motifs

numbers.quantity: PP1 regulatory proteins bound via RVxF groove

text: The PP1 regulatory subunit Spinophilin is unstructured in its unbound form but folds upon interaction with PPP1C, binding a large surface of the catalytic subunit including the RVxF and C-terminal binding grooves.

For instance, the PP1 regulatory 
subunit Spinophilin is unstructured in its unbound form, but upon interaction with the 
PPP1C folds and binds to a large surface of the catalytic subunit, including the RVxF and 
C-terminal binding grooves [64].

experiment.system: Spinophilin–PPP1C complex
experiment.perturbation: binding of Spinophilin to PPP1C
experiment.measurement: structural determination of folding and binding surface

text: A highly conserved binding pocket in a HEAT repeat helix found in all B56 isoforms binds the LxxIxE motif in substrates, and in a subset of LxxIxE-containing proteins the interaction is enhanced by a dynamic charge-charge interaction between a positively charged motif and a negatively charged groove on B56.

quotes.quote:
A highly conserved binding pocket in a HEAT repeat helix 
found in all isoforms of B56 binds to a LxxIxE motif found in substrates (Figure 2A) 
[10,65–67]. In a subset of LxxIxE-containing proteins, the interaction is enhanced by a 
dynamic charge-charge interaction between a positively charged motif which interacts with a 
negatively charged groove on B56 [68].

experiment.system: PP2A-B56 regulatory subunits and substrate proteins
experiment.perturbation: observational structural and binding analysis of B56–substrate motif complexes
experiment.measurement: motif binding pocket identification and interaction affinity

text: Two substrate interaction modes were identified for PP2A-B55: a conserved acidic pocket on B55 binding basic residues N-terminal of phosphosites, and a common sequence motif [RK]-[VIL]-x-x-[VILM]-[RK] found in p107, Tau and MAP2; follow-up work on FAM122A showed this motif is not a SLiM but a structural short α-helix binding B55.

quotes.quote:
For the PP2A-B55 holoenzyme, two substrate interaction motifs have been identified. A 
conserved acidic pocket on the B55 regulatory subunit binds to basic residues N-terminal of 
the phosphorylation sites [11,39]. Additionally, investigations into the mode of interaction 
of the PP2A-B55 substrates p107, Tau, and MAP2 identified a common sequence motif 
[RK]-[VIL]-x-x-[VILM]-[RK] (Figure 2A) [69]. A follow-up study on the interaction of 
PP2A-B55 and its substrate FAM122A revealed that this motif is not a SLiM but a structural 
motif in the form of a short α-helix that binds to the B55 regulatory subunit [70].

experiment.system: PP2A-B55 holoenzyme with substrates p107, Tau, MAP2 and FAM122A
experiment.perturbation: observational structural/biochemical interaction mapping
experiment.measurement: identification of B55-binding sequence/structural motifs

text: CN recognizes two SLiMs — PxIxIT binding a pocket on CNA near the active site and LxVP binding a pocket at the CNA–CNB interface — and the immunosuppressants cyclosporin A and FK506, in complex with cyclophilin and FKBP respectively, inhibit CN by blocking LxVP binding.

quotes.quote:
CN recognizes two SLiMs: the PxIxIT motif, which binds to a binding pocket on CNA 
close to the active site, and the LxVP motif, which binds to a pocket at the interface of 
CNA and CNB (Table 1; Figure 2A) [47,72–75]. CN is inhibited by the fungal-derived 
immunosuppressants cyclosporin A (CSA) and FK506

both molecules in complex with their 
respective endogenous protein receptors (cyclophilin for CSA, FKBP for FK506) inhibit CN 
by blocking binding to the LxVP [47].

experiment.system: calcineurin holoenzyme with substrate motifs and immunosuppressant–immunophilin complexes
experiment.perturbation: treatment with cyclosporin A/cyclophilin and FK506/FKBP complexes
experiment.measurement: structural and biochemical assessment of motif binding and CN inhibition

text: SLiM composition tunes affinity: a proline at the fourth position of the PP1 RVxF motif greatly decreases PP1 binding while a tryptophan instead of phenylalanine at that position enhances affinity, and acidic residues C-terminal to the B56 LxxIxE core motif increase binding affinity to B56.

quotes.quote:
For instance, a proline at the fourth position in the RVxF motif greatly decreases its binding 
capability to PP1, whereas a tryptophan residue instead of phenylalanine in the fourth 
position enhances the binding affinity (Figure 2A) [55]. For the B56 SLiM LxxIxE, acidic 
residues C-terminal to the core motif increase its binding affinity to B56 (Figure 2A) [10].

experiment.system: PP1 with RVxF motif peptides and B56 with LxxIxE motif peptides
experiment.perturbation: substitution of residues within/around the docking motifs
experiment.measurement: binding affinity

text: For CN, LxVP binding affinity is not correlated with amino acid composition but with the on-rate, which can vary by ~100-fold between LxVP sequences.

quotes.quote:
Surprisingly, for CN, the binding affinity is not correlated with the amino acid composition 
of the LxVP SLiM but with the on-rate, which can vary by ~100-fold between LxVP 
sequences [73].

experiment.system: calcineurin with LxVP SLiM peptide variants
experiment.perturbation: variation of LxVP sequence composition
experiment.measurement: binding affinity and association on-rate

text: The binding sites on the PP1 catalytic subunit can theoretically generate more than 4,000 unique combinations of binding motifs, and multiple SLiMs increase specificity and affinity through avidity while reducing substrate number.

quotes.quote:
The binding sites on the PP1 catalytic subunit can theoretically 
generate more than 4,000 unique combinations of binding motifs, explaining the broad 
range of biological functions, specific interactions, and catalytic activities connected to PP1 
[52,53,60,64,76,77]. Comparable to kinases, larger interaction surfaces through multiple 
SLiMs or structural motifs increase the stringency of the dephosphorylation reaction while 
reducing the number of substrates [78].

experiment.system: PP1 catalytic subunit docking sites
experiment.perturbation: observational combinatorial analysis of PP1 binding motifs
experiment.measurement: number of theoretical motif combinations and effect of multivalency on specificity

numbers.quantity: theoretical unique PP1 binding motif combinations

text: Phosphorylation oppositely modulates PP1 and PP2A-B56 docking: phosphorylation of the S/T at the x position of the PP1 RVxF motif reduces interaction affinity, whereas phosphorylation of S/T in or adjacent to the PP2A-B56 LxxIxE motif increases B56 interaction; for Repo-man, Cdk1 phosphorylation of its LxxIxE motif increases PP2A-B56 binding while phosphorylation of its RVxF motif decreases PP1 binding.

quotes.quote:
For PP1, the x position in the PP1 RVxF motif is frequently an S or 
T (Figure 2A), and phosphorylation of this residue reduces the affinity of the interaction 
[62,79,80]. Conversely, phosphorylation of an S or T residue in any of the x positions of 
the PP2A-B56 LxxIxE motif or residues directly adjacent to it increases the interaction with 
B56 [10,65]. For example, Cdk1 phosphorylation of the Repo-man LxxIxE motif increases 
its binding to PP2A-B56, while the phosphorylation of its RVxF motif decreases its 
binding to PP1

experiment.system: PP1 and PP2A-B56 with motif-containing regulators/substrates including Repo-man

text: A phosphoproteomic global analysis of PP2A-B56 substrates found only 5% of identified PP2A-B56-dependent phosphorylation sites are on proteins with known or predicted LxxIxE-motif, while 75% were on proteins known to interact with LxxIxE-motif-containing proteins, supporting indirect substrate recruitment via scaffolds such as BubR1 at the kinetochore and the Ebola virus nucleoprotein for VP30.

The LxxIxE SLiM-containing protein BubR1 recruits PP2A-B56 
to the kinetochore to dephosphorylate Aurora kinase B substrates [80], and the Ebola 
virus nucleoprotein recruits PP2A-B56 via a LxxIxE-motif to dephosphorylate the viral 
transcription factor VP30 [82]. Furthermore, a phosphoproteomic-based global analysis 
of the PP2A-B56 substrates revealed that only 5% of identified PP2A-B56-dependent 
phosphorylation sites are located on proteins with known or predicted LxxIxE-motif, while 
75% were found on proteins known to interact with LxxIxE-motif-containing proteins 
[29].

phosphorylation motifs [29].

text: PP2A-B55 is inhibited from late G2 until anaphase onset via Cdk1-dependent phosphorylation of the PP2A catalytic subunit and Greatwall kinase phosphorylation of Arpp19 on S62 and Ensa on S67 at the conserved FDSGD sequence; phosphorylated Arpp19/Ensa inhibit PP2A-B55 by substrate competition, binding tightly but being dephosphorylated slowly with a Kcat of ~0.02s−1 versus 21–25s−1 for proline-directed sites.

quotes.quote:
To achieve high 
phosphorylation occupancy of Cdk1 substrates, PP2A-B55 is inhibited from late G2 until 
the onset of anaphase [84,86,87,90]. Inhibition of PP2A-B55 is triggered by the Cdk1-
dependent phosphorylation of the PP2A catalytic subunit and the activation of Greatwall 
kinase, which in turn phosphorylates Arpp19 (cAMP regulated phosphoprotein 19) on 
S62 and Ensa (endosulfine alpha) on S67 at a conserved amino acid sequence FDSGD 
[87,88,90,91]. Phosphorylated Arpp19/Ensa inhibit PP2A-B55 through competition with 
PP2A-B55 substrates [87,88,91]. Arpp19/Ensa bind PP2A-B55 tightly, but the FDpSGD 
sequence is a poor consensus motif for PP2A-B55, and dephosphorylation occurs slowly 
with a Kcat of ~0.02s−1 compared to a Kcat of 21–25s−1 of proline-directed phosphorylation 
sites (Figure 3B) [92].

text: The order of APC/C activation at mitotic exit is encoded by phosphoacceptor identity: Cdc20 is phosphorylated by Cdk1 on TP and Cdh1 on SP, so the PP2A-B55 preference for pTP over pSP dephosphorylates Cdc20 before Cdh1; likewise rapid PP2A-B55 dephosphorylation of a pTP site on INCENP is required for mitotic and meiotic transitions, and mutation to an SP impedes cell cycle progression.

quotes.quote:
While Cdc20 is 
phosphorylated by Cdk1 on TP, Cdh1 is phosphorylated on SP [8]. Thus, the preference of 
PP2A-B55 for pTP over pSP results in the dephosphorylation of Cdc20 before Cdh1 [8]. 
Similarly, rapid dephosphorylation of a pTP site on the chromosomal passenger complex 
protein INCENP (Inner centromere protein) by PP2A-B55 is required for proper mitotic and 
meiotic transitions, and mutation to an SP impedes cell cycle progression (Figure 3C) [8,94].

text: KNL1 recruits PP1 catalytic subunits via RVxF, SILK, and ΦΦ motifs; Aurora B phosphorylation of the KNL1 RVxF motif at kinetochores lacking tension inhibits PP1 binding, while PP2A-B56 opposes Aurora B and dephosphorylates the RVxF motif to promote PP1 recruitment.

One of the kinetochore substrates of PP2A-B56 is the protein KNL1, which 
recruits PP1 catalytic subunits via RVxF, SILK, and ΦΦ motifs [96,97]. Phosphorylation 
of the RVxF motif by Aurora kinase B on kinetochores not under tension due to lack 
of or incorrect microtubule attachments inhibits PP1 catalytic subunit binding [79,96,98]. 
PP2A-B56 opposes Aurora B and dephosphorylates the KNL1 RVxF motif, promoting 
PP1 catalytic subunit recruitment (Figure 3D).

text: These specificity mechanisms are conserved across species: in budding yeast PP2A-B55 (PP2ACdc55) preferentially dephosphorylates pTP over pSP to counteract Cdk activity, in the sea star Patiria miniata the PP2A-B55 pTP over pSP preference is crucial for the meiosis I–meiosis II transition, and in C. elegans Bub1 targets PP2A-B56 to chromosomes via an LxxIxE motif whose phosphorylation increases affinity for B56.

quotes.quote:
For instance, as in human 
cells, in the budding yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae, PP2A-B55 (PP2ACdc55) preferentially 
dephosphorylates pTP over pSP sites to counteract Cdk activity and order cell cycle 
progression [28]. Similarly, in the sea star Patiria miniata, the preference of PP2A-B55 for 
pTP over pSP dephosphorylation is crucial for the proper coordination of meiosis I-meiosis 
II transition [94]. In Caenorhabditis elegans, Bub1 targets PP2A-B56 to chromosomes via 
an LxxIxE motif; phosphorylation of this motif increases its affinity for B56 [99].
