text: The pentose phosphate pathway is elevated in LPS-activated macrophages, and suppression of the sedoheptulose kinase CARKL — which is highly expressed in M2 macrophages and limits pentose phosphate pathway flux — makes macrophages M1-like.

quotes.quote:
The pentose phosphate pathway has been shown to be elevated in LPS-activated 
macrophages21.

This enzyme 
limits the flux through the pentose phosphate pathway, and it has been shown to be highly 
expressed in M2 macrophages33. If CARKL is suppressed, macrophages become M1-like

experiment.system: macrophages
experiment.perturbation: LPS activation; suppression of CARKL
experiment.measurement: pentose phosphate pathway flux and macrophage polarization phenotype

text: In M1 macrophages the TCA cycle is reported to be broken in two places — after citrate and after succinate — whereas M2 macrophages have an intact TCA cycle coupled to oxidative phosphorylation that generates UDP-GlcNAc for glycosylation of M2-associated receptors.

quotes.quote:
In M2 macrophages, there is an intact TCA cycle that is 
coupled to oxidative phosphorylation25. This allows the generation of UDP-GlcNAc 
intermediates that are necessary for the glycosylation of M2-associated receptors, such as 
the mannose receptor25.

the TCA cycle has been shown to be broken in two places — after citrate (owing 
to a decrease in expression of isocitrate lyase) and after succinate21,25.

experiment.system: polarized M1 and M2 macrophages
experiment.perturbation: LPS/IFNγ versus IL-4 polarization
experiment.measurement: metabolomic and transcriptional profiling of TCA cycle intermediates and enzyme expression

text: Citrate accumulating in M1 macrophages is exported via the citrate transporter and used for fatty acid production for membrane biogenesis, for nitric oxide and prostaglandin generation, and for itaconic acid, which has direct bactericidal effects on Salmonella Typhimurium and Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

quotes.quote:
The citrate that accumulates in M1 macrophages has been shown to be exported from the 
mitochondria via the citrate transporter. It is then utilized for the production of fatty acids, 
which in turn are used for membrane biogenesis.

A third metabolite generated from citrate is itaconic 
acid, which has been shown to have direct bactericidal effects on species such as Salmonella 
enterica subsp. enterica serovar Typhimurium and Mycobacterium tuberculosis36.

experiment.system: M1 macrophages and activated dendritic cells; bacterial species
experiment.perturbation: inflammatory activation of macrophages; exposure of bacteria to itaconic acid
experiment.measurement: citrate export and downstream metabolite production; bacterial killing

text: Succinate accumulating in M1 macrophages inhibits prolyl hydroxylases, stabilizing HIF1α and sustaining IL-1β production, a mechanism reported to operate under normoxia as well as hypoxia.

quotes.quote:
One mechanism involved is 
inhibition of prolyl hydroxylases by succinate, leading to the stabilization of HIF1α and the 
sustained production of IL-1β21. This pathway will operate under normoxia as well as in 
hypoxia

experiment.system: LPS-activated (M1) macrophages
experiment.perturbation: LPS activation causing succinate accumulation; normoxic versus hypoxic conditions
experiment.measurement: HIF1α stabilization and IL-1β production

text: Increased intracellular unsaturated fatty acids (oleic, linoleic, arachidonic acid), but not saturated fatty acids, stimulate IL-1α production in foam cells leading to increased inflammation in vivo, while enforced expression of constitutively active CPT1A in macrophage cell lines increased fatty acid oxidation, reduced lipid accumulation and reduced inflammatory cytokine production.

quotes.quote:
Recent work showed that 
increased intracellular levels of unsaturated fatty acids (including oleic acid, linoleic acid 
and arachidonic acid), but not saturated fatty acids, stimulates the production of IL-1α in 
foam cells, leading to increased inflammation in vivo41.

enforced expression of 
constitutively active CPT1A ... in macrophage cell-lines increased fatty acid oxidation, reduced lipid 
accumulation and reduced the production of inflammatory cytokines42.

experiment.system: foam cells/macrophage cell lines and in vivo atherosclerosis models
experiment.perturbation: loading with unsaturated versus saturated fatty acids; enforced constitutively active CPT1A expression
experiment.measurement: IL-1α and inflammatory cytokine production, fatty acid oxidation, lipid accumulation

text: M2 macrophages activated by IL-4 rely on fatty acid oxidation promoted by STAT6 and PGC1β, but a recent report showed Cpt2 deletion did not affect M2 polarization despite impaired fatty acid oxidation — the authors suggest CPT1 may have a role beyond fatty acid transport.

quotes.quote:
M2 macrophages (as defined by activation with IL-4) rely on a programme of 
fatty acid oxidation that is promoted by signal transducer and activator of transcription 6 
(STAT6) and PPARγ-co-activator 1β (PGC1β) and works to inhibit inflammatory 
signals43,44.

Added complexity has emerged, however, in a recent report showing that Cpt2 
deletion did not affect M2 macrophage polarization, despite impaired fatty acid oxidation45.

experiment.system: macrophages, including Cpt2-deleted macrophages
experiment.perturbation: IL-4 polarization; genetic deletion of Cpt2
experiment.measurement: fatty acid oxidation and M2 polarization markers

text: Treg cells exhibit increased fatty acid oxidation relative to TH1, TH2 and TH17 cells, fatty acid oxidation promotes Treg generation while inhibiting effector T cell polarization, Treg cells have increased expression of fatty acid oxidation genes including Cpt1a versus TH17 cells, and PD1 ligation increases CPT1A expression and fatty acid oxidation.

quotes.quote:
it has been shown that Treg cells exhibit increased fatty acid oxidation 
relative to TH1, TH2 and TH17 cells and that fatty acid oxidation promotes the generation of 
Treg cells while inhibiting effector T cell polarization13.

Subsequent work showed that Treg 
cells have increased expression of genes involved in fatty acid oxidation, including Cpt1a, 
when compared to TH17 cells26.

ligation of the 
inhibitory programmed death 1 (PD1) receptor on T cells resulted in increased expression of 
CPT1A and elevated fatty acid oxidation47.

experiment.system: CD4+ T cell subsets (TH1, TH2, TH17, Treg) and PD1-ligated T cells
experiment.perturbation: in vitro polarization; promotion/inhibition of fatty acid oxidation; PD1 receptor ligation
experiment.measurement: fatty acid oxidation rates, fatty acid oxidation gene expression, T cell subset generation

text: Memory CD8+ T cells require fatty acid oxidation for timely antigen responses; IL-15 stimulation increases CPT1A expression and fatty acid oxidation and increases survival; and memory CD8+ T cells synthesize fatty acids de novo and oxidize them in a cell-intrinsic futile cycle whose reason is stated to be unknown.

quotes.quote:
appear to require fatty acid oxidation to respond to antigen stimulation in a timely 
manner49. Stimulation of memory CD8+ T cells with IL-15 increases their expression of 
CPT1A and promotes fatty acid oxidation, resulting in increased cell survival50.

they have been found to synthesize fatty acids de novo to support this process and 
subsequently oxidize these products in a cell intrinsic futile cycle, the reason for which is 
not known34.

experiment.system: memory CD8+ T cells
experiment.perturbation: IL-15 stimulation; antigen stimulation; fatty acid tracing
experiment.measurement: CPT1A expression, fatty acid oxidation, cell survival, de novo fatty acid synthesis

text: SREBP1c is upregulated during M-CSF-driven differentiation of monocytes into macrophages, increasing FASN expression and lipid synthesis, and this increase in fatty acid synthesis was crucial to macrophage differentiation and inflammatory function; UCP2 stimulates fatty acid synthesis via FASN to promote NLRP3 inflammasome activation during polymicrobial sepsis.

quotes.quote:
sterol regulatory 
element-binding transcription factor 1c (SREBP1c) was found to be upregulated during the 
differentiation of monocytes into macrophages following treatment with macrophage 
colony-stimulating factor (M-CSF), leading to increased expression of fatty acid synthesis-
related target genes such as FASN and a functional increase in lipid synthesis.

mitochondrial uncoupling protein 2 (UCP2) stimulates fatty acid synthesis 
through regulation of FASN to promote NLRP3 inflammasome activation, which leads to a 
harmful inflammatory response during polymicrobial sepsis54.

experiment.system: human monocytes differentiating into macrophages; mouse polymicrobial sepsis model
experiment.perturbation: M-CSF treatment; manipulation of UCP2/FASN
experiment.measurement: SREBP1c and FASN expression, lipid synthesis, inflammatory function, NLRP3 inflammasome activation

text: Fatty acid synthesis is upregulated during TLR-mediated DC activation and required for DC activation and stimulation of CD8+ T cell responses; T cell-specific deletion of ACC1 reduced blasting efficacy and accumulation of antigen-specific CD8+ T cells, defects rescued by exogenous fatty acids.

quotes.quote:
Fatty acid synthesis was found to be upregulated during 
Toll-like receptor (TLR)-mediated DC activation, and this increased fatty acid synthesis was 
necessary for DC activation and their stimulation of CD8+ T cell responses20.

T cell-
specific deletion of acetyl-CoA carboxylase 1 (ACC1) — the rate-limiting enzyme in fatty 
acid synthesis — results in reduced blasting efficacy and lower accumulation of antigen-
specific CD8+ T cells. Importantly, these defects could be overcome by supplementing 
ACC1-deficient T cells with exogenous fatty acids57.

experiment.system: dendritic cells and T cells
experiment.perturbation: TLR stimulation; T cell-specific ACC1 deletion; exogenous fatty acid supplementation
experiment.measurement: fatty acid synthesis, DC activation, CD8+ T cell blasting and antigen-specific accumulation

text: Pharmacological or genetic inhibition of ACC1 in CD4+ T cell subsets showed fatty acid synthesis is required for TH17 differentiation but not for Treg cell generation and function.

quotes.quote:
Pharmacological or genetic inhibition of ACC1 in CD4+ 
T cell subsets showed that fatty acid synthesis is required for proper TH17 cell 
differentiation but not for Treg cell generation and function58.

experiment.system: CD4+ T cell subsets
experiment.perturbation: pharmacological or genetic ACC1 inhibition
experiment.measurement: TH17 differentiation and Treg cell generation/function

text: CD5L is expressed in non-pathogenic TH17 cells, binds fatty acid synthase and is thought to promote polyunsaturated fatty acid production; the type of fatty acid synthesized is proposed to govern TH17 cytokine output, with PUFAs driving IL-10 and saturated fatty acids promoting IL-23 and IL-17 via modulation of cholesterol-derived RORγt ligands.

quotes.quote:
showed that a protein termed CD5 antigen-like (CD5L) is expressed in so-
called ‘non-pathogenic’ TH17 cells.

CD5L binds fatty acid synthase and is thought to promote the production of polyunsaturated 
fatty acids (PUFAs). The authors demonstrate that PUFAs are likely to modulate production 
of cholesterol-derived ligands for RORγt

PUFAs drive production of the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10, while saturated fatty acids 
limit IL-10 production and promote the synthesis of pro-inflammatory cytokines.

experiment.system: pathogenic and non-pathogenic TH17 cells
experiment.perturbation: CD5L expression manipulation and lipidomic analysis in the cited study
experiment.measurement: fatty acid species produced, RORγt ligands, IL-10/IL-17/IL-23 production

text: Glutamine is required for LPS-induced IL-1 production by macrophages and for nitric oxide production, with glutaminase inhibition or glutamine withdrawal decreasing nitric oxide production by BCG-activated macrophages in vitro; glutamine is fluxed into the TCA cycle and hexosamine pathway and promotes IL-4-driven M2 polarization, whereas LPS-stimulated M1 macrophages do not require glutamine.

quotes.quote:
Adequate supplies of glutamine have been found to be 
required for the induction of IL-1 by macrophages in response to LPS stimulation66.

pharmacological inhibition of glutaminase 
activity or glutamine withdrawal from culture medium resulted in decreased nitric oxide 
production by bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG)-activated macrophages in vitro67,68.

glutamine is extensively fluxed into the TCA cycle 
and the hexosamine pathway and promotes M2 macrophage polarization in response to IL-4 
stimulation, whereas LPS-stimulated M1 macrophages do not require glutamine for their 
development25.

experiment.system: murine macrophages in vitro
experiment.perturbation: LPS, BCG or IL-4 activation with glutaminase inhibition or glutamine withdrawal
experiment.measurement: IL-1 production, nitric oxide production, metabolic flux and polarization state

text: Genetic loss of the amino acid transporter ASCT2 in T cells impaired TH1 and TH17 generation and function without altering Treg generation, and ASCT2 loss or reduced glutamine in media reduced mTORC1 activity coinciding with the effector T cell defects; heterozygous glutaminase knockout increased ROS levels, further increased by hypoxia.

quotes.quote:
heterozygous knockout of glutaminase resulted in increased ROS levels that were increased 
by hypoxia, indicating a role for glutamine metabolism in controlling ROS stress71.

the genetic loss of the transporter protein ASCT2 ... in T cells resulted in impaired 
generation and function of TH1 and TH17 cells, whereas Treg cell generation was not 
altered72.
this same study found that ASCT2 loss or reduction of

glutamine levels in culture media brought about a reduction in mTORC1 activity that 
coincided with the observed effector T cell defects.

experiment.system: mouse T cells (and B cells) with genetic manipulation
experiment.perturbation: ASCT2 deletion, glutaminase heterozygous knockout, glutamine reduction in culture media, hypoxia
experiment.measurement: TH1/TH17/Treg generation and function, mTORC1 activity, ROS levels

text: Macrophage arginine flux into the iNOS/nitric oxide pathway is associated with an M1 inflammatory phenotype — macrophages from iNOS-deficient mice show defective killing of bacteria and tumour cells in vitro and LPS-induced septic shock toxicity was reduced in iNOS-deficient mice — whereas arginase pathway flux is associated with a tolerant, wound-healing response, with arginase expression limiting effector T cell inflammatory potential and correlating positively with severity of visceral leishmaniasis and HIV infection.

quotes.quote:
macrophages derived from iNOS-deficient mice 
show defective killing of bacteria and tumour cells in vitro. Further pointing to an in vivo 
role for iNOS in mediating inflammatory activity, toxicity from LPS-induced septic shock 
was reduced in iNOS-deficient mice75.

arginine flux through the arginase 
pathway is associated with a more tolerant immune response, often associated with wound 
healing76. Interestingly, arginase expression in macrophages limits the inflammatory 
potential of effector T cells77 and is positively correlated with the disease severity of both 
visceral leishmaniasis and HIV infection78.

experiment.system: macrophages and mice, including iNOS-deficient mice; patients with visceral leishmaniasis and HIV
experiment.perturbation: iNOS gene deficiency; LPS-induced septic shock; observational patient sampling
experiment.measurement: bacterial and tumour cell killing, septic shock toxicity, arginase activity versus disease severity

text: Arginine is reported to regulate T cell receptor component expression and promote human T cell proliferation, and mTORC1 activity in T cells is suppressed in arginine-depleted in vitro cultures.

quotes.quote:
arginine has been found to regulate the 
expression of components of the T cell receptor79 and to promote proliferation of human T 
cells80. Similarly to what has been observed in glutamine deficiency, mTORC1 activity in T 
cells is suppressed in arginine-depleted in vitro cultures81.

experiment.system: human/mouse T cells in vitro
experiment.perturbation: arginine depletion or supplementation of culture
experiment.measurement: TCR component expression, T cell proliferation, mTORC1 activity

text: IDO expression is induced by LPS exposure and by IFNγ; tryptophan catabolism in host cells can prevent growth of bacterial and parasitic pathogens by denying substrate; T cells require tryptophan to proliferate in vitro, and driving IDO expression in antigen-presenting cells blunts T cell stimulation, with tryptophan insufficiency leading to accumulation of charged tRNAs and GCN2 activation.

quotes.quote:
IDO expression has long been known to be 
stimulated by LPS exposure84 and, intriguingly, numerous studies have shown that one of 
many cellular responses to IFNγ is to increase the catabolic metabolism of tryptophan by 
driving the expression of IDO85,86.

tryptophan 
catabolism in host cells may prevent the growth of bacterial and parasitic pathogens by 
denying them a necessary substrate for anabolic growth87,88

it was shown that T cells require tryptophan to proliferate in vitro89, and driving 
IDO expression and tryptophan catabolism in antigen-presenting cells blunts T cell 
stimulation90. Indeed, tryptophan insufficiency can lead to an accumulation of charged 
tRNAs and activation of the unfolded protein response protein GCN2 (REF. 91).

experiment.system: host cells, antigen-presenting cells and T cells in vitro; pathogen growth assays
experiment.perturbation: LPS or IFNγ exposure, enforced IDO expression, tryptophan deprivation
experiment.measurement: IDO expression, pathogen growth, T cell proliferation, GCN2 activation

text: In many tumours IDO is expressed in tumour cells and tumour-associated stromal cells, increased IDO levels correlate with poor prognosis in some cancer types, and enforced IDO expression in tumour cells impaired antitumour T cell responses, which could be overcome by pharmacological IDO inhibition with 1-methyltryptophan.

quotes.quote:
In many types of tumours, IDO expression is seen in both tumour cells and in tumour-
associated stromal cells93,94 and increased IDO expression levels have been correlated with 
a poor prognosis in some cancer types95,96.

Recent work has shown that enforced expression 
of IDO in tumour cells impaired the antitumour immune responses of T cells, but this could 
be overcome by pharmacological inhibition of IDO with 1-methyltryptophan97.

experiment.system: tumour cells and tumour-bearing mice; human tumour samples
experiment.perturbation: enforced IDO expression in tumour cells; IDO inhibition with 1-methyltryptophan; observational expression profiling
experiment.measurement: antitumour T cell responses and prognosis correlation with IDO expression

text: The authors note recent work demonstrating profound effects of inhibiting metabolic pathways in models of systemic lupus erythematosus and transplantation, without any apparent toxicity.

quotes.quote:
Recent work demonstrating profound effects of inhibiting metabolic pathways in models of 
systemic lupus erythematosus98 and transplantation99, without any apparent toxicity, means 
we can also anticipate therapeutic interventions

experiment.system: mouse models of systemic lupus erythematosus and transplantation
experiment.perturbation: pharmacological inhibition of metabolic pathways
experiment.measurement: disease outcome and apparent toxicity

text: The authors report that about 115 SH2 domains and 253 SH3 domains are encoded by the human genome, illustrating that a limited set of interaction domains is reused in many combinations.

quotes.quote:
about 115 SH2 domains and 253 SH3 do-
mains are encoded by the human genome (6)

experiment.system: human genome/proteome
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: counting of domain-containing sequences by consensus amino acid sequence identification (unpublished data, ref 6)

text: Interaction domains bind exposed motifs on partners or phospholipid head groups with dissociation constants in the low nanomolar to high micromolar range, typically recognizing a core determinant with flanking or noncontiguous residues adding selectivity.

quotes.quote:
they bind the charged head groups of
phospholipids in membranes, with dissocia-
tion constants in the low nanomolar to high
micromolar range

experiment.system: isolated protein interaction domains and their peptide/phospholipid ligands
experiment.perturbation: observational (in vitro binding)
experiment.measurement: dissociation constants of domain-ligand binding

text: The Csk SH3 domain recognizes a core PXXP motif in the tail of the PEP tyrosine phosphatase and additionally contacts two more C-terminal hydrophobic residues in PEP through a separate binding pocket, yielding a selective association in vivo.

quotes.quote:
the Csk SH3 domain also contacts two
more C-terminal hydrophobic residues in
PEP through a separate binding pocket to
yield a selective association of the two
proteins in vivo (4)

experiment.system: Csk SH3 domain bound to a peptide from the C-terminal tail of the PEP tyrosine phosphatase
experiment.perturbation: observational (structural analysis of domain-peptide complex)
experiment.measurement: binding contacts/structure of the SH3-peptide complex

text: The SAP SH2 domain has an extended phosphopeptide-binding surface recognizing a threonine at the –2 position and binds an unphosphorylated SLAM receptor peptide with a dissociation constant of ~500 nM, so recognition is not entirely dependent on phosphorylation of the target.

quotes.quote:
binds an
unphosphorylated peptide from the SLAM
receptor with a dissociation constant of 500
nM. In this case, specificity is enhanced but
recognition is not entirely dependent on phos-
phorylation of the binding target (43, 44).

experiment.system: SAP SH2 domain and SLAM receptor peptides
experiment.perturbation: peptide phosphorylation state (unphosphorylated versus phosphorylated)
experiment.measurement: dissociation constant of peptide binding

numbers.quantity: Kd of SAP SH2 for unphosphorylated SLAM peptide

text: β-Catenin has a central region of 12 Arm repeats forming a superhelix with a positively charged groove spanning repeats 1 to 10, which binds E-cadherin tail, APC, Tcf transcription factors, and ICAT, each through a related core motif with distinct flanking contacts.

quotes.quote:
has a
central region composed of 12 Arm repeats
that form a superhelix with an extended pos-
itively charged groove spanning repeats 1 to
10.

experiment.system: β-catenin Arm repeat domain in complex with E-cadherin, APC, Tcf, and ICAT
experiment.perturbation: observational (structural analysis of complexes)
experiment.measurement: structure of the Arm superhelix and binding mode of partner motifs

numbers.quantity: Arm repeats in β-catenin central region
repeats spanned by the binding groove

text: Hydroxylation of HIF1α on Pro402 and Pro564 under normal oxygen nucleates a hydrogen-bond network with VHL that increases binding affinity by three orders of magnitude, leading to HIF1α ubiquitination and degradation; loss of hydroxylation at low oxygen stabilizes the protein.

quotes.quote:
hydroxylation of HIF1 on Pro402 and
Pro564 nucleates a network of hydrogen bonds
between HIF1 and its binding partner VHL
that increases binding affinity by three orders of
magnitude, resulting in ubiquitination and deg-
radation of HIF1 (54, 55)

experiment.system: HIF1α–VHL complex in cells and in vitro
experiment.perturbation: oxygen-dependent proline hydroxylation of HIF1α (present versus lost at low oxygen tension)
experiment.measurement: binding affinity of HIF1α peptide for VHL and HIF1α stability/degradation

text: An SH3-mediated interaction network derived from the 28 SH3 proteins of Saccharomyces cerevisiae, analyzed by phage display and yeast two-hybrid, is unequally connected: it is focused around a core of hub proteins centered on Las17, each making at least six connections, with remaining nodes less highly connected.

quotes.quote:
the yeast Saccharomyces
cerevisiae, which contains 28 SH3 proteins
whose binding properties have been analyzed
by both phage display and yeast two-hybrid
techniques (10)

the network is focused around a core
of hub proteins (centered on the actin regu-
lator and WAVE/WASP ortholog Las17),
each of which makes at least six connections,
with the remaining protein nodes being less
highly connected.

experiment.system: Saccharomyces cerevisiae SH3 domain proteins
experiment.perturbation: observational (phage display and yeast two-hybrid screens)
experiment.measurement: SH3-mediated interaction network connectivity

text: Vaccinia virus A36R requires phosphorylation on Tyr112 and Tyr132 to induce actin polymerization; phospho-Tyr112 recruits Nck, which couples via its SH3 domains to N-WASP/WIP and the Arp2/3 complex, while Tyr132 plays an ancillary role by recruiting Grb2; the EPEC Tir protein uses a very similar Nck-binding motif (EHIpYDSVA and EHIpYDEVA).

quotes.quote:
This activity of A36R requires its phos-
phorylation on Tyr112 and Tyr132. Phosphoryl-
ated Tyr112 recruits the SH2 domain of the Nck
SH2-SH3 adaptor

the Tir protein of enteropathogenic Escherichia
coli (EPEC) also couples to the cytoskeleton
through Nck, using a very similar motif to that
of vaccinia A36R (EHIpYDSVA and EHIpY-
DEVA, respectively) (133)

experiment.system: vaccinia virus A36R in infected cells and EPEC Tir
experiment.perturbation: tyrosine phosphorylation of A36R at Tyr112/Tyr132 and Nck recruitment
experiment.measurement: actin polymerization/intracellular motility and adaptor recruitment

text: In yeast, Ste11 signaling can be routed selectively to the mating or osmosensing pathway by fusion to the relevant MAPK kinase or scaffold, and the requirement for Ste11 or Ste7 association with Ste5 in mating can be overcome by fusing complementary heterodimerizing PDZ domains, indicating precise spatial organization on Ste5 is not essential for biological specificity.

quotes.quote:
Ste11
signaling can, however, be routed selectively
down one pathway or the other by its fusion
to the relevant MAPK kinase or scaffold
(134), and a chimeric Ste5-Pbs2 scaffold can
channel an -factor mating pheromone signal
to the osmosensing pathway (135).

A precise
spatial organization of the interacting pro-
teins assembling on the Ste5 scaffold is there-
fore not essential for biological specificity

experiment.system: yeast MAP kinase mating and osmosensing pathways
experiment.perturbation: engineered fusions of Ste11 to MAPKK/scaffold, chimeric Ste5-Pbs2 scaffold, and heterodimerizing PDZ domain fusions to kinases and Ste5
experiment.measurement: pathway routing of signaling output (mating versus osmosensing response)

text: Recruitment of the CDK inhibitor Sic1 to the F-box protein Cdc4 requires that Sic1 be phosphorylated on six or more sites, a mechanism proposed to provide an ultrasensitive switch for entry into S phase.

quotes.quote:
Recruitment of
Sic1 to Cdc4 requires that Sic1 be phospho-
rylated on six or more sites, a mechanism that
may provide a timing device in passage
through the G1 phase of the cell cycle and an
ultrasensitive switch for entry into S phase
(13, 51).

experiment.system: yeast Sic1 and the WD40 domain of the F-box protein Cdc4 (SCF E3 ubiquitin ligase)
experiment.perturbation: phosphorylation of Sic1 on Ser/Thr sites by G1 CDK (varying site number)
experiment.measurement: Sic1 binding to Cdc4 and subsequent ubiquitination/degradation

text: On the mAKAP scaffold, PKA phosphorylates the adjacent phosphodiesterase PDE4D3 at Ser13 and Ser54, inducing a factor of 3 increase in the Vmax of the phosphodiesterase and attenuating cAMP signaling.

quotes.quote:
PKA phosphorylates, among
other targets, the adjacent PDE4D3 at Ser13
and Ser54, inducing a factor of 3 increase in
the Vmax of the phosphodiesterase and atten-
uating cAMP signaling.

experiment.system: mAKAP-scaffolded PKA (RII subunit) and PDE4D3 complex in cells
experiment.perturbation: hormonal stimulation raising cAMP and PKA phosphorylation of PDE4D3
experiment.measurement: Vmax of the phosphodiesterase and cAMP/PKA activity kinetics

numbers.quantity: increase in PDE4D3 Vmax upon PKA phosphorylation

text: Binding of the GSK-3β protein kinase and its substrate β-catenin to the scaffolding protein axin increases β-catenin phosphorylation by a factor of 20,000 relative to the rate of the unscaffolded reaction.

quotes.quote:
the binding of
the GSK-3 protein kinase and its substrate
-catenin to the scaffolding protein axin in-
creases -catenin phosphorylation by a factor
of 20,000 relative to the rate of the unscaf-
folded reaction (146).

experiment.system: GSK-3β, β-catenin, and the axin scaffold
experiment.perturbation: presence versus absence of axin scaffolding
experiment.measurement: rate of β-catenin phosphorylation

numbers.quantity: fold increase in β-catenin phosphorylation with axin

text: Sustained MAPK signaling phosphorylates Ser362 and Ser374 in the C terminus of c-Fos, exposing an FTYP docking motif for Erk that yields a more stable kinase–transcription factor complex, phosphorylation of additional N-terminal threonines, and stabilization of the AP-1 complex, whereas at low MAPK activity c-Fos protein is unstable.

quotes.quote:
more
sustained MAPK signaling phosphorylates
Ser362 and Ser374 in the C terminus of c-Fos,
and this exposes a docking motif (FTYP) for
Erk, leading to a more stable complex be-
tween the kinase and transcription factor

experiment.system: Erk MAPK and c-Fos transcription factor in cells
experiment.perturbation: transient versus sustained MAPK activation
experiment.measurement: c-Fos phosphorylation, Erk–c-Fos complex stability, and immediate early gene expression

text: Comparison of the autoinhibited structures of Abl and Src shows the Src SH2 domain engages a pTyr site in the C-terminal tail whereas the Abl SH2 domain docks with helices in the large lobe of the kinase domain; these distinct conformations underlie Gleevec's selective inhibition of Abl even though it contacts residues conserved between the two kinases.

quotes.quote:
the Src SH2 domain undergoes an
intramolecular interaction with a pTyr site in
the enzyme’s C-terminal tail, whereas the Abl
SH2 domain docks directly with helices in the
large lobe of the kinase domain (142)

Gleevec selectively in-
hibits Abl kinase activity, even though it inter-
acts with residues that are conserved between
the two kinases (142, 144)

experiment.system: autoinhibited Abl and Src cytoplasmic tyrosine kinases
experiment.perturbation: Gleevec (STI-571) binding
experiment.measurement: structural comparison of autoinhibited kinase conformations and kinase inhibition selectivity

text: PSD-95 acts as a nexus in the postsynaptic density; genetic inactivation of PSD-95 in the mouse affects synaptic function and spatial learning, and blocking the PDZ-mediated interaction between NMDA receptors and PSD-95 decreases ischemic brain damage in a rat model of stroke.

quotes.quote:
Genetic inac-
tivation of PSD-95 in the mouse affects syn-
aptic function and spatial learning (115), and
blocking the PDZ-mediated interaction be-
tween NMDA receptors and PSD-95 decreas-
es ischemic brain damage in a rat model of
stroke (116).

experiment.system: mouse neurons/behavior and a rat stroke model
experiment.perturbation: genetic inactivation of PSD-95; blockade of the NMDA receptor–PSD-95 PDZ interaction
experiment.measurement: synaptic function and spatial learning; extent of ischemic brain damage

text: The human SAP protein, composed almost entirely of a single SH2 domain, uses its phosphopeptide-binding surface to engage a pTyr motif in the T cell SLAM receptor and simultaneously recognizes the Fyn SH3 domain through a distinct basic surface centered on Arg78, juxtaposing Fyn and SLAM and stimulating SLAM phosphorylation.

quotes.quote:
SAP also recognizes the SH3 domain
of the Fyn tyrosine kinase through a distinct basic
surface centered on Arg78 of the SH2 domain.
These interactions juxtapose Fyn and SLAM and
stimulate SLAM phosphorylation

experiment.system: SAP (SH2D1A), SLAM receptor, and Fyn kinase in T cells
experiment.perturbation: observational (structural and biochemical analysis of SAP-mediated complexes)
experiment.measurement: binding surfaces used and SLAM phosphorylation/recruitment of SH2 proteins

text: Par-6 assembles a polarity complex using an N-terminal PB1 domain that heterodimerizes with the PB1 domain of atypical PKC, a central CRIB motif that binds selectively to GTP-bound Cdc42, and a PDZ domain that associates with the first of the three PDZ domains of Par-3.

quotes.quote:
Par-6 has an N-terminal
PB1 (Phox and Bem1) domain that het-
erodimerizes with the PB1 domain of atypical
protein kinase C (aPKC 	 and 
), and a central
CRIB (Cdc42-Rac interactive binding) motif
that associates selectively with GTP-bound
Cdc42, followed by a PDZ domain (98–100).
The PDZ domain of Par-6 can itself associate
with the first of three PDZ domains of Par-3

experiment.system: Par-3/Par-6/aPKC/Cdc42 polarity complex (C. elegans embryos and metazoan cells)
experiment.perturbation: observational (domain-based binding analyses; Cdc42 nucleotide state)
experiment.measurement: domain-mediated interactions constituting the polarity complex

text: The Bcr-Abl oncoprotein is oligomerized through its N-terminal Bcr region and autophosphorylated at Tyr177, a site that engages the Grb2 SH2 domain in leukemic cells and contributes to oncogenicity and disease spectrum in mouse models.

quotes.quote:
is oligomerized
through its N-terminal Bcr region and is con-
sequently autophosphorylated at Tyr177 with-
in the Bcr sequence; this site engages the
Grb2 SH2 domain in leukemic cells and con-
tributes to the oncogenicity and disease spec-
trum of Bcr-Abl in mouse models (131).

experiment.system: Bcr-Abl chimeric oncoprotein in leukemic cells and mouse models
experiment.perturbation: chromosomal rearrangement creating Bcr-Abl; Tyr177 autophosphorylation/Grb2 binding
experiment.measurement: Grb2 SH2 engagement and oncogenicity/disease spectrum in mice

text: The review states that nearly 60 cytokines, including interleukins, colony stimulating factors, hormone-like cytokines and growth factors, use the JAK-STAT pathway as their predominant, requisite mode of initiating transcription.

quotes.quote:
We now know that nearly 60 cytokines including 
many interleukins, colony stimulating factors, hormone-like cytokines and growth factors 
use the JAK-STAT pathway as their predominant, requisite mode of initiating transcription.

experiment.system: mammalian cytokine signaling literature
experiment.perturbation: observational (review synthesis of cytokine-receptor signaling studies)
experiment.measurement: count of cytokines assigned to JAK-STAT as predominant transcription-initiating mode

text: Genome completion revealed only 4 members of the JAK family, with JAK3 the last identified and having more selective expression; JAK3 activation is restricted to a subset of cytokines using the common gamma chain.

quotes.quote:
it became clear that there are only 
4 members of the JAK family based on their distinctive structure. The final member of the 
JAK family identified was JAK3, which has more selective expression, unlike other family 
members

JAK3 activation is restricted to a subset 
of cytokines that employ the common gamma chain (γc)

experiment.system: human and other sequenced genomes; cytokine-stimulated cells
experiment.perturbation: observational (genome sequence analysis and cytokine stimulation)
experiment.measurement: number of JAK family genes; JAK3 activation across cytokines

text: A structure of full-length JAK1 complexed with the intracellular domain of a cytokine receptor showed that JAK1 domains form an extended structural unit that facilitates dimerization of the receptor/JAK complex via packing of the pseudokinase domains.

quotes.quote:
only recently has the structure of full-length JAK1 
complexed with the intracellular domain of a cytokine receptor been obtained (Figure 3) 
(Glassman et al., 2022). This work revealed that JAK1 domains form an extended structural 
unit that facilitates the dimerization of the cytokine receptor/JAK complex via packing of the 
PK domains from the monomeric receptor/kinase complex.

experiment.system: purified full-length JAK1 bound to a cytokine receptor intracellular domain
experiment.perturbation: observational (structural determination of the complex)
experiment.measurement: domain architecture and dimerization interface

text: Proteomic analysis of IL-2-stimulated T cells reported that 90% of the phospho-proteome of IL-2 activated T cells is JAK-dependent, with the remainder mediated by SRC family kinase signaling.

quotes.quote:
Based on proteomic analysis of IL-2-stimulated 
cells, 90% of the phospho-proteome of IL-2 activated T cells are JAK-dependent, with the 
remainder being mediated by SRC family kinase signaling

experiment.system: IL-2-activated T cells
experiment.perturbation: IL-2 stimulation with JAK inhibition/dependency assessment
experiment.measurement: phosphoproteomic quantification of JAK-dependent phosphosites

numbers.quantity: fraction of IL-2 phospho-proteome that is JAK-dependent

text: Eight SOCS proteins are encoded in the human genome (SOCS1-7 and CIS), containing a central SH2 domain and a carboxy-terminal SOCS box, and they interfere with cytokine signaling by binding receptors, competing with STATs, and inducing ubiquitination and degradation via elongin BC and Cullin5.

quotes.quote:
Eight SOCS 
proteins are encoded in the human genome, including SOCS1-7 and CIS, which contain 
a central SH2 domain and a carboxy-terminal SOCS box.

cytokine signaling by binding to cytokine receptors, competing with STATs, and inducing 
their ubiquitination and degradation via elongin BC and the E3 ligase Cullin5.

experiment.system: human genome and cytokine-stimulated cells
experiment.perturbation: observational (genome annotation plus biochemical studies of SOCS action)
experiment.measurement: SOCS gene count, domain composition, and inhibitory mechanisms

numbers.quantity: SOCS proteins encoded in human genome

text: Tyrosine phosphorylation regulates the equilibrium between parallel and antiparallel STAT1 homodimer conformations: P-STAT1 is primarily parallel and U-STAT1 primarily antiparallel, with the antiparallel dimer's coiled-coil interactions preventing DNA access.

quotes.quote:
in the antiparallel homo-dimer, the DBDs reciprocally interact through their coiled-coil 
domains (CCDs), preventing access to DNA (Zhong et al., 2005). Tyrosine phosphorylation 
regulates the equilibrium between these two conformations. For example, P-STAT1 is 
primarily parallel and U-STAT1 is primarily antiparallel

experiment.system: purified STAT1 dimers/crystal structures
experiment.perturbation: presence or absence of tyrosine phosphorylation
experiment.measurement: dimer conformation and DNA binding

text: Electron microscopic and biochemical analyses showed that U-STAT1:U-STAT2 heterodimers adopt a very stable antiparallel conformation and that U-STAT1:U-STAT2 and U-STAT2:IRF9 dimers are mutually exclusive, so the complex previously called 'U-ISGF3' is now primarily the U-STAT2:IRF9 dimer.

quotes.quote:
Recent evidence from electron microscopic and biochemical analyses reveals 
that U-STAT1 and U-STAT2 heterodimers adopt a very stable antiparallel conformation 
(Wang et al., 2021). It is clear though that U-STAT1:U-STAT2 and U-STAT2:IRF9 dimers 
are mutually exclusive

experiment.system: unphosphorylated STAT1, STAT2 and IRF9 complexes
experiment.perturbation: observational (electron microscopy and biochemical binding assays)
experiment.measurement: dimer conformation and mutual exclusivity of complex formation

text: Two regulatory phosphorylations of STAT2 have opposing effects: phosphorylation of T387 favors formation of U-STAT1:U-STAT2 heterodimers at the expense of tyrosine-phosphorylated heterodimers and ISGF3, whereas T404, phosphorylated by IKKi or TBK1, disrupts the stable U-dimer and increases ISGF3 affinity for ISREs.

quotes.quote:
The phosphorylation of 
T387 favors the formation of U-STAT1:U-STAT2 heterodimers at the expense of tyrosine-
phosphorylated heterodimers and ISGF3 (Wang et al., 2017b). On the other hand, T404 
is phosphorylated by IKKi or TBK1, disrupting the very stable U-STAT1:U-STAT2 dimer, 
facilitating the response to IFN-I and dramatically increasing the affinity of ISGF3 affinity

experiment.system: IFN-I-responsive cells expressing STAT2
experiment.perturbation: phosphorylation of STAT2 at T387 or T404 (IKKi/TBK1)
experiment.measurement: dimer composition and ISGF3 affinity for ISREs

text: shRNA interference with H2A.Z resulted in greater ISGF3 occupancy, increased ISG mRNA production, and a more potent antiviral state with more robust inhibition of virus replication; inhibition of GCN5 or BRD2 disrupted both H2A.Z removal and ISG transcription, while CBP, HDACs and RVB1 were dispensable for H2A.Z removal but needed for ISG transcription.

quotes.quote:
shRNA interference 
with H2A.Z results in greater ISGF3 occupancy, increased ISG mRNA production, and 
created a more potent antiviral state leading to more robust inhibition of virus replication.

inhibition of 
either the HAT GCN5 or the bromodomain protein BRD2 disrupts both H2A.Z removal 
and ISG transcription. It is important to note that well known coactivators including 
CBP, HDACs, and RVB1 are dispensable for H2A.Z removal but strictly needed for ISG 
transcription.

experiment.system: IFN-stimulated cells with ISG promoters
experiment.perturbation: shRNA knockdown of H2A.Z; inhibition of GCN5, BRD2, CBP, HDACs, RVB1
experiment.measurement: ISGF3 occupancy, ISG mRNA, virus replication, H2A.Z removal

text: A small fraction of STAT1, STAT3, and STAT5 (5–10% of the total) is found in mitochondria functioning independently of nuclear gene activation; in Ras-transformed cells lacking STAT3, ATP levels are decreased and activities of electron transport chain Complexes II and V are diminished, and S727 rather than Y705 phosphorylation appears required for mitochondrial function.

quotes.quote:
a small fraction of 
STAT1, STAT3, and STAT5 (5–10% of the total) is found in the mitochondria where it 
functions independent of cytoplasmic signaling and nuclear gene activation.

In Ras-transformed cells, ATP levels are decreased, and 
the activities of Complexes II and V of the electron transport chain are diminished in the 
absence of STAT3 (Gough et al., 2009). Tyrosine 705 phosphorylation, which is crucial for 
canonical nuclear functions of STAT3, is not needed to drive its mitochondrial functions 
but phosphorylation of STAT3 on S727 seems to be needed instead

experiment.system: Ras-transformed mammalian cells and mitochondrial fractions
experiment.perturbation: STAT3 absence; STAT3 Y705 vs S727 phosphorylation site variants
experiment.measurement: mitochondrial STAT fraction, ATP levels, ETC Complex II/V activity

text: Loss-of-function mutations of JAK3 cause SCID in humans and mice, with patients and mice otherwise normal; the TYK2 P1104A loss-of-function variant is associated with reduced incidence of autoimmune disease and increased risk of tuberculosis; JAK2-deficient mice die in utero with bone marrow failure; JAK1-deficient mice die perinatally with impaired organogenesis and dwarfism.

quotes.quote:
JAK3 autosomal recessive loss-of-functions 
(LOF) mutations were also sought and found to be a cause of SCID (Macchi et al., 1995; 
Russell et al., 1995) and confirmed in mouse models (Park et al., 1995; Thomis et al., 1995). 
Notably, these patients and mice are otherwise normal
A LOF variant of TYK2 in humans

(P1104A) is associated with reduced incidence of autoimmune disease and increased risk of 
tuberculosis.

JAK2-
deficient mice die in utero with bone marrow failure

JAK1-deficient mice die 
perinatally with impaired organogenesis and dwarfism

experiment.system: human patients with JAK mutations and gene-targeted mice
experiment.perturbation: germline loss-of-function mutation/gene targeting of JAK1, JAK2, JAK3, TYK2
experiment.measurement: immunodeficiency, viability, developmental and disease phenotypes

text: JAK2 gain-of-function mutations were identified in patients with myeloproliferative neoplasms, the most common being V617F in the pseudokinase domain, which results in constitutive activity and cytokine-independent proliferation; other MPN-associated mutations include R683G, R683S, and R683T.

quotes.quote:
JAK2 GOF mutations were identified in patients with 
myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPN), including polycythemia vera, primary myelofibrosis 
and essential thrombocytopenia (Kralovics et al., 2005; Zhang et al., 2012). The most 
common mutation is V617F located in the JAK2 PK domain, which results in constitutive 
activity and cytokine-independent proliferation (Hammaren et al., 2015); other mutations 
also associated with MPN include R683G, R683S, and R683T.

experiment.system: patients with myeloproliferative neoplasms; JAK2 mutant cells
experiment.perturbation: observational genotyping plus expression of JAK2 mutants
experiment.measurement: mutation frequency, kinase activity, cytokine-independent proliferation

text: STAT5A and STAT5B are adjacent in the genome and >90% identical; Stat5a knockout mice lose prolactin-mediated mammary gland development, Stat5b-deficient mice have impaired sexually dimorphic growth, and Stat5a/b double-deficient mice die within a few weeks of birth, are infertile, and have defective mammary gland development and hypocellular bone marrow.

quotes.quote:
STAT5A and STAT5B are >90% identical. Stat5a knockout mice 
have loss of prolactin-mediated mammary gland development, whereas Stat5b-deficient 
mice have impaired sexually dimorphic growth. Stat5a/b double-deficient mice die within 
a few weeks of birth, are infertile and have defective mammary gland development, as 
well as hypocellular bone marrow.

experiment.system: Stat5a, Stat5b and Stat5a/b knockout mice
experiment.perturbation: germline gene deletion
experiment.measurement: mammary development, growth, survival, fertility, bone marrow cellularity

text: A STAT4 coding variant (Glu128Val) doubles the risk of rheumatoid arthritis, and STAT4 variants are associated with lupus, rheumatoid arthritis, and Sjogren's syndrome with the risk allele associated with more severe disease.

quotes.quote:
STAT4 
variants are associated with lupus, rheumatoid arthritis (RA), and Sjogren’s syndrome with 
the presence of the risk allele being associated with more severe disease (Hasni et al., 2021; 
Remmers et al., 2007). Moreover, a STAT4 coding variant (Glu128Val) doubles the risk of 
RA (Saevarsdottir et al., 2022).

experiment.system: human genetic association cohorts
experiment.perturbation: observational (genotype-phenotype association)
experiment.measurement: disease risk associated with STAT4 variants

numbers.quantity: RA risk increase for STAT4 Glu128Val

text: A constitutively active STAT3 generated with two cysteine substitutions in the SH2 domain causes spontaneous dimerization, DNA binding, transcriptional activation, and cellular transformation, anticipating common SH2-domain mutations of STAT3 and STAT5 in hematopoietic malignancies; the STAT5 N642H mutation alone is sufficient to drive leukemogenesis in mice.

quotes.quote:
generation 
of a constitutively active version of STAT3 with two cysteine substitutions in the 
SH2 domain that causes spontaneous dimerization, binding to DNA, and transcriptional 
activation results in cellular transformation (Bromberg et al., 1999).

One 
common mutation, STAT5 N642H, is sufficient to drive leukemogenesis in mice (Kollmann 
et al., 2021).

experiment.system: cultured cells expressing engineered STAT3; mice carrying STAT5 N642H
experiment.perturbation: two cysteine substitutions in the STAT3 SH2 domain; STAT5 N642H mutation
experiment.measurement: dimerization, DNA binding, transcriptional activation, transformation, leukemogenesis

numbers.quantity: cysteine substitutions in STAT3 SH2 domain

text: In many tumors U-STAT1, U-STAT2 and IRF9 are constitutively expressed at high levels forming U-ISGF3, which drives expression of most ISGs; high U-ISGF3 correlates with resistance to DNA damage via the IRDS signature, and in lung cancer cells high levels of U-STAT2 promote an aggressive phenotype and confer resistance to cisplatin-induced cell death.

quotes.quote:
In many tumors, STAT1 and STAT2 lacking tyrosine phosphorylation (U-STATs) and IRF9 are 
expressed constitutively at high levels, forming U-ISGF3, which drives the expression of 
most ISGs, some of which encode important pro-tumor proteins.

In many cancers, high levels of U-ISGF3 correlate with resistance to DNA damage by 
inducing the expression of “Interferon-Related DNA Damage resistance gene Signature”, or 
IRDS (Weichselbaum et al., 2008). In lung cancer cells, high levels of U-STAT2 promote an 
aggressive phenotype and confer resistance to cisplatin-induced cell death (Nan et al., 2018).

experiment.system: human tumors and lung cancer cell lines
experiment.perturbation: observational expression profiling plus manipulation of U-STAT2 levels; cisplatin challenge
experiment.measurement: ISG expression, DNA damage resistance signature, cell death

text: Ten jakinibs are now approved to treat a variety of immune-mediated disorders; ruxolitinib, a JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor, was the first approved (for MPN), tofacitinib was the first jakinib used in vivo in an allograft rejection model and the first approved for immune-mediated disease, and deucravacitinib, an allosteric inhibitor targeting the pseudokinase domain, is approved for plaque psoriasis.

quotes.quote:
Ten jakinibs are now approved to treat a wide, and still expanding, 
variety of disorders driven by both innate and adaptive immune mechanisms (Table II).

Tofacitinib was the first jakinib used in vivo using a model of allograft rejection (Changelian 
et al., 2003). However, ruxolitinib, a JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor, was the first jakinib to receive 
approval for treatment of MPN

deucravacitinib, an allosteric 
JAK2 inhibitor that targets the PK domain (Burke et al., 2019). Deucravacitinib is approved 
for that treatment of plaque psoriasis.

experiment.system: human patients and preclinical models (allograft rejection)
experiment.perturbation: pharmacologic JAK inhibition with individual jakinibs
experiment.measurement: regulatory approval status and disease indications

text: The review reports that STAT inhibitors developed by interfering with SH2-mediated dimerization, DNA binding, transactivation, or by inducing STAT degradation are in multiple clinical trials, but no agents have been approved at this time.

quotes.quote:
Various strategies have been employed to develop STAT inhibitors, 
including interfering with SH2 mediated dimerization, DNA binding, or transactivation and 
inducing STAT degradation. Multiple inhibitors are in clinical trials, but no agents have been 
approved at this time.

experiment.system: clinical development pipeline for STAT-directed agents
experiment.perturbation: observational survey of STAT inhibitor trials
experiment.measurement: trial and approval status

text: Genomic analyses show that while motifs bound by STATs always reveal the canonical palindromic motifs, a substantial proportion of STAT-bound regions depart from the classical motif.

quotes.quote:
while genomic analysis of motifs bound 
by STATs always reveals the canonical palindromic motifs, a substantial proportion of 
STAT-bound regions depart from the classical motif.

experiment.system: cytokine-stimulated cells assayed by STAT ChIP-seq
experiment.perturbation: observational (genome-wide binding-site motif analysis)
experiment.measurement: proportion of STAT-bound regions matching the canonical palindromic motif

text: STATs can drive accessibility in regions lacking LDTF-binding motifs, and JAK inhibition prevents histone marking and PU.1 recruitment at latent enhancers, indicating primacy of STATs over lineage-defining transcription factors in establishing enhancer recognition in some settings such as STATs and T-bet in NK cells.

quotes.quote:
On the other hand, STATs can drive accessibility in 
regions that lack LDTF-binding motifs.

Consistent with the primacy of STATs over 
LDTFs in establishing enhancer recognition, JAK inhibition prevents histone marking and 
PU.1 recruitment (Ostuni et al., 2013).

experiment.system: stimulated immune cells (including NK cells and macrophages) assayed for chromatin accessibility and histone marks
experiment.perturbation: cytokine stimulation with or without JAK inhibition; STAT deficiency
experiment.measurement: chromatin accessibility, histone marks, PU.1 recruitment

text: A high-throughput protein–DNA interaction screen identified 17,718 direct protein–DNA interactions between 460 DNA motifs and 4191 human proteins, among them ERK2, which binds the DNA sequence G/CAAAG/C independently of its catalytic kinase activity and directly suppresses transcriptional elements including the gamma activated transcriptional element (GATE); the suppression is relieved by interferon-γ treatment, which depletes ERK2 from the regulated promoters.

quotes.quote:
A comprehensive screen identiﬁed not less than 17,718 direct protein–
DNA interactions between 460 DNA motifs and 4191 human proteins.

One of these proteins was ERK2, which was found
to bind to the DNA sequence G/CAAAG/C, independent of its catalytic
kinase activity.

ERK2 was shown to mainly repress
interferon-γ-induced genes that are normally regulated by GATE, and
this suppression is relieved upon interferon-γ treatment, by depleting
the ERK2 molecules from the regulated promoters

verdict_note: Core claim and all three numbers match p.4 verbatim; the experiment field's 'use of catalytically inactive ERK2' is a mild inference from the paper's 'independent of its catalytic kinase activity' but does not alter the assertion.

experiment.system: human proteins and DNA motifs in a protein-DNA interactome screen (protein microarray-type high-throughput profiling), plus interferon-γ-responsive gene reporters
experiment.perturbation: interferon-γ treatment; use of catalytically inactive ERK2
experiment.measurement: protein–DNA interaction profiles and transcriptional element activity/promoter occupancy

text: Stimulation of cells induces phosphorylation of the ERK1/2 substrate Elk1 on no less than 6–9 distinct sites, most of which were shown to activate the factor; the phosphorylation depends on direct binding via the D-domain of Elk1 to the CD/CRS domain of ERK1/2 and the hydrophobic DEF region of Elk1.

quotes.quote:
Stimulation of cells by various agents induces the
phosphorylation of Elk1 on no less than 6–9 distinct sites, and most of
these phosphorylations were shown to induce the activation of this
factor

experiment.system: cultured cells expressing the transcription factor Elk1
experiment.perturbation: stimulation by various extracellular agents
experiment.measurement: site-specific phosphorylation of Elk1 and its transcriptional activation

text: Phosphorylation of c-Fos on Ser374 and Ser362 in its C-terminus by nuclear ERK1/2 and their downstream RSKs is the first step in stabilizing c-Fos, which without phosphorylation is rapidly degraded and expressed for only several minutes.

quotes.quote:
Without phosphorylation, c-Fos is rapidly degraded, and
therefore, is expressed for only several minutes. However, phosphor-
ylation by nuclear ERK1/2 and their downstream RSKs on Ser374 and
Ser362 in the C-terminus of c-Fos is the ﬁrst step in its stabilization

experiment.system: stimulated mammalian cells expressing the immediate early gene product c-Fos
experiment.perturbation: mitogenic stimulation (ERK1/2 activation) versus resting/unphosphorylated c-Fos
experiment.measurement: c-Fos protein phosphorylation, stability and expression duration

text: In serum-starved cells Erf1 is dephosphorylated and nuclear, where it suppresses transcription; upon mitogenic stimulation translocated active ERK1/2 phosphorylate Erf1 via two FXF motifs interacting with the DEF-binding domain of ERK1/2, inducing CRM1-dependent nuclear export that relieves suppression, and preventing Erf1 phosphorylation reversed RAS-induced tumorigenicity and arrested fibroblasts in G0/G1.

quotes.quote:
Thus, in serum-
starved cells, Erf1 is dephosphorylated and located in the nucleus
where it suppresses transcription. Upon mitogenic and other
stimulations, Erf1 is phosphorylated by the translocated active
ERK1/2. This phosphorylation, in turn, induces CRM1-dependent
nuclear export of Erf1

Prevention of Erf1
phosphorylation was shown to reverse RAS-induced tumorigenicity
and to arrest ﬁbroblasts in the G0/G1 phase of the cell cycle.

experiment.system: serum-starved and mitogen-stimulated fibroblasts expressing Erf1 (Ets2 repressor factor)
experiment.perturbation: mitogenic stimulation; prevention of Erf1 phosphorylation (mutation)
experiment.measurement: Erf1 phosphorylation, nuclear export, transcriptional suppression, tumorigenicity and cell cycle arrest

text: HDAC4 directly interacts with ERK1/2 and is probably phosphorylated by it, and activation of the ERK1/2 cascade induced translocation of HDAC4 into the nucleus.

quotes.quote:
histone deacetylase 4
(HDAC4), which is a member of a family of enzymes that catalyze
the removal of acetyl groups from core histones, directly interacts
with ERK1/2, and is probably phosphorylated by it [109]. In addition,
activation of the ERK1/2 cascade induced translocation of HDAC4 into
the nucleus.

experiment.system: cultured cells expressing HDAC4 and ERK1/2
experiment.perturbation: activation of the ERK1/2 cascade
experiment.measurement: HDAC4–ERK1/2 interaction and HDAC4 subcellular localization

text: PARP1 catalytic activity is stimulated by the ERK1/2 cascade not through phosphorylation of PARP1 but by a direct interaction with ERK1/2, and activated PARP-1 in turn increased ERK2-catalyzed phosphorylation of Elk1; a similar non-catalytic activation by ERK1/2 was shown for topoisomerase 2α.

quotes.quote:
It was shown that the
catalytic activity of this protein is stimulated not only by DNA strand
breaks, but also by the ERK1/2 cascade [111]. Interestingly, the effect
of ERK1/2 on PARP1 activity was not mediated by phosphorylation
of the protein, but rather was induced by a direct interaction with
ERK1/2. In addition to its possible effects on chromatin function, the
activated PARP-1 also increased ERK2-catalyzed phosphorylation of
Elk1

experiment.system: PARP1 and ERK1/2 (biochemical/cellular assays)
experiment.perturbation: ERK1/2 cascade activation / direct ERK1/2 interaction versus DNA strand breaks
experiment.measurement: PARP1 polyADP-ribosylation activity and ERK2-catalyzed Elk1 phosphorylation

text: NUP50 was identified as a bona fide ERK1/2 substrate; ERK1/2 phosphorylate the FG repeat of NUP50 and other NUPs, reducing their affinity for importin-β family proteins, and ERK phosphorylation of NUP50 impaired translocation of importin-β and transportin.

quotes.quote:
a more informative study
has recently identiﬁed NUP50 as a bona ﬁde substrate of ERK1/2
[124]. It was further shown that ERK1/2 phosphorylate the FG
repeat of this NUP as well as other NUPs, and this phosphorylation
reduces their afﬁnity for importin-β family proteins. Importantly,
ERK phosphorylation of NUP50 resulted in impaired translocation of
importin-β and transportin

experiment.system: nucleoporins (NUP50) and importin-β/transportin in phosphoproteomic and transport assays
experiment.perturbation: ERK1/2-mediated phosphorylation of NUP FG repeats
experiment.measurement: NUP–importin-β binding affinity and importin-β/transportin translocation

text: When the leucine-rich NES of MEK1 is interrupted by replacing the sequence's Leu with Ala residues, MEK1 is found both in the nucleus and the cytoplasm, in contrast to wild-type MEK1 which is found exclusively in the cytoplasm.

quotes.quote:
when the NES is interrupted by
replacing the sequence's Leu with Ala residues, MEK1 is found both
in the nucleus and in the cytoplasm, in contrast to the wild-type
MEK1, which is found exclusively in the cytoplasm

experiment.system: cultured cells expressing wild-type or NES-mutated MEK1
experiment.perturbation: Leu-to-Ala substitution in the N-terminal NES of MEK1
experiment.measurement: subcellular localization of MEK1

text: ERK5's unique C-terminal half exhibits potent intrinsic stimulus-dependent transcriptional activity, is required for maximal MEF2 activity in response to calcium flux in T cells and for activation of the endogenous Nur77 gene when recruited to the Nur77 promoter via MEF2 sites; the transactivation is enhanced by ERK5 kinase activation and by autophosphorylation of the C-terminal half.

quotes.quote:
was shown to exhibit potent intrinsic stimulus-
dependent transcriptional activity [72]. This transcriptional activa-
tion domain of ERK5 is required for maximal MEF2 activity in
response to calcium ﬂux in T cells, and for the activation of the
endogenous Nur77 gene, when recruited to the Nur77 promoter via
MEF2 sites.

active ERK5 can autopho-
sphorylate itself at the C-terminal-half, and this was found to be
necessary for the enhancement of the transactivation activity of the
protein.

experiment.system: T cells expressing ERK5 and MEF2-dependent reporters/endogenous Nur77
experiment.perturbation: calcium flux stimulation; ERK5 activation and C-terminal autophosphorylation
experiment.measurement: MEF2 transcriptional activity, Nur77 gene activation and ERK5 transactivation activity

text: In cells where ERK5 is cytoplasmic, stimulation-induced phosphorylation of its TEY motif disrupts an intramolecular N-terminal/C-terminal interaction and hinders the NES, so that the exposed NLSs drive nuclear translocation; in resting cells the more potent CRM1/NES system yields predominant cytoplasmic localization, and the translocation requires phosphorylation by MEK5.

quotes.quote:
This translocation requires phosphor-
ylation by the upstream MEK5, which is essential not only for the
activation of ERK5, but also for conformational changes that allow the
nuclear accumulation [193].

After
stimulation, phosphorylation of the TEY motif in the kinase domain
of the ERK5 disrupts the intramolecular interaction and hinders the
NES domain, thus preventing ERK5 interaction with the nuclear
export machinery. As a result, ERK5 translocates into the nucleus due
to its NLSs, which continue to be exposed

experiment.system: cell lines in which ERK5 is cytoplasmic in resting state
experiment.perturbation: stimulation/MEK5-mediated TEY phosphorylation of ERK5
experiment.measurement: ERK5 intramolecular folding, NES/NLS exposure and nuclear accumulation

text: Mutation of residues in the kinase insert domain of ERK2 identified a Ser-Pro-Ser sequence (residues 244–246 of ERK2) whose mutation to Ala or deletion prevented ERK1/2 nuclear translocation; mass spectrometry and an anti p-SPS antibody confirmed stimulation-induced phosphorylation of the site, and phosphomimetic mutations of the two Ser residues accelerated nuclear translocation.

quotes.quote:
The sequence contained two Ser
residues separated by a Pro (Ser-Pro-Ser; SPS; 244–246 of ERK2)
that, when mutated to Ala or deleted, prevented the translocation.

Mass spectroscopic analysis,
as well as anti p-SPS antibody that was raised, conﬁrmed that this
site is indeed phosphorylated upon stimulation. As expected,
phosphomimetic mutations of the two Ser residues resulted in
accelerated nuclear translocation

experiment.system: cultured cells expressing wild-type and mutant ERK2 constructs
experiment.perturbation: Ala substitution, deletion, or phosphomimetic mutation of the SPS (244–246) site in the ERK2 kinase insert domain; mitogenic stimulation
experiment.measurement: ERK1/2 nuclear translocation, mass spectrometric and anti p-SPS antibody detection of phosphorylation

text: The 19 amino acids of the ERK1/2 KID acted autonomously as a nuclear translocation signal when ligated to a β-galactosidase-GFP construct (~145 kDa) or a 2GFP chimera (~55 kDa): a small portion entered nuclei basally and shuttling was facilitated by stimulation, a non-phosphorylatable 19 amino-acid stretch prevented translocation, and phosphomimetic mutants accelerated it without further effect of stimulation.

quotes.quote:
This was shown by ligating the 19 amino acids of ERK1/2's KID to
β-galactodidase-GFP construct (~145 kDa), or to a chimera of 2GFP
(~55 kDa). Only a small portion of this large protein was detected in
the nuclei of transfected cells, which was probably mediated by
endogenous basal phosphorylation, and this shuttle was facilitated by
stimulation. The attachment of non-phosphorylatible 19 amino-acid
stretch prevented the translocation, whereas phosphomimetic
mutants accelerated it without any further effect upon cellular
stimulation.

experiment.system: transfected cells expressing chimeric reporter proteins carrying the ERK1/2 KID
experiment.perturbation: ligation of wild-type, non-phosphorylatable, or phosphomimetic 19-amino-acid KID to β-galactosidase-GFP or 2GFP; cellular stimulation
experiment.measurement: nuclear accumulation of the chimeric proteins

text: An Si-RNA screen of nuclear shuttlers showed that only importin7 knockdown reduced both non-stimulated and stimulated nuclear translocation of ERK1/2; importin7 directly interacts with ERK1/2 with the interaction enhanced upon mitogenic stimulation dependent on SPS phosphorylation, whereas ERK1/2 interaction with certain NUPs is prevented by SPS phosphorylation.

quotes.quote:
we used Si-RNA of most of these nuclear
shuttlers. We found that only the Si-RNA of importin7 reduced
both non-stimulated and stimulated nuclear translocation of ERK1/2.
Moreover, we found that importin7 directly interacts with ERK1/2, and
this interaction is enhanced upon mitogenic stimulation dependent
on SPS phosphorylation. We also found that ERK1/2 can interact with

text: Kinetic measurements of Ca2+ blockade of Na+-CRAC currents give an association rate of ~4 × 10^6 M−1·s−1, conserved in native T-cell and recombinant STIM1-gated Orai1 and Orai3 channels, which is 100-fold slower than the rate in L-type CaV channels (~4 × 10^8 M−1·s−1).

Kinetic measurements of Ca2 blockade of the Na-CRAC
currents indicate that the association rate of Ca2 for its
block site is 4   106 M1·s1 (299, 420, 422). This rate,
which is conserved both in native T-cell and in recombinant
STIM1-gated Orai1 and Orai3 channels, is 100-fold slower
than the association rate of Ca2 in L-type Cav channels
(4   108 M1·s1; Ref. 184)

text: Upon readdition of extracellular Ca2+ to store-depleted cells, a small fraction of ICRAC appears instantaneously followed by a severalfold exponential increase over 10–20 s (calcium-dependent potentiation), while perfusion of divalent-free solutions diminishes CRAC channel activity by ~80% over tens of seconds; noise analysis suggests CDP reflects recruitment of channels from a silent state to high open probability, and the E106D mutation nearly completely eliminates depotentiation of Na+-ICRAC.

quotes.quote:
A small fraction of the current
appears instantaneously, representing channels active at the
time of Ca2 readdition (461). This instantaneous current is
followed by a severalfold exponential increase in current
over the following 10–20 s. Conversely, the removal of
extracellular Ca2 by perfusing divalent-free (DVF) solu-
tions diminishes CRAC channel activity by 80% over tens
of seconds due to reversal of CDP, or depotentiation.

Noise analysis suggests that CDP occurs through the
recruitment of CRAC channels from a “silent” state to one
of high open probability

the E106D mutation, which
affects ion selectivity, nearly completely eliminates depoten-
tiation of Na-ICRAC (420).

cantly narrowing the pore

(237)

text: Slow Ca2+-dependent inactivation of ICRAC appears during whole cell recordings as a decline in current over tens of seconds as [Ca2+] rises above ~200 nM, is strongly inhibited by slow intracellular Ca2+ buffering that captures Ca2+ only beyond ~100 nm from the channel, and can be attributed to mitochondrial depolarization since it is prevented by metabolic substrates and reinstated by mitochondrial inhibitors.

quotes.quote:
It appears during
whole cell recordings as a decline in current over tens of
seconds as [Ca2] rises to levels above 200 nM. The site of
action of Ca2 is global rather than local to CRAC chan-
nels, because slow inactivation is strongly inhibited by slow
intracellular Ca2 buffering conditions that can only cap-
ture incoming Ca2 effectively at distances 100 nm from
the channel (460).

In whole-cell recordings, slow inactivation can
be attributed to mitochondrial depolarization, as it can be
prevented by supplying the cell with metabolic substrates
and under these conditions be reinstated by mitochondrial
inhibitors (118, 149).

text: Activation of ICRAC is steeply temperature dependent with an abrupt decline around 21°C that is not observed once channels are already activated; separately, heating cells above 35°C causes STIM1 clustering without store depletion, but these heat-induced clusters do not trap or activate Orai1 and Ca2+ influx only occurs during cool-down below 37°C.

the activation of ICRAC is
steeply temperature dependent, displaying an abrupt de-
cline around 21°C (361). This nonlinearity appeared spe-
ciﬁc to the channel activation process, because it was not
