experiment.system: single mammalian cells with p53 reporter
experiment.perturbation: g-irradiation versus UV radiation
experiment.measurement: p53 dynamics and cell fate (arrest/recovery vs apoptosis)

text: Alternating ionophore/chelator 'patch-clamp' treatment showed that different calcium frequencies activate none, some, or all of NF-kB, NFAT, and Oct/OAP, and photoactivatable InsP3 release showed specific calcium frequencies could optimize gene expression.

quotes.quote:
This ‘‘patch-clamp’’ setup has revealed
that different frequencies of calcium activate none, some, or
all of the transcription factors NF-kB, NFAT, and Oct/OAP

the use of photoactivatable
inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate, the intracellular trigger for calcium
release, led to the same striking conclusion: speciﬁc frequencies
of intracellular calcium release could optimize gene expression

experiment.system: mammalian cells
experiment.perturbation: alternating calcium ionophores and chelators, or photoactivatable InsP3, to impose different calcium frequencies
experiment.measurement: transcription factor activation and gene expression

text: Genetic perturbation of NF-kB circuitry maps dynamics to gene specificity: IkBa-knockout MEFs show sustained rather than transient NF-kB upon TNFa and reveal that genes such as RANTES require sustained nuclear NF-kB, while LPS treatment of Tnf-deficient MEFs shows de novo TNFa production drives the sustained phase.

quotes.quote:
Knockout mouse embryonic ﬁbroblasts (MEFs)
lacking NF-kB’s negative regulator, IkBa, show sustained rather
than transient NF-kB activity upon TNFa treatment (Hoffmann
et al., 2002). This perturbation reveals that speciﬁc genes such
as RANTES require sustained activity of nuclear NF-kB.

Treatment with LPS
in Tnf-deﬁcient MEFs reveals that de novo TNFa production is
responsible for the sustained phase of NF-kB activity

experiment.system: mouse embryonic fibroblasts (IkBa-knockout or Tnf-deficient)
experiment.perturbation: genetic knockout of IkBa or Tnf, with TNFa or LPS stimulation
experiment.measurement: NF-kB activity dynamics and target gene expression

text: Leptomycin B blocks nuclear export and traps the inactive NF-kB-IkBa complex in the nucleus, so nuclear NF-kB localization is sustained but transcriptional activity is only transient, while natural NF-kB oscillations drive a monotonic increase in a fluorescent reporter gene; a later study found LMB does not affect early genes but inhibits intermediate and late target genes.

quotes.quote:
treatment of cells with leptomycin B (LMB) blocks
nuclear export, thereby trapping the inactive NF-kB-IkBa com-
plex in the nucleus (Nelson et al., 2004) (Figure 4A). As a result,
nuclear localization of the NF-kB protein is sustained, but its
transcriptional activity is only transient. In contrast, natural oscil-
lations of NF-kB trigger a monotonic increase in a ﬂuorescent
reporter gene.

a more recent study shows that LMB has no effect on the expres-
sion of early genes but leads to inhibition of intermediate and
late target genes

experiment.system: mammalian cells with fluorescent NF-kB and reporter genes
experiment.perturbation: leptomycin B treatment to block nuclear export
experiment.measurement: NF-kB nuclear localization dynamics and target gene expression

text: Timed doses of Nutlin-3 switched p53 dynamics from pulsed to sustained in g-irradiated cells, activating genes associated with irreversible fates such as apoptosis and senescence and pushing cells toward senescence — an outcome different from the apoptosis produced by comparable naturally sustained dynamics after UV.

quotes.quote:
Using carefully timed doses of the
small molecule Nutlin-3, which stabilizes p53 levels, we artiﬁ-
cially switched p53 dynamics from pulsed to sustained. This
switch in p53 dynamics led to activation of genes associated
with irreversible cellular fates such as apoptosis and senescence
and pushed cells toward senescence

the artiﬁcially sustained dynamics
in response to g-radiation lead to a different cellular outcome
(senescence) than would be predicted from the comparable
dynamics produced naturally by UV treatment (apoptosis)

experiment.system: mammalian cells that naturally pulse p53 after g-radiation
experiment.perturbation: timed doses of Nutlin-3 to sustain p53 levels
experiment.measurement: p53 dynamics, target gene activation, and cell fate (senescence)

text: Microfluidic, inhibitor-controlled modulation of Msn2 nuclear localization showed gene expression follows a Hill function-like response to Msn2 amplitude, a linear relationship with duration of nuclear localization, and a nonlinear increase with pulse frequency.

quotes.quote:
gene expression
exhibits a Hill function-like response to Msn2 amplitude, a linear
relationship with the duration of Msn2 nuclear localization, and
a nonlinear increase with increasing Msn2 pulse frequency.

A mutant isoform of protein kinase A that can be
controlled by a small-molecule inhibitor modulates nuclear accu-
mulation of Msn2 (Hao and O’Shea, 2012). This setup, which
includes a microﬂuidic device to dynamically administer inhibitor
treatment, alters the amplitude, frequency, and duration of Msn2
nuclear localization.

experiment.system: yeast with analog-sensitive PKA mutant and fluorescent Msn2 transcriptional reporter
experiment.perturbation: dynamic small-molecule inhibitor dosing via microfluidics to set Msn2 amplitude, frequency, and duration
experiment.measurement: reporter gene expression versus each dynamical feature

text: Target gene activation is nonlinear in cumulative transcription factor signal: Msn2 oscillations give lower target gene expression than sustained Msn2 at similar cumulative Msn2, and sustained p53 gives greater senescence gene expression than pulsed p53 at the same cumulative p53 signal.

quotes.quote:
The level of target gene expression in response to
Msn2 oscillations is lower than under sustained Msn2 even for
similar levels of cumulative Msn2 (Hao and O’Shea, 2012). Simi-
larly, sustained p53 leads to greater expression of senescence
genes than pulsed p53 even at the same cumulative p53 signal

experiment.system: single yeast cells (Msn2) and single mammalian cells (p53)
experiment.perturbation: imposed oscillatory versus sustained transcription factor dynamics
experiment.measurement: target gene expression compared against cumulative signal (area under the curve) per cell

text: Distinct feedback architectures explain ERK dynamics: negative feedback between ERK and SOS in the EGF pathway plus continued NGF signaling after receptor internalization and positive feedback on ERK through PKC account for transient versus sustained ERK.

quotes.quote:
the differences in ERK dynamics in response to EGF or NGF
arise in part because of a negative feedback between ERK
and Son of Sevenless (SOS) in the EGF pathway. In addition,
NGF, but not EGF, signaling continues after receptor internali-
zation, which contributes to the sustained activation of ERK
(Sasagawa et al., 2005). There is also evidence for positive
feedback on ERK activation through PKC

experiment.system: mammalian ERK/MAPK pathway in growth-factor-stimulated cells
experiment.perturbation: EGF versus NGF stimulation with modeling and pathway-component analysis
experiment.measurement: ERK activation dynamics attributed to specific feedback interactions

text: NF-kB dynamics are shaped by distinct network structures: transient TNFa response via NF-kB/IkB negative feedback, long-term dampening by A20 which has a longer half-life and acts farther upstream than IkB, and sustained LPS response via autocrine positive feedback through de novo TNFa production downstream of TLR4.

quotes.quote:
The transient activation of NF-kB in response
to TNFa is mediated by a negative feedback loop involving
NF-kB and one of its target gene products, IkB.

The A20 protein has a longer half-life and
acts farther upstream than IkB, which explains why it dampens
the long-term phase of NF-kB dynamics

sustained activation of NF-kB
in response to LPS is attributed to positive feedback through
an autocrine pathway that involves de novo TNFa production.

experiment.system: mammalian NF-kB signaling network (cells and mathematical models)
experiment.perturbation: TNFa or LPS stimulation with genetic perturbation of regulators (IkB, A20, TNF)
experiment.measurement: NF-kB activation dynamics attributed to specific feedback loops

text: An additional Wip1-mediated negative feedback between p53 and ATM distinguishes the g-radiation network from the UV network, and silencing Wip1 after g-radiation produces UV-like p53 dynamics; the g-radiation response, but not the UV response, is excitable, with low transient inputs sufficient to trigger a full p53 pulse.

quotes.quote: the network responding to g-radiation

includes an additional negative feedback between p53 and ATM
mediated by Wip1 (Figure 5B). This feedback is essential for trig-
gering p53 pulses in response to g-radiation because silencing
Wip1 after g-radiation produces UV-like dynamics (Batchelor
et al., 2008). In addition, the response to g-radiation, but not to
UV, is excitable, in which low transient inputs are sufﬁcient for
triggering a full p53 pulse.

experiment.system: single mammalian cells with p53 reporter
experiment.perturbation: g-radiation or UV, with silencing of Wip1
experiment.measurement: p53 pulse dynamics and excitability

text: Effector affinity and degradation rate can decode calcium dynamics: JNK and NF-kB have low affinity for calcium and slow degradation so they stay elevated after brief strong bursts, whereas NFAT has high affinity and rapid degradation so low sustained calcium preferentially activates NFAT.

quotes.quote:
JNK
and NF-kB, which respond to strong transient calcium bursts,
have a low afﬁnity for calcium and therefore require high concen-
trations for activity. This property, combined with a slow rate of
degradation, allows these downstream factors to stay elevated
after a brief stimulation with calcium. NFAT, in contrast, has
a high afﬁnity for calcium and a rapid rate of degradation.
Thus, low and sustained calcium levels will preferentially activate
NFAT over JNK and NF-kB

experiment.system: mammalian cells with calcium-responsive transcription factors
experiment.perturbation: transient versus sustained calcium stimulation
experiment.measurement: activation of JNK, NF-kB, and NFAT relative to affinity and degradation rates

text: Immediate early gene products act as a persistence detector for ERK: transient ERK induces c-Fos which is rapidly degraded, whereas persistent ERK directly phosphorylates newly synthesized c-Fos and stabilizes it in the nucleus, forming a feedforward loop with a fast arm (ERK activation) and slow arm (c-Fos accumulation).

quotes.quote:
When ERK activation is transient, gene products such as c-Fos
are induced but then undergo rapid degradation. When ERK
levels are persistent, however, newly synthesized c-Fos is
directly phosphorylated by the still-active kinase, which stabi-
lizes c-Fos in the nucleus.

a feedforward loop comprised of a fast arm (ERK activa-
tion) and a slow arm (c-Fos accumulation) serves as a persis-
tence detector for the duration of ERK activation

experiment.system: mammalian cells with ERK signaling
experiment.perturbation: transient versus persistent ERK activation
experiment.measurement: c-Fos induction, phosphorylation, stability, and downstream gene programs

text: A TLR4 gene regulatory circuit discriminates transient from persistent signals: Il6 expression requires persistent TLR4 activation while transient stimulation is filtered out; NF-kB and ATF3 in a first transcriptional wave control C/EBPd, which autoregulates for positive feedback and synergizes with NF-kB to allow productive Il6 expression, and the mechanism controls tens of additional host defense genes.

quotes.quote:
Expression of key inﬂam-
matory response genes such as interleukin 6 (Il6) requires persis-
tent TLR4 activation, whereas transient TLR4 stimulation is
effectively ﬁltered out.

Persistent activation of NF-kB induces expression of C/EBPd,
which regulates itself to provide strong positive feedback. In
addition, C/EBPd synergizes with NF-kB to allow productive
expression of Il6 and other inﬂammation genes (Figure 5D).
This sophisticated decoding mechanism controls not only Il6
but tens of additional genes associated with host defense
against infection

experiment.system: macrophage/TLR4 inflammatory signaling system
experiment.perturbation: transient versus persistent LPS (TLR4 agonist) stimulation
experiment.measurement: time-series gene expression profiling identifying transcriptional waves and Il6 expression

text: Insulin temporal patterns are multiplexed by the AKT network: intracellular AKT activation follows the same dynamical trends as external insulin, and distinct downstream effectors decode different features — S6K responding to the transient insulin response and G6Pase responding to low insulin concentrations.

quotes.quote:
The authors ﬁrst note that intra-
cellular AKT activation follows the same dynamical trends as
external insulin levels. By subjecting cells to different dynamical
patterns of insulin, they identify downstream effectors that
decode different features of the temporal proﬁle of AKT.

ribo-
somal protein S6 kinase (S6K), which is involved in protein
synthesis, responded to the transient insulin response that might
appear after a meal. Glucose-6-phosphatase (G6Pase), which is
involved in gluconeogenesis, responds to low insulin concentra-
tions that may be present during fasting.

experiment.system: insulin-sensing cells (e.g., liver) with AKT pathway
experiment.perturbation: application of different dynamical patterns of insulin
experiment.measurement: AKT activation dynamics and downstream effector (S6K, G6Pase) responses, compared with a computational model

text: A computational search over all possible three-node enzyme network topologies identified those capable of biochemical adaptation, a dynamical response that returns to baseline regardless of stimulus strength.

quotes.quote:
Ma et al. (2009) performed a compu-
tational search for all possible three-node enzyme network
topologies to identify those that could achieve biochemical
adaptation, a dynamical response that returns to baseline levels
regardless of stimulus strength.

experiment.system: in silico three-node enzyme network models
experiment.perturbation: exhaustive enumeration of network topologies with simulated stimulus
experiment.measurement: whether the topology achieves biochemical adaptation

text: Yeast Crz1 shows calcium-dependent frequency-modulated nuclear localization bursts, and this frequency modulation ensures target genes are transcribed in the same proportion regardless of promoter affinities for Crz1.

quotes.quote:
the yeast transcription factor Crz1, which shows
bursts of nuclear localization in response to calcium (Cai et al.,
2008). The concentration of calcium controls the frequency of
Crz1 bursts

Further
examination showed that the frequency of Crz1 activation
ensures that target genes are transcribed in the same proportion
regardless of promoter afﬁnities for Crz1

experiment.system: yeast cells expressing labeled Crz1
experiment.perturbation: varying extracellular calcium concentration
experiment.measurement: frequency of Crz1 nuclear localization bursts and relative target gene expression

text: Individual human cells vary widely in basal and peak ERK2 nuclear levels upon EGF stimulation, but the fold change in ERK relative to starting levels gives very similar response dynamics across cells.

quotes.quote:
Studies on the dynamics of ERK2 translocation in indi-
vidual human cells reveal a large variation in basal ERK2 nuclear
levels (Cohen-Saidon et al., 2009). Upon EGF stimulation, cells
show widely varying peak levels of ERK2. However, when the
fold change in ERK is quantiﬁed relative to the starting levels,
the dynamics of the responses are very similar

experiment.system: individual living human cells with tagged endogenous ERK2
experiment.perturbation: EGF stimulation
experiment.measurement: absolute and fold-change ERK2 nuclear translocation dynamics across single cells

text: In Bacillus subtilis, time-lapse imaging of the master regulator Spo0A in individual cells shows sporulation deferral time is controlled by a positive feedback loop allowing Spo0A to accumulate to a critical level across multiple cell-cycle generations.

quotes.quote:
Time-lapse imaging of the master-regulator
Spo0A in individual cells reveals that the deferral time is
controlled by a positive feedback loop that allows Spo0A to
accumulate to a critical level during multiple cell-cycle genera-
tions.

experiment.system: Bacillus subtilis individual cells
experiment.perturbation: observational time-lapse imaging under sporulation-deferring conditions
experiment.measurement: Spo0A pulse accumulation dynamics and sporulation deferral time

text: Oscillations of p53 have been observed in mice after total body irradiation.

quotes.quote:
Oscillations of p53, for example, have been shown to occur
in mice after total body irradiation (Hamstra et al., 2006).

experiment.system: live mice
experiment.perturbation: total body irradiation
experiment.measurement: p53 oscillatory behavior in vivo (bioluminescent imaging)

text: The authors state that experimentally-determined labeling radii for HRP, APEX, BioID, and TurboID enzymes fall in the range of 1-10 nm in living cells, and that labeling is better described as a contour map whose reactant concentration is highest at the enzyme and falls off nanometer by nanometer.

quotes.quote:
The experimentally-determined 
labeling radii for HRP, APEX, BioID, and TurboID enzymes fall in the range of 1-10 
nm in living cells16,17. However, instead of a fixed radius, it is more accurate to think of 
labeling by PL enzymes as a “contour map” in which the reactant concentration is highest 
at the PL enzyme and falls off nanometer by nanometer from the source17,18.

experiment.system: HRP, APEX, BioID and TurboID proximity labeling enzymes in living cells
experiment.perturbation: genetic fusion of PL enzyme and addition of small-molecule substrate generating diffusible reactive species
experiment.measurement: experimentally determined labeling radius (nm)

text: Peroxidase- and biotin-ligase generated reactive species are membrane impermeant, so the labeling contour map ends at membrane boundaries.

quotes.quote:
Peroxidase- 
and biotin-ligase generated reactive species are also membrane impermeant19, and thus the 
contour map ends at membrane boundaries.

experiment.system: peroxidase- and biotin ligase-based PL enzymes in cells
experiment.perturbation: observational (review of prior labeling experiments across membranes)
experiment.measurement: spatial extent of biotinylation relative to membrane boundaries

text: Roux et al. fused BioID, a promiscuous mutant of the E. coli biotin ligase BirA, directly to lamin A/C in HeLa cells and identified residents of the nuclear membrane and previously unknown interactors such as the nuclear pore complex.

quotes.quote:
To map lamin A/C’s interaction partners by PL, Roux et al. used BioID, a 
promiscuous mutant of the E. coli biotin ligase BirA12, and fused it directly to lamin A/C in 
HeLa cells11. Residents of the nuclear membrane and other previously unknown interactors, 
such as the nuclear pore complex were identified11.

experiment.system: HeLa cells expressing BioID fused to lamin A/C
experiment.perturbation: biotin addition to drive promiscuous biotinylation by BioID-lamin A/C fusion
experiment.measurement: streptavidin enrichment and mass spectrometry identification of biotinylated interactors

text: Chou et al. fused BioID to TDP43 to identify interactors of TDP43 aggregates and identified nucleocytoplasmic transport machinery, with follow-up studies implicating disruption of nucleoporin and transport factor functions as a pathology mechanism.

quotes.quote:
Chou et al. used BioID 
to identify interactors of TDP43 aggregates, a common histopathological marker of 
neurodegenerative disease, including ALS and frontotemporal dementia disease61. By 
fusing BioID to TDP43 to perform PL, the authors identified nucleocytoplasmic transport 
machinery and follow-up studies implicated TDP43 aggregates’ disruption of nucleoporin 
and transport factor functions as a mechanism for pathology61.

experiment.system: cells expressing BioID fused to TDP43 aggregates
experiment.perturbation: proximity biotinylation by BioID-TDP43 fusion
experiment.measurement: mass spectrometry identification of biotinylated interactors

text: By mapping the interactomes of 19 Hippo pathway proteins using BioID, the authors generated protein interaction networks for the Hippo pathway and identified numerous putative regulators and kinase substrates.

quotes.quote:
By mapping the interactomes 
of 19 pathway proteins using BioID, the authors generated protein interaction networks 
for the Hippo pathway and identified numerous putative regulators and kinase substrates36.

experiment.system: mammalian cells expressing BioID fusions to Hippo pathway proteins
experiment.perturbation: BioID fusion to 19 pathway proteins with biotin labeling
experiment.measurement: mass spectrometry-based interactome mapping

text: Etienne et al. used BioID with pharmacological proteasome inhibition to probe interactors of SCF E3 ligases β-TrCP1 and β-TrCP2 and validated twelve new substrates, including proteins involved in nuclear membrane integrity and translation control.

quotes.quote:
Etienne et al. used BioID in conjunction with pharmacological proteasome 
inhibition to probe interactors of SCF E3 ligases β-TrCP1 and β-TrCP240. Using this 
approach, the authors validated twelve new substrates, including proteins involved in nuclear 
membrane integrity and translation control.

experiment.system: cells expressing BioID fused to SCF E3 ligases β-TrCP1 and β-TrCP2
experiment.perturbation: pharmacological proteasome inhibition plus proximity biotinylation
experiment.measurement: mass spectrometry identification and validation of substrates

text: Cutler et al. fused BioID to p190 and p210 BCR-ABL tyrosine kinases, identified distinct interactomes of each fusion, and revealed that the Src family kinase Lyn is a preferential substrate of the p190 BCR-ABL fusion.

quotes.quote:
Cutler et al. fused BioID to p190 and p210 BCR-ABL 
tyrosine kinases, oncogenic protein fusions that result from chromosomal translocations42. 
Using PL, the authors identified distinct interactomes of each fusion and revealed that the 
Src family kinase Lyn, critical for transformation and drug resistance, is a preferential 
substrate of the p190 BCR-ABL fusion.

verdict_note: Claim text matches the paper, but the experiment field asserts 'interactome and phosphoproteome analysis by mass spectrometry'; the review only states that PL identified distinct interactomes of each fusion and that Lyn is a preferential substrate — no phosphoproteomic measurement is described.

experiment.system: cells expressing BioID fused to p190 and p210 BCR-ABL kinases
experiment.perturbation: proximity biotinylation by each kinase fusion
experiment.measurement: interactome and phosphoproteome analysis by mass spectrometry

text: Paek et al. applied APEX-based PL to AT1R and β2AR GPCR signaling in response to agonist activation; proteomic analysis of the changing interactome supported a role of endocytosis in secluding GPCRs from G-proteins and showed differing endocytosis kinetics for different GPCRs.

quotes.quote:
Paek et al. applied APEX-
based PL to AT1R and β2AR GPCR signaling, in response to agonist activation38, and 
proteomic analysis of the changing interactome supported the role of endocytosis in 
secluding GPCRs from G-proteins and demonstrated differing endocytosis kinetics for 
different GPCRs.

experiment.system: cells expressing APEX fusions to AT1R and β2AR GPCRs
experiment.perturbation: agonist activation followed by short APEX labeling
experiment.measurement: time-resolved quantitative proteomics of biotinylated interactomes

text: Lobingier et al. used APEX with a time-course and spatial references to capture the δ-opioid receptor interactome after agonist treatment and identified two ubiquitin-pathway proteins implicated as mediators of DOR endosomal trafficking to the lysosome.

quotes.quote:
Additionally, APEX has been used to capture snapshots of the δ-opioid 
receptor (DOR) interactome following treatment with agonist39. By identifying a time-
course of protein interactions and using a set of spatial references to increase specificity 
in the context of receptor internalization and trafficking, Lobingier et al. identified two 
ubiquitin-pathway proteins implicated as mediators of DOR endosomal trafficking to the 
lysosome39.

experiment.system: living cells expressing APEX-tagged δ-opioid receptor plus spatial reference APEX constructs
experiment.perturbation: agonist treatment time-course
experiment.measurement: proteomic identification of biotinylated interactors

text: Grainger et al. used the rapidity of APEX labeling to map the proteome specifically during Fzd9b receptor activation and identified EGFR as a key mediator of Wnt9a-Fzd9b interactions.

quotes.quote:
After 
demonstrating that Wnt9a signals by binding the Fzd9b receptor through an unknown 
factor, Grainger et al. leveraged the rapidity of APEX labeling to map the proteome 
specifically during receptor activation and identified EGFR as a key mediator of Wnt9a-
Fzd9b interactions70.

experiment.system: cells with APEX-tagged Fzd9b receptor
experiment.perturbation: Wnt9a-induced receptor activation with rapid APEX labeling
experiment.measurement: proteomic identification of proximal proteins

text: James et al. used rapamycin-dependent recruitment of nuclear-targeted APEX2-FKBP to inner nuclear membrane-localized FRB-VAPB but not ER membrane-localized FRB-VAPB, to probe only the inner nuclear membrane pool of VAPB.

quotes.quote:
By 
taking advantage of the chemically inducible dimerization FRB-FKBP system, the authors 
employed rapamycin-dependent recruitment of nuclear-targeted APEX2-FKBP to inner 
nuclear membrane-localized FRB-VAPB but not ER membrane-localized FRB-VAPB71.

experiment.system: cells expressing FRB-VAPB and nuclear-targeted APEX2-FKBP
experiment.perturbation: rapamycin-induced FRB-FKBP dimerization
experiment.measurement: proteomic mapping of biotinylated binding partners

text: Schopp et al. fused fragments of split-BioID to Ago2 and TNRC6, and to Ago2 and Dicer, and were able to differentiate the distinct interactomes of the two miRISC subcomplexes.

quotes.quote:
By fusing fragments of split-
BioID to Ago2 and TNRC6, and then to Ago2 and Dicer, the authors were able to 
differentiate distinct interactomes of each of the respective subcomplexes73.

experiment.system: cells expressing split-BioID fragments on Ago2/TNRC6 and Ago2/Dicer pairs
experiment.perturbation: reconstitution of split-BioID activity by subcomplex formation
experiment.measurement: proteomic comparison of biotinylated interactomes of each subcomplex

text: Zhang et al. used TurboID for biotin labeling in live N. benthamiana plants to identify interactors of the plant immune receptor N, identifying UBR7, a putative E3 ligase that downregulates N and mediates plant immunity against plant pathogens.

quotes.quote:
Zhang et al. utilized TurboID to 
identify interactors of a plant immune receptor called N78. By using TurboID to perform 
biotin labeling in live N. benthamiana plants, the authors identified the interactor UBR7, 
a putative E3 ligase that downregulates N and mediates plant immunity against plant 
pathogens.

experiment.system: live N. benthamiana plants expressing TurboID fused to immune receptor N
experiment.perturbation: biotin labeling in planta
experiment.measurement: mass spectrometry identification of biotinylated interactors

text: In the first in vivo mouse PL study, Dingar et al. fused BioID to c-Myc, expressed the fusion in xenografted cells, and performed biotin labeling over the course of two days before proteomic analysis; a subsequent mouse study by Uezu et al. used BioID to map the inhibitory postsynaptic density over seven days of biotin labeling, long labeling times the authors attribute to the low activity of BioID.

quotes.quote:
In the first in vivo mouse PL study, Dingar et al. fused BioID to the oncogene 
c-Myc, expressed this fusion construct in xenografted cells, and performed biotin labeling 
over the course of two days before proteomic analysis56. In a subsequent mouse study, Uezu 
et al. used BioID to map the inhibitory postsynaptic density over a course of seven days of 
biotin labeling before proteomic analysis55. These long labeling times were likely required 
for generating sufficient biotinylated material for mass spectrometry due to the low activity 
of BioID.

experiment.system: mice bearing BioID-c-Myc xenografts; mouse brain expressing BioID fusion at inhibitory postsynaptic density
experiment.perturbation: in vivo biotin administration for two days or seven days
experiment.measurement: mass spectrometry proteomic analysis of biotinylated proteins

numbers.quantity: biotin labeling duration, c-Myc xenograft study
biotin labeling duration, postsynaptic density study

text: APEX-seq uses an APEX fusion protein to directly biotinylate proximal endogenous RNAs after 1 minute labeling in live cells, with streptavidin enrichment for RNA-seq; an improved variation uses the more efficient substrate biotin-aniline to improve RNA capture efficiency.

quotes.quote:
APEX-seq bypasses the need for RNA-protein 
crosslinking altogether, and uses an APEX fusion protein to directly biotinylate proximal 
endogenous RNAs (Fig. 2b) 98,99. After 1 minute labeling in live cells, streptavidin is 
used to enrich tagged RNAs for RNA-seq. An improved variation of APEX-seq uses a 
more efficient substrate, biotin-aniline, which improves RNA capture efficiency100.

experiment.system: live cells expressing APEX fusion proteins
experiment.perturbation: 1 minute proximity biotinylation of endogenous RNA (with biotin-phenol or biotin-aniline substrate)
experiment.measurement: streptavidin enrichment followed by RNA-seq capture efficiency

text: Fazal et al. used APEX-seq to generate a transcriptome-wide subcellular RNA atlas in HEK293T cells, correlating RNA-transcript location with genome architecture and protein localization; the authors also used APEX-seq to quantify RNA dynamics at the outer mitochondrial membrane in response to drug perturbations and identified two distinct pathways for mRNA localization there.

quotes.quote:
Fazal et 
al. used APEX-seq to generate a transcriptome-wide subcellular RNA atlas in HEK293T 
cells, uncovering numerous functional insights and correlating RNA-transcript location 
with genome architecture and protein localization98. By taking advantage of APEX’s 
rapid kinetics, we used APEX-seq to quantify RNA dynamics at the outer mitochondrial 
membrane in response to drug perturbations and identified two distinct pathways for mRNA 
localization to the outer mitochondrial membrane98.

experiment.system: HEK293T cells with APEX targeted to multiple subcellular compartments including the outer mitochondrial membrane
experiment.perturbation: drug perturbations plus rapid APEX RNA biotinylation
experiment.measurement: RNA-seq of biotinylated transcripts (subcellular RNA localization and dynamics)

numbers.quantity: mRNA localization pathways to OMM identified

text: CAP-seq uses light-activated miniSOG for proximity-dependent photo-oxidation of RNA nucleobases captured by amine probes, with a temporal resolution of ~20 min, lower than that of APEX-seq (<1 min).

quotes.quote:
An alternative protein-centric PL method, CAP-seq, incorporates light-activated miniSOG 
for proximity-dependent photo-oxidation of RNA nucleobases, which can be subsequently 
captured by amine probes and identified by high-throughput sequencing101 (Fig. 2c). 
Although the temporal resolution of CAP-seq (~20 min) is lower than that of APEX-
seq (<1 min), both approaches offer distinct mechanisms of RNA labeling and may be 
complementary.

experiment.system: cells expressing miniSOG fusions for RNA labeling
experiment.perturbation: blue light illumination driving photo-oxidation, amine probe capture
experiment.measurement: high-throughput sequencing of labeled RNA; labeling time resolution

text: RaPID, the first RNA-centric PL method, tags an RNA of interest with a BoxB aptamer to recruit a λ-N–BASU biotin ligase fusion that biotinylates RNA binding proteins, and was used to discover host proteins that interact with Zika virus RNA.

quotes.quote:
The 
first RNA-centric PL method reported, RaPID (RNA-protein interaction detection), allows 
for the biotinylation of RNA binding proteins (RBPs) by tagging an RNA of interest with 
a BoxB aptamer to recruit a fusion protein of λ-N and the biotin ligase BASU14 (Fig. 2d). 
RaPID was used to discover host proteins that interact with Zika virus RNA14.

experiment.system: cells expressing BoxB-tagged RNA of interest and λ-N–BASU fusion
experiment.perturbation: aptamer-mediated recruitment of biotin ligase to target RNA
experiment.measurement: mass spectrometry identification of biotinylated RBPs

text: Han et al. targeted catalytically inactive RfxCas13d fused with APEX2 and a double-stranded RNA binding domain to human telomerase RNA and discovered a previously unknown interaction between hTR and the m6A demethylase ALKBH5, with subsequent studies showing ALKBH5 regulation affects telomerase complex assembly and activity.

quotes.quote:
Han et al. targeted catalytically inactive RfxCas13d fused 
with APEX2 and a double-stranded RNA binding domain (dsRBD) (to enhance its binding 
affinity) to human telomerase RNA (hTR)109 (Fig. 2f). Using this approach, the authors 
discovered a previously unknown interaction between hTR and the N6-methyladenosine 
(m6A) demethylase, ALKBH5, and subsequent studies showed that post-transcriptional 
regulation by ALKBH5 affects both telomerase complex assembly and activity.

experiment.system: human cells expressing dRfxCas13d-dsRBD-APEX2 with guides targeting hTR
experiment.perturbation: CRISPR-guided targeting of APEX2 to endogenous hTR and biotinylation
experiment.measurement: mass spectrometry identification of RNA-associated proteins

text: ALaP, an APEX-mediated chromatin labeling and purification method conceptually analogous to APEX-RIP, offers improved sensitivity but decreased specificity compared to traditional ChIP-seq, and has been adapted to map genomic contact sites of PML bodies.

quotes.quote:
ALaP (for APEX-
mediated chromatin labeling and purification) is conceptually analogous to APEX-RIP 
for RNA identification114, and offers improved sensitivity but decreased specificity in 
comparison to traditional ChIP-seq. ALaP has also been further adapted for mapping the 
genomic contact sites of promyelocytic leukemia (PML) bodies, phase-separated nuclear 
structures that physically interact with chromatin.

experiment.system: living cells expressing APEX fused to a chromatin-associated protein of interest
experiment.perturbation: APEX biotinylation followed by formaldehyde crosslinking of proteins to DNA
experiment.measurement: streptavidin enrichment and next-generation sequencing of associated DNA regions, compared with ChIP-seq

text: Fusing APEX2 with catalytically inactive dCas9 to target specific genomic loci such as telomeres and centromeres allowed associated proteins to be biotinylated, enriched, and analyzed by mass spectrometry.

quotes.quote:
Fusing APEX2 with catalytically inactive dCas9 to target specific genomic 
loci (e.g. telomeres and centromeres) allowed associated proteins to be biotinylated, 
enriched, and analyzed by mass spectrometry115,116

experiment.system: cells expressing dCas9-APEX2 with targeting guide RNAs
experiment.perturbation: guide-directed targeting to telomeres/centromeres plus APEX2 biotinylation
experiment.measurement: streptavidin enrichment and mass spectrometry of locus-associated proteins

text: ChromID, which fuses BASU to engineered readers specific to chromatin modifications, was used to interrogate protein interactomes at specific chromatin marks and identified novel promoter regions modified by H3K4me3 and H3K27me3.

quotes.quote:
ChromID was used to interrogate protein interactomes at specific chromatin 
marks by fusing BASU to engineered readers specific to chromatin modifications120 (Fig. 
2h). ChromID identified novel promoter regions modified by H3K4me3 and H3K27me3120.

experiment.system: cells expressing BASU fused to engineered chromatin-mark reader domains
experiment.perturbation: reader-directed proximity biotinylation at chromatin marks
experiment.measurement: identification of associated proteins and modified promoter regions

text: APEX-based PL applied to mapping proteins associated with mitochondrial DNA uncovered seven previously unknown mitochondrial nucleoid-associated proteins.

quotes.quote:
APEX-based PL has also been applied for mapping proteins 
associated with mitochondrial DNA, uncovering seven previously unknown mitochondrial 
nucleoid-associated proteins26.

experiment.system: living cells with APEX targeted to mitochondrial DNA/nucleoids
experiment.perturbation: proximity biotinylation of nucleoid-proximal proteins
experiment.measurement: mass spectrometry identification of mtDNA-associated proteins

text: The authors used APEX2 to generate a highly specific proteome of the outer mitochondrial membrane by comparing the extent of biotinylation of proteins by APEX2 targeted to the OMM versus APEX2 expressed in the cytosol, and note this ratiometric analysis filters out dual-localized proteins residing in both cytosol and OMM.

quotes.quote:
For example, we have previously used APEX2 to generate a highly 
specific proteome of the outer mitochondrial membrane (OMM) by comparing the extent 
of biotinylation of proteins by APEX2 targeted to the OMM versus APEX2 expressed 
in the cytosol23. However, PL-based technology may exhibit decreased sensitivity due to 
various reasons. For instance, in the example described above, the ratiometric analysis filters 
out dual-localized proteins - proteins that reside in both the cytosol and on the OMM.

experiment.system: living human cells expressing APEX2 targeted to the OMM or to the cytosol
experiment.perturbation: comparison of OMM-targeted versus cytosolic APEX2 biotinylation
experiment.measurement: ratiometric quantitative mass spectrometry of biotinylated proteins

text: The authors state that proteins lacking surface-exposed tyrosines (for APEX) or lysines (for BioID/TurboID) may not be detected, and that different PL enzymes may exhibit biases towards labeling certain protein substrates.

quotes.quote:
Furthermore, proteins that lack surface exposed tyrosines (in the case of APEX) or lysines 
(in the case of BioID/TurboID) may not be detected, and different PL enzymes may exhibit 
biases towards labeling certain protein substrates121.

experiment.system: PL enzymes (APEX, BioID/TurboID) labeling cellular proteomes
experiment.perturbation: observational (comparison of enzyme labeling chemistries across substrates)
experiment.measurement: detection of biotinylated proteins by mass spectrometry as a function of residue availability

text: A crystal structure of the ternary complex of agonist-occupied monomeric β2AR with nucleotide-free Gs heterotrimer was determined at 3.2 Å overall resolution, from a T4L-β2AR-Gs-Nb35 complex crystallized in lipidic cubic phase; crystals grew to 250 microns and diffracted to 2.9 Å, with a 3.2 Å data set compiled from 20 crystals and solved by molecular replacement.

quotes.quote:
The T4L-β2AR-Gs-Nb35 complex was 
used to obtain crystals that grew to 250 microns (Fig. S2) in LCP (monoolein 7.7) and 
diffracted to 2.9 Å. A 3.2 Å data set was obtained from 20 crystals and the structure was 
determined by molecular replacement (Online Methods).

We report this structure to an overall 
resolution of 3.2 Å.

experiment.system: agonist (BI-167107)-bound T4L-β2AR fused protein in complex with nucleotide-free Gs heterotrimer plus nanobody Nb35, in lipidic cubic phase (MAG 7.7)
experiment.perturbation: complex formation with apyrase-mediated GDP removal, detergent exchange into MNG-3, Nb35 addition, LCP crystallization
experiment.measurement: X-ray diffraction data collection at APS 23ID-B, molecular replacement structure solution and refinement

text: Relative to the inactive carazolol-bound β2AR, the active-state β2AR in the Gs complex shows a 14 Å outward movement of TM6 measured at the Cα of E268, plus a smaller outward movement and α-helical extension of the cytoplasmic end of TM5 by 7 residues, with 26 amino acids of ICL3 disordered and ICL2 forming an α-helix.

quotes.quote:
The largest difference between the inactive and active structures is a 14 Å outward 
movement of TM6 when measured at the Cα carbon of E268. There is a smaller outward 
movement and extension of the cytoplasmic end of the TM5 helix by 7 residues. A stretch of 
26 amino acids in the third intracellular loop (ICL3) is disordered.

which 
forms an extended loop in the inactive β2AR structure and an α-helix in the β2AR-Gs 
complex

experiment.system: β2AR-Gs complex crystal structure vs. previously determined inactive carazolol-bound β2AR structure
experiment.perturbation: agonist occupancy and nucleotide-free Gs coupling (structural comparison)
experiment.measurement: comparison of atomic coordinates; distance of TM6 Cα displacement, helix extension length

text: The β2AR in the β2AR-Gs complex closely resembles the nanobody-stabilized active-state β2AR-Nb80 structure, with an overall root mean square deviation of approximately 0.6 Å and a largest divergence of a 3 Å outward movement at the end of helix 6 in the β2AR-Gs complex; among conserved E/DRY and NPxxY residues only Arg131 differs significantly.

quotes.quote:
The overall root mean square deviation between the β2AR components in the β2AR-Gs and 
β2AR-Nb80 structures is approximately 0.6 Å, and they differ most at the cytoplasmic ends 
of transmembrane helices 5 and 6 where they interact with the different proteins (Fig 3b-d). 
The largest divergence is a 3 Å outward movement at the end of helix 6 in the β2AR-Gs 
complex.

Of these residues, only Arg131 differs significantly between these two 
structures.

experiment.system: β2AR-Gs crystal structure compared with β2AR-Nb80 active-state structure
experiment.perturbation: observational structural comparison (Gs versus G-protein mimetic nanobody Nb80 as stabilizer)
experiment.measurement: root mean square deviation of atomic coordinates and residue-level displacement

text: The β2AR contacts only the Ras-like domain of Gαs, with no direct interactions with Gβ or Gγ; the total buried surface of the β2AR-GαsRas interface is 2576 Å2 (1300 Å2 for GαsRas and 1276 Å2 for the β2AR), formed by ICL2, TM5 and TM6 of the receptor and the α5-helix, αN-β1 junction, top of the β3-strand and α4-helix of GαsRas.

quotes.quote:
There are no direct interactions with Gβ or Gγ subunits. The total buried surface of the 
β2AR-GαsRas interface is 2576 Å2 (1300 Å2 for GαsRas and 1276 Å2 for the β2AR). This 
interface is formed by ICL2, TM5 and TM6 of the β2AR, and by α5-helix, the αN-β1 
junction, the top of the β3-strand, and the α4-helix of GαsRas

experiment.system: β2AR-Gs complex crystal structure
experiment.perturbation: observational (structure analysis)
experiment.measurement: buried surface area calculation and identification of interface segments

text: Phe139, at the beginning of the ICL2 helix, sits in a hydrophobic pocket formed by Gαs His41, Val213 and Phe376, Arg380 and Ile383 of the α5-helix, and the ICL2 helix is stabilized by an interaction between Asp130 of the conserved DRY sequence and Tyr141.

quotes.quote:
a noteworthy interaction 
involves Phe139, which is located at the beginning of the ICL2 helix and sits in a 
hydrophobic pocket formed by Gαs His41 at the beginning of the β1-strand, Val213 at the 
start of the β3-strand and Phe376, Arg380 and Ile383 in the α5-helix (Fig 4c).

the ICL2 helix is stabilized by an 
interaction between Asp130 of the conserved DRY sequence and Tyr141 in the middle of 
the ICL2 helix (Fig. 4c).

experiment.system: β2AR-Gs complex crystal structure
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: inspection of residue contacts in the refined structure

text: In the nucleotide-free complex the α-helical domain of Gαs is greatly displaced relative to the Ras-like domain, an approximately 127° rotation about the domain junction, with GαsAH moving as a rigid body; the authors note its crystallographic position likely reflects only one of an ensemble of conformations, stabilized by crystal packing.

quotes.quote:
The most surprising observation in the β2AR-Gs complex is the large displacement of the 
GαsAH relative to GαsRas (an approximately 127° rotation about the junction between the 
domains) (Fig. 5a). GαsAH moves as a rigid body as shown by the alignment of β2AR-Gs 
with GαsAH from the crystal structure of Gαs-GTPγS26

its location in this crystal structure most likely 
reflects only one of an ensemble of conformations that it can adopt under physiological 
conditions, but has been stabilized by crystal packing interactions

experiment.system: β2AR-Gs complex crystal structure compared with Gαs-GTPγS structure (1AZT)
experiment.perturbation: nucleotide-free state produced by apyrase-mediated GDP removal upon receptor coupling
experiment.measurement: superposition of Ras domains and measurement of rotation angle of the α-helical domain

numbers.quantity: rotation of GαsAH relative to GαsRas

text: Nb35, used as a crystallization chaperone, binds at the interface between Gβ and GαsRas and none of its Ras-domain contacts are involved in interactions with GαsAH; superimposing Gαs-GTPγS (1AZT) or aligning Gβ of the Gi-GDP heterotrimer (1GP2) with β2AR-Gs shows no overlap between Nb35 and the alpha helical domain, arguing Nb35 is not responsible for the GαsAH displacement.

quotes.quote:
None of the Nb35 contacts 
on the Ras domain are involved in interactions with GαsAH based on the crystal structure of 
Gαs-GTPγS (1AZT). Moreover, if we superimpose the structures of the Ras domains of 
Gαs-GTPγS (1AZT) and β2AR-Gs, there is no overlap between Nb35 and the alpha helical 
domain of Gαs-GTPγS (Fig. S6). Similarly, if we align the Gβ subunits of the Gi-GDP 
heterotrimer (1GP2) with that of β2AR-Gs, there is no overlap between Nb35 and the alpha 
helical domain of Gi (Fig. S6).

experiment.system: β2AR-Gs crystal structure with Nb35, compared to Gαs-GTPγS (1AZT) and Gi-GDP heterotrimer (1GP2)
experiment.perturbation: in silico superposition of Ras domains / Gβ subunits
experiment.measurement: steric overlap between Nb35 and the Gα α-helical domain

text: Based on comparison with the GDP-bound Gi heterotrimer structure, the authors do not observe large changes in interactions between GαsRas and Gβγ upon complex formation with β2AR, while noting that because Nb35 binds at the GαsRas-Gβ interface they cannot exclude that it influences the relative orientation of that interface.

quotes.quote:
Based on the structure of the GDP-bound Gi heterotrimer 31, we do not observe 
large changes in interactions between GαsRas and Gβγ upon formation of the complex with 
β2AR.

therefore, we cannot exclude the possibility that Nb35 may influence the relative orientation of the GαsRas-Gβγ 
interface in the crystal structure.

experiment.system: β2AR-Gs complex structure compared with GDP-bound Gi heterotrimer structure
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: comparison of Gα-Gβγ interface contacts

text: Compared with metarhodopsin II bound to a transducin carboxyl-terminal peptide, the conformational changes in TM5 and TM6 are smaller in metarhodopsin II and the carboxyl terminal alpha helix of transducin is tilted by approximately 30° relative to the homologous region of Gs.

quotes.quote:
The conformational changes in TM5 and 
TM6 are smaller in metarhodopsin II, and the position of the carboxyl terminal alpha helix 
of transducin is tilted by approximately 30° relative to the position of the homologous region 
of Gs.

experiment.system: β2AR-Gs complex structure versus metarhodopsin II-transducin C-terminal peptide structure (PDB 3PQR)
experiment.perturbation: observational structural comparison
experiment.measurement: tilt angle of the G protein C-terminal helix and extent of TM5/TM6 movement

numbers.quantity: tilt of transducin C-terminal helix relative to Gs

text: In competition binding with [3H]-DHA and isoproterenol, the fraction of β2AR in the Ki high state is 0.55 for β2AR reconstituted in HDL particles with Gs heterotrimer and 0.68 for the β2AR-Gαs peptide fusion expressed in Sf9 cell membranes.

quotes.quote:
The fraction of β2AR in the Ki high state for the β2AR with 
Gs is 0.55.

The fraction of β2AR in the Ki high state for the β2AR-Gαs peptide 
fusion is 0.68.

experiment.system: β2AR reconstituted in HDL particles ± Gs heterotrimer; β2AR and β2AR-Gαs peptide fusion in Sf9 cell membranes
experiment.perturbation: presence of Gs heterotrimer or fused Gαs C-terminal peptide
experiment.measurement: [3H]-DHA/isoproterenol competition binding fitted to a two-site model, fraction in high-affinity Ki state

numbers.quantity: fraction in Ki high state, β2AR with Gs
fraction in Ki high state, β2AR-Gαs peptide fusion

text: A stable β2AR-Gs complex was formed by mixing purified GDP-Gs at approximately 100 μM with molar excess agonist (BI-167107)-bound β2AR in dodecylmaltoside and adding apyrase to hydrolyze released GDP; removal of GDP was essential because both GDP and GTP disrupt the high-affinity β2AR-Gs interaction.

quotes.quote:
We found that a relatively stable 
β2AR-Gs complex could be prepared by mixing purified GDP-Gs (approximately 100 μM 
final concentration) with a molar excess of purified β2AR bound to a high affinity agonist 
(BI-167107, Boehringer Ingelheim)12 in dodecylmaltoside solution. Apyrase, a non-
selective purine pyrophosphatase, was added to hydrolyze GDP released from Gs on 
forming a complex with the β2AR. Removal of GDP was essential since both GDP and GTP 
can disrupt the high-affinity interaction between β2AR and Gs (Fig. S1a).

experiment.system: purified β2AR and Gs heterotrimer in detergent solution
experiment.perturbation: agonist BI-167107 binding, apyrase addition to remove GDP, versus presence of GDP/GTP
experiment.measurement: complex stability assessed by chromatography (size exclusion/affinity purification)

text: Complex stability was enhanced by exchange into a maltose neopentyl glycol detergent (MNG-3), identified from screening over 50 amphiphiles; the β2AR-Gs complex in DDM shows significant dissociation after 48 hours at 4°C, whereas in MNG-3 the complex could be incubated at room temperature for 24 hrs without noticeable degradation.

quotes.quote:
The stability of the complex was enhanced by exchanging it into a recently 
developed maltose neopentyl glycol detergent (NG-310, Anatrace)13. The complex could be 
incubated at room temperature for 24 hrs without any noticeable degradation

The β2AR-Gs complex in DDM shows significant dissociation after 48 hours at 4°C (figure 
S11a). We screened and characterized over 50 amphiphiles (data not shown) and identified 
MNG-3 12,13 (NG-310, Affymetrix-Anatrace) and its closely related analogs as detergents 
that substantially stabilize the complex (figure S11a,b).

experiment.system: purified β2AR-Gs complex in detergent solution
experiment.perturbation: detergent exchange from DDM into MNG-3; incubation at 4°C or room temperature
experiment.measurement: gel filtration/chromatographic assessment of complex dissociation over time

text: Nanobodies Nb35 and Nb37, raised in llamas against the cross-linked β2AR-Gs-BI-167107 ternary complex, bind the ternary complex but not the free receptor in ELISA and protect the complex from dissociation by GTPγS.

quotes.quote:
We obtained a nanobody (Nb35) that binds to the complex and prevents 
dissociation of the complex by GTPγS (Fig. S1).

Nb35 and Nb37 were selected for further 
characterization because they bind the β2AR-Gs-BI-167107 ternary complex but not the free 
receptor in an ELISA assay. Nanobody binding to the β2AR-Gs complex was confirmed by 
size exclusion chromatography (figure S1d), and it was noted that both nanobodies protected 
the complex from dissociation by GTPγS

experiment.system: llama-derived nanobody phage display library selected against BS2G cross-linked β2AR-Gs-BI-167107 complex in biotinylated HDL particles
experiment.perturbation: immunization/biopanning; GTPγS challenge of the complex
experiment.measurement: ELISA binding to complex vs free receptor; size exclusion chromatography of complex integrity

text: BI-167107, identified from screening approximately 50 different β2AR agonists, has a dissociation half-time of approximately 30 hrs, providing greater stabilization of the active G protein-bound receptor than other full agonists such as isoproterenol.

quotes.quote:
BI-167107, which was identified from screening 
and characterizing approximately 50 different β2AR agonists (data not shown), has a 
dissociation half-time of approximately 30 hrs, providing higher degree of stabilization to 
the active G protein-bound receptor than other full agonists such as isoproterenol 12.

experiment.system: purified β2AR with candidate agonists
experiment.perturbation: screening of approximately 50 β2AR agonists
experiment.measurement: ligand dissociation half-time and stabilization of the agonist-bound receptor

text: The complex crystallized in space group P21 with a single complex per asymmetric unit, arrayed in alternating aqueous and lipidic layers with lattice contacts formed almost exclusively between soluble components, leaving receptors widely separated in the membrane plane; the electron density is highest at the β2AR-GαsRas interface and much weaker for the extracellular half of the receptor.

quotes.quote:
The β2AR-Gs complex crystallized in space group P21, with a single complex in each 
asymmetric unit.

Complexes are 
arrayed in alternating aqueous and lipidic layers with lattice contacts formed almost 
exclusively between soluble components of the complex, leaving receptor molecules 
suspended between G protein layers and widely separated from one another in the plane of 
the membrane.

The quality of the electron density maps for the β2AR is highest at the β2AR-GαsRas 
interface, and much weaker for the extracellular half.

experiment.system: T4L-β2AR-Gs-Nb35 crystals grown in lipidic cubic phase
experiment.perturbation: observational (crystallographic analysis)
experiment.measurement: space group determination, lattice packing analysis, electron density map quality

text: Anisotropy analysis of the final diffraction dataset indicated diffraction along the a* axis was superior to other directions, and reflections were anisotropically truncated at resolution limits of 2.9, 3.2, and 3.2 Angstroms along a*, b*, and c* on the basis of an F/σ(F) cutoff of 3.

quotes.quote:
Analysis of the final dataset by the UCLA diffraction anisotropy 
server 38 indicated that diffraction along the a* axis was superior to that in other directions. 
On the basis of an F/σ(F) cutoff of 3 along each reciprocal space axis, reflections were 
subjected to an anisotropic truncation with resolution limits of 2.9, 3.2, and 3.2 Angstroms 
along a*, b*, and c* prior to use in refinement.

experiment.system: final compiled diffraction dataset from 20 T4L-β2AR-Gs-Nb35 crystals
experiment.perturbation: anisotropic truncation of reflections
experiment.measurement: resolution limits along reciprocal axes by F/σ(F) criterion

numbers.quantity: anisotropic resolution limits along a*, b*, c*

text: In the T4L-β2AR construct, mutation of M96 and M98 in the first extracellular loop to Thr increased the otherwise low expression level without affecting [3H]-DHA binding affinity, but caused a small, approximately two-fold decrease in affinity for isoproterenol.

quotes.quote:
M96 and M98 in the first extracellular loop were each 
replaced by Thr to increase the otherwise low expression level of T4L-β2AR. The threonine 
mutations did not affect ligand binding affinity for [3H]-DHA, but caused a small, 
approximately two-fold decrease in affinity for isoproterenol (data not shown).

experiment.system: T4L-β2AR fusion construct expressed in insect cells
experiment.perturbation: M96T and M98T mutations in extracellular loop 1
experiment.measurement: expression level and radioligand binding affinity for [3H]-DHA and isoproterenol

text: The β2AR-Gs complex in MNG-3 remained stable up to 10 mM TCEP by gel filtration and crystal growth improved at TCEP concentrations above 1 mM, whereas DDM-solubilized β2AR loses its ability to bind [3H]-DHA in 10 mM TCEP; iodoacetamide could not be used to block reactive cysteines as it caused complex dissociation.

quotes.quote:
it was discovered later that crystal growth 
improved at even higher TCEP concentrations (above 1 mM) compared to 100 μM TCEP, 
and that the integrity of the β2AR-Gs complex in MNG-3 was stable to 10 mM TCEP as 
measured by gel filtration analysis (figure S12c). In contrast, DDM-solubilized β2AR loses 
its ability to bind the high-affinity antagonist [3H]-dihydroalprenolol ([3H]-DHA) in 10 mM 
TCEP (data not shown)

Iodoacetamide could not be used to block reactive cysteines on Gs alpha and beta subunits 
as it caused dissociation of the β2AR-Gs complex (figure S12b).

experiment.system: purified β2AR-Gs complex in MNG-3 and DDM-solubilized β2AR
experiment.perturbation: varying TCEP concentration (100 μM to 10 mM) and iodoacetamide treatment
experiment.measurement: gel filtration analysis of complex integrity, [3H]-DHA binding, crystal growth

numbers.quantity: TCEP tolerated by complex in MNG-3

text: Single particle EM of the purified complex confirmed it was monodisperse but revealed a large detergent micelle leaving little polar extracellular surface for lattice contacts, and increased variability in the position of GαsAH relative to the T4L-β2AR-GαsRAS-Gβγ complex in the absence of guanine nucleotide.

quotes.quote:
The results, which are described in detail in a companion 
manuscript (Westfield et al.), confirmed that the complex was monodisperse, but revealed 
two potential problems for obtaining diffraction of quality crystals. First, the detergent used 
to stabilize the complex formed a large micelle, leaving little polar surface on the 
extracellular side of the β2AR-Gs complex for the formation of crystal lattice contacts.

EM 2D averages and 3D reconstructions show 
that in the absence of guanine nucleotide, GαsAH has a variable position relative to the 
complex of T4L-β2AR-GαsRAS-Gβγ (Fig. 1b)

experiment.system: purified detergent-solubilized β2AR-Gs complex
experiment.perturbation: nucleotide-free condition (guanine nucleotide absent)
experiment.measurement: single particle negative stain electron microscopy, 2D class averages and 3D reconstructions

text: A minimal 55-amino-acid c-Jun peptide (Jun(29-84)) containing the JNK docking site, phosphorylation sites S63 and S73, and an NES was sufficient to change fluorescent protein localization upon anisomycin stimulation; translocation was blocked by a JNK inhibitor and by the non-phosphorylatable S73A mutant.

quotes.quote:
Further fragment analysis revealed that a minimal 
peptide of 55 amino acids (Jun(29-84)), containing the JNK docking site, two phosphorylation 
sites (S63 and S73) and the identified NES, is sufficient to alter the localization of the 
fluorescent protein in the presence of anisomycin

This 
translocation can be blocked with both a specific JNK inhibitor as well as a non-
phosphorylatable mutant construct (S73A).

experiment.system: 3T3 cells expressing c-Jun fragments fused to Clover
experiment.perturbation: anisomycin (50 ng/ml) stimulation, JNK inhibitor VIII pretreatment, S73A mutation
experiment.measurement: epifluorescence imaging of nucleocytoplasmic localization

text: Expression of Jun(29-84)-Clover did not alter endogenous c-Jun phosphorylation by JNK, both were phosphorylated and dephosphorylated with similar dynamics, and c-Jun dependent gene expression was unchanged.

quotes.quote:
Quantitative Western blot 
analysis revealed that expressing Jun(29-84)-Clover does not alter endogenous c-Jun 
phosphorylation by JNK and that both are phosphorylated and dephosphorylated with 
similar dynamics (Figures S2A and S2B). Moreover, c-Jun dependent gene expression 
remained unaltered in Jun(29-84)-Clover expressing cells

experiment.system: 3T3 cells expressing Jun(29-84)-Clover
experiment.perturbation: reporter expression vs control; stimulation time course
experiment.measurement: quantitative Western blot of phospho-c-Jun and qPCR gene expression

text: Combining a negatively phospho-regulated bipartite NLS with a positively phospho-regulated NES in one construct increased the dynamic range of nucleocytoplasmic transport by threefold, yielding the JNK KTR.

quotes.quote:
By combining a negatively phospho-regulated NLS with a positively phospho-regulated 
NES into a single construct, we were able to increase the dynamic range of 
nucleocytoplasmic transport by threefold

experiment.system: 3T3 cells expressing Jun(29-84)-Clover sequence variants
experiment.perturbation: rational NLS/NES mutagenesis; anisomycin (50 ng/ml)
experiment.measurement: per-cell dynamic range of cytoplasmic/nuclear ratio, (anisomycin-basal)/basal normalized to wild type

text: JNK KTR translocation was specifically inhibited by targeting JNK but not p38, and a p38 inhibitor caused hyper-activation of JNK KTR; the non-phosphorylatable JNK KTRAA localized to the nucleus while the phosphomimetic JNK KTREE was restricted to the cytoplasm.

quotes.quote:
This localization change could be specifically inhibited by 
targeting JNK, but not p38 (Figures 1E, 1G, S3A and S3B). We also observed that a p38 
inhibitor caused hyper-activation of JNK KTR

a non-phosphorylatable mutant (JNK KTRAA) localized strictly to the nucleus, whereas a 
phosphomimetic mutant (JNK KTREE) was restricted to the cytoplasm

experiment.system: 3T3 cells expressing JNK KTR (WT, AA, EE)
experiment.perturbation: anisomycin (50 ng/ml) with 10μM JNK inhibitor VIII or 10μM SB203580 pretreatment
experiment.measurement: imaging and quantification of cytoplasmic/nuclear intensity ratio

text: In response to IL-1β, JNK and c-Jun phosphorylation measured by Western blot or immunofluorescence strongly correlated with JNK KTR data at population and single-cell levels, and JNK KTR expression level did not impact measured C/N ratios.

quotes.quote:
Results showed that JNK and c-Jun phosphorylation measured by WB or 
IF strongly correlates with JNK KTR data at both population and single-cell levels

the level of JNK KTR expression did not impact the 
measured cytoplasmic:nuclear (C/N) ratios of the JNK KTR

of raptor

was sufficient to render the mTORC1 pathway, as judged by the phosphorylation of S6K1,
resistant to amino acid starvation (Figure 6A). In contrast, the expression of wild-type raptor
or raptor-Rheb15ΔCAAX did not affect the amino acid sensitivity of the pathway

In HEK-293E cells, the expression of raptor-Rheb15 made S6K1 phosphorylation
insensitive to amino acid starvation, but did not affect its regulation by insulin (Figure 6B).

lysosomally-targeted but not wild-type raptor, mTOR was always associated with
lysosomes, irrespective of amino acids (Figure 6C). As with the transient expression of
raptor-Rheb15, its stable expression rendered the mTORC1 pathway fully resistant to amino
acid starvation (Figure 6D). Furthermore, under normal growth conditions these cells had an

although the stable expression of a raptor variant consisting of
raptor fused to the last 25 amino acids of H-Ras (raptor-HRas25) (Figures 5A and S5B) was

while in control cells the
RNAi-mediated knockdown of both RagA and RagB strongly blunted the activation of
mTORC1 by amino acids, it did not reduce the amino acid-insensitive mTORC1 activity
observed in raptor-Rheb15 expressing cells (Figure 7A).

Expression of RagBGDP-

no effect on the amino acid-insensitive mTORC1 activity of cells expressing raptor-Rheb15
(Figure 7B).

the stable expression of raptor-Rheb15,

When Rheb1-HRas25 was stably co-expressed with
raptor-HRas25, but not wild-type raptor, the mTORC1 pathway became insensitive to amino
acid starvation (Figure 7G). Importantly, mTORC1 signaling remained amino acid-sensitive
in cells in which either Rheb or mTORC1, but not both, was targeted to the plasma

text: In vitro, rapamycin-induced recruitment of MAPK3 and ELK1 into SUMO10/SIM6 condensates increased ELK1WT phosphorylation by 22% and ELK1DM (docking-motif mutant) by 91%, with the condensate phase constituting less than 3% of total reaction volume.

quotes.quote:
Upon ELK1 and MAPK3 recruitment into condensates, phosphorylation of ELK1WT 
increased by 22% compared with control (Figure 1E).

The reaction acceleration 
in this experiment appears relatively small (22% for ELK1WT, 91% for ELK1DM); however, 
the condensate phase only constituted a tiny fraction of the total reaction volume (less than 
3%).

experiment.system: in vitro reconstituted SUMO10 + FKBP12-SIM6 condensates with FRB-mCherry-MAPK3(R84S) and FRB-GFP-ELK1 C terminus (WT or docking-motif mutant)
experiment.perturbation: rapamycin-induced recruitment of kinase and substrate into condensates versus DMSO control
experiment.measurement: [γ-32P]ATP radiolabeled kinase assay quantified from phosphor screen

text: In S. cerevisiae, co-recruitment of MAPK3-SIM and ELK1-SIM into SUMO10-SIM6 condensates increased ELK1 S383 phosphorylation 3.8-fold (ELK1WT-SIM) and 4.9-fold (ELK1DM-SIM), whereas a non-condensing SUMO dimer scaffold did not significantly increase phosphorylation.

quotes.quote:
However, ELK1WT-SIM and ELK1DM-SIM phosphorylation 
at S383 was substantially increased when co-recruited with MAPK3-SIM into condensates 
(3.8-fold and 4.9-fold, respectively, p < 0.001; Figure 1G, top graph, Figure S1D).

SUMO2 expression did not significantly increase ELK1WT-SIM or ELK1DM-
SIM phosphorylation, indicating that recruitment to a condensed phase was required for 
increased phosphorylation.

experiment.system: budding yeast W303 expressing SUMO10-SIM6 condensates with SIM-tagged MAPK3(R84S) and ELK1 (WT or docking mutant)
experiment.perturbation: co-expression with condensate-forming SUMO10-SIM6 versus non-condensing SUMO2 dimer scaffold
experiment.measurement: western blot with ELK1 S383 phospho-specific antibody, normalized to total ELK1

text: Endogenous yeast kinases contribute to condensate-driven ELK1-SIM phosphorylation: deletion of FUS3, KSS1 or PHO85 partly reduced phosphorylation, and a fus3Δ kss1Δ pho85Δ triple mutant completely lost the SUMO10-SIM6-dependent increase.

quotes.quote:
We found that deletion of the MAP kinases FUS3 or KSS1, 
and the CDK PHO85 partly reduced phosphorylation. A fus3Δ, kss1 Δ, and pho85Δ triple 
knockout mutant completely lost the increase in ELK1-SIM phosphorylation in the presence 
of SUMO10-SIM6 condensates (Figure S1E).

experiment.system: yeast expressing ELK1-SIM with SUMO10-SIM6 condensates, without MAPK3-SIM
experiment.perturbation: single and triple gene deletions of FUS3, KSS1, PHO85
experiment.measurement: western blot of ELK1-SIM phosphorylation

text: Recruitment to condensates produced multisite hyperphosphorylation of ELK1: slow-migrating bands increased 220-fold for ELK1DM-SIM and 380-fold for ELK1WT-SIM, and were lost upon lambda phosphatase treatment or mutation of eleven S/T-P consensus sites to alanine.

quotes.quote:
Quantification of slow-migrating bands indicated a 220-fold increase 
in hyperphosphorylation when ELK1DM-SIM was recruited to condensates (Figure 1G, 
bottom graph, p < 0.001) and a 380-fold increase in the hypershifted band for ELK1WT-SIM 
(Figure S1D, bottom graph, p < 0.001).

ELK1 contains eleven 
serines or threonines immediately followed by proline, corresponding to consensus MAPK3 
phosphorylation sites (Cruzalegui et al., 1999). Substitution all of these serines/threonines 
(Figure S1G) with alanine (ELK1–11A mutant) led to the loss of almost all hypershifted 
bands (Figure S1H).

experiment.system: yeast expressing SIM-tagged ELK1 and MAPK3 with SUMO10-SIM6 condensates
experiment.perturbation: condensate recruitment; lambda phosphatase treatment; alanine substitution of consensus sites
experiment.measurement: western blot quantification of hypershifted band intensity

text: The yeast MAP kinase Fus3, tagged with a double SIM, phosphorylated the non-native substrate ELK1-SIM when recruited to SUMO10-SIM6 condensates: S383 phosphorylation rose ~7-fold before α-factor and ~15-fold after 5 min α-factor, with hypershifted bands induced ~600-fold; SUMO2 scaffold gave no significant increase.

quotes.quote:
Western 
blot results showed that ELK1-SIM phosphorylation on S383 increased ~7-fold when Fus3–
2xSIM was colocalized in SUMO10-SIM6 condensates even prior to addition of α-factor 
(Figure 2B, top graph, third lane, p < 0.01).

However, the level of ELK1-SIM S383 phosphorylation was further increased to ~15-fold 
above background upon activation of Fus3 by addition of α-factor for 5 min (Figure 2B, 
top graph, p < 0.001). Furthermore, the hypershifted bands were even more strongly induced 
by α-factor (~600-fold, p < 0.001, Figure 2B, bottom graph).

experiment.system: yeast with endogenous FUS3 tagged with 2xSIM, ELK1-SIM, and SUMO10-SIM6 or SUMO2 scaffold
experiment.perturbation: condensate recruitment ± 2 μM α-factor pathway activation
experiment.measurement: western blot of ELK1 pS383 and hypershifted bands

text: Cdk1-SIM recruited into SUMO10-SIM6 condensates phosphorylated ELK1-SIM, increasing S383 phosphorylation ~10-fold and hypershifted bands ~300-fold, while a SUMO2 scaffold gave no increase over background.

quotes.quote:
Co-
recruitment of ELK1-SIM and Cdk1-SIM led to high levels of phosphorylation of ELK1-
SIM, both in terms of S383 phosphorylation (~10-fold increase, p < 0.001; Figure 2C, top 
graph) and levels of hypershifted bands (~300-fold increase, p < 0.01; Figure 2C, bottom 
graph).

experiment.system: yeast with endogenous Cdk1 tagged with a single SIM, ELK1-SIM, SUMO10-SIM6 or SUMO2 scaffold
experiment.perturbation: recruitment of Cdk1-SIM and ELK1-SIM into condensates versus non-condensing scaffold
experiment.measurement: western blot of pS383 and hypershifted bands

text: A live-cell NLS-GFP-2xWW phospho-reporter showed cell-cycle-dependent localization: reporter intensity in condensates was highest immediately before anaphase, dropped and relocalized to the nucleus approximately 20–30 min after anaphase, and began rising again after 10–20 min.

quotes.quote:
Reporter intensity within condensates 
was highest immediately prior to anaphase, the point at which Cdk1 activity is highest 
(Enserink and Kolodner, 2010). Approximately 20–30 min after anaphase, reporter signal 
was reduced within condensates and relocalized to the nucleus (Figure 2D; Video S1).

Subsequently, after 10–20 
min, a time when Cdk1 activity is rising, the reporter intensity in condensates also started 
to increase (Figures 2D and S3F).

text: A minimal ELK1 peptide (min383, residues 370–394) lacking both docking sites was strongly phosphorylated by MAPK3 within condensates, with hypershifted bands accounting for almost 50% of total min383; deletion of four consecutive N-terminal non-consensus serines abolished the slow-migrating bands.

First, we used a short 
peptide flanking serine383 in ELK1 as a substrate (residues 370–394, referred to as min383 
hereafter) to completely remove the D box and F box docking sites.

We noticed that there were multiple hypershifted bands, accounting for almost 50% of total 
min383 (Figure S4D) within SUMO10-SIM6 condensates.

Deletion of four consecutive serines at the N terminus almost completely abolished 
slowly migrating bands (Figure S4H), suggesting that these four non-consensus serines were 
phosphorylated by MAPK3.

text: Cdk1 phosphorylated peptides lacking its primary specificity determinants when recruited to condensates: P53 serine9 and serine37 peptides were more highly phosphorylated, and RPS6 serine235/236 was also phosphorylated in condensates.

Western blot results showed that peptides from 
serine9 and serine37 in P53 were more highly phosphorylated by Cdk1 when recruited to

in condensates.

Western blotting showed that hyperphosphorylation of

present at equivalent concentration to ELK1-SIMWT, there was still a 2-fold decrease

However, ELK1-SIM hyperphosphorylation within SUMO7-SIM6

text: In a rigid engineered two-component condensate (hexamer-E9 plus SUMO-Im2 dimer with an 18 nm coiled coil), recruitment of ELK1-SIM and MAPK3-SIM gave only ~50% increase in S383 phosphorylation and ~35-fold hyperphosphorylation, ~10-fold less than in SUMO10-SIM6 condensates.

We found that recruitment of ELK1-SIM and 
MAPK3-SIM to SUMO domains within this ordered condensate led to a slight increase in

Again, each 2xSUMO or 
3xSUMO is held 18 nm distant from its partner by the rigid antiparallel coiled-coil of the

We engineered two 
Sang et al.

interaction strengths between the two scaffold components, either in the micromolar (Kd ~

a slight increase (~2-fold) in hyperphosphorylation in the strain expressing the high-affinity

text: Osmotic compression (1 M sorbitol, 1 h) of hog1Δ cells decreased average condensate area ~35% and increased GFP-MAPK3-SIM recruitment ~70% in both SUMO10-SIM6 and SUMO7-SIM6 condensates, but hyperphosphorylation rose only about 10% in SUMO10-SIM6 versus ~2-fold in SUMO7-SIM6.

decreased by around 35%, likely due to oncotic compression, and recruitment of GFP-
MAPK3-SIM increased 70% (Figures S6A and S6B), but ELK1-SIM hyperphosphorylation 
was only increased about 10% (Figure S6C, lanes 3 and 4).

However, the degree of ELK1-SIM hyperphosphorylation 
in SUMO7-SIM6 condensates was increased ~2-fold (Figure S6C, lanes 1 and 2).

However, ELK1-SIM hyperphosphorylation increased similarly 
upon osmotic shock in hog1Δ; fus3Δ double-mutant strains and hog1Δ strains (Figure S6D).

Consistent with the hypothesis, there was 
no significant change in ELK1-SIM hyperphosphorylation upon osmotic compression in

Upon osmotic compression, condensate area was only slightly 
decreased (~10%; Figure 4C), but the concentration of GFP-MAPK3-SIM clients increased 
in the condensates to a similar degree as in SUMO7-SIM6 condensates, by ~60% (Figure 
4B).
decreased by ~50% upon osmotic compression (p < 0.05; Figures 4D and 4E).

text: 40nm-GEM tracking gave a baseline Deff of 0.157 μm2 s−1 in W303 hog1Δ (predicting 23 μM ribosomes), rising to ~0.462 mm2 s−1 after 2 h of 1 mM rapamycin (15.5 μM ribosomes); sfp1Δ gave 16.4 μM, and 1 M sorbitol for 1 h decreased Deff more than 10-fold in all conditions, consistent with ~32 μM ribosome concentration.

quotes.quote:
Using the same method (Figure S8A), we found that the baseline Deff for W303 hog1Δ 
was 0.157 μm2 s−1 (predicting 23 μM ribosomes) and that this value increased to ~0.462 
mm2 s−1 upon 2 h treatment with 1 mM rapamycin (Figure 5C), consistent with an almost 
one third reduction of ribosome concentration to 15.5 μM (Figure 5C). Deletion of SFP1 
(sfp1Δ mutant) gave a similar decrease in ribosome concentration, to 16.4 μM, but in this 
case, without perturbation to mTORC1 kinase activity (Figure 5C). Osmotic compression of 
cells with 1M sorbitol for 1 h led to more than 10-fold decrease in 40nm-GEM Deff in all 
conditions (Figures 5B and 5C), consistent with increased macromolecular crowding to ~32 
μM ribosome concentration.

experiment.measurement: single-particle tracking at 100 Hz, MSD-derived effective diffusion coefficient, ribosome concentration inferred via Doolittle equation

text: ELK1-SIM hyperphosphorylation in SUMO7-SIM6 condensates tracked macromolecular crowding: it fell ~5-fold after rapamycin and rose >4-fold after osmotic compression, correlating positively with ribosome concentration (Spearman ρ = 0:826; p = 0:008).

Hyperphosphorylation was reduced in conditions with decreased macromolecular 
crowding (e.g., 5-fold decease after rapamycin treatment) and increased in conditions with 
increased macromolecular crowding (e.g., >4-fold increase after osmotic compression). 
Plotting hyperphosphorylation as a function of ribosome concentration showed a significant 
positive correlation (Figure 5E; Spearman’s rank ρ = 0:826; p = 0:008 < 0:01).

there was a significant positive monotonic correlation between GFP-MAPK3-

or hyperphosphorylation (ρmCherry - ELK1 = 0:615; pCherry - ELK1 = 0:056 > 0:05;

text: Low-dose (10 mg/kg) axitinib lowered total tumor and T cell hypoxia in B16-bearing mice, made intratumoral T cells phenotypically less exhausted and more polyfunctional, and sensitized mice to CTLA-4 and PD-1 blockade, decreasing tumor burden and improving survival.

treating B16-bearing mice with low-dose (10 mg/kg) 
axitinib lowered total tumor and T cell hypoxia as measured by pimonidazole (Fig. 7g,h). 
Intratumoral T cells were phenotypically less exhausted (Fig. 7i) and more polyfunctional 
(Fig. 7j)
