text: Genome-wide CRISPRa screens targeting >18,800 protein-coding genes with >112,000 sgRNAs, sorting IL-2-producing CD4+ and IFN-γ-producing CD8+ T cells into high and low bins, showed sgRNAs targeting IL2 and IFNG enriched in the respective cytokine-high populations while nontargeting controls were not enriched, and were reproducible across two donors.

quotes.quote:
we scaled up our platform to perform pooled 
genome-wide CRISPRa screens targeting >18,800 protein-coding genes with >112,000 
single-guide RNAs (sgRNAs) (22)

Subsequent sgRNA quantification confirmed that 
sgRNAs targeting IL-2 (IL2) and IFN-γ (IFNG) were strongly enriched in the respective 
cytokine high populations, and nontargeting control sgRNAs were not enriched in either bin 
(Fig. 1B). Both CRISPRa screens were highly reproducible in two different human blood 
donors

experiment.system: primary human CD4+ and CD8+ T cells from two blood donors
experiment.perturbation: genome-wide pooled CRISPRa (Calabrese libraries)
experiment.measurement: sgRNA enrichment by sequencing after FACS into cytokine high/low bins

text: Gene-level analysis of the CRISPRa screens revealed 444 hits for IL-2 and 471 for IFN-γ, including 171 shared hits.

quotes.quote:
Gene-level statistical analysis of the IL-2 
and IFN-γ CRISPRa screens revealed 444 and 471 hits, respectively, including 171 shared 
hits (Fig. 1E; fig. S3, G and H; and tables S1 and S2).

experiment.system: primary human T cells from two donors
experiment.perturbation: genome-wide CRISPRa
experiment.measurement: MAGeCK gene-level hit calling (median |log2FC|>0.5, FDR<0.05)

text: CRISPRa of TBX21 selectively enhanced IFN-γ while GATA3 activation had the opposite effects; activation of proximal TCR signaling components (VAV1, CD28, LCP2, LAT) enriched sgRNAs in both cytokine-high bins, whereas negative regulators MAP4K1 and SLA2 were depleted.

quotes.quote:
Activation of TBX21 (encoding T-bet), which promotes both 
memory CD8+ T cell and CD4+ T helper cell 1 (TH1) differentiation (24–26), selectively 
enhanced the signature type I cytokine IFN-γ (Fig. 1E). By contrast, sgRNAs activating 
GATA3, which promotes type II differentiation by antagonizing T-bet (25, 27), had the 
opposite effects

Overexpression of members of the proximal TCR signaling 
complex, such as VAV1, CD28, LCP2 (encoding SLP-76), and LAT (28, 29) reinforced 
T cell activation and were enriched in both cytokine-high bins. Conversely, the negative 
TCR signaling regulators MAP4K1 and SLA2 were depleted in these bins

experiment.system: primary human CD4+ and CD8+ T cells
experiment.perturbation: genome-wide CRISPRa targeting individual genes
experiment.measurement: sgRNA log2-fold change between cytokine high and low sorted bins

text: Reciprocal genome-wide CRISPRi screens identified 226 IL-2 and 203 IFN-γ gene hits, including 92 shared hits, with CRISPRi hits biased toward highly expressed genes while CRISPRa additionally identified genes expressed at low or undetectable levels (e.g., PIK3AP1 and IL1R1, hits by CRISPRa but not CRISPRi).

quotes.quote:
The CRISPRi IL-2 and IFN-γ screens identified 226 
and 203 gene hits, respectively, including 92 shared hits (Fig. 2, A and B). As expected, the 
CRISPRi hits were biased toward genes with high mRNA expression, including members of 
the CD3 complex, whereas CRISPRa additionally identified regulators that were expressed 
either at low levels or not at all in T cells under the screened conditions

For example, PIK3AP1 and IL1R1 were expressed at low levels under the screened 
conditions (fig. S7A). They are potentially inducible in some T cell contexts (fig. S7, B to 
D); however, they were detected as hits by CRISPRa but not CRISPRi.

experiment.system: primary human T cells from two donors
experiment.perturbation: genome-wide CRISPRi (Dolcetto libraries) compared with CRISPRa
experiment.measurement: sgRNA enrichment/gene-level hit calling after cytokine FACS; mRNA expression of hits

text: CRISPRi detected a required TCR–NF-κB circuit for IFN-γ production (MALT1, BCL10, TRAF6, TAK1/MAP3K7, and the IκB complex genes CHUK, IKBKB, IKBKG), whereas CRISPRa instead revealed TNFRSF members and IL1R1 as positive IFN-γ regulators that also signal through NF-κB but were not individually required.

quotes.quote:
CRISPRi detected a circuit of T cell stimulation signaling 
through MALT1, BCL10, TRAF6, and TAK1 (encoded by MAP3K7) to the inhibitor of the 
NF-κB complex (IκB complex, encoded by CHUK, IKBKB, and IKBKG) that promotes 
IFN-γ production (Fig. 2, E and F, and fig. S8A). By contrast, CRISPRa revealed a set 
of positive IFN-γ regulators that included members of the tumor necrosis factor receptor 
superfamily (TNFRSF) and IL1R1. These regulators also signal through NF-κB even though 
they are not individually required and therefore not detected by CRISPRi

experiment.system: primary human CD8+ (CD4−) T cells

experiment.measurement: sgRNA log2-fold change for IFN-γ high vs low sorted bins

We found that a few genes were identified across all screens (e.g., 
ZAP70 as a positive regulator and CBLB as a negative regulator), representing core 
regulators of stimulation-responsive cytokine production in T cells. Most hits, however, were

either cytokine-specific (IL-2 in CD4+ T cells or IFN-γ in CD8+ T cells) or perturbation-
specific (activation or interference) (fig. S8D). For a few target genes, including PTPRC 
(CD45), CRISRPa and CRISPRi both influenced cytokine production in the same direction

quotes.quote:
led us to perform additional genome-wide CRISPRa screens for IL-2, IFN-γ, and 
TNF-α in CD4+ T cells, allowing for direct comparisons of type 1 cytokine regulators in 
CD4+ T cells (fig. S9). Many of the strongest positive (e.g., VAV1, CD28, and LCP2) and

or decrease individual cytokines selectively.

This included calcium pathway signaling genes (e.g., PLCG1, PLCG2, PRKCB, 
PRKD2, and NFATC2), and cytokine signaling genes (e.g., STAT3, JAK1, JAK3, and 
SOCS3), the latter suggesting feedback circuits among cytokine signals. In particular, 
CRISPRa identified regulators absent from previous literature (e.g., APOBEC3A/D/C, 
FOXQ1, and EMP1) (Fig. 2H)

text: CRISPRa Perturb-seq was performed in ~56,000 primary human T cells targeting 70 hits and controls; sgRNAs led to significant increases in target gene expression, and UMAP showed discrete separation of resting and restimulated cells with even distribution of cells from two donors.

We performed CRISPRa Perturb-seq characterization of regulators of stimulation responses 
in ~56,000 primary human T cells, targeting 70 hits and controls from our genome-wide 
CRISPRa cytokine screens (Fig. 4, A and B, and fig. S17, A to C). First, we confirmed that

uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) dimensionality reduction revealed 
discrete separation of the resting and restimulated cells (fig. S17E) and showed relatively 
even distribution of cells from two donors

mouse IL-33 are 55% identical at the amino acid level.
The IL-1 family member most closely related to IL-33 is
IL-18

pressed as a prodomain containing polypeptide. Incu-
bation of in vitro translated IL-33 with caspase-1 led to

noprecipitated in the presence of IL-33 (Figure 3A, lane

fected only with the GFP-reporter gene construct, ex-

experiment.perturbation: incubation with anti-ST2 antibody with/without competing hIL-33, or with biotinylated hIL-33
experiment.measurement: FACS staining (anti-rat IgG-PE or streptavidin-PE)

text: IL-33 stimulation of WTMC mast cells induced NF-kB phosphorylation peaking at 15 min and decreasing at 30 min, plus activation of Erk1/2, p38 and JNK; NF-kB and kinase phosphorylation were blocked by preincubation with a neutralizing anti-ST2 antibody but not by control antibody, and anti-ST2 alone did not activate NF-kB.

quotes.quote: Phosphorylation of NF-kB was

observed in the total cell lysate after IL-33 stimulation
with a peak of phosphorylation occurring at 15 min
and decreased levels at 30 min. NF-kB phosphorylation
could be signiﬁcantly blocked by preincubation of the
cells with a neutralizing anti-ST2 antibody prior to stim-
ulation with IL-33 (Figure 4B). A control antibody was not

capable of reducing phosphorylation (Figure 4B), and
neither was the anti-ST2 antibody on its own able to in-
duce activation of NF-kB. In addition to NF-kB, IL-33
also induced activation of Erk1/2 and p38 (Figure 4C).
Phosphorylation of these kinases could also be inhibited
by anti-ST2 antibody. Activation of JNK kinases was
also observed (data not shown).

experiment.system: WTMC mouse mast cell line
experiment.perturbation: stimulation with 1.5 ng/ml IL-33 for various times, with or without preincubation with anti-mST2 mAb or isotype control (1 mg/ml)
experiment.measurement: phospho-specific Western blots for p65 NF-kB, IkB-a, Erk1/2, p38

numbers.quantity: IL-33 concentration used on mast cells

text: In vitro polarized TH2 cells, but not TH1 cells, responded to IL-33 upon anti-CD3/CD28 restimulation with increased IL-5 and IL-13 production; IL-4 was already high and not further increased, and IFNg from TH1 cells was reduced with IL-33.

quotes.quote:
After three rounds of polarization,
cells were restimulated with anti-CD3 and anti-CD28
with or without IL-33 (20 ng/ml), and supernatants were
tested for the expression of IFNg, IL-4, IL-5, and IL-13.
TH2 cells but not TH1 cells responded to IL-33 stimulation
with increased production of IL-5 and IL-13 (Figure 4D).
The production of IL-4 was already high and not further
increased with the addition of IL-33. As expected, TH1
cells produced high levels of IFNg. Interestingly, this
level was reduced when the cells were incubated with
IL-33.

experiment.system: naive CD4+CD62L+ T cells from C57BL/6 spleens polarized to TH1 (IL-12) or TH2 (IL-4)
experiment.perturbation: restimulation with plate-bound anti-CD3 and anti-CD28 with or without IL-33 (20 ng/ml) for 48 hr
experiment.measurement: supernatant IFNg, IL-4, IL-5, IL-13 by Beadlyte/luminex

text: Mice treated i.p. daily with 0.4 or 4 mg IL-33 for 7 days developed splenomegaly with significantly higher numbers of splenic eosinophils, mononuclear cells and plasma cells but not neutrophils, increased blood eosinophils and lymphocytes with no significant change in blood neutrophils or monocytes, and significantly higher serum IgE and IgA.

quotes.quote:
Mice treated daily with 0.4 or 4 mg of IL-33
for 7 days developed splenomegaly with signiﬁcantly
higher numbers of eosinophils, mononuclear cells, and
plasma cells, but not neutrophils (Figures 5A and 5B).
The increased number of splenic eosinophils and mono-
nuclear cells correlated with an increase in blood

eosinophils and lymphocytes (Figure 5C). No signiﬁcant
changes were observed in the numbers of blood neutro-
phils and monocytes. Evaluation of circulating Ig levels
showed that IL-33-treated mice had signiﬁcantly higher
serum levels of IgE and IgA (Figure 5D).

experiment.system: C57BL/6 mice (n = 4–5)
experiment.perturbation: daily i.p. injection of 0.4 mg or 4 mg IL-33 protein or PBS for 7 days
experiment.measurement: spleen weight and cellularity, Haema3-stained cytospin differentials, blood cell counts (Advia 120), serum Ig isotypes by sandwich ELISA

text: IL-33 treatment of mice strongly induced IL-13 mRNA in all tissues tested (thymus, spleen, liver, small intestine, lung) and higher IL-4 and IL-5 mRNA in thymus, spleen, liver and lung, with no change in IL-1a, IL-2, TNFa, IL-10, IL-12 or IFNg; serum IL-5 and IL-13 were highly increased while other serum cytokines were undetectable or unchanged.

quotes.quote:
IL-33 treat-
ment strongly induced gene expression of IL-13 in all tis-
sues tested, including thymus, spleen, liver, small intes-
tine, and lung (Figure 6A and data not shown). mRNA
expression of both IL-4 and IL-5 was higher in thymus,
spleen, liver, and lung of IL-33-treated mice. There was
no change in the gene expression of IL-1a, IL-2, TNFa,
IL-10, IL-12, or IFNg (data not shown). The serum of
IL-33-treated mice showed highly increased levels of
IL-5 and IL-13 (Figure 6B). Serum levels of IL-2, IL-4,
IL-6, IL-10, IL-12, TNFa, IFNg, or MCP-1 were either
not detectable or did not change in comparison to
PBS-treated animals

experiment.system: C57BL/6 mice (tissue mRNA pool of 3 mice; serum n = 3–5 per group)
experiment.perturbation: daily treatment with 0.4 or 4 mg IL-33 protein or PBS for 7 days
experiment.measurement: real-time quantitative PCR of tissue IL-4/IL-5/IL-13 mRNA; serum IL-5 by cytometric bead array and IL-13 by sandwich ELISA

text: IL-5 and IL-13 were detectable in the serum of mice as early as 3 days after IL-33 administration.

quotes.quote:
we can detect IL-5 and IL-13 in the serum of mice as
early as 3 days after administration of IL-33.

experiment.system: C57BL/6 mice
experiment.perturbation: daily i.p. IL-33 protein administration
experiment.measurement: serum IL-5 (cytometric bead array) and IL-13 (ELISA) over time

text: IL-33-treated mice showed gross and histological pathology in mucosal organs: enlarged spleen and stomach, mucus- and bile-filled duodenum, pulmonary vascular medial hypertrophy with eosinophil/mononuclear infiltrates, hypertrophied mucus-laden bronchial epithelium (PAS/alcian blue positive), esophageal epithelial hyperplasia with inflammatory infiltrates, hypertrophied and hyperplastic intestinal goblet cells, and splenic extramedullary hematopoiesis with distorted red and white pulp.

quotes.quote:
We also observed gross anatomical changes in IL-33-
treated mice, including enlargement of spleen and stom-
ach and mucus- and bile-ﬁlled duodenum. Microscopic
examination showed striking histological changes in
mucosal tissues, including the lung, esophagus, and
small intestine.

Changes in-
cluded minimal to moderate medial hypertrophy and
the presence of myeloid cells within the vascular lumen
and inﬁltrates of eosinophils and/or mononuclear cells
beneath the endothelium, within the vessel wall, and ad-
jacent to the vessels.

The epithelial lining of the airways
was hypertrophied and appeared to contain large
amounts of mucus. Periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) and alcian
blue staining highlighted the presence of mucus within
the epithelial lining.

In the small and large intestines, the
goblet cells were hypertrophied and hyperplastic (Fig-
ures 7G and 7H)

The micro-
scopic investigation of the enlarged spleen showed ex-
tramedullary hematopoesis attended by the distortion of
red and white pulp

experiment.system: C57BL/6 mice receiving IL-33 protein (0.4 mg for 7 days) vs PBS
experiment.perturbation: daily i.p. IL-33 protein administration for 7 days
experiment.measurement: gross anatomy and histology of formalin-fixed sections stained with H&E or PAS/alcian blue

text: IL-13 knockout mice treated with IL-33 for 7 days showed no epithelial changes in the lungs.

quotes.quote:
We conﬁrmed this by treating IL-13 KO
mice with IL-33 for 7 days. No epithelial changes were
observed in the lungs of these IL-33-treated IL-13 KO
mice (see Figure S1

experiment.system: IL-13 knockout mice
experiment.perturbation: treatment with IL-33 for 7 days
experiment.measurement: lung histology for epithelial changes

text: In initial in vitro culture experiments the authors did not observe a role for IL-33 in driving TH2 cell development, in contrast to its TH2 effector activity.

quotes.quote:
In initial experiments
to address this issue, we do not see, at least under
in vitro culture conditions, a role for IL-33 in driving
TH2 cell development (J.S., unpublished results).

experiment.system: in vitro cultured naive mouse T cells
experiment.perturbation: addition of IL-33 during in vitro polarization culture
experiment.measurement: TH2 cell development (unpublished observations)

text: Inhibition of protein translation with cycloheximide extends the duration of ISG transcription after IFN treatment and shortens the interval needed for reactivation, indicating new protein synthesis is required to establish and maintain the IFN-desensitized state.

quotes.quote:
Inhibition of protein translation with cycloheximide 
extends the length of time that ISGs are transcribed following IFN treatment and decreases 
the interval of time necessary for reactivation, thereby demonstrating that new protein 
synthesis is required to establish and maintain an IFN-desensitized state (41).

experiment.system: cultured cells treated with IFN
experiment.perturbation: cycloheximide inhibition of protein translation
experiment.measurement: duration of ISG transcription and interval to reactivation

text: Usp18-/- mice show a dramatic increase in ISGylation, are hypersensitive to type I IFN and more resistant to virus infection, and Usp18-/- cells in culture show prolonged JAK-STAT signaling and increased apoptosis upon IFN-β treatment.

quotes.quote:
Accordingly, Usp18−/− mice display a dramatic increase in 
the level of ISGylation (104, 105).

Usp18−/− mice are hypersensitive to type I IFN and more resistant to virus infection (106). 
In 2003, studies with Usp18−/− cells in culture revealed that JAK-STAT signaling is 
prolonged and that a dramatic increase in apoptosis occurs upon IFN-β treatment

experiment.system: Usp18-/- mice and cells
experiment.perturbation: Usp18 knockout; IFN-β treatment
experiment.measurement: ISGylation levels, IFN sensitivity, virus resistance, JAK-STAT signaling, apoptosis

text: A catalytically inactive USP18 confers the same level of IFN desensitization as wild-type, acting by binding the intracellular domain of IFNAR2 to prevent JAK1 binding; mutation of USP18 arginine residues disrupting IFNAR2 binding impairs inhibition of IFN signaling.

quotes.quote:
it was later 
demonstrated that a catalytically inactive form of USP18 confers the same level of IFN 
desensitization as the wild-type protein (107). This isopeptidase-independent activity is 
mediated by the binding of USP18 to the intracellular domain of IFNAR2, which prevents 
the binding of JAK1. Mutation of arginine residues in USP18 that disrupt binding to 
IFNAR2 impairs its ability to inhibit IFN signaling (107).

experiment.system: cells expressing USP18 variants
experiment.perturbation: catalytically inactive USP18; arginine mutations disrupting IFNAR2 binding
experiment.measurement: degree of IFN desensitization / inhibition of IFN signaling

text: Cells prestimulated with type I or III IFN are refractory to type I IFN signaling due to USP18 upregulation while type III IFN signaling remains intact, and the desensitization is differential: IFN-α signaling is blocked whereas IFN-β continues to activate JAK-STAT.

quotes.quote:
studies have shown that type III IFN signaling remains intact in the 
presence of USP18, but cells that are prestimulated with type I or III IFN are refractory to 
type I IFN signaling due to USP18 upregulation (111, 112). These studies have also found 
that USP18-mediated desensitization to type I IFN is differential—IFN-α signaling is 
blocked, whereas IFN-β continues to activate the JAK-STAT pathway (111, 112).

experiment.system: cultured cells
experiment.perturbation: prestimulation with type I or type III IFN, then restimulation with IFN-α or IFN-β
experiment.measurement: JAK-STAT pathway activation

text: Elevated USP18 mRNA levels predict a poor treatment response to IFN-α therapy for hepatitis C virus infection.

quotes.quote:
elevated levels of USP18 
mRNA predict a poor treatment response to IFN-α therapy for hepatitis C virus (HCV) 
infection (114, 115).

experiment.system: HCV patients on IFN-α therapy
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: USP18 mRNA levels vs treatment response

text: Mutations abolishing Mx1 self-oligomerization result in loss of antiviral activity against LaCrosse and influenza A viruses.

quotes.quote:
formation of these structures is important for its antiviral activity, as mutations that abolish 
self-oligomerization result in the loss of antiviral activity against LaCrosse and influenza A 
viruses (116).

experiment.system: cells expressing Mx1 variants
experiment.perturbation: mutations abolishing self-oligomerization
experiment.measurement: antiviral activity against LaCrosse and influenza A virus

text: Mx2 overexpression potently inhibits HIV-1 and HIV-2 but has less potent or no activity against other retroviruses or influenza A; Mx2 acts at nuclear entry, and HIV-1 capsid mutations render the virus resistant to Mx2.

quotes.quote:
Overexpression of Mx2 potently inhibits HIV-1 and HIV-2 (120–122) but has less potent or 
no antiviral activity against other retrovirus family members (120, 121) or the 
orthomyxovirus influenza A (122).

Mx2 acts at the level of nuclear entry 
and keeps the reverse-transcribed genome from reaching its nuclear destination

mutations in the HIV-1 capsid protein render the virus 
resistant to Mx2-mediated inhibition

experiment.system: cell culture infection assays
experiment.perturbation: Mx2 overexpression; HIV-1 capsid mutations
experiment.measurement: virus infection/nuclear entry and integration

text: Treating cells with 25HC or transferring supernatants from CH25H-expressing cells protects against a diverse set of enveloped viruses but has no impact on adenovirus, a nonenveloped virus; 25HC also inhibits replication of HCV subgenomic replicons.

quotes.quote:
Treating cells directly with 25HC 
or transferring supernatants from CH25H-expressing cells protects against infection by a 
diverse set of enveloped viruses yet has no impact on infection by adenovirus, a 
nonenveloped virus (126, 127).

25HC also inhibits the 
replication of HCV subgenomic viral RNA (virus replicon), thereby displaying antiviral 
activity even in the absence of membrane fusion (139–142).

experiment.system: cultured cells infected with enveloped viruses, adenovirus, or bearing HCV replicons
experiment.perturbation: 25HC treatment or CH25H-conditioned supernatant
experiment.measurement: infection/replication levels

text: Blanc et al. found 25HC inhibits MCMV at a postentry step at or prior to viral DNA replication, and higher concentrations of the enantiomer ent-25HC are required to achieve the same MCMV inhibition as 25HC, evidence that sterol biosynthesis negative feedback contributes.

quotes.quote:
Blanc et al. (127) also tested an additional herpesvirus—murine cytomegalovirus (MCMV)
—and found that inhibition occurs at a postentry step (and thus post-membrane fusion), at or 
prior to viral DNA replication. Using the enantiomer of 25HC (ent-25HC)

found that higher concentrations of ent-25HC are required to achieve the same level of 
MCMV inhibition seen with 25HC.

experiment.system: MCMV infection of cells
experiment.perturbation: 25HC vs ent-25HC treatment at varying concentrations
experiment.measurement: stage and extent of virus inhibition

text: IFITM family members display selectivity: IFITM1 inhibits SARS-CoV, Ebola and Marburg more efficiently than IFITM3, IFITM3 has higher potency against influenza A, HCV is inhibited by IFITM1 but not IFITM3, and for HIV-1 IFITM1 does not affect entry but inhibits virus production while IFITM2 and IFITM3 affect both.

quotes.quote:
IFITM1 
inhibits SARS-coronavirus (CoV) and the filoviruses, Ebola and Marburg, with greater 
efficiency than does IFITM3 (144). IFITM3, on the other hand, has higher potency against 
influenza A virus. In contrast, HCV infection is inhibited by IFITM1, but not by IFITM3 
(145).

IFITM1 has no effect on HIV-1 entry, but it effectively inhibits virus 
production (147). IFITM2 and IFITM3 also inhibit HIV-1 virus production, but they affect 
entry as well (147).

experiment.system: cells expressing individual IFITM family members
experiment.perturbation: IFITM1/2/3 expression
experiment.measurement: infection of SARS-CoV, filoviruses, influenza A, HCV, HIV-1 entry and production

text: Deletion of 21 amino acids from the IFITM3 N terminus causes loss of endosome association and peripheral localization, and a GWAS of patients hospitalized with severe influenza found statistically significant enrichment of an IFITM3 polymorphism generating an altered splice acceptor producing IFITM3 lacking those 21 amino acids.

quotes.quote:
When 
21 amino acids are deleted from the N terminus of IFITM3, its association with endosomes 
is lost and it localizes to the periphery of the cell (152).

This study uncovered a statistically significant enrichment for a polymorphism in 
the IFITM3 gene (153). Interestingly, this polymorphism generates an altered splice acceptor 
site resulting in an IFITM3 protein lacking 21 amino acids from the N terminus.

experiment.system: cells expressing truncated IFITM3; human GWAS cohort of severe influenza patients vs controls
experiment.perturbation: N-terminal 21-amino-acid deletion; observational genotyping
experiment.measurement: IFITM3 subcellular localization; polymorphism enrichment

text: IFITM3 restricts infection with reovirus, a nonenveloped virus.

quotes.quote:
IFITM3 has recently been 
shown to restrict infection with reovirus, a nonenveloped virus (146).

experiment.system: cells expressing IFITM3
experiment.perturbation: IFITM3 expression
experiment.measurement: reovirus infection

text: ISG15 was found to be preferentially conjugated cotranslationally to newly synthesized proteins, suggesting ISGylation may be a general, nonspecific mechanism of host defense.

quotes.quote:
ISG15 was found to be preferentially conjugated to newly synthesized proteins 
cotranslationally, which suggests that ISGylation may be a general, nonspecific mechanism

experiment.system: IFN-stimulated cells
experiment.perturbation: observational/biochemical analysis of ISG15 conjugation
experiment.measurement: ISGylation of newly synthesized vs preexisting proteins

text: In vivo ISG15 phenotypes differ by pathogen: wild-type and ISG15-/- mice are equally susceptible to VSV and LCMV, while ISG15-/- mice are more susceptible to influenza A and B, HSV-1 and Sindbis virus; ISG15 protects in vaccinia infection only when the virus lacks the E3 antagonist.

quotes.quote:
One study found that wild-type and ISG15−/− mice are 
equally susceptible to vesicular stomatitis virus and lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus 
(109); in contrast, ISG15−/− mice are more susceptible to infection with influenza A and B, 
HSV-1, and Sindbis virus (186). Furthermore, ISG15 plays a protective role in vaccinia 
virus infection, but only when the virus lacks the E3 viral antagonist (187).

experiment.system: ISG15-/- vs wild-type mice
experiment.perturbation: ISG15 knockout; infection with various viruses
experiment.measurement: susceptibility to infection

text: Patients with inborn ISG15 deficiency suffer increased risk of severe mycobacterial infections yet have no history of increased viral susceptibility.

quotes.quote:
a study performed on patients with inborn 
ISG15 deficiencies suggested that secreted ISG15 may be clinically important because these 
individuals suffer from increased risk of severe mycobacterial infections yet have no history 
of increased viral susceptibility (189).

experiment.system: human patients with inborn ISG15 deficiency
experiment.perturbation: observational (genetic deficiency)
experiment.measurement: infection history/susceptibility

text: Viperin expression is stimulated directly by human cytomegalovirus glycoprotein B and, upon HCMV infection, viperin is relocalized to mitochondria by vMIA where it interacts with the mitochondrial trifunctional protein, inhibiting ATP generation and facilitating HCMV infection.

quotes.quote:
viperin expression is stimulated directly by human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) 
glycoprotein B to the benefit of the virus, and therefore in at least one known case, viperin 
has been usurped to act as a proviral factor (196).

Upon HCMV infection, viperin is relocalized to mitochondria by the 
HCMV-encoded mitochondrial inhibitor of apoptosis (vMIA) protein where it interacts with 
the mitochondrial trifunctional protein, leading to the inhibition of ATP generation (196).

experiment.system: HCMV-infected cells
experiment.perturbation: HCMV infection / glycoprotein B stimulation
experiment.measurement: viperin expression and localization, ATP generation, infection

text: Viperin inhibits HIV-1 and influenza A virus budding at the host cell membrane by inhibiting farnesyl diphosphate synthase, altering membrane fluidity, and also inhibits RNA replication of HCV subgenomic replicons via interactions with VAP-A and NS5A.

quotes.quote:
Viperin 
inhibits HIV-1 and influenza A virus budding at the host cell membrane by inhibiting 
farnesyl diphosphate synthase (FPPS), an enzyme involved in isoprenoid biosynthesis (198, 
199).

viperin inhibits 
RNA replication of HCV subgenomic replicons (200).

verdict_note: The HCV portion drops the paper's hedge: the paper states only that viperin interacts with VAP-A and NS5A and that this binding 'might disrupt the VAP-A/NS5A interaction, resulting in inhibition of HCV genome replication'; the claim asserts the interaction-based mechanism as established.

experiment.system: cells infected with HIV-1 or influenza A, or bearing HCV replicons
experiment.perturbation: viperin expression
experiment.measurement: virus budding/particle release and HCV RNA replication

text: Tetherin, encoded by BST2, inhibits virus budding by using two membrane anchors to trap HIV-1 virions on the plasma membrane, and multiple viral proteins (HIV-1 Vpu, HIV-2 Env, SIV Nef, Ebola VP40, KSHV K5, influenza A NA) antagonize it by degradation or sequestration.

quotes.quote:
Tetherin is encoded by the ISG BST2 and inhibits virus budding by using two 
membrane anchors to trap HIV-1 virions on the plasma membrane (Figure 4) (205).

Both HIV-1 Vpu and KSHV K5 are 
involved in tetherin ubiquitination—Vpu by recruiting the E3 ubiquitin ligase complex and 
K5 by directly catalyzing the reaction—resulting in tetherin degradation (206).

experiment.system: virus-infected cell cultures
experiment.perturbation: tetherin expression; viral antagonist proteins
experiment.measurement: virion release/tetherin localization and degradation

text: An shRNA screen identified ISGs important for IFN-β inhibition of West Nile virus and identified ASCC3, which confirmatory experiments showed to be involved in negative regulation of IFN signaling.

quotes.quote:
a recent report identified a number of ISGs that are important for the 
ability of IFN-β to inhibit infection by West Nile virus. This screen also identified the ISG 
activating signal cointegrator complex 3 (ASCC3), and further confirmatory experiments 
showed it to be involved in negative regulation of IFN signaling (215).

experiment.system: cells infected with West Nile virus
experiment.perturbation: lentiviral shRNA knockdown of ISGs
experiment.measurement: IFN-β-mediated virus inhibition; IFN signaling

text: Ectopic overexpression screens identified antiviral ISGs: 7 ISGs in murine fibroblasts against alphavirus, 18 and 29 ISGs against HCV replicons, 36 ISGs against dengue and West Nile virus replicons, and 39 genes against West Nile virus in primary neurons.

quotes.quote:
overexpression of 7 ISGs in murine fibroblasts 
identified genes with the ability to inhibit alphavirus infection (216). Similarly, the 
individual overexpression of 18 (217) and 29 (218) ISGs identified inhibitors of HCV 
replicons, and overexpression of 36 ISGs identified inhibitors of dengue virus and West Nile 
virus replicons (219). More recently, 39 genes were screened for their ability to inhibit West 
Nile virus in primary neurons (220).

experiment.system: murine fibroblasts, replicon cells, primary neurons
experiment.perturbation: ectopic overexpression of individual ISGs
experiment.measurement: virus/replicon inhibition

numbers.quantity: ISGs overexpressed vs HCV replicons (second study)
genes screened vs WNV in primary neurons

text: A large-scale screen of a library of over 380 ISGs against a diverse virus panel found every virus susceptible to several ISGs, with IRF1 and cGAS among the few showing broad potent antiviral activity; most ISGs individually do not inhibit infection or show moderate effects, while net antiviral activity increases when ISG pairs are expressed.

quotes.quote:
a comprehensive large-scale screen for antiviral ISGs was performed with a 
library of over 380 ISGs against a diverse panel of viruses (89, 221). Each virus tested was 
susceptible to inhibition by several ISGs, some that are broadly inhibitory and others that 
display virus-specific activity. The transcription factor IRF1 and cGAS (formerly c6orf150) 
were among the few ISGs that displayed broad, potent antiviral activity.

most ISGs do not inhibit virus infection when expressed 
individually, and those that do display moderate effects. Net antiviral activity does, 
however, increase when various ISGs are expressed in combination, as has been shown by 
measuring the inhibition of virus infection following the expression of ISG pairs (89).

experiment.system: cells ectopically expressing ISGs, diverse virus panel
experiment.perturbation: overexpression of individual ISGs and ISG pairs
experiment.measurement: virus infection inhibition

text: IRF1 overexpression transcriptionally activates a set of genes overlapping those induced by type I IFN, and experiments with cGAS-/- mice suggested cGAS may protect cells from infection by RNA viruses.

quotes.quote:
IRF1 overexpression was found to transcriptionally activate a set of genes that overlaps with 
those induced by type I IFN (89), and cGAS was shown to play an important role in 
activating the innate pathogen sensor STING (79, 81). Subsequently, experiments performed 
using cGAS−/− mice suggested that cGAS may protect cells from infection by RNA viruses

experiment.system: cells overexpressing IRF1; cGAS-/- mice
experiment.perturbation: IRF1 overexpression; cGAS knockout
experiment.measurement: gene induction profile; RNA virus infection

text: An ISG overexpression screen performed in a ZAP-inducible cell line identified ISGs that enhance ZAP's antiviral activity.

quotes.quote:
performing an ISG overexpression screen in a ZAP-inducible cell line identified 
ISGs that enhance ZAP’s antiviral activity (89, 222).

experiment.system: ZAP-inducible cell line
experiment.perturbation: ISG overexpression on ZAP-induced background
experiment.measurement: enhancement of ZAP antiviral activity

text: NeST, a lncRNA at the locus containing the IFN-γ gene, positively impacts IFN-γ mRNA and protein production and is expressed at very low levels in CD8+ T cells under immune activation; the authors proposed it recruits a methyltransferase complex to the IFN-γ locus.

quotes.quote:
Gomez et al. (236) found that NeST expression had a positive impact on the 
production of IFN-γ mRNA and protein. The authors then went on to show that NeST was 
expressed at very low levels in CD8+ T cells under conditions of immune activation and 
proposed a model in which NeST RNA acts by recruiting a methyltransferase complex to 
the IFN-γ locus

experiment.system: B10.S mice / CD8+ T cells
experiment.perturbation: NeST lncRNA expression
experiment.measurement: IFN-γ mRNA and protein production; NeST expression levels

text: Following IFN signaling, ADAR1 transcription initiates from an upstream alternative transcriptional start site, giving rise to an extended protein predominantly localized to the cytoplasm; IFN-γ stimulation also produces alternative isoforms of tryptophanyl-tRNA synthetase with antiproliferative and antiangiogenic effects.

quotes.quote:
IFN-γ stimulation 
leads to the production of alternative isoforms of tryptophanyl-tRNA synthetase, resulting in 
antiproliferative and antiangiogenic effects (239).

Following 
IFN signaling, transcription initiates from an upstream alternative transcriptional start site, 
giving rise to an extended protein that is predominantly localized to the cytoplasm (240).

experiment.system: IFN-stimulated cells
experiment.perturbation: IFN-γ / IFN stimulation
experiment.measurement: transcript isoform usage, protein localization, antiproliferative/antiangiogenic effects

text: On average, IFN treatment leads to transcriptional stimulation of up to 5% of the total number of cellular genes, a statistic that captures only genes with changes in mRNA abundance.

quotes.quote:
On average, IFN treatment leads to transcriptional stimulation of up to 5% of the total 
number of cellular genes; however, this statistic only captures those genes with changes in 
mRNA abundance.

experiment.system: IFN-treated cells
experiment.perturbation: IFN treatment
experiment.measurement: fraction of cellular genes transcriptionally stimulated

numbers.quantity: cellular genes transcriptionally stimulated by IFN

text: Quantitative mass spectrometry of the secretome of LPS-activated macrophages found cytokines, protease inhibitors, and complement components secreted in a time-resolved fashion, many of which showed neither increased transcription nor increased intracellular protein levels.

quotes.quote:
Meissner et al. (248) employed a high-sensitivity quantitative mass spectrometry 
approach to characterize the secretome of macrophages activated with LPS. A variety of 
pro-and anti-inflammatory cytokines, protease inhibitors, and complement components were 
found to be secreted in a time-resolved fashion. Many of these proteins showed neither 
increased transcription nor increased intracellular protein levels

experiment.system: macrophages
experiment.perturbation: LPS activation
experiment.measurement: quantitative mass spectrometry of secreted proteins over time

text: IFN-α mediates cell-to-cell transfer of exosomes containing antiviral factors that facilitate pathogen defense in cells rendered incapable of IFN signaling by viral antagonism.

quotes.quote:
Li et al. (249) recently described IFN-α-mediated cell-to-cell transfer of exosomes 
containing antiviral factors. These exosome “care packages” facilitate pathogen defense in 
cells that have been rendered incapable of IFN signaling by viral antagonism.

experiment.system: co-cultured cells including IFN-signaling-deficient recipients
experiment.perturbation: IFN-α stimulation; exosome transfer
experiment.measurement: transfer of antiviral factors and pathogen defense

text: An elevated baseline level of SOCS1 protein expression in the absence of IFN signaling renders some cells less responsive to IFN, believed to be partly responsible for the weak type I IFN response of human pluripotent stem cells.

quotes.quote:
for some cells, in the absence of IFN signaling an elevated 
baseline level of SOCS1 protein expression renders cells less responsive to IFN (102). This 
reduced responsiveness is believed to be partly responsible for the weak response to type I 
IFN that results from IFN stimulation of human pluripotent stem cells (102).

experiment.system: human pluripotent stem cells and other cell types
experiment.perturbation: observational baseline SOCS1 levels; type I IFN stimulation
experiment.measurement: IFN responsiveness

text: PIAS1 inhibits STAT1 independently of SUMOylation, although STAT1 can itself be SUMOylated and this modification impacts ISG induction.

quotes.quote:
PIAS1 has been shown to inhibit STAT1 
independently of SUMOylation (Figure 3b) (99); however, STAT1 proteins can be 
SUMOylated, and this modification impacts ISG induction as well (100, 101).

text: Downregulation of APPL1 by morpholinos in zebrafish leads to widespread apoptosis during development, mediated by inactivation of the Akt–GSK3β axis and rescued by expression of functional APPL1, whereas the Akt–mTOR axis does not seem affected; in HeLa cells APPL-containing endosomes seem necessary for ERK1/ERK2 activation and Akt signalling to both GSK3β and mTOR, and in sympathetic neurons and PC12 cells APPL recruitment to endosomal NTRK1 was necessary for ERK and Akt activation and NGF-induced neurite outgrowth.

quotes.quote:
downregulation of APPL1 by morpholinos in
zebrafish leads to widespread apoptosis during development74. This effect is mediated by the
inactivation of the Akt-GSK3β (glycogen synthase kinase 3β) signalling axis and can be
rescued by the expression of functional APPL1.

the Akt-mTOR (mammalian target or
rapamycin) signalling axis does not seem to be affected by APPL1 knockdown

In cultured mammalian Hela cells, however, APPL-containing
endosomes seem to be necessary for ERK1 and ERK2 activation and Akt signalling to both
GSK3β and mTOR73.

recruitment of APPL proteins, which interact with NTRK1 directly or indirectly through the adaptor protein GIPC (GAIP-
interacting protein, C-terminus)72,75, to endosomal NTRK1 was also necessary for the
activation of both ERK and Akt, and for NGF-induced neurite outgrowth75.

experiment.system: zebrafish embryos; HeLa cells; sympathetic neurons and PC12 cells
experiment.perturbation: morpholino/knockdown of APPL1 (with rescue by functional APPL1)
experiment.measurement: apoptosis during development, Akt–GSK3β/mTOR and ERK1/ERK2 activation, neurite outgrowth

text: Overexpression of the E3 ubiquitin ligase Deltex promotes ligand-independent Notch ubiquitylation and endocytosis, leading to accumulation of full-length Notch in MVBs containing late endosomal markers, which is required for Notch signalling during D. melanogaster embryonic development.

quotes.quote:
Deltex promotes Notch ubiquitylation and endocytosis, leading to the
accumulation of full-length Notch in MVBs that contain markers of late endosomes, which is
required for Notch signalling during D. melanogaster embryonic development77

experiment.system: Drosophila melanogaster embryos
experiment.perturbation: overexpression of the E3 ubiquitin ligase Deltex
experiment.measurement: Notch ubiquitylation, localization in MVBs/late endosomes and Notch signalling

text: Inhibiting EGFR ubiquitylation by mutating receptor ubiquitin-conjugation sites enhances EGFR signalling, whereas increasing receptor ubiquitylation by inhibiting deubiquitylation accelerates RTK degradation and downregulates signalling.

quotes.quote:
Inhibiting EGFR ubiquitylation by
mutating the receptor ubiquitin-conjugation sites enhances EGFR signalling86. By contrast,
increasing receptor ubiquitylation by inhibiting deubiquitylation accelerates the degradation
of RTKs and down-regulates signalling.

experiment.perturbation: mutation of receptor ubiquitin-conjugation sites; inhibition of deubiquitylation

text: Mice with conditional knockout of the deubiquitylation enzyme UBPY have reduced expression of several RTKs, decreased rates of cell proliferation and liver failure in adults, whereas RNAi knockdown of UBPY in cultured mammalian cells causes reduced EGFR degradation, and knockdown of AMSH enhanced degradation.

quotes.quote:
Mice in which the deubiquitylation enzyme UBPY
(also known as USP8) has been conditionally knocked out have reduced expression levels of
several RTKs, which results in decreased rates of cell proliferation and causes liver failure in
adult mice87. However, RNA interference-mediated knockdown of UBPY causes the opposite
effect (reduced EGFR degradation) in cultured mammalian cells, and knockdown of the distinct
endosome-associated deubiquitylating enzyme AMSH (also known as STAMBP) enhanced

experiment.system: mice and cultured mammalian cells
experiment.perturbation: conditional knockout or RNAi knockdown of UBPY/USP8; RNAi knockdown of AMSH
experiment.measurement: RTK expression levels, EGFR degradation, cell proliferation and liver phenotype

text: Inhibition of HRS translation by the microRNA miR296 enhances vascular endothelial growth factor receptor activity and increases angiogenesis.

quotes.quote:
Inhibition of HRS translation by microRNAs (specifically miR296) enhances the activity of
vascular endothelial growth factor receptor and increases angiogenesis92.

experiment.system: angiogenic endothelial cells
experiment.perturbation: miR296-mediated inhibition of HRS translation
experiment.measurement: VEGF receptor activity and angiogenesis

text: RAB4-dependent recycling resensitizes GPCRs such as β2AR, apparently by promoting dephosphorylation by endosome-associated phosphatase 2A, and RAB4-dependent recycling is required for sustaining normal physiological responsiveness of β1ARs and β2ARs in intact cardiac muscle.

The subsequent endocytosis and RAB4-

dephosphorylation by the endosome-associated phosphatase 2A94,95.

it has been shown that RAB4-dependent recycling is
required for sustaining normal physiological responsiveness of both β1ARs and β2ARs in
intact cardiac muscle96,97.

text: RNAi-mediated depletion of cellular ECE1 inhibited ligand proteolysis in endosomes and reduced recycling of CLR and NK1R, producing a prolonged reduction in subsequent receptor responsiveness.

RNA interference-mediated depletion of cellular ECE1 inhibited ligand
proteolysis in endosomes and reduced receptor recycling. This resulted in a prolonged
reduction in subsequent receptor responsiveness, which suggests that ligand proteolysis
promotes efficient receptor recycling and functional resensitization98,99.

experiment.perturbation: RNAi depletion of endothelin-converting enzyme ECE1
experiment.measurement: endosomal ligand proteolysis, receptor recycling and subsequent responsiveness

text: In isolated cardiac myocytes, β2AR activation elicits a transient increase in contraction rate mediated by Gs coupling followed by a decrease mediated by Gi coupling, and this switch of G protein coupling specificity requires β2AR endocytosis and recycling.

quotes.quote:
ligand-induced activation elicits a transient increase in
cellular contraction rate that is mediated by receptor coupling to Gs-type trimeric G proteins,

recycling

experiment.perturbation: β2AR agonist activation with blockade of endocytosis/recycling
experiment.measurement: cellular contraction rate and G protein coupling specificity

text: EGFRs internalized through clathrin-dependent endocytosis are recycled back to the plasma membrane more efficiently, and degraded less efficiently, than receptors internalized by clathrin-independent endocytosis, explaining the role of CDE of EGFR in ERK and Akt signalling.

quotes.quote:
EGFRs internalized through CDE are recycled back to the plasma membrane
more efficiently, and degraded less efficiently, than receptors internalized by CIE. This
difference in post-endocytic sorting explains the important role of the CDE of EGFR in ERK
and Akt signalling34.

experiment.perturbation: routing of EGFR through clathrin-dependent versus clathrin-independent endocytosis (varied EGF dose/pathway blockade)

text: With the EGFR agonist TGFα, which is released from the receptor in the acidic environment of endosomes, EGFR is not significantly downregulated and each recycled receptor can be activated by TGFα many times.

quotes.quote:
The EGFR agonist TGFα, for
example, is released from the receptor in the acidic environment of endosomes. In this case,
EGFR is not significantly downregulated, and each recycled receptor can be activated by
TGFα many times101.

experiment.perturbation: stimulation with TGFα versus EGF (pH-sensitive ligand–receptor interaction)

text: Ligand-induced activation of EGFR in sympathetic neurons produced a rapid increase in the total number and surface density of clathrin-coated pits, and EGFR or NTRK1 activation increases the pool of cellular clathrin associated with the plasma membrane of HeLa or PC12 cells respectively, in a manner dependent on Src kinase activity.

ligand-induced activation of EGFR in these cells
produced a rapid increase in the total number and surface density of clathrin-coated pits103.

that is associated with the plasma membrane of HeLa or PC12 cells, respectively, and this

text: Depletion of AP2 reduces the number of clathrin-coated pits in HeLa cells, and EGFR activation in these cells leads to de novo formation of clathrin-coated pits containing EGFR and GRB2 but not transferrin receptors; however, live-cell imaging in HeLa cells expressing AP2 at physiological levels showed activated EGFRs are recruited into pre-existing clathrin-coated pits.

Depletion of AP2 reduces the number of clathrin-coated
pits in HeLa cells, and activation of EGFR in these cells leads to de novo formation of c lathrin-
coated pits that contain EGFR and the adaptor GRB2 (REF. 106). These clathrin-coated pits
do not contain transferrin receptors

live-
cell imaging of EGFR endocytosis showed that, in HeLa cells expressing AP2 at physio logical

experiment.perturbation: AP2 depletion versus physiological AP2 levels; EGF-induced EGFR activation

text: β2ARs concentrated uniformly in clathrin-coated pits in HEK293 cells overexpressing β-arrestin, but in cells expressing β-arrestin at physiological levels ligand-activated β2ARs selectively concentrated in a fraction of clathrin-coated pits, and β2AR presence regulated the period individual coated pits remained at the surface, measured as the interval between clathrin coat deposition and membrane scission.

text: EGFR activation was found to slow endosome maturation and to increase the number of intraluminal vesicles in multivesicular bodies.

quotes.quote:
EGFR activation

in MVBs117.

experiment.perturbation: EGF-induced EGFR activation

the A-RAF isoform of the Raf kinase family is located in recycling

text: In the yeast GPCR Ste2 system, Gpa1 translocates to endosomes and binds the endosome-associated protein Vps15; GTP-bound Gpa1 is thought to activate the PI3K Vps34, increasing endosomal PtdIns3P and recruiting the FYVE domain protein Bem1 to potentiate MAPK and Cdc42 signalling.

recently born sisters were

already increasing CDK2inc trajectories.

experiment.system: asynchronously cycling MCF10A cells expressing DHB-Ven
experiment.perturbation: 100 nM MEK inhibitor (PD032591) added after 8 hr preimaging; analysis restricted to cells 1-3 hr post-anaphase
experiment.measurement: single-cell CDK2 activity traces aligned to anaphase

text: The bifurcation at mitotic exit also occurred in Hs68 primary human fibroblasts (39% CDK2low) and murine Swiss 3T3 cells (77% CDK2low), with longer CDK2low durations than MCF10A.

quotes.quote:
Both
cell types displayed a bifurcation in CDK2 activity at mitotic exit, similar to MCF10A cells.
However, the fraction of CDK2low cells was slightly larger in Hs68 cells (39%, Figure 3D)
compared to MCF10A cells, and much larger in Swiss 3T3 cells (77%, Figure 3E). For both
Hs68 and Swiss 3T3 fibroblasts, cells also tended to persist in the CDK2low state for longer
durations than MCF10A cells.

experiment.system: Hs68 primary human foreskin fibroblasts and murine Swiss 3T3 fibroblasts expressing DHB-Ven
experiment.perturbation: observational (asynchronous cycling cultures)
experiment.measurement: single-cell CDK2 activity traces aligned to anaphase; fraction CDK2low

text: In cycling cells, siRNA against cyclin E during the previous cell cycle prevented post-mitotic CDK2 buildup (cells behaved like CDK2low), while cyclin A was required to raise CDK2 activity above a Cyt/Nuc ratio of one.

quotes.quote:
Cells treated with siRNA targeting cyclin E during the previous cell cycle failed to build
up CDK2 activity after mitosis and behaved similarly to CDK2low cells (Figure 3F). As in
cells emerging from quiescence, cyclin A was required to raise CDK2 activity above a
Cyt/Nuc DHB-Ven ratio of one.

experiment.system: asynchronously cycling MCF10A cells expressing DHB-Ven
experiment.perturbation: siRNA pools against cyclin E1/E2 or cyclin A2 vs nontargeting siRNA
experiment.measurement: single-cell CDK2 activity traces aligned to anaphase

text: Neither CDK2inc nor reactivating CDK2low cells entered S phase until DHB-Ven exceeded a Cyt/Nuc ratio of approximately one, and EdU-marked S phase was restricted to a window of DHB-Ven Cyt/Nuc ratio 0.9–1.1.

quotes.quote:
we found that neither the CDK2inc nor the reactivating CDK2low
MCF10A cells entered into S phase until DHB-Ven rose above a Cyt/Nuc ratio of
approximately one (Figures 3G and 3H).

When we used EdU incorporation to monitor
DNA replication in individual cells, we found that S phase was restricted to a window of
CDK2 activity that corresponds to a DHB-Ven Cyt/Nuc ratio of 0.9–1.1 (Figure 3I).

experiment.system: cycling MCF10A cells expressing DHB-Ven and Cer-Cdt1
experiment.perturbation: observational; 10 μM EdU pulse for 15 min then fixation
experiment.measurement: Cyt/Nuc DHB-Ven at S-phase onset (Cdt1 degradation) and vs EdU incorporation

numbers.quantity: DHB-Ven Cyt/Nuc window of S phase

text: The M-to-S interval scaled with intermitotic time with a slope close to one and explained 70% of the variance in cell-cycle duration; CDK2inc cells had short M-to-S intervals of 5–7 hr with coefficient of variation 0.26 versus 0.42 for all cells with a finite M-to-S interval.

quotes.quote:
The relationship between
the duration of the M-to-S interval and the intermitotic time had a slope close to one (Figure
3K), arguing that an increase of 1 hr in the M-to-S interval results in an increase of 1 hr in
total cell-cycle time. Moreover, the time that individual cells spent between M and S
explained 70% of the variance in the overall cell-cycle duration. Cells that pass through the
CDK2low state had long and variable M-to-S intervals, whereas the time spent between M
and S for CDK2inc cells was short (5–7 hr) and relatively invariant (Figure 4L; coefficient of
variation = 0.26 for CDK2inc cells versus coefficient of variation = 0.42 for all cells with a
finite M-to-S interval).

experiment.system: cycling MCF10A cells expressing DHB-Ven, Cer-Cdt1, H2B-Chy
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: M-to-S interval versus intermitotic time (n = 176; histogram n = 250), linear regression and coefficient of variation

numbers.quantity: variance in cell-cycle duration explained by M-to-S interval
CV for all cells with finite M-to-S interval

text: CDK1/2 inhibitor addition lowered the Cyt/Nuc DHB-Ven ratio of CDK2inc cells below their mitotic-exit level to that of CDK2low cells, while producing no further reduction in CDK2low cells, indicating CDK2inc cells exit mitosis with residual CDK2 activity.

quotes.quote:
addition of CDK1/2 inhibitor to CDK2inc cells reduced the Cyt/Nuc ratio of DHBVen to a
level lower than that observed at mitotic exit and similar to that of CDK2low cells (blue,
Figures 4A and 4B), confirming that CDK2inc cells exit mitosis with residual CDK2
activity. In contrast, addition of CDK1/2 inhibitor to CDK2low cells did not further reduce
the Cyt/Nuc ratio

experiment.system: cycling MCF10A cells expressing DHB-Ven
experiment.perturbation: 10 μM CDK1/2 inhibitor added after 22 hr of imaging
experiment.measurement: difference (Δ) between Cyt/Nuc DHB-Ven at mitotic exit and after drug addition

text: Sister cells chose the same CDK2inc or CDK2low fate 98% of the time, while local cell density was similar between the two fates under subconfluent conditions.

quotes.quote:
We first tested whether local cell density plays a role, but found that the
number of neighboring cells was similar in CDK2inc and CDK2low cells under our
experimental conditions in which cells remain subconfluent (Figure S4). We also noted that
sister cells chose the same CDK2inc or CDK2low fate 98% of the time

experiment.system: cycling MCF10A cells expressing DHB-Ven
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: fate concordance between sister cells and neighbor counts from tracked time-lapse data

text: Of a panel of candidate regulators (cMyc, cyclin D1, cyclin E, cyclin A2, p21, p27, phospho-Rb, phospho-p38, gH2AX), only phospho-Rb and p21 levels differed statistically between CDK2inc and CDK2low cells immediately after the bifurcation.

quotes.quote:
We used this method to
monitor a number of potential regulators of the bifurcation including cMyc, cyclin D1,
cyclin E, cyclin A2, p21, p27, phospho-Rb, the stress marker phospho-p38, and the DNA
damage marker gH2AX. We found that only phospho-Rb and p21 levels were clearly

statistically different in CDK2inc and CDK2low cells immediately after the bifurcation
(Figures 4D–4H, and S4).

experiment.system: asynchronous MCF10A cells expressing DHB-Ven
experiment.perturbation: observational; fixation after time-lapse followed by antibody staining with jitter-corrected cell matching
experiment.measurement: immunofluorescence levels of candidate regulators 2–3.5 hr after anaphase, rank-sum test

text: CDK2inc cells were born with hyperphosphorylated Rb whereas most CDK2low cells showed low Rb phosphorylation, with the two phospho-Rb subpopulations evident within the first hour after anaphase; ~75% of MCF10A cells exit mitosis with residual CDK2 activity and hyperphosphorylated Rb.

quotes.quote:
CDK2inc cells were born
with hyper-phosphorylated Rb. In contrast, most cells in the CDK2low state showed low Rb
phosphorylation (Figures 4E and 4F). These two distinct sub-populations of phospho-Rb
were already evident within the first hour after anaphase (Figure S4).

Thus, ~75% of MCF10A cells
exit mitosis with residual CDK2 activity and hyperphosphorylated Rb.

experiment.system: MCF10A cells expressing DHB-Ven
experiment.perturbation: observational; time-lapse imaging followed by fixation and pRb807/811 immunofluorescence
experiment.measurement: phospho-Rb level reconstructed as a function of time since anaphase; density scatter of Cyt/Nuc DHB-Ven vs pRb

numbers.quantity: fraction of MCF10A cells exiting mitosis with residual CDK2 activity and hyperphosphorylated Rb

text: Endogenous p21 was elevated in cells born into the CDK2low state and remained low in CDK2inc cells; in single cells high p21 and high Cyt/Nuc DHB-Ven were mutually exclusive.

quotes.quote:
The levels of p21 were
elevated in cells born into the CDK2low state, whereas p21 levels remained low in CDK2inc
cells throughout the cell cycle.

When we plotted the
DHB-Ven versus p21 signal in single cells, we found that the two are mutually exclusive:
cells with high p21 always had low Cyt/Nuc DHB-Ven ratios, whereas cells with low p21
had intermediate to high Cyt/Nuc DHB-Ven ratios (Figure 4J).

experiment.system: asynchronously cycling MCF10A cells expressing DHB-Ven
experiment.perturbation: observational; time-lapse followed by p21 immunofluorescence
experiment.measurement: p21 level versus time since anaphase and versus Cyt/Nuc DHB-Ven in single cells

text: p21–/– MCF10A cells very rarely entered the CDK2low state (<2% versus 26% for parental cells), while CDK2inc intermitotic times were similar in both lines.

quotes.quote:
we found
that p21–/– MCF10A very rarely entered the CDK2low state (<2% CDK2low for p21–/– cells
versus 26% for parental cells) (Figure 5A). The intermitotic times of CDK2inc cells were
similar in parental and p21–/– MCF10A cells

experiment.system: parental and p21–/– MCF10A cells transduced with DHB-Ven
experiment.perturbation: p21 gene knockout, imaged in parallel with parental cells
experiment.measurement: fraction of cells entering CDK2low state and intermitotic times from anaphase-aligned traces

text: Acute TMP-induced stabilization of DHFR-mCherry-p21 in p21–/– MCF10A cells during G2/M controlled the CDK2inc/CDK2low split dose-dependently, with 100% of cells entering CDK2low at the highest TMP dose.

quotes.quote:
we found that we were able to
control, in a dose-dependent manner, the fraction of CDK2inc versus CDK2low cells simply
by regulating the level of p21. At an intermediate dose of TMP, resulting in intermediate
levels of p21, a fraction of cells entered the CDK2low state (Figure 5C, middle, red), while
the remainder built up CDK2inc activity (Figure 5C, middle, blue; these were invariably the
cells with lower p21 levels). At the highest dose of TMP, resulting in high levels of p21,
100% of cells entered the CDK2low state after mitosis (Figure 5C, bottom).

experiment.system: p21–/– MCF10A cells expressing DHFR-mCherry-p21 and DHB-Ven
experiment.perturbation: DMSO or 0.05 μM or 5 μM TMP added to asynchronous cultures, analyzing cells treated 0–4 hr prior to anaphase
experiment.measurement: mCherry-p21 intensity and CDK2 activity traces aligned to anaphase; fraction entering CDK2low

numbers.quantity: fraction entering CDK2low at highest TMP dose

text: Every MCF10A cell that had initiated CDK2 buildup completed mitosis even when mitogens were withdrawn at any time in G1, S, or G2; withdrawal did not significantly alter the ongoing cell-cycle duration but promoted CDK2low entry after the subsequent mitosis, with similar results in Hs68 and Swiss 3T3 cells.

quotes.quote:
Every MCF10A cell that initiated a buildup in CDK2 activity continued on its
trajectory and completed mitosis even if mitogens were withdrawn at any time within G1, S,
or G2. Mitogen withdrawal did not significantly alter the duration of the ongoing cell cycle
but did promote entry into the CDK2low state after the subsequent mitosis (Figures 6B–6E).
We obtained similar results in Hs68 and Swiss 3T3 cells (Figure S6).

experiment.system: asynchronous MCF10A, Hs68, and Swiss 3T3 cells expressing DHB-Ven and Cer-Cdt1
experiment.perturbation: preimaging for cell-cycle phase, then washing into mitogen-free starvation media
experiment.measurement: single-cell CDK2 activity traces and cell-cycle completion after withdrawal

text: Mitogen removal more than 8 hr before mitosis drove cells into the CDK2low state after mitosis; removal 0–8 hr prior to mitosis gave a decreasing probability of proliferative entry with a midpoint approximately 3 hr prior to anaphase; removal after mitosis left CDK2inc entry unchanged, and MEK inhibition gave similar results.

quotes.quote:
It then became
apparent that if mitogens were removed more than 8 hr before mitosis, cells would enter the
CDK2low state after mitosis and become quiescent. If mitogens were removed in a window
0–8 hr prior to mitosis, cells showed a decreasing probability of entering the proliferative
state with a midpoint approximately 3 hr prior to anaphase (Figure 6E). If mitogens were
withdrawn after mitosis, cells entered the CDK2inc state with the same probability as control
cells and completed one additional cell cycle before becoming quiescent.

We therefore suppressed
growth factor signaling by adding a MEK inhibitor to cycling cells and obtained similar
results (Figures 6D and 6E and Movie S4).

experiment.system: asynchronously cycling MCF10A cells expressing DHB-Ven
experiment.perturbation: mitogen withdrawal or 100 nM MEKi (PD032591) after 8 hr preimaging, cells sorted by time of mitosis (M0)
experiment.measurement: heatmap of CDK2 activity and probability of quiescence (DHB-Ven Cyt/Nuc < 1 at 6 hr after M0)

numbers.quantity: time before mitosis beyond which mitogen removal causes quiescence

text: In Swiss 3T3 cells, CDK2inc cells (only 20% of cells) were immune to serum withdrawal at any time in G1, S, or G2 but entered CDK2low after the next mitosis, whereas the majority (80%) that naturally enter CDK2low remained serum-sensitive while CDK2 activity stayed low.

quotes.quote:
we found that CDK2inc Swiss 3T3 cells (only 20% of cells) were
immune to serum withdrawal at any time in G1, S, or G2, but would enter into the CDK2low
state after completing the next mitosis (Figures 6F and 6G). However, a majority (80%) of
Swiss 3T3 cells naturally enter the CDK2low state after mitosis (Figure 3E) and therefore
remain sensitive to serum withdrawal as long as they have low CDK2 activity

experiment.system: cycling murine Swiss 3T3 cells expressing DHB-Ven
experiment.perturbation: serum withdrawal at varying cell ages after preimaging
experiment.measurement: heatmap of CDK2 activity sorted by time of mitosis; cell age at serum removal versus subsequent intermitotic time

numbers.quantity: fraction of Swiss 3T3 cells that are CDK2inc
fraction of Swiss 3T3 cells entering CDK2low

text: Run-on transcription analysis of HeLa cells treated with purified IFN-β showed a large increase (>30-fold) in transcription of interferon-stimulated genes, occurring within 15 min and unaffected by prior cycloheximide treatment, indicating the responsible proteins pre-existed in the cells.

quotes.quote:
We immediately tested by run-on analysis and found a large increase (>30-fold) in the
transcriptional rate of these interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs). Two important points came
from these experiments. The transcriptional activation came very quickly (within 15 min)
and blocking protein synthesis with cycloheximide before IFN treatment did not affect the
transcriptional increase.

experiment.system: HeLa cells with cDNA libraries from IFN-treated and untreated cells
experiment.perturbation: IFN-β treatment, with or without cycloheximide pretreatment
experiment.measurement: run-on transcription assay of ISG transcription rate

numbers.quantity: fold increase in ISG transcription rate

text: Comparison of the 5′ sequences of two IFN-induced genes revealed a conserved ~25 base pair region ~100 nucleotides upstream of the mRNA start site, and mutations in these interferon-stimulated response elements (ISREs) blocked IFN-dependent reporter responses.

quotes.quote:
a highly
conserved ∼25 base pair region was evident ∼100 nucleotides upstream of the start site for
each of these mRNAs. Mutations within these “promoters,” termed interferon-stimulated
response elements (ISREs), blocked the IFN-dependent reporter responses.

experiment.system: cloned genomic promoters of IFN-induced genes (including ISG15) in reporter assays
experiment.perturbation: sequence comparison and mutation of the conserved upstream element
experiment.measurement: IFN-dependent reporter gene response

text: Gel-shift analysis of extracts from IFN-β-treated cells identified an IFN-dependent ISRE-binding complex, ISGF3, first detected in the cytoplasm after 1 or 2 min of treatment and then accumulating in the nucleus.

quotes.quote:
The factor was first detected in the
cytoplasm after a 1 or 2 min IFN-β treatment and then accumulated in the nucleus.

The large induced complex was
christened ISGF3 for interferon-stimulated gene factor 3.

experiment.system: cell extracts from IFN-treated and untreated cells
experiment.perturbation: IFN-β treatment for 1–2 min
experiment.measurement: electrophoretic mobility (gel-shift) of ISRE probe binding complexes in cytoplasmic and nuclear fractions

numbers.quantity: time of IFN-β treatment before cytoplasmic detection

text: Prior exposure of HeLa cells to IFN-γ enabled a much more vigorous subsequent IFN-α transcriptional response and greatly increased the amount of ISGF3; cytoplasm from IFN-γ-treated cells added to extracts of IFN-α-treated cells greatly increased ISGF3, indicating a limiting IFN-γ-induced component.

quotes.quote:
they found that prior exposure of HeLa cells to IFN-γ enabled a
much more vigorous subsequent IFN-α transcriptional response (Levy et al., 1990).
Additionally, the prior IFN-γ treatment greatly increased the amount of ISGF3, the DNA
promoter-binding complex produced in response to IFN-α and IFN-β. Moreover, the
cytoplasm of the IFN-γ-treated HeLa cells contained a limiting amount of some component
of ISGF3 because such cytoplasm would, when added to cytoplasmic extracts of IFN-α-
treated cells, greatly increase the amount of ISGF3.

experiment.system: HeLa cells and cytoplasmic extracts
experiment.perturbation: IFN-γ pretreatment followed by IFN-α/IFN-β treatment; extract mixing
experiment.measurement: transcriptional response and gel-shift amount of ISGF3

text: Purification of ISGF3 from IFN-treated HeLa cells by gel-shift band excision and then ISRE oligonucleotide affinity chromatography (from 200 l of HeLa cells) identified four proteins of nominally 113, 91, 84, and 48 kDa, which coimmunoprecipitated with 91 kDa or 113 kDa antisera, indicating a multiprotein complex.

quotes.quote:
Bingo—Dan identified clearly four proteins, nominally
113, 91, 84, and 48 kDa.

He made a preparation from 200 l of HeLa
cells in which the 113, 91, 84, and 48 kDa proteins were clearly separated after gel
electrophoresis.

With the 91 kDa or the 113
kDa antisera, Schindler showed that all of the proteins in the 113, 91, 84, and 48 complex
coimmunoprecipitated.

experiment.system: partially purified extracts from IFN-γ-pretreated, IFN-α-treated HeLa cells
experiment.perturbation: gel-shift band excision, oligonucleotide (ISRE) affinity chromatography, antibody immunoprecipitation
experiment.measurement: protein-stained gel electrophoresis, peptide sequencing, coimmunoprecipitation

numbers.quantity: volume of HeLa cell culture used

text: Staurosporin, which also inhibits tyrosine kinases, completely blocked IFN-α-dependent induction of ISGF3, whereas a broad-spectrum serine kinase inhibitor did not; 32P labeling with antibody precipitation showed the vast majority of label in all three proteins was in tyrosine.

quotes.quote:
Cells treated with a broad-spectrum serine kinase inhibitor still activated ISGF3.
But staurosporin, which also inhibits tyrosine kinases, completely blocked IFN-α-dependent
induction of ISGF3 (Schindler et al., 1992b).

demonstrated with 32P protein labeling and antibody precipitation that the vast majority of
the 32P label in all three proteins was in tyrosine, a big surprise.

experiment.system: cultured cells treated with IFN-α
experiment.perturbation: kinase inhibitors (serine kinase inhibitor, staurosporin); 32P metabolic labeling
experiment.measurement: ISGF3 induction (gel-shift) and phosphoamino acid analysis of immunoprecipitated proteins

text: The GAS-binding factor GAF was precipitated by antiserum against the 91 kDa protein and was phosphorylated; its single tyrosine phosphorylation site was identified as Y701 in the 91 kDa protein (STAT1), which could be activated by either IFN-α or IFN-γ.

quotes.quote:
Schindler, Shuai, and others showed that this protein was precipitated with the antiserum
against the 91 kDa protein and was phosphorylated. The single tyrosine phosphorylation site
was identified as Y701 in the 91 kDa protein, which could be activated by either IFN-α or
IFN-γ

experiment.system: IFN-treated cell extracts containing the GAS-binding factor GAF
experiment.perturbation: IFN-α or IFN-γ treatment; immunoprecipitation with anti-91 kDa antiserum
experiment.measurement: gel mobility, phosphorylation and mapping of the tyrosine phosphorylation site

text: Complementation of mutant cell lines with JAK cDNAs showed that IFN-dependent signaling required both JAK1 and TYK2 to tyrosine phosphorylate STAT1 and STAT2 in response to IFN-α, and JAK1 and JAK2 to phosphorylate STAT1 in response to IFN-γ.

quotes.quote:
the Kerr and Stark
labs soon showed that IFN-dependent signaling required both JAK1 and TYK2 to
successfully tyrosine phosphorylate the two substrates STAT1 and STAT2, in response to
IFN-α, and JAK1 and JAK2 to phosphorylate STAT1 in response to IFN-γ (Müller et al.,
1993).

experiment.system: mutant human cell lines defective in IFN signaling
experiment.perturbation: complementation with JAK cDNA expression constructs; IFN-α or IFN-γ treatment
experiment.measurement: tyrosine phosphorylation of STAT1 and STAT2 and IFN responsiveness

text: A total of eight different mutant cell lines were obtained and complemented, each lacking a single protein required for responses to IFN-α, IFN-γ, or both; most were isolated by drug-based selection, while the JAK2-lacking mutant γ1A was found by sorting cells that failed to activate cell surface markers in response to IFN-γ. The lines have been made available to more than 500 additional laboratories.

quotes.quote:
we were able to obtain and
complement a total of eight different mutant cell lines, each lacking a single protein required
for responses to IFN-α, IFN-γ, or both. Although most were isolated by using a drug-based
selection, the mutant γ1A, lacking JAK2, was found by sorting cells that failed to activate
expression of cell surface markers in response to IFN-γ (Watling et al., 1993).

The mutant cell lines have been made available to more than 500 additional
laboratories (still counting)

experiment.system: mutagenized human cell lines
experiment.perturbation: chemical mutagenesis with drug-based selection or FACS sorting for failed IFN-γ-induced surface marker expression; complementation with JAK, STAT, IRF9 and receptor subunit constructs
experiment.measurement: identification of the single missing protein per line

text: Cloning of STAT3 and STAT4 from a lymphocyte cDNA library established their membership in the STAT family by sequence analysis, and tyrosine phosphorylation of STAT3 was shown to occur in response to IL-6 and EGF, while IL-12 activated STAT4.

quotes.quote: cloned STAT3 and STAT4, establishing in the fall of 1993 by sequence

analysis their membership in the STAT family. They showed that tyrosine phosphorylation
of STAT3 occurred in response to IL-6 and EGF and, together with Ken Murphy's lab, that
IL-12 activated STAT4 (Zhong et al., 1994a, 1994b; Jacobson et al., 1995).

experiment.system: lymphocyte cDNA library and cultured cells
experiment.perturbation: cytokine/growth factor stimulation (IL-6, EGF, IL-12)
experiment.measurement: cDNA sequence analysis and tyrosine phosphorylation of STAT3/STAT4

text: Phosphorylation of both STAT1 and STAT3 on S727 was shown in cell culture to be necessary, in addition to tyrosine phosphorylation, for full activation of transcription in response to IFNs and gp130-linked cytokines such as IL-6, respectively, and mouse experiments mutating these serines to alanines extended the cell culture results.

quotes.quote:
In 1995, phosphorylation of both STAT1 and STAT3 on S727 was shown in cell culture
experiments to be necessary, in addition to tyrosine phosphorylation, for full activation of

transcription in response to IFNs and gp130-linked cytokines such as IL-6, respectively
(Wen et al., 1995). Experiments in mice in which these serine residues were mutated to
alanines extended these cell culture results (Varinou et al., 2003; Shen et al., 2004).

experiment.system: cultured cells and mice with serine-to-alanine STAT mutations
experiment.perturbation: S727 mutation; IFN or IL-6 stimulation
experiment.measurement: transcriptional activation

text: STAT1 serine S708 is phosphorylated in response to type I IFNs by IKKε, a modification needed for ISGF3 to activate a subset of IFN-stimulated genes; later work showed S708 phosphorylation inhibits STAT1 homodimerization but not ISGF3 formation, and that STAT1 tyrosine phosphorylation is required for S708 phosphorylation, which leads to IFIT2 expression restricting West Nile virus infection.

quotes.quote:
A
different serine residue of STAT1, S708, is phosphorylated in response to type I IFNs by
IKKε, a modification that is needed for ISGF3 to activate a subset of IFN-stimulated genes
(Tenoever et al., 2007). More recent work from the Maniatis laboratory (Ng et al., 2011)
reveals that S708 phosphorylation inhibits STAT1 homodimerization but not ISGF3
formation

Perwitasari et al. (2011) show that STAT1 tyrosine
phosphorylation is required for STAT1 S708 phosphorylation and that this modification
leads to expression of the IFIT2 gene, imparting innate immunity that restricts West Nile
virus infection.

experiment.system: cells responding to type I IFN and West Nile virus infection
experiment.perturbation: type I IFN treatment; IKKε and STAT1 phosphosite manipulation
experiment.measurement: STAT1 S708 phosphorylation, dimerization/ISGF3 formation, ISG (IFIT2) expression and viral restriction

text: In many different cells, virus infection triggers STING to recruit STAT6 to the endoplasmic reticulum, leading to phosphorylation of S407 and Y641, and homodimers of tyrosine- and serine-phosphorylated STAT6 activate target genes mediating immune cell homing — a JAK- and receptor-independent mode of STAT activation.

quotes.quote:
In many different cells,
virus infection triggers STING (also named MITA or ERIS) to recruit STAT6 to the
endoplasmic reticulum, leading to phosphorylation of S407 and Y641. Homodimers of
tyrosine- and serine-phosphorylated STAT6 then activate specific target genes in the nucleus
that mediate immune cell homing.

experiment.system: virus-infected cells of many types
experiment.perturbation: virus infection triggering STING
experiment.measurement: STAT6 recruitment to ER, phosphorylation of S407 and Y641, target gene activation

text: STAT3 is phosphorylated in nuclei by dimeric pyruvate kinase M2, a JAK-independent mode of STAT phosphorylation that helps promote cell proliferation in response to alterations in glucose metabolism.

quotes.quote:
Another example of JAK-independent STAT
phosphorylation is provided by recent work of Gao et al. (2012) showing that STAT3 is
phosphorylated in nuclei by dimeric pyruvate kinase M2, helping to promote cell
proliferation in response to alterations in glucose metabolism.

experiment.system: cells with altered glucose metabolism
experiment.perturbation: dimeric pyruvate kinase M2 acting as protein kinase
experiment.measurement: nuclear STAT3 phosphorylation and cell proliferation

text: STAT3 is dimethylated on K140 by SET9 in response to IL6 and demethylated by LSD1; these enzymes modify wild-type STAT3 bound to the SOCS3 promoter but not the S727A mutant, showing that prior S727 phosphorylation is required for methylation.

quotes.quote:
STAT3 is dimethylated on K140 by SET9 in response to IL6 and demethylated by LSD1
(Yang et al., 2010). These enzymes, initially discovered based on their ability to modify
histones, also modify wild-type STAT3 bound to the SOCS3 promoter but not the S727A
mutant, showing that prior S727 phosphorylation is required for methylation

experiment.system: cells expressing wild-type or S727A STAT3
experiment.perturbation: IL6 stimulation; SET9/LSD1 activity; S727A mutation
experiment.measurement: K140 dimethylation of promoter-bound STAT3

text: Human autosomal-dominant gain-of-function STAT1 mutations that predispose to severe disseminated fungal infections affect residues far apart in the linear sequence but clustering near R31 in three dimensions; the mutations decrease the ability of R31 to be methylated, increasing binding of PIAS1 to STAT1.

quotes.quote:
Elizabeth
Sampaio and colleagues (personal communication) have analyzed human autosomal-
dominant gain-of-function STAT1 mutations that predispose to severe disseminated fungal
infections. The mutated amino acid residues are far apart in the linear sequence of STAT1
but cluster near R31 in the three-dimensional structure. The mutations decrease the ability of
R31 to be methylated, thus increasing the binding to STAT1 of PIAS1

experiment.system: human patient-derived gain-of-function STAT1 mutants
experiment.perturbation: observational analysis of naturally occurring STAT1 mutations
experiment.measurement: structural clustering of residues, R31 methylation, PIAS1 binding

text: SUMOylation of STAT1 on K703 by PIAS1 inhibits its activation and inhibits formation of STAT1 nuclear paracrystalline arrays, making tyrosine-phosphorylated STAT1 more susceptible to inactivation by nuclear phosphatases; tyrosine-phosphorylated STATs within such arrays are protected from inactivating nuclear phosphatases, prolonging activation.

quotes.quote:
SUMOylation of STAT1
on K703 by PIAS1 inhibits its activation (Ungureanu et al., 2005) and also inhibits the
formation of STAT1 nuclear paracrystalline arrays, which makes tyrosine-phosphorylated
STAT1 more susceptible to inactivation by nuclear phosphatases (Droescher et al., 2011).

Tyrosine-phosphorylated STATs in these
