arrays are protected from inactivating nuclear phosphatases, thus prolonging their activation.

experiment.system: cells expressing STAT1 and PIAS1
experiment.perturbation: PIAS1-mediated SUMOylation of STAT1 K703
experiment.measurement: STAT1 activation, paracrystalline array formation, susceptibility to nuclear phosphatases

text: Acetylation of STAT3 on K685 by p300 was reported as essential for cytokine-stimulated function — work the authors note has been criticized — while later reports show K685 acetylation is important for tyrosine-phosphorylation-independent STAT3 functions: activation via nuclear translocation of CD44, downregulation of STAT3 inhibition of gluconeogenesis, and STAT3-dependent effects of IL-22 in keratinocytes.

quotes.quote:
Although Yuan et al. (2005) indicated that the reversible acetylation of STAT3 on K685 by
the acetyltransferase p300 was essential for its cytokine-stimulated function, this work has
been criticized (O'Shea et al., 2005). Several recent reports have shown that acetylation of
K685 is important for functions of STAT3 that are independent of tyrosine phosphorylation,
namely for the activation of STAT3 mediated by nuclear translocation of CD44 (Lee et al.,

2009), for downregulating the ability of STAT3 to inhibit gluconeogenesis (Nie et al., 2009),
and for the STAT3-dependent effects of IL-22 in keratinocytes (Sestito et al., 2011).

verdict_note: Claim text and quotes match the paper, but the experiment 'measurement' field lists dimerization as an assayed output; the excerpt says nothing about STAT3 dimerization in connection with K685 acetylation.

experiment.system: cultured cells including keratinocytes and hepatic gluconeogenesis models
experiment.perturbation: p300-mediated acetylation / K685 mutation; cytokine (IL-22) stimulation
experiment.measurement: STAT3 function, dimerization, and target gene/metabolic outputs

text: The STAT1 gene responds to IFNs and the STAT3 gene responds to IL-6 through GAS or ISRE elements in their promoters, giving large increases in protein concentration; while tyrosine-phosphorylation-driven responses are downregulated rapidly, responses to the increased unphosphorylated STATs persist for many days, and the STAT1 and STAT3 responses are distinct, regulating completely different gene sets.

quotes.quote:
the STAT1 gene responds to IFNs and the STAT3 gene responds to
IL-6 (and related cytokines) through conventional GAS or ISRE elements in the respective
promoters, leading to large increases in the concentrations of each protein after cytokine
treatment. Although the initial responses to IFNs and IL-6 that are due to tyrosine
phosphorylation are downregulated rapidly, through a variety of mechanisms but especially
through the activities of the SOCS proteins, the responses to increased concentrations of U-
STATs persist for many days. The STAT1 and STAT3 responses are distinct: the STAT1
gene does not respond to IL-6 and the STAT3 gene does not respond to IFNs, and
completely different sets of genes are regulated to the two different U-STATs.

experiment.system: cultured cells treated with cytokines
experiment.perturbation: IFN or IL-6 treatment
experiment.measurement: STAT1/STAT3 protein concentrations and duration/identity of gene expression responses

text: Genes regulated by U-STAT3 are distinct from those induced by tyrosine-phosphorylated STAT3 and include MRAS and MET with described roles in oncogenesis; some U-STAT3 target genes are regulated through a complex with NF-κB, in which NF-κB provides the DNA-binding and transactivation domains and STAT3 is responsible for nuclear translocation.

quotes.quote:
The genes
regulated by U-STAT3 are also distinct from those induced by tyrosine-phosphorylated
STAT3, and several of them, such as MRAS and MET, have well-described roles in
oncogenesis, thus potentially contributing to the major role of STAT3 in cancer (Yang et al.,
2005). Some genes are regulated by U-STAT3 through a complex transcription factor
formed in combination with NF-κB, in which NF-κB provides the DNA-binding and
transactivation domains and STAT3 is responsible for nuclear translocation (Yang et al.,
2007).

experiment.system: cells accumulating unphosphorylated STAT3 in response to IL-6
experiment.perturbation: comparison of U-STAT3- versus tyrosine-phosphorylated STAT3-driven expression; STAT3/NF-κB complex formation
experiment.measurement: target gene expression and nuclear translocation

text: U-STAT1 prolongs expression of a subset of IFN-induced genes in combination with U-STAT2 and IRF9; three forms of ISGF3 are described — YP2-ISGF3 with both STAT1 and STAT2 tyrosine phosphorylated in response to type I IFNs, YP1-ISGF3 with only STAT1 phosphorylated in response to IFN-γ, and U-ISGF3 formed when the concentrations of the three constituent proteins increase — with U-ISGF3-induced antiviral proteins prolonging resistance to virus infection for many days and mediating DNA damage resistance in cancers overexpressing U-ISGF3.

quotes.quote:
U-STAT1 prolongs the expression of a subset of IFN-induced genes (Cheon and
Stark, 2009), in combination with U-STAT2 and IRF9, the other two components of ISGF3

Thus, there are three
forms of ISGF3: YP2-ISGF3 is formed when both STAT1 and STAT2 are tyrosine
phosphorylated in response to type I IFNs; YP1-ISGF3 is formed when only STAT1 is
tyrosine phosphorylated in response to IFN-γ (Morrow et al., 2011); and U-ISGF3 is formed
when the concentrations of the three constituent proteins are increased in response to IFNs

their continued expression,
long after the initial response to IFN has been downregulated, serves to prolong resistance to
virus infection for many days. Some of the U-ISGF3-induced proteins are also able to
mediate resistance to DNA damage in the many cancers in which U-ISGF3 is overexpressed

experiment.system: IFN-treated cells and cancers overexpressing U-ISGF3
experiment.perturbation: IFN treatment increasing STAT1, STAT2 and IRF9 concentrations
experiment.measurement: ISG expression duration, antiviral resistance, DNA damage resistance

text: Angiotensin II-dependent signaling induces increased expression of U-STAT3 through an unknown mechanism, contributing to angiotensin II-induced cardiac hypertrophy, and U-STAT2 is constitutively bound to many IFN-activated promoters before IFN treatment, contributing to their basal regulation.

quotes.quote:
Yue et
al. (2010) show that angiotensin II-dependent signaling induces increased expression of U-
STAT3 through an unknown mechanism, contributing to angiotensin II-induced cardiac
hypertrophy, and Testoni et al. (2011) show that U-STAT2 is constitutively bound to many
IFN-activated promoters before IFN treatment, contributing to their basal regulation.

experiment.system: cardiac cells/tissue and IFN-responsive cells
experiment.perturbation: angiotensin II signaling; observational chromatin binding before IFN treatment
experiment.measurement: U-STAT3 expression and cardiac hypertrophy; U-STAT2 promoter occupancy and basal gene regulation

text: STAT3 has roles outside the nucleus: mitochondrial STAT3 has been reported to support RAS-dependent oncogenic transformation, to participate in cellular respiration, and to protect against stress-induced changes in the electron transport chain that generate reactive oxygen species.

quotes.quote:
important roles for STAT3 outside
the nucleus, including in mitochondria, where STAT3 has been reported to support RAS-
dependent oncogenic transformation (Gough et al., 2009), and to participate in cellular
respiration (Wegrzyn et al., 2009). More recently, Szczepanek et al. (2011) have shown that
mitochondrial STAT3 protects against stress-induced changes in the electron transport chain
that result in the generation of reactive oxygen species.

experiment.system: cells and mitochondria containing STAT3
experiment.perturbation: mitochondrial targeting/manipulation of STAT3; stress to the electron transport chain
experiment.measurement: oncogenic transformation, cellular respiration, reactive oxygen species generation

text: Both U-STAT5A and U-STAT5B are associated with the Golgi apparatus and rough endoplasmic reticulum in vascular cells, with dramatic effects on the stability of these organelles after STAT5 knock-down.

quotes.quote:
Lee et al. (2012) have shown that both U-STAT5A and U-STAT5B are associated with the
Golgi apparatus and rough endoplasmic reticulum in vascular cells, with dramatic effects on
the stability of these organelles after STAT5 knock-down.

experiment.system: vascular cells
experiment.perturbation: STAT5 knock-down
experiment.measurement: localization of U-STAT5A/B and stability of Golgi and rough ER

text: In human cells, chromatin carrying the entire MHC locus loops out in response to IFN-γ treatment, and this phenomenon depends upon tyrosine phosphorylation of STAT1.

quotes.quote:
The work of Christova et al. (2007) in human cells reveals that
chromatin carrying the entire major histocompatibility complex (MHC) locus loops out in
response to treatment with IFN-γ and that this phenomenon is dependent upon the tyrosine
phosphorylation of STAT1.

experiment.system: human cells
experiment.perturbation: IFN-γ treatment; dependence on STAT1 tyrosine phosphorylation
experiment.measurement: higher-order chromatin looping of the MHC locus

text: STAT5 tetramers formed in response to IL-7 bind the Igκ intronic enhancer and recruit the histone lysine methyl transferase EZH2, which trimethylates H3K27, creating a repressive mark that blocks Igκ expression.

quotes.quote:
STAT5 tetramers, formed in response to IL-7, bind to the Igκ intronic
enhancer, recruiting the histone lysine methyl transferase EZH2, which in turn trime-thylates
H3K27, creating a repressive mark that blocks Igκ expression (Mandal et al., 2011).

experiment.system: lymphocytes at the Igκ locus
experiment.perturbation: IL-7 stimulation driving STAT5 tetramer formation
experiment.measurement: enhancer binding, EZH2 recruitment, H3K27 trimethylation, Igκ expression

text: Ferroptosis is defined as a form of regulated cell death caused by lethal, iron-dependent lipid peroxidation, and cell death occurring exclusively by ferroptosis can be suppressed by iron chelators, lipophilic antioxidants, inhibitors of lipid peroxidation, and depletion of polyunsaturated fatty acids, while correlating with accumulation of lipid peroxidation markers.

quotes.quote:
Ferroptosis describes a form of regulated cell death that occurs as a consequence of lethal 
lipid peroxidation. Cell death occurring exclusively by ferroptosis can be suppressed by iron 
chelators, lipophilic antioxidants, inhibitors of lipid peroxidation, and depletion of 
polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs), and correlates with the accumulation of markers of 
lipid peroxidation.

experiment.system: mammalian cells undergoing ferroptosis (as reviewed)
experiment.perturbation: pharmacological/genetic suppression with iron chelators, lipophilic antioxidants, lipid peroxidation inhibitors, or PUFA depletion
experiment.measurement: cell death rescue and lipid peroxidation markers

text: Erastin inhibits cystine import, depleting glutathione and inactivating GPX4, and inactivation of GPX4 either by GSH depletion with erastin or by the direct inhibitor (1S,3R)-RSL3 results in overwhelming lipid peroxidation that causes cell death.

quotes.quote:
the form of cell 
death induced by the small molecule erastin, which inhibits the import of cystine, leading to 
glutathione depletion and inactivation of the phospholipid peroxidase glutathione peroxidase 
4 (GPX4)

Inactivation of 
GPX4 through depletion of GSH with erastin, or with the direct GPX4 inhibitor (1S,3R)-
RSL3 (hereafter referred to as RSL3), ultimately results in overwhelming lipid peroxidation 
that causes cell death

experiment.system: cultured mammalian cancer cells
experiment.perturbation: treatment with erastin or (1S,3R)-RSL3
experiment.measurement: GSH levels, GPX4 activity, lipid peroxidation, cell death

text: Human fibroblasts cultured in cystine-free medium die due to glutathione depletion, and this death is prevented by the lipophilic antioxidant alpha-tocopherol or by iron chelators such as deferoxamine.

quotes.quote:
human fibroblasts cultured in cystine-free medium die due to glutathione depletion, and this 
death is prevented by the lipophilic antioxidant α-tocopherol (Bannai et al., 1977). In 
addition, iron chelators, such as deferoxamine, prevent this cell death (Murphy et al., 1989).

experiment.system: cultured human fibroblasts
experiment.perturbation: cystine-free medium, with or without α-tocopherol or deferoxamine
experiment.measurement: cell death and glutathione levels

text: A genome-wide siRNA screen for suppressors of erastin-induced ferroptosis showed that knockdown of cysteinyl-tRNA synthetase (CARS) upregulates the transsulfuration pathway and confers resistance to erastin-induced ferroptosis, detectable by cystathionine beta synthase (CBS) mRNA abundance.

quotes.quote:
A genome-wide short interfering RNA (siRNA) screen for suppressors of erastin-induced 
ferroptosis revealed that knockdown of cysteinyl-tRNA synthetase (CARS) results in 
upregulation of the transsulfuration pathway and resistance to erastin-induced ferroptosis

which can be detected by measuring the 
abundance of cystathionine beta synthase (CBS) mRNA

experiment.system: human cancer cells
experiment.perturbation: genome-wide siRNA knockdown, erastin treatment
experiment.measurement: ferroptosis suppression; CBS mRNA abundance

text: System xc- exchanges glutamate for cystine in a 1:1 ratio, so high extracellular glutamate concentrations inhibit system xc- and induce ferroptosis; system xc- knockout mice are protected from neurotoxic insults due to decreased extracellular brain glutamate.

quotes.quote:
Glutamate is exchanged for cystine in a 1:1 ratio by system xc-, so glutamate levels impact 
system xc- function. Indeed, high extracellular concentrations of glutamate inhibit system xc- 
and induce ferroptosis

system xc- knockout 
mice are protected from neurotoxic insults due to decreased extracellular brain glutamate 
levels

experiment.system: cultured cells and system xc- knockout mice
experiment.perturbation: elevated extracellular glutamate; genetic knockout of system xc-
experiment.measurement: ferroptotic cell death; protection from neurotoxic insults; extracellular glutamate levels

text: Glutaminolysis is required for ferroptosis: in the absence of glutamine or when glutaminolysis is inhibited, cystine starvation and blockage of cystine import fail to induce ROS accumulation, lipid peroxidation, and ferroptosis, and only GLS2 (not GLS1) is required for ferroptosis.

quotes.quote:
In the 
absence of glutamine, or when glutaminolysis is inhibited, cystine starvation and blockage 
of cystine import fail to induce the accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), lipid 
peroxidation, and ferroptosis.

Although these enzymes are structurally and enzymatically similar, only 
GLS2 is required for ferroptosis (Gao et al., 2015).

experiment.system: cultured cells
experiment.perturbation: glutamine withdrawal or glutaminolysis inhibition; GLS1 vs GLS2 loss; cystine starvation
experiment.measurement: ROS accumulation, lipid peroxidation, ferroptotic death

text: Lipidomic studies indicate that phosphatidylethanolamines containing arachidonic acid (C20:4) or adrenic acid (C22:4) are the key phospholipids that undergo oxidation and drive ferroptotic death, and hydroperoxy derivatives of PUFA-PEs cause ferroptotic death when added to cells with inactivated GPX4.

quotes.quote:
Lipidomic studies suggest that phosphatidylethanolamines (PEs) containing 
arachidonic acid (C20:4) or its elongation product, adrenic acid (C22:4), are key 
phospholipids that undergo oxidation and drive cells towards ferroptotic death

Hydroperoxy derivatives of PUFA-PEs also cause ferroptotic death when added to 
cells with inactivated GPX4

experiment.system: cultured cells undergoing ferroptosis
experiment.perturbation: GPX4 inactivation; addition of hydroperoxy PUFA-PE derivatives
experiment.measurement: LC-MS lipidomic profiling of oxidized phospholipids; cell death

text: Loss of ACSL4 or LPCAT3 depletes substrates for lipid peroxidation and increases resistance to ferroptosis, whereas supplementation of cells with arachidonic acid or other PUFAs sensitizes them to ferroptosis.

quotes.quote:
Loss of these gene products depletes 
the substrates for lipid peroxidation and increases resistance to ferroptosis (Dixon et al., 
2015; Doll et al., 2017; Kagan et al., 2017; Yuan et al., 2016b). Conversely, cells that are 
supplemented with arachidonic acid or other PUFAs are sensitized to ferroptosis

experiment.system: cultured mammalian cells
experiment.perturbation: knockdown/knockout of ACSL4 or LPCAT3; PUFA supplementation
experiment.measurement: ferroptosis sensitivity

text: Genetic depletion of lipoxygenases protects against erastin-induced ferroptosis, supporting a contribution of LOXs to ferroptotic peroxidation.

quotes.quote:
genetic depletion of LOXs protects against erastin-induced ferroptosis (Yang et al., 2016), 
suggesting LOXs contribute to ferroptosis.

experiment.system: cultured cells
experiment.perturbation: genetic depletion of lipoxygenases; erastin treatment
experiment.measurement: ferroptotic cell death

text: A cell line selected for erastin resistance showed several-hundred-fold upregulation of AKR1C family genes, which encode aldoketoreductases that reduce reactive end-products of lipid peroxidation to unreactive compounds.

quotes.quote:
a cell line selected for erastin resistance showed several-hundred-fold 
upregulation of AKR1C family genes (Dixon et al., 2014), which encode aldoketoreductases 
that, among other functions, reduce reactive end-products of lipid peroxidation to unreactive 
compounds

experiment.system: cultured cancer cell line selected for erastin resistance
experiment.perturbation: selection for erastin resistance
experiment.measurement: gene expression of AKR1C family genes

text: Iron handling controls ferroptosis: transferrin and transferrin receptor are required for ferroptosis, silencing of IREB2 decreases ferroptosis sensitivity, and ferritinophagy via the cargo receptor NCOA4 enhances ferroptosis sensitivity by releasing free iron.

quotes.quote:
Transferrin 
and transferrin receptor, which import iron from the extracellular environment, are required 
for ferroptosis (Gao et al., 2015; Yang and Stockwell, 2008), while silencing of the iron 
metabolism master regulator IREB2 decreases sensitivity to ferroptosis

Selective autophagy of ferritin, referred to 
as ferritinophagy, enhances ferroptosis sensitivity, by controlling iron availability

Ferritin is recognized by 
the specific cargo receptor NCOA4, which recruits ferritin to autophagosomes for lysosomal 
degradation and the release of free iron

experiment.system: cultured mammalian cells
experiment.perturbation: depletion of transferrin/transferrin receptor, IREB2 silencing, modulation of ferritinophagy/NCOA4
experiment.measurement: ferroptosis sensitivity and iron availability

text: CoQ10 acts as an endogenous membrane antioxidant inhibitor of ferroptosis; FIN56 depletes CoQ10 by modulating squalene synthase activity, and statins inhibiting HMG CoA reductase sensitize cells to ferroptosis, presumably by depleting CoQ10 and possibly by inhibiting TRIT1-dependent tRNA isopentenylation required for GPX4 biosynthesis.

quotes.quote:
CoQ10 moonlights as an 
endogenous inhibitor of ferroptosis by serving an antioxidant function in membranes 
(Shimada et al., 2016b). The ferroptosis-inducing compound FIN56 depletes CoQ10 by 
modulating squalene synthase activity (SQS), which in part drives accumulation of lethal 
lipid peroxidation
Statin drugs, which inhibit HMG CoA reductase,

the rate-limiting enzyme of the mevalonate pathway, sensitize cells to ferroptosis, 
presumably by depleting CoQ10, and possibly by also inhibiting downstream tRNA 
isopentenylation via TRIT1, which is required for the biosynthesis of GPX4

experiment.system: cultured mammalian cells
experiment.perturbation: FIN56 treatment, statin treatment, mevalonate pathway inhibition
experiment.measurement: CoQ10 abundance, lipid peroxidation, ferroptosis sensitivity

text: NADPH levels are a biomarker of ferroptosis sensitivity across many cancer cell lines, and selenium supplementation promotes ferroptosis resistance while selenium depletion promotes sensitivity, presumably by modulating GPX4 abundance and activity.

quotes.quote:
Indeed, NADPH levels are 
a biomarker of ferroptosis sensitivity across many cancer cell lines (Shimada et al., 2016a).

selenium supplementation promotes ferroptosis resistance, 
while selenium depletion promotes ferroptosis sensitivity, presumably by modulating GPX4 
abundance and activity

experiment.system: panels of cancer cell lines
experiment.perturbation: observational profiling of NADPH; selenium supplementation or depletion
experiment.measurement: ferroptosis sensitivity

text: NRF2 promotes resistance to ferroptosis by controlling expression of AKR1C, MT-1G and other antioxidant genes, iron-signaling proteins including ferritin and ferroportin, pentose phosphate pathway enzymes, and glutathione synthesis genes SLC7A11, GCLC/GLCM and GSS.

quotes.quote:
The NRF2 transcription factor promotes resistance to ferroptosis (Sun et al., 2016b): NRF2 
controls the expression of AKR1C, the metal-binding protein MT-1G (Sun et al., 2016a), 
and other antioxidant genes, the expression of key proteins in iron signaling, including 
ferritin and ferroportin, and the expression of enzymes in the pentose phosphate pathway, 
which generate the bulk of cellular NADPH.

experiment.system: cancer cells (e.g., hepatocellular carcinoma cells)
experiment.perturbation: modulation of NRF2 pathway activity
experiment.measurement: target gene expression and ferroptosis sensitivity

text: Ferroptosis inhibitors such as ferrostatins and liproxstatins protect from ischemic injury in mouse models of liver, kidney, brain and heart injury, and are protective in models of degenerative brain disorders including Parkinson's, Huntington's and Alzheimer's diseases and traumatic and hemorrhagic brain injury.

quotes.quote:
Inhibitors of ferroptosis, such as ferrostatins and liproxstatins, protect from ischemic injury 
in mouse models in the liver, kidney, brain, and heart

These inhibitors are also protective in models of degenerative brain disorders, including 
Parkinson's, Huntington's, and Alzheimer's Diseases, as well as in other forms of 
neurodegeneration and traumatic and hemorrhagic brain injury

experiment.system: mouse models of ischemic organ injury and neurodegeneration
experiment.perturbation: administration of ferrostatins or liproxstatins
experiment.measurement: tissue injury/protection

text: Inducible deletion of gpx4 in adult mice causes hippocampal neuronal loss with astrogliosis, as seen in Alzheimer's disease, providing genetic evidence linking brain degeneration to ferroptosis.

quotes.quote:
inducible deletion of 
gpx4 in adult mice causes hippocampal neuronal loss with astrogliosis, as seen in AD (Yoo 
et al., 2012).

experiment.system: adult mice
experiment.perturbation: inducible genetic deletion of gpx4
experiment.measurement: hippocampal neuronal loss and astrogliosis

text: Agents that inhibit cystine uptake via system xc- (e.g., sulfasalazine) arrest tumor growth and can induce ferroptosis, and direct depletion of cystine from plasma with an engineered cyst(e)inase enzyme conjugate arrests tumor growth and triggers cell death.

quotes.quote:
Agents that inhibit 
cystine uptake via the cystine/glutamate antiporter (system xc-), such as sulfasalazine, arrest 
tumor growth and can induce ferroptosis in some circumstances

direct depletion of cystine from plasma using an 
engineered cystine-degrading enzyme conjugate (i.e., cyst(e)inase) arrests tumor growth and 
triggers cell death

experiment.system: tumor models and cancer cells
experiment.perturbation: sulfasalazine treatment; systemic cyst(e)inase-mediated cystine depletion
experiment.measurement: tumor growth and cell death

text: Cancer cell lines have highly varied sensitivity to ferroptosis in a large-scale characterization, with HT-1080 fibrosarcoma and Panc-1 pancreatic cancer cells showing robust ferroptotic responses; mouse embryonic fibroblasts are generally sensitive even when lacking BAX and BAK.

quotes.quote:
A large-scale characterization of ferroptosis sensitivity of cancer cell lines found that cancer 
cell lines have highly varied sensitivity to ferroptosis (Yang et al., 2014). Cell lines such as 
HT-1080 fibrosarcoma cells and Panc-1 pancreatic cancer cells have robust ferroptotic 
responses

mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) are generally sensitive to ferroptosis, even 
when lacking the apoptotic regulators BAX and BAK

experiment.system: panel of cancer cell lines and MEFs
experiment.perturbation: treatment with ferroptosis inducers; BAX/BAK deletion
experiment.measurement: ferroptotic cell death sensitivity

text: Arabidopsis seedlings exposed to 55 °C heat stress have been used as a model for ferroptotic-like cell death in plants.

quotes.quote:
Arabidopsis seedlings 
exposed to 55 °C heat stress have been used as a model for ferroptotic-like cell death in 
plants (Distefano et al., 2017).

experiment.system: Arabidopsis seedlings
experiment.perturbation: 55 °C heat stress
experiment.measurement: ferroptotic-like cell death

text: Four classes of ferroptosis inducers are currently in use: system xc- inhibitors (erastin and analogs, sulfasalazine, glutamate, sorafenib); GPX4 inhibitors such as RSL3 and ML162; FIN56, which depletes GPX4 protein and CoQ10; and FINO2, which indirectly inhibits GPX4 activity and stimulates lipid peroxidation.

quotes.quote:
There are four classes of ferroptosis inducers currently in use (Yang and Stockwell, 2016): 
(i) system xc- inhibitors (erastin and its analogs, sulfasalazine, glutamate, and sorafenib); (ii) 
GPX4 inhibitors, such as RSL3 and ML162; (iii) FIN56, which depletes GPX4 protein, and 
the lipophilic antioxidant CoQ10 (Shimada et al., 2016b); and (iv) FINO2, which indirectly 
inhibits GPX4 activity and stimulates lipid peroxidation

experiment.system: cultured cells used in ferroptosis studies
experiment.perturbation: treatment with compounds of each inducer class
experiment.measurement: induction of ferroptotic death; GPX4/CoQ10 status and lipid peroxidation

text: Selectively bis-allylic deuterated PUFAs suppress propagation of lipid peroxidation and suppress ferroptosis induced by RSL3 and erastin, although they are more effective against RSL3 than erastin.

quotes.quote:
Selectively 
bis-allylic deuterated PUFAs suppress propagation of lipid peroxidation and have been 
found to suppress ferroptosis induced by RSL3 and erastin, although they are more effective 
against the former than the latter

experiment.system: cultured cells
experiment.perturbation: supplementation with bis-allylic deuterated PUFAs; RSL3 or erastin treatment
experiment.measurement: lipid peroxidation and ferroptotic death

text: The necroptosis inhibitor necrostatin-1 has off-target activity that can suppress ferroptosis at high concentrations, unrelated to necroptosis, and many LOX inhibitors and the MEK inhibitor U0126 exhibit antioxidant activity that probably underlies their suppression of ferroptosis.

quotes.quote:
many LOX inhibitors and the MEK inhibitor U0126 exhibit 
antioxidant activity, which is probably the basis of their ability to suppress ferroptosis. In 
addition, the necroptosis inhibitor necrostatin-1 has off-target activity, which can suppress 
ferroptosis at high concentrations (Friedmann Angeli et al., 2014), but this is unrelated to 
necroptosis.

experiment.system: cultured cells undergoing ferroptosis
experiment.perturbation: treatment with necrostatin-1, LOX inhibitors, or U0126
experiment.measurement: suppression of ferroptosis; antioxidant/iron-chelating activity

text: Ferroptosis proceeds in the absence of key apoptotic effectors (BAX, BAK, caspases) and of key necroptosis components (MLKL, RIPK1, RIPK3), and both ferroptosis and necroptosis contribute to ischemic injury such that simultaneous prevention of both provides maximum benefit.

quotes.quote:
Both ferroptosis and necroptosis contribute to ischemic injury, such that prevention of 
ferroptosis and necroptosis at the same time provides maximum benefit (Linkermann et al., 
2014).

Ferroptosis proceeds even in the absence of key effectors of apoptosis, such as BAX, BAK 
and caspases. Likewise, ferroptosis proceeds in the absence of the key components of 
necroptosis, such as MLKL, RIPK1 and RIPK3.

experiment.system: cells and mouse ischemia-reperfusion models
experiment.perturbation: genetic loss of apoptotic or necroptotic effectors; combined ferroptosis and necroptosis inhibition
experiment.measurement: cell death and tissue injury

text: Cells dying by ferroptosis primarily exhibit shrunken and damaged mitochondria by electron microscopy with nuclei remaining intact, distinguishing ferroptosis morphologically from apoptosis, necroptosis, and pyroptosis.

quotes.quote:
Cells dying by ferroptosis 
primarily exhibit shrunken and damaged mitochondria by electron microscopy, with few 
other morphological changes evident prior to the point of cell death
in particular, nuclei remain intact during ferroptosis

experiment.system: cultured cells undergoing ferroptosis
experiment.perturbation: treatment with ferroptosis inducers
experiment.measurement: electron microscopy morphology

text: Among clinicopathological features of dementia consistent with ferroptosis, a large randomized control trial of patients with mild-moderate Alzheimer's disease showed that vitamin E, a low potency anti-ferroptotic agent, slowed cognitive decline by 19% / yr.

experiment.system: patients with mild-moderate Alzheimer's disease
experiment.perturbation: vitamin E treatment in a large randomized controlled trial
experiment.measurement: rate of cognitive/functional decline

numbers.quantity: slowing of cognitive decline with vitamin E

text: Long-term use of pioglitazone, a recently discovered ACSL4 inhibitor, abnegates the increased risk of dementia in non-insulin dependent diabetes patients.

quotes.quote:
Long-term use of pioglitazone, a recently discovered ACSL4 
inhibitor, abnegates the increased risk of dementia in non-insulin 
dependent diabetes patients

experiment.system: human non-insulin dependent diabetes patients (observational epidemiology)
experiment.perturbation: long-term pioglitazone medication use
experiment.measurement: incidence/risk of dementia

text: Treatment with the iron chelator deferiprone was reported to be beneficial in a randomized controlled trial for Parkinson's disease.

quotes.quote:
treatment with the iron chelator deferiprone was recently reported to be beneficial in a 
randomized controlled trial for PD (Devos et al., 2014)

experiment.system: patients with Parkinson's disease
experiment.perturbation: deferiprone iron chelation in a randomized controlled trial
experiment.measurement: clinical benefit

text: Membrane-attached phosphorylated LAT plus Grb2 and Sos1 formed submicron clusters within 1 minute on supported lipid bilayers; clustering required LAT tyrosine phosphorylation, and adding the phosphatase PTP1B (2 µM) dissolved the clusters.

quotes.quote:
Upon addition of Grb2 and Sos1, submicron-sized clusters formed within 1 minute and gradually 
grew in size. Cluster formation required tyrosine phosphorylation of LAT (fig. S1D). 
Furthermore, dephosphorylation of pLAT by high concentrations of the soluble protein tyrosine 
phosphatase 1B (PTP1B, 2 µM) caused the clusters to disassemble

experiment.system: purified His8-pLAT on Ni2+-containing supported lipid bilayers with Grb2 and Sos1
experiment.perturbation: addition of Grb2/Sos1; use of unphosphorylated LAT; addition of PTP1B (2 µM)
experiment.measurement: TIRF imaging of cluster formation/disassembly

text: Cluster formation in vitro required both Grb2 and Sos1; pLAT also clustered with Gads and SLP-76 but less efficiently, and clustering efficiency increased with addition of Nck.

quotes.quote:
pLAT, 
Grb2, and Sos1 all colocalized within clusters, and clusters did not form if either Grb2 or Sos1 
was omitted (fig. S1E, F). pLAT also clustered with Gads and SLP-76, two other components of 
LAT clusters in cells (6, 7), but less efficiently than with Grb2 and Sos1 (fig. S2A, B). Clustering 
efficiency, however, increased dramatically with the addition of Nck (fig. S2C)

experiment.system: pLAT on supported lipid bilayers with adaptor combinations
experiment.perturbation: omission of Grb2 or Sos1; substitution with Gads/SLP-76; addition of Nck
experiment.measurement: TIRF imaging of clustering and colocalization

text: pLAT clusters showed liquid-like behavior: fluctuating rounded edges on a seconds timescale, fusion events, FRAP recovery of pLAT, and slow single-molecule diffusion inside versus rapid diffusion outside clusters.

quotes.quote:
The rounded edges 
of clusters fluctuated (extending and retracting) on a time scale of seconds and clusters 
sometimes fused with one another (movie S2). pLAT molecules exchanged into and out of

clusters, as revealed by fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) (Fig. 1C). Single 
pLAT molecules diffused rapidly outside of clusters but slowly within them (fig. S3A-C).

experiment.system: reconstituted pLAT/Grb2/Sos1 clusters on planar lipid bilayers
experiment.perturbation: observational (photobleaching pulse for FRAP)
experiment.measurement: TIRF time-lapse, FRAP recovery, single-molecule tracking/MSD

text: Both SH3 domains of Grb2 were required for cluster formation, and clustering first increased then decreased with increasing pLAT membrane density.

quotes.quote:
Both SH3 domains of Grb2 were required for cluster formation, indicating a role of protein 
cross-bridging by this adaptor protein (Fig. 1D and fig. S4A). Clustering initially increased with 
increasing pLAT density but then decreased at higher pLAT densities on the membrane (fig. 
S4B), consistent with a theoretical multivalent interaction model (19).

experiment.system: pLAT-Alexa488 on supported lipid bilayers with Sos1
experiment.perturbation: wild-type Grb2 vs Grb2∆SH3; titration of pLAT membrane density
experiment.measurement: TIRF imaging of cluster formation and cluster fluorescence intensity

text: In vitro clustering depended on LAT phospho-tyrosine valency: it progressively decreased upon mutating one, two, or all three Grb2-binding tyrosines and was enhanced by doubling the number of tyrosines.

quotes.quote:
Clustering in vitro progressively 
decreased by mutating one, two, or all three tyrosines and was enhanced by doubling the number 
of tyrosines (Fig. 1E and fig. S5).

experiment.system: pLAT valency mutants (2xYYY, YYY, FYY, YFY, YYF, FFY, FFF) at ~300 molecules/µm2 on bilayers with Grb2 and Sos1
experiment.perturbation: tyrosine-to-phenylalanine mutation or tyrosine duplication; Grb2/Sos1 concentration titration
experiment.measurement: TIRF imaging with clustering quantified as fractional intensity

text: FRAP showed molecules exchange into and out of LAT clusters faster in T cells than in vitro (t1/2 of 12 sec versus 76 sec).

quotes.quote:
FRAP revealed that molecules exchange into and out of 
clusters in cells faster than in vitro (t1/2 of 12 sec versus 76 sec), possibly due to different cluster 
size (see Supplementary Text) or membrane fluidity.

experiment.system: LAT-mCitrine clusters in OKT3-activated Jurkat T cells versus reconstituted pLAT clusters on bilayers
experiment.perturbation: photobleaching pulse
experiment.measurement: FRAP fluorescence recovery half-time

text: In LAT-deficient Jurkat cells expressing LAT tyrosine mutants, a minimum of two Grb2 binding sites was required for robust cluster formation, clustering degree increased with phospho-tyrosine number, and clustering correlated with MAPK(ERK) activation.

quotes.quote:
we 
expressed LAT tyrosine mutants with zero, one, two, three, or six Grb2 binding sites in a LAT-
deficient Jurkat T cell line. A minimum of two Grb2 binding sites was required for robust cluster 
formation and the degree of clustering increased with increasing number of phospho-tyrosine 
sites (Fig. 2B). The degree of clustering correlated with activation of MAPK(ERK) (Fig. 2C)

experiment.system: LAT-deficient Jurkat line (Jcam2.5) stably expressing LAT valency variants
experiment.perturbation: activation by plate-presented anti-CD3 antibody OKT3
experiment.measurement: TIRF quantification of LAT clustering and percentage of pERK-positive cells by immunostaining

text: In a reconstitution containing CD3ζ, Lck, CD45 and ZAP70, adding ATP triggered ZAP70 membrane recruitment and LAT clustering, with ZAP70 enriched in clusters and CD45 excluded; CD45 exclusion was recapitulated in the simpler pLAT/Grb2/Sos1 system.

quotes.quote:
After ATP 
was added to initiate Lck phosphorylation of CD3ζ, ZAP70 was recruited to the membrane and 
LAT clustered (Fig. 3B; fig. S6A). ZAP70 was enriched in the clusters, as observed in T cells 
(7), whereas CD45 was excluded (Fig. 3B). The exclusion of CD45 was recapitulated in a 
simpler system in which clusters were formed by pLAT, Grb2, and Sos1 (Fig. 3C).

experiment.system: supported lipid bilayer with His-tagged CD45, Lck, CD3ζ, LAT plus soluble ZAP70, Grb2, Sos1, Gads, SLP-76
experiment.perturbation: addition of 0.5 mM ATP-Mg to trigger the phosphorylation cascade
experiment.measurement: TIRF time courses of ZAP70 recruitment, CD45 exclusion, LAT clustering

text: Protein partitioning into LAT clusters tracked with charge — positive charge favored inclusion and negative charge exclusion — and CD45-mediated dephosphorylation of pLAT was reduced in clustered compared with unclustered conditions.

quotes.quote:
Assays with a series of 
differentially charged proteins revealed that, in general, positive charge favors inclusion into and 
negative charge favors exclusion from LAT clusters (fig. S7 and Supplementary Text). 
Consistent with limited access of CD45 to pLAT in the cluster center, CD45-mediated 
dephosphorylation of pLAT was reduced compared to that in unclustered conditions (Fig. 3D).

experiment.system: membrane-bound pLAT clusters on bilayers with charge-variant SNAP/GFP proteins; pLAT with Grb2 alone (unclustered) or Grb2+Sos1 (clustered)
experiment.perturbation: varying protein charge; addition of His10-CD45 with reaction stopped after 5 min
experiment.measurement: TIRF partitioning ratios; Western blot of LAT pY191 normalized to total LAT

text: A full reconstitution from CD3ζ phosphorylation to actin assembly showed sequential ZAP70 recruitment, LAT clustering, and actin polymerization from LAT clusters; clusters became rod-like aligned with actin bundles and reverted to round after Latrunculin A depolymerization.

quotes.quote:
When ATP was added to initiate TCR phosphorylation, ZAP70 was recruited 
to the membrane, followed by LAT clustering and then actin polymerization from the LAT 
clusters (Fig. 4B,C and fig. S8). Later, when actin bundles formed, LAT clusters became rod-like 
and aligned with actin bundles (Fig. 4D and movie S4,5). This shape change is reversible, as 
clusters became round following depolymerization of F-actin by Latrunculin A (fig. S9C).

experiment.system: supported bilayer with His-tagged Lck, CD3ζ, LAT plus soluble ZAP70, Gads, SLP-76, Nck, N-WASp, Arp2/3, and rhodamine-actin
experiment.perturbation: addition of ATP; addition of Latrunculin A
experiment.measurement: TIRF time courses of ZAP70 fluorescence, LAT clustering variance, actin fluorescence and cluster shape

text: Membrane-attached Nck drove actin assembly in a density-dependent manner, and at a low Nck density (150 molecules/µm2) clustering Nck with pLAT, Gads and pSLP-76 enhanced total actin assembly on the membrane by 6-fold.

quotes.quote:
Increasing the density of 
Nck on the membrane resulted in a dose-dependent increase in assembly of actin (fig. S10). 
Using a density of Nck (150 molecules/µm2) at which little actin polymerized, we tested whether 
clustering of Nck by pLAT, Gads, and pSLP-76 affected actin assembly. Clustering of Nck 
enhanced total actin assembly on the membrane by 6-fold (Fig. 4E).

experiment.system: His10-Nck attached to Ni-modified planar bilayer with soluble N-WASp, Arp2/3 complex and rhodamine-actin
experiment.perturbation: titrating Nck membrane density; clustering Nck by adding pLAT/Gads/pSLP-76 at fixed Nck density of 150 molecules/µm2
experiment.measurement: TIRF mean actin fluorescence on membrane and Nck clustering variance

numbers.quantity: fold enhancement of actin assembly by Nck clustering

text: LAT clusters formed with the minimal components (LAT, Grb2, Sos1) had size 0.39 + 0.02 µm2, roundness 0.79 + 0.11, and half recovery time 76 + 12 sec, whereas full TCR-LAT-actin pathway clusters were 0.82 + 0.03 µm2, roundness 0.51 + 0.21, and 98 + 37 sec.

quotes.quote:
Minimal components  
(LAT, Grb2, and Sos1) 
0.39 + 0.02 µm2 
(N=277) 
0.79 + 0.11 
(N=277) 
76 + 12 sec  
(N=7) 
Full pathway  
(TCR-LAT-actin) 
0.82 + 0.03 µm2 
(N=301) 
0.51 + 0.21 
(N=301) 
98 + 37 sec  
(N=10)

experiment.system: reconstituted LAT clusters on supported lipid bilayers
experiment.perturbation: minimal (LAT/Grb2/Sos1) versus full TCR-LAT-actin reconstitution
experiment.measurement: cluster size, roundness, and FRAP half recovery time

text: Grb2 cross-bridging was required to maintain clusters: pLAT clusters formed with a PreScission-cleavable Grb2 disassembled upon treatment with PreScission protease.

quotes.quote:
MIDDLE: TIRF imaging of pLAT-Alexa488 (300 
molecules/um2) incubated with Grb2-Cle (0.5 µM) and Sos1 (0.25 µM). Clusters were 
disassembled when treated with PreScission protease (50 nM).

experiment.system: pLAT-Alexa488 on bilayers clustered with cleavable Grb2 (Grb2-Cle) and Sos1
experiment.perturbation: addition of PreScission protease (50 nM) to cleave Grb2 between SH2 and C-terminal SH3
experiment.measurement: TIRF imaging of cluster disassembly and SDS-PAGE of cleavage over 30 min

text: LAT microclusters on the plasma membrane of activated Jurkat T cells fused with one another, as observed on OKT3/ICAM-1-functionalized supported bilayers.

quotes.quote:
(D) Fusion of LAT clusters on the plasma membrane of Jurkat T cells. 
Jurkat T cells expressing LAT-mCherry were plated on supported lipid bilayer 
functionalized with anti-CD3 antibody OKT3 and adhesive molecule ICAM-1.

experiment.system: Jurkat T cells expressing LAT-mCherry on OKT3/ICAM-1 supported lipid bilayers
experiment.perturbation: T cell activation by mobile anti-CD3 antibody OKT3
experiment.measurement: TIRF imaging of microcluster mobility and fusion

text: p100 processing is induced via phosphorylation at C-terminal serine residues (serines 866 and 870), which triggers p100 ubiquitylation via recruitment of the E3 ubiquitin ligase βTrCP; NIK induces p100 phosphorylation via activation of IKKα.

quotes.quote:
The 
processing of p100 is induced via its phosphorylation at specific C-terminal serine residues 
(serines 866 and 870), which triggers p100 ubiquitylation via recruitment of the E3 ubiquitin 
ligase βTrCP10–12. A central signalling component of the non-canonical NF-κB pathway is 
NF-κB-inducing kinase (NIK; also known as MAP3K14), which induces p100 
phosphorylation via the activation of the kinase IKKα10,13.

experiment.system: mammalian cells expressing NF-κB2 p100 (reviewed biochemical/genetic studies)
experiment.perturbation: NIK/IKKα activation and mutation of p100 C-terminal serines; βTrCP manipulation
experiment.measurement: p100 phosphorylation, ubiquitylation and processing to p52

text: LTβR was identified as a non-canonical NF-κB stimulating receptor: LTβR overexpression stimulates NIK-dependent p100 processing, and crosslinking LTβR with an agonistic antibody stimulates p100 processing in a NIK- and IKKα-dependent manner.

quotes.quote:
Overexpression of LTβR stimulates NIK-dependent p100 processing10, 
and crosslinking of LTβR with an agonistic antibody stimulates p100 processing in a NIK- 
and IKKα-dependent manner29.

experiment.system: cells expressing LTβR; NIK- and IKKα-deficient cells
experiment.perturbation: LTβR overexpression or agonistic antibody crosslinking
experiment.measurement: p100 processing

text: MCSF-induced macrophage differentiation from bone marrow cells is associated with induction of p100 processing, and MCSFR associates with TRAF2 and TRAF3.

quotes.quote:
MCSF-induced macrophage differentiation from bone 
marrow cells is associated with the induction of p100 processing, and like TNFRs, MCSFR 
is capable of associating with TRAF2 and TRAF3 (REF 40).

experiment.system: mouse bone marrow cells differentiating into macrophages
experiment.perturbation: MCSF stimulation
experiment.measurement: p100 processing; MCSFR–TRAF2/TRAF3 association

text: In T cells, TCR plus CD28 ligation stimulates p100 processing and nuclear translocation of p52 and RELB, dependent on NIK and on the C-terminal phosphorylation site of p100.

quotes.quote:
In T cells, ligation of the TCR 
and the co-stimulatory receptor CD28 stimulates p100 processing and nuclear translocation 
of p52 and RELB, which is dependent on NIK and the presence of the C-terminal 
phosphorylation site of p100 (REF 25).

experiment.system: mouse T cells, including NIK-deficient and p100 phosphorylation-site mutant cells
experiment.perturbation: TCR and CD28 ligation
experiment.measurement: p100 processing and nuclear translocation of p52 and RELB

text: TRAF3 was identified in a yeast two-hybrid screen as a NIK-binding negative regulator: TRAF3 knockdown or knockout results in NIK stabilization sufficient to induce p100 processing, and a NIK mutant lacking the TRAF3-binding motif escapes degradation and becomes a 'super-stimulator' of the pathway.

quotes.quote:
A yeast two-hybrid screen for NIK-binding proteins identified TRAF3 as a central negative 
regulator of the non-canonical NF-κB pathway53.

TRAF3 knockdown or knockout results in NIK stabilization, which is sufficient for the 
induction of p100 processing53,54. Moreover, a NIK mutant lacking the TRAF3-binding 
motif was shown to escape from TRAF3-mediated degradation and to turn into a ‘super-
stimulator’ of the non-canonical NF-κB pathway53,55.

experiment.system: mammalian cells and TRAF3-deficient mice
experiment.perturbation: TRAF3 knockdown/knockout; expression of NIK mutant lacking TRAF3-binding motif
experiment.measurement: NIK protein levels and p100 processing

text: Deletion of TRAF2 or TRAF3, or simultaneous deletion of cIAP, causes NIK accumulation and p100 processing; small-molecule IAP antagonists that degrade cIAP likewise induce NIK accumulation and p100 processing.

quotes.quote:
Thus, the deletion of either TRAF2 or TRAF3 or a simultaneous deletion of 
cIAP causes NIK accumulation and p100 processing53,54,60–63. Similarly, small-molecule 
antagonists of IAPs, which induce the degradation of cIAP, induce NIK accumulation and 
p100 processing64,65.

experiment.system: cells/mice deficient in TRAF2, TRAF3 or cIAP1/2
experiment.perturbation: genetic deletion or IAP antagonist treatment
experiment.measurement: NIK accumulation and p100 processing

text: NLRP12 interacts with NIK and promotes ubiquitin-dependent NIK degradation in myeloid cells, and also binds TRAF3; NLRP12 deficiency reduces the basal level of TRAF3 in DCs.

quotes.quote:
NLRP12; also known as Monarch 1) physically interacts with NIK and promotes 
ubiquitin-dependent NIK degradation in myeloid cells66,67. NLRP12 also binds to TRAF3 
and maintains the steady level of TRAF3 stability, and NLRP12 deficiency causes a 
reduction in the basal level of TRAF3, as shown in DCs66.

experiment.system: myeloid cells and dendritic cells from NLRP12-deficient mice
experiment.perturbation: NLRP12 deficiency
experiment.measurement: NIK degradation; basal TRAF3 protein levels

text: OTUD7B interacts with TRAF3 in response to CD40 and LTβR signals and inhibits signal-induced TRAF3 degradation by deconjugating K48-linked polyubiquitin chains from TRAF3; its N-terminal ubiquitin-association domain is required for inducible TRAF3 binding.

quotes.quote:
OTUD7B (also known as Cezanne) is a deubiquitinase that interacts with TRAF3 
in response to CD40 and LTβR signals and inhibits signal-induced TRAF3 degradation by 
deconjugating K48-linked polyubiquitin chains from TRAF3 (REF. 68)

The N-
terminal ubiquitin-association domain of OTUD7B is required for its inducible binding to 
TRAF3

experiment.system: cells stimulated through CD40 or LTβR
experiment.perturbation: CD40/LTβR stimulation; OTUD7B domain deletion
experiment.measurement: TRAF3 K48 polyubiquitylation and degradation; OTUD7B–TRAF3 binding

text: IKKα phosphorylates NIK at several C-terminal serine residues to destabilize it as negative feedback, and the IKK-related kinase TBK1 similarly phosphorylates NIK to promote its degradation in B cells responding to BAFFR and CD40 signalling.

quotes.quote:
Upon 
activation by NIK, IKKα phosphorylates NIK at several C-terminal serine residues and 
thereby destabilizes it, thus serving as a negative feedback mechanism

the IKK-related kinase TANK-binding kinase 1 (TBK1) phosphorylates NIK to 
promote NIK degradation, which occurs in B cells in response to BAFFR and CD40 
signalling70.

experiment.system: cells and B cells with IKKα or TBK1 manipulation
experiment.perturbation: NIK-induced IKKα activation; BAFFR/CD40 stimulation of B cells
experiment.measurement: NIK phosphorylation and protein stability

text: RNAi knockdown of major ESCRT subunits causes endosomal accumulation of LTβR and ligand-independent non-canonical NF-κB pathway activation.

quotes.quote:
RNA interference- mediated knockdown of major 
subunits of ESCRT (endosomal sorting complexes required for transport) causes endosomal 
accumulation of LTβR, which leads to non-canonical NF-κB pathway activation in a ligand-
independent manner.

experiment.system: cultured cells expressing LTβR
experiment.perturbation: siRNA knockdown of ESCRT subunits
experiment.measurement: LTβR endosomal accumulation and non-canonical NF-κB activation

text: Alloantibody-induced complement membrane attack complexes stimulate NIK stabilization within as little as 30 minutes without requiring TRAF3 degradation, via MAC-induced AKT phosphorylation and formation of an AKT–NIK signalosome on RAB5+ endosomes, contrasting with TNFRs that typically take hours.

quotes.quote:
In contrast to TNFRs, which typically take hours to trigger 
non-canonical NF-κB signalling, alloantibody-induced MACs have been shown to stimulate

NIK stabilization within as little as 30 minutes, and this mechanism does not require TRAF3 
degradation but involves MAC-induced phosphorylation of the kinase AKT and the 
formation of a signalosome complex that includes AKT and NIK on RAB5+ endosomes, 
whereby activated AKT mediates NIK stabilization75.

verdict_note: Claim text and the 30-minute number match the paper, but the experiment field specifies 'endothelial cells' as the system; the excerpt only says 'alloantibody-induced MACs' and never names a cell type, so this detail cannot be settled from the source.

experiment.system: endothelial cells exposed to complement membrane attack complexes
experiment.perturbation: alloantibody-induced MAC formation
experiment.measurement: kinetics of NIK stabilization, AKT phosphorylation, endosomal signalosome composition

numbers.quantity: time to NIK stabilization by MACs

text: Loss-of-function NIK mutation in Aly/Aly mice impairs lymph node and Peyer's patch development and causes disorganized spleen architecture; similar phenotypes occur in IKKα- and RELB-deficient mice and NF-κB2Lym1 mice, whereas Nfkb2-knockout mice have milder defects and Nfkb1/Nfkb2 double-deficient mice have more severe defects.

quotes.quote:
Loss-of-function 
mutation of NIK in Aly/Aly mice impairs the development of lymph nodes and Peyer's 
patches and causes disorganized spleen architecture28,79. Similar phenotypes have been 
detected in mice deficient in the downstream signalling components IKKα and RELB or 
mice that harbour a mutation in the Nfkb2 gene (NF-κB2Lym1 mice) producing a non-
processable p100 (REFS 13,23,80,81). Compared with these mutant mice, the Nfkb2-
knockout mice have milder defects in secondary lymphoid organ development82,83.

mice deficient in both Nfkb1 and Nfkb2 have more severe defects in lymphoid organ 
development83

experiment.system: mutant mouse strains (Aly/Aly, IKKα-, RELB-deficient, NF-κB2Lym1, Nfkb2-KO, Nfkb1/Nfkb2 double-KO)
experiment.perturbation: genetic mutation/deletion of non-canonical NF-κB components
experiment.measurement: secondary lymphoid organ development and architecture

text: Through LTβR ligation by LTα1β2 on LTi cells, stromal organizer cells express chemokines CXCL13, CCL21 and CCL19 and adhesion molecules; induction of these chemokine genes by LTβR requires the non-canonical NF-κB pathway.

quotes.quote:
Through LTβR ligation, the LTi cells stimulate stromal organizer cells to 
express specific chemokines, including CXC-chemokine ligand 13 (CXCL13; also known as 
BLC), CC-chemokine ligand 21 (CCL21; also known as SLC) and CCL19 (also known as 
ELC), as well as cell adhesion molecules

Induction of these 
chemokine genes by LTβR requires the non-canonical NF-κB pathway29.

experiment.system: stromal organizer cells in developing lymphoid tissue
experiment.perturbation: LTβR ligation; deficiency in non-canonical NF-κB signalling
experiment.measurement: chemokine gene expression (CXCL13, CCL21, CCL19)

text: Mice deficient in NIK, IKKα or RELB, or in the canonical component TRAF6, have severe defects in mTEC development; the non-canonical pathway is dispensable for initial mTEC lineage specification but required for differentiation of mTEC progenitors into mature mTECs.

quotes.quote:
Mice 
deficient in non- canonical NF-κB signalling components, such as NIK, IKKα or RELB, or 
the canonical NF-κB signalling component TRAF6, have severe defects in mTEC 
development87–91. Recent studies suggest that the non-canonical NF-κB pathway is 
dispensable for initial mTEC lineage specification but is required for the further 
differentiation of mTEC progenitors into mature mTECs92,93.

experiment.system: thymi of NIK-, IKKα-, RELB- or TRAF6-deficient mice
experiment.perturbation: gene deficiency
experiment.measurement: medullary thymic epithelial cell development and differentiation

text: Mice deficient in NF-κB2 p52 have a defect in Aire expression in mTECs associated with impaired central tolerance, and the Aire gene contains a conserved non-coding sequence that binds and responds to non-canonical and canonical NF-κB members and is required for Aire expression and immune tolerance.

quotes.quote:
Mice deficient 
in the non-canonical NF-κB family member NF-κB2 p52 have a defect in Aire expression in 
mTECs, which is associated with impaired central tolerance94.

the Aire gene contains a conserved non-coding sequence that 
binds and responds to non-canonical and canonical NF-κB family members and is required 
for Aire gene expression and immune tolerance95,96.

experiment.system: NF-κB2-deficient mice and mice with mutated Aire conserved non-coding sequence
experiment.perturbation: genetic deficiency/enhancer mutation
experiment.measurement: Aire expression in mTECs and central tolerance

text: Studies using Aly/Aly mice and DC-specific NIK-knockout mice suggest non-canonical NF-κB signalling is dispensable for DC development, maturation and antigen presentation to CD4+ T cells but is required for DC cross-priming of CD8+ T cells.

quotes.quote:
More recent studies using Aly/Aly mice and mice with a 
DC-specific knockout of NIK suggest that non-canonical NF-κB pathway signalling is 
dispensable for DC development and maturation or for antigen presentation to CD4+ T cells 
but is required for DC cross-priming of CD8+ T cells101,102.

experiment.system: Aly/Aly mice and DC-specific NIK-knockout mice
experiment.perturbation: NIK loss of function in dendritic cells
experiment.measurement: DC development/maturation, CD4+ T cell antigen presentation, CD8+ T cell cross-priming

text: siRNA-mediated knockdown of NIK or IKKα in human DCs inhibits IDO1 induction in vitro; the author notes it remains to be examined whether NIK and non-canonical NF-κB signalling regulate IDO1 in vivo.

quotes.quote:
RNA (siRNA)-mediated knockdown of NIK or IKKα in human DCs was shown to inhibit 
IDO1 induction in vitro104,105. It remains to be examined whether NIK and non- canonical 
NF-κB signalling have an in vivo role in regulating IDO1 expression and the tolerogenic 
function of DCs.

experiment.system: human dendritic cells in vitro
experiment.perturbation: siRNA knockdown of NIK or IKKα
experiment.measurement: IDO1 induction

text: Macrophages from Map3k14-knockout and Nfkb2Lym1 mice display elevated type I IFN induction by vesicular stomatitis virus and Sendai virus, whereas macrophages expressing stable NIKΔT3 have reduced type I IFN induction; p52 and RELB appear to suppress Ifnb transcription by competing with RELA at the Ifnb enhancer.

quotes.quote:
Macrophages derived from Map3k14-
knockout mice (which lack NIK) and Nfkb2Lym1 mice display elevated levels of type I IFN 
induction by vesicular stomatitis virus and Sendai virus, whereas macrophages expressing a 
stable form of NIK that lacks the TRAF3-binding sequence (NIKΔT3) have reduced type I 
IFN induction40. The non-canonical NF-κB family members p52 and RELB seem to 
suppress the transcription of Ifnb by competing with the canonical NF-κB family member 
RELA for binding to the Ifnb gene enhancer.

experiment.system: mouse macrophages from Map3k14-knockout, Nfkb2Lym1 and NIKΔT3 mice
experiment.perturbation: infection with vesicular stomatitis virus or Sendai virus
experiment.measurement: type I IFN induction; Ifnb enhancer binding

text: GC formation requires activation of p52 and RELB and the kinases NIK and IKKα in both lymphoid stromal cells and B cells; GC B cell-specific NIK-deficient mice show defects in GC formation/maintenance and immunoglobulin class switching, simultaneous deletion of Nfkb2 and RelB in GC B cells collapses established GCs, and NIK is important for survival of class-switched B cells and plasma cells.

quotes.quote:
GC formation requires the 
activation of the non-canonical NF-κB family members p52 and RELB, as well as the 
upstream kinases NIK and IKKα, in both lymphoid stromal cells and B cells112–116.

the non-canonical NF-κB pathway not only 
mediates the survival of naive B cells but also regulates GC formation and maintenance as 
well as immunoglobulin class switching, as demonstrated by recent studies using GC B cell-
specific NIK-deficient mice117,118

simultaneous 
deletion of Nfkb2 and RelB in GC B cells causes the collapse of established GCs119. 
Interestingly, NIK is also important for the survival of B cells that have undergone class 
switching, as well as the survival of fully differentiated plasma cells118.

experiment.system: mouse germinal centres; GC B cell-specific NIK-deficient and Nfkb2/RelB-deleted mice
experiment.perturbation: conditional gene deletion in GC B cells
experiment.measurement: GC formation and maintenance, class switching, B cell and plasma cell survival

text: Non-canonical NF-κB activation by BAFFR and CD40 maintains high ICOSL expression in B cells and TFH cell differentiation; patients with loss-of-function NIK mutations have impaired B cell ICOSL expression and impaired TFH cell generation, and patients with NFKB2 mutations producing non-processable p100 have reduced B cell and TFH cell numbers and develop common variable immunodeficiency.

quotes.quote:
Non-canonical NF-κB activation by BAFFR and 
CD40 is important for maintaining high levels of ICOSL expression in B cells and, thus, 
antigen-stimulated TFH cell differentiation121

Patients with loss-of-function 
mutations in the gene encoding NIK have been found to have impaired ICOSL expression in 
B cells and impaired TFH cell generation107. Similarly, patients with mutations in NFKB2, 
producing non-processable p100 mutants lacking C-terminal phosphorylation sites, have 
reduced numbers of B cells and TFH cells and develop common variable 
immunodeficiency108,110,122,123.

experiment.system: mouse B cells and human patients with NIK or NFKB2 germline mutations
experiment.perturbation: observational (genetic loss-of-function mutations); BAFFR/CD40 stimulation in mice
experiment.measurement: ICOSL expression on B cells, B cell and TFH cell numbers, immunodeficiency phenotype

text: The non-canonical NF-κB pathway is dispensable for initial activation of naive T cells via TCR signalling but is crucial for in vivo generation and maintenance of effector and memory T cells, and has a cell-intrinsic role in OX40-stimulated TH9 cell induction contributing to airway inflammation.

quotes.quote:
The non-canonical NF-κB 
pathway is dispensable for the initial activation of naive T cells through TCR signalling but 
is crucial for the in vivo generation and maintenance of effector and memory T 
cells25,126,127.

Non-canonical NF-κB s ignalling has a 
cell-intrinsic role in mediating the induction of TH9 cells stimulated by OX40, a member of 
the TNFR family, which contributes to the pathogenesis of airway inflammation42.

experiment.system: mouse T cells with NIK/NF-κB2 deficiency in vivo
experiment.perturbation: TCR stimulation; OX40 ligation; genetic deficiency of non-canonical NF-κB components
experiment.measurement: T cell activation, effector/memory T cell generation, TH9 induction and airway inflammation

text: NIK-deficient and NF-κB2Lym1 mice show a crucial role for the non-canonical pathway in TH1 and TH17 effector cell induction in EAE, whereas the pathway is much less important for TH1/TH17 differentiation in vitro with agonistic TCR- and CD28-targeted antibodies plus polarizing cytokines; p52 also promotes TH17 pathological function by inducing GM-CSF.

quotes.quote:
Recent studies using NIK-deficient mice and NF-κB2Lym1 mice have also demonstrated a 
crucial role of the non-canonical NF-κB pathway in the induction of TH1 and TH17 effector 
cells in the neuroinflammation model experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis 
(EAE)25,126,127. Compared with the situation in vivo, the non-canonical NF-κB pathway is 
much less important for TH1 and TH17 cell differentiation in an in vitro system, in which T 
cells are stimulated using agonistic TCR- and CD28-targeted antibodies in the presence of 
polarizing cytokines25,100.

the non-canonical NF-
κB family member p52 promotes the pathological function of TH17 cells in 
neuroinflammation by mediating the induction of the cytokine GM-CSF25.

experiment.system: NIK-deficient and NF-κB2Lym1 mice; in vitro T cell polarization cultures
experiment.perturbation: EAE induction in vivo; in vitro anti-TCR/anti-CD28 stimulation with polarizing cytokines
experiment.measurement: TH1/TH17 effector cell induction, GM-CSF expression, neuroinflammation

text: T cell-specific deletion of NIK reduces the frequency and absolute number of Treg cells in the spleen and lymph nodes, although not in the thymus, demonstrating a T cell-intrinsic role for the non-canonical pathway in peripheral Treg maintenance.

quotes.quote:
T cell-specific deletion of NIK reduces the frequency and absolute number of 
Treg cells in the spleen and lymph nodes, although not in the thymus126.

experiment.system: mice with conditional depletion of NIK in T cells; bone marrow adoptive transfer
experiment.perturbation: T cell-specific NIK deletion
experiment.measurement: Treg cell frequency and absolute number in spleen, lymph nodes and thymus

text: NIK is highly expressed in synovial endothelial cells of patients with rheumatoid arthritis and promotes pathogenic angiogenesis and synovial inflammation through induction of chemokines such as CXCL12.

quotes.quote:
NIK is highly expressed in the synovial endothelial cells of patients with RA and promotes 
pathogenic angiogenesis and synovial inflammation through the induction of chemokines 
such as CXCL12 (REFS 138,139).

experiment.system: synovial tissue/endothelial cells from patients with RA and models
experiment.perturbation: observational expression analysis; NIK activation in endothelial cells
experiment.measurement: NIK expression, chemokine (CXCL12) induction, angiogenesis and synovial inflammation

text: Defects in non-canonical NF-κB signalling lead to p100 accumulation acting as an IκB and impaired osteoclast generation, whereas dysregulated activation via TRAF3 deletion or transgenic NIKΔT3 expression causes increased osteoclast formation and bone loss; the pathway is also required for bone erosion in animal models of inflammatory arthritis.

quotes.quote:
Defects in 
non-canonical NF-κB signalling lead to an accumulation of p100, which serves as an IκB to 
prevent the activation of several NF-κB members, resulting in impaired osteoclast 
generation77. The non-canonical NF-κB pathway is also required for bone erosion in animal 
models of inflammatory arthritis142,143. Conversely, dysregulated non-canonical NF-κB 
activation, owing to TRAF3 deletion or the transgenic expression of NIKΔT3 (a stable form 
of NIK), causes increased osteoclast formation and bone loss144,145.

experiment.system: mouse osteoclast precursor cells and inflammatory arthritis models
experiment.perturbation: genetic defects in non-canonical NF-κB signalling; TRAF3 deletion or NIKΔT3 transgene
experiment.measurement: osteoclast formation, bone erosion and bone loss

text: BAFF overproduction in BAFF-transgenic mice promotes aberrant survival of autoreactive B cells and autoimmunity, and patients with RA or SLE often have elevated BAFF levels associated with disease severity/activity; the BAFF-neutralizing antibody belimumab has been approved for SLE therapy.

quotes.quote:
overproduction of BAFF, as revealed in BAFF-
transgenic mice, promotes the aberrant survival of autoreactive B cells and the development 
of autoimmunity147. Patients with RA often have elevated levels of BAFF in the serum and 
synovial fluid, which is associated with disease severity146.

Patients with SLE frequently have 
elevated serum levels of BAFF, which is associated with disease activity150,151. Belimumab, 
a BAFF-neutralizing antibody, has been approved for SLE therapy

experiment.system: BAFF-transgenic mice; patients with RA and SLE
experiment.perturbation: transgenic BAFF overexpression; observational patient BAFF measurement; BAFF neutralization
experiment.measurement: autoreactive B cell survival, autoimmunity, serum/synovial BAFF levels and disease activity

text: Mouse models show dysregulated non-canonical NF-κB activation in B cells due to loss of the negative regulator TBK1 is associated with elevated serum IgA and nephropathy-like symptoms including antibody deposition in kidney glomeruli and signs of kidney dysfunction; similar phenotypes occur in mice overexpressing BAFF in B cells.

quotes.quote:
Studies of mouse models suggest that dysregulated non-
canonical NF-κB pathway activation in B cells (owing to the loss of the negative regulator 
TBK1) is associated with elevated serum levels of IgA and nephropathy-like disease 
symptoms, including antibody deposition in kidney glomeruli and signs of kidney 
dysfunction70. Similar pathological phenotypes have been detected in transgenic mice that 
overexpress BAFF in B cells154.

experiment.system: mice with B cell TBK1 loss or B cell BAFF overexpression
experiment.perturbation: genetic deletion of TBK1 in B cells; BAFF transgene
experiment.measurement: serum IgA levels, glomerular antibody deposition, kidney dysfunction

text: TWEAK engagement of FN14 on kidney cells stimulates both canonical and non-canonical NF-κB pathways, with the non-canonical pathway mediating TWEAK-induced CCL21 expression involved in T cell recruitment and kidney inflammation and fibrosis.

quotes.quote:
TWEAK 
engages FN14 on kidney cells, including tubular epithelial cells, mesangial cells and 
podocytes, and stimulates both the canonical and non-canonical NF-κB pathways, thereby 
inducing the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemo kines. The non-canonical 
NF-κB pathway mediates TWEAK-induced expression of CCL21

experiment.system: kidney tubular epithelial cells, mesangial cells and podocytes
experiment.perturbation: TWEAK stimulation of FN14
experiment.measurement: canonical/non-canonical NF-κB activation and CCL21 and cytokine expression

text: NIK is activated in hepatocytes in mouse models of dietary and genetic obesity; NIK deficiency or liver-specific kinase-dead NIK reduces glucagon responses and hepatic glucose production, while hepatocyte-specific overexpression of wild-type NIK increases them, mechanistically via NIK phosphorylation and stabilization of CREB1.

quotes.quote:
NIK is activated in hepatocytes in a mouse model 
of dietary and genetic obesity161. Moreover, NIK deficiency or the liver-specific expression

of a kinase-dead NIK mutant results in reduced glucagon responses and hepatic glucose 
production, whereas hepatocyte-specific over expression of wild-type NIK increases 
glucagon responses and hepatic glucose production161.

NIK 
phosphorylates CREB1 and stabilizes CREB1 via both phosphorylation-dependent and 
independent mechanisms.

experiment.system: mouse models of dietary and genetic obesity; hepatocytes
experiment.perturbation: NIK deficiency, liver-specific kinase-dead NIK, hepatocyte-specific wild-type NIK overexpression
experiment.measurement: glucagon responses, hepatic glucose production, CREB1 phosphorylation/stability

text: NIK overexpression in hepatocytes induces fatal liver injury and fibrosis, and a small-molecule NIK inhibitor protects mice from toxin-induced liver inflammation and injury.

quotes.quote:
NIK 
over expression in hepatocytes induces fatal liver injury and fibrosis165,166. Inhibition of 
NIK with a small-molecule inhibitor protects mice from toxin-induced liver inflammation 
and injury167.

experiment.system: mouse liver/hepatocytes
experiment.perturbation: hepatocyte NIK overexpression; small-molecule NIK inhibitor with toxin challenge
experiment.measurement: liver injury, fibrosis and inflammation

text: Non-canonical NF-κB activation in pancreatic β-cells via conditional deletion of TRAF2 or TRAF3 reduces insulin secretion and exacerbates glucose intolerance in diet-induced obese mice, and NIK induction by SMAC mimetics impairs glucose-induced insulin secretion in mouse and human islets.

quotes.quote:
non-canonical NF-κB pathway activation in pancreatic β-cells 
via the conditional deletion of TRAF2 or TRAF3, which act as negative regulators of NIK, 
reduces insulin secretion and causes exacerbated glucose intolerance in a mouse model of 
diet-induced obesity163. Consistent with these findings, NIK induction by SMAC mimetics, 
which induce the degradation of the NIK-inhibitory cIAP proteins, impairs glucose-induced 
insulin secretion in mouse and human islets163.

experiment.system: mouse pancreatic β-cells with conditional TRAF2/TRAF3 deletion; mouse and human islets
experiment.perturbation: conditional TRAF2 or TRAF3 deletion; SMAC mimetic treatment; diet-induced obesity
experiment.measurement: insulin secretion and glucose tolerance

text: NIK-deficient mice develop hypereosinophilic syndrome-like disease with aberrant TH2 responses; bone marrow adoptive transfer indicates dependence on non-haematopoietic cells, and mice carrying an IKKα activation loop mutation do not develop the syndrome, suggesting the phenotype may be independent of IKKα and non-canonical NF-κB signalling.

quotes.quote:
NIK-deficient mice 
develop hypereosinophilic syndrome-like disease involving aberrant TH2 cell responses. 
However, bone marrow adoptive transfer experiments suggest that the disease development 
in NIK-deficient mice depends on non-haematopoietic cells16. Furthermore, as mice 
carrying a mutation in the activation loop of IKKα (the phosphorylation site of NIK) do not 
develop hypereosinophilic syndrome, this pathological phenotype in NIK-deficient mice 
may be independent of IKKα and non-canonical NF-κB pathway signalling16.

experiment.system: NIK-deficient mice and IKKα activation-loop mutant mice
experiment.perturbation: NIK deficiency; bone marrow adoptive transfer; IKKα activation loop mutation
experiment.measurement: hypereosinophilic syndrome-like disease and TH2 responses

text: Epidermal cell-specific Traf2-knockout (Traf2EKO) mice show NIK accumulation and constitutive non-canonical NF-κB activation with heightened inflammatory cytokine expression and psoriasis-like skin inflammation; deletion of both Nfkb2 and Tnf in Traf2EKO mice completely prevents skin inflammation.

quotes.quote:
A recent study using epidermal cell-specific Traf2-knockout (Traf2EKO) mice suggest that 
TRAF2 deficiency in keratinocytes causes NIK accumulation and constitutive non-canonical 
NF-κB activation, which is associated with heightened expression of inflammatory
cytokines and the development of psoriasis-like skin inflammation171.

deletion of both Nfkb2 and Tnf in the 
Traf2EKO mice completely prevents skin inflammation171.

experiment.system: Traf2EKO mice (epidermal Traf2 deletion), with additional Nfkb2 and Tnf deletion
experiment.perturbation: keratinocyte-specific TRAF2 deletion; combined Nfkb2/Tnf deletion
experiment.measurement: NIK accumulation, inflammatory cytokine expression, psoriasis-like skin inflammation

text: NLRP12-deficient mice are hypersensitive to induction of colitis and colitis-associated cancer, an anti-inflammatory function involving inhibition of non-canonical NF-κB activation; consistently Nfkb2-knockout mice resist DSS-induced colitis and colitis-associated colon cancer.

quotes.quote:
The NLRP12-deficient mice are hypersensitive to the induction of colitis and 
colitis-associated cancer, and this anti-inflammatory function of NLRP12 involves the 
inhibition of non- canonical NF-κB pathway activation. In line with this study, Nfkb2-
knockout mice show resistance to dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis and colitis- 
associated colon cancer174.

experiment.system: NLRP12-deficient and Nfkb2-knockout mice
experiment.perturbation: chemical induction of colitis/colitis-associated cancer (including DSS)
experiment.measurement: colitis severity and tumour development

text: Defects in non-canonical NF-κB signalling render mice more sensitive to the intestinal pathogen Citrobacter rodentium with gut inflammation, whereas enhanced activation of the pathway promotes host defence against infections.

quotes.quote:
Defects in non- canonical NF-κB signalling render mice more 
sensitive to the intestinal pathogen Citrobacter rodentium, leading to gut inflammation, 
whereas enhanced activation of the non-canonical NF-κB pathway promotes host defence 
against infections68,175–177.

experiment.system: mice with defective or enhanced non-canonical NF-κB signalling
experiment.perturbation: Citrobacter rodentium infection
experiment.measurement: susceptibility to infection and gut inflammation

text: Viral oncoproteins stimulate the non-canonical pathway by distinct mechanisms: Tio induces NIK-dependent activation by interacting with and degrading TRAF3; LMP1 and STP-A11 act via TRAF-binding sequences in a NIK-dependent manner; whereas Tax and vFLIP activation is independent of NIK but requires IKKγ and IKKα.

quotes.quote:
Tio is a transmembrane protein that resembles TNFRs 
and mediates NIK-dependent non-canonical NF-κB activation by interacting with, and 
inducing the degradation of, TRAF3 (REF. 50). LMP1 and STP-A11 are also 
transmembrane proteins that contain TRAF-binding sequences, which are required for non- 
canonical NF-κB activation in a NIK-dependent manner47,49. By contrast, non-canonical 
NF-κB activation by Tax and vFLIP is independent of NIK but requires IKKγ and 
IKKα46,48.

experiment.system: cells expressing viral oncoproteins (Tio, LMP1, STP-A11, Tax, vFLIP)
experiment.perturbation: viral oncoprotein expression, TRAF-binding motif mutation, NIK/IKK deficiency
experiment.measurement: TRAF3 degradation and non-canonical NF-κB activation

text: In a study analyzing mediastinal large B cell lymphoma cases, translocations of the PD-L1/PD-L2 locus were identified in 20% of cases and amplification in 29% of cases, and samples with genomic aberrations showed increased PD-L1 and PD-L2 expression.

quotes.quote:
In a subsequent study that analyzed 571 cases of mediastinal large B cell lymphoma, genetic 
aberrations were also observed frequently, with translocations being identified in 20% of the 
cases and amplification in 29% of the cases (Twa et al., 2014).

In both of these studies, samples 
harboring genomic aberrations show increased PD-L1 and PD-L2 expression

experiment.system: 571 cases of human mediastinal large B cell lymphoma
experiment.perturbation: observational (genomic analysis)
experiment.measurement: frequency of translocations/amplifications at the 9p24.1 PD-L1/PD-L2 locus and PD-L1/PD-L2 expression

text: In-depth analysis of a larger cohort of Hodgkin's lymphomas showed alterations of the PD-L1 PD-L2 locus in 97% of the cases tested.

quotes.quote:
Furthermore, in-depth 
analysis of a larger cohort of Hodgkin’s lymphomas showed alterations of the PD-L1 PD-L2 
locus in 97% of the cases tested (Roemer et al., 2016).

experiment.system: cohort of human Hodgkin's lymphomas
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: frequency of PD-L1/PD-L2 locus alterations

text: In a murine sarcoma model, treatment with IFN-γ-blocking antibodies largely abrogated PD-L1 expression on tumor cells but only partially reduced PD-L1 levels on tumor-associated macrophages.

quotes.quote:
In a sarcoma mouse model, treatment of mice with IFN-γ-
blocking antibodies largely abrogated PD-L1 expression on tumor cells but only partially 
reduced PD-L1 levels on tumorassociated macrophages (Noguchi et al., 2017).

experiment.system: mouse sarcoma model
experiment.perturbation: treatment with IFN-γ-blocking antibodies
experiment.measurement: PD-L1 expression on tumor cells and tumor-associated macrophages

text: Selective disruption of PD-L1 on tumor cells in a murine transplantable sarcoma system resulted in tumor control in most but not all animals, and escaping PD-L1-negative tumors were still sensitive to antibody-mediated PD-L1 blockade.

quotes.quote:
In this setting, selective disruption of PD-L1 on tumor cells resulted in 
tumor control in most, but not all, animals. Of note, those PD-L1-negative tumors that 
escaped immune elimination were still sensitive to antibody-mediated PD-L1 blockade

experiment.system: murine transplantable sarcoma in mice
experiment.perturbation: selective genetic disruption of PD-L1 on tumor cells; antibody-mediated PD-L1 blockade
experiment.measurement: tumor control/immune elimination

text: Transplantation of PD-L1-proficient or -deficient tumor cells into wild-type or PD-L1-deficient mice showed that absence of PD-L1 from either compartment impaired tumor growth, with optimal tumor control when PD-L1 was absent from both compartments.

quotes.quote:
Lau et al. (2017) 
transplanted either PD-L1-proficient or -deficient tumor cells in either wild-type or PD-L1-
