deficient mice and observed that absence of PD-L1 from either of the two cell compartments 
impaired tumor growth, with optimal tumor control being observed when PD-L1 was absent 
from both cell compartments.

experiment.system: mouse tumor transplantation model
experiment.perturbation: PD-L1 deficiency in tumor cells and/or host
experiment.measurement: tumor growth/control

text: Implanting PD-L1-proficient tumors of differing immunogenicity into wild-type, PD-L1 plus PD-L2-deficient, or PD-1-deficient mice showed PD-L1 on non-tumor cells was dispensable for the most immunogenic line MC38, whereas for less immunogenic lines PD-L1 on both compartments contributed to tumor growth.

quotes.quote:
In these experiments, PD-L1 on 
non-tumor cells played a dispensable role in case of MC38, the most immunogenic cell line.

In contrast, in case of the less immunogenic cell lines, PD-L1 expression on both the tumor 
and non-tumor compartment contributed to tumor growth (Juneja et al., 2017).

experiment.system: immunogenic and mildly immunogenic murine tumor cell lines implanted in wild-type, PD-L1/PD-L2-deficient, or PD-1-deficient mice
experiment.perturbation: host genetic deficiency of PD-L1/PD-L2 or PD-1
experiment.measurement: tumor growth

text: In a melanoma combination trial, the added value of CTLA-4 blockade over anti-PD-1 monotherapy appeared restricted to patients with tumors that were PD-L1 negative before start of treatment.

quotes.quote:
Strikingly, the added value of CTLA-4 blockade in this study appeared restricted to those 
patients with tumors that were PD-L1 negative before start of treatment (Larkin et al., 2015)

experiment.system: melanoma patients
experiment.perturbation: combination anti-PD-1 plus anti-CTLA-4 versus anti-PD-1 monotherapy
experiment.measurement: progression-free survival stratified by pre-treatment PD-L1 status

text: IRF1 plays a central role in IFN-γ-mediated induction of PD-L1, downstream of JAK-STAT (preferentially STAT1) signaling.

quotes.quote:
Of 
those factors, IRF1 has been shown to play a central role in the IFN-γ-mediated induction of 
PD-L1 (Lee et al., 2006).

experiment.system: cultured cells responsive to IFN-γ
experiment.perturbation: IFN-γ stimulation and interference with IRF1
experiment.measurement: PD-L1 (B7-H1) expression

text: Type I interferons induce PD-L1 in cultured melanoma cells, endothelial cells, monocytes and dendritic cells, with a much greater effect on PD-L2 than PD-L1 in melanoma cells; silencing of MAK14, CRKL, and PI3K greatly impairs IFN-γ-mediated PD-L1 expression.

quotes.quote:
Next to IFN-γ, type I interferons, i.e., IFN-α and IFN-β, can also induce PD-L1 expression 
in cultured melanoma cells, endothelial cells, monocytes, and dendritic cells

exposure to type I 
interferons has a much greater effect on PD-L2 than on PD-L1 expression in melanoma 
cells

of MAK14, CRKL, and PI3K greatly impairs IFN-γ-mediated PD-L1 expression in these 
tumor cell types (Garcia-Diaz et al., 2017).

experiment.system: cultured melanoma cells, endothelial cells, monocytes, dendritic cells
experiment.perturbation: type I / type II interferon exposure; siRNA silencing of signaling genes
experiment.measurement: PD-L1 and PD-L2 expression

text: Genetic or pharmacological inactivation of MYC reduces PD-L1 expression in multiple mouse and human tumor cell models, and ChIP analysis revealed that MYC binds to the PD-L1 promoter.

quotes.quote:
Genetic or 
pharmacological inactivation of MYC has been shown to result in reduced PD-L1 expression 
in multiple mouse and human tumor cell models including melanoma, NSCLC, leukemia, 
lymphoma, and HCC

chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) analysis revealed that MYC binds to the 
PD-L1 promoter (Casey et al., 2016)

experiment.system: mouse and human tumor cell models (melanoma, NSCLC, leukemia, lymphoma, HCC)
experiment.perturbation: genetic or pharmacological MYC inactivation
experiment.measurement: PD-L1 expression; ChIP occupancy at PD-L1 promoter

text: Both HIF-1a and HIF-2a physically interact with the hypoxia response element in the PD-L1 promoter, with HIF-1a regulating PD-L1 in mouse melanoma, human breast, prostate, NSCLC cells and MDSCs, and HIF-2a in renal cell carcinoma cells.

quotes.quote:
Specifically, both HIF-1a and HIF-2a have been shown to physically interact with the 
hypoxia response element (HRE) in the promoter region of PD-L1

PD-L1 expression has been shown to be regulated by HIF-1a in mouse 
melanoma, human breast cancer, prostate cancer, NSCLC cells, and myeloid-derived 
suppressor cells (MDSCs)

experiment.system: mouse melanoma, human breast/prostate/NSCLC/RCC cells and MDSCs
experiment.perturbation: perturbation of HIF gene expression; hypoxia
experiment.measurement: PD-L1 expression and HIF binding to the PD-L1 promoter HRE

text: In melanoma cells that developed resistance to BRAF inhibition, constitutive PD-L1 expression is mediated by both JUN and STAT3, as interference with expression of either one blocked PD-L1 expression.

quotes.quote:
In melanoma cells that have developed 
resistance to BRAF inhibition, constitutive PD-L1 expression (here defined as PD-L1 
expression that is not dependent on external stimuli) can be mediated by both JUN and 
STAT3, as interference with expression of either one blocked PD-L1 expression (Jiang et al., 
2013).

experiment.system: BRAF-inhibitor-resistant melanoma cells
experiment.perturbation: interference with JUN or STAT3 expression
experiment.measurement: constitutive PD-L1 expression

text: CDK5 regulates PD-L1 by destabilizing IRF2, a competitive repressor of IRF1, via posttranslational modification of the co-repressor IRF2BP2, leading to IRF1-mediated induction of PD-L1.

quotes.quote:
Mechanistically, CDK5 destabilizes IRF2, a 
competitive repressor of IRF1, by posttranslational modification of the co-repressor 
IRF2BP2, and this destabilization then leads to IRF1-mediated induction of PD-L1 (Dorand 
et al., 2016).

experiment.system: medulloblastoma and other tumor cells
experiment.perturbation: Cdk5 disruption
experiment.measurement: IRF2/IRF2BP2 stability and PD-L1 expression

text: Pharmacological inhibition of PI3K-AKT signaling suppressed IFN-γ-induced PD-L1 expression, while loss of PTEN strengthens PD-L1 expression in CRC and NSCLC cells.

quotes.quote:
pharmacological inhibition of PI3KAKT signaling suppressed 
IFN-γ-induced PD-L1 expression, while loss of PTEN (a tumor-suppressor gene that 
negatively regulates PI3K-AKT signaling) strengthens PD-L1 expression in CRC and 
NSCLC cells

experiment.system: CRC and NSCLC cell lines
experiment.perturbation: PI3K-AKT inhibitors; PTEN loss
experiment.measurement: IFN-γ-induced and constitutive PD-L1 expression

text: Chemical or genetic suppression of MEK inhibits IFN-γ-induced STAT1 phosphorylation and PD-L1 transcription in multiple myeloma cells, while MEK-ERK activation by PMA or constitutively active MEK (MEK-DD) increases PD-L1 expression, an effect abolished by MEK inhibition.

quotes.quote:
Chemical or genetic suppression of MEK has been shown to inhibit 
IFN-γ-induced STAT1 phosphorylation and PD-L1 transcription in multiple myeloma cells 
(Liu et al., 2007). In line with this, activation of MEK-ERK signaling by PMA or by a 
constitutively active variant of MEK (MEK-DD) increases PD-L1 expression, and this effect 
can be abolished by MEK inhibition in multiple myeloma cells

experiment.system: multiple myeloma cells
experiment.perturbation: chemical/genetic MEK suppression; PMA or MEK-DD activation
experiment.measurement: STAT1 phosphorylation and PD-L1 transcription/expression

text: In some KRAS mutant NSCLC cells, RNAi silencing of KRAS decreases ERK activation and suppresses PD-L1 expression, while ectopic expression of mutant KRAS increases PD-L1 expression in bronchial epithelial cells; RAS-MEK signaling also controls PD-L1 in part by modulating PD-L1 transcript stability.

quotes.quote:
In some KRAS mutant NSCLC cells, silencing of 
KRAS by RNAi decreases ERK activation which in turn can suppress PD-L1 expression

ectopic expression of mutant 
KRAS results in increased PD-L1 expression in bronchial epithelial cells

it was shown that RASMEK signaling in part controls expression of PD-
L1 in NSCLC cells by modulating the stability of the PD-L1 transcript (Coelho et al., 2017).

experiment.system: KRAS mutant NSCLC cells and bronchial epithelial cells
experiment.perturbation: RNAi silencing or ectopic expression of mutant KRAS
experiment.measurement: ERK activation, PD-L1 expression and PD-L1 transcript stability

text: Activating EGFR mutations and EGF stimulation induce PD-L1 expression in bronchial epithelial, NSCLC, head and neck, and breast cancer cells, and pharmacological EGFR inhibition reduces constitutive and IFN-γ-induced PD-L1 expression; the EGFR-driven increase can be blocked by rapamycin and by an ERK inhibitor.

quotes.quote:
Activating mutations in EGFR, and also stimulation with EGF, induce PD-L1 expression in 
bronchial epithelial cells, NSCLC, head and neck cancer (HNC), and breast cancer cells. 
Consistent with these data, pharmacological inhibition of EGFR reduces constitutive and 
IFN-γ-induced PD-L1 expression

The increase in PD-L1 expression that 
occurs as a result of EGFR activation in NSCLC cells can be blocked by rapamycin 
(Lastwika et al., 2016) and by an ERK inhibitor (Chen et al., 2015)

experiment.system: bronchial epithelial, NSCLC, head and neck, and breast cancer cells
experiment.perturbation: EGFR activating mutations, EGF stimulation, EGFR/mTOR/ERK inhibitors
experiment.measurement: constitutive and IFN-γ-induced PD-L1 expression

text: Oncogenic ALK fusions drive PD-L1: the NPM-ALK fusion protein promotes PD-L1 expression via STAT3 and MEK-ERK in lymphomas, and in NSCLC cells harboring EML4-ALK, PD-L1 expression is increased by the constitutively active ALK kinase with ERK, AKT, STAT3, and HIF1a as downstream mediators.

quotes.quote:
the NPM-ALK fusion protein has been shown to promote PD-L1 expression via STAT3 and 
MEK-ERK in lymphomas (Marzec et al., 2008; Yamamoto et al., 2009). Likewise, in 
NSCLC cells harboring the EML4-ALK fusion gene, PD-L1 expression is increased by the 
constitutively active ALK kinase, with ERK, AKT, STAT3, and HIF1a as downstream 
mediators

experiment.system: lymphoma and NSCLC cell lines with ALK fusions
experiment.perturbation: expression/inhibition of NPM-ALK or EML4-ALK and downstream pathway components
experiment.measurement: PD-L1 expression

text: In two other studies MEK inhibitor treatment had no effect or even increased PD-L1 expression in mouse breast cancer, NSCLC, and melanoma cells, contrasting with reports of positive MEK-ERK regulation; time-course experiments show PD-L1 expression can fluctuate during treatment of KRAS mutant NSCLC cells with a MEK or AKT inhibitor.

quotes.quote:
in two 
other studies MEK inhibitor treatment had no effect or even increased PD-L1 expression in 
mouse breast cancer, NSCLC, and melanoma cells

time-course experiments that show that 
PD-L1 expression can fluctuate during treatment of KRAS mutant NSCLC cells with either 
a MEK inhibitor or AKT inhibitor

experiment.system: mouse breast cancer, NSCLC and melanoma cell lines; KRAS mutant NSCLC cells
experiment.perturbation: MEK or AKT inhibitor treatment (time course)
experiment.measurement: PD-L1 expression

text: Two large-scale genetic screens in pancreatic cancer cells and CML-derived haploid cells identified CMTM6 as a positive regulator of PD-L1; interference with CMTM6 reduces constitutive and IFN-γ-induced PD-L1 protein with no effect on PD-L1 mRNA levels, and CMTM6 binds PD-L1 to increase its half-life.

quotes.quote:
In two 
large-scale genetic screens in pancreatic cancer cells and CML-derived haploid cells, 
CMTM6 was identified as a positive regulator of PD-L1 expression (Burr et al., 2017; 
Mezzadra et al., 2017). Interference with CMTM6 expression reduces both constitutive and 
IFN-γ-induced PD-L1 protein expression, with no effect on PD-L1 mRNA levels.

Mechanistically, CMTM6 was shown to bind to PD-L1 and thereby 
increase its half-life, presumably by preventing ubiquitination and lysosomal degradation

experiment.system: pancreatic cancer cells and CML-derived haploid cells; multiple tumor cell lines
experiment.perturbation: large-scale genetic screens and CMTM6 knockdown/knockout
experiment.measurement: PD-L1 protein and mRNA levels, PD-L1 half-life

text: A modifier genetic screen in CMTM6-deficient cells identified CMTM4 as a second PD-L1 regulator, and the magnitude of CMTM6-mediated PD-L1 regulation differs substantially across cell models tested.

quotes.quote:
A 
modifier genetic screen in CMTM6-deficient cells identified CMTM4 as a second PD-L1 
regulator.

However, the magnitude of CMTM6-
mediated PD-L1 regulation does differ substantially across the cell models tested.

experiment.system: CMTM6-deficient cells and a panel of tumor cell models
experiment.perturbation: modifier genetic screen; CMTM6 modulation
experiment.measurement: PD-L1 expression

text: PD-L1 protein levels fluctuate during the cell cycle and the cyclin D-CDK4 cascade regulates PD-L1 in human cervical and breast cancer cells: CDK4 phosphorylates SPOP, an adaptor of CUL3 that serves as an E3 ubiquitin ligase for PD-L1, making CDK4 a negative regulator of PD-L1.

quotes.quote:
it was demonstrated that the level of PD-L1 protein fluctuates during the cell cycle 
and that the cyclin D-CDK4 cascade participates in the regulation of PD-L1 levels in human 
cervical cancer and breast cancer cells. CDK4 phosphorylates SPOP, which stabilizes the 
latter by dissociating it from the ubiquitin E3-ligase complex APC/CCdh1.

Thus, CDK4 functions as a negative regulator of PD-L1 expression by indirectly 
regulating its ubiquitination (Zhang et al., 2017a).

experiment.system: human cervical cancer and breast cancer cells
experiment.perturbation: cell-cycle synchronization and modulation of cyclin D-CDK4/SPOP
experiment.measurement: PD-L1 protein levels and ubiquitination

text: Mutations in JAK1 and JAK2 have been described in tumors that were unresponsive to PD-1 blockade despite a high number of somatic mutations.

quotes.quote:
Importantly, 
mutations in JAK1 and JAK2 have been described in tumors that were unresponsive to PD-1 
blockade despite a high number of somatic mutations.

experiment.system: patient tumors treated with PD-1 blockade
experiment.perturbation: anti-PD-1 therapy (observational genomic analysis)
experiment.measurement: JAK1/JAK2 mutation status, mutational burden and clinical response

text: MSI-H tumors, which carry an uncommonly high mutational load, respond particularly well to inhibition of the PD-L1-PD-1 pathway compared to other tumors of the same histology, and in most but not all studies the number of non-synonymous DNA mutations correlates with likelihood of response.

quotes.quote:
in most (Goodman et al., 2017; Rizvi et al., 
2015; Rosenberg et al., 2016) but not all (Hugo et al., 2016) studies, the number of non-
synonymous DNA mutations in human tumors has been shown to correlate with the 
likelihood of response to PD-1 axis blocking therapies

MSI-H tumors, which carry an uncommonly high 
mutational load, respond particularly well to inhibition of the PD-L1-PD-1 pathway as 
compared to other tumors of the same histology

experiment.system: human tumors of diverse histology treated with PD-1 axis blockade
experiment.perturbation: anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy
experiment.measurement: correlation of non-synonymous mutation number / MSI status with clinical response

text: Predictive markers of intratumoral T cell activity — presence of CD8-positive cells at the tumor invasive margin, clonality of the intratumoral TCR repertoire, and an IFN-γ-response gene transcriptional signature — form positive predictive markers of response, while an RNA-seq-derived profile including IL-10 correlates with lack of response.

quotes.quote:
the presence of CD8-positive cells at the tumor invasive 
margin (Tumeh et al., 2014), clonality of the intratumoral TCR repertoire (Snyder et al., 
2017; Tumeh et al., 2014), and a transcriptional signature in which interferon (IFN)-γ-
response genes are included (Ayers et al., 2017; Fehrenbacher et al., 2016; Seiwert et al., 
2016) all form positive predictive markers.

RNA-seq data have also been utilized to derive a specific 
transcriptional profile that correlates with lack of response to anti-PD-1 therapies with some 
of the genes that show increased expression in non-responders, such as IL-10, known to be 
immunosuppressive

experiment.system: patients treated with PD-1/PD-L1 blockade
experiment.perturbation: anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy
experiment.measurement: immunohistochemistry, TCR sequencing, and RNA-seq signatures correlated with clinical response

text: Genetic screens identified inhibition and inactivation of the IFN-γ receptor pathway as a mechanism of tumor cell resistance to T cell attack both in vitro and in vivo, consistent with IFN-γ receptor pathway defects found in patients with acquired resistance to PD-1 blockade.

quotes.quote:
genetic screens have identified inhibition and inactivation of the IFN-γ receptor 
pathway as a mechanism of resistance of tumor cells to T cell attack, both in vitro (Patel et 
al., 2017) and in vivo (Manguso et al., 2017).

experiment.system: tumor cells in genetic screens (in vitro and in vivo mouse models); patient tumors
experiment.perturbation: genome-wide genetic screening/CRISPR perturbation; PD-1 blockade in patients
experiment.measurement: resistance of tumor cells to T cell attack; IFN-γ receptor pathway defects

caspase-1 activation78. Although both K+ efflux-dependent stimuli (nigericin) and K+ efflux-
independent stimuli (imiquimod) induce dTGN formation and NLRP3 recruitment, K+ 
efflux is only necessary for NLRP3 recruitment and not for dTGN formation78.

text: Cytosolic LPS is sensed by human caspase-4/caspase-5 and murine caspase-11, triggering oligomerization and auto-proteolytic activation, GSDMD cleavage and pyroptosis, with the resulting K+ efflux activating NLRP3-caspase-1-dependent IL-1β secretion; oxPAPC also binds caspase-11 to activate this pathway, though another study reports oxPAPC suppresses it.

Cytosolic LPS during Gram-negative bacterial infection is sensed by human caspase-4 and 
caspase-5, and murine caspase-11, to induce non-canonical NLRP3 inflammasome 
activation90, 91, 92, 93.

GSDMD is cleaved by activated caspases 4, 5 or 11 and this induces pyroptosis80, 98. The K
+ efflux caused by pyroptosis activates NLRP3-caspase-1 dependent IL-1β secretion. The 
oxidized phospholipid 1-palmitoyl-2-arachidonoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphorylcholine 
(oxPAPC) also binds to caspase-11 and activates this non-canonical pathway99.

a recent study suggests that oxPAPC 
suppresses rather than activates the caspase-11-dependent inflammasome101

text: In mouse bone marrow-derived macrophages, simultaneous stimulation of TLR2, TLR4, TLR7 or TLR9 with extracellular ATP rapidly activates NLRP3 leading to IL-18 secretion independent of de novo transcription, without IL-1β secretion or pyroptosis.

quotes.quote:
Stimulation of TLR2, TLR4, TLR7 or TLR9, together with 
extracellular ATP, rapidly activates NLRP3. Although this type of NLRP3 activation does 
not promote IL-1β secretion and pyroptosis, it does however lead to IL-18 secretion, which 
occurs independent of de novo transcription107.

experiment.system: mouse bone marrow-derived macrophages
experiment.perturbation: simultaneous TLR agonist and extracellular ATP
experiment.measurement: IL-18 and IL-1β secretion, pyroptosis, transcription dependence

text: Multiple stimuli engage two sensors: Salmonella activates NLRP3 and NLRC4 which colocalize during infection; malaria inflammasome activation depends on plasmodium gDNA sensed by AIM2 and haemozoin sensed by NLRP3; cGAMP from cGAS-STING promotes NLRP3 and AIM2 activation and controls MCMV; in BlaER1 cells AIM2 is dispensable and DNA activates inflammasomes solely via cGAS-STING-NLRP3.

quotes.quote:
Salmonella species activate both NLRP3 and NLRC4108, and the colocalization of NLRP3 
and NLRC4 during infection has been shown by microscopic analysis113.

During malaria infection, inflammasome activation depends on 
plasmodium gDNA (sensed by AIM2) and haemozoin (sensed by NLRP3)109.

which produces the secondary messenger cGAMP, which 
further promotes activation of the NLRP3 and AIM2 inflammasomes and is important for 
control of MCMV112

AIM2 is dispensable for DNA-induced inflammasome 
activation in the human monocyte-like cell line BlaER1; in BlaER1 cells, DNA activates 
inflammasomes solely through a cGAS-STING-NLRP3 pathway115

experiment.perturbation: Salmonella, malaria, MCMV or cytosolic DNA; sensor deficiency
experiment.measurement: inflammasome activation, sensor colocalization, pathogen control

text: NLRP3 is ubiquitylated in resting macrophages and deubiquitylated upon priming and activation; FBXL2 recognizes Trp73 of NLRP3 for ubiquitylation and proteasomal degradation, and LPS priming extends NLRP3 half-life by inducing FBOX3 which degrades FBXL2.

quotes.quote:
NLRP3 is ubiquitylated in resting macrophages and is deubiquitylated upon priming and 
activation117. FBXL2, a SCF (SKP1-cullin-F-box) E3 ligase complex subunit, recognizes 
Trp73 of NLRP3 and targets it for ubiquitylation and proteasomal degradation118. LPS 
priming extends the half-life of NLRP3 by inducing another SCF subunit FBOX3, which 
degrades FBXL2118.

experiment.system: macrophages
experiment.perturbation: LPS priming; FBXL2/FBOX3 manipulation
experiment.measurement: NLRP3 ubiquitylation, protein half-life

text: TRIM31 interacts with the NLRP3 PYD in resting cells and induces Lys48-linked ubiquitylation and proteasomal degradation; LPS or IL-1β treatment further increases TRIM31 expression.

quotes.quote:
the E3 ubiquitin ligase TRIM31 interacts with the PYD 
of NLRP3 and induces Lys48-linked ubiquitylation and proteasomal degradation of 
NLRP3119. LPS or IL-1β treatment further increase TRIM31 expression

experiment.system: cells expressing NLRP3 and TRIM31
experiment.perturbation: TRIM31 expression; LPS or IL-1β treatment
experiment.measurement: NLRP3 ubiquitylation and degradation, TRIM31 expression

text: Dopamine D1 receptor signaling raises cAMP which binds NLRP3 and promotes MARCH7-dependent Lys48-linked ubiquitylation of the NLRP3 LRR domain and autophagic degradation, while the Lys63-specific deubiquitinase BRCC3 deubiquitylates the LRR domain and is required for NLRP3 oligomerization and activation.

quotes.quote:
Dopamine signaling via 
dopamine D1 receptor increases intracellular levels of cAMP, which then binds to NLRP3. 
This promotes MARCH7-dependent Lys48-linked ubiquitylation of the LRR domain of 
NLRP3 promoting its autophagic degradation120. Finally, Lys63-specific deubiquitinase 
BRCC3 deubiquitylates the LRR domain of NLRP3 and is required for NLRP3 
oligomerization and activation121.

experiment.system: macrophages/cell lines
experiment.perturbation: dopamine D1 receptor signaling; MARCH7 or BRCC3 manipulation
experiment.measurement: NLRP3 ubiquitylation, degradation, oligomerization and activation

text: TLR priming induces JNK1-mediated phosphorylation of NLRP3 Ser198 (human; Ser194 mouse), promoting BRCC3 binding, deubiquitylation, self-association and activation, and PKD at the Golgi phosphorylates Ser295 (Ser291 mouse) to promote activation.

quotes.quote:
TLR priming induces the phosphorylation of NLRP3 on Ser198 (in human NLRP3; Ser194 
in mouse NLRP3) by JUN N-terminal kinase 1 (JNK1; also known as MAPK8), and 
promotes NLRP3 self-association and activation123. Mechanistically, Ser198 (or Ser194) 
phosphorylation promotes BRCC3 binding and subsequent deubiquitylation123. After 
NLRP3 activator stimulation, protein kinase D (PKD) at the Golgi phosphorylates NLRP3 
on Ser295 (in human NLRP3; Ser291 in mouse NLRP3) and promotes NLRP3 activation124.

experiment.system: human and mouse macrophages
experiment.perturbation: TLR priming, NLRP3 activator stimulation, kinase/site mutation
experiment.measurement: NLRP3 phosphorylation, deubiquitylation, self-association, activation

Phosphorylation at NLRP3 
Ser5 (in human NLRP3; Ser3 in mouse NLRP3) within the PYD prevents inflammasome 
activation owing to electrostatic repulsion of the ASC PYD125, whereas protein phosphatase 
2A dephosphorylates Ser5 (or Ser3) to enhance NLRP3 nucleation with ASC125.

protein tyrosine phosphatase, non-receptor type 22 (PTPN22) interacts with 
NLRP3 in an ASC-dependent manner, and dephosphorylates NLRP3 at Tyr861 (in human

experiment.system: macrophages and reconstituted cells
experiment.perturbation: phospho-site mutation; PP2A or PTPN22 manipulation
experiment.measurement: NLRP3-ASC nucleation and inflammasome activation

text: Bile acids and prostaglandin E2 suppress the NLRP3 inflammasome by inducing PKA-mediated phosphorylation of NLRP3 Ser295 (Ser291 mouse), which attenuates NLRP3 ATPase activity and blocks activation.

quotes.quote:
Bile acids and 
prostaglandin E2 can suppress the NLRP3 inflammasome by inducing protein kinase A 
(PKA)-mediated phosphorylation on NLRP3 Ser295 (in human NLRP3; Ser291 in mouse 
NLRP3)127, 128, which can occur both prior to and after NLRP3 activation127. Ser295 (or 
Ser291) phosphorylation attenuates NLRP3 ATPase activity and blocks NLRP3 
activation127.

experiment.perturbation: bile acid or PGE2 treatment; PKA signaling
experiment.measurement: NLRP3 Ser295 phosphorylation, ATPase activity, inflammasome activation

text: NLRP3 is sumoylated at multiple sites by MUL1 in resting cells, restraining activation, and is desumoylated by SENP6 and SENP7 upon activation; a Lys689Arg sumoylation-defective mutation causes NLRP3 hyperactivation phenocopying CAPS mutations.

quotes.quote:
NLRP3 is sumoylated at multiple sites by the E3 SUMO protein ligase 
MUL1 (also known as MAPL), which restrains NLRP3 activation. Upon activation, NLRP3 
becomes desumoylated by sentrin-specific protease 6 (SENP6) and SENP7, promoting 
inflammasome activation129. Notably, a defect in sumoylation of NLRP3 due to a 
Lys689Arg mutation causes hyperactivation of NLRP3, which phenocopies the reported 
mutations found in patients with CAPS129.

experiment.system: cells expressing NLRP3
experiment.perturbation: MUL1/SENP6/SENP7 manipulation; Lys689Arg mutation
experiment.measurement: NLRP3 sumoylation and inflammasome activation

text: POP1 and POP2 PYDs share 64% and 37% identity respectively with the ASC PYD, and in in vitro overexpression systems both bind ASC and inhibit the NLRP3-ASC interaction.

POP2 bind to ASC and inhibit the NLRP3-ASC interaction130, 131.

COP1 (also known as CARD16), ICEBERG (also known as CARD18) and INCA (also

IL-1β blockade or IL-1R1 deficiency failed to rescue the lethality in a mouse

non-canonical NLRP3 inflammasome activation in both mouse and human macrophages in

a Phase II clinical trial of MCC950 for rheumatoid arthritis was suspended

MCC950 is not able to inhibit the release of IL-1α and prevent

text: CY-09, an analogue of the CFTR inhibitor C172 lacking CFTR-inhibitory activity, specifically inhibits the NLRP3 inflammasome but not NLRC4 and AIM2 nor TLR-mediated priming, by binding the ATP-binding Walker A motif of NLRP3 and inhibiting ATPase activity and oligomerization.

CY-09 specifically inhibits the NLRP3 inflammasome, but not the 
NLRC4 and AIM2 inflammasomes nor TLR-mediated priming signals148.

and oligomerization149.

NACHT domain of NLRP3 abolishing the NLRP3-NLRP3 interaction and oligomerization

text: Oridonin specifically inhibits the NLRP3 inflammasome but not AIM2 and NLRC4, irreversibly binding NLRP3 Cys279 via a covalent carbon-carbon bond and blocking the NLRP3-NEK7 interaction; the dose required for its NF-κB and MAPK inhibitory effects was ten times higher than that needed for NLRP3 inhibition.

quotes.quote:
Oridonin, an ent-kaurane diterpenoid, is the main 
ingredient in Rabdosia rubescens and it has been shown to specifically inhibit the NLRP3 
inflammasome, but not AIM2 and NLRC4 inflammasomes153. Oridonin irreversibly binds 
NLRP3 Cys279 via a covalent carbon-carbon bond, and blocks the NLRP3-NEK7 
interaction140.

Although Oridonin has NF-κB and MAPK inhibitory effects, the dose 
required for this was ten times higher than that needed for NLRP3 inhibition154.

experiment.measurement: inflammasome activation, NLRP3-NEK7 interaction, dose response

fasting hyperglycemia, and profound glucose intoler-
ance occur (275).

experiment.system: mice with POMC-neuron-specific rictor deletion
experiment.perturbation: rictor deletion in POMC neurons
experiment.measurement: body weight/obesity, food intake, fasting glycemia, glucose tolerance

text: In glioblastoma, mTORC2 enhances aerobic glycolysis Akt-independently by phosphorylating and inactivating class IIa HDACs (HDAC4, HDAC5/7), upregulating FoxO1/FoxO3 acetylation and derepressing c-Myc; mTORC2 also increases H3K56 acetylation in glioma affecting glycolytic gene expression via Sirt6 recruitment.

quotes.quote:
mTORC2 promotes phosphorylation of class IIa
HDACs such as HDAC4 and HDAC5/7, thereby inacti-
vating them, which then upregulates acetylation of
FoxO1 and FoxO3, resulting in derepression of c-Myc
(268). mTORC2 also increases acetylation levels of the
histone H3K56 in glioma, which inﬂuence glycolytic
gene expression due to enhanced recruitment of Sirt6
in the promoter of these genes (269).

experiment.system: glioblastoma/glioma cells
experiment.perturbation: mTORC2 activity manipulation
experiment.measurement: HDAC phosphorylation, FoxO/H3K56 acetylation, c-Myc levels, glycolytic gene expression

text: Rapamycin lowers mitochondrial membrane potential, ATP synthetic capacity, and oxygen consumption and alters the mitochondrial phosphoproteome; raptor deficiency reduces oxygen consumption rate, impairs oxidative capacity, diminishes OXPHOS and mitochondrial biogenesis gene expression, and reduces TCA cycle intermediates.

quotes.quote:
Rapamycin
lowers mitochondrial membrane potential, ATP synthetic
capacity, and oxygen consumption and alters the mito-
chondrial phosphoproteome (276)

Raptor
deﬁciency reduces the rate of oxygen consumption,
impairs oxidative capacity, diminishes expression of
genes involved in oxidative phosphorylation and mito-
chondrial biogenesis, and reduces amounts of TCA cycle
intermediates (277–279).

experiment.system: mammalian cells/tissues (as reviewed)
experiment.perturbation: rapamycin treatment or raptor deficiency
experiment.measurement: mitochondrial membrane potential, ATP synthesis, oxygen consumption, gene expression, TCA intermediates

text: mTORC1 regulates mitochondrial dynamics via 4E-BP1-mediated negative control of MTFP1 translation, whereas S6K1 does not appear to mediate mitochondrial respiration or glucose flux to pyruvate and lactate, and S6K1 knockdown did not significantly decrease mitochondrial gene expression.

quotes.quote:
The translation of MTFP1 is
negatively modulated by 4E-BP1, whereas the other
mTORC1 target, S6K1, does not seem to be involved in
mediating mitochondrial respiration or glucose ﬂux to
pyruvate and lactate (278). Furthermore, S6K1 knock-
down did not result in any signiﬁcant decreases of mito-
chondrial gene expression (281).

experiment.system: cultured mammalian cells (as reviewed)
experiment.perturbation: 4E-BP1 and S6K1 knockdown
experiment.measurement: MTFP1 translation, mitochondrial respiration, glucose flux, mitochondrial gene expression

text: Knockdown of rictor stimulates mitochondrial respiration and decreases a-KG levels, suggesting a negative regulatory role for mTORC2.

quotes.quote:
However, knockdown of
rictor stimulates mitochondrial respiration, suggesting that
mTORC2 could have a negative regulatory role (278).
Since depletion of rictor also decreases a-KG levels (278)

experiment.system: cultured cells (as reviewed)
experiment.perturbation: rictor knockdown
experiment.measurement: mitochondrial respiration and a-ketoglutarate levels

text: In kidney-specific TSC1-null renal cell carcinoma mouse models, upregulated mTORC1 activity caused mTOR-dependent downregulation of fumarate hydratase, and increased fumarate promotes oncogenesis via HIF1a activation and epigenetic/posttranslational modifications.

quotes.quote:
In kidney-speciﬁc TSC1-null renal cell carci-
noma mouse models, upregulated mTORC1 activity
caused an mTOR-dependent downregulation of fumarate
hydratase. Increased levels of fumarate promote onco-
genesis via activation of HIF1a, epigenetic and posttransla-
tional modiﬁcations.

experiment.system: kidney-specific TSC1-null mouse renal cell carcinoma model
experiment.perturbation: TSC1 deletion (mTORC1 hyperactivation)
experiment.measurement: fumarate hydratase expression, fumarate levels, tumorigenesis

text: The oncometabolite 2-hydroxyglutarate activates mTOR by decreasing DEPTOR protein stability, a consequence of inactivating KDM4A, an a-KG-dependent lysine demethylase that associates with DEPTOR.

quotes.quote:
The activation of mTOR by 2-HG occurs
via a decrease in DEPTOR protein stability as a conse-
quence of the inactivation of KDM4A, an a-KG-dependent
enzyme of the Jumonji family of lysine demethylases that
associates with DEPTOR (286).

experiment.system: tumor cells with IDH1/2 gain-of-function mutations (as reviewed)
experiment.perturbation: 2-hydroxyglutarate accumulation / KDM4A inactivation
experiment.measurement: DEPTOR protein stability and mTOR activation

text: mTORC1 represses SIRT4 transcription by promoting proteasome-mediated degradation of CREB2, thereby relieving SIRT4 inhibition of GDH and promoting anaplerotic glutamine conversion to a-KG.

quotes.quote:
mTORC1 promotes the proteasome-mediated degrada-
tion of CREB2. Because CREB2 contains a recognition
motif in the promoter region of SIRT4, mTORC1-medi-
ated degradation of CREB2 also represses SIRT4 tran-
scription
(299).

By inhibiting GDH,
SIRT4 prevents anaplerotic conversion of glutamine to
a-KG, thus sparing glutamine in the mitochondria (301).

experiment.system: mammalian cells (as reviewed)
experiment.perturbation: mTORC1 activity modulation
experiment.measurement: CREB2 degradation, SIRT4 transcription, GDH activity/glutamine anaplerosis

text: In lung cancer cells, glutamine depletion decreases mTORC1 activity while increasing mTORC2 activity and sestrin2 stability.

quotes.quote:
Second, in lung cancer cells, gluta-
mine
depletion
decreases
mTORC1
activity
while
increasing mTORC2 activity and sestrin2 stability (103).

experiment.system: lung cancer cells
experiment.perturbation: glutamine depletion
experiment.measurement: mTORC1 and mTORC2 activity; sestrin2 stability

text: Silencing of either raptor or rictor diminishes, while their combined knockdown completely blocks, system A and system L amino acid transport activity.

quotes.quote:
Silencing of either
raptor or rictor diminishes, while their combined knock-
down completely blocks, system A (alanine preferring)
and
L
(leucine
preferring)
transport
activity
(317).

experiment.system: cultured mammalian cells (as reviewed)
experiment.perturbation: raptor and/or rictor knockdown
experiment.measurement: system A and system L amino acid transport activity

text: mTORC2 is directly involved in amino acid transport via phosphorylation of Ser26 of the cystine-glutamate antiporter xCT, restricting glutamate efflux and cystine influx.

quotes.quote:
mTORC2 is also directly involved in amino
acid transport via phosphorylation of Ser26 of the cys-
tine-glutamate antiporter xCT, which restricts the efﬂux
of glutamate and inﬂux of cystine (320).

experiment.system: mammalian cells (as reviewed)
experiment.perturbation: mTORC2 phosphorylation of xCT
experiment.measurement: xCT Ser26 phosphorylation and glutamate/cystine transport

text: In a mouse model of Leigh syndrome, rapamycin mitigates the buildup of glycolytic intermediates by shifting metabolism toward amino acid catabolism, enhancing survival and preventing disease progression.

quotes.quote:
In a mouse model of
Leigh syndrome, characterized by mitochondrial dys-
function, rapamycin mitigates the buildup of glycolytic
intermediates by shifting metabolism toward amino acid
catabolism (327). Such treatment enhances survival and
prevents disease progression

experiment.system: mouse model of Leigh syndrome
experiment.perturbation: rapamycin treatment
experiment.measurement: glycolytic intermediate levels, amino acid catabolism, survival and disease progression

text: About 5-30% of glucose fluxes through the pentose phosphate pathway, whose rate-limiting reaction is catalyzed by glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase.

quotes.quote:
About 5–30% of glucose ﬂuxes
through the PPP. The rate-limiting reaction is catalyzed
by glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) (328).

experiment.system: mammalian cells (as reviewed)
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: fractional glucose flux through the pentose phosphate pathway

text: The mTORC1 target S6K1 directly phosphorylates CAD on Ser1859 and enhances its oligomerization, promoting de novo pyrimidine synthesis in response to growth factor or amino acid stimulation.

quotes.quote:
The mTORC1 target S6K1
directly phosphorylates CAD on Ser1859 and enhances
its oligomerization (202). mTORC1 and S6K promote the
de novo pyrimidine synthesis in response to growth fac-
tor or amino acid stimulation, although they are not
required for de novo synthesis per se (331).

experiment.system: mammalian cells (as reviewed)
experiment.perturbation: growth factor or amino acid stimulation; S6K1 activity
experiment.measurement: CAD Ser1859 phosphorylation, oligomerization, de novo pyrimidine synthesis

text: mTORC1 senses adenylate via TSC and Rheb independently of AMPK, and is not acutely sensitive to guanylate levels, though prolonged guanylate depletion decreases Rheb levels.

quotes.quote:
mTORC1
senses
adenylate
via
the
TSC
and
Rheb,
but

independently of AMPK. Interestingly, mTORC1 is not
acutely sensitive to guanylate levels, but prolonged
depletion leads to decreased Rheb levels.

experiment.system: mammalian cells (as reviewed)
experiment.perturbation: purine nucleotide (adenylate/guanylate) depletion
experiment.measurement: mTORC1 activity and Rheb levels

text: mTORC2 controls mRNA and protein expression as well as phosphorylation of GFAT1, the rate-limiting HBP enzyme; under glucose limitation Xbp1s promotes GFAT1 transcription mTORC2-dependently, and under glutamine deprivation mTORC2 maintains GFAT1 Ser243 phosphorylation to increase its stability and sustain UDP-GlcNAc production.

quotes.quote:
mTOR, as part
of mTORC2, controls mRNA and protein expression as
well as phosphorylation of the rate-limiting enzyme of the
HBP, glutamine:fructose-6-phosphate amidotransferase 1
(GFAT1), and thereby controls ﬂux through the HBP in
response to nutrient levels (101, 347).

Under glutamine deprivation, mTORC2 maintains the
phosphorylation of GFAT1 at Ser243 to increase its stabil-
ity and sustain production of UDP-GlcNAc despite nutrient
starvation (347).

experiment.system: cultured cells (as reviewed)
experiment.perturbation: glucose or glutamine deprivation; mTORC2 disruption
experiment.measurement: GFAT1 mRNA/protein expression, Ser243 phosphorylation, UDP-GlcNAc production

text: Only 2-3% of fructose-6-phosphate enters the hexosamine biosynthesis pathway under physiological conditions.

quotes.quote:
Although only 2–3% of fructose-6-
phosphate enters the HBP under physiological conditions,
this pathway serves as a central hub to integrate metabo-
lites from major biosynthetic pathways.

experiment.system: mammalian cells (as reviewed)
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: fraction of fructose-6-phosphate entering the HBP

text: TSC2-deficient fibroblasts with hyperactive mTORC1 display a rapamycin-sensitive increase in de novo lipid biosynthesis, and expression of constitutively active Rheb in adipocytes increases de novo lipogenesis while suppressing lipolysis.

quotes.quote:
TSC2-deﬁcient ﬁbro-
blasts
with
hyperactive
mTORC1
signals
display
rapamycin-sensitive increase in de novo lipid biosynthe-
sis (228). Likewise, expression of constitutively active
Rheb in adipocytes increases de novo lipogenesis while
suppressing lipolysis (354).

experiment.system: TSC2-deficient fibroblasts and adipocytes
experiment.perturbation: TSC2 loss with rapamycin; constitutively active Rheb expression
experiment.measurement: de novo lipid biosynthesis and lipolysis

text: During feeding, mTOR phosphorylates CRTC2 at Ser136 to attenuate its suppression of COPII-dependent SREBP-1 processing, and this phosphorylation is rapamycin sensitive.

quotes.quote:
During feeding, mTOR phosphorylates CRTC2 at Ser136
to
attenuate
its
suppression
of
COPII-dependent
SREBP-1 processing (361). This phosphorylation is rapa-
mycin sensitive

experiment.system: liver/feeding models
experiment.perturbation: feeding; rapamycin treatment
experiment.measurement: CRTC2 Ser136 phosphorylation and SREBP-1 processing

text: In response to feeding/insulin, mTORC1 phosphorylates the liver histone demethylase JMJD1C at Thr505, leading to demethylation of H3K9me2 and induction of lipogenic genes.

quotes.quote:
In response to feeding/in-
sulin, mTORC1 phosphorylates the liver histone demethyl-
ase JMJD1C at Thr505, leading to its demethylation of
H3K9me2 (364).

experiment.system: liver
experiment.perturbation: feeding/insulin stimulation
experiment.measurement: JMJD1C Thr505 phosphorylation, H3K9me2 demethylation, lipogenic gene induction

text: Raptor-deficient T cells show diminished protein expression of SREBP-1 and SREBP-2, attenuated Myc protein, attenuated mRNA of glycolytic enzymes, and defective de novo lipid synthesis upon TCR stimulation.

quotes.quote:
In raptor-deﬁcient T
cells, protein expression of both SREBP-1 and SREBP-2
is diminished (279).

In raptor-deﬁcient CD41 T cells, there is
attenuated protein expression of Myc, accompanied by
attenuated mRNA expression of glycolytic enzymes
(279). These cells also display defective de novo lipid syn-
thesis and fail to induce genes involved in lipogenic path-
ways upon TCR stimulation (279).

experiment.system: CD4+ T cells
experiment.perturbation: raptor deletion; TCR stimulation
experiment.measurement: protein/mRNA expression of SREBPs, Myc, glycolytic and lipogenic genes; de novo lipid synthesis

text: Mice with liver-specific rictor knockout have a marked decrease in lipogenesis from loss of SREBP-1c activity while retaining mTORC1 activity, and expression of constitutively active Akt2 in these hepatocytes restores de novo lipogenesis, glucose flux, and SREBP-1c activity.

quotes.quote:
Mice
with
liver-speciﬁc rictor knockout have
a marked
decrease in lipogenesis resulting from loss of SREBP-1c
activity (272, 375). These mice retain functional mTORC1
activity

Expression of constitutively active
Akt2 in hepatocytes with Rictor knockout restores glu-
cose ﬂux and lipogenesis with glucokinase and SREBP-
1c activity (272).

experiment.system: mouse liver / hepatocytes
experiment.perturbation: liver-specific rictor knockout; expression of constitutively active Akt2
experiment.measurement: de novo lipogenesis, glucose flux, SREBP-1c activity

text: Knockdown of rictor in bovine mammary epithelial cells decreases PPARγ and lipogenic gene expression and reduces intracellular triacylglycerol and FA levels and lipid accumulation in the culture medium.

quotes.quote:
Knockdown of rictor in bovine mammary epithelial cells
decreases expression of the transcription factor PPARc
and several lipogenic genes. The intracellular levels of tri-
acylglycerol and FA and accumulation of lipids in the cul-
ture medium are also reduced (378).

experiment.system: bovine mammary epithelial cells
experiment.perturbation: rictor knockdown
experiment.measurement: PPARγ and lipogenic gene expression; triacylglycerol, FA, and lipid accumulation

text: Loss of rictor in Myf5 precursors prevents brown adipose tissue growth and reprograms metabolism to a more oxidative, less lipogenic state, and the absence of mTORC2 prevents obesity and metabolic disease in these mice.

quotes.quote:
Loss of rictor
in Myf5 precursors prevents BAT growth and repro-
grams their metabolism to a more oxidative and less
lipogenic state (383). The absence of mTORC2 prevents
obesity and metabolic disease in these mice.

experiment.system: mouse Myf5-lineage brown adipose precursors
experiment.perturbation: rictor deletion
experiment.measurement: BAT growth, metabolic phenotype, obesity/metabolic disease

text: Methionine starvation decreases SAM levels and promotes association of the SAM sensor SAMTOR with GATOR1, inhibiting mTORC1 activity.

quotes.quote:
Methionine starvation decreases SAM levels and promotes
the association of SAMTOR with GATOR1, leading to inhibi-
tion of mTORC1 activity.

experiment.system: mammalian cells
experiment.perturbation: methionine starvation
experiment.measurement: SAM levels, SAMTOR-GATOR1 association, mTORC1 activity

text: In a brain-specific TSC2-knockout mouse model, constitutive mTORC1 activation leads to a marked reduction in levels of methionine, SAM, and other transmethylation metabolites.

quotes.quote:
In a brain-speciﬁc TSC2-knockout
mouse model, the resulting constitutive mTORC1 acti-
vation leads to a marked reduction in the levels of methi-
onine,
SAM,
and
other
metabolites
involved
in
transmethylation.

experiment.system: mouse brain
experiment.perturbation: brain-specific TSC2 knockout
experiment.measurement: metabolite levels (methionine, SAM, transmethylation metabolites)

text: Deletion of mTORC1 inhibits glycolysis and reduces T cell effector functions, whereas deletion of mTORC2 enhances glycolysis and increases T effector functions.

quotes.quote:
Whereas deletion of
mTORC1 inhibits glycolysis and reduces effector func-
tions, deletion of mTORC2 enhances glycolysis and
increases T effector functions (430).

experiment.system: T cells
experiment.perturbation: genetic deletion of mTORC1 or mTORC2
experiment.measurement: glycolytic activity and effector function

text: Pancreatic islets isolated from human patients with T2D show increased mTORC1 activity and decreased mTORC2 activity, and genetic or chemical inhibition of mTORC1-S6K1 signaling restores insulin secretion and mTORC2-Akt signaling.

quotes.quote:
Pancreatic islets isolated from
human patients with T2D are marked by increased
mTORC1 activity and decreased mTORC2 activity (469).
Genetic or chemical inhibition of mTORC1-S6K1 signaling
restores insulin secretion as well as mTORC2-Akt signal-
ing

experiment.system: human pancreatic islets from T2D patients
experiment.perturbation: genetic or chemical inhibition of mTORC1-S6K1
experiment.measurement: mTORC1/mTORC2 signaling activity and insulin secretion

text: Rictor knockout in pancreatic beta-cells of mice fed a high-fat diet caused glucose intolerance and impaired glucose-stimulated insulin secretion compared with control mice on the same diet; another Rictor-null study reported mild hyperglycemia and glucose intolerance from reduced beta-cell mass, proliferation, pancreatic insulin content, and glucose-stimulated insulin secretion.

quotes.quote:
Rictor knockout in pancreatic b-cells of mice
fed a high-fat diet showed glucose intolerance and
impaired glucose-stimulated insulin secretion compared
with control mice on the same diet (471). In another study
of Rictor-null mice, mild hyperglycemia and glucose
intolerance occurred because of reduction in b-cell
mass, b-cell proliferation, pancreatic insulin content, and
glucose-stimulated
insulin
secretion
(470).

experiment.system: mouse pancreatic beta-cells
experiment.perturbation: beta-cell-specific Rictor knockout; high-fat diet
experiment.measurement: glucose tolerance, glucose-stimulated insulin secretion, beta-cell mass and proliferation

text: Overexpression of DEPTOR in the mediobasal hypothalamus prevents high-fat diet-induced obesity and improves glucose metabolism, whereas DEPTOR overexpression specifically in POMC neurons does not affect energy balance but mildly elevates fasting blood glucose and insulin resistance.

quotes.quote:
Overexpression of
DEPTOR, the mTORC1 (and mTORC2) negative regulator,
speciﬁcally in the mediobasal hypothalamus prevents
high-fat diet-induced obesity and improves glucose me-
tabolism (479). When DEPTOR is overexpressed speciﬁ-
cally in POMC neurons, it does not affect energy balance
regulation but mildly elevates fasting blood glucose and
insulin resistance (480).

experiment.system: mouse hypothalamus / POMC neurons
experiment.perturbation: DEPTOR overexpression; high-fat diet
experiment.measurement: body weight/obesity, glucose metabolism, fasting blood glucose, insulin resistance

text: Neuron-specific disruption of rictor increases fat composition and adiposity and impairs glucose tolerance and behavioral leptin resistance; POMC-specific rictor deletion caused obesity, hyperphagia, fasting hyperglycemia, and glucose intolerance, whereas AgRP-specific deletion caused only mild glucose intolerance.

quotes.quote:
Neuron-speciﬁc disruption of rictor leads
to a profound increase in fat composition and adiposity
and impairs glucose tolerance and behavioral leptin resist-
ance (275). When rictor was deleted speciﬁcally in the
POMC neurons, the mice demonstrated obesity and hy-
perphagia, fasting hyperglycemia, and dramatic glucose
intolerance, whereas AgRP-speciﬁc deletion did not affect
energy balance but only caused mild glucose intolerance.

experiment.system: mouse CNS neurons (pan-neuronal, POMC, AgRP)
experiment.perturbation: conditional rictor deletion
experiment.measurement: adiposity, food intake, glucose tolerance, leptin response

text: In mice lacking PTEN in the brain, deletion of rictor, but not raptor, prolongs life span, prevents seizures, rescues AD-like behaviors and long-term memory, and normalizes brain metabolic changes.

quotes.quote:
In mice lacking PTEN in the brain,
deletion of rictor, but not raptor, prolongs life span, pre-
vents seizures, and rescues AD-like behaviors and long-
term memory, as well as normalizes metabolic changes in
the brain (493).

experiment.system: brain PTEN-deficient mice
experiment.perturbation: deletion of rictor or raptor
experiment.measurement: life span, seizures, AD-like behavior/memory, brain metabolites

text: In Parkinson's disease models, depletion of mTOR induces autophagy and clearance of A53T α-synuclein, while in models with elevated REDD1 and low mTORC1 activity, depletion of TSC2 to reconstitute mTOR activity is neuroprotective.

quotes.quote:
Depletion of mTOR results in
the induction of autophagy, leading to clearance of
A53T a-synuclein (498).

When REDD1 levels are elevated, recon-
stituting mTOR activity by depletion of TSC2 has neuro-
protective effects (499).

experiment.system: cellular/animal models of Parkinson's disease
experiment.perturbation: mTOR depletion; TSC2 depletion
experiment.measurement: autophagy induction, A53T α-synuclein clearance, neuroprotection

text: In Huntington's disease models, deletion of TSC1 accelerates death, whereas expression of constitutively active Rheb mitigates mitochondrial dysfunction and abnormal cholesterol metabolism and increases autophagy, and exogenous Rhes expression rescues motor deficits and enhances mTORC1 signals in HD mice with low endogenous Rhes.

quotes.quote:
Conditions that enhance mTORC1 activ-
ity, such as deletion of TSC1, accelerate death in an HD
mouse model (500). However, in murine models of HD,
expression of a constitutively active Rheb, an mTORC1
regulator,
mitigates
mitochondrial
dysfunction
and
abnormal cholesterol metabolism and increases autoph-
agy in HD (501).

Exogenous
expression of another Rheb-related protein, Rhes, which
activates mTORC1, also rescues motor deﬁcits and
enhances mTORC1 signals in HD mice that have low en-
dogenous Rhes levels (501).

experiment.system: mouse models of Huntington's disease
experiment.perturbation: TSC1 deletion; constitutively active Rheb or Rhes expression
experiment.measurement: survival, mitochondrial function, cholesterol metabolism, autophagy, motor deficits, mTORC1 signaling

text: Inhibition of mTORC2 signaling by depletion of rictor either specifically in the liver or in the whole body decreases male but not female life span, and deletion of rictor in the hypothalamus also reduces life span, decreases physical activity, confers obesity susceptibility, impairs glucose homeostasis, and raises fat mass.

quotes.quote:
Inhibition of mTORC2 signaling by depletion of
rictor either speciﬁcally in the liver or in the whole body
decreases male but not female life span, suggesting
that mTORC2 activity has a sex-speciﬁc positive effect
on longevity (518). In agreement with a positive role for
mTORC2 in longevity, deletion of rictor in the hypothal-
amus also reduces life span (519). The loss of rictor
decreases physical activity level and confers susceptibil-
ity to obesity. These mice also have impaired glucose ho-
meostasis and have higher fat mass.

experiment.system: mice
experiment.perturbation: liver-specific, whole-body, or hypothalamic rictor depletion
experiment.measurement: life span by sex, physical activity, obesity susceptibility, glucose homeostasis, fat mass

text: Haploinsufficiency of Akt1 extends life span in mice, accompanied by lower body weight but normal glucose metabolism, decreased ribosome biogenesis, decreased mitochondrial DNA content, and oxidative stress.

quotes.quote:
Haploinsufﬁ-
ciency of Akt1, an mTORC2 substrate and mediator of
IIS signals, extends life span in mice (517). Decreased
Akt is accompanied by lower body weight but normal
glucose metabolism, decreased ribosome biogenesis,
decreased mitochondrial DNA content, and oxidative
stress.

experiment.system: mice
experiment.perturbation: Akt1 haploinsufficiency
experiment.measurement: life span, body weight, glucose metabolism, ribosome biogenesis, mtDNA content, oxidative stress

text: Mice with rictor deficiency in adipose tissue exposed to a calorically restricted diet remained long-lived despite insulin resistance.

quotes.quote:
mice with rictor deﬁciency in adipose
tissue that were exposed to a calorically restricted diet
remained long-lived despite insulin resistance (521).

experiment.system: mice with adipose-specific rictor deficiency
experiment.perturbation: caloric restriction diet
experiment.measurement: life span and insulin sensitivity

text: In mice fed a high-fat diet, weekly treatments with lower-dose rapamycin inhibit mTORC1, protect against insulin resistance, and maintain mTORC2 activity; low-dose rapamycin also did not inhibit mTORC2 in a diet-induced obesity model on a high-fat, high-sucrose diet for 20 wk, where mice showed reduced plasma glucose, improved insulin sensitivity, and reductions in triglycerides, weight gain, and adiposity.

quotes.quote:
In mice fed a high-fat diet, weekly treatments
with lower-dose rapamycin inhibit mTORC1, protect
against insulin resistance, and maintain mTORC2 activity
(464). Low-dose rapamycin treatment also did not inhibit
mTORC2 in a murine model of diet-induced obesity sub-
jected to high-fat, high-sucrose diet for 20 wk. Mice
demonstrated reduced plasma glucose and improved
insulin sensitivity, with reductions in triglycerides, weight
gain, and adiposity (465).

experiment.system: mouse models of diet-induced obesity
experiment.perturbation: weekly low-dose rapamycin treatment with high-fat or high-fat/high-sucrose diet
experiment.measurement: mTORC1/mTORC2 activity, plasma glucose, insulin sensitivity, triglycerides, weight gain, adiposity

text: In humans, the rapalog everolimus induced hyperglycemia occurring within 3–8 wk after treatment by decreasing insulin production, with no effect on insulin sensitivity in liver, skeletal muscle, or adipose tissue.

quotes.quote:
In humans, the rapalog everoli-
mus induced hyperglycemia occurring within 3–8 wk

after treatment by decreasing insulin production (466).
Nevertheless, there was no effect on insulin sensitivity in
the liver, skeletal muscle, or adipose tissue.

experiment.system: humans
experiment.perturbation: everolimus (rapalog) treatment
experiment.measurement: blood glucose, insulin production, tissue insulin sensitivity

text: mTORC2 signaling is enhanced by metformin in the liver in vivo and in primary hepatocytes through AMPK-mediated phosphorylation of mTOR and Rictor, which is sufficient to increase mTORC2 catalytic activity toward Akt.

quotes.quote:
mTORC2 sig-
naling is enhanced by metformin in the liver in vivo and
in primary hepatocytes by AMPK-mediated phosphoryla-
tion of mTOR and Rictor, which is sufﬁcient to increase
mTORC2 catalytic activity toward Akt and downstream
signaling (102).

experiment.system: mouse liver in vivo and primary hepatocytes
experiment.perturbation: metformin treatment
experiment.measurement: mTOR/Rictor phosphorylation and mTORC2 catalytic activity toward Akt

text: In a human study, there was no difference in mTORC1 activity in pancreatic islets from patients with T2D versus nondiabetic subjects, but mTORC1 activity was higher in those with impaired fasting glucose compared with nondiabetic subjects.

quotes.quote:
In a human study, there was no difference in
mTORC1 activity in human pancreatic islets isolated from
patients with T2D and nondiabetic subjects; however,
mTORC1 activity was higher from those with impaired
fasting glucose compared with nondiabetic subjects
(473).

experiment.system: human pancreatic islets
experiment.perturbation: observational (T2D, impaired fasting glucose, nondiabetic groups)
experiment.measurement: mTORC1 activity

text: Phosphatidic acid binds the FRB domain of mTOR and binds both mTORC1 and mTORC2 to modulate their stability and activity; exogenously added fatty acids stimulate mTOR via de novo PA synthesis, and even in the absence of amino acids PA mediates mTORC1 translocation to the lysosome.

quotes.quote:
Phosphatidic acid (PA),
the product of the phospholipase D-catalyzed conver-
sion of phosphatidylcholine to choline and PA, binds to
the FRB domain of mTOR (385, 386). PA binds to both
mTORC1 and mTORC2 to modulate their stability and ac-
tivity (387). Exogenously added fatty acids stimulate
mTOR via de novo PA synthesis (95). Even in the ab-
sence of amino acids, PA mediates the translocation of
mTORC1 to the lysosome (388).

experiment.system: mammalian cells
experiment.perturbation: exogenous fatty acid addition / amino acid withdrawal; PA binding
experiment.measurement: PA binding to mTOR FRB domain, mTORC stability/activity, mTORC1 lysosomal translocation

text: In cultured human trophoblasts, silencing either rictor or raptor decreases expression of the folate transporters Folate Receptor-a (FR-a) and Reduced Folate Carrier (RFC).

quotes.quote:
The
expression
of
the
folate
transporter
Folate
Receptor-a (FR-a) and Reduced Folate Carrier (RFC) are
decreased in cultured human trophoblasts when either
rictor or raptor expression is silenced.

experiment.system: cultured human trophoblasts
experiment.perturbation: rictor or raptor silencing
experiment.measurement: folate transporter (FR-a, RFC) expression

text: Inhibition of NAMPT blocks mTOR signaling in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and hepatocarcinoma cells, inhibits mTORC1 signaling and promotes autophagy in multiple myeloma, and the dual NAMPT/PAK4 inhibitor KPT-9274 downregulates the mTORC2 pathway in triple-negative breast cancer.

quotes.quote:
Inhibition of NAMPT with pharmacological inhibitors
blocks mTOR signaling in pancreatic ductal adenocarci-
noma and hepatocarcinoma cells (396, 397). Blocking of

text: Structural comparison across kinase families shows that the Activation Segment geometry of active kinases is remarkably well conserved, whereas inactive kinases adopt very different, sometimes disordered, Activation Segment conformations; the authors state that a kinase will never be in an active conformation if its R-spine is broken and that open versus closed is not a criterion for activity.

An active kinase can be in an open or closed conformation, but a kinase will never be in an active conformation if its R-spine is broken.

text: The R-spine can be disassembled in different ways: in the insulin receptor and PKB (Akt) the DFG phenylalanine flips over and occupies the C-spine position filled by the adenine ring of ATP ("DFG-out"), sterically blocking ATP binding, whereas in inactive Src and CDK2 the DFG motif is in the "in" configuration and the R-Spine is broken by displacement of the C-Helix (Leu95).

quotes.quote: An apparently common mechanism for breaking the R-spine is exemplified by the insulin receptor and PKB (also called Akt) where the DFG phenylalanine actually flips over and occupies the position in the C-spine that is filled by the adenine ring of ATP in the active conformation [30, 31]. In these cases the incorrect positioning of the DFG motif also sterically blocks binding of ATP.
In Src and CDK2 the R-Spine is broken because the C-Helix is displaced. If Leu95 in the C-helix moves out the kinase is also inactive even though the Activation Segment has a “DFG-in” configuration.

Vaccinia related kinase 3 (VRK3), for example, has a series of hydrophobic mutant residues that fill the adenine binding pocket and complete the C-spine without ATP [56].

text: Structural comparison of ELKs and EPKs indicates that two segments were added to the conserved core in EPKs — the Activation Segment inserted between β9 and the F-Helix, and the GHI-subdomain following the F-Helix — which the authors describe as coevolved features enabling dynamic regulation and substrate/regulatory protein docking.

Across the population of ~25 cells, a
clear saturatable response was observed, but there was a very high level of variability
(Figure 3D). When analyzed at the single-cell level, however, the SOScat-to-Erk dose

response showed much higher precision (Figure 3E), tracing out dose-response curves (with
a Hill coefficient ~2) that could be reproducibly repeated over many hours (Figure S2I;
Movie S2). These responses did not show any memory—regardless of past history, a given
level of SOScat recruitment led to a reproducible level of intermediate nuclear Erk for each
cell (Figures S2E–S2G). Nevertheless, the maximum Erk amplitude and the input switching
threshold varied between individual cells (Figure 3C), explaining the higher population-level
variability.

we repeated these dose-response measurements in
clonally derived 3T3 cell lines with stable optogenetic component expression. Even among
these identical cells, we observed high cell-to-cell dose-response variability (Figure S2J).

text: Fourier-transform-based frequency-response analysis of single cells showed that the Ras/Erk module acts as a high-bandwidth, low-pass filter: the gain curve is largely flat for input timescales from 4 min to 2 hr, while transmission efficiency drops dramatically for input pulses shorter than 4 min; the cutoff timescale was highly reproducible between cells, and similar results were obtained with single-frequency sinusoidal stimulation.

quotes.quote:
After measuring membrane
fluctuations in SOScat recruitment and Erk nuclear translocation in each cell once per
minute for ~3 hr (Figure 4B), we computed the Ras/Erk pathway’s gain (Figure 4B) and
phase shift (Figure S3F) as a function of input frequency. Similar results are obtained when
we use the lower-throughput approach of stimulating cells with individual frequency
sinusoidal inputs (Figures S3E–S3G).

The frequency-response curve
(Figure 4B) is largely flat across frequencies that correspond to input timescales ranging
from 4 min to 2 hr.

for sufficiently high-frequency stimulation—short
input pulses of less than 4 min—the Erk transmission efficiency drops dramatically (Figure
4B). In this respect, the Ras/Erk module is a low-pass filter that suppresses transmission of
input pulses of less than 4 min. This critical timescale marking the boundary of signal
transmission and suppression is highly reproducible between cells.

matches both the experimentally measured gain and phase shift across all frequencies tested
(Figures 4B and S3). Overall, short (1 min) input pulses led to attenuated Erk responses,
whereas longer (5 and 10 min) pulses drove high-amplitude Erk output (Figure 4D).

text: In an RPPA screen of 180 phospho- and total protein probes in opto-SOS NIH 3T3 cells stimulated with sustained (120 min) light, transient (20 min) light pulse, or PDGF, 27 probes showed significant changes and clustered into three classes: class I (PDGF-responsive but not light-activated), class II (12 proteins responding to both transient and sustained light), and class III (seven proteins responding only to sustained Ras activity).

quotes.quote:
we took advantage of
reverse-phase protein arrays (RPPA), a high-throughput proteomic technique for measuring
180 phospho- and total protein levels (Amit et al., 2007; Tibes et al., 2006). NIH 3T3 cells
expressing opto-SOS were stimulated with either a constant 120 min light stimulus
(sustained) or a 20 min light pulse (transient). Lysates were collected at 0, 15, 30, 60, and
120 min after initiation of stimulation.

Of the 180 antibody probes tested, 27 showed
significant changes in response to PDGF or optogenetic Ras activation (Figures 5B, 5C, and
S4A; full RPPA data set is available upon request). The 27 hits clustered into 3 classes of
responders, which we termed classes I–III (Figure 5B).

Class II responding proteins are potently activated by both PDGF and light and track both
transient and sustained light input dynamics (Figure 5B, middle panel). These 12 proteins
are members of “fast” response modules

class III responding proteins are activated by PDGF but were only triggered by
sustained optogenetic Ras activity, ignoring a transient light pulse (class III; Figure 5B).
These seven proteins are members of response modules capable of differentiating sustained
from transient Ras/Erk pathway inputs.

experiment.system: NIH 3T3 cells expressing opto-SOS
experiment.perturbation: constant 120 min light (sustained), 20 min light pulse (transient), or PDGF
experiment.measurement: reverse-phase protein array of 180 phospho/total protein probes at 0, 15, 30, 60, 120 min

text: Class I (PDGF-responsive, light-unresponsive) nodes included activated EGFR and HER2, Src, Jnk, and Akt, while class II (fast, light-tracking) nodes included phosphorylated Raf, Mek, Erk, P90RSK, GSK3, and unexpectedly PKCβ, which responded quickly to light-activated Ras reaching levels comparable to PDGF treatment.

quotes.quote:
Members of this class include the canonical MAPK cascade members
(phosphorylated Raf, Mek, and Erk), the Erk target P90RSK, and the mTOR pathway’s
upstream signaling kinase GSK3. We found that PKCβ quickly responds to light-activated
Ras, reaching levels comparable to those seen after PDGF treatment, an unexpected result
because PLCγ/PKC signaling is typically thought to be induced by receptor-level activation,
not Ras (we hypothesized that PKCβ would be a member of class I).

experiment.perturbation: sustained light, transient light pulse, or PDGF
experiment.measurement: RPPA antibody signals per protein over time

This class includes components involved in
mTORC1/2 signal transduction (Rictor, p70S6K, S6, and NDRG1) (Garcίa-Martίnez and
Alessi, 2008), as well as the epithelial-mesenchymal transition transcriptional repressor
SNAIL. Perhaps the most striking response was the phosphorylation of STAT3, which only
increased after more than 1 hr of sustained light input, rising to a level comparable to that
induced by PDGF by 2 hr.
