experiment.perturbation: sustained (120 min) light, 20 min transient light pulse, or PDGF
experiment.measurement: RPPA phospho-protein levels over a 0–120 min time course

text: Western blotting of NIH 3T3 and PC12 opto-SOS lysates showed that phospho-c-Fos, and to a lesser extent total c-Fos, selectively responded to sustained but not transient light stimulation, consistent with a class III response; c-Fos was not on the RPPA antibody panel.

quotes.quote:
c-Fos was not a member of the RPPA antibody panel. We therefore used western
blotting to directly probe for total and phosphorylated c-Fos in both NIH 3T3 and PC12
opto-SOS cell lysates. We observed that phospho-c-Fos (and to a lesser extent total c-Fos)
selectively responded to sustained but not transient light stimulation, consistent with a class
III response (Figures S4B and S4C).

experiment.system: NIH 3T3 and PC12 opto-SOS cell lysates
experiment.perturbation: sustained versus transient light stimulation
experiment.measurement: western blots for total and phospho-c-Fos

text: In cocultures of opto-SOS 3T3 cells with wild-type 3T3 receiver cells, light induced nuclear phospho-STAT3 in WT cells only when they were cocultured with opto-SOS cells, indicating a secreted extracellular factor; recombinant IL-6 induced high nuclear phospho-STAT3 in both cell types as a control.

quotes.quote:
we performed optogenetic stimulation experiments on a two-cell system—we cocultured 3T3
cells containing opto-Sos with wild-type (WT) 3T3 cells that could not respond to red light.

In a control experiment, when stimulated with recombinant IL-6, both
WT and opto-SOS cells induced high levels of nuclear phospho-STAT3 (Figure 6B). As
predicted by our paracrine signaling model, we found that light induces STAT3
phosphorylation in WT 3T3 cells only when they are cocultured with opto-SOS 3T3 cells,
which presumably are secreting an extracellular factor (Figures 6B and S5A–S5C).

experiment.system: coculture of opto-SOS NIH 3T3 cells and wild-type NIH 3T3 receiver cells
experiment.perturbation: red-light stimulation or recombinant IL-6
experiment.measurement: immunofluorescence of nuclear phospho-STAT3, with opto-SOS cells identified by Phy-mCherry-CAAX/TagBFP-PIF-SOScat fluorescence

text: The light-induced paracrine STAT3 signal was transcription and Erk dependent and acted through IL-6 family receptors, as a neutralizing antibody to the GP130 receptor subunit blocked the effect; cytokine array studies suggested the mediating cytokine is not IL-6 but leukemia inhibitory factor (LIF).

quotes.quote:
Further
investigation indicated that this paracrine signaling is transcription and Erk dependent

(Figures S6A and S6B). The paracrine signal acts through IL-6 family receptors, as a
neutralizing antibody to the GP130 receptor subunit blocked the effect (Figure S5D).
Additional cytokine array studies suggest that the cytokine mediating the effect is not IL-6
but the related cytokine leukemia inhibitory factor (LIF) (Figures S5E–S5G).

experiment.system: opto-SOS / WT NIH 3T3 coculture
experiment.perturbation: light stimulation with transcription or Erk inhibition, GP130 neutralizing antibody
experiment.measurement: nuclear phospho-STAT3 immunofluorescence; cytokine array

text: Opto-SOS cells did not phosphorylate STAT3 in response to light (no autocrine activation) even though both WT and opto-SOS cells respond to exogenous IL-6 family cytokines; this cytokine sensitivity was decreased in opto-SOS cells previously stimulated with light, supporting a model in which light-activated Ras/Erk signaling triggers paracrine ligand secretion while intracellularly inhibiting the cell's own autocrine STAT3 response.

quotes.quote:
we did not observe autocrine activation: opto-SOS cells did not
phosphorylate STAT3 in response to light (Figures 6B and 6C). This observation is not due
solely to the expression of the opto-SOS genetic constructs, as both WT and opto-SOS cells
respond to exogenous IL-6 family cytokines (Figure 6B). However, this sensitivity is
decreased in opto-SOS cells previously stimulated with light (Figures 6C–6E).

experiment.system: opto-SOS and WT NIH 3T3 cells in coculture
experiment.perturbation: light stimulation, exogenous IL-6 family cytokine, or light pretreatment followed by cytokine
experiment.measurement: nuclear phospho-STAT3 immunofluorescence per cell type

text: The Erk-to-STAT3 paracrine circuit behaves as a persistence detector: in coculture, two sequential 1 hr light pulses separated by 1 hr of inactivating light produced no measurable STAT3 activation, whereas a single continuous 2 hr pulse robustly activated STAT3, despite equal total light duration; the result was not due to short cytokine lifetime, as STAT3 activation from a 2 hr input remained sustained 2 hr after inactivation and incubation in the dark.

quotes.quote:
we stimulated cells with inputs that each
consisted of 2 hr of total activation time, either delivered in a continuous pulse or as two 1 hr
pulses of activating (650 nm) light separated by 1 hr of inactivating (750 nm) light (Figure
6D).

in coculture experiments, we found that sequential 1 hr light inputs did not result
in any measurable STAT3 activation, whereas a single 2 hr pulse robustly activated STAT3
(Figures 6E and 6F), despite the fact that the same total duration of light was delivered in
both cases. This behavior is consistent with a persistence detector. This result was not due
merely to a short cytokine lifetime after secretion, as a 2 hr light input triggered STAT3
activation that was still sustained 2 hr after inactivation and incubation in the dark (Figures
S6H and S6I).

experiment.system: coculture of opto-SOS and WT NIH 3T3 cells
experiment.perturbation: continuous 2 hr 650 nm light versus two 1 hr pulses separated by 1 hr of 750 nm light; also 2 hr light followed by 2 hr dark
experiment.measurement: immunofluorescence quantification of nuclear phospho-STAT3

numbers.value: two 1 hr pulses separated by 1 hr

numbers.quantity: duration STAT3 activation persisted in the dark

text: From position weight matrices and specificity potential (SP) scores computed for 72 PDZ domains with more than ten peptides, essentially all domains recognize the last three ligand positions (0, -1, -2), the majority recognize positions -3 and -4, and some recognize positions -5 and -6, so that most binding sites achieve specificity via multiple features of the last seven ligand residues.

quotes.quote:
For 72 PDZ domains, we had sufﬁcient peptide
data (n . 10) to calculate reliable SP scores. Our analysis
reveals that essentially all PDZ domains recognize the last
three ligand positions (0, 1, and 2), the majority recognize
positions 3 and 4, and some recognize positions 5 and 6

most PDZ domain binding sites achieve high speciﬁcity
through recognition of multiple features of the last seven
residues of C-terminal peptide ligands

experiment.system: 72 PDZ domains with >10 selected peptides
experiment.perturbation: observational (PWM analysis of phage-selected peptides)
experiment.measurement: Specificity potential (SP) score per ligand position; fraction of domains with SP > 0.2

text: Total specificity scores (SP t) did not differ significantly between worm domains (mean = 3.2 ± 0.9) and human domains (mean = 3.1 ± 1.0), which the authors interpret as increased human genome complexity not being accompanied by increased overall PDZ domain specificity.

quotes.quote:
there is no signiﬁcant difference between the SP t
values for worm (mean ¼ 3.2 6 0.9) and human domains
(mean ¼ 3.1 6 1.0), indicating that increased human genome
complexity has not been accompanied by a corresponding
increase in overall PDZ domain speciﬁcity.

experiment.system: Worm and human PDZ domain specificity profiles
experiment.perturbation: observational (cross-species comparison)
experiment.measurement: Total specificity potential SP t summed over the last nine ligand positions

text: Hierarchical clustering of the binding profiles of all 82 mapped PDZ domains placed approximately 90% of the domains (73 of 82) into 16 distinct specificity classes, with the remainder representing unique specificities, extending the canonical two-class system based on position -2.

quotes.quote:
This map reveals that
approximately 90% of the domains ﬁt into 16 distinct
speciﬁcity classes, and the remainder represent unique
speciﬁcities.

Of the 82
domains, 73 are assigned to one of 16 classes, labeled to the right of each domain name.

experiment.system: 82 phage-mapped human and worm PDZ domain specificity profiles
experiment.perturbation: observational (hierarchical agglomerative clustering of PWMs with custom distance metric, manual class annotation)
experiment.measurement: Number of specificity classes and fraction of domains assigned

text: Considering each ligand position independently, the specificity profiles of 72 PDZ domains reveal eight, seven, eight, seven, five, and three distinct specificities for ligand positions 0, -1, -2, -3, -4, and -5, respectively.

quotes.quote:
The specificity profiles of 72 PDZ domains reveal eight, seven, eight, seven, five, and three distinct specificities for ligand positions 0, 1, 2,3, 4, and
5, respectively.

experiment.system: 72 phage-mapped PDZ domains
experiment.perturbation: observational (per-position analysis of specificity profiles)
experiment.measurement: Number of distinct specificities per ligand position

numbers.value: eight, seven, eight, seven, five, and three

text: Phage selections at 4 °C succeeded for all 91 single-residue mutants of ten core binding-site positions of the Erbin PDZ domain (ERBB2IP-1), yielding approximately 3,400 unique ligands; all mutants still selected C-terminal ligands, indicating the binding site functions under high mutational pressure.

quotes.quote:
we mutated
ten Erbin PDZ domain (ERBB2IP-1) core binding-site
positions and determined speciﬁcity proﬁles for each of the
91 single-residue mutants.

Phage selections were successful in all
cases, and a total of approximately 3,400 unique ligands were
sequenced.

The clear selection of ligands by all PDZ mutants shows
that the domain can function under high mutational
pressure.

experiment.system: Erbin PDZ domain (ERBB2IP-1) and 91 single-residue point mutants at ten core binding-site positions
experiment.perturbation: Site-directed point mutagenesis; phage selection with a random heptapeptide library at 4 °C
experiment.measurement: Success of ligand selection and specificity profiles (PWMs) per mutant

text: 35 of the 91 Erbin PDZ mutants caused a significant change in specificity for at least one ligand position, so mutations frequently changed rather than abolished function.

quotes.quote:
Furthermore, 35 of 91 mutations analyzed caused
a signiﬁcant change in speciﬁcity for at least one ligand
position (Figure 4). Taken together, these results show that
PDZ domains are versatile and robust, as mutations
frequently cause a change, rather than a loss of function.

experiment.system: 91 Erbin PDZ domain point mutants
experiment.perturbation: Single-residue mutations at ten binding-site positions
experiment.measurement: PWM distance between mutant and wild-type specificity profiles per ligand position, significance at >1 SD from column mean

text: Specificity for upstream ligand positions was affected by mutations at multiple positions, most not in direct contact: six mutations at four positions expanded position -1 specificity, and mutations at seven PDZ positions affected position -3 specificity although only three of these (b2-2, b3-4, b3-5) directly contact that ligand position.

quotes.quote:
Wild-type ERBB2IP-1 prefers W at ligand position 1, and
although no mutation completely alters this preference, six
mutations expand speciﬁcity to include other residue types.
These mutations occur at four positions spread throughout
the PDZ domain, and only the effects at one position (b3:a1–
1) can be explained by changes in direct residue contacts.

Mutations at seven PDZ positions affect speciﬁcity for
position 3, but only three of these positions (b2–2, b3–4, and
b3–5) are in direct contact with this ligand position.

experiment.system: Erbin PDZ domain point mutants
experiment.perturbation: Single-residue mutations at binding-site positions
experiment.measurement: Changes in phage-derived specificity profiles at ligand positions -1 and -3, compared to structural contact assignments

text: Among the 82 mapped domains, 44 contain an H at the a2-1 position and 37 (84%) of these prefer ligands with T/S at position -2; no other strong correlations between individual PDZ domain positions and ligand specificity were detected.

quotes.quote:
there is a strong correla-
tion between speciﬁcity for ligand position 2 and the
sequence at the a2–1 position, as 44 of our 82 mapped
domains (Figure 2) contain an H at the a2–1 position, and 37
(84%) of these prefer ligands containing T/S at position 2.
We were not able to detect other strong correlations between
individual PDZ domain positions and ligand speciﬁcity.

experiment.system: 82 phage-mapped PDZ domains
experiment.perturbation: observational (sequence-specificity correlation analysis)
experiment.measurement: Count of domains with H at a2-1 and their position -2 preference

text: Six worm/human ortholog gene pairs with PDZ domains mapped in both species were identified; four pairs have nearly identical specificity profiles and two are very similar, indicating conservation across the divergence of worm and human.

quotes.quote:
Our dataset
contains six worm/human ortholog gene pairs with mapped
PDZ domain binding speciﬁcity in both species (Figure 6).
Four of these pairs have nearly identical speciﬁcity proﬁles,
and two are very similar.

experiment.system: Worm/human orthologous PDZ-containing protein pairs
experiment.perturbation: observational (comparison of phage-derived specificity profiles between orthologs)
experiment.measurement: Similarity of specificity profiles within ortholog pairs

numbers.quantity: ortholog pairs mapped in both species

text: PDZ domain pairs with binding-site sequence identity greater than 70% have specificity profile similarity equivalent to that within a specificity map class; using this rule, 69 of the remaining 254 unmapped worm and human domains are predicted to have near-identical binding profiles, raising coverage to 45% of the 336 predicted worm and human PDZ domains. Domains with greater than 50% overall sequence identity also exhibit highly similar profiles.

quotes.quote:
Domain pairs with binding-site sequence identi-
ties greater than 70% have speciﬁcity proﬁles with equivalent
similarity to those within a speciﬁcity map class (Figure 7).

We ﬁnd that 69 of the remaining 254
unmapped worm and human PDZ domains have greater than
70% binding-site identity to mapped domains, and thus are
predicted to have near identical binding proﬁles

An analogous analysis using full-length PDZ
domain sequences reveals that domains with greater than
50% overall identity also exhibit highly similar speciﬁcity
proﬁles (Figure S2). Thus, by combining experimentally
mapped and predicted PDZ domain binding speciﬁcities, we
roughly double the size of our PDZ domain speciﬁcity map
and achieve 45% coverage of 336 predicted worm and human
PDZ domains.

experiment.system: Pairs of phage-mapped PDZ domains and unmapped worm/human PDZ domain sequences
experiment.perturbation: observational (correlation of binding-site sequence identity with PWM profile similarity; sequence-based prediction)
experiment.measurement: Binding-site sequence identity vs specificity profile similarity; number of domains predicted

text: PWM-based scanning of the human proteome with a stringent threshold produced a predicted network of 322 interactions between the 54 experimentally mapped human PDZ domains and 228 human proteins; 27 of these interactions are already known, a significant enrichment (p = 8.6 x 10^-18) relative to shuffled controls.

quotes.quote:
The network of
potential human PDZ domain mediated protein interactions
obtained in this manner contains 322 interactions between
our 54 experimentally mapped PDZ domains and 228 human
proteins. These high-scoring ligands are signiﬁcantly en-
riched in known PDZ interactors (27 interactions are known,
p ¼ 8.6 3 1018)

The p-value was
computed by calculating the overlap of 1,000 random shufﬂings of
our prioritized interactions with the UniHI benchmark.

experiment.system: RefSeq human proteome C termini scored against PWMs of 54 mapped human PDZ domains
experiment.perturbation: observational (in silico PWM scoring with automatic stringent score thresholds)
experiment.measurement: Number of predicted interactions and overlap with known UniHI interactions, p-value from 1,000 random shufflings

text: Using a less stringent score threshold for the three DLG1 PDZ domains, the predicted ligand list captured eight of the 11 known DLG1 ligands plus additional candidates with comparable scores, and was enriched in GO annotations consistent with DLG homolog functions.

quotes.quote:
Our predicted interactions capture eight of the 11 known
ligands for DLG1 (Table S7) and identify many additional
potential ligands with scores comparable to those of the
known ligands.

experiment.system: Three DLG1 PDZ domains scored against the human proteome
experiment.perturbation: observational (PWM scoring with a relaxed score threshold)
experiment.measurement: Recovery of known DLG1 ligands from PDZBase; GO term enrichment

text: Computational scanning of the viral proteome identified 89 viral proteins whose C termini match mapped PDZ specificities better than the best predicted endogenous interactors, covering all PDZ domain specificity classes.

quotes.quote:
we computationally identiﬁed 89 viral proteins
with C termini matching mapped PDZ domain speciﬁcities
better than the potential endogenous interactors deﬁned
above. These cover all PDZ domain speciﬁcity classes (Table
S5).

experiment.system: RefSeq viral proteome (~54,600 proteins) scored against mapped PDZ domain PWMs
experiment.perturbation: observational (in silico PWM scoring with viral cutoff set better than best human match)
experiment.measurement: Number of viral proteins with matching C termini and their class coverage

text: Competition ELISA IC50 measurements of ten synthesized peptides representing predicted viral C termini showed each peptide interacts with at least one SCRIB PDZ domain but generally not with the first PDZ domain of ZO-1 (TJP1-1); a Herpes virus peptide matching both SCRIB and ZO-1 profiles bound both, while a peptide matching only the ZO-1 profile bound only that domain.

quotes.quote:
We measured in vitro afﬁnities of ten potential SCRIB viral
ligands using synthesized peptides (peptides 1–10, Figure 9A).

Each peptide interacts with at least one SCRIB PDZ domain,
but not, in general, with the ﬁrst PDZ domain of ZO-1 (TJP1–
1), which has an overlapping, but different, speciﬁcity [20]. As
a further test, we found that a Herpes virus ligand (peptide
12) matching the speciﬁcity proﬁles of SCRIB and ZO-1 PDZ
domains bound to both, while another ligand (peptide 13)
matching only the ZO-1 PDZ domain speciﬁcity proﬁle
interacted only with this domain.

experiment.system: SCRIB PDZ domains and ZO-1 PDZ1 (TJP1-1) with synthetic peptides representing viral C termini
experiment.perturbation: Addition of synthesized viral C-terminal peptides as competitors
experiment.measurement: IC50 values by competition ELISA (high affinity IC50 < 10 uM; moderate IC50 > 10 uM; no detectable interaction IC50 > 500 uM)

text: OmniPath combines 103 resources into five integrated databases (network, enzyme-PTM, complexes, annotations, intercell) built by the pypath Python package.

quotes.quote:
The ensemble of these five databases is what we call OmniPath,
combining data from 103 resources (Fig 1A and Dataset EV1).

It combines 103 resources to
build an integrated database of molecular interactions, enzyme-PTM
(post-translational modification) relationships, protein complexes
and annotations about intercellular communication, and other func-
tional attributes of proteins.

experiment.system: OmniPath database build from public signaling/annotation resources
experiment.perturbation: observational (resource integration via pypath)
experiment.measurement: count of integrated resources and constituent databases

text: The authors defined eight major and 17 minor generic functional categories of intercellular signaling roles, ten locational categories and 994 specific categories, totaling 1,170 categories, yielding 54,330 functional annotations about intercellular communication roles of 5,781 proteins, with every entry checked manually against UniProt datasheets.

quotes.quote:
We defined eight major
(Fig 2) and 17 minor generic functional categories of intercellular
signaling roles (Datasets EV6 and EV10). We also defined ten loca-
tional categories (e.g., plasma membrane peripheral)

Furthermore, we provide 994 specific categories (e.g., neurotrophin
receptors).

Overall we defined 1,170 cate-
gories
and
provided
54,330
functional
annotations
about
intercellular communication roles of 5,781 proteins.

we
checked every entry in each category manually against UniProt data-
sheets to exclude wrong annotations

experiment.perturbation: observational (category definition and manual curation)
experiment.measurement: counts of categories, annotations, annotated proteins

text: Combining annotations from 27 resources with interaction networks from 48 resources (including ten ligand–receptor resources) yielded 14,348 unique, directed transmitter–receiver connections, around seven times more than the largest single resource providing such data.

quotes.quote:
We collected the proteins for each intercellular communication
functional category using data from 27 resources (Fig 2B, Dataset
EV6). Combining them with molecular interaction networks from 48
resources (Dataset EV2), we created a corpus of putative intercellu-
lar communication pathways

We obtained 14,348 unique, directed
transmitter–receiver (e.g., ligand–receptor) connections, around
seven times more than the largest of the resources providing such
kind of data.

experiment.perturbation: observational (integration of annotation and interaction resources)

text: Mapping a textbook table of 131 cytokine–receptor interactions onto the ligand–receptor resources showed that many of the resources cover more than 90% of these well-known interactions.

quotes.quote:
We also mapped a textbook table (Cameron & Kelvin,
2013) of 131 cytokine–receptor interactions to the ligand–receptor
resources. As the textbook contains well-known interactions, many
of the resources cover more than 90% of them (Fig 2D).

text: The OmniPath resource contained 103,396 PPI interactions between 12,469 proteins from 38 original resources, with the combined PPI network covering 53% of the human proteome (SwissProt) and showing an enrichment of kinases and cancer driver genes.

quotes.quote:
In total, the resource contained
103,396 PPI interactions between 12,469 proteins from 38 original
resources (Dataset EV2).

The combined PPI
network covered 53% of the human proteome (SwissProt), with an
enrichment of kinases and cancer driver genes (Fig 3C).

experiment.perturbation: observational (resource merging)

text: OmniPath included 61 network resources overall; miRNA–mRNA and TF–miRNA interactions were integrated from five and two literature curated resources, giving 6,213 and 1,803 interactions respectively.

quotes.quote:
The miRNA–mRNA and TF–miRNA interactions
were integrated from five and two literature curated resources, with
6,213 and 1,803 interactions, respectively.

Overall, we included 61 network resources in OmniPath
(Dataset EV2).

experiment.perturbation: observational (integration of regulatory interaction resources)

text: Eleven enzyme–PTM resources were combined into 39,201 enzyme–PTM relationships, with 1,821 enzymes targeting 16,467 PTM sites; phosphorylation accounted for 94% of all relationships and dephosphorylation 3%, 60% of interactions were described by only one resource and 92% by only one literature reference, and self-modifications and modifications within the same complex comprised 4 and 18% of interactions.

We combined 11 resources of enzyme–PTM rela-
tionships mostly covering phosphorylation (94% of all) and dephos-
phorylations (3%) (Fig 3F). Overall, we included 39,201 enzyme–
PTM relationships, 1,821 enzymes targeting 16,467 PTM sites

resource, and 92% of them by only one literature reference (Fig 3E).
Self-modifications,
e.g.,
autophosphorylation
and
modifications
between members of the same complex comprised 4 and 18% of the
interactions, respectively (Fig 3G).

text: The protein complex database collects 22,005 protein complexes described by 12 resources from 4,077 articles; 14% were homomultimers, 54% had four or fewer unique components, 20% had 18 or more, and 71% had stoichiometry information.

quotes.quote:
we added to OmniPath a compre-
hensive collection of 22,005 protein complexes described by 12
resources from 4,077 articles (Fig 3D).

14% of them were homo-
multimers, 54% had four or less unique components while 20%
of them had 18 or more. 71% of the complexes had stoichiome-
try information.

text: The annotations database, compiled from 49 resources, included 5,475,532 records about 20,365 proteins, 19,566 complexes and 182 miRNAs, with the majority of complex annotations inferred in silico from shared member annotations.

We
compiled the annotations database from 49 resources.

Overall, the annotations database included 5,475,532 records
about 20,365 proteins, virtually the whole protein-coding genome,
19,566 complexes, and 182 miRNAs. The majority of the annota-
tions for complexes were the result of our in silico inference

text: Homology translation of the network and enzyme–PTM relationships to mouse and rat via NCBI HomoloGene covered 81 and 31% of the interactions respectively.

quotes.quote:
We translated the network
and the enzyme–PTM relationships to mouse and rat by protein
homology using NCBI HomoloGene, covering 81 and 31% of the
interactions for mouse and rat, respectively (Dataset EV9).

text: In an OmniPath-based NicheNet analysis of SARS-CoV-2-infected Calu3 lung epithelial cancer cells, 12 of the 117 ligands over-expressed after infection were selected as best predictors of inflammatory response genes, and their NicheNet scores on inflammatory genes were significantly higher than on randomly selected gene sets (average P-value = 3.25e-08 from Fisher's exact tests after 10 cross-validation rounds).

Out of 117 ligands over-expressed in
SARS-CoV-2 infection, we selected for subsequent analysis the 12
best predictors of inflammatory response genes according to the
distribution of correlation values

NicheNet scores describing the potential influence of
the 12 selected ligands on the set of inflammatory genes are signifi-
cantly higher than on sets of randomly selected genes (average P-
value = 3.25e-08 from Fisher’s exact tests after 10 cross-validation
rounds).

text: Among the top predicted SARS-CoV-2-induced ligands the authors found cytokines including interleukins (IL23A and IL1A), tumor necrosis factors (TNF and TNFSF13B) and chemokines (CXCL5, CXCL9, CXCL10), and the signaling paths linking them to target genes contained key JAK-STAT pathway proteins (JAK2, STAT1, STAT3, STAT4) as well as ligands potentially triggering the MAPK pathway.

Among them, we found various cytokines: interleukins (IL23A and
IL1A), tumor necrosis factors (TNF and TNFSF13B), and chemokines
(CXCL5, CXCL9, and CXCL10), known to be involved in the inflamma-
tory response.

We identified
several key proteins of the JAK-STAT pathway (JAK2, STAT1, STAT3,
and STAT4), a main regulator of the inflammatory response

We also found ligands that potentially trigger the MAPK path-
way that has also been reported to be promoted by SARS-CoV-2 infec-
tion

text: Drug annotation of the genes in the reconstructed SARS-CoV-2 signaling network identified minocycline, an antibiotic and anti-inflammatory drug targeting CASP3 and TNF, which the authors note had recently been proposed to alleviate effects of severe SARS-CoV-2 infection in the central nervous system.

quotes.quote:
we inves-
tigated the drugs targeting the genes shown in Fig 5A (Dataset EV14).
Among the most interesting results, we identified minocycline, an
antibiotic, and anti-inflammatory drug targeting CASP3 and TNF.

text: In single-cell RNA-Seq data from ulcerative colitis across five cell types, the total number of cell–cell connections was similar between healthy and UC conditions while their identity and distribution differed: in healthy condition all cell types were tightly connected to dendritic cells, whereas in UC they were connected to regulatory T cells, with a higher amount of ligand–receptor and adhesion connections between Treg cells and the other four cell types in UC and fewer cell junction type connections.

The
total number of cell–cell connections was similar (Table EV1), while
their identity and distribution were different between healthy and
UC conditions. In healthy condition, all cell types were tightly
connected to DCs while in UC to Treg cells (Fig 5B).

We found that in both healthy state and UC the ligand–receptor and
adhesion connections were dominant and the cell junction type
connections were less abundant in UC

Also in UC, we found a higher
amount of ligand–receptor and adhesion connections between Treg
cells and the other four cell types

If it is considered 
that the presence of a docking domain positions a 
substrate within a 10 nm sphere of the kinase active 
site, then the effective concentration of the substrate 
would be 3 mM68; this alone could be sufficient to 
greatly increase the rate of phosphorylation of a scarce 
substrate.

experiment.system: Kinase–substrate pair tethered by a docking interaction
experiment.perturbation: observational (theoretical local-concentration calculation)
experiment.measurement: Effective substrate concentration within a defined radius of the active site

text: Cyclins carry a hydrophobic patch located about 40 Å from the CDK active site that binds RXL motifs in specific substrates, and this patch is required in vivo for proper substrate recognition — for example the hydrophobic patch of the yeast S-phase cyclin Clb5 has an important role in regulating DNA replication.

quotes.quote:
This docking domain is a 
small hydrophobic patch that is located on the cyclin 
partner about 40 Å away from the active site of the 
CDK17,53,71,72 and that interacts with an RXL motif on 
specific substrates

For example, the hydrophobic patch of the yeast S-phase 
cyclin Clb5 has an important role in regulating DNA 
replication74,75, presumably by directing Cdk1 to specific 
S-phase substrates.

verdict_note: Minor hedge compression ('appears to be required' → 'is required'), but the paper's own example and in vivo emphasis carry the claim.

experiment.system: CDK2–cyclin A structures (PDB 2CCI) and yeast Clb5–Cdk1
experiment.perturbation: mutation of the cyclin hydrophobic patch / RXL docking sequences
experiment.measurement: Substrate recruitment and affinity; DNA replication regulation in yeast

numbers.quantity: distance of hydrophobic patch from CDK active site

text: CKS1 proteins are small (9–18 kDa) CDK-binding proteins that also bind phosphorylated amino acids in CDK substrates and are important for phosphorylation of at least some essential substrates.

quotes.quote:
CKS1 proteins are small (9–18 kDa) CDK-binding 
proteins that can also bind phosphorylated amino acids 
in CDK substrates77,78.

it does play an important part in the phosphorylation 
of at least some essential substrates79

experiment.system: CDK–CKS1 (Suc1) complexes and their substrates
experiment.perturbation: structural and mutational analysis of CKS1 binding to CDK and phosphorylated substrates
experiment.measurement: CKS1 size, phospho-amino-acid binding, and substrate phosphorylation dependence

text: PLK1's polo-box domain binds substrates that have been previously phosphorylated at the consensus S-pS/pT-P/X, and in the absence of substrate the PBD binds and inhibits the PLK1 kinase domain, so that the free kinase is held inactive until it binds a phosphorylated substrate.

quotes.quote:
the polo-like kinase PLK1 
contains a polo-box domain (PBD)81 that binds to phos-
phorylated substrates that have the consensus sequence 
S-pS/pT-P/X (REFS 81,82)

Furthermore, in the absence 
of any substrate, the PBD binds to the kinase domain of 
PLK1 and inhibits it82.

experiment.system: PLK1 and phosphopeptide substrates
experiment.perturbation: proteomic phosphopeptide screening and structural analysis of PBD binding
experiment.measurement: PBD binding consensus and effect on PLK1 kinase activity

text: Overexpression of cyclin B2 with CDK1AF causes Golgi disassembly with little other phenotype while cyclin B1 overexpression causes chromatin condensation, nuclear-envelope breakdown, microtubule reorganization and Golgi disassembly; swapping their localizations (cyclin B1 to the Golgi, cyclin B2 to the cytoplasm) reverses the phenotypes, indicating location rather than intrinsic specificity dictates which mitotic events they regulate.

quotes.quote:
Cyclin B2 
overexpression causes the Golgi to disassemble as it nor-
mally would during mitosis, but causes little else in the 
way of phenotypes92. Overexpressing cyclin B1 causes 
chromatin condensation, nuclear-envelope breakdown 
and microtubule reorganization, as well as Golgi dis-
assembly. However, localizing cyclin B1 to the Golgi and 
cyclin B2 to the cytoplasm reverses their overexpression 
phenotypes. This suggests that the location of the two 
cyclin B–CDK1 complexes, rather than their intrinsic 
substrate specificity, dictates which mitotic events they 
regulate92.

experiment.system: Vertebrate (human) cells expressing cyclin B1 or B2 with a G0–G1-active CDK1 (CDK1AF)
experiment.perturbation: cyclin overexpression and artificial retargeting of cyclin B1 to the Golgi and cyclin B2 to the cytoplasm
experiment.measurement: Mitotic phenotypes: Golgi disassembly, chromatin condensation, nuclear-envelope breakdown, microtubule reorganization

text: Cyclin B1 cannot normally support DNA replication in Xenopus laevis egg extracts depleted of cyclin E, but does support replication when artificially targeted to the nucleus; similarly, reversing the localizations of Cln2 and Cln3 in S. cerevisiae swaps their functions in promoting G1 progression.

quotes.quote:
cyclin B1 cannot normally support 
DNA replication in Xenopus laevis egg extracts that are 
depleted of cyclin E, but it does support replication if 
it is artificially targeted to the nucleus, where cyclin E 
normally functions93. Finally, in S. cerevisiae, reversing 
the localizations of cyclin-2 (Cln2) and Cln3 swaps their 
functions in promoting G1 progression71,94.

experiment.system: Xenopus laevis egg extracts depleted of cyclin E; S. cerevisiae G1 cyclins
experiment.perturbation: artificial nuclear targeting of cyclin B1; swapping subcellular localization signals of Cln2 and Cln3
experiment.measurement: DNA replication in extracts; G1 progression function in yeast

text: ERK2 localization determines PC12 cell outcome: NGF-driven neurite outgrowth depends on ERK2 activation and translocation to the nucleus, an active nuclear form of ERK2 is sufficient for neurite outgrowth without NGF, whereas EGF promotes mitogenesis through ERK2 without driving nuclear localization.

quotes.quote:
Treatment of PC12 cells with nerve growth factor (NGF) 
drives neurite outgrowth that is dependent on ERK2 
activation and translocation from the cytoplasm to the 
nucleus. An active form of ERK2 in the nucleus is enough 
to drive neurite outgrowth in the absence of NGF96. The 
treatment of PC12 cells with epidermal growth factor 
(EGF) promotes mitogenesis through ERK2 but does not 
appear to drive the nuclear localization of ERK2.

experiment.system: PC12 cells
experiment.perturbation: NGF or EGF treatment; expression of a constitutively active nuclear form of ERK2
experiment.measurement: Neurite outgrowth, mitogenesis, and ERK2 subcellular localization

text: PKC isoforms have similar peptide-substrate specificity but are distributed to different subcellular compartments; RACK proteins bind and localize active PKC, and binding of a RACK to some PKC isoforms enhances their activity by several fold.

quotes.quote:
the peptide-substrate specificity 
of the many isoforms of PKC are similar but the isoforms 
are distributed to different subcellular compartments

Some RACKs also appear 
to be allosteric activators of PKC activity: binding of 
a RACK to some PKC isoforms enhances their activity 
by several fold98.

experiment.system: PKC isoforms and receptors for activated C-kinase (RACKs) in cells
experiment.perturbation: observational localization of isoforms; RACK binding to PKC
experiment.measurement: Peptide-substrate specificity, subcellular distribution, and PKC activity

text: AKAPs are a family of >30 proteins with little sequence homology that bind inactive PKA through its regulatory subunits and have distinct subcellular targeting mechanisms; the authors calculate that assuming a diffusion coefficient of ~10 µm2 sec–1, PKA must be inactivated within a second or so of release from the AKAP to produce a gradient of active PKA.

quotes.quote:
A-kinase anchoring proteins (AKAPs) 
are a family of >30 proteins with little sequence homo-
logy, but which all bind inactive PKA through the 
regulatory subunits

Assuming a diffusion coefficient of ~10 µm2 sec–1 (a 
typical value for a cytoplasmic protein), then PKA must 
be inactivated within a second or so of its release from 
the AKAP to produce a gradient of active PKA mole-
cules.

experiment.system: AKAP–PKA complexes in cells
experiment.perturbation: observational; theoretical diffusion/inactivation analysis
experiment.measurement: AKAP family size and PKA binding; calculated inactivation timescale required for a spatial gradient of active PKA

text: The yeast MAPKKK Ste11 is a component of three distinct MAPK cascades (mating, invasive growth, high-osmolarity), and the choice of scaffold determines at least in part which process Ste11 regulates and prevents cross-talk.

quotes.quote:
the yeast 
MAPK kinase kinase (MAPKKK) Ste11 (sterile-11) is 
a component of three distinct MAPK cascades that are 
involved in three different biological processes: the mat-
ing, invasive growth and high-osmolarity responses103

The choice of scaffold determines, at least in 
part, the process that Ste11 regulates and ensures that 
active Ste11 activates only one of the three pathways to 
prevent cross-talk with other MAPK cascades103.

experiment.system: Saccharomyces cerevisiae MAPK pathways sharing Ste11
experiment.perturbation: pathway stimulation and genetic manipulation of scaffold components (Ste5, Pbs2)
experiment.measurement: Pathway-specific transcriptional and physiological outputs

text: Artificial scaffolds can generate novel kinase–substrate interactions: chimeric scaffolds made from yeast mating and high-osmolarity MAPK pathway components convert a mating signal into an osmolarity response, and in mammalian cells chimeric adaptors linking growth-factor receptors to apoptotic signalling proteins convert proliferative signals into pro-apoptotic responses.

quotes.quote:
chimeric scaffolds made from 
components of the yeast mating and high osmolarity 
MAPK pathways can convert a mating signal into an 
osmolarity response104. In mammalian cells, chimeric 
adaptor proteins that link growth-factor receptors to 
apoptotic signalling proteins can be used to convert 
proliferative signals into pro-apoptotic responses105.

experiment.system: Yeast MAPK pathways and mammalian growth-factor receptor signalling
experiment.perturbation: engineering of chimeric scaffold/adaptor proteins that re-tether pathway components
experiment.measurement: Pathway output rerouted (osmolarity response to mating signal; apoptosis from proliferative signal)

text: The yeast Ste5 scaffold allosterically activates autophosphorylation of a Tyr in the activation loop of the MAPK Fus3, and active Fus3 then phosphorylates Ste5 as part of an apparent negative feedback loop downregulating mating pathway output.

quotes.quote:
The yeast Ste5 scaffold allosterically activ-
ates the autophosphorylation of a Tyr in the activation 
loop of the MAPK Fus3 (cell fusion-3)109. The active 
form of Fus3 then phosphorylates Ste5 and appears to 
be part of a negative feedback loop that downregulates 
signalling output from the mating pathway.

experiment.system: Yeast mating pathway Ste5–Fus3
experiment.perturbation: Ste5 binding to Fus3 (scaffold-dependent activation) and Fus3 phosphorylation of Ste5
experiment.measurement: Fus3 activation-loop Tyr autophosphorylation and mating pathway signalling output

text: In an ordinary-differential-equation model of a kinase phosphorylating two substrates against a constitutive phosphatase, steady-state stimulus–response curves for A and B are similar when only one substrate is present, but phosphorylation of the poorer substrate B is dramatically reduced when A is also present, building a kinase-level threshold and temporal lag; the model used koff for B 30 times greater than koff for A.

quotes.quote:
Rate constants can be chosen such that the steady-state 
stimulus–response curves for A and B are similar if only 
one of the two substrates is present, but the phosphoryla-
tion of the poorer substrate (substrate B) is dramatically 
reduced if A is present as well.

the presence of A builds a kinase-level threshold and a 
temporal lag into the phosphorylation of B.
the koff for substrate B is 30 times greater than the koff for substrate A.

experiment.system: Theoretical model of one kinase, two substrates (A and B) and a constitutive phosphatase
experiment.perturbation: presence versus absence of the competing good substrate A; varying kinase concentration
experiment.measurement: Modelled steady-state fraction of each substrate phosphorylated (ODE simulation)

text: Loog and Morgan estimated that the total concentration of Cdk1 consensus sites in S. cerevisiae is approximately 1 mM whereas typical Km values are 1–100 µM, which suggests Cdk1 is probably saturated by substrates and that substrate competition could contribute importantly to CDK specificity.

quotes.quote:
Loog and Morgan estimated that the total 
concentration of Cdk1 consensus sites in S. cerevisiae 
is approximately 1 mM, whereas typical Km values are

1–100 µM117, which suggests that Cdk1 is probably 
saturated by substrates.

experiment.system: Saccharomyces cerevisiae Cdk1 and its consensus-site-containing substrates
experiment.perturbation: observational (estimation of site concentration from proteome, comparison with measured Km values)
experiment.measurement: Total consensus-site concentration versus Km

text: Pheromone addition to yeast leads to Ste5-scaffold-mediated activation of the Ste11–Ste7–Fus3 cascade as well as significant activation of the filamentation MAPK Kss1; cross-pathway inhibition prevents filamentation gene expression via Fus3 phosphorylating Tec1 and targeting it for degradation, and expression of a non-phosphorylatable Tec1 causes the pheromone signal to activate filamentation gene expression.

quotes.quote:
pheromone addition to 
yeast leads to Ste5-scaffold-mediated activation of the 
Ste11–Ste7–Fus3 MAPK cascade as well as significant 
activation of the filamentation-specific MAPK Kss1

This is achieved by Fus3 phospho-
rylating the filamentation-specific transcription factor 
Tec1, which targets Tec1 for degradation and prevents 
the transcription of filamentation-specific genes124,125. 
Expression of a non-phosphorylatable Tec1 results in 
a loss of signalling specificity such that the pheromone 
signal now activates filamentation gene expression124,125.

experiment.system: Saccharomyces cerevisiae pheromone and filamentation MAPK pathways
experiment.perturbation: pheromone addition; expression of a non-phosphorylatable Tec1 mutant
experiment.measurement: MAPK activation, Tec1 degradation, and filamentation gene expression

text: The human genome encodes ~500 protein kinases (~400 Ser/Thr, ~90 Tyr, ~40 dual-specificity) and ~200 protein phosphatases (~40 Ser/Thr, ~100 Tyr, ~50 dual-specificity); specificity of Ser/Thr phosphatases appears to arise mainly through regulatory subunits, with PP1C forming complexes with >50 regulatory subunits.

quotes.quote:
The human genome encodes ~500 
protein kinases (~400 Ser/Thr, ~90 Tyr, ~40 dual-specificity) and ~200 protein 
phosphatases (~40 Ser/Thr, ~100 Tyr, ~50 dual-specificity)129–131.

For example, phosphatase-1C (PP1C) can form 
complexes with >50 regulatory subunits that target the catalytic core to different 
cellular locations and target substrates132.

experiment.system: Human genome / kinome and phosphatome catalogues
experiment.perturbation: observational (genome annotation and biochemical characterization of PP1C complexes)
experiment.measurement: Counts of kinases and phosphatases by class; number of PP1C regulatory subunits

text: Although most Ser/Thr kinases and phosphatases disfavour a Pro at the P+1 position, more than a quarter of the sites identified in global phosphorylation studies are pSer-Pro or pThr-Pro sites (pSer-Pro:pThr-Pro = 5:1); Pro-directed kinases such as CDK2 and Pro-directed phosphatases such as CDC14 accommodate the Pro ring by creating an apolar pocket.

quotes.quote:
The vast majority of Ser/Thr kinases and phosphatases disfavour substrates that 
contain a Pro in the P+1 position. However, more than a quarter of the sites identified 
in global phosphorylation studies are phosphorylated (p)Ser-Pro or pThr-Pro sites 
(pSer-Pro:pThr-Pro = 5:1).

Pro-directed kinases such as cyclin-dependent kinase-2 (CDK2) and Pro-directed 
phosphatases such as CDC14 both use a similar strategy for accommodating the Pro 
ring by creating an apolar pocket that cannot satisfy the hydrogen-bonding 
requirements of the amide nitrogen of other residues133.

experiment.system: Global phosphorylation site datasets; CDK2 and CDC14 structures
experiment.perturbation: observational (site-motif tally and structural comparison)
experiment.measurement: Fraction of phosphosites followed by Pro; structural basis of Pro accommodation

numbers.quantity: fraction of global sites that are pSer-Pro/pThr-Pro

text: Docking motifs occur in different parts of the kinase molecule in the two kinase classes: in Tyr kinases they tend to be in modular domains separate from the kinase domain (SH2, SH3, PH, JAK homology and others), whereas in Ser/Thr kinases the docking domains are often part of the kinase domain and additional modular interaction domains seem less common.

quotes.quote:
In Tyr kinases, docking motifs 
tend to be found in modular domains that are separate 
from the kinase domains.

In 
Ser/Thr kinases, the docking domains are often part of 
the kinase domain and additional modular protein–
protein interaction domains seem to be less common.

experiment.system: Tyr and Ser/Thr protein kinase families
experiment.perturbation: observational (comparative domain-architecture survey)
experiment.measurement: Location of docking motifs relative to the catalytic domain

text: The authors report that ex vivo studies in inflammasome-stimulated Gsdmd-/- BMDMs showed mature IL-1β, IL-18, IL-1α and HMGB1 are retained intracellularly, supporting pyroptosis as the route of extracellular release.

quotes.quote:
Firstly, ex vivo studies in inflammasome-stimulated 
Gsdmd-/- BMDMs have shown that fully matured IL-1β and IL-18 as well as IL-1α and 
HMGB1 are retained intracellularly, supporting the notion that pyroptosis mediates 
extracellular release of these inflammasome-dependent cytokines and DAMPs

experiment.system: Gsdmd-/- mouse bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs)
experiment.perturbation: genetic deletion of Gsdmd plus inflammasome stimulation
experiment.measurement: intracellular versus extracellular amounts of IL-1β, IL-18, IL-1α and HMGB1

text: Single-cell imaging of transgenic macrophages expressing a caspase-1 FRET sensor showed that IL-1β secretion fully coincides with pyroptosis induction in the same cells.

quotes.quote:
a single cell imaging analysis of transgenic 
macrophages expressing a caspase-1 fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) sensor 
shows that IL-1β secretion fully coincides with pyroptosis induction in the same cells

experiment.system: transgenic macrophages expressing a caspase-1 FRET sensor
experiment.perturbation: inflammasome stimulation (observational single-cell imaging)
experiment.measurement: single-cell FRET imaging of caspase-1 activity and timing of IL-1β secretion versus pyroptosis

text: Gsdmd-deficient mice with defective pyroptosis induction are highly susceptible to Francisella novicida infection.

quotes.quote:
Defective pyroptosis induction renders Gsdmd-deficient mice highly susceptible to 
Francisella novicida infection

experiment.system: Gsdmd-deficient mice
experiment.perturbation: Francisella novicida infection
experiment.measurement: host susceptibility to infection

text: Caspase-11-deficient and Gsdmd-/- mice resist high dose LPS-induced lethality, indicating caspase-11-dependent pyroptosis rather than caspase-1-dependent IL-1β/IL-18 secretion is the prominent driver of LPS-induced lethal shock; caspase-1-mediated IL-1β and IL-18 signaling contributes to lethality at lower LPS doses.

quotes.quote:
Caspase-1-mediated IL-1β and 
IL-18 signaling contributes to lethality by lower LPS doses, but this protective effect is not 
sustained at higher LPS doses

caspase-11-deficient and Gsdmd-/- mice also resist high dose LPS-induced lethality, 
indicating that caspase-11–dependent pyroptosis rather than caspase-1–dependent secretion 
of IL-1β and IL-18 is the prominent mechanism that drives LPS-induced lethal shock

experiment.system: caspase-11-deficient, Gsdmd-/- and caspase-1-deficient mice
experiment.perturbation: LPS challenge at low and high doses
experiment.measurement: survival/lethality

text: Pyroptotic myeloid cells shed tissue factor-containing microvesicles, causing systemic intravascular blood clotting and lethality in LPS-challenged mice.

quotes.quote:
pyroptotic myeloid cells shed tissue factor-containing 
microvesicles, which results in systemic intravascular blood clotting and lethality

experiment.system: LPS-challenged mice and myeloid cells
experiment.perturbation: LPS challenge inducing pyroptosis
experiment.measurement: tissue factor-containing microvesicle shedding, intravascular clotting and lethality

text: Gasdermin family members form oligomeric membrane pores with an inner diameter of 12-20 nm, but in vitro studies indicate GSDMD is the only member that is a substrate of inflammatory caspases.

quotes.quote:
The gasdermin family consists of several 
members that exert the ability to form large oligomeric membrane pores with an inner 
diameter of 12-20 nm in the inner layer of the plasma membrane and intracellular organelles

but in vitro studies suggest that GSDMD is the only member that is a substrate of 
inflammatory caspases

experiment.system: gasdermin family proteins in membranes and in vitro cleavage assays
experiment.perturbation: in vitro reconstitution/cleavage by inflammatory caspases
experiment.measurement: pore inner diameter and caspase substrate specificity

text: An activating Nlrp1aQ593P mutation drives IL-1-dependent leukopenia in mice, linked to excessive inflammasome activation and pyroptosis in hematopoietic progenitor cells.

quotes.quote:
a reported activating Nlrp1aQ593P mutation that drives IL-1-dependent leukopenia in mice 
linked to excessive inflammasome activation and pyroptosis in hematopoietic progenitor 
cells

experiment.system: mice carrying an Nlrp1a mutation
experiment.perturbation: activating Nlrp1aQ593P mutation
experiment.measurement: leukopenia, inflammasome activation and pyroptosis in hematopoietic progenitor cells

text: Pharmacological inhibitors of DPP8 and DPP9 activate NLRP1 and CARD8 to induce pyroptosis in human keratinocytes, THP-1 cells and primary peripheral blood mononuclear cells.

quotes.quote: pharmacological inhibitors of the cytosolic post-

proline dipeptidyl peptidases (DPP)8 and DPP9 activate NLRP1 and CARD8 to induce 
pyroptosis in human keratinocytes, the human monocytic-like cell line THP-1 and in 
primary peripheral blood mononuclear cells, respectively

experiment.system: human keratinocytes, THP-1 cells, primary PBMCs
experiment.perturbation: pharmacological DPP8/DPP9 inhibition
experiment.measurement: NLRP1/CARD8 inflammasome activation and pyroptosis

text: DPP8/DPP9 inhibition induced pyroptosis without caspase-1 autocleavage or IL-1β secretion in murine C57BL/6J macrophages, whereas in J774.A1 cells and BMDMs from mice with a LeTx-responsive Nlrp1b allele it elicited rapid pyroptosis with caspase-1 maturation, ASC speck assembly and mature IL-1β and IL-18 secretion.

quotes.quote:
pharmacological inhibition of DPP8 and DPP9 protease activity has been 
shown to induce pyroptosis without eliciting other inflammasome hallmark responses such 
as caspase-1 autocleavage, and secretion of IL-1β in murine C57BL/6J macrophages

DPP8 and DPP9 inhibition in the 
BALB/c-derived monocyte cell line J774.A1 and in primary bone marrow-derived 
macrophages (BMDM) of mice that express a LeTx-responsive Nlrp1b allele elicited a rapid 
pyroptotic response concomitant with caspase-1 maturation, ASC speck assembly and 
secretion of mature IL-1β and IL-18

experiment.system: C57BL/6J macrophages, J774.A1 cells, BMDMs from LeTx-responsive Nlrp1b mice
experiment.perturbation: pharmacological DPP8/DPP9 inhibition
experiment.measurement: pyroptosis, caspase-1 autocleavage/maturation, ASC speck assembly, IL-1β and IL-18 secretion

text: The K+ efflux channel TWIK2 promotes ATP-induced NLRP3 inflammasome activation in cultured macrophages, and its genetic deletion dampens polymicrobial sepsis- and LPS-induced endotoxemia-induced inflammatory lung injury in mice.

quotes.quote:
The K+ efflux channel TWIK2 has been recently shown to promote ATP-induced 
NLRP3 inflammasome activation in cultured macrophages, and its genetic deletion dampens 
polymicrobial sepsis- and LPS-induced endotoxemia-induced inflammatory lung injury in 
mice

experiment.system: cultured macrophages and mice
experiment.perturbation: ATP stimulation; genetic deletion of TWIK2; polymicrobial sepsis and LPS endotoxemia
experiment.measurement: NLRP3 inflammasome activation and inflammatory lung injury

text: The TLR7 agonist imiquimod and related molecules activate NLRP3 through a K+ efflux-independent mechanism, primarily interrogated in murine BMDCs, and imiquimod also engages NLRP3 in BMDMs.

quotes.quote:
the Toll-like receptor 7 (TLR7) agonist imiquimod and related molecules 
have been shown to activate NLRP3 through a K+ efflux-independent mechanism

The mechanism of imiquimod-induced NLRP3 activation 
has primarily been interrogated in murine bone-marrow derived dendritic cells (BMDCs), 
but imiquimod also engages the NLRP3 inflammasome in BMDMs

experiment.system: murine bone marrow-derived dendritic cells and BMDMs
experiment.perturbation: imiquimod (TLR7 agonist) stimulation
experiment.measurement: NLRP3 inflammasome activation and K+ efflux dependence

text: In GM-CSF-derived BMDCs, a subpopulation of monocyte-derived macrophages rather than dendritic cells is responsible for NLRP3-mediated caspase-1 activation and IL-1β secretion.

quotes.quote:
a recent examination of granulocyte–macrophage 
colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF)-derived BMDCs reveals that a subpopulation of 
monocyte-derived macrophages, rather than dendritic cells, are responsible for NLRP3-
mediated caspase-1 activation and IL-1β secretion

experiment.system: GM-CSF-derived murine bone marrow dendritic cell cultures
experiment.perturbation: NLRP3 stimulation with cell-subset resolution
experiment.measurement: caspase-1 activation and IL-1β secretion by cell subpopulation

text: An alternative NLRP3 inflammasome pathway promotes IL-1β secretion from human monocytes stimulated with the TLR4 agonist LPS without K+ efflux, ASC speck formation or pyroptosis.

quotes.quote:
An alternative 
NLRP3 inflammasome pathway has been described that promotes IL-1β secretion from 
human monocytes stimulated with the TLR4 agonist LPS without eliciting K+ efflux and 
classical inflammasome hallmarks such as ASC speck formation and pyroptosis

experiment.system: human monocytes
experiment.perturbation: LPS (TLR4 agonist) stimulation
experiment.measurement: IL-1β secretion, K+ efflux, ASC speck formation, pyroptosis

text: The AIM2 inflammasome provokes a detrimental inflammatory response to genomic dsDNA breaks in mice subjected to subtotal body irradiation-induced gastrointestinal syndrome and total body irradiation-induced hematopoietic failure.

quotes.quote:
The AIM2 inflammasome has also been 
reported to provoke a detrimental inflammatory response to genomic dsDNA breaks in mice 
subjected to subtotal body irradiation-induced gastrointestinal syndrome and total body 
irradiation-induced hematopoietic failure

experiment.system: mice
experiment.perturbation: subtotal and total body irradiation
experiment.measurement: AIM2-dependent inflammatory response, gastrointestinal syndrome and hematopoietic failure

text: Pyrin phosphorylation (at S208/S242 in human Pyrin; S205/S241 in murine Pyrin) keeps the protein autoinhibited by recruiting 14-3-3 proteins in naïve macrophages, and RhoA-inactivating bacterial toxins relieve inhibition by stimulating dephosphorylation and disrupting 14-3-3 binding.

quotes.quote:
In naïve macrophages, Pyrin phosphorylation (at 
S208/S242 in human Pyrin; S205/S241 in murine Pyrin) keeps the protein autoinhibited by 
recruiting 14-3-3 proteins (Masters et al., 2016). The above-mentioned toxins relieve 
inhibition by stimulating Pyrin de-phosphorylation and disrupting 14-3-3 binding.

experiment.system: naïve macrophages expressing human or murine Pyrin
experiment.perturbation: treatment with RhoA-inactivating bacterial toxins
experiment.measurement: Pyrin phosphorylation status and 14-3-3 binding

text: A functional microtubule network is required downstream of Pyrin dephosphorylation in toxin-stimulated macrophages for ASC speck assembly and caspase-1-mediated cytokine secretion, although the authors state the mechanism remains to be addressed.

quotes.quote:
A 
functional microtubule network is required downstream of Pyrin dephosphorylation in toxin-
stimulated macrophages for assembly of ASC specks and caspase-1-mediated cytokine 
secretion, although future experimentation should address the mechanism involved

experiment.system: toxin-stimulated macrophages
experiment.perturbation: microtubule network disruption during Pyrin inflammasome activation
experiment.measurement: ASC speck assembly and caspase-1-mediated cytokine secretion

text: Extracellular release of the DAMPs IL-1α and HMGB1 from macrophages infected with Escherichia coli, Citrobacter rodentium and Vibrio cholerae was fully caspase-11-dependent, consistent with caspase-11 autonomously cleaving GSDMD to induce pyroptosis.

quotes.quote:
Murine caspase-11 autonomously cleaves GSDMD to induce pyroptosis as 
highlighted by the observation that extracellular release of the DAMPs IL-1α and HMGB1 
from macrophages infected with Escherichia coli, Citrobacter rodentium and Vibrio cholerae 
was fully caspase-11-dependent

experiment.system: murine macrophages, caspase-11-deficient versus wild-type
experiment.perturbation: infection with E. coli, C. rodentium or V. cholerae
experiment.measurement: extracellular release of IL-1α and HMGB1

text: Bacterial vacuoles are lysed by GBPs to promote caspase-11 activation by leaked E. coli and C. rodentium LPS in the cytoplasm, and GBPs recruit IRGB10 to intracellular bacteria to facilitate AIM2 inflammasome activation by Francisella novicida and non-canonical inflammasome activation by E. coli and C. rodentium.

quotes.quote:
bacterial vacuoles in infected host cells that shield Gram-negative pathogens 
from innate immune detection are lysed by GBPs to promote caspase-11 activation by 
leaked Escherichia coli and Citrobacter rodentium LPS in the cytoplasm

GBPs recruit the murine interferon-inducible 
protein IRGB10 to intracellular bacteria to facilitate activation of the AIM2 inflammasome 
by Francisella novicida, and activation of the non-canonical inflammasome by E. coli and C. 
rodentium

experiment.system: infected murine macrophages
experiment.perturbation: bacterial infection with GBP/IRGB10 deficiency
experiment.measurement: vacuole lysis, caspase-11 and AIM2 inflammasome activation

text: LPS internalization and caspase-11 activation in LPS-challenged mice is mediated by hepatocyte-released HMGB1, which binds LPS in circulation and facilitates cytosolic access via RAGE binding followed by lysosomal membrane permeabilization.

quotes.quote:
a recent study suggests that LPS internalization and 
caspase-11 activation in LPS-challenged mice is mediated by hepatocyte-released HMGB1, 
which physically binds LPS in circulation and facilitates its access into the cytosol of 
myeloid and endothelial cells by binding the receptor for advanced glycation end-products 
(RAGE) followed by permeabilization of the lysosomal membrane

verdict_note: The paper hedges: 'a recent study suggests that LPS internalization and caspase-11 activation ... is mediated by hepatocyte-released HMGB1'. The claim states the mechanism flatly as established, dropping the 'suggests' caveat; the listed experiment ('hepatocyte HMGB1/RAGE manipulation') is also not described in the excerpt.

experiment.system: LPS-challenged mice, myeloid and endothelial cells
experiment.perturbation: LPS challenge with hepatocyte HMGB1/RAGE manipulation
experiment.measurement: LPS internalization and caspase-11 activation

text: Genetic evidence indicates caspase-11 self-cleavage at the linker peptide separating the large and small catalytic subunits is indispensable for caspase-11 activation, unlike caspase-1, which in ASC-deficient macrophages retains the ability to induce pyroptosis to NLRC4 and NLRP1b stimuli in the apparent absence of autocleavage.

quotes.quote:
a recent report presented genetic evidence that caspase-11 self-cleavage at the 
linker peptide that separates the large and small catalytic subunits is indispensable for

text: Caspase-2 protease activity counteracts genomic instability and tumorigenesis upon cytokinesis failure and in cells with extra centrosomes by cleaving the p53 repressor MDM2, inducing cell cycle arrest.

tumorigenesis upon cytokinesis failure and in cells with extra centrosomes by cleaving the 
p53 repressor MDM2, which induces cell cycle arrest

experiment.system: cells with cytokinesis failure or extra centrosomes
experiment.perturbation: cytokinesis failure / supernumerary centrosomes with caspase-2 activity

text: Studies in genetically ablated mice established a role for caspase-14 in keratinocyte differentiation and maintenance of a normal stratum corneum, with the authors noting further analysis is required to understand the mechanisms.

Studies in

differentiation and the maintenance of a normal stratum corneum, but further analysis is 
required to fully understand the underlying mechanisms

experiment.perturbation: genetic ablation of caspase-14

text: Murine caspase-12 is a functional protease that undergoes self-cleavage in the linker peptide separating the large and small catalytic subunits at ATAD318.

murine caspase-12 is a functional protease that undergoes self-cleavage in 
the linker peptide that separates the large and small catalytic subunits at ATAD318

text: Human caspase-12 is considered a pseudoprotease: the catalytic histidine is followed by serine instead of the conserved glycine, and recombinantly purified human caspase-12 fails to cleave the synthetic peptide substrate Ac-ATAD-amc that mouse caspase-12 readily processes.

quotes.quote:
Whereas in murine caspase-12 and other caspases the catalytic histidine residue is 
invariantly followed by an evolutionary conserved glycine, this amino acid is mutated to 
serine in human caspase-12

recombinantly purified human caspase-12 fails to cleave the synthetic peptide substrate Ac-
ATAD-amc that is readily processed by mouse caspase-12 (Demon D and Lamkanfi M, 
unpublished results)

experiment.system: recombinantly purified human and mouse caspase-12
experiment.perturbation: in vitro incubation with synthetic peptide substrate Ac-ATAD-amc
experiment.measurement: substrate cleavage activity

text: A C>T single nucleotide polymorphism (rs497116) in the caspase-12 open reading frame that arose 100,000-500,000 years ago likely ablates caspase-12 protein expression in most humans, while 20-30% of the population of North and Sub-Saharan Africa lack or are heterozygous for rs497116 and express full-length caspase-12.

quotes.quote:
This is 
because of a C>T single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP; rs497116) in the caspase-12 open 
reading frame that arose 100,000-500,000 years ago, and likely causes nonsense-mediated 
decay of the corresponding transcripts. Interestingly, 20-30% of the population of North and 
Sub-Saharan Africa, lack or are heterozygous for the rs497116 SNP, and express full-length 
capase-12

experiment.system: human populations
experiment.perturbation: observational population genotyping of the caspase-12 rs497116 SNP
experiment.measurement: allele frequency and caspase-12 protein expression

text: The authors state that for human caspase-12 it is generally accepted that 75% of the population is knock-out while the remaining 25% carry a proteolytically inactive pseudoprotease.

quotes.quote:
for human caspase-12, it is generally accepted that 75% of the 
population is knock-out, while the remaining 25% carry a proteolytically inactive 
pseudoprotease (h*)

experiment.system: human population caspase-12 genotypes
experiment.perturbation: observational classification of caspase-12 alleles

text: Mice with myeloid-selective deletion of A20 develop severe inflammatory arthritis independently of TNF but mediated by NLRP3 inflammasome-induced IL-1 signalling, and RIPK1-dependent necroptosis drives inflammasome activation and inflammatory pathology in this model.

quotes.quote:
Mice with a myeloid-selective deletion 
of the NF-κB regulator A20 present with severe inflammatory arthritis that develops 
independently of TNF but is mediated by NLRP3 inflammasome-induced IL-1 signalling

RIPK1-dependent necroptosis drives inflammasome activation and inflammatory pathology 
in this mouse model of inflammatory arthritis

experiment.system: mice with myeloid-selective A20 deletion
experiment.perturbation: conditional A20 deletion, with TNF/NLRP3/IL-1/RIPK1 pathway manipulation
experiment.measurement: arthritis severity, inflammasome activation

text: Caspase-1-deficient macrophages induce caspase-8-mediated apoptosis in response to NLRP3 and AIM2 agonists, and caspase-8 activation occurs in cytosolic ASC specks during apoptosis in caspase-1-deficient macrophages, a mechanism also present in intestinal epithelial cells.

quotes.quote:
caspase-1-deficient 
macrophages induce caspase-8-mediated apoptosis in response to NLRP3 and AIM2 
agonists

caspase-8 activation occurs in cytosolic ASC specks during apoptosis in caspase-1-deficient 
macrophages, and that this mechanism also is present in intestinal epithelial cells

experiment.perturbation: caspase-1 deficiency with NLRP3, AIM2, NLRP1b or NLRC4 agonist stimulation
experiment.measurement: caspase-8 activation in ASC specks and apoptosis

text: TLR agonists upregulate c-FLIP expression in primed macrophages, suppressing caspase-8-mediated apoptosis downstream of ASC speck assembly, which the authors note is surprising given ASC expression and TLR priming were previously shown dispensable for NLRP1b- and NLRC4-induced pyroptosis.

quotes.quote:
TLR agonists upregulate c-FLIP expression in primed macrophages, which 
suppresses caspase-8-mediated apoptosis downstream of ASC speck assembly

experiment.system: primed murine macrophages
experiment.perturbation: TLR agonist priming during inflammasome activation
experiment.measurement: c-FLIP expression and caspase-8-mediated apoptosis

text: Deletion of GSDMD reroutes the inflammasome-induced cell death response to apoptosis, and caspase-1 induced apoptosis in GSDMD-deficient macrophages by engaging caspase-3 downstream of BID cleavage and the apoptosome through the intrinsic apoptosis pathway.

quotes.quote:
deletion of GSDMD similarly 
reroutes the inflammasome-induced cell death response to apoptosis

a recent report shows that caspase-1 induced apoptosis in GSDMD-deficient 
macrophages by engaging caspase-3 downstream of BID cleavage and the apoptosome 
through the intrinsic apoptosis pathway

experiment.system: GSDMD-deficient macrophages
experiment.perturbation: genetic deletion of GSDMD plus inflammasome activation
experiment.measurement: cell death mode, BID cleavage, caspase-3 activation

text: Caspase-1 activates the apoptotic executioner caspase-7 in S. Typhimurium-infected macrophages and in response to the NLRP3 agonists ATP and nigericin; deletion of caspase-7 does not protect cells from pyroptosis.

quotes.quote:
Caspase-1 has also been 
shown to activate the apoptotic executioner caspase-7 in S. Typhimurium-infected 
macrophages and in response to the NLRP3 agonists ATP and nigericin (Lamkanfi et al., 
2008). Deletion of caspase-7 does not protect cells from pyroptosis

experiment.system: macrophages
experiment.perturbation: S. Typhimurium infection or ATP/nigericin stimulation; caspase-7 deletion
experiment.measurement: caspase-7 activation and pyroptosis

text: C. difficile enterotoxins TcdA and TcdB trigger Pyrin inflammasome-dependent pyroptosis in macrophages, whereas intestinal epithelial cells lack Pyrin expression and instead engage the intrinsic apoptosis pathway, contributing to in vivo host defence against C. difficile.

quotes.quote:
C. difficile infection of macrophages 
triggers pyroptosis upon Pyrin inflammasome activation by the enterotoxins TcdA and TcdB

intestinal epithelial cells 
- the physiologic targets of TcdA and TcdB - lack Pyrin expression and the intrinsic 
apoptosis pathway instead is engaged by these enterotoxins in a process that contributes to in 
vivo host defence against C. difficile infection

experiment.system: macrophages and intestinal epithelial cells; mouse C. difficile infection
experiment.perturbation: C. difficile infection / TcdA and TcdB enterotoxin exposure
experiment.measurement: pyroptosis versus apoptosis and host defence

text: Gain-of-function NLRP1 mutations predispose patients to skin inflammation and skin cancer, with primary keratinocytes from these patients showing spontaneous inflammasome activation and elevated IL-1β amounts; other NLRP1 mutations causing elevated systemic caspase-1 and IL-18 were identified in patients with skin dyskeratosis, arthritis and periodic fever.

quotes.quote:
gain-of-function mutations in 
NLRP1 predispose patients to skin inflammation and skin cancer (Zhong et al., 2016). 
Primary keratinocytes from these patients show spontaneous inflammasome activation and 
elevated IL-1β amounts. Additionally, NLRP1 mutations that result in elevated systemic 
amounts of caspase-1 and IL-18 have been identified in patients that present with skin 
dyskeratosis, arthritis and periodic fever

experiment.system: patients with germline NLRP1 mutations and their primary keratinocytes
experiment.perturbation: naturally occurring gain-of-function NLRP1 mutations (observational)
experiment.measurement: inflammasome activation, IL-1β, systemic caspase-1 and IL-18 amounts, clinical phenotype

text: Studies in an FCAS mouse model pinpoint caspase-1-mediated cell death, IL-18 and TNF secretion as pathophysiological mechanisms in addition to IL-1β.

quotes.quote:
studies in an FCAS mouse model pinpoint caspase-1-mediated cell 
death, IL-18 and TNF secretion as additional pathophysiological mechanisms

experiment.system: FCAS (NLRP3 gain-of-function) mouse model
experiment.perturbation: NLRP3 gain-of-function mutation with cytokine/cell death pathway manipulation
experiment.measurement: cell death, IL-18 and TNF secretion, disease pathology

text: Deletion of GSDMD fully rescues systemic inflammatory pathology in mouse models of FMF and CAPS.

quotes.quote:
Recent studies show that deletion of GSDMD fully rescues systemic 
inflammatory pathology in mouse models of FMF and CAPS

experiment.system: mouse models of Familial Mediterranean Fever and CAPS
experiment.perturbation: genetic deletion of GSDMD
experiment.measurement: systemic inflammatory pathology

text: Gain-of-function NLRC4 mutations are associated with periodic fever syndromes with high circulating IL-18 and increased macrophage activation syndrome risk, and an infant with NLRC4-associated hyperinflammation diagnosed with MAS was effectively treated with recombinant IL-18 binding protein after anti-IL-1β and anti-TNF therapies were unsuccessful.

quotes.quote:
Gain-of-function mutations in NLRC4 
have been associated with periodic fever syndromes that induce high circulating IL-18 
amounts and increased risk for the development of macrophage activation syndrome (MAS)

an infant with life-threatening NLRC4-
associated hyperinflammation that was diagnosed with MAS has been effectively treated 
with recombinant IL-18 binding protein whereas anti-IL-1β and anti-TNF therapies had 
been unsuccessful

experiment.system: patients with NLRC4 gain-of-function mutations, including one infant with MAS
experiment.perturbation: treatment with recombinant IL-18 binding protein versus anti-IL-1β and anti-TNF
experiment.measurement: circulating IL-18, clinical response

text: Patients with inactivating SNPs in human CASP1 that temper or block caspase-1 protease activity and IL-1β secretion nonetheless present with severe inflammation, proposed to result from a more robust interaction between catalytically inactive caspase-1 and RIPK2.

quotes.quote:
patients with inactivating SNPs in human 
CASP1 also presented with autoinflammatory disease. While the genetic variants tempered 
or blocked caspase-1 protease activity and IL-1β secretion, the patients present with severe 
inflammation, which has been proposed to be a consequence of a more robust interaction 
between catalytically inactive caspase-1 and the NF-κB-activating kinase RIPK2

experiment.system: patients carrying inactivating CASP1 SNPs and caspase-1 variant biochemistry
experiment.perturbation: naturally occurring inactivating CASP1 variants (observational)
experiment.measurement: caspase-1 protease activity, IL-1β secretion, clinical inflammation, caspase-1–RIPK2 interaction

text: Constitutive neutralization of IL-1β carries increased risk for potentially life-threatening infections, as documented in rheumatoid arthritis patients taking anakinra and in a large cohort of atherosclerosis patients on canakinumab in the CANTOS study.

quotes.quote:
constitutive neutralization of IL-1β comes with increased risk 
for potentially life-threatening infections, as documented in rheumatoid arthritis patients 
taking anakinra (Galloway et al., 2011), and in a large cohort of atherosclerosis patients on 
canakinumab in the recently reported CANTOS study

experiment.system: rheumatoid arthritis patients and an atherosclerosis patient cohort (CANTOS)
experiment.perturbation: anakinra or canakinumab treatment (IL-1 blockade)
experiment.measurement: incidence of serious/life-threatening infections

text: Activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome in influenza A-infected cells is relayed by ZBP1 and RIPK1 together with induction of necroptosis and apoptosis.

quotes.quote:
Recent work establishes that activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome in influenza 
A-infected cells is relayed by Z-DNA binding protein 1 (ZBP1) and RIPK1 together with the 
induction of necroptosis and apoptosis

experiment.system: influenza A virus-infected cells
experiment.perturbation: influenza A infection with ZBP1/RIPK1 deficiency
experiment.measurement: NLRP3 inflammasome activation, necroptosis and apoptosis

text: The apoptosome is a cytosolic wheel-shaped multi-protein complex composed of caspase-9 and 7-8 Apaf-1 units that bind dATP and mitochondrial cytochrome c.

quotes.quote:
In addition to caspase-9, this cytosolic wheel-shaped multi-protein complex is 
composed of 7-8 Apoptotic peptidase activating factor 1 (Apaf-1) units that bind the 
nucleotide dATP and mitochondrial cytochrome c

experiment.system: apoptosome complex in the intrinsic apoptosis pathway
experiment.perturbation: observational structural/biochemical characterization
experiment.measurement: complex composition and stoichiometry

text: Generation of caspase-1-deficient mice confirmed the essential role of caspase-1 in IL-1β secretion and demonstrated that caspase-1 is largely dispensable for apoptosis.

The subsequent generation of caspase-1-deficient mice confirmed the essential role of caspase-1 
in IL-1β secretion and demonstrated that caspase-1 is largely dispensable for apoptosis.

text: Extensive apoptosis and active caspase-3 staining have been documented in splenic white pulp regions of critically ill patients, and caspase inhibition significantly improves survival rates in animal models of sepsis.

quotes.quote:
Extensive apoptosis and active caspase-3

experiment.perturbation: observational staining; caspase inhibition in animal models

Extensive apoptosis also contributes to hepatocellular pathology in a mouse 
model of anti-Fas antibody-induced fulminant hepatitis by inducing activation of caspase-8

experiment.perturbation: anti-Fas antibody administration
experiment.measurement: caspase-8 and caspase-9 activation and hepatocellular pathology

text: Caspase-1-mediated cleavage of gasdermin D promotes formation of GSDMD membrane pores and cell lysis, identifying the necrotic execution mechanism of pyroptosis.

the discovery that caspase-1-mediated cleavage of the cytosolic protein gasdermin D

much needed light on the necrotic execution mechanism of pyroptosis

experiment.perturbation: caspase-1-mediated GSDMD cleavage / GSDMD deletion
experiment.measurement: membrane pore formation and cell lysis

text: The requirement for FADD in necroptosis is cell-type dependent: absence of FADD sensitizes some cells, including Jurkat lymphocytes, to necrotic cell death, whereas MEFs from FADD-deficient mice are resistant to TNF-induced necroptosis.

The absence of FADD sensitizes some cells, including Jurkat 
lymphocytes, to necrotic cell death9,35. In contrast, MEFs 
isolated from FADD-deficient mice are resistant to 
TNF-induced necroptosis57.

experiment.perturbation: FADD deficiency
experiment.measurement: susceptibility to necrotic/TNF-induced necroptotic cell death

text: TRADD's role in complex II is contested: TNF-induced apoptosis and necroptosis are blocked in TRADD-deficient cells, whereas TRADD is undetectable in complex II formed with SMAC mimetics and RNAi knockdown of TRADD stimulates complex II formation in some cell types.
