experiment.perturbation: nigericin (10 μM) or ATP (4 mM) 1 h; ± EtBr mtDNA depletion
experiment.measurement: agarose gel electrophoresis of fractionated DNA

numbers.quantity: size of mtDNA retained in mitochondria

text: Only a 591 bp, not a 5698 bp, mtDNA stretch could be PCR-amplified from the cytosol and only after NLRP3 activator exposure; the entire 16299 bp mitochondrial genome was higher after LPS priming but lower after agonist challenge.

quotes.quote:
We PCR amplified 591 bp or 5698 bp 
mtDNA stretches from the mitochondrial and cytosolic DNA pools of LPS-primed BMDM 
challenged with different NLRP3 activators. Although LPS increased the amounts of both 
DNA stretches in the mitochondrial pool, only the shorter DNA could be amplified from 
the cytosol and only after exposure to NLRP3 activators (Figure 5B). PCR amplification 
revealed that amounts of the entire mitochondrial genome (16299 bp) were higher after LPS 
priming, but lower after NLRP3 agonist challenge (Figure S5C).

experiment.system: LPS-primed BMDM mitochondrial and cytosolic DNA pools
experiment.perturbation: challenge with different NLRP3 activators
experiment.measurement: long-range PCR amplification of 591 bp, 5698 bp and 16299 bp mtDNA stretches

text: Silencing of Mgme1 or Fen1, but not Mre11a, attenuated NLRP3 inflammasome activation and inhibited cytosolic Ox-mtDNA and mtDNA release; Mgme1 silencing reduced mtDNA amounts in LPS-primed cells while Fen1 silencing did not.

quotes.quote:
silencing of mitochondrial genome maintenance exonuclease 1 (Mgme1) or flap structure-
specific endonuclease 1 (Fen1), but not meiotic recombination 11 homolog A (Mre11a), 
all of which participate in mtDNA metabolism (Fontana and Gahlon, 2020), attenuated 
NLRP3 inflammasome activation (Figures 5C, 5D and S5D). Accordingly, Mgme1 or 
Fen1 silencing inhibited cytosolic Ox-mtDNA and mtDNA release (Figures 5E and 5F).
reduced mtDNA amounts in LPS-primed cells, Fen1 silencing did not (Figure S5E)

experiment.system: LPS-primed BMDM transduced with shCtrl, shMgme1, shMre11a or shFen1
experiment.perturbation: shRNA knockdown plus ATP (4 mM, 1 h) challenge
experiment.measurement: immunoblot of Casp1 p20/IL-1β and cytosolic Ox-mtDNA/mtDNA quantification

text: Fen1 silencing inhibited mtDNA fragmentation and cytosolic release and attenuated mtDNA integrity loss in ATP- or nigericin-challenged BMDM.

quotes.quote:
Fen1 silencing inhibited mtDNA fragmentation and cytosolic release (Figure 
5G), and attenuated mtDNA integrity loss in ATP or nigericin challenged BMDM (Figures 
5H and 5I).

experiment.system: LPS-primed shCtrl- or shFen1-transduced BMDM
experiment.perturbation: ATP or nigericin challenge
experiment.measurement: agarose gel of cytosolic/mitochondrial DNA and long-range mtDNA PCR

text: The FEN1 inhibitor FEN1-IN-4 abrogated mtDNA fragmentation and cytosolic Ox-mtDNA and mtDNA release, causing dose-dependent inhibition of Casp1 activation and IL-1β but not TNF secretion, without affecting LPS-stimulated mtDNA synthesis, Ox-mtDNA generation, mtROS, mPTP opening or VDAC oligomerization.

quotes.quote:
The FEN1 inhibitor FEN1-IN-4 (Exell et al., 2016), also abrogated mtDNA 
fragmentation and cytosolic Ox-mtDNA and mtDNA release (Figures 5J–L), resulting in 
dose-dependent inhibition of Casp1 activation and IL-1β, but not TNF, secretion (Figures 
5M and S5F–S5H). FEN1-IN-4 did not affect LPS-stimulated mtDNA synthesis (Figure 
S5I) and like Fen1 shRNA, had no effect on Ox-mtDNA generation or mtROS production 
(Figures S5J and S5K). Moreover, FEN1 did not affect mPTP opening (Figure S5L) 
or VDAC oligomerization (Figures S5M and S5N)

experiment.system: BMDM
experiment.perturbation: FEN1-IN-4 (10 μM, 16 h) pretreatment, LPS priming, ATP or nigericin challenge
experiment.measurement: agarose gel DNA analysis, cytosolic mtDNA/Ox-mtDNA, immunoblot/ELISA, calcein and VDAC cross-linking assays

text: FEN1-IN-4 inhibited alum-induced IL-1β production in vivo and reduced neutrophil and monocyte infiltration without affecting TNF.

quotes.quote:
FEN1-IN-4 inhibited alum-induced NLRP3 
inflammasome-dependent IL-1β production in vivo and reduced neutrophil and monocyte 
infiltration, without an effect on TNF secretion (Figures 5N and 5O).

experiment.system: mice with alum-induced peritonitis
experiment.perturbation: FEN1-IN-4 (40 mg/kg) 16 h prior to i.p. alum or PBS
experiment.measurement: peritoneal IL-1β/TNF ELISA and flow cytometry of neutrophils and monocytes

text: ccf-mtDNA was elevated in BALF of LPS-challenged ARDS mice and in peritoneal exudates after alum challenge, and both were reduced in mt-Ogg1Tg mice; alum-induced ccf-mtDNA contained oxidative lesions that were reduced by mt-OGG1.

quotes.quote:
BALF of 
LPS-challenged mice undergoing ARDS contained elevated ccf-mtDNA amounts that were 
reduced in mt-Ogg1Tg mice (Figure 6A). Cell-free peritoneal exudates isolated 4 hrs after 
alum challenge also contained more ccf-mtDNA than exudates from PBS-injected mice, and 
this was reduced in mt-Ogg1Tg mice (Figure 6B).

Alum-induced ccf-mtDNA contained oxidative lesions and that 
was reduced by mt-OGG1 (Figure 6C).

experiment.system: WT and mt-Ogg1Tg mice
experiment.perturbation: LPS-induced ARDS or alum-induced peritonitis
experiment.measurement: qPCR of ccf-mtDNA in BALF/peritoneal exudate and Fpg-sensitive qPCR for oxidative lesions

text: FEN1-IN-4 inhibited ccf-mtDNA and Ox-mtDNA secretion into peritoneal exudates isolated 4 and 16 hrs post-challenge.

quotes.quote:
FEN1-IN-4 inhibited ccf-mtDNA and 
Ox-mtDNA secretion into peritoneal exudates isolated 4 and 16 hrs post-challenge (Figures 
6D, 6E, S6A and S6B)

experiment.system: alum-challenged mice
experiment.perturbation: FEN1-IN-4 pretreatment
experiment.measurement: qPCR of ccf-mtDNA and Fpg-based Ox-mtDNA in peritoneal exudates at 4 and 16 hrs

text: Gsdmd−/− BMDM released much less Ox-mtDNA but generated as much Ox-mtDNA as WT BMDM.

quotes.quote:
gasdermin 
D deficient BMDM (Gsdmd−/−) released much less Ox-mtDNA but generated as much 
Ox-mtDNA as WT BMDM (Figures S6C–E).

experiment.system: WT and Gsdmd−/− BMDM
experiment.perturbation: NLRP3 activator challenge
experiment.measurement: extracellular and intracellular Ox-mtDNA quantification

text: Cell-free mtDNA released by challenged BMDM induced Il1b, Il6, Tnf and the ISGs Cxcl10, Isg15, Ifit3 and Irf7 in naïve macrophages in a DNase I sensitive manner; EtBr pretreatment of donors reduced cell-free mtDNA and its immunostimulatory activity, and CsA, VBIT-4 and FEN1-IN-4 inhibited both release and activity.

quotes.quote:
When applied to naïve macrophages, cell-free 
mtDNA induced NF-κB-dependent cytokine mRNAs, Il1b, Il6 and Tnf, and IFN-stimulated 
genes (ISGs), Cxcl10, Isg15, Ifit3 and Irf7 in a DNase I sensitive manner (Figure 6I). EtBr 
pretreatment greatly reduced cell-free mtDNA amounts and immunostimulatory activity 
(Figures S6F and S6G), validating its mitochondrial origin. CsA, VBIT-4 and FEN1-IN-4 
also inhibited cell-free mtDNA release (Figure S6H) and immunostimulatory activity 
(Figure 6J).

experiment.system: recipient naïve BMDM incubated with cell-free DNA from donor BMDM
experiment.perturbation: donor treatment with NLRP3 activators ± EtBr, CsA, VBIT-4, FEN1-IN-4; ± DNase I digestion of DNA
experiment.measurement: qPCR of cytokine and ISG mRNAs and extracellular mtDNA quantification

text: Pitstop2, an inhibitor of clathrin-mediated endocytosis, diminished cytokine mRNA induction by extracellular mtDNA.

quotes.quote:
we used Pitstop2, 
an inhibitor of clathrin-mediated endocytosis (von Kleist et al., 2011) and found it to 
diminish cytokine mRNA induction by extracellular mtDNA (Figure S6I).

experiment.system: recipient BMDM
experiment.perturbation: Pitstop2 treatment during extracellular mtDNA exposure
experiment.measurement: qPCR of cytokine mRNAs

text: cGAS or STING ablation blunted cytokine and ISG mRNA induction by extracellular mtDNA.

quotes.quote:
cGAS or STING ablation also blunted cytokine and ISG mRNA induction by extracellular 
mtDNA (Figures S7A and S7B).

experiment.system: cGAS−/− and Sting−/− BMDM
experiment.perturbation: treatment with extracellular mtDNA
experiment.measurement: qPCR of cytokine and ISG mRNAs

text: ATP or nigericin stimulation of LPS-primed BMDM induced rapid formation of Ser365-phosphorylated STING puncta, diminished by mtOGG1 expression and by CsA, VBIT-4 and FEN1-IN-4.

quotes.quote:
cytosolic release of Ox-mtDNA in LPS-
primed BMDM stimulated with ATP or nigericin induced rapid formation of Ser365 
phosphorylated STING puncta, which are essential for interferon regulatory factor-3 (IRF3) 
binding and activation (Chen et al., 2016; Liu et al., 2015). That was diminished by 
mtOGG1 expression and CsA, VBIT-4 and FEN1-IN-4 treatments (Figures 7A, 7B, S7C 
and S7D).

experiment.system: LPS-primed WT and mt-Ogg1Tg BMDM
experiment.perturbation: ATP or nigericin stimulation ± CsA, VBIT-4, FEN1-IN-4
experiment.measurement: phospho-STING (Ser365) puncta immunofluorescence

text: ATP-induced STING Ser365 phosphorylation was detectable by immunoblot, was undetectable in EtBr-treated mtDNA-depleted BMDM, and the response to ATP and nigericin was abolished in mt-Ogg1Tg BMDM.

quotes.quote:
ATP-induced STING Ser365 phosphorylation was also detected by immunoblot 
analysis and was strictly dependent on mtDNA as it was undetectable in EtBr-treated 
BMDM (Figures 7C and 7D). Nigericin also led to immunoblot detectable STING Ser365 
phosphorylation and the response to it and ATP were abolished in mt-Ogg1Tg BMDM 
(Figures S7E and S7F).

experiment.system: BMDM, EtBr-depleted BMDM, mt-Ogg1Tg BMDM
experiment.perturbation: EtBr (450 ng/mL, 4 days) mtDNA depletion; LPS priming and ATP or nigericin
experiment.measurement: immunoblot of p-STING Ser365 relative to total STING

text: Nlrp3−/− BMDM exhibited enhanced ATP-induced STING Ser365 phosphorylation, which was completely blocked by CsA, VBIT-4 or FEN1-IN-4.

quotes.quote:
we observed that Nlrp3−/− BMDM, in which Casp1 is 
not activated, exhibited enhanced ATP-induced STING Ser365 phosphorylation, that was 
completely blocked by CsA, VBIT-4 or FEN1-IN-4 (Figures 7E and 7F)

experiment.system: LPS-primed WT and Nlrp3−/− BMDM
experiment.perturbation: ATP stimulation ± CsA (1 μM), VBIT-4 (10 μM) or FEN1-IN-4 (10 μM)
experiment.measurement: immunoblot of p-STING Ser365 relative to total STING

text: Increasing the binding valency from 3 to 4 reduces the threshold to form condensates between proline-rich motifs and SH3 domains by about 10-fold, illustrating a non-linear relationship between valency and phase separation threshold.

quotes.quote:
For example, increasing the binding valency from 3 to 4 reduces the threshold to form 
condensates between proline-rich motifs and SH3 domains by about 10-fold18.

experiment.system: Purified multivalent proline-rich motif and SH3 domain proteins in vitro (reconstituted droplets)
experiment.perturbation: Varying binding valency from 3 to 4
experiment.measurement: Concentration threshold for condensate formation

numbers.quantity: fold reduction in phase separation threshold

text: The protein concentration threshold to induce condensates on a 2D membrane is much lower than in 3D solution, which the authors attribute to membranes restricting protein motion and increasing effective macromolecular concentrations.

quotes.quote:
First, membranes restrict the motion of proteins, which increases their 
effective macromolecular concentrations and accelerates biochemical reactions by orders of 
magnitude as compared to a 3D environment35. Indeed, the protein concentration threshold 
to induce condensates on the 2D membrane is much lower than in 3D solution19, 20, 36.

experiment.system: Membrane-bound versus solution reconstitution of multivalent signalling proteins
experiment.perturbation: Comparing protein condensation on 2D membranes versus in 3D solution
experiment.measurement: Protein concentration threshold for condensate formation

text: Phosphorylation of LAT downstream of antigenic TCR stimulation drives liquid-like microcluster formation via LLPS of LAT and its binding partners, shown in a supported lipid bilayer-based reconstitution system.

quotes.quote:
To 
determine the mechanism of microcluster formation in the context of the plasma membrane, 
a supported lipid bilayer-based reconstitution system was established61. It was shown that 
LAT microclusters have liquid-like properties and are formed through LLPS of LAT and 
its binding partners2.

antigenic stimuli to TCR trigger the downstream 
phosphorylation of LAT, which drives liquid-like microcluster formation to promote T cell 
activation2

experiment.system: Supported lipid bilayer reconstitution of TCR signalling components; T cells
experiment.perturbation: Phosphorylation of LAT downstream of TCR/antigen engagement
experiment.measurement: Imaging of microcluster formation and liquid-like properties

text: LAT condensates promote tyrosine phosphorylation by enriching kinases and excluding phosphatases; the exclusion is charge-dependent, with negatively charged LAT condensates partially excluding the negatively charged phosphatase CD45, and can also be mediated by protein size.

quotes.quote:
LAT condensates promote tyrosine 
phosphorylation, which is a key activation marker for the TCR signaling pathway. This 
is achieved by the enrichment of kinases in clusters, but exclusion of phosphatases. 
Interestingly, the exclusion properties of LAT condensates are dependent on charge: LAT 
condensates are negatively charged and therefore partially exclude negatively charged 
phosphatases such as CD452. In addition to charge, the exclusion can also be mediated 
by other factors including protein size65.

experiment.system: Reconstituted LAT condensates on supported lipid bilayers
experiment.perturbation: Condensate formation and variation of partitioning molecule charge/size
experiment.measurement: Partitioning/exclusion of kinases and phosphatases; tyrosine phosphorylation

text: LAT condensates promote downstream RAS signalling and actin remodelling by increasing the membrane dwell time of SOS1 and N-WASp.

quotes.quote:
Moreover, LAT condensates promote downstream 
signaling pathways by increasing the membrane dwell time of SOS1 and N-WASp, which 
activate the RAS signaling pathway and actin remodeling, respectively3, 66.

experiment.system: Reconstituted LAT condensates with SOS1 and N-WASp on membranes
experiment.perturbation: LAT condensate formation
experiment.measurement: Single-molecule membrane dwell time and downstream pathway activation

text: LAT is dispensable for microcluster formation of chimeric antigen receptors, unlike its essential role in TCR pathway microclusters.

quotes.quote:
although LAT is the key to driving microcluster formation in the TCR signaling pathway, 
it is dispensable for microcluster formation of chimeric antigen receptors (CARs)69.

experiment.system: T cells expressing chimeric antigen receptors
experiment.perturbation: Loss/absence of LAT
experiment.measurement: Imaging of receptor microcluster formation

text: SLP65 forms liquid-like condensates with trimeric CIN85 through SH3-domain/proline-rich motif multivalent interactions; the condensates are pre-formed in the cytoplasm of resting B cells and associate with the plasma membrane after BCR activation.

quotes.quote:
It has been shown 
that SLP65 forms liquid-like condensates with its binding partner CIN85 (also known 
as SH3KBP1) through a classical multivalent interaction between the SH3 domains of 
trimeric CIN85 and the proline-rich motifs of SLP65 (FIG. 3)4, 73.

SLP65 
condensates are pre-formed in the cytoplasm of resting B cells and associate with the 
plasma membrane following BCR activation74.

experiment.system: Purified SLP65 and CIN85 in vitro and B cells
experiment.perturbation: BCR activation; reconstitution of SLP65–CIN85 interaction
experiment.measurement: Imaging of condensate formation and subcellular localization

text: SLP65's N-terminal lipid-binding domain recognizes small unilamellar vesicles with radii of 20 nm but not large unilamellar vesicles with radii of 60 nm, and Cryo-ET showed liposomes in reconstituted condensates spaced on average 5 nm apart.

quotes.quote: SLP65 contains an amino-terminal lipid-binding domain that recognizes small

unilamellar vesicles with radii of 20 nm, but not large unilamellar vesicles with radii of 
60 nm4.

Cryo-electron tomography (Cryo-ET) imaging has shown that liposomes in the in vitro-
reconstituted condensates are spaced on average 5 nm apart.

experiment.system: In vitro reconstituted SLP65–CIN85–vesicle condensates
experiment.perturbation: Varying liposome size (small vs large unilamellar vesicles)
experiment.measurement: Binding assays and Cryo-ET imaging of inter-liposome spacing

numbers.quantity: radius of small unilamellar vesicles bound
radius of large unilamellar vesicles not bound

text: SLP65 mutants lacking the N-terminal vesicle-binding domain fail to form condensates and show BCR signalling defects such as impaired calcium influx, which are rescued by fusing the vesicle-recognizing N-BAR domain to the truncation mutant.

quotes.quote:
SLP65 mutants lacking the N-terminal 
vesicle-binding domain cannot form condensates either in the cytoplasm or on the 
plasma membrane, which is accompanied by defects in BCR signaling (for example, 
calcium influx). Importantly, these defects can be rescued by fusing another vesicle-
recognizing domain (N-BAR) to the N-terminal truncation mutant of SLP654.

experiment.system: B cells expressing SLP65 truncation and N-BAR fusion mutants
experiment.perturbation: Deletion of the SLP65 N-terminal vesicle-binding domain and rescue with N-BAR fusion
experiment.measurement: Condensate formation imaging and BCR-induced calcium influx

text: In B cell membranes, BCRs are selectively enriched in the liquid-ordered phase, which is enriched in LYN and depleted of CD45; increasing cholesterol promoted BCR signalling by stimulating calcium influx whereas decreasing cholesterol reduced calcium influx.

quotes.quote:
BCRs are selectively enriched in 
liquid-ordered phase and BCR nanoclusters overlap with specific lipid and protein probes on 
the B cell membrane77. Increasing cholesterol levels promoted BCR signaling by stimulating 
calcium influx, whereas decreasing cholesterol levels resulted in reduced calcium influx. 
The liquid-ordered phase is also enriched in the Src kinase LYN and depleted of the 
phosphatase CD45, which thereby promoted signaling propagation5.

experiment.system: B lymphocyte plasma membranes
experiment.perturbation: Increasing or decreasing membrane cholesterol levels
experiment.measurement: Imaging of BCR/probe partitioning into ordered phase and calcium influx

text: DNA binding induces cGAS liquid-like condensates whose formation requires multivalent elements including the positively charged N-terminal domain of cGAS, long DNA strands (>100 base pairs) and free zinc ions, with an additional DNA-binding domain in the catalytic core enhancing condensation; condensation promotes cGAS activity by protecting DNA from TREX1 degradation.

quotes.quote:
Several essential multivalent 
elements are involved in the formation of cGAS–dsDNA condensates, including the 
positively charged N-terminal domain of cGAS, long DNA strands (>100 base pairs) and 
free zinc ions. A newly identified DNA-binding domain in the catalytic core of cGAS also 
enhances condensate formation85. Functionally, the formation of condensates can promote 
cGAS activity by protecting DNA from degradation by the exonuclease TREX186.

experiment.system: Purified cGAS with dsDNA in vitro and cells
experiment.perturbation: Varying DNA length, zinc, and cGAS domain mutations
experiment.measurement: Condensate formation imaging, DNA degradation by TREX1, cGAS activity

numbers.quantity: DNA length required for cGAS condensates

text: cGAS forms liquid-like condensates with dsRNA, but dsRNA does not activate cGAS to produce cGAMP.

quotes.quote:
In 
addition to DNA, cGAS also forms liquid-like condensates with dsRNA though dsRNA 
does not activate cGAS to produce cGAMP6.

experiment.system: Purified cGAS with nucleic acids
experiment.perturbation: Addition of dsRNA versus dsDNA
experiment.measurement: Condensate formation and cGAMP production

text: Two tumour-associated cGAS mutations, G303E and K432T, at one of the DNA-binding sites reduce the ability to form cGAS condensates and decrease cGAMP production; the authors note the mutations may also affect DNA binding and enzymatic activity, so causality is unresolved.

quotes.quote:
Two tumor-associated mutations, G303E and K432T, at one of the DNA-binding sites 
of cGAS result in a reduced ability to form cGAS condensates and decreased cGAMP 
production85. However, these mutations may also affect DNA binding and enzymatic 
activity, so it is not known whether the reduced ability to form condensates explains the 
decreased cGAMP production.

experiment.system: Human cGAS with DNA-binding-site mutations
experiment.perturbation: G303E and K432T point mutations
experiment.measurement: Condensate formation and cGAMP production

text: Streptavidin, a secreted protein from Streptomyces avidinii, binds cGAS to enhance cGAS–DNA interactions and promote LLPS of the complex, resulting in enhanced cGAS activation and interferon-β production.

quotes.quote:
Streptavidin, 
a secreted protein from the bacterium Streptomyces avidinii, binds to cGAS to enhance

cGAS–DNA interactions and promote LLPS of this complex. This results in enhanced 
cGAS activation and interferon-β production88.

experiment.system: cGAS–DNA system with bacterial streptavidin
experiment.perturbation: Addition of streptavidin
experiment.measurement: cGAS–DNA binding, phase separation, cGAS activation and IFN-β production

text: Herpesvirus proteins ORF52 and VP22 inhibit cGAS activity by disrupting cGAS–DNA droplet formation through forming new droplets of viral protein and DNA; DNA preferentially forms droplets with ORF52 rather than cGAS even though ORF52's DNA-binding affinity is lower than that of cGAS.

quotes.quote:
herpesvirus protein ORF52 and VP22, which 
inhibit cGAS activity, disrupt cGAS-DNA droplet formation. This disruption depends on 
the formation of new droplets composed of viral proteins and DNA. Interestingly, DNA 
preferentially forms droplets with ORF52 other than cGAS, even though the DNA-binding 
affinity of ORF52 is lower than the one of cGAS89.

experiment.system: In vitro cGAS–DNA droplets with herpesvirus tegument proteins
experiment.perturbation: Addition of ORF52 or VP22
experiment.measurement: Droplet composition/formation and cGAS activity

text: G3BP1 is required for efficient DNA sensing and cGAS activation: the percentage of cells containing cGAS condensates was significantly reduced in G3BP1-deficient cells, and this regulatory function does not depend on stress granules.

quotes.quote:
The percentage 
of cells containing cGAS condensates was significantly reduced in G3BP1-deficient cells. 
Interestingly, the regulatory function of G3BP1 on cGAS phase separation does not depend 
on stress granules91.

experiment.system: G3BP1-deficient versus control cells
experiment.perturbation: G3BP1 deficiency
experiment.measurement: Percentage of cells containing cGAS condensates; cGAS activation

text: In the presence of excess cGAMP, STING forms condensates with stacked ER membrane that recruit TBK1 but exclude IRF3 and thereby lose the ability to trigger robust interferon production, whereas the multivalent STING agonist PC7A triggers STING condensates that stimulate prolonged pro-inflammatory cytokine production.

quotes.quote:
A recent study showed that STING forms condensates 
with stacked ER membrane in the presence of excess amount of cGAMP. The STING 
condensates recruit the downstream signaling kinase TBK1 but exclude the transcription 
factor IRF3, and thereby lose the ability to trigger robust interferon production7. 
Interestingly, another recent study showed that a multivalent STING agonist PC7A triggers 
STING condensate formation and stimulates the prolonged production of pro-inflammatory 
cytokines93.

experiment.system: Cells expressing STING
experiment.perturbation: Excess cGAMP or treatment with the multivalent agonist PC7A
experiment.measurement: STING condensate formation, TBK1/IRF3 partitioning, interferon and cytokine production

text: RNA binding triggers LLPS of TRIM25, which recruits RIG-I to condensates and increases its ubiquitylation by TRIM25 (reported in a preprint the authors note is not yet peer reviewed).

quotes.quote:
A recent preprint 
(not yet peer-reviewed) showed that RNA binding triggers LLPS of TRIM25, which recruits 
RIG-I to condensates and increases its ubiquitylation by TRIM258 (FIG. 4b).

experiment.system: TRIM25 and RIG-I with RNA
experiment.perturbation: RNA binding to TRIM25
experiment.measurement: Condensate formation, RIG-I recruitment, RIG-I ubiquitylation

text: G3BP1 acts as a positive regulator of RIG-I signalling: it interacts with RNF125 in virus-induced stress granules to promote its auto-ubiquitylation and degradation, and interacts with RIG-I to enhance its binding to dsRNA and downstream signalling.

quotes.quote:
G3BP1, the core component of phase-separated stress granules, directly 
interacts with RNF125 in virus-induced stress granules to promote its auto-ubiquitylation 
and degradation. G3BP1 also interacts with RIG-I to enhance its binding to dsRNA and 
downstream signaling pathways94, 97.

experiment.system: Virus-infected cells with stress granules
experiment.perturbation: Virus infection / G3BP1 interaction with RNF125 and RIG-I
experiment.measurement: RNF125 ubiquitylation and degradation; RIG-I–dsRNA binding and downstream signalling

text: In respiratory syncytial virus-infected cells the NF-κB subunit p65 is rapidly sequestered into perinuclear intracytoplasmic puncta (inclusion bodies) and cannot translocate into the nucleus to activate downstream transcription; MAVS and MDA5 are similarly recruited into RSV-induced inclusion bodies, inhibiting interferon-β expression, and sequestration of phosphorylated p38 MAPK and O-linked N-acetylglucosamine transferase suppresses MK2 signalling and stress granule formation.

quotes.quote:
In RSV-infected cells, the NF-κB subunit 
p65 is rapidly sequestered into perinuclear intracytoplasmic puncta that are synonymous 
with inclusion bodies (FIG. 4c). The trapped p65 cannot translocate into the nucleus to 
activate the downstream transcription of pro-inflammatory cytokine genes and other antiviral 
genes9. Similarly, MAVS and MDA5, two upstream regulators of the NF-κB pathway, 
are recruited into RSV-induced inclusion bodies as a mechanism to inhibit the expression 
of interferon-β104.

the sequestration of phosphorylated p38 mitogen-
activated protein kinase (MAPK) and O-linked N-acetylglucosamine transferase into RSV-
induced inclusion bodies can suppress MAPK-activated protein kinase 2 signaling and stress 
granule formation, respectively, both of which would otherwise inhibit RSV replication105.

experiment.system: Cells infected with respiratory syncytial virus
experiment.perturbation: RSV infection
experiment.measurement: Localization of p65, MAVS, MDA5, p-p38 and OGT to inclusion bodies; nuclear translocation, IFN-β expression, stress granule formation

text: In a library with fixed Pro at pS+2 and four degenerate residues on each side, all 14-3-3 isotypes strongly selected Arg at pS-4, with preference values generally exceeding 4, approximately 1.7-fold higher than those for Arg at pS-3.

quotes.quote:
All 14-3-3 isotypes strongly selected for
peptides with Arg in the pS 24 position (Table 1), with
preference values generally exceeding 4, approximately
1.7-fold higher than those observed for Arg in the pS 23
position.

experiment.system: GST- or MBP-fusions of 14-3-3 isotypes
experiment.perturbation: screening with library MAXXXXpSXPXXAKK
experiment.measurement: selectivity (preference) values from sequencing of bound peptides

numbers.quantity: preference value for Arg at pS-4

text: In the complex the bound peptide adopts an extended main chain conformation at either edge of the conserved channel of the 14-3-3 dimer, with the phosphoserine coordinated by salt bridges to Arg-56, Arg-127 and Lys-49 and a hydrogen bond to Tyr-128; Arg-60 adjoins the basic pocket but does not contact the phosphate.

quotes.quote:
The structure of the complex shows that the bound
peptide adopts an extended main chain conformation
(Figures 4A and 4B) and is situated at either edge of
the conserved channel of the 14-3-3 dimer (Figure 4C).
Phosphoserine coordination includes salt bridges to the
the side chains of Arg-56, Arg-127, and Lys-49, and a
hydrogen bond to the hydroxyl group of Tyr-128

Arg-60 adjoins the basic pocket but does not interact
directly with the pSer phosphate.

experiment.system: 14-3-3z:mT phosphopeptide cocrystal
experiment.perturbation: observational (structure determination)
experiment.measurement: electron density maps and modeled atomic interactions at 2.6 A

text: Weighted screening of all mammalian sequences in SWISS-PROT using mode 1 or mode 2 preference values found about 30,000 potential sites in 12,000 protein sequences examined; known and several novel candidate 14-3-3 partners appeared within the top 5% of highest scores.

quotes.quote: About 30,000 potential sites

were identified in 12,000 protein sequences examined
and further evaluated. A variety of potentially important
14-3-3 interacting proteins were identified within the top
5% of highest scores, some of which are listed in Table
3.

experiment.system: mammalian sequences in the SWISS-PROT database
experiment.perturbation: observational; weighted scoring using peptide library preference values for mode 1 and mode 2 motifs
experiment.measurement: number of predicted sites and ranking of candidate binding proteins

text: ErbB3 lacks intrinsic kinase activity and ErbB2 has no known high-affinity ligand, so neither can support linear signalling in isolation.

quotes.quote:
ErbB3 is devoid of
intrinsic kinase activity12,whereas ErbB2 seems to have
no direct ligand13.Therefore,in isolation neither ErbB2
nor ErbB3 can support linear signalling

ErbB2 (also known as HER2) is a more potent
oncoprotein than the other ErbBs, but no known lig-
and binds it with high affinity.

experiment.system: human/rodent ErbB receptors expressed in cells and as recombinant proteins (reviewed)
experiment.perturbation: observational; comparison of isolated receptors versus dimeric combinations
experiment.measurement: intrinsic tyrosine kinase activity and ligand binding

text: Heterodimeric ErbB combinations are more mitogenic and transforming than homodimers, with ErbB2-containing heterodimers the most potent, and the ErbB2-ErbB3 heterodimer the most transforming and mitogenic complex that also increases cell motility on ligand stimulation.

quotes.quote:
homodimeric receptor combinations are
less mitogenic and transforming than the correspond-
ing heterodimeric combinations,and ErbB2-containing
heterodimers are the most potent complexes21–23

although neither ErbB2
nor ErbB3 alone can be activated by ligand, the het-

cytes revealed a nanometer proximity between subpo-
pulations of AC5 and the L-type Ca2+ subunit Cav1.2.

ity, increased [Ca2+]i, and vasoconstriction

first report documenting localization of PDEs at this

text: In breast cancer cells, inhibition of EPAC1 disrupted the association of AKAP9 with the microtubule cytoskeleton and delocalized AKAP9 from the centrosome, with effects on cell migration and cell death.

In breast cancer cells, inhibition of EPAC1 was

the centrosome, with effects on cell migration and cell
death (Kumar et al., 2017).

coexpres-

thy (Tang et al., 2013).

text: In cardiomyocytes fluorescence recovery after photobleaching showed RI, similarly to RII, is largely anchored to AKAPs, and targeted cAMP FRET sensors demonstrated that PKA type I and type II define distinct intracellular signaling compartments.

text: Disruption of the mAKAP-AC5 interaction in neonatal cardiac myocytes increases cAMP and produces hypertrophy without agonist stimulation, consistent with PKA feedback phosphorylation inhibiting AC5 in the mAKAP complex.

AC5 activity is inhibited by PKA feedback phosphory-
lation when the cyclase is associated with the mAKAP

mAKAP is
expressed at very low levels in myocytes, such that loss

text: In HEK-293 cell nuclei, AC10-generated cAMP activates a resident nuclear PKA holoenzyme once local cAMP exceeds the threshold kept low by AKAP8-assembled PDE4D3/5, giving faster activation kinetics than catalytic-subunit translocation; the authors note that Yang et al. failed to reproduce these observations in primary rat neonatal cardiac myocytes and attribute the kinetics to diffusion and protein kinase inhibitor expression.

Sample et al. reported the activation of a resident pool of
PKA holoenzyme in the nuclei of HEK-293 cells by AC10.

when
cAMP is produced locally by AC10 and above that
threshold, activation of the local PKA occurs, resulting
in faster activation kinetics compared with slow kinetics
associated with translocation of C subunit to the nucleus
(Sample et al., 2012).

However, Yang et al. failed to
reproduce these observations in primary rat neonatal
cardiac myocytes.

text: In retinal ganglion cells, real-time cAMP imaging plus tools generating or buffering cAMP in restricted domains showed that a decrease in cAMP at the plasma membrane proximal to lipid rafts mediates ephrine-A-induced axon retraction in vitro and arbor pruning in vivo, whereas manipulation at nonraft domains had no effect on pruning and raft manipulation had no effect on axon outgrowth.

the study found that it is specifically a de-
crease in cAMP occurring at the plasma membrane
proximally to lipid rafts that is responsible for the

A recent study using targeted cAMP
FRET-based reporters demonstrated that b-AR stimu-
lation results in distinct signals at these sites and that
the cAMP increase is delayed and attenuated at the
myofilaments compared with the plasmalemma and
sarcoplasmic reticulum (Surdo et al., 2017).

upon application of PDE
inhibitors, a maneuver that generates overall a larger
increase in cAMP but abolishes local differences, a weaker
contraction was detected.

text: In experimental models of cardiac hypertrophy and heart failure, the b-AR-stimulated cAMP signal was nearly abolished at the myofilament but well preserved at plasmalemma and sarcoplasmic reticulum.

quotes.quote:
in experimental
models of cardiac disease, such as cardiac hypertrophy
and heart failure, which are characterized by down-
regulation of the adrenergic pathway, the cAMP signal
triggered by b-AR stimulation was nearly abolished
at the myofilament but was well preserved at plasma-
lemma and sarcoplasmic reticulum.

experiment.perturbation: b-AR stimulation
experiment.measurement: targeted cAMP reporter signals at myofilament, plasmalemma, SR

text: mAKAP-bound PKA phosphorylates a perinuclear pool of RyRs, promoting Ca2+ release from perinuclear stores and local calcineurin activation, which induces NFAT- and MEF2-dependent hypertrophic gene expression in cardiac myocytes.

mAKAPb-bound PKA can phosphorylate a small pool of

nuclear stores and local activation of CaN, which in turn
induces nuclear factor of activated T-cells (NFAT) and
MEF2-dependent gene expression associated with hy-
pertrophy (Li et al., 2010).

text: ChIP-seq with YAP and TAZ antibodies in MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells identified 7107 peaks by both antibodies, including promoters of previously established YAP/TAZ targets.

quotes.quote:
we performed chromatin 
immunoprecipitation assays with YAP and TAZ antibodies followed by next-generation 
sequencing (ChIP-seq) in MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells, bearing genetic inactivation of 
the Hippo pathway (NF2 null)7. 7107 peaks were identified by both antibodies (Fig. 1a).

experiment.system: MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells (NF2 null)
experiment.perturbation: observational (ChIP with YAP and TAZ antibodies)
experiment.measurement: ChIP-seq peak calling / overlap of YAP and TAZ peaks

text: Motif analysis of YAP/TAZ peaks found the TEAD consensus in at least 75% of peaks, typically at peak summits, while motifs for other proposed YAP/TAZ DNA-binding partners were not significantly enriched except RUNX in a minority of peaks.

quotes.quote:
their consensus sequence was present in at least 75% 
of YAP/TAZ peaks, typically at the summit of YAP/TAZ peaks (Supplementary Figs. 1e-f).

surprisingly no motifs for the other proposed DNA-binding 
platforms of YAP/TAZ were significantly enriched (with the exception of RUNX, found in a 
minority of peaks, see Supplementary Table 1)

experiment.system: YAP/TAZ ChIP-seq peaks in MDA-MB-231 cells
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: de novo and known motif enrichment analysis (Homer/JASPAR)

text: Endogenous TEAD4 ChIP-seq showed 78% (5522) of YAP/TAZ peaks overlap TEAD4 peaks with coincident summits and correlated signal, and YAP chromatin binding is strongly reduced by combined TEAD1/2/3/4 knockdown.

quotes.quote:
we performed a ChIP-seq experiment for endogenous TEAD4 and 
found that 78% (5522) of YAP/TAZ peaks overlapped with TEAD4 peaks (Fig. 1b and 
Supplementary Table 2); furthermore, the summits of TEAD4 peaks coincide with the 
summit of the corresponding YAP/TAZ peaks (Fig. 1c)

binding of YAP to chromatin is strongly affected by combined knockdown of 
TEAD1/2/3/4 as assessed by ChIP-qPCR (Fig. 1e)

experiment.system: MDA-MB-231 cells
experiment.perturbation: TEAD4 ChIP-seq; siRNA knockdown of TEAD1/2/3/4
experiment.measurement: peak overlap, summit position, signal correlation; YAP ChIP-qPCR

text: Comparing YAP/TAZ/TEAD4 peaks with H3K4me1/H3K4me3 maps in MDA-MB-231 cells, only 3.6% of peaks are on promoters while 91% lie in enhancer regions, mostly active enhancers marked by H3K27 acetylation and reduced nucleosome occupancy.

quotes.quote:
only a very small fraction (3.6%) of YAP/TAZ/TEAD4 peaks are located on 
promoters; instead, 91% of peaks are located in enhancer regions (Figs. 1h-i). Furthermore, 
most of these enhancers are in an active state as revealed by H3K27 acetylation and reduced 
nucleosome occupancy at the peak center

experiment.perturbation: observational

text: GO analysis of YAP/TAZ direct positive targets showed 135 genes linked to cell cycle progression — binding sites exclusively on distal enhancers for 115 of them and on both promoters and enhancers for 11 — while 13.5% of positive targets relate to RNA metabolism and transport.

quotes.quote:
A large fraction of positive 
targets (135) are linked to processes related to cell cycle progression (Fig. 2a; 
Supplementary Tables 4 and 5); YAP/TAZ/TEAD binding sites are located exclusively on 
distal enhancers for 115 of these genes, and both on promoters and enhancers for other 11

Other positive targets (13.5% of the total) are connected to RNA metabolism and 
RNA transport.

experiment.perturbation: observational (bioinformatic)
experiment.measurement: DAVID Gene Ontology Biological Process enrichment (FDR ≤ 5%)

text: qRT-PCR on about 40 selected proliferation genes confirmed their expression depends on both YAP/TAZ and TEAD1-4, and all these genes were associated with YAP/TAZ/TEAD peaks located on enhancers.

We selected about 40 of these 
genes (containing representative genes belonging to each of the above mentioned categories)

TEAD1-4 (Fig. 2b). All these new YAP/TAZ/TEAD-regulated genes were associated to

text: YAP/TAZ-depleted MDA-MB-231 cells stop proliferating and accumulate in G1; TEAD depletion phenocopies this, and growth is rescued by wild-type YAP or TAZ but not by their TEAD-binding deficient mutants.

We found that YAP/
TAZ-depleted cells stop proliferating and accumulate in the G1 phase (Figs. 3a-b). These 
effects are phenocopied by TEAD depletion (Supplementary Figs. 3b-c); moreover, the 
growth of YAP/TAZ-depleted cells can be fully rescued by re-introduction of wild-type YAP

3d).

substantial increase of cells in the G1 phase, in part phenocopying the requirement of YAP/
TAZ. Overexpression of MYC in YAP/TAZ-depleted cells triggered a significant, but only a 
partial rescue of cell proliferation (Fig. 3d).

text: In a compendium of >3600 clinically annotated breast cancer samples, the validated YAP/TAZ/TEAD direct target signature was differentially expressed between G3 and G1 tumors and identified patients with poor prognosis (log-rank p-value < 0.0001), and correlated with independent YAP/TAZ signatures and TAZ mRNA levels.

the validated YAP/TAZ/TEAD direct targets (see Fig. 2b) was differentially expressed in G3 
and G1 tumors, and identified tumors with poor prognosis as determined by Kaplan-Meier

metastasis-free survival (log-rank p-value < 0.0001).

the signature of direct targets statistically correlates with the 
expression of independent YAP/TAZ signatures, and with the levels of TAZ mRNA

The majority of YAP/TAZ/TEAD peaks (70%) contained 
both a TEAD and an AP-1 motif, with a median distance of about 60 bp.

By ChIP-seq we 
identified >24,000 JUN binding sites. JUN was present in 78% of YAP/TAZ/TEAD binding 
sites (4306/5522; Figs. 4a-b), and 93% of these shared binding sites are located on active 
enhancers.

on the enhancers of 85% 
of the new targets defining the YAP/TAZ/TEAD cell-proliferation program (as in Fig. 4c). 
We indeed re-validated by ChIP-qPCR the presence of both JUN and FOSL1 in all tested 
binding sites

text: In situ proximity ligation assays placed YAP and TEAD1 in close proximity with AP-1 proteins (JUN, FOSL1, JUND) in nuclei of MDA-MB-231, A549 and HCT116 cells, and endogenous FOSL1, JUN and JUND co-immunoprecipitated with Flag-tagged TEAD1 while endogenous TEAD1 co-purified with endogenous FOSL1 and JUND.

By in situ proximity ligation assay (PLA)22, we found YAP and TEAD1 
in close proximity with AP-1 proteins (JUN, FOSL1, JUND) in the nuclei of MDA-MB-231

luciferase reporters containing CTGF and ANKRD1 regulatory sequences; both contain

activity (Fig. 4i), indicating that both sites are required to mediate YAP/TAZ-dependent

of FOSL1, FOSL2, JUN or JUND severely reduced mammosphere formation by MII-

monitoring anchorage-independent growth in soft-agar and mammosphere assays, we found

expression of AP-1, while per se 
insufficient to induce tumors, strongly enhanced the growth of YAP-induced tumors, as

binding deficient YAP instead developed no tumors, irrespectively of the expression of AP-1

although AP-1 alone was 
insufficient to turn on the YAP/TAZ/TEAD proliferative program, it strongly synergized 
with YAP to activate transcription of these genes (Fig. 5h)

text: The E2F consensus was not enriched at YAP/TAZ/TEAD-bound regions, though the E2F motif is present in 67% of the promoters of genes in the YAP/TAZ proliferative program.

(Table S3).

crystal form, with two molecules in the asymmetric unit.

density is present for the N-terminal base of the activation
loop, which forms a helical turn, stabilizing the outwardly
displaced helix aC (Figures 1C and 3B). Our structure
also permits visualization of the loop leading into helix
aC (Figures 1C and 3B), which is disordered in the Lapati-
nib complex.

a double mutant EGFRkinase-dead(V924R) (defective C-

text: Sequence alignment of EGFR family members shows the asymmetric-interface residues are essentially invariant in EGFR, HER2, and HER4, while in ErbB3 the C-lobe (cyclin-like) face residues are conserved but the N-lobe face residues are divergent, suggesting ErbB3 functions as a cyclin-like activator only.

that the residues involved in the N- or the C-lobe faces of

the three catalytically active EGFR family members
(EGFR, HER2, and HER4) (Figure 7A)

In contrast, residues in ErbB3 that correspond
to the N-lobe face (i.e., on the kinase domain that is being
activated) are divergent (Figure 7A). This suggests that the
catalytically inactive ErbB3 molecule functions essentially
as a cyclin-like activator for other EGFR family members.

experiment.measurement: signature gene overlap counts and NicheNet ligand-target inference

quotes.quote:
we found that tumor samples
could be clustered into eight groups (C1 to
C8) (Fig. 5A). The C1 and C2 harbored high
frequencies of terminal Tex cells, and C1 also
had the highest frequency of TNFRSF9+ Treg
cells. Tumors of C3 to C8 harbored a low fre-
quency of terminal Tex cells and high fre-
quency of CD8+ZNF683+CXCR6+ Trm cells and
could be further divided into groups domi-
nated by naïve T cell (C7), enriched naïve T cell
(C8), enriched Temra cell (C6), enriched Tc17 or

Using immune type sig-
natures to stratify the TCGA cancer patients,

Reanalysis of published data of PD-1 anti-
body treatment for melanoma (42) indicated
that responsive tumors had a lower frequency

cell connection was reproduced in another

loTrm
hi tumors

in responders also had a higher frequency of
Tc17 (Fig. 5C)

text: The reprocessed structure resolved elements missing from the previous model, including the arrestin C-edge loop from residue 340 through 342, poly N-acetyl-D-glucosamine at the rhodopsin N15 glycosylation site, and most of the rhodopsin C-terminal tail (residues 330–343) including two phosphate groups at T336 and S338; the four complexes in the asymmetric unit have Cα RMSDs between 0.5~0.7 Å.

quotes.quote:
we observed electron density for the 
membrane-touching loop of arrestin (C-edge loop) from residue 340 through 342 (Figure 
S1C).

We also observed electron density for poly N-acetyl-D-
glucosamine at the N15 glycosylation site of each rhodopsin molecule (Figure S1D), and 
most of the rhodopsin C-terminal tail (residues 330–343) including two phosphate groups at 
T336 and S338

root-mean-square deviations (RMSDs) of Cα atoms 
among four complexes are between 0.5~0.7 Å

experiment.system: crystal structure of four T4L-rhodopsin-arrestin fusion complexes per asymmetric unit
experiment.perturbation: observational (model building/refinement against reprocessed XFEL data)
experiment.measurement: electron density for previously unmodelled elements; Cα RMSD between complexes

text: The rhodopsin C-tail portion from K339 to T342 adopts a β-strand that forms an extended intermolecular β-sheet with arrestin β-strand I (V12 to K16), while residues D330 through S338 form an extended stretch; the linker K325 through G329 is disordered, D330-S335 varies among the four complexes, and the K339-T342 β-strand is identical in all four.

quotes.quote:
Of the 
resolved rhodopsin C-tail, the C-terminal portion from K339 to T342 adopts a β-strand that 
forms an extended intermolecular β-sheet with β-strand I, from V12 to K16, of the N-
terminal domain of arrestin (Figure 2).

Residues N-terminal to the C-tail β-strand of 
rhodopsin, D330 through S338, form an extended stretch that interacts with arrestin and 
connects the β-strand to helix 8 through a flexible linker region (K325 through G329) that is 
disordered in the crystal structure.

The 
conformation and position of residues D330-S335 are slightly different among the four 
complexes in the crystal structure, indicating the dynamic nature of this region. In contrast, 
the β-strand (K339-T342) of the rhodopsin C-tail adopts the same structure in all four 
complexes

experiment.system: XFEL crystal structure of phosphorhodopsin-visual arrestin complex
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: secondary structure and residue positions at the C-tail/arrestin interface

text: Mass spectrometry detected phosphate groups at S334, T336 and S338 of the rhodopsin C-tail, whereas the crystal structure showed the phosphate at S338 in all four rhodopsin molecules and at T336 only in molecules A and B, with no phosphate observed at S334.

quotes.quote:
While the rhodopsin C-tail contains six serine or threonine residues, mass spectrometry 
analysis detected phosphate groups at S334, T336 and S338 in our protein samples (Figure 
S2). In our crystal structure, however, we observed the phosphate group at S338 in all four 
rhodopsin molecules and at T336 only in molecules A and B. The phosphate group at S334 
was not observed in the structure

experiment.system: rhodopsin-arrestin fusion protein expressed in HEK293 cells
experiment.perturbation: observational (endogenous phosphorylation)
experiment.measurement: LC-MS/MS phosphosite detection compared with crystallographic electron density

numbers.quantity: serine or threonine residues in rhodopsin C-tail

text: Phosphorylated T336 and S338 and the acidic E341 of rhodopsin engage three positively charged arrestin pockets — A (K16, R19, R172), B (K16, R30, K301) and C (K15, K111) — and the nine positive charges of the arrestin N-terminal surface are matched by eight or ten negative charges from the rhodopsin interface residues, indicating an overall electrostatic balance.

quotes.quote:
The three positively charged pockets are formed by three groups of 
basic residues: K16, R19 and R172 (pocket A), K16, R30 and K301 (pocket B), and K15 
and K111 (pocket C), which accommodate phosphate groups at T336 and S338, and the 
negatively charged E341, respectively, of the rhodopsin C-tail

the total 
number of positive charges on this arrestin N-terminal surface is nine (Figure 2C), which is 
equivalent to eight or ten total negative charges of the phosphate groups and acidic amino 
acid residues at the interface (depending on the phosphorylation of S334, detected by mass 
spectrometry but not observed in our crystal structure), indicating an overall electrostatic 
balance at this rhodopsin-arrestin interface

experiment.system: XFEL crystal structure of phosphorhodopsin-visual arrestin complex
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: electrostatic contacts and charge counting at the interface

numbers.quantity: positive charges on arrestin N-terminal surface

text: Disulfide cross-linking across the interface (13 arrestin and seven rhodopsin cysteine mutants, 63 co-expression combinations) showed rhodopsin E332 cross-linked strongly with arrestin R19, K167 and K168, D331 cross-linked weakly, A333/S334/A335 cross-linked with only R19, T336 with both K16 and R19, and E341 with K111 but not with β-strand I residues.

quotes.quote:
A total of 
13 cysteine mutants of arrestin together with seven cysteine mutants of rhodopsin were 
expressed. A total of 63 co-expression combinations were tested and monitored by SDS-
PAGE followed by Western blotting

Examples show that rhodopsin E332 strongly cross-linked with R19, K167 and K168 of 
arrestin (Figure 4A), as E332 faces toward these positively charged residues, while D331 of
rhodopsin weakly cross-linked, because it faces away from the arrestin surface

Rhodopsin residues A333, S334 and A335 cross-linked with only R19, and T336 
crosslinked with both K16 and R19 of arrestin

Rhodopsin E341 cross-linked with K111 on helix I, but did not cross-link with residues on 
β-strand I of arrestin, probably due to unfavorable geometry

verdict_note: Claim text and counts match p.5–6 verbatim; the experiment-field details (HA/Flag tags, 1 mM H2O2) lie outside the excerpt but are consistent with the AD293 co-expression/Western-blot method described.

experiment.system: AD293 cells co-expressing HA-tagged rhodopsin and Flag-tagged arrestin cysteine mutants
experiment.perturbation: engineered cysteine pairs across the interface plus 1 mM H2O2 oxidation
experiment.measurement: SDS-PAGE/Western blot detection of cross-linked rhodopsin-arrestin product

text: HDX mass spectrometry showed that rhodopsin binding protects arrestin regions including the N-terminal β-strands (residues 11 to 52, and 115 to 120) and helix I (residues 104 to 110) from hydrogen-deuterium exchange relative to free pre-activated arrestin, protection the authors state could not be explained by the previous structure lacking the rhodopsin C-tail.

quotes.quote:
Compared to the free pre-activated arrestin, the 
binding of rhodopsin protects arrestin against hydrogen-deuterium exchange in several 
regions (Figure S3B). Notably, the arrestin regions protected from hydrogen-deuterium 
exchange include the N-terminal β-strands (residues 11 to 52, and 115 to 120) and helix I 
(residues 104 to 110) (Figure S3B). The protection of these structural elements in the 
arrestin N-domain could not be explained by our previous structure that lacks the rhodopsin 
C-tail

experiment.system: purified arrestin, free pre-activated versus rhodopsin-bound
experiment.perturbation: rhodopsin binding versus free arrestin
experiment.measurement: hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry deuterium uptake by peptide

text: In two independent three-microsecond all-atom MD simulations the ionic network of pT336, pS338 and E341 with arrestin pockets A, B and C was maintained with average interaction frequencies upwards of 80% for most crystallographic contacts; RMSDs of pT336, pS338 and E341 generally remained within 3.0 Å of crystallographic positions while D330 and S334 reached values upwards of 19 Å, and an RMSF cut-off of 1.7 Å defined a key interaction range of C-tail residues A335 to E341.

quotes.quote:
performing two independent, three microsecond-long all-
atom molecular dynamics simulations. Throughout both simulations the charged interaction 
network connecting the phosphorylated T336 and S338, and the negatively charged E341 of 
rhodopsin with the positively charged arrestin residues comprising pockets A, B and C were 
well maintained with average interaction frequencies upwards of 80% for most 
crystallographic contacts

Overall, the RMSDs of pT336, pS338 
and E341 generally remained within 3.0 Å of their crystallographic positions, consistent 
with maintenance of the interwoven ionic network, while residues D330 and S334 located 
N-terminally to pT336 exhibit a number of metastable states whose RMSDs reached values 
upwards of 19 Å (Figure 5C).

By defining an RMSF cut-off of 1.7 Å, both 
simulations suggest a key interaction range comprising C-tail residues A335 to E341

experiment.system: chain A of the rhodopsin-arrestin complex embedded in a POPC bilayer, GROMACS/CHARMM36
experiment.perturbation: two independent 3 µs production simulations (6 µs combined)
experiment.measurement: contact interaction frequencies, RMSD of C-tail residues, RMSF of alpha carbons

numbers.quantity: average interaction frequency for most crystallographic contacts
RMSD reached by D330 and S334

text: Superposition of the V2R-β-arrestin-1 structure (4JQI) with the rhodopsin-arrestin structure shows the V2R β-strand (residues 360–365) resembles the rhodopsin C-terminal β-strand (residues 338–343), with phosphorylated S357 and T360 of V2R nearly superposable on phosphorylated T336 and S338 of rhodopsin and pS363–K107 mirroring E341–K111; the authors state that V2R residues N-terminal to pS357 would clash with the visual arrestin finger loop, so the V2R peptide structure likely represents a tail-engaged state and the rhodopsin complex the fully-engaged state.

quotes.quote:
Superposition of the V2R-
β-arrestin-1 structure (PDB code: 4JQI) with our rhodopsin-arrestin complex structure 
reveals a noticeable similarity between the β-strand of V2R (residues 360–365) and the C-
terminal β-strand (residues 338–343) of rhodopsin (Figures 6A–B). The phosphorylated 
residues S357 and T360 of the V2R C-tail are nearly superposable with the phosphorylated 
T336 and S338 of rhodopsin C-tail (Figure 6B). In addition, the ionic interaction between 
the phosphorylated S363 of V2R and K107 of β-arrestin-1 is comparable to the interaction 
of rhodopsin E341 with K111 of visual arrestin

The position of those V2R 
residues would clash with the corresponding residues in the finger loop of visual arrestin in 
the fully-engaged state, thus the structure of β-arrestin-1 in complex with the phosphorylated 
V2R C-tail likely represents a tail-engaged state, whereas the structure of the phosphorylated 
rhodopsin–arrestin complex represents the fully-engaged state.

experiment.system: rhodopsin-visual arrestin complex structure and V2R C-tail peptide-β-arrestin-1 structure (PDB 4JQI)
experiment.perturbation: observational (structural superposition)
experiment.measurement: residue-level superposition of phospho-residues and β-strands

text: From the spacing constraints between the three arrestin phosphate pockets — one residue between the first and second phosphates in rhodopsin and two residues between the second and third, versus two-residue separations at both positions in V2R — the authors derive phosphorylation codes PxPxxP/E/D (short code) and PxxPxxP/E/D (long code), with sequence alignment revealing only two phosphorylation codes in each of the rhodopsin and V2R C-tails.

quotes.quote:
In our rhodopsin–arrestin complex, the 
space between the first and the second phosphate groups on the C-tail (Space 1 in Figure 6C) 
is one residue, while the space between the second and the third phosphate groups (the third 
one is glutamic acid in this case) (Space 2 in Figure 6C) is two residues.

Based on these space constraints, a 
phosphorylation code required for high-affinity arrestin binding is predicted to be 
PxPxxP/E/D (denoted as short code) or PxxPxxP/E/D (denoted as long code), in which P 
represents a phospho-serine or phospho-threonine, and x any amino acid residue, except 
proline in the second xx occurrence.

Sequence alignment 
reveals that there are only two phosphorylation codes in both rhodopsin and V2R C-tails 
(Figure 6C).

experiment.system: rhodopsin-visual arrestin and V2R C-tail-β-arrestin-1 structures plus receptor C-tail sequence alignment
experiment.perturbation: observational (structure-based derivation of a sequence motif)
experiment.measurement: residue spacing between phosphate-binding pockets; motif occurrence in aligned sequences

numbers.quantity: codes found in rhodopsin and V2R C-tails

text: Tango assays showed that rhodopsin C-tail mutations T336A/S338A/T340A and T336A/S338A/T343A significantly reduced visual arrestin recruitment, and that V2R C-tail mutations S357A/T360A/S363A (3A) or S357A/T360A/S362A/S363A/S364A (6A) in a β2AR-V2R chimera significantly reduced β-arrestin-1 binding; dose-response analysis indicated the code mutations affect Emax but not EC50.

quotes.quote:
we generated multiple mutations T336A/S338A/T340A and T336A/S338A/
T343A in rhodopsin C-terminal tail to test their effect on arrestin recruitment using a cell-
based Tango assay (Barnea et al., 2008; Kang et al., 2015). Those mutations significantly 
reduced recruitment efficiency of visual arrestin by rhodopsin (Figure 6D).

We further tested the 
effects of the phosphorylation code of V2R C-tail on arrestin binding by mutations of 
S357A/T360A/S363A (3A) or S357A/T360A/S362A/S363A/S364A (6A) that respectively 
disrupt either the first phosphorylation code SCTTAS or both codes SCTTAS and SCTTASS 
on the V2R C-tail of a β2AR-V2R chimeric receptor. Tango assay showed significant 
reduction of binding efficiency of the mutated chimeric receptors with β-arrestin-1 (Figure 
6E).

Full dose-response curve on key mutations suggested that the phosphorylation code 
mutations do not affect the shape of the dose-response curve (EC50), but affect the maximal 
activity (Emax) observed in Tango assay (Figure S7).

experiment.system: HTL cells expressing rhodopsin-TEV-tTA or β2AR-V2R chimera fusions with arrestin-TEV protease
experiment.perturbation: alanine substitution of phosphorylation-code serine/threonine residues in rhodopsin or V2R C-tails
experiment.measurement: Tango luciferase reporter signal normalized to Renilla (arrestin recruitment); dose-response EC50/Emax

text: PhosCoFinder analysis of the GPCR database found phosphorylation codes in all major GPCR subfamilies, with 52.3% of class A, 66.6% of class B, 59.1% of class C and 45.5% of class F members carrying short, long or both codes.

quotes.quote:
By 
analyzing the GPCR database with PhosCoFinder, we found that phosphorylation codes 
exist in all major GPCR subfamilies (Figures S6A–B). The percentage of the GPCR 
members that have either short, long or both phosphorylation codes is 52.3% for class A, 
66.6% for class B, 59.1% for class C, and 45.5% for class F (Figure S6A).

experiment.system: GPCR database sequences
experiment.perturbation: observational (in silico motif scan with the PhosCoFinder web/Python tool)
experiment.measurement: percentage of subfamily members containing short and/or long phosphorylation codes

text: Among 825 UniProt-annotated GPCRs, 436 contained full or partial codes in their C-terminal tails; of the 389 without tail codes, 308 (~79%) were olfactory receptors and 48 of the remaining 81 contained full or partial codes within ICL3, so the code analysis accounts for 96% of the GPCR proteome.

quotes.quote:
Among 825 annotated GPCRs, 436 were found to contain 
full or partial codes in their C-terminal tails (http://tools.vai.org/phoscofinder/
downloads.php). Of the 389 receptors without codes in their tails, 308 (~79%) were found to 
belong to the olfactory receptor family

Analysis of the remaining 81 receptors found that 48 contained full or partial codes within 
their ICL3

In total, our phosphorylation code 
analysis accounts for 96% of the GPCR proteome.

experiment.system: UniProt-annotated GPCR proteome
experiment.perturbation: observational (PhosCoFinder motif search of C-terminal tails and ICL3)
experiment.measurement: counts and percentages of receptors containing full or partial codes

text: Phosphorylation code occurrence correlates with Oakley et al.'s arrestin-binding classification: all "class A" GPCRs possess none or at most one complete code whereas all "class B" receptors possess at least two complete codes, and the β3-adrenergic receptor, which does not directly interact with β-arrestins, had no full or partial code.

quotes.quote:
Our search for phosphorylation codes revealed that 
the classification of GPCRs based on their arrestin-binding properties strongly correlates 
with the occurrence of complete phosphorylation codes in their C-terminal tails (Figure 
S6C). All “class A” GPCRs possess none or at most one complete phosphorylation code, 
whereas all “class B” receptors possess at least two complete phosphorylation codes. 
Consistent with the experimental classification, analysis of the β3-adrenergic receptor that 
does not directly interact with β-arrestins failed to identify any full or partial 
phosphorylation code

experiment.system: C-terminal tail sequences of GPCRs previously classified as arrestin-binding class A or class B
experiment.perturbation: observational (motif search)
experiment.measurement: number of complete phosphorylation codes per receptor tail versus published binding class

text: Extending the search to non-GPCR membrane proteins with C-terminal cytoplasmic tails identified complete phosphorylation codes in numerous proteins experimentally shown to bind β-arrestins, including TRPV1, IGF1R, TGFβR3, VE-cadherin, LRP4, CD247, killer cell immunoglobulin-like receptor 2DL1 and 2DL4, and voltage-gated potassium channel subunit beta-1; the authors state the role of these motifs in arrestin binding has to be tested experimentally.

quotes.quote:
We further expanded our search for complete phosphorylation codes to non-GPCR 
membrane proteins that contain C-terminal cytoplasmic tails, and interestingly found 
numerous proteins that were experimentally shown to bind β-arrestins, including TRPV1
The role of these motifs in arrestin binding has to be tested experimentally.

experiment.system: non-GPCR membrane proteins with C-terminal cytoplasmic tails
experiment.perturbation: observational (PhosCoFinder motif search)
experiment.measurement: presence of Px(x)PxxP motifs in proteins with reported β-arrestin binding

text: Including the C-terminal tail, the rhodopsin-arrestin complex buries 2,420 Å2 of interface surface area in complex A, compared with 1,300 Å2 in the previous structure lacking the C-tail.

quotes.quote:
Including the C-terminal 
tail, the rhodopsinarrestin complex buries 2,420 Å2 of surface area in the interface (complex 
A), compared with 1,300 Å2 in the previous structure (Kang et al., 2015), illustrating the 
crucial role of the C-terminal tail in arrestin recruitment.

experiment.system: XFEL crystal structure of the phosphorhodopsin-arrestin complex (complex A)
experiment.perturbation: observational (comparison with previously published model)
experiment.measurement: buried interface surface area

text: Macrophages and fibroblasts reciprocally express growth factors and receptors forming three possible connections: fibroblast Csf1 to macrophage Csf1r, macrophage Pdgfb to fibroblast Pdgfra/Pdgfrb, and a fibroblast autocrine loop via Pdgfd and Hbegf.

quotes.quote:
we found four growth factors with the potential to support proliferation of either 
macrophages or fibroblasts (Figure 1B, S1D). These growth factors and their receptors 
constitute three possible connections between macrophages and fibroblasts

First, fibroblasts express high levels of Csf1, while Csf1 receptor (Csf1r) is 
expressed exclusively on macrophages.

Third, we observed a possible 
autocrine loop for fibroblasts via members of the PDGF (Pdgfd) and EGF (Hbegf) families.

experiment.system: murine bone marrow-derived macrophages and murine embryonic fibroblasts
experiment.perturbation: daily addition of 50 ng/ml recombinant Csf1, Pdgfb, Pdgfd, or Hbegf; observational expression profiling
experiment.measurement: qPCR/RNAseq expression of growth factors and receptors; cell numbers over 3 days

text: Macrophages and fibroblasts co-cultured at initial ratios spanning a range of up to 2500-fold converged to a stable ratio over a 2-week period, and each cell type could converge to stable numbers.

quotes.quote:
We mixed the two cell types with initial ratios 
spanning a range of up to 2500-fold and followed the kinetics of both populations by flow 
cytometry (Figure S2B). Strikingly, over a 2-week period, the two cell types reached a stable 
ratio (Figure 2A, S2C, S2D). In addition, macrophages and fibroblasts could each converge 
to stable numbers

experiment.system: in vitro macrophage-fibroblast co-culture
experiment.perturbation: varying initial MP:FB seeding ratios up to 2500-fold
experiment.measurement: flow cytometric population ratios and numbers over 2 weeks

text: Analytical screening of all 144 possible two-cell circuit topologies found that 48 allow a stable steady state over a wide parameter range (each parameter varying at least 10-fold), 24 of these also show an 'ON-OFF' state, while 60/144 never show a stable ON state and 36/144 only for a very restricted parameter range.

quotes.quote: we generated all 144 possible two-cell circuit topologies

We find that 48 of these 144 topologies allow a stable steady state for a wide range of 
parameters. Each parameter, such as growth factor production and consumption rates, and 
cell removal and proliferation rates, can vary by at least 10-fold around a biologically 
plausible value and stability is still maintained.

24 of these 48 circuits 
show a third steady state fixed point: an ‘ON-OFF’ state

The 
remaining 96 topologies either can never show a stable ON state for any parameter set 
(60/144), or show a stable ON state only for a very restricted range of parameters (36/144).

experiment.system: mathematical models of two-cell growth factor circuits (ODEs for cells X1, X2 and growth factors C12, C21)
experiment.perturbation: enumeration of cross-regulation, autocrine production, and endocytosis options; scanning rate parameters
experiment.measurement: existence and robustness of stable steady states (fixed points)

text: The screen identified a necessary and sufficient condition for a stable 'ON' state when one cell type is close to carrying capacity: the growth factor of the cell far from carrying capacity must undergo negative regulation by internalization or cross-repression — the 'Spring-and-Ceiling' model, satisfied by all 48 stable circuits.

quotes.quote:
a necessary and sufficient condition for a stable ‘ON’ state is that the 
growth factor of the cell far from carrying capacity must undergo negative regulation (either 
by internalization or cross-repression) (Fig 3D) (Adler et al., 2018). This requirement is 
found in all of the 48 circuits in the screen which showed a stable ‘ON’ state. We name this 
mechanism for stability the “Spring–and-Ceiling” model.

experiment.system: analytical model of all two-cell circuit topologies
experiment.perturbation: imposing carrying-capacity constraint on one cell type and varying regulation type
experiment.measurement: stability analysis of ON-state fixed points across topologies

text: Fibroblast proliferation is negatively correlated with cell density whereas macrophage proliferation is largely density-independent, indicating fibroblasts but not macrophages are limited by carrying capacity; doubling well area doubled the cell number at which fibroblast proliferation reached zero.

quotes.quote:
Doubling the area of the well doubled the cell number at which 
proliferation reached zero, suggesting that in this setting, carrying capacity is proportional to 
space (Fig S4A). Using this system, we further observed that fibroblast proliferation is 
negatively correlated with cell density, whereas macrophage proliferation is largely density-
independent (Figure 4B, Figure S4D & E). This demonstrates that fibroblasts, but not 
macrophages, are limited by carrying capacity.

experiment.system: monocultures of murine embryonic fibroblasts and bone marrow-derived macrophages plated at different densities
experiment.perturbation: varying cell density and tissue culture well area
experiment.measurement: EdU+ percentage as proliferation rate; x-intercept of proliferation vs cell number as carrying capacity

text: Varying available space changed carrying capacity but not proliferation, whereas varying nutrient levels altered both; altering nutrient levels in co-culture did not affect macrophage to fibroblast ratios. Recombinant Csf1 enhanced macrophage proliferation and recombinant Pdgfb increased both fibroblast carrying capacity and proliferation.

quotes.quote:
Varying the available space only changed carrying capacity but not 
proliferation (Figure S4A), whereas varying nutrient levels altered both carrying capacity 
and cell proliferation (Figure S4B). However, altering nutrient levels in the co-culture did 
not affect system stability, as macrophage to fibroblast ratios were similar in co-cultures 
regardless of serum concentration (Figure S4C). Macrophages showed enhanced 
proliferation in response to recombinant Csf1 (Figure S4D & F), while fibroblasts exhibited 
a significant increase in both carrying capacity and cell proliferation in response to 
recombinant Pdgfb

experiment.system: macrophage and fibroblast mono- and co-cultures
experiment.perturbation: varying well area, serum/nutrient concentration, addition of recombinant Csf1 or Pdgfb
experiment.measurement: EdU-based carrying capacity and proliferation rate; MP:FB ratio by flow cytometry

text: After growth factor stimulation, surface receptor expression decreased within minutes (t1/2 ~ 1.5 min for Csf1r, t1/2 ~ 3–6 min for Pdgfra/b) and supernatant growth factors were quickly depleted, indicating internalization is the dominant removal mechanism for Csf1 and Pdgfb.

quotes.quote:
After stimulation with growth factors, the 
surface expression of receptors for Csf1 and Pdgfb decreased within minutes (t1/2 ~ 1.5 min 
for Csf1r, t1/2 ~ 3–6 min for Pdgfra/b) (Figure 4C, Figure S4G). Furthermore, the available 
growth factors in the supernatant were quickly depleted (Figure S4H). These data suggest 
that internalization is the dominant mechanism for removal of both Csf1 and Pdgfb.

experiment.system: BMDMs and MEFs in culture
experiment.perturbation: stimulation with 50 ng/ml Csf1 or Pdgfb (uptake assay 10 ng/mL)
experiment.measurement: flow cytometric surface receptor expression over time; ELISA of supernatant growth factor

text: Cross-regulation is unidirectional: exogenous Pdgfb did not influence Csf1 expression in fibroblasts, while exogenous Csf1 down-regulated Pdgfb expression in macrophages; modeling suggests this cross-regulation does not significantly affect the dynamics since fibroblasts are mainly regulated by carrying capacity.

quotes.quote:
We did not observe 
cross-regulation of Csf1: expression of Csf1 in fibroblasts was not influenced by exogenous 
Pdgfb (Figure 4D). Conversely, we observed cross-regulation in the other direction: 
exogenous Csf1 down-regulated the expression of Pdgfb in macrophages. Interestingly, 
modeling suggests that this cross-regulation does not significantly affect the dynamics, since 
fibroblasts are mainly regulated by their carrying capacity.

experiment.system: BMDM and MEF cultures
experiment.perturbation: addition of 50 ng/ml Csf1 and 50 ng/ml Pdgfb for 24 hr
experiment.measurement: qPCR of Pdgfb in MP and Csf1 in FB normalized to Hprt1

text: An experimental phase portrait of MP-FB co-culture spanning three orders of magnitude in cell density reproduced the three predicted states ('ON', 'OFF', and fibroblast-only 'ON-OFF'), with macrophages not surviving without fibroblasts and fibroblasts collapsing below a threshold Allee density.

ptotic actions in many cell types (194). In several carcinogenesis

motif must also be separated by a minimal number of amino acids

text: The protein Ser/Thr metallophosphatase PPM1J (PP2Cζ) was found to harbor a JNK-binding motif, which was also found in the related PPM1H phosphatase and is broadly conserved across the animal kingdom.

the protein Ser/Thr metallophospha-

However, the docking site of JNK cannot bind rhodanese do-

text: The JIP1 PTB domain associates with canonical NPxY motifs in cytoplasmic tails of transmembrane or perimembrane proteins, and this interaction does not require phosphorylation within the NPxY motifs.

this domain can associate with the ca-
nonical NPxY motifs located in the cytoplasmic tails of transmem-
brane or perimembrane proteins as well as with other motifs, but

within the NPxY motifs (131, 132).

text: The MINT2 (APBA2) protein, distantly similar to JIP1 and JIP2, enables JNK-mediated phosphorylation of β-APP, with a possible impact on regulation of amyloid β production.

the MINT2 (APBA2) pro-
tein, distantly similar to JIP1 and JIP2, enables JNK-mediated

quotes.quote:
Insulin receptor signaling (where

experiment.system: insulin receptor signaling in cells

text: Phosphorylation of the PPM1J phosphatase at Ser92, part of a potential FBW7-type phosphodegron (AVQSPPDTGR), can profoundly reduce its activity in cells, although the impact of JNK-mediated phosphorylation on PPM1J ubiquitinylation and half-life has not been specifically studied.

Phosphorylation of the
PPM1J phosphatase at Ser92 (part of a potential FBW7-type phos-
phodegron, AVQSPPDTGR) can also profoundly reduce its activ-
ity in cells (71), albeit that the impact of JNK-mediated phosphor-
ylation on PPM1J ubiquitinylation and its half-life have not been

experiment.system: PPM1J phosphatase in cells
experiment.perturbation: JNK-mediated phosphorylation at Ser92
experiment.measurement: phosphatase activity in cells

text: The Jun partner protein JDP2 is targeted for proteasomal degradation after phosphorylation at Thr148; a homologous site exists on ATF3, but ATF3 levels appear to be controlled by JNK much more weakly than JDP2.

the Jun partner protein JDP2 is tar-
geted for proteasomal degradation by unspeciﬁed ubiquitin li-
gases after its phosphorylation at Thr148 (330).

but ATF3 levels appear to be controlled by
JNK in a much weaker manner than is JDP2 (330).

experiment.system: JDP2 and ATF3 proteins in cells
experiment.perturbation: phosphorylation at Thr148 (JNK)
experiment.measurement: proteasomal degradation / protein levels

text: JNK-dependent phosphorylation of Stathmin-2 (SCG10) at Ser62 and Ser73 induces proteasome-dependent degradation of the protein, although involvement of ubiquitin ligases has not been studied.

quotes.quote:
JNK-dependent phosphorylation of the mi-
crotubule regulatory protein Stathmin-2 (also known as SCG10)
at Ser62 and Ser73 can also induce proteasome-dependent degra-
dation of the protein, although the involvement of ubiquitin li-

text: Phosphorylation of the regulatory C terminus of S6K1 promotes its ubiquitinylation and degradation, but the effect is likely indirect since C-terminally truncated proteins were more unstable.

The phosphorylation of the regulatory C terminus of
S6K1 (p70-RSK) also promotes its ubiquitinylation and degrada-
tion (333). However, this unusual target region (SPRRFIGSPRTP

text: Phosphorylation of an intrinsically disordered transactivator motif on two adjacent positions (Thr69 and Thr71 in human ATF2) is a prerequisite for activation of promoters to which ATF2 family proteins bind.

quotes.quote:
phosphorylation of an intrinsically disordered transactiva-
tor motif on two adjacent positions (Thr69 and Thr71 in human

experiment.system: ATF2 family transcription factors
experiment.perturbation: phosphorylation at Thr69/Thr71
experiment.measurement: promoter activation

text: Paxillin can be phosphorylated by JNK at least on Ser178; its major tyrosine sites Tyr88 (SSPVYGSS) and Tyr181 (LSPLYGVPE) lack N-terminal negative charges but contain SP sites, so MAPK phosphorylation can promote tyrosine phosphorylation and subsequent Crk and/or Src binding, stronger FAK binding, Src activation, and greater tyrosine phosphorylation.

quotes.quote:
it can
also be phosphorylated (at least on Ser 178) by
JNK (268, 269).

two major tyrosine phosphorylation sites (shown in
bold) in paxillin (Tyr88, SSPVYGSS, and Tyr181, LSPLYGVPE)
lack these charged positions. Instead, they contain SP sites (under-
lined), allowing MAPK-dependent phosphorylation events to
provide the necessary negative charges. Thus, ERK2 or JNKs can
promote tyrosine phosphorylation and subsequent Crk and/or
Src binding of paxillin, which leads to stronger focal adhesion
kinase binding, Src kinase activation, and greater tyrosine phos-
phorylation (350).

experiment.system: focal adhesion protein paxillin
experiment.perturbation: ERK2/JNK Ser/Thr phosphorylation
experiment.measurement: tyrosine phosphorylation and Crk/Src/FAK binding

text: At least four sites of YAP1 (two highly conserved) were identified as JNK targets in response to genotoxic stress and all play a role in YAP1 transactivation; Ser128 lies inside a LATS-phosphorylated 14-3-3 binding site (HVRAHSSP), giving JNK potential to counteract Hippo/LATS kinases and free YAP1 to interact with TEAD.

quotes.quote:
At least four sites (of which two are highly conserved) were
identiﬁed as JNK targets in response to genotoxic stress (351), and
all play a role in transactivation by YAP1

Ser128 (underlined in the following sequence; it is also
conserved in TAZ) lies near the TEAD-binding region of YAP1,
