ing sites (HVRAHSSP). This endows JNK with the potential to
counteract Hippo/LATS kinases, setting YAP1 free to interact
with TEAD transcription factors (351).

experiment.system: YAP1 coactivator in cells
experiment.perturbation: genotoxic stress-induced JNK phosphorylation
experiment.measurement: site identification and YAP1 transactivation

text: The transcription factor p73 has at least seven potential JNK phosphorylation sites; experiments suggest these motifs are important for transactivation of p73-dependent genes and for stabilization of p73 by protecting it from ubiquitinylation.

quotes.quote:
The transcription factor p73 has at least seven potential JNK
phosphorylation sites, of which several are highly conserved and
also found in its close paralog, p63.

Experiments suggest that these motifs (such as the N-ter-
minal SPY motifs) are important for transactivation of p73-de-
pendent genes as well as stabilization of the p73 protein by
protecting it from ubiquitinylation (239).

experiment.system: p73 transcription factor
experiment.perturbation: JNK phosphorylation site motifs
experiment.measurement: transactivation of p73-dependent genes and protein stabilization

numbers.quantity: potential JNK phosphorylation sites on p73

text: Of three phosphorylation sites identified in human hnRNP-K, two (Ser216 and Ser284) are conserved in most other vertebrates; Ser216 is probably required for hnRNP-K interaction with ribosomes, essential for translation of associated mRNA in developing neurons to support axon outgrowth.

quotes.quote:
Of
the three phosphorylation sites identiﬁed in human hnRNP-K,
two (Ser216 and Ser284) are conserved in most other vertebrate
species.

It is probably
required for its interaction with the ribosomes, essential for the
translation of associated mRNA in developing neurons, in order
to support axon outgrowth (257).

experiment.system: hnRNP-K RNA-binding protein in developing neurons
experiment.perturbation: JNK phosphorylation site identification/conservation
experiment.measurement: ribosome interaction and mRNA translation/axon outgrowth

numbers.quantity: phosphorylation sites identified in human hnRNP-K

text: Phosphorylation of the conserved MAP2 'perimicrotubular' motif TPGTPGTPS (Thr1619, Thr1622, Thr1625) increased microtubule binding, although molecular details were not fully explored.

quotes.quote:
For MAP2, the phosphorylation
of a conserved “perimicrotubular” motif (TPGTPGTPS, contain-
ing Thr1619, Thr1622, and Thr1625 [underlined] of MAP2) in-
creased microtubule binding, although the molecular details of

experiment.system: MAP2 microtubule-associated protein
experiment.perturbation: phosphorylation of perimicrotubular motif
experiment.measurement: microtubule binding

text: Although Tau phosphorylation at Thr231 and Ser235 was originally reported to inhibit its microtubule-binding ability, more recent research suggests modification of these sites may not be sufficient to induce Tau dissociation from microtubules.

quotes.quote:
Although phosphorylation was originally
reported to inhibit the microtubule-binding ability of Tau, more
recent research suggests that modiﬁcation of these sites may not be
sufﬁcient to induce Tau dissociation from microtubules (354,
355).

experiment.system: Tau protein and microtubules
experiment.perturbation: phosphorylation of Thr231/Ser235 (with GSK3)
experiment.measurement: microtubule binding/dissociation

text: JNK-mediated phosphorylation of WDR62, a microtubule-binding protein and established JNK interactor, regulates its subcellular localization, with the critical Thr1053 site in a highly conserved vertebrate context.

quotes.quote:
the JNK-mediated phosphorylation of
WDR62, a microtubule-binding protein and established JNK in-
teractor, regulates its subcellular localization (213, 357). The crit-
ical Thr1053 phospho-site, together with its surroundings (PQTP
EQEKFLRHHFELTLT), is highly conserved in vertebrates

experiment.system: WDR62 in cells
experiment.perturbation: JNK-mediated phosphorylation (Thr1053)
experiment.measurement: subcellular localization

text: Phosphorylation of PSD-95 by JNK on Ser295, in the linker between the second and third PDZ domains, enhanced its synaptic localization, though the molecular details of this motif's function remain unknown.

its phosphorylation by JNK on
Ser295, located in the ﬂexible linker between the second and third

experiment.perturbation: JNK phosphorylation at Ser295
experiment.measurement: synaptic localization

quotes.quote:
The highly con-
served cytoplasmic tail of the AMPA-type glutamate receptor

the phar-
macological blockade of JNK pathways impaired the ability of
these channels to be reincorporated into the membrane after in-
ternalization.

experiment.system: AMPA-type glutamate receptors GluR4/GluR2

experiment.measurement: receptor reincorporation into membrane after internalization

text: Concomitant phosphorylation of three sites in MARCKSL1 (Ser120, Thr148, Thr178 in the human protein) enhanced its F-actin-binding capacity, even though none of these sites lies in the central actin-binding motif.

concomitant
phosphorylation of three sites (corresponding to Ser120, Thr148,

ing capacity (266).

Phosphorylation of a mobile loop pro-
truding from the ligand-binding domain of RXR leads to its

The phosphorylation of eNOS at Ser114 (lying on a

tiated its activity (358).

JNK
“primes” the so-called SRR1 (Ser-rich region 1) motif of NFAT4

nuclear localization (240).

phosphorylation was proposed to act through an enhanced nu-
clear export of receptors (241).

the basic helix-loop-helix (bHLH) transcription factor
Twist1 was described as being stabilized by JNK phosphorylation

with only 3 amino acids lying between the two motifs

tion of both, but especially the C-terminal site, provided a pro-

tration by prolonging its half-life (234).

ing
motif

That
JNK-dependent phosphorylation of IRS1 and IRS2 leads to a
strong inhibition of its tyrosine phosphorylation during insulin

development of insulin resistance

another site was
identiﬁed more recently (Ser491 in human IRS2, within the

text: JNK can phosphorylate JIP1 at over a dozen different sites, most in its disordered N terminus or flexible loops; with the exception of Thr448, none is conserved in JIP2, and the known regulatory sites Thr103 and Ser421 of JIP1 are not found in JIP2.

JNK can phosphor-
ylate JIP1 at over a dozen different sites, most of them lying within

in JIP2

Known regulatory sites of JIP1 (Thr103, located in the second

JNK can bind and phosphorylate the mitochondrial
outer membrane coiled-coil protein Sab (or SH3BP5) (378). We

ylation, but the extensive conservation of sequence over a long
stretch (PRSECSGASSPECEVERGDRAEGAE) surrounding the

latory role

text: Single-JNK knockout mice (JNK1-/-, JNK2-/-, JNK3-/-) and JNK2-/- JNK3-/- double knockouts are viable, whereas JNK1-/- JNK2-/- mice die early in embryogenesis (E11.5), fail to undergo neural tube closure, and display exencephaly.

quotes.quote:
While single-JNK knockout mice, JNK1/,
JNK2/, or JNK3/, are viable, as are double-knockout
JNK2/ JNK3/ mice; JNK1/ JNK2/ mice die early in em-
bryogenesis (embryonic day 11.5 [E11.5])

not undergo neural tube closure, and they also display exenceph-
aly (179).

numbers.quantity: embryonic day of lethality for JNK1-/- JNK2-/- mice

text: Compound disruption of both the MKK4 and MKK7 genes results in severe growth retardation and embryonic lethality at E9.5; in vivo RNAi screens identified MKK4 as a key regulator of liver regeneration, and MKK7-/- mice revealed a critical need for MKK7 in axon elongation in the developing cerebral cortex.

in vivo RNA interference
(RNAi) screens have identiﬁed MKK4 as a key regulator of liver
regeneration (389), whereas studies in MKK7/ mice have re-
vealed the critical need for MKK7 in axon elongation in the devel-
oping cerebral cortex (390). The compound disruption of both
the MKK4 and MKK7 genes results in severe growth retardation
and embryonic lethality (E9.5).

experiment.perturbation: gene deletion of MKK4 and/or MKK7
experiment.measurement: growth, embryonic lethality, liver regeneration, axon elongation

numbers.quantity: embryonic day of lethality for MKK4/MKK7 compound disruption

text: Genetic deletion of JIP3, an important target and regulator of JNK and its upstream kinases, causes axon guidance defects, consistent with JNK activity being required for correct axon trajectories downstream of guidance cues such as netrins and semaphorins.

In the developing central nervous system, JNKs
are activated by various guidance cues, including netrins and
semaphorins, and JNK activity is required for correct axon trajec-
tories (180, 385, 386). In line with this, the genetic deletion of JIP3,

nases, causes axon guidance defects (387).

experiment.system: developing central nervous system in mice
experiment.perturbation: genetic deletion of JIP3
experiment.measurement: axon guidance/trajectories

text: JNK3-/- mice are resistant to kainite-induced seizures, and pharmacological inhibition of JNK protects neurons from NMDA-induced excitotoxicity in vitro and from cerebral ischemia in animal models.

JNK3/ mice are resistant
to kainite-induced seizures (403). Conversely, the pharmacologi-
cal inhibition of JNK protects neurons from N-nitrosyldimethyl-
amine (NMDA)-induced excitotoxicity in vitro and from cerebral
ischemia in animal models (402, 404).

experiment.perturbation: JNK3 deletion; pharmacological JNK inhibition

text: Only simultaneous knockdown of JNK1, -2, and -3 was sufficient to confer neuroprotection, and inhibition of JNK activity in the nucleus, rather than blocking specific JNK isoforms globally, protected cells from undergoing apoptosis.

However, only a
simultaneous knockdown of JNK1, -2, and -3 was sufﬁcient to

more, the inhibition of JNK activity in the nucleus, rather than

in axonal regeneration of adult neurons, as their speciﬁc inhi-
bition in vitro reduces neuritogenesis (408). Similarly, JNK in-
hibition slowed nerve regeneration in a sciatic nerve transec-
tion-regeneration model (409).

rupting the JNK3 gene have recently been identiﬁed in patients
with hereditary intellectual disability (411)

text: JNK activation is critical for TNF-α-stimulated AP-1-dependent gene expression and has a dual role in TNF-α-stimulated death of fibroblasts, suppressing TNF-α-stimulated apoptosis while potentiating TNF-α-stimulated necrosis; JNKs also negatively regulate autocrine TGF-β1 expression in fibroblasts.

JNK activation is criti-
cal for TNF--stimulated AP-1-dependent gene expression (413)
and has a dual role in the TNF--stimulated death of ﬁbroblasts
by not only suppressing TNF--stimulated apoptosis but also po-
tentiating TNF--stimulated necrosis (414). Moreover, JNKs
negatively regulate the autocrine expression of TGF-1 in ﬁbro-
blasts (414).

transformed B lymphoblasts, JNK1 signals cell survival, as its ge-
netic disruption in mice causes defective transformation of pre-B
cells by BCR-ABL (417). Moreover, JNKs play a key role in Ras-
induced tumorigenesis, for example, in lung tumor development

text: MEKK1 (MAP3K1) was found to be often mutated in breast cancer, with 12% of luminal A tumors containing inactivating mutations in MAP3K1 and MAP2K4; MKK4 mutants harboring cancer-associated somatic mutations had lower enzymatic activity and also caused anchorage-independent cell growth.

be often mutated in breast cancer, and 12% of luminal A tumors
contained inactivating mutations in MAP3K1 and MAP2K4
(420). Interestingly, MKK4 mutants harboring cancer-associated
somatic mutations had lower enzymatic activity and also caused
anchorage-independent cell growth (421).

experiment.system: human breast tumor genomes; cells expressing MKK4 mutants
experiment.perturbation: observational tumor sequencing; expression of cancer-associated MKK4 mutants
experiment.measurement: mutation frequency; enzymatic activity; anchorage-independent growth

numbers.quantity: luminal A tumors with inactivating MAP3K1/MAP2K4 mutations

text: Feeding mice a high-fat diet causes activation of JNK1 in insulin-responsive peripheral tissues including fat, muscle, and liver, and ultimately leads to insulin resistance; JNK1-/- mice, but not wild-type or JNK2-/- mice, are resistant to obesity-induced insulin resistance.

quotes.quote:
Feeding mice a high-fat diet causes
activation of JNK1 in insulin-responsive peripheral tissues, in-
cluding fat, muscle, and liver, and ultimately leads to insulin re-
sistance in these tissues (181).

JNK1 knockout prevents both diet-induced obesity and insulin
resistance. JNK1/ mice, but not wild-type or JNK2/ mice, are
resistant to obesity-induced insulin resistance (336).

experiment.system: mice on high-fat diet; JNK1-/- and JNK2-/- mice
experiment.perturbation: high-fat diet feeding; JNK1 or JNK2 knockout
experiment.measurement: JNK1 activation in tissues, obesity, insulin resistance

text: JNK1 deficiency in adipose tissue or muscle promotes insulin sensitivity, whereas hepatocyte-specific JNK1 deficiency promotes insulin resistance; JNK presence in macrophages appears required for establishment of obesity-induced insulin resistance and inflammation.

quotes.quote:
The presence of JNK in macrophages appears
to be required for the establishment of obesity-induced insulin
resistance and inﬂammation (424). JNK1 in adipose tissue or in
the muscle regulates insulin resistance, and JNK1 deﬁciency in
these tissues promotes insulin sensitivity (423, 425). In contrast,
hepatocyte-speciﬁc JNK1 deﬁciency promotes insulin resistance
(423, 426).

experiment.system: tissue-specific JNK1 knockout mice
experiment.perturbation: tissue-specific genetic ablation of JNK1 (adipose, muscle, hepatocyte, macrophage)
experiment.measurement: insulin sensitivity/resistance and inflammation

text: Analysis of mutant knock-in mice demonstrated that the Ser312 site of IRS1 (Ser307 in mice) is not essential for the development of insulin resistance, although it was initially considered the main mediator of JNK1-driven insulin resistance.

quotes.quote:
JNK1-
mediated insulin resistance was initially considered mainly medi-
ated by the insulin receptor adapter protein IRS1, phosphorylated
on Ser312 (Ser307 in mice), which disrupts the interaction of the
IRS1 phosphotyrosine-binding (PTB) domain with the tyrosine-
phosphorylated receptor (428). However, analysis of mutant,
knock-in mice demonstrated that the Ser312 site of IRS1 is not
essential for the development of insulin resistance (427).

experiment.system: IRS1 Ser307Ala knock-in mice
experiment.perturbation: knock-in substitution of the IRS1 JNK site
experiment.measurement: development of insulin resistance

text: JNK2-deficient cells exhibit a defect in induction of type I interferons in response to viral infection or double-stranded RNA, allowing more robust viral infection.

quotes.quote:
JNK2-deﬁcient cells ex-
hibit a defect in induction of type I interferons in response to viral
infection or double-stranded RNA that allows more robust viral
infection (439).

experiment.system: JNK2-deficient cells
experiment.perturbation: viral infection or dsRNA challenge
experiment.measurement: type I interferon induction and viral infection

text: JNK1-/- or JNK2-/- mice have normal lymphocytes and JNK activity is not required for all forms of thymocyte apoptosis, yet both JNK1 and JNK2 respond to T cell activators and are required for induction of T cell cytokines; in peripheral T cells both isozymes contribute to induction of NF-AT rather than AP-1 activity.

quotes.quote:
JNK1/ or JNK2/ mice have nor-
mal lymphocytes, and JNK activity is not required for all forms of
thymocyte apoptosis (435). Nonetheless, both JNK1 and JNK2

respond to T cell activators (436) and are required for the induc-
tion of T cell cytokines (182, 437).

where both JNK isozymes
contribute to the induction of NF-AT rather than AP-1 activity
(435, 438).

experiment.system: JNK1-/- and JNK2-/- mice, thymocytes and peripheral T cells
experiment.perturbation: JNK1 or JNK2 gene deletion; T cell activation
experiment.measurement: lymphocyte numbers, thymocyte apoptosis, cytokine induction, NF-AT/AP-1 activity

text: JNK was essential for hepatitis by being critically required for TNF-α expression in hematopoietic cells including resident inflammatory cells in the liver, rather than being required for TNF-α-stimulated cell death during disease development.

quotes.quote:
JNK was essential for hepatitis by
being critically required for TNF- expression in hematopoietic
cells, including resident inﬂammatory cells in the liver (e.g.,
Kupffer cells, which are specialized macrophages located in the
liver, and natural killer T cells) (442), rather than being required
for TNF--stimulated cell death during the development of the
disease.

experiment.system: mouse hepatitis model, hematopoietic/liver inflammatory cells
experiment.perturbation: loss of JNK in hematopoietic cells
experiment.measurement: TNF-α expression and hepatitis development

text: The YopJ enzyme of Yersinia pestis uses acetyl-CoA in acetyltransferase-mediated modification of critical residues in MAP2K activation loops, blocking their phosphorylation and activation by MAP3Ks.

quotes.quote:
The YopJ enzyme of Yersinia pestis was one of the ﬁrst path-
way-subverting enzymes identiﬁed; its use of acetyl-coenzyme A
(CoA) as a substrate in an acetyltransferase-mediated modiﬁca-
tion of critical residues in MAP2K activation loops thereby
blocked their phosphorylation and thus activation by MAP3Ks
(447).

experiment.system: MAP2K enzymes and Yersinia pestis YopJ
experiment.perturbation: YopJ acetyltransferase activity with acetyl-CoA
experiment.measurement: MAP2K activation-loop phosphorylation/activation

text: AvrA from Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium directly acetylates the activation loop of MKK7, rendering it permanently inactive and unable to be phosphorylated, and is more selective for JNK pathway inhibition than YopJ.

quotes.quote:
Unlike YopJ, which also
targets the NF-B pathway, the AvrA enzyme from Salmonella
enterica serovar Typhimurium is more selective for JNK pathway
inhibition. AvrA was found to directly acetylate the activation
loop of MKK7, rendering it permanently inactive, unable to be
phosphorylated (450).

experiment.system: MKK7 and Salmonella AvrA acetyltransferase
experiment.perturbation: AvrA-mediated acetylation
experiment.measurement: MKK7 activation-loop phosphorylation/activity

text: The VopA acetyltransferase of Vibrio parahaemolyticus targets a catalytic site lysine of different MAP2K enzymes including MKK6, disrupting ATP coordination, thereby shutting down both the JNK and p38 pathways and suppressing host cytokine production.

quotes.quote:
the VopA acetyltransferase of Vibrio para-
haemolyticus targets a catalytic site lysine of different MAP2K en-
zymes (including MKK6, but others as well), disrupting ATP co-
ordination (451). VopA thus efﬁciently shuts down both the JNK
and p38 pathways and suppresses host cytokine production.

experiment.system: host MAP2K enzymes and Vibrio parahaemolyticus VopA
experiment.perturbation: VopA acetylation of catalytic lysine
experiment.measurement: JNK/p38 pathway activity and cytokine production

text: The Eis acetyltransferase from Mycobacterium tuberculosis modifies the MAPK phosphatase MKP7 (DUSP16) to produce a hyperactive phosphatase that suppresses both JNK and p38 activity.

quotes.quote:
the Eis acetyltransferase from Mycobac-
terium tuberculosis modiﬁes the MAPK phosphatase MKP7 (also
known as DUSP16) to produce a hyperactive phosphatase that
suppresses both JNK and p38 activity (452).

experiment.system: MKP7/DUSP16 phosphatase and M. tuberculosis Eis
experiment.perturbation: Eis-mediated acetylation of MKP7
experiment.measurement: phosphatase activity and JNK/p38 activity

text: The NleD protease of enteropathogenic Escherichia coli cleaves JNK at its activation loop, resulting in JNK degradation and immune suppression.

quotes.quote:
The
NleD protease produced by enteropathogenic Escherichia coli
(EPEC) strains cleaves JNK at its activation loop, resulting in JNK
degradation and immune suppression (453).

experiment.system: host JNK and EPEC NleD protease
experiment.perturbation: NleD proteolytic cleavage
experiment.measurement: JNK cleavage/degradation and immune suppression

text: The lethal factor protease of Bacillus anthracis cleaves N-terminal docking motifs from MAP2Ks; the truncated MAP2Ks are unable to propagate ERK1/2, JNK, and p38 signaling and may act as dominant-negative inhibitors at the MAP3K level.

quotes.quote:
the catalytic site of this protease recognizes substrates with a con-
sensus similar to many MAPK docking motifs found in the host
and is known to cleave the N-terminal docking motifs from
MAP2Ks (454). The truncated MAP2Ks are unable to propagate
ERK1/2, JNK, and p38 signaling, and they may even act as domi-
nant-negative inhibitors at the MAP3K level

experiment.system: host MAP2Ks and B. anthracis lethal factor
experiment.perturbation: LF-mediated cleavage of MAP2K docking motifs
experiment.measurement: MAPK signal propagation

text: The G63 protease of Leishmania major cleaves multiple host substrates including the adaptor Tab1, without which TNF-α, Toll, and NOD receptors cannot recruit TAK1, necessary for both JNK and p38 pathway activation.

quotes.quote:
The G63 protease produced by the eukaryotic intracellular
parasite Leishmania major cleaves multiple substrates within host
cells, including the adaptor protein Tab1 (455). Without this crit-
ical scaffolding component acting at the MAP3K level, the TNF-,
Toll, and NOD receptors are unable to recruit the TAK1 kinase,
which is necessary for both JNK and p38 pathway activation.

experiment.system: host cells infected with Leishmania major
experiment.perturbation: G63 protease cleavage of Tab1
experiment.measurement: TAK1 recruitment and JNK/p38 pathway activation

text: The OspF enzyme of Shigella flexneri is a MAPK-phosphothreonine-lyase that removes a phosphate from the MAPK activation loop leaving no hydroxyl group, making rephosphorylation and MAPK reactivation impossible; OspF displays much higher activity on ERK2 or p38 than on JNKs, while the related Spvc enzyme from Salmonella Typhimurium targets phospho-JNK and phospho-ERK2.

quotes.quote:
The OspF enzyme of Shigella ﬂex-
neri, originally believed to be a phosphatase, is a MAPK-phospho-
threonine-lyase (456). After removal of a phosphate from the
activation loop of MAPKs, the lyase leaves no hydroxyl group
behind, making rephosphorylation and hence MAPK reactivation
impossible (457). Although OspF displays a much higher activity
on ERK2 or p38 than on JNKs, the related Spvc enzyme from
Salmonella Typhimurium targets phospho-JNK and phospho-
ERK2 (458).

experiment.system: host MAPKs and bacterial lyases OspF/Spvc
experiment.perturbation: lyase-mediated dephosphorylation of MAPK activation loop
experiment.measurement: MAPK phosphorylation state and substrate preference

text: In Theileria annulata, oncogenic transformation of host cells is elicited via secretion of TaPIN1, a protein related to mammalian Pin1 peptidyl-prolyl cis-trans isomerase, which acts by disabling the host FBW7 ubiquitin ligase system and thereby allowing c-Jun overproduction.

quotes.quote:
In the case of Theileria annulata, oncogenic trans-
formation is elicited via secretion of the protein TaPIN1 into the
host cells. This enzyme is related to the mammalian Pin1 peptidyl-
prolyl cis-trans isomerase and acts by disabling the host FBW7
ubiquitin ligase system, thereby allowing c-Jun overproduction
(460).

experiment.system: host cells infected with Theileria annulata
experiment.perturbation: secretion of TaPIN1 into host cells
experiment.measurement: FBW7 ubiquitin ligase function, c-Jun levels, oncogenic transformation

text: Epstein-Barr virus LMP1, which recruits TRAF6 and interacts with TRADD to recruit TRAF2, mimics activated TNF-α-like receptors and increases JNK and NF-κB activation; in infected B cells JNK pathway activation can promote survival and stop apoptosis when coactivated with NF-κB.

quotes.quote:
The latter contains two critical
linear motifs, one for the recruitment of TRAF6 and another for

LMP1 can mimic activated TNF--like receptors; it
interferes with the B cell proliferation response by turning on
TRAFs and increasing JNK and NF-B activation. In infected B
cells, JNK pathway activation can promote survival and stop
apoptosis when coactivated with NF-B (462).

experiment.system: Epstein-Barr virus-infected B lymphocytes
experiment.perturbation: LMP1 expression/TRAF recruitment
experiment.measurement: JNK and NF-κB activation, B cell survival/apoptosis

text: Highly localized JNK activity is detected at the axonal growth cone tips of neuroblasts and is required to guide the axon to its destination as part of normal physiology.

quotes.quote:
In the context of neu-
roblasts, highly localized JNK activity is detected at the axonal
growth cone tips (122) and is required to guide the axon to its
destination as part of normal physiology.

experiment.system: neuroblasts/developing axons
experiment.perturbation: observational (localized JNK activity detection)
experiment.measurement: subcellular JNK activity and axon guidance

text: A Jun-based FRET biosensor reported JNK activity and its subsequent targeting to different intracellular locations, and such cell-based assays were instrumental in revealing the all-or-none behavior of stress-activated JNK signaling.

quotes.quote:
This has
been shown with a Jun-based ﬂuorescence resonance energy
transfer (FRET) biosensor, which reported JNK activity and its
subsequent targeting to different intracellular locations (468).
Furthermore, such cell-based assays have and will allow the exam-
ination of system-level behavior of the JNK cascade and have been
instrumental in revealing the all-or-none behavior of stress-acti-
vated JNK signaling (468).

experiment.system: cells expressing a Jun-based FRET biosensor
experiment.perturbation: stress activation of JNK signaling
experiment.measurement: FRET-reported JNK activity and its intracellular localization

text: Database searches with conserved catalytic motifs and whole PTP domains identified 107 genes in the human genome encoding PTP family members, 105 of which have a mouse ortholog.

quotes.quote:
The list contains 107
genes, 105 of which have a mouse ortholog (one of
the missing genes has a rat ortholog).

we used conserved catalytic motifs and whole
PTP domains to search the publicly available databases,
as well as the SEED database, for genes encoding PTPs
or PTP-like genes.

experiment.system: human genome sequence databases (public, SEED, Celera, Incyte)
experiment.perturbation: observational; iterative homology search with PTP catalytic motifs and domains
experiment.measurement: count of genes encoding PTP-family catalytic domains and presence of mouse orthologs

text: Of the 107 human PTP genes, 106 are covered by expressed sequence tags; the sole gene lacking EST coverage, DUSP27 (DUPD1), was shown to be expressed by amplifying a partial cDNA from testis and muscle mRNA.

quotes.quote:
Of the 107 hu-
man genes, 106 are covered by expressed sequence
tags (ESTs). The only gene lacking EST coverage is
DUSP27 (DUPD1)

We have been able to amplify a partial cDNA
of this gene from testis and muscle mRNA, demonstra-
ting that this gene, too, is expressed.

experiment.system: human EST databases; human testis and muscle mRNA
experiment.perturbation: observational; RT-PCR amplification of DUSP27 partial cDNA
experiment.measurement: EST coverage per gene; presence of amplified cDNA product

text: The human DUSP13 locus at 10q22.2 comprises two phosphatase genes (designated DUSP13A/BEDP and DUSP13B/TMDP) similar to the adjacent four-exon DUSP27 at 10q22.3; the syntenic mouse chromosome 14 region also contains three tandem PTP genes, and a chimpanzee DUSP27 is 99% identical to the human across the four exons.

quotes.quote:
DUSP27 has four
exons and is located at 10q22.3 adjacent to DUSP13
at 10q22.2, which in fact consists of two phosphatase
genes, which we designate as DUSP13A and DUSP13B
(encoding BEDP and TMDP, respectively), which are
similar to the catalytic domain of DUSP27.

In the chimpan-
zee genome, there is also a DUSP27 gene, which is 99%
identical to the human within the four exons

experiment.system: human, mouse and chimpanzee genome sequences
experiment.perturbation: observational; comparative genomic analysis of the 10q22 locus
experiment.measurement: exon-intron structure, chromosomal location, gene order, and percent sequence identity

numbers.quantity: chimpanzee-human DUSP27 identity within four exons

text: Nine of the 107 human PTP genes had not been previously reported, including six small phosphatases (DUSP15, DUSP27, and the newly designated DUSP23, DUSP24, DUSP25, DUSP26) and two myotubularin-related genes designated MTMR14 and MTMR15, of which MTMR15 encodes a catalytically inactive myotubularin.

quotes.quote:
as many as nine of
the 107 human PTP genes have not been previously
reported

These genes include six small phosphatases, DUSP15,
DUSP27 (DUPD1), and four genes for which we propose
the genomic designations DUSP23, DUSP24, DUSP25,
and DUSP26.

MTMR15
encodes a catalytically inactive member of the myotubu-
larin group.

experiment.system: human genome and EST databases
experiment.perturbation: observational; comparison of identified PTP gene set against published literature
experiment.measurement: count of previously unreported genes and their assigned designations

text: VHZ, the 150 amino acid residue protein encoded by DUSP25, is the smallest catalytically active PTP, is conserved through evolution with a 147 amino acid homolog in Thermococcus kodakaraensis that is 30.3% identical and 49.7% similar over 145 residues, and a 16 kDa VHZ protein was verified in human cells by immunoblotting.

quotes.quote:
The 150 amino acid residue VHZ (VH1-
related member Z) encoded by DUSP25 is the smallest
of all catalytically active PTPs (Alonso et al., 2004) and
is remarkably well conserved through evolution and
even has a 147 amino acid homolog in Thermococcus
kodakaraensis, which is 30.3% identical and 49.7% simi-
lar over 145 residues. We have verified the existence of
a 16 kDa VHZ protein in human cells by immunoblotting.

experiment.system: human cells; DUSP25/VHZ sequence and archaeal homolog
experiment.perturbation: observational; sequence alignment plus immunoblot detection
experiment.measurement: protein length, percent identity/similarity, apparent molecular weight on immunoblot

text: Of the 107 PTP genes, 11 are catalytically inactive, 2 dephosphorylate mRNA and 13 dephosphorylate inositol phospholipids, leaving 81 active protein phosphatases able to dephosphorylate phosphotyrosine, a number close to the 85 of the 90 PTKs thought to be catalytically active.

quotes.quote:
of the 107 PTP genes, 11 are catalytically inactive,
2 dephosphorylate mRNA, and 13 dephosphorylate ino-
sitol phospholipids. Thus, 81 PTPs are active protein
phosphatases with the ability to dephosphorylate phos-
photyrosine. Of the 90 PTKs, 85 are through to be cata-
lytically active.

experiment.system: human PTP gene set (107 genes) compared with the human kinome PTK set
experiment.perturbation: observational; annotation of catalytic status and substrate class
experiment.measurement: counts of active/inactive enzymes per substrate category

text: PTPs and PTKs display comparable tissue distribution patterns, with individual cells expressing 30%–60% of the entire complement of PTPs and PTKs.

quotes.quote:
Both
types of enzymes also display comparable tissue distri-
bution patterns, from ubiquitous to cell type restricted,
so that individual cells express 30%–60% of the entire
complement of PTPs and PTKs.

experiment.system: human cells/tissues
experiment.perturbation: observational; survey of expression data for PTP and PTK genes
experiment.measurement: fraction of the PTP/PTK complement expressed per cell type

numbers.quantity: fraction of PTP/PTK complement expressed per cell

text: Eleven of the 61 VH1-like PTPs are MAP kinase phosphatases specific for Erk, Jnk and p38, characterized by dual phosphothreonine/phosphotyrosine specificity and a CH2 region with MAP kinase targeting motifs, while the PTEN (5 genes) and myotubularin (16 genes) subgroups dephosphorylate the D3-phosphate of inositol phospholipids.

quotes.quote:
Eleven of the 61 VH1-like
PTPs encoded by the human genome are specific for
the mitogen-activated protein (MAP) kinases Erk, Jnk,
and p38

the two last subgroups of DSPs, the
PTENs (5 genes) and myotubularins (16 genes), have
evolved to specifically dephosphorylate the D3-phos-
phate of inositol phospholipids

experiment.system: human VH1-like DSP genes
experiment.perturbation: observational; sequence/domain classification with reference to reported substrate specificities
experiment.measurement: subgroup gene counts and assigned substrate specificity

text: The single human class II gene ACP1 encodes the 18 kDa low Mr phosphatase, which is highly conserved: the human LMPTP is 31% identical to its Saccharomyces cerevisiae counterpart and 39% identical to the YfkJ protein of Bacillus subtilis.

quotes.quote:
This family is represented in the human genome by a
single gene, referred to as ACP1, which encodes the
18 kDa low Mr phosphatase (LMPTP).

the human LMPTP is
31% identical to the corresponding protein in Saccharo-
myces cerevisiae and 39% identical to the YfkJ protein
in Bacillus subtilis.

experiment.system: human ACP1/LMPTP and orthologs in yeast and bacteria
experiment.perturbation: observational; cross-species sequence comparison
experiment.measurement: protein molecular weight and percent sequence identity

text: At least 79 of the 107 PTPs contain at least one additional motif or domain outside their catalytic PTP domain, and the domain set only partly overlaps that of PTKs: only two human PTPs (SHP1 and SHP2) have tandem SH2 domains and no PTPs have SH3 domains, while PTPs use CRAL/TRIO and FYVE domains where PTKs use PH domains.

quotes.quote:
At least 79 of the 107 PTPs contain
at least one additional motif or domain (Table 2) out-
side of their catalytic PTP domain.

only two human PTPs (SHP1 and
SHP2) have SH2 domains organized in a tandem fashion
like in the Syk family PTKs.

In contrast, there are no
PTPs with SH3 domains.

experiment.system: human PTP and PTK protein sequences
experiment.perturbation: observational; domain annotation of all 107 PTPs
experiment.measurement: count of PTPs with accessory domains and comparison of domain repertoires

text: Among class I cysteine-based PTPs there are at least 14 catalytically inactive PTP domains, including the D2 domains of CD45, RPTPγ and RPTPζ, IA-2, STYX, MK-STYX, tensin, C1-ten, and the myotubularin-related MTMR5, MTMR9, MTMR11, MTMR12, MTMR13 and MTMR15.

quotes.quote:
Among the class I cysteine-based PTPs, there are at
least 14 catalytically inactive PTP domains, in which
critical catalytic residues have been altered.

experiment.system: human class I cysteine-based PTP domain sequences
experiment.perturbation: observational; inspection of catalytic residues in aligned PTP domains
experiment.measurement: count and identity of domains with altered critical catalytic residues

numbers.quantity: catalytically inactive class I PTP domains

text: Alternative splicing of PTP transcripts occurs in at least half of all PTPs and can create isoforms with catalytically inactive PTP domains or lacking them altogether.

quotes.quote:
In addition to these
inherently inactive PTP domains, alternative splicing of
PTP transcripts (which occurs in at least half of all PTPs)
can create isoforms that have catalytically inactive PTP
domains (Tailor et al., 1999), or lack them altogether
(Bult et al., 1997).

experiment.system: human PTP transcripts
experiment.perturbation: observational; survey of reported splice variants across the PTP gene set
experiment.measurement: fraction of PTPs with alternative splicing and the domain content of resulting isoforms

text: Ligand binding to the tandem SH2 domains of SHP1 or SHP2 opens the autoinhibited conformation, in which the N-terminal SH2 domain inserts a loop into the catalytic pocket, and activates the enzyme some 100-fold.

quotes.quote: the more N-terminal SH2 domain folds onto the catalytic

encounter a tyrosine phosphorylated ligand, the closed
conformation opens and the enzyme is activated some
100-fold (Pei et al., 1994; Pluskey et al., 1995).

experiment.system: purified SHP1/SHP2 phosphatases
experiment.perturbation: binding of tyrosine phosphorylated SH2 domain ligand
experiment.measurement: fold change in phosphatase catalytic activity

numbers.quantity: activation of SHP1/SHP2 by SH2 ligand

text: Charcot-Marie-Tooth type 4B is caused by mutation of either the catalytically active MTMR2 or the catalytically inactive MTMR13, in both cases with identical pathology and symptoms; the two proteins form a heterodimer in which MTMR2 activity depends on MTMR13.

quotes.quote:
as shown by the
human disease Charcot-Marie-Tooth type 4B, which is
caused by mutation of the catalytically active MTMR2
(Bolino et al., 2000) or the catalytically inactive MTMR13
(Azzedine et al., 2003), in both cases with identical pa-
thology and symptoms. It turns out that these two pro-
teins form a heterodimer, in which the activity of MTMR2
depends on MTMR13.

experiment.system: human patients with Charcot-Marie-Tooth type 4B; MTMR2/MTMR13 proteins
experiment.perturbation: disease-causing mutations in MTMR2 or MTMR13
experiment.measurement: clinical pathology/symptoms and MTMR2 phosphatase activity in the heterodimer

text: Two groups of DSPs are lipid-modified: VHY (DUSP15) and VHX (DUSP22) are N-terminally myristylated, while the PRLs are C-terminally farnesylated; at least 15 PTPs have been reported to be tyrosine phosphorylated, and many PTPs become noticeably more tyrosine phosphorylated when expressed as catalytically inactive mutants.

quotes.quote:
Two groups
of DSPs are modified by fatty acids: VHY (DUSP15) and
VHX (DUSP22) are N-terminally myristylated in a manner
reminiscent of Src family PTKs (Alonso et al., 2004),
while the PRLs are C-terminally farnesylated similar to
Ras GTPases.
At least 15

PTPs have been reported to be tyrosine phosphorylated,
but the physiological significance remains unclear in
most cases.

In fact, many
PTPs become noticeably more phosphorylated on tyro-
sine when expressed as catalytically inactive mutants.

experiment.system: human PTPs expressed in cells
experiment.perturbation: expression of catalytically inactive PTP mutants; survey of reported posttranslational modifications
experiment.measurement: lipid modification status and tyrosine phosphorylation of PTPs

text: Oxidation of PTP1B does not yield a stable sulfenic acid at the catalytic cysteine but rapidly transforms into a sulfenyl amide ring involving the adjacent serine residue, a form resistant to further irreversible oxidation and readily reduced back to the catalytically active free cysteinyl form.

quotes.quote:
An exciting new development was the discovery
that oxidation of PTP1B does not result in a stable sul-
fenic acid derivative of the catalytic site cysteine, but
rapidly transforms into a sulfenyl amide ring involving
the adjacent serine residue (Salmeen et al., 2003; van
Montfort et al., 2003). This form is resistant to further
oxidation, which would be irreversible, and is readily
reduced back to the free cysteinyl, catalytically active
form.

experiment.system: purified PTP1B
experiment.perturbation: oxidation of the catalytic site cysteine, followed by reduction
experiment.measurement: chemical/structural state of the catalytic cysteine and recovery of catalytic activity

text: At least 30 PTPs have been implicated in cancer, in addition to PTPs linked to metabolic, neurological, muscle and autoimmune diseases; disruption of the PTP1B gene in mice indicated that this PTP acts as a negative regulator of insulin signaling.

quotes.quote:
The effect of disruption of the
PTP1B gene in mice, which indicated that this PTP acts
as a negative regulator of insulin signaling (Elchebly
et al., 1999), ignited the interest of the pharmaceutical
industry.

In addition to metabolic, neurological, muscle,
and autoimmune diseases, at least 30 PTPs have been
implicated in cancer (listed in Andersen et al. [2004]).

experiment.system: PTP1B knockout mice; literature survey of human PTP disease associations
experiment.perturbation: gene disruption of PTP1B in mice
experiment.measurement: insulin signaling phenotype; number of PTPs reported implicated in cancer

text: Modeling of a set of class I PTP catalytic domains from PTP crystal structures, colored by surface-exposed residue charge, showed striking diversity in surface topology and charge distribution among class I PTPs; for PTP1B a unique second PTyr binding site was used to develop highly specific bidentate inhibitors binding both sites.

quotes.quote:
Figure 3 shows the surface topology and
charge distribution of a representative set of catalytic
PTP domains to illustrate the striking diversity within
the class I PTPs.

These structures were modeled using the crystal structures of PTPs, and the models are colored according to charge of surface-exposed
amino acid residues.

for PTP1B it was found
that a unique second PTyr binding site (Puius et al.,
1997; Salmeen et al., 2000) could be used to develop
highly specific bidentate inhibitors that bind both sites
(Zhang, 2002).

experiment.system: class I PTP catalytic domains; PTP1B
experiment.perturbation: observational; homology modeling from PTP crystal structures and structure-based inhibitor design
experiment.measurement: surface charge/topology of modeled catalytic domains; inhibitor specificity and binding sites

text: Overexpression of Cbl-b or Cbl-3 in CHO cells accelerated removal of coexpressed EGFR from the cell surface and enhanced its ubiquitination and degradation, while the SH2-defective short variant Cbl-3S did not affect EGFR ubiquitination and the oncogenic variants v-Cbl and 70Z-Cbl inhibited rather than stimulated receptor downregulation.

quotes.quote: Overexpression of Cbl-b or Cbl-3 in Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells led to an accelerated removal from the cell surface of a cooverexpressed EGFR (Figure 1A and data not shown). Concomitant with accelerated endocytosis, the receptor underwent enhanced ubiquitination and degradation (Figure 1B). Interestingly, an alternatively spliced short variant of Cbl-3 (Cbl-3S), whose SH2 domain is defective, did not affect ubiquitination of EGFR. On the other hand, the two known oncogenic variants of Cbl, v-Cbl and 70Z-Cbl (Langdon et al., 1989), inhibit rather than stimulate the rate of receptor downregulation

experiment.system: CHO cells cotransfected with EGFR, HA-ubiquitin, and Cbl-family plasmids

text: Cross-linked FLAG-RagB immunoprecipitates from HEK-293T cells contained Mios, a 100 kDa WD40-repeat protein, and recombinant Mios co-immunoprecipitated endogenous RagA and RagC.

we treated human embryonic
kidney (HEK)-293T cells expressing FLAG-tagged RagB with a chemical cross-linker, and
identified via mass spectrometry proteins that co-immunoprecipitate with FLAG-RagB. This

as well as Mios, a 100 kDa WD40-repeat protein not previously studied

endogenous RagA and RagC co-immunoprecipitated with
recombinant Mios expressed in HEK-293T cells

text: Mios is necessary for amino acid signaling to TORC1: RNAi of Mios in human cells inhibited amino acid-induced S6K1 phosphorylation, and dsRNA against the fly ortholog Mio ablated dTORC1 signaling and reduced S2 cell size.

quotes.quote:
Suppression of Mios, by RNA interference (RNAi) in human cells,
strongly inhibited the amino acid-induced activation of mTORC1, as detected by the
phosphorylation state of its substrate S6K1 (Fig. 1B, S2B). Moreover, in Drosophila S2
cells, dsRNAs targeting Mio (10), the fly ortholog of Mios, ablated dTORC1 signaling and
also reduced cell size

experiment.system: HEK-293T cells and Drosophila S2 cells
experiment.perturbation: shRNA/dsRNA knockdown of Mios/Mio with amino acid starvation and restimulation
experiment.measurement: immunoblotting of S6K1 phosphorylation; cell size histogram

text: GATOR1 mediates the GATOR-Rag interaction: FLAG-DEPDC5 co-immunoprecipitated much more endogenous RagA and RagC than FLAG-WDR24, and amino acid starvation increased Rag binding to DEPDC5.

co-immunoprecipitated much more endogenous RagA and RagC than FLAG-WDR24, as

depletion of other GATOR2
components or their Drosophila orthologs strongly blunted amino acid-induced activation of
mTORC1 and dTORC1, respectively (Fig. 2, A, C, and D; S2, A, B, C, and D). In contrast,

mTORC1 and dTORC1 normally caused by amino acid deprivation

dsRNAs targeting dSeh1L or dDEPDC5 decreased and increased, respectively, S2

text: GATOR1 and GATOR2 have opposite effects on mTOR lysosomal localization: Mios or Seh1L knockdown blocked amino acid-induced mTOR translocation to LAMP2-positive membranes, whereas DEPDC5 knockdown caused constitutive lysosomal mTOR and DEPDC5 overexpression blocked translocation; GATOR2 is not needed for proper Rag localization.

amino acid-induced translocation of mTOR to the lysosomal surface (Fig. 3C). Unlike

in vitro GATOR1 preferentially
interacted with the RagBQ99L-containing heterodimer

(TCGA) identified a subset of glioblastomas and ovarian cancers with nonsense or
frameshift mutations or truncating deletions in DEPDC5 or NPRL2. In most of these tumors,

inactivating mutations in GATOR1
components are present in low single digit percentages of glioblastomas and ovarian
cancers

The extracellular CRD is perched on 
top of the LD, which forms a wedge between TMD and CRD. At the apex of this wedge, the 
CRD contacts the TMD through the elongated TMD extracellular loop 3 (ECL3)
The overall architecture is stabilised by nine disulphide bridges

cholesterol did not significantly change the conformational stability of 
the SMO TMD (Fig. 4b)

the thermostability of purified 
SMOΔC was reduced when cholesterol was depleted with methyl-β-cyclodextrin

We determined the crystal 
structure of SMO in complex with vismodegib, a potent TMD antagonist, to 3.3 Å resolution

ring of Phe484. Asp473, a residue mutated in vismodegib-resistant cancers14,29,30 stabilises 
the potential hydrogen-bonding network around Arg400

text: cGAS shows remarkable fold similarity to OAS1 — overall fold, several active site features, lobe arrangement and platform elements including the long spine helix — but OAS1 is activated by A-form RNA while cGAS is activated by B-form DNA, with the Zn-thumb present in cGAS and missing in OAS1.

quotes.quote: cGAS has remarkable fold similarity to the antiviral protein oligoadenylate synthase 1 (OAS1) 29,30 (Fig. 5). OAS1 synthesizes 2’-5’ linked oligoadenylate chains (2-5OA) in response to binding to cytosolic dsRNA. The structural similarity not only embraces the overall fold, several active site features, and arrangement of lobes 1 and 2, but also certain structural elements of the platform, including the long “spine” helix.

while OAS1 is activated by A-form RNA, cGAS is activated by B-form DNA. The Zn-thumb in cGAS, missing in OAS1, likely acts a molecular “ruler” to specifically trigger activation in response to B-form but not A-form nucleic acids

experiment.system: genomes of model organisms
experiment.perturbation: observational (sequence ortholog search)
experiment.measurement: presence or absence of SAMTOR gene orthologs

text: Overexpression of SAMTOR suppresses mTORC1 signaling in a dose-dependent fashion, as measured by S6K1 Thr389 phosphorylation.

quotes.quote: SAMTOR expression suppressed mTORC1 signaling in a

dose-dependent fashion (Fig. 2A), establishing SAMTOR as a negative regulator of the 
pathway.

experiment.system: HEK-293T cells
experiment.perturbation: transfection with increasing amounts of HA-SAMTOR cDNA plus 2 ng FLAG-S6K1
experiment.measurement: immunoblotting for phospho-Thr389 S6K1

text: Overexpressed GFP-SAMTOR displaces mTOR from lysosomes to an extent similar to GFP-Sestrin2.

quotes.quote:
overexpression of green fluorescent protein (GFP)-tagged SAMTOR 
displaced mTOR from lysosomes to an extent similar to that seen with GFP-Sestrin2, an 
inhibitor of GATOR2 (21, 22) (Fig. 2B).

experiment.system: wild-type HEK-293T cells
experiment.perturbation: transient expression of GFP-metap2, GFP-SAMTOR, or GFP-Sestrin2
experiment.measurement: immunofluorescence colocalization of mTOR with lysosomal marker LAMP2

text: SAMTOR overexpression inhibits mTORC1 signaling with wild-type RagA/RagC but not with the constitutively active RagA Q66L/RagC S75N heterodimer, and not in cells lacking a GATOR1 or KICSTOR component, placing SAMTOR upstream of the Rag GTPases and dependent on GATOR1 and KICSTOR.

quotes.quote:
Overexpression of SAMTOR inhibited 
mTORC1 signaling when coexpressed with the wild type RagA and RagC heterodimer, but 
not with the constitutively active mutant heterodimer (RagA Q66L and RagC S75N) that 
bypasses the requirement for amino acids for maintaining mTORC1 activity (Fig. 2C)

In addition, SAMTOR did not inhibit mTORC1 signaling in cells lacking either a GATOR1 
or KICSTOR component.

experiment.system: HEK-293T cells, wild-type, Nprl3-deficient or SZT2-deficient
experiment.perturbation: coexpression of SAMTOR with wild-type or constitutively active Rag heterodimers; amino acid starvation 50 min and restimulation 10 min
experiment.measurement: FLAG-S6K1 immunoprecipitation and immunoblotting for phosphorylation

text: SAMTOR binds SAM with a dissociation constant of approximately 7 μM and also binds SAH in a competition assay.

quotes.quote:
determined 
that SAMTOR binds SAM with a dissociation constant of approximately 7 μM (Fig. 3B). A 
competition binding assay revealed that, as with other SAM-binding proteins, SAMTOR can 
also bind S-adenosylhomocysteine (SAH), the demethylated form of SAM (Fig. 3B).

experiment.system: purified FLAG-SAMTOR protein
experiment.perturbation: incubation with [3H]SAM and unlabeled SAM or SAH at indicated concentrations
experiment.measurement: equilibrium radioligand binding assay

numbers.quantity: dissociation constant of SAMTOR for SAM

text: SAM and SAH, but not methionine, homocysteine, adenosine, 5-methylthioadenosine, leucine, or isoleucine, disrupt the SAMTOR–GATOR1-KICSTOR interaction when added to the immunopurified complex; disruption occurs with 100 μM SAM or SAH but not 1 mM of the other compounds.

quotes.quote:
SAM and SAH, but not methionine, homocysteine, 
adenosine, 5-methylthioadenosine, leucine, or isoleucine, disrupted the interaction when 
added directly to the immunopurified complex kept at 4°C (Fig. 3 C and D).

The interaction between SAMTOR and GATOR1 is disrupted by 100 μM SAM or SAH, 
but not by 1mM methionine, homocysteine, adenosine, 5-methylthioadenosine, leucine, or 
isoleucine.

experiment.system: FLAG immunoprecipitates from endogenously FLAG-tagged Depdc5 HEK-293T cells
experiment.perturbation: direct addition of SAM, SAH, or other metabolites to immunoprecipitates at 4°C
experiment.measurement: immunoblotting for SAMTOR retained in the immunoprecipitate

text: SAMTOR mutants G172A and D190A no longer bind SAM, coimmunoprecipitate more endogenous GATOR1 and KICSTOR than wild-type, are insensitive to SAM in vitro, yet inhibit mTORC1 signaling comparably to wild-type SAMTOR despite lower expression.

quotes.quote:
Mutagenesis of highly conserved residues in human SAMTOR yielded two mutants, Gly172-
>Ala (G172A) and Asp190->Ala (D190A), that no longer bound SAM (Fig. 3E and fig. S2, 
A and B). These mutants coimmunoprecipitated greater amounts of endogenous GATOR1 
and KICSTOR than did wild-type SAMTOR, and the purified complexes were insensitive to 
SAM in vitro (Fig. 3F). Moreover, these mutants inhibited mTORC1 signaling comparably 
to wild-type SAMTOR, despite their lower expression (Fig. 3G).

experiment.system: HEK-293T cells expressing wild-type or mutant HA-SAMTOR
experiment.perturbation: point mutations G172A and D190A; SAM addition to immunoprecipitates
experiment.measurement: [3H]SAM binding assay, HA immunoprecipitation immunoblotting, S6K1 phosphorylation

text: Methionine starvation lowers cellular SAM concentrations from above to below the SAMTOR dissociation constant for SAM, whereas SAH concentrations remain below the Ki of SAMTOR for SAH in both replete and starved cells.

quotes.quote:
SAM concentrations in HEK-293T cells 
decreased upon methionine starvation, falling from above the dissociation constant of 
SAMTOR for SAM to below it (Fig. 4A). In contrast, in both methionine replete and starved 
cells, SAH concentrations were lower than the Ki of SAMTOR for SAH (Fig. 4A)

HEK-293Tcells were incubated with or withoutmethionine for 2 hours before sample 
preparation for liquid chromatography/mass spectrometry (LC/MS)– based measurements of 
the absolute amounts of the indicated metabolites.

experiment.system: HEK-293T cells
experiment.perturbation: incubation with or without methionine for 2 hours
experiment.measurement: LC/MS absolute quantification of SAM and SAH

text: Methionine starvation strongly increases the SAMTOR–GATOR1 interaction in cells, and re-addition of methionine or SAM returns the interaction to baseline.

quotes.quote:
methionine starvation strongly increased this 
interaction in cells. The addition to the methionine-starved cells of either methionine or 
SAM, which can enter cells when used at high concentrations, reduced the interaction to 
baseline levels (Fig. 4B).

starved of methionine for 2 hours (–Met) and then restimulated for 20 
min with 100 μM methionine (+Met) or 1 mM SAM (+SAM)

experiment.system: HEK-293T cells transiently expressing HA-metap2 or HA-SAMTOR
experiment.perturbation: 2 hour methionine starvation, then 20 min restimulation with 100 μM methionine or 1 mM SAM
experiment.measurement: HA immunoprecipitation and immunoblotting for GATOR1 components

text: Methionine starvation weakens the GATOR1–GATOR2 interaction in a SAMTOR-dependent fashion, and SAMTOR overexpression alone dose-dependently disrupts that interaction.

quotes.quote:
Methionine starvation weakened the interaction between GATOR1 and GATOR2 in a 
SAMTOR-dependent fashion, whereas methionine addition restored the interaction to 
normal levels (fig. S3, A and B). Additionally, in a dose-dependent manner, SAMTOR 
overexpression was sufficient to disrupt the interaction between GATOR1 and GATOR2 (fig. 
S3, C and D).

experiment.system: HEK-293T cells with and without SAMTOR
experiment.perturbation: methionine starvation and re-addition; graded SAMTOR overexpression
experiment.measurement: coimmunoprecipitation immunoblotting of GATOR1 and GATOR2 components

text: Methionine starvation inhibits mTORC1 signaling in a SAMTOR-dependent fashion across multiple cell types, whereas loss of SAMTOR does not prevent inhibition by leucine, arginine, or growth factor withdrawal.

quotes.quote:
in multiple cell types, 
methionine starvation inhibited mTORC1 signaling in a SAMTOR-dependent fashion, as 
measured by the phosphorylation of the mTORC1 substrates S6K1 at Thr389 and 4E-BP1 at 
Ser65 (Fig. 4C and fig. S4, A to C). In contrast, loss of SAMTOR did not prevent the 
inhibition of mTORC1 signaling caused by withdrawal of leucine, arginine (Fig. 4D) or 
growth factors (fig. S4D).

experiment.system: HEK-293T cells stably coexpressing Cas9 and guides targeting SAMTOR, and other cell types
experiment.perturbation: 2 hour starvation of methionine, leucine, or arginine
experiment.measurement: immunoblotting for phospho-S6K1 Thr389 and phospho-4E-BP1 Ser65

text: Methionine starvation reduces mTOR–lysosome colocalization in wild-type but not SAMTOR-null cells, and reexpression of wild-type SAMTOR, but not a SAM-binding deficient mutant, restores methionine sensing in SAMTOR-null cells.

quotes.quote:
methionine starvation 
also reduced the colocalization of mTOR with lysosomes in wild-type but not SAMTOR-
null cells (Fig. 4E). Furthermore, reexpression of wild-type SAMTOR, but not a SAM-
binding deficient mutant, restored the capacity of the mTORC1 pathway to sense methionine 
in the SAMTOR-null HEK-293T cells (Fig. 4F).

experiment.system: SAMTOR-deficient and control HEK-293T cells
experiment.perturbation: 2 hour methionine starvation; transfection with wild-type or G172A SAMTOR cDNA
experiment.measurement: immunofluorescence mTOR/LAMP2 colocalization; S6K1 phosphorylation immunoblotting

text: Methionine starvation partially reduces SAMTOR levels in a proteasome-dependent manner, but this degradation is not required for mTORC1 to respond to methionine starvation.

quotes.quote:
Methionine starvation partially reduced 
SAMTOR levels in a proteasome-dependent manner (Fig. 4, B, C, and F, and fig. S4D) but 
this degradation was not required for mTORC1 to respond to methionine starvation (fig. 
S4E).

experiment.system: HEK-293T cells
experiment.perturbation: methionine starvation with proteasome inhibition
experiment.measurement: immunoblotting for SAMTOR levels and mTORC1 substrate phosphorylation

text: In Drosophila S2R+ cells, dTOR signaling responds to methionine and leucine; knockdown of dSamtor (CG3570) prevents inhibition of dTOR by methionine starvation while dSesn dsRNA prevents inhibition by leucine starvation.

quotes.quote:
we found that knock-down of dSamtor (encoded by the gene CG3570), but not of dSesn, 
prevented inhibition of dTOR signaling by methionine starvation (Fig. 4G and fig. S4F). 
However, the dsRNA targeting dSesn did prevent inhibition of dTOR by leucine starvation.

as detected by the phosphorylation of dS6K at 
residue Thr398 (Fig. 4G)

experiment.system: Drosophila S2R+ cells
experiment.perturbation: dsRNA-induced RNAi against dSamtor or dSesn; 1 hour methionine or leucine starvation
experiment.measurement: immunoblotting for dS6K Thr398 phosphorylation

text: Addition of SAM to methionine-starved cells reactivates mTORC1 signaling, and acute doxycycline-mediated loss of MAT2A greatly attenuates mTORC1 sensing of methionine while leaving activation by SAM largely intact.

quotes.quote:
the 
addition of SAM to methionine-starved cells reactivated mTORC1 signaling (Fig. 4H), 
indicating that it is the drop in SAM levels that mediates the inhibitory effects of methionine 
restriction on mTORC1.

the loss of 
MAT2A greatly attenuated the capacity of mTORC1 to sense methionine while leaving its 
activation by SAM largely intact (Fig. 4H).

MAT2A 
dox-off HEK-293Tcells were treated with doxycycline (30 ng/ml) for 50 hours before 
starving them as in (C).

experiment.system: MAT2A doxycycline-repressible (dox-off) HEK-293T cells
experiment.perturbation: doxycycline (30 ng/ml) for 50 hours to suppress MAT2A; methionine starvation and SAM or methionine restimulation
experiment.measurement: immunoblotting for mTORC1 substrate phosphorylation

text: In a phase 1 trial of 129 patients with KRAS p.G12C-mutant advanced solid tumors (59 NSCLC, 42 colorectal, 28 other), no dose-limiting toxic effects or treatment-related deaths were observed; 73 patients (56.6%) had treatment-related adverse events and 15 (11.6%) had grade 3 or 4 events.

quotes.quote:
A total of 129 patients (59 with NSCLC, 42 with colorectal cancer, and 28 with 
other tumors) were included in dose escalation and expansion cohorts.

No dose-
limiting toxic effects or treatment-related deaths were observed. A total of 73 patients (56.6%) had 
treatment-related adverse events; 15 patients (11.6%) had grade 3 or 4 events.

experiment.system: patients with advanced solid tumors harboring KRAS p.G12C mutation
experiment.perturbation: oral sotorasib once daily (180, 360, 720, 960 mg) in dose escalation and expansion cohorts
experiment.measurement: safety: incidence of dose-limiting toxic effects and treatment-related adverse events graded by CTCAE v5.0

numbers.quantity: patients with grade 3 or 4 treatment-related events

text: Patients enrolled were heavily pretreated, with a median of 3 (range, 0 to 11) previous lines of anticancer therapy for metastatic disease and 78 patients (60.5%) having received 3 or more previous lines; median follow-up was 11.7 months.

quotes.quote:
with a median of 3 (range, 0 to 11) previous lines of anticancer therapy for 
metastatic disease; 78 patients (60.5%) had received 3 or more previous lines, and 75% of 
patients with NSCLC and 98% with colorectal cancer had received 2 or more previous lines 
of therapy.
The median follow-up was 11.7 months (range, 4.6 to 21.2).

experiment.system: 129 enrolled phase 1 trial patients with KRAS p.G12C-mutant advanced solid tumors
experiment.perturbation: observational (baseline characteristics)
experiment.measurement: prior lines of systemic therapy, follow-up duration

text: ASC-deficient macrophages failed to activate caspase-1 and release IL-1β in response to transfected poly(dA-dT), while macrophages lacking NLRP3, NLRP6 and NLRP12 responded normally.

quotes.quote:
Although ASC-deficient macrophages failed to activate caspase-1 and 
trigger IL-1β release in response to poly(dA-dT) · poly(dA-dT) [hereafter referred to as 
poly(dA-dT)])2, macrophages lacking NLRP3, −6 and −12 responded normally (Fig. 1a).

experiment.system: LPS-primed bone marrow derived macrophages from wild type and inflammasome-deficient (ASC, NLRP3, NLRP6, NLRP12) mice
experiment.perturbation: transfection of poly(dA-dT)
experiment.measurement: IL-1β ELISA and cleaved caspase-1 immunoblot

text: ASC-deficient macrophages produced higher levels of IFNβ and IL-6 after poly(dA-dT), which was not seen in cells lacking NLRP3 or the IL1R, and poly(dA-dT)-induced cell death was ASC-dependent; the authors speculate the increased cytokine production relates to resistance to cell death.

quotes.quote:
Surprisingly, we found that macrophages lacking ASC had higher levels of IFNβ and IL-6 in 
response to poly(dA-dT), which was not observed in cells lacking NLRP3, the IL1R or to a 
lesser extent caspase-1 (Supplementary Fig. 1a–d). Poly(dA-dT) induced cell death also 
occurred in an ASC-dependent manner (Supplementary Fig. 1e–f).

experiment.system: macrophages from ASC-, NLRP3-, IL1R- and caspase-1-deficient mice
experiment.perturbation: transfection of poly(dA-dT)
experiment.measurement: IFNβ and IL-6 (qRT-PCR/ELISA) and cell death

text: dsDNA from natural sources activated caspase-1 cleavage, whereas ISD, long ssDNA poly(dI), transfected dsRNA and Sendai virus failed to trigger this response in NLRP3-deficient macrophages.

quotes.quote:
In addition to poly(dA-dT), dsDNA from natural sources activated 
caspase-1 cleavage (Supplementary Fig. 2a–b). In contrast, a small immunostimulatory 
oligonucleotide (ISD)3, long ssDNA (poly(dI)), transfected dsRNA or the ssRNA virus 
Sendai virus failed to trigger this response in NLRP3-deficient macrophages 
(Supplementary Fig. 2c).

experiment.system: NLRP3-deficient murine macrophages
experiment.perturbation: transfection of natural dsDNA, ISD, poly(dI), dsRNA, or Sendai virus infection
experiment.measurement: caspase-1 cleavage by immunoblot

text: IFIX, IFI16 and MNDA were predicted and observed to localize to the nucleus, whereas AIM2 was predicted cytosolic and its fluorescent chimera was almost exclusively cytoplasmic.

quotes.quote:
Sequence analysis of IFIX, IFI16 and MNDA 
predicted their nuclear localization, in contrast to AIM2, which was predicted to be cytosolic 
(Fig. 1c, lower panel). Consistent with these predictions, fluorescent protein chimeras of 
IFIX, IFI16 and MNDA localized to the nucleus, while AIM2 was almost exclusively 
cytoplasmic (Fig. 1d).

experiment.system: 293T cells expressing CFP-tagged human PYHIN proteins; PSORTII sequence analysis
experiment.perturbation: observational (localization prediction and expression of tagged constructs)
experiment.measurement: confocal microscopy subcellular localization

text: Of the PYHIN PYD domains tested, only AIM2-PYD formed cytosolic complexes with ASC-YFP, and only AIM2-PYD and NLRP3-PYD co-immunoprecipitated with HA-tagged ASC; full-length AIM2-CFP but not IFIX, IFI16 or MNDA gave similar results.

quotes.quote:
Of all the 
PYHIN-PYD proteins tested, only AIM2-PYD led to complex formation with ASC (Fig. 2a, 
b and Supplementary Fig. 4). Similar results were obtained with full-length AIM2-CFP but 
not full-length IFIX, IFI16 or MNDA
only AIM2-PYD and NLRP3-PYD were found to
bind HA-tagged ASC in co-immunoprecipitation studies (Fig. 2c).

experiment.system: HEK293 cells stably expressing polydispersed ASC-YFP; 293T cells
experiment.perturbation: overexpression of PYD-CFP fusions or full-length PYHIN proteins with HA-ASC
experiment.measurement: confocal imaging of ASC-YFP aggregation and anti-HA co-immunoprecipitation/immunoblot

text: Endogenous ASC associated with endogenous AIM2, but not IFI16, in primed THP-1 cells.

quotes.quote:
Finally, endogenous ASC 
associated with endogenous AIM2, but not IFI16 in primed THP-1 cells (Fig. 2d).

experiment.system: PMA-differentiated THP-1 cells primed with Sendai virus
experiment.perturbation: observational (endogenous protein interaction after priming)
experiment.measurement: anti-ASC immunoprecipitation followed by AIM2 and IFI16 immunoblot

text: Only NLRP3-PYD and AIM2-PYD activated an NF-κB reporter in the presence of ASC, with full-length AIM2 more dramatic; ASC was absolutely required and no substantial IFNβ promoter activation was seen with any PYHIN member.

quotes.quote:
Only NLRP3-PYD and AIM2-PYD led to potent NF-κB activation (Fig. 2e). The 
effect of full length AIM2 was even more dramatic (Fig. 2e, bottom panel). The full-length 
versions of IFIX, IFI16 and MNDA failed to activate NF-κB (Supplementary Fig. 5c). ASC 
was absolutely required, since no substantial NF-κB reporter activity was observed in cells 
not transfected with ASC. No substantial activation of the IFNβ promoter reporter gene was 
observed with any of the PYHIN family members (Supplementary Fig. 6).

experiment.system: cells transfected with PYD/full-length PYHIN constructs with or without ASC
experiment.perturbation: overexpression of PYHIN proteins ± ASC
experiment.measurement: NF-κB and IFNβ luciferase reporter gene activity

text: In reconstituted 293T cells, only NLRP3-PYD and AIM2-PYD induced pro-IL-1β maturation when ASC and caspase-1 were co-expressed, with full-length AIM2 more potent than AIM2-PYD; IFIX, IFI16 and MNDA constructs did not induce cleavage.

quotes.quote:
Among the PYD proteins tested, only that of 
NLRP3-PYD and AIM2-PYD induced maturation of pro-IL-1β, when ASC and caspase-1 
were co-expressed (Fig. 3a). Full-length AIM2 was even more potent than AIM2-PYD (Fig. 
3a, lower panel). Neither the PYD domain nor the full-length versions of IFIX, IFI16 or 
MNDA induced IL-1β cleavage (Supplementary Fig. 7).

experiment.system: 293T cells
experiment.perturbation: transient co-overexpression of PYHIN proteins with ASC, caspase-1 and flag-tagged pro-IL-1β
experiment.measurement: immunoblot of pro-IL-1β cleavage

text: AIM2 was expressed constitutively in primary macrophages and B6-MCLs and further induced by poly(dA-dT) or Sendai virus; of three shRNAs tested, two (AIM2 #2 and #3) strongly reduced AIM2 expression.

quotes.quote:
AIM2 
was expressed constitutively in both primary macrophages and in B6-MCLs and was further 
induced by poly(dA-dT) or Sendai virus (Supplementary Fig. 8). Three different shRNAs 
were tested, of which two (shRNA AIM2 #2 and AIM2 #3) resulted in a strong reduction of 
AIM2 expression (Fig. 3b).

experiment.system: primary murine macrophages and immortalized macrophage cell lines (B6-MCLs)
experiment.perturbation: lentiviral shRNA knockdown of AIM2; stimulation with poly(dA-dT) or Sendai virus
experiment.measurement: AIM2/HPRT1 expression by quantitative RT-PCR

text: Knockdown of AIM2, but not of an unrelated gene, strongly attenuated poly(dA-dT)-mediated IL-1β release and caspase-1 cleavage in macrophages, and siRNA targeting of AIM2 in THP1 cells corroborated this.

quotes.quote:
Knocking down AIM2, but not an unrelated gene, resulted in a 
strong attenuation of poly(dA-dT)-mediated IL-1β release (Fig. 3c) and caspase-1 cleavage 
(Fig. 3d). Targeting AIM2 in THP1 cells using siRNA corroborated these findings 
(Supplementary Fig. 8d and e).

experiment.system: LPS-primed shRNA-transduced murine macrophage cell lines and siRNA-transfected THP1 cells
experiment.perturbation: shRNA/siRNA knockdown of AIM2 followed by poly(dA-dT) transfection
experiment.measurement: IL-1β ELISA and caspase-1 cleavage immunoblot

text: AIM2 knockdown markedly enhanced poly(dA-dT)-mediated type I IFN induction while the IFNβ response to Sendai virus was unaffected, and AIM2 shRNA-targeted macrophages were resistant to poly(dA-dT)-triggered cell death.

quotes.quote:
knocking down AIM2 resulted in a marked 
enhancement of poly(dA-dT)-mediated type I IFN induction (Supplementary Fig. 8b). This 
effect was specific since the IFNβ response to Sendai virus was unaffected (Supplementary 
Fig. 8c).

macrophages that were targeted with AIM2 shRNAs were resistant to 
poly(dA-dT) triggered cell death (Fig. 3e).

experiment.system: shRNA-transduced murine macrophage cell lines
experiment.perturbation: AIM2 knockdown with poly(dA-dT) transfection or Sendai virus infection
experiment.measurement: IFNβ by quantitative RT-PCR; cell counting 24h after transfection

text: Vaccinia virus-induced caspase-1 cleavage was ASC-dependent but NLRP3-independent and required AIM2, since AIM2 shRNA impaired vaccinia-induced but not anthrax lethal toxin-induced caspase-1 cleavage; vaccinia-triggered cell death was also strongly reduced in AIM2-targeted macrophages.

quotes.quote:
vaccinia virus-induced caspase-1 cleavage occurred in an ASC-dependent but 
NLRP3-independent manner (Fig. 3f). This effect was also dependent on AIM2, since 
shRNA-mediated knock down of AIM2 impaired vaccinia virus induced caspase-1 cleavage 
but not that induced by anthrax lethal toxin (Fig. 3g).

Vaccinia virus-
triggered cell death was also strongly reduced in AIM2 shRNA targeted macrophages, but 
not in control macrophages (Fig. 3h).

experiment.system: macrophages from ASC- and NLRP3-deficient mice and NLRP3-deficient shRNA-expressing macrophage lines
experiment.perturbation: vaccinia virus (WR strain) infection or anthrax lethal toxin, with AIM2 or control shRNA knockdown
experiment.measurement: caspase-1 cleavage immunoblot after 6h; cell survival by calcein AM staining 24h later

text: Full-length AIM2 and the AIM2-HIN domain, but not AIM2-PYD or NLRP3, co-localized with FITC-labeled poly(dA-dT) forming cytosolic DNA/protein aggregates, and flow-cytometric FRET showed a dose-dependent increase between full-length AIM2 and FITC-dsDNA while AIM2-PYD gave no measurable FRET.

quotes.quote:
While cells expressing NLRP3 or AIM2-PYD showed no co-
localization of the respective proteins with FITC-dsDNA, full-length AIM2 and AIM2-HIN 
domain showed extensive co-localization with FITC-dsDNA and led to the formation of 
DNA/protein aggregates in the cytosol (Fig. 4a).

A dose-dependent increase in FRET between full-length AIM2 and FITC-dsDNA 
was seen, while AIM2-PYD did not lead to measurable FRET. Other proteins such as 
NLRP3 or IFI16 did not show any FRET (data not shown).

experiment.system: 293T cells
experiment.perturbation: co-transfection of FITC-labeled poly(dA-dT) with CFP-tagged full-length AIM2, AIM2-HIN, AIM2-PYD or NLRP3
experiment.measurement: confocal co-localization and single-cell flow cytometry FRET efficiency

text: In binding assays with purified proteins, only full-length AIM2 or the AIM2-HIN domain bound biotinylated poly(dA-dT) with high affinity, and binding was specific since AIM2 did not bind biotin-LPS, which bound soluble CD14 under similar conditions.

quotes.quote:
binding studies 
using purified AIM2, AIM2-HIN domain and AIM2-PYD domain with biotinylated 
poly(dA-dT) (biotin-dsDNA) revealed that AIM2 directly interacted with poly(dA-dT) with 
high affinity; only full-length AIM2 or the AIM2-HIN domain were able to bind biotin-
dsDNA (Fig. 4c). Binding of poly(dA-dT) to AIM2 was specific, since AIM2 did not bind 
biotin-LPS, which bound to soluble CD14 under similar assay conditions (Fig. 4c).

experiment.system: FLAG/HIS-purified AIM2, AIM2-HIN and AIM2-PYD proteins expressed in 293T cells
experiment.perturbation: incubation with biotinylated poly(dA-dT) or biotin-LPS
experiment.measurement: AlphaScreen association assay luminescence

text: The affinity of the morphinan agonist BU72 for the μOR is enhanced 47 fold when the receptor is coupled to the G protein Gi.

quotes.quote:
In the case of the μOR, 
the affinity for the morphinan agonist BU72 is enhanced by 47 fold when coupled to the G 
protein Gi (Fig. 1b, c).

In the presence of Gi, the affinity of the 
morphinan agonist BU72 increases 47 fold.

experiment.system: purified μOR reconstituted into HDL particles
experiment.perturbation: addition of 500 nM heterotrimeric Gi
experiment.measurement: 3H-diprenorphine radioligand competition binding

numbers.quantity: fold increase in BU72 affinity with Gi

text: In the presence of 5 μM nanobody 39 (Nb39), the affinity of BU72 for μOR increases from 470 pM to 16 pM (a 29-fold increase in affinity), and Nb39 also enhances affinity of DAMGO and endomorphin-2.

quotes.quote:
In presence of 5 μM nanobody 39 (Nb39), the affinity of 
the potent morphinan agonist BU7227 increases from 470 pM to 16 pM (Fig. 1b).

Nb39 also enhances the affinity of μOR agonists DAMGO and endomorphin-2, indicating 
that the effect is not limited to morphinan agonists

A similar 29-fold increase 
in affinity is observed in presence of Nb39.

experiment.system: purified μOR reconstituted into HDL particles
experiment.perturbation: addition of 5 μM Nb39
experiment.measurement: 3H-DPN agonist competition binding affinity

text: The dissociation half-life of BU72 from μOR is 43 minutes and increases to 140 minutes in the presence of Nb39.

quotes.quote:
BU72 has 
a dissociation half-life of 140 minutes in the presence of Nb39 (Extended Data Fig. 1b).
The dissociation t1/2 of BU72 is 43 minutes and increases to 140 minutes in presence of Nb39.

experiment.system: purified μOR in HDL particles
experiment.perturbation: BU72 with or without Nb39
experiment.measurement: dissociation kinetics via 3H-DPN association rate (Motulsky-Mahan method)

text: A 2.1 Å X-ray crystal structure of μOR bound to BU72 and the G protein-mimetic nanobody Nb39 was obtained from lipidic mesophase crystals, with the complete data set produced by merging diffraction data from four crystals; Nb39 binds the intracellular surface of the receptor.

quotes.quote:
we obtained a 2.1 Å X-ray 
crystal structure of the μOR bound to the morphinan agonist BU72 and stabilized by a G protein-
mimetic camelid-antibody fragment

Crystals of the μOR bound to BU72 and Nb39 were obtained in a monoolein lipidic 
mesophase28 and a complete data set to 2.1 Å was obtained by merging diffraction data from 
four crystals (Extended Data Table 1). Nb39 binds to the intracellular surface of μOR

experiment.system: μOR-BU72-Nb39 complex in monoolein lipidic cubic phase
experiment.perturbation: agonist BU72 and Nb39 stabilization; crystallization
experiment.measurement: X-ray diffraction, structure determination by molecular replacement and refinement

text: In the crystal lattice the active μOR shows a parallel dimeric packing interaction involving TM1, TM2, ECL1 and helix 8 burying 460 Å2, similar to the 615 Å2 interface in the inactive structure; the more extensive TM5/TM6 interface (1460 Å2) seen in the inactive structure would not be compatible with the active-state conformational changes.

quotes.quote:
We 
observe a limited parallel dimeric packing interaction between μOR molecules involving the 
extracellular end of transmembrane helix 1 (TM1), TM2, the first extracellular loop (ECL1), 
and helix 8 with a buried surface area of 460 Å2 (Fig. 1e). A similar interface between TM1, 
TM2, and helix 8 was also observed in the inactive structure of μOR with a slightly larger 
buried surface area of 615 Å2 (Fig. 1e). The inactive structure also identified a more 
extensive parallel dimer interaction involving TM5 and TM6 with a buried surface area 
1460 Å2 (Fig. 1f). This interaction involving TM5 and TM6 would not be compatible with 
the conformational changes we observe in the active state

experiment.system: μOR-BU72-Nb39 crystal lattice compared with inactive μOR structure
experiment.perturbation: observational (structure comparison)
experiment.measurement: buried surface area of crystallographic dimer interfaces

relatively small (Fig. 2a) with the exception of the proximal N-terminus

text: The μOR amino-terminus forms a lid over the ligand-binding pocket with residue H54 positioned 2.6 Å from the secondary amine of BU72, but H54A does not alter BU72 affinity (wild-type Ki = 21 pM vs H54A Ki = 30 pM) or Gi activation EC50 (79±17 pM wild-type vs 67±20 pM H54A), which the authors state makes the specific interaction unlikely to be physiologically relevant.

quotes.quote:
We also observe an unexpected interaction between BU72 and the amino-terminus of the 
μOR, which forms a lid over the ligand-binding pocket (Fig. 3d and Extended Data Fig. 5). 
In particular, the amino-terminal residue H54 is positioned 2.6 Å from secondary amine of 
BU72.

the specific 
interaction observed here is unlikely to be physiologically relevant as H54 is not highly 
conserved and the H54A mutation does not alter the affinity of BU72 in μOR with the full 
length amino-terminus (μOR wild-type Ki = 21 pM and μOR H54A Ki = 30 pM in HEK293 
membranes).

we 
observe no significant difference in the EC50 of Gi activation by BU72 between the wild-
type receptor and the H54A mutant (EC50 for wild-type of 79±17 pM and H54A mutant of 
67±20 pM).

text: Two features of the modelled BU72 remain unexplained: strong positive Fo-Fc density between the H54 side chain and the BU72 amine whose source could not be identified, and near-planar geometry at the sp3 carbon bearing the pendant phenyl; a minor amount of a candidate alternative compound was seen by mass spectrometry of the BU72 preparation but not in the crystallography complex, and the authors modelled a higher-energy conformation of BU72.

density (Fo-Fc signal) between the H54 side chain and the BU72 amine (Extended Data Fig.

alternative ligand structure and the presence an anomalous signal for a coordinated metal 
were unsuccessful

Another unexpected finding is the near-planar 
geometry of the sp3 hybridized carbon of BU72 to which the pendant phenyl group is 
attached
We observed a minor fraction of such a

compound by mass spectrometry in our preparation of BU72. However, this compound was 
not observed in mass spectrometry of the μOR-ligand-Nb39 complex used for 
crystallography. Ultimately, we modeled a higher-energy conformation of BU72 within the 
observed electron density
