text: The high-resolution active μOR maps reveal an extensive water-mediated polar network connecting the orthosteric pocket to the G protein-coupling interface, with more ordered waters than other reported active-state GPCR structures; comparison with the 1.8 Å inactive δOR (versus the 2.8 Å inactive μOR) highlights many hydrogen bonds that must be broken and reformed to reach the active conformation.

quotes.quote:
comparison of inactive and active 
structures of μOR reveals an extensive network of polar interactions between the orthosteric 
binding pocket and the G protein-coupling interface that must rearrange upon activation 
(Fig. 5a). The high-resolution electron density maps of the active μOR allow us to detect 
more ordered water molecules within this polar network than have been observed in other 
active-state GPCR structures reported to date.

The inactive structure of δOR at a resolution of 1.8 Å identifies more water 
molecules within this polar network than the 2.8 Å inactive structure of μOR

These hydrogen bonds represent many low energy 
molecular switches that have to be broken and reformed in a concerted manner to achieve 
the active conformation.

experiment.system: active μOR structure compared with high-resolution inactive δOR and inactive μOR structures
experiment.perturbation: observational structural comparison
experiment.measurement: ordered water molecules and hydrogen bonds in electron density maps

text: Many polar-network residues are conserved, and the waters resolved in the active β2AR occupy the same positions as in μOR while the conserved side chains lining the polar core of β2AR and M2R are nearly identical to those of μOR, suggesting a similar hydrogen-bonding network across Family A GPCRs.

quotes.quote:
Many of the residues in the polar network are conserved (Extended Data Fig. 8a, b, e and f), 
suggesting that the polar network may also be conserved and play a similar role in activation 
of other Family A GPCRs. While there are fewer water molecules observed in the active 
state structure of the β2AR, the ones that are resolved are in the same positions as those 
observed in the μOR.

the positions of the conserved 
side chains lining the polar core of the β2AR and M2R are nearly identical to those of the 
μOR (Extended Data Fig. 8f), suggesting that they are stabilized by a similar hydrogen 
bonding network.

experiment.system: active-state structures of μOR, β2AR and M2R

text: No sodium ion is observed in the active μOR structure and the residues forming the sodium site (including S3.39 and N3.35) rearrange to preclude sodium binding, consistent with the ordered sodium coordinated by D2.50, N3.35, S3.39 and, via water, W6.48 in the inactive δOR and with allosteric inhibition of agonist binding/G protein activation by sodium.

quotes.quote:
In the high-resolution inactive state structure of the δOR, there is an ordered sodium ion that 
is adjacent to the conserved core triad and is coordinated by the side chains of D2.50, N3.35 
and S3.39, as well as by W6.48 through a water molecule (Fig. 5b,c).

Consistent with 
allosteric stabilization of the inactive state by sodium, we do not observe a sodium ion in the active 
state structure of the μOR, and the residues that formed the sodium-binding site rearrange to 
preclude sodium binding in the active state (Fig. 5c).

experiment.system: active μOR structure compared with inactive δOR structure
experiment.perturbation: observational structural comparison
experiment.measurement: presence/absence of ordered sodium ion and coordinating side-chain conformations

text: Comparison of inactive rhodopsin and δOR shows the δOR has a more extensive polar network on the cytoplasmic side of the ligand-binding pocket, particularly hydrogen bonds maintaining TM6 in the inactive conformation, which the authors relate to the weaker allosteric coupling in μOR and β2AR — where DEER and NMR showed only 20% of β2AR has TM6 in an active-like conformation at saturating isoproterenol.

quotes.quote:
Using both double 
electron-electron resonance (DEER) spectroscopy and NMR spectroscopy we observed that 
in the presence of a saturating concentration of the catecholamine agonist isoproterenol only 
20% of β2AR has TM6 in an active-like conformation24.

Comparison of the inactive 
state structures of rhodopsin and the δOR reveals that the δOR has a more extensive polar 
network on the cytoplasmic side of the ligand binding pocket (Extended Data Fig. 9).

the polar network in the 
μOR and β2AR help to maintain unliganded receptors in an inactive state, but the need to 
disrupt this network makes activation of these receptors energetically less efficient.

sequence alignment of experimentally validated OTUs, indicated
an OTU domain with a complete catalytic triad in the uncharac-

prises 352 amino acids (aa), and the OTU domain spans the

against diubiquitin (diUb) of all eight linkage types revealed that

mained Met1 linkage speciﬁc at a 1 mM concentration

hibited’’
conformation
(occupancy
70%),
Asp336
pulls

bations (Figures S2E and S2F), but His339 was now in the active

bition of the catalytic triad in the absence of substrate (Figure 3D)

quotes.quote:
an insertion domain (denoted
Hel2i, residues 470–608), which is a bundle of ﬁve long, antipar-
allel a helices (a22–a26)

The most striking feature of RIG-I helicase is an elbow-like helical
structure that emerges from Hel2 and that will be referred to as
the bridging domain (also named the pincer domain

bend at conserved residue Trp772 leading
into a second helix (a32, 774–793), which would connect to the
CTD

The
proximal end of a31 has counterparts in other helicases (e.g.,
Hef, Figure 1D, and DPB5; see below), but the elbow structure
bridging to the Hel1 domain is speciﬁc to RIG-I.

In all ligand-free structures,
the helicase is in an open conformation with Hel2 and Hel2i form-
ing a single rigid-body unit (Hel2i-Hel2 module).

The two hinge regions lie between residues
456 and 460 in the linker between Hel1 and b8 of Hel2 and
744–748 preceding the bridging helix a31. This highlights the
intrinsic ﬂexibility of the open form of the helicase

text: Co-operative dsRNA and ATP binding produces a dramatic conformational change in which all three helicase subdomains (Hel1, Hel2i, Hel2) move relative to each other, bringing the two RecA domains into intimate contact and creating the mature dsRNA- and ATP-binding sites, with previously disordered loops becoming ordered and participating in RNA or ATP binding.

quotes.quote:
Co-operative dsRNA and ATP bind-
ing results in a dramatic conformational
change of the RIG-I helicase with all three
subdomains (Hel1, Hel2i, and Hel2) mov-
ing relative to each other (Figure 1F;
Movie S2). This brings the two RecA domains into intimate
contact, creating the mature dsRNA- and ATP-binding sites

Almost all the previously disordered loops from
both RecA domains are now well deﬁned and take part in RNA
or ATP binding

text: In the ternary complex, ADP-AlF3-Mg++ is directly bound by residues from motif Q (Lys245, Gln250, Arg247), motif I (Walker A, 270-GxGKT), motif Ia (308-QQ), motif II (Walker B, 375-DE), motif Va (Gly704, Asp706) and motif VI (Gln727, Arg731, Arg733), and conserved bridging-helix residues Met762 and E759 stabilize ATP-binding elements motif III and motif VI.

quotes.quote:
Direct ADP-AlF3-Mg++ binding involves residues from
motif Q (Lys245 and Gln250 deﬁne the adenine speciﬁcity,
Arg247 stacks on the adenine base), motif I (Walker A, 270–
GxGKT), motif Ia (308–QQ), motif II (Walker B, 375–DE), motif
Va (Gly704, Asp706-ribose), and motif VI (Gln727, Arg731,
Arg733) (Figure 2E).

Sequencing individual clones revealed S32L, R68G, D72N, T87R 
and Q182R mutations in the C2 domain of Jag1JV1 (Fig. 1B, Fig. S1). Enhanced binding of 
Notch1 to Jag1JV1 relative to that of wild-type (WT) Jag1 was confirmed in a flow cytometry-
based assay

Only two of the five mutations, S32L and 
T87R, strongly affected the affinity of Jag1JV1

text: By SPR, Jag1JV1(N-3) bound Notch1(8-12) with a KD of 0.81µM and Notch1(11-12) with a KD of 5.4µM (a 6.4-fold difference), whereas DLL4(N-3) bound Notch1(8-12) and Notch1(11-12) with KD values of 9.7µM and 12.8µM, indicating EGF8-10 contributes to Jag1JV1 binding but has a minimal role in Notch1-DLL4 engagement.

quotes.quote:
We determined that Jag1JV1(N-3) bound to Notch1 EGF domains 8 to 12 [Notch1(8-12)] 
with a KD of 0.81µM and to Notch1 EGF domains 11 and 12 [Notch1(11-12)] with a KD of 
5.4µM (Fig. 1C), a 6.4-fold difference in affinity, indicating that EGF8-10 contributes to Jag1JV1-
Notch1 binding energetics (Fig. 1C). On the other hand, Notch1(8-12) and Notch1(11-12) bound 
to DLL4(N-3) with KD values of 9.7µM and 12.8µM, respectively, indicating that EGF8-10 had 
a minimal role in Notch1-DLL4 engagement

experiment.system: Purified recombinant rat Notch1(8-12) or Notch1(11-12) immobilized on a streptavidin SPR chip with soluble His-tagged Jag1JV1(N-3) or DLL4(N-3)
experiment.perturbation: Varying ligand concentration; comparison of Notch1 fragments with and without EGF8-10
experiment.measurement: Surface plasmon resonance steady-state binding fitted to a 1:1 model to obtain Kd

text: In the structure, the Notch1 Thr466 O-fucose in the C2–EGF12 interface hydrogen bonds to the Tyr82 backbone carbonyl of Jag1 C2 and makes VDW contacts with Glu81, Tyr82 and Gln84, while the Notch1 EGF8 Thr311 O-fucose contacts Jag1 EGF3 by hydrogen bonding to Jag1 Asn298; the Jag1 EGF8-interface residue Val324 corresponds to the 'jigsaw' mutation that selectively ablates Notch1-Jag1 interactions.

quotes.quote:
The interface between the Jag1 C2 domain and Notch1 EGF12 contained a functionally 
important Notch1 Thr466 O-fucose modification (Fig. 2A)(23), which formed a hydrogen bond 
(H-bond) with the backbone carbonyl of Tyr82 of the Jag1 C2 domain, and formed Van der 
Waals (VDW) interactions with the side chains of Glu81 and Tyr82, and with main chain atoms of 
Tyr82 and Gln84

An O-linked fucose modification on Thr311 of Notch1 EGF8 contacted EGF3 of Jag1 by 
forming an H-bond with the side chain of Jag1 Asn298

a conserved Val324 residue that, when mutated to a methionine (termed 
the “jigsaw” mutation), selectively ablates Notch1-Jag1 interactions

experiment.perturbation: observational

text: Reporter cells expressing Notch1 with O-fucose sites mutated (T311V, T466V, or both) showed that cells lacking both EGF8 and EGF12 fucose moieties had a pronounced decrease in Jag1 binding but a decrease in activation similar to that of cells lacking only the EGF8 fucose (P<0.0001), indicating the EGF8 O-fucose is of greater functional importance than the EGF12 modification for Jag1.

Cells lacking both EGF 8 and EGF12 fucose moieties 
exhibited a pronounced decrease in Jag1 binding but a similar decrease in activation to that seen 
in cells lacking only the EGF8 fucose (P<0.0001) (Fig. 2B). Thus, the O-fucose of Notch1 EGF8 
appears to be of greater functional importance than the EGF12 modification in the context of 
Jag1, and both O-glycans appear to be required for optimal receptor engagement.

text: In tension gauge tether assays with tethers of 4 pN, 12 pN and 54 pN tension tolerance, WT Jag1 activated Notch through the 12 pN and 54 pN TGTs but not the 4 pN TGT, whereas Jag1JV1 and DLL4 activated Notch even with the 4 pN TGT.

quotes.quote:
Cells were exposed to ligands tethered to a surface through rupturable tethers 
(3, 5) with estimated tension tolerances of 4 pN, 12 pN and 54 pN (Fig. 3). WT Jag1 activated 
Notch when it was linked to the surface through the 12 pN and 54 pN TGTs but not through the 
4 pN TGT. Thus, Notch activation through WT Jag1, like that through DLL1(5), appears to 
require tension larger than 4 pN but smaller than 12 pN.

In contrast, Jag1JV1 
activated Notch even with the 4 pN TGT (Fig. 3).

TGT experiments with DLL4 indicated that Notch 
was activated even with the 4 pN TGT, in contrast to Jag1, which required tension above 4pN

experiment.system: Transgenic CHO-K1 Notch reporter cells (Gal4-NICD/UAS H2B-YFP) on ProG-TGT surfaces displaying Fc-tagged Jag1(N-3), Jag1JV1(N-3) or DLL4(N-3)
experiment.perturbation: Ligand tethering via DNA tethers calibrated to rupture at 4, 12 or 54 pN
experiment.measurement: H2B-YFP fluorescence intensity per cell by microscopy after 48 h

text: BFP force-clamp spectroscopy of single Notch1(8-12)-ligand bonds showed that at tensions below 9 pN the bound-state lifetime was longer for Jag1JV1 than for Jag1, becoming comparable at forces of 9 pN or greater because lifetimes increased with tension for Jag1 (a catch bond) but decreased for Jag1JV1 (a slip bond); DLL4 had a bond lifetime versus tension profile similar to Jag1, which the authors interpret as the higher affinity of DLL4 resulting from a higher kon.

quotes.quote:
At “low” tension values below 9 pN (the tension range 
relevant to Notch activation according to the TGT analysis), the lifetime of the bound state was 
longer for JagJV1 than for Jag1, suggesting that much of the higher affinity of JagJV1 at zero force 
may reflect a lower koff (Fig. 4A). The bond lifetime became comparable between Jag1 and 
Jag1JV1 at forces of 9 pN or greater, probably because of tension-induced changes in lifetimes, 
which increased for Jag1 (a ‘catch bond’) but decreased for JagJV1 (a ‘slip bond’)

BFP experiments revealed that DLL4 had a similar bond lifetime vs. tension profile to 
that of Jag1, indicating that the higher affinity of DLL4 results from its higher kon (Fig. 4A).

experiment.system: Single-molecule biomembrane force probe with a Notch1(8-12)-coated bead against beads coated with biotinylated Jag1(N-3), Jag1JV1(N-3) or DLL4(N-3)
experiment.perturbation: Clamping at defined tensile forces between 0 pN and 25 pN after 20 pN impingement contact
experiment.measurement: Bond lifetime at each force level, binned and averaged with SEM; adhesion frequency kept ≤20% to favor single bonds

like movements, the most dramatic of which is a 32° pivot about the C2-DSL linker that shifts

repressor form of the transcription factor GLI3

MbCD:cholesterol induced a concentration-dependent, bell-

nell, 2000) pool of cholesterol in the plasma membrane, as shown by increased cell-surface labeling

concentration was held constant at 1.25 mM while the cholesterol concentration was varied. Under

tive— neither its enantiomer (ent-cholesterol) nor an epimer with an inverted configuration only at

the number or the position of double bonds in the tetracyclic sterol nucleus were altered in 7-dehy-
drocholesterol (7-DHC) and lathosterol, two endogenous biosynthetic precursors of cholesterol.
Interestingly, desmosterol, another immediate biosynthetic precursor of cholesterol that contains an
additional double-bond in the iso-octyl chain, retained signaling activity.

text: Ift27 deficiency impairs Hh signaling with atypical ciliary trafficking of Smo and Gli2 and defective Gli3 processing; in Ift27 mutant cells Gli2, SuFu and Kif7 still enter cilia but are no longer concentrated at cilia tips, and unlike Ift172 or Ift88 defects, loss of Ift27 does not impair ciliogenesis.

quotes.quote:
Deﬁciency of another anterograde IFT component, Ift27, impairs Hh pathway signaling
resulting in atypical ciliary trafﬁcking of Smo and Gli2, and defective processing of Gli3 [119,120].
Gli2, SuFu and Kif7 enter the cilia in Ift27 mutant cells, but are no longer concentrated at cilia tips.

unlike
defects in Ift172 or Ift88, loss of Ift27 does not impair ciliogenesis.

experiment.system: Ift27 mutant mouse cells
experiment.perturbation: loss of Ift27
experiment.measurement: ciliary trafficking/tip accumulation of Smo, Gli2, SuFu, Kif7; Gli3 processing; ciliogenesis

text: Defects of tubulin glutamylation or forced dynamic deglutamylation in cilia impair tip accumulation of Gli3; the authors note it remains controversial whether the effect is due to slower anterograde IFT or is IFT-independent.

quotes.quote:
either defects of tubulin glutamylation or forced dynamic deglutamylation
in the cilia impair the tip accumulation of Gli3 [122,123]. Whether the effect is due to slower anterograde
IFT [123] or is IFT-independent [122] remains somewhat controversial.

experiment.system: ciliated cells
experiment.perturbation: disruption of axonemal tubulin glutamylation / induced deglutamylation
experiment.measurement: Gli3 accumulation at cilium tip

text: Sequence analysis identified two NLS sequences in Gli1 conserved in Drosophila Ci and Gli2/3: NLS1 (amino acids 79–84) and NLS2 (amino acids 383–401aa), with NLS2 playing a more dominant role in importin α/β1-mediated nuclear import.

quotes.quote:
Sequence analysis identiﬁed two NLS sequences in Gli1, which are conserved in Drosophila Ci
and in Gli2/3: NLS1 (amino acids 79–84), and NLS2 (amino acids 383–401aa; Figure 1) [133,134].

Both NLS sequences are involved in Gli
protein nuclear import via importin α/β1 [112,133,135,137], with NLS2 playing a more dominant
role

experiment.system: Gli1 protein sequence and cultured cells
experiment.perturbation: sequence analysis and NLS mutation/import assays
experiment.measurement: nuclear import of Gli proteins

text: Importin β1 binding to Gli1 is inhibited by PKA-mediated phosphorylation of a threonine near NLS2; the corresponding threonine in Gli2 (Thr556) was never found to be phosphorylated.

quotes.quote:
First, importin β1
binding to Gli1 is inhibited by the PKA-mediated phosphorylation of a threonine near NLS2 [47].
This threonine is present also in Gli2 (Thr556) but it was never found to be phosphorylated

experiment.system: Gli1/Gli2 in mammalian cells
experiment.perturbation: PKA-mediated phosphorylation near NLS2
experiment.measurement: importin β1 binding; phosphorylation site detection

text: Gli2 protein lacking the N-terminal repressor domain can induce skin tumors even in the absence of primary cilia, suggesting it enters the nucleus without involvement of cilia.

quotes.quote:
It was shown that the Gli2 protein lacking
the N-terminal repressor domain can induce skin tumors even in the absence of primary cilia [142],
suggesting that it must enter the cell nucleus without the involvement of cilia.

experiment.system: mouse skin
experiment.perturbation: expression of N-terminally truncated Gli2 in cilia-deficient background
experiment.measurement: skin tumor formation

text: Early work identified two Gli2 activator domains, A1 and A2, corresponding to amino acids 642–1183 and 1184–1544 in mouse Gli2, with the C-terminal end (amino acids 1451–1544) of A2 critical to counteract the repressive activity of the N-terminal Gli2 domain.

quotes.quote:
Early work
identiﬁed two activator domains, known as A1 and A2, corresponding to amino acids 642–1183 and
1184–1544, respectively, in mouse Gli2 [44]. Speciﬁcally, the C-terminal end (amino acids 1451–1544)
of the A2 domain was shown as critical to counteract the repressive activity of the N-terminal Gli2

experiment.system: mouse Gli2 domain constructs
experiment.perturbation: domain deletion/fusion mapping of Gli2
experiment.measurement: transcriptional activation vs repression activity

text: The Taf9/TafII-31 subunit of TFIID binds Gli1 and Gli2 but not Gli3, and abrogating this binding by a point mutation decreases, but does not completely abrogate, Gli1's potency as a transcriptional activator.

quotes.quote:
The Taf9/TafII-31 subunit of TFIID binds to Gli1 and Gli2, but not Gli3. Abrogation of this binding by
a point mutation decreases the potency of Gli1 as a transcriptional activator

mutation of the critical amino acids that mediate the interaction of Gli1 with Taf9 does not completely
abrogate its ability to induce target genes but rather weakens it

experiment.system: Gli–TFIID interaction in cultured cells
experiment.perturbation: point mutation abrogating Gli1–Taf9 binding
experiment.measurement: target gene transcriptional activation by Gli1

text: Gli3 interacts with mediator subunits Med1, Med12, Med14, Med23 and CDK8 via a domain corresponding to amino acids 1090–1583 of mouse Gli3 (1045–1544 for mouse Gli2), with different Mediator subcomplexes either inducing or repressing Gli activity and the Med12 subcomplex playing an inhibitory role.

quotes.quote:
Gli3 interacts with several subunits
of the mediator complex, including Med1, Med12, Med14, Med23, and CDK8 via a domain that
corresponds to the C-terminal part of A1 and the whole A2 domain (corresponding to amino acids
1090–1583 of mouse Gli3, or 1045–1544 for mouse Gli2) [146]. It appears that different subcomplexes
of the Mediator either induce or repress the transcriptional activity of Gli proteins, with the Med12
subcomplex playing an inhibitory role

experiment.system: mouse Gli3/Gli2 and Mediator complex
experiment.perturbation: domain mapping of Gli3–Mediator interaction
experiment.measurement: subunit binding and Gli transcriptional activity

text: Parafibromin/Hprt2, a Paf1 complex component, binds the N-terminal conserved region of Gli proteins corresponding to amino acids 279–348 in mouse and human Gli3 and is involved in Gli1/2-mediated transcriptional activation.

quotes.quote:
Paraﬁbromin/Hprt2, a component of the Paf1 complex, binds the N-terminal conserved region
of Gli proteins corresponding to amino acids 279–348 in mouse and human Gli3 and is involved
in Gli1/2-mediated transcriptional activation

experiment.system: Gli proteins and Paf1 complex in cells
experiment.perturbation: mapping of Parafibromin/Hprt2 binding region
experiment.measurement: binding and Gli1/2-mediated transcriptional activation

text: CBP binds domain A1 (amino acids 827–1132) and domain A2 (amino acids 1090–1596) of Gli3 and enhances transcriptional activation by Gli3 but not Gli1.

quotes.quote:
CBP binds both
domain A1 [149] (amino acids 827–1132) and domain A2 [146] (amino acids 1090–1596) of Gli3, and
was shown to enhance transcriptional activation by Gli3, but not Gli1.

experiment.system: Gli3 and Gli1 with CBP coactivator in cells
experiment.perturbation: CBP binding to Gli3 A1/A2 domains
experiment.measurement: transcriptional activation by Gli3 and Gli1

text: In a screen of mammalian histone acetyltransferases, Ep300 but not Cbp was required for receptor-mediated induction of Gli-protein-mediated transcription, and Pcaf physically interacts with Gli1 with its depletion reducing Hh target gene expression and target promoter acetylation.

quotes.quote:
In a more recent screen of mammalian histone acetyltransferases, Ep300, but not Cbp, was found
to be required for receptor-mediated induction of Gli-protein-mediated transcription [90]

Pcaf physically interacts with Gli1, and its
depletion reduces the expression of Hh target genes and the acetylation of target gene promoters

experiment.system: mammalian cells, histone acetyltransferase screen
experiment.perturbation: depletion of individual HATs (Ep300, Cbp, Pcaf)
experiment.measurement: Hh/Gli target gene expression and promoter histone acetylation

text: Upon activation, Gli2 and Gli1 bind the histone demethylase Jmjd3, which reduces H3K27me3 levels at Gli target gene promoters and increases target gene expression.

quotes.quote:
Upon activation, Gli2 and Gli1 bind to the histone demethylase Jmjd3,
which reduces H3K27me3 levels at Gli target gene promoters and increases the expression of target
genes

experiment.system: Hh-activated mammalian cells
experiment.perturbation: pathway activation and Gli–Jmjd3 interaction
experiment.measurement: H3K27me3 at target promoters and target gene expression

text: The Swi/Snf ATPase Brg1/Smarca4 binds repressor and activator domains of Gli1/2/3 and cooperates with Gli3R in repressing and with Gli1/2A in activating Hh target genes, with these functions appearing independent of its ATPase activity; the coactivator function appears dominant in cerebellar development and medulloblastoma.

quotes.quote:
The ATPase Brg1/Smarca4, which is the catalytic
component of Swi/Snf, has a dual function—it binds to the repressor and activator domains of

Gli1/2/3 and cooperates with Gli3R in repressing Hh target genes, as well as with Gli1/2A in
activating them [155]. Brg1’s functions both as a repressor and activator appear to be independent
of its ATPase activity

The coactivator function of Brg1 appears to be dominant over the corepressor function, at least in
cerebellar development and medulloblastoma

experiment.system: neural development / cerebellum and medulloblastoma models
experiment.perturbation: Brg1/Smarca4 manipulation, ATPase-dead variants
experiment.measurement: Hh target gene activation/repression and developmental/tumor phenotypes

text: Deletion of the Swi/Snf component Srg3/Smarcc1 both derepresses genes typically inhibited by Gli3R and prevents full activation of GliA-regulated genes during limb development.

quotes.quote:
Deletion of Srg3 both derepresses
target genes typically inhibited by Gli3R and prevents full activation of GliA-regulated genes, which is
in line with the bifunctional role of the Swi/Snf complex.

experiment.system: mouse limb development
experiment.perturbation: Srg3/Smarcc1 deletion
experiment.measurement: expression of Gli3R-repressed and GliA-activated target genes

text: SAP18 interacts with the N-terminal domain of Gli proteins via SuFu, and Gli1, SuFu, SAP18 and Sin3 can form a complex on DNA; Ski binds the N-terminal domain of Gli3 and Gli2 but not Gli1, and antagonizing Ski via RNAi or anti-Ski antibodies impairs Gli3R-dependent transcriptional repression.

quotes.quote:
SAP18, a component of the Sin3
HDAC complex, was shown to interact with the N-terminal domain of Gli proteins via SuFu. Gli1,
SuFu, SAP18 and Sin3 are capable of forming a complex on DNA [165].

Ski
binds to the N-terminal domain of Gli3 and Gli2, but not Gli1. Antagonizing Ski function via RNAi or
anti-Ski antibodies impairs Gli3R-dependent transcriptional repression

experiment.system: Gli corepressor complexes in cultured cells
experiment.perturbation: Ski RNAi or anti-Ski antibody; complex reconstitution on DNA
experiment.measurement: complex formation and Gli3R-dependent transcriptional repression

text: p66β and HDAC1 of the NuRD complex are recruited to Gli2 and Gli3 via SuFu to inhibit target gene transcription, but p66β binds full-length and not truncated repressor forms of Gli2 and Gli3.

quotes.quote:
p66β, a component of the NuRD complex,
as well as HDAC1, are recruited to Gli2 and Gli3 via SuFu to inhibit transcription of target genes.
Interestingly, p66β binds full-length, but not truncated repressor forms of Gli2 and Gli3

experiment.system: Gli2/Gli3–SuFu–NuRD complexes in cells
experiment.perturbation: binding assays with full-length vs truncated Gli forms
experiment.measurement: p66β/HDAC1 recruitment and target gene transcription

text: Snf5 acts exclusively as a Gli co-repressor: Snf5, Baf57/Smarce1 and Baf170/Smarcc2 bind Gli1, loss of Snf5 activates the Hh pathway, and Snf5 expression in Gli1-dependent malignant rhabdoid tumors suppresses Gli1 activity and tumor growth.

quotes.quote:
Snf5, as well as
Baf57/Smarce1 and Baf170/Smarcc2 were identiﬁed as binding partners of Gli1. Loss of Snf5 leads to
the activation of the Hh pathway, whereas its expression in the Gli1-dependent malignant rhabdoid
tumors suppresses Gli1 activity and tumor growth

experiment.system: malignant rhabdoid tumor cells
experiment.perturbation: Snf5 loss or re-expression
experiment.measurement: Hh pathway activation, Gli1 activity, tumor growth

text: Gli2 null mice die before birth with defects in tissues including the central nervous system, skeleton and lungs, whereas Gli3 null mice die perinatally with severe craniofacial defects, central nervous system malformations and polydactyly; unlike Gli2, Gli3 is haploinsufficient with viable heterozygotes showing developmental malformations.

quotes.quote:
Gli2 null mice die before birth with defects
in various tissues including the central nervous system, skeleton, and lungs [237–241].

Gli3 null
mice die perinatally and are characterized by severe craniofacial defects, central nervous system
malformations, and polydactyly [244]. Unlike Gli2, Gli3 is haploinsufﬁcient: Gli3 heterozygotes
are viable, but have various developmental malformations

experiment.system: mouse embryos and pups
experiment.perturbation: Gli2 or Gli3 germline knockout (homozygous and heterozygous)
experiment.measurement: survival and developmental phenotypes

text: When Gli1 is expressed from the Gli2 locus it can substitute for Gli2 in most developmental processes, suggesting Gli2 is a bona fide activator throughout development.

quotes.quote:
when Gli1 is expressed from the Gli2 locus, it can substitute for the latter in most developmental
processes, suggesting that Gli2 is a bona ﬁde activator throughout development

experiment.system: knock-in mice expressing Gli1 from the Gli2 locus
experiment.perturbation: Gli1 knock-in replacing Gli2
experiment.measurement: developmental phenotypes/rescue

text: Mice expressing constitutive Gli3R instead of full-length Gli3 from both alleles are viable at birth but die before weaning due to developmental defects of the skeleton, digestive tract, upper respiratory tract, kidneys and adrenal glands.

quotes.quote:
Mice expressing constitutive Gli3R instead of full-length Gli3
from both alleles are viable at birth, but die before weaning, due to various developmental defects at
the level of the skeleton, digestive tract, upper respiratory tract, kidneys, and adrenal glands [247].

experiment.system: mice homozygous for constitutive Gli3R allele
experiment.perturbation: replacement of full-length Gli3 with constitutive Gli3R
experiment.measurement: survival and organ developmental defects

text: Gli2A is crucial for development of ventral cell types (floor plate, V3 interneurons) in the caudal spinal cord while Gli3A is sufficient to induce ventral cell fates in head and thorax, and embryos deficient in Gli3 and either Shh or Smo indicate Gli3 is required and sufficient for repression of V0–V2 interneuron markers in the absence of upstream signal.

quotes.quote:
Gli2A is crucial for the development of ventral cell types (ﬂoor plate, V3 interneurons) in the caudal
(trunk and tail) region of the spinal cord, while Gli3A is sufﬁcient to induce ventral cell fates in the
head and thorax [238,241].

experiments performed on embryos deﬁcient
in Gli3 and either Shh or Smo indicate that Gli3 is required and sufﬁcient for the repression of V0–V2
interneuron markers in the absence of upstream signal

experiment.system: mouse embryo neural tube
experiment.perturbation: Gli2/Gli3 mutants; compound Gli3;Shh or Gli3;Smo deficiency
experiment.measurement: ventral cell fate and interneuron marker expression

text: Gli2 mutant mice display defects in bone development in the craniofacial skeleton, vertebrae, long bones of the limb (stylopod and zeugopod) and sternum, and Gli2 is required for induction of cartilage vascularization.

quotes.quote:
Gli2 mutant mice
display various defects in bone development in the craniofacial skeleton, vertebrae, long bones of the
limb (stylopod and zeugopod), and sternum [240]. Mechanistically, Gli2 is required for the induction
of cartilage vascularization

experiment.system: Gli2 mutant mice
experiment.perturbation: Gli2 loss-of-function mutation
experiment.measurement: skeletal development and cartilage vascularization

text: Induction of Gli2A and inhibition of Gli3R formation by inhibiting PKA activity induces ectopic ossification in the joints, and analyses of Gli1 KO fetuses showed early osteoblast development requires Gli1 as well as Gli2 and Gli3, although adult Gli1 mutant mice appear to have normal bones.

quotes.quote:
induction of Gli2A and
inhibition of Gli3R formation by inhibiting PKA activity induces ectopic ossiﬁcation in the joints [266].
Although adult Gli1 mutant mice appear to have normal bones, analyses of Gli1 KO fetuses showed
that the early development of osteoblasts requires Gli1 as well as Gli2 and Gli3 [267].

experiment.system: mouse joints and Gli1 knockout fetuses
experiment.perturbation: PKA inhibition; Gli1 knockout
experiment.measurement: ectopic ossification and osteoblast development

text: Loss of Gli3 induces abnormal calvaria development characterized by premature ossification of the interfrontal suture (craniosynostosis) caused by abnormal osteoprogenitor proliferation and differentiation.

quotes.quote:
Loss of Gli3 induces abnormal development of the calvaria characterized by
premature ossiﬁcation of the interfrontal suture (craniosynostosis) caused by abnormal osteoprogenitor
proliferation and differentiation

experiment.system: mouse skull/calvaria
experiment.perturbation: Gli3 loss of function
experiment.measurement: interfrontal suture ossification, osteoprogenitor proliferation and differentiation

text: Gli3R controls overall growth levels of the mid-hindbrain region and suppresses expression of the anteroposterior organizer Fgf8, and Gli3R can rescue most phenotypes caused by overactive Gli signaling due to targeted loss of SuFu in the mid-hindbrain.

quotes.quote:
Gli3R controls the overall levels of growth of
the mid-hindbrain region and suppresses the expression of the anteroposterior organizer Fgf8 [270].
Moreover, Gli3R can rescue most of the phenotypes caused by overactive Gli signaling due to targeted
loss of SuFu in the mid-hindbrain.

experiment.system: mouse mid-hindbrain
experiment.perturbation: targeted SuFu loss with/without Gli3R expression
experiment.measurement: growth, Fgf8 expression, cerebellar/hindbrain phenotypes

text: Gli2, and to a lesser degree Gli1, are involved in pituitary gland formation, and deletion of both genes results in complete loss of the pituitary gland.

quotes.quote:
Gli2, and to a lesser degree Gli1, are involved in pituitary
gland formation, and deletion of both genes results in complete loss of the pituitary gland [237].

experiment.system: mouse pituitary development
experiment.perturbation: deletion of Gli1 and Gli2
experiment.measurement: pituitary gland formation

text: Homozygous truncating GLI1 mutations were found to cause developmental defects in humans with symptoms such as postaxial polydactyly, mental retardation and shortened lower limbs overlapping Ellis-van Creveld syndrome, phenotypes that are absent in mouse Gli1 knockouts.

quotes.quote:
Homozygous truncating GLI1 mutations were recently found
to cause developmental defects whose symptoms, such as postaxial polydactyly, mental retardation,
and shortened lower limbs, overlap with those of Ellis-van Creveld syndrome [298]. These phenotypes
are absent in mouse Gli1 knockouts [237].

experiment.system: human patients with GLI1 mutations and mouse Gli1 knockouts
experiment.perturbation: homozygous truncating GLI1 mutation
experiment.measurement: developmental/clinical phenotypes

text: Interference with Shh signaling impairs generation of new neurons in the olfactory bulb of adult mice, mostly by promoting constitutive Gli3R formation.

quotes.quote:
interference with Shh signaling results in the impaired generation of new neurons in the olfactory
bulb of adult mice mostly by promoting constitutive Gli3R formation

experiment.system: adult mouse postnatal neural progenitors/olfactory bulb
experiment.perturbation: interference with Shh signaling
experiment.measurement: generation of new neurons and Gli3R formation

text: Non-synonymous heterozygous GLI2 mutations underlie a significant fraction of congenital hypopituitarism and also cause holoprosencephaly-like malformations including abnormal craniofacial development, growth retardation, and microcephaly.

quotes.quote:
Non-synonymous heterozygous GLI2 mutations
underlie a signiﬁcant fraction of congenital hypopituitarism and also cause holoprosencephaly-
like malformations, including abnormal craniofacial development, growth retardation, and
microcephaly [293–295].

experiment.system: human patients
experiment.perturbation: observational (heterozygous non-synonymous GLI2 mutations)
experiment.measurement: congenital hypopituitarism and craniofacial/growth phenotypes

text: The Nod2 sequence contains two potential in-frame translation initiation sites separated by 81 nucleotides, and both are used in transfected HEK293T cells, with the most N-terminal initiation codon being more efficient.

quotes.quote:
Because the Nod2
sequence contained two potential in-frame translation initia-
tion sites separated by 81 nucleotides (Fig. 3C), we determined
their usage by transfection of a Nod2 construct containing both
translation initiation sites into HEK293T cells.

The analysis revealed that both translation initiation sites in
the Nod2 open reading frame were used, although the most
N-terminal translation initiation codon was more efficient as
assessed by immunoblotting of cell extracts with an antibody
that recognizes a C-terminal HA tag (Fig. 3D).

experiment.system: HEK293T cells
experiment.perturbation: transfection of a C-terminally truncated HA-tagged Nod2 construct (lacking residues 302–1040) containing both initiation sites, or constructs expressing each site separately in a Kozak motif
experiment.measurement: anti-HA immunoblotting of cell extracts

text: Expression of as little as 3 ng of wild type Nod2 induced 18-fold activation of NF-kB in HEK293T cells.

quotes.quote:
Expres-
sion of as little as 3 ng of wt Nod2 induced 18-fold activation of
NF-kB (Fig. 4C).

experiment.system: HEK293T cells, triplicate cultures
experiment.perturbation: transfection of wt Nod2 expression plasmid (as little as 3 ng)
experiment.measurement: pBVIx-Luc luciferase NF-kB reporter activity normalized to pEF-BOS-b-gal

text: Domain mapping showed a Nod2 mutant lacking the LRRs had enhanced NF-kB activation while LRRs or NBD alone were inactive; deletion of the CARDs singly or together abolished activity, and both CARDs alone (but not each singly) were sufficient for NF-kB activation.

quotes.quote:
Expression of a Nod2 mutant form lacking the
LRRs resulted in enhanced NF-kB activation, whereas mu-
tants expressing the LRRs or the NBD alone were inactive (Fig.
4C).

Deletion of the CARDs of Nod2, either singly or in combination,
resulted in total loss of NF-kB activity (Fig. 4C). However,
expression of both CARDs alone, but not each CARD sepa-
rately, was sufficient for NF-kB activation (Fig. 4C).

experiment.system: HEK293T cells, triplicate cultures
experiment.perturbation: transfection of a panel of deletion mutants of Nod2 (LRRs, NBD, CARD1, CARD2, CARDs)
experiment.measurement: NF-kB luciferase reporter activity and anti-HA immunoblotting of mutant expression

text: Replacement of the conserved P-loop lysine with arginine in Nod2 (K305R) diminished NF-kB activity, which was rescued at least in part by deletion of the LRRs.

quotes.quote:
Similarly, replacement of the corresponding
lysine for arginine in Nod2 resulted in diminished NF-kB ac-
tivity that was rescued at least in part by deletion of the LRRs
(Fig. 4C).

experiment.system: HEK293T cells, triplicate cultures
experiment.perturbation: transfection of Nod2 P-loop site-directed mutants K305R and 1–744K305R (LRR deletion)
experiment.measurement: NF-kB luciferase reporter activity

text: Overexpression of Nod2 did not induce apoptosis by itself but enhanced apoptosis induced by caspase-9 expression (reported as unpublished results).

quotes.quote:
We found that overexpression of Nod2 did not induce apoptosis
by itself but enhanced apoptosis induced by caspase-9 expres-
sion.2

experiment.system: transfected cells (unpublished data cited by the authors)
experiment.perturbation: overexpression of Nod2 alone or with caspase-9
experiment.measurement: apoptosis induction

text: NF-kB activation induced by Nod2 and by TNFa was greatly inhibited by dominant negative IKKa, IKKb, IKKg, and IkBa; in the experiment shown Nod2 induced 58 ± 8-fold and TNFa (10 ng/ml) induced 14 ± 1-fold NF-kB activation.

quotes.quote:
The NF-kB
activity induced by Nod2 as well as that induced by TNFa
stimulation were greatly inhibited by mutant IKKa, IKKb,
IKKg, and IkBa (Fig. 5A).

In the experiment shown, Nod2 and TNFa induced 58 6 8-fold
and 14 6 1-fold activation of NF-kB, respectively.

transfected with 30 ng of Nod2 plasmid (open bars) or stimulated with
10 ng/ml of TNFa for 4 h (closed bars) and 70 ng of I-kBa S32A/S36A,
IKKa K44A, IKKb K44A, RICK (406–540), or RIP (558–671) expres-
sion plasmid

experiment.system: HEK293T cells, triplicate cultures
experiment.perturbation: transfection of 30 ng Nod2 plasmid or stimulation with 10 ng/ml TNFa, plus 70 ng dominant negative IkBa S32A/S36A, IKKa K44A, IKKb K44A, or IKKg (134–419)
experiment.measurement: pBVIx-Luc NF-kB luciferase reporter activity normalized to b-gal

text: NF-kB activation induced by Nod2 was inhibited by a truncated RICK containing its CARD (residues 406–540) but not by a RIP death effector domain mutant; conversely the RICK mutant did not block TNFa-induced NF-kB, which was inhibited by the RIP mutant.

quotes.quote:
We found that NF-kB activa-
tion induced by Nod2 was inhibited by mutant RICK but not by
a mutant form of RIP that expresses its death effector domain
(Fig. 5A). The inhibition by the CARD of RICK was specific in
that it did not interfere with ability of TNFa to induce NF-kB,
an activity that was inhibited by the RIP mutant (Fig. 5A).

experiment.system: HEK293T cells, triplicate cultures
experiment.perturbation: cotransfection of Nod2 (or TNFa stimulation) with RICK (406–540) or RIP (558–671) dominant negative plasmids
experiment.measurement: NF-kB luciferase reporter activity

text: Nod2, like Nod1 and TNFa, induced NF-kB activity in parental Rat1 fibroblasts but not in IKKg-deficient 5R cells, whereas IKKb expression activated NF-kB in both lines, indicating Nod2 acts through IKKg/IKKa/IKKb.

quotes.quote:
We found that Nod2, as well as Nod1 and TNFa, induced
NF-kB activity in parental Rat1 cells but not in IKKg-deficient
5R cells (Fig. 5B). As a control, expression of IKKb, which
functions downstream of IKKg, induced NF-kB activation in
both Rat1 and 5R cell lines (Fig. 5B). These results indicate
that Nod2 acts through IKKg/IKKa/IKKb to activate NF-kB.

experiment.system: parental Rat1 fibroblasts and IKKg-defective 5R derivative cell line
experiment.perturbation: transfection of Nod2, Nod1, or IKKb plasmids, or TNFa stimulation
experiment.measurement: pBVIx-Luc NF-kB luciferase reporter activity in triplicate cultures

text: RICK coimmunoprecipitated with Nod2 in HEK293T cells; association required both CARDs of Nod2 and only the CARD of RICK (residues 374–540), not RICK lacking the CARD (residues 1–374), bound Nod2, defining a homophilic CARD-CARD interaction.

quotes.quote:
Immunoblotting with anti-
FLAG antibody revealed that RICK associated with Nod2 (Fig.
6A). The association was mediated by both CARDs of Nod2,
because only Nod2 proteins containing both CARDs were ca-
pable of interacting with RICK (Fig. 6, A and B).

The analysis showed that only the CARD of RICK coim-
munoprecipitated with Nod2 (Fig. 6C). Thus, Nod2 and RICK
associate via a homophilic CARD-CARD interaction.

experiment.system: HEK293T cells
experiment.perturbation: cotransfection of HA-tagged wt or mutant Nod2 with FLAG-tagged wt RICK, RICK (1–374), or RICK (374–540)
experiment.measurement: coimmunoprecipitation with anti-HA or anti-FLAG antibody followed by immunoblotting

text: Nod2 association was specific: Nod2 did not associate with several CARD-containing proteins (Apaf-1, caspase-1, caspase-4, c-IAP-1, c-IAP2, procaspase-9, Bcl-10, RAIDD, Ced-4) nor with NF-kB-activating molecules TRAF-1, TRAF-2, TRAF-5, TRAF-6, RIP, NIK, TRADD, IKKa, IKKb, or IKKg (unpublished results).

quotes.quote:
The associa-
tion of Nod2 with RICK was specific in that Nod2 did not
associate with several CARD-containing proteins including
Apaf-1, caspase-1, caspase-4, c-IAP-1, c-IAP2, procaspase-9,
Bcl-10, RAIDD, and Ced-4 nor with several molecules that
activate NF-kB including TRAF-1, TRAF-2, TRAF-5, TRAF-6,
RIP, NIK, TRADD, IKKa, IKKb, or IKKg.2

experiment.system: HEK293T cells (data cited as unpublished)
experiment.perturbation: cotransfection of Nod2 with a panel of CARD-containing and NF-kB-activating proteins
experiment.measurement: coimmunoprecipitation and immunoblotting

text: Enforced oligomerization with the ligand AP1510 (500 nM) of suboptimal amounts (1 ng) of Nod2-Fpk3 chimeras induced NF-kB activation in a ligand-dependent manner; oligomerization of both CARDs but not each CARD singly induced activation, and it enhanced activity of the K305RDLRR P-loop mutant, while a Nod2-Fpk3 construct lacking the LRRs activated NF-kB with and without AP1510.

quotes.quote:
Under these experimen-
tal
conditions,
expression
of
Nod2-Fpk3
induced
NF-kB
activation in a ligand-dependent manner (Fig. 7B). Consistent
with the results shown in Fig. 4C, enforced oligomerization of
both CARDs but not each CARD singly induced NF-kB activa-
tion. Similarly, NF-kB activation induced by a Nod2 P-loop
mutant lacking the LRRs (K305RDLRR), which have reduced
ability to induce NF-kB activation, was enhanced by enforced
oligomerization (Fig. 7B).

LRRs induced NF-kB activation in the absence and presence of
AP1510 (Fig. 7B).

fected with 1 ng of the indicated plasmids in the presence of pBVIx-luc
and pEF-BOS-b-gal. 8 h post-transfection, cells were treated with 500

text: In HL60 cells differentiated toward monocytic cells with 200 ng/ml phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate for 36 h, transient expression of Nod2 induced NF-kB activation, and enforced oligomerization of wild type Nod2-Fpk3 or CARDs-Fpk3 was sufficient for NF-kB activation.

Similarly to the case of
HEK293T cells, transient expression of Nod2 induced NF-kB
activation in monocytic HL60 cells (Fig. 7C, left panel). Fur-
thermore, enforced oligomerization of wild type Nod2-Fpk3 or

200 ng/ml of phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate for 36 h to induce mono-
cytic differentiation. Differentiated cells were transfected with 500 ng
(left panel) or 50 ng (right panel) of the indicated plasmids

experiment.system: HL60 cells differentiated into monocytic cells
experiment.perturbation: 200 ng/ml phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate for 36 h, then transfection with 500 ng or 50 ng of Nod2 / Fpk3-Nod2 plasmids ± 500 nM AP1510
experiment.measurement: kB-dependent luciferase transcription in triplicate cultures

text: The review states that YAP and TAZ are cytoplasmic in cells experiencing low mechanical signalling, such as rounded cells on soft ECM (typically below 1.5 kPa for epithelial cells) or small adhesive areas (i.e., 300 μm2), and nuclear in cells on rigid substrates (typically at >5/10 kPa) or stretching over an area > 3000 μm2.

quotes.quote:
YAP and TAZ are localized in the cytoplasm in 
cells experiencing low levels of mechanical signalling, such as in rounded cells attached to a 
soft ECM (typically below 1.5 kPa for epithelial cells) or to a small adhesive area (i.e., 300 
μm2); YAP and TAZ are instead nuclear in cells perceiving high mechanical signalling, such 
as cells cultured on rigid substrates (typically at >5/10 kPa) or experiencing deformation and 
cytoskeletal tension (e.g., cells stretching over an area > 3000 μm2)

experiment.system: cultured cells (e.g. epithelial cells) on substrates of defined rigidity and microprinted adhesive areas
experiment.perturbation: varying ECM stiffness and adhesive area/cell shape
experiment.measurement: YAP and TAZ subcellular localization (nuclear vs cytoplasmic)

numbers.quantity: soft ECM stiffness threshold for epithelial cells
spread cell area promoting nuclear YAP/TAZ

text: YAP and TAZ mechanotransduction requires actin cytoskeleton integrity, being abolished by F-actin inhibitors, but is not explained by the G-actin/F-actin ratio, since rounded cells contain more total F-actin than spread cells yet have inhibited YAP and TAZ.

quotes.quote:
YAP and TAZ mechanotransduction requires integrity of the actin cytoskeleton and YAP and 
TAZ activity is experimentally abolished by inhibitors of filamentous actin (F-
actin)

rounded cells contain more total F-actin than spread cells48, and yet, in 
rounded cells YAP and TAZ are inhibited.

experiment.system: cultured cells
experiment.perturbation: pharmacological inhibition of F-actin; comparison of rounded vs spread cell shapes
experiment.measurement: YAP and TAZ activity and total F-actin content

text: F-actin capping and severing proteins CAPZ, ADF and CFL potently inhibit YAP and TAZ activity, and mutant mice lacking cofilin/ADF in skin and liver show cytoskeletal remodelling, F-actin accumulation and massive organ overgrowth within few days, phenocopying YAP and TAZ activation.

quotes.quote:
the potent inhibitory 
effects of F-actin capping proteins, such as CAPZ (capping actin protein of muscle Z-line), 
ADF (actin depolymerizing factor) and CFL (Cofilin), on YAP and TAZ activity

mutant mice lacking cofilin/ADF in skin and liver, where extensive 
cytoskeletal remodeling and F-actin accumulation is accompanied by induction of massive 
organ overgrowth occurring in just few days (phenocopying the effects of YAP and TAZ 
activation)

experiment.system: cultured cells and mutant mice lacking cofilin/ADF in skin and liver
experiment.perturbation: genetic loss of cofilin/ADF; expression of F-actin capping proteins
experiment.measurement: YAP and TAZ activity, F-actin accumulation, organ size

text: In the early mouse embryo, inhibition of contractile pulling forces with Blebbistatin or ROCK inhibitors abolishes nuclear YAP localization in outer cells and their trophoblast commitment.

quotes.quote:
Inhibition of such pulling forces 
by exposing mouse embryos to Blebbistatin (an inhibitor of myosin II and microfilament 
contractility), or ROCK inhibitors, abolishes nuclear localization of YAP in outer cells and 
their trophoblast commitment

experiment.system: early mouse embryos/blastocysts
experiment.perturbation: exposure to Blebbistatin or ROCK inhibitors
experiment.measurement: YAP nuclear localization in outer cells and trophoblast fate commitment

text: Human embryonic stem cells have nuclear YAP and TAZ on stiff substrates but relocalize them to the cytoplasm and differentiate when forced to adopt a rounded shape by low mechanical signals.

quotes.quote:
YAP and TAZ are nuclear 
localized in hESCs cultured under standard conditions on stiff substrates, but relocalize to 
the cytoplasm when cells are forced to adopt a rounded shape by low mechanical signals. 
Coherently with YAP and TAZ inhibition, hESCs differentiate in these mechanically 
inhibited conditions

experiment.system: human embryonic stem cells (hESCs)
experiment.perturbation: culture on stiff substrates vs conditions forcing rounded cell shape (low mechanical signals)
experiment.measurement: YAP and TAZ localization and differentiation status

text: YAP and TAZ couple substrate compliance to hMSC differentiation: their depletion impairs osteogenic differentiation on stiff substrates and skews cells to adipogenesis, while a hyperactive YAP form redirects hMSCs to osteogenic fate on soft substrates; Yap+/-;Taz+/- MSCs show impaired osteogenesis under permissive conditions.

quotes.quote:
YAP and 
TAZ transcriptional activity couples substrate compliance to hMSC differentiation, as YAP and 
TAZ depletion impairs osteogenic differentiation on stiff substrates, skewing MSCs towards 
adipogenic differentiation; conversely, overexpression of an hyperactive form of YAP is 
sufficient to redirect hMSCs towards an osteogenic fate on soft substrates

Yap+/-;Taz+/- 
MSCs display impaired osteogenesis despite being cultured under permissive conditions

experiment.system: human mesenchymal stem cells and Yap+/-;Taz+/- MSCs
experiment.perturbation: YAP/TAZ depletion or hyperactive YAP overexpression on stiff vs soft substrates; heterozygous Yap/Taz deletion
experiment.measurement: osteogenic vs adipogenic differentiation

text: In 3D collagen gels, MT1-MMP (Mmp14) remodels collagen to promote cytoskeletal tension and cell spreading needed for YAP and TAZ activation; Mmp14-/- skeletal stem cells show impaired osteogenic and enhanced adipogenic differentiation in vitro and in vivo, genetically dependent on YAP and TAZ dosage.

quotes.quote:
Mmp14-/- SSCs display impaired osteogenic differentiation and enhanced 
adipogenic differentiation, both in vitro and in vivo in a manner that is genetically dependent 
on YAP and TAZ dosage

experiment.system: skeletal stem cells (SSCs) embedded in 3D collagen gels, in vitro and in vivo
experiment.perturbation: Mmp14 knockout combined with altered YAP and TAZ dosage
experiment.measurement: osteogenic vs adipogenic differentiation

text: N-cadherin engagement reduces the contractile state and nuclear YAP and TAZ localization in MSCs, altering their interpretation of ECM rigidity.

quotes.quote:
the engagement of N-cadherin (involved in 
cell–cell interactions) reduced the contractile state and thereby nuclear YAP and TAZ 
localization in MSCs, resulting in altered interpretation of ECM rigidity

experiment.system: mesenchymal stem cells in vitro
experiment.perturbation: engagement of N-cadherin-based cell–cell adhesion on substrates of varying rigidity
experiment.measurement: cell contractility and nuclear YAP/TAZ localization

text: Culturing MSCs on microfluidic chips mimicking interstitial shear stress increases YAP and TAZ activity in a Rho–ROCK dependent manner and enhances osteogenic and fibrochondrogenic differentiation, whereas culture under microgravity blunts TAZ nuclear accumulation and reduces osteogenesis.

quotes.quote:
Culturing MSCs on microfluidic chips that mimic interstitial shear 
stress increases YAP and TAZ activity in a Rho–ROCK dependent manner, to enhance 
osteogenic and fibrochondrogenic differentiation

culturing MSCs under microgravity indeed 
resulted in blunted TAZ nuclear accumulation and reduced osteogenesis

experiment.system: mesenchymal stem cells
experiment.perturbation: interstitial-level shear stress on microfluidic chips; simulated microgravity
experiment.measurement: YAP/TAZ activity and nuclear accumulation, osteogenic and fibrochondrogenic differentiation

text: In mouse incisor tooth progenitors, high nuclear YAP and TAZ activity drives pool expansion and requires ECM signalling transduced by integrin α3 and FAK, in a LATS-independent manner.

quotes.quote:
YAP 
and TAZ activation in this context requires signalling from the surrounding ECM transduced 
by integrin α3 and FAK, and is LATS-independent

experiment.system: mouse incisor epithelial progenitor cells
experiment.perturbation: genetic perturbation of integrin α3/FAK and LATS signalling
experiment.measurement: YAP and TAZ activity and progenitor pool expansion

text: In muscle, mechanical overload sustains YAP activity in mouse models and can induce hypertrophy and protect from denervation atrophy; in vitro high YAP promotes muscle stem cell proliferation while YAP inactivation by soft substrates fosters myogenic differentiation, and in chick embryos contraction of post-mitotic fibres yields nuclear YAP activating NOTCH in adjacent progenitors.

quotes.quote:
In mouse models, mechanical 
overload sustains YAP activity. This overload in turn can induce hypertrophy and is required 
to protect from atrophy caused by denervation. In skeletal muscle cells cultured in vitro, 
high YAP activity promotes proliferation of muscle stem cells, whereas YAP inactivation by 
soft substrates fosters myogenic differentiation

in the chick embryo contraction of post-mitotic muscle fibres led to 
nuclear YAP, in turn leading to activation of NOTCH signalling in adjacent muscle 
progenitor cells, which prevented their differentiation

experiment.system: mouse skeletal muscle in vivo, cultured skeletal muscle cells, chick embryo muscle
experiment.perturbation: mechanical overload, denervation, soft substrate culture, muscle contraction/paralysis
experiment.measurement: YAP activity/localization, muscle stem cell proliferation and differentiation, NOTCH activation, muscle size

text: Contact inhibition of proliferation is explained by mechanical inhibition of YAP and TAZ (largely LATS-independent) and is overcome by ECM stiffening, loss of actin capping and severing proteins, or cell stretching.

quotes.quote:
CIP can be molecularly explained by inhibition of YAP and 
TAZ91, simply because crowding confines cells to small areas, putting them into a low 
contractility and YAP and TAZ repressive cytoskeletal states24

CIP is overcome either by ECM stiffening92, 
loss of actin capping and severing proteins, or cell stretching24,44

experiment.system: dense epithelial cell monolayers in culture
experiment.perturbation: cell crowding; ECM stiffening, depletion of actin capping/severing proteins, mechanical stretching
experiment.measurement: YAP and TAZ activity and cell proliferation (contact inhibition)

text: After pneumonectomy, stretching and CDC42-dependent actin polymerization in AT2 cells promotes YAP nuclear localization required for AT2 expansion and AT1 replenishment; genetic deletion of CDC42 or YAP impairs regeneration.

quotes.quote:
Pneumonectomy induces stretching and 
actin polymerization in AT2 cells through a mechanism that depends on the Rho-GTPase 
CDC42. In turn, cell stretching promotes YAP nuclear localization and transcriptional 
activities (Figure 2), which are required for the expansion of AT2 cells and replenishment of 
AT1 cells. Accordingly, genetic deletion of CDC42 or YAP impairs regeneration after 
pneumonectomy

experiment.system: mouse lung after pneumonectomy (surgical removal of part of lung tissue)
experiment.perturbation: pneumonectomy; genetic deletion of CDC42 or YAP
experiment.measurement: YAP nuclear localization, AT2 expansion and AT1 replenishment, lung regeneration

text: YAP and TAZ are activated in basal keratinocytes near skin wounds and are required for proper wound closure; loss of integrin-β1 causes impaired wound closure similar to YAP and TAZ knockout, and mechanical activation of YAP/TAZ preserves epidermal stemness by suppressing Notch.

quotes.quote: YAP and TAZ are activated in basal keratinocytes close to the wound
and are required for proper wound closure94.

loss of integrin-β1 results in impaired wound closure similarly to 
YAP and TAZ knockout

this is required for preserving epidermal stemness 
(Figure 3), which occurs through the suppression of the Notch pathway

experiment.system: mouse skin/epidermis wound healing and cultured basal keratinocytes
experiment.perturbation: wounding; YAP and TAZ knockout; integrin-β1 loss; varying cell spreading and ECM rigidity
experiment.measurement: YAP/TAZ activation, wound closure, epidermal stemness and Notch pathway activity

text: Transgenic expression of ROCK2 in mouse skin induces epidermal hyperplasia, attenuated by inhibition of FAK, LIMK or myosin ATPase.

quotes.quote:
unscheduled activation of 
actomyosin-mediated cellular tension in the skin of transgenic mice by expressing ROCK2 
induces epidermal hyperplasia in a manner that is attenuated by inhibition of FAK, LIM 
domain Kinase 1 (LIMK) or myosin ATPase

experiment.system: transgenic mouse skin
experiment.perturbation: ROCK2 expression, with FAK/LIMK/myosin ATPase inhibition
experiment.measurement: epidermal hyperplasia

text: YAP and TAZ localize to the nucleus of murine cardiac cells at the infarction border zone and are instrumental for cardiomyocyte proliferation at specific rigidities; YAP activation increases cardiomyocyte proliferation, reduces scar size and improves cardiac regeneration in a myocardial infarction model.

quotes.quote:
YAP and TAZ are expressed and localized in the nucleus of murine 
cardiac cells at the infarction border zone98. YAP and TAZ have key functions in adult 
cardiac progenitor mechano-sensing responses, being instrumental for cardiomyocyte 
proliferation at specific rigidities98. YAP activation indeed increases cardiomyocyte 
proliferation, reduces scar size, and improves cardiac regeneration in a myocardial infarction 
model

experiment.system: murine myocardial infarction model and cardiac progenitor cells on substrates of defined rigidity
experiment.perturbation: myocardial infarction; forced YAP activation
experiment.measurement: YAP/TAZ nuclear localization, cardiomyocyte proliferation, scar size, cardiac regeneration

text: YAP and TAZ knockdown impairs proliferation of endothelial cells spread on big microprinted islands, while YAP overexpression inhibits apoptosis and rescues proliferation of endothelial cells seeded on small islands.

quotes.quote:
YAP and TAZ knockdown impairs proliferation of endothelial cells allowed to stretch over 
big microprinted islands, whereas YAP overexpression inhibits apoptosis and rescues 
proliferation of endothelial cells seeded on small islands

experiment.system: endothelial cells on large vs small microprinted adhesive islands
experiment.perturbation: YAP and TAZ knockdown or YAP overexpression
experiment.measurement: cell proliferation and apoptosis

text: YAP and TAZ are inhibited in endothelial cells cultured under static fluid flow but nuclear under disturbed (oscillatory) flow, where they foster endothelial proliferation and expression of monocyte adhesive factors; YAP is genetically required for the atherogenic response of endothelial cells in vivo.

quotes.quote:
YAP and TAZ are inhibited in endothelial cells 
cultured under static fluid flow (which is atheroprotective), whereas they localize to the 
nucleus when cultured under disturbed (oscillatory) flow conditions (which mimic 
atherogenic mechanical stress)40,41 (Figure 1). In these in vitro conditions, nuclear YAP 
and TAZ foster endothelial cell proliferation and expression of adhesive factors for 
monocytes
YAP is also genetically required for this atherogenic response of endothelial cells in vivo41

experiment.system: cultured endothelial cells and in vivo animal models of atherogenesis
experiment.perturbation: static vs disturbed (oscillatory) flow; genetic YAP deletion
experiment.measurement: YAP/TAZ localization, endothelial proliferation, monocyte adhesion factor expression, atherogenic response

text: Yap1-null zebrafish larvae showed vessel regression with vessel stenosis and retraction between 4.5 and 6.5 days post fertilization.

quotes.quote:
Recent work on Yap1-null zebrafish embryos showed vessel regression in mutant larvae, 
with vessel stenosis and retraction between 4.5 and 6.5 days post fertilization.

experiment.system: zebrafish embryos/larvae
experiment.perturbation: Yap1 null mutation
experiment.measurement: vessel regression, stenosis and retraction over developmental time

numbers.quantity: time window of vessel stenosis and retraction

text: Yap knockout in smooth muscle cells in mice results in embryonic lethality possibly due to abnormal aortic development, and YAP/TAZ-driven VSMC proliferation and migration can be blunted by inhibition of Rho, ROCK or F-actin remodelling, resulting in VSMC apoptosis.

quotes.quote:
Yap 
knockout in smooth muscle cells in mice results in embryonic lethality possibly due to 
abnormal aortic development101.

These responses can be blunted by inhibition of Rho, ROCK or F-actin remodelling, which 
interfere with YAP and TAZ activation and result in VSMC apoptosis

experiment.system: mouse vascular smooth muscle cells in vivo and in vitro (vessel restenosis context)
experiment.perturbation: smooth-muscle-specific Yap knockout; Rho/ROCK/F-actin remodelling inhibitors
experiment.measurement: embryonic viability and aortic development; VSMC proliferation, migration and apoptosis

text: In pulmonary hypertension, stiff ECM activates YAP and TAZ in vivo and in vitro to trigger proliferation of adventitial fibroblasts, endothelial cells and VSMCs and increase ECM deposition; LOX inhibitors reduced ECM stiffening, blunted nuclear YAP and TAZ and ameliorated end-stage disease in murine models.

quotes.quote:
a stiff ECM activates YAP and TAZ in vivo and in vitro, 
triggering proliferation of adventitial fibroblasts, endothelial cells and VSMCs; in turn, YAP

reduction of ECM 
stiffening with LOX inhibitors blunted nuclear YAP and TAZ and ameliorated the end-stage 
manifestations of pulmonary hypertension in murine models106

experiment.system: murine models of pulmonary hypertension and cultured vascular cells
experiment.perturbation: ECM stiffening; treatment with lysyl oxidase (LOX) inhibitors
experiment.measurement: YAP/TAZ nuclear localization, cell proliferation, ECM deposition, disease manifestations

text: In liver fibrosis, YAP is activated in hepatic stellate cells upon liver damage in vivo and ECM stiffening ex-vivo, increasing collagen deposition and smooth muscle actin expression; myofibroblasts in fibrotic livers of hepatitis C patients showed strong YAP nuclear staining and stellate cell activation was reversed by pharmacologic YAP inhibition.

quotes.quote:
In liver fibrosis, YAP is activated in hepatic stellate cells in response to liver damage in vivo 
and to ECM stiffening ex-vivo108,109.

in the fibrotic 
areas of livers from patients suffering from hepatitis C, myofibroblasts displayed strong YAP 
nuclear staining and hepatic stellate cell activation could be reversed by pharmacologic 
inhibition of YAP108.

experiment.system: mouse hepatic stellate cells in vivo/ex vivo and human hepatitis C fibrotic liver tissue
experiment.perturbation: liver damage, ECM stiffening, pharmacologic YAP inhibition
experiment.measurement: YAP nuclear localization/levels, collagen deposition, smooth muscle actin expression, stellate cell activation

text: YAP and TAZ are induced in lungs of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis patients and sustain a pro-fibrotic programme in human lung fibroblasts, and Taz-heterozygous mice were resistant to bleomycin-induced lung fibrosis.

quotes.quote:
YAP and TAZ are also induced in the lungs of patients suffering from idiopathic pulmonary 
fibrosis, and YAP and TAZ sustain a pro-fibrotic transcriptional programme in human lung 
fibroblasts both in vitro and in vivo110,111

Taz-
heterozygous mice were resistant to bleomycin-induced lung fibrosis112.

experiment.system: human lung fibroblasts, IPF patient lungs, and Taz-heterozygous mice
experiment.perturbation: bleomycin-induced fibrosis; Taz heterozygosity
experiment.measurement: YAP/TAZ induction, pro-fibrotic gene programme (collagen/fibronectin deposition, cytokine secretion), fibrosis severity

text: In a mouse model of corneal squamous cell metaplasia, corneal wounding induces chronic inflammation and excessive ECM deposition with ensuing YAP and TAZ nuclear localization, driving epithelial stem and progenitor cells to transdifferentiate into keratinizing epidermal-like cells.

quotes.quote:
In a mouse 
model of corneal squamous cell metaplasia, corneal wounding induces chronic inflammation 
and excessive deposition of ECM by the corneal stroma and ensuing YAP and TAZ nuclear 
localization. In this mechanically aberrant environment, epithelial stem and progenitor cells 
are then driven to transdifferentiate into keratinizing, epidermal-like cells, resulting in 
metaplasia and ocular surface blindness116

experiment.system: mouse cornea
experiment.perturbation: corneal wounding inducing chronic inflammation and ECM deposition
experiment.measurement: YAP and TAZ nuclear localization and epithelial cell fate (metaplasia)

text: In LMNA-mutant congenital muscular dystrophy cells, YAP remains nuclear in soft hydrogel cultures where control myoblasts show cytoplasmic YAP, yet YAP activity is blunted in mutant cells challenged by cycles of stretch and relaxation.

quotes.quote:
YAP is cytoplasmic in healthy control myoblasts when these are 
cultured on a soft ECM, but remains nuclear in soft hydrogel cultures of LMNA mutant 
cells. Paradoxically, YAP activity is blunted in these mutant cells when they are challenged 
by cycles of stretch and relaxation117.

experiment.system: myoblasts from patients carrying LMNA mutations and healthy controls
experiment.perturbation: culture on soft hydrogels; cycles of stretch and relaxation
experiment.measurement: YAP subcellular localization and activity

text: The review notes that despite widespread YAP and TAZ activation in tumours, activating mutations in YAP or TAZ have not been reported in human cancers and Hippo pathway mutations are rare and not yet detected in carcinomas.

quotes.quote:
in spite of their widespread activation in 
tumours, activating mutations in YAP or TAZ have not been reported in human cancers; 
moreover, Hippo pathway mutations are rare in human tumors and not yet detected in 
carcinomas.

experiment.system: human tumours
experiment.perturbation: observational (survey of reported cancer genome mutations)
experiment.measurement: presence of activating YAP/TAZ or Hippo pathway mutations

text: Drugs targeting geranylgeranyl synthesis (statins, bisphosphonates, geranylgeranyl transferase-1 inhibitors) inhibit YAP and TAZ in several cancer cell types, and statins and bisphosphonates reduce growth of tumour xenografts, with effects appearing stronger in vitro than in vivo.

quotes.quote:
drugs that target 
geranylgeranyl synthesis, thereby blocking Rho GTPase recruitment to the membrane, such 
as statins, bisphosphonates and geranylgeranyl transferase-1 inhibitors, display YAP and 
TAZ inhibiting abilities in several cancer cell types32. Statins and bisphosphonates also 
reduce the growth of tumour xenografts32,35,125, although their effects appeared stronger 
in vitro than in vivo.

experiment.system: cancer cell lines and tumour xenografts
experiment.perturbation: treatment with statins, bisphosphonates or geranylgeranyl transferase-1 inhibitors
experiment.measurement: YAP and TAZ activity and tumour xenograft growth

text: In several tumours, cancer-associated fibroblast properties of increasing ECM stiffness and promoting invasion and angiogenesis rely on YAP activation downstream of ECM stiffening, and increased YAP activity in CAFs promotes contractility and ECM restructuring, forming a self-sustaining positive feedback loop.

quotes.quote:
These properties rely on 
activation of YAP in CAFs, and occur downstream of ECM stiffening36. In turn, increased 
YAP activity in CAFs promotes contractility and restructuring of the ECM, locking 
fibroblast in a vicious mechanically-activated positive feedback loop that self-sustains YAP 
and TAZ activation in both CAFs and tumour cells

experiment.system: cancer-associated fibroblasts and tumour niches
experiment.perturbation: ECM stiffening and YAP manipulation in CAFs
experiment.measurement: ECM stiffness/remodelling, CAF contractility, tumour invasion and angiogenesis

text: Force transfer from cytoplasm to nucleus through the LINC complex is essential for activation of the YAP and TAZ pathway, and the nuclear lamina has been shown to be mechanosensitive and to affect YAP and TAZ activity.

quotes.quote:
force transfer from the cytoplasm to the nucleus through the linker 
of nucleoskeleton and cytoskeleton (LINC) protein complex is essential for activation of the 
YAP and TAZ pathway128. Moreover, the nuclear lamina has been recently shown to be 
mechanosensitive and indeed affecting YAP and TAZ activity129.

experiment.system: cultured cells (including mesenchymal stem cells)
experiment.perturbation: disruption of LINC complex-mediated cytoskeletal-to-nuclear strain transfer; alteration of nuclear lamina
experiment.measurement: YAP and TAZ pathway activation

text: Growth and shaping of the fly wing primordium is YAP dependent and controlled by global patterns of mechanical stress originating from its stretched tissue border.

quotes.quote:
growth and shaping of the fly wing primordium is YAP dependent and controlled by 
global patterns of mechanical stress that originate from its stretched tissue border131.

experiment.system: Drosophila wing imaginal disc (wing primordium)
experiment.perturbation: observational/genetic analysis of mechanical stress patterns and YAP (Yorkie) dependence
experiment.measurement: tissue growth and shape

text: YAP appearance predates multicellularity, being first detected in the genome of the closest unicellular relatives of the animals.

quotes.quote:
YAP 
appearance predates multicellularity, being first detected in the genome of the closest 
unicellular relatives of the animals133.

experiment.system: genomes of unicellular relatives of animals
experiment.perturbation: observational (comparative genomics)
experiment.measurement: presence of YAP/Hippo pathway genes

text: Intestinal organoids embedded in fully defined synthetic hydrogels show growth inhibited in soft substrates but dramatically fostered by more rigid matrices, a condition accompanied by and requiring nuclear accumulation of YAP and TAZ; increasing cell crowding as the organoid expands progressively limits YAP and TAZ activity and promotes differentiation.

quotes.quote:
when intestinal organoids are embedded 
in fully defined synthetic hydrogels, their growth is inhibited in soft substrates, but 
dramatically fostered by more rigid matrices, a condition accompanied by, and requiring, 
nuclear accumulation of YAP and TAZ45

As cells accumulate and the 
organoid expands, increased cell crowding progressively limits YAP and TAZ activity 
(Figure 1), promoting differentiation.

experiment.system: intestinal organoids from adult crypts in defined synthetic hydrogels
experiment.perturbation: varying hydrogel stiffness (soft vs rigid); organoid expansion/cell crowding
experiment.measurement: organoid growth, YAP and TAZ nuclear accumulation, differentiation

text: In human airway organoids YAP and TAZ are nuclear in basal (progenitor) cells and absent in differentiated cells, and mechano-activation of YAP and TAZ by raising F-actin cytoskeletal tension is essential for branching morphogenesis in vitro.

quotes.quote:
in human airway organoids YAP and TAZ are nuclear in basal 
(progenitor) cells and absent in differentiated cells. Similarly to intestinal organoids, 
mechano-activation of YAP and TAZ by raising tension in F-actin cytoskeleton is 
essential for branching morphogenesis of these lung organoids in vitro136.

experiment.system: human airway (lung) organoids in vitro
experiment.perturbation: raising F-actin cytoskeletal tension
experiment.measurement: YAP and TAZ localization by cell type and branching morphogenesis

text: Sucrose gradient centrifugation of a 105,000 x g cytosolic fraction from uteri of rats injected with [3H]estradiol showed the estradiol radioactivity sedimenting in a nearly symmetrical peak at 9.5S, and this cytosolic binding was stereospecific and eliminated by proteases.

quotes.quote:
Toft and Gorski (17) prepared a 105,000 3 g cy-
tosolic fraction from uteri of rats injected with [3H]estradiol
and centrifuged the cytosol components through a gradient
of 5–20% sucrose. The estradiol radioactivity sedimented in
a nearly symmetrical peak at 9.5S

the cytosolic estradiol binding recovered at ;9S
was stereospecific and eliminated by proteases (17)

experiment.system: rat uterine cytosol after in vivo [3H]estradiol injection
experiment.perturbation: sucrose density gradient centrifugation (5–20%), protease treatment
experiment.measurement: sedimentation coefficient of bound radioactivity

text: Adding [3H]estradiol directly to cytosol from untreated rat uteri yielded a 9S complex appearing identical to that obtained after in vivo hormone administration, which the authors describe as the first direct demonstration of hormone binding to a receptor protein in a cell-free system.

quotes.quote:
Toft et al. (18) demonstrated that addition of
[3H]estradiol directly to cytosol prepared from uteri of un-
treated rats yielded a 9S complex that appeared identical to
the complex obtained after in vivo hormone administration.
This publication represents the first direct demonstration of
hormone or drug binding to a receptor protein in a cell-free
system.

experiment.system: cytosol from uteri of untreated rats
experiment.perturbation: direct addition of [3H]estradiol in vitro
experiment.measurement: sedimentation of the steroid-bound complex

numbers.quantity: sedimentation coefficient of complex formed in vitro

text: Treatment of cytosol with 0.3 m KCl followed by sucrose gradient centrifugation in KCl converted the cytosolic ER from a 9S to a 4S form, a dissociation occurring whether or not the receptor was estrogen-bound.

quotes.quote:
it was found that treatment of cytosol with 0.3 m KCl
(followed by subsequent centrifugation on a sucrose gradient
containing KCl) “transformed” the cytosolic ER from a 9S to
a 4S form (27–29)

a dissociation that occurred regard-
less of whether the receptor was free or bound with estrogen
(28)

experiment.system: uterine cytosolic estrogen receptor
experiment.perturbation: 0.3 m KCl treatment
experiment.measurement: sucrose gradient sedimentation coefficient

text: Salt-extracted nuclear ER sedimented at 5S in sucrose gradients containing 0.4 m KCl, and the nuclear 5S ER was generated in a temperature-dependent manner at the expense of the cytosolic 9S ER; nuclei incubated directly with [3H]estradiol did not yield a steroid-receptor complex unless exposed to cytosol containing the 9S complex.

quotes.quote:
solubilize the
ER from uterine nuclei by repeated extraction with 0.3 m KCl
and show that the salt-extracted nuclear receptor sedimented
at 5S in sucrose gradients containing 0.4 m KCl

the nuclear 5S ER was generated in a temperature-
dependent manner at the expense of the cytosolic 9S ER
complex. Incubation of the uterine cell nuclear fraction with
[3H]estradiol did not yield a steroid-receptor complex, and it
was only when nuclei were exposed to cytosol containing the
[3H]estradiol-bound 9S complex that subsequent extraction
with salt yielded the 5S receptor.

text: Glucocorticoid receptors were reported to be present as 9S complexes that dissociate to 4S in rat hepatoma cell (HTC) cytosol in the presence of 0.5 m KCl.

Baxter and Tomkins (64) were the first to report
that GRs were present as 9S complexes that dissociate to 4S
in rat hepatoma cell (HTC) cytosol in the presence of 0.5 m
KCl.

experiment.perturbation: 0.5 m KCl
experiment.measurement: sedimentation coefficient of [3H]glucocorticoid-bound receptor

text: Kinetic and thermodynamic analysis of GR transformation showed it was of apparent first order with a free energy of thermodynamic activation of DG* 5 21.3 kcal, and high positive enthalpy (DH* 5 31.4 kcal) and entropy (DS* 5 34 cal/degree) values similar to those described for protein denaturation.

quotes.quote:
They showed that trans-
formation was of apparent first order and that the free energy
of thermodynamic activation was much higher (DG* 5 21.3
kcal) than expected for an enzymatic process. They noted that
high positive values for enthalpy (DH* 5 31.4 kcal) and entropy
(DS* 5 34 cal/degree) were similar to those described for pro-
tein denaturation

experiment.system: cytosolic glucocorticoid receptor
