text: At 25 C, steroid binding to the receptor required a moderate activation energy (DG* 5 110.6 kcal) and gave a complex of markedly lower free energy (DG 5 -11.3 kcal), whereas receptor transformation required a high activation energy (DG* 5 121.3 kcal) and produced a transformed receptor at a free energy similar to the untransformed one (DG 5 20.24 kcal).

quotes.quote:
they found that binding
of steroid to the receptor requires a moderate thermodynamic
activation energy (DG* 5 110.6 kcal), but the complex corre-
sponds to a markedly lower level of free energy (DG 5 -11.3
kcal). A high energy of activation (DG* 5 121.3 kcal) is required
for receptor transformation, but the transformed receptor is at
a level of free energy similar to that of the untransformed
receptor (DG 5 20.24 kcal).

experiment.measurement: free energies and activation energies

text: In suspensions of rat thymocytes assayed by DEAE chromatography, a rapid shift from untransformed to transformed GR occurred with a half-time of less than 2.5 min, while after injection of [3H]triamcinolone acetonide into rats the analogous shift in hepatic cytosolic GR had a longer half-time of 10–15 min.

quotes.quote:
Using suspensions of rat thymocytes, Munck and
Foley (197) found that a rapid shift from untransformed to
transformed state occurred with a half-time of ,2.5 min.

Markovic and Litwack (198) demonstrated a similar shift in
DEAE elution behavior of GR recovered in hepatic cytosol,
with a longer half-time (10–15 min) for transformation

text: Transfection of hormone-free cells with mutant human GR and ER cDNAs showed that steroid-inducible receptor forms were recovered in molybdate-stabilized cytosols entirely as 9S complexes, whereas constitutively active mutant receptors were recovered only in the 4S form.

quotes.quote:
Analysis of recep-
tors produced after transfection of hormone-free cells with
mutant human GR and ER cDNAs demonstrated that ste-
roid-inducible forms of the receptor were recovered in mo-
lybdate-stabilized cytosols entirely as 9S complexes, whereas
mutant receptors with constitutive activity were recovered
only in the 4S form (200–202).

experiment.system: hormone-free cells transfected with mutant human GR and ER cDNAs
experiment.perturbation: receptor mutations conferring constitutive activity; molybdate stabilization
experiment.measurement: sedimentation form (9S vs 4S) in cytosol

text: In L cell cytosol containing 10 mm molybdate, the half-time for inactivation of glucocorticoid steroid-binding activity at 25 C increased from 30–60 min to more than 1 day, and at 37 C from about 2 min to 2 h.

quotes.quote:
In L cell cytosol, for example, the half-time for inacti-
vation of steroid-binding activity at 25 C went from 30–60
min to more than 1 day, and the half-time at 37 C went from
;2 min to 2 h when 10 mm molybdate was present (83).

experiment.perturbation: addition of 10 mm molybdate, incubation at 25 C or 37 C
experiment.measurement: half-time of loss of glucocorticoid-binding activity

text: Molybdate present in DEAE-cellulose loading and eluting buffers completely prevented GR transformation during a KCl gradient, yielding a well defined high-salt peak and a 33-fold purification of the untransformed receptor, which was later shown to coelute with hsp90.

quotes.quote:
The presence of
molybdate in both the loading buffer and eluting buffer
completely prevented transformation during the running of
the KCl gradient, with the GR eluting from DEAE-cellulose
in a well defined high salt peak that yielded a 33-fold pu-
rification of the untransformed receptor (147). It was later
shown that the molybdate-stabilized, untransformed GR
coelutes with hsp90 (148).

experiment.system: cytosolic glucocorticoid receptor
experiment.perturbation: molybdate in DEAE-cellulose chromatography buffers with KCl gradient elution
experiment.measurement: receptor elution position and fold purification; coelution with hsp90

text: With molybdate present during ammonium sulfate fractionation of cytosol, the GR precipitated in the 45–55% range of saturation, while the bulk of hsp90 precipitated at 50–70% and transformed receptor at 20–30% of saturation.

quotes.quote:
When cytosol is submitted to
ammonium sulfate fractionation in the presence of molyb-
date, the GR is precipitated out in the 45–55% range of sat-
uration, whereas the bulk of the hsp90 is precipitated at
50–70% and transformed receptor at 20–30% of saturation
(147, 148).

experiment.system: cytosol containing glucocorticoid receptor
experiment.perturbation: ammonium sulfate fractionation with molybdate
experiment.measurement: saturation range at which receptor/hsp90 precipitate

numbers.quantity: ammonium sulfate saturation precipitating untransformed GR

text: Stabilization of the GR by molybdate, vanadate, or tungstate was not blocked by preincubation of receptors with enough methyl methanethiosulfonate to derivatize all of the thiols, which the authors state argues strongly against relevance of metal oxyanion-sulfur interactions to receptor stabilization.

quotes.quote:
the observation that stabilization of the GR by molyb-
date, vanadate, or tungstate is not blocked by preincubation
of receptors with enough methyl methanethiosulfonate to
derivatize all of the thiols (223, 287) argues strongly against
a proposal that interactions of the metal oxyanions with
sulfur moieties in the receptor heterocomplex are relevant to
receptor stabilization.

experiment.system: cytosolic glucocorticoid receptor heterocomplex
experiment.perturbation: preincubation with methyl methanethiosulfonate to derivatize thiols, then molybdate/vanadate/tungstate
experiment.measurement: receptor stabilization

text: Affinity chromatography plus DEAE-cellulose chromatography achieved about 7,000-fold purification of the 9S PR from chicken oviduct cytosol, yielding a single denaturing-gel band at Mr about 85,000; a separate deoxycorticosterone-agarose based protocol purified the molybdate-stabilized chicken PR about 6,000-fold, giving 9S receptor with a major Coomassie-stained polypeptide of Mr about 90,000 plus an additional Mr about 104,000 band in component II.

quotes.quote:
Renoir et al. (304) employed affinity
chromatography followed by DEAE-cellulose chromatogra-
phy to achieve ;7,000-fold purification of the 9S PR from
chicken oviduct cytosol. Analysis by denaturing gel electro-
phoresis revealed a single band migrating at Mr ;85,000

purified the molybdate-stabilized chicken PR ;6,000-fold by
ammonium sulfate precipitation, affinity chromatography,
and gel filtration (307)

with both components containing a single
major Coomassie blue-stained polypeptide of Mr ;90,000
and an additional band of Mr ;104,000 being recovered with
component II (307)

experiment.system: chicken oviduct cytosol progesterone receptor
experiment.perturbation: molybdate stabilization plus affinity/DEAE/gel filtration chromatography
experiment.measurement: fold purification, sedimentation, denaturing gel band molecular weights

text: The two forms of highly purified 9S PR were shown to contain a common non-steroid-binding 90-kDa component together with separate approximately 79-kDa and approximately 110-kDa steroid-binding components identified by site-specific cross-linking with steroid affinity ligands.

quotes.quote:
The puzzle was resolved in 1984 when the two
forms of the highly purified 9S PR were shown to contain a
common non-steroid-binding 90-kDa component and sepa-
rate ;79-kDa and ;110-kDa steroid-binding components
that were identified by site-specific cross-linking with steroid
affinity ligands (309, 310).

experiment.system: highly purified molybdate-stabilized 9S chicken progesterone receptor
experiment.perturbation: site-specific cross-linking with steroid affinity ligands
experiment.measurement: identity/size of steroid-labeled vs unlabeled polypeptides on denaturing gels

text: Purification of avian PR from oviduct tissue minces incubated with [32P]orthophosphate showed the 90-kDa polypeptide was highly phosphorylated on serine residues, as was the approximately 110-kDa B isoform of the PR; the authors note this 1982 paper is the first direct demonstration of phosphorylation of any hormone receptor, although hsp90 was mistakenly identified as a form of the PR.

quotes.quote:
Dougherty et al. (311) purified the
avian PR from oviduct tissue minces incubated with
[32P]orthophosphate and showed that the 90-kDa polypep-
tide was highly phosphorylated on serine residues, as was
the ;110-kDa B isoform of the PR.

The 1982
paper by Dougherty et al. (311) stands as the first direct
demonstration of phosphorylation of any hormone receptor
(although in this study, hsp90 was mistakenly identified to
also be a form of the PR).

experiment.system: chicken oviduct tissue minces
experiment.perturbation: metabolic labeling with [32P]orthophosphate followed by PR purification
experiment.measurement: 32P incorporation and phosphoamino acid identity of receptor-associated polypeptides

text: Affinity purification of the molybdate-stabilized GR from mouse L cells labeled with [32P]orthophosphate recovered a major Mr about 90,000 phosphoprotein and a minor Mr about 100,000 phosphoprotein stereospecifically; neither was recovered from glucocorticoid-resistant L cells possessing only 5% of the steroid-binding capacity of sensitive cells. Only the 100-kDa protein was labeled with [3H]dexamethasone mesylate, and the 90-kDa component was immunologically distinct from the murine GR.

quotes.quote:
A major phosphopro-
tein of Mr ;90,000 and a minor phosphoprotein of Mr
;100,000 were both recovered in a stereospecific manner
from the affinity resin, and neither protein was recovered
upon affinity chromatography of cytosol from glucocor-
ticoid-resistant L cells possessing only 5% of the steroid
binding capacity of sensitive cells (318).

it
was subsequently shown that only the 100-kDa phospho-
protein was labeled with the glucocorticoid-binding, site-
specific affinity ligand [3H]dexamethasone mesylate and
that the 90 kDa non-steroid-binding component of the
complex was immunologically distinct from the 100 kDa
murine GR (319).

experiment.system: mouse L cells (glucocorticoid-sensitive and -resistant) labeled with [32P]orthophosphate
experiment.perturbation: steroid affinity chromatography with molybdate stabilization; labeling with [3H]dexamethasone mesylate
experiment.measurement: phosphoprotein bands on denaturing gels, affinity labeling, immunological reactivity

numbers.quantity: steroid-binding capacity of resistant L cells

text: The rat monoclonal antibody BF4, raised against highly purified 9S chicken PR, did not interact with the 4S PR but reacted with 9S PR, ER, AR, and GR in chicken oviduct cytosol, and the common component recognized was shown by immunoblotting to be a 90-kDa protein.

quotes.quote:
The
highly purified 9S chicken PR was then used to prepare the
rat monoclonal antibody BF4 (325), which did not interact
with the 4S PR but did react with 9S PR, ER, AR, and GR
in chicken oviduct cytosol (326, 327). The common com-
ponent of 9S receptors recognized by BF4 was shown by
immunoblotting to be a 90-kDa protein.

experiment.system: chicken oviduct cytosol steroid receptors
experiment.perturbation: immunoreaction with monoclonal antibody BF4 raised against purified 9S chicken PR
experiment.measurement: antibody reactivity with 9S vs 4S receptor forms; immunoblot band size

text: Three papers published in late 1985 established that the receptor-associated 90-kDa protein is hsp90: BF4 reacted with a [35S]methionine-labeled 90-kDa protein of heat-stressed chick embryo fibroblasts, the chicken PR-associated 90-kDa protein comigrated on two-dimensional gels with mammalian hsp90 and gave the same peptide map, antibodies against the pp60v-src-associated hsp90 recognized and shifted the PR-associated protein, and the 90-kDa protein coimmunoadsorbed with mouse GR reacted with an antiserum against purified chicken hsp90.

quotes.quote:
Three papers published in late 1985 established that the
receptor-associated protein was hsp90 (333–335). Catelli et al.
(333) showed that the BF4 antibody against the chicken PR-
associated 90-kDa protein reacted with a [35S]methionine-
labeled 90 kDa protein of heat-stressed chick embryo fibro-
blasts.

the 90-kDa protein in the
9S chicken PR comigrated on two-dimensional gel electro-
phoresis with mammalian hsp90

Sanchez et al. (335) showed that the 90-kDa protein coim-
munoadsorbed with the mouse GR from L cell cytosol re-
acted with a rabbit antiserum prepared by Kelley and
Schlesinger (338) against purified chicken hsp90.

experiment.system: chick embryo fibroblasts, chicken oviduct PR, mouse L cell GR
experiment.perturbation: heat stress; [35S]methionine labeling; immunoadsorption with anti-90-kDa and anti-hsp90 antibodies
experiment.measurement: antibody cross-reactivity, two-dimensional gel comigration, peptide mapping

text: Using a coimmunoadsorption assay, hsp90 was shown to dissociate from the GR when cytosolic receptors were transformed, with dissociation prevented by molybdate, and hsp90 was also shown to dissociate when steroid-bound GRs were transformed in intact cells.

quotes.quote:
using a
coimmunoadsorption assay, it was shown that hsp90 disso-
ciated from the GR when cytosolic receptors were trans-
formed, with dissociation being prevented by molybdate
(335). Importantly, Mendel et al. (186) showed that hsp90
dissociated when steroid-bound GRs were transformed in
intact cells.

experiment.system: L cell cytosolic GR and intact cells
experiment.perturbation: receptor transformation with or without molybdate; steroid treatment of intact cells
experiment.measurement: coimmunoadsorption of hsp90 with receptor

text: hsp90 was demonstrated by direct techniques to be present in untransformed ER, AR, MR, and DR complexes, whereas hsp90 was shown not to be associated with newly translated thyroid hormone or retinoic acid receptors.

quotes.quote:
hsp90
was demonstrated by direct techniques to be present in un-
transformed ER (340), AR (341), MR (91), and DR (342, 343)
complexes. In contrast, it was shown that hsp90 is not as-
sociated with newly translated thyroid hormone (344) or
retinoic acid (345) receptors.

experiment.system: untransformed nuclear receptor complexes (ER, AR, MR, DR) and newly translated thyroid hormone/retinoic acid receptors
experiment.perturbation: observational comparison across receptor types
experiment.measurement: direct detection of hsp90 in receptor complexes

text: hsp90 is the most abundant constitutive hsp in eukaryotic cells, accounting for 1–2% of cytosolic protein, and it purifies under nondenaturing conditions as a 165,000–180,000 dalton dimer that can form oligomers of four or more units under certain conditions.

quotes.quote:
hsp90 Is the most abundant constitutive hsp
in eukaryotic cells, accounting for 1–2% of cytosolic protein.

hsp90 Purifies under
nondenaturing conditions as a 165,000–180,000 dalton dimer
(336), and under certain conditions, it can form oligomers of
four or more units (354).

experiment.system: eukaryotic cell cytosol / purified hsp90
experiment.perturbation: observational; nondenaturing purification
experiment.measurement: abundance as fraction of cytosolic protein; native molecular mass

text: Human hsp90a has 86% amino acid homology with hsp90b; human hsp90b is 78% homologous with the Drosophila 83-kDa hsp and 61% homologous with yeast hsp90, and the Escherichia coli hsp90 homolog is a 63-kDa protein whose predicted sequence is 42% identical to human hsp90.

quotes.quote:
two genes encode hsp90, with the
human hsp90a having 86% amino acid homology with
hsp90b (351). There is extensive homology with lower spe-
cies; the human hsp90b, for example, is 78% homologous
with the Drosophila 83-kDa hsp and 61% homologous with
yeast hsp90 (352). The hsp90 homolog in Escherichia coli is a
63-kDa protein with a predicted amino acid sequence that is
42% identical to human hsp90 (353).

experiment.system: hsp90 gene/protein sequences across human, Drosophila, yeast, E. coli
experiment.perturbation: observational sequence comparison
experiment.measurement: percent amino acid homology/identity

numbers.quantity: E. coli homolog size and identity

text: Coimmunoadsorption with antibodies specific for hsp86 and hsp84 showed that hsp86zhsp84 heterodimers exist as native complexes, while another laboratory detected only aza and bzb homodimers.

quotes.quote:
Using anti-
bodies specific for hsp86 and hsp84, respectively, Perdew et
al.
(355)
have
shown
by
coimmunoadsorption
that
hsp86zhsp84 heterodimers exist as native complexes. Despite
the fact that the Yahara laboratory has detected only aza and
bzb homodimers (356, 357)

experiment.system: mouse cell native hsp90 complexes
experiment.perturbation: immunoadsorption with isoform-specific antibodies
experiment.measurement: coadsorption of the other hsp90 isoform

text: The C-terminal region of hsp90a was shown to be required for both homodimer formation and rescue of a lethal double hsp90 mutant of yeast.

quotes.quote:
Minami et al.
(357) have shown that the C-terminal region of hsp90a is
required for both homodimer formation and rescue of a
lethal double hsp90 mutant of yeast

experiment.system: yeast carrying a lethal double hsp90 mutation; hsp90a constructs
experiment.perturbation: deletion of the hsp90a C-terminal region
experiment.measurement: homodimer formation and rescue of lethality

text: Cross-linking of untransformed receptors in cytosol and steroid-free receptors in intact cells recovered species containing one molecule of receptor and two molecules of hsp90, and progressively more extensive cross-linking of GRs revealed an additional protein of about 50 kDa, giving a heterotetrameric structure of one steroid-binding protein, two hsp90s, and one 50-kDa polypeptide, demonstrated in intact cells and for GR, PR, and ER.

quotes.quote:
After cross-linking of both untransformed re-
ceptors in cytosol and steroid-free receptors in intact cells,
species containing one molecule of receptor and two mole-
cules of hsp90 were recovered. From a careful analysis of GRs
submitted to progressively more extensive cross-linking,
Rexin et al. (391) deduced the existence of another protein of
;50 kDa, proposing a heterotetrameric structure of one ste-
roid-binding protein, two hsp90s, and one 50-kDa polypep-
tide.

this heterotetrameric
structure has been demonstrated in intact cells (377, 391, 394,
395), and the same structures have been demonstrated for
GR, PR, and ER (376, 377, 390–395).

experiment.system: untransformed steroid receptor heterocomplexes in cytosol and intact cells
experiment.perturbation: chemical cross-linking with bifunctional reagents at increasing extent
experiment.measurement: size/composition of cross-linked species

text: Immunoadsorption of receptorzhsp90 complexes from cells labeled to steady state with [35S]methionine, with molecular ratios calculated from known methionine content, gave a stoichiometry of two molecules of hsp90 to one molecule of GR and showed no preferential binding of hsp90a or hsp90b; the data eliminate the possibility that the GR binds only heterodimers.

quotes.quote:
A stoichiometry of two molecules of
hsp90 to one molecule of GR was determined in a different
way by Mendel and Orti (396), who immunoadsorbed
receptorzhsp90 complexes from cells that were labeled to
steady state with [35S]methionine and calculated molecular
ratios from the known methionine content of each protein.
With this technique, they also determined that there was no
preferential binding of hsp90a or hsp90b in the receptor
heterocomplex.

The data of Mendel and Orti (396) do eliminate
the possibility that the GR binds only heterodimers.

experiment.system: cells labeled to steady state with [35S]methionine
experiment.perturbation: immunoadsorption of receptorzhsp90 complexes
experiment.measurement: molar ratios from 35S incorporation and methionine content

text: GR heterocomplexes immunopurified from [35S]methionine-labeled L cells showed an hsp90 to GR ratio of 2:1 under stringent washing conditions and about 4:1 under mild washing, and the core labeled heterocomplex contained a approximately 55-kDa protein with several isomorphs now known to be the immunophilin FKBP52.

quotes.quote:
The ratio of hsp90 to GR under
stringent washing conditions was 2:1, but under mild wash-
ing conditions the ratio was ;4:1.

the core [35S]methionine-labeled GR het-
erocomplex contained a ;55-kDa protein with several iso-
morphs (188), which is now known to be the immunophilin
FKBP52 (397).

experiment.system: [35S]methionine-labeled mouse L cells
experiment.perturbation: immunopurification of GR heterocomplexes with mild vs stringent washing in the presence of molybdate
experiment.measurement: hsp90:GR ratio and identity of coadsorbed polypeptides

text: Hydrodynamic analysis of complexes formed between purified, molybdate-stabilized 9S ER and antibodies against receptor or hsp90 led to the conclusion that two steroid-binding subunits were associated with two molecules of hsp90, a stoichiometry differing from the one ER to two hsp90 determined by cross-linking.

quotes.quote:
From hydrodynamic analysis of complexes formed between
the purified, molybdate-stabilized 9S ER and antibodies di-
rected against either the receptor or hsp90, Redeuilh et al.
(340) concluded that two steroid-binding subunits were as-
sociated with two molecules of hsp90. This stoichiometry
differs from the stoichiometry of one molecule of ER and two
molecules of hsp90 determined by Segnitz and Gehring (377)
using the cross-linking method.

experiment.system: purified molybdate-stabilized 9S estrogen receptor
experiment.perturbation: addition of antibodies against receptor or hsp90
experiment.measurement: hydrodynamic properties of the antibody-complexes to infer subunit stoichiometry

text: Transfected human GR deleted for the HBD does not form the 9S heterocomplex, and trypsin cleavage of molybdate-stabilized rat liver GR isolated a 27-kDa fragment containing the HBD that was bound to hsp90; the GR HBD alone was sufficient to confer tight hsp90 binding onto chimeric proteins, and bacterially expressed GR HBD bound rabbit hsp90 when incubated with reticulocyte lysate.

quotes.quote:
Pratt et al. (200) subsequently
showed that transfected human GR deleted for the HBD does
not form the 9S heterocomplex, consistent with the HBD
being necessary for hsp90 binding. Denis et al. (138) cleaved
the molybdate-stabilized rat liver GR with trypsin and iso-
lated a 27-kDa fragment that contained the HBD and was
bound to hsp90. It was subsequently shown that the GR HBD
alone was sufficient to confer the property of tight hsp90
binding onto chimeric proteins (400) and that the GR HBD
expressed in bacteria could be bound to rabbit hsp90 when
it was incubated with rabbit reticulocyte lysate (401)

experiment.perturbation: HBD deletion, tryptic cleavage, domain swapping, lysate incubation
experiment.measurement: 9S complex formation and hsp90 binding

text: Immunoadsorption with anti-hsp90 antibody of in vitro translated [35S]methionine-labeled GR C-terminal deletion mutants showed a minimal region from amino acids 604–659 (mouse GR) was required for a high yield of high-affinity hsp90 binding, while region 556–604 was sufficient to yield some hsp90 binding; transfection studies dividing the HBD into three subregions showed each region was sufficient to confer hsp90 binding as measured by 9S complex formation.

quotes.quote:
Dalman et al. (230) translated GR-containing C-terminal
deletions of various lengths and immunoadsorbed the newly
translated, [35S]methionine-labeled receptors with a mono-
clonal antibody against hsp90. A minimal region from amino
acids 604–659 (mouse GR) was required for a high yield of
high-affinity hsp90 binding. Using the same approach,
Howard et al. (402) found that the region 556–604 (mouse
GR) was sufficient to yield some hsp90 binding.

Cadepond et al. (201) divided the HBD of the GR into
three subregions of roughly equal length and showed that
each region was sufficient to confer hsp90 binding onto a
receptor fragment as determined by 9S complex formation in
transfected cells.

experiment.system: in vitro translated mouse GR deletion mutants in reticulocyte lysate; transfected cells expressing GR HBD subregions
experiment.perturbation: C-terminal deletions and HBD subdivision
experiment.measurement: coimmunoadsorption with anti-hsp90 antibody; 9S complex formation

numbers.quantity: minimal region for high-yield hsp90 binding
region sufficient for some hsp90 binding

text: Tryptic cleavage of the steroid-free, molybdate-stabilized GR defined a 16-kDa core fragment of the HBD (525–661, mouse) that bound dexamethasone with a 23-fold lower affinity than the intact GR but retained wild-type binding specificity and was bound to hsp90; this fragment contains three cysteines of which any two can form an intramolecular disulfide.

quotes.quote:
Simons and his co-workers cleaved the steroid-free,
molybdate-stabilized GR with trypsin until they defined a
16-kDa core fragment of the HBD (525–661, mouse) that
bound dexamethasone with a 23-fold lower affinity than the
intact GR but retained the same specificity of binding as the
wild-type receptor (227). This 16-kDa core steroid-binding
fragment of the HBD is bound to hsp90 (139).

The 16-kDa fragment contains
three cysteines, of which any two can form an intramolecular
disulfide (226).

experiment.system: steroid-free, molybdate-stabilized glucocorticoid receptor
experiment.perturbation: limited tryptic digestion
experiment.measurement: fragment size, dexamethasone binding affinity/specificity, hsp90 association, disulfide formation

text: A mutant mouse GR (D574–632) deleted for a conserved 20-amino acid steroid receptor sequence (583–602, mouse GR) is bound to hsp90 but less stably than wild-type receptor, and a peptide spanning 80% of the conserved sequence inhibited GRzhsp90 heterocomplex assembly by the reticulocyte lysate system; the same conserved region is present in thyroid hormone and retinoic acid receptors, which do not form tight hsp90 complexes.

quotes.quote:
A mutant mouse GR
(D574–632) deleted for this region is bound to hsp90, but the
binding is less stable than that of wild-type receptor (405),
suggesting that the region may define a structure of some
importance in hsp90 binding. A peptide spanning 80% of the
conserved sequence was found to inhibit GRzhsp90 hetero-
complex assembly by the reticulocyte lysate system (230)

this 20-amino acid region is conserved
in both thyroid hormone and retinoic acid receptors, neither
of which form tight complexes with hsp90 (344, 345); thus,
the conserved region itself is not sufficient for detectible
hsp90 binding.

experiment.system: mouse GR deletion mutant and reticulocyte lysate heterocomplex assembly system
experiment.perturbation: deletion D574–632; addition of a peptide spanning 80% of the conserved sequence
experiment.measurement: stability of hsp90 binding and heterocomplex assembly

numbers.quantity: fraction of conserved sequence spanned by inhibitory peptide

text: Deletion analysis of chicken PR expressed in COS cells showed the entire HBD had to be deleted before hsp90 binding (9S complex formation) was eliminated, and the HBD alone was sufficient for complex formation with hsp90.

quotes.quote:
transfected
COS cells with mutant cDNAs for the chicken PR and found
that it was necessary to delete the entire HBD of the A
isoform before hsp90 binding (9S complex formation) was
eliminated

As with the GR, expression of just the HBD was suf-
ficient for formation of a complex with hsp90 (407).

text: In chicken PR mutants expressed in quail fibroblasts, three separate regions of the HBD each partially restored hsp90 complex formation to a PR mutant lacking the HBD, and deletion of individual regions did not abolish binding.

quotes.quote:
Schowalter et al. (408) found that three separate
regions of the HBD were able to partially restore hsp90 com-
plex formation to a PR mutant lacking the HBD

text: In a model of Drosophila wing vein boundary formation, mutual inactivation of Notch and DSL in cis generates sharp Notch signaling side-bands without any feedback of Notch signaling on Notch or DSL, whereas an alternative model lacking mutual inactivation requires a bandpass filter of Notch activity.

quotes.quote:
In the mutual inactivation (MI) model (Fig. 2C), mutually
exclusive signaling states generate sharp side-bands (as observed
experimentally) where ‘sender’ cells contact ‘receiver’ cells near the
crossing of the Notch and DSL production rate profiles. This
model does not consider any feedback of Notch signaling on either
DSL or Notch itself in the same cell

Alternatively, in the ‘bandpass’ (BP) model a similar Notch
activity profile can be generated in the absence of mutual
inactivation, but this requires a bandpass filter of Notch activity
level which we represent phenomenologically as the product of
increasing and decreasing Hill functions

experiment.system: Mathematical model of Drosophila wing vein boundary formation with a linear DSL production gradient and constant Notch production, with (MI) or without (BP) cis mutual inactivation
experiment.perturbation: Presence versus absence of the cis mutual-inactivation terms in the model equations
experiment.measurement: Simulated spatial profiles of Notch target reporter concentration

text: Across a wide range of morphogen gradient slopes, the MI model's signaling band width remained nearly constant (with band amplitude changing systematically with slope), while the BP model showed substantial broadening of the bands at lower gradient slopes.

nearly constant across a wide range of morphogen gradient slopes
(Fig. 2D, middle). This resulted from the sharp switch from a
sending to a receiving state at the bN~bD(x) intersection. In
contrast, the amplitude of the signaling bands changed systemat-
ically with the magnitude of the slope.

In contrast, the BP model shows substantial broadening of the
bands at lower values of the gradient slope (Fig. 2D, bottom).

experiment.system: MI and BP models of boundary formation simulated on a hexagonal cell array
experiment.perturbation: Systematic variation of morphogen (DSL) gradient slope with the threshold position held at a fixed distance from the vein center
experiment.measurement: Width and amplitude of the Notch reporter signaling bands

text: The BP model supports a sharp boundary only for sufficiently large cooperativity p and sufficiently high gradient slopes, whereas in the MI model band sharpness is preserved across a broad range of cis-interaction strengths kc and morphogen slopes.

supports a sharp boundary only for sufficiently large p and
sufficiently high slopes (Fig. 2E, bottom). In contrast, with the MI
model, band sharpness is preserved across a broad range of kc
values and morphogen slopes (Fig. 2E, top). Thus, mutual
inactivation enables a more robust patterning mechanism.

experiment.system: MI and BP boundary-formation models
experiment.perturbation: Scanning cis-interaction strength kc (MI) or bandpass cooperativity p (BP) against morphogen gradient slope
experiment.measurement: Reporter peak width w as a function of slope and the model parameter

text: The MI model reproduces the ratiometric dependence of vein width on Notch and DSL gene copy number, because the Notch signaling band sits where Notch and DSL production rates are equal, a position unchanged when both rates are scaled by the same factor; vein width increases with increasing DSL-to-Notch effective copy number ratio.

quotes.quote:
This
ratiometric dependence of the vein width cannot be derived from
the several known feedbacks operating in the Drosophila wing vein,
but emerges automatically from the MI model. This is because the
position of the Notch signaling band occurs where Notch and DSL
production rates are equal. This position remains unchanged
when both rates are multiplied by the same factor. By the same
reasoning, the vein width (distance between side bands) increases
with increasing ratios between the effective copy numbers of DSL
and Notch, as shown in Figs. 3A, S2.

experiment.system: MI model of wing vein boundary formation compared with published Notch/Delta heterozygous mutant wing phenotypes
experiment.perturbation: Varying maximal DSL production rate bmax_D and Notch production rate bN (mimicking gene copy number changes)
experiment.measurement: Simulated distance between the two Notch reporter peaks (vein width)

text: When the maximal DSL production rate falls below the Notch production rate everywhere, all cells become receivers and Notch signaling no longer restricts vein width, yielding a broad diffuse vein; the authors state this makes the quantitative prediction that the maximal DSL production rate should be less than twice the constitutive Notch production rate in the wing vein system.

quotes.quote:
Here, since all cells are
essentially ‘receivers’ we expect negligible levels of Notch signaling,
leading to a phenotype of an unsharpened, diffusely-defined vein,
that defaults to the pre-patterned vein-competent region.

This result
makes a quantitative prediction: the maximal DSL (Delta ligand in
the case of the wing vein) production rate should be less than twice
the constitutive Notch production rate in this system.

text: In dynamical simulations at matched parameters, the lateral inhibition with mutual inactivation (LIMI) model diverges from homogeneity and reaches the patterned state faster than the standard lateral inhibition (LI) model, a difference observed over a large region of parameter space; the authors attribute the acceleration to the cis-inactivation terms acting as effective degradation terms active only when Notch and DSL are simultaneously present.

The LI model initially spends a
considerable time in a nearly homogeneous state (left of the dashed
line in Fig. 4D) before DSL concentrations diverge (red and blue
curves, right of the dashed line). In contrast, in the LIMI model, DSL
concentrations diverge much earlier (Fig. 4E). The LIMI process
approaches the final patterned state more rapidly than the LI process

A key
difference in the LIMI model is the inactivation terms, which are
equivalent to effective degradation terms

in the LIMI
model the additional degradation only occurs when both Notch
and DSL are simultaneously present on the same cell.

expression implements lateral inhibition with only a single level of

alanine (M535A) also reversed V617F-driven proliferation. In contrast, a conservative

text: Focused classification with symmetry expansion and signal subtraction resolved two major insulin-occupancy classes: 63% of particles have four insulins bound (two each at sites 1 and 2) and 33% have three insulins (two at site 1, one at site 2); structures with three or four insulins differ only subtly, and 96% of T-shaped particles have at least one insulin at site 2 or 2'.

In particular, 63% of the particles

insulins to both sites 2 and 2’ is not required for the maintenance of the T-shaped IR dimer

at least one insulin bound to site 2 or 2’, suggesting that insulin binding to site 2 is important for IR

text: Insulin binding produces two hinge motions in the IR protomer without internal rearrangement of the L1/CR or FnIII-1/-2/-3 segments: L1/CR rotates ~90° toward L2 around the CR–L2 hinge loop (residues 302–310, stabilized by an Glu287–Lys310 salt bridge), and FnIII-1,-2,-3 rotate away from L2 by ~50°, converting the protomer into an inverted 'J' shape that forms new inter-domain contacts.

The structures of the L1/CR segment and the FnIII-1/-2/-3 segment of insulin-bound IR can be super-

the L1/CR domains of IR rotate ~90˚ toward the L2 domain upon insulin binding, cre-
ating two new inter-domain contacts

bridge to stabilize the insulin-bound loop conformation.

Notch1 ice, a minimal Notch1 mutant in which the extracellular domain is missing and the entire intracellular domain is replaced by 6Myc epitope tags (31), was also cleaved at Val1711 (supplemental Fig. 3B) indicating that the minimal sequence requirements for S2 cleavage are contained within the 15 juxtamembrane amino acids encompassing Val1711 and possibly the Notch1 TMD.

experiment.system: transfected cells expressing truncated Notch1 constructs (LNR, ΔE, Δice) ± AV→VH
experiment.perturbation: domain deletions and S2 site mutation
experiment.measurement: Val1711/Val1744 immunoblotting and RBP-Jk/CSL reporter activity

numbers.quantity: juxtamembrane amino acids containing minimal S2 requirements

text: The LNR A1710E (AV→EV) mutant, which retains Val1711, was furin-cleaved and constitutively S3-cleaved but, unlike L1594P, showed no GSI-induced accumulation of NEXT fragment or Val1711 epitope, indicating cleavage at other scissile bonds when the preferred site is mutated.

quotes.quote: AV 3 EV-transfected cells treated with GSI showed no accumulation of a NEXT fragment (detected with Myc) or of the Val1711 epitope (supplemental Fig. 4).
Collectively, these data show that HD mutations enhance ligand-independent cleavage at a preferred site (Val1711), but when this site is mutated, proteases cleave other scissile bonds.

experiment.system: transfected cells expressing Notch1 LNR A1710E (AV→EV) or L1594P
experiment.perturbation: S2 site substitution A1710E; GSI treatment
experiment.measurement: anti-Myc, Val1711, Val1744 immunoblots

text: Ligand-induced endogenous Notch1 S2 cleavage at Val1711 and subsequent S3 cleavage proceeded normally in Adam17 knock-out fibroblasts and in cells lacking Adam9, -12 and -15.

quotes.quote: In the absence of Adam17, endogenous Notch1 activation by ligand was similar to wild type cells, and S2 cleavage occurred at Val1711 and was followed by S3 cleavage at Val1744 (Fig. 5A). Furthermore, ligand-induced Notch1 proteolysis proceeded normally in cells lacking Adam9, -12, and -15 (supplemental Fig. 5).

experiment.system: Adam17 knock-out and Adam9/12/15-deficient mouse fibroblasts expressing endogenous Notch1
experiment.perturbation: co-culture with Jagged1-retrovirus-transduced knock-out cells
experiment.measurement: Notch1, Val1711, Val1744 immunoblotting

text: Cells lacking Adam10 showed dramatically reduced ligand-induced S2 cleavage at Val1711 and reduced S3 cleavage compared with wild type, though residual S2 cleavage remained, indicating ADAM10 is the main but not sole protease; Adam10-deficient ligand-expressing cells could still activate Notch1 in wild type receptor cells.

quotes.quote: In contrast, in cells lacking Adam10, S2 cleavage at Val1711 was dramatically reduced when compared with wild type controls, resulting in reduced S3 cleavage (Fig. 5B).

However, because residual S2 cleavage was still observed in the absence of ADAM10 (Fig. 5B, arrowhead), other protease(s) have the ability to cleave Notch1 at Val1711, albeit inefficiently, in Adam10-deficient cells.

experiment.system: Adam10 knock-out and wild type fibroblasts expressing endogenous Notch1
experiment.perturbation: co-culture with Jagged1-expressing cells (Adam10-deficient or wild type)
experiment.measurement: Notch1, Val1711, Val1744, Jagged1 and TACE immunoblotting

text: PMA and APMA enhanced shedding of LNR L1594P and increased S3 cleavage, and APMA dramatically enhanced Val1711 epitope detection even without GSI, indicating NEXT accumulation is not an indirect GSI effect and that local γ-secretase activity can be saturated by excess substrate.

quotes.quote: Both compounds enhanced shedding of LNR L1594P mutant molecules, which increased S3 cleavage (Fig. 6). Importantly, APMA dramatically enhanced detection of the Val1711 epitope even in the absence of GSI, demonstrating that NEXT accumulation is not an indirect effect of GSI and that local -secretase activity could be saturated in vivo by excess substrate (43).

experiment.system: HEK293 cells transfected with LNR L1594P 6Myc
experiment.perturbation: PMA (50 ng/ml) or APMA (250 µM) treatment ± GSI
experiment.measurement: Myc, Val1711, Val1744 immunoblots

text: Surface biotinylation of LNR CC→SS-transfected U2OS cells enriched transmembrane/intracellular domain and S2-Val1711 fragments but not full-length or S3-cleaved Notch1 or cytoplasmic HIF1α, consistent with S2 cleavage at the plasma membrane.

quotes.quote: This was efficiently enriched for transmembrane and intracellular domain and S2-Val1711 Notch1 fragments, the latter labeled on Lys1712 (Fig. 7A). Full-length Notch1 (present only in endoplasmic reticulum and early Golgi) and S3-cleaved Notch1 (intracellular) were not enriched by biotinylation.
These results are consistent with S2 cleavage at the plasma membrane.

experiment.system: U2OS cells transfected with active Notch1 LNR CC→SS (C1675S/C1682S) 6Myc
experiment.perturbation: cell-surface NHS-biotin labeling (± biotin control; FLAG-HIF1α control)
experiment.measurement: streptavidin pulldown followed by Myc, Val1711, Val1744 immunoblotting

text: Immunofluorescence of LNR CC→SS-mCherry-transfected U2OS cells showed nuclear Val1744 staining without GSI and, with GSI, loss of Val1744 nuclear staining and gain of Val1711 staining predominantly at the plasma membrane with some cytoplasmic vesicles, supporting cell-surface S2 cleavage.

quotes.quote: Upon GSI inhibition, Val1744 nuclear staining and nuclear mCherry were lost, but Val1711 staining was gained decorating the plasma membrane in permeabilized cells.
Combined, these experiments show for the first time that S2 cleavage of Notch1 receptors occurs at the cell surface and strongly suggest that S3 cleavage follows in the same compartment.

experiment.system: U2OS cells transfected with constitutively active Notch1 LNR CC→SS-mCherry
experiment.perturbation: GSI treatment versus untreated
experiment.measurement: confocal immunofluorescence for Val1711 and Val1744 with mCherry and TO-PRO3 nuclear stain

text: Constitutive Val1711 shedding of LNR L1594P was completely inhibited by GM6001, BB94, TAPI-2 and the ADAM10/17-specific inhibitor GW280264X, whereas the ADAM10-selective inhibitor GI254023X could not inhibit Notch1 processing.

quotes.quote: Constitutive shedding of LNR L1594P at Val1711 could be completely inhibited by the broad spectrum inhibitor GM6001 (Galardin) as well as the more ADAM-specific inhibitors BB94 (Batimastat) and TAPI-2 (IC-3), and the ADAM10/17-specific inhibitor GW280264X (44) (Fig. 8A). Unexpectedly, the reported ADAM10-selective inhibitor GI254023X (44) could not inhibit Notch1 processing (Fig. 8A, arrowhead).

experiment.measurement: Val1711 and Val1744/Myc immunoblotting

text: A range of broad spectrum cysteine (E-64) and serine protease inhibitors (antipain, chymostatin, α1-antitrypsin), and a β-secretase inhibitor, failed to inhibit Val1711 or Val1744 proteolysis of Notch1.

experiment.perturbation: E-64 (10 µM), antipain, chymostatin, α1-antitrypsin, Ser-Cys inhibitor mixture, β-secretase inhibitor
experiment.measurement: Val1711 and Val1744 immunoblotting

text: In RelA-DsRed 3T3 fibroblasts stimulated with non-repeating sequences of four inflammatory ligands in a microfluidic device, prior exposure history primarily attenuated NF-κB responses to subsequent ligands, with response amplitude decreasing from S1 to S4; the initial dataset comprised 72 conditions and more than 10,000 single cells.

quotes.quote:
In our initial dataset of 72 conditions, we analyzed 
more than 10,000 single cells (Fig 2A–C, Supp. Fig 1F–Supp. Fig 3) with a range of prior 
histories and stimulus doses.

we observed that response for each 
ligand decreased from S1 to S4 (Fig 2D)

From 
these observations, we concluded that prior exposure history primarily attenuates signaling 
responses to subsequent ligands.

experiment.system: RelA−/− NIH/3T3 fibroblasts expressing RelA-DsRed in a microfluidic live-cell imaging device
experiment.perturbation: non-repeating sequences of TNF-α, IL-1β, LPS, PAM at 2-hour intervals, at high/mid/low doses
experiment.measurement: single-cell nuclear/cytoplasmic NF-κB response amplitude and AUC per stimulus interval

text: Repeated stimulation with the same ligand weakened subsequent responses: LPS and PAM only produced a response after the first stimulus, while TNF-α and IL-1β exhibited weak responses after the second to fourth stimulus depending on dose.

quotes.quote:
LPS and PAM only produced a response after the first stimulus, while TNF-α and IL-1β 
exhibited weak responses after the second to fourth stimulus depending on dose (Fig. 2A–
C).

experiment.perturbation: four repeated stimulations with the same ligand at 2-hour intervals
experiment.measurement: live-cell imaging of nuclear NF-κB translocation

text: Attenuation patterns were ligand- and dose-dependent: even at high dose cells responded to TNF-α irrespective of prior history, while at mid and low dose LPS and TNF-α responses showed the weakest attenuation and IL-1β and PAM responses varied greatly with prior history.

quotes.quote:
Even at high dose, where attenuation was 
strongest, cells responded to TNF-α stimulus irrespective of prior history (Fig 2A, Supp. 
Fig 4A). At mid and low dose, each ligand displayed different history responses. LPS and 
TNF-α responses exhibited the weakest attenuation, with some level of stimulus response 
retained across most conditions, while IL-1β and PAM responses showed large variability in 
response depending on prior stimulus history

experiment.system: RelA-DsRed 3T3 fibroblasts
experiment.perturbation: 24 non-repeating four-ligand sequences at high, mid, and low doses
experiment.measurement: single-cell NF-κB response amplitude normalized to mean S1 response

text: Ligand-specific channel capacity generally rose at S2 and remained elevated at S3-4, except TNF-α at high dose and LPS at low dose which gained little information from prior history.

quotes.quote:
We found that the CC specific to each ligand generally rose at S2 and remained 
elevated at S3-4.

However, TNF-α at high dose and LPS at low dose gained little information 
from prior history

experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: channel capacity among samples within each ligand/position group

we found that the CC from a single feature (Fig 3B red 
lines, 3D) are substantially lower than the CC from the dynamic measurement (Fig 3B 
blue lines, 3C). This indicates that alteration of NF-κB activation dynamics plays a role in 
transmitting information about prior history

verdict_note: Claim text and quote match ('CC from a single feature ... substantially lower than the CC from the dynamic measurement'); the '6-dimension response vector' detail in the experiment field is not in the excerpt but is a methods-level specification that does not alter the claim.

experiment.perturbation: observational; comparison of single-feature versus 6-dimension response vector
experiment.measurement: channel capacity

text: Pairwise mutual information among 16 S1/S2 conditions per dose showed dose-dependent patterns: at low and mid dose distinguishability was driven by TNF-α/IL-1β versus LPS/PAM dynamics, whereas at high dose all TNF-α responses became highly distinguishable from other samples.

We focused on the naïve responses to a ligand at S1 and following another ligand at S2, resulting in a 
comparison of 16 conditions for each dose (Fig 3E).

mutual information patterns at low and mid dose were primarily driven by differences between 
TNF-α or IL-1β response dynamics and LPS or PAM response dynamics

At high dose, the pattern of 
mutual information changed such that all TNF-α responses became highly distinguishable 
from other samples.

experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: pairwise mutual information between ligand response dynamics

text: Prior TNF-α weakly attenuated subsequent MyD88-dependent ligand responses and vice versa, whereas prior MyD88-dependent ligands attenuated subsequent MyD88-dependent signaling in a dose-dependent manner, significantly more than prior TNF-α at high and mid doses.

quotes.quote:
We found that, following TNF-α stimulus, the response 
to MyD88-dependent ligands was weakly attenuated (Fig 4D, blue). Likewise, the response 
to TNF-α following MyD88-dependent stimuli was weakly attenuated (Fig 4D, green). 
In contrast, MyD88-dependent ligands attenuated subsequent signaling by other MyD88-
dependent ligands in a dose-dependent manner (Fig 4D, red). At high and mid doses, 
exposure to MyD88-dependent ligands resulted in significantly attenuated signaling from 
other MyD88-dependent ligands compared to previous TNF-α exposure.

experiment.perturbation: S1 ligand followed by S2 ligand (TNF-α vs MyD88-dependent ligand pairs) at high, mid, low dose

text: Attenuation among MyD88-dependent ligands was symmetric at high dose but asymmetric at mid and low doses, where only prior LPS strongly attenuated subsequent MyD88-dependent signaling while IL-1β and PAM allowed significantly stronger subsequent responses; JNK measurements reproduced this asymmetry.

At high 
dose, all three MyD88-dependent ligands indeed strongly attenuated subsequent responses 
(Fig 4E). In contrast, at mid and low doses, only LPS strongly attenuated subsequent 
MyD88-dependent signaling (Fig 4E, red), while IL-1β and PAM allowed significantly 
stronger subsequent responses

we saw that symmetric attenuation took place at 
high dose, but at mid dose, only LPS maintained strong attenuation of MyD88-dependent 
JNK activation (Supp. Fig 5F–H)

text: MyD88 knockout abolished all NF-κB response to LPS in these cells, indicating the MyD88-independent TRIF/TRAM pathway had minimal influence.

we 
found that the MyD88-independent pathway for LPS had minimal influence in these cells, as

text: Extending the interval between the first and second stimulus to 4, 6, and 8 hours preserved ligand- and dose-specific attenuation, including LPS attenuating IL-1β but not vice versa at mid dose, though TNF-α-dependent and IL-1β-dependent attenuation strengthened at longer intervals.

extended the duration between S1 and S2 to 4, 6, and 8 hours (Supp. Fig 5I–L).

text: Attenuation of the IL-1β (3 ng/ml) response by high dose LPS (400 ng/ml) was fast and strong at all intervals except the shortest (10 min), whereas at lower LPS doses (12.5–400 ng/ml range) the IL-1β response became gradually attenuated with increasing LPS stimulus duration.

We stimulated cells with various doses of LPS (12.5 – 400 ng/ml), then stimulated 
the cells with high dose of IL-1β (3 ng/ml) after 10–120 minutes of LPS stimulus (Fig 4F,

doses of LPS, the IL-1β response became gradually attenuated depending on duration of

the response to IL-1β following LPS gradually decreased over time, while

high dose stimulus triggers 
rapid inactivation of the IRAK1 population, leading to depletion of available IRAK1 (Supp.
