identified a Sestrin2 mutant (S190W) that still binds leucine but has a severely decreased 
capacity to bind GATOR2 (Fig. 3C and D). In Sestrin1-3 triple null HEK-293T cells, 
mTORC1 signaling was active and unaffected by leucine deprivation (Fig. 3E). In these 
cells expression of wild-type Sestrin2 restored the leucine sensitivity of the mTORC1 
pathway, but that of Sestrin2 S190W had no effect (Fig. 3E).

experiment.system: Sestrin1-3 triple null HEK-293T cells generated with CRISPR/Cas9, expressing FLAG-tagged wild-type or S190W Sestrin2
experiment.perturbation: leucine starvation 50 minutes and leucine restimulation 10 minutes; S190W point mutation
experiment.measurement: co-immunoprecipitation of GATOR2, leucine binding assay, and immunoblotting of mTORC1 pathway phosphorylation

text: Sestrin2 mutants L261A and E451A do not bind leucine appreciably, their GATOR2 interaction was not significantly affected by leucine in vitro, and in Sestrin1-3 triple null cells they inhibited mTORC1 signaling and rendered it insensitive to leucine; mTOR lysosomal localization in the presence of leucine was decreased while RagC localization was unaffected.

quotes.quote:
we identified two Sestrin2 mutants, L261A and E451A, which do 
not bind leucine to an appreciable degree (Fig. 4A). Leucine did not significantly affect the 
interaction of the mutants with GATOR2 in vitro

but that of either mutant inhibited signaling and rendered it 
insensitive to leucine (Fig. 4C and S3A). Furthermore, in Sestrin1-3 triple null cells 
expressing the mutants, the localization of mTOR to lysosomes in the presence of leucine 
was decreased, while that of RagC was not affected

experiment.system: Sestrin1-3 triple null HEK-293T cells expressing Sestrin2 L261A or E451A
experiment.perturbation: leucine-binding-deficient point mutations; leucine starvation/restimulation
experiment.measurement: [3H]leucine binding, GATOR2 co-immunoprecipitation, S6K1 phosphorylation immunoblot, immunofluorescence of mTOR and RagC lysosomal localization

text: Blocking E-cadherin expression by transfection of antisense RNA does not induce a full EMT, and forced E-cadherin expression is insufficient to restore the epithelial phenotype in spindle carcinoma cells or to reverse induced EMT.

quotes.quote: blocking E-cadherin expression by transfection of antisense RNA does not induce a full EMT [7]. Furthermore, forced E-cadherin expression is insufficient to restore the epithelial phenotype in spindle carcinoma cells and does not reverse induced EMT [8-12].

experiment.system: epithelial and spindle carcinoma cells in culture
experiment.perturbation: antisense RNA knockdown of E-cadherin; forced E-cadherin expression
experiment.measurement: epithelial versus mesenchymal phenotype (EMT status)

text: Upon TGF-β treatment, epithelial cells changed from cuboidal to an elongated spindle shape, showed decreased epithelial marker expression and enhanced expression of fibronectin and vimentin, with increased motility; TGF-β1, TGF-β2 and TGF-β3 all induce EMT in epithelial cells.

quotes.quote:
Upon TGF-β 
treatment, epithelial cells changed from cuboidal to an elongated spindle shape, and showed 
decreased expression of epithelial markers and enhanced expression of mesenchymal 
markers fibronectin and vimentin [17]. These changes were accompanied by increased 
motility.

TGF-β1, TGF-β2 
and TGF-β3 share the capacity to induce EMT in epithelial cells [17, 27, 28].

experiment.system: epithelial cells in culture
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β1/β2/β3 treatment
experiment.measurement: cell morphology, epithelial/mesenchymal marker expression, motility

text: TGF-β1 null mouse embryos present severe cardiac abnormalities including defective atrioventricular junction, TGF-β2-deficient mice present atrioventricular and outflow tract defects, and blocking TGF-β with antibodies or antisense oligonucleotides inhibits EMT in chicken atrioventricular explants and TGF-β2-induced EMT in mouse explant cultures.

quotes.quote:
In mice, TGF-β1 null embryos present severe cardiac abnormalities including defective 
atrioventricular junction. Moreover, TGF-β2-deficient mice present atrioventricular and 
outflow tract defects. Finally, blocking TGF-β activity using antibodies or antisense 
oligonucleotides inhibits EMT in chicken atrioventricular explants and TGF-β2-induced 
EMT in mouse explant cultures [33, 34].

experiment.system: mouse embryos and chicken/mouse atrioventricular explant cultures
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β1 or TGF-β2 gene deletion; TGF-β blocking antibodies/antisense oligonucleotides
experiment.measurement: cardiac morphology and EMT in explants

text: TGF-β3 is highly expressed at sites of palatal shelf fusion and TGF-β3 null mice present a cleft palate resulting from the lack of fusion of the two palatal shelves.

quotes.quote:
high TGF-
β3 expression is apparent at these sites [35]. TGF-β3 null mice present a cleft palate, 
resulting from the lack of fusion of the two palatal shelves [36].

experiment.system: mouse palatal development
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β3 gene knockout (observational expression analysis)
experiment.measurement: TGF-β3 expression and palatal shelf fusion/cleft palate phenotype

text: Transgenic expression of activated TGF-β1 correlates with conversion of squamous into more invasive spindle cell carcinomas in chemical carcinogenesis studies in vivo, and transgenic mice with increased TGF-β1 expression develop renal fibrosis.

quotes.quote:
Chemical carcino-genesis studies in 
vivo showed that transgenic expression of activated TGF-β1 correlates with the conversion 
of squamous into more invasive spindle cell carcinomas [39].

transgenic mice with increased expression of TGF-β1 develop renal 
fibrosis [42].

experiment.system: transgenic mice
experiment.perturbation: transgenic expression of activated TGF-β1 with chemical carcinogenesis
experiment.measurement: tumor histology (squamous vs spindle carcinoma), renal fibrosis

text: Dominant negative interference with TGF-β type II receptor function reverses EMT in colon cancer cells in culture and inhibits EMT in skin and mammary cancer models in vivo, and loss of the TGF-β type II receptor is associated with decreased EMT at cancer loci in a mouse skin carcinoma model.

quotes.quote:
Dominant 
negative interference with the TGF-β type II receptor function reverses EMT in colon cancer 
cells in culture and inhibits EMT in skin and mammary cancer models in vivo [47, 48]. 
Furthermore, loss of the TGF-β type II receptor has been associated with decreased EMT at 
cancer loci in a mouse skin carcinoma model [49].

experiment.system: colon cancer cells in culture; mouse skin and mammary cancer models
experiment.perturbation: dominant negative TβRII expression; TβRII loss
experiment.measurement: EMT status at cancer loci

text: Expression of activated ALK-5 (TβRI) or ActRIB/ALK-4 recapitulates TGF-β-induced EMT in NMuMG cells, while dominant negative forms of either type I receptor block TGF-β-induced EMT; a chemical TβRI inhibitor also blocks EMT and promotes an enhanced epithelial phenotype, and interference with TβRI in vivo suppresses EMT during cardiac valve formation.

quotes.quote:
expression 
of an activated version of the TβRI receptor ALK-5, the major TGF-β type I receptor, or of 
ActRIB/ALK-4, the major type I receptor for activin and nodal, recapitulates TGF-β-
induced EMT in NMuMG cells [27, 28], while dominant negative forms of either type I 
receptor block TGF-β-induced EMT [28]. Inhibition of TβRI function using a chemical 
inhibitor also blocks EMT and promotes an enhanced epithelial phenotype in cell culture 
[50, 51], while interference with TβRI function in vivo suppresses EMT and decreases 
mesenchymal differentiation during cardiac valve formation [52].

experiment.system: NMuMG cells and cell culture models; cardiac valve formation in vivo
experiment.perturbation: activated or dominant negative TβRI/ALK-4 expression; chemical TβRI inhibitor
experiment.measurement: EMT phenotype and mesenchymal differentiation

text: Increased expression of Smad2 or Smad3 with Smad4 induces or enhances EMT in NMuMG cells while dominant negative Smad2 or Smad3 blocks TGF-β-induced EMT; Smad3-deficient renal tubular epithelial cells fail to undergo EMT in response to TGF-β or mechanical stress, and Smad3–/– keratinocytes show reduced migration in response to TGF-β.

quotes.quote:
Increased 
expression of Smad2 or Smad3 with Smad4 induces EMT, or enhances the induction of 
EMT by the activated form of TβRI, in NMuMG cells [27, 28], whereas expression of 
dominant negative versions of Smad2 or Smad3 blocks TGF-β-induced EMT in this cell 
system [28]. Consistent with the pivotal role of Smad3 in EMT, renal tubular epithelial cells 
deficient in Smad3 fail to undergo EMT in response to TGF-β or mechanical stress [53], and 
keratinocytes derived from Smad3–/– mice show reduced migration in response to TGF-β 
[54].

experiment.system: NMuMG cells, renal tubular epithelial cells, mouse keratinocytes
experiment.perturbation: Smad2/3/4 overexpression, dominant negative Smads, Smad3 deficiency, TGF-β or mechanical stress
experiment.measurement: EMT induction and cell migration

text: Knockdown or dominant negative inhibition of Smad4 results in preserved E-cadherin expression, suppressed type I collagen synthesis in vitro and decreased bone metastasis in vivo, and genetic ablation of Smad4 leads to preservation of epithelial markers and a lower degree of EMT in adenocarcinoma.

quotes.quote:
RNA interference-mediated 
knockdown of Smad4 expression or expression of a dominant negative mutant of Smad4 
results in preserved E-cadherin expression [22, 28, 58, 59], suppression of fibrotic type I 
collagen synthesis in vitro [59], and decreased bone metastasis in vivo [22]. Furthermore, 
genetic ablation of Smad4 leads to preservation of epithelial markers and a lower degree of 
EMT in adenocarcinoma [60].

experiment.system: epithelial/carcinoma cells in vitro and mouse tumor models
experiment.perturbation: Smad4 RNAi knockdown, dominant negative Smad4, genetic ablation
experiment.measurement: E-cadherin/epithelial marker expression, collagen synthesis, bone metastasis, EMT degree

text: Smad3 mediates TGF-β induction of Snail1 by binding and activating the Snail1 promoter; Smad3-deficient renal tubular epithelial cells fail to activate Snail1 upon TGF-β treatment and interference with Smad4 attenuates TGF-β1-induced Snail1 expression; Smad3 also activates the Snail2 promoter in MDCK cells in complex with myocardin-related transcription factors.

quotes.quote:
Smad3; Smad3 binds to the Snail1 promoter and activates its transcription [55, 76]. Renal 
tubular epithelial cells deficient in Smad3 expression fail to activate Snail1 expression upon 
TGF-β treatment [53], and interference with Smad4 expression attenuates TGF-β1-induced 
Snail1 expression in epithelial cell lines [22, 58, 59]. Smad3 also mediates TGF-β-induced 
expression of Snail2 in MDCK cells, whereby Smad3 forms a complex with myocardin-
related transcription factors and binds to the Snail2 promoter to activate transcription [77].

experiment.system: renal tubular epithelial cells, epithelial cell lines, MDCK cells
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β treatment with Smad3 deficiency or Smad4 interference
experiment.measurement: Snail1/Snail2 promoter binding and expression

text: Ectopic expression of Snail1 or Snail2 suppresses E-cadherin and plakoglobin expression and enhances vimentin and fibronectin expression leading to a full EMT phenotype, whereas silencing Snail expression reverses this process; Snail1-deficient mouse embryos fail to complete EMT, form a defective mesodermal layer maintaining E-cadherin, and die at gastrulation, and Snail2 silencing in chick embryos causes mesodermal malformation and neural crest emigration failure.

quotes.quote:
Ectopic expression of Snail1 or Snail2 suppresses 
E-cadherin and plakoglobin expression and enhances vimentin and fibronectin expression, 
leading to a full EMT phenotype, whereas silencing of Snail expression reverses this process 
[15, 69, 79-81]. Snail1-deficient mouse embryos are unable to complete the EMT process 
and form a defective mesodermal layer that maintains E-cadherin expression, causing the 
mutant embryos to die at gastrulation [82]. Silencing of Snail2 expression in chick embryos 
results in mesodermal malformation and neural crest emigration failure [83].

experiment.system: epithelial cell lines, mouse embryos, chick embryos
experiment.perturbation: ectopic Snail1/Snail2 expression, Snail silencing, Snail1 deficiency
experiment.measurement: epithelial/mesenchymal marker expression, EMT phenotype, embryonic mesoderm and neural crest development

text: At the E-cadherin promoter Snail1 binds E-box elements and recruits a complex of HDAC1, HDAC2 and mSin3A to repress transcription, whereas Snail2 binds the same E-box elements but recruits HDAC1/3 and CTBP; silencing of the Snail1 gene can restore E-cadherin levels, yet forced E-cadherin expression is unable to counteract Snail1-induced EMT.

quotes.quote:
At the E-cadherin promoter, Snail1 binds to E-box elements, recruits a complex 
consisting of HDAC1, HDAC2 and mSin3A, and thus represses gene transcription [15, 69, 
81]. Snail2 similarly represses E-cadherin through binding to the same E-box elements, but 
recruits a different combination of co-repressors, i.e. HDAC1/3 and CTBP [70, 80, 81].

silencing of the Snail1 gene can restore E-cadherin levels [69, 81]. However, forced 
expression of E-cadherin is unable to counteract Snail1-induced EMT [11, 12]

experiment.system: epithelial/tumor cell lines
experiment.perturbation: Snail1/Snail2 expression or silencing; forced E-cadherin expression
experiment.measurement: E-cadherin promoter binding, co-repressor recruitment, E-cadherin levels, EMT phenotype

text: Snail1 represses claudin-3, -4 and -7 at their promoters and both Snail1 and Snail2 repress claudin-1 and occludin, while Snail1 does not dramatically decrease ZO-1 and p120 levels but alters their distribution from peripheral to diffuse cytoplasmic.

quotes.quote:
Snail1 represses the expression of claudin-3, -4 and -7 at their 
promoters [11, 84], whereas Snail1 and Snail2 both repress the expression of claudin-1 and 
occludin [84-86]. In contrast, Snail1 expression does not dramatically decrease the levels of 
cytoplasmic components of tight junctions, such as ZO-1 and p120, but their distribution is 
altered from peripheral localization to a diffused cytoplasmic pattern [84].

experiment.system: epithelial cells in culture
experiment.perturbation: Snail1 or Snail2 expression
experiment.measurement: tight junction gene/protein expression and protein localization

text: Snail1 binds the E-box element in the Crumbs3 promoter and inhibits Crumbs3 expression, leading to disassembly of the Crumbs complex, but Snail1 expression does not affect the Par complex.

quotes.quote: Snail1 binds to the E-box element in

the Crumbs3 promoter and inhibits Crumbs3 expression, leading to disassembly of the 
Crumbs complex [88]. However, Snail1 expression does not affect the Par complex, another 
important polarity complex [88].

experiment.system: epithelial cells
experiment.perturbation: Snail1 expression
experiment.measurement: Crumbs3 promoter binding/expression and polarity complex assembly

text: Snail1 expression decreases expression of cytokeratin 17, 18, 19 and 20, with cytokeratins 17 and 18 identified as direct targets of Snail1 by chromatin immunoprecipitation.

quotes.quote:
Snail1 expression also results in decreased expression of a 
subset of cytokeratins, i.e. cytokeratin 17, 18, 19 and 20, thus affecting the epithelial 
cytoskeletal organization. Cytokeratins 17 and 18 have been identified as direct targets of 
Snail1 by chromatin immunoprecipitation [11, 84, 89].

experiment.system: epithelial cells
experiment.perturbation: Snail1 expression
experiment.measurement: cytokeratin expression and chromatin immunoprecipitation

text: Through direct repression of HNF-1β transcription Snail1 suppresses cadherin-16 expression and induces EMT in cell culture, and in hepatocytes Snail1 represses HNF-4α resulting in loss of epithelial markers and expression of mesenchymal proteins.

quotes.quote:
Through direct repression of HNF-1β transcription, 
Snail1 suppresses cadherin-16 expression and induces EMT in cell culture, reminiscent of 
the development of kidney fibrosis in vivo [91, 92]. In hepatocytes, Snail1 represses another 
HNF transcription factor, HNF-4α, resulting in loss of epithelial markers and expression of 
mesenchymal proteins [93].

experiment.system: kidney epithelial cells and hepatocytes in culture
experiment.perturbation: Snail1 expression
experiment.measurement: HNF-1β/HNF-4α and cadherin-16 expression, epithelial/mesenchymal markers

text: TGF-β induces ZEB expression during EMT indirectly, mediated in part by Ets-1, and ZEB proteins interact with Smad3 and directly repress epithelial marker genes, possibly by recruiting the co-repressor CTBP; ZEB1 is also induced by TGF-β during smooth muscle differentiation where it synergizes with Smad3 and SRF to transactivate smooth muscle α-actin and smooth muscle myosin heavy chain genes.

quotes.quote:
TGF-β signaling induces the expression of ZEB proteins during EMT through an indirect 
mechanism mediated in part by Ets-1 [21]. ZEB proteins then interact with Smad3 and 
directly repress the expression of epithelial marker genes, possibly by recruiting the co-
repressor CTBP [97, 98]. ZEB1 is also induced by TGF-β during smooth muscle 
differentiation, in which it synergistically interacts with Smad3 and SRF to transactivate the 
genes encoding smooth muscle α-actin and smooth muscle myosin heavy chain [99].

experiment.system: epithelial cells undergoing EMT and smooth muscle differentiation models
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β treatment
experiment.measurement: ZEB expression, Smad3 interaction, target gene transcription

text: The miR-200 family and miR-205 post-transcriptionally repress ZEB factors and are dramatically downregulated in cells undergoing EMT, and forced expression of the miR-200 family is sufficient to block TGF-β-induced EMT.

quotes.quote:
The expression of ZEB factors is also post-transcriptionally repressed by 
microRNAs, miR-200 family and miR-205 [100-102]. This group of microRNAs is 
dramatically downregulated in cells undergoing EMT, allowing expression of ZEB 
transcription factors. Thus, forced expression of miR-200 family is sufficient to block TGF-
β-induced EMT [100-102].

experiment.system: epithelial cells undergoing EMT
experiment.perturbation: forced miR-200 family expression; TGF-β treatment
experiment.measurement: microRNA and ZEB expression, EMT induction

text: ZEB proteins directly repress E-cadherin independently of Snail transcription factors in mouse mammary epithelial cells; ZEB2 directly represses claudin-4 and ZO-3 and plakophilin-2, and induces vimentin, N-cadherin and matrix metalloproteinase-2, while ZEB1 directly represses Crumbs3 and mucin-1, with ZEB1 depletion restoring Crumbs3 and PATJ expression.

quotes.quote:
ZEB proteins directly repress E-cadherin 
expression independently of the Snail transcription factors in mouse mammary epithelial 
cells [21, 106].

ZEB2 directly represses the expression of the tight junction proteins claudin-4 and 
ZO-3 [107]. ZEB2 also suppresses the expression of the desmosome protein plakophilin-2 
[107] and induces the expression of the mesenchymal proteins vimentin [108], N-cadherin 
[107] and matrix metalloproteinase-2 [95]

depletion of ZEB1 restores the expression of Crumbs3 and PATJ, 
major components of the Crumbs3 polarity complex [109, 110]. ZEB1 also directly 
represses the expression of mucin-1 [89].

experiment.system: mouse mammary and other epithelial cells
experiment.perturbation: ZEB1/ZEB2 expression or depletion
experiment.measurement: epithelial junction, polarity and mesenchymal gene expression

text: Ectopic expression of E12 or E47 represses E-cadherin and plakoglobin expression, induces vimentin and fibronectin expression, and promotes migration and invasion, with E-cadherin repression antagonized by Id factors that interact with E2A proteins.

quotes.quote:
Ectopic expression of E12 or E47 represses E-cadherin and plakoglobin 
expression, induces vimentin and fibronectin expression, and promotes migration and 
invasion [80, 112, 113].

their repression 
of E-cadherin transcription can be antagonized by Id factors, which interact with E2A 
proteins [113].

experiment.system: epithelial cells in culture
experiment.perturbation: ectopic E12/E47 expression; Id factor expression
experiment.measurement: epithelial/mesenchymal marker expression, migration and invasion

text: TGF-β represses Id1, Id2 and Id3 expression—for Id1 through rapid ATF3 induction and binding of an ATF3/Smad3/Smad4 complex to the Id1 promoter—and ectopic Id2 or Id3 expression dose-dependently blocks TGF-β-induced E-cadherin repression, inhibits TGF-β-induced ZO-1 delocalization and represses TGF-β-induced smooth muscle actin expression.

quotes.quote:
The expression of Id1, Id2 and Id3 is repressed in response to TGF-β, which 
in the case of Id1, occurs through the rapid activation of expression of the transcription 
repressor ATF3 by TGF-β and the subsequent binding of an ATF3/Smad3/Smad4 complex 
to the Id1 promoter [114, 115]. Consequently, loss of Id protein expression correlates with a 
decrease in E-cadherin expression, and ectopic expression of Id2 or Id3 dose-dependently 
blocks TGF-β-induced repression of E-cadherin expression, inhibits TGF-β-induced ZO-1 
delocalization and represses TGF-β-induced smooth muscle actin expression [113, 114].

experiment.system: epithelial cells
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β treatment; ectopic Id2/Id3 expression
experiment.measurement: Id expression, Id1 promoter occupancy, E-cadherin expression, ZO-1 localization, smooth muscle actin expression

text: Ectopic expression of Twist1 or Twist2 decreases E-cadherin, occludin and claudin-7 expression, increases vimentin and N-cadherin expression, and enhances migration and invasion, and both synergize with HRas to induce a full EMT.

quotes.quote:
Ectopic expression of Twist1 or Twist2 decreases E-
cadherin, occludin and claudin-7 expression, increases vimentin and N-cadherin expression, 
and enhances migration and invasion [9, 10]. In addition, Twist1 and Twist2 both synergize 
with HRas to induce a full EMT [10].

experiment.system: epithelial cells in culture
experiment.perturbation: ectopic Twist1/Twist2 expression, with or without HRas
experiment.measurement: epithelial/mesenchymal marker expression, migration and invasion

text: TGF-β induces a drastic increase in HMGA2 expression through a Smad3/Smad4-dependent mechanism, and ectopic HMGA2 expression is able to induce the expression of Snail1/2 and Twist1.

quotes.quote:
TGF-β induces a drastic increase in HMGA2 expression through a Smad3/
Smad4-dependent mechanism, and ectopic HMGA2 expression is able to induce the 
expression of Snail1/2 and Twist1 [120].

experiment.system: epithelial cells undergoing EMT
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β treatment; ectopic HMGA2 expression
experiment.measurement: HMGA2, Snail1/2 and Twist1 expression

text: In response to TGF-β, ShcA associates with and is phosphorylated on tyrosine by TβRI, providing a docking site for Grb2 and Sos and allowing the Shc/Grb2/Sos complex to initiate Ras activation upstream of the Raf-MEK1/2-Erk cascade; separately, integrin αvβ3 interaction with TβRII results in Src-mediated tyrosine phosphorylation of TβRII and association of Shc and Grb2 with TβRII.

quotes.quote:
In 
response to TGF-β, ShcA associates with and is phosphorylated on tyrosine by TβRI, thus 
offering a docking site for the recruitment of Grb2 and Sos, and allowing the Shc/Grb2/Sos 
complex to initiate Ras activation upstream from the kinase cascade [126]. In addition to this 
role of Shc, the interaction of the integrin αvβ3 with TβRII was shown to result in tyrosine 
phosphorylation of TβRII by Src, leading in turn to association of Shc and Grb2 with the 
TβRII receptor [127].

experiment.system: cultured cells with TGF-β receptors
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β stimulation
experiment.measurement: ShcA/TβRII tyrosine phosphorylation and adaptor complex association, Ras-Erk activation

text: Increased Ras-Erk MAP kinase signaling, from growth factor stimulation or mutant Ras expression, enhances TGF-β-induced EMT with morphological changes and E-cadherin downregulation, while a chemical MEK1/2 inhibitor inhibits TGF-β-induced EMT; MEK/Erk activation enhances TGF-β transcription responses, downregulating E-cadherin and upregulating N-cadherin and matrix metalloproteinase expression.

quotes.quote:
Increased Ras-Erk MAP kinase signaling, e.g. in 
response to growth factor stimulation or due to expression of mutant Ras, enhances TGF-β-
induced EMT, as apparent by the morphological changes and downregulation of E-cadherin 
expression [124, 128-130]. Consistent with this cooperation, blocking the kinase function of 
MEK1/2 using a chemical inhibitor, thus resulting in inactivation of the Erk1/2 MAP
kinases, inhibits TGF-β-induced EMT [131].

activation of MEK/Erk MAP kinase signaling enhances TGF-β-
induced transcription responses, leading to down-regulation of E-cadherin, upregulation of 
N-cadherin and upregulation of matrix metalloproteinase expression [128, 130].

experiment.system: epithelial cells in culture
experiment.perturbation: growth factor stimulation or mutant Ras expression; chemical MEK1/2 inhibitor; TGF-β treatment
experiment.measurement: EMT morphology and E-cadherin/N-cadherin/MMP expression

text: Oncogenic Ras hyperactivity results in enhanced TGF-β signaling with increased autocrine TGF-β secretion, Smad phosphorylation and nuclear accumulation, and TGF-β-specific transcriptional responses; in vivo, ectopic expression of activated Smad2 enhances the metastatic potential of cells expressing activated Ras, and Erk5 activation stabilizes Snail1 expression.

quotes.quote:
oncogenic Ras hyperactivity was shown 
to result in enhanced TGF-β signaling concomitant with increased autocrine TGF-β 
secretion, phosphorylation and nuclear accumulation of Smads, and TGF-β-specific 
transcriptional responses [124]. In vivo, ectopic expression of an activated version of Smad2 
enhances the metastatic potential of cells expressing activated Ras [57]. Additionally, 
activation of Erk5 MAP kinase, another member of Erk family, which can also occur in 
response to TGF-β, stabilizes Snail1 expression [133].

experiment.system: epithelial/tumor cells in culture and in vivo metastasis models
experiment.perturbation: oncogenic Ras expression; ectopic activated Smad2; Erk5 activation
experiment.measurement: TGF-β secretion, Smad phosphorylation/localization, transcriptional responses, metastatic potential, Snail1 stability

text: TGF-β induces phosphorylation of p38 MAP kinase, and a chemical p38 inhibitor prevents TGF-β-induced EMT in mammary epithelial cells without affecting Smad phosphorylation.

quotes.quote:
TGF-β was shown to 
induce phosphorylation of p38 MAP kinase [134, 135]. The observation that a chemical 
inhibitor of p38 MAP kinase prevents TGF-β-induced EMT in mammary epithelial cells 
without affecting Smad phosphorylation suggests a role of p38 MAP kinase in TGF-β-
induced EMT [134, 135].

experiment.system: mammary epithelial cells
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β treatment with chemical p38 MAP kinase inhibitor
experiment.measurement: p38 and Smad phosphorylation, EMT induction

text: Epithelial cells deficient in JNK1 and keratinocytes transfected with JNK antisense oligonucleotides were unable to undergo EMT upon TGF-β treatment, and a chemical JNK inhibitor blocks the TGF-β-induced increase in fibronectin, vimentin and α-smooth muscle actin expression and decrease in E-cadherin expression during EMT.

quotes.quote:
epithelial cells 
deficient in JNK1 expression, and keratinocytes transfected with antisense oligonucleotides 
targeting JNK, were unable to undergo EMT upon TGF-β treatment [137, 138]. Moreover, a 
chemical inhibitor of JNK blocks the TGF-β-induced increase in fibronectin, vimentin and 
α-smooth muscle actin expression, and decrease in E-cadherin expression observed during 
EMT [137, 139].

experiment.system: epithelial cells and keratinocytes
experiment.perturbation: JNK1 deficiency, JNK antisense oligonucleotides, chemical JNK inhibitor plus TGF-β
experiment.measurement: EMT induction and marker expression

text: TGF-β induces phosphorylation of p38 MAP kinase and of upstream kinases MKK3, MKK6 and TAK1; TAK1 is required for JNK MAPK activation in response to TGF-β through MKK4, and TAK1 activation requires interaction of the ubiquitin ligase TRAF6 with the TGF-β receptor complex followed by direct activation of TAK1 by TRAF6.

quotes.quote:
TGF-β has been 
shown to induce phosphorylation of p38 MAP kinase, as well as upstream kinases that 
mediate p38 activation, i.e. MKK3 and MKK6, and TAK1, which can activate MKK3 and 
MKK6 [137, 138]. In addition, TAK1 has been shown to be required for JNK MAPK 
activation in response to TGF-β signaling through activation of MKK4 [141, 142]. The 
activation of TAK1 was reported to require the interaction of the ubiquitin ligase TRAF6

with the TGF-β receptor complex followed by a consequent direct activation of TAK1 by 
TRAF6 [143, 144].

experiment.system: cultured cells responsive to TGF-β
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β stimulation; TAK1/TRAF6 manipulation
experiment.measurement: kinase phosphorylation and JNK/p38 activation

text: During embryonic chick heart development RhoA is necessary for normal EMT in the atrioventricular canal and antibodies against TGF-β lead to a dramatic reduction of RhoA mRNA; TGF-β induces increased levels of active GTP-RhoA, which in lens epithelial cells occurs biphasically within the first 30 minutes and then after 1 to 2 days.

quotes.quote:
During embryonic chick heart development, RhoA is necessary for normal EMT in 
the atrioventricular canal and antibodies against TGF-β lead to a dramatic reduction of 
RhoA mRNA [145]. TGF-β induces increased levels of active GTP-RhoA, which in lens 
epithelial cells occurs in a biphasic manner within the first 30 minutes and then after 1 to 2 
days [146].

experiment.system: embryonic chick heart atrioventricular canal; lens epithelial cells
experiment.perturbation: anti-TGF-β antibodies; TGF-β treatment
experiment.measurement: RhoA mRNA levels, active GTP-RhoA levels, EMT

text: Downregulation of LIM kinase expression using siRNA inhibits TGF-β-induced actin reorganization in fibroblasts, and chemical inhibition of ROCK or antisense downregulation of Rho mRNA inhibits TGF-β-induced actin reorganization and α-smooth muscle actin expression accompanying EMT without affecting Smad activation.

quotes.quote:
Downregulation of LIM kinase expression using siRNA 
inhibits TGF-β-induced actin reorganization in fibroblasts [148]. Chemical inhibition of 
ROCK activity or downregulating Rho mRNA levels using antisense oligonucleotides 
results in inhibition of TGF-β-induced actin reorganization and α-smooth muscle actin 
expression that accompany EMT, without affecting Smad activation [145, 146, 149].

experiment.system: fibroblasts and epithelial cells
experiment.perturbation: LIM kinase siRNA, ROCK chemical inhibitor, Rho antisense oligonucleotides with TGF-β
experiment.measurement: actin reorganization, α-smooth muscle actin expression, Smad activation

text: At tight junctions Par6 interacts with TβRI and TGF-β induces association of TβRII with the TβRI/Par6 complex, permitting TβRII to phosphorylate Par6 at a defined serine, which recruits the E3 ubiquitin ligase Smurf1, resulting in enhanced RhoA ubiquitination and degradation at tight junctions.

quotes.quote:
Par6 was found to interact with TβRI 
and TGF-β induces the association of TβRII with the TβRI/Par6 complex, permitting TβRII 
to phosphorylate Par6 at a defined serine [150]. This event in turn recruits the E3 ubiquitin 
ligase Smurf1, resulting in enhanced RhoA ubiquitination by Smurf1 and degradation at 
tight junctions.

experiment.system: epithelial cell tight junctions
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β stimulation
experiment.measurement: receptor/Par6 complex association, Par6 serine phosphorylation, RhoA ubiquitination and degradation

text: TGF-β rapidly activates PI3 kinase leading to Akt activation in diverse cell systems, the regulatory subunit of PI3 kinase interacts with TβRII and TβRI, and PI3 kinase activity increases upon TGF-β stimulation.

quotes.quote:
TGF-β has 
been shown to rapidly activate PI3 kinase, leading to activation of the Akt kinase, in diverse 
cell systems [151-156]. Consistent with this observation, the regulatory subunit of PI3 
kinase was found to interact with the TβRII and TβRI receptors, and the PI3 kinase activity 
increases upon TGF-β stimulation [157].

experiment.system: diverse cultured cell systems
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β stimulation
experiment.measurement: PI3 kinase activity, Akt activation, receptor interaction

text: Inhibitors of PI3 kinase and Akt, or a dominant negative form of Akt, inhibit TGF-β-induced morphological transition, α-smooth muscle actin expression and E-cadherin downregulation.

quotes.quote:
Inhibitors of 
PI3 kinase and Akt, or a dominant negative form of Akt, were found to inhibit TGF-β-
induced morphological transition, α-smooth muscle actin expression and E-cadherin down-
regulation [151, 159].

experiment.system: epithelial cells undergoing TGF-β-induced EMT
experiment.perturbation: PI3 kinase/Akt inhibitors or dominant negative Akt
experiment.measurement: cell morphology, α-smooth muscle actin and E-cadherin expression

text: In palate medial-edge epithelial cells, Smad2 and Smad4 form a complex with LEF1 at the E-cadherin promoter resulting in transcriptional repression, and Smad4 and LEF1 are also required for upregulation of vimentin and fibronectin and for the acquisition of migratory behavior.

quotes.quote: it has been reported that Smad2 and Smad4 form a complex with LEF1 at the E-

cadherin promoter, resulting in transcriptional repression in palate medial-edge epithelial 
cells. Smad4 and LEF1 are also required for the upregulation of mesenchymal markers 
vimentin and fibronectin, as well as for the acquisition of migratory behavior that 
characterizes cells that have undergone EMT [163].

experiment.system: palate medial-edge epithelial cells
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β/Smad and LEF1 manipulation
experiment.measurement: E-cadherin promoter complex and transcription, vimentin/fibronectin expression, migration

text: Mouse embryos lacking β-catenin expression showed defective septum formation, and β-catenin deficient endocardial cells showed dramatically reduced actin stress fiber formation and failed to invade ex vivo.

quotes.quote:
Mouse embryos that lack β-catenin 
expression showed defective septum formation, suggesting an impaired EMT process. In 
fact, β-catenin deficient endocardial cells showed dramatically reduced actin stress fiber 
formation and failed to invade ex vivo [162].

experiment.system: mouse embryonic heart and endocardial cells ex vivo
experiment.perturbation: β-catenin deletion
experiment.measurement: septum formation, actin stress fiber formation, invasion

text: In epithelial cells Hey1, a Notch target gene, is required for TGF-β-induced EMT and migration, and TGF-β induces biphasic Hey1 expression: an immediate-early Smad3-dependent, Notch-independent induction and a delayed Notch-dependent induction mediated by Smad3 and Erk-induced Jagged1 expression.

quotes.quote:
In epithelial cells, Hey1, a well-known target gene of 
Notch signaling, was found to be required for TGF-β-induced EMT and migration. TGF-β 
induces a biphasic expression of Hey1: the immediate-early induction is Smad3-dependent 
and Notch-independent, whereas the delayed induction is Notch-dependent, and mediated by 
Smad3 and Erk-induced Jagged1 expression [164].

experiment.system: epithelial cells
experiment.perturbation: TGF-β treatment with Notch/Smad3 pathway manipulation
experiment.measurement: Hey1 expression kinetics, EMT and migration

text: Activation of Notch1 induces Snail1 expression in mice and Snail2 expression in chicks, leading to repression of VE-cadherin and promotion of endocardial cell migration and invasion into the cardiac jelly, while mutations in Notch1 or RBPJK cause reduction in TGF-β2 and Snail1 expression accompanied by persistent VE-cadherin expression.

quotes.quote:
Activation of Notch1 was shown to induce Snail1 
expression in mice and Snail2 expression in chicks, which then lead to repression of VE-
cadherin expression and promote endocardial cell migration and invasion into the cardiac 
jelly. Mutations in the Notch pathway components Notch1 or RBPJK cause reduction in 
TGF-β2 and Snail1 expression, accompanied by persistent VE-cadherin expression [165, 
166].

experiment.system: mouse and chick endocardial cushion development
experiment.perturbation: Notch1 activation; Notch1 or RBPJK mutation
experiment.measurement: Snail1/Snail2, TGF-β2 and VE-cadherin expression, endocardial cell migration and invasion

text: Core PCP proteins segregate into an Fz-Fmi-Dsh-Dgo complex on one side of the cell and a Vang-Fmi-Pk complex on the other, with intracellular antagonism (Pk binds Dsh and antagonizes its Fz-mediated membrane recruitment, and Dgo binding to Dsh competes with Pk binding).

quotes.quote:
these core PCP signaling molecules interact with each other both across cell 
membranes and intracellularly to segregate two complexes to opposing sides of each cell, 
leading to the formation of an Fz-Fmi-Dsh-Dgo complex on one side and a Vang-Fmi-Pk 
complex on the other

Pk can bind Dsh and antagonize its 
Fz-mediated membrane recruitment (Tree et al. 2002)

experiment.system: Drosophila epithelial cells (wing/eye) and vertebrate PCP models (mouse inner ear, skin, limb; zebrafish presomitic mesoderm)
experiment.perturbation: genetic loss/gain of function of core PCP genes and biochemical binding assays
experiment.measurement: subcellular localization of core PCP proteins and protein-protein binding/competition

text: fz mutant clones reorient adjacent wild-type cells toward the clone whereas Vang mutant clones reorient neighbors away, and fz, Vang double mutant clones reorient hairs toward the clone like single fz clones, indicating Fz sends and Vang receives the polarity signal.

quotes.quote:
Not only do mutant 
clones lacking Fz show PCP defects, they also reorient adjacent cells toward the clone, 
whereas cells lacking Vang reorient neighboring cells to point away

fz, Vang double mutant clones reorient hairs to point 
toward the clone, very much like single fz mutant clones (Wu & Mlodzik 2008)

experiment.system: Drosophila adult cuticle (wing hairs)
experiment.perturbation: mosaic mutant clones of fz, Vang, and fz Vang double mutants
experiment.measurement: orientation of hairs in mutant clones and neighboring wild-type cells

text: dsh, pk, and dgo null mutations affect PCP only within mutant clones and not in adjacent cells, indicating these factors act cell-autonomously.

quotes.quote:
dsh, pk, 
and dgo null mutations appear to affect PCP only within mutant clones and not within 
adjacent cells

experiment.system: Drosophila epithelia
experiment.perturbation: null mutant clones of dsh, pk, dgo
experiment.measurement: PCP/hair orientation inside clones versus in neighboring cells

text: Loss of inturned does not affect localization of core PCP gene products, although Inturned itself becomes localized to proximal cell membranes, placing it downstream of the core module.

quotes.quote:
Inturned, for example, is initially localized in a uniform apical ring in wing cells and 
subsequently becomes localized exclusively to proximal cell membranes, but the loss of 
inturned does not affect the localization of the core PCP gene products (Adler et al. 2004)

experiment.system: Drosophila wing cells
experiment.perturbation: loss of inturned
experiment.measurement: subcellular localization of Inturned and of core PCP proteins

text: Furrowed, a Drosophila selectin, is required to stabilize Fz in plasma membrane complexes, promotes homophilic adhesion, and mediates intercellular Fz-Vang binding; PCP defects in fw, fmi double mutants are not more severe than in fz null flies.

quotes.quote:
required to stabilize Fz in plasma membrane complexes and also to promote homophilic cell 
adhesion (Chin & Mlodzik 2013, Usui et al. 1999). Fw also mediates intercellular binding/
interactions between Fz and Vang

the PCP defects in fw, fmi 
double mutants are not more severe than those in fz null flies

experiment.system: Drosophila wing, eye, and thorax
experiment.perturbation: fw and fmi loss-of-function single and double mutants; coimmunoprecipitation with Fz
experiment.measurement: PCP phenotype severity, Fz membrane localization, protein association

text: VhaPRR coimmunoprecipitates with both Fz and Fmi but directly associates only with Fmi, and is generally required for trafficking, also affecting Fz2, Notch, and E-cad membrane levels.

quotes.quote:
VhaPRR can be coimmunoprecipitated with 
both Fz and Fmi but only directly physically associates with Fmi (Hermle et al. 2013).

VhaPRR appears to be generally required for trafficking, as it also affects Fz2 (canonical 
Wingless/Wg signaling), Notch, and E-cad levels in the membrane

experiment.system: Drosophila eye and wing epithelia
experiment.perturbation: VhaPRR loss of function; coimmunoprecipitation/binding assays
experiment.measurement: protein association with Fz and Fmi; membrane levels of Fz2, Notch, E-cad

text: Misexpression of Wg and dWnt4 in the Drosophila wing alters Fz/PCP core complex protein localization and polarity axis orientation largely orthogonal to the Wnt expression domain, and temperature-sensitive wg alleles combined with dWnt4 null mutants show the two Wnts are redundantly required for PCP establishment.

quotes.quote:
GOF 
experiments with Wg and dWnt4 in the Drosophila wing show that these proteins serve an 
instructive role, as their misexpression alters Fz/PCP core complex protein localization and 
polarity axis orientation, largely orthogonal to the expression domain of the Wnts

requiring the use of temperature-sensitive wg alleles combined with dWnt4 
null mutants (Wu et al. 2013)

experiment.system: Drosophila wing imaginal disc
experiment.perturbation: misexpression (GOF) of Wg and dWnt4; temperature-sensitive wg alleles combined with dWnt4 null mutants
experiment.measurement: core PCP protein localization and polarity axis orientation

text: Wg and Wnt4 antagonize Fz-Vang binding across cell membranes, and co-overexpression of Fz and Wnt4 lets them buffer each other's effects in vivo.

quotes.quote:
they antagonize Fz-Vang binding across cell membranes. Co-
overexpression of Fz and Wnt4 allows them to buffer each other’s effects in vivo, 
suggesting that Wnts inhibit Fz-Vang interaction (Wu et al. 2013)

experiment.system: Drosophila wing
experiment.perturbation: co-overexpression of Fz and Wnt4
experiment.measurement: intercellular Fz-Vang interaction and PCP phenotype

text: Asymmetrical core PCP protein localization is conserved across vertebrate tissues: Pk and Dvl at anterior and posterior edges of zebrafish presomitic cells, Pk2/Vangl1/Vangl2 anterior and Dvl2/Dvl3 posterior in node cells, Vangl2 proximal in limb chondrocytes, Vangl2 anterior and Fzd6 posterior in mouse epidermis, and Vangl1/Vangl2/Pk1 distal versus Fzd3/Dvl1/Dvl3 proximal in airway epithelium.

quotes.quote:
Pk and Dvl proteins in presomitic zebrafish cells undergoing CE are localized to the anterior and posterior cell edges, 
respectively (Yin et al. 2008)

localization of Pk2, Vangl1, and Vangl2 (Antic et al. 2010, Song et al. 2010) and posterior 
localization of Dvl2 and Dvl3 in node cells

In the mouse epidermis, Vangl2 and Fzd6 
proteins are asymmetrically localized to the anterior and posterior sides of the cells, 
respectively

In the airway epithelial cells, Vangl1, 
Vangl2, and Pk1 are localized distally, whereas Fzd3, Dvl1, and Dvl3 are localized 
proximally

experiment.system: zebrafish presomitic mesoderm, mouse node, limb chondrocytes, epidermis, and airway epithelium
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: immunolocalization of core PCP proteins along tissue axes

text: In inner ear sensory epithelium, Vangl1 and Vangl2 are not colocalized with Fzd in the same hair cells but are asymmetrically localized to the lateral side of juxtaposed supporting cells.

quotes.quote: Instead, Vangl1 and Vangl2 are asymmetrically localized to the lateral side of juxtaposed supporting cells (Ezan & Montcouquiol 2013)

experiment.system: mouse organ of Corti inner ear sensory epithelium
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: immunolocalization of Vangl1/Vangl2 relative to Fzd in hair cells and supporting cells

text: Domineering nonautonomy is conserved in vertebrates: wild-type cells transplanted into trilobite/Vangl2 mutant zebrafish embryos fail to undergo CE, ciliary orientation is reversed in cells anterior to Vangl2-overexpressing tissue, and wild-type hair follicle explants remain unpolarized when flanked by a homozygous Vangl2 mutant epidermis.

quotes.quote:
wild-type cells transplanted into trilobite (tri )/Vangl2 mutant embryos fail to 
undergo CE in zebrafish ( Jessen et al. 2002), and ciliary orientation is reversed in cells 
anterior to tissues that overexpress Vangl2 (Mitchell et al. 2009)

Wild-type hair follicle explants can be repolarized by a wild-type epidermis, 
but they remain unpolarized when flanked by a homozygous Vangl2 mutant epidermis.

experiment.system: zebrafish embryos and mouse skin explants
experiment.perturbation: transplantation of wild-type cells into Vangl2 mutant hosts; Vangl2 overexpression; hair follicle explant grafting onto wild-type or Vangl2 mutant epidermis
experiment.measurement: convergent extension behavior, ciliary orientation, hair follicle polarization

text: In zebrafish the Vangl2 mutant tri, the Wnt5b mutant pipetail, and the Wnt11 mutant silberblick all exhibit a shortened and broadened anterior-posterior body axis with defective convergent extension movements.

quotes.quote:
In zebrafish, the Vangl2 
mutant tri exhibits a shortened and broadened A-P axis, owing to defects in CE movements. 
The Wnt5b mutant pipetail ( ppt) and the Wnt11 mutant silberblick (slb) also exhibit a 
broadened and shortened A-P body axis with defective CE movement

experiment.system: zebrafish embryos
experiment.perturbation: tri/Vangl2, pipetail/Wnt5b, and silberblick/Wnt11 mutations
experiment.measurement: A-P body axis dimensions and convergent extension movements

text: Asymmetrical Vangl2 localization is detected in newly formed chondrocytes along the proximal-distal limb axis but not in interdigital mesenchyme or early limb mesenchyme cells prior to cartilage formation.

quotes.quote:
the identification of asymmetrical Vangl2 localization in newly formed chondrocytes along the 
Pr–Di limb axis (Figure 4) (Gao et al. 2011). Asymmetrical Vangl2 localization is not 
detected in interdigital mesenchyme or in early limb mesenchyme cells prior to cartilage 
formation.

experiment.system: developing mouse limb bud
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: Vangl2 immunolocalization in chondrocytes versus mesenchymal cells

text: Vangl2−/− and dominant-negative Loop-tail (Vangl2Lp) mutant mice have shortened limbs, and additional deletion of Vangl1 in the Vangl2 mutant background makes limb shortening even more severe.

quotes.quote:
in the Vangl2−/− and Vangl2 dominant negative Loop-tail mutant (Vangl2Lp), 
limbs are shortened (Gao et al. 2011, Song et al. 2010, Wang et al. 2011). If Vangl1, the 
second mammalian Vang homolog, is also deleted in the Vangl2 mutant background, the 
limb shortening defects are even more severe (Song et al. 2010).

experiment.system: mouse limb
experiment.perturbation: Vangl2 null, Vangl2Lp, and Vangl1/Vangl2 combined deletion
experiment.measurement: limb length/skeletal phenotype

text: Wnt5a and Ror2 null mouse mutants both lose Vangl2 asymmetrical localization and show a shorter and broader cartilage phenotype, and a Ror2−/−, Vangl2−/− double mutant phenocopies Wnt5a−/− in the limb with failure of digit outgrowth and long bone elongation.

quotes.quote:
both 
Wnt5a and Ror2 null mouse mutants exhibit loss of Vangl2 asymmetrical localization and a 
shorter and broader cartilage phenotype

a Ror2−/−, Vangl2−/−double mutant phenocopies Wnt5a−/− 
mutants in the limb, exhibiting failure of digit outgrowth and long bone elongation (Gao et 
al. 2011)

experiment.system: mouse developing limb
experiment.perturbation: Wnt5a, Ror2, Vangl2 null mutations, singly and in combination
experiment.measurement: Vangl2 asymmetrical localization, cartilage shape, digit outgrowth and long bone elongation

text: Wnt5a induces Ror2-Vangl2 receptor complex formation and phosphorylation of Vangl2 at two clusters of conserved Thr/Ser residues in a dose-dependent manner, with phosphorylation of more residues correlating with stronger Vangl2 activity in zebrafish assays.

quotes.quote:
Wnt5a induces Ror2-Vangl2 receptor 
complex formation

this receptor complex 
formation leads to the phosphorylation of Vangl2 at two clusters of conserved Thr/Ser 
residues (Gao et al. 2011). Vangl2 phosphorylation is induced by Wnt5a in a dose-
dependent manner and is functionally important

Phosphorylation of more Vangl2 
Thr/Ser residues correlates with stronger Vangl2 activity in zebrafish assays

experiment.system: mouse limb / cultured cells and zebrafish activity assays
experiment.perturbation: Wnt5a stimulation at varying doses; Vangl2 phospho-site variants
experiment.measurement: Ror2-Vangl2 complex formation, Vangl2 phosphorylation, Vangl2 activity in zebrafish

numbers.quantity: clusters of conserved Thr/Ser residues phosphorylated in Vangl2

text: More sensitive imaging revealed that PCP in Drosophila wings is already established in wing imaginal discs at late larval stages, rather than only at the mid-pupa stage as long thought.

quotes.quote:
in Drosophila wings, PCP was long thought to be 
established at the mid-pupa stage, but more sensitive imaging and detection methods have 
recently revealed that PCP is already established in wing imaginal discs at late larval stages

experiment.system: Drosophila wing imaginal disc
experiment.perturbation: observational, using more sensitive imaging and detection methods
experiment.measurement: timing of detectable core PCP protein asymmetry

text: Retrovirally expressed Vangl2 or dominant-negative Fzd7 in the chick growth plate affects the division plane of proliferative chondrocytes, and activating Wnt/PCP components promotes columnar organization of dissociated growth plate chondrocytes in vitro, with the best columns formed by a combination of Ror2, Fzd7, and Wnt5a.

quotes.quote:
retrovirally expressed Vangl2 or dominant-negative Fzd7 in the chick growth plate affects the division 
plane of proliferative chondrocytes

they can promote columnar organization of dissociated growth plate 
chondrocytes when they form cell pellets in vitro by activating Wnt/PCP pathway 
components. The best columns form with a combination of Ror2, Fzd7, and Wnt5a.

experiment.system: chick growth plate in vivo and dissociated growth plate chondrocyte pellets in vitro
experiment.perturbation: retroviral expression of Vangl2 or dominant-negative Fzd7; activation of Wnt/PCP components (Ror2, Fzd7, Wnt5a)
experiment.measurement: chondrocyte division plane and columnar organization

text: In early Wnt5a mutant limb buds prior to cartilage formation, distal mesenchymal cells still move toward the overlying ectoderm but at reduced velocity and efficiency compared with wild type, while their division orientation is normal; Wnt5a null mutants show no sign of planar polarity.

quotes.quote:
distal limb mesenchymal cells located adjacent to the apical ectodermal 
ridge (AER) still move toward the overlying ectoderm, albeit at reduced velocity and 
efficiency compared with those in the wild-type limb. In addition, the division orientation of 
these distal mutant cells is normal (Gros et al. 2010).

Wnt5a null mutants 
show no sign of planar polarity (Gao et al. 2011)

experiment.system: mouse early limb bud
experiment.perturbation: Wnt5a null mutation
experiment.measurement: cell movement velocity/efficiency toward ectoderm, division orientation, planar polarity readouts

text: Wnt5a is expressed in a distal-to-proximal gradient in the developing limb bud and is the only Wnt expressed in the limb mesenchyme; this expression is required for limb and cartilage elongation through a pathway independent of β-catenin activation.

quotes.quote:
Wnt5a is expressed in a distal-to-
proximal gradient in the developing limb bud and is the only Wnt expressed in the limb 
mesenchyme. This expression is required for limb and cartilage elongation through a 
pathway independent of β-catenin activation

experiment.system: developing mouse limb bud
experiment.perturbation: Wnt5a loss of function; expression analysis
experiment.measurement: Wnt5a expression pattern, limb and cartilage elongation, β-catenin dependence

text: Mammalian genomes contain nineteen different Wnt proteins and ten Fzd genes, with most cells expressing multiple Fzd genes; most mouse Fzd mutants show PCP defects less severe and more tissue specific than Vangl2 mutants, while Vangl proteins have just two family members and are dedicated to PCP.

quotes.quote: Nineteen different Wnt proteins exist in mammalian genomes

Most 
mouse Fzd mutants exhibit PCP defects that are less severe and tissue specific than in 
Vangl2 mutants (e.g., Yu et al. 2010, Wang et al. 2010). As 10 different Fzd genes exist in 
the mammalian genome, and most cells express multiple Fzd genes

Vangl proteins, 
which have fewer family members (just two) and are dedicated to PCP.

experiment.system: mouse genetics and mammalian genome analysis
experiment.perturbation: Fzd and Vangl2 mutant mice
experiment.measurement: gene family counts and severity/tissue specificity of PCP phenotypes

numbers.quantity: Fzd genes in the mammalian genome

text: Human mTORC1 purified by tandem gel filtration contains equimolar mTOR, raptor and mLST8 with substoichiometric PRAS40, and its kinase activity toward S6K1 is sensitive to FKBP12-rapamycin and Torin1.

quotes.quote:
Purified mTORC1 consists
of equimolar quantities of mTOR, raptor, and mLST8, and of PRAS40 at substoichiometric
level (Figure 1B and C). The kinase activity of purified mTORC1 towards S6K1 was
sensitive to FKBP12-rapamycin and Torin1, an ATP-competitive inhibitor of mTOR

experiment.system: human mTORC1 purified from a HEK-293T line stably expressing FLAG-tagged raptor
experiment.perturbation: FKBP12-rapamycin or Torin1 treatment in vitro
experiment.measurement: SDS-PAGE/silver and Coomassie staining, immunoblotting, and in vitro kinase assay on S6K1

text: Negative stain EM class averages from 10,080 particle images show mTORC1 as an elongated, rhomboid particle with a central stain-filled cavity, "feet-like" protrusions and two-fold symmetry, supporting an obligate dimer.

quotes.quote:
Projection averages
calculated from the classification of 10,080 particle images illustrated that mTORC1 has an
elongated, rhomboid shape with a central, stain-filled cavity and “feet-like” protrusions
emanating from both ends of the molecule (Figure 1E, inset, and Figure S1). The averages
displayed a two-fold symmetry.

experiment.system: purified human mTORC1
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: negative stain EM particle classification and projection averaging

text: The cryo-EM structure shows a central cavity, oval from one face and rectangular from the opposite face, with two troughs at the extensions linking the central core to the "feet-like" structures; the cavity size is ~40 Å × 28 Å.

quotes.quote:
The cryo-EM structure reveals a central cavity that has an oval shape when viewed from one
face, but a rectangular shape from the opposite face, with two troughs located at the
extensions linking the central core to the “feet-like” structures.

its size (~40 Å × 28 Å) is large enough to accommodate double-
stranded DNA (dsDNA)

experiment.system: cryo-EM density map of human mTORC1
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: inspection/measurement of the 3D reconstruction

text: Antibody labeling localizes mLST8 to the distal "foot-like" structures, PRAS40 to small tips in the mid-section of the central core, and the N-terminus of raptor to the corner of the core.

quotes.quote:
We discovered that mLST8 localizes to the distal “foot-like” structures,
PRAS40 to the small tips in the mid-section of the central core, and the N-terminus of raptor
to the corner of the core (Figure 2C).

experiment.system: purified human mTORC1
experiment.perturbation: antibody labeling of raptor (via FLAG tag), mLST8 and PRAS40
experiment.measurement: negative stain EM imaging with classification and image averaging

text: Docking of two raptor reconstructions and two beta-propeller models into the mTORC1 map indicates each mTOR contacts two raptor molecules — its N-terminus with the flat face of one raptor (interface I) and its C-terminus with the side of the second raptor (interface II) — while each mLST8 contacts only one mTOR.

quotes.quote: we deduced that the N-terminus of mTOR interacts with the flat face of one raptor

molecule (bottom left view in Figure 3C), forming interface I, whereas the C-terminus
interacts with the side of the second raptor molecule (top right view in Figure 3C), forming
interface II.

In
contrast, each mLST8 contacts only one mTOR within the complex.

experiment.system: cryo-EM map of human mTORC1
experiment.perturbation: observational (computational docking of raptor EM reconstruction and WD40 beta-propeller models, PDB 3EMH, guided by antibody labeling)
experiment.measurement: fitting/subtraction of docked densities to assign subunit boundaries

text: PRAS40 localizes close to raptor in the composite model, and some class averages of purified free raptor show an additional small density that may be bound PRAS40, supported by immunoblots detecting PRAS40 in the analyzed raptor fraction.

quotes.quote:
According to our data and composite model, PRAS40 localizes in close proximity to raptor
(asterisk in Figure 3D), which is in agreement with the known binding of PRAS40 to raptor

some class averages of purified raptor
showed an additional, small density, which may represent bound PRAS40 (indicated by red
arrow in Figures 3B and S3). This interpretation is supported by immunoblots that show
PRAS40 to be present in the analyzed raptor fraction (Figure 3A).

experiment.system: purified free raptor fraction and mTORC1 composite model
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: negative stain EM class averages and immunoblotting of gel filtration fraction

text: After a 15-minute incubation with GST-FKBP12 and 50 nM rapamycin, about 10% of mTORC1 particles showed one additional density assigned to FKBP12-rapamycin bound to the mTOR region opposite raptor; particles or averages with two extra densities were not observed.

quotes.quote:
we incubated
mTORC1 with N-terminal GST-tagged FKBP12 in the presence of 50 nM rapamycin for 15
minutes, and then visualized the particles by negative stain EM (Figure S4).

image classification
showed that about 10% of the particles featured an additional density, likely constituting
FKBP12-rapamycin, tethered to the region we assigned to mTOR and directly opposite of
raptor (Figure 4A). Interestingly, we did not observe individual particles or averages of
mTORC1 showing two extra densities

experiment.system: purified human mTORC1
experiment.perturbation: 15-minute incubation with GST-FKBP12 and 50 nM rapamycin
experiment.measurement: negative stain EM imaging and class-average analysis for extra density

numbers.quantity: fraction of particles with extra density

text: Extended incubation with FKBP12-rapamycin drastically reduced intact mTORC1 particles, with virtually none detectable after a one-hour incubation and only smaller fragments and undefined aggregates remaining, whereas Torin1 did not affect mTORC1 stability even after extended incubation.

quotes.quote:
extended incubations resulted in a drastic reduction in the total number of
intact mTORC1 particles. Many smaller fragments appeared in the background

After a one-hour incubation,
virtually no intact mTORC1 particles could be detected, and the sample contained only
smaller fragments, likely representing free mTOR or its subcomplexes, and undefined
aggregates (Figure 4B). In contrast, Torin1 did not affect mTORC1 stability even after
extended incubation (Figure 4C).

experiment.system: purified human mTORC1
experiment.perturbation: treatment with 50 nM rapamycin plus 0.02 μg/μl GST-FKBP12, or 100 nM Torin1, over a time course
experiment.measurement: negative stain EM imaging of particles at indicated time points

numbers.quantity: incubation time for loss of intact particles

text: In vitro, FKBP12-rapamycin inhibited mTORC1 phosphorylation of 4E-BP1 only after at least 60 minutes of drug incubation, while it rapidly blocked S6K1 phosphorylation and Torin1 quickly blocked phosphorylation of both substrates; in vivo experiments showed similar time-dependent rapamycin effects on endogenous 4E-BP1 but not S6K1.

quotes.quote:
FKBP12-
rapamycin significantly inhibited the in vitro phosphorylation of 4E-BP1 by mTORC1 only

after mTORC1 had been incubated with the drug for at least 60 minutes (Figure 4D). In
contrast, FKBP12-rapamycin rapidly blocked the phosphorylation of S6K1 by mTORC1,
and Torin1 quickly blocked the phosphorylation of both S6K1 and 4E-BP1. In close
agreement with in vitro kinase assays, in vivo experiments produced similar time-dependent
effects of rapamycin on endogenous 4E-BP1, but not S6K1 (Figure S4).

experiment.system: mTOR immunoprecipitates with 4E-BP1 or S6K1 as substrate, plus in vivo cell experiments
experiment.perturbation: time-course treatment with 100 nM rapamycin plus 0.02 μg/μl FKBP12 or 100 nM Torin1
experiment.measurement: in vitro kinase assay analyzed by immunoblotting for phosphorylation states

text: Raptor-free mTORC1 could not support 4E-BP1 phosphorylation but did phosphorylate full-length S6K1, and this S6K1 phosphorylation was still inhibited by FKBP12-rapamycin, indicating raptor is dispensable for rapamycin-sensitive S6K1 phosphorylation in vitro.

quotes.quote:
While raptor-free mTORC1, as predicted
(Hara et al., 2002), could not support 4E-BP1 phoshorylation, it was capable of
phosphorylating full-length S6K1 (Figure 4E). Furthermore, the phosphorylation of S6K1
by raptor-free mTORC1 was still inhibited by FKBP12-rapamycin. Thus, contrary to
previous assumptions, raptor is dispensable for mTORC1 to phosphorylate S6K1 in a
rapamycin-sensitive fashion in vitro.

experiment.system: mTOR immunoprecipitates prepared in lysis buffers containing 0.3% CHAPS or 1% Triton X-100 (raptor-free mTORC1)
experiment.perturbation: removal of raptor by detergent conditions, with or without FKBP12-rapamycin
experiment.measurement: in vitro kinase assay on 4E-BP1 or full-length S6K1 with immunoblotting for phosphorylation

text: Genetic inactivation of Warts, Hippo, Salvador, or Mats in Drosophila mosaic screens for tumor suppressor genes all produced a similar phenotype of robust tissue overgrowth.

quotes.quote:
The Hippo pathway was first defined in Drosophila by
genetic mosaic screens for tumor suppressor genes. Ge-
netic inactivation of genes, including Warts (Wts)

all resulted in a similar phenotype with robust
tissue overgrowth

experiment.system: Drosophila

to that of mer or ex mutations. However, when a kibra
mutation was combined with either a mer or ex muta-

overexpression increases Hpo, Wts, and Yki phosphory-
lation. In mammalian cells, overexpression of the kibra
homolog also potently induces Lats1/2 phosphorylation.

text: Mst1 and Mst2 double knockout in liver largely abolished YAP phosphorylation and induced an enlarged liver resembling YAP overexpression, but Mst1/2 ablation increased size in liver and stomach and not in kidney and limb.

duced an enlarged liver phenotype strikingly similar

ablation on organ size is more dramatic in some organs,
such as liver and stomach, than in others, such as kidney
and limb, which do not show an increase in size

phorylation in early embryos (S Oh et al. 2009).

fractionation
experiments showing that a Lats1/2-independent kinase

gous mice are prone to tumorigenesis (Lee et al. 2008).

fected

pending on cellular context

mic localization and inhibition of Yki

in 14–3–3

YAP–TEAD interaction blunts the regulation of the ma-
jority of YAP-dependent genes and largely diminishes the

transformation, and EMT (Zhao et al. 2008b). Conversely,
when TEAD was fused with VP16 transactivation domain,
it produced a gene expression profile similar to that ac-

sembles YAP knockout mice with decreased proliferation
and increased apoptosis

experiment.perturbation: TEAD knockdown, YAP–TEAD interaction disruption, TEAD-VP16 fusion, TEAD1/2 double knockout
experiment.measurement: gene expression profiles, proliferation, transformation, EMT, mouse phenotype

The
TEAD C-terminal domain forms a globular structure
with a b-sandwich fold surrounded by four a-helices on
one side. The YAP N-terminal domain wraps around
TEAD, forming extensive interactions.

Mutation of S94 in YAP or mu-
tation of Y406 in TEAD1 disrupts the YAP–TEAD inter-
action and abolishes YAP-induced gene expression (Zhao
et al. 2008b).

The three-dimensional structure
shows clearly that S94 directly forms a hydrogen bond
with TEAD1 Y406

creases the interaction with YAP, and mutation of the

tenance of pluripotency. It is noteworthy that TAZ binds
to Smad2/3 through the coiled-coil region instead of the

text: The hypervariable NH2-terminal extension contributes to receptor function: deletions in this region of the glucocorticoid receptor reduce activity by 10- to 20-fold; NTi glucocorticoid receptor mutants with an altered NH2-terminus bind hormone but are not biologically functional; an estrogen receptor with an NH2-terminal deletion regulates the vitellogenin promoter normally but is tenfold less active on the estrogen-responsive promoter p52; and progesterone receptor A and B forms differing by 128 amino acids at the NH2-terminus may have strikingly different regulatory capacities.

quotes.quote:
Deletions in this region of the glucocorti-
coid receptor reduce activity by 10- to 20-fold (48, 60).

NT
glucocorticoid receptors appear to
contain an altered NH2-terminus and, although they can bind
hormone, they are not biologically functional. Similarly, an estrogen
receptor with an NH2-terminal deletion is able to regulate the
vitellogenin promoter in a normal fashion, but is tenfold less active
in regulating the expression of the estrogen-responsive promoter
p52 (62). Finally, preliminary evidence with the progesterone
receptor indicates that the A and B forms, which differ by 128
amino acids at the NH2-terminus, may have strikingly different
capacities to regulate gene expression (63).

experiment.perturbation: NH2-terminal deletions and NTi mutations; comparison of PR A vs B forms
experiment.measurement: transcriptional activity of responsive promoters and hormone binding

reduced activity of NH2-terminally deleted ER on p52

text: Two thyroid hormone receptors have been identified, and their tissue-specific expression is supported by identification of an abundant neuronal form of the thyroid hormone receptor.

Current-
ly, two thyroid hormone receptors have been identified and there
may be more (37, 40, 41).

This notion has
already been confirmed by the identification of an abundant neuro-
nal form ofthe thyroid hormone receptor (40).

The protein product of v-erbA is a derivative of the thyroid
hormone receptor that has been proposed to promote leukemogene-
sis by acting as a thyroxin-independent transcription factor (37, 38).
By unknown means, changes in the ligand-binding domain of the

text: Exchanging the DNA-binding domain of the retinoic acid receptor for the comparable region of the glucocorticoid receptor generated a hybrid molecule that activates GRE-responsive promoters such as the MMTV-LTR in response to retinoic acid, enabling discovery of the retinoic acid receptor.

The discovery of the retinoic acid receptor (42, 43) was made
possible from the demonstration that conserved regions in the
receptors correspond to discrete functional domains. Thus, by
exchanging the DNA-binding domain of the retinoic receptor for
the comparable region from the glucocorticoid receptor, a hybrid
molecule was generated that activates GRE-responsive promoters
(such as the MMTV-LTR) in response to retinoic acid (Fig. 4) (42).

text: Retinoic acid was demonstrated to be the substance responsible for establishment of the anterior-posterior axis in the developing chick limb bud, and it induces differentiation of teratocarcinoma cells to parietal endoderm.

Recently, Thaller and Eichele (70) demon-
strated that retinoic acid is indeed the substance responsible for
establishment of the anterior-posterior axis in the developing chick
limb bud. The ability of retinoic acid to induce differentiation in
teratocarcinoma cells (71) to parietal endoderm suggests a role for it
in the earliest stages of embryonic development.

The identification of a transactivation function (Tj) in the NH2-
tenminus of the glucocorticoid receptor leads to an unexpected
conclusion (52). Since the NH2-terminus is not conserved among
different receptors, they each may achieve this function by distinct
means.

Likewise, the T, region is
acidic and so is the activation domain of another yeast regulator,
GCN4 (74).

which in turn enables DNA binding.

cotransfec-
tion of the retinoid X receptor-a (RXRa) expression plasmid

ence of clofibric acid

cotransfection of expression plasmids for both PPAR and

promoter

cotransfection of either PPAR or RXRa expression plasmids 
in the presence of clofibric acid or 9-cis retinoic acid, respec-
tively, resulted in induction of reporter expression

coexpression of PPAR and RXRa in the presence of 
both activators resulted in a synergistic increase in PPREr TK-
LUC expression

when mixed, polyclonal antiserum against 
RXRa efficiently co precipitated PPAR, indicating the formation

Neither PPAR nor 
RXRa alone bound efficiently to the radiolabelled PPRE (Fig. 
2b, lanes 2 and 3). Mixing the PPAR and RXRa proteins,

heterodimers formed between 
RXRa and the VDR, TR or RAR interacted most strongly with

PPAR-RXRa complex interacted with the DR-1 oligonucleo-
tide only. The RAR-RXRa complex also bound to DR-1

quotes.quote:
the 
PPAR-RXRa complex interacted strongly with other natural 
DR-I-like HREs found in the 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase, chicken 
ovalbumin and cellular retinol-binding protein type II promoters 
as well as the PPRE (Fig. 3b, lanes 1-4). In contrast, the 
PPAR-RXRa complex bound only weakly to the retinoic acid 
response element of the RAR-f3 promoter and the thyroid hor-
mone response element of the Moloney leukaemia virus long 
terminal repeat, and not at all to the osteopontin vitamin D
response element (Fig. 3b, lanes 6-8)

text: Rat liver nuclear extracts have PPRE binding activity that is markedly enhanced by addition of in vitro-synthesized PPAR, and anti-RXRa antiserum reduced complex formation to roughly the level of nuclear extract alone while forming a new slower-migrating complex, indicating RXRa is the main liver protein enhancing PPAR binding to the PPRE in vitro.

quotes.quote:
liver 
nuclear extracts have PPRE binding activity (lane 4), but

addition of in vitro-synthesized PPAR results in a marked en-
hancement in DNA binding (Fig. 4; compare lanes 4 and 5), 
demonstrating a cooperative activity in the extract. Addition of 
RXRa-specific antiserum to the reaction resulted in a reduction 
in complex formation to roughly the level in nuclear extracts 
alone, and the concomitant formation of a new complex with 
reduced electrophoretic mobility (Fig. 4, lane 6). These results

text: A 3.01 Å cryo-EM reconstruction of the human GR:Hsp90:FKBP52 complex reveals a fully closed Hsp90 dimer with a single GR and a single FKBP52 occupying the same side of Hsp90; only GRLBD was visible despite a multi-domain GR construct.

quotes.quote:
A 3.01 Å cryo-EM reconstruc-
tion of the GR:Hsp90:FKBP52 complex was obtained (Fig. 1a,b, Table 1 
and Extended Data Figs. 1f and 2a,b), revealing a fully closed Hsp90 
dimer (Hsp90A and Hsp90B) with a single GR and a single FKBP52, both 
occupying the same side of Hsp90

Despite 
using a multi-domain GR construct, only GRLBD was visible on the map.

experiment.system: Human GR DBD–LBD (residues 418–777, F602S) chaperone cycle reconstituted in vitro with Hsp70, Hsp40, Hop, Hsp90, p23 and FKBP52
experiment.perturbation: observational (complex stabilized with sodium molybdate, purified and lightly crosslinked)
experiment.measurement: single-particle cryo-EM reconstruction and atomic model building

text: FKBP52 engages closed Hsp90 at three interfaces: FKBP52 H7e binding the Hsp90A/Hsp90B CTD dimer interface (~1,109 Å2 BSA), Hsp90B MEEVD binding the FKBP52 TPR helical bundle (~779 Å2 BSA), and FKBP52 Helix5/6 binding Hsp90B CTD (~193 Å2 BSA), with the MEEVD peptide bound in an orientation opposite to the FKBP52:Hsp90MEEVD crystal structure.

quotes.quote:
FKBP52H7e (FKBP52387–424) binds in a hydrophobic cleft formed by 
Hsp90ACTD/Hsp90BCTD at the closed dimer interface (approximately 
1,109 Å2 BSA)

In interface 2, Hsp90BMEEVD binds in the FKBP52TPR helical bundle 
(approximately 779 Å2 BSA)

the 
MEEVD peptide binds in an opposite orientation relative to the 
FKBP52:Hsp90MEEVD crystal structure17

Interface 3 is composed of FKBP52Helix5/6 
in the TPR domain binding to Hsp90BCTD, stabilized by multiple 
hydrogen bonds (approximately 193 Å2 BSA)

experiment.perturbation: observational

text: Single point mutations at each of the three FKBP52:GR interfaces (S118A, Y161D, W259D) significantly reduce FKBP52-dependent GR potentiation in a yeast GR activation assay, as does deletion of FK1.

quotes.quote:
We also demonstrate 
that the FKBP52S118A mutation significantly reduces FKBP52-dependent 
GR potentiation in vivo (Fig. 2e)

we show that 
the FKBP52Y161D mutation significantly reduces FKBP52-dependent 
GR potentiation in vivo, demonstrating the importance of this 
interaction (Fig. 2e)

reduces FKBP52-dependent GR potentiation in vivo, demonstrating

text: GR is not bound in the FKBP52 PPIase active site and no GR prolines were found isomerized relative to other GR structures; docking of FK506 and rapamycin into the PPIase site shows the inhibitors would sterically block the FKBP52 FK1:GR interface.

While FKBP52FK1 is known to have PPIase enzymatic activity, GR 
is not bound in the PPIase active site and, accordingly, no GR prolines 
were found to have been isomerized compared to other GR struc-
tures (PDB IDs: 1M2Z (ref. 48) and 7KRJ (ref. 13)).

docking 
of PPIase inhibitors (FK506 and rapamycin) into the PPIase active 
site demonstrates that the inhibitors would sterically block the 
FKBP52FK1:GR interface

text: FKBP52 competes with p23 for the GR:Hsp90 complex without direct steric conflict: GR:Hsp90:FKBP52 classes showed no apparent p23 density despite high p23 concentration, GR:Hsp90:p23 complexes were seen at low abundance (~74,000 particles), and FKBP52 was found only with the rotated GR position.

quotes.quote:
Surprisingly, FKBP52 competes with p23 to bind the GR:Hsp90 complex, 
although there is no direct steric conflict between FKBP52 and p23 
binding (Fig. 3a). During 3D classification on the cryo-EM dataset, 
GR:Hsp90:p23 complexes were observed at low abundance (~74,000 
particles); however, the GR:Hsp90:FKBP52 complexes showed no 
apparent p23 density (Extended Data Fig. 2a,b), despite p23 being 
present at high concentration in the reconstitution.

FKBP52 was only found associated with the rotated GR position, while 
the GR position in the p23-containing classes was only consistent with 
the GR–maturation complex.

experiment.perturbation: observational (3D classification of particle populations)
experiment.measurement: presence/absence of p23 density and particle counts per class

Addition of FKBP52 to the GR chaperone cycle 
resulted in the enhancement of GR ligand binding above the already 
enhanced GR + chaperones control reaction at equilibrium (Fig. 3e)

addition of FKBP52 to the reaction fully rescued GR ligand binding in 
the p23Δhelix background (Fig. 3e)

Additionally, in the p23Δhelix background, FKBP52 potentiated ligand 
binding to a greater extent than in the wild-type p23 background.

versus chaperones + 52) 0.0002, P(chaperones + 52 versus chaperones with

p23Δhelix + 52) <0.0001.

Interestingly, FKBP52 also affected GR ligand 
binding independent of Hsp90, with addition of FKBP52 to GR resulting 
in enhanced ligand binding, probably due to an Hsp90-independent 
chaperoning effect15,52 (Extended Data Fig. 5d).

The addition of 
FKBP52 in place of p23 results in a small increase in ligand binding but

addition of molybdate to the reactions containing 
FKBP52 without p23 resulted in a full reactivation of ligand binding

able to functionally replace p23 if Hsp90NTD closure is stabilized.

value (Extended Data Fig. 8a), unlike FKBP52 which potentiated GR

that the residues at the FKBP52:GR interfaces are conserved across
