text: Biochemical fractionation of L929 cytosolic extracts through three independent purification routes achieved 8000- to 15,000-fold purification with 2 to 5% recovery of cGAMP-synthesizing activity, but silver staining revealed no clear copurifying protein bands.

quotes.quote:
We estimated that we achieved a range of 8000- to
15,000-fold purification and 2 to 5% recovery of
the activity from these routes of fractionation.

silver staining of the fractions
did not reveal clear protein bands that copurified
with the cGAS activity

experiment.system: Cytosolic extracts (S100) from murine fibrosarcoma cell line L929
experiment.perturbation: Three independent four-step chromatographic purification routes, one including biotinylated ISD affinity step
experiment.measurement: cGAMP activity assayed by IRF3 dimerization (native gel) in PFO-permeabilized Raw264.7 cells; silver staining of fractions

text: Label-free quantitative mass spectrometry of peak and adjacent fractions identified only three proteins copurifying with cGAS activity in all three purification routes, of which E330016A19 was covered by more than 24 unique peptides representing 41% coverage of the 507-amino acid protein.

quotes.quote:
only three proteins copuri-
fied in all three routes. All three were putative
uncharacterized proteins: E330016A19 (NCBI
accession number NP_775562), Arf-GAP with
dual PH domain–containing protein 2 (NP_742145),
and signal recognition particle 9-kD protein
(NP_036188). Among these, more than 24 unique
peptides were identified in E330016A19, repre-
senting 41% coverage in this protein of 507
amino acids

experiment.system: Peak and adjacent fractions from the last step of each of three L929 purification routes
experiment.perturbation: observational (comparison of active peak fractions versus weak/no-activity adjacent fractions)
experiment.measurement: SDS-PAGE followed by nano-LC-MS with label-free quantification (MaxQuant)

numbers.quantity: proteins copurifying in all three routes

text: E330016A19 shows structural and sequence homology to the catalytic domain of human OAS1, contains the nucleotidyltransferase-family Gly[Gly/Ser]x9–13[Glu/Asp]h[Glu/Asp]h motif and a C-terminal Mab21 domain, with the NTase and Mab21 domains highly conserved from zebrafish to human while N-terminal sequences are much less conserved.

quotes.quote:
E330016A19, which exhibited structural and se-
quence homology to the catalytic domain of hu-
man oligoadenylate synthase (OAS1)

E330016A19 contains a conserved
Gly[Gly/Ser]x9–13[Glu/Asp]h[Glu/Asp]h motif

Sequence
alignment revealed that the C-terminal NTase
and Mab21 domains are highly conserved from
zebrafish to human

experiment.system: Mouse E330016A19, human cGAS, and human OAS1 protein sequences
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: Multiple sequence and structure alignment (PROMALS3D) and bioinformatic motif/domain analysis

text: cGAS expression is cell-type dependent: m-cGAS RNA was low in immortalized MEFs but high in L929, Raw264.7, and bone marrow–derived macrophages, and h-cGAS RNA and protein were very low/undetectable in HEK293T cells but high in THP1 cells.

quotes.quote:
the
expression of m-cGAS was low in immortalized
mouse embryo fibroblasts (MEFs) but high in
L929 cells, Raw264.7 cells, and bone marrow–
derived macrophages (Fig. 1B).

expression of h-cGAS RNA was very low in
human embryonic kidney (HEK) 293T cells but
high in the human monocytic cell line THP1
(Fig. 1C). Immunoblotting further confirmed that
h-cGAS protein was expressed in THP1 cells but
not HEK293T cells

experiment.system: Murine (MEF, L929, Raw264.7, spleen-derived and bone marrow–derived macrophage) and human (HEK293T, THP1) cell lines
experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: Quantitative RT-PCR of cGAS RNA and immunoblotting of endogenous protein

text: IFN-b induction by cGAS was comparable to that by MAVS and higher by several orders of magnitude than induction by the other putative DNA sensors DAI, IFI16, and DDX41; among all proteins overexpressed in HEK293T-STING cells, only cGAS produced cGAMP activity.

quotes.quote:
The magnitude of IFN-b induction by c-GAS
was comparable to that induced by MAVS (an
adaptor protein that functions downstream of
the RNA sensor RIG-I) and was higher than that
induced by other putative DNA sensors, includ-
ing DAI, IFI16, and DDX41, by several orders
of magnitude (Fig. 2C).

Among all the pro-
teins expressed in HEK293T-STING cells, only
cGAS was capable of producing the cGAMP ac-
tivity in the cells.

experiment.system: HEK293T-STING cells
experiment.perturbation: Transfection of expression vectors for DAI, IFI16, DDX41, cGAS, MAVS, or empty vector (20, 200, 2000 ng)
experiment.measurement: IFN-b RNA by qRT-PCR; cGAMP activity of heat-treated cell extracts assayed by IRF3 dimerization in PFO-permeabilized Raw264.7 cells

text: Flag-cGAS purified from transfected HEK293T cells produced cGAMP activity in vitro for wild-type m-cGAS and h-cGAS but not catalytically inactive mutants, and this in vitro activity required HT-DNA; in cells, HT-DNA markedly enhanced IFN-b induction by low (10 and 50 ng) but not high (200 ng) doses of cGAS plasmid, whereas IFI16 and DDX41 did not induce IFN-b even with HT-DNA.

quotes.quote:
Wild-type m-cGAS and h-cGAS, but not the
catalytically inactive mutants of cGAS, were able
to produce the cGAMP activity, which stimulated
IRF3 dimerization in permeabilized Raw264.7
cells (fig. S3A). We found that the in vitro activ-
ities of both m-cGAS and h-cGAS were depen-
dent on the presence of HT-DNA (Fig. 2E).

HT-DNA markedly enhanced IFN-b induction
by low (10 and 50 ng) but not high (200 ng)
doses of cGAS plasmid.

In contrast to cGAS, IFI16 and DDX41
did not induce IFN-b even when HT-DNA was
cotransfected.

experiment.system: Flag-tagged m-cGAS and h-cGAS affinity-purified from HEK293T cells; HEK293T-STING cells
experiment.perturbation: In vitro incubation with ATP and GTP with or without HT-DNA; cotransfection of varying cGAS plasmid doses with or without HT-DNA
experiment.measurement: cGAMP activity via IRF3 dimerization in permeabilized Raw264.7 cells; IFN-b RNA by qRT-PCR

numbers.quantity: cGAS plasmid doses enhanced by HT-DNA

text: Knockdown of m-cGAS in L929 cells by two siRNA pairs or two distinct shRNAs severely compromised IFN-b induction by HT-DNA, with inhibition correlating with knockdown efficiency.

quotes.quote:
We used
two different pairs of small interfering RNA
(siRNA) to knock down m-cGAS in L929 cells,
and found that both siRNA oligos strongly in-
hibited IFN-b induction by HT-DNA; moreover,
the degree of inhibition correlated with the
efficiency of knocking down m-cGAS RNA
(fig. S4A).

The ability of these cells to induce
IFN-b in response to HT-DNA was severely com-
promised relative to another cell line expressing
a control shRNA against green fluorescent pro-
tein (shGFP; Fig. 3A).

experiment.system: L929 cells
experiment.perturbation: siRNA or stable shRNA knockdown of m-cGAS (two distinct target regions) versus shGFP control, then HT-DNA transfection
experiment.measurement: IFN-b RNA by qRT-PCR over a time course

text: Epistasis analysis placed cGAS upstream of STING: in L929–sh-cGAS cells, expression of cGAS, STING, or MAVS, or delivery of cGAMP, restored IFN-b induction, whereas in L929-shSTING cells cGAS expression or cGAMP delivery failed to induce IFN-b while STING or MAVS expression restored it.

quotes.quote:
Expression of cGAS in the L929–sh-cGAS
cells restored IFN-b induction (Fig. 3B). Expres-
sion of STING or MAVS in these cells (Fig. 3B)
or delivery of cGAMP to these cells (Fig. 3C) also
induced IFN-b. In contrast, expression of cGAS
or delivery of cGAMP failed to induce IFN-b
in L929-shSTING cells, whereas expression of
STING or MAVS restored IFN-b induction in
these cells

experiment.system: L929 cells stably expressing shRNA against GFP, cGAS, or STING
experiment.perturbation: Transfection of pcDNA3 vector or plasmids expressing cGAS, STING, or MAVS; or delivery of cGAMP (100 nM) into digitonin-permeabilized cells
experiment.measurement: IFN-b RNA by qRT-PCR

text: cGAS knockdown in L929 cells severely compromised IRF3 dimerization in response to HSV-1 infection but did not affect IRF3 activation by the RNA virus Sendai virus.

quotes.quote:
L929 cells
expressing shRNA against m-cGAS, but not
against GFP, were severely compromised in IRF3
dimerization in response to HSV-1 infection (Fig.
3D). In contrast, knockdown of cGAS did not
affect IRF3 activation by Sendai virus, an RNA
virus (Fig. 3E).

experiment.system: L929 cells stably expressing shRNA against GFP or cGAS
experiment.perturbation: Infection with HSV1 (DICP34.5) or Sendai virus for indicated times
experiment.measurement: IRF3 dimerization by native gel electrophoresis/immunoblot

text: cGAS knockdown largely abolished the cGAMP activity generated by DNA transfection or HSV-1 infection in L929 cells, and quantitative mass spectrometry using SRM showed cGAMP abundance was markedly reduced in cGAS-depleted cells.

quotes.quote:
Knockdown of cGAS
largely abolished the cGAMP activity generated
by DNA transfection or HSV-1 infection (Fig. 3F,
bottom). Quantitative mass spectrometry using
selective reaction monitoring (SRM) showed that
the abundance of cGAMP induced by DNA
transfection or HSV-1 infection was markedly
reduced in L929 cells depleted of cGAS (Fig.
3G).

experiment.system: L929-shGFP and L929–sh-cGAS cells
experiment.perturbation: HT-DNA transfection or HSV-1 infection for 6 hours
experiment.measurement: cGAMP activity via IRF3 dimerization in permeabilized Raw264.7 cells; C18 HPLC fractionation and SRM mass spectrometry quantitation of cGAMP

text: In human THP1 cells, shRNA knockdown of h-cGAS strongly inhibited IFN-b induction by HT-DNA transfection or vaccinia virus infection but not by Sendai virus, and inhibited HSV-1–induced IRF3 dimerization, confirmed with a second shRNA targeting a different region.

quotes.quote:
The knock-
down of h-cGAS strongly inhibited IFN-b in-
duction by HT-DNA transfection or infection
by vaccinia virus, another DNA virus, but not
by Sendai virus (fig. S4D). The knockdown of
h-cGAS also inhibited IRF3 dimerization in-
duced by HSV-1 infection in THP1 cells (fig.
S4E). This result was further confirmed in an-
other THP1 cell line expressing a shRNA target-
ing a different region of h-cGAS (fig. S4F).

experiment.system: Human THP1 monocytic cell lines stably expressing shRNA targeting h-cGAS
experiment.perturbation: HT-DNA transfection, vaccinia virus, Sendai virus, or HSV-1 infection
experiment.measurement: IFN-b RNA by qRT-PCR; IRF3 dimerization

text: Purified Flag–h-cGAS catalyzed cGAMP production in the presence of HT-DNA, activity abolished by DNase I treatment; the activity was also stimulated by poly(dA:dT), poly(dG:dC), and ISD but not by the RNA poly(I:C), and cGAMP synthesis required both ATP and GTP but not CTP or UTP.

quotes.quote:
In the
presence of HT-DNA, purified c-GAS protein cat-
alyzed the production of cGAMP activity, which
stimulated IRF3 dimerization in permeabilized
Raw264.7 cells (Fig. 4B). Deoxyribonuclease I
(DNase I) treatment abolished this activity. The
cGAS activity was also stimulated by other DNAs,
including poly(deoxyadenosine-deoxythymidine),
poly(deoxyguanosine-deoxycytidine), and ISD,
but not by the RNA poly(inosine-cytidine). The
synthesis of cGAMP by cGAS required both ATP
and GTP but did not require cytidine triphos-
phate (CTP) or uridine triphosphate (UTP) (Fig.
4C).

experiment.system: Flag–h-cGAS expressed in HEK293T cells and purified to apparent homogeneity (silver staining)
experiment.perturbation: In vitro reactions with different nucleic acids (HT-DNA, poly(dA:dT), poly(dG:dC), ISD, poly(I:C), DNase I–treated HT-DNA) and different nucleotide triphosphate combinations
experiment.measurement: cGAMP generation assessed by IRF3 dimerization in permeabilized Raw264.7 cells

text: SUMO–m-cGAS expressed in E. coli generated cGAMP activity in a DNA-dependent manner, but after SUMO tag removal m-cGAS catalyzed cGAMP synthesis DNA-independently; the authors state the reason for this loss of DNA dependency is unclear but could be due to conformational changes after SUMO removal.

quotes.quote:
After purification,
SUMO–m-cGAS generated the cGAMP activity
in a DNA-dependent manner (fig. S5, A and C).
However, after the SUMO tag was removed by a
SUMO protease, the m-cGAS protein catalyzed
cGAMP synthesis in a DNA-independent man-
ner (fig. S5, B and C). The reason for this loss
of DNA dependency is unclear but could be due
to some conformational changes after SUMO re-
moval.

experiment.system: m-cGAS expressed in Escherichia coli as a SUMO fusion protein
experiment.perturbation: SUMO protease cleavage of the SUMO tag; in vitro reaction with or without DNA
experiment.measurement: cGAMP activity via IRF3 dimerization assay

text: Recombinant cGAS protein at less than 1 nM produced detectable IRF3 dimerization, whereas the catalytically inactive mutant failed to activate IRF3 even at high concentrations; nano-LC-MS with SRM detected cGAMP in a 60-min reaction containing purified cGAS, ATP, and GTP, with CID fragmentation m/z values matching chemically synthesized cGAMP.

quotes.quote:
Titration experiments showed that re-
combinant cGAS protein at less than 1 nM led
to detectable IRF3 dimerization, whereas the
catalytically inactive mutant of cGAS failed to
activate IRF3 even at high concentrations (Fig.
4D).

cGAMP
was detected in a 60-min reaction containing
purified cGAS, ATP, and GTP (Fig. 4E).

The fragmentation pattern of cGAMP
synthesized by purified cGAS revealed product
ions whose mass/charge ratio (m/z) values matched
those of chemically synthesized cGAMP (fig.
S5D).

experiment.system: Wild-type and GS>AA mutant m-cGAS purified from E. coli
experiment.perturbation: Titration of cGAS protein (0, 0.8, 4, 20, 100 nM) in reactions with ATP, GTP, and DNA; 0 or 60 min incubation
experiment.measurement: IRF3 dimerization assay; nano-LC-MS using SRM and collision-induced dissociation fragmentation

numbers.quantity: cGAS concentration giving detectable IRF3 dimerization

text: GST–m-cGAS and GST–h-cGAS, but not GST–RIG-I(N), were precipitated by biotinylated ISD, and biotinylated RNA did not bind cGAS.

quotes.quote:
Indeed, both GST (glutathione
S-transferase) fused to the N terminus of m-CGAS
(GST–m-cGAS) and GST–h-cGAS, but not GST–
RIG-I N terminus [RIG-I(N)], were precipitated by
biotinylated ISD (Fig. 5A). In contrast, biotinylated
RNA did not bind cGAS (Fig. 5B).

experiment.system: GST fusion proteins purified from E. coli; Flag–h-cGAS purified from HEK293T cells
experiment.perturbation: Incubation with streptavidin beads in the presence of ISD, biotin-ISD, or biotin-RNA
experiment.measurement: Streptavidin pull-down followed by immunoblotting with GST or Flag antibody

text: Confocal immunofluorescence of L929 cells stably expressing Flag–m-cGAS showed cGAS distributed throughout the cytoplasm and also in the nuclear or perinuclear region; after transfection with Cy3-labeled ISD for 2 or 4 hours, punctate cGAS overlapped with DNA fluorescence in more than 50% of cells under observation.

quotes.quote:
The cGAS protein was distributed
throughout the cytoplasm but could also be ob-
served in the nuclear or perinuclear region. After the
cells were transfected with Cyanine 3 (Cy3)–labeled
ISD for 2 or 4 hours, punctate forms of cGAS were
observed, and they overlapped with the DNA
fluorescence. Such colocalization and apparent
aggregation of cGAS and Cy3-ISD was observed
in more than 50% of the cells under observation.

experiment.system: L929 cells stably expressing Flag–m-cGAS
experiment.perturbation: Transfection with Cy3-labeled ISD for 2 or 4 hours
experiment.measurement: Confocal immunofluorescence microscopy with anti-Flag staining and DAPI

text: Overexpression of DAI, IFI16, or DDX41 did not lead to production of cGAMP, and siRNA knockdown of DDX41 and p204 (a mouse homolog of IFI16) did not inhibit generation of cGAMP activity in HT-DNA–transfected L929 cells; the authors note it remains possible that distinct DNA sensors exist in different cell types.

quotes.quote:
Overexpres-
sion of DAI, IFI16, or DDX41 did not lead to
the production of cGAMP. We also found that
knockdown of DDX41 and p204 (a mouse ho-
molog of IFI16) by siRNA did not inhibit the
generation of cGAMP activity in HT-DNA–
transfected L929 cells (fig. S7). Nonetheless, it
is possible that distinct DNA sensors exist in dif-
ferent cell types.

experiment.system: HEK293T-STING cells (overexpression) and L929 cells (knockdown)
experiment.perturbation: Overexpression of DAI, IFI16, or DDX41; siRNA knockdown of DDX41 and p204 followed by HT-DNA transfection
experiment.measurement: cGAMP activity assay via IRF3 dimerization in permeabilized Raw264.7 cells

text: An expression screen of approximately 5,500 human and 9,000 murine full length cDNAs transfected into 293T cells carrying an IFN-b-Luc reporter identified STING, a protein with five predicted transmembrane motifs existing as a 379 amino acid protein in human cells and 378 amino acids in murine cells.

quotes.quote:
we employed an expression screening system in which approximately
5,500 human and 9,000 murine full length complementary DNAs
were individually transfected into 293T cells harbouring a luciferase
gene under control of the IFN-b promoter (IFN-b-Luc).

which we referred to as STING that harboured five predicted trans-
membrane motifs (in humans) and existed as a 379 amino acid pro-
tein in human cells and 378 amino acids in murine cells

experiment.system: 293T cells with IFN-b-Luc reporter
experiment.perturbation: individual transfection of ~5,500 human and 9,000 murine full-length cDNAs
experiment.measurement: IFN-b promoter luciferase induction; protein sequence/motif prediction

text: STING is ubiquitously expressed across a variety of tissues and predominantly resides in the ER region of the cell, as determined by northern analysis, confocal microscopy and fractionation.

quotes.quote:
STING was found to be
ubiquitously expressed in a variety of tissues, as determined by north-
ern analysis, and was found to predominantly reside in the ER region
of the cell as determined by confocal microscopy and fractionation
analysis (Fig. 1 c–e).

e, Fractionation
experiments confirm that STING resides in the ER. Control antibodies
indicate accuracy of fractionation (Calreticulin, ER; COX IV, mitochondria;
b-actin, cytosol).

experiment.system: human multiple tissue RNA blots; HEK 293 cells transfected with HA-tagged human STING; HUVEC subcellular fractions
experiment.perturbation: observational (expression profiling); ectopic tagged STING expression with organelle markers
experiment.measurement: northern blot, confocal colocalization with ER-dsRed/MitoTracker/Golgi-dsRed, sucrose gradient fractionation immunoblot

text: Overexpression of STING in 293T cells induced IFN-b-Luc by up to 400-fold, IRF3-responsive PRD-III-I-Luc up to 1,000-fold, NF-kB-Luc 12-fold and ISRE-Luc up to 800-fold, but not the control TK promoter or RB, p53 or E2F reporters.

quotes.quote:
Overexpression of STING in 293T cells was subsequently con-
firmed to robustly induce the expression of the IFN promoter
(IFN-b-Luc) by up to 400-fold, but not a control TK promoter driv-
ing luciferase (pRL-TK), interferon regulatory factor 3 (IRF3)
responsive promoters (PRD-III-I-Luc) up to 1,000-fold, an NF-kB
responsive promoter (NF-kB-Luc) 12-fold, and interferon-inducible
promoters (interferon sensitive response element, ISRE-Luc) up to
800-fold (Fig. 2 a–d). STING did not activate control promoters
driving luciferase reporters such as those derived from the RB, p53
or E2F genes

experiment.system: 293T cells
experiment.perturbation: transfection of increasing amounts of human or murine STING versus control DRIG-I/empty vector
experiment.measurement: luciferase reporter activity (IFN-b-Luc, PRD-III-I-Luc, NF-kB-Luc, ISRE-Luc, pRL-TK)

text: STING expression increased IRF3 dimerization in 293T cells, which the authors interpret as STING acting upstream of IRF3 activation, dimerization and translocation.

quotes.quote:
Increased dimerization of IRF3
was also observed in STING expressing 293T cells, confirming that
STING regulates the induction of type I IFN at locations upstream of
IRF3 activation, dimerization and translocation

experiment.system: 293T cells
experiment.perturbation: STING overexpression versus control
experiment.measurement: native PAGE immunoblot of IRF3 dimerization

text: Transient transfection of STING into murine embryonic fibroblasts significantly induced endogenous Ifnb mRNA and IFN-b protein, and microarray analysis of STING-expressing 293T cells showed induction of primary innate immune response genes.

quotes.quote:
Endogenous Ifnb mRNA and IFN-b protein was induced sig-
nificantly in murine embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) transiently trans-
fected with STING (Fig. 2e, f). DNA microarray analysis of STING
expression in 293T cells further emphasized STING’s ability to
induce
primary
innate
immune
response
genes

e, MEFs were
transfected as in a, and Ifnb mRNA was analysed by qRT–PCR. f, Medium
from transfected MEFs was analysed for IFN-b protein by ELISA.

experiment.system: murine embryonic fibroblasts; 293T cells
experiment.perturbation: transient transfection of human or murine STING versus vector
experiment.measurement: qRT-PCR of Ifnb mRNA, ELISA of secreted IFN-b, Affymetrix U133 Plus 2.0 microarray

text: MEFs expressing STING or IPS-1 were significantly resistant to vesicular stomatitis virus infection.

quotes.quote:
MEF cells expressing STING or IPS-1 were significantly
resistant to vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) infection (Fig. 2h, i).

h, MEFs
transfected with STING or DRIG-I or IPS-1 are resistant to VSV-GFP
infection (m.o.i., 1). Top panel is light microscopy, lower panel is fluorescent
microscopy. i, Plaque assay from h.

experiment.system: murine embryonic fibroblasts
experiment.perturbation: transfection of STING, DRIG-I or IPS-1 followed by VSV-GFP infection (m.o.i. 1)
experiment.measurement: fluorescence/light microscopy and plaque assay viral titre

text: STING function was ablated in MEFs lacking the IkB kinase family member TBK-1, and STING did not exert robust activity in the absence of FADD.

quotes.quote:
Subsequent analysis indicated that STING function was ablated in
the absence of the IkB kinase family member TBK-1, confirming that
STING’s activity involved activation of IRF3 and was indeed
upstream of this kinase (Fig. 2 j)15. Finally, we observed that
STING did not exert robust activity in the absence of FADD

experiment.system: Tbk-1+/+ and Tbk-1-/- MEFs; Fadd+/+ and Fadd-/- MEFs
experiment.perturbation: STING overexpression in kinase/adaptor-deficient versus wild-type MEFs
experiment.measurement: IFN-b-Luc luciferase reporter activity

text: Neither the N-terminal region of STING containing the five putative transmembrane regions (amino acids 1–230) nor the carboxyl region alone (amino acids 173–379) significantly induced IFN-b-Luc, and the carboxyl region acted as a dominant-negative that impeded full-length STING's stimulation of IFN-b-Luc; C-terminal HA tagging preserved activity whereas GFP tagging abolished it.

quotes.quote:
the N-terminal
region of STING containing the five putative transmembrane regions
(amino acids 1–230) or just the carboxyl region of STING (amino
acids 173–379) did not exhibit significant ability, alone, to induce the
IFN-b-Luc promoter (Fig. 2k, l). Thus, full length, intact STING is
required for efficient function. However, we further observed that the
carboxyl region of STING exerted a dominant-negative inhibitory
effect and could impede the ability of full-length STING to stimulate
IFN-b-Luc

while STING that had been tagged with
HA at the carboxy region retained activity, this activity was lost when
STING was tagged at the amino terminus or C terminus with GFP

experiment.system: 293T cells
experiment.perturbation: transfection of full-length hSTING, hSTING-N (aa 1–230) or hSTING-C (aa 173–379), alone or with increasing amounts alongside full-length STING
experiment.measurement: IFN-b-Luc luciferase reporter activity

numbers.quantity: putative transmembrane regions in N-terminal fragment

text: STING-deficient (Sting-/-) mice generated by targeted homologous recombination were born at the Mendelian ratio and developed and bred normally.

quotes.quote:
we generated STING deficient (Sting2/2) mice by targeted
homologous
recombination
in
embryonic
stem
(ES)
cells
(Supplementary Fig. 4). Sting2/2 animals were born at the
Mendelian ratio, and developed and bred normally.

experiment.system: mice on a C57BL/6J background from targeted E14.1 (129SvEv) ES cells
experiment.perturbation: germline knockout of Sting
experiment.measurement: observational: genotype ratios by PCR, development and breeding

text: Loss of STING reduced the ability of Sendai virus to induce IFN-b, whereas no strong requirement for STING was seen for transfected poly I:C-induced IFN-b, and EMCV neither effectively induced IFN-b nor replicated differently regardless of STING.

quotes.quote:
Similar analysis also indicated that loss of
STING also reduced the ability of Sendai virus to induce IFN-b
(Fig. 3f). In contrast, we did not observe a strong requirement for
STING to mediate the ability of transfected poly I:C to induce IFN-b
induction, which is largely governed by the intracellular RIG-I
homologue MDA5 (ref. 18) (Supplementary Fig. 5). We also
observed that the positive-stranded encephalomyocarditis virus
(EMCV), a member of the picornavirus family, did not effectively
induce IFN-b or replicate differently, regardless of the presence of
STING

experiment.system: Sting-/- and control MEFs
experiment.perturbation: infection with Sendai virus (m.o.i. 1) or EMCV, or transfection of poly I:C
experiment.measurement: endogenous IFN-b by ELISA; viral replication

text: The DNA-sensing defect was also observed in STING-lacking bone marrow derived macrophages and GM-CSF-cultured dendritic cells, whereas exogenous poly I:C or LPS induction of IFN-b (TLR3- and TLR4-dependent) was unaffected, and Sting-/- GM-DCs and BMDMs were less susceptible to VSV-GFP than Sting-/- MEFs.

quotes.quote:
This effect was similarly observed in murine
STING-lacking bone marrow derived macrophages (BMDM) or
bone marrow derived dendritic cells (GM-DC) cultured using gran-
ulocyte-monocyte
colony
stimulating
factor
(GM-CSF)
(Supplementary Fig. 6). However, no significant difference was
observed in the ability of exogenous poly I:C or lipopolysaccharide
(LPS) to induce IFN-b, when comparing Sting2/2 BMDMs or GM-
DCs to controls, events which depend on TLR3 and TLR4, respect-
ively. Whereas loss of STING rendered MEFs highly susceptible to
VSV-GFP, less susceptibility was observed following VSV-GFP infec-
tion of Sting2/2 GM-DCs or BMDMs

experiment.system: Sting-/- and control murine BMDMs and GM-CSF-cultured bone marrow derived dendritic cells
experiment.perturbation: transfected DNA, exogenous poly I:C, LPS, or VSV-GFP infection
experiment.measurement: IFN-b induction and susceptibility to VSV-GFP infection

text: In co-transfected 293T cells FLAG-tagged RIG-I but not MDA5 associated with HA-tagged STING, and this binding was augmented upon Sendai virus infection; endogenous RIG-I associated with endogenous STING in HUVECs.

quotes.quote:
Co-
immunoprecipitation experiments in 293T cells principally indicated
that FLAG-tagged RIG-I but not MDA5 could associate with HA-
tagged STING in co-transfection experiments (Fig. 4a). The binding
of RIG-I to STING was augmented upon infection of 293T cells with
Sendai virus (Fig. 4a). We confirmed in normal human umbilical vein
endothelial cells (HUVECs) that endogenous RIG-I could associate
directly,orindirectlyasacomplex,withendogenousSTING(Fig.4b).

experiment.system: 293T cells and HUVECs
experiment.perturbation: co-transfection of HA-STING with FLAG-RIG-I or FLAG-MDA5, with or without Sendai virus infection (m.o.i. 1); endogenous IP in HUVECs

text: The CARD domains of RIG-I (amino acids 1–284) preferentially associated with HA-STING in transfected 293T cells, and not RIG-I-C (amino acids 218–925); RIG-I colocalized with STING, and the carboxyl region of STING inhibited RIG-I function.

change can be described as movements of the CTD and

8 (Mastermind), residues 49–132, were cloned into pGEX-6P-1.

experiment.measurement: final purified protein yield per liter of culture

text: Observed via total internal reflection fluorescence microscopy, the muscarinic acetylcholine M2 receptor appeared predominantly monomeric but reversibly formed dimers at the plasma membrane of transformed Chinese Hamster Ovary cells, a cardiac cell line, primary cardiomyocytes and tissue slices from pre-natal and post-natal mice.

quotes.quote:
When observed via total internal reﬂection ﬂuorescence microscopy the muscarinic
acetylcholine M2 receptor (M2R) appeared to exist pre-
dominantly as a monomer but was able to reversibly form
dimers at the plasma membrane of each of transformed
Chinese Hamster Ovary cells, a cardiac cell line, primary
cardiomyocytes and tissue slices from pre-natal and post-
natal mice

experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: total internal reflection fluorescence microscopy of receptor oligomeric state

text: By contrast, fluorescence correlation spectroscopy with photon counting histogram studies reported the M2 receptor as being organized intrinsically as a dimer in a transfected cell line, while FRET-based approaches including step-wise photo-bleaching and ligand binding studies were interpreted as showing the receptor to exist predominantly as tetramers in both transfected cells and native tissue.

quotes.quote:
ﬂuorescence correlation spec-
troscopy (FCS) with photon counting histogram studies
reported this receptor as being organized intrinsically as a
dimer in a transfected cell line [7], whilst Fluorescence
Resonance Energy Transfer (FRET)-based approaches,
including the application of step-wise photo-bleaching
protocols, and ligand binding studies have been consis-
tent with and interpreted as showing this receptor to exist
predominantly as tetramers in both transfected cells and
native tissue

experiment.perturbation: observational
experiment.measurement: FCS with photon counting histograms; FRET with step-wise photo-bleaching; ligand binding

text: A study of three distinct class A GPCRs — the b2-adrenoceptor, the cannabinoid CB1 receptor and opsin — in proteoliposomes found the extent of receptor organization to be receptor type specific and sensitive to environmental effectors including protein density and membrane curvature.

quotes.quote:
A very recent study in which the
oligomerization characteristics of three distinct class A
GPCRs, the b2-adrenoceptor (b2-AR), the cannabinoid
CB1 receptor and opsin, were investigated in proteolipo-
somes highlighted how the extent of receptor organiza-
tion 
is 
receptor 
type 
speciﬁc 
and 
sensitive 
to

environmental effectors, including protein density and
membrane curvature

experiment.system: b2-adrenoceptor, cannabinoid CB1 receptor and opsin reconstituted in single proteoliposomes
experiment.perturbation: variation of protein density and membrane curvature
experiment.measurement: high-content analysis of oligomer stoichiometries and association constants

text: Single-molecule analysis of fluorescently labelled b1-adrenoceptors and b2-adrenoceptors indicated both were organized as a mixture of different sized complexes at the plasma membrane of Chinese Hamster Ovary cells, with the b2-AR showing higher complexity at equal expression levels, and the complexity of the b2-AR increasing with receptor density at the cell surface.

quotes.quote:
Single-molecule
analysis of ﬂuorescently labelled b1-adrenoceptors and
b2-adrenoceptors indicated these were both organized as
a mixture of different sized complexes at the plasma
membrane of Chinese Hamster Ovary cells, with the
b2-AR showing higher complexity at equal expression
levels [17]. Moreover, the complexity of particularly the
b2-AR was observed to increase with receptor density at
the cell surface, consistent both with transient interac-
tions and effects of mass-action

experiment.system: fluorescently labelled b1- and b2-adrenoceptors in CHO cells
experiment.perturbation: variation of receptor expression density
experiment.measurement: single-molecule imaging of complex size distribution

text: Increasing quaternary complexity with higher levels of expression has also been reported via single molecule tracking of the dopamine D2 receptor.

quotes.quote:
Increasing
quaternary complexity with higher levels of expression
has also been reported via single molecule tracking of the
dopamine D2 receptor (D2R)

experiment.system: dopamine D2 receptor in cells
experiment.perturbation: variation of receptor expression level
experiment.measurement: single-molecule tracking of quaternary complexity

text: The half-life of the interaction between unliganded dopamine D2 receptors was measured to be about 0.5 s at 24 °C; binding of antagonists did not alter the observed equilibrium between monomers and dimers, whereas binding of agonists did.

quotes.quote:
the half-
life of the interaction between unliganded D2Rs was
measured to be about 0.5 s at 24 C and although binding
of antagonists to the receptor did not alter the observed
equilibrium between monomers and dimers, the binding
of agonists did

experiment.system: dopamine D2 receptors at the plasma membrane
experiment.perturbation: addition of antagonists or agonists
experiment.measurement: single-molecule measurement of protomer interaction half-life and monomer-dimer equilibrium

numbers.quantity: half-life of unliganded D2R protomer interaction

text: Others measured the half-life of the interaction between unliganded D2R protomers to be roughly 68 ms at 37 °C; the antagonist UH-232 did not alter this, while dopamine or quinpirole stabilized dimers, increasing the half-life to 99 and 104 ms, respectively.

quotes.quote:
others have measured the
half-life of the interaction between unliganded-D2R pro-
tomers to be roughly 68 ms at 37 C and, although the
addition of the antagonist UH-232 did not alter this,
treatment with either the endogenous agonist dopamine
or the synthetic agonist quinpirole stabilized dimers,
increasing the half-life to 99 and 104 ms, respectively

experiment.system: dopamine D2 receptor protomers in cell membranes
experiment.perturbation: addition of antagonist UH-232, dopamine, or quinpirole
experiment.measurement: single-molecule tracking of dimer interaction half-life

text: In SpIDA studies of the serotonin 5-HT2C receptor, the receptor was predominantly monomeric at steady-state and relatively low density with a clearly observed fraction of dimers, while increasing receptor density correlated strongly with increasing organizational complexity and a substantial proportion of higher-order oligomers as well as dimers.

quotes.quote:
In studies on the serotonin
5-HT2C receptor (5-HT2CR), which is a target for anti-
obesity medications, at steady-state and at relatively low
density the receptor was predominantly monomeric, but
with a clearly observed fractions of dimers [20]. However,
with increasing receptor density there was a strong corre-
lation with increasing receptor organizational complexity,
and a substantial proportion of higher-order oligomers as
well as dimers was observed

experiment.system: 5-HT2C receptor tagged with mEGFP expressed in mammalian cells
experiment.perturbation: variation of receptor expression density
experiment.measurement: Spatial Intensity Distribution Analysis of quantal brightness on the basolateral membrane

text: A number of distinct ligand chemotypes with affinity as 5-HT2CR antagonists decreased the complexity of organization of the receptor, essentially converting it to a monomeric state; the effect was concentration-dependent and following wash-out the initial complexity of receptor organization was fully restored.

quotes.quote:
A number a distinct ligand chemotypes
with afﬁnity as 5-HT2CR antagonists acted to decrease
the complexity of organization of this receptor, essentially
converting the receptor to monomeric state

the effect of these
compounds was concentration-dependent and following
their wash-out the initial complexity of receptor organi-
zation was fully restored

experiment.system: 5-HT2C-mEGFP expressed in mammalian cells
experiment.perturbation: treatment with distinct chemotypes of 5-HT2CR antagonists, and wash-out
experiment.measurement: SpIDA quantal brightness / oligomeric organization

text: Ongoing SpIDA studies verified and extended the initial 5-HT2CR findings, including for the drug ritanserin, the ligand used to stabilize the 5-HT2CR for crystallization studies, suggesting that all 5-HT2CR antagonists may destabilize dimers and oligomers of this receptor.

quotes.quote:
Ongoing
studies have veriﬁed and extended these initial ﬁndings
(Figure 2), including for the drug ritanserin, which was
the ligand used to stabilize the 5-HT2CR for crystalliza-
tion studies [21]. This suggests that all 5-HT2CR antago-
nists may destabilize dimers and oligomers of this recep-
tor.

experiment.system: 5-HT2C receptor expressed in cells
experiment.perturbation: treatment with ritanserin and other 5-HT2CR antagonists
experiment.measurement: SpIDA of receptor quaternary organization

text: In SpIDA studies on the dopamine D3 receptor, a number of, but not all, antagonists promoted monomerization of the receptor.

quotes.quote:
in SpIDA studies on the closely
related dopamine D3 receptor (D3R) a number of, but not
all, antagonists also promoted monomerization of the
receptor

experiment.system: dopamine D3 receptor expressed in cells
experiment.perturbation: treatment with a panel of D3R antagonists
experiment.measurement: SpIDA of receptor quaternary organization

text: A mutant D3R unable to bind the antagonist spiperone showed the same basal quaternary organization as wild type at equal receptor density but was completely unaffected upon addition of spiperone, indicating the ligand effect reflects binding to the receptor rather than an off-target membrane effect.

quotes.quote:
Mar-
sango et al. [22] assessed this by generating a mutant of
the D3R that is unable to bind the antagonist spiperone.
This mutated receptor showed the same basal quaternary
organization as the wild type at equal receptor density but
now this was completely unaffected upon addition of
spiperone

experiment.system: wild type and spiperone-binding-deficient mutant dopamine D3 receptor expressed in cells
experiment.perturbation: mutation abolishing spiperone binding plus spiperone addition
experiment.measurement: SpIDA of basal and ligand-treated quaternary organization at equal receptor density

text: A mutational approach to define potential dimerization interfaces of the D3R predicted roles for both sections of transmembrane domain I and for amino acids in transmembrane domains IV and V, indicating multiple interfaces able to promote and stabilize dimeric interactions.

quotes.quote:
In earlier studies Mar-
sango et al. [23] had taken a mutational approach to
deﬁne potential dimerization interfaces of the D3R. This
lead to predictions of roles for both sections of trans-
membrane domain I and for amino acids in transmem-
brane domains IV and V and, therefore, indicated that
there must be multiple interfaces able to promote and
stabilize dimeric interactions.

experiment.system: human dopamine D3 receptor
experiment.perturbation: mutagenesis of candidate transmembrane interface residues
experiment.measurement: analysis of receptor quaternary structure

text: Molecular dynamics simulations of ligand binding to the D3R indicated spiperone increased the distance between reference carbon atoms near the extracellular face of transmembrane domains IV and V compared to the apo-protein, whereas haloperidol did not alter this distance but instead increased the distance between reference carbon atoms in transmembrane domains I and II; eticlopride altered neither distance and did not affect basal receptor quaternary organization.

quotes.quote:
Molec-
ular dynamics simulations of the binding of these ligands
to the D3R indicated that spiperone increased the dis-
tance between reference carbon atoms near the extra-
cellular face of transmembrane domains IV and V com-
pared to the apo-protein. By contrast, although binding
of haloperidol did not alter this distance it instead
increased the distance between reference carbon atoms
in transmembrane domains I and II [22]. By contrast
ligands such as eticlopride did not alter either of these
intra-molecular distances and also did not affect basal
receptor quaternary organization

experiment.system: dopamine D3 receptor in silico and in cells
experiment.perturbation: binding of spiperone, haloperidol or eticlopride versus apo-protein
experiment.measurement: molecular dynamics inter-carbon distances plus SpIDA quaternary organization

text: Combined modelling and mutagenesis studies were used to predict specific roles of molecules of cholesterol in stabilizing a tetrameric configuration of the D3R, while computational studies also predict roles of cholesterol in dimerization of a broad range of chemokine receptors.

quotes.quote:
combined model-
ling and mutagenesis studies were used to predict-spe-
ciﬁc roles of molecules of cholesterol in stabilizing a
tetrameric conﬁguration of the D3R [22] whilst compu-
tational studies also predict roles of cholesterol in dimer-
ization of a broad range of chemokine receptors

experiment.measurement: predicted stabilization of tetrameric/dimeric configurations

text: SpIDA on HEK 293-derived cells expressing monomeric eGFP-tagged muscarinic M1 receptor showed that at steady-state only a small portion of the regions of interest examined on the basolateral membrane contained receptor organized predominantly as dimers/oligomers, across expression densities ranging from 20–120 receptor per mm2.

quotes.quote:
SpIDA on HEK 293-
derived 
cells 
engineered 
to

a

interest examined on the basolateral membrane of these
cells contained the receptor organized predominantly as
dimers/oligomers and this was the case across expression

quotes.quote:
the selective M1 receptor antago-
nists pirenzepine and telenzepine increased, rather than
decreased, the level of steady-state association, although
even at concentrations of the drugs predicted to provide
full 
receptor 
occupancy 
this 
remained 
far 
from

quantitative. Moreover, common anti-muscarinic drugs
such as atropine did not produce this effect

text: Studies using acceptor photo-bleaching-FRET and computational approaches including molecular dynamics simulations combined with multi-ensemble Markov state models reached conclusions of a low proportion of steady-state dimers of the m-opioid receptor.

quotes.quote:
Recent
studies 
using 
acceptor 
photo-bleaching-FRET 
and
computational approaches, including molecular dynamics
simulations combined with multi-ensemble Markov state

(MOR)

Synthetic peptides derived from
speciﬁc transmembrane domains have been central to
addressing this question, and this approach recently
translated from in vitro to in vivo studies that indicated
a key role for transmembrane domain I in interactions
between rhodopsin protomers [27]. Alternatively, how-
ever, a mutagenic approach instead suggested a key role
for transmembrane domain V residues in human red cone
opsin

assuming that a signiﬁcant fraction
of the b2-AR can indeed exist as dimers, transmembrane
domain I may play an integral role [29]. This is also the
case for the thromboxane A2 receptor [30] and, intrigu-
ingly in the context of physiology and disease, patients

reduced platelet function

each of domains IV, V, VI, and VII were recently impli-

quotes.quote:
studies on the
secretin receptor identiﬁed a key role for transmembrane
domain IV and here mutation of a pair of amino acids in
the middle of this domain was originally suggested to
convert the receptor from strict dimer to monomer. This
is associated with altered capacity of the agonist secretin
to stimulate levels of cyclic AMP. Recent SpIDA-based
studies have supported the idea that these speciﬁc muta-
tions do substantially reduce the propensity of this recep-
tor to form a dimeric complex but added a degree of
further subtlety in suggesting that these mutants modu-
late the propensity for rather than deﬁne a strict monomer
to dimer transition

experiment.perturbation: mutation of a pair of amino acids in the middle of transmembrane domain IV
experiment.measurement: SpIDA quantification of homodimerization; secretin-stimulated cyclic AMP levels

text: Cryo-electron microscopy experiments on purified 5-HT2A receptor in the presence or absence of molecules of cholesterol were interpreted to show that this receptor formed dimers in the presence of cholesterol while it existed only as a monomer when cholesterol was removed.

Recent cryo-electron microscopy experiments performed
on puriﬁed 5-HT2A receptor in the presence or absence of
molecules of cholesterol were interpreted to show that
this receptor was able to form dimers in the presence of
cholesterol while, in contrast, it existed only as a mono-
mer when cholesterol was removed

Whilst a
trimeric population of the 5-HT1A receptor was prevalent

text: p38 MAPKs are activated by dual phosphorylation of the Thr-Gly-Tyr motif in the activation loop; MKK6 phosphorylates all four family members, whereas MKK3 activates p38alpha, p38gamma and p38delta but not p38beta, and p38alpha can also be phosphorylated by MKK4.

p38 MAPKs are
activated by dual phosphorylation in the activation loop sequence
Thr-Gly-Tyr.

MKK6
can phosphorylate the four p38 MAPK family members,
whereas MKK3 activates p38α, p38γ and p38δ, but not p38β.

In addition, p38α can be also phophorylated by MKK4, an
activator of the JNK (c-Jun N-terminal kinase) pathway [24,25].

quotes.quote:
Additional p38
MAPK family members, which are approx. 60% identical in their
amino acid sequence, were subsequently cloned

with p38α being ubiquitously expressed at signiﬁcant
levels in most cell types, whereas the others seem to be expressed
in a more tissue-speciﬁc manner; for example, p38β in brain,
p38γ in skeletal muscle and p38δ in endocrine glands.

numbers.quantity: amino acid sequence identity among p38 MAPK family members

text: Osmotic shock-induced phosphorylation of SAP97/hDlg is usually mediated by p38gamma, but in the absence of p38gamma other p38 MAPKs can perform this function, demonstrating functional redundancy.

quotes.quote:
the osmotic shock-induced
phosphorylation of SAP (synapse-associated protein) 97/hDlg
(human discs large) is usually mediated by p38γ , but, in the
absence of this kinase, other p38 MAPKs can perform this
function [15].

text: The p38alpha splice isoform Mxi2 is identical with p38alpha in amino acids 1-280 but has a unique C-terminus of 17 amino acids, shows reduced binding to p38 MAPK substrates, binds ERK1/2 and regulates their nuclear import.

Mxi2 is identical with p38α in amino acids 1–280, but
has a unique C-terminus of 17 amino acids. This isoform displays
reduced binding to p38 MAPK substrates, whereas it can bind to
ERK1/2 MAPKs and regulates their nuclear import [16].

numbers.quantity: identical region of Mxi2 with p38alpha

text: Activated p38gamma exists as a monomer in solution and its crystal structure does not reveal a dimer interface, unlike active ERK2, although its activation-loop conformation is almost identical with that of active ERK2.

The structure of phosphorylated p38γ has been
also determined, and the conformation of the activation loop
was found to be almost identical with the one in active ERK2.

reveal a dimer interface. This observation is supported by studies
indicating that activated p38γ exists as a monomer in solution

experiment.perturbation: observational (structural determination of phosphorylated kinase)
experiment.measurement: X-ray crystal structure and oligomeric state in solution

text: The three-dimensional structure of p38beta is highly similar to p38alpha but differences in the relative orientation of the N- and C-terminal domains reduce the size of the p38beta ATP-binding pocket.

The
three-dimensional structure of p38β is highly similar overall
to that of p38α; however, there are some differences in the
relative orientation of the N- and C-terminal domains that cause
a reduction in the size of the p38β ATP-binding pocket.

text: In T-lymphocytes, TCR-proximal tyrosine kinases ZAP70 and p56lck phosphorylate p38alpha on Tyr323, leading to p38alpha autophosphorylation on the activation loop and increased kinase activity; GADD45alpha inhibits this pathway by binding p38alpha and preventing Tyr323 phosphorylation.

This involves phosphorylation of p38α
on Tyr323 by the TCR-proximal tyrosine kinases ZAP70 (ζ-chain-
associated protein kinase of 70 kDa) and p56lck, which leads
to p38α autophosphorylation on the activation loop and, as a
consequence, increases its kinase activity towards substrates [36].

appears to act as an endogenous inhibitor of the alternative
p38α-activation pathway in T-cells, by binding to p38α and
preventing Tyr323 phosphorylation [37].

text: p38alpha-knockin mice with Tyr323 replaced by phenylalanine are viable and fertile, but their T-cells fail to activate p38alpha upon TCR stimulation, showing a modest delay in cell-cycle entry and decreased IFNgamma production.

quotes.quote:
generating p38α-knockin mice in which Tyr323 was
replaced by phenylalanine. These mice are viable and fertile

in T-cells from these mice, p38α
is not activated upon TCR stimulation

results
in a modest delay in cell-cycle entry, but once this point has
been passed, cells apparently undergo normal division. Moreover,
IFNγ (interferon γ ) production is decreased in TCR-activated
knockin T-lymphocytes.

experiment.system: p38alpha Tyr323-to-phenylalanine knockin mice and their T-lymphocytes
experiment.perturbation: knockin mutation of Tyr323; TCR stimulation
experiment.measurement: viability/fertility, p38alpha activation, cell-cycle entry and IFNgamma production

text: TAB1 binds p38alpha but not other p38 MAPK family members and induces p38alpha autophosphorylation in the activation loop; the authors note that direct activation of p38alpha by TAB1 using purified proteins has been difficult to reproduce.

TAB1 (TAK1-binding protein 1), which can bind to p38α,
but not to other p38 MAPK family members, and induces
p38α autophosphorylation in the activation loop [39,40]. The
direct activation of p38α by TAB1 using puriﬁed proteins has
been difﬁcult to reproduce [41]

text: Biochemical studies show that p38alpha phosphorylated on both Thr180 and Tyr182 is 10-20-fold more active than p38alpha phosphorylated only on Thr180, whereas p38alpha phosphorylated on Tyr182 alone is inactive.

Biochemical studies have shown that p38α phosphorylated on
both Thr180 and Tyr182 is 10–20-fold more active than p38α
phosphorylated only on Thr180, whereas p38α phosphorylated
on Tyr182 alone is inactive [47].

experiment.perturbation: mono- versus dual phosphorylation of Thr180/Tyr182
experiment.measurement: in vitro kinase activity

numbers.quantity: activity of dually phosphorylated p38alpha relative to Thr180-only

text: A p38alpha mutant that cannot be tyrosine-phosphorylated (Y182F) shows some catalytic activity in vitro and activates reporter genes in cells, although to a much lower extent than wild-type p38alpha.

quotes.quote:
Moreover, a p38α mutant that
cannot be tyrosine-phosphorylated (Y182F) shows some catalytic
activity in vitro and is able to activate reporter genes in cells,
although to a much lower extent than wild-type p38α

experiment.system: in vitro kinase assays and cultured cells expressing p38alpha Y182F
experiment.perturbation: Y182F mutation of p38alpha
experiment.measurement: catalytic activity in vitro and reporter gene activation in cells

text: In LPS-stimulated RAW macrophages MKP1 becomes acetylated on Lys57 by p300, which promotes MKP1 interaction with p38 MAPK and dephosphorylation of p38 MAPK; MKP1-knockout mice do not respond to the inflammation-reducing effect of HDAC inhibitors.

When RAW
macrophages are stimulated with LPS, MKP1 becomes acetylated
on Lys57 by p300. Acetylation of this residue, which is located
within the substrate-binding domain, promotes MKP1 interaction
with p38 MAPK, resulting in dephosphorylation of p38 MAPK.

ﬂammation-reducing effect of HDAC (histone deacetylase)
inhibitors

experiment.system: RAW macrophages and MKP1-knockout mice
experiment.perturbation: LPS stimulation; HDAC inhibitor treatment; MKP1 knockout
experiment.measurement: MKP1 acetylation, MKP1–p38 interaction, p38 dephosphorylation and inflammation

text: MKP5 controls p38 MAPK activation in neutrophils; MKP5 inactivation increases p38 MAPK-mediated phosphorylation of Ser345 of mouse p47phox, resulting in NADPH oxidase priming and superoxide production at inflammatory sites, a function not substituted by MKP1.

MKP5 regulates p38 MAPK activation, which in turn can
phosphorylate Ser345 of mouse p47phox, a component of the
NADPH oxidase complex. Thus MKP5 inactivation increases p38
MAPK-mediated phosphorylation of p47phox, resulting in NADPH
oxidase priming and superoxide production at inﬂammatory sites.

such as MKP1, that have similar substrate speciﬁcity [59].

experiment.perturbation: genetic MKP5 inactivation
experiment.measurement: p38 MAPK activation, p47phox Ser345 phosphorylation and superoxide production

text: Bacterial type III secretion system effectors including Shigella OspF, Salmonella SpvC and Pseudomonas syringae HopAl1 remove the phosphate from the phosphothreonine residue in the MAPK activation loop, showing high phosphothreonine lyase activity towards p38alpha.
