including Shigella OspF, Salmonella SpvC
and Pseudomonas syringae HopAl1, can remove the phosphate
from the phosphothreonine residue in the activation loop and
inactivate MAPKs in the host cells. These enzymes show high
phosphothreonine lyase activity towards p38α.

experiment.system: host cells infected with Gram-negative bacterial pathogens and purified effector enzymes
experiment.perturbation: expression/action of TTSS phosphothreonine lyase effectors
experiment.measurement: activation-loop phosphothreonine removal and MAPK inactivation

text: MK2/MK3-double-knockout cells display significantly reduced levels of p38alpha, and MK2 levels are decreased in p38alpha-deficient cells, indicating reciprocal stabilization of these kinases.

quotes.quote:
Thus MK2/MK3-double-
knockout cells display signiﬁcantly reduced levels of p38α [71]
and, interestingly, MK2 levels are also decreased in p38α-
deﬁcient cells [72].

experiment.system: MK2/MK3-double-knockout and p38alpha-deficient cells
experiment.perturbation: gene knockout of MK2/MK3 or p38alpha
experiment.measurement: protein levels of p38alpha and MK2

text: Phosphorylation of p38 MAPK on Thr123, a residue in the docking groove that can be phosphorylated in vitro by GRK2, decreases association of p38 MAPK with MKK6 and its ability to bind and phosphorylate substrates.

quotes.quote:
the phosphorylation on Thr123 [73], a residue located
at the docking groove for substrates and regulators. This
phosphorylation decreases the association of p38 MAPK with
its activator MKK6, as well as the ability of p38 MAPK to
bind to and phosphorylate substrates. Interestingly, Thr123 can be
phosphorylated in vitro by the G-protein-coupled receptor kinase
GRK2 [73]

experiment.system: in vitro kinase reactions with GRK2 and p38 MAPK
experiment.perturbation: GRK2-mediated Thr123 phosphorylation
experiment.measurement: p38–MKK6 association and substrate binding/phosphorylation

text: MKK4 protein levels increase in senescent human fibroblasts through enhanced translation regulated by four microRNAs (miR-15b, miR-24, miR-25 and miR-141) targeting the untranslated regions of MKK4 mRNA.

quotes.quote:
The levels of MKK4 protein also increase in
senescent human ﬁbroblasts through enhanced translation, which
seems to be regulated by four microRNAs (miR-15b, miR-24,
miR-25 and miR-141) that target the 5′ and 3′ untranslated regions
of the MKK4 mRNA [69].

experiment.system: senescent human fibroblasts
experiment.perturbation: replicative senescence; microRNA targeting of MKK4 mRNA
experiment.measurement: MKK4 protein levels and translation

text: p38alpha translocates to the nucleus upon activation by stimuli that induce DNA double-strand breaks but not other stimuli; the translocation does not require p38alpha catalytic activity but is induced by a conformational change triggered by Thr180 and Tyr182 phosphorylation.

quotes.quote:
since p38α translocates to the nucleus upon
activation by stimuli that induce DNA double-strand breaks, but
not other stimuli [78]. Such translocation does not require p38α
catalytic activity, but it is induced by a conformational change
triggered by the phosphorylation on Thr180 and Tyr182 at the
activation loop [78].

experiment.system: cultured mammalian cells expressing p38alpha
experiment.perturbation: treatment with DNA double-strand break-inducing versus other stimuli; catalytically inactive p38alpha
experiment.measurement: subcellular localization of p38alpha

text: In Schizosaccharomyces pombe a phosphorylation-deficient ATF1 mutant is fully proficient for hotspot recombination, suggesting the p38 MAPK Spc1 regulates ATF1 chromosome binding during meiotic recombination without affecting ATF1 phosphorylation.

quotes.quote:
However, a phosphorylation-deﬁcient mutant of ATF1 was
found to be fully proﬁcient for hotspot recombination, and
further characterization suggests that Spc1 may regulate ATF1
binding to chromosomes during meiotic recombination without
affecting ATF1 phosphorylation [82].

experiment.system: Schizosaccharomyces pombe
experiment.perturbation: phosphorylation-deficient ATF1 mutant
experiment.measurement: hotspot meiotic recombination and ATF1 chromosome binding

text: In S. cerevisiae, mutation of all Hog1 phosphorylation sites in the Hot1 transcription factor affects neither the kinetics nor the levels of expression of stress-induced genes.

quotes.quote:
but mutation of all of the Hog1
phosphorylation sites in Hot1 affects neither the kinetics nor the
levels of expression of stress-induced genes [83,84].

experiment.system: Saccharomyces cerevisiae under osmotic stress
experiment.perturbation: mutation of all Hog1 phosphorylation sites in Hot1
experiment.measurement: kinetics and levels of stress-induced gene expression

text: p38gamma has been suggested to play a phosphorylation-independent role in Ras-induced transformation of rat intestinal epithelial cells, since K-Ras induces p38gamma expression without increasing its phosphorylation and p38gamma down-regulation impairs K-Ras-induced transformation.

quotes.quote:
on the basis of the observation that K-Ras induces p38γ
expression without increasing its phosphorylation, and that
p38γ down-regulation impairs K-Ras-induced transformation.

experiment.system: rat intestinal epithelial cells
experiment.perturbation: K-Ras expression and p38gamma down-regulation
experiment.measurement: p38gamma expression/phosphorylation and cell transformation

text: Selectivity of docking interactions between MAP2Ks and MAPKs favours within-pathway interactions over non-cognate interactions by about an order of magnitude.

quotes.quote:
It has been also reported that the selectivity of the
interaction between MAP2Ks and MAPKs is such that within-
pathway interactions are in general preferred by about an order
of magnitude over non-cognate interactions [94].

experiment.system: purified MAP2K and MAPK proteins/docking sites
experiment.perturbation: comparison of cognate versus non-cognate pairings
experiment.measurement: binding selectivity of docking sites

text: p38gamma is unique among MAPKs in having a C-terminal sequence that docks directly to PDZ domains of proteins such as alpha1-syntrophin, SAP90/PSD95 and SAP97/hDlg, and phosphorylation of these proteins by p38gamma depends on PDZ-domain binding.

quotes.quote:
Of note, p38γ
is unique among MAPKs in that it has a C-terminal sequence
which docks directly to PDZ domains of several proteins, such
as α1-syntrophin, SAP90/PSD95 (postsynaptic density 95) and
the scaffold protein SAP97/hDlg, and phosphorylation of these
proteins by p38γ is dependent on its binding to the PDZ domains

experiment.system: p38gamma and PDZ-domain-containing substrate proteins
experiment.perturbation: disruption of C-terminal/PDZ-domain binding
experiment.measurement: substrate phosphorylation by p38gamma

text: The p38alpha inhibitor CMPD1 selectively prevents in vitro phosphorylation of MK2 by p38alpha without affecting ATF2 phosphorylation, and neither competes with ATP nor interferes with p38alpha–MK2 binding.

quotes.quote:
the p38α chemical
inhibitor CMPD1 has been reported to selectively prevent the
in vitro phosphorylation of MK2 by p38α without affecting
the phosphorylation of ATF2.

CMPD1 neither competes with ATP nor interferes with
the binding of p38α to MK2.

experiment.system: in vitro p38alpha kinase reactions with MK2 and ATF2 substrates
experiment.perturbation: treatment with the chemical inhibitor CMPD1
experiment.measurement: substrate phosphorylation, ATP competition and p38alpha–MK2 binding

text: MK2 phosphorylates Ago2 in vitro on Ser387, identified as the major Ago2 phosphorylation site in cells, and mutation of Ser387 to alanine impairs Ago2 localization to processing bodies.

quotes.quote:
MK2 was found to phosphorylate in vitro the Ago2 (Argonaute
2) protein on Ser387, which was identiﬁed as the major Ago2
phosphorylation site in cells, and mutation of Ser387 to alanine
impairs Ago2 localization to the RNA-containing granules termed
processing bodies [102].

experiment.system: in vitro kinase assays and cultured cells expressing Ago2
experiment.perturbation: MK2 phosphorylation; Ser387-to-alanine mutation
experiment.measurement: Ago2 phosphorylation site mapping and localization to processing bodies

text: p38 MAPKs phosphorylate the ubiquitin ligase Siah2 on Thr24 and Ser29, regulating its activity towards PHD3, and p38alpha-mediated phosphorylation stabilizes Siah2 at high cell density, down-regulating Sprouty2 and leading to EGFR ubiquitination and degradation and contact inhibition.

quotes.quote:
p38 MAPKs phosphorylate the ubiquitin
ligase Siah2 on Thr24 and Ser29, regulating its activity towards
PHD3 (prolyl hydroxylase 3) [104]. Phosphorylation by p38α
also leads to the stabilization of Siah2 under conditions of high
cell density, which in turn down-regulates Sprouty2

experiment.system: cultured mammalian cells at varying cell density
experiment.perturbation: p38 MAPK-mediated phosphorylation of Siah2
experiment.measurement: Siah2 stability/activity, Sprouty2 levels and EGFR degradation

text: p38 MAPK phosphorylates FGFR1 on Ser777 to permit its translocation to cytosol and nucleus; the S777A mutation abolishes FGFR1 translocation whereas phosphomimetic mutants bypass the requirement for active p38 MAPK.

quotes.quote:
FGFR1 translocation requires p38 MAPK activation,
which phosphorylates the C-terminal tail of FGFR1 on Ser777.
Interestingly, the mutation S777A abolishes FGFR1 translocation,
whereas phosphomimetic mutants bypass the requirement for
active p38 MAPK for translocation [111].

experiment.system: target cells expressing FGFR1 variants
experiment.perturbation: S777A and phosphomimetic FGFR1 mutations; p38 MAPK activation
experiment.measurement: FGFR1 translocation to cytosol and nucleus

text: After gamma-irradiation, transiently activated p38alpha phosphorylates HuR on Thr118, causing HuR cytoplasmic accumulation and enhanced binding to p21Cip1 mRNA, increasing its stability and supporting G1 cell-cycle arrest.

quotes.quote:
When cells are irradiated, p38α is transiently activated and
phosphorylates HuR on Thr118, which results in HuR cytoplasmic
accumulation and enhanced binding to the p21Cip1 mRNA. HuR
binding increases p21Cip1 mRNA stability, therefore allowing the
expression of the appropriate p21Cip1 protein levels required for
G1 cell-cycle arrest [112].

experiment.system: cultured mammalian cells
experiment.perturbation: gamma-radiation
experiment.measurement: HuR phosphorylation/localization, p21Cip1 mRNA stability and G1 arrest

text: p38 MAPKs phosphorylate TACE/ADAM17 on Thr735 in its cytoplasmic domain in response to inflammatory stimuli, a phosphorylation required for TACE-mediated ectodomain shedding of TGFalpha family ligands and consequent EGFR signalling and cell proliferation.

quotes.quote:
MAPKs phosphorylate the membrane-associated metalloprotease
TACE (TNFα-converting enzyme)/ADAM17 (a disintegrin and
metalloproteinase domain 17) on Thr735, located in its cytoplasmic
domain. Such phosphorylation is required for TACE-mediated
ectodomain shedding of TGFα family ligands, which results in
the activation of EGFR signalling and cell proliferation [110].

experiment.system: mammalian cells expressing TACE/ADAM17
experiment.perturbation: inflammatory stimuli activating p38 MAPKs
experiment.measurement: TACE Thr735 phosphorylation, ectodomain shedding, EGFR signalling and proliferation

text: p38alpha regulates lineage choices during myelopoiesis through phosphorylation of C/EBPalpha on Ser21, and a core network of 16 transcription factors has been proposed to mediate p38alpha regulation of human squamous carcinoma cell quiescence.

quotes.quote:
Recent results
have established a role for p38α in the regulation of lineage
choices during myelopoiesis through phosphorylation of C/EBPα
on Ser21 [114]. A core network of 16 transcription factors has also
been recently proposed to mediate the regulation by p38α of
human squamous carcinoma cell quiescence [115].

experiment.system: myeloid progenitor cells and human squamous carcinoma cells
experiment.perturbation: p38 MAPK-mediated phosphorylation of C/EBPalpha; computational/experimental analysis of p38alpha-regulated transcription factors
experiment.measurement: neutrophil/myeloid lineage development and transcription factor network mediating quiescence

numbers.quantity: transcription factors in the p38alpha-regulated core network

text: Promoters of inflammatory genes including IL-6, IL-8, IL-12p40 and MCP-1 show p38 MAPK-dependent enrichment of histone H3 Ser10 phosphorylation in LPS-stimulated myeloid cells, enhancing accessibility of cryptic NF-kappaB-binding sites; the phosphorylation is not carried out directly by p38 MAPK but more likely through MSK1.

quotes.quote:
such as IL-6, IL-8, IL-12p40 and MCP-1 (monocyte
chemoattractant protein 1), display a p38 MAPK-dependent
enrichment of histone H3 phosphorylation on Ser10 in LPS-
stimulated myeloid cells. This phosphorylation enhances the
accessibility of the cryptic NF-κB-binding sites marking
promoters for increased NF-κB recruitment. Importantly, H3
phosphorylation is not carried out directly by p38 MAPK, but
more likely through MSK1 [117].

experiment.system: LPS-stimulated myeloid cells
experiment.perturbation: LPS stimulation with p38 MAPK pathway inhibition
experiment.measurement: histone H3 Ser10 phosphorylation at inflammatory promoters and NF-kappaB recruitment

text: Recruitment of Ash2L-containing methyltransferase complexes during muscle differentiation requires p38 MAPK-mediated phosphorylation of MEF2D on Thr308 and Thr315, essential for histone H3 Lys4 modification and subsequent gene expression.

quotes.quote:
In this case, Ash2L recruitment requires p38 MAPK-
mediated phosphorylation of MEF2D on Thr308 and Thr315, which
is essential for histone H3 Lys4 modiﬁcation and subsequent gene
expression [119].

experiment.system: differentiating muscle cells
experiment.perturbation: p38 MAPK-mediated MEF2D phosphorylation at Thr308/Thr315
experiment.measurement: Ash2L complex recruitment, histone H3 Lys4 methylation and gene expression

text: In response to DNA damage p38alpha phosphorylates p18Hamlet in at least four threonine residues, increasing its stability; phosphorylated p18Hamlet enhances transcription of p53-dependent genes such as Noxa and is necessary for UV- or cisplatin-induced recruitment of p53 to the Noxa promoter.

quotes.quote:
In response to DNA
damage, p38α phosphorylates the p18Hamlet protein in at least
four threonine residues, increasing its stability. Phosphorylated
p18Hamlet enhances the transcription of several p53-dependent
genes, such as Noxa, involved in the apoptotic response.

p18Hamlet is necessary for the UV-
or cisplatin-induced recruitment of p53 to the Noxa promoter

experiment.system: mammalian cells subjected to genotoxic stress (UV or cisplatin)
experiment.perturbation: DNA damage; p38alpha-mediated phosphorylation of p18Hamlet
experiment.measurement: p18Hamlet stability, p53-dependent gene transcription and p53 promoter recruitment

numbers.quantity: threonine residues of p18Hamlet phosphorylated by p38alpha

text: p18Hamlet is required for incorporation of histone H2A.Z into the myogenin promoter, and overexpression of wild-type p18Hamlet, but not of a non-phosphorylatable mutant, suffices to initiate myogenesis; p38 MAPK-mediated phosphorylation of p18Hamlet appears necessary for SRCAP complex assembly.

quotes.quote:
p18Hamlet is required for the
incorporation of histone H2A.Z into the myogenin promoter,
which is a crucial event for the initiation of the myogenic
transcriptional programme. Differentiation conditions induce the
phosphorylation of p18Hamlet by p38 MAPK, and overexpression
of the wild-type p18Hamlet, but not of a non-phosphorylatable
mutant, sufﬁces to initiate myogenesis. Moreover, p38 MAPK-
mediated phosphorylation of p18Hamlet appears to be necessary
for assembly of the SRCAP complex.

experiment.system: muscle cells under differentiation conditions
experiment.perturbation: overexpression of wild-type versus non-phosphorylatable p18Hamlet
experiment.measurement: histone H2A.Z incorporation at myogenin promoter, SRCAP complex assembly and myogenesis

text: p38 MAPK signalling causes rapid inactivation of the ERK1/2 pathway in normal cells by stimulating physical association between PP2A and the MKK1/2-ERK1/2 complex, leading to MKK1/2 dephosphorylation.

quotes.quote:
p38 MAPK activity stimulates
the physical association between PP2A and the MKK1/2–ERK1/2
complex, leading to MKK1/2 dephosphorylation by PP2A.

experiment.system: normal mammalian cells
experiment.perturbation: modulation of p38 MAPK activity
experiment.measurement: PP2A association with MKK1/2–ERK1/2 and MKK1/2 dephosphorylation

text: p38alpha inactivates GSK3beta by direct phosphorylation of the C-terminal residue Ser389, leading to beta-catenin accumulation, primarily in brain and thymocytes; conversely GSK3beta inhibits p38 MAPK and JNK activation by phosphorylating MEKK4.

quotes.quote:
p38α also inactivates GSK3β by direct phosphorylation of the
C-terminal residue Ser389, leading to β-catenin accumulation.
This non-canonical p38 MAPK-dependent phosphorylation of
GSK3β seems to occur primarily in the brain and thymocytes

GSK3β
has been reported to inhibit p38 MAPK (and JNK) activation by
phosphorylating the MAP3K MEKK4 [134].

experiment.system: mouse brain and thymocytes and cultured cells
experiment.perturbation: p38alpha-mediated Ser389 phosphorylation of GSK3beta; GSK3beta phosphorylation of MEKK4
experiment.measurement: GSK3beta activity, beta-catenin levels and p38/JNK activation

text: Akt inhibits p38alpha activation, for example by phosphorylation of ASK1 on Ser83, while p38alpha negatively modulates Akt activity independently of PI3K by regulating the caveolin-1/PP2A interaction, and genetic ablation of p38alpha suppresses Akt activation in mouse macrophages.

quotes.quote:
shown that Akt inhibits the activation of p38α, for example by
phosphorylation of ASK1 on Ser83 [135]

p38α may negatively modulate Akt activity, independently
of PI3K (phosphoinositide 3-kinase), by regulating the interaction
between caveolin-1 and PP2A through a mechanism dependent on
cell attachment [137]. Finally, genetic ablation of p38α suppresses
Akt activation in mouse macrophages

experiment.system: cultured mammalian cells and mouse macrophages
experiment.perturbation: Akt-mediated ASK1 phosphorylation; genetic ablation of p38alpha
experiment.measurement: p38alpha activation and Akt activation

text: Sustained activation of p38 MAPK by stable expression of a constitutively active MKK6 (MKK6EE) is sufficient to induce a permanent and irreversible G1 cell-cycle arrest with morphological and biochemical features of senescence, and leads to growth arrest and terminal differentiation in rhabdomyosarcoma cells, whereas inflammatory cytokines that only transiently activate p38 MAPK do not promote differentiation in these cells.

quotes.quote:
sustained activation of p38
MAPK by stable expression of a constitutively active form of
MKK6 (MKK6EE) is sufﬁcient to induce a permanent and irr-
eversible G1 cell-cycle arrest with both morphological and
biochemical features of senescence [142]. Enforced activation
of p38 MAPK by MKK6EE also leads to growth arrest and
terminal differentiation in rhabdomyosarcoma cells. However,
p38 MAPK activation by inﬂammatory cytokines do not promote
differentiation in these cells

experiment.system: cultured mammalian cells including human rhabdomyosarcoma cells
experiment.perturbation: stable expression of constitutively active MKK6EE versus inflammatory cytokine stimulation
experiment.measurement: cell-cycle arrest, senescence markers and terminal differentiation

text: Negative-feedback mechanisms limit p38 MAPK signalling: p38alpha regulates MKK6 mRNA stability in non-stimulated cells, phosphorylates TAB1 leading to inhibition of TAK1, and induces up-regulation of phosphatases such as Wip1 and MKPs.

quotes.quote:
p38α regulates MKK6 mRNA stability in non-stimulated cells,
potentially limiting the intensity and duration of the signal [144].
Also, p38α phosphorylates TAB1, leading to inhibition of the
MAP3K TAK1

p38α induces the up-regulation, usually at the transcriptional
level, of phosphatases such as Wip1 and MKPs

experiment.system: cultured mammalian cells
experiment.perturbation: modulation of p38alpha activity
experiment.measurement: MKK6 mRNA stability, TAK1 activity and phosphatase expression

text: Mice with constitutive deletion of p38alpha die during embryonic development owing to a defect in placental organogenesis, and MKK3/MKK6-double-knockout mice also die during embryogenesis owing to a placental defect, whereas mice deficient only in MKK3 or MKK6 are viable but show immune response defects.

quotes.quote:
Mice
with a constitutive deletion of p38α die during embryonic
development owing to a defect in placental organogenesis [145–
147]. Interestingly, MKK3/MKK6-double-knockoutmice also die
during embryogenesis owing to a placental defect [25], whereas
mice deﬁcient only in MKK3 or MKK6 are viable, but show
defects in the immune response [67,148].

experiment.system: gene-targeted mice
experiment.perturbation: constitutive deletion of p38alpha, MKK3, MKK6 or both MKK3/MKK6
experiment.measurement: embryonic viability, placental development and immune responses

text: Conditional inactivation of p38alpha in adult mice significantly affects lung homoeostasis and results in enhanced proliferation of primary cells including cardiomyocytes, hepatocytes and haemopoietic cells, possibly via EGFR down-regulation or negative regulation of the JNK/c-Jun pathway.

quotes.quote:
Inactivation of p38α signiﬁcantly affects lung homoeostasis,
reﬂecting the importance of this pathway in the co-ordination of
proliferation and differentiation in lung epithelial cells [149,150].
Of note, p38α ablation results in enhanced proliferation of other
types of primary cells, including cardiomyocytes, hepatocytes
and haemopoietic cells [150,151].

experiment.system: adult mice with conditional p38alpha alleles and primary cells
experiment.perturbation: conditional inactivation/ablation of p38alpha
experiment.measurement: lung homoeostasis and cell proliferation

text: p38alpha-deficient mice are sensitized to K-RasG12V-induced lung tumorigenesis and chemically induced liver cancer, supporting a tumour suppressor function of p38alpha in vivo.

quotes.quote:
p38α-deﬁcient mice are sensitized to K-RasG12V-
induced lung tumorigenesis [149] or chemically induced liver
cancer [150,154], supporting the function of p38α as a tumour
suppressor in vivo.

experiment.system: p38alpha-deficient mice
experiment.perturbation: K-RasG12V expression or chemical carcinogen treatment
experiment.measurement: lung and liver tumour development

text: Mice expressing a dominant-negative p38alpha allele with activation-loop sites mutated (T180A and Y182F) show enhanced pancreatic islet proliferation and regeneration correlating with attenuated age-induced expression of CDK inhibitors relative to wild-type littermates of the same age.

quotes.quote:
the expression in mice of a dominant-negative allele of p38α
with the activation-loop phosphorylation sites mutated (T180A
and Y182F). The pancreatic islets of these mice show enhanced
proliferation and regeneration, which correlates with attenuated
age-induced expression of CDK inhibitors when compared with
wild-type littermates of the same age [155].

experiment.system: mice expressing dominant-negative p38alpha (T180A, Y182F)
experiment.perturbation: expression of dominant-negative p38alpha allele
experiment.measurement: pancreatic islet proliferation/regeneration and CDK inhibitor expression

text: Mice deficient in p38beta, p38gamma or p38delta are viable and were initially reported to have no obvious phenotypes, in contrast with p38alpha.

quotes.quote:
In contrast with p38α, mice deﬁcient in p38β, p38γ or p38δ are
viable and were initially reported to have no obvious phenotypes
[15,156].

experiment.system: gene-targeted mice lacking p38beta, p38gamma or p38delta
experiment.perturbation: genetic deletion of individual p38 family members
experiment.measurement: viability and phenotypic characterization

text: Mice lacking p38delta display improved glucose tolerance owing to enhanced insulin secretion from pancreatic beta-cells, correlating with PKD activation due to loss of p38delta-mediated inhibitory phosphorylation, and are protected against high-fat-feeding-induced insulin resistance and oxidative stress-mediated beta-cell failure; p38delta-deficient mice also have reduced susceptibility to skin carcinogenesis.

quotes.quote:
Mice lacking
p38δ display improved glucose tolerance owing to enhanced
insulin secretion from pancreatic β-cells, which correlates with
the activation of PKD (protein kinase D) owing to the lack
of p38δ-mediated inhibitory phosphorylation. Moreover, p38δ-
null mice are protected against high-fat-feeding-induced insulin
resistance and oxidative stress-mediated β-cell failure.

p38δ-deﬁcient mice have also reduced susceptibility to skin
carcinogenesis [158].

experiment.system: p38delta-null mice
experiment.perturbation: p38delta gene deletion; high-fat feeding; skin carcinogenesis protocol
experiment.measurement: glucose tolerance, insulin secretion, PKD activation, beta-cell survival and skin tumour development

text: p38gamma blocks premature differentiation of skeletal muscle satellite cells by promoting association between MyoD and the histone methyltransferase KMT1A, which act in a complex to repress premature myogenin expression, whereas p38alpha activity promotes skeletal muscle differentiation.

quotes.quote:
studies in mice have
suggested its role in blocking the premature differentiation
of satellite cells, a skeletal muscle stem cell population that
participates in adult muscle regeneration [159]. In particular, p38γ
promotes the association between the transcription factor MyoD
and the histone methyltransferase KMT1A, which act together
in a complex to repress the premature expression of myogenin.

since p38α activity is well known
to promote skeletal muscle differentiation at different levels [121].

experiment.system: mouse skeletal muscle satellite cells
experiment.perturbation: genetic manipulation of p38gamma in mice
experiment.measurement: MyoD–KMT1A association, myogenin expression and satellite cell differentiation

text: Pyridinyl-imidazole inhibitors such as SB203580 inhibit p38alpha and p38beta but not p38gamma and p38delta at low concentrations, a specificity based on Thr106 being replaced by methionine in p38gamma/p38delta; replacing Thr106 with methionine abolishes SB203580 binding to p38alpha whereas replacing Met106 in p38gamma and p38delta with threonine enhances drug sensitivity.

quotes.quote:
At low concentrations, these compounds inhibit
p38α and p38β, but not p38γ and p38δ (reviewed in [162]).

In particular, Thr106 of p38α and
p38β is replaced by methionine in p38γ and p38δ, precluding
inhibitor binding. In fact, replacing Thr106 with a more bulky
residue (such as methionine) abolishes SB203580 binding to
p38α, whereas replacing Met106 in p38γ and p38δ with threonine
enhances their sensitivity to the drug [163,164].

experiment.system: p38 MAPK family members and point mutants at residue 106
experiment.perturbation: treatment with SB203580; Thr106/Met106 substitutions
experiment.measurement: inhibitor binding and kinase inhibition

text: BIRB796 represents a class of p38 inhibitors that function allosterically, causing a conformational reorganization in the kinase that prevents ATP binding and activation, in contrast with the majority of ATP-competitive inhibitors.

quotes.quote:
a new class of inhibitors has also been
reported that function allosterically, such as BIRB796, leading
to a conformational reorganization in the kinase that prevents
ATP binding and activation [168].

experiment.system: p38 MAPK protein with small-molecule inhibitors
experiment.perturbation: treatment with the allosteric inhibitor BIRB796
experiment.measurement: kinase conformation, ATP binding and activation

text: Despite good anti-inflammatory effects in pre-clinical animal models, p38 MAPK inhibitors with diverse chemical structures have repeatedly failed in clinical trials, mainly due to side effects such as liver and neural problems.

quotes.quote:
Although p38 MAPK inhibitors with diverse chemical
structures have good anti-inﬂammatory effects in pre-clinical
animal models, they have repeatedly failed in clinical trials,
mainly due to side effects such as liver and neural problems
[170].

experiment.system: pre-clinical animal models and human clinical trials
experiment.perturbation: administration of p38 MAPK inhibitors
experiment.measurement: anti-inflammatory efficacy and adverse effects

text: Human cells contain 518 protein kinases, and MAPKs appear to be involved in most signal transduction pathways.

quotes.quote:
Eukaryotic cells contain a wide repertoire of protein
kinases (518 in human cells)

experiment.system: human cells
experiment.perturbation: observational (genome-wide kinase cataloguing)
experiment.measurement: number of protein kinases encoded

text: In Drosophila cells MEKK1 controls activation of p38 MAPKs by UV or peptidoglycan, heat-shock-induced activation signals through both MEKK1 and ASK1, and maximal activation of p38 MAPKs by hyperosmolarity requires four MAP3Ks.

quotes.quote:
in Drosophila cells, MEKK1 controls
the activation of p38 MAPKs by UV or peptidoglycan,
whereas heat-shock-induced activation signals through both
MEKK1 and ASK1, and maximal activation of p38 MAPKs by
hyperosmolarity requires four MAP3Ks [30].

experiment.system: Drosophila cells
experiment.perturbation: UV, peptidoglycan, heat shock or hyperosmolarity with specific MAP3K depletion
experiment.measurement: p38 MAPK activation

numbers.quantity: MAP3Ks required for maximal hyperosmolarity-induced p38 activation

text: TRAF6 is required for activation of p38 MAPKs and JNKs by TGFbeta receptors: TRAF6 interacts with TGFbeta receptors, this interaction is necessary for TGFbeta-induced auto-ubiquitination of TRAF6 promoting TAK1 activation, and TRAF6 regulates TAK1 independently of the canonical Smad pathway and of TGFbeta receptor kinase activity.

quotes.quote:
TRAF6 has been shown to be required for the
activation of p38 MAPKs (and JNKs) by TGFβ receptors [33,34].
TRAF6 interacts with TGFβ receptors, and this interaction
is necessary for the TGFβ-induced auto-ubiquitination of
TRAF6, promoting its association with and subsequent activation
of TAK1 [33,34]. Importantly, TRAF6 regulates the activation of
TAK1 independently of both the canonical Smad pathway and the
kinase activity of the TGFβ receptor.

experiment.system: mammalian cells with TGFbeta receptor signalling
experiment.perturbation: TGFbeta stimulation and TRAF6 manipulation
experiment.measurement: TRAF6 ubiquitination, TAK1 activation and p38 MAPK/JNK activation

text: In B-lymphocytes, beta2-adrenergic receptor stimulation induces PKA-dependent phosphorylation of HePTP on Ser23, inactivating HePTP and releasing bound p38 MAPK for phosphorylation by MAP2Ks and subsequent IgE up-regulation.

quotes.quote:
β2-adrenergic receptor stimulation induces the PKA
(protein kinase A)-dependent phosphorylation of HePTP on Ser23,
which inactivates HePTP and releases bound p38 MAPK, making
it available for phosphorylation by MAP2Ks and subsequent IgE
up-regulation [51].

experiment.system: B-lymphocytes
experiment.perturbation: beta2-adrenergic receptor stimulation
experiment.measurement: HePTP Ser23 phosphorylation, p38 MAPK activation and IgE production

text: Endocytosis of the mu-opioid receptor is controlled by p38alpha-dependent phosphorylation of the Rab5 effector EEA1, and clathrin-mediated EGFR internalization induced by inflammatory cytokines and UV irradiation depends on p38alpha-mediated phosphorylation of EGFR itself and of Rab5 effectors.

quotes.quote:
endocytosis of
the μ-opioid receptor, a key regulator of opioid pharmacological
effects, is controlled by the p38α-dependent phosphorylation of
the Rab5 effector EEA1 (early endosome antigen 1A) [108].
In addition, clathrin-mediated EGFR internalization induced by
inﬂammatory cytokines and UV irradiation depends on p38α-
mediated phosphorylation of EGFR itself as well as of Rab5
effectors [109].

neurin caused increased nuclear localization of all three

atively regulated by JNK1 (15). However, this phenotype could

ies of transgenic mice also demonstrate inhibition of NFAT-

text: AKT phosphorylation and Lys63-linked ubiquitylation of AKT and p85a were increased by TGF-b in wild-type but not Smad7-/- MEFs, consistent with a prior report that SMAD7 is required for TGF-b-induced AKT activation.

in wild-type MEFs, TGF-b induced polyubiquitylation and phosphorylation of AKT, neither of which was seen in p85−/−MEFs

polyubiquitylation of p85a was enhanced by TGF-b stimulation in wild-type but not in TRAF6−/−MEFs (Fig. 3B), and p85 underwent Lys63-linked ubiquitylation in a TRAF6 dose-dependent manner
TGF-b induced p85a ubiquitylation in PC-3U cells (Fig. 3D), as well as p85a ubiquitylation and AKT activation in RAW264.7 macrophages transfected with wild-type but not C70A mutant TRAF6

text: Prior work established TSC1 and TSC2 form a heterodimeric complex critical for cell growth regulation through RheB GTP hydrolysis antagonizing mTOR signaling, and disease-associated mutations in TSC1/TSC2 cause substantial decreases in protein level, suggesting protein turnover plays a critical role in TSC regulation but the ubiquitin ligase for TSC2 was previously unidentified.

Many disease-associated mu-tations in TSC1 and TSC2 result in a substantial de-crease in the level of hamartin and tuberin, respectively (Inoki et al. 2002; Nellist et al. 2005), suggesting that protein turnover plays a critical role in TSC regulation. text: BCR-induced MEK1 kinase activity was completely blocked by 10 µM LY294002, and MEK phosphorylation (detected by anti-phospho-MEK antibody) was similarly affected by PI 3-kinase inhibition.

text: 50 nM ionomycin closely mimics BCR-induced calcium influx but does not itself induce ERK phosphorylation, does not enhance BCR-induced ERK phosphorylation, and does not restore BCR-induced ERK phosphorylation in the presence of LY294002, indicating PI 3-kinase affects ERK through a calcium-independent pathway.

PI 3-kinase influences ERK by a calcium-independent pathway.

text: The EGFR kinase core has low catalytic efficiency in solution (kcat/KM = 0.0049 ± 0.0005 s-1mM-1), and introduction of the L834R lung-cancer mutation increases activity ~14-fold.

quotes.quote: the catalytic efficiency, kcat/KM, is 0.0049 ± 0.0005 s−1mM−1, Figure 2A
Introduction of the L834R mutation, commonly found in lung cancer patients, increases the activity of the kinase core by ~14-fold

experiment.perturbation: L834R lung-cancer mutation vs wild type

text: Attaching the juxtamembrane segment to the wild-type kinase domain increases catalytic efficiency to 0.33 ± 0.02 s-1mM-1, ~70-fold greater than the kinase core alone, achieved in solution without membrane concentration.

quotes.quote: The value of kcat/KM for the JM-kinase construct (0.33 ± 0.02 s−1mM−1) is ~70-fold greater than for the kinase core alone.

experiment.perturbation: addition of juxtamembrane segment to kinase core

text: Deletion of the JM-A segment reduces catalytic efficiency ten-fold, to 0.032 ± 0.003 s-1mM-1, showing the juxtamembrane segment is required for full activation.

quotes.quote: Deletion of the JM-A segment reduces catalytic efficiency by ten-fold, to 0.032 ± 0.003 s−1mM−1 (Figure 2A)

experiment.perturbation: deletion of JM-A segment
experiment.measurement: kinetic assay (kcat/KM) in solution

text: Mixing activator-impaired (V924R) and receiver-impaired (I682Q) JM-kinase constructs recovers ~50% of the activity of wild-type JM-kinase constructs in solution, while both mutants alone have low activity; activity is reduced significantly if JM-A is additionally missing from either mutant.

quotes.quote: mixing these constructs recovers ~50% of the activity of wild type JM-kinase constructs in solution
activity is reduced significantly if the JM-A segment on either the activator-impaired or the receiver-impaired kinase is missing

experiment.system: purified EGFR JM-kinase activator-impaired (V924R) and receiver-impaired (I682Q) constructs, in vitro

text: The core kinase domain is monomeric while the JM-kinase construct is predominantly dimeric with a dimerization KD of ~200 nM; deletion of JM-A raises the midpoint concentration to at least ~8 µM, a >40-fold increase in KD, evidencing a role for JM-A in dimerization.

quotes.quote: the dissociation constant (KD) for dimerization is estimated to be ~200 nM (Figure 2C)
Deletion of the JM-A segment increases the midpoint value of the concentration dependence curve to at least ~8 µM (Figure 2C)
The >40 fold increase in the estimated values for KD for dimerization upon deletion of the JM-A segment provides strong evidence for a role of the JM-A segment in dimerization.

experiment.system: purified EGFR JM-kinase construct (with and without JM-A), in vitro
experiment.perturbation: deletion of JM-A segment; concentration variation

text: In transfected COS7 cells at ~5-fold lower DNA levels than a previous study, intracellular-domain-only EGFR shows very low autophosphorylation, while a construct with the transmembrane segment (TM-ICD) shows high activity comparable to a GCN4-enforced-dimerization construct (GCN4-ICD), indicating the juxtamembrane/transmembrane effect resembles enforced dimerization.

quotes.quote: We transfected COS7 cells with a ~5-fold lower level of DNA than used in the previous study (Thiel and Carpenter, 2007) (Figure 2D).

The activity of the TM-ICD construct is about the same as that for the GCN4-ICD construct, indicating that the effect of the juxtamembrane segment, when fused to the transmembrane domain and localized to membranes, is comparable to that of enforced dimerization.

text: Introduction of the V924R mutation into the GCN4-ICD construct, expected to disrupt the asymmetric dimer interface, results in complete loss of activity, showing that even enforced dimerization requires formation of the asymmetric dimer for activity.

quotes.quote: Introduction of the V924R mutation in the GCN4-ICD construct, which is expected to disrupt the asymmetric dimer interface, results in a complete loss of activity (Figure 2D).

experiment.system: COS7 cells transfected with GCN4-ICD EGFR construct
experiment.perturbation: V924R activator-impairing mutation
experiment.measurement: immunoprecipitation and anti-phosphotyrosine Western blot

text: Analysis of the Her4 kinase domain crystal structure (bound to a covalent inhibitor, including the JM-B segment) reveals an asymmetric dimer in which the JM-B segment forms a 'juxtamembrane latch' running from the receiver's N-lobe across to engage the C-lobe of the activator kinase domain, a feature not noted by the original authors.

quotes.quote: Although the authors do not comment on this fact, the kinase domains in their crystal structure form an asymmetric dimer that is similar in general terms to that seen in other crystal structures for active forms of EGFR and Her4.

the rest of the JM-B segment, provided by the kinase domain in the receiver position, latches two kinase domains together by running along the surface of the C-lobe of the activator kinase domain (Figure 3A).

experiment.system: crystal structure of Her4 kinase domain bound to covalent inhibitor (PDB 2R4B)
experiment.perturbation: observational (crystallographic analysis)
experiment.measurement: X-ray crystal structure analysis

text: The last ten residues of JM-B had been previously visualized at the asymmetric dimer interface and shown to be critical for EGFR activation, but the role of the rest of the JM-B segment as a latch was not previously recognized.

quotes.quote: The last ten residues of JM-B (corresponding to Gly 672 to Ile 682 in EGFR) have been visualized previously at the asymmetric dimer interface, and are critical for EGFR activation (Zhang et al., 2006).

experiment.system: EGFR kinase domain asymmetric dimer structure (Zhang et al., 2006)
experiment.perturbation: observational (prior crystallographic/mutational study)
experiment.measurement: crystal structure and mutagenesis

text: A six-residue motif (EPLTPS) in the juxtamembrane latch closely matches a motif in the EGFR inhibitor Mig6 (EPLSPS, residues 323-327), suggesting Mig6 functions in part by blocking formation of the juxtamembrane latch.

quotes.quote: A six residue motif (EPLTPS) in the juxtamembrane latch is almost identical in sequence with six residues in Mig6 (residues 323–327, with sequence EPLSPS).
This indicates that part of the function of Mig6 is to prevent formation of the juxtamembrane latch.

experiment.system: sequence/structural comparison of Mig6 and EGFR juxtamembrane latch
experiment.perturbation: observational (sequence and structural modeling)
experiment.measurement: sequence alignment and structural docking model

text: Co-transfection of receiver-impaired and activator-impaired EGFR shows EGF-dependent activity; introducing the latch-disrupting R953A mutation only reduces activity when placed in the receiver-impaired (activator-serving) construct and has essentially no effect when placed in the activator-impaired (receiver-serving) construct, consistent with a closed dimer in which the latch is engaged only by the activator.

quotes.quote: If the mutation is introduced only in the receiver-impaired EGFR construct, which presumably serves only as an activator, activity is reduced in co-transfection experiments.
There is essentially no effect on EGFR activity if the R953A mutation is introduced in the activator-impaired kinase domain.

experiment.perturbation: R953A mutation disrupting juxtamembrane latch, introduced selectively into one variant

text: In full-length EGFR cell transfection assays, replacing Arg656 and Arg657 in the JM-A LRRLL motif with glycines significantly reduces activity more than alanine substitutions, and this differential effect (glycine weakens helix more than alanine) holds when mutated on either activator or receiver individually, supporting a helical JM-A conformation important on both protomers.

quotes.quote: This led to a significant reduction in EGFR activity (Figure 4B and Figure S3A).
The effect of alanine substitutions is smaller than that of glycine substitutions, consistent with a helical conformation for the JM-A segment (Figure 4B and Figure S3A).
replacement of Arg 656 and Arg 657 by glycines on either the activator or receiver kinase individually also results in a reduction of EGFR activity relative to alanine substitutions

experiment.system: full length EGFR transfected in mammalian cells, including activator-impaired/receiver-impaired variants
experiment.perturbation: glycine vs alanine substitution of Arg656/Arg657 in JM-A LRRLL motif

text: NMR on a 35-residue tandem-repeat JM-A peptide shows transient helical structure and NOE data consistent with an antiparallel rather than parallel orientation of the two JM-A helices, with the first leucine of the LRRLL motif at the d position of a heptad repeat.

quotes.quote: Data from Nuclear Overhauser Effect (NOE) experiments are consistent with an antiparallel rather than parallel orientation of two JM-A helices.

the significance of these NMR data arises from the evidence that it provides for a specific register in the antiparallel interaction, in which the first leucine of the LRRLL motif is at the d position of a heptad repeat, with the second two leucines at the g and a positions, respectively

text: Alignment of EGFR sequence onto the Her2 transmembrane NMR structure places Cα atoms corresponding to Arg647 ~20 Å apart, close to the 18 Å distance between the Cα atoms of Arg651 in the modeled antiparallel JM-A helix dimer, suggesting the JM-A and transmembrane dimers can be bridged by a short connecting segment.

text: Acidic sidechains (Asp979, Glu980, Glu981) in the 'electrostatic hook' turn form ion pairs with kinase domain residues (His749, His826, Lys828, Lys822) near the hinge region, and the C-terminal tail conformation following this hook mimics how the JM-B segment engages the activator C-lobe in the active latch, indicating the inactive dimer blocks formation of the activating juxtamembrane latch, similar to Mig6.

text: Eight lysine residues (689, 692, 704, 715 in each subunit) cluster on one face of the inactive symmetric dimer, opposite the region of negative electrostatic potential occupied by the engaged C-terminal tail, suggesting a membrane-docking orientation that would sequester the JM-A segments away from the membrane.

quotes.quote: Eight lysine residues (residues 689, 692, 704, 715 in each subunit) are clustered together on the face of the dimer that is opposite to the internally engaged position of the C-terminal tail, which is a region of negative electrostatic potential.

text: Several research groups had previously studied growth factor-induced SOS phosphorylation but did not reach the same conclusion: some studies suggested SOS1 phosphorylation induces disassembly of the Grb2-SOS1 complex terminating Ras activation, while others reported phosphorylation does not affect SOS1-Grb2 binding but instead induces dissociation of the Grb2-SOS complex from the activated EGF receptor; notably, none of these prior studies examined the role of multiplicity of phosphorylation sites.

the phosphorylation of SOS1 is suggested to induce disassembly of the Grb2-SOS1 complex, thereby termi-nating SOS1-dependent Ras activation (9–11). text: Curdlan-induced production of IL-10 and IL-2 by BMDCs was dependent on dectin-1, Syk and CARD9 but largely independent of the TLR adaptors MyD88 and TRIF.

text: Triggering a streptavidin-binding peptide-tagged wild-type dectin-1 with streptavidin-sepharose was sufficient to induce DC maturation and cytokine production, unlike a signaling-deficient dectin-1 mutant (Y15F), and this was unaffected by absence of MyD88 and TRIF, confirming dectin-1 triggering alone suffices for DC activation.

text: In HUVECs preexposed to flow, TNF-α-induced c-Jun and NF-κB transcriptional activity were significantly inhibited compared to static cells, while flow alone caused no significant increase.

Src kinase inactive form (Src-KN) significantly inhibited TNF-–induced c-Jun transcriptional activity in a dose-dependent manner

experiment.perturbation: PP2 (Src family kinase inhibitor) or transfection with kinase-inactive Src mutant, plus TNF-α stimulation

phosphatase,

crease in the GTP-bound Ras (59). ... They also showed that this interaction was unnecessary for

ity.

Consistent with a phospho-dependent interaction,

we asked whether the PMA-induced binding of SOS1 to 14-
3-3 would be blocked by pharmacological inhibition of MEK–

Secondly, we expressed a constitutively active allele of RSK1

down RSK expression using RNAi and found that this prevented
the PMA- and EGF-induced interaction of SOS1 with 14-3-
3 (Figure 4C).

Lck-deﬁcient JCaM1 cells, however, failed to activate either MAPK in response to anti-TCR, although phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA) was effective.

text: Edman degradation and HPLC mapping identified Tyr323 as the residue on p38 phosphorylated by Src family kinases and Zap70; the label was removed at cycle 27 of 30 cycles of Edman degradation, and this was confirmed using Y323F p38, in which Tyr182 phosphorylation by upstream MAPKK was unaffected by the Y323F substitution.

quotes.quote: the label was removed at cycle 27 (Fig. 4a, right inset). Based on the predicted tryptic cleavage products, this identiﬁed the site as Tyr323

verdict_note: The claim's clause 'confirmed using Y323F p38, in which Tyr182 phosphorylation by upstream MAPKK was unaffected by the Y323F substitution' misstates the paper: the text says substitution of Tyr182 (not Tyr323) with Phe had no effect on the tryptic profile at Tyr323 ('substitution of Tyr182 with a Phe had no effect on the profile of tryptic peptides'), the reverse relationship from what the claim asserts, and this point is unrelated to the Y323F confirmation of the Tyr323 site.

experiment.perturbation: in vitro kinase reaction, trypsin digestion
experiment.measurement: HPLC peptide mapping and Edman degradation sequencing

numbers.quantity: Edman degradation cycle at which radiolabel was removed

text: Lck enhanced the activity of wild-type p38 and Y342F p38 (an irrelevant tyrosine substitution) but had no effect on the activity of Y323F p38, and Zap70 also failed to enhance Y323F p38 activity, demonstrating that T cell Src family kinases and Zap70 activate p38 by phosphorylating Tyr323.

quotes.quote: Lck enhanced the activity of wild-type p38 and Y342F p38 (an irrelevant tyrosine substitution) but had no effect on the activity of Y323F p38 (Fig. 4b). Zap70 also failed to enhance Y323F p38 activity (Fig. 4c). Thus, T cell Src family kinases and Zap70 activate p38 by phosphorylating Tyr323.

experiment.perturbation: incubation with recombinant Lck or Zap70
experiment.measurement: in vitro kinase activity assay

text: TCR-mediated activation of Jurkat and primary CD4+ T cells, but not anti-IgM stimulation of primary B cells, resulted in an increase in p38 phosphorylated at Tyr323, detectable by a specific antiserum, and TCR-mediated activation of LAT-deficient JCaM2 cells still resulted in phosphorylation of p38 Tyr323, inhibitable by PP2.

quotes.quote: Notably, TCR-mediated activation of Jurkat and primary CD4+ T cells, but not stimulation of primary B cells mediated by anti-IgM, resulted in an increase in phosphorylated p38 detectable by antibodies speciﬁc for both phosphorylated Tyr323 and phosphorylated Thr180-Tyr182
Whereas TCR-mediated activation of LAT-deﬁcient JCaM2 cells was incapable of activating Erks, it did result in phos-phorylation of p38 Try323 in a way that could be inhibited by PP2

experiment.measurement: immunoblot with phospho-Tyr323-specific antiserum and phospho-Thr180-Tyr182 antibody

text: Zap70-deficient Jurkat subclone P116 failed to show anti-TCR-induced phosphorylation of p38 Tyr323 or Thr180-Tyr182; reconstitution with kinase-inactive Zap70 did not restore this, but reintroduction of wild-type Zap70 did, and since P116 cells have functional Lck, Lck is concluded to act upstream of Zap70 in activating p38.

quotes.quote: Unlike results with wild-type Jurkat cells, anti-TCR stimulation of P116 did not result in phosphorylation of p38 Tyr323 or Thr180-Tyr182. Recon-stitution of P116 cells with a kinase-inactive mutant of Zap70 (ref. 24) did not restore a normal phenotype, but reintroduction of wild-type Zap70 did. Because P116 cells have functional Lck25, we conclude that Lck is required for activation of Zap70, which in turn phosphorylates and activates p38.

experiment.perturbation: anti-TCR stimulation; reconstitution with kinase-inactive or wild-type Zap70
experiment.measurement: immunoblot for phospho-Tyr323 and phospho-Thr180-Tyr182 p38

text: In Jurkat cells transiently expressing Myc-tagged p38, wild-type p38 activity was upregulated by anti-TCR stimulation, whereas Y323F p38 activity was barely affected by anti-TCR; in contrast, both wild-type and Y323F p38 were stimulated to similar degrees by PMA, and Thr180-Tyr182 phosphorylation after TCR stimulation was much lower for Y323F p38.

quotes.quote: Notably, whereas wild-type p38 activity was upregulated by anti-TCR stimulation, Y323F p38 activity was barely affected; in contrast, both were stimu-lated to similar degrees by PMA. Similarly, phosphorylation of p38 Thr180-Tyr182 after TCR stimulation was much lower for Y323F p38.

experiment.perturbation: anti-TCR or PMA stimulation
experiment.measurement: immunoprecipitation and in vitro kinase activity assay, immunoblot

text: In T cells, activation-induced increase of Thr180-Tyr182 p38 phosphorylation was prevented by blockade of p38 activity with SB203580, whereas in activated B cells inhibition of p38 activity had no effect on Thr180-Tyr182 phosphorylation, indicating that dual phosphorylation is mediated by different mechanisms in T versus B cells.

quotes.quote: In T cells, the activation-induced increase of Thr180-Tyr182 phosphorylation was prevented by blockade of p38 activity. Inhibition of p38 activity had no effect on Thr180-Tyr182 phosphorylation in activated B cells.

experiment.system: purified CD4+ T cells and B cells
experiment.perturbation: anti-CD3 or anti-IgM stimulation with or without SB203580 (p38 inhibitor)
experiment.measurement: immunoblot for p38 Thr180-Tyr182 phosphorylation

text: Prior work had found that in Jurkat T cells p38 activation requires Zap70 and suggested that anti-TCR is coupled to p38 via the Vav guanine nucleotide-exchange factor and the small GTPase Rac1, though CD28 was co-triggered in those experiments; another study found that Rac2-deficient mice showed only modestly reduced p38 activation after TCR crosslinking, so a direct link from TCR to p38 through the classic MAPK cascade regulators had not been firmly established.

quotes.quote: In Jurkat T cells, it was found that p38 activation requires Zap70, and it was suggested that anti-TCR is coupled to p38 by the guanine nucleotide–exchange factor Vav and the small Rho family GTPase Rac1, but the costimulatory molecule CD28 was also triggered along with the TCR in those experiments26. In another study it was shown that mice deﬁcient in the hematopoietic-speciﬁc Rac2 protein demonstrate modestly reduced p38 activation after TCR crosslinking27. Thus, although it has been generally assumed, a direct link from the TCR to p38 through the usual upstream regulators of the MAPK cascade has not been ﬁrmly established.

experiment.system: Jurkat T cells (Salojin et al.); Rac2-deficient mouse T cells (Yu et al.)
experiment.perturbation: anti-TCR/CD28 costimulation; TCR crosslinking in Rac2-deficient mice
experiment.measurement: p38 activation assays

text: Prior work with GADD45a-deficient mice showed p38 is spontaneously activated in the absence of detectable MKK3 or MKK6 activity, and like TCR-activated normal T cell p38, p38 in primary resting Gadd45a-/- T cells was phosphorylated on Tyr323, supporting the idea that TCR-driven p38 activation is independent of upstream MAPKK.

quotes.quote: The idea that p38 activation by the TCR is independent of upstream MAPKK is supported by observations made using T cells from GADD45a-deﬁcient mice, whose p38 is sponta-neously activated in the absence of detectable MKK3 or MKK6 activity28. Like p38 from TCR-activated normal T cells, p38 in primary resting Gadd45a/ T cells was phosphorylated on Tyr323.

experiment.system: GADD45a-deficient mouse primary T cells
experiment.perturbation: genetic knockout of Gadd45a, observational resting state
experiment.measurement: assessment of MKK3/MKK6 activity and p38 Tyr323 phosphorylation

text: Modular response analysis uncovered different feedback regulation from Erk1/2 to Raf-1 depending on growth factor: a negative feedback for EGF stimulation and positive feedback for NGF stimulation.

text: Both EGF and NGF stimulated networks showed positive regulatory connections from Raf-1 to Mek1/2 to Erk1/2, and negative feedback between Erk1/2 and Mek1/2.

quotes.quote: We thus confirmed the positive regulatory connections from Raf-1 to Mek1/2 to Erk1/2, for both EGF and NGF stimulated cells. The observed negative feedback between Erk1/2 and Mek1/2 for both EGF and NGF activated networks has also been described in another cell system13, where Erk directly phosphorylates Mek1.

experiment.perturbation: siRNA knockdown of Raf-1/B-Raf, Mek1/2, Erk1/2 with EGF or NGF stimulation
experiment.measurement: modular response analysis (MRA) local response coefficients

text: The likelihood that the feedback from Erk to Raf is negative on EGF and positive on NGF stimulation was highly significant (P = 0.96 and P = 1.00, respectively).

quotes.quote: The likelihood that the feedback from Erk to Raf is negative on EGF and positive on NGF stimulation was highly significant (P = 0.96 and P = 1.00, respectively).

experiment.perturbation: siRNA perturbation with EGF or NGF stimulation
experiment.measurement: Monte Carlo simulation of local response coefficient probability distributions from MRA

probability Erk-Raf feedback positive on NGF

text: Inhibition of Mek activity using PD184352 resulted in the loss of Raf-1-sustained activity after NGF stimulation, confirming the existence of the NGF-driven positive feedback.

quotes.quote: Furthermore, inhibition of Mek activity using PD184352 resulted in the loss of Raf-1-sustained activity after NGF stimulation (see Supplementary Information, Fig. S1e), confirming the existence of the NGF-driven positive feedback.

quotes.quote: Furthermore, EGF stimulation in conjunction with PKC activation by PMA gave rise to a sustained Erk1/2 activation profile (Fig. 4c and see Supplementary Information, Fig. S4c). ... Importantly, the cells activated with EGF, in conjunction with PMA, differentiated as if stimulated by NGF (Fig. 4d and see Supplementary Information, Fig. S4e). Moreover, this was shown to be specifically dependent on PKCδ using RNAi experiments. On downregulation of PKCδ levels, the number of cells that differentiated was substantially lower than on NGF stimulation or on EGF stimulation in the presence of PMA (Fig. 4d and see Supplementary Information, Fig. S4e).
